skills.description: Use when raw, noisy MinION 16S rRNA amplicon reads (2D or 1D2) must be clustered de novo into OTUs and accurate full-length consensus sequences called without reference-based mapping.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-consensus-calling
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-consensus-calling Use when raw, noisy MinION 16S rRNA amplicon reads (2D or 1D2) must be clustered de novo into OTUs and accurate full-length consensus sequences called without reference-based mapping. Reads can be confidently mapped to a complete reference database (e.g., SILVA) and reference-based clustering is acceptable — the de novo route here is specifically motivated by incorrect mapping and discarded reads for organisms absent from the reference Only taxonomy classification is needed and closely related sequences need not be differentiated — classification-only approaches risk false detections but suffice for coarse profiling Input is already consensus-quality short-read (e.g., Illumina MiSeq) data with low error rates; the homopolymer-deletion error profile addressed here is nanopore-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 De novo generation of full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences from noisy Oxford Nanopore amplicon reads (2D/1D2 MinION), using nanoClust read partitioning-based clustering and within-cluster consensus calling after chopSeq fragmentation and orientation correction, achieving ~99.5% accuracy without reference databases. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: De novo generation of full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences from noisy Oxford Nanopore amplicon reads (2D/1D2 MinION), using nanoClust read partitioning-based clustering and within-cluster consensus calling after chopSeq fragmentation and orientation correction, achieving ~99.5% accuracy without reference databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads can be confidently mapped to a complete reference database (e.g., SILVA) and reference-based clustering is acceptable — the de novo route here is specifically motivated by incorrect mapping and discarded reads for organisms absent from the reference Only taxonomy classification is needed and closely related sequences need not be differentiated — classification-only approaches risk false detections but suffice for coarse profiling Input is already consensus-quality short-read (e.g., Illumina MiSeq) data with low error rates; the homopolymer-deletion error profile addressed here is nanopore-specific

skills.description: Use when you have full-length 16S rRNA consensus sequences built de novo from nanopore amplicon reads (2D or 1D2) and need a quantitative accuracy metric by aligning them to a SILVA reference of the known organism, e.g., to characterize a reads-per-consensus accuracy curve.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-reference-alignment Use when you have full-length 16S rRNA consensus sequences built de novo from nanopore amplicon reads (2D or 1D2) and need a quantitative accuracy metric by aligning them to a SILVA reference of the known organism, e.g., to characterize a reads-per-consensus accuracy curve. The true organism reference sequence is unknown or the community is uncharacterized — the article emphasizes de novo consensus generation precisely to avoid reliance on reference databases Sequences are raw noisy nanopore reads rather than post-nanoClust consensus sequences; raw read error rates make direct reference-identity uninformative Data are short Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM amplicon reads rather than full-length ONT MinION amplicon consensus sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aligns de novo nanoClust-derived full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences against a SILVA 16S reference sequence of the target organism and computes sequence identity as the consensus accuracy metric, used to characterize how accuracy changes with reads-per-OTU depth (e.g., >99% beyond 5 reads, plateau at ~10-15, stable at >=50). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Aligns de novo nanoClust-derived full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences against a SILVA 16S reference sequence of the target organism and computes sequence identity as the consensus accuracy metric, used to characterize how accuracy changes with reads-per-OTU depth (e.g., >99% beyond 5 reads, plateau at ~10-15, stable at >=50).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The true organism reference sequence is unknown or the community is uncharacterized — the article emphasizes de novo consensus generation precisely to avoid reliance on reference databases Sequences are raw noisy nanopore reads rather than post-nanoClust consensus sequences; raw read error rates make direct reference-identity uninformative Data are short Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM amplicon reads rather than full-length ONT MinION amplicon consensus sequences

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a 1D CNN architecture and input signal length when classifying RNA classes directly from raw nanopore signal windows and prediction speed on CPU/GPU must be traded against accuracy.
skills.name: 1d-convolutional-network-hyperparameter-training
skills.search_text: 1d-convolutional-network-hyperparameter-training Decision support for choosing a 1D CNN architecture and input signal length when classifying RNA classes directly from raw nanopore signal windows and prediction speed on CPU/GPU must be traded against accuracy. Reads are already basecalled sequence — sequence-based adaptive sampling (basecalling + mapping to a target list) is the alternative, not signal-space CNN training The target RNA class has poorly characterized 3'-end signal (e.g., lncRNAs with cell type-specific expression), which the article notes remains challenging to identify accurately Input is bulk-fast5 playback testing of an already-trained RISER model rather than model development and hyperparameter selection http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains and hyperparameter-benchmarks 1D convolutional architectures (vanilla CNN, ResNet, TCN) on the first ≤4 s of raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) signals for mRNA/non-mRNA binary classification, selecting the architecture that best balances accuracy against per-batch prediction latency for real-time read-until deployment. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Trains and hyperparameter-benchmarks 1D convolutional architectures (vanilla CNN, ResNet, TCN) on the first ≤4 s of raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) signals for mRNA/non-mRNA binary classification, selecting the architecture that best balances accuracy against per-batch prediction latency for real-time read-until deployment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already basecalled sequence — sequence-based adaptive sampling (basecalling + mapping to a target list) is the alternative, not signal-space CNN training The target RNA class has poorly characterized 3'-end signal (e.g., lncRNAs with cell type-specific expression), which the article notes remains challenging to identify accurately Input is bulk-fast5 playback testing of an already-trained RISER model rather than model development and hyperparameter selection

skills.description: Use when MinION amplicon data from NanoAmpli-Seq (Calus et al. 2018) exists as both 2D and 1D2 basecalled read sets (single-organism and multi-organism mock communities) and each set must be processed and compared separately, e.g. to reproduce OTU-inflation benchmarks.
skills.name: 2d-vs-1d2-basecalling-readset-handling
skills.search_text: 2d-vs-1d2-basecalling-readset-handling Use when MinION amplicon data from NanoAmpli-Seq (Calus et al. 2018) exists as both 2D and 1D2 basecalled read sets (single-organism and multi-organism mock communities) and each set must be processed and compared separately, e.g. to reproduce OTU-inflation benchmarks. Reads are not INC-Seq consensus reads corrected by chopSeq (e.g., raw noisy nanopore reads intended for reference mapping) — the per-mode read-set handling is defined for the NanoAmpli-Seq post-chopSeq full-length amplicons The analysis goal is diversity estimation via the partition-based nanoClust approach rather than benchmarking direct clustering behaviour — pooling or reference-based workflows would be the intended path Data comes from a single basecalling mode only and no 2D-vs-1D2 comparison is required — then a single read-set pipeline suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Handles the 2D and 1D2 MinION basecalled read sets of the NanoAmpli-Seq workflow as parallel, separately processed datasets — running each (e.g., post-chopSeq full-length amplicon reads) through clustering/OTU-counting steps independently so 2D vs 1D2 behaviour (e.g., OTU inflation and singleton fractions) can be compared and validated against reported counts. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Handles the 2D and 1D2 MinION basecalled read sets of the NanoAmpli-Seq workflow as parallel, separately processed datasets — running each (e.g., post-chopSeq full-length amplicon reads) through clustering/OTU-counting steps independently so 2D vs 1D2 behaviour (e.g., OTU inflation and singleton fractions) can be compared and validated against reported counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not INC-Seq consensus reads corrected by chopSeq (e.g., raw noisy nanopore reads intended for reference mapping) — the per-mode read-set handling is defined for the NanoAmpli-Seq post-chopSeq full-length amplicons The analysis goal is diversity estimation via the partition-based nanoClust approach rather than benchmarking direct clustering behaviour — pooling or reference-based workflows would be the intended path Data comes from a single basecalling mode only and no 2D-vs-1D2 comparison is required — then a single read-set pipeline suffices

skills.description: Use when comparing nanopore sequencing chemistries (2D vs 1D2) for artifacts such as tandem repeats in INC-Seq consensus reads, or when testing whether an artifact metric depends on the aligner used during consensus calling.
skills.name: 2d-vs-1d2-run-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: 2d-vs-1d2-run-comparison-analysis Use when comparing nanopore sequencing chemistries (2D vs 1D2) for artifacts such as tandem repeats in INC-Seq consensus reads, or when testing whether an artifact metric depends on the aligner used during consensus calling. Input reads are raw nanopore reads rather than chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads — repeat patterns in raw noisy reads are not the target of this comparison. The analysis goal is consensus accuracy or homopolymer error profiling (e.g. the 99.5% accuracy or deletion-in-homopolymer findings) rather than chemistry-dependent tandem repeat structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A comparative analysis skill that contrasts tandem repeat prevalence and repeat length distributions in chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads between ONT MinION 2D and 1D2 sequencing chemistries, and tests dependence on the aligner used during consensus calling. It distinguishes the unimodal 2D repeat-length distribution from the longer, bimodal 1D2 distribution. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: A comparative analysis skill that contrasts tandem repeat prevalence and repeat length distributions in chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads between ONT MinION 2D and 1D2 sequencing chemistries, and tests dependence on the aligner used during consensus calling. It distinguishes the unimodal 2D repeat-length distribution from the longer, bimodal 1D2 distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are raw nanopore reads rather than chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads — repeat patterns in raw noisy reads are not the target of this comparison. The analysis goal is consensus accuracy or homopolymer error profiling (e.g. the 99.5% accuracy or deletion-in-homopolymer findings) rather than chemistry-dependent tandem repeat structure.

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore FAST5 reads from plant genomes (A. thaliana, O. sativa, B. nigra) must be converted into per-read 5mC probabilities and per-site methylation frequencies across CG/CHG/CHH contexts.
skills.name: 5mc-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: 5mc-methylation-calling Use when raw Nanopore FAST5 reads from plant genomes (A. thaliana, O. sativa, B. nigra) must be converted into per-read 5mC probabilities and per-site methylation frequencies across CG/CHG/CHH contexts. Input is short-read bisulfite sequencing data (this skill consumes native Nanopore signal; bisulfite is used here only as the gold-standard reference for training/evaluation) Non-plant 5mC or other modifications (e.g. 6mA, 5hmC) — the pre-trained arabnrice2-1 model was trained on A. thaliana/O. sativa 5mC only R10.4.1/POD5-era data handled with modern tools — Tombo (R9 path) is deprecated by ONT (see Remora); the R10 route uses Dorado basecalling instead of Guppy+Tombo http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Detects genome-wide 5mC cytosine methylation in all three sequence contexts (CG/CHG/CHH) from plant Oxford Nanopore reads using DeepSignal-plant, a BiLSTM deep-learning model trained on A. thaliana/O. sativa R9.4 data. It replaces CpG-only or statistics-based methods (Tombo, nanopolish, Megalodon) that miss non-CpG methylation abundant in plant genomes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Detects genome-wide 5mC cytosine methylation in all three sequence contexts (CG/CHG/CHH) from plant Oxford Nanopore reads using DeepSignal-plant, a BiLSTM deep-learning model trained on A. thaliana/O. sativa R9.4 data. It replaces CpG-only or statistics-based methods (Tombo, nanopolish, Megalodon) that miss non-CpG methylation abundant in plant genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read bisulfite sequencing data (this skill consumes native Nanopore signal; bisulfite is used here only as the gold-standard reference for training/evaluation) Non-plant 5mC or other modifications (e.g. 6mA, 5hmC) — the pre-trained arabnrice2-1 model was trained on A. thaliana/O. sativa 5mC only R10.4.1/POD5-era data handled with modern tools — Tombo (R9 path) is deprecated by ONT (see Remora); the R10 route uses Dorado basecalling instead of Guppy+Tombo

skills.description: Use when FASTQ files from long-read (ONT/PacBio) sequencing of 10x Genomics scRNA-seq cDNA libraries or targeted amplicons need alignment, variant calling, and per-cell genotype calls keyed by 10x cell barcodes.
skills.name: 5p10xgex-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: 5p10xgex-pipeline-execution Use when FASTQ files from long-read (ONT/PacBio) sequencing of 10x Genomics scRNA-seq cDNA libraries or targeted amplicons need alignment, variant calling, and per-cell genotype calls keyed by 10x cell barcodes. Input data are Illumina short-read libraries, since short-read sequencing is suboptimal for long fragments and cannot resolve structural transcriptomic variants such as fusions or isoforms The goal is full-transcriptome quantification rather than targeted genotyping of specific loci; nanoranger targets loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcript lengths shorter than 4 kB Cells lack 5'-anchored 10x Genomics cDNA structure (e.g. 3'-only chemistries), since the pipeline depends on 5' cell barcodes and UMIs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Executes the nanoranger long-read single-cell analysis pipeline in 5p10XGEX mode, aligning amplicon reads from 5'-anchored 10x Genomics whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries and calling SNVs to build per-cell genotyping matrices for somatic mutations. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Executes the nanoranger long-read single-cell analysis pipeline in 5p10XGEX mode, aligning amplicon reads from 5'-anchored 10x Genomics whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries and calling SNVs to build per-cell genotyping matrices for somatic mutations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are Illumina short-read libraries, since short-read sequencing is suboptimal for long fragments and cannot resolve structural transcriptomic variants such as fusions or isoforms The goal is full-transcriptome quantification rather than targeted genotyping of specific loci; nanoranger targets loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcript lengths shorter than 4 kB Cells lack 5'-anchored 10x Genomics cDNA structure (e.g. 3'-only chemistries), since the pipeline depends on 5' cell barcodes and UMIs

skills.description: Use when encoding protein sequences with property-based autocorrelation descriptors (e.g. NMBAC) and you need the six AAindex property tables — hydrophobicity, solvent accessibility, side-chain volume, polarity, polarizability, net charge index — standardized per amino acid.
skills.name: aaindex-physicochemical-property-retrieval
skills.search_text: aaindex-physicochemical-property-retrieval Use when encoding protein sequences with property-based autocorrelation descriptors (e.g. NMBAC) and you need the six AAindex property tables — hydrophobicity, solvent accessibility, side-chain volume, polarity, polarizability, net charge index — standardized per amino acid. Sequences contain non-standard amino acids — the property tables and descriptor are defined over the 20 natural amino acids only The descriptor computation is already done and feature_NMBAC_*.mat files are available for the target dataset (PDB186/PDB594/PDB1075) The goal is evolutionary-profile encoding (PSSM-DBT or PSSM-DWT), which uses PSI-BLAST PSSMs rather than AAindex property tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Retrieves amino acid physicochemical property value sets (six properties from the AAindex Database) and standardizes them across the 20 natural amino acids so they can drive autocorrelation descriptors such as the 200-dimension NMBAC used in iDBP-DEP. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Retrieves amino acid physicochemical property value sets (six properties from the AAindex Database) and standardizes them across the 20 natural amino acids so they can drive autocorrelation descriptors such as the 200-dimension NMBAC used in iDBP-DEP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences contain non-standard amino acids — the property tables and descriptor are defined over the 20 natural amino acids only The descriptor computation is already done and feature_NMBAC_*.mat files are available for the target dataset (PDB186/PDB594/PDB1075) The goal is evolutionary-profile encoding (PSSM-DBT or PSSM-DWT), which uses PSI-BLAST PSSMs rather than AAindex property tables

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare genome annotation methods (e.g., StringTie assembly-based annotation vs ab-initio/evidence-driven predictors like BRAKER1/2, TSEBRA, AUGUSTUS) on genomes with known reference GTFs.
skills.name: ab-initio-gene-prediction-benchmarking
skills.search_text: ab-initio-gene-prediction-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively compare genome annotation methods (e.g., StringTie assembly-based annotation vs ab-initio/evidence-driven predictors like BRAKER1/2, TSEBRA, AUGUSTUS) on genomes with known reference GTFs. The organism lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI-available GTF annotation, since the pipeline requires both (e.g., no reference GTF means no ground truth for gffcompare). You need validated protein-level evidence for novel isoforms rather than structural annotation benchmarking — the F1 scores do not confirm protein products. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark gene prediction pipelines (annotate_my_genomes vs BRAKER1, BRAKER2, TSEBRA, AUGUSTUS) by comparing each pipeline's GTF against a reference annotation with gffcompute and compiling precision, recall, and harmonic-mean F1-score at six annotation levels. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Benchmark gene prediction pipelines (annotate_my_genomes vs BRAKER1, BRAKER2, TSEBRA, AUGUSTUS) by comparing each pipeline's GTF against a reference annotation with gffcompute and compiling precision, recall, and harmonic-mean F1-score at six annotation levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI-available GTF annotation, since the pipeline requires both (e.g., no reference GTF means no ground truth for gffcompare). You need validated protein-level evidence for novel isoforms rather than structural annotation benchmarking — the F1 scores do not confirm protein products.

skills.description: Use when you need to attribute measured performance of a multi-stage classification or analysis pipeline to a specific stage, especially to test whether a stage added to overcome batch effects or other confounders is genuinely critical.
skills.name: ablation-comparison-of-pipeline-stages
skills.search_text: ablation-comparison-of-pipeline-stages Use when you need to attribute measured performance of a multi-stage classification or analysis pipeline to a specific stage, especially to test whether a stage added to overcome batch effects or other confounders is genuinely critical. The pipeline has only one stage or no parameter exists to disable the stage under test, so an ablated variant cannot be run on identical inputs Query and reference data lack significant batch effects or uncovered cell types, so the stage under test (e.g. second-round RBC) is expected to have little effect and the ablation would not be informative True query labels are unavailable, making accuracy-based comparison between modes impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify the contribution of an individual pipeline stage (e.g. scMAGIC's second-round reference-based classification) by running the full pipeline versus a variant with the stage disabled, then computing accuracy in both modes on the same query data and reference to isolate the stage's effect. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Quantify the contribution of an individual pipeline stage (e.g. scMAGIC's second-round reference-based classification) by running the full pipeline versus a variant with the stage disabled, then computing accuracy in both modes on the same query data and reference to isolate the stage's effect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline has only one stage or no parameter exists to disable the stage under test, so an ablated variant cannot be run on identical inputs Query and reference data lack significant batch effects or uncovered cell types, so the stage under test (e.g. second-round RBC) is expected to have little effect and the ablation would not be informative True query labels are unavailable, making accuracy-based comparison between modes impossible

skills.description: Use when you need contiguity and N-content statistics on a draft assembly or gap-filled scaffolds (e.g., after ntLink gap_fill) to judge whether scaffold gaps were filled with real sequence rather than ambiguous Ns.
skills.name: abyss-assembly-fasta-statistics
skills.search_text: abyss-assembly-fasta-statistics Use when you need contiguity and N-content statistics on a draft assembly or gap-filled scaffolds (e.g., after ntLink gap_fill) to judge whether scaffold gaps were filled with real sequence rather than ambiguous Ns. The assembly contains no N-runs/scaffold gaps (e.g., a pure contig assembly), where --split-scaffold contig-vs-scaffold comparisons are uninformative You need read-level or variant-level QC rather than assembly-level contiguity and N-content statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute assembly contiguity and N-content statistics (NG50/NGA50, # N's per 100 kbp) on scaffolds using abyss-fac from ABySS v2.3.0+ and QUAST with --split-scaffold, to quantify gap-filling quality after ntLink scaffolding. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Compute assembly contiguity and N-content statistics (NG50/NGA50, # N's per 100 kbp) on scaffolds using abyss-fac from ABySS v2.3.0+ and QUAST with --split-scaffold, to quantify gap-filling quality after ntLink scaffolding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly contains no N-runs/scaffold gaps (e.g., a pure contig assembly), where --split-scaffold contig-vs-scaffold comparisons are uninformative You need read-level or variant-level QC rather than assembly-level contiguity and N-content statistics

skills.description: Use when you have per-test annotation accuracies for multiple RBC methods across many benchmark tests and need to compare performance stability as classification difficulty (batch effects, incomplete reference coverage) increases.
skills.name: accuracy-versus-difficulty-regression
skills.search_text: accuracy-versus-difficulty-regression Use when you have per-test annotation accuracies for multiple RBC methods across many benchmark tests and need to compare performance stability as classification difficulty (batch effects, incomplete reference coverage) increases. skills.search_text: alignment-based-ground-truth-overlap-generation Use when benchmarking an overlap detection tool (e.g. Fedrann, minimap2, MHAP) on simulated long-read datasets where a reference genome exists, so true overlaps can be derived from read-to-reference alignments. Real (non-simulated) reads with no reference genome — ground truth from read-to-reference alignment is not available and assembly-based benchmarks (e.g. BUSCO with primates_odb10) are more appropriate Evaluation of final assembly contiguity/quality rather than overlap graph quality — use assembly metrics instead Reads shorter than the paper's reference-read cutoffs (length < 5 kb, aligned fraction < 50%) would be excluded from ground truth and bias the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Generates ground-truth read overlap sets by aligning simulated long reads back to their reference sequence with minimap2 and applying the FEDRANN paper's alignment and reference-read filters, enabling quantitative evaluation of overlap graph error rates. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Generates ground-truth read overlap sets by aligning simulated long reads back to their reference sequence with minimap2 and applying the FEDRANN paper's alignment and reference-read filters, enabling quantitative evaluation of overlap graph error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real (non-simulated) reads with no reference genome — ground truth from read-to-reference alignment is not available and assembly-based benchmarks (e.g. BUSCO with primates_odb10) are more appropriate Evaluation of final assembly contiguity/quality rather than overlap graph quality — use assembly metrics instead Reads shorter than the paper's reference-read cutoffs (length < 5 kb, aligned fraction < 50%) would be excluded from ground truth and bias the comparison

skills.description: Use when running TULIP with multiple nanopore alignment files (e.g. R7.3, R9 1D/2D, R9.4 1D against eel_seeds_285.fasta) and a config file mapping each short SAM to its original FASTA is required.
skills.name: alignment-configuration-file-preparation
skills.search_text: alignment-configuration-file-preparation Use when running TULIP with multiple nanopore alignment files (e.g. R7.3, R9 1D/2D, R9.4 1D against eel_seeds_285.fasta) and a config file mapping each short SAM to its original FASTA is required. Input alignments are not in SAM format (earlier TULIP versions supported e.g. DALIGNER output, but current TULIP 0.4 accepts SAM only) Read identifiers are not unique per FASTA file because data were naively concatenated — the config-file approach exists precisely to avoid concatenation http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Prepare a TULIP configuration file (alignments.txt) that tab-delimits each SAM alignment file with its format token ('sam') and the original long-read FASTA, after generating chemistry-specific BWA MEM alignments of nanopore reads against 285 bp seed sequences. TULIP reads this file to associate each seed-alignment set with the corresponding raw reads during graph construction. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Prepare a TULIP configuration file (alignments.txt) that tab-delimits each SAM alignment file with its format token ('sam') and the original long-read FASTA, after generating chemistry-specific BWA MEM alignments of nanopore reads against 285 bp seed sequences. TULIP reads this file to associate each seed-alignment set with the corresponding raw reads during graph construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments are not in SAM format (earlier TULIP versions supported e.g. DALIGNER output, but current TULIP 0.4 accepts SAM only) Read identifiers are not unique per FASTA file because data were naively concatenated — the config-file approach exists precisely to avoid concatenation

skills.description: Use when benchmarking genome polishing or assembly accuracy against a trusted reference: fragment the reference into pseudo-long reads, align them to each assembly, and filter mappings by query coverage and identity thresholds to compute comparable QV-style accuracy metrics.
skills.name: alignment-coverage-identity-filtering
skills.search_text: alignment-coverage-identity-filtering Use when benchmarking genome polishing or assembly accuracy against a trusted reference: fragment the reference into pseudo-long reads, align them to each assembly, and filter mappings by query coverage and identity thresholds to compute comparable QV-style accuracy metrics. The ground truth is a variant benchmark set (e.g. GIAB high-confidence variants) rather than a trusted reference genome, in which case variant-counting evaluation (as done for HG005 against GRCh37) is more appropriate The assembly lacks a high-quality trusted reference, so k-mer-based QV estimation with Merqury/yak is the only feasible accuracy assessment Alignments come from noisy real long reads rather than reference-derived pseudo-reads, where coverage/identity filtering thresholds calibrated for pseudo-reads would be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 An alignment-based accuracy evaluation scheme in which ground-truth reference sequences (pseudo-long reads) are aligned to genome assemblies and only high-quality alignments are retained — filtering out mappings with query coverage ≤90% or alignment identity ≤98% — before computing alignment-identity QV and 100%-identity read fractions to compare polishing tools such as NextPolish2 and RM. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: An alignment-based accuracy evaluation scheme in which ground-truth reference sequences (pseudo-long reads) are aligned to genome assemblies and only high-quality alignments are retained — filtering out mappings with query coverage ≤90% or alignment identity ≤98% — before computing alignment-identity QV and 100%-identity read fractions to compare polishing tools such as NextPolish2 and RM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ground truth is a variant benchmark set (e.g. GIAB high-confidence variants) rather than a trusted reference genome, in which case variant-counting evaluation (as done for HG005 against GRCh37) is more appropriate The assembly lacks a high-quality trusted reference, so k-mer-based QV estimation with Merqury/yak is the only feasible accuracy assessment Alignments come from noisy real long reads rather than reference-derived pseudo-reads, where coverage/identity filtering thresholds calibrated for pseudo-reads would be invalid

skills.description: Use when genome FASTA references (e.g. A. thaliana TAIR10 GCF_000001735.4 or O. sativa IRGSP-1.0) must be scanned for near-identical duplicated regions to build paired comparison units for methylation contrasts.
skills.name: alignment-filtering-threshold-application
skills.search_text: alignment-filtering-threshold-application Use when genome FASTA references (e.g. A. thaliana TAIR10 GCF_000001735.4 or O. sativa IRGSP-1.0) must be scanned for near-identical duplicated regions to build paired comparison units for methylation contrasts. When the analysis goal is per-read or per-site methylation calling from Nanopore signals — use the DeepSignal-plant call_mods/call_freq pipeline instead When studying highly repetitive regions rather than duplicated pairs — bisulfite/alignment approaches may not cover them and this pairing step is not designed for that question When the input is already a repeat-pair table or methylation-frequency table — proceed directly to the |rmet1−rmet2| >= 0.5 differential-methylation filtering step http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identifies segmental-duplication repeat pairs by whole-genome self-alignment with MUMmer, retaining aligned region pairs longer than 100 bp with identity score >0.99 that contain at least one cytosine, to serve as the substrate for downstream differential-methylation analysis. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Identifies segmental-duplication repeat pairs by whole-genome self-alignment with MUMmer, retaining aligned region pairs longer than 100 bp with identity score >0.99 that contain at least one cytosine, to serve as the substrate for downstream differential-methylation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is per-read or per-site methylation calling from Nanopore signals — use the DeepSignal-plant call_mods/call_freq pipeline instead When studying highly repetitive regions rather than duplicated pairs — bisulfite/alignment approaches may not cover them and this pairing step is not designed for that question When the input is already a repeat-pair table or methylation-frequency table — proceed directly to the |rmet1−rmet2| >= 0.5 differential-methylation filtering step

skills.description: Use when scaffolding or mate-pair linking requires read placement on contigs for short (Illumina) or long (PacBio/Nanopore) reads and full alignment is too slow or unnecessary.
skills.name: alignment-free-read-placement
skills.search_text: alignment-free-read-placement Use when scaffolding or mate-pair linking requires read placement on contigs for short (Illumina) or long (PacBio/Nanopore) reads and full alignment is too slow or unnecessary. Base-level alignment accuracy (e.g., CIGAR strings, mismatch positions) is required rather than contig-level placement/linking Gap-size estimation depends on precise insert-size distributions of 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL mate-pair data, where read-pair orientation may be unknown (article flags this as challenging) Insert-size requirement exceeds the actual long-read size, since the synthetic library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read length http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Place short or long reads onto contigs without base-level alignment using Fast-SG: an ntHash rolling-hash k-mer look-up against a unique-k-mer index (KMC3 + BBHash + quasi_dictionary), windowed hit-vector scoring, and pair rescue, emitting pair locations in SAM format. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Place short or long reads onto contigs without base-level alignment using Fast-SG: an ntHash rolling-hash k-mer look-up against a unique-k-mer index (KMC3 + BBHash + quasi_dictionary), windowed hit-vector scoring, and pair rescue, emitting pair locations in SAM format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Base-level alignment accuracy (e.g., CIGAR strings, mismatch positions) is required rather than contig-level placement/linking Gap-size estimation depends on precise insert-size distributions of 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL mate-pair data, where read-pair orientation may be unknown (article flags this as challenging) Insert-size requirement exceeds the actual long-read size, since the synthetic library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read length

skills.description: Use when building a scaffolding graph from raw or error-corrected long reads (PacBio, Nanopore) or Illumina reads without a read aligner, or when extracting synthetic mate-pair libraries from long reads to feed short-read scaffolders.
skills.name: alignment-free-scaffolding-graph-construction
skills.search_text: alignment-free-scaffolding-graph-construction Use when building a scaffolding graph from raw or error-corrected long reads (PacBio, Nanopore) or Illumina reads without a read aligner, or when extracting synthetic mate-pair libraries from long reads to feed short-read scaffolders. The task requires per-base read alignments or variant calls — Fast-SG only builds a scaffolding graph and extracts synthetic libraries, it does not align reads to contigs Only a single very short long-read library is available — synthetic library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size, so long-range links cannot be extracted Gap-size estimation for long-range mate-pair technologies like 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL is the goal — linking information there comes from a range of insert sizes with possibly unknown pair orientation, unlike Fast-SG synthetic libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Construct a scaffolding graph from short or long reads without aligning reads to contigs, using Fast-SG's ultrafast alignment-free algorithm with light-weight data structures (KMC k-mer counting, ntHash rolling hashes, BBHash minimal perfect hashing). This enables reuse of efficient short-read scaffolders on long-read data via synthetic mate-pair libraries. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Construct a scaffolding graph from short or long reads without aligning reads to contigs, using Fast-SG's ultrafast alignment-free algorithm with light-weight data structures (KMC k-mer counting, ntHash rolling hashes, BBHash minimal perfect hashing). This enables reuse of efficient short-read scaffolders on long-read data via synthetic mate-pair libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires per-base read alignments or variant calls — Fast-SG only builds a scaffolding graph and extracts synthetic libraries, it does not align reads to contigs Only a single very short long-read library is available — synthetic library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size, so long-range links cannot be extracted Gap-size estimation for long-range mate-pair technologies like 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL is the goal — linking information there comes from a range of insert sizes with possibly unknown pair orientation, unlike Fast-SG synthetic libraries

skills.description: Use when performing hybrid long-read correction (e.g., PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads aligned to Illumina short reads) and you must quantify each aligned short read's mapping identity and base quality to select an optimal correction policy for questionable bases.
skills.name: alignment-identity-estimation
skills.search_text: alignment-identity-estimation Use when performing hybrid long-read correction (e.g., PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads aligned to Illumina short reads) and you must quantify each aligned short read's mapping identity and base quality to select an optimal correction policy for questionable bases. Bases already covered by at least 90% consensus (η = 0.9) should be handled by HECIL's quick correction stage, not this optimization-based correction Self-correction scenarios with no second-generation short reads (e.g., HGAP-style correction from long reads alone) — this weight scheme requires aligned Illumina short reads with PHRED qualities If localized per-read information (base quality, mapping identity) is intentionally ignored, as in hybrid correctors that do not systematically use it — this skill is specifically the localized-weight approach http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 HECIL's method for estimating a normalized mapping-identity weight (exact matches of an aligned Illumina short read to the long read, divided by the short read's length) that is combined with a PHRED-quality weight into the cost J_k = 1/2*(quality + similarity) used to select the winning correction for questionable long-read bases. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: HECIL's method for estimating a normalized mapping-identity weight (exact matches of an aligned Illumina short read to the long read, divided by the short read's length) that is combined with a PHRED-quality weight into the cost J_k = 1/2*(quality + similarity) used to select the winning correction for questionable long-read bases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bases already covered by at least 90% consensus (η = 0.9) should be handled by HECIL's quick correction stage, not this optimization-based correction Self-correction scenarios with no second-generation short reads (e.g., HGAP-style correction from long reads alone) — this weight scheme requires aligned Illumina short reads with PHRED qualities If localized per-read information (base quality, mapping identity) is intentionally ignored, as in hybrid correctors that do not systematically use it — this skill is specifically the localized-weight approach

skills.description: Use when corrected or uncorrected PacBio long reads (e.g., HECIL iterations 1–5) must be scored against a reference genome such as E. coli K-12 MG1655 using BLASR-derived PI and % matched bases metrics.
skills.name: alignment-identity-metric-computation
skills.search_text: alignment-identity-metric-computation Use when corrected or uncorrected PacBio long reads (e.g., HECIL iterations 1–5) must be scored against a reference genome such as E. coli K-12 MG1655 using BLASR-derived PI and % matched bases metrics. There is no trusted reference genome for the organism — HECIL's hybrid correction itself is short-read-based, but this PI/% matched-bases validation specifically requires a reference (e.g., K-12 MG1655) to align against with BLASR Evaluation target is a de novo assembly rather than reads — use QUAST and MUMmer's dnadiff on Canu assemblies instead Evaluation target is k-mer complexity of corrected reads — compute unique k-mer counts with Jellyfish instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies long-read correction quality by aligning uncorrected and HECIL-corrected PacBio long reads to a reference genome with BLASR and computing percent identity (PI) and % matched bases per iteration, tracking gains across iterative-learning rounds. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Quantifies long-read correction quality by aligning uncorrected and HECIL-corrected PacBio long reads to a reference genome with BLASR and computing percent identity (PI) and % matched bases per iteration, tracking gains across iterative-learning rounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no trusted reference genome for the organism — HECIL's hybrid correction itself is short-read-based, but this PI/% matched-bases validation specifically requires a reference (e.g., K-12 MG1655) to align against with BLASR Evaluation target is a de novo assembly rather than reads — use QUAST and MUMmer's dnadiff on Canu assemblies instead Evaluation target is k-mer complexity of corrected reads — compute unique k-mer counts with Jellyfish instead

skills.description: Use when reference-based clustering of low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads has left reads with missing (NA) or misassigned chromosome classes and overlap-based label propagation is needed to correct them before per-chromosome de novo assembly.
skills.name: alignment-label-graph-label-propagation
skills.search_text: alignment-label-graph-label-propagation Use when reference-based clustering of low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads has left reads with missing (NA) or misassigned chromosome classes and overlap-based label propagation is needed to correct them before per-chromosome de novo assembly. Input reads are noisy long reads (ONT or PacBio CLR) rather than high-fidelity HiFi reads — the framework is designed for HiFi at ~5x coverage Hi-C or nanopore data integration is required — the article states this is left to future efforts and not yet implemented Reads already carry consistent, correct 'chr' chromosome classes and the assembly is run at sufficient coverage, so overlap-graph class correction adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 De novo chromosome class correction in HiFiCCL: a bidirectional Alignment Label Graph (ALG) is built from inter-sequence comparison of minimap2-aligned low-coverage HiFi reads, contained shorter nodes are collapsed, and a Z-drop-inspired heuristic traversal propagates chromosomal classes by majority vote with a minimum support threshold. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: De novo chromosome class correction in HiFiCCL: a bidirectional Alignment Label Graph (ALG) is built from inter-sequence comparison of minimap2-aligned low-coverage HiFi reads, contained shorter nodes are collapsed, and a Z-drop-inspired heuristic traversal propagates chromosomal classes by majority vote with a minimum support threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are noisy long reads (ONT or PacBio CLR) rather than high-fidelity HiFi reads — the framework is designed for HiFi at ~5x coverage Hi-C or nanopore data integration is required — the article states this is left to future efforts and not yet implemented Reads already carry consistent, correct 'chr' chromosome classes and the assembly is run at sufficient coverage, so overlap-graph class correction adds no value

skills.description: Use when you need to attribute residual errors in nanopore consensus reads (e.g., NanoAmpli-Seq OTU sequences) to indel classes by computing alignment-length/reference-length ratios from blastn output.
skills.name: alignment-length-ratio-quantification
skills.search_text: alignment-length-ratio-quantification Use when you need to attribute residual errors in nanopore consensus reads (e.g., NanoAmpli-Seq OTU sequences) to indel classes by computing alignment-length/reference-length ratios from blastn output. Reads have not been corrected through the INC-Seq / chopSeq / nanoClust stages (raw noisy nanopore reads will not yield interpretable residual-error attribution). The goal is general consensus accuracy estimation rather than diagnosing the indel class or homopolymer localization of residual errors. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies per-read read-to-reference alignment length ratios from blastn alignments of NanoAmpli-Seq reads (INC-Seq consensus, chopSeq-fragmented, nanoClust OTU consensus) to attribute residual sequencing errors to deletions versus insertions, particularly in homopolymer regions. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Quantifies per-read read-to-reference alignment length ratios from blastn alignments of NanoAmpli-Seq reads (INC-Seq consensus, chopSeq-fragmented, nanoClust OTU consensus) to attribute residual sequencing errors to deletions versus insertions, particularly in homopolymer regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not been corrected through the INC-Seq / chopSeq / nanoClust stages (raw noisy nanopore reads will not yield interpretable residual-error attribution). The goal is general consensus accuracy estimation rather than diagnosing the indel class or homopolymer localization of residual errors.

skills.search_text: alignment-matrix-backtracking-traceback Use when computing probability divergence ProDiv between two equal-length DNA barcode sequences requires a global edit-distance DP matrix plus a deterministic deletion-first traceback to obtain unique alignment counts (m, s, i, d). Computing edit distances between barcodes and flanking sequences, where PRO uses semiglobal alignment rather than the global matrix-plus-traceback used for ProDiv between equal-length barcodes Data from platforms whose errors are not base-level independent substitution/indel events — the paper notes no PacBio tests have been performed Demultiplexing an already-selected barcode kit, where PRO-dex applies the precomputed divergence rather than re-deriving alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implements the edit-distance dynamic-programming alignment and deterministic traceback used by PRO to count matches, substitutions, insertions, and deletions between two DNA barcode sequences, enabling the probability divergence ProDiv(X,Y) computation that underpins barcode generation and demultiplexing. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
skills.summary: Implements the edit-distance dynamic-programming alignment and deterministic traceback used by PRO to count matches, substitutions, insertions, and deletions between two DNA barcode sequences, enabling the probability divergence ProDiv(X,Y) computation that underpins barcode generation and demultiplexing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Computing edit distances between barcodes and flanking sequences, where PRO uses semiglobal alignment rather than the global matrix-plus-traceback used for ProDiv between equal-length barcodes Data from platforms whose errors are not base-level independent substitution/indel events — the paper notes no PacBio tests have been performed Demultiplexing an already-selected barcode kit, where PRO-dex applies the precomputed divergence rather than re-deriving alignments

skills.description: Decision support for prioritizing SNP candidates detected in MinION read alignments (LAST/last-split MAF) when variant calls must be weighted by local alignment quality rather than raw coverage alone.
skills.name: alignment-quality-p-error-estimation
skills.search_text: alignment-quality-p-error-estimation Decision support for prioritizing SNP candidates detected in MinION read alignments (LAST/last-split MAF) when variant calls must be weighted by local alignment quality rather than raw coverage alone. The goal is consensus sequence calling only — for the majority-rule consensus NanoPipe uses a different rule (minimum 10 reads per position; IUPAC ambiguity codes when two nucleotides differ by ≤20%), not the SNP p-error filter The input is metagenomic data — the article states metagenomics analysis is not yet supported in NanoPipe Reads are very short/noisy fragments; NanoPipe lets users set a read length limit (e.g. 200 nucleotides) to avoid noise from too-short reads, and candidates below 30% of maximum contig coverage are dropped regardless http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 A NanoPipe filter step that assesses alignment quality around each SNP candidate by estimating a p-error from LAST reliability scores over a window of up to 10 nucleotides flanking the variant (excluding the SNP position itself). It ranks transition/transversion-weighted polymorphism candidates so that confidence reflects local alignment reliability of noisy MinION reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: A NanoPipe filter step that assesses alignment quality around each SNP candidate by estimating a p-error from LAST reliability scores over a window of up to 10 nucleotides flanking the variant (excluding the SNP position itself). It ranks transition/transversion-weighted polymorphism candidates so that confidence reflects local alignment reliability of noisy MinION reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is consensus sequence calling only — for the majority-rule consensus NanoPipe uses a different rule (minimum 10 reads per position; IUPAC ambiguity codes when two nucleotides differ by ≤20%), not the SNP p-error filter The input is metagenomic data — the article states metagenomics analysis is not yet supported in NanoPipe Reads are very short/noisy fragments; NanoPipe lets users set a read length limit (e.g. 200 nucleotides) to avoid noise from too-short reads, and candidates below 30% of maximum contig coverage are dropped regardless

skills.name: alignment-read-filtering
skills.search_text: alignment-read-filtering Use when a pipeline must pre-partition SV-candidate reads from a BAM/CRAM (paired-end bwa-mem or long-read minimap2/ngmlr alignments) before variant calling, mirroring dysgu's fetch criteria and depth-skipping rules. Input is already the dysgu temporary reads BAM (temp_dir/input.dysgu_reads.bam) — proceed directly to 'dysgu call' instead of re-fetching. skills.summary: Reconstructs dysgu's 'fetch' stage: scan a sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM and partition reads carrying structural-variant signals (MAPQ >=1, soft-clip >=15 bp, discordant insert size/orientation, supplementary alignments, cigar gaps >=30 bp, inter-chromosomal mates) into a temporary SV-reads BAM for downstream calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already the dysgu temporary reads BAM (temp_dir/input.dysgu_reads.bam) — proceed directly to 'dysgu call' instead of re-fetching. skills.name: alignment-runtime-measurement-across-duplication-levels
skills.search_text: alignment-runtime-measurement-across-duplication-levels Use when comparing wall-clock alignment time and SP accuracy of MSA tools as sequence count grows multiplicatively (20x/50x/100x duplication), especially to test whether an accelerator like FMAlign2 retains >50% time savings at the largest scale. Sequences are ultra-long but not numerous — the benchmark targets scaling in sequence count (duplication levels), not per-sequence length variation You need alignment accuracy alone without runtime measurement — a single SP-score evaluation suffices rather than the full timing matrix Protein sequences — FMAlign2 is designed for nucleotide sequence alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the mtDB large-scale acceleration benchmark (Suppl. Table S2) by timing FMAlign2 and four MSA backends (MAFFT, Clustal Omega, HAlign3, HAlign4) on mitochondrial genomes duplicated 20x, 50x, and 100x, and verifying with SP scores that speedups do not sacrifice alignment accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae014
skills.summary: Reproduces the mtDB large-scale acceleration benchmark (Suppl. Table S2) by timing FMAlign2 and four MSA backends (MAFFT, Clustal Omega, HAlign3, HAlign4) on mitochondrial genomes duplicated 20x, 50x, and 100x, and verifying with SP scores that speedups do not sacrifice alignment accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are ultra-long but not numerous — the benchmark targets scaling in sequence count (duplication levels), not per-sequence length variation You need alignment accuracy alone without runtime measurement — a single SP-score evaluation suffices rather than the full timing matrix Protein sequences — FMAlign2 is designed for nucleotide sequence alignment

skills.description: Use when mapping quality-controlled ARG-containing ONT/PacBio reads to an ARG-tailored GTDB reference and you need abundant secondary alignments plus per-species alignment-score filtering to build candidate host species sets.
skills.name: alignment-score-based-secondary-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: alignment-score-based-secondary-alignment-filtering Use when mapping quality-controlled ARG-containing ONT/PacBio reads to an ARG-tailored GTDB reference and you need abundant secondary alignments plus per-species alignment-score filtering to build candidate host species sets. Input is short-read data — Argo takes quality-controlled long reads (Nanopore or PacBio) and the -x map-ont preset is tuned for ONT reads. The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — the article states assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited there. ARGs arise from point mutations — read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors, so such ARGs are excluded from Argo's database. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Argo's host-collection step: ARG-containing long reads are base-level aligned with minimap2 against an ARG-tailored GTDB database (10,000 bp ARG-containing regions from 596,663 GTDB R09-RS220 assemblies, 1,394,827 clustered sequences), then alignment scores (AS) are used to retain only valid read-species pairs that are aggregated into candidate species sets for set-cover labeling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Argo's host-collection step: ARG-containing long reads are base-level aligned with minimap2 against an ARG-tailored GTDB database (10,000 bp ARG-containing regions from 596,663 GTDB R09-RS220 assemblies, 1,394,827 clustered sequences), then alignment scores (AS) are used to retain only valid read-species pairs that are aggregated into candidate species sets for set-cover labeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — Argo takes quality-controlled long reads (Nanopore or PacBio) and the -x map-ont preset is tuned for ONT reads. The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — the article states assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited there. ARGs arise from point mutations — read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors, so such ARGs are excluded from Argo's database.

skills.description: Use when you need to validate an SV caller's assembled haplotype contigs by remapping them to an independent high-quality diploid assembly and computing the fraction that map back as expected at the called breakpoint.
skills.name: alignment-success-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: alignment-success-fraction-quantification Use when you need to validate an SV caller's assembled haplotype contigs by remapping them to an independent high-quality diploid assembly and computing the fraction that map back as expected at the called breakpoint. You are evaluating call-set accuracy against a variant benchmark (use truvari bench/refine instead of contig realignment) The contigs come from raw read assemblies rather than sawfish's candidate-breakpoint SV haplotype contigs, so no expected locus/orientation is defined No independent diploid assembly of the same sample is available to serve as an alignment target http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Quantifies the fraction of assembled SV haplotype consensus contigs that align directly (correct locus and breakend orientation) to an independent diploid assembly, providing an assembly-level precision check for an SV caller's local assemblies. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of assembled SV haplotype consensus contigs that align directly (correct locus and breakend orientation) to an independent diploid assembly, providing an assembly-level precision check for an SV caller's local assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are evaluating call-set accuracy against a variant benchmark (use truvari bench/refine instead of contig realignment) The contigs come from raw read assemblies rather than sawfish's candidate-breakpoint SV haplotype contigs, so no expected locus/orientation is defined No independent diploid assembly of the same sample is available to serve as an alignment target

skills.description: Use when raw long reads (Nanopore R9/R10 or PacBio CLR) from a diploid genome must be error-corrected where the sequencing error rate exceeds haplotype divergence and heterozygote alleles would otherwise be collapsed into the consensus.
skills.name: allele-based-read-scoring-and-haplotype-reweighting
skills.search_text: allele-based-read-scoring-and-haplotype-reweighting Use when raw long reads (Nanopore R9/R10 or PacBio CLR) from a diploid genome must be error-corrected where the sequencing error rate exceeds haplotype divergence and heterozygote alleles would otherwise be collapsed into the consensus. Input is PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex data — the paper reports PECAT achieves mediocre performance on these, and accurate SNP calling from corrected reads alone is not possible (unlike Hifiasm on HiFi reads). The goal is consensus/polishing of an already assembled contig (use a reference-based polisher such as Medaka or Racon instead of haplotype-aware read correction). Regions of very low heterozygosity rate — the method may not distinguish small sequencing errors from heterozygote alleles even with highly accurate reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 PECAT's haplotype-aware POA-based error correction: supporting reads are scored +1/-1 against the template read at dominant heterozygous branches, high-scoring (same-haplotype) reads are selected and re-weighted as consensus evidence, so heterozygote alleles survive while sequencing errors are corrected. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: PECAT's haplotype-aware POA-based error correction: supporting reads are scored +1/-1 against the template read at dominant heterozygous branches, high-scoring (same-haplotype) reads are selected and re-weighted as consensus evidence, so heterozygote alleles survive while sequencing errors are corrected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex data — the paper reports PECAT achieves mediocre performance on these, and accurate SNP calling from corrected reads alone is not possible (unlike Hifiasm on HiFi reads). The goal is consensus/polishing of an already assembled contig (use a reference-based polisher such as Medaka or Racon instead of haplotype-aware read correction). Regions of very low heterozygosity rate — the method may not distinguish small sequencing errors from heterozygote alleles even with highly accurate reads.

skills.description: Use when comparing population allele frequencies (e.g., gnomAD AF) between the previous and current annotation snapshots of a submitted variant, to decide whether the shift is large enough to notify the user or should be silently ignored.
skills.name: allele-frequency-order-of-magnitude-comparison
skills.search_text: allele-frequency-order-of-magnitude-comparison Use when comparing population allele frequencies (e.g., gnomAD AF) between the previous and current annotation snapshots of a submitted variant, to decide whether the shift is large enough to notify the user or should be silently ignored. The two allele-frequency values differ by less than 1 order of magnitude (e.g., 3.830e-06 to 3.979e-06) — the rule explicitly suppresses such sub-threshold shifts Comparing string-valued annotation fields (e.g., ClinVar CLNSIG classification, transcript name) — use exact-difference comparison instead, reporting any difference Detecting first-time presence of an annotation (e.g., new COSMIC entry) — check absent-in-old/present-in-new rather than magnitude change http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 VariantAlert's field-type-aware change-detection rule for allele frequencies: a difference in gnomAD allele frequency between the previous and current annotation snapshots is reported only if it spans at least 1 order of magnitude, filtering out negligible drift that should not trigger user email notifications. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.24495
skills.summary: VariantAlert's field-type-aware change-detection rule for allele frequencies: a difference in gnomAD allele frequency between the previous and current annotation snapshots is reported only if it spans at least 1 order of magnitude, filtering out negligible drift that should not trigger user email notifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two allele-frequency values differ by less than 1 order of magnitude (e.g., 3.830e-06 to 3.979e-06) — the rule explicitly suppresses such sub-threshold shifts Comparing string-valued annotation fields (e.g., ClinVar CLNSIG classification, transcript name) — use exact-difference comparison instead, reporting any difference Detecting first-time presence of an annotation (e.g., new COSMIC entry) — check absent-in-old/present-in-new rather than magnitude change

skills.description: Use when the task requires simulating or visualizing how allele frequencies change through time at a biallelic locus under selection, drift, or their combination — e.g., reproducing dominance-regime dynamics (overdominance, underdominance, codominance) or Wright–Fisher drift-selection trajectories.
skills.name: allele-frequency-trajectory-simulation
skills.search_text: allele-frequency-trajectory-simulation Use when the task requires simulating or visualizing how allele frequencies change through time at a biallelic locus under selection, drift, or their combination — e.g., reproducing dominance-regime dynamics (overdominance, underdominance, codominance) or Wright–Fisher drift-selection trajectories. The question concerns phenotypic trait evolution or game theory dynamics rather than biallelic allele-frequency change — learnPopGen provides separate functions for those phenomena A multi-allelic or continuous-trait model is required; selection() and drift.selection() are defined for a biallelic locus with three genotype fitnesses The user cannot use R and only needs static visualizations — the article notes web interfaces exist for many functions for students 'less adept in the R environment' http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Simulates allele-frequency trajectories at a biallelic locus under deterministic selection and stochastic genetic drift using the learnPopGen R package's selection() and drift.selection() functions, exporting generation-by-generation trajectories and trajectory plots. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412
skills.summary: Simulates allele-frequency trajectories at a biallelic locus under deterministic selection and stochastic genetic drift using the learnPopGen R package's selection() and drift.selection() functions, exporting generation-by-generation trajectories and trajectory plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns phenotypic trait evolution or game theory dynamics rather than biallelic allele-frequency change — learnPopGen provides separate functions for those phenomena A multi-allelic or continuous-trait model is required; selection() and drift.selection() are defined for a biallelic locus with three genotype fitnesses The user cannot use R and only needs static visualizations — the article notes web interfaces exist for many functions for students 'less adept in the R environment'

skills.description: Use when you have called SV VCFs (e.g. from VolcanoSV, cuteSV, Sniffles2, pbsv, DeBreak) and a GIAB-style truth set, and need to measure how F1 depends on Truvari matching thresholds plus how accurately TP pairs recover breakpoints and allele sequences.
skills.name: allele-sequence-similarity-pairing
skills.search_text: allele-sequence-similarity-pairing Use when you have called SV VCFs (e.g. from VolcanoSV, cuteSV, Sniffles2, pbsv, DeBreak) and a GIAB-style truth set, and need to measure how F1 depends on Truvari matching thresholds plus how accurately TP pairs recover breakpoints and allele sequences. Genotyping-accuracy evaluation of reciprocal translocations — the study only calculated F1 and GT_F1 for INVs and DUPs because genotyping reciprocal TRAs is ambiguous Evaluating somatic SVs against an incomplete high-confidence callset (e.g. HCC1395), where only recall should be plotted rather than precision/F1 Input is not a compared pair of SV VCFs against a curated truth set — this skill is a benchmarking/robustness protocol, not a caller itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks SV caller VCFs against the GIAB HG002 gold standard with Truvari bench, then uses Truvari's MatchID pairing to extract per-variant breakpoint-shift distances and alternate allele sequence similarity for true-positive pairs, and sweeps Truvari parameters (p, P, O, r) to test robustness of precision/recall/F1. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Benchmarks SV caller VCFs against the GIAB HG002 gold standard with Truvari bench, then uses Truvari's MatchID pairing to extract per-variant breakpoint-shift distances and alternate allele sequence similarity for true-positive pairs, and sweeps Truvari parameters (p, P, O, r) to test robustness of precision/recall/F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genotyping-accuracy evaluation of reciprocal translocations — the study only calculated F1 and GT_F1 for INVs and DUPs because genotyping reciprocal TRAs is ambiguous Evaluating somatic SVs against an incomplete high-confidence callset (e.g. HCC1395), where only recall should be plotted rather than precision/F1 Input is not a compared pair of SV VCFs against a curated truth set — this skill is a benchmarking/robustness protocol, not a caller itself

skills.description: Use when haplotagged nanopore reads carry per-read mCG log-likelihood-ratio or 6mA-region calls and you need to find regions (CGIs, ChIP peaks) with statistically significant allele-specific methylation.
skills.name: allele-specific-methylation-testing
skills.search_text: allele-specific-methylation-testing Use when haplotagged nanopore reads carry per-read mCG log-likelihood-ratio or 6mA-region calls and you need to find regions (CGIs, ChIP peaks) with statistically significant allele-specific methylation. The locus or sample lacks a sufficient density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs for Margin/WhatsHap phasing, since haplotype phasing depends on that density The analysis goal is strand- or haplotype-agnostic methylation quantification (e.g. correlation with WGBS), which instead only requires CpGs with coverage depth ≥20 by both WGBS and nanoHiMe-seq Region read coverage is below 20 reads, below the paper's threshold for allele-specific analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Identifies genomic regions where CpG methylation or 6mA enrichment differs significantly between haplotypes, by combining haplotagged nanoHiMe-seq reads with per-region 2x2 contingency testing. As applied in this paper, it yielded 1292 allele-specific CGIs and 1416 allele-specific H3K27me3 6mA regions in GM12878. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Identifies genomic regions where CpG methylation or 6mA enrichment differs significantly between haplotypes, by combining haplotagged nanoHiMe-seq reads with per-region 2x2 contingency testing. As applied in this paper, it yielded 1292 allele-specific CGIs and 1416 allele-specific H3K27me3 6mA regions in GM12878.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus or sample lacks a sufficient density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs for Margin/WhatsHap phasing, since haplotype phasing depends on that density The analysis goal is strand- or haplotype-agnostic methylation quantification (e.g. correlation with WGBS), which instead only requires CpGs with coverage depth ≥20 by both WGBS and nanoHiMe-seq Region read coverage is below 20 reads, below the paper's threshold for allele-specific analysis

skills.description: Use when ONT reads (e.g., HG002 R10.4 BAM) must be partitioned into haplotype-specific subsets (HP:i:1 / HP:i:2) to enable allele-specific methylation calling downstream.
skills.name: allele-specific-read-partitioning
skills.search_text: allele-specific-read-partitioning Use when ONT reads (e.g., HG002 R10.4 BAM) must be partitioned into haplotype-specific subsets (HP:i:1 / HP:i:2) to enable allele-specific methylation calling downstream. No phased heterozygous variant VCF is available for the sample, so whatshap haplotag cannot assign informative tags to reads The analysis goal is per-site methylation calling only, with no interest in allele-specific methylation patterns or parent-of-origin partitioning Input is short-read data lacking overlaps with informative heterozygous variants; HP tagging would yield mostly unassigned reads Assigns Oxford Nanopore reads to paternal or maternal haplotypes by tagging reads with whatshap using a phased VCF, then splitting the tagged BAM into hp1/hp2 read sets to enable allele-specific methylation analysis as done in the DeepBAM study. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Assigns Oxford Nanopore reads to paternal or maternal haplotypes by tagging reads with whatshap using a phased VCF, then splitting the tagged BAM into hp1/hp2 read sets to enable allele-specific methylation analysis as done in the DeepBAM study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No phased heterozygous variant VCF is available for the sample, so whatshap haplotag cannot assign informative tags to reads The analysis goal is per-site methylation calling only, with no interest in allele-specific methylation patterns or parent-of-origin partitioning Input is short-read data lacking overlaps with informative heterozygous variants; HP tagging would yield mostly unassigned reads

skills.description: Use when nanopore reads carry haplotype tags (maternal/paternal) plus per-read CpG methylation calls, and the goal is to identify allele-specific methylation or allelic DMRs between homologous chromosomes.
skills.name: allelic-dmr-detection
skills.search_text: allelic-dmr-detection Use when nanopore reads carry haplotype tags (maternal/paternal) plus per-read CpG methylation calls, and the goal is to identify allele-specific methylation or allelic DMRs between homologous chromosomes. Reads are not haplotype-phased — without parental haplotype tags there is no basis for allelic aggregation and DMR calling between homologs. Data come from older R9.4 pores where the DeepBAM 9-mer R10.4-trained model is not applicable; use the R9.4-based allele-specific DMR sets as reference instead. The goal is single-molecule methylation calling accuracy benchmarking rather than detecting regions of allelic methylation difference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Detect allele-specific differentially methylated regions (DMRs) by aggregating DeepBAM per-read CpG methylation calls on haplotype-phased nanopore reads into maternal/paternal methylation frequency tracks and testing each region with the DSS beta-binomial framework. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Detect allele-specific differentially methylated regions (DMRs) by aggregating DeepBAM per-read CpG methylation calls on haplotype-phased nanopore reads into maternal/paternal methylation frequency tracks and testing each region with the DSS beta-binomial framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not haplotype-phased — without parental haplotype tags there is no basis for allelic aggregation and DMR calling between homologs. Data come from older R9.4 pores where the DeepBAM 9-mer R10.4-trained model is not applicable; use the R9.4-based allele-specific DMR sets as reference instead. The goal is single-molecule methylation calling accuracy benchmarking rather than detecting regions of allelic methylation difference.

skills.description: Use when long-read contigs of single breakend SVs annotated 'Satellite/centr' by RepeatMasker must be scored for consistency with chromosome-specific centromeric HOR structure (canonical vs non-canonical HORs).
skills.name: alpha-satellite-hor-definition-curation
skills.search_text: alpha-satellite-hor-definition-curation Use when long-read contigs of single breakend SVs annotated 'Satellite/centr' by RepeatMasker must be scored for consistency with chromosome-specific centromeric HOR structure (canonical vs non-canonical HORs). The input contigs are not centromeric/satellite (not annotated 'Satellite/centr' by RepeatMasker) — HORmon monomer sets are chromosome-specific and only meaningful for alpha-satellite sequence Analyzing canonical two-breakpoint somatic SVs — this skill scores only single breakend contigs whose free end lies in centromeric repeats No HORmon-curated monomer/HOR definitions (cen*_monomers.fa, cen*_hors.tsv) exist for the chromosome of interest, since the scoring is defined against these curated files Curates alpha-satellite high-order repeat (HOR) definitions from HORmon output (cen*_monomers.fa, cen*_hors.tsv) and scores centromere-bound single-breakend contigs by monomer-decomposition concordance with StringDecomposer, yielding a per-contig HOR match score in [0,1]. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Curates alpha-satellite high-order repeat (HOR) definitions from HORmon output (cen*_monomers.fa, cen*_hors.tsv) and scores centromere-bound single-breakend contigs by monomer-decomposition concordance with StringDecomposer, yielding a per-contig HOR match score in [0,1].
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input contigs are not centromeric/satellite (not annotated 'Satellite/centr' by RepeatMasker) — HORmon monomer sets are chromosome-specific and only meaningful for alpha-satellite sequence Analyzing canonical two-breakpoint somatic SVs — this skill scores only single breakend contigs whose free end lies in centromeric repeats No HORmon-curated monomer/HOR definitions (cen*_monomers.fa, cen*_hors.tsv) exist for the chromosome of interest, since the scoring is defined against these curated files

skills.summary: Sort read IDs enumerated from POD5 nanopore files alphabetically in ascending or descending lexicographic order, mirroring the pod5Viewer file navigator's sort buttons so users can locate specific reads predictably.
