skills.description: Use when generating candidate SNV loci from ONT read pileups and you must decide which position/allele combinations pass to genotyping based on alternative allele support ratio.
skills.name: alternative-allele-ratio-thresholding
skills.search_text: alternative-allele-ratio-thresholding Use when generating candidate SNV loci from ONT read pileups and you must decide which position/allele combinations pass to genotyping based on alternative allele support ratio. Input is already a called VCF of genotyped variants — this skill operates on raw read pileups during candidate discovery, not post-genotyping. Alignments lack base quality tags or mapping quality, since the pileup counting depends on baseQ >= 13 and MAPQ >= 20 filters. Calling indels/SVs — this thresholding applies to single nucleotide variant alleles only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 A candidate-SNV filtering step from miniSNV that marks a genome position with a specific alternative allele as a candidate locus only when the supporting read ratio (R_alt) exceeds a user-defined threshold (default 0.2), evaluated per allele from ONT read pileups. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: A candidate-SNV filtering step from miniSNV that marks a genome position with a specific alternative allele as a candidate locus only when the supporting read ratio (R_alt) exceeds a user-defined threshold (default 0.2), evaluated per allele from ONT read pileups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a called VCF of genotyped variants — this skill operates on raw read pileups during candidate discovery, not post-genotyping. Alignments lack base quality tags or mapping quality, since the pileup counting depends on baseQ >= 13 and MAPQ >= 20 filters. Calling indels/SVs — this thresholding applies to single nucleotide variant alleles only.

skills.description: Use when you have tail-trimmed PacBio CCS reads from full-length cDNA (e.g., PAIso−seq of mouse GV oocytes) and need to count how many poly(A) sites each gene uses and quantify the per-gene APA site distribution.
skills.name: alternative-polyadenylation-event-quantification
skills.search_text: alternative-polyadenylation-event-quantification Use when you have tail-trimmed PacBio CCS reads from full-length cDNA (e.g., PAIso−seq of mouse GV oocytes) and need to count how many poly(A) sites each gene uses and quantify the per-gene APA site distribution. Input reads are short Illumina reads without full-length cDNA and poly(A) tails — tail clipping and TAPIS poly(A) site detection cannot be applied The goal is quantifying poly(A) tail length or non-A residues within tails rather than counting distinct polyadenylation sites per gene CCS reads lack the ≥15 nt poly(A) clip with ≥5 continuous adenosines required for site determination http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Detect per-gene alternative polyadenylation (APA) events from full-length PAIso−seq CCS reads by mapping with GMAP to mm10, extracting qualifying poly(A) tail clips, and running the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py) to count distinct poly(A) sites per gene against Ensembl GRCm38 release-92 annotation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9

Input is short-read-only RNA-seq without full-length LRTS alignments — segment-graph event definition from IsoTools requires long-read transcript structures The goal is transcriptome reconstruction or QC metric computation from raw bam files rather than event classification from an already-reconstructed transcriptome Only differential splicing statistics (beta-binomial) between sample groups are needed and events are already defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Defines and classifies alternative splicing events (IR, ES, 3AS, 5AS, ME) from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) data using IsoTools' segment-graph method, and exports events in rMATS/MISO format so PSI values can be cross-validated against short-read quantification. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Defines and classifies alternative splicing events (IR, ES, 3AS, 5AS, ME) from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) data using IsoTools' segment-graph method, and exports events in rMATS/MISO format so PSI values can be cross-validated against short-read quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read-only RNA-seq without full-length LRTS alignments — segment-graph event definition from IsoTools requires long-read transcript structures The goal is transcriptome reconstruction or QC metric computation from raw bam files rather than event classification from an already-reconstructed transcriptome Only differential splicing statistics (beta-binomial) between sample groups are needed and events are already defined

skills.description: Use when you have aligned full-length long-read transcripts (bam) for sample groups (e.g. CTL vs VPA-treated hepatocytes) and need event-level PSI values and differential splicing statistics like q-values for specific exons.
skills.name: alternative-splicing-event-quantification-from-long-read-transcriptomes

skills.description: Use when single-cell cDNA libraries (e.g., 10x Genomics 5' GEX FASTQs/amplicons) must be enriched for target genes and genotyped per-cell for somatic SNVs, fusions, or isoforms via long-read sequencing.

skills.search_text: amplicon-target-enrichment-analysis Use when single-cell cDNA libraries (e.g., 10x Genomics 5' GEX FASTQs/amplicons) must be enriched for target genes and genotyped per-cell for somatic SNVs, fusions, or isoforms via long-read sequencing. skills.description: Use when a germline variant reporting workflow must emit classified variants as a bgzipped annotated VCF companion to its interactive HTML and TSV report outputs.
skills.name: annotated-vcf-output-emission
skills.search_text: annotated-vcf-output-emission Use when a germline variant reporting workflow must emit classified variants as a bgzipped annotated VCF companion to its interactive HTML and TSV report outputs. The query data are somatic tumor variants (SNVs/InDels, CNAs, RNA fusions) rather than germline calls from a single cancer-patient sample — that is PCGR's remit, not CPSR's VCF emission Input VCF records are not designated 'PASS' in the FILTER column, or contain multi-allelic sites that have not been decomposed — the reporting pipeline excludes the former and requires decomposition of the latter first Only the interactive HTML report is the deliverable and no downstream consumer needs a machine-readable annotated variant track http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3396 CPSR's output-emission step: alongside the interactive HTML variant report, the workflow writes a bgzipped annotated VCF (<sample_id>.cpsr.<genome_assembly>.vcf.gz) carrying CPSR INFO annotation tags, keeping ACMG/AMP-classified germline variants machine-readable together with companion JSON and TSV outputs. genomics/v1 10.1002/ijc.33749
skills.summary: CPSR's output-emission step: alongside the interactive HTML variant report, the workflow writes a bgzipped annotated VCF (<sample_id>.cpsr.<genome_assembly>.vcf.gz) carrying CPSR INFO annotation tags, keeping ACMG/AMP-classified germline variants machine-readable together with companion JSON and TSV outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data are somatic tumor variants (SNVs/InDels, CNAs, RNA fusions) rather than germline calls from a single cancer-patient sample — that is PCGR's remit, not CPSR's VCF emission Input VCF records are not designated 'PASS' in the FILTER column, or contain multi-allelic sites that have not been decomposed — the reporting pipeline excludes the former and requires decomposition of the latter first Only the interactive HTML report is the deliverable and no downstream consumer needs a machine-readable annotated variant track

skills.description: Use when exon predictions from a splice graph or assembler (e.g. EXFI's GFA1 output, gfa1_to_fasta exons) must be quantitatively benchmarked against a reference GFF3 annotation to obtain precision, recall and F1.
skills.name: annotation-based-exon-metric-computation
skills.search_text: annotation-based-exon-metric-computation Use when exon predictions from a splice graph or assembler (e.g. EXFI's GFA1 output, gfa1_to_fasta exons) must be quantitatively benchmarked against a reference GFF3 annotation to obtain precision, recall and F1. No reference genome or GFF3 annotation exists for the organism (non-model species with only draft assemblies) — use mappability-based assessment instead The question is whether predicted exon sequences are usable for downstream analysis rather than coordinate-exact — mappability is a more optimistic metric than exon precision Evaluating whole-transcript or splice-graph topology rather than individual exon spans http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Scores a set of predicted exon coordinates against a reference GFF3 annotation by converting both to transcript-based BED format, testing mutual overlap with BEDTools intersect (>=95% in both directions), and computing precision (TP/(TP+FP)), recall (TP/(TP+FN)) and F1 (2PR/(P+R)) per parameter setting. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Scores a set of predicted exon coordinates against a reference GFF3 annotation by converting both to transcript-based BED format, testing mutual overlap with BEDTools intersect (>=95% in both directions), and computing precision (TP/(TP+FP)), recall (TP/(TP+FN)) and F1 (2PR/(P+R)) per parameter setting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome or GFF3 annotation exists for the organism (non-model species with only draft assemblies) — use mappability-based assessment instead The question is whether predicted exon sequences are usable for downstream analysis rather than coordinate-exact — mappability is a more optimistic metric than exon precision Evaluating whole-transcript or splice-graph topology rather than individual exon spans

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a splice-aware aligner for PacBio Iso-Seq FLNC reads based on whether a reference genome GTF annotation exists; trigger when building or reproducing the nf-core/isoseq mapping step.
skills.name: annotation-conditional-tool-dispatch
skills.search_text: annotation-conditional-tool-dispatch Decision support for choosing a splice-aware aligner for PacBio Iso-Seq FLNC reads based on whether a reference genome GTF annotation exists; trigger when building or reproducing the nf-core/isoseq mapping step. The analysis target is not FLNC long reads from PacBio Iso-Seq data being mapped onto a reference genome. A single aligner is mandated upstream (e.g. only minimap2 is permitted), so no annotation-dependent dispatch is needed. The reference GTF is known to be malformed and the bioperl spurious-alignment filter has been removed — the pipeline will stop instead of proceeding cleanly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A conditional dispatch pattern from the nf-core/isoseq mapping step: align FLNC PacBio Iso-Seq reads with uLTRA when a reference GTF annotation is available, otherwise fall back to splice-aware minimap2. uLTRA exploits the annotation to detect small exons, while minimap2 keeps the pipeline runnable for unannotated genomes. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: A conditional dispatch pattern from the nf-core/isoseq mapping step: align FLNC PacBio Iso-Seq reads with uLTRA when a reference GTF annotation is available, otherwise fall back to splice-aware minimap2. uLTRA exploits the annotation to detect small exons, while minimap2 keeps the pipeline runnable for unannotated genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is not FLNC long reads from PacBio Iso-Seq data being mapped onto a reference genome. A single aligner is mandated upstream (e.g. only minimap2 is permitted), so no annotation-dependent dispatch is needed. The reference GTF is known to be malformed and the bioperl spurious-alignment filter has been removed — the pipeline will stop instead of proceeding cleanly.

skills.search_text: annotation-difference-tracking Use when a stored list of variants (single variants or CSV/VCF batch files) must be re-annotated daily from external REST resources and changes — e.g. ClinVar classification, gnomAD allele frequency, presence in COSMIC/CIViC — must be detected and notified. You need annotation sources not yet integrated, such as Genomenon's MasterMind or DisGeNET — these are planned but not implemented. skills.description: Use when extending a variant re-annotation pipeline (e.g. VariantAlert, Django/Python) with a new external annotation database accessible via REST API, by implementing a module that mirrors the existing MyVariant.info client interface.
skills.name: annotation-source-interface-abstraction
skills.search_text: annotation-source-interface-abstraction Use when extending a variant re-annotation pipeline (e.g. VariantAlert, Django/Python) with a new external annotation database accessible via REST API, by implementing a module that mirrors the existing MyVariant.info client interface. The goal is to re-annotate variants using the already-integrated sources (gnomAD, COSMIC, ClinVar, CIViC) — use VariantAlert's existing daily re-annotation workflow instead of adding a new module. The new annotation source has no REST API (e.g. requires manual file upload or offline annotation, like iVar) — the interface-abstraction pattern depends on programmatic API access. Variant identifiers are not mappable to the target API's query scheme (e.g. non-HGVS identifiers that cannot be converted to genomic HGVS format). http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Extends VariantAlert's annotation pipeline by adding new external annotation sources (e.g. DisGeNET, Genomenon's MasterMind) as pluggable modules that follow the same REST-API client interface VariantAlert already uses for MyVariant.info. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.24495

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to re-annotate variants using the already-integrated sources (gnomAD, COSMIC, ClinVar, CIViC) — use VariantAlert's existing daily re-annotation workflow instead of adding a new module. skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq counts contain multiple cells per individual/sample and you must decide, gene by gene, which genes warrant random effects (in the mean and/or zero-inflation component) before a full mixed-model TWO-SIGMA fit.
skills.name: anova-based-random-effect-screening
skills.search_text: anova-based-random-effect-screening Use when scRNA-seq counts contain multiple cells per individual/sample and you must decide, gene by gene, which genes warrant random effects (in the mean and/or zero-inflation component) before a full mixed-model TWO-SIGMA fit. Gene set testing with twosigmag: the README explicitly states the ad hoc procedure is not recommended there because set-level testing requires a common gene-level null, which is unclear when some genes get random effects and others do not When you already know the random-effect specification: set adhoc=FALSE and pass mean_re/zi_re (or use twosigma_custom with (1|id) terms) instead of screening When a formal test of whether variance components equal zero is required — the ad hoc p-value is a screening statistic, not the likelihood-ratio test of the variance component(s) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 The TWO-SIGMA ad hoc procedure: per gene, fit a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model without random effects via glmmTMB, compute Pearson residuals, run a one-way ANOVA of residuals on individual ID, and use the F-test p-value to screen which genes most need random intercept terms. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: The TWO-SIGMA ad hoc procedure: per gene, fit a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model without random effects via glmmTMB, compute Pearson residuals, run a one-way ANOVA of residuals on individual ID, and use the F-test p-value to screen which genes most need random intercept terms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene set testing with twosigmag: the README explicitly states the ad hoc procedure is not recommended there because set-level testing requires a common gene-level null, which is unclear when some genes get random effects and others do not When you already know the random-effect specification: set adhoc=FALSE and pass mean_re/zi_re (or use twosigma_custom with (1|id) terms) instead of screening When a formal test of whether variance components equal zero is required — the ad hoc p-value is a screening statistic, not the likelihood-ratio test of the variance component(s)

skills.description: Use when constructing or updating a curated ARG reference database for read-based environmental surveillance (e.g., SARG+ for Argo/Lynx) from CARD, NDARO, SARG, and RefSeq PGAP-annotated proteins.
skills.name: antibiotic-resistance-gene-database-curation
skills.search_text: antibiotic-resistance-gene-database-curation Use when constructing or updating a curated ARG reference database for read-based environmental surveillance (e.g., SARG+ for Argo/Lynx) from CARD, NDARO, SARG, and RefSeq PGAP-annotated proteins. The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in novel, understudied environments — the article notes assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods are better suited for that. Applications requiring ORF-based annotation or detailed ARG sequence typing (e.g., distinguishing blaOXA-1 from blaOXA-1042), since the clustering step deliberately merges highly similar ARGs into single subtypes. Detection of point-mutation-derived ARGs is required — such ARGs are consistently excluded from the database because read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Curates SARG+, a species-level antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) protein reference database, by merging CARD, NDARO, and SARG into a consistent type/subtype/sequence hierarchy, extending it with RefSeq homologs sharing PGAP annotation evidence, and deduplicating via MMseqs2 clustering to yield 104,529 sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Curates SARG+, a species-level antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) protein reference database, by merging CARD, NDARO, and SARG into a consistent type/subtype/sequence hierarchy, extending it with RefSeq homologs sharing PGAP annotation evidence, and deduplicating via MMseqs2 clustering to yield 104,529 sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in novel, understudied environments — the article notes assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods are better suited for that. Applications requiring ORF-based annotation or detailed ARG sequence typing (e.g., distinguishing blaOXA-1 from blaOXA-1042), since the clustering step deliberately merges highly similar ARGs into single subtypes. Detection of point-mutation-derived ARGs is required — such ARGs are consistently excluded from the database because read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors.

The goal is exact nearest-neighbor search or sequence alignment (e.g., minimap2/BLAST-style overlap detection), not approximate search parameter selection The input is raw sequencing reads rather than an already-reduced embedding matrix — feature extraction and dimensionality reduction must be run first via the Fedrann pipeline You need end-to-end overlap-graph quality or assembly contiguity evaluation rather than ANN method comparison (use the kNN-overlap-finder benchmarking workflows instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarks multiple approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) schemes — NNDescent, HNSW, PQ, IVF-PQ, and RPF — on low-dimensional embeddings (e.g., SRP-reduced k-mer feature matrices) by measuring neighbor precision against exact brute-force neighbors and index-build/query runtime, then ranks methods on their speed-accuracy trade-off for a downstream task such as overlap graph construction. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048

skills.search_text: approximate-nearest-neighbor-graph-search Use when you have a low-dimensional embedding matrix of long sequencing reads (e.g. ICF/IDF-weighted SRP features from FASTQ/FASTA) and need ranked candidate overlaps for each read to build an overlap graph for de novo assembly. skills.description: Use when a CRAQ run has produced CRE/CSE breakpoint BED files (out_final.CRE.bed, out_final.CSE.bed) and you must convert normalized error counts into R-AQI/S-AQI scores with quality-class labels for an assembly.
skills.name: aqi-quality-metric-computation
skills.search_text: aqi-quality-metric-computation Use when a CRAQ run has produced CRE/CSE breakpoint BED files (out_final.CRE.bed, out_final.CSE.bed) and you must convert normalized error counts into R-AQI/S-AQI scores with quality-class labels for an assembly. Heterozygous loci have not been removed: CRAQ stresses 'the importance of removing heterozygous loci during assembly assessment', and it outputs CRH/CSH coordinates so heterozygous signal can be excluded before scoring — applying AQI computation to raw, heterozygosity-contaminated error calls inflates error counts. The genome is polyploid: the paper states 'evaluation of genome assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here'. You need to detect the CRE/CSE errors themselves (read mapping, clipping-ratio cutoffs f = 0.75, h = 0.4-0.6, coverage m = 2 / M = 5x) — that is a separate CRAQ detection step; this skill only consumes its BED outputs. Transforms CRAQ-detected Clip-based Regional Error (CRE) and Clip-based Structural Error (CSE) counts into regional (R-AQI) and structural (S-AQI) assembly quality indexes using harmonic sliding-window normalization, then classifies quality (AQI > 90 reference, 80-90 high, 60-80 draft, < 60 low). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Transforms CRAQ-detected Clip-based Regional Error (CRE) and Clip-based Structural Error (CSE) counts into regional (R-AQI) and structural (S-AQI) assembly quality indexes using harmonic sliding-window normalization, then classifies quality (AQI > 90 reference, 80-90 high, 60-80 draft, < 60 low).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Heterozygous loci have not been removed: CRAQ stresses 'the importance of removing heterozygous loci during assembly assessment', and it outputs CRH/CSH coordinates so heterozygous signal can be excluded before scoring — applying AQI computation to raw, heterozygosity-contaminated error calls inflates error counts. The genome is polyploid: the paper states 'evaluation of genome assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here'. You need to detect the CRE/CSE errors themselves (read mapping, clipping-ratio cutoffs f = 0.75, h = 0.4-0.6, coverage m = 2 / M = 5x) — that is a separate CRAQ detection step; this skill only consumes its BED outputs.

skills.description: Use when a CRAQ run has produced AQI, R-AQI, or S-AQI scores for one or more assemblies and you need to assign a quality class, compare against LAI/QV/BUSCO/N50, or decide whether to split misjoined scaffolds.
skills.name: aqi-score-interpretation
skills.search_text: aqi-score-interpretation Use when a CRAQ run has produced AQI, R-AQI, or S-AQI scores for one or more assemblies and you need to assign a quality class, compare against LAI/QV/BUSCO/N50, or decide whether to split misjoined scaffolds. Assessing assemblies of polyploid species: the article states 'evaluation of genome assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' Judging genome completeness alone (use BUSCO) — S-AQI reflects structural quality that QV, BUSCO, and N50 do not capture, so a high S-AQI does not certify completeness Input is raw SAM/BAM read-mapping data rather than computed AQI scores — run the CRAQ pipeline (clip extraction, CRE/CSE classification, normalization) first http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Interprets CRAQ's assembly quality indicators, where normalized Clip-based Regional Error (CRE) counts become R-AQI and normalized Clip-based Structural Error (CSE) counts become S-AQI, and maps scores to published quality classes (AQI > 90 reference quality; 80-90 high; 60-80 draft; < 60 low). It also frames R-AQI/S-AQI against existing metrics (LAI, QV, BUSCO, N50), since S-AQI captures structural quality these metrics do not. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Interprets CRAQ's assembly quality indicators, where normalized Clip-based Regional Error (CRE) counts become R-AQI and normalized Clip-based Structural Error (CSE) counts become S-AQI, and maps scores to published quality classes (AQI > 90 reference quality; 80-90 high; 60-80 draft; < 60 low). It also frames R-AQI/S-AQI against existing metrics (LAI, QV, BUSCO, N50), since S-AQI captures structural quality these metrics do not.

skills.name: arg-abundance-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: arg-abundance-benchmark-evaluation Use when you need to quantify how detection coverage thresholds differ between read-based, assembly-based, and binning-based ARG profiling pipelines on simulated long-read metagenomes of known composition. The input is a real environmental or clinical metagenome with unknown true ARG composition — no ground truth exists to compute precision/recall/F1 against The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in understudied environments, where assembly- and binning-based approaches are the article's recommended choice The question concerns point-mutation-derived ARGs (e.g., SNP-driven resistance), which Argo's reference-based database explicitly excludes http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark protocol for comparing read-based (Argo), assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2), and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) ARG profiling pipelines against a ground-truth expectation derived by DIAMOND mapping of reference genomes to SARG+, scoring type- and subtype-level accuracy with precision, recall, F1, Pearson correlation, and L1/L2 distances across simulated coverages from 1× to 32×. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for comparing read-based (Argo), assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2), and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) ARG profiling pipelines against a ground-truth expectation derived by DIAMOND mapping of reference genomes to SARG+, scoring type- and subtype-level accuracy with precision, recall, F1, Pearson correlation, and L1/L2 distances across simulated coverages from 1× to 32×.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a real environmental or clinical metagenome with unknown true ARG composition — no ground truth exists to compute precision/recall/F1 against The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in understudied environments, where assembly- and binning-based approaches are the article's recommended choice The question concerns point-mutation-derived ARGs (e.g., SNP-driven resistance), which Argo's reference-based database explicitly excludes

skills.description: Use when validating a species-resolved ARG profiler against mock communities with known member genomes, or when comparing estimated cpg-based ARG abundances to ground-truth expected profiles via Pearson correlation and precision/recall/F1.
skills.name: arg-abundance-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: arg-abundance-correlation-analysis Use when validating a species-resolved ARG profiler against mock communities with known member genomes, or when comparing estimated cpg-based ARG abundances to ground-truth expected profiles via Pearson correlation and precision/recall/F1. Samples are real complex metagenomes without known member genomes — no expected ARG profile exists to correlate against, so this validation design does not apply Input reads are short second-generation reads — Argo relies on long-read overlapping of Nanopore/PacBio reads and is not applicable Species fall below 1× genome copy coverage — Argo marks such ARGs 'unclassified', making abundance correlation uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark Argo's species-resolved ARG profiling on sequenced long-read mock communities (D6300, MSA2006, MSA1003, D6331) by comparing estimated versus expected ARG profiles, scoring type/subtype precision, recall, F1-score, and Pearson correlation of ARG copies-per-genome (cpg) abundances. This validates that a long-read overlapping profiler recovers true ARG composition and abundance under varying read lengths and quality scores. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Benchmark Argo's species-resolved ARG profiling on sequenced long-read mock communities (D6300, MSA2006, MSA1003, D6331) by comparing estimated versus expected ARG profiles, scoring type/subtype precision, recall, F1-score, and Pearson correlation of ARG copies-per-genome (cpg) abundances. This validates that a long-read overlapping profiler recovers true ARG composition and abundance under varying read lengths and quality scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are real complex metagenomes without known member genomes — no expected ARG profile exists to correlate against, so this validation design does not apply Input reads are short second-generation reads — Argo relies on long-read overlapping of Nanopore/PacBio reads and is not applicable Species fall below 1× genome copy coverage — Argo marks such ARGs 'unclassified', making abundance correlation uninformative

skills.description: Use when long-read metagenomic ARG profiling has produced species-resolved ARG detections and read clusters, and absolute abundances must be expressed as ARG copies per genome (cpg) rather than raw coverage.
skills.name: arg-abundance-normalization-per-genome-copy
skills.search_text: arg-abundance-normalization-per-genome-copy Use when long-read metagenomic ARG profiling has produced species-resolved ARG detections and read clusters, and absolute abundances must be expressed as ARG copies per genome (cpg) rather than raw coverage. Input reads are short (second-generation) reads — Argo's overlap-graph clustering and Melon genome-copy estimation require long reads Coverage is extremely low or species fall below 1× genome copy, where Argo reports 'unclassified' and cpg normalization is unstable Goal is ORF-level or sequence-typing resolution: highly similar ARGs are clustered (e.g. blaOXA-1 and blaOXA-1042 as blaOXA), so cpg cannot resolve sub-ARG-level abundance http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Normalize summed ARG copy coverage by species genome-copy estimates computed with Melon, yielding ARG copies per genome (cpg) — equivalent to ARG copies per cell under a single-genome-per-cell assumption — written as a tab-delimited abundance table. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Normalize summed ARG copy coverage by species genome-copy estimates computed with Melon, yielding ARG copies per genome (cpg) — equivalent to ARG copies per cell under a single-genome-per-cell assumption — written as a tab-delimited abundance table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short (second-generation) reads — Argo's overlap-graph clustering and Melon genome-copy estimation require long reads Coverage is extremely low or species fall below 1× genome copy, where Argo reports 'unclassified' and cpg normalization is unstable Goal is ORF-level or sequence-typing resolution: highly similar ARGs are clustered (e.g. blaOXA-1 and blaOXA-1042 as blaOXA), so cpg cannot resolve sub-ARG-level abundance

skills.description: Use when you have quality-controlled long reads (Nanopore/PacBio FASTQ) from complex metagenomes and need to subset and annotate reads carrying antibiotic resistance genes before species-level host assignment.
skills.name: arg-containing-read-extraction-annotation
skills.search_text: arg-containing-read-extraction-annotation Use when you have quality-controlled long reads (Nanopore/PacBio FASTQ) from complex metagenomes and need to subset and annotate reads carrying antibiotic resistance genes before species-level host assignment. Input is already an annotated ARG table or assembled contigs with gene calls rather than raw long reads The goal is de novo identification of novel ARGs or point-mutation-derived ARGs — SARG+ excludes ARGs arising from point mutations because SNPs cannot be distinguished from sequencing errors in read-based profiling Short-read data requiring per-read species typing of highly similar ARG alleles, where the SARG+ clustering of near-identical genes (e.g., blaOXA-1/blaOXA-1042 as blaOXA) lowers resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Isolates ARG-carrying long reads from metagenomic read sets using DIAMOND frameshift-aware blastx against the SARG+ database, so that downstream host-identification classifiers operate only on resistance-relevant reads. This filtering step underpins species-resolved ARG profiling with Argo and its benchmark comparisons. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Isolates ARG-carrying long reads from metagenomic read sets using DIAMOND frameshift-aware blastx against the SARG+ database, so that downstream host-identification classifiers operate only on resistance-relevant reads. This filtering step underpins species-resolved ARG profiling with Argo and its benchmark comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated ARG table or assembled contigs with gene calls rather than raw long reads The goal is de novo identification of novel ARGs or point-mutation-derived ARGs — SARG+ excludes ARGs arising from point mutations because SNPs cannot be distinguished from sequencing errors in read-based profiling Short-read data requiring per-read species typing of highly similar ARG alleles, where the SARG+ clustering of near-identical genes (e.g., blaOXA-1/blaOXA-1042 as blaOXA) lowers resolution

skills.description: Use when profiling ARGs at species resolution in quality-controlled Nanopore/PacBio long-read metagenomes (FASTA/FASTQ), especially when linking ARGs to microbial hosts and distinguishing chromosomal vs plasmid carriers is required.
skills.name: arg-profiling-with-argo
skills.search_text: arg-profiling-with-argo Use when profiling ARGs at species resolution in quality-controlled Nanopore/PacBio long-read metagenomes (FASTA/FASTQ), especially when linking ARGs to microbial hosts and distinguishing chromosomal vs plasmid carriers is required. Input reads are short (second-generation) reads — Argo relies on long-read overlapping and requires Nanopore or PacBio data Goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited Application requires ORF-based annotation or detailed sequence typing of highly similar ARGs (e.g., distinguishing blaOXA-1 from blaOXA-1042), which Argo's clustered subtypes cannot resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Species-resolved profiling of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in long-read metagenomes using Argo, which assigns taxonomy collectively to read clusters via long-read overlapping and set covering, producing ARG types/subtypes, carriers, and abundances as copies per genome (cpg). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Species-resolved profiling of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in long-read metagenomes using Argo, which assigns taxonomy collectively to read clusters via long-read overlapping and set covering, producing ARG types/subtypes, carriers, and abundances as copies per genome (cpg).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short (second-generation) reads — Argo relies on long-read overlapping and requires Nanopore or PacBio data Goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited Application requires ORF-based annotation or detailed sequence typing of highly similar ARGs (e.g., distinguishing blaOXA-1 from blaOXA-1042), which Argo's clustered subtypes cannot resolve

skills.description: Use when building or updating an ARG protein reference database (e.g., from CARD, NDARO, SARG) that needs a uniform type/subtype hierarchy and deduplicated sequences for read-based metagenomic AMR surveillance.
skills.name: arg-reference-hierarchy-standardization
skills.search_text: arg-reference-hierarchy-standardization Use when building or updating an ARG protein reference database (e.g., from CARD, NDARO, SARG) that needs a uniform type/subtype hierarchy and deduplicated sequences for read-based metagenomic AMR surveillance. The goal is allele-level or SNP-level ARG sequence typing — SARG+ deliberately clusters highly similar ARGs (e.g., blaOXA-1/blaOXA-1042) and excludes point-mutation-derived ARGs, lowering resolution for ORF-based annotation. You need de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in unstudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) approaches are better suited than reference curation. The input FASTA already follows the SARG+ type/subtype hierarchy and the target MMseqs2 clustering thresholds; re-curation would only duplicate the published database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Curates the SARG+ ARG reference database by merging CARD, NDARO, and SARG protein sequences into a consistent type (class/family) → subtype (subclass/gene) → sequence hierarchy, then extending and deduplicating it with MMseqs2 so that species-level read-based profilers like Argo can use stringent cutoffs without losing sensitivity. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Curates the SARG+ ARG reference database by merging CARD, NDARO, and SARG protein sequences into a consistent type (class/family) → subtype (subclass/gene) → sequence hierarchy, then extending and deduplicating it with MMseqs2 so that species-level read-based profilers like Argo can use stringent cutoffs without losing sensitivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is allele-level or SNP-level ARG sequence typing — SARG+ deliberately clusters highly similar ARGs (e.g., blaOXA-1/blaOXA-1042) and excludes point-mutation-derived ARGs, lowering resolution for ORF-based annotation. You need de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in unstudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) approaches are better suited than reference curation. The input FASTA already follows the SARG+ type/subtype hierarchy and the target MMseqs2 clustering thresholds; re-curation would only duplicate the published database.

skills.description: Use when detecting tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, tRNA halves) from small RNA-seq and you need an index that forces tncRNA assignments to come only from tRNA loci plus 50 nt leader/trailer flanks.
skills.name: artificial-genome-masked-index-construction
skills.search_text: artificial-genome-masked-index-construction Use when detecting tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, tRNA halves) from small RNA-seq and you need an index that forces tncRNA assignments to come only from tRNA loci plus 50 nt leader/trailer flanks. The analysis goal is general small RNA annotation (miRNA, piRNA, rRNA-derived reads) rather than tRNA-derived reads — a SPORTS1.0-style annotation pipeline is more appropriate The genome lacks reliable tRNA annotations or tRNAscan-SE cannot be run for the organism, so masking coordinates and mature/leader/trailer FASTAs cannot be generated Input data is paired-end or long-read RNA-seq rather than single-end small RNA reads of 14–50 nt, which is the size class this artificial genome design was built to classify http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Builds a Bowtie1 'artificial genome' in which genuine tRNA gene regions are masked with 50 nt 5'/3' flanks so that sRNA-seq reads are classified as tncRNAs only if they map exclusively to the tRNA-derived artificial chromosomes, avoiding ambiguous assignments from non-tRNA regions. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Builds a Bowtie1 'artificial genome' in which genuine tRNA gene regions are masked with 50 nt 5'/3' flanks so that sRNA-seq reads are classified as tncRNAs only if they map exclusively to the tRNA-derived artificial chromosomes, avoiding ambiguous assignments from non-tRNA regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is general small RNA annotation (miRNA, piRNA, rRNA-derived reads) rather than tRNA-derived reads — a SPORTS1.0-style annotation pipeline is more appropriate The genome lacks reliable tRNA annotations or tRNAscan-SE cannot be run for the organism, so masking coordinates and mature/leader/trailer FASTAs cannot be generated Input data is paired-end or long-read RNA-seq rather than single-end small RNA reads of 14–50 nt, which is the size class this artificial genome design was built to classify

skills.name: assembler-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: assembler-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing assembler quality on downsampled (~5x) HiFi read sets and you need misassembled contig length, NG50/NGA50, BUSCO/Merqury deltas plus wall-time and max-RSS ratios between pipelines. Reads are high coverage (e.g. 25-40x) where hifiasm alone already produces high-quality assemblies — the skill targets ~5x low-coverage HiFi data Data are noisy long reads (ONT or PacBio CLR) rather than HiFi — HiFiCCL is designed specifically for low-coverage high-fidelity reads No high-quality reference genome is available — the HiFiCCL pipeline requires a reference (e.g. CHM13v2.0) for reference-guided chromosome-by-chromosome binning http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark contig-level quality of HiFiCCL-Hifiasm against hifiasm-alone on low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi human read sets using QUAST, BUSCO 5.4.7 and Merqury, quantifying misassembled contig length (MCL) reduction, NG50/NGA50, and runtime/memory cost. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Benchmark contig-level quality of HiFiCCL-Hifiasm against hifiasm-alone on low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi human read sets using QUAST, BUSCO 5.4.7 and Merqury, quantifying misassembled contig length (MCL) reduction, NG50/NGA50, and runtime/memory cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are high coverage (e.g. 25-40x) where hifiasm alone already produces high-quality assemblies — the skill targets ~5x low-coverage HiFi data Data are noisy long reads (ONT or PacBio CLR) rather than HiFi — HiFiCCL is designed specifically for low-coverage high-fidelity reads No high-quality reference genome is available — the HiFiCCL pipeline requires a reference (e.g. CHM13v2.0) for reference-guided chromosome-by-chromosome binning

skills.name: assembler-corrector-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: assembler-corrector-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing how error correctors or assemblers preserve heterozygote alleles in corrected long reads across heterozygosity rates, e.g. validating a haplotype-aware corrector against Canu/MECAT/NECAT baselines. Evaluating assemblers on Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi reads — the paper reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on these high-accuracy data types, so the correction-retention benchmark is not representative Assessing haplotype-resolved assembly quality (phase block NG50, QV) on real diploid datasets rather than correction-stage allele retention on simulated reads Quantifying SNP calling from assemblies or raw reads — the paper notes corrected reads alone cannot accurately call SNPs the way Hifiasm does with HiFi reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark error-correction/assembling tools (PECAT vs Canu, MECAT, NECAT) on simulated diploid long reads by quantifying how well heterozygous SNP alleles survive correction, replicating the Fig. 2a SNP allele accuracy comparison. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Benchmark error-correction/assembling tools (PECAT vs Canu, MECAT, NECAT) on simulated diploid long reads by quantifying how well heterozygous SNP alleles survive correction, replicating the Fig. 2a SNP allele accuracy comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating assemblers on Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi reads — the paper reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on these high-accuracy data types, so the correction-retention benchmark is not representative Assessing haplotype-resolved assembly quality (phase block NG50, QV) on real diploid datasets rather than correction-stage allele retention on simulated reads Quantifying SNP calling from assemblies or raw reads — the paper notes corrected reads alone cannot accurately call SNPs the way Hifiasm does with HiFi reads

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assembler outputs via rnaQUAST and you need a per-assembler CSV of quality metrics verified against published anchor values before downstream ranking or reproduction claims.
skills.name: assembler-metric-tabulation-and-validation
skills.search_text: assembler-metric-tabulation-and-validation Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assembler outputs via rnaQUAST and you need a per-assembler CSV of quality metrics verified against published anchor values before downstream ranking or reproduction claims. Input assemblies are from real (non-simulated) RNA-Seq datasets where the paper's anchor values (309/126 misassemblies, 1.74/1.93 duplication ratios) do not apply and re-derivation of expectations is required The goal is de novo assembly itself rather than post-hoc quality comparison of existing assemblies Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the article notes its approach was designed for single-organism RNA-Seq and metatranscriptomic quality-evaluation pipelines remain future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Extracts benchmark metrics (95%-assembled genes/isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, duplication ratio) from rnaQUAST reports for each transcriptome assembler on the Human simulated RNA-Seq dataset and tabulates them into a CSV, validating against paper-reported anchor values (e.g. rnaSPAdes 309 misassemblies, Trans-ABySS 126 misassemblies, duplication ratios 1.74/1.93/2.19). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Extracts benchmark metrics (95%-assembled genes/isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, duplication ratio) from rnaQUAST reports for each transcriptome assembler on the Human simulated RNA-Seq dataset and tabulates them into a CSV, validating against paper-reported anchor values (e.g. rnaSPAdes 309 misassemblies, Trans-ABySS 126 misassemblies, duplication ratios 1.74/1.93/2.19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input assemblies are from real (non-simulated) RNA-Seq datasets where the paper's anchor values (309/126 misassemblies, 1.74/1.93 duplication ratios) do not apply and re-derivation of expectations is required The goal is de novo assembly itself rather than post-hoc quality comparison of existing assemblies Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the article notes its approach was designed for single-organism RNA-Seq and metatranscriptomic quality-evaluation pipelines remain future work

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a new overlap detection or read-processing module can be swapped into an established assembler (e.g. Fedrann into Shasta) and comparing whole-genome assembly quality against the native baseline on identical long-read datasets.
skills.name: assembler-pipeline-integration-benchmarking
skills.search_text: assembler-pipeline-integration-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a new overlap detection or read-processing module can be swapped into an established assembler (e.g. Fedrann into Shasta) and comparing whole-genome assembly quality against the native baseline on identical long-read datasets. You only need to compare overlap graph quality (precision/recall) rather than end-to-end assembly quality — use the overlap-level benchmarking workflow in kNN-overlap-finder instead. The candidate module cannot be decoupled from the assembler's internal data structures; the article notes integration is non-trivial due to undocumented in-memory structures and tight stage coupling. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Substitutes a third-party overlap detection stage into an existing long-read assembler's pipeline and benchmarks the resulting assembly head-to-head against the unmodified assembler using contiguity (N50, longest contig), completeness (BUSCO), and accuracy (k-mer QV) metrics. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Substitutes a third-party overlap detection stage into an existing long-read assembler's pipeline and benchmarks the resulting assembly head-to-head against the unmodified assembler using contiguity (N50, longest contig), completeness (BUSCO), and accuracy (k-mer QV) metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to compare overlap graph quality (precision/recall) rather than end-to-end assembly quality — use the overlap-level benchmarking workflow in kNN-overlap-finder instead. The candidate module cannot be decoupled from the assembler's internal data structures; the article notes integration is non-trivial due to undocumented in-memory structures and tight stage coupling.

skills.description: Reference for benchmarking read-based ARG profilers against assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) pipelines, or when coverage is high enough (≥8× for assembly, >32× for binning) to justify contig-based or MAG-based ARG host assignment.
skills.name: assembly-based-arg-profiling
skills.search_text: assembly-based-arg-profiling Reference for benchmarking read-based ARG profilers against assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) and binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) pipelines, or when coverage is high enough (≥8× for assembly, >32× for binning) to justify contig-based or MAG-based ARG host assignment. Coverage is low (below ~8× for assembly-based, below ~32× for binning-based profiling) — F1 stays at or below 0.5 and a read-based profiler such as Argo is preferred The goal is rapid ARG surveillance with species-level resolution without the compute and coverage cost of assembly and binning Input is already assembled contigs or MAGs — run the Kraken2/GTDB-Tk classification steps directly instead of re-assembling http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarked strategy for ARG detection and host attribution that assembles long Nanopore reads into contigs (metaFlye), taxonomically classifies contigs (Kraken2), and optionally bins them into MAGs (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk), then compares the resulting ARG profiles against expected abundances. It serves as the assembly/binning-based baseline against which the read-based Argo profiler is measured across 1×–32× sequencing coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: A benchmarked strategy for ARG detection and host attribution that assembles long Nanopore reads into contigs (metaFlye), taxonomically classifies contigs (Kraken2), and optionally bins them into MAGs (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk), then compares the resulting ARG profiles against expected abundances. It serves as the assembly/binning-based baseline against which the read-based Argo profiler is measured across 1×–32× sequencing coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Coverage is low (below ~8× for assembly-based, below ~32× for binning-based profiling) — F1 stays at or below 0.5 and a read-based profiler such as Argo is preferred The goal is rapid ARG surveillance with species-level resolution without the compute and coverage cost of assembly and binning Input is already assembled contigs or MAGs — run the Kraken2/GTDB-Tk classification steps directly instead of re-assembling

skills.description: Use when building or validating a truth set of TE insertions (Alu, L1, HERV, SVA) from de novo long-read assemblies, or when benchmarking read-based TE callers against an assembly-derived callset for samples like HG002 or HG01071.
skills.name: assembly-based-insertion-calling
skills.search_text: assembly-based-insertion-calling Use when building or validating a truth set of TE insertions (Alu, L1, HERV, SVA) from de novo long-read assemblies, or when benchmarking read-based TE callers against an assembly-derived callset for samples like HG002 or HG01071. Input is short-read (Illumina) data — this method depends on long-read assemblies or reads for resolving full-length TE insertions You only need to re-call insertions from an existing BAM/CRAM rather than generate an assembly-based truth set — a read-based caller like sTELLeR directly on the BAM is appropriate The analysis targets old/divergent insertions — the <15% divergence filter is intentionally biased toward recent intact insertions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Generate a per-sample truth callset of non-reference transposable element insertions by calling candidate insertions from de novo genome assemblies with SVIM-asm, labeling them by TE family with RepeatMasker, and applying divergence and length filters. This assembly-based callset (HG002, HG01071) serves as the ground truth for benchmarking long-read TE callers such as sTELLeR. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Generate a per-sample truth callset of non-reference transposable element insertions by calling candidate insertions from de novo genome assemblies with SVIM-asm, labeling them by TE family with RepeatMasker, and applying divergence and length filters. This assembly-based callset (HG002, HG01071) serves as the ground truth for benchmarking long-read TE callers such as sTELLeR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina) data — this method depends on long-read assemblies or reads for resolving full-length TE insertions You only need to re-call insertions from an existing BAM/CRAM rather than generate an assembly-based truth set — a read-based caller like sTELLeR directly on the BAM is appropriate The analysis targets old/divergent insertions — the <15% divergence filter is intentionally biased toward recent intact insertions

skills.description: Use when the goal is to detect and benchmark large germline structural variants (e.g. >7000 bp) from de novo assembly FASTAs of low-coverage HiFi reads, against truth sets such as GIAB Tier 1 or T2T-HG002-Q100.
skills.name: assembly-based-structural-variant-detection
skills.search_text: assembly-based-structural-variant-detection Use when the goal is to detect and benchmark large germline structural variants (e.g. >7000 bp) from de novo assembly FASTAs of low-coverage HiFi reads, against truth sets such as GIAB Tier 1 or T2T-HG002-Q100. When reads are available at high coverage (e.g. HG00438 requiring 41x HiFi) — standard read-level SV calling on full-depth data is the appropriate route instead of low-coverage assembly-based detection When the target variants are small (<7000 bp) — this workflow filters explicitly to SVs larger than 7000 bp and the benchmark thresholds are tuned for large SVs When a reference genome is unavailable — HiFiCCL relies on reference-guided chromosome-by-chromosome binning of reads before assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detects large structural variants from de novo genome assemblies by aligning contigs to a reference and calling SVs in assembly-to-reference alignment space, then benchmarking calls against truth sets. Used here to show HiFiCCL-combined assemblies improve detection of SVs >7000 bp on low-coverage (~5x–8x) HiFi data. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Detects large structural variants from de novo genome assemblies by aligning contigs to a reference and calling SVs in assembly-to-reference alignment space, then benchmarking calls against truth sets. Used here to show HiFiCCL-combined assemblies improve detection of SVs >7000 bp on low-coverage (~5x–8x) HiFi data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are available at high coverage (e.g. HG00438 requiring 41x HiFi) — standard read-level SV calling on full-depth data is the appropriate route instead of low-coverage assembly-based detection When the target variants are small (<7000 bp) — this workflow filters explicitly to SVs larger than 7000 bp and the benchmark thresholds are tuned for large SVs When a reference genome is unavailable — HiFiCCL relies on reference-guided chromosome-by-chromosome binning of reads before assembly

skills.description: Use when long-read TR caller output (e.g., TRiCoLOR BCF calls) for a sample with an available assembly-based truth set must be independently confirmed, by checking whether non-reference alleles appear in the truth set.
skills.name: assembly-based-tr-allele-confirmation
skills.search_text: assembly-based-tr-allele-confirmation Use when long-read TR caller output (e.g., TRiCoLOR BCF calls) for a sample with an available assembly-based truth set must be independently confirmed, by checking whether non-reference alleles appear in the truth set. The sample has no available assembly-based truth set — in that case rely on Illumina FM-index validation with <= 2 bp discrepancy tolerance instead The calls are reference-genotype TRs rather than non-reference alleles, since the confirmation ratio is defined only over non-reference alleles Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions (centromeres, telomeres), which neither TRiCoLOR nor assembly-based truth sets can cover http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Confirm non-reference tandem repeat alleles called from long-read data against an assembly-based truth set, as done for HG00733 where 42/58 (~75%) of TRiCoLOR-called non-reference alleles were confirmed. This provides an orthogonal, reference-free validation layer complementing Illumina FM-index validation. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Confirm non-reference tandem repeat alleles called from long-read data against an assembly-based truth set, as done for HG00733 where 42/58 (~75%) of TRiCoLOR-called non-reference alleles were confirmed. This provides an orthogonal, reference-free validation layer complementing Illumina FM-index validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample has no available assembly-based truth set — in that case rely on Illumina FM-index validation with <= 2 bp discrepancy tolerance instead The calls are reference-genotype TRs rather than non-reference alleles, since the confirmation ratio is defined only over non-reference alleles Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions (centromeres, telomeres), which neither TRiCoLOR nor assembly-based truth sets can cover

skills.name: assembly-contamination-detection
skills.search_text: assembly-contamination-detection Use when you need to verify whether public NCBI/GenBank genome assemblies carry detectable Nanopore rapid-barcode (SQK-RBK114-96) or adapter-flank sequences, and to locate which records and contig positions contain them. Input is raw Nanopore reads that need demultiplexing/trimming rather than a finished assembly — use `barbell kit` demux/annotate workflow instead The sequencing kit is outside Barbell's tested presets (RNA and Twist kits are exceptions to its supported DNA kits) Queries are patterns well beyond the ~1000 nt range where Sassy works well (it targets short 20–100 nt barcodes/flanks) http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Screens public genome assemblies (e.g. GenBank records CP131573.1 and CP165501.1) for residual Nanopore rapid-barcode contamination by searching barcode/flank sequences from SQK-RBK114-96 with Sassy-style edit-distance matching. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Screens public genome assemblies (e.g. GenBank records CP131573.1 and CP165501.1) for residual Nanopore rapid-barcode contamination by searching barcode/flank sequences from SQK-RBK114-96 with Sassy-style edit-distance matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Nanopore reads that need demultiplexing/trimming rather than a finished assembly — use `barbell kit` demux/annotate workflow instead The sequencing kit is outside Barbell's tested presets (RNA and Twist kits are exceptions to its supported DNA kits) Queries are patterns well beyond the ~1000 nt range where Sassy works well (it targets short 20–100 nt barcodes/flanks)

skills.description: Use when comparing two long-read whole-genome assemblies and you need to determine whether a tandem/repetitive locus (e.g., the ~40 kb HLA repeat unit) was collapsed to one copy in one assembly but resolved into two copies in the other.
skills.name: assembly-contig-partitioning
skills.search_text: assembly-contig-partitioning Use when comparing two long-read whole-genome assemblies and you need to determine whether a tandem/repetitive locus (e.g., the ~40 kb HLA repeat unit) was collapsed to one copy in one assembly but resolved into two copies in the other. The locus of interest is not repetitive or contains a single copy per haplotype — copy-number partitioning adds no discriminating information You only need overlap detection itself (Fedrann's core FE/DR/ANN pipeline on reads) rather than downstream assembly contig comparison The assemblies to compare were produced by the same assembler with identical parameters and differ only in polishing, where repeat resolution is unlikely to change http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Partitions assembly contigs that map to a target locus (e.g., the human HLA region) into groups representing distinct copies of a repeat unit, then makes per-assembly copy-number calls to detect collapsed or correctly resolved repeats when comparing two assemblers (e.g., native Shasta vs Fedrann-Shasta). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Partitions assembly contigs that map to a target locus (e.g., the human HLA region) into groups representing distinct copies of a repeat unit, then makes per-assembly copy-number calls to detect collapsed or correctly resolved repeats when comparing two assemblers (e.g., native Shasta vs Fedrann-Shasta).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus of interest is not repetitive or contains a single copy per haplotype — copy-number partitioning adds no discriminating information You only need overlap detection itself (Fedrann's core FE/DR/ANN pipeline on reads) rather than downstream assembly contig comparison The assemblies to compare were produced by the same assembler with identical parameters and differ only in polishing, where repeat resolution is unlikely to change

skills.description: Use when comparing a draft assembly (e.g. celegans_flye.fa) against one or more scaffolder outputs (e.g. *ntLink.scaffolds.fa, per-round ntLink_rounds intermediates) to quantify N50/NG50 gains and misassembly trade-offs.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-assessment
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-assessment Use when comparing a draft assembly (e.g. celegans_flye.fa) against one or more scaffolder outputs (e.g. *ntLink.scaffolds.fa, per-round ntLink_rounds intermediates) to quantify N50/NG50 gains and misassembly trade-offs. Input is raw long reads (e.g. SRR10028109 ONT FASTQ) rather than assembled contig/scaffold FASTAs — run the scaffolder first. The goal is to perform scaffolding or gap-filling itself (Basic Protocols 1–3) rather than to evaluate the contiguity of existing assemblies. The claim of interest is sequence-level base accuracy rather than contiguity/misassembly metrics — use a polishing/consensus evaluation instead. Quantifies contiguity improvements of draft vs. scaffolded genome assemblies using abyss-fac (ABySS v2.3.0+) for N50/total-length statistics and QUAST (with --split-scaffold) for NG50, genome fraction, and misassembly-aware metrics, as demonstrated in the ntLink C. elegans Flye protocols. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Quantifies contiguity improvements of draft vs. scaffolded genome assemblies using abyss-fac (ABySS v2.3.0+) for N50/total-length statistics and QUAST (with --split-scaffold) for NG50, genome fraction, and misassembly-aware metrics, as demonstrated in the ntLink C. elegans Flye protocols.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long reads (e.g. SRR10028109 ONT FASTQ) rather than assembled contig/scaffold FASTAs — run the scaffolder first. The goal is to perform scaffolding or gap-filling itself (Basic Protocols 1–3) rather than to evaluate the contiguity of existing assemblies. The claim of interest is sequence-level base accuracy rather than contiguity/misassembly metrics — use a polishing/consensus evaluation instead.

skills.description: Use when assemblies built from raw, corrected, or polished long reads (Miniasm or Flye) must be compared via reference-based metrics — NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, errors per 100 kbp, misassemblies — e.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-metric-extraction
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metric-extraction Use when assemblies built from raw, corrected, or polished long reads (Miniasm or Flye) must be compared via reference-based metrics — NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, errors per 100 kbp, misassemblies — e. No reference genome is available for the dataset — NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, and errors per 100 kbp are reference-based QUAST-LG metrics and cannot be computed. Input is raw or corrected long reads rather than assembled contigs — metrics are per-assembly, so reads must first go through Miniasm or Flye assembly. The goal is to assess the error rate of the corrected reads themselves rather than the downstream assembly quality that correction confers. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies assembly contiguity and accuracy for long-read assembly comparisons: raw, CONSENT-corrected, and polished assemblies are evaluated with QUAST-LG against a reference genome to extract contig counts, NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, errors per 100 kbp, and misassembly counts. This lets a practitioner decide which error-correction tool (or correction-vs-polishing pipeline order) actually improves assembly quality. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Quantifies assembly contiguity and accuracy for long-read assembly comparisons: raw, CONSENT-corrected, and polished assemblies are evaluated with QUAST-LG against a reference genome to extract contig counts, NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, errors per 100 kbp, and misassembly counts. This lets a practitioner decide which error-correction tool (or correction-vs-polishing pipeline order) actually improves assembly quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available for the dataset — NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, and errors per 100 kbp are reference-based QUAST-LG metrics and cannot be computed. Input is raw or corrected long reads rather than assembled contigs — metrics are per-assembly, so reads must first go through Miniasm or Flye assembly. The goal is to assess the error rate of the corrected reads themselves rather than the downstream assembly quality that correction confers.

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between cross-sample merged and individual assemblies when evaluating contig sets from multiple assemblers or related samples by contiguity metrics.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-metrics-comparison
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metrics-comparison Decision support for choosing between cross-sample merged and individual assemblies when evaluating contig sets from multiple assemblers or related samples by contiguity metrics. Input is raw reads with no prior assembly — MeGAMerge operates on assembled contigs, not reads The assemblies come from unrelated samples or data types that MeGAMerge's overlap-layout-consensus merging cannot align (no shared sequence) The goal is to compare total assembly size or N50/N90 only — the paper notes these metrics are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' and are affected by removal of small contigs http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compare contiguity statistics (largest contig length, total bases in contigs >2 kb, number of predicted genes) of a MeGAMerge cross-sample merge against the best within-sample merges to quantify whether merging improves the assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Compare contiguity statistics (largest contig length, total bases in contigs >2 kb, number of predicted genes) of a MeGAMerge cross-sample merge against the best within-sample merges to quantify whether merging improves the assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads with no prior assembly — MeGAMerge operates on assembled contigs, not reads The assemblies come from unrelated samples or data types that MeGAMerge's overlap-layout-consensus merging cannot align (no shared sequence) The goal is to compare total assembly size or N50/N90 only — the paper notes these metrics are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' and are affected by removal of small contigs

skills.name: assembly-contiguity-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metrics-computation Use when you have ≥2 assemblies (contig FASTA files) — e.g. a modified assembler pipeline vs a baseline — and need reproducible contiguity (N50, longest contig) and quality (BUSCO, k-mer QV) comparisons on human long-read data. Input is raw reads or overlap files (e.g. Fedrann overlaps.tsv) rather than assembled contig FASTA files — this skill evaluates assemblies, not pre-assembly artifacts You only need overlap graph quality (precision/recall of candidate overlaps); use the article's benchmarking workflow with alignment filtering instead The reference lineage database or reference genome appropriate to the organism is unavailable — BUSCO against primates_odb10 and QV against T2T-CHM13 v2.0 are human-specific choices http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes whole-genome assembly contiguity and quality metrics — contig N50, longest contig, BUSCO v5.8.0 completeness against primates_odb10, and k-mer quality value (QV) against T2T-CHM13 v2.0 — from contig FASTA files, to benchmark de novo assemblies such as Fedrann-Shasta vs native Shasta. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Computes whole-genome assembly contiguity and quality metrics — contig N50, longest contig, BUSCO v5.8.0 completeness against primates_odb10, and k-mer quality value (QV) against T2T-CHM13 v2.0 — from contig FASTA files, to benchmark de novo assemblies such as Fedrann-Shasta vs native Shasta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or overlap files (e.g. Fedrann overlaps.tsv) rather than assembled contig FASTA files — this skill evaluates assemblies, not pre-assembly artifacts You only need overlap graph quality (precision/recall of candidate overlaps); use the article's benchmarking workflow with alignment filtering instead The reference lineage database or reference genome appropriate to the organism is unavailable — BUSCO against primates_odb10 and QV against T2T-CHM13 v2.0 are human-specific choices

skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metrics-computation Use when comparing diploid genome assemblies from long noisy reads (PacBio CLR, Nanopore R9/R10) and you need NG50, phase block NG50, Hamming error, BUSCO, or reference-based accuracy figures to reproduce published Tables 1-2. skills.description: Use when comparing genome assemblies from several assemblers on the same sample and you need reference-based QUAST metrics (contig count, genome fraction, NGA50, misassemblies, # mismatches/# indels per 100 kbp) plus wall-clock time and peak memory to rank the tools.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-metrics-evaluation
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metrics-evaluation Use when comparing genome assemblies from several assemblers on the same sample and you need reference-based QUAST metrics (contig count, genome fraction, NGA50, misassemblies, # mismatches/# indels per 100 kbp) plus wall-clock time and peak memory to rank the tools. No reference genome exists for the sample — the NGA50, genome fraction, and misassembly counts in this benchmark all come from reference-guided QUAST evaluation. The goal is base-level error correction rather than structural comparison — the paper notes most small local assembly mistakes (including mismatch and indel errors) can be fixed by further polishing with tools such as Pilon or Racon. You need a phased assembly of a diploid genome — the paper states the current version of HASLR does not generate a phased assembly for diploid genomes, so phasing metrics fall outside this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A QUAST-driven benchmarking skill that scores each assembler's contigs against a reference genome to compare contiguity (genome fraction, NGA50), structural errors (misassemblies), and base accuracy (# mismatches / # indels per 100 kbp), alongside wall-clock time and peak memory. In the HASLR paper it reproduces the Table 1 comparison of HASLR against 11 other assemblers on simulated E. coli, yeast, C. elegans, and human datasets. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: A QUAST-driven benchmarking skill that scores each assembler's contigs against a reference genome to compare contiguity (genome fraction, NGA50), structural errors (misassemblies), and base accuracy (# mismatches / # indels per 100 kbp), alongside wall-clock time and peak memory. In the HASLR paper it reproduces the Table 1 comparison of HASLR against 11 other assemblers on simulated E. coli, yeast, C. elegans, and human datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome exists for the sample — the NGA50, genome fraction, and misassembly counts in this benchmark all come from reference-guided QUAST evaluation. The goal is base-level error correction rather than structural comparison — the paper notes most small local assembly mistakes (including mismatch and indel errors) can be fixed by further polishing with tools such as Pilon or Racon. You need a phased assembly of a diploid genome — the paper states the current version of HASLR does not generate a phased assembly for diploid genomes, so phasing metrics fall outside this skill.

skills.name: assembly-contiguity-statistics
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-statistics Use when you have a draft assembly FASTA (e.g. DBG2OLC's backbone_raw.fasta) and need N50/NG50 contiguity figures to decide whether to tune parameters, proceed to consensus, or compare against published metrics. skills.summary: Quantifies the contiguity of a draft genome assembly (N50, NG50 and related statistics) using AssemblyUtility's AssemblyStatistics, optionally cross-checked with QUAST 3.0, to judge whether an assembly stage (e.g. the unpolished DBG2OLC backbone) is good enough before investing in consensus/polishing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The contigs are not raw DBG contigs — the README warns that contigs processed by repeat-resolving techniques such as gap closing or scaffolding introduce errors and can yield poor downstream results, so statistics on such input do not reflect the intended pipeline stage The goal is base-level accuracy after polishing, not draft contiguity — the consensus step (~90% of DBG2OLC runtime, ~2000 CPU hours on human) is a separate evaluation problem You intend to change the assembly pipeline itself rather than measure its output; this skill only reports statistics and gives no tuning advice

skills.search_text: assembly-gap-filling Use when a draft long-read assembly (e.g. FASTA with N-gaps from Flye) should be scaffolded with long reads and have its Ns replaced by spanning read sequence, to improve N50 and gap-free contiguity. The input assembly contains no N-gaps and only single-round scaffolding is needed — use ntLink scaffolding with overlap detection (Basic Protocol 1) instead of gap-filling rounds. The goal is misassembly correction rather than gap closure — use ntLink mappings with Tigmint-long (Alternate Protocol 2) instead. No long-read data spanning the gaps is available, so gap-filling with raw read sequence cannot proceed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fill N-gaps in a long-read-draft genome assembly during ntLink scaffolding, using raw long-read sequence spanning the gaps; demonstrated with ONT reads (SRR10028109) scaffolded on a Flye C. elegans assembly. Gap-filling is combined with in-code scaffolding rounds to maximize contiguity gains. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Fill N-gaps in a long-read-draft genome assembly during ntLink scaffolding, using raw long-read sequence spanning the gaps; demonstrated with ONT reads (SRR10028109) scaffolded on a Flye C. elegans assembly. skills.search_text: attenuation-coefficient-approximation-comparison Use when auditing or configuring the attenuation-coefficient source of a CASYMIR detector cascade, e.
