skills.search_text: bacterial-methylome-pipeline-execution Use when raw WGA/native nanopore signal datasets for bacterial strains must be turned into de novo methylation motif calls and compared against REBASE reference motifs or a baseline method such as nanodisco automatic mode. Input is already a modBAM/bedMethyl from a basecaller's modified-base model (use modkit pileup instead of de novo discovery) The analysis needs only motif typing/fine mapping of known candidate motifs rather than de novo motif discovery The genome is not bacterial or no paired WGA/native nanopore data exist, since the enrichment module relies on WGA-vs-native signal differences http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Execute the Nanoident/nanodisco bacterial methylome pipeline: preprocess WGA and native nanopore signal into difference RDS files with added features (std, time, reference-base proportion, quality score), run de novo methylation motif enrichment, and benchmark recovered motifs against REBASE references. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf397
skills.summary: Execute the Nanoident/nanodisco bacterial methylome pipeline: preprocess WGA and native nanopore signal into difference RDS files with added features (std, time, reference-base proportion, quality score), run de novo methylation motif enrichment, and benchmark recovered motifs against REBASE references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a modBAM/bedMethyl from a basecaller's modified-base model (use modkit pileup instead of de novo discovery) The analysis needs only motif typing/fine mapping of known candidate motifs rather than de novo motif discovery The genome is not bacterial or no paired WGA/native nanopore data exist, since the enrichment module relies on WGA-vs-native signal differences

skills.description: Use when read depth alone is insufficient — e.g. suspected copy number-neutral LOH, or when a CNV/CNA/genotype call needs maximum-likelihood BAF level, homozygous/heterozygous counts, and a BAF P-value from SNP data.
skills.name: baf-likelihood-allele-imbalance-quantification
skills.search_text: baf-likelihood-allele-imbalance-quantification Use when read depth alone is insufficient — e.g. suspected copy number-neutral LOH, or when a CNV/CNA/genotype call needs maximum-likelihood BAF level, homozygous/heterozygous counts, and a BAF P-value from SNP data. No SNP/genotype VCF data exist for the sample — BAF likelihood cannot be computed, so the RD-only workflow (-rd, -his, -partition, -call) must be used instead. The variant file contains variant classes other than SNPs and single-letter indels; CNVpytor ignores all other variants, so BAF evidence would be silently incomplete. The goal is purely coverage-based de novo CNV discovery without any variant-level validation or LOH assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 CNVpytor converts B-allele frequencies of SNPs and single-letter indels from a VCF into per-bin BAF likelihood profiles (symmetrized beta distribution), used as additional evidence for CNVs/CNAs and as primary evidence for copy number-neutral losses of heterozygosity. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: CNVpytor converts B-allele frequencies of SNPs and single-letter indels from a VCF into per-bin BAF likelihood profiles (symmetrized beta distribution), used as additional evidence for CNVs/CNAs and as primary evidence for copy number-neutral losses of heterozygosity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No SNP/genotype VCF data exist for the sample — BAF likelihood cannot be computed, so the RD-only workflow (-rd, -his, -partition, -call) must be used instead. The variant file contains variant classes other than SNPs and single-letter indels; CNVpytor ignores all other variants, so BAF evidence would be silently incomplete. The goal is purely coverage-based de novo CNV discovery without any variant-level validation or LOH assessment.

skills.description: Use when a WGS analysis needs B-allele frequency information from VCF SNPs/small indels converted into per-bin likelihood profiles to support CNV/CNA calling or detect copy number-neutral loss of heterozygosity.
skills.name: baf-likelihood-computation
skills.search_text: baf-likelihood-computation Use when a WGS analysis needs B-allele frequency information from VCF SNPs/small indels converted into per-bin likelihood profiles to support CNV/CNA calling or detect copy number-neutral loss of heterozygosity. The variant file contains no SNPs or single-letter indels — CNVpytor ignores all other variant types, so BAF likelihoods cannot be computed The goal is read-depth-only CNV calling with no allele-imbalance or copy number-neutral LOH evidence Strict file size constraints preclude storing the likelihood matrix and run-time recomputation during '-call' is not acceptable http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Computes per-bin B-allele frequency (BAF) likelihood profiles in CNVpytor by multiplying symmetrized beta distribution likelihoods of all SNPs/small indels within each bin, using BAF as additional evidence for CNVs/CNAs and primary evidence for copy number-neutral LOH. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Computes per-bin B-allele frequency (BAF) likelihood profiles in CNVpytor by multiplying symmetrized beta distribution likelihoods of all SNPs/small indels within each bin, using BAF as additional evidence for CNVs/CNAs and primary evidence for copy number-neutral LOH.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant file contains no SNPs or single-letter indels — CNVpytor ignores all other variant types, so BAF likelihoods cannot be computed The goal is read-depth-only CNV calling with no allele-imbalance or copy number-neutral LOH evidence Strict file size constraints preclude storing the likelihood matrix and run-time recomputation during '-call' is not acceptable

skills.description: Use when a .pytor file contains BAF likelihood data from heterozygous SNPs and it must be exported into JBrowse/igv.js-compatible track files at 10-kb and 100-kb bin resolutions.
skills.name: baf-track-conversion
skills.search_text: baf-track-conversion Use when a .pytor file contains BAF likelihood data from heterozygous SNPs and it must be exported into JBrowse/igv.js-compatible track files at 10-kb and 100-kb bin resolutions. The goal is exporting read-depth (RD) signal rather than BAF — RD is exported at 1, 10, and 100 kb bins, not the 10/100 kb BAF resolutions The .pytor file lacks SNP data because no '-snp file.vcf' and '-baf 10000 100000' steps were run; there is no BAF likelihood data to convert Interactive plotting or call filtering (Q0_range, size_range, p_range) is the goal rather than static genome-browser track export http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts CNVpytor's B-allele frequency (BAF) likelihood data from the .pytor HDF5 container into coordinate-indexed genome-browser track files at multiple bin resolutions for JBrowse/igv.js visualization. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Converts CNVpytor's B-allele frequency (BAF) likelihood data from the .pytor HDF5 container into coordinate-indexed genome-browser track files at multiple bin resolutions for JBrowse/igv.js visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exporting read-depth (RD) signal rather than BAF — RD is exported at 1, 10, and 100 kb bins, not the 10/100 kb BAF resolutions The .pytor file lacks SNP data because no '-snp file.vcf' and '-baf 10000 100000' steps were run; there is no BAF likelihood data to convert Interactive plotting or call filtering (Q0_range, size_range, p_range) is the goal rather than static genome-browser track export

skills.description: Use when comparing resquiggled ONT signal events between a native sample and a WGA control to rank k-mers by signal-level distribution shift and emit candidate methylation motifs.
skills.name: balanced-sampling-signal-distributions
skills.search_text: balanced-sampling-signal-distributions Use when comparing resquiggled ONT signal events between a native sample and a WGA control to rank k-mers by signal-level distribution shift and emit candidate methylation motifs. No matched WGA control multi-fast5 dataset is available, since the KS test requires paired native/control signal distributions Genome coverage depth is below the minimal coverage threshold (default 40), making balanced N=200 per-k-mer sampling unreliable The goal is single-base modification calling rather than de novo motif/k-mer enrichment, for which Tombo's alternative-model detection may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Balanced per-k-mer sampling of normalized nanopore signal events from native and WGA control multi-fast5 data, followed by a two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test, to identify k-mers whose signal distributions differ and which likely carry a modified base. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Balanced per-k-mer sampling of normalized nanopore signal events from native and WGA control multi-fast5 data, followed by a two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test, to identify k-mers whose signal distributions differ and which likely carry a modified base.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched WGA control multi-fast5 dataset is available, since the KS test requires paired native/control signal distributions Genome coverage depth is below the minimal coverage threshold (default 40), making balanced N=200 per-k-mer sampling unreliable The goal is single-base modification calling rather than de novo motif/k-mer enrichment, for which Tombo's alternative-model detection may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when you need to measure how much a consensus-generation step (e.g., SPOA/POA) lowers raw read error rates of ONT or PacBio long reads, or when benchmarking consensus accuracy on simulated VISOR reads against published reduction figures.
skills.name: bam-alignment-base-error-profiling
skills.search_text: bam-alignment-base-error-profiling Use when you need to measure how much a consensus-generation step (e.g., SPOA/POA) lowers raw read error rates of ONT or PacBio long reads, or when benchmarking consensus accuracy on simulated VISOR reads against published reduction figures. Reads are already high-accuracy (e.g., Illumina or HiFi) — the ~77%/~88% reduction figures apply to error-prone third-generation ONT/PB reads The goal is tandem repeat genotyping itself (use the full TRiCoLOR SENSoR/REFER/profiling pipeline) rather than error-rate benchmarking of its consensus step Repeats or reads lie in unassembled genomic regions (e.g., centromeres, telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot be applied and the error model is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantify per-base sequencing error (substitutions, insertions, deletions) in error-prone long reads versus POA-derived consensus sequences, expressed as percentage error reduction. Grounded in TRiCoLOR's REFER module, which uses SPOA partial order alignment to achieve ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PacBio) error reduction. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Quantify per-base sequencing error (substitutions, insertions, deletions) in error-prone long reads versus POA-derived consensus sequences, expressed as percentage error reduction. Grounded in TRiCoLOR's REFER module, which uses SPOA partial order alignment to achieve ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PacBio) error reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already high-accuracy (e.g., Illumina or HiFi) — the ~77%/~88% reduction figures apply to error-prone third-generation ONT/PB reads The goal is tandem repeat genotyping itself (use the full TRiCoLOR SENSoR/REFER/profiling pipeline) rather than error-rate benchmarking of its consensus step Repeats or reads lie in unassembled genomic regions (e.g., centromeres, telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot be applied and the error model is undefined

skills.description: Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) reads have been aligned to a reference FASTA and you need to process the resulting BAM/CRAM for SNV calling and haplotyping, or to emit haplotype-separated reads.
skills.name: bam-alignment-file-processing
skills.search_text: bam-alignment-file-processing Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) reads have been aligned to a reference FASTA and you need to process the resulting BAM/CRAM for SNV calling and haplotyping, or to emit haplotype-separated reads. The task is calling indels or structural variants de novo — Longshot only calls SNVs and can only genotype indels given in an input VCF The input is unaligned reads (FASTQ) with no BAM/CRAM alignment and indexed reference available The data are short Illumina reads better served by short-read callers such as GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Prepare and consume sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM alignments of error-prone single-molecule long reads (PacBio SMRT, ONT) as input to Longshot diploid SNV calling, with coverage/mapping-quality filters shaping which positions become candidate SNVs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Prepare and consume sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM alignments of error-prone single-molecule long reads (PacBio SMRT, ONT) as input to Longshot diploid SNV calling, with coverage/mapping-quality filters shaping which positions become candidate SNVs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is calling indels or structural variants de novo — Longshot only calls SNVs and can only genotype indels given in an input VCF The input is unaligned reads (FASTQ) with no BAM/CRAM alignment and indexed reference available The data are short Illumina reads better served by short-read callers such as GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes

skills.description: Use when a hybrid RNA-seq dataset (e.g. PacBio PRJEB36569 plus Illumina PRJEB36584 aligned to galGal6) has produced separate per-technology BAM files and a genome-guided assembly input is needed for StringTie.
skills.name: bam-alignment-merging
skills.search_text: bam-alignment-merging Use when a hybrid RNA-seq dataset (e.g. PacBio PRJEB36569 plus Illumina PRJEB36584 aligned to galGal6) has produced separate per-technology BAM files and a genome-guided assembly input is needed for StringTie. Only one sequencing technology is available — assemble directly from the single-technology BAM (though note the merged assembly had superior BUSCO quality in this study) No reference genome assembly exists for genome-guided assembly — the pipeline requires a reference genome as a guide Transcripts are already assembled in GTF form — proceed directly to annotate_my_genomes rather than re-merging alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3569 Merge coordinate-sorted BAM alignment files from complementary sequencing technologies — here minimap2-aligned PacBio long reads and HISAT2-aligned fastp-trimmed Illumina short reads — into a single BAM to feed genome-guided transcript assembly with StringTie. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Merge coordinate-sorted BAM alignment files from complementary sequencing technologies — here minimap2-aligned PacBio long reads and HISAT2-aligned fastp-trimmed Illumina short reads — into a single BAM to feed genome-guided transcript assembly with StringTie.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one sequencing technology is available — assemble directly from the single-technology BAM (though note the merged assembly had superior BUSCO quality in this study) No reference genome assembly exists for genome-guided assembly — the pipeline requires a reference genome as a guide Transcripts are already assembled in GTF form — proceed directly to annotate_my_genomes rather than re-merging alignments

skills.description: Use when you have sorted, indexed alignment BAM files (e.g. ONT cDNA or Illumina TruSeq alignments against a plasmid/mRNA reference FASTA) and need automated QC reports covering coverage homogeneity, per-nucleotide error rates, and consensus accuracy.
skills.name: bam-alignment-qc-reporting
skills.search_text: bam-alignment-qc-reporting Use when you have sorted, indexed alignment BAM files (e.g. ONT cDNA or Illumina TruSeq alignments against a plasmid/mRNA reference FASTA) and need automated QC reports covering coverage homogeneity, per-nucleotide error rates, and consensus accuracy. Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than sorted, indexed BAM alignments — first preprocess (Porechop barcode removal, Minimap2 alignment, SAMtools indexing) You need direct detection of nucleoside modifications (e.g. N1-methylpseudouridine) — that requires direct RNA sequencing analysis, not BAM QC reporting A single summary read-length or run-quality statistic suffices and NanoPlot alone answers the question — Mana's ~10 minute analysis is aimed at full mRNA QC reporting http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Automated BAM alignment quality-control reporting for mRNA sequencing using the Mana toolkit, which internally orchestrates SAMtools, BCFtools, Pysam, pysamstats, and bedtools to produce per-nucleotide coverage, per-nucleotide error profiles, and consensus statistics from alignment BAMs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Automated BAM alignment quality-control reporting for mRNA sequencing using the Mana toolkit, which internally orchestrates SAMtools, BCFtools, Pysam, pysamstats, and bedtools to produce per-nucleotide coverage, per-nucleotide error profiles, and consensus statistics from alignment BAMs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than sorted, indexed BAM alignments — first preprocess (Porechop barcode removal, Minimap2 alignment, SAMtools indexing) You need direct detection of nucleoside modifications (e.g. N1-methylpseudouridine) — that requires direct RNA sequencing analysis, not BAM QC reporting A single summary read-length or run-quality statistic suffices and NanoPlot alone answers the question — Mana's ~10 minute analysis is aimed at full mRNA QC reporting

skills.description: Use when input is haplotype-resolved ONT/PacBio BAM alignments and the goal is de novo detection of candidate repetitive regions without known motifs or prior TR annotations.
skills.name: bam-alignment-read-parsing
skills.search_text: bam-alignment-read-parsing Use when input is haplotype-resolved ONT/PacBio BAM alignments and the goal is de novo detection of candidate repetitive regions without known motifs or prior TR annotations. Regions of interest are already annotated as tandem repeats and motif-aware profiling (e.g. REFER module) can be applied directly to the alignments Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify Input alignments are not haplotype-resolved or come from polyploid/haploid chromosomes (e.g. the human Y chromosome), which are outside TRiCoLOR's scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Iterate over haplotype-resolved long-read alignments in BAM format (via pysam) to compute per-read Shannon entropy over non-overlapping 20 bp windows, flagging low-entropy windows as candidate repetitive sequence for downstream tandem-repeat discovery (TRiCoLOR SENSoR step). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Iterate over haplotype-resolved long-read alignments in BAM format (via pysam) to compute per-read Shannon entropy over non-overlapping 20 bp windows, flagging low-entropy windows as candidate repetitive sequence for downstream tandem-repeat discovery (TRiCoLOR SENSoR step).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Regions of interest are already annotated as tandem repeats and motif-aware profiling (e.g. REFER module) can be applied directly to the alignments Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify Input alignments are not haplotype-resolved or come from polyploid/haploid chromosomes (e.g. the human Y chromosome), which are outside TRiCoLOR's scope

skills.description: Use when you have a sorted, indexed BAM of reads aligned to a plasmid or mRNA reference and need to partition reads into on-target mRNA product versus off-target classes (upstream, downstream, antisense, cryptic TSS, E. coli contaminants) with fractional abundances.
skills.name: bam-coordinate-strand-filtering
skills.search_text: bam-coordinate-strand-filtering Use when you have a sorted, indexed BAM of reads aligned to a plasmid or mRNA reference and need to partition reads into on-target mRNA product versus off-target classes (upstream, downstream, antisense, cryptic TSS, E. coli contaminants) with fractional abundances. Input is raw FASTQ reads not yet aligned and sorted/indexed to a reference BAM — alignment (e.g. Minimap2 -ax map-ont, SAMtools sort/index) must come first The analysis goal is per-nucleotide error or variation profiling rather than read-level on/off-target classification — use pysamstats variation/coverage statistics instead Only aggregate QC metrics (read length, poly(A) tail, sequence identity) are needed and read-coordinate classification relative to feature boundaries is not required http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Classifies primary-aligned sequencing reads from mRNA vaccine (VAX-seq) cDNA libraries as on-target versus off-target RNAs by intersecting sorted BAM alignments with reference mRNA feature boundaries in a strand-aware manner, quantifying cryptic TSS, antisense, upstream/downstream, and contaminant (e.g. E. coli) read fractions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Classifies primary-aligned sequencing reads from mRNA vaccine (VAX-seq) cDNA libraries as on-target versus off-target RNAs by intersecting sorted BAM alignments with reference mRNA feature boundaries in a strand-aware manner, quantifying cryptic TSS, antisense, upstream/downstream, and contaminant (e.g. E. coli) read fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads not yet aligned and sorted/indexed to a reference BAM — alignment (e.g. Minimap2 -ax map-ont, SAMtools sort/index) must come first The analysis goal is per-nucleotide error or variation profiling rather than read-level on/off-target classification — use pysamstats variation/coverage statistics instead Only aggregate QC metrics (read length, poly(A) tail, sequence identity) are needed and read-coordinate classification relative to feature boundaries is not required

skills.description: Use when a basecalling stage has produced multiple per-input BAM files (one per POD5) that must be combined into one unmapped BAM before mapping or modification extraction.
skills.name: bam-file-merging
skills.search_text: bam-file-merging Use when a basecalling stage has produced multiple per-input BAM files (one per POD5) that must be combined into one unmapped BAM before mapping or modification extraction. Input BAMs are already mapped/aligned — merging unmapped basecalled BAMs is specific to the pre-mapping stage; use remap-style entry points instead Only a single POD5/BAM exists, so no consolidation is needed The goal is to manipulate modified-base records in an aligned modBAM — use modkit rather than raw BAM merging http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Consolidates the per-POD5 BAMs produced by parallel Dorado basecalling in the Dogme Nextflow pipeline into a single unmapped BAM (merged.bam) that serves as the input for downstream minimap2 mapping. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Consolidates the per-POD5 BAMs produced by parallel Dorado basecalling in the Dogme Nextflow pipeline into a single unmapped BAM (merged.bam) that serves as the input for downstream minimap2 mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAMs are already mapped/aligned — merging unmapped basecalled BAMs is specific to the pre-mapping stage; use remap-style entry points instead Only a single POD5/BAM exists, so no consolidation is needed The goal is to manipulate modified-base records in an aligned modBAM — use modkit rather than raw BAM merging

skills.description: Use when adapter-trimmed plant sRNA-seq reads must be aligned to a masked/artificial tRNA genome and the resulting sorted BAM fed to HAMR or tncRNA classification.
skills.name: bam-file-processing
skills.search_text: bam-file-processing Use when adapter-trimmed plant sRNA-seq reads must be aligned to a masked/artificial tRNA genome and the resulting sorted BAM fed to HAMR or tncRNA classification. Input is already a modification-call table or tncRNA count matrix — no BAM alignment step is needed Aligning to the full (unmasked) reference genome instead of the masked artificial genome — reads from non-tRNA regions would be ambiguously misclassified as tncRNAs Data are not high-throughput small RNA/tRNA-derived sequencing; HAMR's mismatch-signature model is tuned for tRNA modifications and conventional RNA-seq suffers from tRNA modification biases http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Processing of sorted BAM alignments from small RNA-seq reads mapped to the masked artificial tRNA genome (tRNA genes ±50 nt flanks as artificial chromosomes), used as the direct input to HAMR v1.2 for nucleoside modification calling on tncRNAs. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Processing of sorted BAM alignments from small RNA-seq reads mapped to the masked artificial tRNA genome (tRNA genes ±50 nt flanks as artificial chromosomes), used as the direct input to HAMR v1.2 for nucleoside modification calling on tncRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a modification-call table or tncRNA count matrix — no BAM alignment step is needed Aligning to the full (unmasked) reference genome instead of the masked artificial genome — reads from non-tRNA regions would be ambiguously misclassified as tncRNAs Data are not high-throughput small RNA/tRNA-derived sequencing; HAMR's mismatch-signature model is tuned for tRNA modifications and conventional RNA-seq suffers from tRNA modification biases

skills.description: Use when long-read (ONT/PacBio) SAM alignments from minimap2 must be converted, coordinate-sorted and indexed into BAM before breakpoint browsing in AgileStructure or IGV, e.g. for tandem-duplication annotation.
skills.name: bam-file-processing-and-indexing
skills.search_text: bam-file-processing-and-indexing Use when long-read (ONT/PacBio) SAM alignments from minimap2 must be converted, coordinate-sorted and indexed into BAM before breakpoint browsing in AgileStructure or IGV, e.g. for tandem-duplication annotation. The input BAM is already coordinate-sorted and indexed (re-running sort/index adds nothing). The data are short Illumina reads — AgileStructure and the map-ont preset target long-read data; short data will not yield the split-read evidence the downstream annotation relies on. The SAM comes from an aligner other than a long-read-specific one (minimap2/lra), so alignment semantics differ from the AgileStructure workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Prepares long-read alignments for manual structural-variant inspection by converting minimap2 SAM output (using the '-ax map-ont' preset with '--secondary=no') into a coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM via Samtools, so tools like AgileStructure can randomly access and browse breakpoint-spanning reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Prepares long-read alignments for manual structural-variant inspection by converting minimap2 SAM output (using the '-ax map-ont' preset with '--secondary=no') into a coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM via Samtools, so tools like AgileStructure can randomly access and browse breakpoint-spanning reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAM is already coordinate-sorted and indexed (re-running sort/index adds nothing). The data are short Illumina reads — AgileStructure and the map-ont preset target long-read data; short data will not yield the split-read evidence the downstream annotation relies on. The SAM comes from an aligner other than a long-read-specific one (minimap2/lra), so alignment semantics differ from the AgileStructure workflow.

skills.description: Use when trimmed nanopore FASTQ reads should be aligned to a supplied reference sequence (params.ref) to generate alignment statistics and coverage reports prior to consensus genome reconstruction.
skills.name: bam-mapping-quality-reporting
skills.search_text: bam-mapping-quality-reporting Use when trimmed nanopore FASTQ reads should be aligned to a supplied reference sequence (params.ref) to generate alignment statistics and coverage reports prior to consensus genome reconstruction. No reference sequence is available and the sample must instead be reconstructed via VirDetector's automated hybrid assembly branch (params.canu_genome_size). Input files are already FASTA assemblies rather than reads — VirDetector only uses them from the alignment step onwards, so read mapping against a reference from raw reads does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Map filtered nanopore reads to a user-provided reference genome with minimap2, sort/index the resulting BAM with samtools, and characterise mapping quality and coverage with Qualimap. This is the reference-based branch VirDetector uses to produce a reliable viral consensus genome before consensus calling. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Map filtered nanopore reads to a user-provided reference genome with minimap2, sort/index the resulting BAM with samtools, and characterise mapping quality and coverage with Qualimap. This is the reference-based branch VirDetector uses to produce a reliable viral consensus genome before consensus calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference sequence is available and the sample must instead be reconstructed via VirDetector's automated hybrid assembly branch (params.canu_genome_size). Input files are already FASTA assemblies rather than reads — VirDetector only uses them from the alignment step onwards, so read mapping against a reference from raw reads does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you have primary short-read alignments from NextGenMap plus re-aligned soft-clipped reads from YAHA and must combine them into one BAM before SV calling or coverage normalization.
skills.name: bam-merge-with-picard
skills.search_text: bam-merge-with-picard Use when you have primary short-read alignments from NextGenMap plus re-aligned soft-clipped reads from YAHA and must combine them into one BAM before SV calling or coverage normalization. The YAHA split-read alignments are already contained in the NextGenMap primary BAM (no separate merge step is needed). The goal is merging SV call sets (VCF consensus) rather than read alignments — that is SURVIVOR merge territory, not Picard BAM merging. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Merges YAHA split-read (clipped-read) alignments with primary NextGenMap alignments into a single merged BAM per S. pombe strain using Picard-tools, so downstream SV callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPs) see both discordant-pair and split-read evidence in one file. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Merges YAHA split-read (clipped-read) alignments with primary NextGenMap alignments into a single merged BAM per S. pombe strain using Picard-tools, so downstream SV callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPs) see both discordant-pair and split-read evidence in one file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The YAHA split-read alignments are already contained in the NextGenMap primary BAM (no separate merge step is needed). The goal is merging SV call sets (VCF consensus) rather than read alignments — that is SURVIVOR merge territory, not Picard BAM merging.

skills.description: Use when validating metagenome contig assemblies (e.g., MeGAMerge MergedContigs.fasta or individual CLC bio/Velvet/SOAPdenovo assemblies) by quantifying what fraction of contig bases are covered by mapped reads.
skills.name: bam-parsing-coverage-statistics
skills.search_text: bam-parsing-coverage-statistics Use when validating metagenome contig assemblies (e.g., MeGAMerge MergedContigs.fasta or individual CLC bio/Velvet/SOAPdenovo assemblies) by quantifying what fraction of contig bases are covered by mapped reads. No contig FASTA exists yet — coverage validation requires assembled contigs to serve as BWA reference databases, not raw unassembled reads Estimating reference genome coverage or identifying chimeric contigs — the article obtains reference genome coverage by aligning contigs to genome sequences using Nucmer, not by read mapping Comparing assemblies on total assembly size or N50/N90 — the article notes these are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance', and this skill yields coverage percentages instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates metagenome contig assemblies (the final MeGAMerged MergedContigs.fasta and individual assembler FASTAs) by mapping trimmed reads with BWA and parsing the sorted, indexed BAM with SAMtools to compute per-contig and per-assembly percentage of contig bases covered by mapped reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Validates metagenome contig assemblies (the final MeGAMerged MergedContigs.fasta and individual assembler FASTAs) by mapping trimmed reads with BWA and parsing the sorted, indexed BAM with SAMtools to compute per-contig and per-assembly percentage of contig bases covered by mapped reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No contig FASTA exists yet — coverage validation requires assembled contigs to serve as BWA reference databases, not raw unassembled reads Estimating reference genome coverage or identifying chimeric contigs — the article obtains reference genome coverage by aligning contigs to genome sequences using Nucmer, not by read mapping Comparing assemblies on total assembly size or N50/N90 — the article notes these are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance', and this skill yields coverage percentages instead

skills.description: Use when you have one or more aligned BAM files (e.g. nanopore reads aligned by minimap2, NGMLR, or lra) and need MAPQ-thresholded genome coverage fractions, median depth, or per-base depth to characterize a dataset or support coverage-based SV refinement.
skills.name: bam-quality-filtered-coverage-computation
skills.search_text: bam-quality-filtered-coverage-computation Use when you have one or more aligned BAM files (e.g. nanopore reads aligned by minimap2, NGMLR, or lra) and need MAPQ-thresholded genome coverage fractions, median depth, or per-base depth to characterize a dataset or support coverage-based SV refinement. Input is raw FASTQ with no alignment — read QC/length statistics require NanoStat, not coverage computation; a BAM/CRAM is required. You need to call SVs or validate SV types other than deletions and duplications — coverage analysis in this paper only supports filtering/polishing of deletions and duplications, and disCoverage is not a variant caller. Coverage in the sample is highly non-uniform with local peaks and valleys — coverage alone does not prove an SV, so do not use it as sole evidence for variant detection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes quality-filtered genome-wide coverage statistics from nanopore BAM alignments using mosdepth, e.g. reproducing the NA19240 control dataset's 93/92/91% genome coverage (MAPQ ≥ 20) and 16/17/15× median coverage for the lra/minimap2/NGMLR alignments (Table 2). genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Computes quality-filtered genome-wide coverage statistics from nanopore BAM alignments using mosdepth, e.g. reproducing the NA19240 control dataset's 93/92/91% genome coverage (MAPQ ≥ 20) and 16/17/15× median coverage for the lra/minimap2/NGMLR alignments (Table 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ with no alignment — read QC/length statistics require NanoStat, not coverage computation; a BAM/CRAM is required. You need to call SVs or validate SV types other than deletions and duplications — coverage analysis in this paper only supports filtering/polishing of deletions and duplications, and disCoverage is not a variant caller. Coverage in the sample is highly non-uniform with local peaks and valleys — coverage alone does not prove an SV, so do not use it as sole evidence for variant detection.

skills.description: Use when you have a mapped nanopore BAM plus a phased VCF for the same sample and need to separate reads into haplotype-specific sets, e.g. for allele-specific methylation analysis on HG002 R10.4 data.
skills.name: bam-read-assignment-by-haplotype
skills.search_text: bam-read-assignment-by-haplotype Use when you have a mapped nanopore BAM plus a phased VCF for the same sample and need to separate reads into haplotype-specific sets, e.g. for allele-specific methylation analysis on HG002 R10.4 data. No phased VCF is available for the sample — haplotag depends on informative heterozygous variants to assign HP tags Input reads are not aligned to the same reference build as the phased VCF The goal is bulk CpG methylation frequency calling rather than allele-specific (haplotype-resolved) methylation analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Annotates mapped nanopore reads with paternal/maternal haplotype tags using whatshap haplotag against a phased VCF, then splits the tagged BAM into HP:i:1 and HP:i:2 read subsets for allele-specific methylation analysis. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Annotates mapped nanopore reads with paternal/maternal haplotype tags using whatshap haplotag against a phased VCF, then splits the tagged BAM into HP:i:1 and HP:i:2 read subsets for allele-specific methylation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No phased VCF is available for the sample — haplotag depends on informative heterozygous variants to assign HP tags Input reads are not aligned to the same reference build as the phased VCF The goal is bulk CpG methylation frequency calling rather than allele-specific (haplotype-resolved) methylation analysis

skills.description: Use when haplotype-resolved long-read BAM files (e.g., minimap2-aligned ONT or PacBio alignments) and a BED file of candidate repeat regions are available and reads fully spanning each region must be extracted for POA consensus building.
skills.name: bam-read-fetching-by-region
skills.search_text: bam-read-fetching-by-region Use when haplotype-resolved long-read BAM files (e.g., minimap2-aligned ONT or PacBio alignments) and a BED file of candidate repeat regions are available and reads fully spanning each region must be extracted for POA consensus building. The candidate region exceeds the long-read length such that no sequencing read entirely spans R = [S, E]; the fetch-and-trim step requires full-spanning reads Alignments are not haplotype-resolved; TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved long-read alignments as input The target is an unassembled genomic region (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats Fetch, from haplotype-specific long-read BAM alignments, all sequencing reads that entirely span a candidate repetitive region R = [S, E] listed in a BED file, and trim each read so only the sequence between S and E is retained, preparing haplotype-specific read sets for partial order alignment (POA) consensus generation. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Fetch, from haplotype-specific long-read BAM alignments, all sequencing reads that entirely span a candidate repetitive region R = [S, E] listed in a BED file, and trim each read so only the sequence between S and E is retained, preparing haplotype-specific read sets for partial order alignment (POA) consensus generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate region exceeds the long-read length such that no sequencing read entirely spans R = [S, E]; the fetch-and-trim step requires full-spanning reads Alignments are not haplotype-resolved; TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved long-read alignments as input The target is an unassembled genomic region (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats

skills.description: Use when preparing long-read BAM alignments for Longshot candidate SNV discovery and you must enforce Longshot's read-level (min_mapq) and position-level (min_cov, max_cov) filters before allelotyping or genotyping.
skills.name: bam-read-pileup-filtering
skills.search_text: bam-read-pileup-filtering Use when preparing long-read BAM alignments for Longshot candidate SNV discovery and you must enforce Longshot's read-level (min_mapq) and position-level (min_cov, max_cov) filters before allelotyping or genotyping. Calling structural variants (Longshot only calls SNVs; SVs > 50 bp are unsupported — use Delly or an assembly-based method instead) Short-read variant calling where GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the appropriate tools and Longshot's long-read error model does not apply The input is not an aligned, sorted and indexed BAM/CRAM with a matching indexed FASTA reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Filters reads and positions from a sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM of long error-prone reads (PacBio SMRT / Oxford Nanopore) so that only high-confidence read observations feed Longshot's pileup-based candidate SNV identification and downstream allelotyping. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Filters reads and positions from a sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM of long error-prone reads (PacBio SMRT / Oxford Nanopore) so that only high-confidence read observations feed Longshot's pileup-based candidate SNV identification and downstream allelotyping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling structural variants (Longshot only calls SNVs; SVs > 50 bp are unsupported — use Delly or an assembly-based method instead) Short-read variant calling where GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the appropriate tools and Longshot's long-read error model does not apply The input is not an aligned, sorted and indexed BAM/CRAM with a matching indexed FASTA reference

skills.description: Use when basecalled DRS reads have been aligned to a reference transcriptome (e.g. with minimap2) and downstream steps need a sorted, indexed BAM — such as samtools view filtering, jvarkit sam2tsv conversion, or feature extraction in RedNano.
skills.name: bam-sorting-and-indexing
skills.search_text: bam-sorting-and-indexing Use when basecalled DRS reads have been aligned to a reference transcriptome (e.g. with minimap2) and downstream steps need a sorted, indexed BAM — such as samtools view filtering, jvarkit sam2tsv conversion, or feature extraction in RedNano. Alignments already coordinate-sorted and indexed (re-sorting is redundant) Alignment to a whole genome reference instead of a transcriptome — RedNano's resquiggle and feature extraction assume transcript-level coordinates When only basecalled FASTQ exists without an alignment step having been run first http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Sort position-sorted BAM alignments of Nanopore DRS reads to a reference transcriptome and index them with samtools, as required in the RedNano preprocessing pipeline before read-feature extraction and m6A site prediction. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae375
skills.summary: Sort position-sorted BAM alignments of Nanopore DRS reads to a reference transcriptome and index them with samtools, as required in the RedNano preprocessing pipeline before read-feature extraction and m6A site prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Alignments already coordinate-sorted and indexed (re-sorting is redundant) Alignment to a whole genome reference instead of a transcriptome — RedNano's resquiggle and feature extraction assume transcript-level coordinates When only basecalled FASTQ exists without an alignment step having been run first

skills.description: Use when raw SAM alignments from Nanopore/cDNA/dRNA reads must be converted to sorted, indexed BAM before read-fate QC, per-nucleotide error profiling, or genome-viewer inspection.
skills.name: bam-sorting-and-indexing
skills.search_text: bam-sorting-and-indexing Use when raw SAM alignments from Nanopore/cDNA/dRNA reads must be converted to sorted, indexed BAM before read-fate QC, per-nucleotide error profiling, or genome-viewer inspection. Input is already a sorted, indexed BAM ready for Mana or pysamstats — re-sorting adds no value The analysis goal is raw read QC (read length/N50) that operates directly on FASTQ and does not require alignment, e.g. NanoPlot v1.38.1 summaries Alignments are short-read Illumina mappings from a different aligner workflow where the map-ont preset and this SAMtools step were not part of the validated chain http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Convert Minimap2 SAM alignments into sorted, indexed BAM files with SAMtools v1.15 so downstream QC tools (Mana, pysamstats, IGV) can consume them. This is a prerequisite step in the VAX-seq mRNA vaccine quality pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Convert Minimap2 SAM alignments into sorted, indexed BAM files with SAMtools v1.15 so downstream QC tools (Mana, pysamstats, IGV) can consume them. This is a prerequisite step in the VAX-seq mRNA vaccine quality pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a sorted, indexed BAM ready for Mana or pysamstats — re-sorting adds no value The analysis goal is raw read QC (read length/N50) that operates directly on FASTQ and does not require alignment, e.g. NanoPlot v1.38.1 summaries Alignments are short-read Illumina mappings from a different aligner workflow where the map-ont preset and this SAMtools step were not part of the validated chain

skills.description: Use when an indexed BAM of long reads (e.g. ONT reads aligned with minimap2 -ax map-ont --secondary=no) must be scanned for split-read junctions to locate large-scale genomic rearrangement breakpoints.
skills.name: bam-split-read-parsing
skills.search_text: bam-split-read-parsing Use when an indexed BAM of long reads (e.g. ONT reads aligned with minimap2 -ax map-ont --secondary=no) must be scanned for split-read junctions to locate large-scale genomic rearrangement breakpoints. Input reads are short Illumina reads rather than PacBio/ONT long reads — short reads rarely span breakpoints and cannot supply the linked primary/secondary split alignments this method relies on. The BAM was produced with secondary alignments suppressed inconsistently or by an aligner that does not emit linked split-alignment records, since junction positions cannot be reconstructed from primary alignments alone. The goal is de novo variant calling with base-level sensitivity for SNVs or small indels rather than large-scale structural rearrangement breakpoint detection. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Parses an indexed long-read BAM file to recover split-read alignment junctions and call putative structural-rearrangement breakpoints, the core detection mechanism behind AgileStructure's breakpoint identification from aligned PacBio/ONT data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Parses an indexed long-read BAM file to recover split-read alignment junctions and call putative structural-rearrangement breakpoints, the core detection mechanism behind AgileStructure's breakpoint identification from aligned PacBio/ONT data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads rather than PacBio/ONT long reads — short reads rarely span breakpoints and cannot supply the linked primary/secondary split alignments this method relies on. The BAM was produced with secondary alignments suppressed inconsistently or by an aligner that does not emit linked split-alignment records, since junction positions cannot be reconstructed from primary alignments alone. The goal is de novo variant calling with base-level sensitivity for SNVs or small indels rather than large-scale structural rearrangement breakpoint detection.

skills.description: Use when a FLNC read set produced by PacBio isoseq3 refine exists only as a BAM file and downstream steps (e.g. TAMA gstama_polyacleanup) require FASTA input.
skills.name: bam-to-fasta-conversion
skills.search_text: bam-to-fasta-conversion Use when a FLNC read set produced by PacBio isoseq3 refine exists only as a BAM file and downstream steps (e.g. TAMA gstama_polyacleanup) require FASTA input. The reads are already in FASTA/FASTQ format and the next step (e.g. TAMA cleanup or an aligner) can consume them directly. You need to preserve BAM-specific per-read tags or quality information — conversion to FASTA discards everything except the sequence records. You are working with short-read BAM alignments that need sorting or SAM conversion rather than sequence export to FASTA. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts PacBio FLNC read files from BAM format into FASTA format using BAMTools convert, the intermediate step in nf-core/isoseq between isoseq3 refine (chimera removal) and TAMA cleanup (polyA trimming), because downstream TAMA cleanup consumes FASTA input. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: Converts PacBio FLNC read files from BAM format into FASTA format using BAMTools convert, the intermediate step in nf-core/isoseq between isoseq3 refine (chimera removal) and TAMA cleanup (polyA trimming), because downstream TAMA cleanup consumes FASTA input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already in FASTA/FASTQ format and the next step (e.g. TAMA cleanup or an aligner) can consume them directly. You need to preserve BAM-specific per-read tags or quality information — conversion to FASTA discards everything except the sequence records. You are working with short-read BAM alignments that need sorting or SAM conversion rather than sequence export to FASTA.

skills.description: Use when meth_phaser_parallel has finished writing block-relationship outputs into a work directory and the re-phased VCF and haplotag-updated BAM are needed to complete the phasing workflow.
skills.name: bam-vcf-haplotag-post-processing
skills.search_text: bam-vcf-haplotag-post-processing Use when meth_phaser_parallel has finished writing block-relationship outputs into a work directory and the re-phased VCF and haplotag-updated BAM are needed to complete the phasing workflow. The input BAM still contains secondary or supplementary alignments — these must be removed first, otherwise a pysam MM tag reading error is triggered The phasing target is a sex chromosome — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, so MethPhaser (including its post-processing) will not work The meth_phaser_parallel work directory has not been produced yet — post-processing is strictly downstream of the block-relationship step http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 MethPhaser's post-processing step that consumes the methylation-based block-relationship work directory and emits the final re-phased VCF plus a re-haplotagged BAM in which reads carry methylation-informed haplotype tags. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: MethPhaser's post-processing step that consumes the methylation-based block-relationship work directory and emits the final re-phased VCF plus a re-haplotagged BAM in which reads carry methylation-informed haplotype tags.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAM still contains secondary or supplementary alignments — these must be removed first, otherwise a pysam MM tag reading error is triggered The phasing target is a sex chromosome — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, so MethPhaser (including its post-processing) will not work The meth_phaser_parallel work directory has not been produced yet — post-processing is strictly downstream of the block-relationship step

skills.description: Use when preprocessing SLR (e.g. 10X linked-read) BAMs with BX tags before barcode-aware sliding-window assembly, to exclude poorly aligned reads while retaining barcode-based retrieval.
skills.name: barcode-aware-bam-read-filtering
skills.search_text: barcode-aware-bam-read-filtering Use when preprocessing SLR (e.g. 10X linked-read) BAMs with BX tags before barcode-aware sliding-window assembly, to exclude poorly aligned reads while retaining barcode-based retrieval. The input BAM is not position-sorted and indexed or lacks BX barcode tags, so M(B) queries cannot be built or resolved You want no poorly aligned reads collected at all — use the hidden -n option instead of running this filter Reads are plain long reads (PacBio Hi-Fi / ONT) rather than SLR reads with barcode tags; Blackbird's SLR mode and its filter are designed around SLR BAM input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A filtering step in Blackbird that scans a position-sorted, indexed SLR read BAM with BX barcode tags, flags badly aligned read pairs (unplaced/soft-clipped over >20% of length at Phred >20, or zero/absent AM tag), and indexes the resulting read set R in a parallel flat hash map (read map M) so reads sharing barcodes can be retrieved as M(B) during barcode-based local assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: A filtering step in Blackbird that scans a position-sorted, indexed SLR read BAM with BX barcode tags, flags badly aligned read pairs (unplaced/soft-clipped over >20% of length at Phred >20, or zero/absent AM tag), and indexes the resulting read set R in a parallel flat hash map (read map M) so reads sharing barcodes can be retrieved as M(B) during barcode-based local assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAM is not position-sorted and indexed or lacks BX barcode tags, so M(B) queries cannot be built or resolved You want no poorly aligned reads collected at all — use the hidden -n option instead of running this filter Reads are plain long reads (PacBio Hi-Fi / ONT) rather than SLR reads with barcode tags; Blackbird's SLR mode and its filter are designed around SLR BAM input

skills.description: Use when performing local assembly of medium-size SV regions (50–10,000 bp) from position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAMs, and you must define 50 kbp segments and decide which barcodes support each segment before assembly.
skills.name: barcode-aware-genome-segmentation-sliding-window
skills.search_text: barcode-aware-genome-segmentation-sliding-window Use when performing local assembly of medium-size SV regions (50–10,000 bp) from position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAMs, and you must define 50 kbp segments and decide which barcodes support each segment before assembly. The goal is a whole-genome assembly — Blackbird explicitly avoids whole-genome assembly in favor of local sliding-window segments The SLR BAM is not position-sorted/indexed or lacks BX barcode tags, so B(s) selection and barcode-linked read extraction cannot be performed Only short reads without barcodes are available and no SLR data exists — Blackbird requires SLR barcodes for this stage http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Blackbird's local assembly stage: instead of whole-genome assembly, the BWA-indexed reference is divided into overlapping 50 kbp sliding-window segments, and for each segment a barcode list B(s) of synthetic long-read (SLR) barcodes is built to pull in barcode-linked reads for a modified SPAdes (spades_for_blackbird) assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Blackbird's local assembly stage: instead of whole-genome assembly, the BWA-indexed reference is divided into overlapping 50 kbp sliding-window segments, and for each segment a barcode list B(s) of synthetic long-read (SLR) barcodes is built to pull in barcode-linked reads for a modified SPAdes (spades_for_blackbird) assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a whole-genome assembly — Blackbird explicitly avoids whole-genome assembly in favor of local sliding-window segments The SLR BAM is not position-sorted/indexed or lacks BX barcode tags, so B(s) selection and barcode-linked read extraction cannot be performed Only short reads without barcodes are available and no SLR data exists — Blackbird requires SLR barcodes for this stage

skills.description: Use when detecting and placing novel sequence insertions (>300 bp) in linked-read data (10X Genomics barcoded BAMs), when short-read SV callers fail to resolve large insertions.
skills.name: barcode-aware-local-assembly
skills.search_text: barcode-aware-local-assembly Use when detecting and placing novel sequence insertions (>300 bp) in linked-read data (10X Genomics barcoded BAMs), when short-read SV callers fail to resolve large insertions. Insertions of interest are shorter than ~300 bp: Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes per insertion, and small insertions usually have too few associated barcodes and insufficient coverage for anchor assembly The input is a whole-genome de novo assembly task or a general SV discovery problem beyond NRS insertions (e.g. deletions, inversions, duplications) Data lacks barcoded synthetic long-read structure (e.g. standard short-read or long-read-only data without barcodes) — the method depends on barcode and long-fragment information http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Detects and assembles non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions from synthetic long-read (linked-read) data by combining non-trivial read alignment signatures with barcode information, avoiding whole-genome de novo assembly. Novel-X implements this as a Snakemake pipeline for 10X Genomics, TELL-Seq and stLFR datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Detects and assembles non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions from synthetic long-read (linked-read) data by combining non-trivial read alignment signatures with barcode information, avoiding whole-genome de novo assembly. Novel-X implements this as a Snakemake pipeline for 10X Genomics, TELL-Seq and stLFR datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Insertions of interest are shorter than ~300 bp: Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes per insertion, and small insertions usually have too few associated barcodes and insufficient coverage for anchor assembly The input is a whole-genome de novo assembly task or a general SV discovery problem beyond NRS insertions (e.g. deletions, inversions, duplications) Data lacks barcoded synthetic long-read structure (e.g. standard short-read or long-read-only data without barcodes) — the method depends on barcode and long-fragment information

skills.description: Use when input is a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR bam aligned to a BWA-indexed reference and the goal is sensitive insertion/deletion SV calling, optionally boosted by paired PacBio HiFi long-read bam/FASTQ.
skills.name: barcode-aware-local-assembly-sv-detection
skills.search_text: barcode-aware-local-assembly-sv-detection Use when input is a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR bam aligned to a BWA-indexed reference and the goal is sensitive insertion/deletion SV calling, optionally boosted by paired PacBio HiFi long-read bam/FASTQ. The question requires whole-genome assembly or SVs outside the 50–10,000 bp medium-size range that Blackbird targets Input lacks BX barcode tags or is not a position-sorted, indexed bam — required inputs for Blackbird's barcode-aware sliding window Only short-read data is available and no SLR or long-read data exist; SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range 'cannot be resolved with short-read sequencing' per the article http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Detect medium-size structural variants (50–10,000 bp) from synthetic long reads (SLR) alone or hybrid SLR + low-coverage long reads using Blackbird, which performs barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly instead of whole-genome assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151

skills.description: Use when CCS reads from PacBio subreads (movieX.ccs.bam/fasta) contain PAIso-seq spike-in cDNAs with the 16-nt barcode 5'-GAGTGCTACTCTAGTA-3' that must be assigned to tail-length groups before tail-length accuracy assessment.
skills.name: barcode-demultiplexing-of-spikein-cdnas
skills.search_text: barcode-demultiplexing-of-spikein-cdnas Use when CCS reads from PacBio subreads (movieX.ccs.bam/fasta) contain PAIso-seq spike-in cDNAs with the 16-nt barcode 5'-GAGTGCTACTCTAGTA-3' that must be assigned to tail-length groups before tail-length accuracy assessment. Reads lack the 16-nt spike-in barcode 5'-GAGTGCTACTCTAGTA-3' (e.g. biological GV-oocyte cDNAs barcoded with distinct dU-containing templates rather than the synthetic spike-in barcode), since trim.py matching would fail Analysis goal is transcriptome-wide poly(A) tail annotation of native transcripts rather than spike-in accuracy validation, which requires genome alignment with minimap2 -x splice and the TAPIS pipeline instead of barcode grouping http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Demultiplexes PAIso-seq spike-in CCS reads by the 16-nt barcode (5'-GAGTGCTACTCTAGTA-3') and trims the 25-nt 3'-adapter (5'-GTACTCTGCGTTGATACCACTGCTT-3') so per-read poly(A) tail lengths can be assigned to each synthetic tail-length group (expected 10/30/50/70/100 nt). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Demultiplexes PAIso-seq spike-in CCS reads by the 16-nt barcode (5'-GAGTGCTACTCTAGTA-3') and trims the 25-nt 3'-adapter (5'-GTACTCTGCGTTGATACCACTGCTT-3') so per-read poly(A) tail lengths can be assigned to each synthetic tail-length group (expected 10/30/50/70/100 nt).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads lack the 16-nt spike-in barcode 5'-GAGTGCTACTCTAGTA-3' (e.g. biological GV-oocyte cDNAs barcoded with distinct dU-containing templates rather than the synthetic spike-in barcode), since trim.py matching would fail Analysis goal is transcriptome-wide poly(A) tail annotation of native transcripts rather than spike-in accuracy validation, which requires genome alignment with minimap2 -x splice and the TAPIS pipeline instead of barcode grouping

skills.description: Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads with Barbell and you need to understand, reproduce, or tune how barcode/flank edit-distance costs are converted into accept/reject decisions during annotation.
skills.name: barcode-edit-distance-scoring
skills.search_text: barcode-edit-distance-scoring Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads with Barbell and you need to understand, reproduce, or tune how barcode/flank edit-distance costs are converted into accept/reject decisions during annotation. The goal is basecalling or alignment rather than barcode match scoring — Barbell scores barcode/flank edits only (Dorado covers basecalling/modification calling). Reads contain no barcode constructs or flanking adapter sequences to align against (random Fflank matches should not be scored as barcodes). skills.description: Use when preparing a hybrid short-read/long-read scRNA-seq experiment (e.g., 10x Chromium split into Illumina SR and ONT LR pools) and you need a compact whitelist of top SR barcodes that covers most reads before trie-based LR–SR barcode matching.
skills.name: barcode-selection-threshold-tuning
skills.search_text: barcode-selection-threshold-tuning Use when preparing a hybrid short-read/long-read scRNA-seq experiment (e.g., 10x Chromium split into Illumina SR and ONT LR pools) and you need a compact whitelist of top SR barcodes that covers most reads before trie-based LR–SR barcode matching. The experiment is not 10x Genomics scRNA-seq — scTagger in its current form is specific for 10x Genomics, and other platforms are only supported if the LR template includes a fixed sequence next to the barcode You want to avoid short reads entirely — use the extract_sr_bc_from_lr alternative that builds the whitelist by exact-matching 10x barcodes on long-read segments instead The expected number of relevant barcodes is much larger than tens of thousands — scTagger's design is not expected to scale well beyond that regime http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Tunes scTagger's stage-1 short-read (SR) barcode selection: iteratively retain the most frequent SR barcodes in batches of 1,000 until an added batch contributes less than t=0.5% of total SR coverage, balancing barcode whitelist size against SR throughput loss (9–17% on the paper's real datasets). genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104530

skills.name: base-converted-long-read-pileup-extraction
skills.search_text: base-converted-long-read-pileup-extraction Use when you have C-to-T and G-to-A converted nanopore reads already mapped and -aligned (output_CT.sorted.bam, output_GA.sorted.bam) and need per-CpG methylation frequencies. Input is native (unconverted) nanopore signal data — use nanopolish call-methylation instead, which reads methylation directly from electric signals without enzymatic conversion The question requires distinguishing 5-methylcytosine from 5-hydroxymethylcytosine on the same molecule — nanoEM's conversion approach cannot separate mC and hmC Only short-read (non-converted) methylation data such as EMseq/bisulfite FASTQ is available — this pipeline's minimap2 map-ont alignment and dual-pileup logic applies to long converted reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extract per-CpG methylation observations from nanoEM data by pileup-ing the C-to-T and G-to-A converted BAM files at CpG sites, then combining the two strands' pileups into per-site methylation frequencies. This is the core methylation-calling step of the nanoEM enzymatic-conversion + nanopore pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397

skills.description: Use when calling SVs from PE or LR BAM/CRAM data and you need per-breakpoint consensus contigs assembled from supporting read bases, or when benchmarking the linear-time behavior of the consensus stage.
skills.name: base-quality-weighted-graph-vertex-construction
skills.search_text: base-quality-weighted-graph-vertex-construction Use when calling SVs from PE or LR BAM/CRAM data and you need per-breakpoint consensus contigs assembled from supporting read bases, or when benchmarking the linear-time behavior of the consensus stage. The goal is full de novo assembly of SVs or resolution of multi-allelic sites and full-length insertions in PE data — the paper notes these remain unresolved because dysgu has no de novo assembly stage. Input reads are already consensus contigs or variant calls (VCF) rather than per-base aligned supporting reads, since vertex construction requires individual supporting bases with base qualities. Only read-support information (no sequence) is wanted — the README's '--contigs False' model removes all sequence-related metrics and bypasses this stage. Reconstructs dysgu's consensus-sequence generator for SV breakpoints: a positional de Bruijn graph-inspired DAG whose vertices are individual bases weighted by summed base quality, resolved to a consensus by longest-path back-tracing with soft-clip trimming. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Reconstructs dysgu's consensus-sequence generator for SV breakpoints: a positional de Bruijn graph-inspired DAG whose vertices are individual bases weighted by summed base quality, resolved to a consensus by longest-path back-tracing with soft-clip trimming.

skills.description: Use when a per-motif methylation-type and methylated-position prediction from Nanoident inference must be validated against basecall base features, e.g. a predicted 6mA position that is not an A in the motif sequence, to recover position-mapping accuracy (~+6.34%).
skills.name: basecall-feature-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: basecall-feature-consistency-checking Use when a per-motif methylation-type and methylated-position prediction from Nanoident inference must be validated against basecall base features, e.g. a predicted 6mA position that is not an A in the motif sequence, to recover position-mapping accuracy (~+6.34%). The input is not Nanoident model output — e.g. already pileup-converted ONT modified-base calls (modBAM/bedMethyl via modkit), which have no per-motif position probability distribution to re-rank. The methylation type of the motif is unknown or outside 4mC/5mC/6mA, since the consistency rule maps each type to an expected nucleotide (A or C). Working on the 7-sample, 46-motif LOOCV training dataset rather than the independent 12-motif test set, where the correction module's reported gain was measured. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A post-processing consistency check from Nanoident that verifies whether the predicted methylated position within a motif actually carries the nucleotide implied by the predicted methylation type (4mC→A, 5mC→C, 6mA→A), and if not, iteratively reassigns the methylated base to the candidate position with the next-highest predicted probability until type-position consistency is achieved. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf397
skills.summary: A post-processing consistency check from Nanoident that verifies whether the predicted methylated position within a motif actually carries the nucleotide implied by the predicted methylation type (4mC→A, 5mC→C, 6mA→A), and if not, iteratively reassigns the methylated base to the candidate position with the next-highest predicted probability until type-position consistency is achieved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not Nanoident model output — e.g. already pileup-converted ONT modified-base calls (modBAM/bedMethyl via modkit), which have no per-motif position probability distribution to re-rank. skills.description: Use when per-read base-calling features (mismatch/deletion frequencies, base quality scores) from ONT direct RNA reads must be pooled into per-site summaries before scoring candidate m6A sites, especially across partial-methylation mixtures.

skills.search_text: bed-coordinate-overlap-analysis Use when comparing pangenome graph constructions (e.g., from 45 low-coverage ~5x human assemblies) against a reference graph, where bubble regions can be emitted as BED and overlap-based TP/FP/FN classification is needed. The evaluation target is per-sample assembly contiguity or misassembly length (e.g., HiFiCCL-Hifiasm vs Hifiasm contig QC) rather than graph-level bubble agreement with an existing reference graph. No reference pangenome graph BED exists to compare against — precision/recall under the 80%-overlap rule cannot be defined. The graph regions of interest are not bubbles (e.g., per-sample path SV calling), where tools like minigraph's -c calling mode or minisv are the intended route. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluates pangenome graph fidelity by converting minigraph-built graphs into bubble-region BED files with gfatools and classifying predicted bubbles against an HPRC reference-graph BED via an 80% reciprocal-overlap rule to compute precision, recall, and F1. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Evaluates pangenome graph fidelity by converting minigraph-built graphs into bubble-region BED files with gfatools and classifying predicted bubbles against an HPRC reference-graph BED via an 80% reciprocal-overlap rule to compute precision, recall, and F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The evaluation target is per-sample assembly contiguity or misassembly length (e.g., HiFiCCL-Hifiasm vs Hifiasm contig QC) rather than graph-level bubble agreement with an existing reference graph. No reference pangenome graph BED exists to compare against — precision/recall under the 80%-overlap rule cannot be defined. The graph regions of interest are not bubbles (e.g., per-sample path SV calling), where tools like minigraph's -c calling mode or minisv are the intended route.

skills.description: Use when you have two BED-format modification-site tables (e.g. mAFiA predictions with modRatio and GLORI reference stoichiometry) and need a coordinate-matched benchmark set to compute stoichiometry correlations.
skills.name: bed-file-coordinate-matching
skills.search_text: bed-file-coordinate-matching Use when you have two BED-format modification-site tables (e.g. mAFiA predictions with modRatio and GLORI reference stoichiometry) and need a coordinate-matched benchmark set to compute stoichiometry correlations. Sites are reported in different genome builds or transcript coordinates that have not been lifted over to a common reference (e.g. GRCh38) The goal is read-level modification probability comparison rather than site-level stoichiometry aggregation Site coverage in the dRNA-Seq data falls below the minimum of 50 reads required for comparison against GLORI measurements Match predicted m6A sites in mAFiA.sites.bed to reference GLORI_chrX.bed stoichiometry by genomic coordinate (chromosome, position, strand) so that site-level modRatio values can be benchmarked against orthogonal chemical measurements. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47661-2
skills.summary: Match predicted m6A sites in mAFiA.sites.bed to reference GLORI_chrX.bed stoichiometry by genomic coordinate (chromosome, position, strand) so that site-level modRatio values can be benchmarked against orthogonal chemical measurements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sites are reported in different genome builds or transcript coordinates that have not been lifted over to a common reference (e.g. GRCh38) The goal is read-level modification probability comparison rather than site-level stoichiometry aggregation Site coverage in the dRNA-Seq data falls below the minimum of 50 reads required for comparison against GLORI measurements

skills.summary: Reconstructs TRiCoLOR's SENSoR module, which scans haplotype-resolved ONT long-read alignments for low Shannon-entropy windows (20 bp windows, entropy <= 1.23, >= 5 read support) and emits a sorted, 3-column candidate_repetitive_regions.bed of merged intervals (~160,000-~260,000 regions, mean ~900 bp per sample).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target regions lie in unassembled parts of the genome (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats in Input is short-read or non-haplotype-resolved data, since the module assumes haplotype-resolved long-read alignments You need profiling of annotated tandem repeats rather than de novo discovery of candidate repetitive regions

skills.description: Use when you have a mapped modBAM of nanopore gDNA with m6A modifications and need open-chromatin signal regions plus per-genome BedGraph tracks from the Dogme open-chromatin entry point.
skills.name: bedgraph-track-generation
skills.search_text: bedgraph-track-generation Use when you have a mapped modBAM of nanopore gDNA with m6A modifications and need open-chromatin signal regions plus per-genome BedGraph tracks from the Dogme open-chromatin entry point. Input is RNA or cDNA rather than genomic DNA modBAMs — the modkit open-chromatin workflow is intended for mapped BAMs with m6A modifications on gDNA. modkit version is below 0.5 — the open-chromatin support requires modkit 0.5 and higher. The goal is transcript isoform quantification rather than chromatin accessibility — that is handled by the kallisto/LR-Kallisto branch of Dogme. Within the Dogme Nextflow pipeline, this skill converts modkit (v0.5+) pileup calls of exogenous-m6A-labeled genomic DNA into a consolidated per-genome open-chromatin BED file and BedGraph tracks, enabling identification of accessible regulatory regions and genome-browser visualization. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066

skills.search_text: bedtools-genomic-interval-intersection Use when two methylation callers/runs (e.g., DeepMod2 output.per_site BED files from RRMS and whole-genome Nanopore sequencing) must be reduced to a common set of CpG sites before computing agreement statistics like Pearson r. skills.when_to_use_negative: The methylation data is still in modBAM form with MM/ML tags and has not yet been summarized to per-site bedMethyl tables — convert with modkit first. The goal is region-level (e.g., differentially methylated region) overlap rather than single-CpG site concordance.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a variant caller on a defined benchmark region such as 1KGp3 common variant sites, where whole-genome call sets must be filtered to a common-site subset before truth-set comparison.
skills.name: benchmark-region-restriction-to-common-sites
skills.search_text: benchmark-region-restriction-to-common-sites Use when benchmarking a variant caller on a defined benchmark region such as 1KGp3 common variant sites, where whole-genome call sets must be filtered to a common-site subset before truth-set comparison. The goal is whole-genome (not common-variant-restricted) performance; the paper reports a separate whole-genome F1 (87.26% for ONT) that should not be mixed with the 1KP common-variant F1 (90.53% for ONT). The truth set or benchmark region is not shared between the callers being compared — filtering only one caller's calls to the common sites would bias the comparison. The task is de novo discovery of rare or novel variants; restricting to 1KGp3 common sites discards exactly those calls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Restricts variant-caller output (e.g., Clairvoyante and Nanopolish calls on ONT data) to 1KGp3 common variant sites before computing benchmark metrics (F1, FPR, FNR, precision) against the GIAB HG001 v3.3.2 truth set, enabling a like-for-like 'common variants' comparison as in the paper's Table 4. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Restricts variant-caller output (e.g., Clairvoyante and Nanopolish calls on ONT data) to 1KGp3 common variant sites before computing benchmark metrics (F1, FPR, FNR, precision) against the GIAB HG001 v3.3.2 truth set, enabling a like-for-like 'common variants' comparison as in the paper's Table 4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is whole-genome (not common-variant-restricted) performance; the paper reports a separate whole-genome F1 (87.26% for ONT) that should not be mixed with the 1KP common-variant F1 (90.53% for ONT). The truth set or benchmark region is not shared between the callers being compared — filtering only one caller's calls to the common sites would bias the comparison. The task is de novo discovery of rare or novel variants; restricting to 1KGp3 common sites discards exactly those calls.
