skills.search_text: binary-threshold-classification Use when you have a per-read feature table from raw nanopore signal mapping (read_id with mapping-quality and chain-score ratios) and must decide each read as 'mapped' or 'unmapped' via a weighted-sum threshold. The task is to actually run the RawHash2 mapper over FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5 signals against a reference genome — use the RawHash2 indexing and mapping pipeline, not the post-hoc decision reconstruction. The features are not the weighted ratios described here (e.g., you have base-level alignments or minimap2 PAF scores); the weighted-sum threshold is specific to the mapping-quality and chain-score ratio features. Multi-class or probabilistic classification is needed; this mechanism produces exactly one binary decision per read. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs RawHash2's mapped/unmapped decision mechanism, in which a weighted sum of per-read score ratios (mapping-quality ratio, best and mean chain-score ratios) is compared against a predefined threshold instead of RawHash's fixed conditional checks. It provides a transparent, reproducible binary classifier over real-time nanopore signal mapping features. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Reconstructs RawHash2's mapped/unmapped decision mechanism, in which a weighted sum of per-read score ratios (mapping-quality ratio, best and mean chain-score ratios) is compared against a predefined threshold instead of RawHash's fixed conditional checks. It provides a transparent, reproducible binary classifier over real-time nanopore signal mapping features.

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from ONT long-read pileups and candidate loci have already been classified as high-quality (known 1000G variants with R_alt > 0.3, or unknown variants with R_alt > 0.7 and no neighbor within 10 bp), and a statistical genotype assignment is needed.
skills.name: binomial-model-snv-genotyping
skills.search_text: binomial-model-snv-genotyping Use when calling SNVs from ONT long-read pileups and candidate loci have already been classified as high-quality (known 1000G variants with R_alt > 0.3, or unknown variants with R_alt > 0.7 and no neighbor within 10 bp), and a statistical genotype assignment is needed. Candidate loci classified as low-quality (unknown variants with R_alt <= 0.7, low-complexity regions) — these require the haplotype-aware consensus/realignment pipeline instead of the binomial model. The task is indel or structural variant calling — miniSNV's binomial genotyping targets single nucleotide variants only. A pre-trained deep-learning caller is preferred for maximum accuracy on well-characterized human data — the statistical binomial approach trades DL model capacity for lightness and cross-species generalization. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3569 miniSNV assigns genotypes to high-quality candidate SNV loci by comparing the likelihoods of the three diploid genotypes (0/0, 0/1, 1/1) under a binomial model with sequencing error probability theta = 0.03, using allele counts from the read pileup rather than a trained deep-learning model. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: miniSNV assigns genotypes to high-quality candidate SNV loci by comparing the likelihoods of the three diploid genotypes (0/0, 0/1, 1/1) under a binomial model with sequencing error probability theta = 0.03, using allele counts from the read pileup rather than a trained deep-learning model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate loci classified as low-quality (unknown variants with R_alt <= 0.7, low-complexity regions) — these require the haplotype-aware consensus/realignment pipeline instead of the binomial model. The task is indel or structural variant calling — miniSNV's binomial genotyping targets single nucleotide variants only. A pre-trained deep-learning caller is preferred for maximum accuracy on well-characterized human data — the statistical binomial approach trades DL model capacity for lightness and cross-species generalization.

skills.search_text: bisulfite-ground-truth-curation Use when benchmarking per-read or per-site 5mC methylation calls from Nanopore reads against short-read bisulfite ground truth to quantify caller accuracy via F1-score. Validating methylation calls against methylation microarray ground truth instead of short-read bisulfite — this skill's thresholds are defined for the EpiQC bisulfite benchmark Evaluating sites with intermediate 20–80% methylation — EpiQC reported poor concordance among short-read methods for these sites, so they must be excluded Calling methylation from signal data itself — this skill curates ground truth and scores calls; use the DeepMod2 methylation-calling workflow to generate output.per_read/output.per_site first http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Curates extreme-methylation CpG ground truth from short-read bisulfite data (EpiQC, GEO GSE186383) and computes per-read and per-site precision/recall/F1 for Nanopore methylation callers such as DeepMod2 on HG002 R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 datasets. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Curates extreme-methylation CpG ground truth from short-read bisulfite data (EpiQC, GEO GSE186383) and computes per-read and per-site precision/recall/F1 for Nanopore methylation callers such as DeepMod2 on HG002 R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Validating methylation calls against methylation microarray ground truth instead of short-read bisulfite — this skill's thresholds are defined for the EpiQC bisulfite benchmark Evaluating sites with intermediate 20–80% methylation — EpiQC reported poor concordance among short-read methods for these sites, so they must be excluded Calling methylation from signal data itself — this skill curates ground truth and scores calls; use the DeepMod2 methylation-calling workflow to generate output.per_read/output.per_site first

skills.description: Use when read-level 5mCpG predictions from PacBio CCS callers need objective scoring against BS-seq ground truth, e.g., reproducing ccsmeth's ~0.90 accuracy and ~0.97 AUC on long (>=10 Kb) HiFi reads.
skills.name: bisulfite-ground-truth-metric-computation
skills.search_text: bisulfite-ground-truth-metric-computation Use when read-level 5mCpG predictions from PacBio CCS callers need objective scoring against BS-seq ground truth, e.g., reproducing ccsmeth's ~0.90 accuracy and ~0.97 AUC on long (>=10 Kb) HiFi reads. Evaluating site-level (genome-wide aggregated) methylation rather than single-molecule read-level calls, where correlations with BS-seq are the appropriate metric The goal is detecting non-CpG 5mC or other modifications such as 6mA, since these models were designed only for symmetric CpG methylation Detecting hemimethylated CpGs, which these methods are incapable of detecting http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Benchmark read-level 5mCpG methylation callers (e.g., ccsmeth vs primrose) by matching per-CpG predictions against bisulfite-sequencing ground truth and computing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC per test set. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Benchmark read-level 5mCpG methylation callers (e.g., ccsmeth vs primrose) by matching per-CpG predictions against bisulfite-sequencing ground truth and computing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC per test set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating site-level (genome-wide aggregated) methylation rather than single-molecule read-level calls, where correlations with BS-seq are the appropriate metric The goal is detecting non-CpG 5mC or other modifications such as 6mA, since these models were designed only for symmetric CpG methylation Detecting hemimethylated CpGs, which these methods are incapable of detecting

skills.description: Use when benchmarking nanopore 5mC callers on plant genomes and balanced ground-truth labels are needed: called cytosines must be intersected with BS-seq-derived positive (100%) and negative (0%) CHH site lists at >=5x coverage.
skills.name: bisulfite-high-confidence-site-annotation
skills.search_text: bisulfite-high-confidence-site-annotation Use when benchmarking nanopore 5mC callers on plant genomes and balanced ground-truth labels are needed: called cytosines must be intersected with BS-seq-derived positive (100%) and negative (0%) CHH site lists at >=5x coverage. Whole-genome methylation frequency correlation with BS-seq is the goal rather than site-level ground truthing — DeepPlant's whole-genome correlation workflow (0.705-0.838 on CHH) is the appropriate alternative Datasets contain no BS-seq data for the species, so balanced 100%/0% high-confidence CHH site lists cannot be derived (scarcity of high-methylation CHH samples remains a challenge) CpG or CHG contexts with different k-mer requirements — DeepPlant uses default CpG/CHG kmer sizes of 51 rather than the CHH kmer size of 13 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Constructs high-confidence ground-truth CHH methylation site lists from BS-seq data — fully methylated (100%) positives and unmethylated (0%) negatives — and intersects them with nanopore methylation calls from tools like DeepPlant and Dorado to compute single-molecule accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC, and AP across plant species. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Constructs high-confidence ground-truth CHH methylation site lists from BS-seq data — fully methylated (100%) positives and unmethylated (0%) negatives — and intersects them with nanopore methylation calls from tools like DeepPlant and Dorado to compute single-molecule accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC, and AP across plant species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Whole-genome methylation frequency correlation with BS-seq is the goal rather than site-level ground truthing — DeepPlant's whole-genome correlation workflow (0.705-0.838 on CHH) is the appropriate alternative Datasets contain no BS-seq data for the species, so balanced 100%/0% high-confidence CHH site lists cannot be derived (scarcity of high-methylation CHH samples remains a challenge) CpG or CHG contexts with different k-mer requirements — DeepPlant uses default CpG/CHG kmer sizes of 51 rather than the CHH kmer size of 13

skills.description: Use when training or evaluating a nanopore CpG methylation model and you need trusted single-molecule labels: derive positive (fully methylated) and negative (fully unmethylated) high-confidence CpG site lists from BS-seq data at >=20x coverage to feed DeepBAM's extract_hc_sites mode.
skills.name: bisulfite-high-confidence-site-curation
skills.search_text: bisulfite-high-confidence-site-curation Use when training or evaluating a nanopore CpG methylation model and you need trusted single-molecule labels: derive positive (fully methylated) and negative (fully unmethylated) high-confidence CpG site lists from BS-seq data at >=20x coverage to feed DeepBAM's extract_hc_sites mode. The goal is modification calling on already-trained models — use DeepBAM's extract_and_call_mods workflow instead of re-curating training sites No bisulfite-seq or fully methylated/unmethylated treated-DNA controls exist for the sample, so trustworthy positive/negative labels cannot be derived Targeting non-CpG methylation contexts — the curation and DeepBAM extraction are specified for CpG (motif_type CG) only http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Curates high-confidence CpG sites from bisulfite-seq (BS-seq) treated DNAs — fully methylated positives and fully unmethylated negatives at sufficient read coverage — to serve as ground-truth labels for DeepBAM's extract_hc_sites feature extraction and Bi-LSTM methylation-model training on nanopore R10.4 data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Curates high-confidence CpG sites from bisulfite-seq (BS-seq) treated DNAs — fully methylated positives and fully unmethylated negatives at sufficient read coverage — to serve as ground-truth labels for DeepBAM's extract_hc_sites feature extraction and Bi-LSTM methylation-model training on nanopore R10.4 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is modification calling on already-trained models — use DeepBAM's extract_and_call_mods workflow instead of re-curating training sites No bisulfite-seq or fully methylated/unmethylated treated-DNA controls exist for the sample, so trustworthy positive/negative labels cannot be derived Targeting non-CpG methylation contexts — the curation and DeepBAM extraction are specified for CpG (motif_type CG) only

skills.description: Use when validating Nanopore per-site CpG methylation frequencies (e.g. DeepMod2 output.per_site.aggregated) against short-read bisulfite sequencing or methylation microarray ground truth via Pearson correlation on shared CpG sites.
skills.name: bisulfite-methylation-ground-truth-matching
skills.search_text: bisulfite-methylation-ground-truth-matching Use when validating Nanopore per-site CpG methylation frequencies (e.g. DeepMod2 output.per_site.aggregated) against short-read bisulfite sequencing or methylation microarray ground truth via Pearson correlation on shared CpG sites. Evaluating per-read methylation accuracy instead of per-site methylation frequency — the paper uses F1-score against binary per-read ground truth (sites ≥90% or <10% methylated) for that, not correlation Detection or quantification of modifications other than 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides 5mCpG models and there is a lack of available training datasets for other modification types Sites with intermediate 20–80% methylation — EpiQC reported poor concordance at these sites both between ONT and short-read methods and among short-read methods, so they should be excluded from the benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark Nanopore per-site CpG methylation calls (e.g. DeepMod2 output.per_site.aggregated) against short-read bisulfite sequencing or methylation microarray ground truth by intersecting shared CpG positions and computing Pearson correlation. This is the correlation-based validation strategy the DeepMod2 paper uses to demonstrate r > 0.95 agreement with short-read sequencing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Benchmark Nanopore per-site CpG methylation calls (e.g. DeepMod2 output.per_site.aggregated) against short-read bisulfite sequencing or methylation microarray ground truth by intersecting shared CpG positions and computing Pearson correlation. This is the correlation-based validation strategy the DeepMod2 paper uses to demonstrate r > 0.95 agreement with short-read sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating per-read methylation accuracy instead of per-site methylation frequency — the paper uses F1-score against binary per-read ground truth (sites ≥90% or <10% methylated) for that, not correlation Detection or quantification of modifications other than 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides 5mCpG models and there is a lack of available training datasets for other modification types Sites with intermediate 20–80% methylation — EpiQC reported poor concordance at these sites both between ONT and short-read methods and among short-read methods, so they should be excluded from the benchmark

skills.description: Use when comparing nanopore methylation callers for a plant genome against a bisulfite-sequencing (BS-seq) ground truth, when you have R10.4 POD5 plus sorted BAM alignments and want genome-wide CHH/CpG/CHG methylation-frequency Pearson r as the accuracy metric.
skills.name: bisulfite-sequence-correlation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: bisulfite-sequence-correlation-benchmarking Use when comparing nanopore methylation callers for a plant genome against a bisulfite-sequencing (BS-seq) ground truth, when you have R10.4 POD5 plus sorted BAM alignments and want genome-wide CHH/CpG/CHG methylation-frequency Pearson r as the accuracy metric. Evaluating single-molecule accuracy or F1 score of a caller — this skill measures aggregate whole-genome methylation-frequency correlation with BS-seq, not per-read agreement Data from the R9.4 platform — tools like Tombo, Megalodon, and DeepSignal-Plant were built for R9.4 and cannot be directly applied to R10.4, and the benchmark correlations reported here are R10.4-specific Benchmarking CpG/CHG-only questions where CHH scarcity is not the concern — the paper's key contribution and hardest benchmark case is CHH, where high-methylation positive samples are scarce http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Benchmark plant 5mC methylation callers (DeepPlant vs Dorado/Dorado*) on ONT R10.4 data by downsampling reads to 5x-30x depth, aggregating per-cytosine methylation rates into genome-wide methylation frequencies, and computing Pearson correlations against whole-genome BS-seq methylation frequencies across CpG, CHG, and especially CHH contexts. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Benchmark plant 5mC methylation callers (DeepPlant vs Dorado/Dorado*) on ONT R10.4 data by downsampling reads to 5x-30x depth, aggregating per-cytosine methylation rates into genome-wide methylation frequencies, and computing Pearson correlations against whole-genome BS-seq methylation frequencies across CpG, CHG, and especially CHH contexts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating single-molecule accuracy or F1 score of a caller — this skill measures aggregate whole-genome methylation-frequency correlation with BS-seq, not per-read agreement Data from the R9.4 platform — tools like Tombo, Megalodon, and DeepSignal-Plant were built for R9.4 and cannot be directly applied to R10.4, and the benchmark correlations reported here are R10.4-specific Benchmarking CpG/CHG-only questions where CHH scarcity is not the concern — the paper's key contribution and hardest benchmark case is CHH, where high-methylation positive samples are scarce

skills.description: Use when comparing the number of methylated cytosine sites detected from Nanopore reads (DeepSignal-plant calls) against bisulfite-sequencing site counts, per CG/CHG/CHH context, to quantify detection coverage gains.
skills.name: bisulfite-vs-nanopore-methylation-count-comparison
skills.search_text: bisulfite-vs-nanopore-methylation-count-comparison Use when comparing the number of methylated cytosine sites detected from Nanopore reads (DeepSignal-plant calls) against bisulfite-sequencing site counts, per CG/CHG/CHH context, to quantify detection coverage gains. Input data is bisulfite-only (no Nanopore FAST5 signals) — there is nothing to re-squiggle or call modifications from Evaluating per-read or per-site methylation accuracy against a bisulfite gold standard (correlations, precision) rather than counting detected-site totals — that is a different comparison task Applying to non-plant or non-R9.4 data without a suitable model — the pre-trained checkpoint is specific to A. thaliana/O. sativa R9.4 1D reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantifies how many 5mC sites DeepSignal-plant detects from Nanopore reads relative to bisulfite sequencing, by counting per-context methylation calls and computing excess percentages. It tests whether Nanopore-based methylation calling (here, DeepSignal-plant at ~100× coverage) profiles more 5mC sites than bisulfite in A. thaliana and O. sativa. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how many 5mC sites DeepSignal-plant detects from Nanopore reads relative to bisulfite sequencing, by counting per-context methylation calls and computing excess percentages. It tests whether Nanopore-based methylation calling (here, DeepSignal-plant at ~100× coverage) profiles more 5mC sites than bisulfite in A. thaliana and O. sativa.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is bisulfite-only (no Nanopore FAST5 signals) — there is nothing to re-squiggle or call modifications from Evaluating per-read or per-site methylation accuracy against a bisulfite gold standard (correlations, precision) rather than counting detected-site totals — that is a different comparison task Applying to non-plant or non-R9.4 data without a suitable model — the pre-trained checkpoint is specific to A. thaliana/O. sativa R9.4 1D reads

skills.description: Use when nanopore (MinION 1d/2d) or PacBio reads must be gapped-aligned to a reference after candidate mapping locations have been ranked, and BLAST-like sensitivity with >95% precision is required.
skills.name: bit-vector-sequence-alignment
skills.search_text: bit-vector-sequence-alignment Use when nanopore (MinION 1d/2d) or PacBio reads must be gapped-aligned to a reference after candidate mapping locations have been ranked, and BLAST-like sensitivity with >95% precision is required. When a lightweight coarse mapping (seed hits or anchors) is sufficient and full gapped alignment cost is unnecessary When index memory is a hard constraint: GraphMap's hash index is ~14x reference size (~42 GB peak for a human genome), unlike BWT-based mappers When reads must be mapped to a transcriptome with spliced alignments — a dedicated spliced-alignment mode was still under development http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Final-stage gapped alignment of long, error-prone nanopore reads using Myers' bit-vector (semiglobal) alignment, applied to top-ranked candidate regions after GraphMap's LCSk chaining and L1-regression filtering produce high-precision (>95%) mappings. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Final-stage gapped alignment of long, error-prone nanopore reads using Myers' bit-vector (semiglobal) alignment, applied to top-ranked candidate regions after GraphMap's LCSk chaining and L1-regression filtering produce high-precision (>95%) mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a lightweight coarse mapping (seed hits or anchors) is sufficient and full gapped alignment cost is unnecessary When index memory is a hard constraint: GraphMap's hash index is ~14x reference size (~42 GB peak for a human genome), unlike BWT-based mappers When reads must be mapped to a transcriptome with spliced alignments — a dedicated spliced-alignment mode was still under development

skills.description: Use when comparing read-sequence compression performance of FASTQ compressors (NanoSpring, Gzip, ENANO, CoLoRd) on nanopore datasets, or when reporting compressed sizes in bits per base.
skills.name: bits-per-base-compression-ratio-calculation
skills.search_text: bits-per-base-compression-ratio-calculation Use when comparing read-sequence compression performance of FASTQ compressors (NanoSpring, Gzip, ENANO, CoLoRd) on nanopore datasets, or when reporting compressed sizes in bits per base. When compressing or measuring full FASTQ files including identifiers and quality scores — NanoSpring intentionally compresses only base sequences, so the metric would not be comparable When reads come from an older basecaller with error rates well above the ~5% range, where ratios outside the reported 0.35–0.65 bpb range are expected (e.g. fast-mode Guppy on S. aureus gives ~0.69 bpb) For reference-based compressors such as RENANO, which the paper evaluates separately and whose size accounting differs http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Compute compressed size in bits per base (bits/base, bpb) for nanopore FASTQ read sequences, the primary compression-ratio metric used by NanoSpring, by dividing the compressed archive size in bits by the total number of sequenced bases. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Compute compressed size in bits per base (bits/base, bpb) for nanopore FASTQ read sequences, the primary compression-ratio metric used by NanoSpring, by dividing the compressed archive size in bits by the total number of sequenced bases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When compressing or measuring full FASTQ files including identifiers and quality scores — NanoSpring intentionally compresses only base sequences, so the metric would not be comparable When reads come from an older basecaller with error rates well above the ~5% range, where ratios outside the reported 0.35–0.65 bpb range are expected (e.g. fast-mode Guppy on S. aureus gives ~0.69 bpb) For reference-based compressors such as RENANO, which the paper evaluates separately and whose size accounting differs

skills.description: Use when comparing compressed sizes of NanoSpring output streams (or any sequence compressor's output) across FASTQ datasets of unequal length, e.g. reproducing a per-stream compression breakdown like Figure 3.
skills.name: bits-per-base-normalization
skills.search_text: bits-per-base-normalization Use when comparing compressed sizes of NanoSpring output streams (or any sequence compressor's output) across FASTQ datasets of unequal length, e.g. reproducing a per-stream compression breakdown like Figure 3. The analysis targets quality score or read identifier compression — NanoSpring does not compress these, so bits-per-base accounting of its streams cannot cover them. Comparing against reference-based compressors whose stream structure differs, so per-stream breakdowns are not directly comparable without redefining stream categories. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Normalizes compressed byte sizes of individual compressed streams (consensus, error, lone-read) by the total number of sequenced bases, yielding bits-per-base per stream so compression contributions can be compared across nanopore FASTQ datasets of different sizes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Normalizes compressed byte sizes of individual compressed streams (consensus, error, lone-read) by the total number of sequenced bases, yielding bits-per-base per stream so compression contributions can be compared across nanopore FASTQ datasets of different sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets quality score or read identifier compression — NanoSpring does not compress these, so bits-per-base accounting of its streams cannot cover them. Comparing against reference-based compressors whose stream structure differs, so per-stream breakdowns are not directly comparable without redefining stream categories.

skills.description: Use when you have hybrid long-read correction results (e.g., HECIL output at iteration 1 and 5) plus a reference genome and need alignment-based accuracy metrics like PI and % matched bases to validate improvement over uncorrected reads.
skills.name: blasr-alignment-based-metrics-validation
skills.search_text: blasr-alignment-based-metrics-validation Use when you have hybrid long-read correction results (e.g., HECIL output at iteration 1 and 5) plus a reference genome and need alignment-based accuracy metrics like PI and % matched bases to validate improvement over uncorrected reads. Input data lacks a reference genome or curated alignments, so alignment-based validation metrics (PI, % matched bases) cannot be computed The task is self-correction of long reads without short reads (e.g., HGAP-style); HECIL is a hybrid method that requires Illumina short reads Evaluating assemblies rather than read-level correction accuracy — use the paper's complementary QUAST/MUMmer dnadiff workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validation workflow from the HECIL paper (Sci Rep 2018) in which uncorrected and iteratively corrected PacBio-style long reads are aligned to a reference genome with BLASR to compute percent identity (PI), % matched bases, and number of aligned reads, demonstrating that hybrid correction improves read accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Validation workflow from the HECIL paper (Sci Rep 2018) in which uncorrected and iteratively corrected PacBio-style long reads are aligned to a reference genome with BLASR to compute percent identity (PI), % matched bases, and number of aligned reads, demonstrating that hybrid correction improves read accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks a reference genome or curated alignments, so alignment-based validation metrics (PI, % matched bases) cannot be computed The task is self-correction of long reads without short reads (e.g., HGAP-style); HECIL is a hybrid method that requires Illumina short reads Evaluating assemblies rather than read-level correction accuracy — use the paper's complementary QUAST/MUMmer dnadiff workflow instead

skills.description: Use when protein-coding transcript translations must be linked to reference protein sequences (e.g., GENCODE Basic translations vs. UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot human canonical or isoform entries) to build genomic-to-protein position mappings.
skills.name: blast-based-sequence-alignment
skills.search_text: blast-based-sequence-alignment Use when protein-coding transcript translations must be linked to reference protein sequences (e.g., GENCODE Basic translations vs. UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot human canonical or isoform entries) to build genomic-to-protein position mappings. Non-identical or cross-species homology is needed — the MetaDome pipeline retains only identical sequence matches, so approximate homologs cannot be recovered here. Input transcripts lack a valid ORF (no ATG start or no stop codon) or their Biopython cDNA translation disagrees with the annotated translation — these are excluded before BLAST rather than realigned. The goal is variant tolerance or meta-domain analysis directly — that requires the downstream MetaDome mapping database and Pfam domain projection, not a fresh BLAST step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Align protein-coding transcript translations to a curated reference proteome with Protein–Protein BLAST to establish transcript-to-protein identity links. In MetaDome, this maps GENCODE Basic translations onto Swiss-Prot canonical/isoform sequences as the basis for genomic-to-protein position mappings. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Align protein-coding transcript translations to a curated reference proteome with Protein–Protein BLAST to establish transcript-to-protein identity links. In MetaDome, this maps GENCODE Basic translations onto Swiss-Prot canonical/isoform sequences as the basis for genomic-to-protein position mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Non-identical or cross-species homology is needed — the MetaDome pipeline retains only identical sequence matches, so approximate homologs cannot be recovered here. Input transcripts lack a valid ORF (no ATG start or no stop codon) or their Biopython cDNA translation disagrees with the annotated translation — these are excluded before BLAST rather than realigned. The goal is variant tolerance or meta-domain analysis directly — that requires the downstream MetaDome mapping database and Pfam domain projection, not a fresh BLAST step.

skills.description: Use when a long-read (MinION/PacBio) mapping pipeline needs per-alignment statistical confidence (E-value, MAPQ) written into a SAM file so alignments can be ranked, filtered, or compared against BLAST-like sensitivity benchmarks.
skills.name: blast-evalue-annotation
skills.search_text: blast-evalue-annotation Use when a long-read (MinION/PacBio) mapping pipeline needs per-alignment statistical confidence (E-value, MAPQ) written into a SAM file so alignments can be ranked, filtered, or compared against BLAST-like sensitivity benchmarks. Input is a short-read (Illumina) mapping task where standard mapper MAPQ conventions suffice and GraphMap's ~14x reference-size hash index (~42 GB peak for human genome) is impractical You need a published, calibrated P-value/E-value interpretation for variant calling rather than a mapper-internal BLAST-style heuristic score The alignment step has already been performed by BLAST itself or another tool that natively reports E-values http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Annotate GraphMap read alignments with a BLAST-style E-value and a meaningful SAM mapping-quality so downstream users can rank and filter nanopore mapping results. GraphMap emits these as custom SAM tags alongside the final alignment. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Annotate GraphMap read alignments with a BLAST-style E-value and a meaningful SAM mapping-quality so downstream users can rank and filter nanopore mapping results. GraphMap emits these as custom SAM tags alongside the final alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a short-read (Illumina) mapping task where standard mapper MAPQ conventions suffice and GraphMap's ~14x reference-size hash index (~42 GB peak for human genome) is impractical You need a published, calibrated P-value/E-value interpretation for variant calling rather than a mapper-internal BLAST-style heuristic score The alignment step has already been performed by BLAST itself or another tool that natively reports E-values

skills.description: Use when input is a PacBio CCS BAM from HIT-scISOseq or 10x-based scIso-Seq libraries and you must identify FLNC reads, demultiplex cell barcodes/UMIs, and trim poly(A) tails before genome mapping.
skills.name: blast-primer-mapping
skills.search_text: blast-primer-mapping Use when input is a PacBio CCS BAM from HIT-scISOseq or 10x-based scIso-Seq libraries and you must identify FLNC reads, demultiplex cell barcodes/UMIs, and trim poly(A) tails before genome mapping. Input is raw subreads BAM rather than CCS reads — generate CCS first (ccs with min-rq 0.75) before primer classification Library construction does not use the PacBio original scIso-Seq or BGI HIT-scISOseq 10x-compatible primers, so primer_F/primer_S sequences would not match the reads You only need gene-level expression matrices and already have FLNC FASTQs — skip to downstream cellBC/UMI correction and scGene_matrix steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Classifies PacBio CCS reads from HIT-scISOseq/10x scIso-Seq libraries as full-length non-concatemer (FLNC) reads by mapping 5' and 3' primer sequences with blastn and running scISA-Tools' classify_by_primer, extracting cell barcodes, UMIs, and trimmed transcripts. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Classifies PacBio CCS reads from HIT-scISOseq/10x scIso-Seq libraries as full-length non-concatemer (FLNC) reads by mapping 5' and 3' primer sequences with blastn and running scISA-Tools' classify_by_primer, extracting cell barcodes, UMIs, and trimmed transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw subreads BAM rather than CCS reads — generate CCS first (ccs with min-rq 0.75) before primer classification Library construction does not use the PacBio original scIso-Seq or BGI HIT-scISOseq 10x-compatible primers, so primer_F/primer_S sequences would not match the reads You only need gene-level expression matrices and already have FLNC FASTQs — skip to downstream cellBC/UMI correction and scGene_matrix steps

skills.description: Use when reassembled insertion sequences from a structural-variant callset must be screened for a known diagnostic motif (e.g., a transduction thumbprint) that standard TE annotation libraries do not model.
skills.name: blast-sequence-similarity-searching
skills.search_text: blast-sequence-similarity-searching Use when reassembled insertion sequences from a structural-variant callset must be screened for a known diagnostic motif (e.g., a transduction thumbprint) that standard TE annotation libraries do not model. The goal is general TE family annotation of all repeats, which RetroInspector already performs via RepeatMasker against Dfam — the BLAST step is a targeted follow-up only for SVA calls. The insertion class of interest is already represented in Dfam and recovered by the standard annotation step, so no thumbprint search is needed. The reference motif is a profile HMM (e.g., Dfam family model) rather than a short transduced fragment; use HMMER/RepeatMasker-style search instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Use BLAST to identify specific sequence signatures inside reassembled insertion sequences — here, detecting the MAST2 thumbprint fragment carried by SVA F1 retrotransposon elements that Dfam/RepeatMasker annotation misses, labeling generic SVA calls as SVA F1. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Use BLAST to identify specific sequence signatures inside reassembled insertion sequences — here, detecting the MAST2 thumbprint fragment carried by SVA F1 retrotransposon elements that Dfam/RepeatMasker annotation misses, labeling generic SVA calls as SVA F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is general TE family annotation of all repeats, which RetroInspector already performs via RepeatMasker against Dfam — the BLAST step is a targeted follow-up only for SVA calls. The insertion class of interest is already represented in Dfam and recovered by the standard annotation step, so no thumbprint search is needed. The reference motif is a profile HMM (e.g., Dfam family model) rather than a short transduced fragment; use HMMER/RepeatMasker-style search instead.

skills.search_text: bridge-scored-greedy-contig-merging Use when scaffolding a short-read (Illumina MiSeq/SPAdes) draft assembly with streaming Oxford Nanopore long reads, and long reads span pairs of unique contigs whose relative order and orientation must be resolved greedily. Input is already a finished scaffold or a closed genome — no bridging or gap-filling is needed. No long reads spanning two unique contigs are available (npScarf builds the backbone from reads aligned to two unique contigs; without them no bridges form). Millisecond-level real-time updating is required — npScarf operates at minute-level temporal resolution and still depends on a base-caller and pre-generated short-read data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Kruskal-style greedy contig merging from long-read bridges: npScarf classifies SPAdes contigs by copy number, groups nanopore reads consistently supporting a relative position into scored bridges, merges unique contigs greedily once a bridge scoring threshold is reached, fills gaps with bridge-read consensus, and inserts repetitive contigs into those gaps. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Kruskal-style greedy contig merging from long-read bridges: npScarf classifies SPAdes contigs by copy number, groups nanopore reads consistently supporting a relative position into scored bridges, merges unique contigs greedily once a bridge scoring threshold is reached, fills gaps with bridge-read consensus, and inserts repetitive contigs into those gaps.

Evaluating single-molecule methylation calling accuracy (AUROC/F1) — use a labeled-site benchmark instead of population-level frequency correlation with BS-seq Data lacks matched BS-seq methylation frequency tracks, so no correlation ground truth can be computed Calling non-CpG methylation (other motif types than CG) — the workflow specifies motif_type=CG only http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies how well genome-wide CpG methylation frequency profiles from nanopore methylation callers (DeepBAM vs Dorado) agree with matched BS-seq tracks by computing Pearson correlations across down-sampled R10.4 human and plant datasets at 10x and 30x coverage. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Quantifies how well genome-wide CpG methylation frequency profiles from nanopore methylation callers (DeepBAM vs Dorado) agree with matched BS-seq tracks by computing Pearson correlations across down-sampled R10.4 human and plant datasets at 10x and 30x coverage.

skills.description: Use when validating per-site methylation frequencies produced from PacBio CCS/HiFi reads against an orthogonal gold standard (BS-seq bedmethyl or nanopore methylation calls) by intersecting matched CpGs and computing Pearson correlation coefficients.
skills.name: bs-seq-vs-ccsmeth-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: bs-seq-vs-ccsmeth-correlation-analysis Use when validating per-site methylation frequencies produced from PacBio CCS/HiFi reads against an orthogonal gold standard (BS-seq bedmethyl or nanopore methylation calls) by intersecting matched CpGs and computing Pearson correlation coefficients. The modification of interest is not symmetric CpG methylation — the approach cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA No orthogonal ground-truth methylation calls (BS-seq or nanopore) are available for the matched CpG sites, so correlations cannot be computed Reads are not PacBio CCS/HiFi — ccsmeth relies on SMRT kinetics features (IPD and PW) specific to CCS reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Benchmark site-level 5mCpG methylation frequencies predicted by ccsmeth from PacBio CCS reads by computing Pearson correlations against BS-seq and nanopore methylation calls on matched CpG sites, validating that ccsmeth reaches >0.90 correlations even at 10x coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Benchmark site-level 5mCpG methylation frequencies predicted by ccsmeth from PacBio CCS reads by computing Pearson correlations against BS-seq and nanopore methylation calls on matched CpG sites, validating that ccsmeth reaches >0.90 correlations even at 10x coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modification of interest is not symmetric CpG methylation — the approach cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA No orthogonal ground-truth methylation calls (BS-seq or nanopore) are available for the matched CpG sites, so correlations cannot be computed Reads are not PacBio CCS/HiFi — ccsmeth relies on SMRT kinetics features (IPD and PW) specific to CCS reads

skills.description: Use when single-cell short-read counts must be projected onto isoforms defined by a bulk long-read transcriptome — e.g. combining ENCODE PacBio mouse cortex/hippocampus isoforms with Tasic Smart-Seq2 scRNA-seq counts to study isoform co-usage across cell types.
skills.name: bulk-long-read-and-scrnaseq-integration
skills.search_text: bulk-long-read-and-scrnaseq-integration Use when single-cell short-read counts must be projected onto isoforms defined by a bulk long-read transcriptome — e.g. combining ENCODE PacBio mouse cortex/hippocampus isoforms with Tasic Smart-Seq2 scRNA-seq counts to study isoform co-usage across cell types. If you only need gene-level scRNA-seq differential expression — this skill resolves isoform-level co-usage, which requires long-read-defined transcriptomes If no bulk long-read data are available and you need de novo functional annotation of isoforms: acorde/isoAnnotLite relies on pre-annotated compatible references (e.g. tappAS mouse RefSeq), and de novo isoform annotation tooling is still work-in-progress If the goal is transcriptome assembly/QC of the long reads themselves — use SQANTI3, which is not part of the acorde package's co-usage analysis block http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A hybrid strategy that integrates bulk long-read (ENCODE PacBio, mouse cortex/hippocampus) transcriptome definition with single-cell Illumina short-read (Smart-Seq2) counts to estimate isoform expression at the single-cell level, enabling downstream isoform co-expression and DIU/coDIU analysis with acorde. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: A hybrid strategy that integrates bulk long-read (ENCODE PacBio, mouse cortex/hippocampus) transcriptome definition with single-cell Illumina short-read (Smart-Seq2) counts to estimate isoform expression at the single-cell level, enabling downstream isoform co-expression and DIU/coDIU analysis with acorde.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you only need gene-level scRNA-seq differential expression — this skill resolves isoform-level co-usage, which requires long-read-defined transcriptomes If no bulk long-read data are available and you need de novo functional annotation of isoforms: acorde/isoAnnotLite relies on pre-annotated compatible references (e.g. tappAS mouse RefSeq), and de novo isoform annotation tooling is still work-in-progress If the goal is transcriptome assembly/QC of the long reads themselves — use SQANTI3, which is not part of the acorde package's co-usage analysis block

skills.search_text: busco-completeness-assessment Use when scoring de novo diploid assemblies built from PacBio CLR, Nanopore R9 or Nanopore R10 reads, where completeness (BUSCO) must be reported next to NG50, phase block NG50 and Hamming error to compare pipelines. The input reads are Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi, where PECAT achieves only mediocre performance and HiFi-specific assemblers like Hifiasm are more appropriate The genome region has very low heterozygosity, where PECAT SNP calling and haplotype-aware error correction are unreliable, making phased-assembly completeness comparisons moot The task is base-level accuracy rather than gene-space completeness — use the reference-based Pomoxis tool instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluate haplotype-specific contigs produced by diploid long-read assemblers (PECAT, Canu+purge_dups, FALCON-Unzip, Flye+HapDup, Shasta) for gene-space completeness with BUSCO, alongside Merqury phase block NG50, Hamming error and Pomoxis reference-based accuracy, to reproduce the paper's Tables 1-2 comparisons. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Evaluate haplotype-specific contigs produced by diploid long-read assemblers (PECAT, Canu+purge_dups, FALCON-Unzip, Flye+HapDup, Shasta) for gene-space completeness with BUSCO, alongside Merqury phase block NG50, Hamming error and Pomoxis reference-based accuracy, to reproduce the paper's Tables 1-2 comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi, where PECAT achieves only mediocre performance and HiFi-specific assemblers like Hifiasm are more appropriate The genome region has very low heterozygosity, where PECAT SNP calling and haplotype-aware error correction are unreliable, making phased-assembly completeness comparisons moot The task is base-level accuracy rather than gene-space completeness — use the reference-based Pomoxis tool instead

skills.description: Use when Illumina FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome to compute read-level deletion fractions at specific homopolymer loci, to test whether observed length variation is biological rather than a sequencing-error artifact.
skills.name: bwa-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: bwa-short-read-alignment Use when Illumina FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome to compute read-level deletion fractions at specific homopolymer loci, to test whether observed length variation is biological rather than a sequencing-error artifact. The analysis goal is single-molecule methylation status of SMRT reads — use SMALR (SMsn/SMp protocols on aligned_reads.cmph5 input) instead; short-read pileups lack the circular-consensus repeated observations SMALR depends on. Only population-level consensus sequence identity is needed (e.g., variant calling or genome assembly) rather than per-read deletion fractions at defined homopolymer loci. The input reads are long SMRT subreads in .cmph5 format; 'bwa mem' here targets short Illumina MiSeq reads against FASTA references. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A short-read alignment workflow that uses 'bwa mem' to align Illumina MiSeq FASTQ reads to indexed reference genomes (e.g., GenBank CP011330/CP011331), then samtools sort/index and pileups to quantify per-locus read-level deletion rates in homopolymer tracts — distinguishing true biological length variation from homopolymer sequencing error. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: A short-read alignment workflow that uses 'bwa mem' to align Illumina MiSeq FASTQ reads to indexed reference genomes (e.g., GenBank CP011330/CP011331), then samtools sort/index and pileups to quantify per-locus read-level deletion rates in homopolymer tracts — distinguishing true biological length variation from homopolymer sequencing error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is single-molecule methylation status of SMRT reads — use SMALR (SMsn/SMp protocols on aligned_reads.cmph5 input) instead; short-read pileups lack the circular-consensus repeated observations SMALR depends on. Only population-level consensus sequence identity is needed (e.g., variant calling or genome assembly) rather than per-read deletion fractions at defined homopolymer loci. The input reads are long SMRT subreads in .cmph5 format; 'bwa mem' here targets short Illumina MiSeq reads against FASTA references.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing raw nanopore FASTQ reads from enzymatic methyl-seq (EMseq/nanoEM) data so that C-to-T-converted reads can be aligned to a C-to-T converted reference genome.
skills.name: c-to-t-base-conversion-of-nanopore-fastq
skills.search_text: c-to-t-base-conversion-of-nanopore-fastq Use when preprocessing raw nanopore FASTQ reads from enzymatic methyl-seq (EMseq/nanoEM) data so that C-to-T-converted reads can be aligned to a C-to-T converted reference genome. Input is direct nanopore WGS data read without base conversion (e.g. for nanopolish signal-level methylation calling) — converting reads there would destroy the native signal context Data are already base-converted short-read bisulfite/enzymatic methyl-seq reads processed by tools like Trim Galore/Bismark You are converting the reference genome, not reads — that step uses convert_ref.py producing output.fa http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 In-silico bismark-like base conversion of nanoEM nanopore reads: all C/Gs in sequencing reads are converted to T/As (C-to-T) with a companion G-to-A converted FASTQ, mirroring the EMseq enzymatic conversion where unmethylated cytosines are read as thymine prior to alignment against a converted reference. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: In-silico bismark-like base conversion of nanoEM nanopore reads: all C/Gs in sequencing reads are converted to T/As (C-to-T) with a companion G-to-A converted FASTQ, mirroring the EMseq enzymatic conversion where unmethylated cytosines are read as thymine prior to alignment against a converted reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is direct nanopore WGS data read without base conversion (e.g. for nanopolish signal-level methylation calling) — converting reads there would destroy the native signal context Data are already base-converted short-read bisulfite/enzymatic methyl-seq reads processed by tools like Trim Galore/Bismark You are converting the reference genome, not reads — that step uses convert_ref.py producing output.fa

skills.description: Use when you have SV calls (VCF) from one or more long-read callers (e.g. NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles) on nanopore alignments and public truth SV call sets (1KG, PacBio) for the same sample/region, and you need caller-level sensitivity/precision numbers.
skills.name: caller-benchmark-precision-sensitivity-evaluation
skills.search_text: caller-benchmark-precision-sensitivity-evaluation Use when you have SV calls (VCF) from one or more long-read callers (e.g. NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles) on nanopore alignments and public truth SV call sets (1KG, PacBio) for the same sample/region, and you need caller-level sensitivity/precision numbers.
