skills.name: clinvar-pathogenic-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: clinvar-pathogenic-variant-filtering Use when a raw ClinVar VCF (e.g. clinvar_YYYYMMDD.vcf.gz) must be reduced to pathogenic SNVs before projecting variants onto Pfam domain consensus positions or comparing against gnomAD population variation. The variant set is already filtered/annotated with pathogenicity and domain positions (e.g. MetaDome prebuilt visualizations) — refiltering would change counts relative to the released dataset The goal is population (benign) variation analysis — gnomAD PASS-filtered variants, not ClinVar pathogenic variants, are the correct input The variants of interest are indels or non-SNV complex variants — the workflow retains only single-nucleotide SNVs http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Reduces a raw ClinVar VCF release to disease-causing (Pathogenic) SNVs—exactly the 34,076 mutations MetaDome ingested—so pathogenic missense variants can be mapped onto Pfam domain consensus positions for meta-domain analysis. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Reduces a raw ClinVar VCF release to disease-causing (Pathogenic) SNVs—exactly the 34,076 mutations MetaDome ingested—so pathogenic missense variants can be mapped onto Pfam domain consensus positions for meta-domain analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant set is already filtered/annotated with pathogenicity and domain positions (e.g. MetaDome prebuilt visualizations) — refiltering would change counts relative to the released dataset The goal is population (benign) variation analysis — gnomAD PASS-filtered variants, not ClinVar pathogenic variants, are the correct input The variants of interest are indels or non-SNV complex variants — the workflow retains only single-nucleotide SNVs

skills.description: Use when training or retraining a variant pathogenicity classifier that needs a labeled ClinVar-derived case/control feature table with population-frequency, conservation, and functional-predictor features.
skills.name: clinvar-training-set-curation
skills.search_text: clinvar-training-set-curation Use when training or retraining a variant pathogenicity classifier that needs a labeled ClinVar-derived case/control feature table with population-frequency, conservation, and functional-predictor features. The goal is to score variants for a new sample — a repository of pre-calculated eDiVA-Scores for all exonic variants already exists and can be used instead of retraining The analysis targets CNVs — CNV analysis is not yet available in eDiVA (integration pending) Prioritization of candidate variants by phenotype/inheritance is needed — that is eDiVA-Prioritize, not training-set curation http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Curates a balanced ClinVar/GnomAD training set and computes the 11 eDiVA-Annotate/eDiVA-DB features used to train the eDiVA-Score random forest variant pathogenicity classifier, so pathogenicity can be estimated independently of prior clinical information. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772
skills.summary: Curates a balanced ClinVar/GnomAD training set and computes the 11 eDiVA-Annotate/eDiVA-DB features used to train the eDiVA-Score random forest variant pathogenicity classifier, so pathogenicity can be estimated independently of prior clinical information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to score variants for a new sample — a repository of pre-calculated eDiVA-Scores for all exonic variants already exists and can be used instead of retraining The analysis targets CNVs — CNV analysis is not yet available in eDiVA (integration pending) Prioritization of candidate variants by phenotype/inheritance is needed — that is eDiVA-Prioritize, not training-set curation

The variant set lacks ClinVar pathogenic/benign (or equivalent trusted) labels — there is no ground truth to compute ROC/AUC Variants under evaluation overlap the eDiVA-Score training set (15,000 ClinVar pathogenic variants), which would inflate benchmark performance The goal is de novo prioritization of an uncharacterized disease trio rather than retrospective classifier benchmarking — use eDiVA-Prioritize inheritance filtering instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0634 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Uses ClinVar's curated 'pathogenic' and 'benign' labels as binary ground-truth (TP/TN) to benchmark variant pathogenicity classifiers such as eDiVA-Score against CADD, DANN, Eigen, Revel, M-CAP, and MetaLR via ROC/AUC analysis. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772

skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant set lacks ClinVar pathogenic/benign (or equivalent trusted) labels — there is no ground truth to compute ROC/AUC Variants under evaluation overlap the eDiVA-Score training set (15,000 ClinVar pathogenic variants), which would inflate benchmark performance The goal is de novo prioritization of an uncharacterized disease trio rather than retrospective classifier benchmarking — use eDiVA-Prioritize inheritance filtering instead

skills.name: clip-based-assembly-error-detection
skills.search_text: clip-based-assembly-error-detection Use when a draft genome assembly must be pinpointed for regional or structural errors from clipping signals of NGS short reads and SMS long reads mapped back to the assembly (CRAQ CRE/CSE workflow). Polyploid genomes: the article notes evaluation of assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked diploid cases When the goal is consensus polishing or variant calling from reads (e.g., medaka-style neural-network polishing) rather than locating misassemblies in the draft assembly When only coverage- or completeness-based assessment is needed (e.g., BUSCO, QUAST) and no read-mapping clipping signal is available http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Detects assembly errors in a draft genome by mining soft/hard-clipped (CIGAR S/H) alignments of NGS short reads and SMS long reads, converting per-position clipping ratios and coverage into CRE/CSE breakpoints and R-AQI/S-AQI quality scores at single-nucleotide resolution, as implemented in CRAQ. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Detects assembly errors in a draft genome by mining soft/hard-clipped (CIGAR S/H) alignments of NGS short reads and SMS long reads, converting per-position clipping ratios and coverage into CRE/CSE breakpoints and R-AQI/S-AQI quality scores at single-nucleotide resolution, as implemented in CRAQ.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Polyploid genomes: the article notes evaluation of assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked diploid cases When the goal is consensus polishing or variant calling from reads (e.g., medaka-style neural-network polishing) rather than locating misassemblies in the draft assembly When only coverage- or completeness-based assessment is needed (e.g., BUSCO, QUAST) and no read-mapping clipping signal is available

skills.description: Use when a draft genome assembly must be assessed and its errors pinpointed reference-free, using raw NGS short reads and SMS long reads (HiFi/PacBio/ONT) mapped back to the assembly to expose clipping signals.
skills.name: clipped-alignment-error-calling
skills.search_text: clipped-alignment-error-calling Use when a draft genome assembly must be assessed and its errors pinpointed reference-free, using raw NGS short reads and SMS long reads (HiFi/PacBio/ONT) mapped back to the assembly to expose clipping signals. Polyploid genome assemblies — the article warns 'evaluation of genome assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here'. Cases requiring a definitive call for ambiguous loci — regions with clipping ratio above h but below f are reported as 'ambiguous heterozygous or error region' without classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 CRAQ-based detection of regional (CRE) and structural (CSE) assembly errors at single-nucleotide resolution by mining clipped alignments (CIGAR S/H) plus coverage signals after mapping NGS short reads and SMS long reads back to a draft assembly, reference-free. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: CRAQ-based detection of regional (CRE) and structural (CSE) assembly errors at single-nucleotide resolution by mining clipped alignments (CIGAR S/H) plus coverage signals after mapping NGS short reads and SMS long reads back to a draft assembly, reference-free.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Polyploid genome assemblies — the article warns 'evaluation of genome assemblies for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here'. Cases requiring a definitive call for ambiguous loci — regions with clipping ratio above h but below f are reported as 'ambiguous heterozygous or error region' without classification.

skills.description: Use when BAM alignments of Illumina short reads and SMS long reads mapped to a draft assembly must be mined for clipped reads (CIGAR S/H) to build per-position clipping tables as the first step of CRAQ assembly-error detection.
skills.name: clipped-alignment-extraction
skills.search_text: clipped-alignment-extraction Use when BAM alignments of Illumina short reads and SMS long reads mapped to a draft assembly must be mined for clipped reads (CIGAR S/H) to build per-position clipping tables as the first step of CRAQ assembly-error detection. Evaluating assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels — the paper states such evaluation 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' Input BAMs still contain unmapped, secondary, QC-failed, PCR-duplicated, or MAPQ<20 records — extraction counts would be inflated and downstream clipping ratios invalid The task is reference-based comparison against a finished genome (e.g. BUSCO/QUAST-style assessment); CRAQ clipping extraction is explicitly reference-free and only needs reads mapped to the draft assembly itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extracts soft/hard-clipped alignment records (CIGAR 'S' or 'H') from filtered NGS and SMS BAMs mapped to a draft assembly and tallies per-position clipped-read counts and coverage — the raw clipping-ratio signal CRAQ converts into CRE/CSE error breakpoints and CRH/CSH heterozygous loci. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Extracts soft/hard-clipped alignment records (CIGAR 'S' or 'H') from filtered NGS and SMS BAMs mapped to a draft assembly and tallies per-position clipped-read counts and coverage — the raw clipping-ratio signal CRAQ converts into CRE/CSE error breakpoints and CRH/CSH heterozygous loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels — the paper states such evaluation 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' Input BAMs still contain unmapped, secondary, QC-failed, PCR-duplicated, or MAPQ<20 records — extraction counts would be inflated and downstream clipping ratios invalid The task is reference-based comparison against a finished genome (e.g. BUSCO/QUAST-style assessment); CRAQ clipping extraction is explicitly reference-free and only needs reads mapped to the draft assembly itself

skills.description: Use when a draft (non-reference) genome assembly must be assessed or corrected for regional and structural errors using raw reads rather than a reference genome, especially when heterozygosity may confound error detection.
skills.name: clipped-read-alignment-analysis
skills.search_text: clipped-read-alignment-analysis Use when a draft (non-reference) genome assembly must be assessed or corrected for regional and structural errors using raw reads rather than a reference genome, especially when heterozygosity may confound error detection. The input is a finished reference-quality genome where AQI > 90 is already expected and error discovery would return mostly noise The goal is k-mer-based or completeness-only assessment (e.g., Merqury, KAT, BUSCO) rather than pinpointing error coordinates — CRAQ requires raw read mapping, which is its most resource-intensive step Genomes with higher ploidy levels (e.g., polyploids), where accuracy may not match the diploid/haploid benchmarked cases http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detects assembly errors and heterozygous loci in draft genome assemblies at single-nucleotide resolution by extracting soft/hard-clipped alignments (CIGAR 'S'/'H') from NGS short-read and SMS long-read mappings back to the assembly, then classifying loci as CREs, CSEs, CRHs, or CSHs via clipping-ratio and coverage cutoffs (CRAQ logic). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Detects assembly errors and heterozygous loci in draft genome assemblies at single-nucleotide resolution by extracting soft/hard-clipped alignments (CIGAR 'S'/'H') from NGS short-read and SMS long-read mappings back to the assembly, then classifying loci as CREs, CSEs, CRHs, or CSHs via clipping-ratio and coverage cutoffs (CRAQ logic).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a finished reference-quality genome where AQI > 90 is already expected and error discovery would return mostly noise The goal is k-mer-based or completeness-only assessment (e.g., Merqury, KAT, BUSCO) rather than pinpointing error coordinates — CRAQ requires raw read mapping, which is its most resource-intensive step Genomes with higher ploidy levels (e.g., polyploids), where accuracy may not match the diploid/haploid benchmarked cases

skills.description: Use when a draft de novo assembly (e.g. Falcon contigs) may contain misjoined/chimeric contigs and the original Illumina short-read and PacBio long-read data are available to remap for clipped-alignment error detection before Hi-C or optical-map scaffolding.
skills.name: clipped-read-assembly-error-detection
skills.search_text: clipped-read-assembly-error-detection Use when a draft de novo assembly (e.g. Falcon contigs) may contain misjoined/chimeric contigs and the original Illumina short-read and PacBio long-read data are available to remap for clipped-alignment error detection before Hi-C or optical-map scaffolding. The genome is polyploid or of higher ploidy — the article states evaluation of higher-ploidy assemblies 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' No original NGS/SMS sequencing reads are available for the assembly — CRAQ is reference-free but requires remapping raw reads to the draft contigs The input is already a finished/reference-quality assembly (AQI > 90) with no suspected structural misjoins, or the target is only small-scale local error repair (CREs) rather than split-then-rescaffold structural correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect large-scale misjoins (CSEs) in a draft genome assembly at single-nucleotide resolution by mining clipped (CIGAR S/H) read alignments from NGS and SMS read remapping with CRAQ, then split chimeric contigs at CSE breakpoints so optical-map or Hi-C scaffolding can fix the errors. Demonstrated on A. oxysepala Falcon contigs, where CRAQ-corrected scaffolds gained S-AQI 58.1 vs 39.0 and N50 28 Mb vs 20 Mb. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Detect large-scale misjoins (CSEs) in a draft genome assembly at single-nucleotide resolution by mining clipped (CIGAR S/H) read alignments from NGS and SMS read remapping with CRAQ, then split chimeric contigs at CSE breakpoints so optical-map or Hi-C scaffolding can fix the errors. Demonstrated on A. oxysepala Falcon contigs, where CRAQ-corrected scaffolds gained S-AQI 58.1 vs 39.0 and N50 28 Mb vs 20 Mb.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome is polyploid or of higher ploidy — the article states evaluation of higher-ploidy assemblies 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' No original NGS/SMS sequencing reads are available for the assembly — CRAQ is reference-free but requires remapping raw reads to the draft contigs The input is already a finished/reference-quality assembly (AQI > 90) with no suspected structural misjoins, or the target is only small-scale local error repair (CREs) rather than split-then-rescaffold structural correction

skills.description: Use when NGS and SMS reads mapped to a draft assembly (filtered BAMs) yield clipped-position tables (SR_clip.coverRate / LR_clip.coverRate) whose candidates must be sorted into CRE, CSE, CRH, or CSH classes by clipping ratio and coverage.
skills.name: clipping-ratio-threshold-classification
skills.search_text: clipping-ratio-threshold-classification Use when NGS and SMS reads mapped to a draft assembly (filtered BAMs) yield clipped-position tables (SR_clip.coverRate / LR_clip.coverRate) whose candidates must be sorted into CRE, CSE, CRH, or CSH classes by clipping ratio and coverage. Genome assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels (e.g. polyploids), for which the article states evaluation 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' Candidates whose clipping ratio lies between the upper heterozygous bound (0.6) and the breakpoint cutoff (0.75) — CRAQ reports these as ambiguous rather than definitive CRE/CSE or CRH/CSH calls CSE identification in repetitive regions where multi-mapped reads dominate, unless multi-mapped reads are filtered as CRAQ does by default http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 CRAQ's two-stage classification that labels clipped-position candidates as heterozygous loci (CRH/CSH) or mapping breakpoints using clipping-ratio cutoffs (h = 0.4–0.6, f = 0.75), then assigns errors to CREs or CSEs from NGS/SMS read-mapping status. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: CRAQ's two-stage classification that labels clipped-position candidates as heterozygous loci (CRH/CSH) or mapping breakpoints using clipping-ratio cutoffs (h = 0.4–0.6, f = 0.75), then assigns errors to CREs or CSEs from NGS/SMS read-mapping status.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genome assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels (e.g. polyploids), for which the article states evaluation 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' Candidates whose clipping ratio lies between the upper heterozygous bound (0.6) and the breakpoint cutoff (0.75) — CRAQ reports these as ambiguous rather than definitive CRE/CSE or CRH/CSH calls CSE identification in repetitive regions where multi-mapped reads dominate, unless multi-mapped reads are filtered as CRAQ does by default

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a co-expression/correlation metric accurately recovers ground-truth feature cluster structure embedded in simulated single-cell data, rather than relying on visual or qualitative assessment.

Input data has no known ground-truth cluster structure — Jaccard agreement against simulated modules cannot be computed on real data The goal is isoform functional annotation or DIU/coDIU detection rather than benchmarking co-expression metric accuracy Evaluation target is differential expression performance rather than co-expression cluster recovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 A benchmarking procedure that quantifies how well co-expression correlation metrics (percentile, Pearson, Spearman, zero-inflated Kendall, rho proportionality) recover known simulated cluster structure, using Jaccard indices between simulated and calculated clusters plus the proportion of within-cluster metric values exceeding 0.8. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w

skills.search_text: clustering-silhouette-evaluation Use when benchmarking feature-level normalization of MTI data (e.g., PRAD-CyCIF .pkl/.h5ad) and you need average silhouette scores, alongside kBET, to judge clustering consistency of raw vs. normalized datasets. skills.description: Use when you need to quantify and compare SV calling accuracy of multiple long-read callers against the GIAB HG002 CMRG SV truth set on HiFi data.
skills.name: cmrg-benchmark-accuracy-comparison-across-callers
skills.search_text: cmrg-benchmark-accuracy-comparison-across-callers Use when you need to quantify and compare SV calling accuracy of multiple long-read callers against the GIAB HG002 CMRG SV truth set on HiFi data. Benchmarking against the GIAB draft T2T SV benchmark (GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1_stvar), which requires truvari bench plus refine with consolidation rather than bench alone Evaluating somatic or CNV-only calling rather than germline SV calls on HiFi data The caller VCFs are not all generated from the same mapped BAM/alignment, making the comparison invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3573 Benchmarks single-sample SV caller accuracy (sawfish vs Sniffles2 vs pbsv) against the GIAB challenging medically relevant genes (CMRG) benchmark of 217 SVs using truvari 4.2.2, yielding precision/recall/F1 per caller (sawfish F1 0.993, Sniffles2 0.964, pbsv 0.971). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-sample SV caller accuracy (sawfish vs Sniffles2 vs pbsv) against the GIAB challenging medically relevant genes (CMRG) benchmark of 217 SVs using truvari 4.2.2, yielding precision/recall/F1 per caller (sawfish F1 0.993, Sniffles2 0.964, pbsv 0.971).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking against the GIAB draft T2T SV benchmark (GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1_stvar), which requires truvari bench plus refine with consolidation rather than bench alone Evaluating somatic or CNV-only calling rather than germline SV calls on HiFi data The caller VCFs are not all generated from the same mapped BAM/alignment, making the comparison invalid

skills.description: Use when comparing phasing methods on HG002 with a GIAB trio-phased truth VCF and you need per-gene CMRG phased-gene counts, genome-wide phase block counts, and flip/switch error rates from block connections.
skills.name: cmrg-gene-phasing-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: cmrg-gene-phasing-coverage-quantification Use when comparing phasing methods on HG002 with a GIAB trio-phased truth VCF and you need per-gene CMRG phased-gene counts, genome-wide phase block counts, and flip/switch error rates from block connections. Benchmarking involves sex chromosomes: MethPhaser phasing is invalid there because of random X inactivation in females, so X/Y must be excluded before counting Input data is below ~30X ONT coverage, where SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) that MethPhaser builds on do not work reasonably The BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors in MethPhaser http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Benchmark how many GIAB CMRG challenging medically relevant genes are fully phased by methylation-extended phasing (MethPhaser) versus SNV-only phasing (HapCUT2) on HG002, and quantify the resulting reduction in phase block number (160 to 140). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Benchmark how many GIAB CMRG challenging medically relevant genes are fully phased by methylation-extended phasing (MethPhaser) versus SNV-only phasing (HapCUT2) on HG002, and quantify the resulting reduction in phase block number (160 to 140).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking involves sex chromosomes: MethPhaser phasing is invalid there because of random X inactivation in females, so X/Y must be excluded before counting Input data is below ~30X ONT coverage, where SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) that MethPhaser builds on do not work reasonably The BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors in MethPhaser

skills.name: cnn-inference-on-variant-encodings
skills.search_text: cnn-inference-on-variant-encodings Use when you have per-sample collapsed candidate VCFs from the ConsensuSV-ONT nextflow pipeline (vcfs output folder) and need to filter them down to high-quality SV calls via CNN scoring before benchmarking with Truvari. Input is short-read (Illumina) SV data — the pipeline and its callers target Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing You already have the final filtered ConsensuSV-ONT VCF and only need benchmarking (go straight to Truvari bench) No trained CNN model is available or the candidates are raw single-caller VCFs that have not been collapsed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Scores collapsed structural variant candidates from ConsensuSV-ONT by encoding each variant as an image-like tensor and running it through the trained 3D convolutional neural network, keeping variants whose sigmoid output exceeds 0.5 as high-quality consensus calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Scores collapsed structural variant candidates from ConsensuSV-ONT by encoding each variant as an image-like tensor and running it through the trained 3D convolutional neural network, keeping variants whose sigmoid output exceeds 0.5 as high-quality consensus calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina) SV data — the pipeline and its callers target Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing You already have the final filtered ConsensuSV-ONT VCF and only need benchmarking (go straight to Truvari bench) No trained CNN model is available or the candidates are raw single-caller VCFs that have not been collapsed

skills.description: Use when comparing read-level 5mCpG detection performance of trained deep-learning models on long PacBio HiFi/CCS reads (≥10 Kb) against bisulfite ground truth and a baseline CNN caller such as primrose.
skills.name: cnn-model-evaluation-on-long-reads
skills.search_text: cnn-model-evaluation-on-long-reads Use when comparing read-level 5mCpG detection performance of trained deep-learning models on long PacBio HiFi/CCS reads (≥10 Kb) against bisulfite ground truth and a baseline CNN caller such as primrose. The goal is site-level (genome-wide aggregated) methylation rather than single-molecule read-level accuracy — ccsmeth has a separate site-level model for that Detecting hemimethylated CpGs or non-CpG 5mC / other modifications such as 6mA — the methods only consider symmetric CpG methylation Evaluating on short (<10 Kb) CCS reads, where the reported ≥0.90 accuracy and ~0.97 AUC performance does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarking a CNN-based deep-learning methylation caller (ccsmeth) against a competing CNN caller (primrose) at single-molecule read level on long (≥10 Kb) PacBio CCS reads, computing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC against bisulfite-sequencing ground truth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Benchmarking a CNN-based deep-learning methylation caller (ccsmeth) against a competing CNN caller (primrose) at single-molecule read level on long (≥10 Kb) PacBio CCS reads, computing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC against bisulfite-sequencing ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is site-level (genome-wide aggregated) methylation rather than single-molecule read-level accuracy — ccsmeth has a separate site-level model for that Detecting hemimethylated CpGs or non-CpG 5mC / other modifications such as 6mA — the methods only consider symmetric CpG methylation Evaluating on short (<10 Kb) CCS reads, where the reported ≥0.90 accuracy and ~0.97 AUC performance does not apply

skills.description: Use when testing a pretrained CNNSplice model (Model 1 .h5 weights from one organism) on a different organism's constructed splice-site dataset to measure cross-organism generalization accuracy.
skills.name: cnn-model-inference-evaluation
skills.search_text: cnn-model-inference-evaluation Use when testing a pretrained CNNSplice model (Model 1 .h5 weights from one organism) on a different organism's constructed splice-site dataset to measure cross-organism generalization accuracy. The goal is to train new CNNSplice models from scratch rather than evaluate pretrained .h5 weights (use the training workflow: python train.py instead). The input genomic data cannot be represented in the CNNSplice constructed-dataset format with a fixed sequence length of 400. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Run inference and compute evaluation metrics with pretrained CNNSplice .h5 CNN models (e.g. the Model 1 balanced acceptor model) on new or cross-organism splice-site datasets, as in CNNSplice's generality test. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.031
skills.summary: Run inference and compute evaluation metrics with pretrained CNNSplice .h5 CNN models (e.g. the Model 1 balanced acceptor model) on new or cross-organism splice-site datasets, as in CNNSplice's generality test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to train new CNNSplice models from scratch rather than evaluate pretrained .h5 weights (use the training workflow: python train.py instead). The input genomic data cannot be represented in the CNNSplice constructed-dataset format with a fixed sequence length of 400.

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate that both the convolutional and recurrent layer sets of Chiron's CNN+RNN+CTC architecture are essential, by training full vs. ablated models on the same raw-signal tfrecord data and comparing read-level accuracy against a reference genome.
skills.name: cnn-rnn-architecture-ablation
skills.search_text: cnn-rnn-architecture-ablation Use when you need to demonstrate that both the convolutional and recurrent layer sets of Chiron's CNN+RNN+CTC architecture are essential, by training full vs. ablated models on the same raw-signal tfrecord data and comparing read-level accuracy against a reference genome. When the goal is only to basecall reads with a pretrained model (use the default DNA/RNA models via 'chiron call') rather than to test architecture components — no retraining is needed. When training labels have not been prepared (raw fast5 without re-squiggle/labeling via Metrichor + Nanoraw error correction) — the tfrecord extraction step requires signal-label pairs. When you only want to tune decoding (beam width vs. greedy decoding) — that is an inference-time choice and does not require retraining ablated architectures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Ablation protocol for Chiron's CNN+RNN+CTC basecalling architecture: retrain the full model and two ablated variants (CNN-only and RNN-only removal) on the same ~4,000-read re-squiggled fast5 training set, then compare read-level accuracy to show each component performs a distinct, necessary step of the signal-to-sequence pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: Ablation protocol for Chiron's CNN+RNN+CTC basecalling architecture: retrain the full model and two ablated variants (CNN-only and RNN-only removal) on the same ~4,000-read re-squiggled fast5 training set, then compare read-level accuracy to show each component performs a distinct, necessary step of the signal-to-sequence pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only to basecall reads with a pretrained model (use the default DNA/RNA models via 'chiron call') rather than to test architecture components — no retraining is needed. When training labels have not been prepared (raw fast5 without re-squiggle/labeling via Metrichor + Nanoraw error correction) — the tfrecord extraction step requires signal-label pairs. When you only want to tune decoding (beam width vs. greedy decoding) — that is an inference-time choice and does not require retraining ablated architectures.

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore fast5 electrical signals must be translated directly into nucleotide sequence without event segmentation, or when an open-source, trainable alternative to ONT's proprietary Albacore/Metrichor basecallers is needed.
skills.name: cnn-rnn-ctc-neural-basecalling
skills.search_text: cnn-rnn-ctc-neural-basecalling Use when raw nanopore fast5 electrical signals must be translated directly into nucleotide sequence without event segmentation, or when an open-source, trainable alternative to ONT's proprietary Albacore/Metrichor basecallers is needed. Input is already segmented/event-tabulated signal (e.g.ONT event data) — prior two-stage basecallers handle that and Chiron's raw-signal slicing is unnecessary Direct-RNA fast5 files with adapter and polyA stall still present — call BoostNano first, since Chiron's RNA model expects preprocessed signal Only FASTQ/FASTA reads are available with no raw signal — there is nothing to basecall; use read-level analysis skills instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 End-to-end basecalling of Oxford Nanopore raw electrical signal using a coupled CNN+RNN+CTC neural network (Chiron), which bypasses the error-prone signal segmentation step by slicing raw fast5 signals, basecalling each window, and assembling overlapping slice basecalls into a consensus read sequence. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: End-to-end basecalling of Oxford Nanopore raw electrical signal using a coupled CNN+RNN+CTC neural network (Chiron), which bypasses the error-prone signal segmentation step by slicing raw fast5 signals, basecalling each window, and assembling overlapping slice basecalls into a consensus read sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already segmented/event-tabulated signal (e.g.ONT event data) — prior two-stage basecallers handle that and Chiron's raw-signal slicing is unnecessary Direct-RNA fast5 files with adapter and polyA stall still present — call BoostNano first, since Chiron's RNA model expects preprocessed signal Only FASTQ/FASTA reads are available with no raw signal — there is nothing to basecall; use read-level analysis skills instead

skills.description: Use when calling deletion SVs from long-read (third-generation) BAM/SAM alignments where alignments can be converted to CIGAR-derived images and encoded sequences, and a deep model must fuse both modalities to output per-region deletion predictions.
skills.name: cnn-structural-variant-classification
skills.search_text: cnn-structural-variant-classification Use when calling deletion SVs from long-read (third-generation) BAM/SAM alignments where alignments can be converted to CIGAR-derived images and encoded sequences, and a deep model must fuse both modalities to output per-region deletion predictions. The goal is insertion or base substitution calling — the article states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling' Input is short-read NGS (Illumina) data rather than third-generation long-read alignments, where the method's motivation and evaluation do not apply Only sequence data is available without aligned BAM/SAM files, since image generation and deletion framing depend on CIGAR fields of quality-controlled alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Classify deletion structural variants from third-generation sequencing alignments by fusing generated deletion-region images (100x100 px, CIGAR-coded RGB) with hard-coded base sequences via a dual-attention mechanism (spatial softmax attention + GAP/GMP channel attention) on a multi-scale ResNet backbone (DASV). genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: Classify deletion structural variants from third-generation sequencing alignments by fusing generated deletion-region images (100x100 px, CIGAR-coded RGB) with hard-coded base sequences via a dual-attention mechanism (spatial softmax attention + GAP/GMP channel attention) on a multi-scale ResNet backbone (DASV).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is insertion or base substitution calling — the article states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling' Input is short-read NGS (Illumina) data rather than third-generation long-read alignments, where the method's motivation and evaluation do not apply Only sequence data is available without aligned BAM/SAM files, since image generation and deletion framing depend on CIGAR fields of quality-controlled alignments

skills.description: Use when a pipeline needs to refine predicted splice-site positions from long-read (Iso-seq) alignments, or when reproducing TAGET's CNN splice-site correction trained on Ensembl-annotated exon/intron boundaries.
skills.name: cnn-training-with-adam-optimizer
skills.search_text: cnn-training-with-adam-optimizer Use when a pipeline needs to refine predicted splice-site positions from long-read (Iso-seq) alignments, or when reproducing TAGET's CNN splice-site correction trained on Ensembl-annotated exon/intron boundaries. Input reads are not Iso-seq/full-length transcript data — TAGET's alignment and CNN correction are designed for PacBio Iso-seq transcripts, not short-read RNA-seq alone Splice sites already match Ensembl annotation (FSM/ISM transcripts) — the CNN correction targets mispredicted novel junctions, not canonically supported ones Reference genome or annotation files (hg38.fa / hg38.ensembl.gtf pickle) are unavailable — the training windows cannot be extracted http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a three-block convolutional neural network on one-hot encoded 21-bp splice-site windows from hg38 to locally correct misaligned splice junctions during TAGET's transcript alignment of PacBio Iso-seq reads, reaching ~98% validation accuracy (Supplementary Fig. 12). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Trains a three-block convolutional neural network on one-hot encoded 21-bp splice-site windows from hg38 to locally correct misaligned splice junctions during TAGET's transcript alignment of PacBio Iso-seq reads, reaching ~98% validation accuracy (Supplementary Fig. 12).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not Iso-seq/full-length transcript data — TAGET's alignment and CNN correction are designed for PacBio Iso-seq transcripts, not short-read RNA-seq alone Splice sites already match Ensembl annotation (FSM/ISM transcripts) — the CNN correction targets mispredicted novel junctions, not canonically supported ones Reference genome or annotation files (hg38.fa / hg38.ensembl.gtf pickle) are unavailable — the training windows cannot be extracted

skills.description: Use when Oxford Nanopore long-read SV candidate calls from the six ConsensuSV-ONT callers need a quality score, i.e. candidate variants must be filtered via image-encoded evidence into a CNN probability.
skills.name: cnn-variant-quality-scoring
skills.search_text: cnn-variant-quality-scoring Use when Oxford Nanopore long-read SV candidate calls from the six ConsensuSV-ONT callers need a quality score, i.e. candidate variants must be filtered via image-encoded evidence into a CNN probability. The input data are short reads (e.g. Illumina-only alignments) — the paper positions this skill for ONT long-read SV detection; note the source card shows Illumina encodings of a large deletion lose coverage signal rather than split-read evidence. You only have raw fastq.gz and expect final variant calls without running the six SV callers first — the CNN scores candidate variants produced by the consensus stage, not raw reads. You need caller names, version numbers, or threshold parameters not documented here — the article notes such implementation details are missing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A Conv3D-based CNN module of ConsensuSV-ONT that encodes candidate structural variants from Oxford Nanopore long-read alignments into 50x50x3 images and scores each with a variant-quality probability for filtering high-quality calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: A Conv3D-based CNN module of ConsensuSV-ONT that encodes candidate structural variants from Oxford Nanopore long-read alignments into 50x50x3 images and scores each with a variant-quality probability for filtering high-quality calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are short reads (e.g. Illumina-only alignments) — the paper positions this skill for ONT long-read SV detection; note the source card shows Illumina encodings of a large deletion lose coverage signal rather than split-read evidence. You only have raw fastq.gz and expect final variant calls without running the six SV callers first — the CNN scores candidate variants produced by the consensus stage, not raw reads. You need caller names, version numbers, or threshold parameters not documented here — the article notes such implementation details are missing.

skills.description: Use when CNV calls already stored in .pytor files must be narrowed by quality (q0), size (e.g. ≥100 kb), and p-value (e.g. ≤1e-5) thresholds before printing, annotating, or multi-sample merging.
skills.name: cnv-call-filtering-by-q0-size-pvalue
skills.search_text: cnv-call-filtering-by-q0-size-pvalue Use when CNV calls already stored in .pytor files must be narrowed by quality (q0), size (e.g. ≥100 kb), and p-value (e.g. ≤1e-5) thresholds before printing, annotating, or multi-sample merging. Input is a raw BAM/CRAM without a .pytor file — the -rd, -his, -partition, and -call steps must run first before any call filtering can be applied The variants to filter are SNPs and small indels in a VCF (handled by the -snp/-baf workflow), not CNV calls in .pytor storage The goal is somatic CNA discovery in cancer or mosaic samples, which relies on the prototype somatic joint caller rather than viewer-mode call filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Filters CNV calls stored in CNVpytor .pytor files using viewer-mode thresholds on Q0 (RD quality), CNV size, and p-value before printing, annotating, or merging calls across samples. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Filters CNV calls stored in CNVpytor .pytor files using viewer-mode thresholds on Q0 (RD quality), CNV size, and p-value before printing, annotating, or merging calls across samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw BAM/CRAM without a .pytor file — the -rd, -his, -partition, and -call steps must run first before any call filtering can be applied The variants to filter are SNPs and small indels in a VCF (handled by the -snp/-baf workflow), not CNV calls in .pytor storage The goal is somatic CNA discovery in cancer or mosaic samples, which relies on the prototype somatic joint caller rather than viewer-mode call filtering

skills.description: Use when you have a VCF/BED of >50-kb DEL/DUP calls from a nanopore pipeline plus a BAM alignment, and need to remove calls lacking coverage evidence or verify coverage support for truth-set SVs.
skills.name: cnv-call-filtering-by-read-depth
skills.search_text: cnv-call-filtering-by-read-depth Use when you have a VCF/BED of >50-kb DEL/DUP calls from a nanopore pipeline plus a BAM alignment, and need to remove calls lacking coverage evidence or verify coverage support for truth-set SVs. SV types other than deletions and duplications — coverage-based filtering cannot be applied to insertions, inversions, or translocations You need a de novo variant caller — disCoverage is not a variant caller and requires putative SV positions from another technique or multi-sample analysis Coverage is highly non-uniform with strong local peaks/valleys or unresolved genome regions, which can produce spurious coverage differences http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Refine nanopore structural variant calls by statistically testing read-depth coverage over each candidate deletion/duplication with disCoverage, discarding calls whose coverage does not support the claimed copy-number change. This addresses the poor specificity of variant callers for large (>50 kb) CNVs in nanopore WGS data. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Refine nanopore structural variant calls by statistically testing read-depth coverage over each candidate deletion/duplication with disCoverage, discarding calls whose coverage does not support the claimed copy-number change. This addresses the poor specificity of variant callers for large (>50 kb) CNVs in nanopore WGS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: SV types other than deletions and duplications — coverage-based filtering cannot be applied to insertions, inversions, or translocations You need a de novo variant caller — disCoverage is not a variant caller and requires putative SV positions from another technique or multi-sample analysis Coverage is highly non-uniform with strong local peaks/valleys or unresolved genome regions, which can produce spurious coverage differences

skills.description: Use when a query asks for the CNV deletion frequency of a specific gene in an intestinal disease and the correlation between CNV state and RNA expression, to interpret whether high RNA expression is driven by copy gain or persists despite deletions.
skills.name: cnv-deletion-frequency-estimation
skills.search_text: cnv-deletion-frequency-estimation Use when a query asks for the CNV deletion frequency of a specific gene in an intestinal disease and the correlation between CNV state and RNA expression, to interpret whether high RNA expression is driven by copy gain or persists despite deletions. The question concerns single-nucleotide polymorphisms (72,248 SNPs) or structural variations rather than gene-level CNV deletion calls The expression data are non-RNA-seq modalities (e.g. circular RNAs, lncRNAs, microRNAs, or m6A modification sites) that are not matched to CNV sample calls Only a single sample is available — deletion frequency and CNV-expression correlation require a cohort of samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3912 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates the deletion frequency of a gene's copy number variation (CNV) across disease samples and quantifies the strength of the CNV-vs-RNA-expression correlation, using CNV genomics and RNA-seq transcriptomics profiles from GutUDB (e.g. METTL3 deletion frequency 0.04 in CRC). genomics/v1 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Estimates the deletion frequency of a gene's copy number variation (CNV) across disease samples and quantifies the strength of the CNV-vs-RNA-expression correlation, using CNV genomics and RNA-seq transcriptomics profiles from GutUDB (e.g. METTL3 deletion frequency 0.04 in CRC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns single-nucleotide polymorphisms (72,248 SNPs) or structural variations rather than gene-level CNV deletion calls The expression data are non-RNA-seq modalities (e.g. circular RNAs, lncRNAs, microRNAs, or m6A modification sites) that are not matched to CNV sample calls Only a single sample is available — deletion frequency and CNV-expression correlation require a cohort of samples

skills.description: Use when a gene-focused question requires pairing CNV deletion calls with RNA-seq expression profiles in GutUDB to test whether copy-number loss explains (or fails to explain) transcript levels.
skills.name: cnv-expression-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cnv-expression-correlation-analysis Use when a gene-focused question requires pairing CNV deletion calls with RNA-seq expression profiles in GutUDB to test whether copy-number loss explains (or fails to explain) transcript levels. The question concerns SNPs, structural variations, or mutated genes rather than CNV deletion calls (GutUDB curates these as separate genomics categories) Only one data modality is available — this skill requires both CNV genomics and RNA-seq transcriptomics profiles for the same gene and cohort The goal is drug-disease or microbe-metabolite association queries, which GutUDB handles through its THERAPY and metabolite modules instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3912 Quantifies how copy number variation (CNV) deletion frequency of a gene relates to its RNA expression in intestinal-disease cohorts using GutUDB's genomics and transcriptomics profiles, e.g. METTL3's 0.04 deletion frequency and weak CNV–RNA correlation in colorectal cancer. genomics/v1 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Quantifies how copy number variation (CNV) deletion frequency of a gene relates to its RNA expression in intestinal-disease cohorts using GutUDB's genomics and transcriptomics profiles, e.g. METTL3's 0.04 deletion frequency and weak CNV–RNA correlation in colorectal cancer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns SNPs, structural variations, or mutated genes rather than CNV deletion calls (GutUDB curates these as separate genomics categories) Only one data modality is available — this skill requires both CNV genomics and RNA-seq transcriptomics profiles for the same gene and cohort The goal is drug-disease or microbe-metabolite association queries, which GutUDB handles through its THERAPY and metabolite modules instead

skills.description: Use when two gene sets (coDIU and DIU) derived from isoform usage analysis must be functionally contrasted to ask which positional features or GO terms are annotated in a significantly higher proportion in one set.

skills.search_text: codiu-vs-diu-gene-set-comparison Use when two gene sets (coDIU and DIU) derived from isoform usage analysis must be functionally contrasted to ask which positional features or GO terms are annotated in a significantly higher proportion in one set. The input transcriptome is de novo and lacks a compatible pre-annotated tappAS reference, since IsoAnnotLite can only transfer functional labels from a compatible annotated reference until a de novo annotation tool is available The gene sets to compare are independent, in which case the partially-overlapping-samples z-test used for the non-independent coDIU/DIU sets is not the correct enrichment statistic The goal is isoform co-expression network construction rather than functional enrichment of already-defined DIU/coDIU gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 This skill runs a tappAS functional enrichment analysis contrasting coDIU genes against DIU genes with the partially-overlapping-samples z-test, testing whether positional functional features and Gene Ontology terms are over-represented in coDIU genes. It recovers the paper's key result that 91 positional functional features and 59 GO terms are significantly enriched in coDIU vs DIU genes (FDR < 0.05, Benjamini-Hochberg corrected). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: This skill runs a tappAS functional enrichment analysis contrasting coDIU genes against DIU genes with the partially-overlapping-samples z-test, testing whether positional functional features and Gene Ontology terms are over-represented in coDIU genes. skills.name: cohort-scale-variant-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: cohort-scale-variant-count-aggregation Reference for reproducing or benchmarking a cohort-wide DNV total from HAT/HAT-FLEX trio output, e.g., aggregating per-trio calls from thousands of SSC or similar WGS/WES trios and checking DNV quality metrics.
