Your goal is demultiplexing or primer/barcode trimming itself rather than coverage–accuracy characterization — use MiniBar directly for that step The reads are short Illumina reads rather than long Nanopore amplicon reads; the majority-vote consensus rationale targets Nanopore's per-read error profile You have no independent high-accuracy reference consensus (e.g. Illumina-derived) to measure consensus error against http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies how Nanopore consensus sequence accuracy improves with sequencing depth by subsampling a demultiplexed, barcode- and primer-trimmed fastq across coverage levels (10–800 reads), building majority-vote consensus sequences, and scoring them against an Illumina-derived reference consensus with Edlib edit distance. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Quantifies how Nanopore consensus sequence accuracy improves with sequencing depth by subsampling a demultiplexed, barcode- and primer-trimmed fastq across coverage levels (10–800 reads), building majority-vote consensus sequences, and scoring them against an Illumina-derived reference consensus with Edlib edit distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is demultiplexing or primer/barcode trimming itself rather than coverage–accuracy characterization — use MiniBar directly for that step The reads are short Illumina reads rather than long Nanopore amplicon reads; the majority-vote consensus rationale targets Nanopore's per-read error profile You have no independent high-accuracy reference consensus (e.g. Illumina-derived) to measure consensus error against

skills.description: Use when a de novo assembly has been generated from Oxford Nanopore long reads (e.g., miniasm unitigs) and an error-corrected FASTA consensus is needed within a Galaxy-based workflow.
skills.name: consensus-error-polishing
skills.search_text: consensus-error-polishing Use when a de novo assembly has been generated from Oxford Nanopore long reads (e.g., miniasm unitigs) and an error-corrected FASTA consensus is needed within a Galaxy-based workflow. The assembly was produced from short reads (150–300 bp) or by a polished/assembler that already emits a corrected consensus — the miniasm-to-Racon chain is specific to noisy long-read drafts. The analysis target is not genome assembly (e.g., NanoGalaxy's metagenomic analysis or AMR use case workflows). Pacific Biosciences data — the article states PB tool support inside Galaxy is untested ('should also work'), since only ONT data were intensively tested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Polishes a raw long-read (nanopore) assembly by mapping the original nanopore reads back onto miniasm unitigs with minimap2 and running Racon to derive an error-corrected consensus, as implemented in the NanoGalaxy Galaxy toolkit. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: Polishes a raw long-read (nanopore) assembly by mapping the original nanopore reads back onto miniasm unitigs with minimap2 and running Racon to derive an error-corrected consensus, as implemented in the NanoGalaxy Galaxy toolkit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly was produced from short reads (150–300 bp) or by a polished/assembler that already emits a corrected consensus — the miniasm-to-Racon chain is specific to noisy long-read drafts. The analysis target is not genome assembly (e.g., NanoGalaxy's metagenomic analysis or AMR use case workflows). Pacific Biosciences data — the article states PB tool support inside Galaxy is untested ('should also work'), since only ONT data were intensively tested.

skills.description: Use when basecalled FASTQ read sets from nanopore simulators must be compared against real experimental reads by de novo bacterial assembly, polishing, and QUAST consensus metrics.
skills.name: consensus-error-quantification
skills.search_text: consensus-error-quantification Use when basecalled FASTQ read sets from nanopore simulators must be compared against real experimental reads by de novo bacterial assembly, polishing, and QUAST consensus metrics. The goal is short-read or Illumina assembly benchmarking rather than ONT nanopore consensus accuracy Input reads are not basecalled FASTQ from a nanopore signal simulator (e.g., raw POD5 signal without basecalling) The reference genome is a complex eukaryote rather than a bacterial genome; the paper's validation criterion (sub-1-mismatch-per-100-kbp, 99.98%–100.00% genome fraction) was established only on the five bacterial species http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks de novo bacterial assembly quality from simulated versus real nanopore reads by running nanoMDBG assembly, Medaka polishing, and QUAST evaluation, extracting mismatches per 100 kbp and genome fraction to test whether a simulator's basecalled reads reproduce experimental consensus accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Benchmarks de novo bacterial assembly quality from simulated versus real nanopore reads by running nanoMDBG assembly, Medaka polishing, and QUAST evaluation, extracting mismatches per 100 kbp and genome fraction to test whether a simulator's basecalled reads reproduce experimental consensus accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is short-read or Illumina assembly benchmarking rather than ONT nanopore consensus accuracy Input reads are not basecalled FASTQ from a nanopore signal simulator (e.g., raw POD5 signal without basecalling) The reference genome is a complex eukaryote rather than a bacterial genome; the paper's validation criterion (sub-1-mismatch-per-100-kbp, 99.98%–100.00% genome fraction) was established only on the five bacterial species

skills.description: Use when benchmarking consensus sequence callers on simulated or real reads and you must verify whether reconstruction error decreases with coverage, differs by sequencing platform, or is elevated for a specific viral lineage.
skills.name: consensus-error-quantification
skills.search_text: consensus-error-quantification Use when benchmarking consensus sequence callers on simulated or real reads and you must verify whether reconstruction error decreases with coverage, differs by sequencing platform, or is elevated for a specific viral lineage. Input is raw read data with no called consensus sequences — consensus calling must precede error quantification Input lacks replication (single observation per condition), so per-replicate spread and effect-size sign consistency cannot be assessed The goal is caller speed or memory benchmarking rather than reconstruction accuracy — the paper's headline result is that ViralConsensus is orders of magnitude faster and more memory-efficient, which does not require error-trend analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify viral consensus genome reconstruction error from ViralConsensus benchmark outputs by stratifying per-replicate error tables over sequencing platform (Illumina vs ONT), SARS-CoV-2 lineage (e.g. BA.1), and coverage depth (30x/40x/50x), then testing trend direction and effect sizes. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Quantify viral consensus genome reconstruction error from ViralConsensus benchmark outputs by stratifying per-replicate error tables over sequencing platform (Illumina vs ONT), SARS-CoV-2 lineage (e.g. BA.1), and coverage depth (30x/40x/50x), then testing trend direction and effect sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read data with no called consensus sequences — consensus calling must precede error quantification Input lacks replication (single observation per condition), so per-replicate spread and effect-size sign consistency cannot be assessed The goal is caller speed or memory benchmarking rather than reconstruction accuracy — the paper's headline result is that ViralConsensus is orders of magnitude faster and more memory-efficient, which does not require error-trend analysis

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending the ViMOP benchmark: you need genome recovery metrics on FASTQ read sets (simulated viruses, host-virus mixtures, real SRA reads) across ViMOP, INSaFLU-TELEVIR, and VirDetector.
skills.name: consensus-genome-recovery-evaluation
skills.search_text: consensus-genome-recovery-evaluation Use when reproducing or extending the ViMOP benchmark: you need genome recovery metrics on FASTQ read sets (simulated viruses, host-virus mixtures, real SRA reads) across ViMOP, INSaFLU-TELEVIR, and VirDetector. The input is a targeted amplicon sequencing dataset rather than untargeted/metagenomic nanopore reads — ViMOP's de novo assembly plus BLAST reference identification is designed for untargeted data Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g., mpox) requiring finished-quality genomes — assemblies should be regarded as draft genomes per the README Only a single tool needs to be run with no cross-tool comparison — use the tool's own pipeline directly instead of the benchmark harness http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark skill for evaluating how well ViMOP recovers viral consensus genomes from untargeted nanopore reads compared to INSaFLU-TELEVIR and VirDetector, using simulated viral reads, host-virus mixtures, and real SRA samples. It produces a per-virus, per-sample tool-comparison table mirroring the paper's Section 2.11. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Benchmark skill for evaluating how well ViMOP recovers viral consensus genomes from untargeted nanopore reads compared to INSaFLU-TELEVIR and VirDetector, using simulated viral reads, host-virus mixtures, and real SRA samples. It produces a per-virus, per-sample tool-comparison table mirroring the paper's Section 2.11.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a targeted amplicon sequencing dataset rather than untargeted/metagenomic nanopore reads — ViMOP's de novo assembly plus BLAST reference identification is designed for untargeted data Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g., mpox) requiring finished-quality genomes — assemblies should be regarded as draft genomes per the README Only a single tool needs to be run with no cross-tool comparison — use the tool's own pipeline directly instead of the benchmark harness

skills.description: Use when building contigs from long, noisy nanopore FASTQ reads without a reference (e.g. inside a lossless compressor), by finding candidate overlapping reads with MinHash sketching and aligning them to a growing consensus graph.
skills.name: consensus-graph-contig-construction
skills.search_text: consensus-graph-contig-construction Use when building contigs from long, noisy nanopore FASTQ reads without a reference (e.g. inside a lossless compressor), by finding candidate overlapping reads with MinHash sketching and aligning them to a growing consensus graph. The task requires compressing quality values or read identifiers — NanoSpring compresses only the base sequences of the FASTQ Input is short, low-error read data (e.g. Illumina) where compressors like SPRING or PgRC that assume short reads are appropriate A high-quality reference genome is available and a reference-based compressor such as RENANO would achieve better compression http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reconstructs NanoSpring's approximate-assembly stage, where contigs are built by greedily extending a directed acyclic consensus graph with minimap2-aligned reads found via MinHash overlap search, enabling reference-free lossless compression of ONT read sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs NanoSpring's approximate-assembly stage, where contigs are built by greedily extending a directed acyclic consensus graph with minimap2-aligned reads found via MinHash overlap search, enabling reference-free lossless compression of ONT read sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires compressing quality values or read identifiers — NanoSpring compresses only the base sequences of the FASTQ Input is short, low-error read data (e.g. Illumina) where compressors like SPRING or PgRC that assume short reads are appropriate A high-quality reference genome is available and a reference-based compressor such as RENANO would achieve better compression

skills.description: Use when multiple replicate/downsampling DE runs with per-method FDR values are available and a robust consensus hit set is needed before isoform co-expression or coDIU analysis.
skills.name: consensus-hit-calling-across-replicates
skills.search_text: consensus-hit-calling-across-replicates Use when multiple replicate/downsampling DE runs with per-method FDR values are available and a robust consensus hit set is needed before isoform co-expression or coDIU analysis. When the goal is differential expression of single isoforms per gene rather than isoform co-usage — the single-DE-isoform-gene exclusion would discard exactly those genes When only one DE run or replicate is available, since the ≥50% run-frequency consensus requires multiple downsampling runs When isoform expression proportions are not available, since the <10% minor-isoform filter cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Derive a consensus set of differential isoform usage (DIU) hits by requiring each isoform to be called significant (FDR<0.05 by at least one acorde method) in ≥50% of 50 downsampling DE runs, then apply acorde's minor-isoform filter and single-DE-isoform-gene exclusion to obtain a robust isoform set for downstream co-usage analysis. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Derive a consensus set of differential isoform usage (DIU) hits by requiring each isoform to be called significant (FDR<0.05 by at least one acorde method) in ≥50% of 50 downsampling DE runs, then apply acorde's minor-isoform filter and single-DE-isoform-gene exclusion to obtain a robust isoform set for downstream co-usage analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential expression of single isoforms per gene rather than isoform co-usage — the single-DE-isoform-gene exclusion would discard exactly those genes When only one DE run or replicate is available, since the ≥50% run-frequency consensus requires multiple downsampling runs When isoform expression proportions are not available, since the <10% minor-isoform filter cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when you need cell- or cluster-level SNV/RNA-editing fractions (e.g. Gria2 R/G site) from ScNaUmi-seq UMI consensus molecules rather than error-prone raw Nanopore reads.
skills.name: consensus-molecule-snps-quantification
skills.search_text: consensus-molecule-snps-quantification Use when you need cell- or cluster-level SNV/RNA-editing fractions (e.g. Gria2 R/G site) from ScNaUmi-seq UMI consensus molecules rather than error-prone raw Nanopore reads. When the long reads have not been UMI-consensus corrected (step 4.b not run) — raw Nanopore error rates would corrupt edit calls When cell barcodes have not been validated (no ValidBarcodes.csv / SelectValidCellBarcode MINUMI/ED0ED1RATIO filtering applied) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Quantify single-nucleotide variants (e.g. A-to-I RNA editing) per cell cluster from Sicelore UMI-consensus molecule BAMs by running the SNPMatrix pipeline and computing edited-molecule fractions per position. This turns long-read Nanopore scRNA-seq data into per-cluster editing/SNV fraction estimates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Quantify single-nucleotide variants (e.g. A-to-I RNA editing) per cell cluster from Sicelore UMI-consensus molecule BAMs by running the SNPMatrix pipeline and computing edited-molecule fractions per position. This turns long-read Nanopore scRNA-seq data into per-cluster editing/SNV fraction estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the long reads have not been UMI-consensus corrected (step 4.b not run) — raw Nanopore error rates would corrupt edit calls When cell barcodes have not been validated (no ValidBarcodes.csv / SelectValidCellBarcode MINUMI/ED0ED1RATIO filtering applied)

skills.description: Use when nanopore amplicon consensus sequences (e.g., nanoClust output from 2D or 1D2 reads) must be quality-scored against reference 16S sequences, or when deciding how many reads (5, 10-15, >=50) are needed per OTU consensus.
skills.name: consensus-sequence-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: consensus-sequence-accuracy-assessment Use when nanopore amplicon consensus sequences (e.g., nanoClust output from 2D or 1D2 reads) must be quality-scored against reference 16S sequences, or when deciding how many reads (5, 10-15, >=50) are needed per OTU consensus. Input is a feature/OTU table or classification-only output rather than raw or INC-Seq-processed nanopore reads — this skill requires re-clustering and consensus calling from reads No reference 16S sequence (e.g., SILVA entry) exists for the organism, so percent identity against a reference cannot be computed Data are short Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM reads, where the nanopore-specific accuracy plateau and homopolymer deletion error modes do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies the accuracy of de novo full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences generated by nanoClust from noisy nanopore reads, by aligning each consensus against a SILVA reference and measuring sequence identity, and characterizes how accuracy depends on the number of reads used per consensus. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Quantifies the accuracy of de novo full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences generated by nanoClust from noisy nanopore reads, by aligning each consensus against a SILVA reference and measuring sequence identity, and characterizes how accuracy depends on the number of reads used per consensus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature/OTU table or classification-only output rather than raw or INC-Seq-processed nanopore reads — this skill requires re-clustering and consensus calling from reads No reference 16S sequence (e.g., SILVA entry) exists for the organism, so percent identity against a reference cannot be computed Data are short Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM reads, where the nanopore-specific accuracy plateau and homopolymer deletion error modes do not apply

skills.description: Use when you have raw .fast5 nanopore signals that were sliced with a fixed window (e.g. 300 samples, step 30, or Chiron's DNA preset segment_len 400 / jump 390) and need the overlapping slice-level basecalls merged into one full-length read sequence.
skills.name: consensus-sequence-assembly
skills.search_text: consensus-sequence-assembly Use when you have raw .fast5 nanopore signals that were sliced with a fixed window (e.g. 300 samples, step 30, or Chiron's DNA preset segment_len 400 / jump 390) and need the overlapping slice-level basecalls merged into one full-length read sequence. Input is already a set of full-length basecalled reads needing reference alignment or de novo assembly rather than within-read slice merging — the paper instead aligns basecalled reads to a reference with graphmap or assembles drafts with Minimap2/Miniasm plus Racon polishing. Input is direct-RNA signal with adapter/polyA tails that still require segmentation and trimming (use BoostNano preprocessing, not consensus assembly). The goal is to recover per-slice basecalls rather than a merged per-read sequence — Chiron already writes per-fast5 fastq/fasta results in the output 'result' folder without assembly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reassembles the short (~10-20 bp) basecalled slices produced by Chiron's 300-sample sliding-window basecaller into a single consensus sequence per raw nanopore read, using pairwise alignment between neighboring slices as described in the Chiron paper's streaming discussion. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: Reassembles the short (~10-20 bp) basecalled slices produced by Chiron's 300-sample sliding-window basecaller into a single consensus sequence per raw nanopore read, using pairwise alignment between neighboring slices as described in the Chiron paper's streaming discussion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of full-length basecalled reads needing reference alignment or de novo assembly rather than within-read slice merging — the paper instead aligns basecalled reads to a reference with graphmap or assembles drafts with Minimap2/Miniasm plus Racon polishing. Input is direct-RNA signal with adapter/polyA tails that still require segmentation and trimming (use BoostNano preprocessing, not consensus assembly). The goal is to recover per-slice basecalls rather than a merged per-read sequence — Chiron already writes per-fast5 fastq/fasta results in the output 'result' folder without assembly.

skills.description: Use when error-prone haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio long reads span candidate repetitive regions (e.g., SENSoR BED output) and low-error consensus sequences are needed before motif detection.
skills.name: consensus-sequence-error-correction
skills.search_text: consensus-sequence-error-correction Use when error-prone haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio long reads span candidate repetitive regions (e.g., SENSoR BED output) and low-error consensus sequences are needed before motif detection. Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres or telomeres, where spanning reads cannot be fetched Input is short-read or high-accuracy data where POA consensus adds little value and the method's error-reduction rationale (~77% ONT, ~88% PB on error-prone reads) does not apply Samples are polyploid or haploid (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compute haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences from error-prone ONT or PacBio long reads spanning candidate tandem repeats, using partial order alignment (SPOA), so that repeat motifs and multiplicity can be resolved downstream by approximate string matching. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Compute haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences from error-prone ONT or PacBio long reads spanning candidate tandem repeats, using partial order alignment (SPOA), so that repeat motifs and multiplicity can be resolved downstream by approximate string matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres or telomeres, where spanning reads cannot be fetched Input is short-read or high-accuracy data where POA consensus adds little value and the method's error-reduction rationale (~77% ONT, ~88% PB on error-prone reads) does not apply Samples are polyploid or haploid (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support

skills.description: Use when a FASTA/FASTQ file of Oxford Nanopore MinION reads has been aligned to a target database and a majority-rule consensus, per-position nucleotide counts, and candidate SNP calls are needed.
skills.name: consensus-sequence-generation
skills.search_text: consensus-sequence-generation Use when a FASTA/FASTQ file of Oxford Nanopore MinION reads has been aligned to a target database and a majority-rule consensus, per-position nucleotide counts, and candidate SNP calls are needed. The analysis goal is metagenomics classification of mixed-species MinION data — NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics analysis. The input is already assembled contigs or a finished genome rather than per-read MinION alignments — no per-position read counts exist to drive the majority-rule consensus. Positions covered by fewer than 10 reads are required to be called definitively — NanoPipe assigns a gap instead of a nucleotide there. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates a majority-rule consensus sequence and per-position nucleotide counts from MinION nanopore reads aligned to a target with NanoPipe (LAST + samtools + nanopipe_calc_polymorphism.py), flagging ambiguous positions with IUPAC codes and candidate SNPs for downstream evaluation. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Generates a majority-rule consensus sequence and per-position nucleotide counts from MinION nanopore reads aligned to a target with NanoPipe (LAST + samtools + nanopipe_calc_polymorphism.py), flagging ambiguous positions with IUPAC codes and candidate SNPs for downstream evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is metagenomics classification of mixed-species MinION data — NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics analysis. The input is already assembled contigs or a finished genome rather than per-read MinION alignments — no per-position read counts exist to drive the majority-rule consensus. Positions covered by fewer than 10 reads are required to be called definitively — NanoPipe assigns a gap instead of a nucleotide there.

skills.description: Use when profiling de novo tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio long-read alignments and the repeat motif and multiplicity must be resolved per haplotype from low-error consensus sequences.
skills.name: consensus-sequence-tr-multiplicity-genotyping
skills.search_text: consensus-sequence-tr-multiplicity-genotyping Use when profiling de novo tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio long-read alignments and the repeat motif and multiplicity must be resolved per haplotype from low-error consensus sequences. Repeats in unassembled genome regions (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres) — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there Polyploid species or haploid chromosomes such as the human Y chromosome — the diploid, haplotype-resolved model does not support them Mini-satellite profiling — TRiCoLOR has been extensively applied only to micro-satellites and mini-satellite parameters are not validated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Resolves the repeat motif and multiplicity of discovered tandem repeats from haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences using TRiCoLOR REFER's fast RegEx-based approximate string-matching algorithm, with default parameters of motifs of length ≤6 bp perfectly repeated ≥5 times, edit distance ≤1, and TRs ≥50 bp stored in BCF-compliant format. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Resolves the repeat motif and multiplicity of discovered tandem repeats from haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences using TRiCoLOR REFER's fast RegEx-based approximate string-matching algorithm, with default parameters of motifs of length ≤6 bp perfectly repeated ≥5 times, edit distance ≤1, and TRs ≥50 bp stored in BCF-compliant format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Repeats in unassembled genome regions (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres) — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there Polyploid species or haploid chromosomes such as the human Y chromosome — the diploid, haplotype-resolved model does not support them Mini-satellite profiling — TRiCoLOR has been extensively applied only to micro-satellites and mini-satellite parameters are not validated

skills.description: Use when a ConsensuSV-ONT run has finished (vcfs/ and alignments/ folders exist) and you need to inspect the consensus deletion/insertion VCFs or explain why specific calls were scored as false positives against a benchmark set.
skills.name: consensus-sv-output-interpretation
skills.search_text: consensus-sv-output-interpretation Use when a ConsensuSV-ONT run has finished (vcfs/ and alignments/ folders exist) and you need to inspect the consensus deletion/insertion VCFs or explain why specific calls were scored as false positives against a benchmark set. Before the pipeline has completed — no vcfs/<sample>/ folder with caller and ConsensuSV-ONT VCFs exists yet For fresh SV calling from FASTQ data; this skill interprets existing consensus output, use the full ConsensuSV-ONT nextflow pipeline instead For short-read or Illumina-only consensus calling — the method is built for Oxford Nanopore long-read data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Interpretation of ConsensuSV-ONT consensus structural variant calls: reading the per-sample VCFs emitted into the pipeline's 'vcfs' output directory (individual caller VCFs plus the final ConsensuSV-ONT consensus calls), and characterising consensus deletions against a ground-truth set by classifying mismatches (merged, partial-overlap, or novel false positives). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Interpretation of ConsensuSV-ONT consensus structural variant calls: reading the per-sample VCFs emitted into the pipeline's 'vcfs' output directory (individual caller VCFs plus the final ConsensuSV-ONT consensus calls), and characterising consensus deletions against a ground-truth set by classifying mismatches (merged, partial-overlap, or novel false positives).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Before the pipeline has completed — no vcfs/<sample>/ folder with caller and ConsensuSV-ONT VCFs exists yet For fresh SV calling from FASTQ data; this skill interprets existing consensus output, use the full ConsensuSV-ONT nextflow pipeline instead For short-read or Illumina-only consensus calling — the method is built for Oxford Nanopore long-read data

skills.description: Use when you have ONT fastq.gz long-read samples and need high-quality SV calls (DEL/INS) as VCFs from a consensus of six callers plus CNN filtering, rather than a single caller.
skills.name: consensus-sv-vcf-generation
skills.search_text: consensus-sv-vcf-generation Use when you have ONT fastq.gz long-read samples and need high-quality SV calls (DEL/INS) as VCFs from a consensus of six callers plus CNN filtering, rather than a single caller. Input data is short-read (Illumina/PacBio) rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, which the six callers and pipeline are designed for You only need calls from a single SV caller and do not want CNN-based filtering overhead You lack the computational environment to run docker/nextflow and cannot use the provided runtime image http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Generate consensus structural variant VCFs by running six independent long-read SV callers inside the ConsensuSV-ONT docker/nextflow pipeline and filtering the collapsed candidate set with a 3D CNN (sigmoid output > 0.5), producing per-sample VCFs alongside the individual callers' VCFs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Generate consensus structural variant VCFs by running six independent long-read SV callers inside the ConsensuSV-ONT docker/nextflow pipeline and filtering the collapsed candidate set with a 3D CNN (sigmoid output > 0.5), producing per-sample VCFs alongside the individual callers' VCFs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is short-read (Illumina/PacBio) rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, which the six callers and pipeline are designed for You only need calls from a single SV caller and do not want CNN-based filtering overhead You lack the computational environment to run docker/nextflow and cannot use the provided runtime image

skills.description: Use when correcting hybrid (long + short read) datasets at the base level and you need a strict, high-confidence rule — e.g., PacBio long reads with ≥90% Illumina consensus at a questionable position — rather than majority voting or optimization.
skills.name: consensus-threshold-base-correction
skills.search_text: consensus-threshold-base-correction Use when correcting hybrid (long + short read) datasets at the base level and you need a strict, high-confidence rule — e.g., PacBio long reads with ≥90% Illumina consensus at a questionable position — rather than majority voting or optimization. A questionable position falls below the η = 0.9 (90%) consensus threshold — such bases must be routed to HECIL's optimization-based correction framework, not quick-corrected You have only long reads and no short-read data — this is a hybrid correction rule requiring Illumina short-read alignments (unlike self-correcting methods such as HGAP) Simple majority voting is the intended rule — HECIL explicitly adopts a stricter-than-majority 90% consensus cutoff, so this skill is wrong for majority-based correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Implements HECIL's Quick Correction stage: at positions on long reads marked questionable (mismatches, insertions, deletions) from BWA-MEM alignment of Illumina short reads, the long-read base is directly replaced with the short-read consensus base only when at least 90% consensus (η = 0.9) is reached, bypassing the optimization-based correction framework. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Implements HECIL's Quick Correction stage: at positions on long reads marked questionable (mismatches, insertions, deletions) from BWA-MEM alignment of Illumina short reads, the long-read base is directly replaced with the short-read consensus base only when at least 90% consensus (η = 0.9) is reached, bypassing the optimization-based correction framework.

skills.search_text: contig-copy-number-classification Use when a draft assembly (e.g. SPAdes contigs from Illumina MiSeq paired-end reads) must be partitioned into unique vs repetitive contigs before scaffolding, gap-filling, or deciding which contigs can anchor long-read bridges. The assembly has no associated short-read data — multiplicity estimation relies on comparing contig short-read coverage to whole-genome coverage and cannot be computed from long reads alone. The assembly is largely fragmented with few contigs over 20 Kb — the depth statistic is only stated to be stable with up to 20 of the largest contigs longer than 20 Kb, so bacterial-genome assumptions may not transfer. The goal is de novo long-read assembly rather than scaffolding a short-read draft (e.g. use Celera Assembler on corrected long reads instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies draft-assembly contigs as unique (copy number 1) or repetitive by comparing each contig's short-read coverage against an iteratively estimated whole-genome depth, a prerequisite for npScarf's scaffolding from unique contigs and gap-filling with repetitive ones. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515

You already have high-quality full read alignments (e.g. minimap2 PAF) and an alignment-based scaffolder is preferred — ntLink's advantage is using lightweight minimizer-based mappings instead of read alignments. The draft contigs are shorter than z=1000 bp, since ntLink restricts scaffold graph nodes to contigs of at least 1000 bp. You need misassembly correction rather than scaffolding — that is a separate downstream application (Tigmint-long using ntLink mappings), not contig join inference. skills.name: contig-terminal-barcode-artifact-detection
skills.search_text: contig-terminal-barcode-artifact-detection Use when screening assembled genomes or plasmid contigs (FASTA) from NCBI for residual native-barcode barcode/flank sequences, especially matches near contig ends that indicate assembler artefacts or cross-sample contamination. Input is raw read data rather than an assembled FASTA — use Barbell's 'kit' demultiplexing workflow ('barbell kit -k <kit-name>') instead Barcodes belong to rapid barcoding kits or non-native kits whose sequences are not in the query FASTA; native kit presets/flanks will not match You expect fully intact barcodes rather than error-laden remnants — edit-distance matching against native barcode+flank queries is specifically for partial/remnant artefacts http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Detects remnant Nanopore native-barcoding barcode sequences (e.g., NB02, NB13 with their shared flanking sequences) left inside public genome assemblies by running Barbell's Sassy-backed edit-distance annotate step on downloaded NCBI FASTA records, revealing contamination footprints such as the NB13 remnant at the end of the 8423 bp plasmid CP142556.1. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Detects remnant Nanopore native-barcoding barcode sequences (e.g., NB02, NB13 with their shared flanking sequences) left inside public genome assemblies by running Barbell's Sassy-backed edit-distance annotate step on downloaded NCBI FASTA records, revealing contamination footprints such as the NB13 remnant at the end of the 8423 bp plasmid CP142556.1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read data rather than an assembled FASTA — use Barbell's 'kit' demultiplexing workflow ('barbell kit -k <kit-name>') instead Barcodes belong to rapid barcoding kits or non-native kits whose sequences are not in the query FASTA; native kit presets/flanks will not match You expect fully intact barcodes rather than error-laden remnants — edit-distance matching against native barcode+flank queries is specifically for partial/remnant artefacts

skills.description: Use when you need to assess whether short-read assembly recovers complex isoforms at multi-isoform loci that long-read RNAseq (ONT/Mandalorion) has already defined, or to flag assembly contigs with no long-read counterpart.
skills.name: contig-to-isoform-alignment-comparison
skills.search_text: contig-to-isoform-alignment-comparison Use when you need to assess whether short-read assembly recovers complex isoforms at multi-isoform loci that long-read RNAseq (ONT/Mandalorion) has already defined, or to flag assembly contigs with no long-read counterpart. When the goal is standard transcript quantification rather than testing assembly completeness against long-read isoforms. When reads are raw ONT/R2C2 reads rather than assembled contigs — Mandalorion's isoform definition pipeline (C3POa/R2C2 consensus) is the appropriate path, not contig-to-isoform comparison. When the gene locus is single-isoform and simple; the comparison adds value mainly for multi-isoform loci like CD37 where short reads cannot resolve full-length isoforms. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking skill that tests whether a short-read de novo assembly (e.g., Trinity on per-cell Illumina RNAseq) can reproduce long-read-identified isoforms (from ONT RNAseq/Mandalorion) by splice-aligning contigs to isoform sequences and classifying coverage as complete, partial, or absent. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms16027
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that tests whether a short-read de novo assembly (e.g., Trinity on per-cell Illumina RNAseq) can reproduce long-read-identified isoforms (from ONT RNAseq/Mandalorion) by splice-aligning contigs to isoform sequences and classifying coverage as complete, partial, or absent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is standard transcript quantification rather than testing assembly completeness against long-read isoforms. When reads are raw ONT/R2C2 reads rather than assembled contigs — Mandalorion's isoform definition pipeline (C3POa/R2C2 consensus) is the appropriate path, not contig-to-isoform comparison. When the gene locus is single-isoform and simple; the comparison adds value mainly for multi-isoform loci like CD37 where short reads cannot resolve full-length isoforms.

skills.description: Use when locally assembled contigs (e.g., from Blackbird/SPAdes sliding-window assembly of synthetic long-read barcode data) must be converted into insertion/deletion calls against a reference genome.
skills.name: contig-to-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: contig-to-reference-alignment Use when locally assembled contigs (e.g., from Blackbird/SPAdes sliding-window assembly of synthetic long-read barcode data) must be converted into insertion/deletion calls against a reference genome. You already have long reads at ~10x coverage and can call SVs directly with a long-read caller such as PBSV or Sniffles2 instead of local assembly The goal is whole-genome assembly rather than segment-local insertion/deletion calling; Blackbird explicitly avoids whole-genome assembly Only short-read data are available: most SVs in the 50-10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short-read sequencing http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Aligns Blackbird's barcode-aware locally assembled contigs against a BWA-indexed reference genome using minimap2, parses the CIGAR strings to call insertions and deletions within assembled segments, and emits a position-sorted VCF of events longer than 50 bp. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Aligns Blackbird's barcode-aware locally assembled contigs against a BWA-indexed reference genome using minimap2, parses the CIGAR strings to call insertions and deletions within assembled segments, and emits a position-sorted VCF of events longer than 50 bp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have long reads at ~10x coverage and can call SVs directly with a long-read caller such as PBSV or Sniffles2 instead of local assembly The goal is whole-genome assembly rather than segment-local insertion/deletion calling; Blackbird explicitly avoids whole-genome assembly Only short-read data are available: most SVs in the 50-10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short-read sequencing

skills.description: Use when you need to test custom contrasts of regression coefficients in a TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated NB model — e.g., joint testing of H0: alpha1 = beta1 = 0 — or to verify that the contrast route reproduces the Z-statistic gene-level set-level p-values.
skills.name: contrast-based-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: contrast-based-hypothesis-testing Use when you need to test custom contrasts of regression coefficients in a TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated NB model — e.g., joint testing of H0: alpha1 = beta1 = 0 — or to verify that the contrast route reproduces the Z-statistic gene-level set-level p-values. When testing a covariate present in both mean and zero-inflation components of the model — use lr.twosigma or lr.twosigma_custom likelihood-ratio testing instead When genes in the test set would have heterogeneous random-effect specifications (adhoc screening applied to some genes only) — the common gene-level null required by twosigmag is violated When the covariate of interest is only in the mean component and a simple gene-level Wald/Z test suffices — the contrast route via twosigmag is unnecessary machinery http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Test fixed-effect contrasts (e.g., disease-status regression coefficients) in the TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model by routing a custom contrast matrix through the twosigmag gene-set testing function, yielding set-level p-values for each contrast row that agree with the Z-statistic gene-level route. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Test fixed-effect contrasts (e.g., disease-status regression coefficients) in the TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model by routing a custom contrast matrix through the twosigmag gene-set testing function, yielding set-level p-values for each contrast row that agree with the Z-statistic gene-level route.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing a covariate present in both mean and zero-inflation components of the model — use lr.twosigma or lr.twosigma_custom likelihood-ratio testing instead When genes in the test set would have heterogeneous random-effect specifications (adhoc screening applied to some genes only) — the common gene-level null required by twosigmag is violated When the covariate of interest is only in the mean component and a simple gene-level Wald/Z test suffices — the contrast route via twosigmag is unnecessary machinery

skills.description: Use when benchmarking read-level 5mCpG detection models on methylation-ground-truth CCS data: controlled M.SssI-treated/PCR-treated paired samples exist, and a fair train/test read split is needed to compare model accuracies and AUCs.
skills.name: controlled-methylation-dataset-splitting
skills.search_text: controlled-methylation-dataset-splitting Use when benchmarking read-level 5mCpG detection models on methylation-ground-truth CCS data: controlled M.SssI-treated/PCR-treated paired samples exist, and a fair train/test read split is needed to compare model accuracies and AUCs. The goal is methylation phasing or haplotype-aware methylation with ccsmethphase rather than controlled read-level benchmarking of 5mCpG callers Input data lacks methylation ground truth (e.g., native HG002/CHM13 reads without M.SssI or PCR controls), so no supervised train/test split can be labeled Evaluation is site-level methylation frequency rather than single-molecule (read-level) 5mCpG classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Organizes matched M.SssI-methyltransferase-treated versus PCR-treated PacBio CCS dataset pairs (e.g., M01&W01, M02&W02, M03&W03) and splits each pair 50/50 at the read level into training and test sets, enabling a controlled, ground-truth benchmark of 5mCpG callers such as ccsmeth against the HK model. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Organizes matched M.SssI-methyltransferase-treated versus PCR-treated PacBio CCS dataset pairs (e.g., M01&W01, M02&W02, M03&W03) and splits each pair 50/50 at the read level into training and test sets, enabling a controlled, ground-truth benchmark of 5mCpG callers such as ccsmeth against the HK model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is methylation phasing or haplotype-aware methylation with ccsmethphase rather than controlled read-level benchmarking of 5mCpG callers Input data lacks methylation ground truth (e.g., native HG002/CHM13 reads without M.SssI or PCR controls), so no supervised train/test split can be labeled Evaluation is site-level methylation frequency rather than single-molecule (read-level) 5mCpG classification

skills.description: Use when building ground-truth benchmarking mixtures of methylated and unmethylated nanopore reads to evaluate per-read or per-site methylation callers, or when preparing METEORE-format score files with known expected methylation frequencies.
skills.name: controlled-methylation-mixture-construction
skills.search_text: controlled-methylation-mixture-construction Use when building ground-truth benchmarking mixtures of methylated and unmethylated nanopore reads to evaluate per-read or per-site methylation callers, or when preparing METEORE-format score files with known expected methylation frequencies. You need per-read methylation predictions on natural samples with unknown methylation status rather than benchmarking against a known ground truth Coverage at candidate CpG sites is below the 50x threshold, so methylated/unmethylated read pools cannot be reliably partitioned at unambiguous single-CpG loci Evaluating tools on WGBS or Cas9-targeted (nCATS) data instead of controlled mixtures of individual nanopore reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Constructs controlled methylation mixture benchmarking datasets from nanopore reads of E. coli methylated (M.SssI-treated) and unmethylated (PCR-amplified) controls, enabling ground-truth evaluation of CpG methylation detection tools at known methylated-read proportions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Constructs controlled methylation mixture benchmarking datasets from nanopore reads of E. coli methylated (M.SssI-treated) and unmethylated (PCR-amplified) controls, enabling ground-truth evaluation of CpG methylation detection tools at known methylated-read proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-read methylation predictions on natural samples with unknown methylation status rather than benchmarking against a known ground truth Coverage at candidate CpG sites is below the 50x threshold, so methylated/unmethylated read pools cannot be reliably partitioned at unambiguous single-CpG loci Evaluating tools on WGBS or Cas9-targeted (nCATS) data instead of controlled mixtures of individual nanopore reads

skills.description: Use when input is base-converted (EMseq/nanoEM) nanopore FASTQ split into *_CT.fq.gz and *_GA.fq.gz and you need strand-aware mapping to a converted reference before methylation calling.
skills.name: converted-read-strand-aware-alignment
skills.search_text: converted-read-strand-aware-alignment Use when input is base-converted (EMseq/nanoEM) nanopore FASTQ split into *_CT.fq.gz and *_GA.fq.gz and you need strand-aware mapping to a converted reference before methylation calling. Input reads are native (unconverted) nanopore WGS to be methylation-called directly with nanopolish — no strand conversion or converted reference is needed Input is short-read WGBS/EMseq data aligned with bisulfite-aware short-read aligners rather than long-read nanopore data The reference genome has not been base-converted with convert_ref.py; aligning converted reads to an unconverted reference will fail to map correctly http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns C-to-T and G-to-A converted nanoEM nanopore reads to a correspondingly converted reference genome with minimap2 (--eqx, map-ont preset) and selects the best alignment across the two strand conversions, enabling per-CpG methylation calling from enzymatically base-converted long reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: Aligns C-to-T and G-to-A converted nanoEM nanopore reads to a correspondingly converted reference genome with minimap2 (--eqx, map-ont preset) and selects the best alignment across the two strand conversions, enabling per-CpG methylation calling from enzymatically base-converted long reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are native (unconverted) nanopore WGS to be methylation-called directly with nanopolish — no strand conversion or converted reference is needed Input is short-read WGBS/EMseq data aligned with bisulfite-aware short-read aligners rather than long-read nanopore data The reference genome has not been base-converted with convert_ref.py; aligning converted reads to an unconverted reference will fail to map correctly

skills.description: Use when correcting residual questionable bases (mismatches, insertions, deletions) on third-generation long reads after the quick-correction stage, when short-read-to-long-read alignments (e.g. BWA-MEM) with FASTQ quality scores are available and a per-base correction policy must be chosen.
skills.name: convex-combination-cost-optimization
skills.search_text: convex-combination-cost-optimization Use when correcting residual questionable bases (mismatches, insertions, deletions) on third-generation long reads after the quick-correction stage, when short-read-to-long-read alignments (e.g. BWA-MEM) with FASTQ quality scores are available and a per-base correction policy must be chosen. Bases already eligible for quick correction (>=90% consensus, η = 0.9) — these are handled by the quick-correction stage, not the optimization framework Self-correcting (non-hybrid) settings where no Illumina short reads or alignments exist — decision weights require base quality and mapping identity from aligned short reads Assigning confidence scores to prior corrections or triggering realignment between iterations — that is the separate Assignment of Confidence / realignment step, not the per-base cost optimization http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 HECIL's optimization-based correction stage that fixes questionable bases remaining on long reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) after quick correction, by scoring each aligned Illumina short read with an equal-weight (1/2, 1/2) convex combination of normalized base-quality and mapping-identity decision weights and selecting the argmax read as the correction source. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: HECIL's optimization-based correction stage that fixes questionable bases remaining on long reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) after quick correction, by scoring each aligned Illumina short read with an equal-weight (1/2, 1/2) convex combination of normalized base-quality and mapping-identity decision weights and selecting the argmax read as the correction source.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bases already eligible for quick correction (>=90% consensus, η = 0.9) — these are handled by the quick-correction stage, not the optimization framework Self-correcting (non-hybrid) settings where no Illumina short reads or alignments exist — decision weights require base quality and mapping identity from aligned short reads Assigning confidence scores to prior corrections or triggering realignment between iterations — that is the separate Assignment of Confidence / realignment step, not the per-base cost optimization

skills.description: Use when you must justify a multi-column/multi-scale CNN architecture over simpler single-scale variants by running controlled ablation comparisons on held-out bacteria (LOOCV) and an independent test set.
skills.name: convolutional-neural-network-ablation-study
skills.search_text: convolutional-neural-network-ablation-study Use when you must justify a multi-column/multi-scale CNN architecture over simpler single-scale variants by running controlled ablation comparisons on held-out bacteria (LOOCV) and an independent test set. The goal is methylation motif discovery or de novo motif enrichment rather than benchmarking an existing CNN architecture Only a pretrained model is needed for prediction — use best_model/Nanoident.pt with postprocess.py instead of retraining ablation variants Input data lacks the five Nanoident features (nanopore raw-signal statistics plus basecall features) required to train the convolutional variants http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Trains single-scale (large L, medium M, small S single-column) ablation variants of the Nanoident multi-column CNN and compares them against the fused multi-scale network on LOOCV and an independent dataset to quantify the benefit of multi-scale receptive-field fusion for bacterial methylation typing and fine mapping. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf397
skills.summary: Trains single-scale (large L, medium M, small S single-column) ablation variants of the Nanoident multi-column CNN and compares them against the fused multi-scale network on LOOCV and an independent dataset to quantify the benefit of multi-scale receptive-field fusion for bacterial methylation typing and fine mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is methylation motif discovery or de novo motif enrichment rather than benchmarking an existing CNN architecture Only a pretrained model is needed for prediction — use best_model/Nanoident.pt with postprocess.py instead of retraining ablation variants Input data lacks the five Nanoident features (nanopore raw-signal statistics plus basecall features) required to train the convolutional variants

skills.description: Use when reimplementing or extending Nanoident's multi-column CNN for classifying methylation types (4mC, 5mC, 6mA) or fine-mapping methylated base positions from five Nanopore-derived motif features.
skills.name: convolutional-neural-network-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: convolutional-neural-network-architecture-implementation Use when reimplementing or extending Nanoident's multi-column CNN for classifying methylation types (4mC, 5mC, 6mA) or fine-mapping methylated base positions from five Nanopore-derived motif features. Input is raw nanopore signal or modBAM rather than the preprocessed five-feature motif data in pkl format The task is de novo methylation motif discovery rather than typing or fine mapping of already known motifs http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstruct Nanoident's multi-scale convolutional architecture in PyTorch: three columns of depthwise-separable convolution (DSC) blocks with large (kernel 4), medium (kernels 3 and 2), and small (three stacked kernel-2) receptive fields, whose outputs are concatenated, adaptively weighted, and fused with a 1x1 pointwise convolution for bacterial methylation motif typing and fine mapping from Nanopore features. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf397
skills.summary: Reconstruct Nanoident's multi-scale convolutional architecture in PyTorch: three columns of depthwise-separable convolution (DSC) blocks with large (kernel 4), medium (kernels 3 and 2), and small (three stacked kernel-2) receptive fields, whose outputs are concatenated, adaptively weighted, and fused with a 1x1 pointwise convolution for bacterial methylation motif typing and fine mapping from Nanopore features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore signal or modBAM rather than the preprocessed five-feature motif data in pkl format The task is de novo methylation motif discovery rather than typing or fine mapping of already known motifs

skills.description: Use when a labelled set of encoded structural-variant images (high-quality vs low-quality) needs a binary deep-learning classifier trained and its per-epoch generalisation behaviour monitored.
skills.name: convolutional-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: convolutional-neural-network-training Use when a labelled set of encoded structural-variant images (high-quality vs low-quality) needs a binary deep-learning classifier trained and its per-epoch generalisation behaviour monitored. The input is raw FASTQ/BAM data rather than already-encoded SV images — variant calling and image encoding must happen first in the nextflow pipeline You need multi-class SV type prediction rather than the binary high-quality/low-quality filter the sigmoid output provides The task is per-sample consensus SV calling rather than training/monitoring the CNN classifier itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train the ConsensuSV-ONT binary CNN that filters high-quality structural variants: three Conv3D+BatchNorm+MaxPooling3D blocks over 50x50x3 encoded SV images, fit in Keras with per-epoch monitoring of AUC, loss, learning rate and Truvari precision/recall/F1. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Train the ConsensuSV-ONT binary CNN that filters high-quality structural variants: three Conv3D+BatchNorm+MaxPooling3D blocks over 50x50x3 encoded SV images, fit in Keras with per-epoch monitoring of AUC, loss, learning rate and Truvari precision/recall/F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ/BAM data rather than already-encoded SV images — variant calling and image encoding must happen first in the nextflow pipeline You need multi-class SV type prediction rather than the binary high-quality/low-quality filter the sigmoid output provides The task is per-sample consensus SV calling rather than training/monitoring the CNN classifier itself

skills.description: Reference for validating whether a sequence-aware variant merge preserves distinct insertion calls at near-identical coordinates that a coordinate-only merger (e.g., SURVIVOR) collapses into one record.
skills.name: coordinate-based-merge-benchmarking-against-survivor
skills.search_text: coordinate-based-merge-benchmarking-against-survivor Reference for validating whether a sequence-aware variant merge preserves distinct insertion calls at near-identical coordinates that a coordinate-only merger (e.g., SURVIVOR) collapses into one record. The input callsets contain no reassembled insertion sequences (callers/reporters without consensus sequences) and reassembly from supporting reads is not possible — merging must remain coordinate-only. The goal is merging non-insertion SV classes (deletions, inversions, duplications), for which the Levenshtein sequence comparison step is not applicable. A single already-merged multi-sample callset is provided and no coordinate-only baseline comparison is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmarks RetroInspector's sequence-aware insertion merging (coordinates + length + Levenshtein distance on reassembled insert sequences) against SURVIVOR's coordinate-only merge to reveal near-coordinate insertion events that coordinate-only merging wrongly collapses. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks RetroInspector's sequence-aware insertion merging (coordinates + length + Levenshtein distance on reassembled insert sequences) against SURVIVOR's coordinate-only merge to reveal near-coordinate insertion events that coordinate-only merging wrongly collapses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input callsets contain no reassembled insertion sequences (callers/reporters without consensus sequences) and reassembly from supporting reads is not possible — merging must remain coordinate-only. The goal is merging non-insertion SV classes (deletions, inversions, duplications), for which the Levenshtein sequence comparison step is not applicable. A single already-merged multi-sample callset is provided and no coordinate-only baseline comparison is required.

skills.description: Use when converting per-read methylation probabilities into coordinate-anchored outputs (per-read TSV/BED, modBAM MM/ML tags, per-site frequencies) or when parsing label files in 'contig position strand label' format for CpG sites.
skills.name: coordinate-based-methylation-label-handling
skills.search_text: coordinate-based-methylation-label-handling Use when converting per-read methylation probabilities into coordinate-anchored outputs (per-read TSV/BED, modBAM MM/ML tags, per-site frequencies) or when parsing label files in 'contig position strand label' format for CpG sites. Input is already a per-site bedMethyl or aggregated methylation frequency table rather than per-read signal-level predictions Only modBAM manipulation or summary statistics is needed and no signal files are available (modkit alone suffices) The target modification is not 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides models for 5mCpG methylation http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Handles 5mC methylation calls keyed to genomic and read coordinates in the DeepMod2 framework: writing per-read TSV/BED records with chromosome/ref_position/read_position/strand/methylation_score columns, adding MM/ML tags to BAM, and aggregating per-read predictions into per-site methylation frequency. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Handles 5mC methylation calls keyed to genomic and read coordinates in the DeepMod2 framework: writing per-read TSV/BED records with chromosome/ref_position/read_position/strand/methylation_score columns, adding MM/ML tags to BAM, and aggregating per-read predictions into per-site methylation frequency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-site bedMethyl or aggregated methylation frequency table rather than per-read signal-level predictions Only modBAM manipulation or summary statistics is needed and no signal files are available (modkit alone suffices) The target modification is not 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides models for 5mCpG methylation

skills.description: Use when matched clonal strain pairs exist where one genome carries a known duplication (CNV genotype) and matched expression data (e.g. microarray/RNA-seq log-phase cultures) are available to test dosage-driven induction.
skills.name: copy-number-expression-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: copy-number-expression-correlation-analysis Use when matched clonal strain pairs exist where one genome carries a known duplication (CNV genotype) and matched expression data (e.g. microarray/RNA-seq log-phase cultures) are available to test dosage-driven induction. The strains compared are not from the same clonal population, so SNP background confounds the expression comparison The goal is differential expression outside duplicated regions (the paper notes some genes outside duplications also change, but that is a distinct analysis) No CNV genotypes are available to define which genes lie within each duplicated region http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Tests whether genes inside naturally occurring duplications are induced by comparing microarray expression of a duplicated strain to a non-duplicated strain from the same clonal S. pombe population, then ranks pairs by Spearman correlation between copy number and induction. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Tests whether genes inside naturally occurring duplications are induced by comparing microarray expression of a duplicated strain to a non-duplicated strain from the same clonal S. pombe population, then ranks pairs by Spearman correlation between copy number and induction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The strains compared are not from the same clonal population, so SNP background confounds the expression comparison The goal is differential expression outside duplicated regions (the paper notes some genes outside duplications also change, but that is a distinct analysis) No CNV genotypes are available to define which genes lie within each duplicated region

skills.description: Use when SV calls from a nanopore variant caller must be turned into per-region coverage profiles (with 1-Mb flanks) before disCoverage's coverage-agreement statistics or p < 0.05 filtering can be applied.
skills.name: copy-number-variant-region-annotation
skills.search_text: copy-number-variant-region-annotation Use when SV calls from a nanopore variant caller must be turned into per-region coverage profiles (with 1-Mb flanks) before disCoverage's coverage-agreement statistics or p < 0.05 filtering can be applied. The goal is de novo SV discovery — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions from an additional technique or multi-sample analysis Calls include SV types other than deletions and duplications (e.g., insertions, inversions) — coverage-based refinement can only be applied to DEL and DUP The candidate region is a very large SV (>10 Mb) encompassing other SVs or centromeres — such calls were deemed artifacts and not considered true http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Convert putative DEL/DUP structural variant calls into a 4-column BED (chromosome, start, end, SV type) and run disCoverage, which internally invokes mosdepth, to obtain per-base coverage over each SV interval plus 1 Mb of up- and downstream flanks. This profile is the prerequisite input for disCoverage's later statistical filtering of nanopore SV calls. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Convert putative DEL/DUP structural variant calls into a 4-column BED (chromosome, start, end, SV type) and run disCoverage, which internally invokes mosdepth, to obtain per-base coverage over each SV interval plus 1 Mb of up- and downstream flanks. This profile is the prerequisite input for disCoverage's later statistical filtering of nanopore SV calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo SV discovery — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions from an additional technique or multi-sample analysis Calls include SV types other than deletions and duplications (e.g., insertions, inversions) — coverage-based refinement can only be applied to DEL and DUP The candidate region is a very large SV (>10 Mb) encompassing other SVs or centromeres — such calls were deemed artifacts and not considered true

skills.description: Use when a merged nanopore SV call set (VCF per aligner) must be split into SV-type classes and only the copy-number classes (DEL/DUP) need coverage-support testing and filtering.
skills.name: copy-number-variant-type-classification
skills.search_text: copy-number-variant-type-classification Use when a merged nanopore SV call set (VCF per aligner) must be split into SV-type classes and only the copy-number classes (DEL/DUP) need coverage-support testing and filtering.
