skills.search_text: coverage-downsampling-to-target-depth Use when a collection of short-read BAM alignments has heterogeneous sequencing depth (e.g. 161 S. pombe strains re-sequenced to different depths) and SV calling or copy-number inference requires uniform coverage before variant discovery. A strain's merged BAM is already below the target coverage (e.g. under 40x) — downsampling cannot raise depth, so the sample must be left as-is or excluded The downstream analysis depends on absolute read depth, such as re-examining read coverage of the 49 CNVs to genotype copy number within clonal populations — downsampling would distort the coverage signal used for copy-number estimation Input is unaligned FASTQ or a raw base-level coverage table rather than a merged alignment BAM Randomly downsamples each strain's merged BAM alignments to a uniform mean coverage (40x in the Jeffares et al. 2017 S. pombe SV study) using Samtools, so that SV callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPs) see comparable depth across all samples and depth differences between strains do not bias SV calling. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Randomly downsamples each strain's merged BAM alignments to a uniform mean coverage (40x in the Jeffares et al. 2017 S. pombe SV study) using Samtools, so that SV callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPs) see comparable depth across all samples and depth differences between strains do not bias SV calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A strain's merged BAM is already below the target coverage (e.g. under 40x) — downsampling cannot raise depth, so the sample must be left as-is or excluded The downstream analysis depends on absolute read depth, such as re-examining read coverage of the 49 CNVs to genotype copy number within clonal populations — downsampling would distort the coverage signal used for copy-number estimation Input is unaligned FASTQ or a raw base-level coverage table rather than a merged alignment BAM

skills.description: Use when you already have putative SV coordinates (e.g. from Sniffles/CuteSV/SVIM/NanoVar on NGMLR-aligned nanopore reads) and need per-base coverage over each SV interval plus 1-Mb flanks to judge coverage support or filter calls.
skills.name: coverage-file-reuse-optimization
skills.search_text: coverage-file-reuse-optimization Use when you already have putative SV coordinates (e.g. from Sniffles/CuteSV/SVIM/NanoVar on NGMLR-aligned nanopore reads) and need per-base coverage over each SV interval plus 1-Mb flanks to judge coverage support or filter calls. The variant list contains SV types other than deletions and duplications (inversions, insertions, translocations) — coverage-based checking can only be applied to DEL/DUP. No putative SV positions exist yet — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs coordinates obtained from a variant caller or another technique first. You need de novo CNV discovery from raw reads — this skill only evaluates coverage agreement at pre-specified candidate regions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Derives per-base coverage profiles for putative DEL/DUP SV calls and their 1-Mb flanking regions by running disCoverage, which internally invokes mosdepth on a nanopore alignment BAM, and reuses the resulting per-region coverage bed.gz files for downstream coverage-support filtering instead of recomputing depth. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Derives per-base coverage profiles for putative DEL/DUP SV calls and their 1-Mb flanking regions by running disCoverage, which internally invokes mosdepth on a nanopore alignment BAM, and reuses the resulting per-region coverage bed.gz files for downstream coverage-support filtering instead of recomputing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant list contains SV types other than deletions and duplications (inversions, insertions, translocations) — coverage-based checking can only be applied to DEL/DUP. No putative SV positions exist yet — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs coordinates obtained from a variant caller or another technique first. You need de novo CNV discovery from raw reads — this skill only evaluates coverage agreement at pre-specified candidate regions.

skills.description: Use when you need to determine the minimum WGS coverage required for reliable exon/splice-graph prediction, or to characterize how prediction quality degrades at very low or very high depth.
skills.name: coverage-response-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: coverage-response-benchmark-analysis Use when you need to determine the minimum WGS coverage required for reliable exon/splice-graph prediction, or to characterize how prediction quality degrades at very low or very high depth. You only need a single-shot exon prediction at a fixed coverage rather than a depth-response characterization The input transcriptome is of unknown quality or single-tissue origin — prediction metrics may reflect transcriptome fragmentation rather than coverage effects No reference annotation exists to compute precision/recall against (the benchmark requires GFF3 ground truth, e.g. Ensembl release 91 GRCz10) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark how WGS sequencing depth affects exon-prediction precision and recall by running a coverage titration series (e.g. Seqtk subsampling in 10% increments) through the EXFI pipeline and tabulating precision/recall/F1 versus coverage, as done for the zebrafish simulation (k=25 bp, >90% by 16x, max 96.7% precision / 94.7% recall at 26-37x). genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Benchmark how WGS sequencing depth affects exon-prediction precision and recall by running a coverage titration series (e.g. Seqtk subsampling in 10% increments) through the EXFI pipeline and tabulating precision/recall/F1 versus coverage, as done for the zebrafish simulation (k=25 bp, >90% by 16x, max 96.7% precision / 94.7% recall at 26-37x).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single-shot exon prediction at a fixed coverage rather than a depth-response characterization The input transcriptome is of unknown quality or single-tissue origin — prediction metrics may reflect transcriptome fragmentation rather than coverage effects No reference annotation exists to compute precision/recall against (the benchmark requires GFF3 ground truth, e.g. Ensembl release 91 GRCz10)

skills.description: Use when running SMALR's SMsn protocol on native-vs-WGA PacBio SMRT data and you need to determine how many passes per molecule (covSM) are required before single-molecule methylation calls reach acceptable sensitivity/specificity.
skills.name: coverage-stratified-sensitivity-specificity-estimation
skills.search_text: coverage-stratified-sensitivity-specificity-estimation Use when running SMALR's SMsn protocol on native-vs-WGA PacBio SMRT data and you need to determine how many passes per molecule (covSM) are required before single-molecule methylation calls reach acceptable sensitivity/specificity. Long (10Kb+) sequencing library preps where each subread spans many distinct motif sites — use the SMp protocol instead, since pooling per molecule, not per-site stratification, is appropriate there Detection of modification types whose kinetic signatures extend into surrounding bases — the article states these require more sophisticated algorithms beyond this framework Mixed bacterial populations (clinical isolates, microbiome samples) — the study validated this on cultures of single bacterial strains only http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Stratifies single-molecule methylation calls (SMSN scores from SMALR) by per-molecule coverage (covSM) and estimates methylation-call sensitivity and specificity at each stratum against a known fully methylated motif landscape (e.g., 6mA at 5'-CTGCAG in E. coli O104:H4 C227-11). Establishes the coverage floor (covSM>=15) needed for accurate single-molecule, single-nucleotide detection. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: Stratifies single-molecule methylation calls (SMSN scores from SMALR) by per-molecule coverage (covSM) and estimates methylation-call sensitivity and specificity at each stratum against a known fully methylated motif landscape (e.g., 6mA at 5'-CTGCAG in E. coli O104:H4 C227-11). Establishes the coverage floor (covSM>=15) needed for accurate single-molecule, single-nucleotide detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Long (10Kb+) sequencing library preps where each subread spans many distinct motif sites — use the SMp protocol instead, since pooling per molecule, not per-site stratification, is appropriate there Detection of modification types whose kinetic signatures extend into surrounding bases — the article states these require more sophisticated algorithms beyond this framework Mixed bacterial populations (clinical isolates, microbiome samples) — the study validated this on cultures of single bacterial strains only

skills.description: Use when benchmarking site-level methylation callers on PacBio CCS/HiFi BAMs at matched low coverage, or when preparing 10x-subampled HG002 15/20/24 Kb, SD0651_P1, and CHM13 libraries for correlation analysis.
skills.name: coverage-subsampling-of-ccs-reads
skills.search_text: coverage-subsampling-of-ccs-reads Use when benchmarking site-level methylation callers on PacBio CCS/HiFi BAMs at matched low coverage, or when preparing 10x-subampled HG002 15/20/24 Kb, SD0651_P1, and CHM13 libraries for correlation analysis. The goal is read-level 5mCpG detection accuracy (e.g., the 0.90 accuracy / 0.97 AUC read-level benchmark), not site-level methylation frequency comparison across coverage conditions. The input data are not PacBio CCS/HiFi reads (e.g., nanopore or short-read BAMs); subsampling to 10x is meaningful only for the CCS-based ccsmeth workflow. The modification of interest is not symmetric 5mCpG methylation — the workflow cannot address hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Subsample PacBio HiFi/CCS read BAMs to a fixed depth (e.g., 10x) alongside full-depth CCS data (HG002 combined 71.0x) so that ccsmeth site-level 5mCpG methylation calls can be benchmarked against BS-seq and nanopore references as a function of coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Subsample PacBio HiFi/CCS read BAMs to a fixed depth (e.g., 10x) alongside full-depth CCS data (HG002 combined 71.0x) so that ccsmeth site-level 5mCpG methylation calls can be benchmarked against BS-seq and nanopore references as a function of coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is read-level 5mCpG detection accuracy (e.g., the 0.90 accuracy / 0.97 AUC read-level benchmark), not site-level methylation frequency comparison across coverage conditions. The input data are not PacBio CCS/HiFi reads (e.g., nanopore or short-read BAMs); subsampling to 10x is meaningful only for the CCS-based ccsmeth workflow. The modification of interest is not symmetric 5mCpG methylation — the workflow cannot address hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA.

skills.description: Use when you need to determine the minimum sequencing coverage required for reliable detection of a variant class (e.g., deletions, insertions, inversions) by sweeping coverage levels and comparing caller output to a simulated ground truth.
skills.name: coverage-sweep-benchmarking
skills.search_text: coverage-sweep-benchmarking Use when you need to determine the minimum sequencing coverage required for reliable detection of a variant class (e.g., deletions, insertions, inversions) by sweeping coverage levels and comparing caller output to a simulated ground truth. Input is real sequencing data with no ground-truth SV set — the sweep's recall/precision/F1 computation requires a simulated truth set Short-read (Illumina-style) data — the protocol is designed for long noisy PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads that span SV breakpoints Only a single coverage level is available — the skill's purpose is the coverage sweep trend, not a one-off SV call http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 A benchmarking protocol that simulates long noisy reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore error profiles) at a coverage sweep (10x, 20x, 30x, 40x) over mutated references and measures SV-calling recall, precision, and F1 per coverage level to determine the minimum coverage needed per SV type. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that simulates long noisy reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore error profiles) at a coverage sweep (10x, 20x, 30x, 40x) over mutated references and measures SV-calling recall, precision, and F1 per coverage level to determine the minimum coverage needed per SV type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real sequencing data with no ground-truth SV set — the sweep's recall/precision/F1 computation requires a simulated truth set Short-read (Illumina-style) data — the protocol is designed for long noisy PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads that span SV breakpoints Only a single coverage level is available — the skill's purpose is the coverage sweep trend, not a one-off SV call

skills.description: Use when benchmarking nanopore methylation callers against WGBS and you need to know if per-site correlation with bisulfite methylation frequencies holds as minimum read coverage increases.
skills.name: coverage-threshold-site-subsampling
skills.search_text: coverage-threshold-site-subsampling Use when benchmarking nanopore methylation callers against WGBS and you need to know if per-site correlation with bisulfite methylation frequencies holds as minimum read coverage increases. You only have per-read methylation calls and no aggregated per-site coverage/frequency BED tables — the threshold subsampling requires site-level coverage. Your comparison regions are not matched to WGBS measurements (e.g., no bisulfite data at the target loci), so no correlation can be computed at any threshold. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Subsamples intersected nanopore-vs-WGBS CpG methylation frequency tables at per-site coverage thresholds (1x, 5x, 10x, 15x, 20x) and computes Pearson correlations per tool to test whether nanopore-WGBS concordance is stable across coverage levels. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Subsamples intersected nanopore-vs-WGBS CpG methylation frequency tables at per-site coverage thresholds (1x, 5x, 10x, 15x, 20x) and computes Pearson correlations per tool to test whether nanopore-WGBS concordance is stable across coverage levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have per-read methylation calls and no aggregated per-site coverage/frequency BED tables — the threshold subsampling requires site-level coverage. Your comparison regions are not matched to WGBS measurements (e.g., no bisulfite data at the target loci), so no correlation can be computed at any threshold.

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample mutation status merged with survival/time-to-event group annotations and need to test whether a mutation is an independent prognostic factor after adjusting for other covariates.
skills.name: cox-proportional-hazards-modeling
skills.search_text: cox-proportional-hazards-modeling Use when you have per-sample mutation status merged with survival/time-to-event group annotations and need to test whether a mutation is an independent prognostic factor after adjusting for other covariates. Input is only a mutational signature abundance matrix (P/S matrices) without any survival outcome or group labels — use RNMF's samPerMutSigs/genePerMutSigs association tests instead Goal is de novo extraction of SBS/DBS/ID mutational signatures from VCF/MAF data — that is the RNMF denovoNMF workflow, not survival modeling Clinical data lack survival or time-to-event information; the article notes treatment methods, medication information and extended follow-up time are incomplete, so Cox modeling is not defensible without a survival outcome Fit a multivariate Cox proportional hazards model in R to test whether a molecular feature (e.g. TP53 hotspot R248Q status from an RNMF-style MAF file) remains an independent prognosticator for survival when modeled alongside survival group labels. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Fit a multivariate Cox proportional hazards model in R to test whether a molecular feature (e.g. TP53 hotspot R248Q status from an RNMF-style MAF file) remains an independent prognosticator for survival when modeled alongside survival group labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only a mutational signature abundance matrix (P/S matrices) without any survival outcome or group labels — use RNMF's samPerMutSigs/genePerMutSigs association tests instead Goal is de novo extraction of SBS/DBS/ID mutational signatures from VCF/MAF data — that is the RNMF denovoNMF workflow, not survival modeling Clinical data lack survival or time-to-event information; the article notes treatment methods, medication information and extended follow-up time are incomplete, so Cox modeling is not defensible without a survival outcome

skills.description: Use when you have a called DNV set (e.g. HAT output prepped with squirrel.py) and need the number of DNVs at CpG sites and their percentage as a call-quality metric.
skills.name: cpg-context-mutation-annotation
skills.search_text: cpg-context-mutation-annotation Use when you have a called DNV set (e.g. HAT output prepped with squirrel.py) and need the number of DNVs at CpG sites and their percentage as a call-quality metric. Your input is raw VCF trio output not yet filtered/run through the HAT de novo variant filter — annotate CpG only on final DNV call sets Your variants are INDELs or MNVs — annotateCpG extracts only SNVs, so CpG status will not be assigned for those variant types The genome build of your DNV coordinates does not match the CpG annotation file build (use cpg_b38.rda only for GRCh38/b38 coordinates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Annotate de novo variants (DNVs) from a HAT/HAT-FLEX call set with whether they occur at CpG sites using the acorn R package, yielding total counts and the percent of DNVs at CpG — a key quality metric for DNV call sets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775
skills.summary: Annotate de novo variants (DNVs) from a HAT/HAT-FLEX call set with whether they occur at CpG sites using the acorn R package, yielding total counts and the percent of DNVs at CpG — a key quality metric for DNV call sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is raw VCF trio output not yet filtered/run through the HAT de novo variant filter — annotate CpG only on final DNV call sets Your variants are INDELs or MNVs — annotateCpG extracts only SNVs, so CpG status will not be assigned for those variant types The genome build of your DNV coordinates does not match the CpG annotation file build (use cpg_b38.rda only for GRCh38/b38 coordinates)

skills.description: Use when comparing nanopore per-site methylation calls (augmented BED files from Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, METEORE) against WGBS methylation frequencies at CpG sites in targeted regions to check regional agreement and coverage stability.
skills.name: cpg-island-hypomethylation-visualization
skills.search_text: cpg-island-hypomethylation-visualization Use when comparing nanopore per-site methylation calls (augmented BED files from Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, METEORE) against WGBS methylation frequencies at CpG sites in targeted regions to check regional agreement and coverage stability. Input is per-read fast5 signal data rather than per-site aggregated methylation frequency tables — this skill operates on the augmented BED per-site outputs produced downstream Analysis goal is single-read methylation status or controlled mixture benchmarking rather than regional agreement with WGBS at CpG sites No matched WGBS methylation frequencies are available for the target regions, so no reference profile exists to compare against http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Visualize and validate CpG island hypomethylation by fitting LOESS smoothing curves of per-site methylation frequency versus genomic position for each nanopore methylation tool and WGBS across Cas9-targeted nCATS regions, and quantify where tool profiles deviate from the WGBS reference. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Visualize and validate CpG island hypomethylation by fitting LOESS smoothing curves of per-site methylation frequency versus genomic position for each nanopore methylation tool and WGBS across Cas9-targeted nCATS regions, and quantify where tool profiles deviate from the WGBS reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is per-read fast5 signal data rather than per-site aggregated methylation frequency tables — this skill operates on the augmented BED per-site outputs produced downstream Analysis goal is single-read methylation status or controlled mixture benchmarking rather than regional agreement with WGBS at CpG sites No matched WGBS methylation frequencies are available for the target regions, so no reference profile exists to compare against

skills.description: Use when per-site methylation frequencies from nanopore methylation callers (Nanopolish, Megalodon, Guppy, Tombo, DeepSignal, DeepMod, METEORE) must be compared against WGBS CpG frequencies to quantify agreement or sequence-context bias.
skills.name: cpg-methylation-frequency-comparison
skills.search_text: cpg-methylation-frequency-comparison Use when per-site methylation frequencies from nanopore methylation callers (Nanopolish, Megalodon, Guppy, Tombo, DeepSignal, DeepMod, METEORE) must be compared against WGBS CpG frequencies to quantify agreement or sequence-context bias. When you only have raw fast5 files and no methylation calls yet — methylation calling pipelines must be run first via METEORE Snakemake workflows When no matched WGBS or otherwise trusted ground-truth methylation data exists for the same sample — correlation/RMSE comparison and discrepancy ranking cannot be computed When analyzing non-CpG methylation (e.g., dam/dcm contexts) — this skill is specific to 5mC at CG dinucleotides http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Benchmark nanopore CpG methylation predictions against WGBS by matching per-site methylation frequencies from augmented BED outputs, computing agreement metrics (N, Pearson r, r^2, Spearman rho, RMSE) per tool, and ranking 8-mer sequence-context discrepancies to reveal AT-rich bias. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Benchmark nanopore CpG methylation predictions against WGBS by matching per-site methylation frequencies from augmented BED outputs, computing agreement metrics (N, Pearson r, r^2, Spearman rho, RMSE) per tool, and ranking 8-mer sequence-context discrepancies to reveal AT-rich bias.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only have raw fast5 files and no methylation calls yet — methylation calling pipelines must be run first via METEORE Snakemake workflows When no matched WGBS or otherwise trusted ground-truth methylation data exists for the same sample — correlation/RMSE comparison and discrepancy ranking cannot be computed When analyzing non-CpG methylation (e.g., dam/dcm contexts) — this skill is specific to 5mC at CG dinucleotides

skills.description: Use when you have per-site CpG methylation calls from nanopore reads (e.g., a DeepBAM or Dorado-modified BAM at a defined coverage such as 10x-30x) plus matched BS-seq frequency tracks, and need genome-wide methylation frequency profiles and BS-seq correlation coefficients.
skills.name: cpg-methylation-frequency-computation
skills.search_text: cpg-methylation-frequency-computation Use when you have per-site CpG methylation calls from nanopore reads (e.g., a DeepBAM or Dorado-modified BAM at a defined coverage such as 10x-30x) plus matched BS-seq frequency tracks, and need genome-wide methylation frequency profiles and BS-seq correlation coefficients. You only need single-molecule read-level methylation state classification (AUROC/F1 evaluation), not aggregated genome-wide frequency comparison No matched BS-seq methylation frequency tracks exist for the dataset, so correlation cannot be computed Input data is not CpG-motif nanopore R10.4 data (e.g., other methylation motifs or PacBio kinetics data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compute genome-wide CpG methylation frequency profiles from single-molecule nanopore methylation calls (e.g., DeepBAM or Dorado on R10.4 data) and quantify their fidelity against bisulfite sequencing (BS-seq) via Pearson correlation. This skill turns per-site modification calls into aggregate methylation frequencies suitable for benchmarking across human and plant datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Compute genome-wide CpG methylation frequency profiles from single-molecule nanopore methylation calls (e.g., DeepBAM or Dorado on R10.4 data) and quantify their fidelity against bisulfite sequencing (BS-seq) via Pearson correlation. This skill turns per-site modification calls into aggregate methylation frequencies suitable for benchmarking across human and plant datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need single-molecule read-level methylation state classification (AUROC/F1 evaluation), not aggregated genome-wide frequency comparison No matched BS-seq methylation frequency tracks exist for the dataset, so correlation cannot be computed Input data is not CpG-motif nanopore R10.4 data (e.g., other methylation motifs or PacBio kinetics data)

skills.description: Use when you have nanopolish eventalign output from MinION nanoHiMe-seq or plain nanopore reads and need per-read/per-site CpG methylation calls (mCG) robust at 10×–30× coverage without bisulfite conversion.
skills.name: cpg-methylation-likelihood-ratio-calling
skills.search_text: cpg-methylation-likelihood-ratio-calling Use when you have nanopolish eventalign output from MinION nanoHiMe-seq or plain nanopore reads and need per-read/per-site CpG methylation calls (mCG) robust at 10×–30× coverage without bisulfite conversion. Input is already bisulfite-converted (WGBS/BiSulfate) data — nanoHiMe calls methylation from nanopore signal events, not bisulfite read counts. You need joint detection of all modified-base combinations (5-hmC, 5-fC, 4-mC, GpC methylation) — no unified calling model for these exists yet per the authors. You only need 6mA-containing region calls — use nanoHiMe's '6mA' mode with a peak BED instead, since whole-genome mCG-style calling is slow and answers a different question. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Call per-CpG methylation states from nanopore signal alignments using nanoHiMe's hidden Markov model in mCG-calling mode, classifying each CpG by log-likelihood-ratio thresholds (+1.5 methylated, −1.5 unmethylated) to enable low-coverage CpG methylation profiling comparable to WGBS. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Call per-CpG methylation states from nanopore signal alignments using nanoHiMe's hidden Markov model in mCG-calling mode, classifying each CpG by log-likelihood-ratio thresholds (+1.5 methylated, −1.5 unmethylated) to enable low-coverage CpG methylation profiling comparable to WGBS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already bisulfite-converted (WGBS/BiSulfate) data — nanoHiMe calls methylation from nanopore signal events, not bisulfite read counts. You need joint detection of all modified-base combinations (5-hmC, 5-fC, 4-mC, GpC methylation) — no unified calling model for these exists yet per the authors. You only need 6mA-containing region calls — use nanoHiMe's '6mA' mode with a peak BED instead, since whole-genome mCG-style calling is slow and answers a different question.

skills.description: Use when calling single-molecule CpG methylation states from ONT R10.4 nanopore signal (POD5) with a BiLSTM model, or when Dorado's calls prove unstable across heterogeneous human/plant datasets.
skills.name: cpg-methylation-state-classification
skills.search_text: cpg-methylation-state-classification Use when calling single-molecule CpG methylation states from ONT R10.4 nanopore signal (POD5) with a BiLSTM model, or when Dorado's calls prove unstable across heterogeneous human/plant datasets. Calling modification types or contexts other than CpG methylation — DeepBAM is a CpG methylation caller. Data from chemistries other than R10.4 — the paper notes only a small number of tools (DeepMod2, Dorado) were compatible with R10.4 and DeepBAM's models are trained/evaluated on R10.4 human and plant datasets. Input is already a methylation-frequency table or BS-seq dataset — this skill classifies methylation from raw nanopore signal, not from existing frequency calls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 BiLSTM-based single-molecule CpG methylation calling for Oxford Nanopore R10.4 reads, as implemented in DeepBAM: parallel sequence- and signal-feature BiLSTM streams are fused in a combined BiLSTM to emit a softmax methylated/unmethylated probability per CpG (avg AUROC 98.47%). genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: BiLSTM-based single-molecule CpG methylation calling for Oxford Nanopore R10.4 reads, as implemented in DeepBAM: parallel sequence- and signal-feature BiLSTM streams are fused in a combined BiLSTM to emit a softmax methylated/unmethylated probability per CpG (avg AUROC 98.47%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling modification types or contexts other than CpG methylation — DeepBAM is a CpG methylation caller. Data from chemistries other than R10.4 — the paper notes only a small number of tools (DeepMod2, Dorado) were compatible with R10.4 and DeepBAM's models are trained/evaluated on R10.4 human and plant datasets. Input is already a methylation-frequency table or BS-seq dataset — this skill classifies methylation from raw nanopore signal, not from existing frequency calls.

skills.description: Use when constructing controlled methylation mixture datasets from nanopore reads and you need to pick well-covered, single-CpG genomic sites before partitioning reads into methylated/unmethylated pools.
skills.name: cpg-site-coverage-filtering
skills.search_text: cpg-site-coverage-filtering Use when constructing controlled methylation mixture datasets from nanopore reads and you need to pick well-covered, single-CpG genomic sites before partitioning reads into methylated/unmethylated pools. The goal is per-site methylation frequency reporting on naturally methylated genomes rather than constructing controlled benchmarking mixtures from methylated/unmethylated controls Sites of interest contain multiple CpG dinucleotides within the analysis window, so per-site assignments would be confounded Coverage is below 50x, making per-site methylation frequency estimates unreliable for benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Selects CpG sites suitable for controlled-methylation benchmarking by requiring a minimum per-site read coverage (>=50x, computed with samtools on Minimap2-aligned E. coli K12 nanopore BAMs) and retaining only sites with exactly one CpG dinucleotide within a 20 nt window, so that per-site methylation calls are unambiguous. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Selects CpG sites suitable for controlled-methylation benchmarking by requiring a minimum per-site read coverage (>=50x, computed with samtools on Minimap2-aligned E. coli K12 nanopore BAMs) and retaining only sites with exactly one CpG dinucleotide within a 20 nt window, so that per-site methylation calls are unambiguous.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-site methylation frequency reporting on naturally methylated genomes rather than constructing controlled benchmarking mixtures from methylated/unmethylated controls Sites of interest contain multiple CpG dinucleotides within the analysis window, so per-site assignments would be confounded Coverage is below 50x, making per-site methylation frequency estimates unreliable for benchmarking

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered DNV callset (e.g. from HAT on GIAB HG002 PacBio HiFi replicates) and need the percentage of DNVs at CpG sites as a call-quality metric or replicate-comparison statistic.
skills.name: cpg-site-fraction-calculation
skills.search_text: cpg-site-fraction-calculation Use when you have a filtered DNV callset (e.g. from HAT on GIAB HG002 PacBio HiFi replicates) and need the percentage of DNVs at CpG sites as a call-quality metric or replicate-comparison statistic. The callset contains only INDELs or MNVs — annotateCpG extracts only SNVs, so CpG fractions would be undefined or misleading The reference genome build is not b38 and no matching pre-computed CpG rda file is available Variants are already annotated with CpG status by another tool and you only need per-sample summaries rather than re-annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Computes the fraction of de novo variant (DNV) SNVs that occur at CpG sites, a standard DNV call-quality metric in the HAT workflow, using the acorn R package's annotateCpG function against a pre-computed CpG annotation file (e.g. cpg_b38.rda). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775
skills.summary: Computes the fraction of de novo variant (DNV) SNVs that occur at CpG sites, a standard DNV call-quality metric in the HAT workflow, using the acorn R package's annotateCpG function against a pre-computed CpG annotation file (e.g. cpg_b38.rda).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The callset contains only INDELs or MNVs — annotateCpG extracts only SNVs, so CpG fractions would be undefined or misleading The reference genome build is not b38 and no matching pre-computed CpG rda file is available Variants are already annotated with CpG status by another tool and you only need per-sample summaries rather than re-annotation

skills.description: Use when building a scaffolding graph from Illumina mate-pair or long reads without a base-level aligner, or when implementing/porting Fast-SG's unique-k-mer index, hit-vector scoring, and pair-rescue logic in C++.
skills.name: cpp-kmer-index-implementation
skills.search_text: cpp-kmer-index-implementation Use when building a scaffolding graph from Illumina mate-pair or long reads without a base-level aligner, or when implementing/porting Fast-SG's unique-k-mer index, hit-vector scoring, and pair-rescue logic in C++. When base-level alignment identity, CIGAR strings, or per-base mismatches are required — the index only reports read locations/scoring, not alignments When gap-size estimation from long-range mate-pair technologies (10X Genomics, DOVETAIL genomics) is the goal — insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size and pair orientation may be unknown For k-mer sizes outside the supported 12-256 range, or single-contig-free inputs with no reference contigs to index http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements Fast-SG's alignment-free C++ k-mer index pipeline: KMC3 counting over contigs, a BBHash minimal perfect hash wrapped in a quasi_dictionary probabilistic membership structure, ntHash rolling-hash look-ups to fill per-read hit vectors, and windowed scoring with pair rescue to emit scaffolding links in SAM format. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Implements Fast-SG's alignment-free C++ k-mer index pipeline: KMC3 counting over contigs, a BBHash minimal perfect hash wrapped in a quasi_dictionary probabilistic membership structure, ntHash rolling-hash look-ups to fill per-read hit vectors, and windowed scoring with pair rescue to emit scaffolding links in SAM format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When base-level alignment identity, CIGAR strings, or per-base mismatches are required — the index only reports read locations/scoring, not alignments When gap-size estimation from long-range mate-pair technologies (10X Genomics, DOVETAIL genomics) is the goal — insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size and pair orientation may be unknown For k-mer sizes outside the supported 12-256 range, or single-contig-free inputs with no reference contigs to index

skills.description: Use when benchmarking runtime, peak memory (GB), thread count, and CPU hours of VolcanoSV-asm or alternative assemblers (hifiasm, Flye) on HG002 HiFi/CLR/ONT WGS BAMs to populate a resource_usage table.
skills.name: cpu-hour-walltime-measurement
skills.search_text: cpu-hour-walltime-measurement Use when benchmarking runtime, peak memory (GB), thread count, and CPU hours of VolcanoSV-asm or alternative assemblers (hifiasm, Flye) on HG002 HiFi/CLR/ONT WGS BAMs to populate a resource_usage table. The goal is SV-calling accuracy evaluation rather than resource profiling — that requires Truvari benchmarking (p=0.5, P=0.5, r=500, O=0.01) against the GIAB gold standard, not walltime/memory capture Running the single-chromosome test example on chr10 from Zenodo — its cost is not representative of whole-genome resource usage The sample is CHM13 or another homozygous/single-haploid source, for which the phased diploid assembly component is unsuitable and its resource profile is not the published benchmark Protocol for reproducing the VolcanoSV-asm computational resource benchmark: measuring wall-clock runtime, peak memory, ncpu, and derived CPU hours (walltime × ncpu) for per-chromosome diploid assembly on HG002 long-read BAMs, and comparing against alternative pipelines (hifiasm for HiFi; Flye+HapDup for CLR/ONT). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Protocol for reproducing the VolcanoSV-asm computational resource benchmark: measuring wall-clock runtime, peak memory, ncpu, and derived CPU hours (walltime × ncpu) for per-chromosome diploid assembly on HG002 long-read BAMs, and comparing against alternative pipelines (hifiasm for HiFi; Flye+HapDup for CLR/ONT).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is SV-calling accuracy evaluation rather than resource profiling — that requires Truvari benchmarking (p=0.5, P=0.5, r=500, O=0.01) against the GIAB gold standard, not walltime/memory capture Running the single-chromosome test example on chr10 from Zenodo — its cost is not representative of whole-genome resource usage The sample is CHM13 or another homozygous/single-haploid source, for which the phased diploid assembly component is unsuitable and its resource profile is not the published benchmark

skills.description: Use when comparing downstream annotation quality of Visium HD cell representations (e.g. bin2cell reconstructed cells versus 8 μm SpaceRanger bins) on human colorectal cancer data, especially for CellTypist confidence, gene coverage, and CMS subtype prediction.
skills.name: crc-cms-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: crc-cms-subtype-classification Use when comparing downstream annotation quality of Visium HD cell representations (e.g. bin2cell reconstructed cells versus 8 μm SpaceRanger bins) on human colorectal cancer data, especially for CellTypist confidence, gene coverage, and CMS subtype prediction. Data are not human colorectal cancer Visium HD or an equivalent morphology-image-paired high-resolution spatial dataset, so CMS2 subtype predictions are not meaningful. The goal is cell reconstruction itself (destripe/segmentation/bin_to_cell) rather than downstream annotation comparison against 8 μm bins. Only a single cell representation is available with no 8 μm comparator, so the confidence/coverage/CMS2 comparison cannot be made. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate Visium HD human colorectal cancer representations (bin2cell reconstructed cells vs default 8 μm bins) with CellTypist following the notebooks/destripe_celltypist.ipynb demo, then compare prediction confidence, per-cell gene coverage, and consensus molecular subtype (CMS2) calls to judge whether reconstructed cells outperform 8 μm bins downstream. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546
skills.summary: Annotate Visium HD human colorectal cancer representations (bin2cell reconstructed cells vs default 8 μm bins) with CellTypist following the notebooks/destripe_celltypist.ipynb demo, then compare prediction confidence, per-cell gene coverage, and consensus molecular subtype (CMS2) calls to judge whether reconstructed cells outperform 8 μm bins downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not human colorectal cancer Visium HD or an equivalent morphology-image-paired high-resolution spatial dataset, so CMS2 subtype predictions are not meaningful. The goal is cell reconstruction itself (destripe/segmentation/bin_to_cell) rather than downstream annotation comparison against 8 μm bins. Only a single cell representation is available with no 8 μm comparator, so the confidence/coverage/CMS2 comparison cannot be made.

skills.description: Use when CRAQ has produced locER_out/out_final.CRE.bed and strER_out/out_final.CSE.bed breakpoint files for a draft assembly and you need normalized error counts (Nw) converted into R-AQI/S-AQI scores with quality-class labels.
skills.name: cre-cse-error-tallying
skills.search_text: cre-cse-error-tallying Use when CRAQ has produced locER_out/out_final.CRE.bed and strER_out/out_final.CSE.bed breakpoint files for a draft assembly and you need normalized error counts (Nw) converted into R-AQI/S-AQI scores with quality-class labels. The input is still raw read alignments or filtered BAM files — mapping, MAPQ filtering (-F 1796 -q 20), and CRE/CSE breakpoint calling must happen first; this skill consumes the resulting BED files. Regions identified as heterozygous (clipping ratio within h = 0.4–0.6, i.e. CRHs/CSHs) rather than error breakpoints — applying the tally to unfiltered heterozygous loci conflates haplotype variation with misassembly. Polyploid genomes, where CRAQ's evaluation accuracy has not been benchmarked. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tallies Clip-based Regional Errors (CREs) and Clip-based Structural Errors (CSEs) from CRAQ breakpoint BED files and transforms the harmonic-normalized error counts into R-AQI and S-AQI assembly quality indexes that classify genome assemblies into reference/high/draft/low quality classes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Tallies Clip-based Regional Errors (CREs) and Clip-based Structural Errors (CSEs) from CRAQ breakpoint BED files and transforms the harmonic-normalized error counts into R-AQI and S-AQI assembly quality indexes that classify genome assemblies into reference/high/draft/low quality classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is still raw read alignments or filtered BAM files — mapping, MAPQ filtering (-F 1796 -q 20), and CRE/CSE breakpoint calling must happen first; this skill consumes the resulting BED files. Regions identified as heterozygous (clipping ratio within h = 0.4–0.6, i.e. CRHs/CSHs) rather than error breakpoints — applying the tally to unfiltered heterozygous loci conflates haplotype variation with misassembly. Polyploid genomes, where CRAQ's evaluation accuracy has not been benchmarked.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a SAM-with-MD-tag output from any long-read aligner can replace minimap2 in a streamed HLAminer.pl pipeline, or when validating aligner-agnostic concordance of HLA allele-group predictions on WGS nanopore data.
skills.name: cross-aligner-hla-prediction-concordance-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-aligner-hla-prediction-concordance-comparison Use when evaluating whether a SAM-with-MD-tag output from any long-read aligner can replace minimap2 in a streamed HLAminer.pl pipeline, or when validating aligner-agnostic concordance of HLA allele-group predictions on WGS nanopore data. The input is short-read (Illumina-sized) data better suited to HPTASR targeted assembly rather than streamed long-read SAM alignments. The alternative aligner cannot emit SAM with MD tags, which the streamed HPRA mode relies on. The sample lacks clinically confirmed HLA types or a minimap2 baseline, so concordance cannot be judged. http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 Tests whether HLAminer v1.4's streaming HPRA protocol is aligner-agnostic by substituting a non-minimap2 SAM-producing long-read aligner (with MD tags) in the piped command and comparing predicted HLA allele groups against the minimap2 baseline and clinically confirmed NA19240 types. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Tests whether HLAminer v1.4's streaming HPRA protocol is aligner-agnostic by substituting a non-minimap2 SAM-producing long-read aligner (with MD tags) in the piped command and comparing predicted HLA allele groups against the minimap2 baseline and clinically confirmed NA19240 types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read (Illumina-sized) data better suited to HPTASR targeted assembly rather than streamed long-read SAM alignments. The alternative aligner cannot emit SAM with MD tags, which the streamed HPRA mode relies on. The sample lacks clinically confirmed HLA types or a minimap2 baseline, so concordance cannot be judged.

skills.description: Use when comparing contiguity and phasing quality of diploid genome assemblies produced by multiple long-read assemblers on the same Nanopore R9/R10 or PacBio CLR datasets.
skills.name: cross-assembler-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-assembler-benchmarking Use when comparing contiguity and phasing quality of diploid genome assemblies produced by multiple long-read assemblers on the same Nanopore R9/R10 or PacBio CLR datasets. Evaluating assemblers on PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex reads — the paper reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on Nanopore duplex and PacBio HiFi reads, so benchmarking conclusions do not transfer Single-haploid (non-diploid) genome assembly comparisons where phase block NG50 and Hamming error phasing metrics are not meaningful Benchmarking against trio-binning pipelines under their native settings — note trio-binning methods require additional parental reads that PECAT does not use http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark PECAT against other diploid assembly pipelines (Canu+purge_dups, FALCON-Unzip, Flye+HapDup, Shasta, NECAT) on seven diploid long-read datasets using NG50, Merqury phase block NG50, Hamming error, BUSCO and Pomoxis metrics. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Benchmark PECAT against other diploid assembly pipelines (Canu+purge_dups, FALCON-Unzip, Flye+HapDup, Shasta, NECAT) on seven diploid long-read datasets using NG50, Merqury phase block NG50, Hamming error, BUSCO and Pomoxis metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating assemblers on PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex reads — the paper reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on Nanopore duplex and PacBio HiFi reads, so benchmarking conclusions do not transfer Single-haploid (non-diploid) genome assembly comparisons where phase block NG50 and Hamming error phasing metrics are not meaningful Benchmarking against trio-binning pipelines under their native settings — note trio-binning methods require additional parental reads that PECAT does not use

skills.description: Use when you have a merged (e.g. MeGAMerge) assembly and one or more individual assembler contig FASTAs for the same metagenomic data and need to quantify gene-count and coding-density improvements.
skills.name: cross-assembly-gene-count-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-assembly-gene-count-comparison Use when you have a merged (e.g. MeGAMerge) assembly and one or more individual assembler contig FASTAs for the same metagenomic data and need to quantify gene-count and coding-density improvements. When assemblies have not been filtered to a common contig-size cutoff — comparing gene counts over unfiltered contig sets (<2 kb included) conflates merging gains with retained error-prone small contigs When the goal is a general assembly-quality metric comparison (N50, total assembly size), which the paper describes as 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' — this skill targets gene prediction specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compares predicted gene counts and coding density across individual metagenomic assemblies versus their MeGAMerge merged assembly using Prodigal 2.6 in metagenomic mode, to quantify whether contig merging yields more predicted genes at microbial-plausible coding density. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Compares predicted gene counts and coding density across individual metagenomic assemblies versus their MeGAMerge merged assembly using Prodigal 2.6 in metagenomic mode, to quantify whether contig merging yields more predicted genes at microbial-plausible coding density.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When assemblies have not been filtered to a common contig-size cutoff — comparing gene counts over unfiltered contig sets (<2 kb included) conflates merging gains with retained error-prone small contigs When the goal is a general assembly-quality metric comparison (N50, total assembly size), which the paper describes as 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' — this skill targets gene prediction specifically

skills.description: Use when two or more basecallers must be compared on the same raw FAST5 datasets and the goal is a per-error-type (insertion/deletion/mismatch) read-accuracy profile across species or datasets.
skills.name: cross-basecaller-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-basecaller-accuracy-comparison Use when two or more basecallers must be compared on the same raw FAST5 datasets and the goal is a per-error-type (insertion/deletion/mismatch) read-accuracy profile across species or datasets. When the comparison target is assembly or consensus accuracy rather than per-read error profiles — that analysis used Minimap2/Miniasm plus 10 rounds of Racon polishing, a different workflow When only overall read-level accuracy identity scores are needed and per-error-type decomposition (insertion vs deletion vs mismatch) is not required When reads cannot be aligned to a common reference (e.g. no reference genome available), since error decomposition depends on CIGAR/MD strings http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Compares read-level accuracy of nanopore basecallers (e.g. Chiron with beam-search decoding versus ONT Albacore v2.0.1) by aligning each basecaller's FASTQ output to a common reference with graphmap and decomposing errors into per-read insertion, deletion, and mismatch rates. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: Compares read-level accuracy of nanopore basecallers (e.g. Chiron with beam-search decoding versus ONT Albacore v2.0.1) by aligning each basecaller's FASTQ output to a common reference with graphmap and decomposing errors into per-read insertion, deletion, and mismatch rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison target is assembly or consensus accuracy rather than per-read error profiles — that analysis used Minimap2/Miniasm plus 10 rounds of Racon polishing, a different workflow When only overall read-level accuracy identity scores are needed and per-error-type decomposition (insertion vs deletion vs mismatch) is not required When reads cannot be aligned to a common reference (e.g. no reference genome available), since error decomposition depends on CIGAR/MD strings

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic binners across multi-sample short-read projects (e.g. human gut, dog gut, ocean, soil) and you need per-binner high-quality bin counts plus percentage improvement over a baseline binner.
skills.name: cross-binner-percentage-gain-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-binner-percentage-gain-analysis Use when benchmarking metagenomic binners across multi-sample short-read projects (e.g. human gut, dog gut, ocean, soil) and you need per-binner high-quality bin counts plus percentage improvement over a baseline binner. Input is a single-sample binning task — the multi_easy_bin multi-sample workflow and its gain figures (82/129/109/101-sample projects) do not transfer to single_easy_bin runs The goal is long-read binning benchmarking — SemiBin2's long-read advantage (13.1-26.3% more high-quality genomes via ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering) is a separate finding from these short-read percentage gains You lack CheckM and GUNC — without completeness/contamination/chimerism assessment you cannot define high-quality bins and the comparison is meaningless Quantifies how many more high-quality metagenomic bins one binner (e.g. SemiBin2) reconstructs than competitors (SemiBin1, VAMB) by running all binners on identical contig+BAM inputs, classifying bins with CheckM/GUNC, and computing percentage gains with Wilcoxon signed-rank significance testing. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209
skills.summary: Quantifies how many more high-quality metagenomic bins one binner (e.g. SemiBin2) reconstructs than competitors (SemiBin1, VAMB) by running all binners on identical contig+BAM inputs, classifying bins with CheckM/GUNC, and computing percentage gains with Wilcoxon signed-rank significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-sample binning task — the multi_easy_bin multi-sample workflow and its gain figures (82/129/109/101-sample projects) do not transfer to single_easy_bin runs The goal is long-read binning benchmarking — SemiBin2's long-read advantage (13.1-26.3% more high-quality genomes via ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering) is a separate finding from these short-read percentage gains You lack CheckM and GUNC — without completeness/contamination/chimerism assessment you cannot define high-quality bins and the comparison is meaningless

skills.description: Use when a variant catalog (e.g., dbDSM pathogenic mutations, 1000 Genomes normals with AF 0.1–0.9) is in hg38 but downstream annotation and scoring tools (ANNOVAR ensGene hg19, hg19_spidex/SPANR) require hg19 coordinates.
skills.name: cross-build-variant-liftover
skills.search_text: cross-build-variant-liftover Use when a variant catalog (e.g., dbDSM pathogenic mutations, 1000 Genomes normals with AF 0.1–0.9) is in hg38 but downstream annotation and scoring tools (ANNOVAR ensGene hg19, hg19_spidex/SPANR) require hg19 coordinates. The variant set is already in hg19 coordinates and directly compatible with hg19 SPIDEX/ensGene resources — liftover would only introduce coordinate drift. The goal is ΔΨ prediction for variants lacking SPANR/SPIDEX scores or lying outside the splice-proximal window — the joined benchmark table cannot be assembled for them. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Lift synonymous variant coordinates from hg38 to hg19 with CrossMap against an indexed UCSC hg19 reference so the variants can be joined to hg19-locked resources (ANNOVAR ensGene, SPANR/SPIDEX ΔΨ scores) used to compile the SynonMut-complete and SynonMut-psi benchmark tables for PredPSI-SVR evaluation. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Lift synonymous variant coordinates from hg38 to hg19 with CrossMap against an indexed UCSC hg19 reference so the variants can be joined to hg19-locked resources (ANNOVAR ensGene, SPANR/SPIDEX ΔΨ scores) used to compile the SynonMut-complete and SynonMut-psi benchmark tables for PredPSI-SVR evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant set is already in hg19 coordinates and directly compatible with hg19 SPIDEX/ensGene resources — liftover would only introduce coordinate drift. The goal is ΔΨ prediction for variants lacking SPANR/SPIDEX scores or lying outside the splice-proximal window — the joined benchmark table cannot be assembled for them.

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark runtime, CPU hours, or memory of a variant/TE caller against competitors on identical BAM inputs, e.g. validating that a caller is 'fast and CPU light' on 60x long-read genomes.
skills.name: cross-caller-runtime-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-caller-runtime-comparison Use when you need to benchmark runtime, CPU hours, or memory of a variant/TE caller against competitors on identical BAM inputs, e.g. validating that a caller is 'fast and CPU light' on 60x long-read genomes. Input is raw fastq reads not yet aligned — align with minimap2 to BAM first, since all callers in this benchmark consume BAM/CRAM The goal is accuracy/precision-recall benchmarking rather than computational cost — use the truth-set comparison workflow with testbamTRUTH.txt instead Short-read (Illumina) data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data such as PacBio or ONT http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A benchmarking skill for comparing wall-clock runtime, CPU hours, and peak memory of a fast tool (sTELLeR) against slower competitive callers (TLDR, xTEA) on identical long-read BAM inputs, here the GIAB Ashkenazim trio PacBio and ONT genomes. It demonstrates how to quantify computational efficiency claims such as '5-48x faster with <2% of the CPU hours'. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing wall-clock runtime, CPU hours, and peak memory of a fast tool (sTELLeR) against slower competitive callers (TLDR, xTEA) on identical long-read BAM inputs, here the GIAB Ashkenazim trio PacBio and ONT genomes. It demonstrates how to quantify computational efficiency claims such as '5-48x faster with <2% of the CPU hours'.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw fastq reads not yet aligned — align with minimap2 to BAM first, since all callers in this benchmark consume BAM/CRAM The goal is accuracy/precision-recall benchmarking rather than computational cost — use the truth-set comparison workflow with testbamTRUTH.txt instead Short-read (Illumina) data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data such as PacBio or ONT

skills.description: Use when comparing SV callsets from multiple assembly-based callers on the same assembly to quantify reference-induced false discoveries, e.g., CHM13 assemblies called against T2T-CHM13 vs GRCh38.
skills.name: cross-caller-sv-callset-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-caller-sv-callset-comparison Use when comparing SV callsets from multiple assembly-based callers on the same assembly to quantify reference-induced false discoveries, e.g., CHM13 assemblies called against T2T-CHM13 vs GRCh38. Evaluating alignment-based read-mapping SV callers against a truth set (e.g., GIAB HG002 gold standard with Truvari) — use a recall/precision benchmark instead The sample is haplotype-diverse and haplotype phasing is needed; CHM13 derives from a single homozygous complete hydatidiform mole, so VolcanoSV-asm phasing is unsuitable here and the pipeline is run only for variant calling Dipcall is being considered for complex SV (TRA/DUP/INV) detection — it was excluded because it was not designed to detect complex SVs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark false discovery rates of assembly-based SV callers (VolcanoSV-vc, PAV, SVIM-asm, Dipcall) by calling SVs from the same CHM13 diploid assembly against T2T-CHM13 versus GRCh38 references and computing the ratio of call counts, annotating false discoveries against centromere/telomere BED tracks. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Benchmark false discovery rates of assembly-based SV callers (VolcanoSV-vc, PAV, SVIM-asm, Dipcall) by calling SVs from the same CHM13 diploid assembly against T2T-CHM13 versus GRCh38 references and computing the ratio of call counts, annotating false discoveries against centromere/telomere BED tracks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating alignment-based read-mapping SV callers against a truth set (e.g., GIAB HG002 gold standard with Truvari) — use a recall/precision benchmark instead The sample is haplotype-diverse and haplotype phasing is needed; CHM13 derives from a single homozygous complete hydatidiform mole, so VolcanoSV-asm phasing is unsuitable here and the pipeline is run only for variant calling Dipcall is being considered for complex SV (TRA/DUP/INV) detection — it was excluded because it was not designed to detect complex SVs
