skills.summary: Benchmark a long-read single-cell workflow (e.g. scywalker) against short-read quantification by computing Pearson correlations of per-cell and gene-per-cell UMI count matrices, plus wall-clock runtime, against competing long-read pipelines such as BLAZE-FLAMES and ONT wf-single-cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched short-read (Cell Ranger) data exist for the sample, so no short-read ground-truth matrix is available for correlation The goal is cell type assignment or isoform discovery rather than quantifying cell-barcode/gene-count accuracy against another platform The pipelines being compared were run on different hardware or core counts, making runtime comparison invalid

skills.description: Use when two sequencing platforms have profiled the identical single-cell cDNA samples and you need to demonstrate concordance of cell-barcode-level or gene-level UMI count matrices via Pearson correlation.
skills.name: cross-platform-gene-count-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-platform-gene-count-comparison Use when two sequencing platforms have profiled the identical single-cell cDNA samples and you need to demonstrate concordance of cell-barcode-level or gene-level UMI count matrices via Pearson correlation. Input samples were not split and run on both platforms — comparing different cDNA samples would confound platform effects with sample effects The goal is isoform-level concordance rather than gene/UMI-level counts; the matrices compared here aggregate UMI counts, not isoform classifications Count matrices are not matched on shared cell barcodes or gene identifiers between platforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify agreement between HIT-scISOseq (PacBio Sequel II CCS) and Illumina short-read NGS measurements of the same single-cell 10x Genomics corneal limbal cDNA samples by computing Pearson correlations of UMI counts aggregated per cell barcode, per gene, and between biological replicates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Quantify agreement between HIT-scISOseq (PacBio Sequel II CCS) and Illumina short-read NGS measurements of the same single-cell 10x Genomics corneal limbal cDNA samples by computing Pearson correlations of UMI counts aggregated per cell barcode, per gene, and between biological replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples were not split and run on both platforms — comparing different cDNA samples would confound platform effects with sample effects The goal is isoform-level concordance rather than gene/UMI-level counts; the matrices compared here aggregate UMI counts, not isoform classifications Count matrices are not matched on shared cell barcodes or gene identifiers between platforms

skills.description: Use when a long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) single-cell count matrix must be validated against a short-read (Illumina Cell Ranger) matrix from the same sample, e.g. checking cellBC/UMI-assigned gene counts agree across platforms before isoform-level analyses.
skills.name: cross-platform-gene-count-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-platform-gene-count-correlation-analysis Use when a long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) single-cell count matrix must be validated against a short-read (Illumina Cell Ranger) matrix from the same sample, e.g. checking cellBC/UMI-assigned gene counts agree across platforms before isoform-level analyses. Input is raw Nanopore/Illumina reads or SAM/BAM records rather than an already-generated gene x cellBC count matrix (use the Sicelore matrix-generation workflow first) The goal is isoform, SNP/RNA-editing, or fusion calling rather than validating gene-count agreement between platforms The Nanopore and Illumina data come from different samples, so shared cell barcodes do not represent the same cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks Nanopore long-read single-cell gene/UMI count matrices (Sicelore PREFIX_genematrix.txt) against same-sample Illumina Cell Ranger matrices by intersecting cell barcodes, computing per-cell gene/UMI totals and per-gene/per-cell Pearson correlations, to verify the long-read data faithfully represent the 10x Genomics transcriptome despite additional full-length PCR and library preparation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Benchmarks Nanopore long-read single-cell gene/UMI count matrices (Sicelore PREFIX_genematrix.txt) against same-sample Illumina Cell Ranger matrices by intersecting cell barcodes, computing per-cell gene/UMI totals and per-gene/per-cell Pearson correlations, to verify the long-read data faithfully represent the 10x Genomics transcriptome despite additional full-length PCR and library preparation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Nanopore/Illumina reads or SAM/BAM records rather than an already-generated gene x cellBC count matrix (use the Sicelore matrix-generation workflow first) The goal is isoform, SNP/RNA-editing, or fusion calling rather than validating gene-count agreement between platforms The Nanopore and Illumina data come from different samples, so shared cell barcodes do not represent the same cells

skills.description: Use when you have long-read single-cell (10x) FASTQs processed with scywalker plus a matched short-read count matrix for the same sample, and you need to quantify cross-platform concordance at cell and per-cell gene-count level.
skills.name: cross-platform-gene-count-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-platform-gene-count-correlation-analysis Use when you have long-read single-cell (10x) FASTQs processed with scywalker plus a matched short-read count matrix for the same sample, and you need to quantify cross-platform concordance at cell and per-cell gene-count level. The data are short-read-only single-cell counts with no long-read FASTQs, so there is no scywalker PacBio run to compare against. You need isoform-level (strict >= 90% transcript coverage) concordance rather than cell-level and per-cell gene-count concordance; this skill validates gene quantification only. The genome contains organelles and scywalker_makerefdir was run without '-organelles', since the IsoQuant-based code can hang or crash on organelle data, invalidating the comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark long-read single-cell scywalker quantification (e.g. PacBio HiFi with '-preset pacbio') against matched short-read quantification by matching cell barcodes and computing Pearson correlations of total counts per cell and gene counts per cell, following the HG002 10x lymphoblastoid validation (R = 0.986 cell level, R = 0.886 per-cell gene counts). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read single-cell scywalker quantification (e.g. PacBio HiFi with '-preset pacbio') against matched short-read quantification by matching cell barcodes and computing Pearson correlations of total counts per cell and gene counts per cell, following the HG002 10x lymphoblastoid validation (R = 0.986 cell level, R = 0.886 per-cell gene counts).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are short-read-only single-cell counts with no long-read FASTQs, so there is no scywalker PacBio run to compare against. You need isoform-level (strict >= 90% transcript coverage) concordance rather than cell-level and per-cell gene-count concordance; this skill validates gene quantification only. The genome contains organelles and scywalker_makerefdir was run without '-organelles', since the IsoQuant-based code can hang or crash on organelle data, invalidating the comparison.

skills.description: Use when validating PacBio CCS 5mCpG calls against bisulfite or nanopore ground truth — e.g. HG002/SD0651_P1/CHM13 WGS with matching BS-seq or nanopore methylation calls available.
skills.name: cross-platform-methylation-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-platform-methylation-comparison Use when validating PacBio CCS 5mCpG calls against bisulfite or nanopore ground truth — e.g. HG002/SD0651_P1/CHM13 WGS with matching BS-seq or nanopore methylation calls available. The target modification is not 5mCpG — the method cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA The input is read-level accuracy assessment rather than site-level methylation frequency comparison No matched BS-seq or nanopore methylation calls exist for the sample, so no orthogonal benchmark can be intersected http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Benchmark ccsmeth-derived site-level CpG methylation frequencies from PacBio HiFi/CCS reads against orthogonal BS-seq and nanopore methylation calls by intersecting matched CpG sites and computing Pearson correlation coefficients per dataset and coverage condition. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Benchmark ccsmeth-derived site-level CpG methylation frequencies from PacBio HiFi/CCS reads against orthogonal BS-seq and nanopore methylation calls by intersecting matched CpG sites and computing Pearson correlation coefficients per dataset and coverage condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target modification is not 5mCpG — the method cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA The input is read-level accuracy assessment rather than site-level methylation frequency comparison No matched BS-seq or nanopore methylation calls exist for the sample, so no orthogonal benchmark can be intersected

skills.description: Use when genome-wide DNA methylation levels estimated from single-molecule sequencing (e.g., ONT mCaller motif-site calls) must be benchmarked against an orthogonal quantitative assay such as MethylFlash ELISA across multiple species or samples.
skills.name: cross-platform-methylation-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-platform-methylation-correlation-analysis Use when genome-wide DNA methylation levels estimated from single-molecule sequencing (e.g., ONT mCaller motif-site calls) must be benchmarked against an orthogonal quantitative assay such as MethylFlash ELISA across multiple species or samples. Comparing per-site methylation calls across platforms rather than genome-wide aggregate levels — the article treats non-motif site discrepancies as method-specific false positives reflecting different noise sources Species or motifs for which the nanopore model was not trained — mCaller notably failed at one S. aureus motif and cannot confidently assign motifs in the two Dikarya fungi (C. neoformans, S. cerevisiae) Estimating m5C or other modifications — PacBio-based validation here addresses m6A and m4C; m5C is better distinguished in nanopore data but this ELISA correlation targets m6A only http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Validates nanopore-derived genome-wide percent m6A estimates by correlating them with orthogonal experimental methylation measurements (MethylFlash ELISA) across microbial reference species, reproducing the Spearman correlation of the McIntyre et al. 2019 Nature Communications study. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Validates nanopore-derived genome-wide percent m6A estimates by correlating them with orthogonal experimental methylation measurements (MethylFlash ELISA) across microbial reference species, reproducing the Spearman correlation of the McIntyre et al. 2019 Nature Communications study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing per-site methylation calls across platforms rather than genome-wide aggregate levels — the article treats non-motif site discrepancies as method-specific false positives reflecting different noise sources Species or motifs for which the nanopore model was not trained — mCaller notably failed at one S. aureus motif and cannot confidently assign motifs in the two Dikarya fungi (C. neoformans, S. cerevisiae) Estimating m5C or other modifications — PacBio-based validation here addresses m6A and m4C; m5C is better distinguished in nanopore data but this ELISA correlation targets m6A only

skills.description: Use when nanopore R10.4 methylation calls must be benchmarked against BS-seq, PacBio CCS, or R9.4 reference methylation profiles, or when allele-specific methylation patterns need cross-platform validation.
skills.name: cross-platform-methylation-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-platform-methylation-correlation-analysis Use when nanopore R10.4 methylation calls must be benchmarked against BS-seq, PacBio CCS, or R9.4 reference methylation profiles, or when allele-specific methylation patterns need cross-platform validation. Data are not CpG methylation calls from ONT R10.4 nanopore reads — DeepBAM's model is trained for CpG motif on R10.4 and only a few tools (DeepMod2, Dorado) support R10.4, so earlier pore chemistries or other motifs need different callers No orthogonal benchmark (BS-seq, CCS, or R9.4 methylation profiles) exists to correlate against — the validation framework has nothing to compare to Reads are unphased and the goal is allele-specific methylation — haplotype aggregation and allelic DMR detection require haplotype-tagged reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Validates nanopore CpG methylation calls by correlating whole-genome and haplotype-specific methylation frequencies against orthogonal benchmarks (BS-seq, PacBio CCS, R9.4 nanopore), then quantifying concordance of downstream differential methylation regions. Grounded in DeepBAM, which achieved >0.95 correlations with BS-seq on four of five datasets and 47,282 allelic DMRs on phased HG002 reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Validates nanopore CpG methylation calls by correlating whole-genome and haplotype-specific methylation frequencies against orthogonal benchmarks (BS-seq, PacBio CCS, R9.4 nanopore), then quantifying concordance of downstream differential methylation regions. Grounded in DeepBAM, which achieved >0.95 correlations with BS-seq on four of five datasets and 47,282 allelic DMRs on phased HG002 reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not CpG methylation calls from ONT R10.4 nanopore reads — DeepBAM's model is trained for CpG motif on R10.4 and only a few tools (DeepMod2, Dorado) support R10.4, so earlier pore chemistries or other motifs need different callers No orthogonal benchmark (BS-seq, CCS, or R9.4 methylation profiles) exists to correlate against — the validation framework has nothing to compare to Reads are unphased and the goal is allele-specific methylation — haplotype aggregation and allelic DMR detection require haplotype-tagged reads

skills.description: Use when validating Nanopore methylation caller output (per-site CpG frequencies from DeepMod2 detect on POD5/FAST5 data) against short-read bisulfite or methylation microarray ground truth via Pearson correlation.
skills.name: cross-platform-methylation-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-platform-methylation-correlation-analysis Use when validating Nanopore methylation caller output (per-site CpG frequencies from DeepMod2 detect on POD5/FAST5 data) against short-read bisulfite or methylation microarray ground truth via Pearson correlation. You lack matched short-read or microarray ground truth for the same sample — correlation cannot be computed without shared CpG positions across platforms Input is raw POD5/FAST5 signal that has not been basecalled with move tables — DeepMod2 requires move-table-aligned basecalls before per-site frequencies exist Per-read (not per-site) caller accuracy is the goal — the article separately benchmarks per-read F1 (~95%), and correlation analysis applies only to aggregated per-site methylation frequencies http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Reproduce the benchmark validation that DeepMod2 per-site CpG methylation calls on Nanopore R9.4.1/R10.4.1 data correlate at r > 0.95 with short-read bisulfite sequencing / methylation microarray ground truth on the Ashkenazim trio (HG002, HG003, HG004), by intersecting per-site methylation frequencies across platforms and computing Pearson correlations. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Reproduce the benchmark validation that DeepMod2 per-site CpG methylation calls on Nanopore R9.4.1/R10.4.1 data correlate at r > 0.95 with short-read bisulfite sequencing / methylation microarray ground truth on the Ashkenazim trio (HG002, HG003, HG004), by intersecting per-site methylation frequencies across platforms and computing Pearson correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack matched short-read or microarray ground truth for the same sample — correlation cannot be computed without shared CpG positions across platforms Input is raw POD5/FAST5 signal that has not been basecalled with move tables — DeepMod2 requires move-table-aligned basecalls before per-site frequencies exist Per-read (not per-site) caller accuracy is the goal — the article separately benchmarks per-read F1 (~95%), and correlation analysis applies only to aggregated per-site methylation frequencies

skills.description: Use when comparing consensus sequences generated on one platform (e.g. Nanopore MinION long rDNA amplicons) against reference consensus sequences from another (e.g. Illumina short reads) to quantify cross-platform error rates.
skills.name: cross-platform-sequence-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-platform-sequence-comparison Use when comparing consensus sequences generated on one platform (e.g. Nanopore MinION long rDNA amplicons) against reference consensus sequences from another (e.g. Illumina short reads) to quantify cross-platform error rates. Comparing qualitative species richness or quantitative abundance recovery in bulk mock communities rather than consensus accuracy — the article notes long rDNA amplicon sequencing 'recover[s] highly skewed diversity estimates' and needs further research before bulk-sample use Raw-read error assessment — this skill operates on polished consensus sequences, not uncorrected MinION reads Input reads have not yet been demultiplexed and trimmed of barcodes/primers with minibar.py — binning and trimming (-T, -F) must precede consensus assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies Nanopore long-amplicon rDNA consensus accuracy by computing pairwise alignment distances between MinION-derived consensus sequences and Illumina-based consensus references, as done for the Peperomia test set at MiniBar index edit distances 2, 3, and 4. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Quantifies Nanopore long-amplicon rDNA consensus accuracy by computing pairwise alignment distances between MinION-derived consensus sequences and Illumina-based consensus references, as done for the Peperomia test set at MiniBar index edit distances 2, 3, and 4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing qualitative species richness or quantitative abundance recovery in bulk mock communities rather than consensus accuracy — the article notes long rDNA amplicon sequencing 'recover[s] highly skewed diversity estimates' and needs further research before bulk-sample use Raw-read error assessment — this skill operates on polished consensus sequences, not uncorrected MinION reads Input reads have not yet been demultiplexed and trimmed of barcodes/primers with minibar.py — binning and trimming (-T, -F) must precede consensus assembly

skills.description: Use when you have InDel genotype calls for two parents and their outbred F1 progeny (CP population) and need to filter markers by Mendelian segregation ratio tests and assign each marker a segregation type before linkage map construction.
skills.name: cross-pollination-population-marker-segregation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-pollination-population-marker-segregation-analysis Use when you have InDel genotype calls for two parents and their outbred F1 progeny (CP population) and need to filter markers by Mendelian segregation ratio tests and assign each marker a segregation type before linkage map construction. Population is a traditional inbred-line type (BC1, BC2, F2) where the seven CP segregation types and their expected ratios do not apply — use the appropriate -p type instead of CP-specific classification Genotypes come from another variant caller rather than the InDelGT genotyping step, so the GQ/MAPQ/MISPCT/depth thresholds and genotype coding the segregation test expects are not in place The goal is variant discovery or catalog generation (steps 1–2 of InDelGT), not marker filtering and segregation-type assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Step 3 of InDelGT: test each cataloged InDel site's genotype segregation in an F1 cross-pollination (CP) hybrid population (e.g., 2 parents and 20 Populus progeny) against expected Mendelian ratios, then classify retained sites into the seven CP segregation types (ab×aa, aa×ab, ab×ab, ab×cc, aa×bc, ab×ac, ab×cd) for genetic linkage mapping. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Step 3 of InDelGT: test each cataloged InDel site's genotype segregation in an F1 cross-pollination (CP) hybrid population (e.g., 2 parents and 20 Populus progeny) against expected Mendelian ratios, then classify retained sites into the seven CP segregation types (ab×aa, aa×ab, ab×ab, ab×cc, aa×bc, ab×ac, ab×cd) for genetic linkage mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Population is a traditional inbred-line type (BC1, BC2, F2) where the seven CP segregation types and their expected ratios do not apply — use the appropriate -p type instead of CP-specific classification Genotypes come from another variant caller rather than the InDelGT genotyping step, so the GQ/MAPQ/MISPCT/depth thresholds and genotype coding the segregation test expects are not in place The goal is variant discovery or catalog generation (steps 1–2 of InDelGT), not marker filtering and segregation-type assignment

skills.description: Use when you have RNA-seq (short or long reads) for at least two comparable samples of the same species or orthologous tissues and need to determine whether each exon's AISO class (upfi vs dofi) and Fupfi value is stable across conditions.
skills.name: cross-sample-aiso-consistency-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-sample-aiso-consistency-correlation-analysis Use when you have RNA-seq (short or long reads) for at least two comparable samples of the same species or orthologous tissues and need to determine whether each exon's AISO class (upfi vs dofi) and Fupfi value is stable across conditions. Your goal is differential gene or transcript expression rather than the relative order in which adjacent introns are spliced — Insplico's upfi/dofi/Fupfi metrics address splicing order, not abundance The samples are not comparable pairs of the same or orthologous tissues/conditions; AISO maintenance fractions are only meaningful between matched biological contexts such as brain vs brain across species Exons have too few informative reads: with N(upfi+dofi)<10 the upfi/dofi classification is not supported, and short reads provide almost no splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the exon http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify the splicing order of adjacent introns (AISO) around each exon genome-wide with Insplico, then measure how consistently upfi/dofi classes and Fupfi values are maintained across sample pairs (replicates, cell types, tissues, species, spliceosome-disrupted conditions) using maintenance fractions and Pearson/Spearman correlations. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Quantify the splicing order of adjacent introns (AISO) around each exon genome-wide with Insplico, then measure how consistently upfi/dofi classes and Fupfi values are maintained across sample pairs (replicates, cell types, tissues, species, spliceosome-disrupted conditions) using maintenance fractions and Pearson/Spearman correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is differential gene or transcript expression rather than the relative order in which adjacent introns are spliced — Insplico's upfi/dofi/Fupfi metrics address splicing order, not abundance The samples are not comparable pairs of the same or orthologous tissues/conditions; AISO maintenance fractions are only meaningful between matched biological contexts such as brain vs brain across species Exons have too few informative reads: with N(upfi+dofi)<10 the upfi/dofi classification is not supported, and short reads provide almost no splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the exon

skills.description: Use when you have independently assembled contig FASTA files (any number of input Multi-FASTA sets) from related metagenome samples and want to merge them via OLC-based assembly into one improved contig set and evaluate contiguity gains.
skills.name: cross-sample-hmp-contig-merge-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-sample-hmp-contig-merge-evaluation Use when you have independently assembled contig FASTA files (any number of input Multi-FASTA sets) from related metagenome samples and want to merge them via OLC-based assembly into one improved contig set and evaluate contiguity gains. The input is raw reads rather than assembled contig FASTA files — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process expecting Multi-FASTA contig sets, not FASTQ reads The samples are unrelated or from very different environments, so contigs are unlikely to share the ≥98% identity overlaps (default -minID) needed for OLC-based merging The combined dereplicated contig pool is very large — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Apply MeGAMerge to pool and OLC-merge independently assembled contig sets from multiple related metagenome samples (e.g., HMP SRA read sets) into a single improved contig set, then compare cross-sample versus within-sample contiguity statistics to confirm the merge yields larger contigs and more bases in large contigs without data replication. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Apply MeGAMerge to pool and OLC-merge independently assembled contig sets from multiple related metagenome samples (e.g., HMP SRA read sets) into a single improved contig set, then compare cross-sample versus within-sample contiguity statistics to confirm the merge yields larger contigs and more bases in large contigs without data replication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw reads rather than assembled contig FASTA files — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process expecting Multi-FASTA contig sets, not FASTQ reads The samples are unrelated or from very different environments, so contigs are unlikely to share the ≥98% identity overlaps (default -minID) needed for OLC-based merging The combined dereplicated contig pool is very large — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size

skills.description: Use when scywalker long-read single-cell runs (10x Oxford nanopore or PacBio) have per-sample per-cell gene/isoform count files plus cell-type assignments and you need per-cell-type pseudobulk counts comparable across samples.
skills.name: cross-sample-pseudobulk-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-sample-pseudobulk-comparison-analysis Use when scywalker long-read single-cell runs (10x Oxford nanopore or PacBio) have per-sample per-cell gene/isoform count files plus cell-type assignments and you need per-cell-type pseudobulk counts comparable across samples. No cell-specific markersets are provided: scsorter will not be used to determine celltypes and making pseudobulk files Input is short-read 10x data or a pre-aggregated feature-barcode matrix rather than scywalker long-read per-cell count output The reference lacks proper markers (e.g. the test markers_chr17.tsv contains placeholder markers 'just made to allow celltyping to at least run'), so cell-type pseudobulk labels are not biologically meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates emptydrops-filtered per-cell gene and isoform counts from scywalker into per-cell-type pseudobulk tables per sample, and produces cross-sample pseudobulk comparison count files (in a compar subdirectory) enabling cell-type-specific comparison of gene and isoform expression, including novel isoforms, between samples. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Aggregates emptydrops-filtered per-cell gene and isoform counts from scywalker into per-cell-type pseudobulk tables per sample, and produces cross-sample pseudobulk comparison count files (in a compar subdirectory) enabling cell-type-specific comparison of gene and isoform expression, including novel isoforms, between samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-specific markersets are provided: scsorter will not be used to determine celltypes and making pseudobulk files Input is short-read 10x data or a pre-aggregated feature-barcode matrix rather than scywalker long-read per-cell count output The reference lacks proper markers (e.g. the test markers_chr17.tsv contains placeholder markers 'just made to allow celltyping to at least run'), so cell-type pseudobulk labels are not biologically meaningful

skills.description: Use when two or more samples' reconstructed transcript sets (e.g., IsoCon vs ICE outputs as FASTA) must be intersected by exact sequence identity, or when counting exact nucleotide matches to known reference CDSs (e.g., 61 Ensembl coding sequences of nine Y ampliconic gene families).
skills.name: cross-sample-transcript-sequence-matching
skills.search_text: cross-sample-transcript-sequence-matching Use when two or more samples' reconstructed transcript sets (e.g., IsoCon vs ICE outputs as FASTA) must be intersected by exact sequence identity, or when counting exact nucleotide matches to known reference CDSs (e.g., 61 Ensembl coding sequences of nine Y ampliconic gene families). Transcripts need assignment to individual gene copies or family-size estimation — the article notes transcriptome-only sequencing does not conclusively assign transcripts to gene copies and further downstream analysis is required Input reads are not pre-processed Iso-Seq reads — IsoCon assumes primers, barcodes, and chimeras have already been removed by the Iso-Seq pipeline Sequences are too divergent for exact/near-exact identity matching to be meaningful, or only approximate homology quantification is needed rather than exact nucleotide matches http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compares reconstructed transcript sets across biological samples and against a reference CDS set by exact nucleotide sequence identity, using pairwise alignment (parasail/edlib) to quantify reproducibility and reference-level precision of methods like IsoCon and ICE. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Compares reconstructed transcript sets across biological samples and against a reference CDS set by exact nucleotide sequence identity, using pairwise alignment (parasail/edlib) to quantify reproducibility and reference-level precision of methods like IsoCon and ICE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Transcripts need assignment to individual gene copies or family-size estimation — the article notes transcriptome-only sequencing does not conclusively assign transcripts to gene copies and further downstream analysis is required Input reads are not pre-processed Iso-Seq reads — IsoCon assumes primers, barcodes, and chimeras have already been removed by the Iso-Seq pipeline Sequences are too divergent for exact/near-exact identity matching to be meaningful, or only approximate homology quantification is needed rather than exact nucleotide matches

skills.description: Use when short-read RNA-seq datasets plus genome FASTA and GTF annotations are available for multiple species and the goal is to identify intron-exon features (splice-site strength, intron length, branch point-to-AG distance) universally associated with AISO patterns.
skills.name: cross-species-aiso-consensus-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-species-aiso-consensus-analysis Use when short-read RNA-seq datasets plus genome FASTA and GTF annotations are available for multiple species and the goal is to identify intron-exon features (splice-site strength, intron length, branch point-to-AG distance) universally associated with AISO patterns. The goal is splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the input exon — short reads can barely provide this; long-read data with Insplico's bias-correction module would be needed Studying cell-type- or condition-specific changes in AISO within a species — the article reports AISO around individual exons is remarkably constant across cell and tissue types Exons exceeding the length quantifiable by short reads, which is limited by read length and paired-end fragment size http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Reproduce the universal intron-exon genomic features associated with adjacent-intron splicing order (AISO) across animal and plant species by quantifying per-exon Fupfi with Insplico, extracting 55 intron-exon features with Matt, and aggregating binned feature-Fupfi relationships across species to derive consensus associations. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Reproduce the universal intron-exon genomic features associated with adjacent-intron splicing order (AISO) across animal and plant species by quantifying per-exon Fupfi with Insplico, extracting 55 intron-exon features with Matt, and aggregating binned feature-Fupfi relationships across species to derive consensus associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the input exon — short reads can barely provide this; long-read data with Insplico's bias-correction module would be needed Studying cell-type- or condition-specific changes in AISO within a species — the article reports AISO around individual exons is remarkably constant across cell and tissue types Exons exceeding the length quantifiable by short reads, which is limited by read length and paired-end fragment size

skills.description: Use when you have RNA-seq FASTQ pairs from replicate, cell-type, tissue, species, or spliceosomal-disruption contrasts (e.g. K562/HeLa, mouse brain vs liver, human vs mouse brain, SF3B1-drug vs DMSO, GSE207459) and need to test whether AISO patterns around exons remain stable across the pairs.
skills.name: cross-species-aiso-conservation-assessment
skills.search_text: cross-species-aiso-conservation-assessment Use when you have RNA-seq FASTQ pairs from replicate, cell-type, tissue, species, or spliceosomal-disruption contrasts (e.g. K562/HeLa, mouse brain vs liver, human vs mouse brain, SF3B1-drug vs DMSO, GSE207459) and need to test whether AISO patterns around exons remain stable across the pairs. You are studying alternative splicing levels (PSI/PIR) rather than splicing ORDER of adjacent introns — Insplico's upfi/dofi quantification addresses AISO, not isoform abundance. The exons of interest are microexons or very long exons: read length and paired-end fragment size limit the maximum quantifiable exon length with short reads, and long-read biases require Insplico's 5'/3' correction module. Only a single sample is available with no comparison pair — AISO consistency cannot be assessed without at least two samples/conditions to compare. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Quantify whether adjacent introns' splicing order (AISO) around individual exons is maintained across samples, cell/tissue types, and species (e.g. human vs mouse brain), by running Insplico on STAR-aligned RNA-seq pairs, classifying exons into upfi/dofi classes, and measuring class-maintenance fractions and Fupfi correlations. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Quantify whether adjacent introns' splicing order (AISO) around individual exons is maintained across samples, cell/tissue types, and species (e.g. human vs mouse brain), by running Insplico on STAR-aligned RNA-seq pairs, classifying exons into upfi/dofi classes, and measuring class-maintenance fractions and Fupfi correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are studying alternative splicing levels (PSI/PIR) rather than splicing ORDER of adjacent introns — Insplico's upfi/dofi quantification addresses AISO, not isoform abundance. The exons of interest are microexons or very long exons: read length and paired-end fragment size limit the maximum quantifiable exon length with short reads, and long-read biases require Insplico's 5'/3' correction module. Only a single sample is available with no comparison pair — AISO consistency cannot be assessed without at least two samples/conditions to compare.

skills.description: Use when the reference scRNA-seq dataset and the query dataset come from different species (e.g. mouse reference, human query or cross-species pairs), so gene identifiers must first be mapped to orthologs before reference-based classification.
skills.name: cross-species-cell-type-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-species-cell-type-mapping Use when the reference scRNA-seq dataset and the query dataset come from different species (e.g. mouse reference, human query or cross-species pairs), so gene identifiers must first be mapped to orthologs before reference-based classification. Reference and query datasets are from the same species and share gene identifiers — direct RBC without ortholog mapping applies No labeled reference or atlas is available at all — reference-free clustering, not cross-species RBC, is appropriate (though scMAGIC_atlas with MCA/HCL remains an option within the same species) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Map query single-cell RNA-seq annotations from one species onto another by restricting reference and query matrices to one-to-one orthologous genes (e.g. via homologene) and running reference-based classification (scMAGIC) on the harmonized matrices, as done in the cross-species situation of the 86-benchmark scMAGIC evaluation. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Map query single-cell RNA-seq annotations from one species onto another by restricting reference and query matrices to one-to-one orthologous genes (e.g. via homologene) and running reference-based classification (scMAGIC) on the harmonized matrices, as done in the cross-species situation of the 86-benchmark scMAGIC evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference and query datasets are from the same species and share gene identifiers — direct RBC without ortholog mapping applies No labeled reference or atlas is available at all — reference-free clustering, not cross-species RBC, is appropriate (though scMAGIC_atlas with MCA/HCL remains an option within the same species)

skills.description: Use when constructing a CHH training set for a nanopore 5mC deep learning model where methylation-positive CHH samples are scarce and per-9-mer context balance between positive and negative classes is required.
skills.name: cross-species-chh-training-set-curation
skills.search_text: cross-species-chh-training-set-curation Use when constructing a CHH training set for a nanopore 5mC deep learning model where methylation-positive CHH samples are scarce and per-9-mer context balance between positive and negative classes is required. Input features are not from a CHH context run (e.g. CpG or CHG motifs), where positive-sample scarcity and the 9-mer balancing criterion do not apply the same way The npz files have not yet been produced by extract_hc_sites — raw pod5/BAM inputs cannot be balanced directly You only need species screening or dataset generation, not class balancing of already-extracted sites http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Curates a class-balanced CHH methylation training dataset for DeepPlant by keeping only 9-mer sequence contexts that have at least 50 positive samples and at least as many negatives, then subsampling so every retained 9-mer contributes equal positive and negative samples. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Curates a class-balanced CHH methylation training dataset for DeepPlant by keeping only 9-mer sequence contexts that have at least 50 positive samples and at least as many negatives, then subsampling so every retained 9-mer contributes equal positive and negative samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features are not from a CHH context run (e.g. CpG or CHG motifs), where positive-sample scarcity and the 9-mer balancing criterion do not apply the same way The npz files have not yet been produced by extract_hc_sites — raw pod5/BAM inputs cannot be balanced directly You only need species screening or dataset generation, not class balancing of already-extracted sites

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a nanopore CpG methylation calling model generalizes across human and plant R10.4 datasets, using bisulfite-seq ground truth and AUC/F1/balanced accuracy metrics.
skills.name: cross-species-methylation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-species-methylation-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a nanopore CpG methylation calling model generalizes across human and plant R10.4 datasets, using bisulfite-seq ground truth and AUC/F1/balanced accuracy metrics. Data is from older non-R10.4 flowcells — the article notes only a small number of tools are compatible with R10.4 (DeepMod2 and Dorado), so benchmark expectations may not transfer You need whole-genome methylation frequency correlation rather than single-molecule calling performance — a separate evaluation (>0.95 correlation with BS-seq) is reported for that Input datasets lack bisulfite-defined ground-truth methylation sites, making AUC/F1/balanced accuracy against high-confidence sites impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks single-molecule CpG methylation callers (DeepBAM vs Dorado) across heterogeneous human and plant Oxford Nanopore R10.4 datasets using ROC AUC, F1, and balanced accuracy against bisulfite-defined ground truth, exposing dataset-dependent variability of the official Dorado model. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-molecule CpG methylation callers (DeepBAM vs Dorado) across heterogeneous human and plant Oxford Nanopore R10.4 datasets using ROC AUC, F1, and balanced accuracy against bisulfite-defined ground truth, exposing dataset-dependent variability of the official Dorado model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is from older non-R10.4 flowcells — the article notes only a small number of tools are compatible with R10.4 (DeepMod2 and Dorado), so benchmark expectations may not transfer You need whole-genome methylation frequency correlation rather than single-molecule calling performance — a separate evaluation (>0.95 correlation with BS-seq) is reported for that Input datasets lack bisulfite-defined ground-truth methylation sites, making AUC/F1/balanced accuracy against high-confidence sites impossible

skills.description: Use when you have per-read ONT methylation calls for several strains and an orthogonal PacBio motif list, and need a species-by-motif percentage table to confirm methyltransferase target motifs across a reference community.
skills.name: cross-species-motif-methylation-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-species-motif-methylation-comparison Use when you have per-read ONT methylation calls for several strains and an orthogonal PacBio motif list, and need a species-by-motif percentage table to confirm methyltransferase target motifs across a reference community. Model has not been trained on a sequence context similar to the target motif - the article notes training biases can decrease accuracy at contexts with lower similarity to the E. coli training examples, as seen for one S. aureus motif You are trying to distinguish methylation types at ambiguous motifs such as GATCGVNY in S. aureus, where both single-molecule methods fail to distinguish between methylation types Working with the two Dikarya fungi (C. neoformans and S. cerevisiae), where the study could not confidently assign motifs or identify consistently detected sites http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Aggregates mCaller per-position methylation predictions across multiple microbial strains and motifs to compute the fraction of PacBio-predicted methyltransferase target motif sites classified as methylated per species and per motif, enabling cross-species confirmation of motif calls in the ZymoBIOMICS reference community. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Aggregates mCaller per-position methylation predictions across multiple microbial strains and motifs to compute the fraction of PacBio-predicted methyltransferase target motif sites classified as methylated per species and per motif, enabling cross-species confirmation of motif calls in the ZymoBIOMICS reference community.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Model has not been trained on a sequence context similar to the target motif - the article notes training biases can decrease accuracy at contexts with lower similarity to the E. coli training examples, as seen for one S. aureus motif You are trying to distinguish methylation types at ambiguous motifs such as GATCGVNY in S. aureus, where both single-molecule methods fail to distinguish between methylation types Working with the two Dikarya fungi (C. neoformans and S. cerevisiae), where the study could not confidently assign motifs or identify consistently detected sites

skills.description: Use when comparing methylation callers (e.g., DeepPlant vs Dorado) across multiple plant species on R10.4 nanopore data, using bisulfite-sequencing high-confidence sites as balanced ground truth for per-read metrics.
skills.name: cross-species-tool-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-species-tool-benchmarking Use when comparing methylation callers (e.g., DeepPlant vs Dorado) across multiple plant species on R10.4 nanopore data, using bisulfite-sequencing high-confidence sites as balanced ground truth for per-read metrics. The flow cell is the older R9.4 platform — tools such as Tombo, Megalodon, and DeepSignal-Plant were developed for R9.4 and cannot be directly applied to R10.4, so this benchmarking design does not transfer The goal is runtime-efficient methylation calling rather than accuracy benchmarking — DeepPlant is less computationally efficient than Dorado (Supplementary Data 10) The context of interest is CpG or CHG only — DeepPlant's key gains are in CHH detection, where positive training samples are scarce http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark DeepPlant against Dorado for single-molecule and whole-genome 5mC detection in plant CHH contexts on ONT R10.4 data, computing F1, accuracy, recall, precision, AUC, and AP per species against BS-seq-derived ground truth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Benchmark DeepPlant against Dorado for single-molecule and whole-genome 5mC detection in plant CHH contexts on ONT R10.4 data, computing F1, accuracy, recall, precision, AUC, and AP per species against BS-seq-derived ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The flow cell is the older R9.4 platform — tools such as Tombo, Megalodon, and DeepSignal-Plant were developed for R9.4 and cannot be directly applied to R10.4, so this benchmarking design does not transfer The goal is runtime-efficient methylation calling rather than accuracy benchmarking — DeepPlant is less computationally efficient than Dorado (Supplementary Data 10) The context of interest is CpG or CHG only — DeepPlant's key gains are in CHH detection, where positive training samples are scarce

skills.description: Use when you have spore-viability measurements for crosses between strains and pairwise variant counts between parents, and need to test which variant classes (SNPs, SVs, rearrangements, CNVs) independently correlate with offspring viability.
skills.name: cross-spore-viability-phenotype-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-spore-viability-phenotype-analysis Use when you have spore-viability measurements for crosses between strains and pairwise variant counts between parents, and need to test which variant classes (SNPs, SVs, rearrangements, CNVs) independently correlate with offspring viability. The goal is estimating heritability or trait variance explained (mixed-model GWAS on 228 quantitative traits), not cross-level viability association — use the mixed model / GWAS workflow instead. You lack per-cross viability measurements or per-parent genotype/variant calls, so distances cannot be computed as unshared variant counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Quantifies whether parental genetic distances (SNPs, all SVs, rearrangements only, CNVs only) correlate inversely with hybrid spore viability in S. pombe crosses, using Kendall tau rank correlations plus partial correlations to disentangle the independent contribution of each variant class to intrinsic reproductive isolation. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Quantifies whether parental genetic distances (SNPs, all SVs, rearrangements only, CNVs only) correlate inversely with hybrid spore viability in S. pombe crosses, using Kendall tau rank correlations plus partial correlations to disentangle the independent contribution of each variant class to intrinsic reproductive isolation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is estimating heritability or trait variance explained (mixed-model GWAS on 228 quantitative traits), not cross-level viability association — use the mixed model / GWAS workflow instead. You lack per-cross viability measurements or per-parent genotype/variant calls, so distances cannot be computed as unshared variant counts.

skills.description: Use when a target publication reports a numeric result (e.g. number of resistance genes) for named isolates and you need to reproduce the count with your own pipeline and account for discrepancies versus the source study.
skills.name: cross-study-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-study-benchmark-comparison Use when a target publication reports a numeric result (e.g. number of resistance genes) for named isolates and you need to reproduce the count with your own pipeline and account for discrepancies versus the source study. The input is raw Nanopore FASTQ reads rather than already-assembled genomes — assemble first with the upstream NanoGalaxy workflow before running Staramr. The comparison study used a resistance-screening database with identical scope (no point-mutation screening) and you need strict like-for-like detection counts rather than an explained excess. The target study does not report a numeric per-isolate feature count that can be tallied and compared. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduce a published benchmark by re-running a tool-based workflow (here, Staramr with PointFinder on NanoGalaxy de novo assemblies) and directly tallying detected features against the counts reported in an earlier study, explaining any excess as database coverage differences. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: Reproduce a published benchmark by re-running a tool-based workflow (here, Staramr with PointFinder on NanoGalaxy de novo assemblies) and directly tallying detected features against the counts reported in an earlier study, explaining any excess as database coverage differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw Nanopore FASTQ reads rather than already-assembled genomes — assemble first with the upstream NanoGalaxy workflow before running Staramr. The comparison study used a resistance-screening database with identical scope (no point-mutation screening) and you need strict like-for-like detection counts rather than an explained excess. The target study does not report a numeric per-isolate feature count that can be tallied and compared.

skills.description: Use when tallying internal alternative splicing events within circRNAs from a long-read full-length isoform catalog (isocirc.out), or when quantitatively comparing EIciRNA/retained-intron circRNA abundance between long-read and short-read RNA-seq studies.
skills.name: cross-study-retained-intron-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-study-retained-intron-comparison Use when tallying internal alternative splicing events within circRNAs from a long-read full-length isoform catalog (isocirc.out), or when quantitatively comparing EIciRNA/retained-intron circRNA abundance between long-read and short-read RNA-seq studies. Input is short-read RNA-seq data, which does not experimentally determine full-length circRNA sequences or exact exonic compositions, so internal event classification is not directly supported The goal is BSJ-only circRNA detection without full-length internal isoform structure — a plain back-splice junction caller is the appropriate choice Estimating absolute circRNA abundance de novo rather than benchmarking event counts; isoCirc is far from saturation at current depth, so counts are lower bounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces isoCirc's internal alternative splicing event counts within circRNAs (5,325 total at minor-isoform readCount>=2, spanning skipped exon, alternative 5' splice site, alternative 3' splice site, and retained intron) and benchmarks the 720 EIciRNA retained-intron events against comparable short-read RNA-seq studies (~20-fold excess expected). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Reproduces isoCirc's internal alternative splicing event counts within circRNAs (5,325 total at minor-isoform readCount>=2, spanning skipped exon, alternative 5' splice site, alternative 3' splice site, and retained intron) and benchmarks the 720 EIciRNA retained-intron events against comparable short-read RNA-seq studies (~20-fold excess expected).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data, which does not experimentally determine full-length circRNA sequences or exact exonic compositions, so internal event classification is not directly supported The goal is BSJ-only circRNA detection without full-length internal isoform structure — a plain back-splice junction caller is the appropriate choice Estimating absolute circRNA abundance de novo rather than benchmarking event counts; isoCirc is far from saturation at current depth, so counts are lower bounds

skills.description: Use when you have independently generated dysgu SV callsets (VCF) from paired-end and long-read data and want to quantify how many additional deletions/insertions the combined callset recovers against a GIAB benchmark.
skills.name: cross-technology-callset-merging
skills.search_text: cross-technology-callset-merging Use when you have independently generated dysgu SV callsets (VCF) from paired-end and long-read data and want to quantify how many additional deletions/insertions the combined callset recovers against a GIAB benchmark. The callsets were not produced by dysgu (its 'merge' command and model-probability field are required for the >=0.5 / >=0.35 filtering step) You need to resolve multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences — the article notes dysgu lacks a de novo assembly stage for these The analysis targets somatic samples with copy-number changes, where a non-diploid dysgu model rather than merged germline callsets is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Merge structural variant calls from Illumina paired-end data into dysgu callsets from low-coverage PacBio/ONT long reads using dysgu's 'merge' command, then filter with technology-specific model-probability thresholds (>=0.5 PacBio, >=0.35 ONT) to boost recall toward GIAB HG002 truth sets. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Merge structural variant calls from Illumina paired-end data into dysgu callsets from low-coverage PacBio/ONT long reads using dysgu's 'merge' command, then filter with technology-specific model-probability thresholds (>=0.5 PacBio, >=0.35 ONT) to boost recall toward GIAB HG002 truth sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The callsets were not produced by dysgu (its 'merge' command and model-probability field are required for the >=0.5 / >=0.35 filtering step) You need to resolve multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences — the article notes dysgu lacks a de novo assembly stage for these The analysis targets somatic samples with copy-number changes, where a non-diploid dysgu model rather than merged germline callsets is appropriate

skills.description: Use when comparing genome-reconstruction performance of viral nanopore assembly pipelines (ViMOP, INSaFLU-TELEVIR, VirDetector) on the same read sets and you need a consolidated benchmark comparison table.
skills.name: cross-tool-comparison-metrics-tabulation
skills.search_text: cross-tool-comparison-metrics-tabulation Use when comparing genome-reconstruction performance of viral nanopore assembly pipelines (ViMOP, INSaFLU-TELEVIR, VirDetector) on the same read sets and you need a consolidated benchmark comparison table. The goal is de novo discovery of novel viruses rather than benchmarking known-virus genome reconstruction against reference databases Input data are not untargeted nanopore fastq read sets shared across all comparator pipelines, so identical-input comparisons cannot be made Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g., mpox) are the target, since ViMOP assemblies for these may be inaccurate drafts that would confound recovery metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces the ViMOP benchmark against INSaFLU-TELEVIR and VirDetector by running each pipeline on identical fastq inputs (simulated viral reads, host-virus mixtures, real SRA samples) and tabulating per-virus, per-sample genome recovery metrics into a single tool-comparison table mirroring Section 2.11 of the paper. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Reproduces the ViMOP benchmark against INSaFLU-TELEVIR and VirDetector by running each pipeline on identical fastq inputs (simulated viral reads, host-virus mixtures, real SRA samples) and tabulating per-virus, per-sample genome recovery metrics into a single tool-comparison table mirroring Section 2.11 of the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo discovery of novel viruses rather than benchmarking known-virus genome reconstruction against reference databases Input data are not untargeted nanopore fastq read sets shared across all comparator pipelines, so identical-input comparisons cannot be made Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g., mpox) are the target, since ViMOP assemblies for these may be inaccurate drafts that would confound recovery metrics

skills.description: Use when multiple gene-prioritization tools have been run on the same benchmark cases and you need per-tool unique top-k hit counts and evidence of complementarity across tools.
skills.name: cross-tool-complementarity-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-tool-complementarity-analysis Use when multiple gene-prioritization tools have been run on the same benchmark cases and you need per-tool unique top-k hit counts and evidence of complementarity across tools. You have only a single tool's output — unique-hit and complementarity analysis requires at least two tools run on identical cases Tool outputs are not harmonized to a shared gene identifier space (e.g., mixed HGNC symbols and NCBI IDs) — the benchmark comparison relies on converting everything to NCBI gene identifiers first Cases lack known causal-gene truth labels, so per-case ranks and unique-hit counts cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Quantifies how many causal genes each phenotype-based prioritization tool (e.g., VIBE, Phenomizer, AMELIE, GADO, hiPHIVE, PhenIX, PhenoTips, PubCaseFinder) uniquely recovers within a fixed rank window (top 20) over a shared benchmark, exposing complementarity among tools rather than declaring a single winner. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Quantifies how many causal genes each phenotype-based prioritization tool (e.g., VIBE, Phenomizer, AMELIE, GADO, hiPHIVE, PhenIX, PhenoTips, PubCaseFinder) uniquely recovers within a fixed rank window (top 20) over a shared benchmark, exposing complementarity among tools rather than declaring a single winner.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single tool's output — unique-hit and complementarity analysis requires at least two tools run on identical cases Tool outputs are not harmonized to a shared gene identifier space (e.g., mixed HGNC symbols and NCBI IDs) — the benchmark comparison relies on converting everything to NCBI gene identifiers first Cases lack known causal-gene truth labels, so per-case ranks and unique-hit counts cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when comparing self-correction tools on real long-read datasets (PacBio S. cerevisiae, ONT D. melanogaster, ONT H. sapiens chr 1) and need a reproducible table of correction quality and resource metrics.
skills.name: cross-tool-correction-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-tool-correction-benchmarking Use when comparing self-correction tools on real long-read datasets (PacBio S. cerevisiae, ONT D. melanogaster, ONT H. sapiens chr 1) and need a reproducible table of correction quality and resource metrics. Simulated datasets only — the article's real-data benchmark (Table 2) targets real PacBio and ONT reads; simulated-read comparisons use different evaluation machinery (ELECTOR's simulation module) Assembly polishing evaluation — this skill benchmarks self-correction only, not CONSENT's polishing feature Datasets lacking a reference genome, since genome coverage and alignment identity require aligning corrected reads back to a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark long-read self-correction methods (CONSENT vs. Canu, Daccord, FLAS, MECAT) on real PacBio and ONT datasets by running each correction recipe, aligning corrected reads back to the reference with ELECTOR/minimap2, and compiling Table 2 metrics (corrected reads, bases, N50, aligned-read proportion, identity, genome coverage, runtime, memory). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read self-correction methods (CONSENT vs. Canu, Daccord, FLAS, MECAT) on real PacBio and ONT datasets by running each correction recipe, aligning corrected reads back to the reference with ELECTOR/minimap2, and compiling Table 2 metrics (corrected reads, bases, N50, aligned-read proportion, identity, genome coverage, runtime, memory).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Simulated datasets only — the article's real-data benchmark (Table 2) targets real PacBio and ONT reads; simulated-read comparisons use different evaluation machinery (ELECTOR's simulation module) Assembly polishing evaluation — this skill benchmarks self-correction only, not CONSENT's polishing feature Datasets lacking a reference genome, since genome coverage and alignment identity require aligning corrected reads back to a reference

skills.description: Use when two error/variant callers (e.g., CRAQ and SyRI) have been run on the same draft assembly and you need to compute what fraction of one tool's breakpoints fall inside the other's SVs, and categorize the unique calls.
skills.name: cross-tool-error-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-tool-error-overlap-analysis Use when two error/variant callers (e.g., CRAQ and SyRI) have been run on the same draft assembly and you need to compute what fraction of one tool's breakpoints fall inside the other's SVs, and categorize the unique calls. Only one caller has been run — there is no second set of SV/error coordinates to intersect, so no overlap analysis is possible The two callers were run against different assemblies or incompatible coordinate systems (e.g., different references), making breakpoint-in-SV-boundary comparison meaningless without liftover Genome has ploidy higher than diploid — the article notes CRAQ accuracy 'for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Quantify the concordance between assembly errors called by CRAQ (CREs/CSEs from clipped-read signals) and structural variants called by an independent tool (e.g., SyRI) on the same assembly, classifying breakpoint overlaps and assigning non-overlapping calls to error categories. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Quantify the concordance between assembly errors called by CRAQ (CREs/CSEs from clipped-read signals) and structural variants called by an independent tool (e.g., SyRI) on the same assembly, classifying breakpoint overlaps and assigning non-overlapping calls to error categories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one caller has been run — there is no second set of SV/error coordinates to intersect, so no overlap analysis is possible The two callers were run against different assemblies or incompatible coordinate systems (e.g., different references), making breakpoint-in-SV-boundary comparison meaningless without liftover Genome has ploidy higher than diploid — the article notes CRAQ accuracy 'for species with higher ploidy levels may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here'

skills.description: Use when comparing exon/IEB prediction tools (EXFI, ChopStitch, GMAP) on the same transcriptomes and WGS reads, needing precision/recall/F1 against a GFF3 reference plus exon mappability via BWA MEM.
skills.name: cross-tool-exon-prediction-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-tool-exon-prediction-comparison Use when comparing exon/IEB prediction tools (EXFI, ChopStitch, GMAP) on the same transcriptomes and WGS reads, needing precision/recall/F1 against a GFF3 reference plus exon mappability via BWA MEM. You need full splice-graph or transcript-path output rather than a tool-vs-tool performance benchmark (EXFI's GFA1 splice graph is the deliverable, not the comparison) The input transcriptome is de novo-assembled from a single tissue — mappability scores fall for all methods in the herring case, so cross-tool ranking may reflect transcriptome quality rather than tool performance You only need IEB positions for SNP genotyping; use EXFI directly instead of running a three-tool benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark exon-prediction approaches — k-mer-based EXFI and ChopStitch versus splice-aware aligner GMAP — by computing precision, recall, F1, and mappability of predicted exons across species with and without reference annotations. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Benchmark exon-prediction approaches — k-mer-based EXFI and ChopStitch versus splice-aware aligner GMAP — by computing precision, recall, F1, and mappability of predicted exons across species with and without reference annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need full splice-graph or transcript-path output rather than a tool-vs-tool performance benchmark (EXFI's GFA1 splice graph is the deliverable, not the comparison) The input transcriptome is de novo-assembled from a single tissue — mappability scores fall for all methods in the herring case, so cross-tool ranking may reflect transcriptome quality rather than tool performance You only need IEB positions for SNP genotyping; use EXFI directly instead of running a three-tool benchmark

skills.description: Use when you need to validate a long-read transcript quantification workflow by measuring replicate-to-replicate Pearson correlations (e.g. >0.971) and cross-tool agreement with an alternative quantifier such as LIQA (~0.83), as in Fig. 5g / Supplementary Table 4.
skills.name: cross-tool-expression-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-tool-expression-benchmarking Use when you need to validate a long-read transcript quantification workflow by measuring replicate-to-replicate Pearson correlations (e.g. >0.971) and cross-tool agreement with an alternative quantifier such as LIQA (~0.83), as in Fig. 5g / Supplementary Table 4. Data are short-read RNA-seq rather than full-length Iso-seq/ONT transcript reads — TAGET is designed for full-length transcript data There are no biological replicates and no independent alternative quantification (e.g. LIQA) to compare against, so reproducibility and cross-tool correlation cannot be computed The goal is novel isoform or gene fusion discovery rather than expression quantification accuracy assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark the reproducibility and accuracy of long-read isoform/gene expression quantification by computing pairwise Pearson correlations across biological replicates within one tool (TAGET on ONT GM12878 replicates, expected >0.971) and cross-tool correlations against an alternative method (LIQA, expected ~0.83), writing results to gm12878_taget_correlations.csv. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Benchmark the reproducibility and accuracy of long-read isoform/gene expression quantification by computing pairwise Pearson correlations across biological replicates within one tool (TAGET on ONT GM12878 replicates, expected >0.971) and cross-tool correlations against an alternative method (LIQA, expected ~0.83), writing results to gm12878_taget_correlations.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are short-read RNA-seq rather than full-length Iso-seq/ONT transcript reads — TAGET is designed for full-length transcript data There are no biological replicates and no independent alternative quantification (e.g. LIQA) to compare against, so reproducibility and cross-tool correlation cannot be computed The goal is novel isoform or gene fusion discovery rather than expression quantification accuracy assessment

skills.description: Use when evaluating which nanopore-based differential RNA modification caller detects m6A stoichiometry changes between two multi-replicate conditions, e.g. WT vs methyltransferase knockout.
skills.name: cross-tool-m6a-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-tool-m6a-benchmarking Use when evaluating which nanopore-based differential RNA modification caller detects m6A stoichiometry changes between two multi-replicate conditions, e.g. WT vs methyltransferase knockout. Single-condition m6A/m5C site and stoichiometry calling without a comparison condition — use CHEUI-solo models instead of CHEUI-diff Data are not nanopore direct RNA reads with per-site modification probabilities (e.g. short-read m6A-seq or antibody-based maps) — the per-read probability and signal-level comparisons do not apply Conditions lack replicates or have fewer than 20 reads per adenosine site in both conditions — sites fall outside the tested set by design Head-to-head benchmarking of differential m6A detection from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA data, comparing CHEUI-diff, Xpore, and Nanocompore on matched WT vs METTL3-KO HEK293 replicates at shared significance thresholds, with validation against m6ACE-seq/miCLIP sites and KO-only false-positive estimation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Head-to-head benchmarking of differential m6A detection from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA data, comparing CHEUI-diff, Xpore, and Nanocompore on matched WT vs METTL3-KO HEK293 replicates at shared significance thresholds, with validation against m6ACE-seq/miCLIP sites and KO-only false-positive estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-condition m6A/m5C site and stoichiometry calling without a comparison condition — use CHEUI-solo models instead of CHEUI-diff Data are not nanopore direct RNA reads with per-site modification probabilities (e.g. short-read m6A-seq or antibody-based maps) — the per-read probability and signal-level comparisons do not apply Conditions lack replicates or have fewer than 20 reads per adenosine site in both conditions — sites fall outside the tested set by design

When the goal is de novo signature extraction rather than refitting — the article states the RNMF de novo framework 'spends more time on a de novo extraction of signature analysis' than previously published software When the mutation catalog or signature set differs across tools, since the speed comparison is only meaningful on the identical ESCC input and the same COSMIC signature set http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark the operating speed of a new method (RNMF's InverseNMF signature-refitting procedure) against established baselines (deconstructSigs, MutationalPatterns) by running all tools on the identical ESCC mutation catalog and COSMIC signature set, then computing wall-clock speed ratios. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Benchmark the operating speed of a new method (RNMF's InverseNMF signature-refitting procedure) against established baselines (deconstructSigs, MutationalPatterns) by running all tools on the identical ESCC mutation catalog and COSMIC signature set, then computing wall-clock speed ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo signature extraction rather than refitting — the article states the RNMF de novo framework 'spends more time on a de novo extraction of signature analysis' than previously published software When the mutation catalog or signature set differs across tools, since the speed comparison is only meaningful on the identical ESCC input and the same COSMIC signature set

skills.search_text: cross-tool-runtime-comparison Use when comparing computational cost (runtime and peak RSS) of multiple SV-calling tools or pipeline variants on a shared dataset, e.g. Blackbird SLR/hybrid vs Sniffles2 and PBSV on HG002. The goal is to compare SV-calling accuracy (F1-score, precision/recall) rather than computational cost — use a variant-benchmarking skill instead The tools operate on different input datasets that are not comparable (e.g. different samples or coverage), making runtime comparison meaningless Only a single tool/mode is being run, so there is no cross-tool comparison to make http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark wall-clock runtime and peak memory of SV callers (Blackbird SLR and hybrid modes versus SvABA, Manta, Sniffles2, PBSV) on the same HG002 dataset by wrapping each run with /usr/bin/time -v on equivalent hardware, so compute cost can be reported alongside call quality. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock runtime and peak memory of SV callers (Blackbird SLR and hybrid modes versus SvABA, Manta, Sniffles2, PBSV) on the same HG002 dataset by wrapping each run with /usr/bin/time -v on equivalent hardware, so compute cost can be reported alongside call quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare SV-calling accuracy (F1-score, precision/recall) rather than computational cost — use a variant-benchmarking skill instead The tools operate on different input datasets that are not comparable (e.g. different samples or coverage), making runtime comparison meaningless Only a single tool/mode is being run, so there is no cross-tool comparison to make

skills.description: Use when benchmarking raw signal mappers head-to-head (RawHash2 vs RawHash/UNCALLED/Sigmap) on R9.4.1 FAST5 data and you need speedup ratios (26.5x/19.2x/4.0x) or sequencing-length reduction (~1.9x).
skills.name: cross-tool-speedup-ratio-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-tool-speedup-ratio-comparison Use when benchmarking raw signal mappers head-to-head (RawHash2 vs RawHash/UNCALLED/Sigmap) on R9.4.1 FAST5 data and you need speedup ratios (26.5x/19.2x/4.0x) or sequencing-length reduction (~1.9x).
