skills.search_text: fastq-demultiplexed-sample-processing Use when MiniBar (-F binning) has produced per-sample FASTQ files of MinION rDNA amplicon reads and they must be cleaned of low-quality, short reads before consensus/barcode analysis. Input reads have not yet been demultiplexed — run minibar.py with the -F option first so records are grouped by identified sample Data are short Illumina reads or short amplicons, where the 3,000 bp length cutoff (sized to the multi-kilobase rDNA amplicon) would discard everything Input is already a filtered/consensus FASTA or a feature table rather than raw demultiplexed Nanopore FASTQ http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quality- and length-filters MiniBar-demultiplexed Nanopore FASTQ reads of long rDNA amplicons with NanoFilt (Phred Q>13, length >3 kb), producing per-sample cleaned FASTQ files whose combined read count for the main run should equal 245,433 reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Quality- and length-filters MiniBar-demultiplexed Nanopore FASTQ reads of long rDNA amplicons with NanoFilt (Phred Q>13, length >3 kb), producing per-sample cleaned FASTQ files whose combined read count for the main run should equal 245,433 reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been demultiplexed — run minibar.py with the -F option first so records are grouped by identified sample Data are short Illumina reads or short amplicons, where the 3,000 bp length cutoff (sized to the multi-kilobase rDNA amplicon) would discard everything Input is already a filtered/consensus FASTA or a feature table rather than raw demultiplexed Nanopore FASTQ

skills.description: Use when a MinION nanopore read set in FASTA or FASTQ format needs a trained LAST scoring scheme (substitution matrix / parameters) fitted to the specific target before mapping with lastal, instead of relying on default or generic scoring.
skills.name: fastq-fasta-read-sampling
skills.search_text: fastq-fasta-read-sampling Use when a MinION nanopore read set in FASTA or FASTQ format needs a trained LAST scoring scheme (substitution matrix / parameters) fitted to the specific target before mapping with lastal, instead of relying on default or generic scoring. The target is one of NanoPipe's precompiled targets, which already ship with best-fitting last-train-derived parameters and substitution matrices, so retraining is redundant The reads do not come from Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing — the estimated insertion/deletion/substitution rates would not reflect the sequencing technology in use The goal is metagenomics analysis, which NanoPipe explicitly does not yet support http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Sample a subset of MinION sequencing reads (FASTA or FASTQ) and train LAST's scoring scheme with last-train against a prebuilt lastdb target index, so the alignment parameters reflect the insertion, deletion, and substitution rates characteristic of MinION data rather than a generic matrix. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Sample a subset of MinION sequencing reads (FASTA or FASTQ) and train LAST's scoring scheme with last-train against a prebuilt lastdb target index, so the alignment parameters reflect the insertion, deletion, and substitution rates characteristic of MinION data rather than a generic matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target is one of NanoPipe's precompiled targets, which already ship with best-fitting last-train-derived parameters and substitution matrices, so retraining is redundant The reads do not come from Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing — the estimated insertion/deletion/substitution rates would not reflect the sequencing technology in use The goal is metagenomics analysis, which NanoPipe explicitly does not yet support

skills.description: Use when raw Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads must have fixed-length primer and adapter sequences stripped from both ends before downstream taxonomic classification, filtering, or de novo/reference-guided assembly.

skills.search_text: fastq-file-format-processing Use when raw Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads must have fixed-length primer and adapter sequences stripped from both ends before downstream taxonomic classification, filtering, or de novo/reference-guided assembly. Input reads are already demultiplexed/trimmed internal read portions without adapter or primer sequence at the termini Reads need quality-score-dependent or probabilistic trimming rather than a fixed number of bases cut from both ends The sample is not untargeted nanopore data processed by a primer-based protocol (e.g., amplicon-free cDNA or direct RNA runs with different end structure) http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Primer/adapter-end trimming of raw nanopore FASTQ reads as implemented in ViMOP: seqtk removes a user-defined number of bases from both the 3' and 5' ends of every read before taxonomic classification and assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Primer/adapter-end trimming of raw nanopore FASTQ reads as implemented in ViMOP: seqtk removes a user-defined number of bases from both the 3' and 5' ends of every read before taxonomic classification and assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already demultiplexed/trimmed internal read portions without adapter or primer sequence at the termini Reads need quality-score-dependent or probabilistic trimming rather than a fixed number of bases cut from both ends The sample is not untargeted nanopore data processed by a primer-based protocol (e.g., amplicon-free cDNA or direct RNA runs with different end structure)

skills.search_text: fastq-quality-filtering-per-sample Use when raw Oxford Nanopore reads (FASTQ, or FAST5/POD5 requiring basecalling) must be quality-filtered per sample before taxonomic classification or genome reconstruction, and per-sample read-quality statistics are needed. skills.description: Use when FASTQ reads with deteriorating 3'-end quality will be used for base-level correction or polishing (e.g. Pilon with Illumina data) and raw per-base qualities must be filtered to a Phred threshold first.
skills.name: fastq-quality-trimming-phred-threshold
skills.search_text: fastq-quality-trimming-phred-threshold Use when FASTQ reads with deteriorating 3'-end quality will be used for base-level correction or polishing (e.g. Pilon with Illumina data) and raw per-base qualities must be filtered to a Phred threshold first. Input is nanopore long-read data being corrected with Racon — Racon takes raw nanopore alignments, not sickle-trimmed Illumina reads Reads are already adapter- and quality-trimmed or come from a technology without quality decay toward the 3'-end You need assembly of long reads only (no Illumina polishing step is planned, so trimming serves no downstream correction) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Adaptive windowed quality trimming of FASTQ reads with sickle before downstream correction/polishing. In the eel nanopore-assembly pipeline, Illumina reads (SRR5235521–SRR5235523) are trimmed to a minimum Phred quality of 30 so Pilon polishing is fed high-confidence bases. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is nanopore long-read data being corrected with Racon — Racon takes raw nanopore alignments, not sickle-trimmed Illumina reads Reads are already adapter- and quality-trimmed or come from a technology without quality decay toward the 3'-end You need assembly of long reads only (no Illumina polishing step is planned, so trimming serves no downstream correction)

skills.description: Use when raw WGS FASTQ reads must be reduced to only those overlapping an assembled transcriptome (exonic/flanking content) before expensive k-mer or graph computations.

skills.search_text: fastq-read-categorization Use when raw WGS FASTQ reads must be reduced to only those overlapping an assembled transcriptome (exonic/flanking content) before expensive k-mer or graph computations. When mapping locations or alignment coordinates are required — BioBloom categorizes sequences but 'does not provide mapping locations' When the reference is not a transcriptome assembly but many targets (>100) — use the multi-index Bloom filter workflow instead When the input transcriptome is poor quality or single-tissue, since missing/fragmented transcripts will cause their reads to be discarded http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Categorize (filter) raw FASTQ WGS reads against a transcriptome-derived Bloom filter using BioBloom Tools (biobloommaker + biobloomcategorizer), discarding reads that share no k-mer with the transcriptome to reduce downstream false positives and computation. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Categorize (filter) raw FASTQ WGS reads against a transcriptome-derived Bloom filter using BioBloom Tools (biobloommaker + biobloomcategorizer), discarding reads that share no k-mer with the transcriptome to reduce downstream false positives and computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When mapping locations or alignment coordinates are required — BioBloom categorizes sequences but 'does not provide mapping locations' When the reference is not a transcriptome assembly but many targets (>100) — use the multi-index Bloom filter workflow instead When the input transcriptome is poor quality or single-tissue, since missing/fragmented transcripts will cause their reads to be discarded

skills.description: Use when hybrid-correcting noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore long reads against aligned Illumina short reads and a questionable position shows ≥90% (η = 0.9) short-read consensus, so the base can be directly replaced without running the optimization-based correction step.
skills.name: fastq-read-manipulation
skills.search_text: fastq-read-manipulation Use when hybrid-correcting noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore long reads against aligned Illumina short reads and a questionable position shows ≥90% (η = 0.9) short-read consensus, so the base can be directly replaced without running the optimization-based correction step. A questionable position lacks ≥90% short-read consensus (η < 0.9) — quick correction must leave it untouched and defer it to the optimization-based correction framework instead. No hybrid short-read data (e.g., Illumina) is available — HECIL's quick correction depends on aligned short reads, unlike self-correcting algorithms such as HGAP. skills.summary: Detects allele-specific CpG methylation and 6mA enrichment in haplotagged nanoHiMe-seq data by building per-region 2×2 contingency tables of methylated/unmethylated (or 6mA/non-6mA) read counts across the two phased haplotypes and testing them with Fisher's exact test, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg correction at 10% FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Regions with read coverage below 20 reads — the article explicitly selects only regions with reads coverage ≥20 for this analysis Genomic loci with a low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs, where haplotype phasing of 6mA-containing regions and CpG methylation is unreliable Data not phased/haplotagged — without haplotype assignment of reads no per-allele 2×2 table can be constructed

skills.description: Use when two categorical classifications (e.g. dofi vs upfi splicing order) must be compared between a regulated set (DeltaPSI > 0.15, control PSI <= 0.2) and a matched control set to test enrichment.
skills.name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing Use when two categorical classifications (e.g. dofi vs upfi splicing order) must be compared between a regulated set (DeltaPSI > 0.15, control PSI <= 0.2) and a matched control set to test enrichment. When the comparison variable is continuous (e.g. PSI or Fupfi distributions) rather than a dichotomous dofi/upfi class — use a distribution test (e.g. via Matt feature comparison) instead. When counts per cell of the contingency table are expected to be very small and an exact 2x2 assumption is violated; the article grounds this test only in the dofi/upfi class counts. When testing AISO constancy across tissues or species rather than enrichment within one contrast; the article treats AISO as remarkably constant, so no enrichment test applies there. http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Fisher's exact test on 2x2 contingency tables to assess enrichment of categorical splicing-order classes (upfi vs dofi) in a regulated exon set versus matched controls, as done to show 58% downstream-intron-first splicing among SRRM4-dependent neural microexons (P = 0.013). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Apply Fisher's exact test on 2x2 contingency tables to assess enrichment of categorical splicing-order classes (upfi vs dofi) in a regulated exon set versus matched controls, as done to show 58% downstream-intron-first splicing among SRRM4-dependent neural microexons (P = 0.013).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison variable is continuous (e.g. PSI or Fupfi distributions) rather than a dichotomous dofi/upfi class — use a distribution test (e.g. via Matt feature comparison) instead. When counts per cell of the contingency table are expected to be very small and an exact 2x2 assumption is violated; the article grounds this test only in the dofi/upfi class counts. When testing AISO constancy across tissues or species rather than enrichment within one contrast; the article treats AISO as remarkably constant, so no enrichment test applies there.

skills.description: Use when per-read or per-site m6A and m5C calls (e.g. CHEUI Model 2 output) are available and the question is whether transcripts co-carried by both modification types are enriched beyond chance, as opposed to within-read co-occurrence.
skills.name: fisher-exact-transcript-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-transcript-enrichment-testing Use when per-read or per-site m6A and m5C calls (e.g. CHEUI Model 2 output) are available and the question is whether transcripts co-carried by both modification types are enriched beyond chance, as opposed to within-read co-occurrence. When the question is read-level co-occurrence of two sites within single mRNA molecules — use the read-level overlap statistic instead; this test only assesses transcript-level co-enrichment. When site calls come from orthogonal methods (miCLIP/m6ACE-seq) without a filtered CHEUI Model 2 probability table — the contingency classes are defined by the strict CHEUI >0.9999 threshold. When testing enrichment of co-occurring sites at a specific genomic distance (1-15 nt) — that requires the distance-resolved observed-vs-expected permutation analysis, not a transcript-level contingency table. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether mRNAs carrying both m6A and m5C modification sites occur more often than expected under independence, by tabulating CHEUI-derived site calls into a 2x2 transcript-level contingency table (both / only m6A / only m5C / neither) and running a two-tailed Fisher's exact test. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Tests whether mRNAs carrying both m6A and m5C modification sites occur more often than expected under independence, by tabulating CHEUI-derived site calls into a 2x2 transcript-level contingency table (both / only m6A / only m5C / neither) and running a two-tailed Fisher's exact test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is read-level co-occurrence of two sites within single mRNA molecules — use the read-level overlap statistic instead; this test only assesses transcript-level co-enrichment. When site calls come from orthogonal methods (miCLIP/m6ACE-seq) without a filtered CHEUI Model 2 probability table — the contingency classes are defined by the strict CHEUI >0.9999 threshold. When testing enrichment of co-occurring sites at a specific genomic distance (1-15 nt) — that requires the distance-resolved observed-vs-expected permutation analysis, not a transcript-level contingency table.

skills.description: Use when comparing binary trait counts (e.g., inverted-Alu-positive vs. Alu-negative BSJs, tissue-specific isoform vs. gene) against a matched control set, and a 2x2 contingency table with scipy.stats.fisher_exact is appropriate.

skills.search_text: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing Use when comparing binary trait counts (e.g., inverted-Alu-positive vs. Alu-negative BSJs, tissue-specific isoform vs. gene) against a matched control set, and a 2x2 contingency table with scipy.stats.fisher_exact is appropriate. skills.summary: Two-sided and one-sided Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables used in the isoCirc paper to test whether known/novel back-splice junctions are enriched for inverted Alu repeats (p < 3.6e-50) and whether tissue-specific circRNA isoforms are enriched in tissue-specific parental genes (p < 2.2e-16).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Counts are not binary or the comparison involves more than two categories per variable (e.g., multi-tissue expression magnitude itself) — use tau index or chi-square/binomial criteria first, not Fisher's exact test directly No matched negative-control or background set is available, so a 2x2 enrichment table cannot be constructed Read-level or alignment-quality assessment of isoCirc data is the goal — that requires the isoCirc pipeline's stringent BSJ filtering rather than an enrichment test

skills.description: Use when filtering candidate SNV lists derived from single-molecule long reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) whose allele observations are significantly over-represented on one read strand prior to haplotype assembly or genotyping.
skills.name: fishers-exact-test-variant-quality-control
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-test-variant-quality-control Use when filtering candidate SNV lists derived from single-molecule long reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) whose allele observations are significantly over-represented on one read strand prior to haplotype assembly or genotyping. Input variants are already final genotype calls rather than candidate SNVs pending haplotype-informed genotyping — this filter is applied pre-genotyping in Longshot's pipeline The goal is structural variant discovery (e.g., Delly) rather than SNV candidate quality control Indel-only variant sets: Longshot only calls SNVs and the strand-bias filter targets SNV candidates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A strand-bias filter for candidate SNVs in error-prone long-read data: build a 2x2 ref/alt-by-forward/reverse-strand contingency table at each candidate site and drop variants whose two-tailed Fisher's exact test p-value is < 0.01 before haplotype-informed genotyping, countering context-specific Oxford Nanopore errors. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: A strand-bias filter for candidate SNVs in error-prone long-read data: build a 2x2 ref/alt-by-forward/reverse-strand contingency table at each candidate site and drop variants whose two-tailed Fisher's exact test p-value is < 0.01 before haplotype-informed genotyping, countering context-specific Oxford Nanopore errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input variants are already final genotype calls rather than candidate SNVs pending haplotype-informed genotyping — this filter is applied pre-genotyping in Longshot's pipeline The goal is structural variant discovery (e.g., Delly) rather than SNV candidate quality control Indel-only variant sets: Longshot only calls SNVs and the strand-bias filter targets SNV candidates

skills.search_text: fishers-exact-testing-of-splicing-order-ratios Use when you have categorical upfi/dofi (or Fupfi) counts from two sequencing modalities or conditions and need to formally test agreement of splicing-order proportions, e.g. validating a long-read bias correction against a short-read reference. When the goal is to compare full Fupfi distributions across many exons rather than aggregate upfi/dofi proportions — the ratio-level test masks per-exon differences When counts are not independent (e.g. replicate-level paired designs) — Fisher's Exact on pooled counts ignores sample structure When the long-read data are already the trusted reference (e.g. long reads span beyond the flanking introns, where short reads provide almost no splicing-order information) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Two-sided Fisher's Exact test on 2x2 contingency tables of upfi/dofi counts to test whether bias-corrected long-read AISO (adjacent intron splicing order) ratios agree with the short-read reference. In the Insplico paper this is the acceptance test for the --biascorr correction on Drexler ONT K562 data (corrected ratio 1.25 vs 1.41 for short reads, P = 0.48). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Two-sided Fisher's Exact test on 2x2 contingency tables of upfi/dofi counts to test whether bias-corrected long-read AISO (adjacent intron splicing order) ratios agree with the short-read reference. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to compare full Fupfi distributions across many exons rather than aggregate upfi/dofi proportions — the ratio-level test masks per-exon differences When counts are not independent (e.g. replicate-level paired designs) — Fisher's Exact on pooled counts ignores sample structure When the long-read data are already the trusted reference (e.g. long reads span beyond the flanking introns, where short reads provide almost no splicing-order information)

skills.search_text: frequency-dependent-selection-modeling Use when modeling frequency-dependent selection or evolutionary game theory dynamics — e.g., two strategies (hawks/doves) whose fitnesses depend on their proportions in the population and a specified pay-off matrix. The selection regime is constant (fitnesses do not depend on strategy frequencies) — use a standard deterministic or stochastic gene-frequency simulation instead of the hawk-dove game function. More than two strategies are involved; the surfaced workflow is built around the two-strategy hawk-dove interaction with a 2x2 pay-off matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_3945 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Simulates the hawk-dove evolutionary game in R using learnPopGen: given an initial hawk frequency and a user-specified pay-off matrix, iteratively updates hawk/dove frequencies through relative fitnesses until a frequency-dependent equilibrium is reached. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412
skills.summary: Simulates the hawk-dove evolutionary game in R using learnPopGen: given an initial hawk frequency and a user-specified pay-off matrix, iteratively updates hawk/dove frequencies through relative fitnesses until a frequency-dependent equilibrium is reached.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The selection regime is constant (fitnesses do not depend on strategy frequencies) — use a standard deterministic or stochastic gene-frequency simulation instead of the hawk-dove game function. skills.description: Use when batch-effect-corrected feature-level MTI data requires aligning per-marker intensity distributions: histograms have been computed over a shared global range and must be registered as functional curves before extracting normalization factors.

This is the middle stage of UniFORM's histogram -> registration -> normalization pipeline and yields the shift/scale factors applied downstream. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172

skills.search_text: functional-data-registration-of-intensity-histograms Use when integrating multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) data across samples/batches (CyCIF, ORION, COMET) where staining-intensity variation must be removed from right-skewed marker distributions that violate Z-score/ComBat assumptions. The question concerns gene frequency change under deterministic or stochastic population genetic processes (drift, selection at a locus) rather than strategic interaction payoffs — learnPopGen provides separate functions for those models The model requires more than two strategies or continuous phenotypic traits rather than a two-strategy hawk-dove game with a 2x2 pay-off matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Simulates frequency-dependent evolutionary game dynamics (e.g., the hawk-dove game) in R using learnPopGen: an initial frequency of hawks and a user-specified pay-off matrix are iterated so that hawks and doves interact in the proportions they occur and relative fitnesses determined by the pay-off matrix update strategy frequencies through time. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412

skills.description: Use when a long-read draft genome assembly (e.g. FASTA with gaps and base errors) needs polishing and gap-filling with available paired short reads, and alignment-based polishers like Pilon or Racon would be too memory-intensive.
skills.name: gap-filling-draft-genome-assemblies
skills.search_text: gap-filling-draft-genome-assemblies Use when a long-read draft genome assembly (e.g. FASTA with gaps and base errors) needs polishing and gap-filling with available paired short reads, and alignment-based polishers like Pilon or Racon would be too memory-intensive. Short-read-only assemblies or assemblies with no gaps/base errors to correct — the protocol is designed to finish long-read draft assemblies using short reads No short-read data is available — ntEdit and Sealer both rely on Bloom filters built from short-read k-mers Memory is not a constraint and alignment-based hybrid polishers such as Pilon or Racon are preferred for their information-rich alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Runs the ntEdit+Sealer Makefile protocol, which uses alignment-free, k-mer-based Bloom filters built from short reads (via ntHits and ABySS-Bloom) to first polish base errors and small indels with ntEdit and then fill assembly gaps and problematic regions with Sealer in a long-read draft assembly. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.442
skills.summary: Runs the ntEdit+Sealer Makefile protocol, which uses alignment-free, k-mer-based Bloom filters built from short reads (via ntHits and ABySS-Bloom) to first polish base errors and small indels with ntEdit and then fill assembly gaps and problematic regions with Sealer in a long-read draft assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short-read-only assemblies or assemblies with no gaps/base errors to correct — the protocol is designed to finish long-read draft assemblies using short reads No short-read data is available — ntEdit and Sealer both rely on Bloom filters built from short-read k-mers Memory is not a constraint and alignment-based hybrid polishers such as Pilon or Racon are preferred for their information-rich alignments

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing FMAlign2's MEM-filtering and partial-chain-formation step, or when deciding which local-alignment anchors are trustworthy for segmenting ultralong nucleotide sequences.

skills.search_text: gap-proportion-alignment-filtering Use when reconstructing or reimplementing FMAlign2's MEM-filtering and partial-chain-formation step, or when deciding which local-alignment anchors are trustworthy for segmenting ultralong nucleotide sequences. You only need the final MSA and do not care about the internal segmentation — just run FMAlign2 end-to-end rather than rebuilding the filtering stage The input is not ultralong nucleotide sequence data; FMAlign2 targets nucleotide sequences reaching billions in length, and MEM/SSW-chain segmentation is unnecessary for short, easy alignments A full global chain of MEMs across all sequences is required — this skill intentionally replaces FMAlign's global-chain search with partial chains http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 FMAlign2's Step 2 mechanism that filters maximal exact matches (MEMs) for colinearity, size, and sequence-coverage threshold c, then uses striped Smith–Waterman (SSW) local alignments — discarding any whose gap proportion exceeds 0.8 — to form partial chains for sequence segmentation. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae014

skills.search_text: gaussian-rate-sampling-model-parameterization Use when validating or benchmarking a kinetic-rate inference model (e.g. Nanodynamo/nano-ID) against ground-truth rates that must be known by construction, via controlled in silico simulation of RNA metabolic labelling data. The goal is to infer rates on real experimental Nanodynamo/nano-ID data (e.g. untreated or drug-treated TNBC cells) rather than validate the inference pipeline on synthetic data with known ground truth Only one replicate or a different labelling time is required — the benchmark design is specifically 2 replicates with a 20-min pulse The task requires quantifying RNA dynamics from Nanopore sequencing reads rather than simulating them http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate a simulated benchmark RNA-dynamics dataset by sampling synthesis, processing, export and degradation rates for 1000 genes from gaussian distributions anchored to INSPEcT 3T9 fibroblast medians with a coefficient of variation of 5, then simulate RNA species expression for 2 replicates with a 20-min metabolic labelling pulse and noise matched to untreated RNA species CVs. skills.description: Use when long Nanopore/PacBio reads must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome and annotated splice junctions from a Gencode GTF (e.g. v38, vM18) need to be converted into a BED file for minimap2's --junc-bed.
skills.name: gencode-gtf-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: gencode-gtf-annotation-parsing Use when long Nanopore/PacBio reads must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome and annotated splice junctions from a Gencode GTF (e.g. v38, vM18) need to be converted into a BED file for minimap2's --junc-bed. skills.search_text: genome-annotation-reconciliation Use when you have a StringTie (or similar) merged assembly GTF from hybrid RNA-seq data and an assembled reference genome with an NCBI annotation in GTF format, and need to reconcile gene models, classify coding vs lncRNA, and flag novel genes absent from the reference. The organism lacks an assembled genome or an NCBI-available annotation in GTF format — the pipeline requires both Input is raw reads rather than an assembled transcriptome GTF; assembly (e.g., StringTie with -p 1 -j 2 -c 2 -v -a 4) must happen first The goal is de novo gene prediction from genome alone (use BRAKER2/3 or MAKER), not reconciliation of an existing transcriptome assembly against a reference annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconcile a genome-guided StringTie transcriptome assembly against an existing GTF reference annotation (e.g., chicken galGal6 NCBI RefSeq) using the annotate_my_genosomes pipeline, producing a final_annotated.gtf with reconciled gene identities plus coding/lncRNA and novel-gene classification. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Reconcile a genome-guided StringTie transcriptome assembly against an existing GTF reference annotation (e.g., chicken galGal6 NCBI RefSeq) using the annotate_my_genosomes pipeline, producing a final_annotated.gtf with reconciled gene identities plus coding/lncRNA and novel-gene classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism lacks an assembled genome or an NCBI-available annotation in GTF format — the pipeline requires both Input is raw reads rather than an assembled transcriptome GTF; assembly (e.g., StringTie with -p 1 -j 2 -c 2 -v -a 4) must happen first The goal is de novo gene prediction from genome alone (use BRAKER2/3 or MAKER), not reconciliation of an existing transcriptome assembly against a reference annotation

skills.description: Use when a new genome assembly quality index (e.g., R-AQI/S-AQI) must be compared against existing metrics (LAI, QV, BUSCO, N50) over a panel of assemblies to prove redundancy or complementary information.
skills.name: genome-assembly-benchmarking-statistics
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-benchmarking-statistics Use when a new genome assembly quality index (e.g., R-AQI/S-AQI) must be compared against existing metrics (LAI, QV, BUSCO, N50) over a panel of assemblies to prove redundancy or complementary information. Assemblies lack the raw NGS short-reads and SMS long-reads needed to run CRAQ, so no R-AQI/S-AQI scores exist to correlate Genome assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels (polyploids), where CRAQ's evaluation may be less accurate than the benchmarked diploid cases The goal is de novo error detection or correction (CRE/CSE breakpoints, chimeric contig splitting) rather than aggregate metric benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks CRAQ's R-AQI and S-AQI assembly-quality indexes against established metrics (LAI, QV, BUSCO completeness, N50) by computing Pearson correlations (r2) across 40 publicly-available genome assemblies, demonstrating which quality dimensions each metric uniquely captures. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks CRAQ's R-AQI and S-AQI assembly-quality indexes against established metrics (LAI, QV, BUSCO completeness, N50) by computing Pearson correlations (r2) across 40 publicly-available genome assemblies, demonstrating which quality dimensions each metric uniquely captures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Assemblies lack the raw NGS short-reads and SMS long-reads needed to run CRAQ, so no R-AQI/S-AQI scores exist to correlate Genome assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels (polyploids), where CRAQ's evaluation may be less accurate than the benchmarked diploid cases The goal is de novo error detection or correction (CRE/CSE breakpoints, chimeric contig splitting) rather than aggregate metric benchmarking

skills.description: Use when comparing assemblies of the same organism produced by different assemblers (e.g., HASLR vs Canu on E. coli, yeast, C. elegans) and you need an ortholog-based completeness metric to supplement contiguity (NGA50) and misassembly counts.
skills.name: genome-assembly-completeness-assessment
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-completeness-assessment Use when comparing assemblies of the same organism produced by different assemblers (e.g., HASLR vs Canu on E. coli, yeast, C. elegans) and you need an ortholog-based completeness metric to supplement contiguity (NGA50) and misassembly counts. The goal is to measure contiguity or misassembly counts rather than gene completeness — use QUAST-like metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassemblies) instead. The organism has no close-matching BUSCO odb10 lineage database, so conserved ortholog classification would be unreliable. Assessment is of raw long reads or intermediate backbone graphs (e.g., backbone.05.superbubble.gfa) rather than a final polished assembly FASTA. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Benchmark gene completeness of hybrid-assembled genomes by running BUSCO in genome mode against lineage-specific odb10 databases, extracting the five percentage categories (complete, single-copy, duplicated, fragmented, missing) to compare assemblers such as HASLR against Canu, MaSuRCA, and PBcR. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Benchmark gene completeness of hybrid-assembled genomes by running BUSCO in genome mode against lineage-specific odb10 databases, extracting the five percentage categories (complete, single-copy, duplicated, fragmented, missing) to compare assemblers such as HASLR against Canu, MaSuRCA, and PBcR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to measure contiguity or misassembly counts rather than gene completeness — use QUAST-like metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassemblies) instead. The organism has no close-matching BUSCO odb10 lineage database, so conserved ortholog classification would be unreliable. Assessment is of raw long reads or intermediate backbone graphs (e.g., backbone.05.superbubble.gfa) rather than a final polished assembly FASTA.

skills.description: Use when you have a finished draft assembly (e.g. DBG2OLC_Consensus.fasta) plus a reference genome and need contiguity metrics (N50, NG50, contig count) or an error-rate estimate against the reference.
skills.name: genome-assembly-contiguity-and-error-evaluation
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-contiguity-and-error-evaluation Use when you have a finished draft assembly (e.g. DBG2OLC_Consensus.fasta) plus a reference genome and need contiguity metrics (N50, NG50, contig count) or an error-rate estimate against the reference. The pipeline's overlap-layout backbone has an unsatisfactory N50 and parameters still need tuning — the README says to check the N50 'otherwise keep tuning and don't proceed' rather than evaluate prematurely The input is raw reads rather than an assembled FASTA — AssemblyStatistics evaluates assemblies, not sequencing data Evaluate de novo genome assemblies for contiguity and base-level accuracy using AssemblyStatistics and QUAST, e.g. confirming that a DBG2OLC hybrid assembly of the E. coli Oxford Nanopore MinION dataset resolves to a single contig with a polished error rate near 0.23%. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Evaluate de novo genome assemblies for contiguity and base-level accuracy using AssemblyStatistics and QUAST, e.g. confirming that a DBG2OLC hybrid assembly of the E. coli Oxford Nanopore MinION dataset resolves to a single contig with a polished error rate near 0.23%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline's overlap-layout backbone has an unsatisfactory N50 and parameters still need tuning — the README says to check the N50 'otherwise keep tuning and don't proceed' rather than evaluate prematurely The input is raw reads rather than an assembled FASTA — AssemblyStatistics evaluates assemblies, not sequencing data

skills.description: Use when you have raw NGS and SMS reads plus a draft assembly (FASTA) and need to pinpoint misassemblies, regional indel errors, or misjoined contigs without a close reference genome.
skills.name: genome-assembly-error-detection
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-error-detection Use when you have raw NGS and SMS reads plus a draft assembly (FASTA) and need to pinpoint misassemblies, regional indel errors, or misjoined contigs without a close reference genome. Evaluating completeness (e.g., gene completeness) rather than error detection — use BUSCO instead Assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels than diploid, where CRAQ accuracy 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' When only one read type (short or long) is available, since CRAQ integrates both NGS and SMS mapping signals http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect regional (CREs) and structural (CSEs) errors in draft genome assemblies at single-nucleotide resolution using CRAQ, which maps NGS short reads and SMS long reads back to the assembly and exploits clipped-alignment signals, read coverage, and filtering of heterozygous loci. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Detect regional (CREs) and structural (CSEs) errors in draft genome assemblies at single-nucleotide resolution using CRAQ, which maps NGS short reads and SMS long reads back to the assembly and exploits clipped-alignment signals, read coverage, and filtering of heterozygous loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating completeness (e.g., gene completeness) rather than error detection — use BUSCO instead Assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels than diploid, where CRAQ accuracy 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases presented here' When only one read type (short or long) is available, since CRAQ integrates both NGS and SMS mapping signals

skills.description: Use when configuring the ntEdit+Sealer Makefile pipeline: ntCard k-mer frequency histograms are available for the protocol's k-mer sizes (e.g. k=80, k=65, k=50) and a Bloom filter size (b) must be chosen for ABySS-Bloom.
skills.name: genome-assembly-finishing-parameter-selection
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-finishing-parameter-selection Use when configuring the ntEdit+Sealer Makefile pipeline: ntCard k-mer frequency histograms are available for the protocol's k-mer sizes (e.g. k=80, k=65, k=50) and a Bloom filter size (b) must be chosen for ABySS-Bloom. No short-read data or ntCard histograms are available — n cannot be estimated and the Bloom filter would be sized arbitrarily The task is hybrid polishing with alignment-based tools (e.g. Pilon, Racon) where memory-intensive read alignments, not Bloom filters, are used A draft long-read assembly for gap filling/polishing does not exist, since k and b are parameters of the ntEdit+Sealer finishing pipeline specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Selects optimal k-mer lengths (k) and Bloom filter size (b) for the ntEdit+Sealer alignment-free finishing protocol by computing k-mer cardinality from ntCard histograms and applying the Bloom filter sizing formula m = Ceil(−n/ln(1−f)) at a target false-positive rate (f ≈ 0.005). genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.442
skills.summary: Selects optimal k-mer lengths (k) and Bloom filter size (b) for the ntEdit+Sealer alignment-free finishing protocol by computing k-mer cardinality from ntCard histograms and applying the Bloom filter sizing formula m = Ceil(−n/ln(1−f)) at a target false-positive rate (f ≈ 0.005).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No short-read data or ntCard histograms are available — n cannot be estimated and the Bloom filter would be sized arbitrarily The task is hybrid polishing with alignment-based tools (e.g. Pilon, Racon) where memory-intensive read alignments, not Bloom filters, are used A draft long-read assembly for gap filling/polishing does not exist, since k and b are parameters of the ntEdit+Sealer finishing pipeline specifically

skills.description: Use when comparing scaffolding-graph construction methods or scaffolders on real read data and you need a reference-based F-score/error table plus coverage-correlation diagnostics to decide which builder wins.
skills.name: genome-assembly-fscore-evaluation
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-fscore-evaluation Use when comparing scaffolding-graph construction methods or scaffolders on real read data and you need a reference-based F-score/error table plus coverage-correlation diagnostics to decide which builder wins. No reference genome is available for the assembled organism, since F-score and error counts are computed relative to a reference The question is scaffolding-graph construction itself (running FAST-SG.pl or an aligner) rather than benchmarking/scoring the resulting scaffolds Evaluating gap-size estimation with long-range mate-pair technologies (10X Genomics, DOVETAIL), where linking information spans a range of insert sizes and read-pair orientation may be unknown, complicating error attribution http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmarks scaffolding graphs and scaffold outputs by computing F-score and error counts against a reference genome, then aggregating per-genome results (e.g., four genomes x five graph-construction methods) into tables plus Pearson correlations of contig read-coverage. This is how Fast-SG demonstrated that its alignment-free scaffolding graph beats Bowtie, Bowtie2, BWA, and BWA-MEM-built graphs. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Benchmarks scaffolding graphs and scaffold outputs by computing F-score and error counts against a reference genome, then aggregating per-genome results (e.g., four genomes x five graph-construction methods) into tables plus Pearson correlations of contig read-coverage. This is how Fast-SG demonstrated that its alignment-free scaffolding graph beats Bowtie, Bowtie2, BWA, and BWA-MEM-built graphs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available for the assembled organism, since F-score and error counts are computed relative to a reference The question is scaffolding-graph construction itself (running FAST-SG.pl or an aligner) rather than benchmarking/scoring the resulting scaffolds Evaluating gap-size estimation with long-range mate-pair technologies (10X Genomics, DOVETAIL), where linking information spans a range of insert sizes and read-pair orientation may be unknown, complicating error attribution

skills.description: Use when a draft genome assembly (e.g., an ABySS or long-read assembler draft FASTA) plus a matching long-read dataset (e.g., FASTQ/FASTA such as SRR10028109) is available and misassembly detection/cutting is needed without full read alignments.
skills.name: genome-assembly-misassembly-correction
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-misassembly-correction Use when a draft genome assembly (e.g., an ABySS or long-read assembler draft FASTA) plus a matching long-read dataset (e.g., FASTQ/FASTA such as SRR10028109) is available and misassembly detection/cutting is needed without full read alignments. The goal is scaffolding (ordering/orienting contigs and gap-filling) rather than cutting misassemblies — use ntLink's Basic Protocols 1–3 instead. Only a polished, reference-validated assembly is available with no long-read data to re-map, so no mapping-discrepancy windows can be computed. The draft was not built from (or is not compatible with) the available long reads; ntLink mappings require long reads that span the assembly contigs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Corrects putative misassemblies in a long-read genome assembly draft by running Tigmint-long on minimizer-based ntLink mappings of long reads to contigs, cutting the draft at windows of mapping discrepancy, and validating the corrected FASTA with QUAST. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Corrects putative misassemblies in a long-read genome assembly draft by running Tigmint-long on minimizer-based ntLink mappings of long reads to contigs, cutting the draft at windows of mapping discrepancy, and validating the corrected FASTA with QUAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scaffolding (ordering/orienting contigs and gap-filling) rather than cutting misassemblies — use ntLink's Basic Protocols 1–3 instead. Only a polished, reference-validated assembly is available with no long-read data to re-map, so no mapping-discrepancy windows can be computed. The draft was not built from (or is not compatible with) the available long reads; ntLink mappings require long reads that span the assembly contigs.

skills.description: Use when a draft long-read genome assembly (e.g. FASTA such as ecoli_shasta.fa) needs base-error correction, small-indel repair, and gap filling using paired short reads (.fq.gz), and alignment-based polishers are too memory-intensive.
skills.name: genome-assembly-polishing
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-polishing Use when a draft long-read genome assembly (e.g. FASTA such as ecoli_shasta.fa) needs base-error correction, small-indel repair, and gap filling using paired short reads (.fq.gz), and alignment-based polishers are too memory-intensive. The input is already a polished, finished assembly with no gaps or base errors to correct — the protocol's ntEdit and Sealer stages would have nothing to resolve. Only long reads are available with no short-read data — the Bloom filters are built from short-read k-mers via ntHits and ABySS-Bloom, so the protocol cannot run without them. A read-alignment-based polisher is preferred and the genome is small enough that alignment memory requirements are not a constraint (the protocol targets memory scalability). http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 An alignment-free, k-mer-based genome finishing protocol (ntEdit+Sealer) that polishes a draft long-read assembly with short reads using memory-efficient Bloom filters built by ntHits and ABySS-Bloom, then gap-fills with Sealer. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.442
skills.summary: An alignment-free, k-mer-based genome finishing protocol (ntEdit+Sealer) that polishes a draft long-read assembly with short reads using memory-efficient Bloom filters built by ntHits and ABySS-Bloom, then gap-fills with Sealer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a polished, finished assembly with no gaps or base errors to correct — the protocol's ntEdit and Sealer stages would have nothing to resolve. Only long reads are available with no short-read data — the Bloom filters are built from short-read k-mers via ntHits and ABySS-Bloom, so the protocol cannot run without them. A read-alignment-based polisher is preferred and the genome is small enough that alignment memory requirements are not a constraint (the protocol targets memory scalability).

skills.description: Use when comparing genome assemblies from different assemblers on the same datasets and you need contiguity/accuracy metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassemblies) plus wall-clock runtime and peak memory to rank tools.
skills.name: genome-assembly-qc-metrics-interpretation
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-qc-metrics-interpretation Use when comparing genome assemblies from different assemblers on the same datasets and you need contiguity/accuracy metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassemblies) plus wall-clock runtime and peak memory to rank tools. Input is a single assembly with no comparator — there is no benchmark table to produce and per-tool runtime/memory ranking is meaningless The task is polishing/consensus correction (e.g. Pilon/Racon) rather than cross-assembler quality comparison Long reads are high-accuracy (HiFi/Q20) or ultra-long ONT, which are outside the HASLR benchmark's error-prone PacBio CLR / standard ONT scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluate de novo genome assemblies with QUAST to obtain contiguity and accuracy metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassemblies) and pair them with runtime, peak memory, and tool-failure records to rank competing assemblers. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Evaluate de novo genome assemblies with QUAST to obtain contiguity and accuracy metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassemblies) and pair them with runtime, peak memory, and tool-failure records to rank competing assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single assembly with no comparator — there is no benchmark table to produce and per-tool runtime/memory ranking is meaningless The task is polishing/consensus correction (e.g. Pilon/Racon) rather than cross-assembler quality comparison Long reads are high-accuracy (HiFi/Q20) or ultra-long ONT, which are outside the HASLR benchmark's error-prone PacBio CLR / standard ONT scope

skills.description: Use when you have a draft long-read assembly and its polished/finished counterpart (e.g. ntEdit+Sealer output) plus a reference genome, and need to quantify mismatches and indels per 100 kbp to confirm polishing improved accuracy.
skills.name: genome-assembly-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-quality-assessment Use when you have a draft long-read assembly and its polished/finished counterpart (e.g. ntEdit+Sealer output) plus a reference genome, and need to quantify mismatches and indels per 100 kbp to confirm polishing improved accuracy. No reference genome is available for the organism, since the mismatch/indel accuracy metrics here are reference-based The input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled FASTA contigs/scaffolds — polishing and finishing (ntEdit+Sealer) should run first You need to evaluate features beyond base accuracy/indels that require the full (non --fast) QUAST mode, e.g. detailed structural variant analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assess the base accuracy and indel error rates of draft versus ntEdit+Sealer-polished genome assemblies using QUAST reference-based evaluation against the E. coli K-12 MG1655 (GCF_000005845.2) reference. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.442
skills.summary: Assess the base accuracy and indel error rates of draft versus ntEdit+Sealer-polished genome assemblies using QUAST reference-based evaluation against the E. coli K-12 MG1655 (GCF_000005845.2) reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available for the organism, since the mismatch/indel accuracy metrics here are reference-based The input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled FASTA contigs/scaffolds — polishing and finishing (ntEdit+Sealer) should run first You need to evaluate features beyond base accuracy/indels that require the full (non --fast) QUAST mode, e.g. detailed structural variant analysis

skills.description: Use when CRAQ output exists as CRE breakpoint files (e.g., locER_out/out_final.CRE.bed) and CSE breakpoint files (strER_out/out_final.CSE.bed) plus total assembly size, and per-fragment or whole-assembly quality scores are needed.
skills.name: genome-assembly-quality-classification
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-quality-classification Use when CRAQ output exists as CRE breakpoint files (e.g., locER_out/out_final.CRE.bed) and CSE breakpoint files (strER_out/out_final.CSE.bed) plus total assembly size, and per-fragment or whole-assembly quality scores are needed. The target genome is polyploid — CRAQ's error detection and AQI accuracy are not established for higher ploidy levels beyond the benchmarked diploid cases. Only raw sequencing reads are available with no classified CRE/CSE breakpoints — read mapping, clipping-based error calling (Minimap2/SAMtools filtering), and CRE/CSE classification must be completed before scoring. Transforms CRAQ-detected CRE/CSE error counts into sliding-window normalized values and computes regional (R-AQI) and structural (S-AQI) assembly quality indexes, then classifies assembly quality into reference/high/draft/low classes using published AQI thresholds. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Transforms CRAQ-detected CRE/CSE error counts into sliding-window normalized values and computes regional (R-AQI) and structural (S-AQI) assembly quality indexes, then classifies assembly quality into reference/high/draft/low classes using published AQI thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target genome is polyploid — CRAQ's error detection and AQI accuracy are not established for higher ploidy levels beyond the benchmarked diploid cases. Only raw sequencing reads are available with no classified CRE/CSE breakpoints — read mapping, clipping-based error calling (Minimap2/SAMtools filtering), and CRE/CSE classification must be completed before scoring.

skills.description: Use when you have multiple assembly versions (e.g. uncorrected long-read, consensus-corrected, polished, and an Illumina draft) and need to quantify sequence-composition convergence or expose platform-specific k-mer biases.
skills.name: genome-assembly-quality-comparison
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-quality-comparison Use when you have multiple assembly versions (e.g. uncorrected long-read, consensus-corrected, polished, and an Illumina draft) and need to quantify sequence-composition convergence or expose platform-specific k-mer biases. You need positional or structural accuracy metrics (N50, misassemblies, optical-map agreement) rather than sequence-composition comparison — this skill compares global 6-mer frequencies only and cannot judge scaffold contiguity or structural correctness. You need reference-guided base-level validation: the article notes that 'In the absence of a high-quality reference, it is not straightforward to establish which assembly is correct' at individual error sites; k-mer composition can only reveal systematic biases, not site-specific correctness. The assemblies differ so much in size or coverage that normalized 6-mer frequencies are no longer comparable (sparse profiles from very low-coverage assemblies will dominate correlation results). http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies how correction stages (TULIP → Racon → Pilon) move a long-read assembly toward a reference-quality draft by comparing canonical 6-mer frequency profiles with Jellyfish and pairwise Pearson correlations, revealing platform-specific biases such as homopolymer underrepresentation in nanopore data and high-CG underrepresentation in Illumina data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Quantifies how correction stages (TULIP → Racon → Pilon) move a long-read assembly toward a reference-quality draft by comparing canonical 6-mer frequency profiles with Jellyfish and pairwise Pearson correlations, revealing platform-specific biases such as homopolymer underrepresentation in nanopore data and high-CG underrepresentation in Illumina data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need positional or structural accuracy metrics (N50, misassemblies, optical-map agreement) rather than sequence-composition comparison — this skill compares global 6-mer frequencies only and cannot judge scaffold contiguity or structural correctness. You need reference-guided base-level validation: the article notes that 'In the absence of a high-quality reference, it is not straightforward to establish which assembly is correct' at individual error sites; k-mer composition can only reveal systematic biases, not site-specific correctness. The assemblies differ so much in size or coverage that normalized 6-mer frequencies are no longer comparable (sparse profiles from very low-coverage assemblies will dominate correlation results).

skills.description: Use when a scaffolded or gap-filled assembly must be validated against a baseline assembly — e.g. to check that gap-filling reduced Ns per 100 kbp while maintaining NG50 — and contig-level vs scaffold-level statistics must be separated.
skills.name: genome-assembly-statistics-evaluation
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-statistics-evaluation Use when a scaffolded or gap-filled assembly must be validated against a baseline assembly — e.g. to check that gap-filling reduced Ns per 100 kbp while maintaining NG50 — and contig-level vs scaffold-level statistics must be separated. The input is raw reads or a read-to-assembly alignment rather than an assembled FASTA — statistics evaluation requires assembled contig/scaffold sequences. The goal is scaffolding or gap-filling itself rather than evaluating its output — use ntLink directly instead of this evaluation skill. Only scaffold-level statistics are needed and contig-vs-scaffold separation is irrelevant — plain abyss-fac alone may suffice without QUAST --split-scaffold. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluates genome assembly contiguity and correctness after scaffolding/gap-filling by computing N-content and NG50/NGA50 statistics with abyss-fac and QUAST --split-scaffold, as done in the ntLink Basic Protocol 2 (C. elegans ONT data). genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Evaluates genome assembly contiguity and correctness after scaffolding/gap-filling by computing N-content and NG50/NGA50 statistics with abyss-fac and QUAST --split-scaffold, as done in the ntLink Basic Protocol 2 (C. elegans ONT data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw reads or a read-to-assembly alignment rather than an assembled FASTA — statistics evaluation requires assembled contig/scaffold sequences. The goal is scaffolding or gap-filling itself rather than evaluating its output — use ntLink directly instead of this evaluation skill. Only scaffold-level statistics are needed and contig-vs-scaffold separation is irrelevant — plain abyss-fac alone may suffice without QUAST --split-scaffold.

skills.description: Use when a draft genome assembly (e.g., a FASTA contig set like the ABySS C. elegans assembly celegans-abyss.fa) and long reads (e.g., SRR10028109 FASTQ) must be turned into read-to-contig PAF mappings for scaffolding or misassembly detection without running a full scaffolding protocol.
skills.name: genome-assembly-target-read-preparation
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-target-read-preparation Use when a draft genome assembly (e.g., a FASTA contig set like the ABySS C. elegans assembly celegans-abyss.fa) and long reads (e.g., SRR10028109 FASTQ) must be turned into read-to-contig PAF mappings for scaffolding or misassembly detection without running a full scaffolding protocol. A complete scaffolded assembly is the goal — use ntLink's full scaffolding protocols (Basic Protocols 1–3 with overlap detection, gap-filling, or in-code iterations) rather than mapping-only pair mode The input mappings are already available in PAF format (e.g., from a prior ntLink run) — proceed directly to the downstream step such as Tigmint-long correction (Alternate Protocol 2) High-accuracy base-level alignment is required rather than lightweight minimizer-based mappings, e.g., for polishing workflows where full read alignments are preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Prepares a draft genome assembly target and long-read sequencing data for ntLink-based read-to-contig mapping, leveraging ntLink's minimizer-based mapping mode as a standalone alternative to alignment tools like minimap2, producing PAF-formatted mappings for downstream applications such as Tigmint-long misassembly correction. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Prepares a draft genome assembly target and long-read sequencing data for ntLink-based read-to-contig mapping, leveraging ntLink's minimizer-based mapping mode as a standalone alternative to alignment tools like minimap2, producing PAF-formatted mappings for downstream applications such as Tigmint-long misassembly correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A complete scaffolded assembly is the goal — use ntLink's full scaffolding protocols (Basic Protocols 1–3 with overlap detection, gap-filling, or in-code iterations) rather than mapping-only pair mode The input mappings are already available in PAF format (e.g., from a prior ntLink run) — proceed directly to the downstream step such as Tigmint-long correction (Alternate Protocol 2) High-accuracy base-level alignment is required rather than lightweight minimizer-based mappings, e.g., for polishing workflows where full read alignments are preferred

skills.description: Use when two de novo assemblies of the same genome (e.g. a new long-read assembly and a published short-read draft such as NCBI WGS AZBK01) must be compared to find unmatched scaffolds and validate structural improvement.
skills.name: genome-assembly-whole-genome-alignment
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-whole-genome-alignment Use when two de novo assemblies of the same genome (e.g. a new long-read assembly and a published short-read draft such as NCBI WGS AZBK01) must be compared to find unmatched scaffolds and validate structural improvement. When only a single assembly is available and the goal is quality assessment (use N50/QUAST-style metrics instead of reciprocal alignment). When reads, not assemblies, need to be aligned to a reference (use BWA MEM or minimap2 read mapping, not nucmer assembly-to-assembly comparison). Whole-genome alignment workflow that compares two genome assemblies (here the uncorrected TULIP nanopore assembly vs. the 2012 Illumina-based AZBK01 draft of A. anguilla) with MUMmer nucmer, delta-filter, and mummerplot to reveal sequence present in one assembly but absent from the other. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Whole-genome alignment workflow that compares two genome assemblies (here the uncorrected TULIP nanopore assembly vs. the 2012 Illumina-based AZBK01 draft of A. anguilla) with MUMmer nucmer, delta-filter, and mummerplot to reveal sequence present in one assembly but absent from the other.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single assembly is available and the goal is quality assessment (use N50/QUAST-style metrics instead of reciprocal alignment). When reads, not assemblies, need to be aligned to a reference (use BWA MEM or minimap2 read mapping, not nucmer assembly-to-assembly comparison).

skills.description: Use when a set of candidate modified k-mers (seq_set) from ONT reads must be scored for over-representation against a reference genome to extract methylation motifs de novo.
skills.name: genome-background-motif-comparison
skills.search_text: genome-background-motif-comparison Use when a set of candidate modified k-mers (seq_set) from ONT reads must be scored for over-representation against a reference genome to extract methylation motifs de novo. The goal is per-read modified-base calling with pre-trained models (e.g. Tombo alternative model) rather than de novo motif enrichment No suitable reference genome is available to serve as the negative background for enrichment statistics Motifs are already known and only need verification rather than de novo discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Computes chi-squared enrichment statistics for candidate k-mers from a Nanopore-derived seq_set against a reference genome used as negative background, driving Snapper's greedy position-specific motif enrichment for methylation motif discovery. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Computes chi-squared enrichment statistics for candidate k-mers from a Nanopore-derived seq_set against a reference genome used as negative background, driving Snapper's greedy position-specific motif enrichment for methylation motif discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-read modified-base calling with pre-trained models (e.g. Tombo alternative model) rather than de novo motif enrichment No suitable reference genome is available to serve as the negative background for enrichment statistics Motifs are already known and only need verification rather than de novo discovery

skills.description: Use when candidate bins have been produced from long-read contig embeddings (e.g., per-epsilon DBSCAN outputs in SemiBin2) and each bin must be scored for completeness, contamination, and F1 before greedy ensemble selection.
skills.name: genome-completeness-contamination-assessment
skills.search_text: genome-completeness-contamination-assessment Use when candidate bins have been produced from long-read contig embeddings (e.g., per-epsilon DBSCAN outputs in SemiBin2) and each bin must be scored for completeness, contamination, and F1 before greedy ensemble selection. Binning short-read samples with the standard (non-ensemble) SemiBin2 pipeline, where DBSCAN is run without the multi-epsilon ensemble and greedy selection Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs that have not yet been clustered into candidate bins — marker-gene scoring requires bins as input Taxonomic annotation of bins is the goal (use CAT/BAT instead); this skill only estimates completeness/contamination http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Scores candidate metagenomic bins (MAGs) for completeness and contamination using 107 prokaryotic single-copy marker genes (via hmmer), and combines the two into an F1-score per Eq. 4 of SemiBin2 for ranking bins during ensemble DBSCAN clustering of long-read data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209
skills.summary: Scores candidate metagenomic bins (MAGs) for completeness and contamination using 107 prokaryotic single-copy marker genes (via hmmer), and combines the two into an F1-score per Eq. 4 of SemiBin2 for ranking bins during ensemble DBSCAN clustering of long-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Binning short-read samples with the standard (non-ensemble) SemiBin2 pipeline, where DBSCAN is run without the multi-epsilon ensemble and greedy selection Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs that have not yet been clustered into candidate bins — marker-gene scoring requires bins as input Taxonomic annotation of bins is the goal (use CAT/BAT instead); this skill only estimates completeness/contamination

skills.description: Use when variant records carry gene assignments but lack genomic coordinates, and you must annotate each gene/variant with chromosome, start, and end positions to build Circos histogram/scatter/highlight inputs.
skills.name: genome-coordinate-annotation-via-ensembl-api
skills.search_text: genome-coordinate-annotation-via-ensembl-api Use when variant records carry gene assignments but lack genomic coordinates, and you must annotate each gene/variant with chromosome, start, and end positions to build Circos histogram/scatter/highlight inputs. Variant records already carry complete chromosome, start, and end coordinates for all genes, so no external coordinate lookup is needed The goal is plotting rather than coordinate annotation — the downstream Circos rendering step is a separate skill The organism/reference is not covered by Ensembl gene annotations (JWES uses the human reference genome hg38) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Retrieves chromosome numbers and start/end coordinates for genes and variants (from snpEff-annotated VCF records or SQL-queried variant records) using the Ensembl API, so per-gene variant counts and genomic positions can be aggregated into Circos-format track files for the JWES visualization module. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261
skills.summary: Retrieves chromosome numbers and start/end coordinates for genes and variants (from snpEff-annotated VCF records or SQL-queried variant records) using the Ensembl API, so per-gene variant counts and genomic positions can be aggregated into Circos-format track files for the JWES visualization module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variant records already carry complete chromosome, start, and end coordinates for all genes, so no external coordinate lookup is needed The goal is plotting rather than coordinate annotation — the downstream Circos rendering step is a separate skill The organism/reference is not covered by Ensembl gene annotations (JWES uses the human reference genome hg38)

skills.description: Use when you have a genome-guided annotated GTF (e.g. annotate_my_genomes final_annotated.gtf) and need to isolate all transcripts of one gene locus for isoform or protein-level verification.
skills.name: genome-coordinate-based-gene-locus-retrieval
skills.search_text: genome-coordinate-based-gene-locus-retrieval Use when you have a genome-guided annotated GTF (e.g. annotate_my_genomes final_annotated.gtf) and need to isolate all transcripts of one gene locus for isoform or protein-level verification. The input is a raw StringTie or gffcompare GTF without reconciled gene_id attributes and reference-coordinate context — run it through annotate_my_genomes first No reference genome or NCBI GTF annotation is available for the organism, since the pipeline approach assumes an assembled genome and NCBI-available GTF annotation The goal is genome-wide annotation quality assessment (F1/precision/recall benchmarking) rather than retrieval of a single locus http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts all transcript/exon records for a target gene (e.g. the chicken SSPO/SCO-spondin locus) from an annotated GTF by combining gene_id matching with genomic coordinate overlap filtering, enabling downstream isoform-level validation (exon counts, CDS/protein extraction). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Extracts all transcript/exon records for a target gene (e.g. the chicken SSPO/SCO-spondin locus) from an annotated GTF by combining gene_id matching with genomic coordinate overlap filtering, enabling downstream isoform-level validation (exon counts, CDS/protein extraction).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw StringTie or gffcompare GTF without reconciled gene_id attributes and reference-coordinate context — run it through annotate_my_genomes first No reference genome or NCBI GTF annotation is available for the organism, since the pipeline approach assumes an assembled genome and NCBI-available GTF annotation The goal is genome-wide annotation quality assessment (F1/precision/recall benchmarking) rather than retrieval of a single locus

skills.description: Use when long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) fecal or environmental metagenomes need per-sample genome-copy normalization, e.g. to convert ARG read counts into cpg within the Argo profiling pipeline.
skills.name: genome-copy-estimation-from-metagenomes
skills.search_text: genome-copy-estimation-from-metagenomes Use when long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) fecal or environmental metagenomes need per-sample genome-copy normalization, e.g. to convert ARG read counts into cpg within the Argo profiling pipeline. Samples with insufficient coverage — normalization is unstable and read clustering for taxonomic classification is hindered Extremely rare species whose abundance falls below 1x genome copy — Argo will mark their ARGs 'unclassified' rather than estimate them Short-read metagenomes or de novo discovery of ARG genomic contexts in new, understudied environments — Argo is reference-based and long-read-only; assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) approaches are better suited http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Estimates per-sample prokaryotic genome copies (cells) from quality-controlled long-read metagenomes — via Melon with Kraken2 PlusPF pre-filtering of non-prokaryotic reads — so that Argo can express ARG counts as copies per genome (cpg). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Estimates per-sample prokaryotic genome copies (cells) from quality-controlled long-read metagenomes — via Melon with Kraken2 PlusPF pre-filtering of non-prokaryotic reads — so that Argo can express ARG counts as copies per genome (cpg).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with insufficient coverage — normalization is unstable and read clustering for taxonomic classification is hindered Extremely rare species whose abundance falls below 1x genome copy — Argo will mark their ARGs 'unclassified' rather than estimate them Short-read metagenomes or de novo discovery of ARG genomic contexts in new, understudied environments — Argo is reference-based and long-read-only; assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) approaches are better suited

skills.description: Use when selecting or validating sparse short seed fragments (e.g. 270 bp or 285 bp FASTA seeds) for a long-read scaffolding pipeline and you need to report or target a specific genome coverage.
skills.name: genome-coverage-estimation-from-seed-sets
skills.search_text: genome-coverage-estimation-from-seed-sets Use when selecting or validating sparse short seed fragments (e.g. 270 bp or 285 bp FASTA seeds) for a long-read scaffolding pipeline and you need to report or target a specific genome coverage. Seed sequences within a file vary in length or use non-numeric/duplicated identifiers, violating TULIP's strict requirements No independent genome size estimate is available, so coverage cannot be computed (or only by inventing a genome size) The goal is read coverage of raw sequencing data rather than coverage represented by a sparse, deliberately non-repetitive seed set http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Estimates the effective genome coverage of a sparse seed set for TULIP assembly by dividing the number of seed fragments of a fixed length by the k-mer-estimated genome size, as done for the European eel where 5,019,778 × 270 bp seeds gave 1.58x and 873,058 × 285 bp seeds gave 0.29x coverage of the ~860 Mbp genome. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Estimates the effective genome coverage of a sparse seed set for TULIP assembly by dividing the number of seed fragments of a fixed length by the k-mer-estimated genome size, as done for the European eel where 5,019,778 × 270 bp seeds gave 1.58x and 873,058 × 285 bp seeds gave 0.29x coverage of the ~860 Mbp genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Seed sequences within a file vary in length or use non-numeric/duplicated identifiers, violating TULIP's strict requirements No independent genome size estimate is available, so coverage cannot be computed (or only by inventing a genome size) The goal is read coverage of raw sequencing data rather than coverage represented by a sparse, deliberately non-repetitive seed set

The organism of interest lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI GTF annotation, since the downstream pipeline is restricted to such organisms You only need a de novo transcriptome without a reference genome guide, as this skill is explicitly genome-guided Your input is already an assembled transcriptome GTF from StringTie — proceed directly to annotation (annotate-my-genomes) rather than re-assembling http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assembles a genome-guided transcriptome from hybrid PacBio + Illumina RNA-seq alignments by merging coordinate-sorted BAM files against the galGal6 (GCA_000002315.5) reference and running StringTie with fixed parameters (-p 1 -j 2 -c 2 -v -a 4), producing a GTF used for downstream annotation with annotate_my_genomes. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
