skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism of interest lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI GTF annotation, since the downstream pipeline is restricted to such organisms You only need a de novo transcriptome without a reference genome guide, as this skill is explicitly genome-guided Your input is already an assembled transcriptome GTF from StringTie — proceed directly to annotation (annotate-my-genomes) rather than re-assembling

skills.description: Use when a VCF of SNPs/indels has been imported into CNVpytor and heterozygous BAF dispersion shows outliers from misalignment or reference problems; the mask filter removes non-P-region variants before BAF-based calling.
skills.name: genome-mask-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: genome-mask-variant-filtering Use when a VCF of SNPs/indels has been imported into CNVpytor and heterozygous BAF dispersion shows outliers from misalignment or reference problems; the mask filter removes non-P-region variants before BAF-based calling. The analysis only uses read depth without SNP/BAF evidence, so heterozygous-SNP contamination cannot affect results (masking is done via -mask_snps on imported VCF variants) Variants were not imported from a VCF into the .pytor file, or the sample is non-human / not alignable to the GRCh37/GRCh38 reference builds for which the 1000 Genomes mask applies Calling somatic CNAs with the prototype joint caller, where a more accurate mask-free approach is still under development http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Filters imported SNP variants to those falling in 'P' (passed) regions of the 1000 Genomes Project strict mask, removing ~22% of variants whose heterozygous BAF values are false positives caused by systematic misalignment, incomplete reference, or site-specific sequencing noise. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Filters imported SNP variants to those falling in 'P' (passed) regions of the 1000 Genomes Project strict mask, removing ~22% of variants whose heterozygous BAF values are false positives caused by systematic misalignment, incomplete reference, or site-specific sequencing noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only uses read depth without SNP/BAF evidence, so heterozygous-SNP contamination cannot affect results (masking is done via -mask_snps on imported VCF variants) Variants were not imported from a VCF into the .pytor file, or the sample is non-human / not alignable to the GRCh37/GRCh38 reference builds for which the 1000 Genomes mask applies Calling somatic CNAs with the prototype joint caller, where a more accurate mask-free approach is still under development

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether methylation-based read phasing extends SNV-only phasing on ONT R9/R10 autosomal data — e.g., reproducing HG002 R9 coverage-sweep N50 fold improvements at 30X/60X/80X with switch-error accounting.
skills.name: genome-phasing-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: genome-phasing-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating whether methylation-based read phasing extends SNV-only phasing on ONT R9/R10 autosomal data — e.g., reproducing HG002 R9 coverage-sweep N50 fold improvements at 30X/60X/80X with switch-error accounting. Phasing or benchmarking on sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females yields inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, so X/Y are excluded Data with high SNV-phasing error (e.g., very high hamming distance in R9 80x) or < 30X coverage — SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above ~30X, and MethPhaser depends on the accuracy of the initial SNV phasing Very short reads (e.g., 12–15 kbp N50 patient blood samples) where initially small phase blocks limit improvement Benchmark and evaluate methylation-assisted long-read haplotype phasing (e.g., MethPhaser) against an SNV-only baseline on ONT data, quantifying phase block N50 fold improvements and switch-error increases at multiple coverage levels. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Benchmark and evaluate methylation-assisted long-read haplotype phasing (e.g., MethPhaser) against an SNV-only baseline on ONT data, quantifying phase block N50 fold improvements and switch-error increases at multiple coverage levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Phasing or benchmarking on sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females yields inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, so X/Y are excluded Data with high SNV-phasing error (e.g., very high hamming distance in R9 80x) or < 30X coverage — SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above ~30X, and MethPhaser depends on the accuracy of the initial SNV phasing Very short reads (e.g., 12–15 kbp N50 patient blood samples) where initially small phase blocks limit improvement

skills.search_text: genome-polishing-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing the computational cost of polishing tools on the same HiFi-assembled genomes, or when reproducing the reported ~1-5x (real data) and ~10x (simulated data) speedup of NextPolish2 over alternative pipelines such as Racon + Merfin (RM). When the goal is accuracy evaluation (QV, overcorrection, switch errors) rather than computational cost — use Merqury/DeepVariant/Paftools.js-based evaluation workflows instead When the input assemblies are not HiFi-derived T2T/high-quality drafts and no >=60X short reads exist to build yak k-mer datasets, since NextPolish2 performance relies heavily on short-read k-mers http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmarks wall-clock runtime and peak memory of genome polishing tools (NextPolish2 vs NextPolish, or NextPolish2 vs Racon+Merfin) on identical HiFi assemblies, using speedup and memory ratios as comparison metrics. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Benchmarks wall-clock runtime and peak memory of genome polishing tools (NextPolish2 vs NextPolish, or NextPolish2 vs Racon+Merfin) on identical HiFi assemblies, using speedup and memory ratios as comparison metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accuracy evaluation (QV, overcorrection, switch errors) rather than computational cost — use Merqury/DeepVariant/Paftools.js-based evaluation workflows instead When the input assemblies are not HiFi-derived T2T/high-quality drafts and no >=60X short reads exist to build yak k-mer datasets, since NextPolish2 performance relies heavily on short-read k-mers

skills.search_text: genome-read-simulation-for-assembly-benchmarking Use when you need ground-truth error loci to measure assembly-evaluator recall/precision/F1 — e.g., benchmarking CRAQ CRE/CSE calls against QUAST-LG, Inspector, or Merqury on simulated data. You need to evaluate assemblies of species with higher ploidy levels — the article states evaluation of polyploid genomes may not be as accurate as the benchmarked diploid cases You lack a known reference genome, so simulated ground-truth error loci cannot be defined or matched against evaluator calls Your goal is quality assessment of a real draft assembly (use CRAQ directly for CRE/CSE/AQI reporting rather than the simulation benchmark) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Construct a simulated benchmark genome (e.g., hg38_sim1/hg38_sim2 from hg38 GCF_000001405.26) by embedding known heterozygous variants, regional/structural errors, and repeat errors, then simulate matching short- and long-read datasets (PBSIM, Wgsim) so that error-detection recall, precision, and F1 of evaluators such as CRAQ, QUAST-LG, Inspector, and Merqury can be computed against ground-truth loci (Table 1). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w

skills.description: Use when preparing a reference genome for long-read (PacBio HiFi / ONT PromethION) WGS alignment for HLA typing: you need updated IMGT/HLA alleles appended to GRCh38 with chr6 removed.
skills.name: genome-reference-merging-compression
skills.search_text: genome-reference-merging-compression Use when preparing a reference genome for long-read (PacBio HiFi / ONT PromethION) WGS alignment for HLA typing: you need updated IMGT/HLA alleles appended to GRCh38 with chr6 removed. Short-read Illumina HLA typing via HPTASR/HPRA — those paths align directly to IMGT/HLA allele databases and do not require the merged genome reference When the input dataset targets RNA-seq or exome data that never spans the genomic HLA loci requiring genome-background alignment When you need reads to align to native chromosome 6 — appending HLA alleles while keeping chr6 would create ambiguous mappings, so the noChr6 genome is essential to this design http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3534 Builds a single long-read alignment reference by concatenating updated IMGT/HLA class I and II genomic allele sequences (HLA-I_II_GEN.fasta) with the GRCh38 chromosome-only genome lacking chromosome 6, compressing the result with pigz into one .fa.gz file so reads spanning the MHC align to HLA alleles rather than missing chr6 sequence. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Builds a single long-read alignment reference by concatenating updated IMGT/HLA class I and II genomic allele sequences (HLA-I_II_GEN.fasta) with the GRCh38 chromosome-only genome lacking chromosome 6, compressing the result with pigz into one .fa.gz file so reads spanning the MHC align to HLA alleles rather than missing chr6 sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short-read Illumina HLA typing via HPTASR/HPRA — those paths align directly to IMGT/HLA allele databases and do not require the merged genome reference When the input dataset targets RNA-seq or exome data that never spans the genomic HLA loci requiring genome-background alignment When you need reads to align to native chromosome 6 — appending HLA alleles while keeping chr6 would create ambiguous mappings, so the noChr6 genome is essential to this design

skills.description: Use when existing contig assemblies (e.g., hifiasm output from ultra-low-coverage HG002/NA19240 HiFi reads) must be placed onto chromosomes against CHM13 (v2.0) and inter-chromosomal mis-scaffolding must be counted and compared between assemblers.
skills.name: genome-scaffolding-with-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: genome-scaffolding-with-reference-alignment Use when existing contig assemblies (e.g., hifiasm output from ultra-low-coverage HG002/NA19240 HiFi reads) must be placed onto chromosomes against CHM13 (v2.0) and inter-chromosomal mis-scaffolding must be counted and compared between assemblers. When the goal is de novo structural variant discovery from the scaffolds: the article notes reference-guided scaffolding may overlook true SVs (only 62.5% of inversion SVs detected), and RagTag's 'correct' function is deliberately avoided here for that reason When input is raw reads rather than an existing contig-level assembly — run the HiFiCCL chromosome-by-chromosome assembly workflow first When a reference-biased, corrected chromosome placement is acceptable — this skill intentionally skips RagTag's correct step, so scaffold positions preserve true SVs instead of matching the reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Scaffold contig-level assemblies (e.g., HiFiCCL-Hifiasm vs Hifiasm primary contigs from low-coverage HiFi data) to chromosome level with RagTag against CHM13 (v2.0), deliberately skipping RagTag's 'correct' step, then quantify inter-chromosomal mis-scaffolding as inter-chromosomal synteny links >100,000 bp with NGenomeSyn. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Scaffold contig-level assemblies (e.g., HiFiCCL-Hifiasm vs Hifiasm primary contigs from low-coverage HiFi data) to chromosome level with RagTag against CHM13 (v2.0), deliberately skipping RagTag's 'correct' step, then quantify inter-chromosomal mis-scaffolding as inter-chromosomal synteny links >100,000 bp with NGenomeSyn.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo structural variant discovery from the scaffolds: the article notes reference-guided scaffolding may overlook true SVs (only 62.5% of inversion SVs detected), and RagTag's 'correct' function is deliberately avoided here for that reason When input is raw reads rather than an existing contig-level assembly — run the HiFiCCL chromosome-by-chromosome assembly workflow first When a reference-biased, corrected chromosome placement is acceptable — this skill intentionally skips RagTag's correct step, so scaffold positions preserve true SVs instead of matching the reference

skills.description: Use when comparing methylation states between duplicated/paralogous genomic regions: you have a genome reference FASTA and need paired homologous regions to test differential cytosine methylation.
skills.name: genome-self-alignment-analysis
skills.search_text: genome-self-alignment-analysis Use when comparing methylation states between duplicated/paralogous genomic regions: you have a genome reference FASTA and need paired homologous regions to test differential cytosine methylation. You need interspecies (not intra-genome) synteny or whole-genome alignment between two different genomes rather than segmental-duplication pairs within one reference. skills.summary: Quantifies genome-wide sequencing coverage and read-length statistics for nanopore WGS data using NanoStat on FASTQ reads and mosdepth on BAM alignments with MAPQ ≥ 20 filtering, as done to characterize the NA19240 control dataset in this pipeline.

skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-interval-analysis Use when a phased ONT BAM/VCF needs phase blocks joined within a specific coordinate window (e.g., HLA chr6:30,400,000-31,300,000) and SNV-only phasing left genes like HLA-E and HLA-C in separate blocks. skills.name: genomic-flanking-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: genomic-flanking-sequence-extraction Use when variants (e.g., a VCF annotated by ANNOVAR ensGene) need underlying genomic sequence — exon plus flanks — retrieved from hg19 to build feature tables for splice-impact prediction. The input is already a computed feature table (e.g., features.tsv with the 42 columns) and no raw sequence retrieval is needed Variants are intergenic or farther than 200 bp from splice sites — the PredPSI-SVR pipeline filters these out before sequence extraction The target genome build is not hg19; the pipeline's ANNOVAR ensGene and SPIDEX annotations are build-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Extract wild-type and mutant exon sequences plus flanking regions from a samtools-faidx-indexed hg19 FASTA so that splice site, splicing-regulatory-element, and secondary-structure features can be computed per vex-seq variant in the PredPSI-SVR pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Extract wild-type and mutant exon sequences plus flanking regions from a samtools-faidx-indexed hg19 FASTA so that splice site, splicing-regulatory-element, and secondary-structure features can be computed per vex-seq variant in the PredPSI-SVR pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a computed feature table (e.g., features.tsv with the 42 columns) and no raw sequence retrieval is needed Variants are intergenic or farther than 200 bp from splice sites — the PredPSI-SVR pipeline filters these out before sequence extraction The target genome build is not hg19; the pipeline's ANNOVAR ensGene and SPIDEX annotations are build-specific

skills.description: Use when you have an exogenous-m6A-labeled nanopore genomic DNA modBAM and need to convert modkit pileup signals into consolidated, high-confidence open-chromatin intervals and per-genome BedGraph tracks.
skills.name: genomic-interval-consolidation
skills.search_text: genomic-interval-consolidation Use when you have an exogenous-m6A-labeled nanopore genomic DNA modBAM and need to convert modkit pileup signals into consolidated, high-confidence open-chromatin intervals and per-genome BedGraph tracks. Input is direct RNA or cDNA data — Dogme routes those to kallisto/LR-Kallisto transcript quantification, not open-chromatin calling. The modBAM was not basecalled with m6A-modification models — modkit pileup will find no m6A signal to consolidate. modkit is older than v0.5 — the open-chromatin workflow explicitly requires modkit 0.5 and higher. Consolidates per-chromosome m6A open-chromatin modification calls from modkit pileups of nanopore gDNA modBAMs into a single per-genome interval set, exported as a compressed BED file (open_chromatin.bed.gz) and BedGraph tracks. This is the open-chromatin module of the Dogme pipeline for m6A-labeled genomic DNA. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Consolidates per-chromosome m6A open-chromatin modification calls from modkit pileups of nanopore gDNA modBAMs into a single per-genome interval set, exported as a compressed BED file (open_chromatin.bed.gz) and BedGraph tracks. This is the open-chromatin module of the Dogme pipeline for m6A-labeled genomic DNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is direct RNA or cDNA data — Dogme routes those to kallisto/LR-Kallisto transcript quantification, not open-chromatin calling. The modBAM was not basecalled with m6A-modification models — modkit pileup will find no m6A signal to consolidate. modkit is older than v0.5 — the open-chromatin workflow explicitly requires modkit 0.5 and higher.

skills.description: Use when you need to corroborate 5′ ends (TSSs) of long-read-derived isoforms against independent 5′-end-enriched short-read data such as CAGE-seq, computing a per-isoform coverage-supported validation fraction.
skills.name: genomic-interval-intersection
skills.search_text: genomic-interval-intersection Use when you need to corroborate 5′ ends (TSSs) of long-read-derived isoforms against independent 5′-end-enriched short-read data such as CAGE-seq, computing a per-isoform coverage-supported validation fraction. When the goal is full-length isoform discovery rather than independent validation of already-cataloged 5′ ends — short CAGE reads cannot resolve multi-kilobase transcript structure. When the isoform catalog has not been filtered (e.g., by exon count, truncations, abundance cutoff), since unfiltered TSS lists include low-confidence artifacts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Independently validates transcription start sites of lrCaptureSeq isoforms by intersecting CAGE-seq 5'-end coverage against cataloged isoform start coordinates in a filtered GFF, quantifying the fraction of TSSs corroborated by an orthogonal short-read dataset. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Independently validates transcription start sites of lrCaptureSeq isoforms by intersecting CAGE-seq 5'-end coverage against cataloged isoform start coordinates in a filtered GFF, quantifying the fraction of TSSs corroborated by an orthogonal short-read dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is full-length isoform discovery rather than independent validation of already-cataloged 5′ ends — short CAGE reads cannot resolve multi-kilobase transcript structure. When the isoform catalog has not been filtered (e.g., by exon count, truncations, abundance cutoff), since unfiltered TSS lists include low-confidence artifacts.

skills.description: Use when per-read, window-level low-entropy or feature-bearing coordinates must be coalesced into non-overlapping genomic intervals (e.g., BED regions) prior to tandem repeat discovery or coverage-filtered profiling.
skills.name: genomic-interval-merging
skills.search_text: genomic-interval-merging Use when per-read, window-level low-entropy or feature-bearing coordinates must be coalesced into non-overlapping genomic intervals (e.g., BED regions) prior to tandem repeat discovery or coverage-filtered profiling. Target regions are already annotated tandem repeats or an existing BED of candidate loci is supplied — use TRiCoLOR's REFER profiling step directly instead of re-deriving candidates. Repeats lie in unassembled regions of the genome (e.g., centromeres and telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify. Data are not haplotype-resolved long-read alignments; short-read or unphased BAMs violate the module's input assumptions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Merges retained low-entropy window coordinates from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments into contiguous candidate repetitive regions, as done by TRiCoLOR's SENSoR module before repeat profiling. Coalescing nearby windows collapses per-read, per-window evidence into stable genomic intervals suitable for downstream motif discovery. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Merges retained low-entropy window coordinates from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments into contiguous candidate repetitive regions, as done by TRiCoLOR's SENSoR module before repeat profiling. Coalescing nearby windows collapses per-read, per-window evidence into stable genomic intervals suitable for downstream motif discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target regions are already annotated tandem repeats or an existing BED of candidate loci is supplied — use TRiCoLOR's REFER profiling step directly instead of re-deriving candidates. Repeats lie in unassembled regions of the genome (e.g., centromeres and telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify. Data are not haplotype-resolved long-read alignments; short-read or unphased BAMs violate the module's input assumptions.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how many nanopore (or Illumina) reads fall inside annotated genomic intervals (ChIP-seq peaks, CpG islands) or to compare read-based metrics across feature classes and technologies.
skills.name: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis Use when you need to quantify how many nanopore (or Illumina) reads fall inside annotated genomic intervals (ChIP-seq peaks, CpG islands) or to compare read-based metrics across feature classes and technologies. The question is base modification calling (6mA/mCpG) per read rather than interval-level read assignment — use the nanoHiMe 6mA/mCG modules instead The input is already a per-peak enrichment matrix or feature count table; no further interval overlap is needed Peaks are not defined by an external annotation and must be discovered de novo from coverage — this skill intersects pre-defined interval sets, it does not call peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Intersects haplotagged nanopore reads (nanoHiMe-seq) against curated genomic interval sets — ENCODE HepG2 H3K4me3/H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks and CpG island annotations — to compute per-feature-class read assignment rates, restricted to regions with read coverage ≥20. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Intersects haplotagged nanopore reads (nanoHiMe-seq) against curated genomic interval sets — ENCODE HepG2 H3K4me3/H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks and CpG island annotations — to compute per-feature-class read assignment rates, restricted to regions with read coverage ≥20.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is base modification calling (6mA/mCpG) per read rather than interval-level read assignment — use the nanoHiMe 6mA/mCG modules instead The input is already a per-peak enrichment matrix or feature count table; no further interval overlap is needed Peaks are not defined by an external annotation and must be discovered de novo from coverage — this skill intersects pre-defined interval sets, it does not call peaks

skills.description: Use when you have two or more structural-variant call sets in reference coordinates and need to isolate tool-specific calls (e.g., inversions found by invMap but missed by competing mappers).
skills.name: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis Use when you have two or more structural-variant call sets in reference coordinates and need to isolate tool-specific calls (e.g., inversions found by invMap but missed by competing mappers). The call sets are already deduplicated and cross-mapped between mappers, so overlap analysis would be redundant. The variant type is not an inversion detectable by long-read mapping (e.g., small indels or SNPs), which is outside invMap's inversion-focused scope. You only have a single call set with no competing mapper calls to compare against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compares inversion/SV call sets from long-read mappers by interval overlap on reference coordinates to isolate calls unique to one tool. Applied to invMap vs Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, and lra on NA12878 real human genome sequencing data to surface invMap-only inversion calls such as the novel 231 bp inversion. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Compares inversion/SV call sets from long-read mappers by interval overlap on reference coordinates to isolate calls unique to one tool. Applied to invMap vs Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, and lra on NA12878 real human genome sequencing data to surface invMap-only inversion calls such as the novel 231 bp inversion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The call sets are already deduplicated and cross-mapped between mappers, so overlap analysis would be redundant. The variant type is not an inversion detectable by long-read mapping (e.g., small indels or SNPs), which is outside invMap's inversion-focused scope. You only have a single call set with no competing mapper calls to compare against.

skills.description: Use when multiple m6A detection tools have returned genomic BED call sets on the same dRNA-seq dataset and you need to quantify how concordant their calls are, independent of any ground-truth reference.
skills.name: genomic-interval-overlap-matrix
skills.search_text: genomic-interval-overlap-matrix Use when multiple m6A detection tools have returned genomic BED call sets on the same dRNA-seq dataset and you need to quantify how concordant their calls are, independent of any ground-truth reference. When the goal is accuracy assessment against a gold-standard m6A peak set (use the --peaksfile benchmarking path instead) — this skill measures tool-vs-tool concordance only When only a single m6A detection tool was run, since a pairwise overlap matrix requires at least two callers per dataset When input is per-read/per-transcript raw signal (e.g. FAST5 or resquiggled data) rather than discrete BED call coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes pairwise concordance matrices of m6A site calls across dRNA-seq detection tools by partitioning the genome into fixed-size bins, labeling each bin as m6A-positive per tool, and measuring bin-level overlap between all tool pairs. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: Computes pairwise concordance matrices of m6A site calls across dRNA-seq detection tools by partitioning the genome into fixed-size bins, labeling each bin as m6A-positive per tool, and measuring bin-level overlap between all tool pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accuracy assessment against a gold-standard m6A peak set (use the --peaksfile benchmarking path instead) — this skill measures tool-vs-tool concordance only When only a single m6A detection tool was run, since a pairwise overlap matrix requires at least two callers per dataset When input is per-read/per-transcript raw signal (e.g. FAST5 or resquiggled data) rather than discrete BED call coordinates

skills.description: Use when you have per-replicate modkit modification site tables (e.g. filtered .bed.gz from Dogme) and need to count or intersect modification sites within one gene or region, such as testing reproducibility at the Pkm locus.
skills.name: genomic-locus-subsetting-of-modification-calls
skills.search_text: genomic-locus-subsetting-of-modification-calls Use when you have per-replicate modkit modification site tables (e.g. filtered .bed.gz from Dogme) and need to count or intersect modification sites within one gene or region, such as testing reproducibility at the Pkm locus. Input is unfiltered modBAM or raw Dorado basecalls rather than filtered, coordinate-annotated modkit site tables The analysis goal is genome-wide modification profiling rather than locus-specific subsetting and replicate comparison Reads have not yet been basecalled and mapped (Dorado basecalling and minimap2 mapping are upstream prerequisites) http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Restricts filtered modkit modification site tables (m6A, m5C, Nm, pseudouridine, inosine) produced by the Dogme pipeline to a genomic locus of interest, enabling per-locus reproducibility analysis across sequencing replicates. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Restricts filtered modkit modification site tables (m6A, m5C, Nm, pseudouridine, inosine) produced by the Dogme pipeline to a genomic locus of interest, enabling per-locus reproducibility analysis across sequencing replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unfiltered modBAM or raw Dorado basecalls rather than filtered, coordinate-annotated modkit site tables The analysis goal is genome-wide modification profiling rather than locus-specific subsetting and replicate comparison Reads have not yet been basecalled and mapped (Dorado basecalling and minimap2 mapping are upstream prerequisites)

skills.description: Use when you hold per-read methylation call tables (read_id, chromosome, pos_in_strand, strand, methylation_rate) or BS-seq calls and need unique-site CpG coverage counts per dataset rather than per-read statistics.
skills.name: genomic-position-deduplication
skills.search_text: genomic-position-deduplication Use when you hold per-read methylation call tables (read_id, chromosome, pos_in_strand, strand, methylation_rate) or BS-seq calls and need unique-site CpG coverage counts per dataset rather than per-read statistics. When the goal is methylation frequency accuracy (e.g. AUROC/F1 or correlation with BS-seq, where DeepBAM achieved 98.47% AUROC and >0.95 correlations) rather than site-coverage counting. When positions are not CpG genomic coordinates — deduplicating arbitrary per-read rows without the (chromosome, pos_in_strand) key would inflate counts by read multiplicity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Counts unique covered CpG genomic sites by deduplicating distinct (chromosome, pos_in_strand) pairs from DeepBAM/Dorado per-read methylation call TSVs and matched BS-seq calls, enabling like-for-like CpG coverage comparison across nanopore and bisulfite datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Counts unique covered CpG genomic sites by deduplicating distinct (chromosome, pos_in_strand) pairs from DeepBAM/Dorado per-read methylation call TSVs and matched BS-seq calls, enabling like-for-like CpG coverage comparison across nanopore and bisulfite datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is methylation frequency accuracy (e.g. AUROC/F1 or correlation with BS-seq, where DeepBAM achieved 98.47% AUROC and >0.95 correlations) rather than site-coverage counting. When positions are not CpG genomic coordinates — deduplicating arbitrary per-read rows without the (chromosome, pos_in_strand) key would inflate counts by read multiplicity.

skills.description: Use when Nanopore dRNA-seq read alignments (BAM) must be assigned to genes and split into mature vs premature classes using GTF intron overlap, e.g. before quantifying RNA pools in subcellular fractions.
skills.name: genomic-read-to-gene-overlap-assignment
skills.search_text: genomic-read-to-gene-overlap-assignment Use when Nanopore dRNA-seq read alignments (BAM) must be assigned to genes and split into mature vs premature classes using GTF intron overlap, e.g. before quantifying RNA pools in subcellular fractions. Processing cytoplasmic or polysomal samples for premature calls — these are removed there because premature status is only interpretable in chromatin/nuclear fractions. Input is already a per-gene count matrix or the reads have already been assigned to genes — this skill's findOverlaps-based gene assignment and intron-overlap classification would be redundant. Reads that overlap more than one gene — these are discarded by design, so the skill cannot be used to force a unique gene assignment for ambiguous reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Assigns Nanopore direct RNA-seq reads to genes by genomic overlap (GenomicRanges findOverlaps in R) and classifies each read as mature or premature based on whether it overlaps annotated introns by at least 10 bases, as implemented in Nanodynamo's fractionsReadsClassification workflow. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Assigns Nanopore direct RNA-seq reads to genes by genomic overlap (GenomicRanges findOverlaps in R) and classifies each read as mature or premature based on whether it overlaps annotated introns by at least 10 bases, as implemented in Nanodynamo's fractionsReadsClassification workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Processing cytoplasmic or polysomal samples for premature calls — these are removed there because premature status is only interpretable in chromatin/nuclear fractions. Input is already a per-gene count matrix or the reads have already been assigned to genes — this skill's findOverlaps-based gene assignment and intron-overlap classification would be redundant. Reads that overlap more than one gene — these are discarded by design, so the skill cannot be used to force a unique gene assignment for ambiguous reads.

skills.description: Use when running scywalker's align-and-reconstruct stages on whole genomes where splitting work over chromosomes or sub-chromosomal regions is needed to parallelise and bound memory.
skills.name: genomic-region-based-job-distribution
skills.search_text: genomic-region-based-job-distribution Use when running scywalker's align-and-reconstruct stages on whole genomes where splitting work over chromosomes or sub-chromosomal regions is needed to parallelise and bound memory. Small or test references with no alt/unplaced contigs (e.g. the scywalker_test chromosome-17 dataset built with scywalker_makerefdir -organelles '') — default grouping already suffices and region splitting is unnecessary Organelle chromosomes (e.g. chrM, chrPt): they must be excluded from the IsoQuant-based region processing via the refdir organelles configuration rather than distributed like standard chromosomes Data that is not coordinate-anchored genomic read data (e.g. already demultiplexed count tables) — region distribution applies to alignment/transcript reconstruction, not downstream counting http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 scywalker distributes alignment (minimap2_splice) and IsoQuant-based transcript reconstruction over genomic regions (~5 Mb target, default distrreg g5000000) and groups small alt/unplaced chromosomes, cutting peak memory and enabling server/cluster parallelisation. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: scywalker distributes alignment (minimap2_splice) and IsoQuant-based transcript reconstruction over genomic regions (~5 Mb target, default distrreg g5000000) and groups small alt/unplaced chromosomes, cutting peak memory and enabling server/cluster parallelisation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Small or test references with no alt/unplaced contigs (e.g. the scywalker_test chromosome-17 dataset built with scywalker_makerefdir -organelles '') — default grouping already suffices and region splitting is unnecessary Organelle chromosomes (e.g. chrM, chrPt): they must be excluded from the IsoQuant-based region processing via the refdir organelles configuration rather than distributed like standard chromosomes Data that is not coordinate-anchored genomic read data (e.g. already demultiplexed count tables) — region distribution applies to alignment/transcript reconstruction, not downstream counting

skills.description: Use when the user names a specific chromosomal interval (e.g. 12:11396601-11436500) and asks for its copy number genotype or region-level RD/BAF statistics from an existing .pytor archive.
skills.name: genomic-region-coordinate-querying
skills.search_text: genomic-region-coordinate-querying Use when the user names a specific chromosomal interval (e.g. 12:11396601-11436500) and asks for its copy number genotype or region-level RD/BAF statistics from an existing .pytor archive. The task is de novo CNV discovery across the whole genome — that requires the -rd/-his/-partition/-call pipeline, not region genotyping No .pytor archive exists yet; the region genotyper cannot parse raw BAM files directly The question concerns SNP-level variant calling rather than copy number of an interval — VCF import via -snp is a different workflow step http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Genotypes a user-supplied genomic region with CNVpytor by computing copy number from read depth: mean RD within the region divided by mean autosomal RD and scaled by 2, optionally enriched with BAF/e-value statistics via the '-a' genotype mode. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Genotypes a user-supplied genomic region with CNVpytor by computing copy number from read depth: mean RD within the region divided by mean autosomal RD and scaled by 2, optionally enriched with BAF/e-value statistics via the '-a' genotype mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is de novo CNV discovery across the whole genome — that requires the -rd/-his/-partition/-call pipeline, not region genotyping No .pytor archive exists yet; the region genotyper cannot parse raw BAM files directly The question concerns SNP-level variant calling rather than copy number of an interval — VCF import via -snp is a different workflow step

skills.description: Use when SNVs from gnomAD r2.0.2 or ClinVar VCFs must be projected onto UniProt/Swiss-Prot residues and Pfam consensus positions for gene-level or meta-domain tolerance analyses.
skills.name: genomic-to-protein-position-variant-mapping
skills.search_text: genomic-to-protein-position-variant-mapping Use when SNVs from gnomAD r2.0.2 or ClinVar VCFs must be projected onto UniProt/Swiss-Prot residues and Pfam consensus positions for gene-level or meta-domain tolerance analyses. The transcript of interest is not mapped to a Swiss-Prot protein — MetaDome only analyzes transcripts linked to a Swiss-Prot entry (others are displayed in gray) The variants of interest are indels or non-PASS variants — the pipeline retains only SNVs meeting the PASS filter criteria You need haplotype context or protein-protein interaction information — aggregating variation via meta-domains loses this specific context http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Translate SNVs from gnomAD and ClinVar VCFs from genomic coordinates to Swiss-Prot protein residues and Pfam domain consensus positions using MetaDome's PostgreSQL mapping database, enabling variant comparison across homologous protein domains. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Translate SNVs from gnomAD and ClinVar VCFs from genomic coordinates to Swiss-Prot protein residues and Pfam domain consensus positions using MetaDome's PostgreSQL mapping database, enabling variant comparison across homologous protein domains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The transcript of interest is not mapped to a Swiss-Prot protein — MetaDome only analyzes transcripts linked to a Swiss-Prot entry (others are displayed in gray) The variants of interest are indels or non-PASS variants — the pipeline retains only SNVs meeting the PASS filter criteria You need haplotype context or protein-protein interaction information — aggregating variation via meta-domains loses this specific context

skills.search_text: genomic-variant-identifier-mapping Use when variant lists (single variants or CSV/VCF batches) must be converted into REST API queries against annotation services like MyVariant.info, or when extending the pipeline with a new API-based annotation source such as DisGeNET. skills.description: Use when calling SNVs/small indels from Illumina, PacBio or Oxford Nanopore (SMS) BAMs with a deep learning caller, and you must convert pileups at candidate loci into fixed-size numeric tensors for a CNN.
skills.name: genomic-variant-tensor-encoding
skills.search_text: genomic-variant-tensor-encoding Use when calling SNVs/small indels from Illumina, PacBio or Oxford Nanopore (SMS) BAMs with a deep learning caller, and you must convert pileups at candidate loci into fixed-size numeric tensors for a CNN. The candidate locus carries two or more alternative alleles — the current Clairvoyante design ignores multi-allelic variants and multi-allelic SNPs are excluded from training You need base-quality-aware calling — the current implementation does not consider sequencing read base quality The indel variant is longer than 4 bp — exact alternative allele is only provided for indel variants ≤4 bp due to scarce long-indel training samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encodes read alignments around candidate variant loci into fixed-size 33x4x4 tensors (33 bp window with 16-bp flanks; four channels: reference base, insertion count, deletion count, alternate-allele count) suitable for the Clairvoyante five-layer multitask CNN that predicts variant type, zygosity, alternative allele and indel length. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Encodes read alignments around candidate variant loci into fixed-size 33x4x4 tensors (33 bp window with 16-bp flanks; four channels: reference base, insertion count, deletion count, alternate-allele count) suitable for the Clairvoyante five-layer multitask CNN that predicts variant type, zygosity, alternative allele and indel length.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate locus carries two or more alternative alleles — the current Clairvoyante design ignores multi-allelic variants and multi-allelic SNPs are excluded from training You need base-quality-aware calling — the current implementation does not consider sequencing read base quality The indel variant is longer than 4 bp — exact alternative allele is only provided for indel variants ≤4 bp due to scarce long-indel training samples

skills.name: genotype-accuracy-computation
skills.search_text: genotype-accuracy-computation Use when benchmarking diploid SV callers (e.g., VolcanoSV vs PAV, SVIM-asm, Dipcall) on long-read HG002 data and you need genotype accuracy per DEL/INS call at multiple coverage depths. Benchmarking genotypes for reciprocal translocations (TRAs), since genotyping is ambiguous — only F1/GT_F1 should be computed for INVs and DUPs in that context Evaluating against the HCC1395 somatic high-confidence callset, which includes SV calls only from alignment-based tools and is incomplete Assessing small indel genotype accuracy on ONT data, where assembly-based small indel detection showed low precision for all tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes genotype (GT) accuracy for structural variant callers by benchmarking caller VCFs against the GIAB HG002 SV gold standard with Truvari v4.0.0 under fixed parameters, extracting GT accuracy alongside recall, precision, and F1 per tool, SV type, and coverage level. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Computes genotype (GT) accuracy for structural variant callers by benchmarking caller VCFs against the GIAB HG002 SV gold standard with Truvari v4.0.0 under fixed parameters, extracting GT accuracy alongside recall, precision, and F1 per tool, SV type, and coverage level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking genotypes for reciprocal translocations (TRAs), since genotyping is ambiguous — only F1/GT_F1 should be computed for INVs and DUPs in that context Evaluating against the HCC1395 somatic high-confidence callset, which includes SV calls only from alignment-based tools and is incomplete Assessing small indel genotype accuracy on ONT data, where assembly-based small indel detection showed low precision for all tools

skills.description: Use when InDel genotypes have been called for 2 parents and progeny (e.g., an F1 Populus hybrid population with 20 progeny) and non-Mendelian or low-quality marker sites must be removed before linkage mapping.
skills.name: genotype-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: genotype-quality-filtering Use when InDel genotypes have been called for 2 parents and progeny (e.g., an F1 Populus hybrid population with 20 progeny) and non-Mendelian or low-quality marker sites must be removed before linkage mapping. When the goal is variant discovery or raw genotype calling rather than filtering already-called InDel genotypes — steps 1 and 2 (catalog generation, genotyping) handle that When the input population type is unsupported by the pipeline's segregation models, or when markers should be retained regardless of segregation distortion (the PVALUE:0.01 cutoff will discard distorted sites) When the pipeline is missing Perl modules (Parallel::ForkManager, Getopt::Long, Statistics::Distributions) or BWA/SAMtools/BCFtools paths are not configured in parameters.ini http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Filters InDel genotypes called across a hybrid population by testing each cataloged InDel site's parental/progeny genotype counts against expected Mendelian segregation ratios (P-value threshold 0.01), after applying genotype-quality thresholds (GQ 30, MAPQ 5, MISPCT 20, HETEROZYGOUS_DEPTH 3, HOMOZYGOUS_DEPTH 5) set in parameters.ini. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Filters InDel genotypes called across a hybrid population by testing each cataloged InDel site's parental/progeny genotype counts against expected Mendelian segregation ratios (P-value threshold 0.01), after applying genotype-quality thresholds (GQ 30, MAPQ 5, MISPCT 20, HETEROZYGOUS_DEPTH 3, HOMOZYGOUS_DEPTH 5) set in parameters.ini.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is variant discovery or raw genotype calling rather than filtering already-called InDel genotypes — steps 1 and 2 (catalog generation, genotyping) handle that When the input population type is unsupported by the pipeline's segregation models, or when markers should be retained regardless of segregation distortion (the PVALUE:0.01 cutoff will discard distorted sites) When the pipeline is missing Perl modules (Parallel::ForkManager, Getopt::Long, Statistics::Distributions) or BWA/SAMtools/BCFtools paths are not configured in parameters.ini

skills.description: Use when you have a GLnexus joint-genotyped trio VCF (GATK HaplotypeCaller and/or DeepVariant calls) and need to enforce Mendelian de novo pattern plus depth, genotype quality, and allele-fraction cutoffs to produce a final DNV callset.
skills.name: genotype-quality-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: genotype-quality-threshold-filtering Use when you have a GLnexus joint-genotyped trio VCF (GATK HaplotypeCaller and/or DeepVariant calls) and need to enforce Mendelian de novo pattern plus depth, genotype quality, and allele-fraction cutoffs to produce a final DNV callset. You only have existing VCFs and no BAM/CRAM files and need a drop-in tool — HAT-FLEX is the caller-agnostic alternative Your input is already a called DNV table needing downstream statistics/annotation — use the acorn R package (after squirrel.py prep) instead You need the variant-calling stage itself (Parabricks/GATK/DeepVariant/Glnexus joint genotyping) rather than post-genotyping filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Apply HAT's genotype- and depth-based quality thresholds to GLnexus family-level joint-genotyped trio VCFs so only high-confidence de novo variants (DNVs) survive. This is the core custom de novo variant filter step of the HAT (Hare And Tortoise) pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775
skills.summary: Apply HAT's genotype- and depth-based quality thresholds to GLnexus family-level joint-genotyped trio VCFs so only high-confidence de novo variants (DNVs) survive. This is the core custom de novo variant filter step of the HAT (Hare And Tortoise) pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have existing VCFs and no BAM/CRAM files and need a drop-in tool — HAT-FLEX is the caller-agnostic alternative Your input is already a called DNV table needing downstream statistics/annotation — use the acorn R package (after squirrel.py prep) instead You need the variant-calling stage itself (Parabricks/GATK/DeepVariant/Glnexus joint genotyping) rather than post-genotyping filtering

skills.description: Use when filtering or benchmarking SNV calls from long-read (ONT/PacBio) data, where a fixed GQ cutoff is inappropriate and the threshold must be matched to median read coverage before computing precision/recall/F1.
skills.name: genotype-quality-variant-thresholding
skills.search_text: genotype-quality-variant-thresholding Use when filtering or benchmarking SNV calls from long-read (ONT/PacBio) data, where a fixed GQ cutoff is inappropriate and the threshold must be matched to median read coverage before computing precision/recall/F1. Calling short indels: Longshot only calls SNVs and can merely genotype indels supplied in an input VCF; accurate de novo indel calling with SMS reads is hampered by the high insertion/deletion error rate Structural variant discovery — use a dedicated SV caller such as Delly instead Short-read (Illumina) data, where a fixed GQ cutoff of 50 applied to short-read callers is the established practice http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calibration and application of genotype-quality (GQ) thresholds to filter long-read SNV calls: a variable GQ cutoff matched to the median read coverage is used for Longshot calls, versus a fixed GQ 50 for short-read callers, when benchmarking against GIAB high-confidence truth sets. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Calibration and application of genotype-quality (GQ) thresholds to filter long-read SNV calls: a variable GQ cutoff matched to the median read coverage is used for Longshot calls, versus a fixed GQ 50 for short-read callers, when benchmarking against GIAB high-confidence truth sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling short indels: Longshot only calls SNVs and can merely genotype indels supplied in an input VCF; accurate de novo indel calling with SMS reads is hampered by the high insertion/deletion error rate Structural variant discovery — use a dedicated SV caller such as Delly instead Short-read (Illumina) data, where a fixed GQ cutoff of 50 applied to short-read callers is the established practice

skills.description: Use when per-cell genotyping rates for targeted somatic SNVs (e.g., AML mutations in DNMT3A, RUNX1, SF3B1) must be computed from nanoranger output and compared to published GoT/nanoranger benchmarks.
skills.name: genotyping-rate-calculation-and-validation
skills.search_text: genotyping-rate-calculation-and-validation Use when per-cell genotyping rates for targeted somatic SNVs (e.g., AML mutations in DNMT3A, RUNX1, SF3B1) must be computed from nanoranger output and compared to published GoT/nanoranger benchmarks. Target loci are not near the 5' end of highly expressed genes or transcripts exceed ~4 kB, since nanoranger genotyping sensitivity depends on transcript representation Input is bulk (non-single-cell) sequencing data without 10x cell barcodes/UMIs, so no per-cell genotyping matrix can be constructed The mutation of interest is rare/private and not covered by the limited primer panel, as the genotyping ceiling is set by low, incomplete transcript representation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Collapse nanoranger long-read variant calls to a per-cell genotyping matrix keyed by 10x Genomics cell barcodes and compute per-mutation genotyping rates, validating them against reported ranges (e.g., 4.8–19.2% for DNMT3AR882H/SF3B1K700E in AML1022). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Collapse nanoranger long-read variant calls to a per-cell genotyping matrix keyed by 10x Genomics cell barcodes and compute per-mutation genotyping rates, validating them against reported ranges (e.g., 4.8–19.2% for DNMT3AR882H/SF3B1K700E in AML1022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target loci are not near the 5' end of highly expressed genes or transcripts exceed ~4 kB, since nanoranger genotyping sensitivity depends on transcript representation Input is bulk (non-single-cell) sequencing data without 10x cell barcodes/UMIs, so no per-cell genotyping matrix can be constructed The mutation of interest is rare/private and not covered by the limited primer panel, as the genotyping ceiling is set by low, incomplete transcript representation

skills.description: Use when ACMG/AMP-classified germline variants from a single sample (PASS-filtered VCF) must be rendered into CPSR's interactive HTML report plus companion VCF/TSV outputs.
skills.name: germline-variant-report-generation
skills.search_text: germline-variant-report-generation Use when ACMG/AMP-classified germline variants from a single sample (PASS-filtered VCF) must be rendered into CPSR's interactive HTML report plus companion VCF/TSV outputs. Input is somatic (tumor) variant data — the companion workflow PCGR handles somatic SNVs/InDels, CNAs and RNA fusions, whereas this skill targets germline variants from a single cancer patient. The goal is variant classification or VEP/variant annotation itself rather than the final report-rendering step; this skill starts from already-classified variants. Input VCF records are not designated PASS in the FILTER column — non-PASS variants are excluded from reporting, so filtering must be redone first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 CPSR's final workflow step renders ACMG/AMP-classified germline SNVs/InDels for a single sample into an interactive HTML report (Settings, Summary of Findings, Variant Classification, Documentation) via the cpsr/pcgrr R packages and Quarto, with companion annotated VCF, JSON and TSV outputs. genomics/v1 10.1002/ijc.33749
skills.summary: CPSR's final workflow step renders ACMG/AMP-classified germline SNVs/InDels for a single sample into an interactive HTML report (Settings, Summary of Findings, Variant Classification, Documentation) via the cpsr/pcgrr R packages and Quarto, with companion annotated VCF, JSON and TSV outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is somatic (tumor) variant data — the companion workflow PCGR handles somatic SNVs/InDels, CNAs and RNA fusions, whereas this skill targets germline variants from a single cancer patient. The goal is variant classification or VEP/variant annotation itself rather than the final report-rendering step; this skill starts from already-classified variants. Input VCF records are not designated PASS in the FILTER column — non-PASS variants are excluded from reporting, so filtering must be redone first.

skills.description: Use when a de novo transcriptome must be represented as a splice graph (exons = nodes, IEBs = edges, transcripts = paths) for downstream SNP genotyping, visualization in Bandage, or comparison against a GFF3 reference annotation.
skills.name: gfa1-splice-graph-encoding
skills.search_text: gfa1-splice-graph-encoding Use when a de novo transcriptome must be represented as a splice graph (exons = nodes, IEBs = edges, transcripts = paths) for downstream SNP genotyping, visualization in Bandage, or comparison against a GFF3 reference annotation. A reference genome and splice-aware alignment (e.g. GMAP) is available to extract IEB coordinates directly Input is raw RNA-Seq reads rather than an assembled transcriptome (EXFI takes the transcriptome assembly plus raw WGS reads) Output must be coordinates-only BED/GFF rather than a graph encoding exon sequences and connections http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Encode EXFI's predicted exons and their connectivity into a GFA1 splice graph file: exon sequences as S segments with coordinates, exon connections as L lines, and transcripts as P-line paths of exons. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Encode EXFI's predicted exons and their connectivity into a GFA1 splice graph file: exon sequences as S segments with coordinates, exon connections as L lines, and transcripts as P-line paths of exons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome and splice-aware alignment (e.g. GMAP) is available to extract IEB coordinates directly Input is raw RNA-Seq reads rather than an assembled transcriptome (EXFI takes the transcriptome assembly plus raw WGS reads) Output must be coordinates-only BED/GFF rather than a graph encoding exon sequences and connections

skills.search_text: gff3-file-manipulation Use when a filtered or unfiltered IsoPops transcript Database must be exported to (or manipulated as) GFF3 genome-annotation format for isoform catalog delivery or downstream visualization. The source transcript structures have not yet been compiled/processed into an IsoPops Database (compile_raw_db/process_db must run first) The target downstream tool requires a different annotation format (e.g. GTF, BED) rather than GFF3 The analysis goal is isoform discovery or quantification rather than exporting existing annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Writing and manipulating GFF3 isoform annotation files from IsoPops Database objects, converting filtered lrCaptureSeq isoform catalogs into the GFF3 genome-annotation format for downstream reuse. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Writing and manipulating GFF3 isoform annotation files from IsoPops Database objects, converting filtered lrCaptureSeq isoform catalogs into the GFF3 genome-annotation format for downstream reuse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source transcript structures have not yet been compiled/processed into an IsoPops Database (compile_raw_db/process_db must run first) The target downstream tool requires a different annotation format (e.g. GTF, BED) rather than GFF3 The analysis goal is isoform discovery or quantification rather than exporting existing annotation

skills.description: Use when plastid genome annotations contain apparent nonsense mutations (internal stop codons) caused by RNA editing that would be rejected by NCBI, and submission-ready GenBank files are needed.
skills.name: gff3-genbank-file-processing
skills.search_text: gff3-genbank-file-processing Use when plastid genome annotations contain apparent nonsense mutations (internal stop codons) caused by RNA editing that would be rejected by NCBI, and submission-ready GenBank files are needed. Input annotations were created in Sequin — ReFernment has a known error and does not produce annotations for Sequin-created files (files exported from Geneious still work) You need prediction of every RNA editing site from RNA-Seq data — ReFernment is not intended to predict every editing site and is not a substitute for manually checking gene annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Process GFF3 annotations and GenBank flat files for plastid genomes with the ReFernment R package to annotate RNA-editing-restored nonsense mutations and generate GenBank-submission-ready output files. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.1216
skills.summary: Process GFF3 annotations and GenBank flat files for plastid genomes with the ReFernment R package to annotate RNA-editing-restored nonsense mutations and generate GenBank-submission-ready output files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input annotations were created in Sequin — ReFernment has a known error and does not produce annotations for Sequin-created files (files exported from Geneious still work) You need prediction of every RNA editing site from RNA-Seq data — ReFernment is not intended to predict every editing site and is not a substitute for manually checking gene annotations

skills.description: Use when benchmarking predicted exons against an annotated reference (e.g. Ensembl release 91 GFF3 for GRCz10/GRCh38) and the predicted coordinates are transcript-based, so reference exons must be transformed to the same BED coordinate frame before comparison.
skills.name: gff3-to-bed-coordinate-conversion
skills.search_text: gff3-to-bed-coordinate-conversion Use when benchmarking predicted exons against an annotated reference (e.g. Ensembl release 91 GFF3 for GRCz10/GRCh38) and the predicted coordinates are transcript-based, so reference exons must be transformed to the same BED coordinate frame before comparison. The reference and predicted exon coordinates are already in the same (transcript-based) frame — re-converting would double-transform minus-strand coordinates The goal is genomic-coordinate analysis (e.g. variant calling or SNP genotyping against the genome), where chromosome-based GFF3 coordinates should be preserved Input annotation is not exon-level GFF3 (e.g. protein domains, CDS-only files without exon features) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts chromosome-based GFF3 reference exon coordinates into transcript-based BED intervals (accounting for strand and exon order) so that EXFI-predicted exons can be benchmarked against the reference using bedtools intersect (mutual overlap ≥95%) and the compare_to_gff3 precision/recall/F1 script. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Converts chromosome-based GFF3 reference exon coordinates into transcript-based BED intervals (accounting for strand and exon order) so that EXFI-predicted exons can be benchmarked against the reference using bedtools intersect (mutual overlap ≥95%) and the compare_to_gff3 precision/recall/F1 script.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference and predicted exon coordinates are already in the same (transcript-based) frame — re-converting would double-transform minus-strand coordinates The goal is genomic-coordinate analysis (e.g. variant calling or SNP genotyping against the genome), where chromosome-based GFF3 coordinates should be preserved Input annotation is not exon-level GFF3 (e.g. protein domains, CDS-only files without exon features)

skills.description: Use when comparing two or more predicted/merged annotation GTFs (e.g. StringTie-based, BRAKER1/2, TSEBRA, AUGUSTUS) against a reference annotation and you need level-resolved accuracy metrics to rank pipelines.
skills.name: gffcompare-transcript-precision-recall-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gffcompare-transcript-precision-recall-benchmarking Use when comparing two or more predicted/merged annotation GTFs (e.g. StringTie-based, BRAKER1/2, TSEBRA, AUGUSTUS) against a reference annotation and you need level-resolved accuracy metrics to rank pipelines. The pipeline under evaluation has no reference GTF available to compare against, since precision/recall cannot be computed without a ground-truth annotation You only need transcript abundance quantification rather than structural annotation accuracy — gffcompare evaluates structure, not expression Annotations are already reconciled/merged and only need visualization (use pyGenomeTracks instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark gene/transcript annotations by running gffcompare against a reference GTF and extracting precision, recall, and their harmonic mean (F1-score) at base, exon, intron, intron-chain, transcript, and locus levels, as used to show annotate_my_genomes surpasses BRAKER1/2 and TSEBRA on StringTie assemblies. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Benchmark gene/transcript annotations by running gffcompare against a reference GTF and extracting precision, recall, and their harmonic mean (F1-score) at base, exon, intron, intron-chain, transcript, and locus levels, as used to show annotate_my_genomes surpasses BRAKER1/2 and TSEBRA on StringTie assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline under evaluation has no reference GTF available to compare against, since precision/recall cannot be computed without a ground-truth annotation You only need transcript abundance quantification rather than structural annotation accuracy — gffcompare evaluates structure, not expression Annotations are already reconciled/merged and only need visualization (use pyGenomeTracks instead)

skills.description: Use when comparing variant caller performance across genomic strata, e.g., quantifying how many NA12878 SNVs fall in segmental duplications vs GIAB high-confidence regions and computing Ts/Tv ratios per stratum.
skills.name: giab-benchmark-region-intersection
skills.search_text: giab-benchmark-region-intersection Use when comparing variant caller performance across genomic strata, e.g., quantifying how many NA12878 SNVs fall in segmental duplications vs GIAB high-confidence regions and computing Ts/Tv ratios per stratum. The goal is calling indels or structural variants — Longshot only calls SNVs and accurate short indel calling with SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate The sample lacks GIAB high-confidence benchmarks or segmental-duplication annotations, so strata cannot be defined Reads are short Illumina reads alone and the question concerns duplicated regions — Illumina calls are unreliable there (Ts/Tv 1.55 vs 1.99 for SMS) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Stratify variant call sets (e.g., Longshot PacBio SNVs vs FreeBayes Illumina SNVs on NA12878) by intersecting them with GIAB high-confidence regions, their complements, and segmental-duplication annotation tracks at identity thresholds of ≥95% and ≥99%, then compute per-stratum SNV counts and Ts/Tv ratios. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Stratify variant call sets (e.g., Longshot PacBio SNVs vs FreeBayes Illumina SNVs on NA12878) by intersecting them with GIAB high-confidence regions, their complements, and segmental-duplication annotation tracks at identity thresholds of ≥95% and ≥99%, then compute per-stratum SNV counts and Ts/Tv ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling indels or structural variants — Longshot only calls SNVs and accurate short indel calling with SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate The sample lacks GIAB high-confidence benchmarks or segmental-duplication annotations, so strata cannot be defined Reads are short Illumina reads alone and the question concerns duplicated regions — Illumina calls are unreliable there (Ts/Tv 1.55 vs 1.99 for SMS)

skills.description: Use when comparing SV/indel callers on GIAB-benchmarked samples (e.g. HG002) and you need region-stratified precision, recall and F1 per event class rather than a single genome-wide number.
skills.name: giab-benchmark-region-stratification
skills.search_text: giab-benchmark-region-stratification Use when comparing SV/indel callers on GIAB-benchmarked samples (e.g. HG002) and you need region-stratified precision, recall and F1 per event class rather than a single genome-wide number. Evaluating long-read-only callers against GIAB v1.1 or CMRG truth sets — use the kcleal/SV_Benchmark_CMRG_GIAB or SV_benchmark_PacBio_HiFi pipelines instead Benchmarking small-variant (SNV/indel) callers where a distance-based evaluator like lh3/CHM-eval (syndip) is the appropriate tool When the input VCFs are the reference truth set itself and no caller comparison is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark structural-variant caller output against the GIAB HG002 (Ashkenazim son) truth set with svbench, PASS-filtering calls and stratifying precision/recall/F1 per SV type and per confidence region (Tier 1 vs all genomic regions) to compare callers on deletions and insertions. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Benchmark structural-variant caller output against the GIAB HG002 (Ashkenazim son) truth set with svbench, PASS-filtering calls and stratifying precision/recall/F1 per SV type and per confidence region (Tier 1 vs all genomic regions) to compare callers on deletions and insertions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating long-read-only callers against GIAB v1.1 or CMRG truth sets — use the kcleal/SV_Benchmark_CMRG_GIAB or SV_benchmark_PacBio_HiFi pipelines instead Benchmarking small-variant (SNV/indel) callers where a distance-based evaluator like lh3/CHM-eval (syndip) is the appropriate tool When the input VCFs are the reference truth set itself and no caller comparison is needed

skills.description: Use when evaluating DEL/INS SV calls from long-read SV callers against the GIAB HG002 gold standard to quantify recall, precision, F1, and genotype accuracy with Truvari.
skills.name: giab-gold-standard-vcf-comparison
skills.search_text: giab-gold-standard-vcf-comparison Use when evaluating DEL/INS SV calls from long-read SV callers against the GIAB HG002 gold standard to quantify recall, precision, F1, and genotype accuracy with Truvari. Evaluating somatic complex SVs against the HCC1395 high-confidence callset, which is incomplete and includes SV calls only from alignment-based tools, so only recall (not precision/F1) is meaningful there Genotyping assessment of reciprocal translocations (TRAs), where genotyping reciprocity is ambiguous — only F1 and GT_F1 are computed for INVs and DUPs instead Estimating false discovery rate against a different reference (e.g., CHM13 vs GRCh38), which uses a ratio-of-counts approach rather than gold-standard benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark structural variant caller VCFs (e.g., VolcanoSV, Dipcall, SVIM-asm, PAV) against the GIAB HG002 SV gold standard using Truvari v4.0.0, computing recall, precision, F1, and genotype accuracy per SV type, dataset, and coverage level. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant caller VCFs (e.g., VolcanoSV, Dipcall, SVIM-asm, PAV) against the GIAB HG002 SV gold standard using Truvari v4.0.0, computing recall, precision, F1, and genotype accuracy per SV type, dataset, and coverage level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating somatic complex SVs against the HCC1395 high-confidence callset, which is incomplete and includes SV calls only from alignment-based tools, so only recall (not precision/F1) is meaningful there Genotyping assessment of reciprocal translocations (TRAs), where genotyping reciprocity is ambiguous — only F1 and GT_F1 are computed for INVs and DUPs instead Estimating false discovery rate against a different reference (e.g., CHM13 vs GRCh38), which uses a ratio-of-counts approach rather than gold-standard benchmarking

skills.description: Use when evaluating the accuracy (precision/recall/FDR) of SNV calls from long-read SMS data on a human genome that has a GIAB high-confidence truth set available.
skills.name: giab-high-confidence-truth-set-comparison
skills.search_text: giab-high-confidence-truth-set-comparison Use when evaluating the accuracy (precision/recall/FDR) of SNV calls from long-read SMS data on a human genome that has a GIAB high-confidence truth set available. The input reads are Illumina short reads — the comparison is designed for long-read SMS data (PacBio/ONT), where short-read callers like GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the appropriate benchmark instead The variant type of interest is indels or structural variants — Longshot calls only SNVs from pileup (indels can be genotyped only if supplied in an input VCF) The genome region lies outside the GIAB high-confidence BED — calls there cannot be scored as TP or FP without additional validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark long-read SNV callers (Longshot, WhatsHap, Clairvoyante) by restricting calls to Genome in a Bottle (GIAB) high-confidence regions of PacBio-sequenced human genomes and computing precision, recall, and FDR against the GIAB truth sets. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read SNV callers (Longshot, WhatsHap, Clairvoyante) by restricting calls to Genome in a Bottle (GIAB) high-confidence regions of PacBio-sequenced human genomes and computing precision, recall, and FDR against the GIAB truth sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are Illumina short reads — the comparison is designed for long-read SMS data (PacBio/ONT), where short-read callers like GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the appropriate benchmark instead The variant type of interest is indels or structural variants — Longshot calls only SNVs from pileup (indels can be genotyped only if supplied in an input VCF) The genome region lies outside the GIAB high-confidence BED — calls there cannot be scored as TP or FP without additional validation

skills.description: Use when aligned ONT reads (e.g., HG002 R10.4 BAM) must be partitioned by parental haplotype to enable allele-specific methylation downstream, and a GIAB phased heterozygous variant VCF is available.
skills.name: giab-phased-vcf-variant-matching
skills.search_text: giab-phased-vcf-variant-matching Use when aligned ONT reads (e.g., HG002 R10.4 BAM) must be partitioned by parental haplotype to enable allele-specific methylation downstream, and a GIAB phased heterozygous variant VCF is available. No phased heterozygous variant VCF exists for the sample or the genome is effectively haploid, so informative heterozygous sites cannot partition reads. Input reads are not aligned (raw POD5/FASTQ) — reads must first be mapped and sorted into a BAM before haplotagging. The goal is single-molecule CpG methylation calling itself — that is performed by DeepBAM/Dorado on the reads, independent of haplotype assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns individual ONT reads to paternal (HP:i:1) or maternal (HP:i:2) haplotypes by running whatshap haplotag with a GIAB phased variant VCF against the mapped BAM, then splitting tagged reads into hp1/hp2 read sets for allele-specific methylation analysis. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Assigns individual ONT reads to paternal (HP:i:1) or maternal (HP:i:2) haplotypes by running whatshap haplotag with a GIAB phased variant VCF against the mapped BAM, then splitting tagged reads into hp1/hp2 read sets for allele-specific methylation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No phased heterozygous variant VCF exists for the sample or the genome is effectively haploid, so informative heterozygous sites cannot partition reads. Input reads are not aligned (raw POD5/FASTQ) — reads must first be mapped and sorted into a BAM before haplotagging. skills.description: Use when clustered seed hits from a coarse seeding stage must be converted into read/reference coordinate anchors for anchor chaining, especially for long, error-prone MinION 1d/2d reads where repetitive loci require separate graph paths.
skills.name: graph-walk-path-extension
skills.search_text: graph-walk-path-extension Use when clustered seed hits from a coarse seeding stage must be converted into read/reference coordinate anchors for anchor chaining, especially for long, error-prone MinION 1d/2d reads where repetitive loci require separate graph paths. Input is raw reads with no stage I candidate regions — stage I gapped spaced seeding must run first to reduce the search space. Very large references when the goal is exhaustive sensitivity: the percentile filter (--freq-percentile) slightly reduces sensitivity; use the composite option -x sensitive to switch off minimizers and percentile filtering instead. Mapping to a transcriptome or circular reference requiring specialized handling — GraphMap routes these through --gtf or circular-genome handling rather than the plain anchor-construction path. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Refines clustered seed hits into alignment anchors by building a k-mer mapping graph (one vertex per k-mer occurrence, at most 9 outbound edges per vertex, identical k-mers kept as distinct vertices) and greedily traversing it with O(1) vertex-update walks, as done in stage II of GraphMap for nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Refines clustered seed hits into alignment anchors by building a k-mer mapping graph (one vertex per k-mer occurrence, at most 9 outbound edges per vertex, identical k-mers kept as distinct vertices) and greedily traversing it with O(1) vertex-update walks, as done in stage II of GraphMap for nanopore reads.

Input is short-read data — SemiBin2 uses a different clustering path for short reads; the ensemble DBSCAN algorithm is specific to long-read binning You only need bins from a single clustering resolution — running DBSCAN at 12 epsilon values plus greedy integration is unnecessary overhead if a single epsilon suffices Contigs lack trained model embeddings (no data.csv/data_split.csv) — the clustering operates on learned deep-learning features, not raw sequence composition http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 SemiBin2's ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering integration for long-read metagenomic binning: run DBSCAN at 12 epsilon values, score candidate bins with 107 single-copy marker genes, and merge per-epsilon results via a greedy best-F1 selection algorithm. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209
