skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — SemiBin2 uses a different clustering path for short reads; the ensemble DBSCAN algorithm is specific to long-read binning You only need bins from a single clustering resolution — running DBSCAN at 12 epsilon values plus greedy integration is unnecessary overhead if a single epsilon suffices Contigs lack trained model embeddings (no data.csv/data_split.csv) — the clustering operates on learned deep-learning features, not raw sequence composition

skills.description: Use when a greedy feature selection has produced a fixed feature subset for an SVR model and you want to verify by ablation that removing specific features (e.g. conservation or distance-based ones) improves CV and blind-test PCC.
skills.name: greedy-feature-subset-ablation
skills.search_text: greedy-feature-subset-ablation Use when a greedy feature selection has produced a fixed feature subset for an SVR model and you want to verify by ablation that removing specific features (e.g. conservation or distance-based ones) improves CV and blind-test PCC. You need the published challenge performance (PCC 0.570 CV / 0.566 blind) of the original 8-feature model rather than the ablation study Your variants are in intergenic regions or more than 200 bp from splice sites — PredPSI-SVR filters these out before feature extraction, so delta-PSI prediction is not applicable The dataset is large enough that deep-learning methods (e.g. MMSplice-style neural networks) are preferable; the article notes the small vex-seq sample size prevented deep learning Tests whether a greedy feature-selection result is globally optimal by ablating selected features from a support vector regression model (here, dropping the CADD-derived priPhyloP and minDistTSS from PredPSI-SVR's 8-feature set) and re-evaluating on 10-fold cross-validation and an independent blind test. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Tests whether a greedy feature-selection result is globally optimal by ablating selected features from a support vector regression model (here, dropping the CADD-derived priPhyloP and minDistTSS from PredPSI-SVR's 8-feature set) and re-evaluating on 10-fold cross-validation and an independent blind test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the published challenge performance (PCC 0.570 CV / 0.566 blind) of the original 8-feature model rather than the ablation study Your variants are in intergenic regions or more than 200 bp from splice sites — PredPSI-SVR filters these out before feature extraction, so delta-PSI prediction is not applicable The dataset is large enough that deep-learning methods (e.g. MMSplice-style neural networks) are preferable; the article notes the small vex-seq sample size prevented deep learning

skills.description: Use when a small-sample regression task (e.g., predicting ΔΨ on vex-seq TR957) has many candidate features (e.g., 42 splicing-related features) and you must identify the minimal subset maximizing cross-validated PCC.
skills.name: greedy-forward-feature-selection
skills.search_text: greedy-forward-feature-selection Use when a small-sample regression task (e.g., predicting ΔΨ on vex-seq TR957) has many candidate features (e.g., 42 splicing-related features) and you must identify the minimal subset maximizing cross-validated PCC. The input is already a small, curated feature set where subset selection would overfit the CV metric The sample size is large enough for embedded feature-selection methods (e.g., regularized or deep models); the paper notes the small number of vex-seq samples is what motivated greedy selection over more powerful algorithms The target task is classification rather than ΔΨ regression evaluated by PCC, and no analogous validation metric is available per subset http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Greedy forward feature selection for high-dimensional ML: at each round add the single remaining feature that maximizes k-fold cross-validation performance, stopping when the metric (here Pearson correlation coefficient) peaks. Used in PredPSI-SVR to shrink 42 splicing-related features down to the eight that contribute most to ΔΨ prediction. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785

skills.description: Use when de novo methylation motif detection from resquiggled ONT multi-fast5 data is needed and existing tools (MEME with Tombo or Nanodisco) lack sensitivity or determinism.
skills.name: greedy-motif-enrichment-algorithm-implementation
skills.search_text: greedy-motif-enrichment-algorithm-implementation Use when de novo methylation motif detection from resquiggled ONT multi-fast5 data is needed and existing tools (MEME with Tombo or Nanodisco) lack sensitivity or determinism. Input is raw, unresquiggled single-read fast5 files — Snapper requires Tombo-resquiggled, multi-fast5 converted data first. The task is generic sequence motif discovery without nanopore signal data (e.g., motif search in a plain FASTA) — this skill is specific to ONT-based methylation motif enrichment. Manual/interactive motif curation is required — Snapper is designed to run the enrichment process without manual control and is deterministic. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Implements Snapper's high-sensitive greedy algorithm for position-specific methylation motif enrichment from Oxford Nanopore reads: it iteratively selects the most over-represented k-mer against a reference genome background, extracts it, filters the seq_set, and repeats until the min_conf/max_motifs termination criteria are met. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Implements Snapper's high-sensitive greedy algorithm for position-specific methylation motif enrichment from Oxford Nanopore reads: it iteratively selects the most over-represented k-mer against a reference genome background, extracts it, filters the seq_set, and repeats until the min_conf/max_motifs termination criteria are met.

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing uTR's greedy unit-selection step for mosaic tandem repeat decomposition — e.g., to validate that on S=ACCGACCGACCG the loop first selects ACCG (extended penalty 7) and terminates with U={ACCG}.
skills.name: greedy-penalty-minimization-algorithm
skills.search_text: greedy-penalty-minimization-algorithm Use when implementing or reproducing uTR's greedy unit-selection step for mosaic tandem repeat decomposition — e.g., to validate that on S=ACCGACCGACCG the loop first selects ACCG (extended penalty 7) and terminates with U={ACCG}. The repeat units of interest are longer than 20 nt — uTR auto-estimates only units of length 20 nt or less, and long units should first be computed with mTR before running this selection loop You need the series of variant units within an already-estimated mosaic tandem repeat pattern (e.g., substitutions/indels per read) — use vTR, not the greedy selection loop You need to cluster reads into haplotype groups to reduce computation time — that is cTR's role, not this decomposition criterion http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reproduces uTR's greedy unit-selection loop, which builds a set U of repeat units by iteratively adding the candidate unit that minimizes an extended penalty — sum_{u in U}(|u|+o(u)) plus the residual length of unexplained decomposition strings — until no unit reduces it. This is the core decomposition criterion that lets uTR output mosaic tandem repeat patterns with different repeat units. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Reproduces uTR's greedy unit-selection loop, which builds a set U of repeat units by iteratively adding the candidate unit that minimizes an extended penalty — sum_{u in U}(|u|+o(u)) plus the residual length of unexplained decomposition strings — until no unit reduces it. This is the core decomposition criterion that lets uTR output mosaic tandem repeat patterns with different repeat units.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The repeat units of interest are longer than 20 nt — uTR auto-estimates only units of length 20 nt or less, and long units should first be computed with mTR before running this selection loop You need the series of variant units within an already-estimated mosaic tandem repeat pattern (e.g., substitutions/indels per read) — use vTR, not the greedy selection loop You need to cluster reads into haplotype groups to reduce computation time — that is cTR's role, not this decomposition criterion

skills.search_text: greedy-weighted-set-cover-taxonomic-labeling Use when a long-read metagenomic pipeline must assign species labels to groups of ARG-carrying reads (e.g., MCL read clusters from an overlap graph) instead of classifying each read individually with a classifier like Kraken2 or Centrifuge. The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts or hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited Species present are unseen in the reference database or have novel plasmid syntenies — Argo is inherently reference-based and may misclassify them Coverage is extremely low (below ~1x genome copy): species ARGs default to 'unclassified', and insufficient coverage yields inadequate read overlaps and unstable clustering/normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 Assigns taxonomic labels (species) to clusters of ARG-containing long reads collectively, rather than per-read, by greedily solving a weighted set cover over species sets whose weights are negative sums of DIAMOND alignment scores (AS). skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare predicted cell segmentation masks against manually annotated ground-truth membranes, especially for tissue segmentation methods on multiplexed imaging (TMA cores, MIBI, IMC).
skills.name: ground-truth-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: ground-truth-annotation-comparison Use when you need to quantitatively compare predicted cell segmentation masks against manually annotated ground-truth membranes, especially for tissue segmentation methods on multiplexed imaging (TMA cores, MIBI, IMC). When ground-truth manual annotations do not exist — DSC/JSC against manual membranes cannot be computed and only qualitative comparison (e.g., Fig. 2G-style overlay inspection) is possible When the target cells are round and non-epithelial — the paper shows Voronoi-style dilation-from-nuclei is inadequate mainly for columnar epithelial cells with elongated, irregular morphologies, so a full border-dilation benchmark may add little When the segmentation method was trained on the annotated tissue itself — the comparison would be circular; note Mesmer was trained on normal mouse small intestine, normal human colon, and colorectal cancer, but not colorectal adenomas http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmarks segmentation outputs (MIRIAM, Mesmer, Voronoi) against manually annotated cell membranes by extracting cell borders, dilating them with a 5-pixel square kernel, and computing image-level and per-cell Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity coefficients. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Benchmarks segmentation outputs (MIRIAM, Mesmer, Voronoi) against manually annotated cell membranes by extracting cell borders, dilating them with a 5-pixel square kernel, and computing image-level and per-cell Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ground-truth manual annotations do not exist — DSC/JSC against manual membranes cannot be computed and only qualitative comparison (e.g., Fig. 2G-style overlay inspection) is possible When the target cells are round and non-epithelial — the paper shows Voronoi-style dilation-from-nuclei is inadequate mainly for columnar epithelial cells with elongated, irregular morphologies, so a full border-dilation benchmark may add little When the segmentation method was trained on the annotated tissue itself — the comparison would be circular; note Mesmer was trained on normal mouse small intestine, normal human colon, and colorectal cancer, but not colorectal adenomas

Evaluation should be on real genomes (NA12878, CHM1, CHM13, HG002) rather than simulated truth sets — use the published VCFs in 1dayac/novel_insertions_supplementary instead of re-simulating The method of interest targets insertions much shorter than 300 bp, since Novel-X's analysis focuses on insertions longer than 300 bp and small insertions often lack sufficient barcode coverage The caller cannot run on either synthetic long reads or standard short reads matched at the same coverage (the benchmark design assumes one of these two input types) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Builds a simulated benchmark for non-reference sequence (NRS) insertion detection by embedding randomly generated DNA sequences into GRCh38 and simulating barcoded synthetic long reads, enabling exact precision/recall evaluation of insertion callers against known truth. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653

The analysis evaluates MR methods only under weak-instrument or pleiotropy conditions and the overlap condition is out of scope. skills.search_text: haplotype-aware-variant-filtering Use when calling SNVs from ONT long reads at loci classified as low-quality or low-complexity, where per-locus binomial genotyping is unreliable and haplotype-level consensus evidence must be generated, realigned, genotyped, and filtered. Loci already classified as high-quality and genotyped by the binomial likelihood model (theta = 0.03, priors over 0/0, 0/1, 1/1) — these skip the haplotype consensus route Short-read (Illumina-style) data — the method's phasing and consensus steps depend on ONT long-read spanning alignments Repetitive regions without sufficient overlapping reads — with <40% overlap ratio and few spanning reads, neither the MSA nor assembly model has adequate support http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 miniSNV's post-consensus variant filtering stage for low-quality loci: haplotype consensus sequences (abPOA MSA or de Bruijn assembly) are realigned with KSW2, hapGT genotypes are assigned, and variants are dropped when phasing support is weak or when preGT is 0/1 but hapGT is 1/1, to avoid systematic-error false positives. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: miniSNV's post-consensus variant filtering stage for low-quality loci: haplotype consensus sequences (abPOA MSA or de Bruijn assembly) are realigned with KSW2, hapGT genotypes are assigned, and variants are dropped when phasing support is weak or when preGT is 0/1 but hapGT is 1/1, to avoid systematic-error false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci already classified as high-quality and genotyped by the binomial likelihood model (theta = 0.03, priors over 0/0, 0/1, 1/1) — these skip the haplotype consensus route Short-read (Illumina-style) data — the method's phasing and consensus steps depend on ONT long-read spanning alignments Repetitive regions without sufficient overlapping reads — with <40% overlap ratio and few spanning reads, neither the MSA nor assembly model has adequate support

skills.description: Use when assembling a diploid genome from long noisy reads (Nanopore R9/R10, PacBio CLR) and the string graph contains heterozygous bubbles/branches that must be split into primary and alternate haplotype contigs.
skills.name: haplotype-bubble-resolution
skills.search_text: haplotype-bubble-resolution Use when assembling a diploid genome from long noisy reads (Nanopore R9/R10, PacBio CLR) and the string graph contains heterozygous bubbles/branches that must be split into primary and alternate haplotype contigs. Input is high-accuracy PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex reads — the article reports PECAT achieves mediocre performance on these data types The organism is haploid or near-clonal with very low heterozygosity — SNP calling accuracy is low in low heterozygosity rate regions and error correction may not distinguish errors from heterozygote alleles Available data coverage is low — PECAT needs higher coverage of data to obtain a high-quality phased assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Resolves heterozygous bubbles in a string graph by scoring best-overlap-graph edges (s_i = (n_i+ * w - n_i-, l_i)), removing SNP-inconsistent overlaps, and applying an alternate-branch heuristic to emit primary and alternate haplotype contigs from long noisy reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Resolves heterozygous bubbles in a string graph by scoring best-overlap-graph edges (s_i = (n_i+ * w - n_i-, l_i)), removing SNP-inconsistent overlaps, and applying an alternate-branch heuristic to emit primary and alternate haplotype contigs from long noisy reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is high-accuracy PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex reads — the article reports PECAT achieves mediocre performance on these data types The organism is haploid or near-clonal with very low heterozygosity — SNP calling accuracy is low in low heterozygosity rate regions and error correction may not distinguish errors from heterozygote alleles Available data coverage is low — PECAT needs higher coverage of data to obtain a high-quality phased assembly

skills.description: Use when ONT POD5/FAST5 + BAM data from diploid samples (e.g. Ashkenazim trio HG002/HG003/HG004) must be phased into parental haplotypes and allele-specific methylation (epihaplotypes) or imprinted regions must be identified.
skills.name: haplotype-phased-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: haplotype-phased-methylation-calling Use when ONT POD5/FAST5 + BAM data from diploid samples (e.g. Ashkenazim trio HG002/HG003/HG004) must be phased into parental haplotypes and allele-specific methylation (epihaplotypes) or imprinted regions must be identified. The sample region falls in long runs of homozygosity where read phasing (and therefore phased methylation analysis of imprinted regions) is not possible. Only aggregate per-site methylation is needed without allele/phase resolution — a direct DeepMod2/Guppy/Dorado per-site call on the unphased BAM suffices. Non-CpG or non-5mC modifications are of interest — DeepMod2 currently provides models only for 5mCpG methylation due to lack of training data for other modifications. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Detect per-read 5mC methylation from Oxford Nanopore signal with DeepMod2 on haplotype-phased BAMs (NanoCaller phasing), yielding phased per-site methylation frequencies (mod_percentage_phase1/phase2) that can be classified into epihaplotype states to predict imprinted control regions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Detect per-read 5mC methylation from Oxford Nanopore signal with DeepMod2 on haplotype-phased BAMs (NanoCaller phasing), yielding phased per-site methylation frequencies (mod_percentage_phase1/phase2) that can be classified into epihaplotype states to predict imprinted control regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample region falls in long runs of homozygosity where read phasing (and therefore phased methylation analysis of imprinted regions) is not possible. Only aggregate per-site methylation is needed without allele/phase resolution — a direct DeepMod2/Guppy/Dorado per-site call on the unphased BAM suffices. Non-CpG or non-5mC modifications are of interest — DeepMod2 currently provides models only for 5mCpG methylation due to lack of training data for other modifications.

skills.name: haplotype-phased-read-grouping
skills.search_text: haplotype-phased-read-grouping Use when nanoHiMe-seq (or similar nanopore) reads must be assigned to haplotypes to test allele-specific CpG methylation or allele-specific 6mA enrichment in CpG islands and ENCODE H3K27me3/H3K4me3 peak regions. Loci with low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs, where the article notes phasing of 6mA regions and CpG methylation is unreliable Regions with read coverage below 20, which the article excludes from allele-specific testing Short-read or bisulfite data without per-read haplotype information — this skill presumes long nanopore reads jointly called for 6mA and mCpG by nanoHiMe http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Groups nanopore reads by parental haplotype using haplotagging and phasing of heterozygous variants (Margin v2.2, WhatsHap v1.4) so that per-read CpG methylation calls and 6mA region calls from nanoHiMe can be compared between alleles for allele-specific epigenetic analysis. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Groups nanopore reads by parental haplotype using haplotagging and phasing of heterozygous variants (Margin v2.2, WhatsHap v1.4) so that per-read CpG methylation calls and 6mA region calls from nanoHiMe can be compared between alleles for allele-specific epigenetic analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci with low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs, where the article notes phasing of 6mA regions and CpG methylation is unreliable Regions with read coverage below 20, which the article excludes from allele-specific testing Short-read or bisulfite data without per-read haplotype information — this skill presumes long nanopore reads jointly called for 6mA and mCpG by nanoHiMe

skills.description: Use when calling haplotype-resolved SVs (including complex translocations, duplications, and inversions) from PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT long-read WGS BAMs, especially when alignment-based callers underperform or low-coverage (10x) data must be handled.
skills.name: haplotype-resolved-assembly-based-sv-calling
skills.search_text: haplotype-resolved-assembly-based-sv-calling Use when calling haplotype-resolved SVs (including complex translocations, duplications, and inversions) from PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT long-read WGS BAMs, especially when alignment-based callers underperform or low-coverage (10x) data must be handled. Calling SVs on sex (X/Y) chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes is very different Using the VolcanoSV-asm component on homozygous samples such as CHM13, which derives from a single homozygous complete hydatidiform mole and is unsuitable for haplotype phasing Detecting small indels from ONT data via assembly — assembly-based small-indel detection proved ineffective for ONT data with low precision for all tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Reproduces VolcanoSV's hybrid SV detection workflow, which combines reference-based read alignment with local de novo assembly to build a phased diploid assembly and call haplotype-resolved structural variants (DEL, INS, DUP, INV, TRA) from long-read sequencing data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Reproduces VolcanoSV's hybrid SV detection workflow, which combines reference-based read alignment with local de novo assembly to build a phased diploid assembly and call haplotype-resolved structural variants (DEL, INS, DUP, INV, TRA) from long-read sequencing data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling SVs on sex (X/Y) chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes is very different Using the VolcanoSV-asm component on homozygous samples such as CHM13, which derives from a single homozygous complete hydatidiform mole and is unsuitable for haplotype phasing Detecting small indels from ONT data via assembly — assembly-based small-indel detection proved ineffective for ONT data with low precision for all tools

skills.description: Use when you have a long-read BAM (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) from a diploid sample and need chromosome-wise phased maternal/paternal contigs to enable haplotype-resolved SV discovery or downstream assembly-based variant benchmarking.
skills.name: haplotype-resolved-long-read-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: haplotype-resolved-long-read-genome-assembly Use when you have a long-read BAM (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) from a diploid sample and need chromosome-wise phased maternal/paternal contigs to enable haplotype-resolved SV discovery or downstream assembly-based variant benchmarking. Input reads are from sex chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosomes because its phasing procedure for sex chromosomes differs fundamentally The sample is haploid/homozygous (e.g. CHM13 derived from a complete hydatidiform mole) — haplotype phasing is inapplicable, as the authors noted for CHM13 You only have short-read (Illumina) data or already possess a finished phased assembly and only need SV calling from it — use VolcanoSV-vc directly or another caller instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates a phased diploid assembly from single-molecule long reads (HiFi, CLR, or ONT) by combining reference-guided phasing of SNPs with local de novo assembly, per autosome, as implemented in VolcanoSV-asm. The phased assembly is the substrate for haplotype-resolved SV calling rather than a standalone assembly product. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Generates a phased diploid assembly from single-molecule long reads (HiFi, CLR, or ONT) by combining reference-guided phasing of SNPs with local de novo assembly, per autosome, as implemented in VolcanoSV-asm. The phased assembly is the substrate for haplotype-resolved SV calling rather than a standalone assembly product.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are from sex chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosomes because its phasing procedure for sex chromosomes differs fundamentally The sample is haploid/homozygous (e.g. CHM13 derived from a complete hydatidiform mole) — haplotype phasing is inapplicable, as the authors noted for CHM13 You only have short-read (Illumina) data or already possess a finished phased assembly and only need SV calling from it — use VolcanoSV-vc directly or another caller instead

skills.description: Use when you have haplotype-phased ONT nanopore reads (e.g. haplotype-tagged HG002 pod5/BAM) and need allele-specific CpG methylation frequencies and allelic DMR detection.
skills.name: haplotype-resolved-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: haplotype-resolved-methylation-calling Use when you have haplotype-phased ONT nanopore reads (e.g. haplotype-tagged HG002 pod5/BAM) and need allele-specific CpG methylation frequencies and allelic DMR detection. Reads are not haplotype-phased, so per-read calls cannot be split into parental methylation tracks Data are not ONT R10.4 nanopore reads or the target motif is not CpG/CG (DeepBAM was developed for CpG methylation states on mainstream R10.4 data) A benchmark comparison to Dorado or DeepSignal-style callers on non-human/plant R10.4 datasets is the goal rather than allelic analysis Calling CpG methylation per-read with DeepBAM on haplotype-phased Oxford Nanopore (R10.4) reads and aggregating calls by parental haplotype to detect allele-specific methylation and DMRs, including at imprinted loci and transposable elements. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Calling CpG methylation per-read with DeepBAM on haplotype-phased Oxford Nanopore (R10.4) reads and aggregating calls by parental haplotype to detect allele-specific methylation and DMRs, including at imprinted loci and transposable elements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not haplotype-phased, so per-read calls cannot be split into parental methylation tracks Data are not ONT R10.4 nanopore reads or the target motif is not CpG/CG (DeepBAM was developed for CpG methylation states on mainstream R10.4 data) A benchmark comparison to Dorado or DeepSignal-style callers on non-human/plant R10.4 datasets is the goal rather than allelic analysis

skills.description: Use when you have haplotype-resolved BAM files and a BED of candidate repetitive regions R = [S, E], and need to prepare span-only read subsets for per-region, per-haplotype consensus generation (e.g., TRiCoLOR REFER).
skills.name: haplotype-resolved-read-trimming
skills.search_text: haplotype-resolved-read-trimming Use when you have haplotype-resolved BAM files and a BED of candidate repetitive regions R = [S, E], and need to prepare span-only read subsets for per-region, per-haplotype consensus generation (e.g., TRiCoLOR REFER). Regions not spanned end-to-end by any long read in a given haplotype — no entirely spanning read can be fetched, so no trimmed read set or consensus can be produced Genomic regions that are unassembled (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres) — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there Haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y chromosome) or polyploid species — outside TRiCoLOR's current diploid haplotype-resolved design http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Trims haplotype-specific long reads (ONT or PacBio BAM alignments) so that only the sequence between the coordinates S and E of a candidate repetitive region is retained, before partial order alignment (POA) computes per-haplotype consensus sequences. Trimming reduces runtime of the downstream SPOA step without sacrificing consensus accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Trims haplotype-specific long reads (ONT or PacBio BAM alignments) so that only the sequence between the coordinates S and E of a candidate repetitive region is retained, before partial order alignment (POA) computes per-haplotype consensus sequences. Trimming reduces runtime of the downstream SPOA step without sacrificing consensus accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Regions not spanned end-to-end by any long read in a given haplotype — no entirely spanning read can be fetched, so no trimmed read set or consensus can be produced Genomic regions that are unassembled (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres) — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there Haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y chromosome) or polyploid species — outside TRiCoLOR's current diploid haplotype-resolved design

skills.description: Use when you have ONT long reads basecalled with MM/ML methylation tags that are haplotagged by SNV phase (WhatsHap haplotag), and you need to find CpGs whose modification probabilities distinguish the two haplotypes.
skills.name: haplotype-specific-methylation-identification
skills.search_text: haplotype-specific-methylation-identification Use when you have ONT long reads basecalled with MM/ML methylation tags that are haplotagged by SNV phase (WhatsHap haplotag), and you need to find CpGs whose modification probabilities distinguish the two haplotypes. Analysis targets human sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females makes haplotype methylation patterns inconsistent (README: autosome only) Input BAM still contains secondary or supplementary alignments — pysam MM tag reading will error Sequencing depth is well below ~30X ONT coverage, where upstream SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) do not work reasonably http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Identify allele-specific (haplotype-specific) CpG methylation from methylation-annotated ONT reads, using the Wilcoxon rank sum test on base modification probabilities of SNV-haplotagged reads as the first step of MethPhaser's methylation-based phasing loop. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Identify allele-specific (haplotype-specific) CpG methylation from methylation-annotated ONT reads, using the Wilcoxon rank sum test on base modification probabilities of SNV-haplotagged reads as the first step of MethPhaser's methylation-based phasing loop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis targets human sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females makes haplotype methylation patterns inconsistent (README: autosome only) Input BAM still contains secondary or supplementary alignments — pysam MM tag reading will error Sequencing depth is well below ~30X ONT coverage, where upstream SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) do not work reasonably

skills.description: Use when comparing polishing pipelines (e.g. NextPolish2 vs Racon+Merfin 'RM') on HiFi assemblies where switch-error rates and QV in heterozygous regions must be benchmarked against reported values.
skills.name: haplotype-switch-error-assessment
skills.search_text: haplotype-switch-error-assessment Use when comparing polishing pipelines (e.g. NextPolish2 vs Racon+Merfin 'RM') on HiFi assemblies where switch-error rates and QV in heterozygous regions must be benchmarked against reported values. The genome is haploid or homozygous (e.g. CHM13), so there are no heterozygous regions in which switch errors can be measured The assembly was not produced from HiFi long reads or lacks phase information/trio binning, making switch-error computation meaningless No independent high-coverage short reads are available to build yak k-mer datasets for k-mer consensus evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Quantifies haplotype switch errors and consensus quality values (QV) of HiFi-assembled genomes before and after polishing, using k-mer-based evaluation (yak/Merqury) on heterozygous diploid and trio-binned assemblies. It exists to verify that polishing tools correct SNV/indel errors without breaking local haplotype consistency. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Quantifies haplotype switch errors and consensus quality values (QV) of HiFi-assembled genomes before and after polishing, using k-mer-based evaluation (yak/Merqury) on heterozygous diploid and trio-binned assemblies. It exists to verify that polishing tools correct SNV/indel errors without breaking local haplotype consistency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome is haploid or homozygous (e.g. CHM13), so there are no heterozygous regions in which switch errors can be measured The assembly was not produced from HiFi long reads or lacks phase information/trio binning, making switch-error computation meaningless No independent high-coverage short reads are available to build yak k-mer datasets for k-mer consensus evaluation

skills.description: Use when a workflow interleaves hardware acquisition steps (e.g. microscope imaging, slide-loader moves) with dependent software steps (e.g. image analysis modules) and you need a dependency-safe schedule plus crash recovery from persisted task states.
skills.name: hardware-software-task-dependency-resolution
skills.search_text: hardware-software-task-dependency-resolution Use when a workflow interleaves hardware acquisition steps (e.g. microscope imaging, slide-loader moves) with dependent software steps (e.g. image analysis modules) and you need a dependency-safe schedule plus crash recovery from persisted task states. The pipeline is purely computational with no robotic/microscope hardware tasks, so serial execution of microscope-dependent modules adds no value. Imaging is a single pass with no analysis-contingent re-imaging step, so there are no hardware-software dependencies to resolve or entry points to resume between. You need a versioned, benchmarked release of the scheduler — OpenHiCAMM exposes no changelog or version number and only qualitative robustness claims are reported. http://edamontology.org/topic_3384 Resolves a directed task-dependency graph mixing robotic microscope hardware tasks and computational image-analysis tasks into a topologically ordered schedule, and persists workflow setup, module configurations, and completed task states in an integrated SQL database so interrupted workflows can be resumed without re-executing finished tasks. Derived from the OpenHiCAMM workflow manager's scheduling and persistence algorithm. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Resolves a directed task-dependency graph mixing robotic microscope hardware tasks and computational image-analysis tasks into a topologically ordered schedule, and persists workflow setup, module configurations, and completed task states in an integrated SQL database so interrupted workflows can be resumed without re-executing finished tasks. Derived from the OpenHiCAMM workflow manager's scheduling and persistence algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline is purely computational with no robotic/microscope hardware tasks, so serial execution of microscope-dependent modules adds no value. Imaging is a single pass with no analysis-contingent re-imaging step, so there are no hardware-software dependencies to resolve or entry points to resume between. You need a versioned, benchmarked release of the scheduler — OpenHiCAMM exposes no changelog or version number and only qualitative robustness claims are reported.

skills.description: Use when per-genomic-position methylation calls from ONT nanopolish data must be aggregated into a single locus-level P-value for tumor-vs-control hypomethylation at somatically inferred LINE1 3' transduction source elements.
skills.name: harmonic-mean-p-value-combination
skills.search_text: harmonic-mean-p-value-combination Use when per-genomic-position methylation calls from ONT nanopolish data must be aggregated into a single locus-level P-value for tumor-vs-control hypomethylation at somatically inferred LINE1 3' transduction source elements. When only a single genomic position (not a multi-locus LINE1 source element) is tested — a one-sided Fisher's exact test on that position suffices and no P-value combination is needed When the question is methylation difference in either direction (two-sided), since the workflow's tests are explicitly one-sided for tumor hypomethylation When the input is not ONT signal-level methylation data (e.g. bisulfite or array methylation), as the nanopolish index/call-methylation front end depends on original fast5 files http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3393 Combines per-locus significance P-values (one-sided Fisher's exact tests on nanopolish methylation frequencies) at a LINE1 source element into a single asymptotically exact combined P-value using the harmonicmeanp R package (v3.0), to test whether tumor methylation is lower than matched control across the whole locus. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Combines per-locus significance P-values (one-sided Fisher's exact tests on nanopolish methylation frequencies) at a LINE1 source element into a single asymptotically exact combined P-value using the harmonicmeanp R package (v3.0), to test whether tumor methylation is lower than matched control across the whole locus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single genomic position (not a multi-locus LINE1 source element) is tested — a one-sided Fisher's exact test on that position suffices and no P-value combination is needed When the question is methylation difference in either direction (two-sided), since the workflow's tests are explicitly one-sided for tumor hypomethylation When the input is not ONT signal-level methylation data (e.g. bisulfite or array methylation), as the nanopolish index/call-methylation front end depends on original fast5 files

skills.description: Use when ONT PromethION reads from an HBV-positive tumor are paired with a matched or dummy control BAM and the goal is to enumerate viral integration sites and resolve complex virus-mediated rearrangement structures at single-breakend resolution.
skills.name: hbv-rearrangement-structure-characterization
skills.search_text: hbv-rearrangement-structure-characterization Use when ONT PromethION reads from an HBV-positive tumor are paired with a matched or dummy control BAM and the goal is to enumerate viral integration sites and resolve complex virus-mediated rearrangement structures at single-breakend resolution. The draft assembly was built from noisy long reads without any HiFi data or >=60X short reads — NextPolish2's error checking depends on short-read k-mer spectra The goal is de novo contig construction from ONT ultra-long reads alone; this skill covers HiFi-based assembly plus consensus polishing, not ONT-only assembly Only interested in variant calling against a reference rather than improving assembly consensus accuracy — DeepVariant-based evaluation may be more appropriate than polishing http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assemble high-quality draft genomes from PacBio HiFi long reads (e.g., with hifiasm) and bring them to T2T-grade consensus accuracy by repeat-aware polishing with NextPolish2, using HiFi alignments (winnowmap/minimap2) plus short-read yak k-mer datasets as evidence. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Assemble high-quality draft genomes from PacBio HiFi long reads (e.g., with hifiasm) and bring them to T2T-grade consensus accuracy by repeat-aware polishing with NextPolish2, using HiFi alignments (winnowmap/minimap2) plus short-read yak k-mer datasets as evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The draft assembly was built from noisy long reads without any HiFi data or >=60X short reads — NextPolish2's error checking depends on short-read k-mer spectra The goal is de novo contig construction from ONT ultra-long reads alone; this skill covers HiFi-based assembly plus consensus polishing, not ONT-only assembly Only interested in variant calling against a reference rather than improving assembly consensus accuracy — DeepVariant-based evaluation may be more appropriate than polishing

skills.description: Use when HiFi/CCS long reads or simulated pseudo-long-reads must be aligned to a genome assembly (e.g., CHM13 T2T) to evaluate assembly accuracy or prepare a HiFi mapping file for polishing with NextPolish2.
skills.name: hifi-read-mapping-with-minimap2
skills.search_text: hifi-read-mapping-with-minimap2 Use when HiFi/CCS long reads or simulated pseudo-long-reads must be aligned to a genome assembly (e.g., CHM13 T2T) to evaluate assembly accuracy or prepare a HiFi mapping file for polishing with NextPolish2. Aligning Oxford Nanopore reads (use -x map-ont / lr:hq presets) or Illumina short reads (use -x sr), since the map-hifi preset is tuned for PacBio HiFi/CCS data Mapping within highly repetitive regions such as centromeric satellite arrays where Winnowmap's weighted minimizer sampling is preferred over minimap2 Quality assessment that requires k-mer-based QV (Merqury/yak) rather than alignment-identity QV against a ground-truth reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Map PacBio HiFi long reads (or pseudo-long-reads derived from a reference) against a genome assembly using minimap2's map-hifi preset, sort and index the resulting BAM with samtools, and filter alignments by query coverage and identity for downstream accuracy evaluation such as alignment-identity QV. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Map PacBio HiFi long reads (or pseudo-long-reads derived from a reference) against a genome assembly using minimap2's map-hifi preset, sort and index the resulting BAM with samtools, and filter alignments by query coverage and identity for downstream accuracy evaluation such as alignment-identity QV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Aligning Oxford Nanopore reads (use -x map-ont / lr:hq presets) or Illumina short reads (use -x sr), since the map-hifi preset is tuned for PacBio HiFi/CCS data Mapping within highly repetitive regions such as centromeric satellite arrays where Winnowmap's weighted minimizer sampling is preferred over minimap2 Quality assessment that requires k-mer-based QV (Merqury/yak) rather than alignment-identity QV against a ground-truth reference

skills.description: Use when a source text (e.g., a Transparent Methods supplement) reports quantitative run metrics for an automated HCS imaging experiment — pass durations, per-slide rates, object-detection counts — that must be extracted, verified, and tabulated.
skills.name: high-content-screening-metrics-tabulation
skills.search_text: high-content-screening-metrics-tabulation Use when a source text (e.g., a Transparent Methods supplement) reports quantitative run metrics for an automated HCS imaging experiment — pass durations, per-slide rates, object-detection counts — that must be extracted, verified, and tabulated. The input is raw microscopy image data that still needs embryo detection or stitching — use the OpenHiCAMM workflow (5x detection pass plus 20x re-imaging) instead of metric tabulation. The source section contains only qualitative capability claims (e.g., the OpenHiCAMM discussion section) with no quantitative benchmark results to extract. The experiment used a single-pass commercial microscope acquisition; two-pass duration/object-count metrics do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Extracts and tabulates the quantitative performance metrics of an autonomous two-pass high-content screening run — Phase 1 low-resolution detection pass and Phase 2 high-resolution re-imaging pass — as reported in the OpenHiCAMM study (iScience, 2018), and writes them to a validated CSV table for reproduction and comparison. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Extracts and tabulates the quantitative performance metrics of an autonomous two-pass high-content screening run — Phase 1 low-resolution detection pass and Phase 2 high-resolution re-imaging pass — as reported in the OpenHiCAMM study (iScience, 2018), and writes them to a validated CSV table for reproduction and comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw microscopy image data that still needs embryo detection or stitching — use the OpenHiCAMM workflow (5x detection pass plus 20x re-imaging) instead of metric tabulation. The source section contains only qualitative capability claims (e.g., the OpenHiCAMM discussion section) with no quantitative benchmark results to extract. The experiment used a single-pass commercial microscope acquisition; two-pass duration/object-count metrics do not apply.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic binners on real short-read projects: bins (FASTA) from SemiBin2, SemiBin1, and VAMB must be scored with CheckM and GUNC to count high-quality bins per project.
skills.name: high-quality-bin-quality-assessment-checkm-gunc
skills.search_text: high-quality-bin-quality-assessment-checkm-gunc Use when benchmarking metagenomic binners on real short-read projects: bins (FASTA) from SemiBin2, SemiBin1, and VAMB must be scored with CheckM and GUNC to count high-quality bins per project. Input is raw reads or assembled contigs that have not yet been binned — this skill evaluates existing bins, not the binning step itself. The goal is taxonomic classification of contigs or MAGs rather than quality screening — use CAT/BAT (CAT_pack) for taxonomic annotation instead. The data is long-read sequencing — the reported high-quality-bin gains (8.3-21.5% vs SemiBin1) apply to real short-read samples; long-read results use the ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering comparison instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assesses metagenome-assembled genomes reconstructed by binners such as SemiBin2, SemiBin1, and VAMB using CheckM for completeness/contamination and GUNC for chimerism, in order to classify high-quality bins and quantify per-project binner performance. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209
skills.summary: Assesses metagenome-assembled genomes reconstructed by binners such as SemiBin2, SemiBin1, and VAMB using CheckM for completeness/contamination and GUNC for chimerism, in order to classify high-quality bins and quantify per-project binner performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or assembled contigs that have not yet been binned — this skill evaluates existing bins, not the binning step itself. The goal is taxonomic classification of contigs or MAGs rather than quality screening — use CAT/BAT (CAT_pack) for taxonomic annotation instead. The data is long-read sequencing — the reported high-quality-bin gains (8.3-21.5% vs SemiBin1) apply to real short-read samples; long-read results use the ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering comparison instead.

skills.description: Use when you need to measure total wall-clock runtime and per-process resource use of a high-throughput Nextflow pipeline run, e.g. quantifying Nallo's 34-hour analysis of 192 PacBio samples at 23× coverage from its execution report.
skills.name: high-throughput-sequencing-pipeline-profiling
skills.search_text: high-throughput-sequencing-pipeline-profiling Use when you need to measure total wall-clock runtime and per-process resource use of a high-throughput Nextflow pipeline run, e.g. quantifying Nallo's 34-hour analysis of 192 PacBio samples at 23× coverage from its execution report. You need the biological outputs of Nallo (variant calls, genome assembly, CpG methylation) rather than measurements of the run's speed and resource consumption. No Nextflow execution trace or workflow report exists for the run (e.g. the pipeline was executed with a different engine), so per-process timestamps and durations cannot be extracted. The run is a short single-sample or test-data execution whose duration is not representative of the high-throughput 68-node cluster scenario this skill profiles. Profiling the wall-clock runtime and per-tool resource use of a high-throughput Nextflow long-read genome pipeline (Nallo) by parsing the Nextflow execution trace embedded in its workflow report — e.g. confirming that Nallo 0.5.1 analyzed 192 in-house PacBio samples at 23× average coverage in 34 hours on a 68-node cluster. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag086
skills.summary: Profiling the wall-clock runtime and per-tool resource use of a high-throughput Nextflow long-read genome pipeline (Nallo) by parsing the Nextflow execution trace embedded in its workflow report — e.g. confirming that Nallo 0.5.1 analyzed 192 in-house PacBio samples at 23× average coverage in 34 hours on a 68-node cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the biological outputs of Nallo (variant calls, genome assembly, CpG methylation) rather than measurements of the run's speed and resource consumption. No Nextflow execution trace or workflow report exists for the run (e.g. the pipeline was executed with a different engine), so per-process timestamps and durations cannot be extracted. The run is a short single-sample or test-data execution whose duration is not representative of the high-throughput 68-node cluster scenario this skill profiles.

skills.description: Use when building a cell-type-specific marker gene set from a well-annotated scRNA-seq reference (e.g. the Tasic SMART-seq primary visual cortex dataset) to validate query cell identities in reference-based classification.
skills.name: highly-expressed-gene-selection
skills.search_text: highly-expressed-gene-selection Use when building a cell-type-specific marker gene set from a well-annotated scRNA-seq reference (e.g. the Tasic SMART-seq primary visual cortex dataset) to validate query cell identities in reference-based classification. When the reference dataset has no cell type labels, use scMAGIC_atlas with the atlas as reference instead of deriving reference-cell-type markers When you already have a curated, hand-validated marker gene list for the reference cell types, re-deriving markers via limma/RUVSeq filtering is unnecessary When query cell types are largely absent from both the reference and the atlas, marker-gene validation cannot assign them and the classification will be uninformative In scMAGIC's first-round RBC, candidate marker genes are drawn from the pool of highly expressed genes within each reference cell type (top 20% expression after pseudo-bulk aggregation), then filtered by differential-expression tests against both other reference cell types and atlas cell types. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: In scMAGIC's first-round RBC, candidate marker genes are drawn from the pool of highly expressed genes within each reference cell type (top 20% expression after pseudo-bulk aggregation), then filtered by differential-expression tests against both other reference cell types and atlas cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the reference dataset has no cell type labels, use scMAGIC_atlas with the atlas as reference instead of deriving reference-cell-type markers When you already have a curated, hand-validated marker gene list for the reference cell types, re-deriving markers via limma/RUVSeq filtering is unnecessary When query cell types are largely absent from both the reference and the atlas, marker-gene validation cannot assign them and the classification will be uninformative

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix needs a statistically tested set of significantly highly variable genes, and dropout-based methods (M3Drop/DANB) should be benchmarked against a mean-variance-based alternative.
skills.name: highly-variable-gene-significance-testing
skills.search_text: highly-variable-gene-significance-testing Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix needs a statistically tested set of significantly highly variable genes, and dropout-based methods (M3Drop/DANB) should be benchmarked against a mean-variance-based alternative. The dataset is UMI-quantified and the goal is dropout-based or Pearson-residual feature selection — M3Drop's DANB model (NBumi functions) is tailored for UMIs instead The gene set is already selected and only downstream clustering or pseudotime analysis is required — feature selection would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detects significantly highly variable genes (HVGs) in scRNA-seq data using the Brennecke et al. (2015) mean-variance significance algorithm, which the M3Drop R package ships alongside its dropout-based (Michaelis-Menten) feature selection specifically for comparison purposes. genomics/v1 10.1002/1873-3468.12684
skills.summary: Detects significantly highly variable genes (HVGs) in scRNA-seq data using the Brennecke et al. (2015) mean-variance significance algorithm, which the M3Drop R package ships alongside its dropout-based (Michaelis-Menten) feature selection specifically for comparison purposes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is UMI-quantified and the goal is dropout-based or Pearson-residual feature selection — M3Drop's DANB model (NBumi functions) is tailored for UMIs instead The gene set is already selected and only downstream clustering or pseudotime analysis is required — feature selection would be redundant

skills.description: Use when comparing normalization methods on multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) marker intensity distributions, especially to test whether peak alignment preserves distribution shape for unimodal (e.g., PD-L1) or bimodal (e.g., ECAD) markers.
skills.name: histogram-distribution-alignment-visualization
skills.search_text: histogram-distribution-alignment-visualization Use when comparing normalization methods on multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) marker intensity distributions, especially to test whether peak alignment preserves distribution shape for unimodal (e.g., PD-L1) or bimodal (e.g., ECAD) markers. Markers with highly heterogeneous or irregular distributions (e.g., CD45 in PRAD-CyCIF) that violate the assumptions of the automatic workflow — these require UniFORM's guided fine-tuning mode instead mIHC (chromogenic) data, where linear normalization factors are unsuitable due to non-linear enzyme-catalyzed signal amplification Pixel-level normalization tasks where segmentation masks for non-cell region exclusion are unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Reproduces UniFORM's marker intensity distribution alignment analysis: computes histograms of log-transformed cell intensities, aligns them via automatic rigid-landmark functional registration (maximum cross-correlation), and visualizes before/after normalization for benchmarks like MxNorm registration, Z score, ComBat, and mean division. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172
skills.summary: Reproduces UniFORM's marker intensity distribution alignment analysis: computes histograms of log-transformed cell intensities, aligns them via automatic rigid-landmark functional registration (maximum cross-correlation), and visualizes before/after normalization for benchmarks like MxNorm registration, Z score, ComBat, and mean division.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Markers with highly heterogeneous or irregular distributions (e.g., CD45 in PRAD-CyCIF) that violate the assumptions of the automatic workflow — these require UniFORM's guided fine-tuning mode instead mIHC (chromogenic) data, where linear normalization factors are unsuitable due to non-linear enzyme-catalyzed signal amplification Pixel-level normalization tasks where segmentation masks for non-cell region exclusion are unavailable

skills.description: Use when WGS long-read FASTQ data (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) is available and clinically confirmed HLA-I/-II allele/group predictions are needed, especially at low (~10x) coverage or with older nanopore chemistry.
skills.name: hla-allele-prediction-from-long-reads
skills.search_text: hla-allele-prediction-from-long-reads Use when WGS long-read FASTQ data (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) is available and clinically confirmed HLA-I/-II allele/group predictions are needed, especially at low (~10x) coverage or with older nanopore chemistry. Input reads are Illumina-sized short reads (100–150 bp) — the README indicates best short-read results come from the HPTASR targeted-assembly mode, not the streamed long-read HPRA workflow The aligner cannot emit SAM output with MD tags, or a strictly allele-level (not group-level) clinical call is required — HLAminer's streamed mode yields fairly accurate group/allele predictions with the noted ambiguities Reads are targeted amplicons or RNA-seq rather than whole-genome shotgun long reads where a chr6-stripped GRCh38 reference alignment is the intended input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Predict HLA class I and class II allele groups from whole-genome shotgun long-read (ONT/PacBio) data by streaming SAM alignments (with MD tags) directly from minimap2 into HLAminer v1.4's HPRA mode, avoiding intermediate SAM files on disk. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Predict HLA class I and class II allele groups from whole-genome shotgun long-read (ONT/PacBio) data by streaming SAM alignments (with MD tags) directly from minimap2 into HLAminer v1.4's HPRA mode, avoiding intermediate SAM files on disk.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are Illumina-sized short reads (100–150 bp) — the README indicates best short-read results come from the HPTASR targeted-assembly mode, not the streamed long-read HPRA workflow The aligner cannot emit SAM output with MD tags, or a strictly allele-level (not group-level) clinical call is required — HLAminer's streamed mode yields fairly accurate group/allele predictions with the noted ambiguities Reads are targeted amplicons or RNA-seq rather than whole-genome shotgun long reads where a chr6-stripped GRCh38 reference alignment is the intended input

skills.description: Use when predicting HLA class I/II alleles from WGS long-read FASTQ data (PacBio HiFi or nanopore), especially when clinically confirmed HLA types are available for benchmarking and disk-heavy SAM intermediates should be avoided.
skills.name: hla-allele-typing-from-wgs
skills.search_text: hla-allele-typing-from-wgs Use when predicting HLA class I/II alleles from WGS long-read FASTQ data (PacBio HiFi or nanopore), especially when clinically confirmed HLA types are available for benchmarking and disk-heavy SAM intermediates should be avoided. Input is Illumina short-read data — the README states best short-read results come from the HPTASR targeted-assembly route with reads 100 bp and up (ideally 150 bp), not streamed long-read HPRA Reads are so short (e.g., 50 bp) that 4-digit HLA allele predictions would be ambiguous, or no long-read aligner output is available to stream The goal is de novo targeted assembly of HLA contigs (HPTASR) rather than direct read-alignment-based prediction from long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Predicts HLA class I and II alleles from whole-genome shotgun long-read sequencing (PacBio HiFi, ONT PromethION) by streaming minimap2 SAM alignments directly into HLAminer v1.4 in read-alignment (HPRA) mode, avoiding intermediate .sam files on disk. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Predicts HLA class I and II alleles from whole-genome shotgun long-read sequencing (PacBio HiFi, ONT PromethION) by streaming minimap2 SAM alignments directly into HLAminer v1.4 in read-alignment (HPRA) mode, avoiding intermediate .sam files on disk.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Illumina short-read data — the README states best short-read results come from the HPTASR targeted-assembly route with reads 100 bp and up (ideally 150 bp), not streamed long-read HPRA Reads are so short (e.g., 50 bp) that 4-digit HLA allele predictions would be ambiguous, or no long-read aligner output is available to stream The goal is de novo targeted assembly of HLA contigs (HPTASR) rather than direct read-alignment-based prediction from long reads

skills.description: Use when setting up the HLAminer long-read (nanopore/PacBio) alignment reference or when the summary must report only P-designated alleles for identical antigen-binding domains.
skills.name: hla-p-designation-file-handling
skills.search_text: hla-p-designation-file-handling Use when setting up the HLAminer long-read (nanopore/PacBio) alignment reference or when the summary must report only P-designated alleles for identical antigen-binding domains. Running the HPTASR short-read targeted-assembly path, which aligns contigs to IMGT/HLA allele references directly rather than to the concatenated GRCh38-noChr6+HLA reference The genome-wide reference already exists, is current, and matches the static Zenodo/BCGSC January 2025 deposit http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Prepares the HLAminer long-read alignment reference by combining updated IMGT/HLA class I and II genomic allele sequences (HLA-I_II_GEN.fasta) with the GRCh38 chromosome-only genome lacking chr6, and fetches the hla_nom_p.txt P-designation file that collapses alleles sharing antigen-binding domains in the prediction summary. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Prepares the HLAminer long-read alignment reference by combining updated IMGT/HLA class I and II genomic allele sequences (HLA-I_II_GEN.fasta) with the GRCh38 chromosome-only genome lacking chr6, and fetches the hla_nom_p.txt P-designation file that collapses alleles sharing antigen-binding domains in the prediction summary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running the HPTASR short-read targeted-assembly path, which aligns contigs to IMGT/HLA allele references directly rather than to the concatenated GRCh38-noChr6+HLA reference The genome-wide reference already exists, is current, and matches the static Zenodo/BCGSC January 2025 deposit

skills.description: Use when HLAminer HPRA predictions have been generated from long-read WGS (PacBio HiFi or ONT PromethION) and a clinically confirmed HLA type list is available to benchmark prediction concordance.
skills.name: hla-prediction-validation-against-clinical-types
skills.search_text: hla-prediction-validation-against-clinical-types Use when HLAminer HPRA predictions have been generated from long-read WGS (PacBio HiFi or ONT PromethION) and a clinically confirmed HLA type list is available to benchmark prediction concordance. Input is Illumina-sized short reads, where the HPTASR targeted-assembly route (reads 100 bp and up, ideally 150 bp) is the recommended HLAminer mode No clinically confirmed HLA reference types exist for the sample, so there is nothing to benchmark predictions against Input reads are already assembled contigs or a published HLA call set rather than raw WGS long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates HLAminer HPRA HLA-I/II predictions from streamed long-read alignments against clinically confirmed HLA types, checking that top-ranked alleles (e.g. B*35:01, DRB1*04:03P) appear in HLAminer_HPRA.csv and that runtime scales as reported (~1 hr 14 min at 30× PacBio HiFi). genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Validates HLAminer HPRA HLA-I/II predictions from streamed long-read alignments against clinically confirmed HLA types, checking that top-ranked alleles (e.g. B*35:01, DRB1*04:03P) appear in HLAminer_HPRA.csv and that runtime scales as reported (~1 hr 14 min at 30× PacBio HiFi).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Illumina-sized short reads, where the HPTASR targeted-assembly route (reads 100 bp and up, ideally 150 bp) is the recommended HLAminer mode No clinically confirmed HLA reference types exist for the sample, so there is nothing to benchmark predictions against Input reads are already assembled contigs or a published HLA call set rather than raw WGS long reads

skills.description: Use when asked to verify or reproduce methylation-based SNV phase block chaining in the HLA region from WhatsHap-haplotagged ONT BAMs and HapCUT2-phased VCFs, or to check whether SNV-only phasing fails to link HLA-E and HLA-C.
skills.name: hla-region-phase-block-verification
skills.search_text: hla-region-phase-block-verification Use when asked to verify or reproduce methylation-based SNV phase block chaining in the HLA region from WhatsHap-haplotagged ONT BAMs and HapCUT2-phased VCFs, or to check whether SNV-only phasing fails to link HLA-E and HLA-C. Analysis targets sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, and the README warns MethPhaser 'won't work on sex chromosomes'; autosomes only Coverage is below ~30X — the README notes SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage The input BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which will trigger pysam MM tag reading errors unless first filtered with samtools view -bF 2304 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reproduces MethPhaser's methylation-assisted extension of SNV phase blocks across the HLA Class I region (chr6:30,400,000-31,300,000) on HG002 R10 ONT data, verifying that HLA-E and HLA-C are linked into a single block with a 132,079 bp extension. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Reproduces MethPhaser's methylation-assisted extension of SNV phase blocks across the HLA Class I region (chr6:30,400,000-31,300,000) on HG002 R10 ONT data, verifying that HLA-E and HLA-C are linked into a single block with a 132,079 bp extension.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis targets sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, and the README warns MethPhaser 'won't work on sex chromosomes'; autosomes only Coverage is below ~30X — the README notes SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage The input BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which will trigger pysam MM tag reading errors unless first filtered with samtools view -bF 2304

skills.description: Use when nanopore FAST5/FASTQ data must be scored for 6mA-containing sites (optionally alongside endogenous mCpGs), e.g. benchmarking callers on E. coli K12 MG1655 or detecting labeled adenines in nanoHiMe-seq reads.
skills.name: hmm-based-6ma-methylation-site-calling
skills.search_text: hmm-based-6ma-methylation-site-calling Use when nanopore FAST5/FASTQ data must be scored for 6mA-containing sites (optionally alongside endogenous mCpGs), e.g. benchmarking callers on E. coli K12 MG1655 or detecting labeled adenines in nanoHiMe-seq reads. Data are short-read bisulfite (WGBS/Bismark) or PacBio — the HMM consumes nanopolish eventalign tables from ONT R9.4.1 signal, not methylation calls from other platforms You only need CpG methylation: use nanoHiMe's 'mCG' mode (thresholds 1.5/-1.5) rather than the 6mA caller Target modifications beyond 6mA and mCpG (5hmC, 5fC, 4-mC, GpC) — the paper notes no unified calling model for these combinations exists yet http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Calls N6-methyladenine (6mA)-containing regions from Oxford Nanopore reads using nanoHiMe's hidden Markov model, which fits Gaussian-mixture emission distributions per 6-mer to nanopolish eventalign data and classifies windows by log likelihood ratio. This is the computational alternative to ONT's Megalodon/Guppy for 6mA detection in any sequence context. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Calls N6-methyladenine (6mA)-containing regions from Oxford Nanopore reads using nanoHiMe's hidden Markov model, which fits Gaussian-mixture emission distributions per 6-mer to nanopolish eventalign data and classifies windows by log likelihood ratio. This is the computational alternative to ONT's Megalodon/Guppy for 6mA detection in any sequence context.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are short-read bisulfite (WGBS/Bismark) or PacBio — the HMM consumes nanopolish eventalign tables from ONT R9.4.1 signal, not methylation calls from other platforms You only need CpG methylation: use nanoHiMe's 'mCG' mode (thresholds 1.5/-1.5) rather than the 6mA caller Target modifications beyond 6mA and mCpG (5hmC, 5fC, 4-mC, GpC) — the paper notes no unified calling model for these combinations exists yet

skills.description: Use when basecalled Nanopore reads (FASTQ) with raw FAST5 signals must be scored for CpG methylation via an HMM, or when comparing GPU vs CPU (OpenMP) methylation-calling performance.
skills.name: hmm-based-methylation-scoring
skills.search_text: hmm-based-methylation-scoring Use when basecalled Nanopore reads (FASTQ) with raw FAST5 signals must be scored for CpG methylation via an HMM, or when comparing GPU vs CPU (OpenMP) methylation-calling performance. Input reads are from R10.4 flowcells — Nanopolish does not support R10.4 for methylation calling Signals are in S/BLOW5 or POD5 format without FAST5 conversion — the indexed FAST5 workflow described here expects FAST5 signal data The goal is methylation frequencies rather than per-site HMM scoring — downstream tools like f5c meth-freq or Nanopolish compare_methylation.py would be more direct http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Detects methylated cytosines in Oxford Nanopore reads by running the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) methylation score calculation of the call-methylation module, as parallelized on GPU in Galaxy-methyl (a fork of f5c/Nanopolish) for ~2x speedup on the HMM step and identical log-likelihood ratio outputs. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbac088
skills.summary: Detects methylated cytosines in Oxford Nanopore reads by running the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) methylation score calculation of the call-methylation module, as parallelized on GPU in Galaxy-methyl (a fork of f5c/Nanopolish) for ~2x speedup on the HMM step and identical log-likelihood ratio outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are from R10.4 flowcells — Nanopolish does not support R10.4 for methylation calling Signals are in S/BLOW5 or POD5 format without FAST5 conversion — the indexed FAST5 workflow described here expects FAST5 signal data The goal is methylation frequencies rather than per-site HMM scoring — downstream tools like f5c meth-freq or Nanopolish compare_methylation.py would be more direct

skills.description: Use when auditing long-read (PacBio/ONT) SNV call sets against a truth set (e.g., GIAB) to determine whether false positives or false negatives are enriched in specific sequence contexts such as homopolymers or indel-proximate sites.

skills.search_text: homopolymer-context-enrichment-analysis Use when auditing long-read (PacBio/ONT) SNV call sets against a truth set (e.g., GIAB) to determine whether false positives or false negatives are enriched in specific sequence contexts such as homopolymers or indel-proximate sites. The goal is calling short indels themselves with long reads — the paper notes accurate calling of short indels using SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate, and Longshot calls only SNVs from pileup. Input alignments are short-read (Illumina) calls — the FP-near-indel and FN-in-homopolymer patterns characterized here are specific to SMS read error profiles and Longshot's indel-blind candidate selection. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Characterize sequence-context biases in long-read SNV call errors by annotating Longshot false-negative SNVs for homopolymer context and false-positive SNVs for proximity to known indels on GIAB PacBio genomes, then quantifying enrichment over random expectation. Grounded in Edge & Bansal 2019, where FNs concentrated in homopolymers of length ≥5 bp and FPs clustered within 5 bp of true indels because Longshot does not consider indels as candidate variants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y

skills.search_text: homozygous-allele-verification-across-catalog-span Use when calling progeny indel genotypes from VCF evidence at known parental InDel catalog sites and needing to distinguish homozygous from heterozygous calls without direct VCF support for the homozygous state. When reads lack sufficient depth (below HOMOZYGOUS_DEPTH:5 across the full span) — homozygous calls cannot be verified and sites will be missing.
