skills.search_text: hpo-code-to-disease-concept-mapping Use when patient symptoms are already encoded as HPO codes (e.g. HP:0002996) and must be translated into disease concepts to retrieve gene-disease associations for phenotype-based candidate gene prioritization. The patient phenotypes are free-text names rather than HPO codes — they must first be matched to HPO v2018-03-08 to obtain corresponding codes You need candidate variants filtered by allele frequency, inheritance mode, or pathogenicity — VIBE only provides phenotype-based candidate genes, not variant-level filtering Privacy or availability rules forbid external web services — VIBE is designed for local installation precisely because external services such as AMELIE 'cannot always be used since privacy and availability are not guaranteed' Maps patient HPO term codes onto disease concepts (UMLS CUIs and ORDO terms via HOOM) and retrieves ranked gene-disease associations from DisGeNET-RDF, as implemented inside the VIBE v2.0 command-line tool for phenotype-based gene prioritization. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Maps patient HPO term codes onto disease concepts (UMLS CUIs and ORDO terms via HOOM) and retrieves ranked gene-disease associations from DisGeNET-RDF, as implemented inside the VIBE v2.0 command-line tool for phenotype-based gene prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The patient phenotypes are free-text names rather than HPO codes — they must first be matched to HPO v2018-03-08 to obtain corresponding codes You need candidate variants filtered by allele frequency, inheritance mode, or pathogenicity — VIBE only provides phenotype-based candidate genes, not variant-level filtering Privacy or availability rules forbid external web services — VIBE is designed for local installation precisely because external services such as AMELIE 'cannot always be used since privacy and availability are not guaranteed'

skills.description: Use when prioritizing candidate causal variants from an annotated trio/family multisample VCF and known disease phenotypes (HPO IDs) are available to boost precision without switching inheritance filtering logic.
skills.name: hpo-phenotype-based-prioritization
skills.search_text: hpo-phenotype-based-prioritization Use when prioritizing candidate causal variants from an annotated trio/family multisample VCF and known disease phenotypes (HPO IDs) are available to boost precision without switching inheritance filtering logic. No HPO terms or phenotype description for the disease exist — the empty-list configuration is the correct baseline and HPO soft filtering cannot contribute signal. CNV-driven disease: CNV analysis is not yet available in eDiVA, so point-mutation prioritization with HPO terms would miss such causes. A strict precision-only screen where recall loss from incomplete public gene-phenotype maps is unacceptable for the cohort at hand. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Soft-filters and ranks candidate causal variants from a ranked multisample VCF using user-supplied Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) term IDs, as implemented in the eDiVA-Prioritize module, to improve precision of familial disease variant prioritization. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772
skills.summary: Soft-filters and ranks candidate causal variants from a ranked multisample VCF using user-supplied Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) term IDs, as implemented in the eDiVA-Prioritize module, to improve precision of familial disease variant prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No HPO terms or phenotype description for the disease exist — the empty-list configuration is the correct baseline and HPO soft filtering cannot contribute signal. CNV-driven disease: CNV analysis is not yet available in eDiVA, so point-mutation prioritization with HPO terms would miss such causes. A strict precision-only screen where recall loss from incomplete public gene-phenotype maps is unacceptable for the cohort at hand.

skills.description: Use when HPO-coded patient phenotypes (e.g. HP:0002996, HP:0001377) must be translated into UMLS CUI sets as a prerequisite for retrieving gene-disease associations or ranking candidate genes.
skills.name: hpo-to-cui-ontology-mapping
skills.search_text: hpo-to-cui-ontology-mapping Use when HPO-coded patient phenotypes (e.g. HP:0002996, HP:0001377) must be translated into UMLS CUI sets as a prerequisite for retrieving gene-disease associations or ranking candidate genes. When phenotypes are given as free-text names rather than HPO codes — first convert them via hp.obo/hp.owl (as done in the VIBE benchmark where phenotype names were matched to HPO release v2018-03-08) When the goal is direct phenotype-to-gene ranking via a different algorithm (e.g. Phenomizer, hiPHIVE, PhenIX, GADO) rather than ontology-based CUI lookup feeding DisGeNET GDAs When external web services are acceptable — VIBE's local triple-store approach exists precisely because external services cannot always be used since privacy and availability are not guaranteed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Maps patient symptoms encoded as Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) codes to UMLS concept unique identifiers (CUIs) using an optimized SPARQL query with three parallel matching branches, as implemented in VIBE 2.0 for phenotype-based gene prioritization. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Maps patient symptoms encoded as Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) codes to UMLS concept unique identifiers (CUIs) using an optimized SPARQL query with three parallel matching branches, as implemented in VIBE 2.0 for phenotype-based gene prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When phenotypes are given as free-text names rather than HPO codes — first convert them via hp.obo/hp.owl (as done in the VIBE benchmark where phenotype names were matched to HPO release v2018-03-08) When the goal is direct phenotype-to-gene ranking via a different algorithm (e.g. Phenomizer, hiPHIVE, PhenIX, GADO) rather than ontology-based CUI lookup feeding DisGeNET GDAs When external web services are acceptable — VIBE's local triple-store approach exists precisely because external services cannot always be used since privacy and availability are not guaranteed

skills.description: Use when you need to call a consensus genome directly from unsorted read alignments (SAM/BAM/CRAM) against a single reference sequence, or pipe mapper output on-the-fly without sorting or intermediate disk I/O.
skills.name: htslib-c-plus-plus-alignment-processing
skills.search_text: htslib-c-plus-plus-alignment-processing Use when you need to call a consensus genome directly from unsorted read alignments (SAM/BAM/CRAM) against a single reference sequence, or pipe mapper output on-the-fly without sorting or intermediate disk I/O. The reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. a human chromosome): memory consumption scales linearly with reference genome length and may require prohibitively large amounts of memory The alignment spans multiple reference sequences — the tool requires a single reference sequence being used for reconstruction You need a small, browser-based run for a reasonably small dataset — the WebAssembly web app may suffice instead of the command-line tool http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Write a C++ program linked against htslib that streams unsorted SAM/BAM/CRAM read alignments on-the-fly and tallies base and insertion counts per reference position to call a consensus genome, as done in ViralConsensus. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Write a C++ program linked against htslib that streams unsorted SAM/BAM/CRAM read alignments on-the-fly and tallies base and insertion counts per reference position to call a consensus genome, as done in ViralConsensus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. a human chromosome): memory consumption scales linearly with reference genome length and may require prohibitively large amounts of memory The alignment spans multiple reference sequences — the tool requires a single reference sequence being used for reconstruction You need a small, browser-based run for a reasonably small dataset — the WebAssembly web app may suffice instead of the command-line tool

skills.description: Use when a de novo human or large-genome assembly (e.g., from HASLR on PacBio + Illumina reads) must be validated for repeat content and contiguity/accuracy before or alongside comparison to published assemblies.
skills.name: human-genome-assembly-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: human-genome-assembly-quality-assessment Use when a de novo human or large-genome assembly (e.g., from HASLR on PacBio + Illumina reads) must be validated for repeat content and contiguity/accuracy before or alongside comparison to published assemblies. The assembly is of a small or non-mammalian genome (e.g., the E. coli, yeast, or C. elegans datasets in the HASLR evaluation) where a mammalian repeat library census is not the relevant quality axis The goal is read-level QC or assembly of raw long reads rather than assessing a completed assembly FASTA Phased or haplotype-resolved assessment is required — the current HASLR version does not generate a phased assembly for diploid genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the quality and biological content of a human genome assembly (e.g., HASLR's CHM1 PacBio+Illumina hybrid assembly) by running RepeatMasker against a curated mammalian repeat library and parsing per-family element counts and genomic span fractions (SINE, LINE, LTR, DNA-transposon, simple repeats, low-complexity). genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Quantifies the quality and biological content of a human genome assembly (e.g., HASLR's CHM1 PacBio+Illumina hybrid assembly) by running RepeatMasker against a curated mammalian repeat library and parsing per-family element counts and genomic span fractions (SINE, LINE, LTR, DNA-transposon, simple repeats, low-complexity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly is of a small or non-mammalian genome (e.g., the E. coli, yeast, or C. elegans datasets in the HASLR evaluation) where a mammalian repeat library census is not the relevant quality axis The goal is read-level QC or assembly of raw long reads rather than assessing a completed assembly FASTA Phased or haplotype-resolved assessment is required — the current HASLR version does not generate a phased assembly for diploid genomes

skills.description: Use when comparing scaffolding quality of Fast-SG synthetic mate-pair libraries (from raw vs error-corrected ONT/PacBio reads) against a long-read baseline scaffolder such as Links, and a metrics table must be produced.
skills.name: hybrid-assembly-benchmark-tabulation
skills.search_text: hybrid-assembly-benchmark-tabulation Use when comparing scaffolding quality of Fast-SG synthetic mate-pair libraries (from raw vs error-corrected ONT/PacBio reads) against a long-read baseline scaffolder such as Links, and a metrics table must be produced. When the goal is scaffolding long reads directly with a purpose-built long-read scaffolder (e.g. Links) rather than benchmarking Fast-SG synthetic libraries against it When insert sizes required for the synthetic library exceed the actual long-read length — the article notes the insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size When input reads are short Illumina reads rather than long ONT/PacBio reads plus a short-read assembly to scaffold http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A benchmarking and tabulation procedure for Fast-SG hybrid assembly experiments: run the alignment-free scaffolding-graph builder on ONT/PacBio long reads against Illumina contigs, scaffold with short-read scaffolders, then tabulate k-mer recall, synthetic mate-pair read recall, outlier percentages, join counts and F-scores per technology/correction-state combination. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: A benchmarking and tabulation procedure for Fast-SG hybrid assembly experiments: run the alignment-free scaffolding-graph builder on ONT/PacBio long reads against Illumina contigs, scaffold with short-read scaffolders, then tabulate k-mer recall, synthetic mate-pair read recall, outlier percentages, join counts and F-scores per technology/correction-state combination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is scaffolding long reads directly with a purpose-built long-read scaffolder (e.g. Links) rather than benchmarking Fast-SG synthetic libraries against it When insert sizes required for the synthetic library exceed the actual long-read length — the article notes the insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size When input reads are short Illumina reads rather than long ONT/PacBio reads plus a short-read assembly to scaffold

skills.description: Use when a draft short-read assembly (e.g. SPAdes contigs.fasta) must be scaffolded and gap-filled using nanopore long reads, especially in real-time/streaming mode or batch BWA-MEM alignment pipelines.
skills.name: hybrid-assembly-gap-filling
skills.search_text: hybrid-assembly-gap-filling Use when a draft short-read assembly (e.g. SPAdes contigs.fasta) must be scaffolded and gap-filled using nanopore long reads, especially in real-time/streaming mode or batch BWA-MEM alignment pipelines. The long-read dataset is already assembled de novo with a long-read assembler (e.g. Celera Assembler) rather than used to scaffold an existing short-read draft Only short-read data are available with no long reads — bridges cannot be formed without alignments spanning two unique contigs Windows/macOS deployment is required without meeting Japsa's Java/HDF5 installation dependencies (npGraph successor targets Linux only) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs the npScarf hybrid scaffolding workflow: short-read (Illumina MiSeq/SPAdes) contigs are scaffolded by streaming Oxford Nanopore long-read bridges via jsa.np.npscarf, with unique contigs forming the backbone and repetitive contigs inserted into gaps. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Reconstructs the npScarf hybrid scaffolding workflow: short-read (Illumina MiSeq/SPAdes) contigs are scaffolded by streaming Oxford Nanopore long-read bridges via jsa.np.npscarf, with unique contigs forming the backbone and repetitive contigs inserted into gaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long-read dataset is already assembled de novo with a long-read assembler (e.g. Celera Assembler) rather than used to scaffold an existing short-read draft Only short-read data are available with no long reads — bridges cannot be formed without alignments spanning two unique contigs Windows/macOS deployment is required without meeting Japsa's Java/HDF5 installation dependencies (npGraph successor targets Linux only)

skills.description: Use when assembling a large genome from 10x-100x long erroneous 3GS reads (PacBio/ONT) plus accurate NGS contigs, and you need overlap/layout without base-level error correction before consensus.
skills.name: hybrid-assembly-overlap-layout
skills.search_text: hybrid-assembly-overlap-layout Use when assembling a large genome from 10x-100x long erroneous 3GS reads (PacBio/ONT) plus accurate NGS contigs, and you need overlap/layout without base-level error correction before consensus. You only have NGS short reads and no 3GS long reads — use the DBG2OLC non-hybrid NGS assembly mode instead. You already have a structurally correct backbone and only need base-level polishing — proceed to the consensus step (BLASR + Sparc/pbdagcon) rather than re-running overlap/layout. The NGS input contains repeat-resolved, gap-closed, or scaffolded contigs — the README warns this 'may have poor final results due to the errors introduced by the heuristics used in short read assembly pipelines'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Performs the DBG2OLC overlap-and-layout stage of hybrid assembly: accurate short-read DBG contigs (e.g. SparseAssembler Contigs.txt) are used as k-mer anchors (k 17) to compress 3GS long reads into ordered contig-identifier lists and emit the assembly backbone (backbone_raw.fasta). This skips base-level errors and corrects only structural errors, cutting compute and sequencing cost. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Performs the DBG2OLC overlap-and-layout stage of hybrid assembly: accurate short-read DBG contigs (e.g. SparseAssembler Contigs.txt) are used as k-mer anchors (k 17) to compress 3GS long reads into ordered contig-identifier lists and emit the assembly backbone (backbone_raw.fasta). This skips base-level errors and corrects only structural errors, cutting compute and sequencing cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have NGS short reads and no 3GS long reads — use the DBG2OLC non-hybrid NGS assembly mode instead. You already have a structurally correct backbone and only need base-level polishing — proceed to the consensus step (BLASR + Sparc/pbdagcon) rather than re-running overlap/layout. The NGS input contains repeat-resolved, gap-closed, or scaffolded contigs — the README warns this 'may have poor final results due to the errors introduced by the heuristics used in short read assembly pipelines'.

skills.description: Use when scaffolding a large (e.g. human) genome from an Illumina-based contig assembly plus shallow (~5X) uncorrected long Nanopore reads, and the goal is a fast, low-cost modular hybrid assembly instead of a full long-read assembly pipeline.
skills.name: hybrid-assembly-scaffolding-of-human-genome
skills.search_text: hybrid-assembly-scaffolding-of-human-genome Use when scaffolding a large (e.g. human) genome from an Illumina-based contig assembly plus shallow (~5X) uncorrected long Nanopore reads, and the goal is a fast, low-cost modular hybrid assembly instead of a full long-read assembly pipeline. When high-coverage corrected long reads are available and a full long-read assembler (rather than a modular hybrid pipeline) is appropriate. When the input long reads are too short to support the desired insert sizes — synthetic library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size. When the target genome lacks a reliable contig assembly to scaffold; Fast-SG scaffolds existing contigs, it does not assemble the genome de novo. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the DFS hybrid assembly (DiscovarDeNovo + Fast-SG + ScaffMatch) of the human NA12878 genome, using Fast-SG to extract alignment-free synthetic mate-pair libraries from shallow (~5X) uncorrected Nanopore reads and ScaffMatch to scaffold the DiscovarDeNovo contigs into long-range scaffolds. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Reproduces the DFS hybrid assembly (DiscovarDeNovo + Fast-SG + ScaffMatch) of the human NA12878 genome, using Fast-SG to extract alignment-free synthetic mate-pair libraries from shallow (~5X) uncorrected Nanopore reads and ScaffMatch to scaffold the DiscovarDeNovo contigs into long-range scaffolds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When high-coverage corrected long reads are available and a full long-read assembler (rather than a modular hybrid pipeline) is appropriate. When the input long reads are too short to support the desired insert sizes — synthetic library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size. When the target genome lacks a reliable contig assembly to scaffold; Fast-SG scaffolds existing contigs, it does not assemble the genome de novo.

skills.description: Use when noisy long reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore, errors up to 20-35%) must be corrected with high-quality Illumina short reads, and consensus thresholds or correction-policy selection must be reproduced.
skills.name: hybrid-error-correction-implementation
skills.search_text: hybrid-error-correction-implementation Use when noisy long reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore, errors up to 20-35%) must be corrected with high-quality Illumina short reads, and consensus thresholds or correction-policy selection must be reproduced. The long reads are already Canu-corrected and the goal is de novo assembly rather than short-read-based correction (though HECIL can further improve Canu-corrected reads, this is a distinct downstream workflow step) Only self-correction from long-read data is desired — HECIL is a hybrid algorithm that requires supplementary short-read sequencing data, unlike self-correcting algorithms such as HGAP Evaluation-only tasks such as k-mer counting (Jellyfish), reference alignment (BLASR), assembly quality assessment (QUAST, MUMmer dnadiff), which are downstream validation steps, not the correction itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs HECIL's hybrid error correction pipeline, in which long reads from third-generation sequencers (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) are corrected using aligned Illumina short reads via a Quick Correction stage plus an optimization-based correction framework with iterative learning. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Reconstructs HECIL's hybrid error correction pipeline, in which long reads from third-generation sequencers (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) are corrected using aligned Illumina short reads via a Quick Correction stage plus an optimization-based correction framework with iterative learning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long reads are already Canu-corrected and the goal is de novo assembly rather than short-read-based correction (though HECIL can further improve Canu-corrected reads, this is a distinct downstream workflow step) Only self-correction from long-read data is desired — HECIL is a hybrid algorithm that requires supplementary short-read sequencing data, unlike self-correcting algorithms such as HGAP Evaluation-only tasks such as k-mer counting (Jellyfish), reference alignment (BLASR), assembly quality assessment (QUAST, MUMmer dnadiff), which are downstream validation steps, not the correction itself

skills.description: Use when both Illumina short-read FASTQ and Nanopore long-read FASTQ from the same sample are available and the goal is a de novo plasmid or genome assembly, especially to resolve circular structures or repetitive regions.
skills.name: hybrid-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: hybrid-genome-assembly Use when both Illumina short-read FASTQ and Nanopore long-read FASTQ from the same sample are available and the goal is a de novo plasmid or genome assembly, especially to resolve circular structures or repetitive regions. Only one read type is available (the comparison — and the hybrid assembly itself — requires both short and long reads) The goal is only metagenomic or AMR analysis rather than de novo plasmid/genome assembly The user needs quantitative assembly benchmarks; validation here is qualitative graph comparison with no stated numeric threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A Unicycler-based hybrid assembly workflow in NanoGalaxy that combines Illumina short reads and Oxford Nanopore long reads to produce clearer plasmid/genome assemblies than either read type alone, visualized with Bandage. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: A Unicycler-based hybrid assembly workflow in NanoGalaxy that combines Illumina short reads and Oxford Nanopore long reads to produce clearer plasmid/genome assemblies than either read type alone, visualized with Bandage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one read type is available (the comparison — and the hybrid assembly itself — requires both short and long reads) The goal is only metagenomic or AMR analysis rather than de novo plasmid/genome assembly The user needs quantitative assembly benchmarks; validation here is qualitative graph comparison with no stated numeric threshold

skills.description: Use when you have error-prone PacBio/ONT long reads plus Illumina short reads from the same sample and need a fast, low-misassembly draft assembly with a genome-size estimate available.
skills.name: hybrid-genome-assembly-execution
skills.search_text: hybrid-genome-assembly-execution Use when you have error-prone PacBio/ONT long reads plus Illumina short reads from the same sample and need a fast, low-misassembly draft assembly with a genome-size estimate available. Only short reads are available — HASLR is a hybrid tool requiring third-generation long reads; use a short-read-only assembler instead. A polished, low-indel-rate finished assembly is required without a post-hoc polishing step — HASLR employs no polishing and typically shows a higher indel rate (fixable with Racon/Pilon). A phased assembly of a diploid genome is needed — the current HASLR version does not generate phased assemblies, and high-heterozygosity regions may remain unresolved because Minia short-read contigs there are fragmented and filtered out. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Executes hybrid de novo genome assembly with HASLR, which combines error-prone third-generation long reads (PacBio/ONT) with high-quality Illumina short reads to rapidly produce accurate assemblies, with the lowest misassembly counts and fastest runtime among compared hybrid assemblers. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Executes hybrid de novo genome assembly with HASLR, which combines error-prone third-generation long reads (PacBio/ONT) with high-quality Illumina short reads to rapidly produce accurate assemblies, with the lowest misassembly counts and fastest runtime among compared hybrid assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only short reads are available — HASLR is a hybrid tool requiring third-generation long reads; use a short-read-only assembler instead. A polished, low-indel-rate finished assembly is required without a post-hoc polishing step — HASLR employs no polishing and typically shows a higher indel rate (fixable with Racon/Pilon). A phased assembly of a diploid genome is needed — the current HASLR version does not generate phased assemblies, and high-heterozygosity regions may remain unresolved because Minia short-read contigs there are fragmented and filtered out.

skills.description: Use when you have paired datasets of noisy third-generation long reads (PacBio/ONT) and accurate Illumina short reads from the same sample and need a fast, low-misasassembly de novo assembly of a genome up to human scale.
skills.name: hybrid-genome-assembly-long-and-short-reads
skills.search_text: hybrid-genome-assembly-long-and-short-reads Use when you have paired datasets of noisy third-generation long reads (PacBio/ONT) and accurate Illumina short reads from the same sample and need a fast, low-misasassembly de novo assembly of a genome up to human scale. Only one sequencing type is available (long reads alone or short reads alone) — HASLR is a hybrid tool requiring both A phased assembly of a diploid genome is required — the current HASLR version does not generate phased assemblies Ultra-long ONT reads are the primary data — ultra-long read support is listed as not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assemble a genome de novo by combining error-prone long reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) with high-quality Illumina short reads, following the HASLR strategy of short-read contigs anchoring a backbone graph onto which long reads are threaded and consensus-called for speed and low misassembly counts. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Assemble a genome de novo by combining error-prone long reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) with high-quality Illumina short reads, following the HASLR strategy of short-read contigs anchoring a backbone graph onto which long reads are threaded and consensus-called for speed and low misassembly counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one sequencing type is available (long reads alone or short reads alone) — HASLR is a hybrid tool requiring both A phased assembly of a diploid genome is required — the current HASLR version does not generate phased assemblies Ultra-long ONT reads are the primary data — ultra-long read support is listed as not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when benchmarking runtime and memory of barcode matching in split hybrid LR-SR scRNA-seq experiments, or when needing a reproducible multi-stage scTagger workflow orchestrated across datasets with timing instrumentation.
skills.name: hybrid-scrnaseq-workflow-orchestration
skills.search_text: hybrid-scrnaseq-workflow-orchestration Use when benchmarking runtime and memory of barcode matching in split hybrid LR-SR scRNA-seq experiments, or when needing a reproducible multi-stage scTagger workflow orchestrated across datasets with timing instrumentation. The goal is accuracy evaluation on simulated data rather than runtime/memory benchmarking on real hybrid datasets The data are not from a 10x Genomics split hybrid LR-SR scRNA-seq protocol — scTagger's current form is specific for 10x Genomics scRNA-seq unless the LR template contains a fixed sequence next to the barcode The number of relevant cellular barcodes greatly exceeds thousands to tens of thousands, where scTagger's trie design is not expected to scale http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Orchestrates the three-stage scTagger pipeline (extract_lr_bc, extract_sr_bc, match_trie) on hybrid long-read/short-read single-cell RNA-seq data, benchmarking runtime and peak memory against FLAMES and an edlib-based brute-force matcher on the real datasets N, NOA1, and NOA2. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104530
skills.summary: Orchestrates the three-stage scTagger pipeline (extract_lr_bc, extract_sr_bc, match_trie) on hybrid long-read/short-read single-cell RNA-seq data, benchmarking runtime and peak memory against FLAMES and an edlib-based brute-force matcher on the real datasets N, NOA1, and NOA2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy evaluation on simulated data rather than runtime/memory benchmarking on real hybrid datasets The data are not from a 10x Genomics split hybrid LR-SR scRNA-seq protocol — scTagger's current form is specific for 10x Genomics scRNA-seq unless the LR template contains a fixed sequence next to the barcode The number of relevant cellular barcodes greatly exceeds thousands to tens of thousands, where scTagger's trie design is not expected to scale

skills.description: Use when calling insertions/deletions (50 bp–10 kbp) from a position-sorted, BX-tagged 10X SLR bam plus a low-coverage long-read bam/FASTQ pair, and short-read-only or SLR-only callers are insufficient.
skills.name: hybrid-slr-long-read-assembly-integration
skills.search_text: hybrid-slr-long-read-assembly-integration Use when calling insertions/deletions (50 bp–10 kbp) from a position-sorted, BX-tagged 10X SLR bam plus a low-coverage long-read bam/FASTQ pair, and short-read-only or SLR-only callers are insufficient. Input lacks one of the paired hybrid files — the long-read bam without its matching long-read FASTQ (or vice versa) is invalid, as --long-bam and --long-read must be paired. The goal is whole-genome assembly — Blackbird deliberately avoids whole-genome assembly and only assembles small sliding-window segments for SV calling. Calls in out.vcf are needed as reliable results — the README states these 'other calls... are not reliable'; only out_50.vcf (>50 bp) should be trusted. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Integrates low-coverage long reads into Blackbird's barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly of synthetic long-read (SLR) data, improving structural variant detection for medium-size events (50–10,000 bp) at reduced long-read coverage (5× vs 10×). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Integrates low-coverage long reads into Blackbird's barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly of synthetic long-read (SLR) data, improving structural variant detection for medium-size events (50–10,000 bp) at reduced long-read coverage (5× vs 10×).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks one of the paired hybrid files — the long-read bam without its matching long-read FASTQ (or vice versa) is invalid, as --long-bam and --long-read must be paired. The goal is whole-genome assembly — Blackbird deliberately avoids whole-genome assembly and only assembles small sliding-window segments for SV calling. Calls in out.vcf are needed as reliable results — the README states these 'other calls... are not reliable'; only out_50.vcf (>50 bp) should be trusted.

skills.description: Use when you have a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAM (e.g. TELL-Seq or stLFR) plus low-coverage long-read BAM/FASTQ (e.g. PacBio HiFi at 5–34x) and need sensitive SV calling with reduced long-read depth.
skills.name: hybrid-slr-longread-variant-calling
skills.search_text: hybrid-slr-longread-variant-calling Use when you have a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAM (e.g. TELL-Seq or stLFR) plus low-coverage long-read BAM/FASTQ (e.g. PacBio HiFi at 5–34x) and need sensitive SV calling with reduced long-read depth. You only have short-read sequencing without SLR barcode information — most SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short reads You have long reads but no synthetic long-read (BX-tagged) dataset — Blackbird's core barcode-aware sliding-window assembly depends on SLR data Calls shorter than 50 bp are needed — Blackbird's reliable output is restricted to events longer than 50 bp; shorter calls land in out.vcf and are unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Call structural variants (insertions/deletions >50 bp) by running Blackbird in hybrid mode, combining barcode-tagged synthetic long reads (SLR) with downsampled long-read data, to match state-of-the-art long-read caller quality with less long-read coverage. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Call structural variants (insertions/deletions >50 bp) by running Blackbird in hybrid mode, combining barcode-tagged synthetic long reads (SLR) with downsampled long-read data, to match state-of-the-art long-read caller quality with less long-read coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have short-read sequencing without SLR barcode information — most SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short reads You have long reads but no synthetic long-read (BX-tagged) dataset — Blackbird's core barcode-aware sliding-window assembly depends on SLR data Calls shorter than 50 bp are needed — Blackbird's reliable output is restricted to events longer than 50 bp; shorter calls land in out.vcf and are unreliable

skills.description: Use when evaluating SV-calling performance of a barcode-aware SLR + long-read pipeline against long-read-only callers, or when determining the minimum long-read coverage needed to match PBSV/Sniffles2 F1 scores.
skills.name: hybrid-slr-plus-long-read-benchmarking
skills.search_text: hybrid-slr-plus-long-read-benchmarking Use when evaluating SV-calling performance of a barcode-aware SLR + long-read pipeline against long-read-only callers, or when determining the minimum long-read coverage needed to match PBSV/Sniffles2 F1 scores. When the input is short-read-only data without SLR barcode (BX) tags — Blackbird's hybrid and SLR modes require barcode-aware sliding window assembly When calling SVs smaller than 50 bp or larger than ~10,000 bp — Blackbird targets the 50–10,000 bp medium-size range and out_50.vcf only contains calls longer than 50 bp When a whole-genome assembly is already available and preferred — Blackbird is designed to avoid computationally expensive whole-genome assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Benchmark Blackbird in hybrid mode (synthetic long reads plus low-coverage PacBio HiFi long reads) against state-of-the-art long-read SV callers PBSV and Sniffles2 on simulated and real (HG002 GIAB) human datasets, using Truvari for recall/precision comparison against ground-truth SV callsets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Benchmark Blackbird in hybrid mode (synthetic long reads plus low-coverage PacBio HiFi long reads) against state-of-the-art long-read SV callers PBSV and Sniffles2 on simulated and real (HG002 GIAB) human datasets, using Truvari for recall/precision comparison against ground-truth SV callsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is short-read-only data without SLR barcode (BX) tags — Blackbird's hybrid and SLR modes require barcode-aware sliding window assembly When calling SVs smaller than 50 bp or larger than ~10,000 bp — Blackbird targets the 50–10,000 bp medium-size range and out_50.vcf only contains calls longer than 50 bp When a whole-genome assembly is already available and preferred — Blackbird is designed to avoid computationally expensive whole-genome assembly

skills.description: Use when building a sparse k-mer feature matrix from long reads (FASTQ/FASTA) and repeated/repetitive k-mers would dominate similarity search; weighting by inverse collection frequency emphasizes informative k-mers prior to DR/ANN.
skills.name: idf-weighting-of-kmers
skills.search_text: idf-weighting-of-kmers Use when building a sparse k-mer feature matrix from long reads (FASTQ/FASTA) and repeated/repetitive k-mers would dominate similarity search; weighting by inverse collection frequency emphasizes informative k-mers prior to DR/ANN. Input is already a dense, weighted feature/embedding matrix — re-weighting would distort downstream ANN distances Data are short reads or small-scale similarity search where BLAST/DALIGN-style direct alignment is feasible and DR-based weighting adds unnecessary complexity No k-mer vocabulary has been counted/filtered yet — apply k-mer counting and multiplicity filtering first http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Weight k-mer features by inverse document frequency (IDF), approximated as inverse collection frequency (ICF), to down-weight repetitive high-frequency k-mers before dimensionality reduction in long-read overlap detection. This weighting is the key transform that makes the subsequent sparse random projection discriminative. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Weight k-mer features by inverse document frequency (IDF), approximated as inverse collection frequency (ICF), to down-weight repetitive high-frequency k-mers before dimensionality reduction in long-read overlap detection. This weighting is the key transform that makes the subsequent sparse random projection discriminative.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a dense, weighted feature/embedding matrix — re-weighting would distort downstream ANN distances Data are short reads or small-scale similarity search where BLAST/DALIGN-style direct alignment is feasible and DR-based weighting adds unnecessary complexity No k-mer vocabulary has been counted/filtered yet — apply k-mer counting and multiplicity filtering first

skills.description: Use when processing nanoHiMe-seq data (e.g., HepG2 H3K27me3) where an antibody-targeted IP sample must be de-noised against a non-specific IgG control, or when benchmarking 6mA callers by discovery efficiency versus background noise.
skills.name: igg-background-correction
skills.search_text: igg-background-correction Use when processing nanoHiMe-seq data (e.g., HepG2 H3K27me3) where an antibody-targeted IP sample must be de-noised against a non-specific IgG control, or when benchmarking 6mA callers by discovery efficiency versus background noise. When no matched non-specific IgG control sequencing data exist for the nanoHiMe-seq experiment — the scaling-factor subtraction cannot be estimated without Rb When the target modification is endogenous mCpG rather than exogenous 6mA labeling — use the mCG-calling mode and CpG-specific thresholds instead When calling over the whole genome without peak regions is acceptable and runtime is not a concern — note the README warns whole-genome 6mA calling 'may be quite slow' http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies and removes non-specific IgG-derived background 6mA signal from nanoHiMe-seq data by calling 6mA on IgG control eventalign data and subtracting a scaled background rate (Rf=Rs−sf*Rb), then uses the IgG noise rate to compute efficiency-to-noise ratios for benchmarking 6mA callers. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Quantifies and removes non-specific IgG-derived background 6mA signal from nanoHiMe-seq data by calling 6mA on IgG control eventalign data and subtracting a scaled background rate (Rf=Rs−sf*Rb), then uses the IgG noise rate to compute efficiency-to-noise ratios for benchmarking 6mA callers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no matched non-specific IgG control sequencing data exist for the nanoHiMe-seq experiment — the scaling-factor subtraction cannot be estimated without Rb When the target modification is endogenous mCpG rather than exogenous 6mA labeling — use the mCG-calling mode and CpG-specific thresholds instead When calling over the whole genome without peak regions is acceptable and runtime is not a concern — note the README warns whole-genome 6mA calling 'may be quite slow'

skills.description: Use when starting a DBG2OLC hybrid assembly from Illumina FASTQ data (e.g. S.cer w303 2x300 reads) and you need a 50x subset and raw DBG contigs (Contigs.txt) before overlap/layout with long reads.
skills.name: illumina-fastq-read-handling
skills.search_text: illumina-fastq-read-handling Use when starting a DBG2OLC hybrid assembly from Illumina FASTQ data (e.g. S.cer w303 2x300 reads) and you need a 50x subset and raw DBG contigs (Contigs.txt) before overlap/layout with long reads. The task requires polished, scaffolded, or repeat-resolved short-read contigs — DBG2OLC explicitly requires raw DBG contigs without gap closing or scaffolding The input is long-read (PacBio/ONT) data rather than Illumina FASTQ — those reads belong to Step2 overlap/layout and Step3 consensus, not SparseAssembler preassembly You want a purely short-read finished assembly — this skill only produces intermediate contigs meant as anchors for long erroneous 3GS reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Handling of highly accurate Illumina FASTQ reads in the DBG2OLC hybrid-assembly workflow: selecting a 50x subset with SelectLongestReads and preassembling them into raw, unscaffolded de Bruijn graph contigs with SparseAssembler. This is the short-read foundation that anchors long erroneous 3GS reads in later steps. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Handling of highly accurate Illumina FASTQ reads in the DBG2OLC hybrid-assembly workflow: selecting a 50x subset with SelectLongestReads and preassembling them into raw, unscaffolded de Bruijn graph contigs with SparseAssembler. This is the short-read foundation that anchors long erroneous 3GS reads in later steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires polished, scaffolded, or repeat-resolved short-read contigs — DBG2OLC explicitly requires raw DBG contigs without gap closing or scaffolding The input is long-read (PacBio/ONT) data rather than Illumina FASTQ — those reads belong to Step2 overlap/layout and Step3 consensus, not SparseAssembler preassembly You want a purely short-read finished assembly — this skill only produces intermediate contigs meant as anchors for long erroneous 3GS reads

skills.description: Use when Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g., 300 bp MiSeq PE at >250-fold coverage) are the input to a short-read assembler such as SPAdes whose contigs will be scaffolded by npScarf, and adapters/low-quality bases must be removed first.
skills.name: illumina-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: illumina-read-quality-trimming Use when Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g., 300 bp MiSeq PE at >250-fold coverage) are the input to a short-read assembler such as SPAdes whose contigs will be scaffolded by npScarf, and adapters/low-quality bases must be removed first. Input reads are nanopore long reads — npScarf consumes these via BWA-MEM streaming alignment, not short-read trimming The Illumina data are already trimmed — the npScarf project distributes pre-trimmed files such as Kp2146_paired_1.fastq.gz, and re-trimming trimmed data is unnecessary The assembly pipeline does not start from a short-read draft (e.g., long-read-only assembly with Celera Assembler or npGraph) http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Trim Illumina MiSeq paired-end reads to strip adapters and low-quality bases with trimmomatic V0.32 before short-read assembly, so that the draft contigs fed into npScarf real-time scaffolding are free of adapter-induced misassemblies. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Trim Illumina MiSeq paired-end reads to strip adapters and low-quality bases with trimmomatic V0.32 before short-read assembly, so that the draft contigs fed into npScarf real-time scaffolding are free of adapter-induced misassemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are nanopore long reads — npScarf consumes these via BWA-MEM streaming alignment, not short-read trimming The Illumina data are already trimmed — the npScarf project distributes pre-trimmed files such as Kp2146_paired_1.fastq.gz, and re-trimming trimmed data is unnecessary The assembly pipeline does not start from a short-read draft (e.g., long-read-only assembly with Celera Assembler or npGraph)

skills.description: Use when matched Illumina short-read BAM/CRAM data are available for a patient genome and you need SV calls (or a short-read recall baseline) to compare against long-read callers on validated breakpoint-junction sets.
skills.name: illumina-short-read-sv-calling
skills.search_text: illumina-short-read-sv-calling Use when matched Illumina short-read BAM/CRAM data are available for a patient genome and you need SV calls (or a short-read recall baseline) to compare against long-read callers on validated breakpoint-junction sets. Input is nanopore long-read data — NanoSV with LAST mapping is the appropriate caller pipeline for that modality Only a small targeted region is of interest rather than genome-wide SV discovery on whole-genome short-read data No validated breakpoint-junction truth set exists and the goal is de novo discovery rather than caller recall benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Calls structural variants from matched Illumina short-read data (e.g., with Manta and Delly) to benchmark their recall against long-read nanopore SV callers such as NanoSV on the same patient genomes. In the source study this established that short-read callers miss de novo chromothripsis breakpoints that NanoSV recovers from MinION reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Calls structural variants from matched Illumina short-read data (e.g., with Manta and Delly) to benchmark their recall against long-read nanopore SV callers such as NanoSV on the same patient genomes. In the source study this established that short-read callers miss de novo chromothripsis breakpoints that NanoSV recovers from MinION reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is nanopore long-read data — NanoSV with LAST mapping is the appropriate caller pipeline for that modality Only a small targeted region is of interest rather than genome-wide SV discovery on whole-genome short-read data No validated breakpoint-junction truth set exists and the goal is de novo discovery rather than caller recall benchmarking

skills.description: Use when an article reports imaging throughput or stage-precision numbers for automated microscopy workflows (s/image tiling rates, minutes-per-slide survey rates, slide-reload displacement, speedup ratios) and these must be captured as structured data.
skills.name: imaging-throughput-metric-extraction
skills.search_text: imaging-throughput-metric-extraction Use when an article reports imaging throughput or stage-precision numbers for automated microscopy workflows (s/image tiling rates, minutes-per-slide survey rates, slide-reload displacement, speedup ratios) and these must be captured as structured data. The source section contains only qualitative capability claims (e.g. the OpenHiCAMM discussion section's 'robust, flexible' statements) with no numeric throughput values to extract A structured benchmark table with condition/value/units already exists — re-extraction adds no information Throughput figures are needed for different hardware: the reported values are tied to the authors' setup (Prior PL-200 slide loader, Zeiss Axioplan 2, Nikon DSLR D5100 camera) and do not transfer to other platforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3397 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts quantitative stage-calibration and acquisition-speed benchmarks from microscope-workflow papers — such as the OpenHiCAMM two-phase imaging metrics (0.059 μm slide-reload displacement, 2.3 s/image at 5×, 20 min/slide SlideSurveyor at 20×) — into structured, unit-annotated records. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Extracts quantitative stage-calibration and acquisition-speed benchmarks from microscope-workflow papers — such as the OpenHiCAMM two-phase imaging metrics (0.059 μm slide-reload displacement, 2.3 s/image at 5×, 20 min/slide SlideSurveyor at 20×) — into structured, unit-annotated records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source section contains only qualitative capability claims (e.g. the OpenHiCAMM discussion section's 'robust, flexible' statements) with no numeric throughput values to extract A structured benchmark table with condition/value/units already exists — re-extraction adds no information Throughput figures are needed for different hardware: the reported values are tied to the authors' setup (Prior PL-200 slide loader, Zeiss Axioplan 2, Nikon DSLR D5100 camera) and do not transfer to other platforms

skills.description: Use when timing tables from a multi-pass microscopy acquisition exist and the goal is per-object imaging cost plus a speedup ratio versus a single-pass full-slide baseline.
skills.name: imaging-workflow-timing-analysis
skills.search_text: imaging-workflow-timing-analysis Use when timing tables from a multi-pass microscopy acquisition exist and the goal is per-object imaging cost plus a speedup ratio versus a single-pass full-slide baseline. No timing/acquisition-duration data exist and the question concerns image-analysis accuracy (e.g., ROIfinder detection quality) rather than throughput cost The workflow is a single-pass full-slide acquisition, so there is no two-pass baseline to normalize against Sample density or slide layout differs (e.g., well-based HCS plates) so the ~300 embryos/slide normalization is invalid Derives per-embryo high-resolution imaging cost and the speedup factor of a two-pass (low-res detect, high-res re-image) microscopy workflow by normalizing two-pass acquisition timing against full-slide 20× single-pass imaging, as done for OpenHiCAMM Drosophila embryo screening (~300 embryos/slide, ~10-fold speedup). genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Derives per-embryo high-resolution imaging cost and the speedup factor of a two-pass (low-res detect, high-res re-image) microscopy workflow by normalizing two-pass acquisition timing against full-slide 20× single-pass imaging, as done for OpenHiCAMM Drosophila embryo screening (~300 embryos/slide, ~10-fold speedup).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No timing/acquisition-duration data exist and the question concerns image-analysis accuracy (e.g., ROIfinder detection quality) rather than throughput cost The workflow is a single-pass full-slide acquisition, so there is no two-pass baseline to normalize against Sample density or slide layout differs (e.g., well-based HCS plates) so the ~300 embryos/slide normalization is invalid

skills.description: Use when evaluating splice site prediction models on test sets where true:false cases are skewed (e.g. 7500 true / 2500 false), to check accuracy robustness rather than only balanced-set performance.
skills.name: imbalanced-dataset-benchmark-testing
skills.search_text: imbalanced-dataset-benchmark-testing Use when evaluating splice site prediction models on test sets where true:false cases are skewed (e.g. 7500 true / 2500 false), to check accuracy robustness rather than only balanced-set performance. When the goal is to assess performance on balanced (5000 true / 5000 false) datasets — use the balanced testing mode instead When input sequences do not conform to the constructed dataset's Sequence Length of 400 constraint When the task is de novo splice site annotation of newly sequenced genomes rather than benchmarking pre-trained models on fixed test sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark pre-trained CNNSplice CNN models on imbalanced (3:1 true:false) acceptor and donor splice site test datasets across five organisms to verify that prediction accuracy is robust to skewed class distributions. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.031
skills.summary: Benchmark pre-trained CNNSplice CNN models on imbalanced (3:1 true:false) acceptor and donor splice site test datasets across five organisms to verify that prediction accuracy is robust to skewed class distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to assess performance on balanced (5000 true / 5000 false) datasets — use the balanced testing mode instead When input sequences do not conform to the constructed dataset's Sequence Length of 400 constraint When the task is de novo splice site annotation of newly sequenced genomes rather than benchmarking pre-trained models on fixed test sets

skills.description: Use when building 5mC training sets from Nanopore signal features where methylated cytosines are rare and label-imbalanced — especially CHH/CHG contexts — and random subsampling degrades model correlation with bisulfite.
skills.name: imbalanced-sample-rebalancing
skills.search_text: imbalanced-sample-rebalancing Use when building 5mC training sets from Nanopore signal features where methylated cytosines are rare and label-imbalanced — especially CHH/CHG contexts — and random subsampling degrades model correlation with bisulfite. Input is already a balanced, denoised training file with >=99% retention from a previous run — re-running the iterative loop would only re-predict and churn samples. Your goal is per-read/per-site modification calling on new reads (use deepsignal_plant call_mods / call_freq), not training-set construction. Working with non-plant Nanopore data where cytosine methylation is abundant (e.g. CpG-rich mammalian data with other callers like Megalodon); the extreme CHH imbalance this skill targets is plant-specific. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A sample-selection strategy for DeepSignal-plant that balances positive (methylated) and negative (unmethylated) k-mer training samples and read coverage per k-mer (Algorithm 1), and iteratively removes false methylated samples (Algorithm 2, I=10, R=3, E=3) so the BiLSTM 5mC model trains on clean, balanced data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: A sample-selection strategy for DeepSignal-plant that balances positive (methylated) and negative (unmethylated) k-mer training samples and read coverage per k-mer (Algorithm 1), and iteratively removes false methylated samples (Algorithm 2, I=10, R=3, E=3) so the BiLSTM 5mC model trains on clean, balanced data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a balanced, denoised training file with >=99% retention from a previous run — re-running the iterative loop would only re-predict and churn samples. Your goal is per-read/per-site modification calling on new reads (use deepsignal_plant call_mods / call_freq), not training-set construction. Working with non-plant Nanopore data where cytosine methylation is abundant (e.g. CpG-rich mammalian data with other callers like Megalodon); the extreme CHH imbalance this skill targets is plant-specific.

skills.description: Use when you have phased per-site methylation output (per_site / per_site.aggregated BED with mod_percentage_phase1 and mod_percentage_phase2 columns) from Nanopore reads of a human sample or trio and need to detect imprinted regions and parent-of-origin methylation.
skills.name: imprint-control-region-annotation
skills.search_text: imprint-control-region-annotation Use when you have phased per-site methylation output (per_site / per_site.aggregated BED with mod_percentage_phase1 and mod_percentage_phase2 columns) from Nanopore reads of a human sample or trio and need to detect imprinted regions and parent-of-origin methylation. The ICR lies in a long run of homozygosity where read phasing is not possible, so phased methylation counts alone are unreliable The target modification is not 5mCpG (DeepMod2 provides models only for 5mCpG; no 5hmC detected in GIAB cell lines HG001-HG007) Input is unphased per-site methylation without mod_percentage_phase1/phase2 columns, so allele-specific epihaplotype classification cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates imprinting control regions (ICRs) with allele-specific methylation state by intersecting phased per-site methylation calls from DeepMod2 with the curated ICR catalog (Jima et al. Supplementary Table S1 / humanicr.org), assigning epihaplotype and parent-of-origin labels from mod_percentage_phase1/phase2 values. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Annotates imprinting control regions (ICRs) with allele-specific methylation state by intersecting phased per-site methylation calls from DeepMod2 with the curated ICR catalog (Jima et al. Supplementary Table S1 / humanicr.org), assigning epihaplotype and parent-of-origin labels from mod_percentage_phase1/phase2 values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ICR lies in a long run of homozygosity where read phasing is not possible, so phased methylation counts alone are unreliable The target modification is not 5mCpG (DeepMod2 provides models only for 5mCpG; no 5hmC detected in GIAB cell lines HG001-HG007) Input is unphased per-site methylation without mod_percentage_phase1/phase2 columns, so allele-specific epihaplotype classification cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when nanoEM (converted long-read) alignments cover an imprinted locus with a heterozygous SNP, and per-allele CpG methylation frequencies must be computed to determine which parental allele is methylated.
skills.name: imprinted-locus-methylation-analysis
skills.search_text: imprinted-locus-methylation-analysis Use when nanoEM (converted long-read) alignments cover an imprinted locus with a heterozygous SNP, and per-allele CpG methylation frequencies must be computed to determine which parental allele is methylated. The locus contains no heterozygous SNP to anchor reads to a parental allele, so reads cannot be assigned to C or G alleles. The biological question is distinguishing 5-methylcytosine from 5-hydroxymethylcytosine on the same molecule — nanoEM cannot separate these. Input data are short-read bisulfite/EMseq alignments rather than nanoEM CT/GA converted long-read BAMs, since short reads cannot span SNP-to-CpG distances needed for allele phasing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Resolves allele-specific methylation at imprinted loci (e.g., GRB10 and MEST) by combining nanoEM C-to-T/G-to-A converted-read pileups with read-level assignment to alleles via a heterozygous SNP, which short-read methylation analysis cannot resolve. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: Resolves allele-specific methylation at imprinted loci (e.g., GRB10 and MEST) by combining nanoEM C-to-T/G-to-A converted-read pileups with read-level assignment to alleles via a heterozygous SNP, which short-read methylation analysis cannot resolve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus contains no heterozygous SNP to anchor reads to a parental allele, so reads cannot be assigned to C or G alleles. The biological question is distinguishing 5-methylcytosine from 5-hydroxymethylcytosine on the same molecule — nanoEM cannot separate these. Input data are short-read bisulfite/EMseq alignments rather than nanoEM CT/GA converted long-read BAMs, since short reads cannot span SNP-to-CpG distances needed for allele phasing.

skills.description: Use when building the first step of a nanoEM-style methylation pipeline: before aligning C-to-T or G-to-A converted reads, you need a reference FASTA in which every C is replaced by T and every G by A.
skills.name: in-silico-c-to-t-conversion
skills.search_text: in-silico-c-to-t-conversion Use when building the first step of a nanoEM-style methylation pipeline: before aligning C-to-T or G-to-A converted reads, you need a reference FASTA in which every C is replaced by T and every G by A. Reads are unconverted native DNA being aligned for direct methylation calling (e.g. nanopolish call-methylation) — use the original reference instead Only the reads need conversion (the *_CT.fq.gz / *_GA.fq.gz step) — that is convert_reads.py, not the reference-conversion step A converted reference for the same genome build already exists and its sequence lengths match the original reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Constructs a C-to-T / G-to-A converted copy of a reference genome (GRCh38.p12 in the nanoEM pipeline) so that enzymatically base-converted nanopore long reads carrying methylation-sensitive C-to-T (or G-to-A) conversions can be aligned to a genome mirroring their converted state. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: Constructs a C-to-T / G-to-A converted copy of a reference genome (GRCh38.p12 in the nanoEM pipeline) so that enzymatically base-converted nanopore long reads carrying methylation-sensitive C-to-T (or G-to-A) conversions can be aligned to a genome mirroring their converted state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are unconverted native DNA being aligned for direct methylation calling (e.g. nanopolish call-methylation) — use the original reference instead Only the reads need conversion (the *_CT.fq.gz / *_GA.fq.gz step) — that is convert_reads.py, not the reference-conversion step A converted reference for the same genome build already exists and its sequence lengths match the original reference

skills.description: Use when benchmarking somatic SV calling methods (e.g. nanomonsv vs detection-subtraction or CAMPHORsomatic) requires ground-truth breakpoints and controlled tumor purity/depth scenarios.
skills.name: in-silico-genome-sv-injection
skills.search_text: in-silico-genome-sv-injection Use when benchmarking somatic SV calling methods (e.g. nanomonsv vs detection-subtraction or CAMPHORsomatic) requires ground-truth breakpoints and controlled tumor purity/depth scenarios. Evaluating callers on real tumor/control long-read data where a validated experimental truth set (e.g. CCLE/hybrid-capture-validated SVs) is available Benchmarking germline-only SV callers, since the injected truth set here is designed around somatic tumor/control contrast Simulating platforms other than ONT (PacBio reads require different simulator profiles) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Constructs an in-silico diploid matched-control genome from GRCh38 by injecting germline SVs with SURVIVOR simSV, then injects a somatic SV truth set to create a tumor genome, enabling benchmarking of somatic SV callers on simulated Nanopore data. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Constructs an in-silico diploid matched-control genome from GRCh38 by injecting germline SVs with SURVIVOR simSV, then injects a somatic SV truth set to create a tumor genome, enabling benchmarking of somatic SV callers on simulated Nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating callers on real tumor/control long-read data where a validated experimental truth set (e.g. CCLE/hybrid-capture-validated SVs) is available Benchmarking germline-only SV callers, since the injected truth set here is designed around somatic tumor/control contrast Simulating platforms other than ONT (PacBio reads require different simulator profiles)

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify methylated vs non-methylated motif-site fractions from SMALR SMsn scores without applying thresholds — e.g., estimating native fraction in native/WGA mixtures or probing the coverage-versus-accuracy tradeoff.
skills.name: in-silico-methylome-mixture-simulation
skills.search_text: in-silico-methylome-mixture-simulation Use when you need to quantify methylated vs non-methylated motif-site fractions from SMALR SMsn scores without applying thresholds — e.g., estimating native fraction in native/WGA mixtures or probing the coverage-versus-accuracy tradeoff. Input is long (10Kb+) library prep data where molecule-wide methylation status should be assessed with the SMp motif-pooled protocol instead of per-site SMsn scoring The goal is reference-free, de novo discovery of methylation motifs rather than estimating the methylated fraction of a known motif A population-level consensus methylation call suffices and single-molecule or mixture-level fraction estimation is not required Simulates in silico mixtures of native and WGA molecules from per-site SMSn scores and fits a two-component Gaussian mixture with PyMix's EM algorithm to estimate the native (methylated) motif-site fraction without subjective score thresholds, testing accuracy across genomic sequence coverages. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: Simulates in silico mixtures of native and WGA molecules from per-site SMSn scores and fits a two-component Gaussian mixture with PyMix's EM algorithm to estimate the native (methylated) motif-site fraction without subjective score thresholds, testing accuracy across genomic sequence coverages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long (10Kb+) library prep data where molecule-wide methylation status should be assessed with the SMp motif-pooled protocol instead of per-site SMsn scoring The goal is reference-free, de novo discovery of methylation motifs rather than estimating the methylated fraction of a known motif A population-level consensus methylation call suffices and single-molecule or mixture-level fraction estimation is not required

skills.description: Use when a long-read isoform catalog yields predicted ORF proteins and you need to enumerate which tryptic peptides are novel relative to a reference proteome (e.g., UniProt mouse) before targeted mass spectrometry.
skills.name: in-silico-protease-digestion-of-orf-proteome
skills.search_text: in-silico-protease-digestion-of-orf-proteome Use when a long-read isoform catalog yields predicted ORF proteins and you need to enumerate which tryptic peptides are novel relative to a reference proteome (e.g., UniProt mouse) before targeted mass spectrometry. Input is an experimentally acquired mass-spectrometry peak list rather than predicted protein sequences — use peptide-spectrum matching instead The isoform catalog has not been filtered (no filter_db with exon_min_count = 4, abund_cutoff = 1, no filter_truncations), so ORFs are unvalidated and the peptide library is noisy The protease is not trypsin or the proline rule should not apply; the diff logic and enrichment-ratio expectations are calibrated for tryptic digestion http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Digests predicted ORF protein sequences (e.g., from the lrCaptureSeq IsoPops isoform catalog) in silico with trypsin plus the proline rule and diffs the resulting peptide set against a trypsin-digested UniProt Mouse Reference proteome to define unannotated peptides for MS-based validation of newly-discovered proteins. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Digests predicted ORF protein sequences (e.g., from the lrCaptureSeq IsoPops isoform catalog) in silico with trypsin plus the proline rule and diffs the resulting peptide set against a trypsin-digested UniProt Mouse Reference proteome to define unannotated peptides for MS-based validation of newly-discovered proteins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an experimentally acquired mass-spectrometry peak list rather than predicted protein sequences — use peptide-spectrum matching instead The isoform catalog has not been filtered (no filter_db with exon_min_count = 4, abund_cutoff = 1, no filter_truncations), so ORFs are unvalidated and the peptide library is noisy The protease is not trypsin or the proline rule should not apply; the diff logic and enrichment-ratio expectations are calibrated for tryptic digestion

skills.description: Use when reprocessing previously published INC-Seq consensus reads (e.g., R7-chemistry Ladder replicate data from Li et al.) to test whether de novo chopSeq/nanoClust consensus calling beats the INC-Seq 97-98% median accuracy baseline.
skills.name: inc-seq-baseline-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: inc-seq-baseline-comparison-analysis Use when reprocessing previously published INC-Seq consensus reads (e.g., R7-chemistry Ladder replicate data from Li et al.) to test whether de novo chopSeq/nanoClust consensus calling beats the INC-Seq 97-98% median accuracy baseline. Input is raw noisy nanopore reads rather than INC-Seq consensus reads — chopSeq is designed for fragmentation and orientation correction of INC-Seq consensus reads, not raw read mapping The analysis goal is reference-based mapping of noisy long reads to databases like SILVA — the whole rationale here is a completely de novo consensus approach without reference mapping A quick classification-only assignment suffices — classification-only analysis is limited in differentiating closely related sequences and risks false detections http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarks a reprocessed nanopore amplicon dataset (e.g., Li et al. INC-Seq R7 Ladder reads) against the published INC-Seq accuracy baseline by running the chopSeq → nanoClust workflow and comparing per-OTU consensus accuracies to the 97–98% median INC-Seq accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Benchmarks a reprocessed nanopore amplicon dataset (e.g., Li et al. INC-Seq R7 Ladder reads) against the published INC-Seq accuracy baseline by running the chopSeq → nanoClust workflow and comparing per-OTU consensus accuracies to the 97–98% median INC-Seq accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw noisy nanopore reads rather than INC-Seq consensus reads — chopSeq is designed for fragmentation and orientation correction of INC-Seq consensus reads, not raw read mapping The analysis goal is reference-based mapping of noisy long reads to databases like SILVA — the whole rationale here is a completely de novo consensus approach without reference mapping A quick classification-only assignment suffices — classification-only analysis is limited in differentiating closely related sequences and risks false detections

skills.search_text: inconsistent-overlap-detection-string-graph Use when reconstructing haplotype-specific contigs from long noisy reads: after a first-round haplotype-collapsed assembly, to phase reads by SNP alleles and flag cross-haplotype overlaps before reassembly. Input reads are PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — the article reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on these accurate read types SNP sites lie in very low heterozygosity-rate regions, where SNP calling accuracy is too low to reliably distinguish haplotypes Dataset coverage is below the SNP-calling floor (sites outside coverage range [10, 1000] cannot be phased) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Identifies and removes overlaps between reads from different haplotypes (inconsistent overlaps) in PECAT's second-round string graph assembly, using SNP allele vectors called from corrected/raw reads on the haplotype-collapsed first-round contigs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
