skills.description: Use when calling InDel genotypes across progeny of a hybrid mapping population (BC1, BC2, F2, or CP) from reads aligned to a reference genome, at InDel sites predefined in a parental InDel catalog.
skills.name: indel-genotype-calling-from-vcf-records
skills.search_text: indel-genotype-calling-from-vcf-records Use when calling InDel genotypes across progeny of a hybrid mapping population (BC1, BC2, F2, or CP) from reads aligned to a reference genome, at InDel sites predefined in a parental InDel catalog. When the parental InDel catalog has not yet been generated — the catalog step must run first (skip it only with --nocatalog on a rerun) When variant sites are SNPs or catalog InDels shorter/longer than the intended marker set, since homozygote calling depends on the catalog start-to-end span When the goal is segregation analysis rather than genotyping — that is the separate third InDelGT step http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Second-step InDelGT procedure that calls per-progeny InDel genotypes at parental catalog sites: heterozygous genotypes are taken directly from sample VCF records (depth ≥ HETEROZYGOUS_DEPTH:3), while homozygous indel genotypes require allele absence across the full catalog InDel start-to-end span at depth ≥ HOMOZYGOUS_DEPTH:5, with all calls filtered by GQ:30. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Second-step InDelGT procedure that calls per-progeny InDel genotypes at parental catalog sites: heterozygous genotypes are taken directly from sample VCF records (depth ≥ HETEROZYGOUS_DEPTH:3), while homozygous indel genotypes require allele absence across the full catalog InDel start-to-end span at depth ≥ HOMOZYGOUS_DEPTH:5, with all calls filtered by GQ:30.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the parental InDel catalog has not yet been generated — the catalog step must run first (skip it only with --nocatalog on a rerun) When variant sites are SNPs or catalog InDels shorter/longer than the intended marker set, since homozygote calling depends on the catalog start-to-end span When the goal is segregation analysis rather than genotyping — that is the separate third InDelGT step

skills.description: Use when emitting a VCF from Clairvoyante variant calling on single-molecule sequencing (PacBio or ONT) data and you must remove long-indel predictions that the network cannot resolve to an exact alternative allele.
skills.name: indel-length-filtering-cnn-variant-caller
skills.search_text: indel-length-filtering-cnn-variant-caller Use when emitting a VCF from Clairvoyante variant calling on single-molecule sequencing (PacBio or ONT) data and you must remove long-indel predictions that the network cannot resolve to an exact alternative allele. You need to detect long indels (>4 bp) — the model was designed to provide exact alternative alleles only for indels ≤4 bp, so filtering would silently discard true calls rather than correct errors Variant calling with tools that resolve full ALT sequences for long indels (e.g., structural variant callers); this filter is specific to Clairvoyante network version 3's output layers Multi-allelic sites or variants with two or more alternative alleles — Clairvoyante already excludes multi-allelic SNPs from training and outputs only one of two possible alternative alleles per position http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Discard CNN-predicted indel calls longer than 4 bp, because Clairvoyante's multi-task network can only output an exact alternative allele for indel variants ≤4 bp due to the scarcity of long indel training samples. This filter keeps the emitted VCF restricted to calls for which the model can supply a precise ALT allele. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Discard CNN-predicted indel calls longer than 4 bp, because Clairvoyante's multi-task network can only output an exact alternative allele for indel variants ≤4 bp due to the scarcity of long indel training samples. This filter keeps the emitted VCF restricted to calls for which the model can supply a precise ALT allele.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to detect long indels (>4 bp) — the model was designed to provide exact alternative alleles only for indels ≤4 bp, so filtering would silently discard true calls rather than correct errors Variant calling with tools that resolve full ALT sequences for long indels (e.g., structural variant callers); this filter is specific to Clairvoyante network version 3's output layers Multi-allelic sites or variants with two or more alternative alleles — Clairvoyante already excludes multi-allelic SNPs from training and outputs only one of two possible alternative alleles per position

skills.description: Use when filtering SNV calls from a long-read variant caller (e.g., Longshot on PacBio BAMs) to reduce indel-proximate false positives, with the goal of lowering FDR (target ~0.3%) while minimally hurting recall.
skills.name: indel-proximity-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: indel-proximity-variant-filtering Use when filtering SNV calls from a long-read variant caller (e.g., Longshot on PacBio BAMs) to reduce indel-proximate false positives, with the goal of lowering FDR (target ~0.3%) while minimally hurting recall. The variant caller already models indels as candidate variants (the filter targets errors arising because Longshot does not consider indels). You need to genotype/phase indels themselves — Longshot currently only calls SNVs and can genotype indels only if supplied in an input VCF. Accurate short indel calls from SMS reads are the goal — the article notes this remains challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A post-calling filter for Longshot SNV calls on long-read (PacBio) data that removes SNVs located near known common indels (Mills + 1000 Genomes Gold Standard Indels), exploiting the fact that many indel-driven false positives arise because Longshot does not consider indels as candidate variants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: A post-calling filter for Longshot SNV calls on long-read (PacBio) data that removes SNVs located near known common indels (Mills + 1000 Genomes Gold Standard Indels), exploiting the fact that many indel-driven false positives arise because Longshot does not consider indels as candidate variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant caller already models indels as candidate variants (the filter targets errors arising because Longshot does not consider indels). You need to genotype/phase indels themselves — Longshot currently only calls SNVs and can genotype indels only if supplied in an input VCF. Accurate short indel calls from SMS reads are the goal — the article notes this remains challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate.

skills.description: Use when a concordant filtered variant list (e.g. PacBio+ONT calls absent from GIAB) must be decomposed into SNP/insertion/deletion counts and quality-checked via its Ti/Tv ratio.
skills.name: indel-snp-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: indel-snp-subtype-classification Use when a concordant filtered variant list (e.g. PacBio+ONT calls absent from GIAB) must be decomposed into SNP/insertion/deletion counts and quality-checked via its Ti/Tv ratio. The input call set still contains multi-allelic SNPs or multi-allelic sites — Clairvoyante's design ignores variants with two or more alternative alleles, so subtype counts would be biased The variant list has not yet been intersected across technologies and subtracted against GIAB truth — classification of the raw concordant calls answers a different question http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies a filtered variant call set into SNP, insertion, and deletion subtypes and computes the transition/transversion (Ti/Tv) ratio, as used to characterize the 3,135-variant HG001 catalog (2,732 SNPs, 298 deletions, 105 insertions, Ti/Tv ~1.42) absent from the GIAB v3.3.2 truth set. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Classifies a filtered variant call set into SNP, insertion, and deletion subtypes and computes the transition/transversion (Ti/Tv) ratio, as used to characterize the 3,135-variant HG001 catalog (2,732 SNPs, 298 deletions, 105 insertions, Ti/Tv ~1.42) absent from the GIAB v3.3.2 truth set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input call set still contains multi-allelic SNPs or multi-allelic sites — Clairvoyante's design ignores variants with two or more alternative alleles, so subtype counts would be biased The variant list has not yet been intersected across technologies and subtracted against GIAB truth — classification of the raw concordant calls answers a different question

skills.description: Use when a protein classifier trained on a benchmark set (e.g. PDB1075) must be scored on a held-out independent set (e.g. PDB186) to report generalization metrics Acc, Sn, Sp, MCC, AUC against published baselines.
skills.name: independent-dataset-validation-of-protein-classifier
skills.search_text: independent-dataset-validation-of-protein-classifier Use when a protein classifier trained on a benchmark set (e.g. PDB1075) must be scored on a held-out independent set (e.g. PDB186) to report generalization metrics Acc, Sn, Sp, MCC, AUC against published baselines. Benchmarking on the training corpora PDB1075 or PDB594 themselves — the paper evaluates those with Jackknife and 10-fold cross-validation, not an independent split The test proteins have no precomputed feature .mat files (DDE186.mat, PSSM_DBT_186.mat, PSSM_DWT_186.mat, feature_NMBAC_186.mat) — PSSM generation via PSI-BLAST and feature extraction (DDE/DBT/DWT/NMBAC) is a separate upstream skill Choosing SVM hyperparameters C or gamma — these must be fixed from grid search on training data (C=1, gamma=0.03125); using PDB186 to tune them would invalidate the independent validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Protocol for independent-dataset validation of the iDBP-DEP DNA-binding protein predictor: train an LIBSVM RBF-kernel SVM (C=1, gamma=0.03125) on PDB1075 top-424 features, score the untouched PDB186 set (93 DBPs / 93 non-DBPs), and report Acc, Sn, Sp, MCC and ROC-AUC against published predictors (Table 8). genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Protocol for independent-dataset validation of the iDBP-DEP DNA-binding protein predictor: train an LIBSVM RBF-kernel SVM (C=1, gamma=0.03125) on PDB1075 top-424 features, score the untouched PDB186 set (93 DBPs / 93 non-DBPs), and report Acc, Sn, Sp, MCC and ROC-AUC against published predictors (Table 8).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking on the training corpora PDB1075 or PDB594 themselves — the paper evaluates those with Jackknife and 10-fold cross-validation, not an independent split The test proteins have no precomputed feature .mat files (DDE186.mat, PSSM_DBT_186.mat, PSSM_DWT_186.mat, feature_NMBAC_186.mat) — PSSM generation via PSI-BLAST and feature extraction (DDE/DBT/DWT/NMBAC) is a separate upstream skill Choosing SVM hyperparameters C or gamma — these must be fixed from grid search on training data (C=1, gamma=0.03125); using PDB186 to tune them would invalidate the independent validation

skills.description: Use when validating or reproducing a modeled MTF/NNPS curve for an indirect-conversion CsI flat-panel detector (e.g., Koning bCT), given a system YAML configuration and expected experimental transfer curves.
skills.name: indirect-conversion-csi-detector-cascade
skills.search_text: indirect-conversion-csi-detector-cascade Use when validating or reproducing a modeled MTF/NNPS curve for an indirect-conversion CsI flat-panel detector (e.g., Koning bCT), given a system YAML configuration and expected experimental transfer curves. The detector is a direct-conversion a-Se device (DM/DBT) — use the direct-conversion cascade variant instead of the CsI indirect pipeline The system is a photon-counting detector or involves adaptive binning, detector lag/ghosting, or Fano noise — CASYMIR does not model these processes Per-energy-bin propagation of signal and noise quantities is required — CASYMIR does not propagate on a per-energy-bin basis http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Reproduce the CASYMIR cascaded linear-systems model of a CsI flat-panel dedicated breast CT (bCT) detector by propagating signal and noise through quantum selection, K-fluorescence, optical blur/coupling, pixel integration, and noise-aliasing blocks, then computing MTF and NNPS against experimental baselines (5.4% RMS MTF and 5.8% normalized RMS NNPS error). genomics/v1 10.1002/mp.18079
skills.summary: Reproduce the CASYMIR cascaded linear-systems model of a CsI flat-panel dedicated breast CT (bCT) detector by propagating signal and noise through quantum selection, K-fluorescence, optical blur/coupling, pixel integration, and noise-aliasing blocks, then computing MTF and NNPS against experimental baselines (5.4% RMS MTF and 5.8% normalized RMS NNPS error).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The detector is a direct-conversion a-Se device (DM/DBT) — use the direct-conversion cascade variant instead of the CsI indirect pipeline The system is a photon-counting detector or involves adaptive binning, detector lag/ghosting, or Fano noise — CASYMIR does not model these processes Per-energy-bin propagation of signal and noise quantities is required — CASYMIR does not propagate on a per-energy-bin basis

skills.description: Use when you need individual-level (not summary-level) simulated GWAS data with direct control over confounding (e.g., Xs_variance_explained_by_U, Y_variance_explained_by_U) for evaluating MR methods, or when benchmarking generate_individual() runtime at large settings.
skills.name: individual-level-gwas-simulation
skills.search_text: individual-level-gwas-simulation Use when you need individual-level (not summary-level) simulated GWAS data with direct control over confounding (e.g., Xs_variance_explained_by_U, Y_variance_explained_by_U) for evaluating MR methods, or when benchmarking generate_individual() runtime at large settings. You only need summary-level GWAS statistics for most simulation studies — generate_summary() is the faster path and is suitable for most simulation studies. You need to set confounding directly at scale but runtime matters more than flexibility — generate_individual() is slower because it builds individual-level genotype and phenotype data before running GWAS. You require multi-iteration Monte Carlo output from one call — both generate_individual() and generate_summary() generate data for a single simulation replicate; use the cli/ pixi workflow for multi-iteration runs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Generate a single replicate of simulated individual-level GWAS genotype and phenotype data for Mendelian randomization using simmrd's generate_individual(), which builds individual-level data before running GWAS. This is the slower but more flexible simmrd path because confounding can be set directly. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Generate a single replicate of simulated individual-level GWAS genotype and phenotype data for Mendelian randomization using simmrd's generate_individual(), which builds individual-level data before running GWAS. This is the slower but more flexible simmrd path because confounding can be set directly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need summary-level GWAS statistics for most simulation studies — generate_summary() is the faster path and is suitable for most simulation studies. You need to set confounding directly at scale but runtime matters more than flexibility — generate_individual() is slower because it builds individual-level genotype and phenotype data before running GWAS. You require multi-iteration Monte Carlo output from one call — both generate_individual() and generate_summary() generate data for a single simulation replicate; use the cli/ pixi workflow for multi-iteration runs.

skills.search_text: insert-size-distribution-estimation Use when Fast-SG synthetic mate-pair libraries (e.g. 200 bp pairs at 1000/2000/3000/5000 bp insert sizes) have been extracted from long reads and per-library scaffold-linking parameters are needed before scaffolding. The linking data are real long-range mate-pair libraries (e.g. 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL Genomics) rather than Fast-SG synthetic libraries — insert sizes span a range and orientation may be unknown, so the fixed-D estimation scheme does not apply Synthetic pairs have not yet been extracted — the estimation step requires aligned within-contig synthetic pairs as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Estimates per-library insert-size mean, standard deviation, and read-pair orientation (FR/RF) by aligning Fast-SG synthetic mate-pair reads back to the contig set and summarizing the within-contig insert-size distribution. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing the read-selection stage of a paired-end SV caller (e.g. dysgu fetch) and you need to classify which reads are SV candidates based on insert-size outliers, soft-clips (≥15 bp), MAPQ (≥1), cigar gaps (≥30 bp), or inter-chromosomal mates.
skills.name: insert-size-outlier-detection
skills.search_text: insert-size-outlier-detection Use when reconstructing or reimplementing the read-selection stage of a paired-end SV caller (e.g. dysgu fetch) and you need to classify which reads are SV candidates based on insert-size outliers, soft-clips (≥15 bp), MAPQ (≥1), cigar gaps (≥30 bp), or inter-chromosomal mates. Input is long-read data — the insert-size/soft-clip paired-end criteria and the ≥200 depth cutoff do not apply (long reads use a ≥150 depth cutoff and discordant-pair signals are not relevant) Reads are unsorted or the BAM lacks an index — dysgu's fetch expects a sorted and indexed .bam/.cram The goal is variant-level (not read-level) filtering — downstream call filtering uses model probability thresholds (≥0.5 PacBio, ≥0.35 ONT), not insert-size outlier read flags http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Flags paired-end reads as SV candidates when their inferred insert size is discordant — an extreme outlier relative to the sample's insert-size distribution (≥ median + 5 standard deviations) — as part of dysgu's 'fetch' stage that partitions SV-associated reads into a temporary BAM. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Flags paired-end reads as SV candidates when their inferred insert size is discordant — an extreme outlier relative to the sample's insert-size distribution (≥ median + 5 standard deviations) — as part of dysgu's 'fetch' stage that partitions SV-associated reads into a temporary BAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data — the insert-size/soft-clip paired-end criteria and the ≥200 depth cutoff do not apply (long reads use a ≥150 depth cutoff and discordant-pair signals are not relevant) Reads are unsorted or the BAM lacks an index — dysgu's fetch expects a sorted and indexed .bam/.cram The goal is variant-level (not read-level) filtering — downstream call filtering uses model probability thresholds (≥0.5 PacBio, ≥0.35 ONT), not insert-size outlier read flags

skills.description: Use when auditing or reproducing VolcanoSV DUP calls from its SV VCF output, or when explaining/comparing VolcanoSV vs SVIM-asm duplication detection performance on simulated long-read datasets.
skills.name: inserted-sequence-realignment-to-reference
skills.search_text: inserted-sequence-realignment-to-reference Use when auditing or reproducing VolcanoSV DUP calls from its SV VCF output, or when explaining/comparing VolcanoSV vs SVIM-asm duplication detection performance on simulated long-read datasets. When evaluating real complex somatic SVs against the HCC1395 high-confidence callset, where only recall is plotted and duplication recovery behavior may differ When the callset was produced by a different SV caller (e.g., SVIM-asm or cuteSV) whose INS records do not carry the full inserted sequence in the ALT allele When analyzing sex chromosomes — the README states VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 A duplication-recovery filter that distinguishes true duplications from insertion calls by extracting the pure inserted sequence from each INS record in a VolcanoSV SV VCF, realigning it to the hg19 reference with minimap2, and re-labeling records whose inserted sequence self-aligns near their own breakpoint as DUP. This mechanistically explains VolcanoSV's elevated DUP F1/GT_F1 scores over SVIM-asm on simulated data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: A duplication-recovery filter that distinguishes true duplications from insertion calls by extracting the pure inserted sequence from each INS record in a VolcanoSV SV VCF, realigning it to the hg19 reference with minimap2, and re-labeling records whose inserted sequence self-aligns near their own breakpoint as DUP. This mechanistically explains VolcanoSV's elevated DUP F1/GT_F1 scores over SVIM-asm on simulated data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When evaluating real complex somatic SVs against the HCC1395 high-confidence callset, where only recall is plotted and duplication recovery behavior may differ When the callset was produced by a different SV caller (e.g., SVIM-asm or cuteSV) whose INS records do not carry the full inserted sequence in the ALT allele When analyzing sex chromosomes — the README states VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes

skills.name: insertion-breakpoint-signature-detection
skills.search_text: insertion-breakpoint-signature-detection Use when orphan contigs from a local-assembly insertion pipeline must be screened against a reference genome to discard spurious placements and output non-reference insertion calls with breakpoints defined by anchor alignments. skills.summary: Filters and places locally assembled insertion contigs onto a reference genome (e.g. GRCh38) using a QUAST-resembling best-alignment-subset procedure, then retains only contigs showing the anchor-pair insertion signature (anchors close on the reference but far apart on the contig) with insertion and summed-anchor lengths exceeding 300 bp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads still need local assembly of the insertion sequence first — this skill operates on already-assembled orphan contigs Short-read-only insertion callers (MindTheGap, Pamir, PopIns2) are the intended approach when no synthetic long-read barcode data exist Insertions of interest are ≤ 300 bp — the output filter and the paper's analysis explicitly restrict to insertions longer than 300 bp

skills.search_text: insertion-deletion-mismatch-quantification Use when you need per-error-type (insertion/deletion/mismatch) read-level profiles of a basecaller or sequencing protocol, rather than a single aggregate accuracy number. skills.description: Use when a contig-to-reference BAM (primary + supplementary split alignments) from a diploid assembly must be converted into large INS/DEL SV signatures, e.g. after running VolcanoSV-asm on HiFi/CLR/ONT reads.
skills.name: insertion-deletion-signature-classification
skills.search_text: insertion-deletion-signature-classification Use when a contig-to-reference BAM (primary + supplementary split alignments) from a diploid assembly must be converted into large INS/DEL SV signatures, e.g. after running VolcanoSV-asm on HiFi/CLR/ONT reads. Input is raw read-to-reference alignments without an assembly: the read-based signature filtering (e.g. supporting-signature-depth bounds lb=0.2/rb=2.6 for HiFi) is a separate downstream step, not this block-geometry classification Target is sex chromosomes: VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes is very different Target is small indels or complex SVs (TRA requires WGS BAM support and is handled by separate VolcanoSV-vc modules) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies large insertion and deletion SV signatures (50–250 bp and larger) by analyzing consecutive split alignment blocks of contigs aligned to a reference, using the Diff_dis reference-distance and Diff_olp overlap metrics with thresholds TH_dis=30 bp and TH_olp=3000 bp. This is the large-indel detection module of VolcanoSV-vc, which ultimately contributes to a phased VCF output. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Classifies large insertion and deletion SV signatures (50–250 bp and larger) by analyzing consecutive split alignment blocks of contigs aligned to a reference, using the Diff_dis reference-distance and Diff_olp overlap metrics with thresholds TH_dis=30 bp and TH_olp=3000 bp. This is the large-indel detection module of VolcanoSV-vc, which ultimately contributes to a phased VCF output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read-to-reference alignments without an assembly: the read-based signature filtering (e.g. supporting-signature-depth bounds lb=0.2/rb=2.6 for HiFi) is a separate downstream step, not this block-geometry classification Target is sex chromosomes: VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes is very different Target is small indels or complex SVs (TRA requires WGS BAM support and is handled by separate VolcanoSV-vc modules)

skills.description: Use when per-sample insertion callsets from long-read callers (e.g., cuteSV-Sniffles2 VCFs) lack a consensus inserted sequence, and downstream merging, genotyping, or annotation requires the actual inserted bases.
skills.name: insertion-sequence-reassembly-from-supporting-reads
skills.search_text: insertion-sequence-reassembly-from-supporting-reads Use when per-sample insertion callsets from long-read callers (e.g., cuteSV-Sniffles2 VCFs) lack a consensus inserted sequence, and downstream merging, genotyping, or annotation requires the actual inserted bases. When the insertion callset already contains reliable consensus inserted sequences from the caller, reassembly adds little and the 15% length filter could discard legitimate support When only coordinate-level merging is required and inserted sequence content is irrelevant (a coordinate-only SURVIVOR merge suffices) When input reads are short reads (e.g., MELT-style Illumina analysis) rather than the nanopore long reads RetroInspector expects Reassembles the inserted nucleotide sequence of TE insertion calls from the nanopore reads supporting each call, since variant callers like cuteSV and Sniffles2 do not reliably report a consensus inserted sequence. The reassembled sequences enable sequence-aware merging of insertion calls and characterization of retrotransposition hallmarks. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Reassembles the inserted nucleotide sequence of TE insertion calls from the nanopore reads supporting each call, since variant callers like cuteSV and Sniffles2 do not reliably report a consensus inserted sequence. The reassembled sequences enable sequence-aware merging of insertion calls and characterization of retrotransposition hallmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the insertion callset already contains reliable consensus inserted sequences from the caller, reassembly adds little and the 15% length filter could discard legitimate support When only coordinate-level merging is required and inserted sequence content is irrelevant (a coordinate-only SURVIVOR merge suffices) When input reads are short reads (e.g., MELT-style Illumina analysis) rather than the nanopore long reads RetroInspector expects

skills.name: interactive-html-report-generation
skills.search_text: interactive-html-report-generation Use when a scywalker run has produced the minimap2_splice BAM, emptydrops-filtered gene counts, and cell-type assignments, and an interactive QC report summarizing them is needed. No cell-type markerset was supplied (scsorter/sctype typing was not run), so the UMAP/typing panel cannot be populated meaningfully. The input is a downstream analysis of an already-produced report (e.g. re-plotting extracted tables) rather than summarizing scywalker pipeline outputs. The run used the organelle-specific algorithm branch on organellar data, where the isoquant-based code path may hang or crash and report completeness is not guaranteed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assembles scywalker pipeline outputs — cramino alignment metrics, knee plot with emptydrops-approved cells, read-length and genes-per-cell histograms, alignment interval-overlap summary, and a cell-type UMAP — into a single interactive HTML report for long-read single-cell quality control and cell type identification review. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Assembles scywalker pipeline outputs — cramino alignment metrics, knee plot with emptydrops-approved cells, read-length and genes-per-cell histograms, alignment interval-overlap summary, and a cell-type UMAP — into a single interactive HTML report for long-read single-cell quality control and cell type identification review.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending published claims about intermediate file size or parse-time performance of a read-depth CNV caller, e.g. verifying CNVpytor's 2-20x parsing speedup and 20-50x smaller intermediate files versus CNVnator.
skills.name: intermediate-file-footprint-measurement
skills.search_text: intermediate-file-footprint-measurement Use when reproducing or extending published claims about intermediate file size or parse-time performance of a read-depth CNV caller, e.g. verifying CNVpytor's 2-20x parsing speedup and 20-50x smaller intermediate files versus CNVnator. The goal is accuracy of CNV calls rather than I/O performance — call-level agreement (>99% overlap between CNVnator and CNVpytor calls) is a separate evaluation and does not follow from footprint benchmarks. The comparison target is not a CNVnator-derived intermediate format, so the reported 20-50x size and 2-20x speed ratios are not applicable baselines. Only final results files (calls, plots, VCF/TSV exports) matter for the analysis and intermediate artifacts are immediately discarded. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks the disk footprint and parse speed of intermediate files produced by CNV callers, comparing CNVpytor's compressed HDF5 (.pytor) files against CNVnator's intermediate output on the same BAM inputs. skills.search_text: internal-membrane-detection-in-watershed-cells Use when watershed segmentation of multiplexed tissue images merges adjacent columnar epithelial cells because incomplete internal membranes were not resolved, and per-cell membrane/cytoplasm/nucleus probability maps from ilastik are available. Cells have no internal membrane-class signal (<10% of cell area) and no internal Mucin 2 expression — the resegmentation step only acts on flagged cells The segmentation is being performed by a non-membrane-aware method (e.g., Voronoi tessellation) rather than MIRIAM's watershed labels — the extension algorithm operates on MIRIAM's own watershed output and probability maps Input lacks multi-marker multiplexed image data needed for ilastik pixel classification of membrane/cytoplasm/nucleus compartments http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 MIRIAM's resegmentation step detects watershed-segmented cells that contain aberrant internal membranes (membrane-class signal inside the cell exceeding 10% of cell area, or internal Mucin 2 expression) and splits them by extending internal membrane segments via a 'connects the dots' endpoint-extension algorithm. This recovers single-cell boundaries that standard watershed under-segments in columnar epithelial tissue.

skills.description: Use when you have aligned PacBio full-length transcript (LRTS) BAM files plus a genome FASTA and reference annotation, and you need to know what fraction of reads per sample group are affected by internal priming, truncation, RTTS, or fragments.
skills.name: internal-priming-artifact-assessment
skills.search_text: internal-priming-artifact-assessment Use when you have aligned PacBio full-length transcript (LRTS) BAM files plus a genome FASTA and reference annotation, and you need to know what fraction of reads per sample group are affected by internal priming, truncation, RTTS, or fragments. Input is short-read RNA-seq data — IsoTools QC artifact tagging is designed for LRTS bam files of aligned full length transcripts You need differential alternative splicing or transcript reconstruction rather than QC artifact fractions — use IsoTools' segment-graph splicing event or beta-binomial differential analysis functionality instead BAM files have not been imported with sample names and groups into a Transcriptome object, so per-group aggregation is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3573 Quantifies the fraction of PacBio LRTS reads affected by technical artifacts — internal priming, transcript truncation, RTTS, and FRAGMENTS (reads lacking a reference TSS/PAS) — by computing per-read QC metrics in IsoTools and aggregating per-group artifact tag fractions, e.g. for CTL vs VPA-treated human hepatocyte samples. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of PacBio LRTS reads affected by technical artifacts — internal priming, transcript truncation, RTTS, and FRAGMENTS (reads lacking a reference TSS/PAS) — by computing per-read QC metrics in IsoTools and aggregating per-group artifact tag fractions, e.g. for CTL vs VPA-treated human hepatocyte samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data — IsoTools QC artifact tagging is designed for LRTS bam files of aligned full length transcripts You need differential alternative splicing or transcript reconstruction rather than QC artifact fractions — use IsoTools' segment-graph splicing event or beta-binomial differential analysis functionality instead BAM files have not been imported with sample names and groups into a Transcriptome object, so per-group aggregation is impossible

skills.description: Use when a plastid genome (e.g., fern or hornwort, high RNA editing) has annotations with internal stop codons that would be rejected by NCBI, and no cDNA/RNA-Seq data is available to confirm editing sites.
skills.name: internal-stop-codon-correction
skills.search_text: internal-stop-codon-correction Use when a plastid genome (e.g., fern or hornwort, high RNA editing) has annotations with internal stop codons that would be rejected by NCBI, and no cDNA/RNA-Seq data is available to confirm editing sites. Files created in Sequin — a known error means ReFernment does not produce annotations for them (use files exported from Geneious instead) The goal is predicting every RNA editing site from RNA-Seq data — ReFernment is not intended for that and relies on assumed C-to-U/U-to-C edits without cDNA The input annotation itself is sloppy — ReFernment is not a substitute for manually checking gene annotations nor a fix for sloppy annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Refines existing plastid gene annotations by detecting internal stop codons and correcting those explainable by C-to-U/U-to-C RNA editing, producing GenBank-ready files with conceptual translations using the ReFernment R package. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.1216
skills.summary: Refines existing plastid gene annotations by detecting internal stop codons and correcting those explainable by C-to-U/U-to-C RNA editing, producing GenBank-ready files with conceptual translations using the ReFernment R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Files created in Sequin — a known error means ReFernment does not produce annotations for them (use files exported from Geneious instead) The goal is predicting every RNA editing site from RNA-Seq data — ReFernment is not intended for that and relies on assumed C-to-U/U-to-C edits without cDNA The input annotation itself is sloppy — ReFernment is not a substitute for manually checking gene annotations nor a fix for sloppy annotation

skills.description: Use when building a protein-domain annotation layer for a sequence-to-genome mapping database: you have matched Swiss-Prot FASTA sequences and need each Pfam domain instance parsed from InterProScan output and loaded per sequence entry into a relational database.
skills.name: interproscan-output-parsing-and-database-loading
skills.search_text: interproscan-output-parsing-and-database-loading Use when building a protein-domain annotation layer for a sequence-to-genome mapping database: you have matched Swiss-Prot FASTA sequences and need each Pfam domain instance parsed from InterProScan output and loaded per sequence entry into a relational database. You only need domain annotations for exploratory browsing rather than populating the mapping database — the MetaDome web server or Pfam web services suffice without building the 'interpro_domains' table Your target sequences are not GENCODE-matched Swiss-Prot canonical/isoform sequences; running InterProScan on raw GENCODE translations would not reproduce the Swiss-Prot-keyed inventory Using MetaDome v2.0 prebuilt releases (Pfam-37.4 domain consensus positions already in the Zenodo mapping-database CSV) — the domain layer is already provided and InterProScan re-annotation is redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates protein sequences with Pfam domain instances by running InterProScan over the Swiss-Prot FASTA set and parsing the output into the PostgreSQL mapping database's domain table, establishing the domain inventory underlying MetaDome's meta-domain analyses. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Annotates protein sequences with Pfam domain instances by running InterProScan over the Swiss-Prot FASTA set and parsing the output into the PostgreSQL mapping database's domain table, establishing the domain inventory underlying MetaDome's meta-domain analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need domain annotations for exploratory browsing rather than populating the mapping database — the MetaDome web server or Pfam web services suffice without building the 'interpro_domains' table Your target sequences are not GENCODE-matched Swiss-Prot canonical/isoform sequences; running InterProScan on raw GENCODE translations would not reproduce the Swiss-Prot-keyed inventory Using MetaDome v2.0 prebuilt releases (Pfam-37.4 domain consensus positions already in the Zenodo mapping-database CSV) — the domain layer is already provided and InterProScan re-annotation is redundant

skills.name: intestine-disease-gene-filtering
skills.search_text: intestine-disease-gene-filtering Use when the input is GutUDB DISEASES-module association data and the goal is to tally gene associations per intestinal disease (colon cancer, colorectal cancer, IBD, constipation, diarrhea, etc.) and intersect gene sets across diseases. The analysis targets non-intestinal diseases outside the 56 intestinal diseases covered by GutUDB The input is raw multiomics profiles (e.g. the ~9 million omics profiles or THERAPY drug-disease interactions) rather than the DISEASES-module gene-association table A per-disease ranked gene list or p-value score is required — this skill produces counts and set intersections only, not statistical rankings http://edamontology.org/topic_3337 A skill for computing per-disease gene-association counts and the set of genes shared across the main intestine-related diseases curated in GutUDB's DISEASES module, using pandas set operations over the 260,790 disease-gene association records. genomics/v1 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: A skill for computing per-disease gene-association counts and the set of genes shared across the main intestine-related diseases curated in GutUDB's DISEASES module, using pandas set operations over the 260,790 disease-gene association records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets non-intestinal diseases outside the 56 intestinal diseases covered by GutUDB The input is raw multiomics profiles (e.g. the ~9 million omics profiles or THERAPY drug-disease interactions) rather than the DISEASES-module gene-association table A per-disease ranked gene list or p-value score is required — this skill produces counts and set intersections only, not statistical rankings

skills.description: Use when you need to extract intron chains from a reference GTF annotation and test whether transcript collapsing or merging tools retain or discard start/end variability among transcripts that share the same intron chain.
skills.name: intron-chain-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: intron-chain-annotation-parsing Use when you need to extract intron chains from a reference GTF annotation and test whether transcript collapsing or merging tools retain or discard start/end variability among transcripts that share the same intron chain. Input is raw long-read sequencing data (HiFi/FLNC reads) rather than an existing annotation/transcript model to parse The goal is collapsing actual Iso-Seq cluster output (PB.X.Y isoforms) across samples rather than benchmarking collapse behavior on synthetic variants http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A skill for parsing reference GTF/GFF annotations to extract transcript models and their intron chains (e.g. LPAR3 isoform ENST00000440086.1), then programmatically generating synthetic truncated 5'/3' variants sharing an identical intron chain to benchmark how collapse/merge tools (isoseq collapse vs gffcompare) treat start/end-coordinate variability. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: A skill for parsing reference GTF/GFF annotations to extract transcript models and their intron chains (e.g. LPAR3 isoform ENST00000440086.1), then programmatically generating synthetic truncated 5'/3' variants sharing an identical intron chain to benchmark how collapse/merge tools (isoseq collapse vs gffcompare) treat start/end-coordinate variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long-read sequencing data (HiFi/FLNC reads) rather than an existing annotation/transcript model to parse The goal is collapsing actual Iso-Seq cluster output (PB.X.Y isoforms) across samples rather than benchmarking collapse behavior on synthetic variants

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether transcript isoforms in a GTF annotation (e.g., GENCODE v39) are uniquely defined by their intron chains, or to count splice-junction signatures shared by multiple transcript start/end combinations.
skills.name: intron-chain-extraction
skills.search_text: intron-chain-extraction Use when you need to test whether transcript isoforms in a GTF annotation (e.g., GENCODE v39) are uniquely defined by their intron chains, or to count splice-junction signatures shared by multiple transcript start/end combinations. Input is raw long-read data (HiFi reads, subreads.bam) rather than an annotated transcript model — run the isoseq > minimap2/pbmm2 > SQANTI3 pipeline first to obtain isoform coordinates The goal is cross-sample differential isoform abundance or read-support deconvolution rather than isoform identity via splice junctions — isoSeQL's comparison and visualization features are the right fit Transcripts are single-exon (e.g., many NNC models), for which no intron chain can be derived http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts the ordered splice-junction (intron chain) signature of every transcript in an annotation such as GENCODE v39 and quantifies how uniquely each chain identifies a transcript, showing that 244,939 transcripts collapse to 215,652 unique intron chains with only 1.03% shared by multiple transcripts. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: Extracts the ordered splice-junction (intron chain) signature of every transcript in an annotation such as GENCODE v39 and quantifies how uniquely each chain identifies a transcript, showing that 244,939 transcripts collapse to 215,652 unique intron chains with only 1.03% shared by multiple transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long-read data (HiFi reads, subreads.bam) rather than an annotated transcript model — run the isoseq > minimap2/pbmm2 > SQANTI3 pipeline first to obtain isoform coordinates The goal is cross-sample differential isoform abundance or read-support deconvolution rather than isoform identity via splice junctions — isoSeQL's comparison and visualization features are the right fit Transcripts are single-exon (e.g., many NNC models), for which no intron chain can be derived

skills.description: Use when you have per-exon AISO quantification (upfi/dofi counts or Fupfi) from Insplico plus genome FASTA/GTF annotations and need to identify which genomic features correlate with splicing order.
skills.name: intron-exon-feature-extraction-matt
skills.search_text: intron-exon-feature-extraction-matt Use when you have per-exon AISO quantification (upfi/dofi counts or Fupfi) from Insplico plus genome FASTA/GTF annotations and need to identify which genomic features correlate with splicing order. If you only need AISO quantification itself without relating it to genomic features — use Insplico alone If the goal is splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the input exon — short reads barely provide such information If exons exceed the length quantifiable by Insplico with short reads, which is limited by read length (75/150 nt) and paired-end fragment size (250/500 bp) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Extracts 55 intron-exon features (splice-site strengths, intron/exon lengths, branch point-to-AG distances) around user-specified exons using Matt's cmpr_features, then relates them to Insplico-derived Fupfi values by binning exons into five equal subsets per feature and plotting mean Fupfi per bin across species. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Extracts 55 intron-exon features (splice-site strengths, intron/exon lengths, branch point-to-AG distances) around user-specified exons using Matt's cmpr_features, then relates them to Insplico-derived Fupfi values by binning exons into five equal subsets per feature and plotting mean Fupfi per bin across species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you only need AISO quantification itself without relating it to genomic features — use Insplico alone If the goal is splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the input exon — short reads barely provide such information If exons exceed the length quantifiable by Insplico with short reads, which is limited by read length (75/150 nt) and paired-end fragment size (250/500 bp)

skills.description: Use when processing chromatin/nuclear-fraction Nanopore dRNA-seq alignments (BAM) with a matching gene annotation (GTF) and you need per-read premature/mature labels before estimating RNA processing and dynamics rates.
skills.name: intronic-overlap-premature-read-classification
skills.search_text: intronic-overlap-premature-read-classification Use when processing chromatin/nuclear-fraction Nanopore dRNA-seq alignments (BAM) with a matching gene annotation (GTF) and you need per-read premature/mature labels before estimating RNA processing and dynamics rates. Processing cytoplasmic or polysomal samples where premature calls are not interpretable — premature classifications should be removed there rather than generated Short-read RNA-seq data where single reads cannot span introns to establish >= 10 base intronic overlap Input is already a gene-level count matrix without per-read alignment information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies each Nanopore direct RNA-seq read from subcellular fractions as premature or mature by intersecting gene-assigned read alignments (BAM) with annotated introns (GTF) in R, using a minimum intronic overlap of 10 bases. This per-read labeling underpins Nanodynamo's quantification of co- vs post-transcriptional processing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Classifies each Nanopore direct RNA-seq read from subcellular fractions as premature or mature by intersecting gene-assigned read alignments (BAM) with annotated introns (GTF) in R, using a minimum intronic overlap of 10 bases. This per-read labeling underpins Nanodynamo's quantification of co- vs post-transcriptional processing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Processing cytoplasmic or polysomal samples where premature calls are not interpretable — premature classifications should be removed there rather than generated Short-read RNA-seq data where single reads cannot span introns to establish >= 10 base intronic overlap Input is already a gene-level count matrix without per-read alignment information

skills.description: Use when building k-mer count feature vectors for long-read overlap detection where frequent/repetitive k-mers would dominate similarity search, and you need cheap TF-IDF-style weighting at genome scale.
skills.name: inverse-collection-frequency-kmer-weighting
skills.search_text: inverse-collection-frequency-kmer-weighting Use when building k-mer count feature vectors for long-read overlap detection where frequent/repetitive k-mers would dominate similarity search, and you need cheap TF-IDF-style weighting at genome scale. The feature representation is not k-mer count based (e.g. minimizer or alignment-based overlap detection), where IDF-style k-mer weighting does not apply Document-frequency values are cheap to compute exactly and a strict IDF formulation is required; ICF is only an approximation of DF-based IDF Memory is severely constrained — the article notes Fedrann's memory consumption is higher than most existing overlap detection tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Down-weights repetitive k-mers and up-weights informative ones before low-dimensional projection in long-read overlap detection, using total collection frequency (CF) as a computationally efficient approximation of inverse document frequency (IDF), as implemented in Fedrann. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Down-weights repetitive k-mers and up-weights informative ones before low-dimensional projection in long-read overlap detection, using total collection frequency (CF) as a computationally efficient approximation of inverse document frequency (IDF), as implemented in Fedrann.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature representation is not k-mer count based (e.g. minimizer or alignment-based overlap detection), where IDF-style k-mer weighting does not apply Document-frequency values are cheap to compute exactly and a strict IDF formulation is required; ICF is only an approximation of DF-based IDF Memory is severely constrained — the article notes Fedrann's memory consumption is higher than most existing overlap detection tools

skills.description: Use when a non-negative mutation count matrix (SBS/DBS/ID from a VCF or MAF file) must be deconvolved against a FIXED reference signature profile to get per-sample contributions, and per-gene or per-mutation-group contribution differences are the endpoint.
skills.name: inverse-nmf-deconvolution
skills.search_text: inverse-nmf-deconvolution Use when a non-negative mutation count matrix (SBS/DBS/ID from a VCF or MAF file) must be deconvolved against a FIXED reference signature profile to get per-sample contributions, and per-gene or per-mutation-group contribution differences are the endpoint. When signatures must be discovered de novo rather than tested against a fixed reference profile — use RNMF's denovoNMF 5-step framework instead When the goal is whole-cohort signature number selection (K) with silhouette coefficient and error gradient rather than testing a known signature's association with gene mutation status Estimate the sample contribution matrix S for a fixed, user-defined mutational signature matrix P (e.g. COSMIC v3.2 SBS1* age signature) using the InverseNMF routine of the RNMF R package, then test whether gene mutation status (e.g. TP53 R342*) shifts per-sample signature contribution. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Estimate the sample contribution matrix S for a fixed, user-defined mutational signature matrix P (e.g. COSMIC v3.2 SBS1* age signature) using the InverseNMF routine of the RNMF R package, then test whether gene mutation status (e.g. TP53 R342*) shifts per-sample signature contribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When signatures must be discovered de novo rather than tested against a fixed reference profile — use RNMF's denovoNMF 5-step framework instead When the goal is whole-cohort signature number selection (K) with silhouette coefficient and error gradient rather than testing a known signature's association with gene mutation status

skills.description: Use when mapping long noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads to a reference genome and inversion structural variants must be detected and reported as candidate SV calls in SAM format.
skills.name: inversion-anchor-transformation
skills.search_text: inversion-anchor-transformation Use when mapping long noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads to a reference genome and inversion structural variants must be detected and reported as candidate SV calls in SAM format. Reads are short rather than long noisy reads — short reads less frequently span the breakpoints of structural variations, which is the regime invMap targets The machine has less than 16G of RAM when mapping sequence datasets to large reference genomes The analysis goal is generic read alignment with no interest in inversion structural variants http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Reconstructs the invMap four-step long-read mapping pipeline (minimizer indexing, chaining-based aligned-region location, nonlinear-to-linear anchor transformation for inversion detection, gap-filling with KSW2) to detect inversion structural variants in long noisy PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726

skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are short rather than long noisy reads — short reads less frequently span the breakpoints of structural variations, which is the regime invMap targets The machine has less than 16G of RAM when mapping sequence datasets to large reference genomes The analysis goal is generic read alignment with no interest in inversion structural variants

skills.description: Use when comparing inversion-detection performance of competing long-read mappers (invMap, Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, lra) on simulated benchmark genomes with known ground-truth inversions, or when compiling per-mapper SV call statistics like sensitivity and precision.
skills.name: inversion-detection-evaluation
skills.search_text: inversion-detection-evaluation Use when comparing inversion-detection performance of competing long-read mappers (invMap, Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, lra) on simulated benchmark genomes with known ground-truth inversions, or when compiling per-mapper SV call statistics like sensitivity and precision. Input is a real human sequencing dataset (e.g. NA12878) rather than a simulated benchmark with SURVIVOR-derived ground truth — no reliable sensitivity/precision can be computed in that setting. The mapper alignments have not yet been produced (no SAM/BAM from the mapping benchmark step); the SV-calling step depends on per-mapper alignment files. Evaluating variant types other than inversion SVs, since this workflow is scoped to inversion structural variant calling and recovery sensitivity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Evaluates long-read mapper pipelines for inversion structural variant (SV) detection by running SVision on each mapper's SAM/BAM alignments and matching calls against a SURVIVOR-derived simulated ground truth, as in the invMap Table 2 benchmark where invMap-SVision achieved 125 total calls with 82 correct and a 2.5%-15.49% sensitivity improvement. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Evaluates long-read mapper pipelines for inversion structural variant (SV) detection by running SVision on each mapper's SAM/BAM alignments and matching calls against a SURVIVOR-derived simulated ground truth, as in the invMap Table 2 benchmark where invMap-SVision achieved 125 total calls with 82 correct and a 2.5%-15.49% sensitivity improvement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a real human sequencing dataset (e.g. NA12878) rather than a simulated benchmark with SURVIVOR-derived ground truth — no reliable sensitivity/precision can be computed in that setting. The mapper alignments have not yet been produced (no SAM/BAM from the mapping benchmark step); the SV-calling step depends on per-mapper alignment files. Evaluating variant types other than inversion SVs, since this workflow is scoped to inversion structural variant calling and recovery sensitivity.

skills.description: Use when mapping PacBio or ONT long reads to a reference genome where inversion structural variants are expected or are the target of detection, or when benchmarking mapper accuracy on SURVIVOR-implanted inversion truth sets.
skills.name: inversion-sensitive-read-mapping
skills.search_text: inversion-sensitive-read-mapping Use when mapping PacBio or ONT long reads to a reference genome where inversion structural variants are expected or are the target of detection, or when benchmarking mapper accuracy on SURVIVOR-implanted inversion truth sets. Reads are short (Illumina-style): invMap targets long noisy PacBio/ONT reads that can span inversion breakpoints The analysis goal is small variant or SNV calling rather than inversion/structural-variant detection The machine lacks the minimum 16G of RAM required for mapping to large reference genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Map long noisy reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) to a reference genome with invMap, a mapper specifically designed to chain anchors and detect inversion structural variants, then call SVs and benchmark accuracy against minimap2, NGMLR, Winnowmap2, and lra. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Map long noisy reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) to a reference genome with invMap, a mapper specifically designed to chain anchors and detect inversion structural variants, then call SVs and benchmark accuracy against minimap2, NGMLR, Winnowmap2, and lra.

skills.description: Use when a long-read mapping study yields inversion SV call sets from multiple mappers and you need to identify calls unique to invMap, distinguishing ground-truth-matching from non-ground-truth novel calls.
skills.name: inversion-variant-call-comparison-across-mappers
skills.search_text: inversion-variant-call-comparison-across-mappers Use when a long-read mapping study yields inversion SV call sets from multiple mappers and you need to identify calls unique to invMap, distinguishing ground-truth-matching from non-ground-truth novel calls. Input consists only of single-mapper SV calls with no competing call sets, so no cross-mapper uniqueness comparison is possible The variants of interest are deletions, duplications, or translocations rather than inversions, which invMap's remaining-anchor check is designed to discover The dataset is short-read sequencing, since invMap targets long noisy reads from PacBio or Oxford Nanopore sequencers http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Compare inversion SV calls from invMap against competing long-read mappers (Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, lra) on the NA12878 real human genome sequencing dataset to isolate invMap-only inversion calls, such as a novel 231 bp inversion absent from the simulated ground truth. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Compare inversion SV calls from invMap against competing long-read mappers (Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, lra) on the NA12878 real human genome sequencing dataset to isolate invMap-only inversion calls, such as a novel 231 bp inversion absent from the simulated ground truth.

skills.description: Use when long noisy reads (PacBio CLR or Oxford Nanopore) must be mapped to a reference and inversion SVs called, or when benchmarking invMap sensitivity/precision against Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, and lra.

skills.search_text: inversion-variant-calling-from-alignments Use when long noisy reads (PacBio CLR or Oxford Nanopore) must be mapped to a reference and inversion SVs called, or when benchmarking invMap sensitivity/precision against Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, and lra.
