Available RAM is below the ~16G minimum required for mapping sequence datasets to large reference genomes.

skills.description: Use when long erroneous 3GS reads must be compressed against DBG contigs and overlapping read pairs identified without all-vs-all base-level alignment, e.g. 10x-100x PacBio data with SparseAssembler contigs.
skills.name: inverted-index-contig-to-read-mapping
skills.search_text: inverted-index-contig-to-read-mapping Use when long erroneous 3GS reads must be compressed against DBG contigs and overlapping read pairs identified without all-vs-all base-level alignment, e.g. 10x-100x PacBio data with SparseAssembler contigs. The long reads have not been compressed against DBG contigs, so no contig identifiers exist to index Coverage is below ~10x, where RemoveChimera is not suggested and read anchors are unreliable Short-read contigs come from repeat-resolved assemblies (gap closing/scaffolding), which the README warns introduce heuristics errors into the final assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 DBG2OLC's overlap-and-layout accelerator: an inverted index maps each short-read contig identifier to the long reads whose compressed representation contains it, so candidate overlapping read pairs are selected by shared contig identifiers before Smith-Waterman alignment of compressed identifier sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: DBG2OLC's overlap-and-layout accelerator: an inverted index maps each short-read contig identifier to the long reads whose compressed representation contains it, so candidate overlapping read pairs are selected by shared contig identifiers before Smith-Waterman alignment of compressed identifier sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long reads have not been compressed against DBG contigs, so no contig identifiers exist to index Coverage is below ~10x, where RemoveChimera is not suggested and read anchors are unreliable Short-read contigs come from repeat-resolved assemblies (gap closing/scaffolding), which the README warns introduce heuristics errors into the final assembly

skills.description: Use when mapping simulated or real long noisy reads (PacBio CCS/CLR, Oxford Nanopore) to a reference genome FASTA and SAM-format alignments are needed as input for downstream accuracy or variant-calling comparisons.
skills.name: invocation-and-execution-of-long-read-aligners
skills.search_text: invocation-and-execution-of-long-read-aligners Use when mapping simulated or real long noisy reads (PacBio CCS/CLR, Oxford Nanopore) to a reference genome FASTA and SAM-format alignments are needed as input for downstream accuracy or variant-calling comparisons. Input reads are short Illumina reads — the compared aligners and their long-read presets are designed for long noisy PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads The goal is de novo assembly or read clustering rather than mapping reads to a reference genome The reference genome is not available as FASTA and only pre-aligned BAM/CRAM data exists http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compile and run long-read alignment tools (invMap, minimap2, Winnowmap2, lra, NGMLR) with their long-read presets to map simulated PacBio CCS/CLR and ONT reads back to reference genomes, producing SAM alignments used for location-accuracy benchmarking. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Compile and run long-read alignment tools (invMap, minimap2, Winnowmap2, lra, NGMLR) with their long-read presets to map simulated PacBio CCS/CLR and ONT reads back to reference genomes, producing SAM alignments used for location-accuracy benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads — the compared aligners and their long-read presets are designed for long noisy PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads The goal is de novo assembly or read clustering rather than mapping reads to a reference genome The reference genome is not available as FASTA and only pre-aligned BAM/CRAM data exists

skills.description: Use when you have FLNC CCS reads (FASTQ/FASTA) from targeted Iso-Seq sequencing of highly similar multigene family copies and need nucleotide-level-precision end-to-end transcripts de novo, without a reference genome.
skills.name: iso-seq-flnc-read-processing
skills.search_text: iso-seq-flnc-read-processing Use when you have FLNC CCS reads (FASTQ/FASTA) from targeted Iso-Seq sequencing of highly similar multigene family copies and need nucleotide-level-precision end-to-end transcripts de novo, without a reference genome. Input reads are unprocessed PacBio subreads that still contain primers, barcodes, or chimeras — IsoCon assumes Iso-Seq pre-processing has already been done You need to distinguish alleles of distinct gene copies or conclusively assign transcripts to individual gene copies — downstream analysis beyond IsoCon is required and transcriptome-only data cannot answer gene family size Short-read (Illumina) data alone is the input — Illumina-based correction (e.g. proovread) is unable to correct most errors in this setting; long reads spanning the region end-to-end are required http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs finished transcript sequences from FLNC (full-length non-chimeric) PacBio Iso-Seq reads using IsoCon, a de novo error-correction and redundancy-removal algorithm for highly similar gene copies, with quality-aware statistical filtering of candidate transcripts. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Reconstructs finished transcript sequences from FLNC (full-length non-chimeric) PacBio Iso-Seq reads using IsoCon, a de novo error-correction and redundancy-removal algorithm for highly similar gene copies, with quality-aware statistical filtering of candidate transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are unprocessed PacBio subreads that still contain primers, barcodes, or chimeras — IsoCon assumes Iso-Seq pre-processing has already been done You need to distinguish alleles of distinct gene copies or conclusively assign transcripts to individual gene copies — downstream analysis beyond IsoCon is required and transcriptome-only data cannot answer gene family size Short-read (Illumina) data alone is the input — Illumina-based correction (e.g. proovread) is unable to correct most errors in this setting; long reads spanning the region end-to-end are required

skills.description: Use when a gene-fusion detection pipeline for PacBio Iso-seq data needs a controlled benchmark with known fusion truth, or when comparing long-read fusion callers (e.g., TAGET vs SQANTI vs JAFFAL) on simulated datasets.
skills.name: iso-seq-fusion-dataset-simulation
skills.search_text: iso-seq-fusion-dataset-simulation Use when a gene-fusion detection pipeline for PacBio Iso-seq data needs a controlled benchmark with known fusion truth, or when comparing long-read fusion callers (e.g., TAGET vs SQANTI vs JAFFAL) on simulated datasets. The goal is detecting fusions in real tumor Iso-seq data rather than benchmarking caller performance on known ground truth Input data is short-read RNA-seq; the simulation and callers here target full-length PacBio Iso-seq (CCS) transcripts A published benchmark fusion dataset with experimental validation already exists for the comparison at hand http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Simulates full-length Iso-seq transcript datasets with known gene-fusion ground truth to benchmark long-read fusion callers such as TAGET against SQANTI and JAFFAL. Grounding fusions in a GM12878 transcript background (CCLE fusions removed) enables direct scoring of sensitivity, specificity, and F-score per caller. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Simulates full-length Iso-seq transcript datasets with known gene-fusion ground truth to benchmark long-read fusion callers such as TAGET against SQANTI and JAFFAL. Grounding fusions in a GM12878 transcript background (CCLE fusions removed) enables direct scoring of sensitivity, specificity, and F-score per caller.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting fusions in real tumor Iso-seq data rather than benchmarking caller performance on known ground truth Input data is short-read RNA-seq; the simulation and callers here target full-length PacBio Iso-seq (CCS) transcripts A published benchmark fusion dataset with experimental validation already exists for the comparison at hand

skills.description: Use when input is a full-length transcript FASTA from PacBio Iso-seq (CCS reads) and accurate splice-junction detection and transcript annotation against a reference genome such as hg38 is needed.
skills.name: iso-seq-long-read-alignment
skills.search_text: iso-seq-long-read-alignment Use when input is a full-length transcript FASTA from PacBio Iso-seq (CCS reads) and accurate splice-junction detection and transcript annotation against a reference genome such as hg38 is needed. Input data is short-read RNA-seq rather than full-length Iso-seq transcripts; TAGET is designed for Iso-seq data from alignment to downstream quantification. Only a high-level gene/transcript expression matrix is needed and no junction-level annotation is required — TransAnnotMerge or RNA-seq-based quantification may be more appropriate. The reference annotation and genome for the target organism are unavailable, since both HISAT2 and minimap2 need the indexed reference genome and a GTF annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align PacBio Iso-seq full-length transcript FASTA reads to a reference genome (e.g., hg38) using TAGET's TransAnnot with minimap2 and/or HISAT2, producing annotated junctions, transcript classifications, and bed/stat outputs. This is the foundational alignment-and-annotation step of the TAGET toolkit for accurate splice-junction recovery. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Align PacBio Iso-seq full-length transcript FASTA reads to a reference genome (e.g., hg38) using TAGET's TransAnnot with minimap2 and/or HISAT2, producing annotated junctions, transcript classifications, and bed/stat outputs. This is the foundational alignment-and-annotation step of the TAGET toolkit for accurate splice-junction recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is short-read RNA-seq rather than full-length Iso-seq transcripts; TAGET is designed for Iso-seq data from alignment to downstream quantification. Only a high-level gene/transcript expression matrix is needed and no junction-level annotation is required — TransAnnotMerge or RNA-seq-based quantification may be more appropriate. The reference annotation and genome for the target organism are unavailable, since both HISAT2 and minimap2 need the indexed reference genome and a GTF annotation.

skills.description: Use when input is a set of pre-processed FLNC PacBio Iso-Seq reads (FASTA/FASTQ with quality values) from targeted RT-PCR sequencing of a gene family with highly similar paralogs, and you need de novo transcript reconstruction and isoform counts without a reference genome.
skills.name: iso-seq-long-read-error-correction
skills.search_text: iso-seq-long-read-error-correction Use when input is a set of pre-processed FLNC PacBio Iso-Seq reads (FASTA/FASTQ with quality values) from targeted RT-PCR sequencing of a gene family with highly similar paralogs, and you need de novo transcript reconstruction and isoform counts without a reference genome. Reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline (primers, barcodes, and chimeras still present) — IsoCon assumes pre-processed FLNC input Sequences do not span the region of interest end-to-end; IsoCon requires reads covering the full transcript/amplicon (unsuited to fragments or reference-guided whole-transcriptome assembly) The goal is to distinguish alleles from distinct gene copies — IsoCon provides no such functionality and downstream analysis is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 De novo error correction and redundancy removal of full-length PacBio CCS (Iso-Seq) reads from targeted sequencing of highly similar multigene families, using IsoCon's iterative clustering plus statistical filtering to recover nucleotide-level transcript isoforms without a reference genome. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: De novo error correction and redundancy removal of full-length PacBio CCS (Iso-Seq) reads from targeted sequencing of highly similar multigene families, using IsoCon's iterative clustering plus statistical filtering to recover nucleotide-level transcript isoforms without a reference genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline (primers, barcodes, and chimeras still present) — IsoCon assumes pre-processed FLNC input Sequences do not span the region of interest end-to-end; IsoCon requires reads covering the full transcript/amplicon (unsuited to fragments or reference-guided whole-transcriptome assembly) The goal is to distinguish alleles from distinct gene copies — IsoCon provides no such functionality and downstream analysis is required

skills.description: Use when comparing transcript-reconstruction tools on targeted Iso-Seq data and you need quantitative accuracy: simulated precision/recall vs ground-truth isoforms, or fraction of predicted positions supported by >=2 agreeing Illumina reads.
skills.name: isoform-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: isoform-accuracy-benchmarking Use when comparing transcript-reconstruction tools on targeted Iso-Seq data and you need quantitative accuracy: simulated precision/recall vs ground-truth isoforms, or fraction of predicted positions supported by >=2 agreeing Illumina reads. Input transcripts already have reference-genome-based validation; the article's methods are de novo and assume no reference Reads are short Illumina-only contigs rather than end-to-end Iso-Seq/CCS reads spanning the region of interest (IsoCon's stated assumption) You need to assign transcripts to specific gene copies or distinguish alleles — the article states transcriptome-only sequencing does not conclusively answer gene-family size or copy assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark de novo transcript reconstruction methods (IsoCon vs ICE vs Illumina-corrected/original CCS) by scoring nucleotide-level precision and recall against simulated ground truth, or by measuring Illumina-read support of predicted positions in experimental data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Benchmark de novo transcript reconstruction methods (IsoCon vs ICE vs Illumina-corrected/original CCS) by scoring nucleotide-level precision and recall against simulated ground truth, or by measuring Illumina-read support of predicted positions in experimental data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transcripts already have reference-genome-based validation; the article's methods are de novo and assume no reference Reads are short Illumina-only contigs rather than end-to-end Iso-Seq/CCS reads spanning the region of interest (IsoCon's stated assumption) You need to assign transcripts to specific gene copies or distinguish alleles — the article states transcriptome-only sequencing does not conclusively answer gene-family size or copy assignment

skills.description: Use when a raw PacBio Iso-Seq isoform annotation (transcript FASTA, abundance table, GFF, ORF FASTA) must be reduced to full-length, high-confidence isoforms via exon-count, truncation, and abundance filters.
skills.name: isoform-catalog-filtering
skills.search_text: isoform-catalog-filtering Use when a raw PacBio Iso-Seq isoform annotation (transcript FASTA, abundance table, GFF, ORF FASTA) must be reduced to full-length, high-confidence isoforms via exon-count, truncation, and abundance filters. The catalog is already filtered (e.g. it is the 4116-isoform fullfilter.gff); re-running the abundance cutoff would remove valid low-rank isoforms The data are short-read RNA-seq assemblies, not full-length PacBio isoform annotations — IsoPops filtering assumes full-length transcript structures with GFF exon boundaries The goal is quantifying CAGE/short-read support for existing TSSs rather than curating the isoform catalog itself (use read-coverage validation instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Curates a raw PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoform database into a high-confidence catalog using the IsoPops three-step filtering rules (minimum exon count, truncation removal, top-abundance cutoff), yielding the paper's final catalog of 4116 isoforms across 30 neural cell-surface genes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Curates a raw PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoform database into a high-confidence catalog using the IsoPops three-step filtering rules (minimum exon count, truncation removal, top-abundance cutoff), yielding the paper's final catalog of 4116 isoforms across 30 neural cell-surface genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The catalog is already filtered (e.g. it is the 4116-isoform fullfilter.gff); re-running the abundance cutoff would remove valid low-rank isoforms The data are short-read RNA-seq assemblies, not full-length PacBio isoform annotations — IsoPops filtering assumes full-length transcript structures with GFF exon boundaries The goal is quantifying CAGE/short-read support for existing TSSs rather than curating the isoform catalog itself (use read-coverage validation instead)

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered single-cell isoform-level expression matrix and need noise-robust isoform-to-isoform co-expression estimates grouped into co-usage modules across cell types, prior to DIU/coDIU analysis.
skills.name: isoform-co-expression-clustering
skills.search_text: isoform-co-expression-clustering Use when you have a filtered single-cell isoform-level expression matrix and need noise-robust isoform-to-isoform co-expression estimates grouped into co-usage modules across cell types, prior to DIU/coDIU analysis. Input is gene-level (not isoform-level) count data — the pipeline requires an isoform-level quantification matrix The goal is bulk-sample isoform co-expression without cell-type structure — percentile correlations are designed for sparse single-cell data summarized per cell type Only two conditions/groups with no multiple cell types — DIU/coDIU analyses are designed to leverage multiple cell types in single-cell data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Semi-automated clustering of isoform co-expression relationships from sparse single-cell data, using acorde's percentile correlations followed by dynamicTreeCut initialization, correlation-based filtering, metatranscript-based cluster merging, and recursive assignment of unclustered isoforms. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Semi-automated clustering of isoform co-expression relationships from sparse single-cell data, using acorde's percentile correlations followed by dynamicTreeCut initialization, correlation-based filtering, metatranscript-based cluster merging, and recursive assignment of unclustered isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is gene-level (not isoform-level) count data — the pipeline requires an isoform-level quantification matrix The goal is bulk-sample isoform co-expression without cell-type structure — percentile correlations are designed for sparse single-cell data summarized per cell type Only two conditions/groups with no multiple cell types — DIU/coDIU analyses are designed to leverage multiple cell types in single-cell data

skills.description: Decision support for choosing an isoform collapsing/merging tool when 5'/3' end variability across samples matters — e.g. simulated or real truncated isoforms sharing the same intron chain must be collapsed and you must know if start/end coordinates survive.
skills.name: isoform-collapse-behavior-benchmarking
skills.search_text: isoform-collapse-behavior-benchmarking Decision support for choosing an isoform collapsing/merging tool when 5'/3' end variability across samples matters — e.g. simulated or real truncated isoforms sharing the same intron chain must be collapsed and you must know if start/end coordinates survive. Input transcripts have distinct intron chains — the benchmark specifically probes collapsing of variants that share the same intron chain, so differing splice junctions test a different property. The goal is cross-sample isoform ID matching over existing SQANTI3 output (PB.X.Y IDs) — use isoSeQL for that instead of re-running collapse benchmarks. You need to collapse raw FLNC read clusters (isoseq cluster2) rather than compare how pre-built transcript models with variable ends are merged. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A controlled benchmarking skill that probes how different long-read isoform collapsing tools (isoseq collapse vs. gffcompare) treat synthetic transcript variants that share an intron chain but differ in start/end coordinates, revealing whether transcript-end variability is retained or discarded during collapsing. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: A controlled benchmarking skill that probes how different long-read isoform collapsing tools (isoseq collapse vs. gffcompare) treat synthetic transcript variants that share an intron chain but differ in start/end coordinates, revealing whether transcript-end variability is retained or discarded during collapsing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transcripts have distinct intron chains — the benchmark specifically probes collapsing of variants that share the same intron chain, so differing splice junctions test a different property. The goal is cross-sample isoform ID matching over existing SQANTI3 output (PB.X.Y IDs) — use isoSeQL for that instead of re-running collapse benchmarks. You need to collapse raw FLNC read clusters (isoseq cluster2) rather than compare how pre-built transcript models with variable ends are merged.

skills.description: Use when you have splice-aligned FLNC reads (SAM from minimimap2) in a long-read isoform sequencing workflow and need a nonredundant isoform set (GTF, representative FASTA, group file) for downstream QC.
skills.name: isoform-collapsing-long-read-rna
skills.search_text: isoform-collapsing-long-read-rna Use when you have splice-aligned FLNC reads (SAM from minimimap2) in a long-read isoform sequencing workflow and need a nonredundant isoform set (GTF, representative FASTA, group file) for downstream QC. Input reads have not yet been splice-aligned to a reference genome — the script consumes a coordinate-sorted SAM, not raw CCS or FLNC fastq alone You are starting from already-collapsed or reference-annotated isoforms (e.g., an Ensembl GTF) rather than per-read alignments needing redundancy removal Your pipeline can use the official isoseq3 collapse tool instead — the cDNA_Cupcake README states isoseq3 collapse is now the preferred tool and Cupcake will remove redundant scripts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Collapse mapped full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) alignments from the HIT-scISOseq pipeline into nonredundant isoform transcripts using cDNA_Cupcake's collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py, merging reads with matching splice junctions under default coverage/identity criteria. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Collapse mapped full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) alignments from the HIT-scISOseq pipeline into nonredundant isoform transcripts using cDNA_Cupcake's collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py, merging reads with matching splice junctions under default coverage/identity criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been splice-aligned to a reference genome — the script consumes a coordinate-sorted SAM, not raw CCS or FLNC fastq alone You are starting from already-collapsed or reference-annotated isoforms (e.g., an Ensembl GTF) rather than per-read alignments needing redundancy removal Your pipeline can use the official isoseq3 collapse tool instead — the cDNA_Cupcake README states isoseq3 collapse is now the preferred tool and Cupcake will remove redundant scripts

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating IsoCon sensitivity curves on simulated PacBio Iso-Seq read sets (e.g., Supplementary Fig. 1) to determine capture depth thresholds per isoform or gene family.
skills.name: isoform-depth-threshold-verification
skills.search_text: isoform-depth-threshold-verification Use when reproducing or validating IsoCon sensitivity curves on simulated PacBio Iso-Seq read sets (e.g., Supplementary Fig. 1) to determine capture depth thresholds per isoform or gene family. When reads are not pre-processed with the Iso-Seq bioinformatic pipeline to remove primers, barcodes, and chimeras — IsoCon assumes this pre-processing When the goal is per-base accuracy benchmarking against ICE on real (not simulated) data rather than isoform capture-depth thresholding When a ground-truth isoform list and per-isoform read counts are unavailable, since fate classification requires mapping output candidates back to simulated isoforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Verifies the minimum per-isoform sequencing depth at which IsoCon recovers simulated transcripts from highly similar multigene families (e.g., TSPY, HSFY), by classifying each isoform as captured, filtered in the statistical step, or lost during error correction. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Verifies the minimum per-isoform sequencing depth at which IsoCon recovers simulated transcripts from highly similar multigene families (e.g., TSPY, HSFY), by classifying each isoform as captured, filtered in the statistical step, or lost during error correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are not pre-processed with the Iso-Seq bioinformatic pipeline to remove primers, barcodes, and chimeras — IsoCon assumes this pre-processing When the goal is per-base accuracy benchmarking against ICE on real (not simulated) data rather than isoform capture-depth thresholding When a ground-truth isoform list and per-isoform read counts are unavailable, since fate classification requires mapping output candidates back to simulated isoforms

skills.description: Use when a genome-guided transcriptome assembly (StringTie GTF from merged PacBio+Illumina BAMs) must be characterized per-isoform at a specific locus by parsing exon features and counting exons per transcript ID.
skills.name: isoform-exon-structure-counting
skills.search_text: isoform-exon-structure-counting Use when a genome-guided transcriptome assembly (StringTie GTF from merged PacBio+Illumina BAMs) must be characterized per-isoform at a specific locus by parsing exon features and counting exons per transcript ID. Input is raw reads or an unannotated StringTie GTF without coding/noncoding reconciliation — run annotate-my-genomes.nf first to obtain final_annotated.gtf The organism lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI GTF annotation, since the pipeline requires both as inputs The goal is de novo isoform discovery without a reference genome; this skill is genome-guided only http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Count exon features per transcript from an annotated GTF (e.g. StringTie assembly reconciled by annotate_my_genomes) to characterize isoform structures of a target gene locus, such as the >105-exon chicken SSPO gene, and validate them against expected exon counts, protein lengths, and BLAST identity. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Count exon features per transcript from an annotated GTF (e.g. StringTie assembly reconciled by annotate_my_genomes) to characterize isoform structures of a target gene locus, such as the >105-exon chicken SSPO gene, and validate them against expected exon counts, protein lengths, and BLAST identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or an unannotated StringTie GTF without coding/noncoding reconciliation — run annotate-my-genomes.nf first to obtain final_annotated.gtf The organism lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI GTF annotation, since the pipeline requires both as inputs The goal is de novo isoform discovery without a reference genome; this skill is genome-guided only

skills.description: Use when a long-read isoform catalog (e.g., PacBio/IsoPops DB .rds) must be benchmarked against public annotations (RefSeq, UCSC Genes GTF) by intron-chain matching to measure database recovery fractions.
skills.name: isoform-splice-junction-comparison
skills.search_text: isoform-splice-junction-comparison Use when a long-read isoform catalog (e.g., PacBio/IsoPops DB .rds) must be benchmarked against public annotations (RefSeq, UCSC Genes GTF) by intron-chain matching to measure database recovery fractions. The isoform catalog has not been filtered (exon count, abundance, truncation) — unfiltered catalogs contain truncated/off-target transcripts that inflate mismatch counts The goal is novel-isoform detection rather than recovery of annotated isoforms — splice-junction database matching only labels full-splice-match status against known annotations Input is short-read RNA-seq without full-length isoform sequences — intron chains of multi-kilobase transcripts cannot be resolved from <200 bp reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Classifies a PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoform catalog against RefSeq and UCSC Genes mm10 annotations by comparing intron chains (donor/acceptor splice junctions) under SQANTI full-splice-match criteria, quantifying the fraction of each database's annotated isoforms recovered by the PacBio catalog (53.9% RefSeq, 72.3% UCSC Genes). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Classifies a PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoform catalog against RefSeq and UCSC Genes mm10 annotations by comparing intron chains (donor/acceptor splice junctions) under SQANTI full-splice-match criteria, quantifying the fraction of each database's annotated isoforms recovered by the PacBio catalog (53.9% RefSeq, 72.3% UCSC Genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The isoform catalog has not been filtered (exon count, abundance, truncation) — unfiltered catalogs contain truncated/off-target transcripts that inflate mismatch counts The goal is novel-isoform detection rather than recovery of annotated isoforms — splice-junction database matching only labels full-splice-match status against known annotations Input is short-read RNA-seq without full-length isoform sequences — intron chains of multi-kilobase transcripts cannot be resolved from <200 bp reads

skills.description: Use when you have a collapsed representative isoform FASTA (e.g., all.collapsed.rep.fa from cDNA_Cupcake's collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py) and need SQANTI3 structural-category assignments and per-sample retained-isoform counts.
skills.name: isoform-structural-classification
skills.search_text: isoform-structural-classification Use when you have a collapsed representative isoform FASTA (e.g., all.collapsed.rep.fa from cDNA_Cupcake's collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py) and need SQANTI3 structural-category assignments and per-sample retained-isoform counts. Input reads have not yet been demultiplexed and collapsed (e.g., raw CCS reads or FLNC reads) — SQANTI3 QC requires a nonredundant isoform set, so scISA-Tools demultiplexing and collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py must come first The analysis goal is gene-level quantification (scGene_matrix) or single-cell isoform count matrices (scIsoform_matrix) rather than transcript structural characterization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify collapsed long-read single-cell isoforms into structural categories (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, antisense, genic, etc.) using SQANTI3 QC against a reference genome and annotation, then tally per-class isoform frequencies as an acceptance check on the HIT-scISOseq corneal limbus dataset. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Classify collapsed long-read single-cell isoforms into structural categories (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, antisense, genic, etc.) using SQANTI3 QC against a reference genome and annotation, then tally per-class isoform frequencies as an acceptance check on the HIT-scISOseq corneal limbus dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been demultiplexed and collapsed (e.g., raw CCS reads or FLNC reads) — SQANTI3 QC requires a nonredundant isoform set, so scISA-Tools demultiplexing and collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py must come first The analysis goal is gene-level quantification (scGene_matrix) or single-cell isoform count matrices (scIsoform_matrix) rather than transcript structural characterization

skills.description: Use when a transcript annotation (GTF) or collapsed long-read isoform set needs redundancy profiling — e.g. testing whether intron chains uniquely identify isoforms before matching PB.X.Y IDs across samples.
skills.name: isoform-structure-redundancy-quantification
skills.search_text: isoform-structure-redundancy-quantification Use when a transcript annotation (GTF) or collapsed long-read isoform set needs redundancy profiling — e.g. testing whether intron chains uniquely identify isoforms before matching PB.X.Y IDs across samples. When the goal is cross-sample comparison of already-annotated Iso-Seq isoforms with full metrics — use isoSeQL directly instead of reimplementing chain counting When input is raw subreads or uncollapsed alignments (pre-isoseq cluster2/collapse) — transcript structures do not exist yet When splice structure alone is insufficient (e.g. TSS/TES polyA diversity is the question, since intron chains ignore start/end position except as redundancy tallies) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how uniquely isoforms are described by their splice structure (intron chain) in a transcript reference: it parses a GTF (e.g. GENCODE v39), derives the ordered intron chain per transcript, and counts how many chains map to more than one transcript start/end combination. skills.summary: Quantifies how uniquely isoforms are described by their splice structure (intron chain) in a transcript reference: it parses a GTF (e.g. GENCODE v39), derives the ordered intron chain per transcript, and counts how many chains map to more than one transcript start/end combination. skills.search_text: kmer-abundance-based-repeat-filtering Use when you need to derive sparse, low-repetitiveness seed sequences (e.g. 270 bp or 285 bp) from merged short reads for a long-read seed-based assembler like TULIP. When seeds with repetitive sequence are acceptable and runtime is not a constraint — the paper notes repetitive seeds 'should be fine' but take much longer to untangle the graph When the goal is genome-size estimation rather than seed selection — k-mer analysis there (~860 Mbp) is used to estimate coverage, not to filter fragments When input fragments already have uniform length and unique identifiers, i.e. are already validated TULIP seeds http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Removes repetitive sequences from Illumina read fragments by counting k-mers (25-mers) with Jellyfish and discarding any fragment containing a k-mer observed more than 25 times, yielding sparse 'not too repetitive' seed fragments for the TULIP assembly of the ~860 Mbp European eel genome. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Removes repetitive sequences from Illumina read fragments by counting k-mers (25-mers) with Jellyfish and discarding any fragment containing a k-mer observed more than 25 times, yielding sparse 'not too repetitive' seed fragments for the TULIP assembly of the ~860 Mbp European eel genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When seeds with repetitive sequence are acceptable and runtime is not a constraint — the paper notes repetitive seeds 'should be fine' but take much longer to untangle the graph When the goal is genome-size estimation rather than seed selection — k-mer analysis there (~860 Mbp) is used to estimate coverage, not to filter fragments When input fragments already have uniform length and unique identifiers, i.e. are already validated TULIP seeds

skills.description: Use when assembling long erroneous 3GS reads (PacBio/ONT) against short-read contigs and you need to find overlapping long-read pairs without all-vs-all base-level alignment, e.g. tuning DBG2OLC's AdaptiveTh, KmerCovTh, MinOverlap.
skills.name: kmer-anchor-candidate-filtering
skills.search_text: kmer-anchor-candidate-filtering Use when assembling long erroneous 3GS reads (PacBio/ONT) against short-read contigs and you need to find overlapping long-read pairs without all-vs-all base-level alignment, e.g. tuning DBG2OLC's AdaptiveTh, KmerCovTh, MinOverlap. You need base-level alignment accuracy for polishing — use the BLASR/Sparc/pbdagcon consensus step instead (~90% of DBG2OLC runtime) The contigs come from a repeat-resolved/scaffolded short-read assembly — the manual warns this introduces heuristics errors and gives poor final results You are doing pure short-read de novo assembly without long reads — the k-mer anchor scoring is defined only between compressed long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstructs DBG2OLC's fast pair-wise overlap-scoring stage: long reads are compressed into contig-identifier sequences, candidate overlapping read pairs are selected via shared k-mer anchors (AdaptiveTh/KmerCovTh), then scored by Smith-Waterman alignment of the compressed identifier sequences and filtered by MinOverlap. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Reconstructs DBG2OLC's fast pair-wise overlap-scoring stage: long reads are compressed into contig-identifier sequences, candidate overlapping read pairs are selected via shared k-mer anchors (AdaptiveTh/KmerCovTh), then scored by Smith-Waterman alignment of the compressed identifier sequences and filtered by MinOverlap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need base-level alignment accuracy for polishing — use the BLASR/Sparc/pbdagcon consensus step instead (~90% of DBG2OLC runtime) The contigs come from a repeat-resolved/scaffolded short-read assembly — the manual warns this introduces heuristics errors and gives poor final results You are doing pure short-read de novo assembly without long reads — the k-mer anchor scoring is defined only between compressed long reads

skills.description: Use when you need to assess whether a polishing tool improved or degraded a HiFi/T2T assembly, by measuring QV and counting changed K-mers and potential overcorrection K-mers against short-read k-mer datasets.
skills.name: kmer-based-assembly-accuracy-quantification
skills.search_text: kmer-based-assembly-accuracy-quantification Use when you need to assess whether a polishing tool improved or degraded a HiFi/T2T assembly, by measuring QV and counting changed K-mers and potential overcorrection K-mers against short-read k-mer datasets. You only need variant-level error counts against a reference benchmark (e.g., GIAB high-confidence variants for HG005 vs GRCh37) — use DeepVariant/paftools comparison instead of k-mer ratios The assembly is not from HiFi long reads and lacks matching high-coverage short reads, since NextPolish2's k-mer checking 'relies heavily on short reads' and yak datasets require >=60X short-read coverage You are evaluating structural/haplotype switch errors rather than base-level consensus accuracy — the article notes switch errors are assessed separately via the built-in phasing evaluation, not via k-mer overcorrection counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies HiFi assembly consensus accuracy (QV) and polishing-induced overcorrection by comparing k-mers of unpolished and polished assemblies against a short-read k-mer ground truth built with yak and counted with meryl. Used in the NextPolish2 benchmark to show RM introduces ~5.31–547.64x more changed K-mers than NextPolish2 on human assemblies without QV gains. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Quantifies HiFi assembly consensus accuracy (QV) and polishing-induced overcorrection by comparing k-mers of unpolished and polished assemblies against a short-read k-mer ground truth built with yak and counted with meryl. Used in the NextPolish2 benchmark to show RM introduces ~5.31–547.64x more changed K-mers than NextPolish2 on human assemblies without QV gains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need variant-level error counts against a reference benchmark (e.g., GIAB high-confidence variants for HG005 vs GRCh37) — use DeepVariant/paftools comparison instead of k-mer ratios The assembly is not from HiFi long reads and lacks matching high-coverage short reads, since NextPolish2's k-mer checking 'relies heavily on short reads' and yak datasets require >=60X short-read coverage You are evaluating structural/haplotype switch errors rather than base-level consensus accuracy — the article notes switch errors are assessed separately via the built-in phasing evaluation, not via k-mer overcorrection counts

skills.description: Use when comparing hybrid error-correction outputs (e.g., HECIL, LSC, PacBioToCA, LoRDEC, proovread, CoLoRMap) on PacBio long reads and you need a k-mer-based quality metric or a stopping rule for iterative correction.
skills.name: kmer-based-correction-evaluation
skills.search_text: kmer-based-correction-evaluation Use when comparing hybrid error-correction outputs (e.g., HECIL, LSC, PacBioToCA, LoRDEC, proovread, CoLoRMap) on PacBio long reads and you need a k-mer-based quality metric or a stopping rule for iterative correction. When the primary evaluation target is assembly-based quality (N50, dnadiff accuracy) rather than per-read correction — QUAST/MUMmer on Canu assemblies is the appropriate path When the input is uncorrected reads alone with no correction to evaluate — the metric requires a corrected read set to be meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluate long-read error correction quality by counting unique k-mers of corrected reads with Jellyfish, using the number of unique k-mers as a proxy metric and as the relative-improvement termination signal in HECIL's iterative learning loop. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Evaluate long-read error correction quality by counting unique k-mers of corrected reads with Jellyfish, using the number of unique k-mers as a proxy metric and as the relative-improvement termination signal in HECIL's iterative learning loop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the primary evaluation target is assembly-based quality (N50, dnadiff accuracy) rather than per-read correction — QUAST/MUMmer on Canu assemblies is the appropriate path When the input is uncorrected reads alone with no correction to evaluate — the metric requires a corrected read set to be meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have an assembled transcriptome (FASTA) and raw WGS reads or a prebuilt abyss-bloom filter (e.g. genome_k25_m100M_l1.bloom, k=25) and need exons, IEBs and a splice graph in GFA1 without a reference genome.
skills.name: kmer-based-intron-exon-boundary-detection
skills.search_text: kmer-based-intron-exon-boundary-detection Use when you have an assembled transcriptome (FASTA) and raw WGS reads or a prebuilt abyss-bloom filter (e.g. genome_k25_m100M_l1.bloom, k=25) and need exons, IEBs and a splice graph in GFA1 without a reference genome. A reference genome and annotation exist and a splice-aware aligner (e.g. GMAP) can align transcripts directly to extract IEB coordinates The input is raw RNA-Seq reads rather than an assembled transcriptome — EXFI consumes a transcriptome assembly plus raw WGS reads The WGS k-mer set is unavailable and cannot be built, since IEB detection relies entirely on transcript k-mers missing from the genomic k-mer set http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 K-mer-based detection of potential intron–exon boundaries (IEBs) and exon construction from a de novo transcriptome assembly against a Bloom filter of whole-genome sequencing k-mers, as implemented in EXFI's build_splice_graph. Because Bloom filters return no false negatives, transcript k-mers absent from the genomic k-mer set flag where an exon ends and the next starts, without a reference genome. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: K-mer-based detection of potential intron–exon boundaries (IEBs) and exon construction from a de novo transcriptome assembly against a Bloom filter of whole-genome sequencing k-mers, as implemented in EXFI's build_splice_graph. Because Bloom filters return no false negatives, transcript k-mers absent from the genomic k-mer set flag where an exon ends and the next starts, without a reference genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome and annotation exist and a splice-aware aligner (e.g. GMAP) can align transcripts directly to extract IEB coordinates The input is raw RNA-Seq reads rather than an assembled transcriptome — EXFI consumes a transcriptome assembly plus raw WGS reads The WGS k-mer set is unavailable and cannot be built, since IEB detection relies entirely on transcript k-mers missing from the genomic k-mer set

skills.description: Use when running HECIL's iterative learning component on long-read/short-read hybrid correction and you need a data-driven stopping criterion and per-iteration quality metric based on unique k-mer counts.
skills.name: kmer-based-iteration-termination-evaluation
skills.search_text: kmer-based-iteration-termination-evaluation Use when running HECIL's iterative learning component on long-read/short-read hybrid correction and you need a data-driven stopping criterion and per-iteration quality metric based on unique k-mer counts. You only want HECIL's core algorithm (iteration 1) result to compare against other hybrid correctors — no iteration loop or termination criterion is needed You are self-correcting long reads without short-read data (e.g. HGAP-style), since HECIL's correction weights and k-mer evaluation depend on aligned short reads Your quality assessment must come from assembly-based metrics (Canu + QUAST + MUMmer dnadiff) rather than per-iteration k-mer counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A decision rule for HECIL's iterative learning loop that counts unique k-mers (via Jellyfish) after each correction iteration to measure correction quality and to terminate iterations, since better corrections collapse erroneous k-mers into fewer unique k-mers. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: A decision rule for HECIL's iterative learning loop that counts unique k-mers (via Jellyfish) after each correction iteration to measure correction quality and to terminate iterations, since better corrections collapse erroneous k-mers into fewer unique k-mers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only want HECIL's core algorithm (iteration 1) result to compare against other hybrid correctors — no iteration loop or termination criterion is needed You are self-correcting long reads without short-read data (e.g. HGAP-style), since HECIL's correction weights and k-mer evaluation depend on aligned short reads Your quality assessment must come from assembly-based metrics (Canu + QUAST + MUMmer dnadiff) rather than per-iteration k-mer counts

skills.description: Reference for assessing assembly consensus accuracy (QV) when no trusted reference exists but high-coverage short reads (≥60X recommended) and a HiFi-based assembly are available, or when auditing where residual erroneous k-mers reside.
skills.name: kmer-based-qv-estimation
skills.search_text: kmer-based-qv-estimation Reference for assessing assembly consensus accuracy (QV) when no trusted reference exists but high-coverage short reads (≥60X recommended) and a HiFi-based assembly are available, or when auditing where residual erroneous k-mers reside. When a high-confidence truth reference or GIAB benchmark set exists — variant-based evaluation (e.g. DeepVariant, paftools.js) is more informative than k-mer QV When short-read coverage is too low for reliable k-mer spectra (NextPolish2 recommends >=60X short reads), since QV will be dominated by coverage gaps rather than true errors When the genome is highly heterozygous without a phasing-aware setup, since Merqury's k-mer completeness and QV assumptions about haplotypes can be violated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Estimate consensus base quality (QV) of genome assemblies by comparing assembly k-mers against short-read k-mer spectra with Merqury/yak, without needing a reference genome. Used here to quantify QV gains from polishing and to stratify residual erroneous k-mers by short-read mapping depth and spanning-read identity. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Estimate consensus base quality (QV) of genome assemblies by comparing assembly k-mers against short-read k-mer spectra with Merqury/yak, without needing a reference genome. Used here to quantify QV gains from polishing and to stratify residual erroneous k-mers by short-read mapping depth and spanning-read identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a high-confidence truth reference or GIAB benchmark set exists — variant-based evaluation (e.g. DeepVariant, paftools.js) is more informative than k-mer QV When short-read coverage is too low for reliable k-mer spectra (NextPolish2 recommends >=60X short reads), since QV will be dominated by coverage gaps rather than true errors When the genome is highly heterozygous without a phasing-aware setup, since Merqury's k-mer completeness and QV assumptions about haplotypes can be violated

skills.description: Use when reads must be quickly matched or filtered against a reference without producing alignments — e.g. removing WGS reads that share no 25-mer with a de novo transcriptome assembly, or pre-screening reads for contamination.
skills.name: kmer-based-sequence-matching
skills.search_text: kmer-based-sequence-matching Use when reads must be quickly matched or filtered against a reference without producing alignments — e.g. removing WGS reads that share no 25-mer with a de novo transcriptome assembly, or pre-screening reads for contamination. You need mapping coordinates or alignment positions — biobloomcategorizer only classifies and does not provide mapping locations You need zero false positives in the retained set — Bloom filters have a tunable but non-zero false-positive rate (no false negatives, but false positives occur) You need full-exon or transcript-level precision from the matching alone — in EXFI the filtering is only the first stage before exon calling and splice-graph construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Filter or classify sequences by hashing k-mers into a Bloom filter and testing membership, as EXFI does by baiting a Bloom filter from the assembled transcriptome and using biobloomcategorizer to discard WGS reads that share no k-mer with it. This avoids costly alignment and shrinks the false-positive rate (BF FPR) of the downstream analysis. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Filter or classify sequences by hashing k-mers into a Bloom filter and testing membership, as EXFI does by baiting a Bloom filter from the assembled transcriptome and using biobloomcategorizer to discard WGS reads that share no k-mer with it. This avoids costly alignment and shrinks the false-positive rate (BF FPR) of the downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need mapping coordinates or alignment positions — biobloomcategorizer only classifies and does not provide mapping locations You need zero false positives in the retained set — Bloom filters have a tunable but non-zero false-positive rate (no false negatives, but false positives occur) You need full-exon or transcript-level precision from the matching alone — in EXFI the filtering is only the first stage before exon calling and splice-graph construction

skills.description: Use when you have Albacore-basecalled R9 nanopore data (fastq + fast5), a reference fasta, eventalign TSVs, and known motif sites (e.g. E. coli GATC) with labels to train methylation classifiers.
skills.name: kmer-context-binary-classifier-training
skills.search_text: kmer-context-binary-classifier-training Use when you have Albacore-basecalled R9 nanopore data (fastq + fast5), a reference fasta, eventalign TSVs, and known motif sites (e.g. E. coli GATC) with labels to train methylation classifiers. Input reads are from R10.4 flowcells — nanopolish states it does not support R10.4 variant/methylation calling via signal-level analysis The target sequence context is dissimilar to the training motifs — mCaller's training biases decrease accuracy at untrained contexts The goal is distinguishing between methylation types (e.g. the GATCGVNY motif in S. aureus), which single-molecule methods here fail to separate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Train mCaller's binary classifiers (NN, RF, NBC, LR) to detect m6A in Oxford Nanopore R9 data by learning from deviations between measured and expected currents over a six-variable k-mer context, using labeled methylated/unmethylated positions confirmed by orthogonal PacBio calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Train mCaller's binary classifiers (NN, RF, NBC, LR) to detect m6A in Oxford Nanopore R9 data by learning from deviations between measured and expected currents over a six-variable k-mer context, using labeled methylated/unmethylated positions confirmed by orthogonal PacBio calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are from R10.4 flowcells — nanopolish states it does not support R10.4 variant/methylation calling via signal-level analysis The target sequence context is dissimilar to the training motifs — mCaller's training biases decrease accuracy at untrained contexts The goal is distinguishing between methylation types (e.g. the GATCGVNY motif in S. aureus), which single-molecule methods here fail to separate

skills.description: Use when PacBio CCS reads with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) must be converted into per-k-mer PW/IPD feature matrices to train classifiers that discriminate modified vs canonical bases in defined sequence contexts.
skills.name: kmer-context-feature-engineering
skills.search_text: kmer-context-feature-engineering Use when PacBio CCS reads with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) must be converted into per-k-mer PW/IPD feature matrices to train classifiers that discriminate modified vs canonical bases in defined sequence contexts. Input reads lack kinetic tags or fail the Median_PW/Median_IPD 0.3-99th-percentile filter, so PW/IPD context features cannot be reliably extracted The analysis target is single-nucleotide Z/A probability calling on reads rather than controlled-context feature-importance modeling (use Z-Calling's k11-mixed-AZ MLP module instead) Context k-mers contain multiple adjacent A/Z bases, which the paper explicitly excludes to avoid interference among adjacent A/Zs http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Builds 21-mer sequence-context feature matrices centered on a target A/Z base from PacBio CCS kinetic signals (PW, IPD), restricted to k-mers with exactly one A/Z and ≥10 observations per condition, for machine-learning discrimination of dZ-DNA from canonical DNA. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: Builds 21-mer sequence-context feature matrices centered on a target A/Z base from PacBio CCS kinetic signals (PW, IPD), restricted to k-mers with exactly one A/Z and ≥10 observations per condition, for machine-learning discrimination of dZ-DNA from canonical DNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack kinetic tags or fail the Median_PW/Median_IPD 0.3-99th-percentile filter, so PW/IPD context features cannot be reliably extracted The analysis target is single-nucleotide Z/A probability calling on reads rather than controlled-context feature-importance modeling (use Z-Calling's k11-mixed-AZ MLP module instead) Context k-mers contain multiple adjacent A/Z bases, which the paper explicitly excludes to avoid interference among adjacent A/Zs

skills.description: Use when PacBio HiFi/CCS BAMs with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) are available and the goal is to test whether a modified base (e.g., dZ vs dA) shifts PW or IPD in a sequence-context-dependent manner across specific motif families (TTZTT vs TTATT, TTZGG vs TTAGG).
skills.name: kmer-context-motif-analysis
skills.search_text: kmer-context-motif-analysis Use when PacBio HiFi/CCS BAMs with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) are available and the goal is to test whether a modified base (e.g., dZ vs dA) shifts PW or IPD in a sequence-context-dependent manner across specific motif families (TTZTT vs TTATT, TTZGG vs TTAGG). The input BAMs lack kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp), so PW/IPD signals cannot be extracted The goal is single-nucleotide Z/A base calling or dZ-DNA read classification rather than kinetic motif analysis — use z-calling-base (k11-mixed-AZ or k21-full-ZA models) instead Candidate k-mers contain multiple adjacent A/Z bases, which the analysis explicitly excludes to avoid interference among neighboring A/Zs http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs sequence-context k-mers (e.g., 21-mers) centered on A/Z target bases from PacBio CCS kinetic tables and computes per-motif Z/A fold-change ratios of polymerase pulse width (PW) and inter-pulse duration (IPD), revealing context-dependent kinetic signatures of the 2,6-diaminopurine (Z) base. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs sequence-context k-mers (e.g., 21-mers) centered on A/Z target bases from PacBio CCS kinetic tables and computes per-motif Z/A fold-change ratios of polymerase pulse width (PW) and inter-pulse duration (IPD), revealing context-dependent kinetic signatures of the 2,6-diaminopurine (Z) base.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAMs lack kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp), so PW/IPD signals cannot be extracted The goal is single-nucleotide Z/A base calling or dZ-DNA read classification rather than kinetic motif analysis — use z-calling-base (k11-mixed-AZ or k21-full-ZA models) instead Candidate k-mers contain multiple adjacent A/Z bases, which the analysis explicitly excludes to avoid interference among neighboring A/Zs

skills.description: Use when constructing a DeepPlant CHH training set from extract_hc_sites npz feature files and you need per-9-mer context parity between methylation-positive and negative samples before model training.
skills.name: kmer-context-set-intersection-subsampling
skills.search_text: kmer-context-set-intersection-subsampling Use when constructing a DeepPlant CHH training set from extract_hc_sites npz feature files and you need per-9-mer context parity between methylation-positive and negative samples before model training. Input is raw pod5/BAM data with no extract_hc_sites output yet — run extract_hc_sites (pod5_dir bam_path reference_path ref_type write_dir pos neg kmer_size num_workers) first to produce the pos/neg npz files. The context is CpG or CHG methylation, where methylation-positive samples are abundant rather than scarce high-methylation CHH contexts. Samples were generated by in vitro enzyme-catalyzed methylation or PCR with modified base substitutions — the paper reports these are ineffective or alter base contexts for CHH positives. Balances CHH methylation training samples across 9-mer sequence contexts for DeepPlant by intersecting positive/negative 9-mer sets, enforcing a ≥50-positive-sample coverage threshold, and subsampling to per-9-mer class parity. This counters the scarcity of methylation-positive CHH samples that otherwise biases the R10.4 nanopore model. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Balances CHH methylation training samples across 9-mer sequence contexts for DeepPlant by intersecting positive/negative 9-mer sets, enforcing a ≥50-positive-sample coverage threshold, and subsampling to per-9-mer class parity. skills.description: Use when assembling a genome from hybrid data: accurate short-read contigs (FASTA from an DBG-assembler) plus low-coverage (10x-20x) erroneous long reads, and a high-contiguity backbone (e.g. N50 583 kbp on yeast) is needed.
skills.name: kmer-contig-anchoring-to-long-reads
skills.search_text: kmer-contig-anchoring-to-long-reads Use when assembling a genome from hybrid data: accurate short-read contigs (FASTA from an DBG-assembler) plus low-coverage (10x-20x) erroneous long reads, and a high-contiguity backbone (e.g. N50 583 kbp on yeast) is needed. You already have high-quality long reads and plan a non-hybrid pipeline (e.g. HGAP/Falcon) — the article compares against these, and hybrid preassembly heuristics may not help Your short-read contigs were produced with gap-closing or scaffolding heuristics — the README warns these errors propagate and give poor final results Coverage is very high (~100x PacBio) without adjusting ChimeraTh/ContigTh and the 50x-100x parameter ranges (KmerCovTh 2-10, MinOverlap 50-150, AdaptiveTh 0.01-0.02) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compresses long erroneous 3GS reads (e.g. PacBio) into k-mer space and anchors accurate preassembled DBG contigs onto them to build a genome backbone, skipping base-level errors while correcting structural errors. skills.description: Use when long-read FASTA/FASTQ and a draft assembly need lightweight, alignment-free read-to-contig mappings — e.g., to infer contig order/orientation for scaffolding or to detect misassemblies.
skills.name: kmer-recursive-spaced-seed-hashing
skills.search_text: kmer-recursive-spaced-seed-hashing Use when long-read FASTA/FASTQ and a draft assembly need lightweight, alignment-free read-to-contig mappings — e.g., to infer contig order/orientation for scaffolding or to detect misassemblies. When full base-level read alignments with per-base identity/accuracy are required (e.g., variant calling or precise alignment QC) — minimizer-based mappings are lightweight and approximate When the input draft contigs are shorter than the minimum length threshold (z=1000 bp), since such contigs are excluded from the scaffold graph When the task is de novo assembly itself rather than scaffolding/correction of an existing draft — ntLink is a scaffolding/mapping tool, not an assembler (assemblers like Flye or ABySS do that) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Computes ordered minimizer sketches of genome sequences (target assembly contigs and long reads) using btllib ntHash2-style recursive spaced-seed hashing (defaults k=32, w=100), enabling lightweight minimizer-based mappings instead of full read alignments for ntLink scaffolding. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Computes ordered minimizer sketches of genome sequences (target assembly contigs and long reads) using btllib ntHash2-style recursive spaced-seed hashing (defaults k=32, w=100), enabling lightweight minimizer-based mappings instead of full read alignments for ntLink scaffolding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When full base-level read alignments with per-base identity/accuracy are required (e.g., variant calling or precise alignment QC) — minimizer-based mappings are lightweight and approximate When the input draft contigs are shorter than the minimum length threshold (z=1000 bp), since such contigs are excluded from the scaffold graph When the task is de novo assembly itself rather than scaffolding/correction of an existing draft — ntLink is a scaffolding/mapping tool, not an assembler (assemblers like Flye or ABySS do that)

skills.description: Use when constructing a scaffolding graph or read-placement map alignment-free from short (Illumina mate-pair) or long reads against contig sequences, without a full read aligner.
skills.name: kmer-rolling-hash-indexing
skills.search_text: kmer-rolling-hash-indexing Use when constructing a scaffolding graph or read-placement map alignment-free from short (Illumina mate-pair) or long reads against contig sequences, without a full read aligner. A base-quality-aware or base-level alignment is required (this is alignment-free: it yields read locations/linking information, not base-resolved alignments) Insert-size or orientation information is needed for long-range mate-pair technologies like 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL, where gap-size estimation is challenging because linking comes from a range of insert sizes and orientation may be unknown The k-mer size needed falls outside the supported 12-256 range http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds a light-weight unique k-mer index over contig sequences (KMC3 counting, BBHash minimal perfect hash, quasi_dictionary probabilistic membership, ~87 bits/k-mer) and queries it with ntHash rolling hashes of read k-mers to localize reads alignment-free for scaffolding graph construction. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048

skills.when_to_use_negative: A base-quality-aware or base-level alignment is required (this is alignment-free: it yields read locations/linking information, not base-resolved alignments) Insert-size or orientation information is needed for long-range mate-pair technologies like 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL, where gap-size estimation is challenging because linking comes from a range of insert sizes and orientation may be unknown The k-mer size needed falls outside the supported 12-256 range

skills.description: Use when polishing a high-quality (e.g., QV > 50) HiFi/hifiasm assembly that still carries consensus errors, especially in repeats or gap-filled ONT regions, and overcorrection or switch errors must be avoided.
skills.name: kmer-scored-consensus-error-correction
skills.search_text: kmer-scored-consensus-error-correction Use when polishing a high-quality (e.g., QV > 50) HiFi/hifiasm assembly that still carries consensus errors, especially in repeats or gap-filled ONT regions, and overcorrection or switch errors must be avoided. The assembly is a draft built from noisy long reads without supplementary short-read k-mer data — performance relies heavily on short reads to check whether a K-mer contains errors The goal is de novo assembly or large structural-variant correction; NextPolish2 targets residual SNV/indel consensus errors in already-high-quality assemblies Trio-binned assemblies where reads of the other haplotype were not discarded before mapping — different-haplotype reads should be removed prior to alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A k-mer-guided genome polishing workflow (NextPolish2) that corrects residual SNV/indel errors in HiFi-assembled T2T genomes using HiFi read alignments plus yak k-mer datasets, while the built-in phasing module (LQR detection with Louvain community grouping) maintains haplotype consistency and avoids overcorrection in repeats. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: A k-mer-guided genome polishing workflow (NextPolish2) that corrects residual SNV/indel errors in HiFi-assembled T2T genomes using HiFi read alignments plus yak k-mer datasets, while the built-in phasing module (LQR detection with Louvain community grouping) maintains haplotype consistency and avoids overcorrection in repeats.

skills.description: Use when coarse seeded candidate regions from a long-read mapper must be converted into precise alignment anchors, especially for noisy Oxford Nanopore MinION or PacBio reads with repetitive reference loci.
skills.name: kmer-seed-graph-construction
skills.search_text: kmer-seed-graph-construction Use when coarse seeded candidate regions from a long-read mapper must be converted into precise alignment anchors, especially for noisy Oxford Nanopore MinION or PacBio reads with repetitive reference loci. The task is full end-to-end read mapping: this skill covers only stage-II anchor construction — stage-III chaining and alignment stages must follow to produce a SAM alignment. The reference is very large and RAM is limited: GraphMap's hash index is ~14x the reference size (~42 GB peak for human), so a BWT/FM-index mapper is preferable unless the (not-yet-implemented-at-publication) memory-reduction option is available. Sensitivity on highly repetitive seeds matters more than speed: setting --freq-percentile 1.0 (or -x sensitive) is required, since the default 0.99 filter skips 1% of the most repetitive seed lookups at a slight sensitivity cost. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Stage II of GraphMap's five-stage read funnel: refine coarse stage-I seed hits by building a k-mer mapping graph (one vertex per k-mer occurrence, ≤l outbound edges per vertex) and greedily traversing it with O(1) vertex updates to construct alignment anchors for long, error-prone nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Stage II of GraphMap's five-stage read funnel: refine coarse stage-I seed hits by building a k-mer mapping graph (one vertex per k-mer occurrence, ≤l outbound edges per vertex) and greedily traversing it with O(1) vertex updates to construct alignment anchors for long, error-prone nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is full end-to-end read mapping: this skill covers only stage-II anchor construction — stage-III chaining and alignment stages must follow to produce a SAM alignment. The reference is very large and RAM is limited: GraphMap's hash index is ~14x the reference size (~42 GB peak for human), so a BWT/FM-index mapper is preferable unless the (not-yet-implemented-at-publication) memory-reduction option is available. Sensitivity on highly repetitive seeds matters more than speed: setting --freq-percentile 1.0 (or -x sensitive) is required, since the default 0.99 filter skips 1% of the most repetitive seed lookups at a slight sensitivity cost.

skills.description: Use when comparing per-site methylation frequencies from nanopore tools against a orthogonal reference (e.g. WGBS) and you need to test whether flanking sequence context explains discrepancies at CpG sites.
skills.name: kmer-sequence-context-discrepancy-analysis
skills.search_text: kmer-sequence-context-discrepancy-analysis Use when comparing per-site methylation frequencies from nanopore tools against a orthogonal reference (e.g. WGBS) and you need to test whether flanking sequence context explains discrepancies at CpG sites. Input data are single-read per-read scores (fast5-level) rather than per-site aggregated methylation frequency files — the discrepancy analysis requires site-level frequencies in augmented BED format The orthogonal reference is another nanopore tool rather than WGBS; this skill specifically benchmarks nanopore against bisulfite-derived methylation frequencies The organism's methylation context is non-CpG (e.g. bacterial dam/dcm); the NNNCGNNN 8-mer extraction is defined on CpG dinucleotides http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A motif-analysis skill that quantifies whether the 8-mer sequence context (NNNCGNNN) centered on CpG sites biases agreement between nanopore methylation calls (Nanopolish, Megalodon, METEORE combined model) and WGBS methylation frequencies in nCATS datasets. It produces ranked k-mer discrepancy tables and low-vs-high discrepancy pLogo motif comparisons to expose AT-rich contexts where nanopore and WGBS disagree most. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: A motif-analysis skill that quantifies whether the 8-mer sequence context (NNNCGNNN) centered on CpG sites biases agreement between nanopore methylation calls (Nanopolish, Megalodon, METEORE combined model) and WGBS methylation frequencies in nCATS datasets. It produces ranked k-mer discrepancy tables and low-vs-high discrepancy pLogo motif comparisons to expose AT-rich contexts where nanopore and WGBS disagree most.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are single-read per-read scores (fast5-level) rather than per-site aggregated methylation frequency files — the discrepancy analysis requires site-level frequencies in augmented BED format The orthogonal reference is another nanopore tool rather than WGBS; this skill specifically benchmarks nanopore against bisulfite-derived methylation frequencies The organism's methylation context is non-CpG (e.g. bacterial dam/dcm); the NNNCGNNN 8-mer extraction is defined on CpG dinucleotides

skills.name: kmer-sequence-feature-construction
skills.search_text: kmer-sequence-feature-construction Use when you have re-squiggled single-read FAST5 files (Tombo, corrected_group RawGenomeCorrected_000) and need per-site 13-mer sequence+signal features to train or run DeepSignal-plant 5mC detection. The features TSV already exists and the goal is methylation calling — proceed directly to `deepsignal_plant call_mods` instead of re-extracting. Input is bisulfite sequencing data, which has no Nanopore signal events to build base-level signal features from. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Constructs the per-cytosine feature matrix for DeepSignal-plant: sequence features from the centered 13-mer (base identity, per-base signal mean, standard deviation, and signal length) plus 13x16 raw signal features extracted from Tombo re-squiggled reads, written to a tab-delimited features TSV that feeds BiLSTM methylation calling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9

skills.search_text: kmer-signal-hash-table-indexing Use when ONT multi-fast5 reads have been Tombo-resquiggled and you must aggregate raw signal events per reference k-mer (default odd k=15) to find modified motifs against a WGA control. Input fast5 files are still single-read and/or not resquiggled with Tombo — Snapper's pipeline expects resquiggled multi-fast5 event data No WGA control sample is available, since the KS-test requires comparing native vs control signal distributions You want probabilistic per-read modified-base calls rather than de novo methylation motif detection — Tombo or Remora are the appropriate tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Indexes Tombo-resquiggled, ont_fast5_api-converted multi-fast5 nanopore signals by genomic k-mer so that per-k-mer native vs WGA signal distributions can be compared with a KS-test (Snapper's signal-comparison stage). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702

skills.search_text: kmer-signal-statistics-analysis Use when you have native and control (e.g., WGA) nanopore fast5 reads plus a reference genome and need de novo detection of methylated k-mers/motifs from raw signal statistics. Input reads are already basecalled motif calls from other methyl callers and no raw fast5 signal is available — resquiggling and k-mer signal statistics require raw signal You need per-read or per-site methylation quantification rather than de novo motif discovery — Snapper is a motif caller, not a per-site annotator Python environment is >3.7 and cannot be downgraded — the README warns later versions might be incompatible because of inner biopython dependencies http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Compute per-k-mer signal statistics from resquiggled ONT raw signal to identify k-mers likely to carry modified bases, then enrich methylation motifs using Snapper's high-sensitive greedy position-specific motif selection algorithm. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702

skills.description: Use when configuring a kinetic-signal k-mer classifier (e.g. Z-Calling full-substitution model) and you must justify which k-mer size trades model strength against compute cost before freezing a production artifact.
skills.name: kmer-size-hyperparameter-sweep
skills.search_text: kmer-size-hyperparameter-sweep Use when configuring a kinetic-signal k-mer classifier (e.g. Z-Calling full-substitution model) and you must justify which k-mer size trades model strength against compute cost before freezing a production artifact. You are tuning the single-nucleotide A/Z model — that uses the k11-mixed-AZ artifact (model/k11-mixed-AZ/scripted_m11.pth, run with -k 11), not the k21 full-substitution sweep. Input reads lack PacBio kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) or have Median_PW/Median_IPD outside the accepted range; the sweep cannot be trained without valid kinetics. The task is per-base Z probability extraction from an already-chosen model — use z-calling-base/z-bam2txt directly rather than re-sweeping k. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Sweeps odd k-mer sizes (7–25 bp) for PacBio PW/IPD kinetic feature matrices and trains a PyTorch MLP per k to pick the k-mer size that balances classification AUC against CPU training/calling cost, resulting in k=21 for the full-substitution dZ-DNA/canonical (full-Z vs full-dA) model. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: Sweeps odd k-mer sizes (7–25 bp) for PacBio PW/IPD kinetic feature matrices and trains a PyTorch MLP per k to pick the k-mer size that balances classification AUC against CPU training/calling cost, resulting in k=21 for the full-substitution dZ-DNA/canonical (full-Z vs full-dA) model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are tuning the single-nucleotide A/Z model — that uses the k11-mixed-AZ artifact (model/k11-mixed-AZ/scripted_m11.pth, run with -k 11), not the k21 full-substitution sweep. Input reads lack PacBio kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) or have Median_PW/Median_IPD outside the accepted range; the sweep cannot be trained without valid kinetics. The task is per-base Z probability extraction from an already-chosen model — use z-calling-base/z-bam2txt directly rather than re-sweeping k.

skills.name: kmer-stratified-sample-balancing
skills.search_text: kmer-stratified-sample-balancing Use when constructing a deep-learning training set from Nanopore signal features (e.g. fast5s.C.features.tsv) where methylated/unmethylated cytosines are heavily skewed across k-mer contexts (CpG, CHG, CHH) and the classifier must not confound methylation with sequence context. skills.summary: Balances DeepSignal-plant's training dataset by first equalizing k-mer types between methylated and unmethylated cytosine samples, then equalizing per-k-mer read counts, so the BiLSTM model learns methylation status from Nanopore signal features rather than k-mer identity.

skills.description: Use when validating m6A site predictions from ONT direct RNA reads by checking that base-calling error signals observed in wild-type are absent in a modification-deficient (ime4Δ) knockout/control strain.
skills.name: knockout-strain-negative-control-analysis
skills.search_text: knockout-strain-negative-control-analysis Use when validating m6A site predictions from ONT direct RNA reads by checking that base-calling error signals observed in wild-type are absent in a modification-deficient (ime4Δ) knockout/control strain. Input is a single sample with no matched knockout/knockdown or demethylase-treated control — EpiNano-Error pairwise mode and the negative-control logic require WT-vs-KO comparison The analysis target is single-molecule (per-read) modification calling — EpiNano aggregates all reads per site and does not predict modifications in individual RNA molecules The modification of interest is not expected to alter base-calling features, or a pretrained SVM model does not exist for it and cannot be trained from matched controls http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Validates nanopore direct RNA sequencing m6A calls by comparing base-calling 'error' features between a wild-type yeast strain (SAy841) and a modification-deficient ime4Δ knockout (SAy966).
