skills.search_text: kruskal-wallis-multi-group-comparison Use when comparing a per-sample numeric quantity (e.g., Argo total ARG cpg) across ≥3 independent groups — such as human fecal samples from CN, KR, SG, DE, US versus NH non-human primates — where normality cannot be assumed. Only two groups are being compared — a plain Mann–Whitney U test on the cpg values suffices without the multi-group Kruskal–Wallis step. Samples are paired or otherwise non-independent (e.g., longitudinal sampling of the same hosts), violating the independence assumption of the test. The goal is de novo discovery of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments rather than group comparison of already-profiled cpg values — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods are better suited there. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Non-parametric testing of a per-sample continuous metric — here total ARG abundance expressed as copies per genome (cpg) from Argo — across three or more independent groups, using Kruskal–Wallis with Bonferroni-corrected pairwise Mann–Whitney follow-ups in R. It establishes group ordering (e.g., a decreasing CN→NH trend) without assuming normality. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y

skills.name: levenshtein-qgram-shape-hashing
skills.search_text: levenshtein-qgram-shape-hashing Use when mapping high-error long reads (e.g. Oxford Nanopore MinION FASTA/FASTQ) to a large reference genome and you need to reproduce or evaluate how a coarse-alignment stage reduces the candidate search space before fine alignment. Reads are short and low-error (e.g. Illumina) — GraphMap's default parameters target long, error-prone third-generation reads, and dense spaced-seed hashing is unnecessary for high-accuracy short reads The goal is fine-grained base-level alignment rather than coarse candidate-region selection — Stage I binning only narrows the search space and must be followed by graph-based anchor refinement and LCSk chaining (Stages II–III) Only very small memory is available and the reference is large — the hash index is ~14x reference size (peak ~42 GB for human), so memory-efficient BWT/FM-index mappers are preferable Reconstructs GraphMap's Stage I 'read-funneling' candidate selection: a reference hash index over Levenshtein gapped q-gram shapes (6-1-6 and 4-1-4-1-4), percentile-thresholded seed lookups, and Hough-transform vote-grid binning of seed hits to nominate candidate genomic regions for high-error nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Reconstructs GraphMap's Stage I 'read-funneling' candidate selection: a reference hash index over Levenshtein gapped q-gram shapes (6-1-6 and 4-1-4-1-4), percentile-thresholded seed lookups, and Hough-transform vote-grid binning of seed hits to nominate candidate genomic regions for high-error nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are short and low-error (e.g. Illumina) — GraphMap's default parameters target long, error-prone third-generation reads, and dense spaced-seed hashing is unnecessary for high-accuracy short reads The goal is fine-grained base-level alignment rather than coarse candidate-region selection — Stage I binning only narrows the search space and must be followed by graph-based anchor refinement and LCSk chaining (Stages II–III) Only very small memory is available and the reference is large — the hash index is ~14x reference size (peak ~42 GB for human), so memory-efficient BWT/FM-index mappers are preferable

skills.description: Use when training an ε-SVR model on a small feature matrix (e.g., tens of samples, dozens of features such as the 42 splicing-related vex-seq features) and you must select C and RBF γ by cross-validated correlation rather than default parameters.
skills.name: libsvm-rbf-kernel-hyperparameter-grid-search
skills.search_text: libsvm-rbf-kernel-hyperparameter-grid-search Use when training an ε-SVR model on a small feature matrix (e.g., tens of samples, dozens of features such as the 42 splicing-related vex-seq features) and you must select C and RBF γ by cross-validated correlation rather than default parameters. Input is already a trained model file or a reduced feature set — the grid search is meant for raw candidate feature matrices before feature selection. The dataset is large enough for more expressive models (e.g., deep learning); the authors note the small vex-seq sample size is what justified SVR, and PredPSI-SVR omits branch point and pre-mRNA secondary structure features for this reason. The task requires predictions on variants more than 200 bp from splice sites or in intergenic regions — PredPSI-SVR filters these out before modeling. Hyperparameter optimization strategy for ε-support vector regression using LIBSVM's RBF kernel, in which the regularization parameter C and kernel width γ are grid-searched under 10-fold cross-validation, used by PredPSI-SVR to predict ΔΨ from 42 splicing-related vex-seq features and reach a cross-validation PCC of 0.570. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Hyperparameter optimization strategy for ε-support vector regression using LIBSVM's RBF kernel, in which the regularization parameter C and kernel width γ are grid-searched under 10-fold cross-validation, used by PredPSI-SVR to predict ΔΨ from 42 splicing-related vex-seq features and reach a cross-validation PCC of 0.570.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a trained model file or a reduced feature set — the grid search is meant for raw candidate feature matrices before feature selection. The dataset is large enough for more expressive models (e.g., deep learning); the authors note the small vex-seq sample size is what justified SVR, and PredPSI-SVR omits branch point and pre-mRNA secondary structure features for this reason. The task requires predictions on variants more than 200 bp from splice sites or in intergenic regions — PredPSI-SVR filters these out before modeling.

skills.description: Use when detecting differential splicing between two sample groups from long-read transcriptome sequencing, and you must account for within-group PSI variability / overdispersion in supporting-read counts rather than assuming a simple binomial.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-test-implementation
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-test-implementation Use when detecting differential splicing between two sample groups from long-read transcriptome sequencing, and you must account for within-group PSI variability / overdispersion in supporting-read counts rather than assuming a simple binomial. Input is short-read RNA-seq data intended for tools like rMATS or MISO rather than LRTS events defined by IsoTools' segment graphs Groups have identical PSI by construction and the goal is differential transcript quantification rather than event-level differential splicing testing Read counts are not overdispersed and a simple binomial LRT is sufficient (the beta-binomial reduces to binomial when overdispersion is zero) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Implements the beta-binomial mixture likelihood ratio test IsoTools uses to detect differential alternative splicing between groups of LRTS samples, modeling within-group PSI variability and overdispersion of supporting-read counts. Overdispersion parameters (alpha/beta) are fit numerically so group-vs-group testing does not falsely inflate significance when PSI varies within groups. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Implements the beta-binomial mixture likelihood ratio test IsoTools uses to detect differential alternative splicing between groups of LRTS samples, modeling within-group PSI variability and overdispersion of supporting-read counts. Overdispersion parameters (alpha/beta) are fit numerically so group-vs-group testing does not falsely inflate significance when PSI varies within groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data intended for tools like rMATS or MISO rather than LRTS events defined by IsoTools' segment graphs Groups have identical PSI by construction and the goal is differential transcript quantification rather than event-level differential splicing testing Read counts are not overdispersed and a simple binomial LRT is sufficient (the beta-binomial reduces to binomial when overdispersion is zero)

skills.description: Use when a covariate (e.g. t2d_sim) is entered in BOTH the mean_covar and zi_covar design matrices of a TWO-SIGMA ZINB mixed-model fit and you need per-gene LR statistics and p-values for its joint association with expression.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-testing-of-regression-coefficients
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-testing-of-regression-coefficients Use when a covariate (e.g. t2d_sim) is entered in BOTH the mean_covar and zi_covar design matrices of a TWO-SIGMA ZINB mixed-model fit and you need per-gene LR statistics and p-values for its joint association with expression. The tested covariate is in only one component, or the zero-inflation component contains only an Intercept — lr.twosigma explicitly assumes the variable is in both components and that the ZI component has more than an Intercept; use lr.twosigma_custom with an explicit lr.df instead. The target is a random-effect variance component rather than a fixed effect — the package designates test.vc.twosigma for variance-component likelihood-ratio tests. Counts are already normalized or log-transformed — twosigma/lr.twosigma expect raw non-negative integer counts and perform no normalization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Per-gene joint likelihood-ratio testing of a fixed-effect covariate (e.g. binary disease status t2d_sim) in the TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model, testing the joint null H0: alpha1 = beta1 = 0 across both the drop-out and conditional-mean components via the twosigma R package. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Per-gene joint likelihood-ratio testing of a fixed-effect covariate (e.g. binary disease status t2d_sim) in the TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model, testing the joint null H0: alpha1 = beta1 = 0 across both the drop-out and conditional-mean components via the twosigma R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tested covariate is in only one component, or the zero-inflation component contains only an Intercept — lr.twosigma explicitly assumes the variable is in both components and that the ZI component has more than an Intercept; use lr.twosigma_custom with an explicit lr.df instead. The target is a random-effect variance component rather than a fixed effect — the package designates test.vc.twosigma for variance-component likelihood-ratio tests. Counts are already normalized or log-transformed — twosigma/lr.twosigma expect raw non-negative integer counts and perform no normalization.

skills.description: Use when paired tumor/control long-read (ONT or PacBio) data has been processed with nanomonsv's mobile element insertion workflow and you need to classify insertions as LINE1-mediated and resolve their 3' transduction source sites to define source element loci.
skills.name: line1-source-element-locus-annotation
skills.search_text: line1-source-element-locus-annotation Use when paired tumor/control long-read (ONT or PacBio) data has been processed with nanomonsv's mobile element insertion workflow and you need to classify insertions as LINE1-mediated and resolve their 3' transduction source sites to define source element loci. When both breakpoints of an SV lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions — the Single breakend SV module cannot detect SVs where both breakpoints are in areas where reference genomes are not well-characterized When the event is a long repeat expansion (VNTR/microsatellite) rather than a LINE1 insertion — the reference-genome-based framework may not capture long repeat expansion events When only short-read tumor/control data is available and full-length inserted sequences cannot be recovered, since tracing 3' transductions to source sites requires full-length insert sequence http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identifies and annotates the genomic source elements of LINE1 3' transductions from somatic mobile element insertions detected by nanomonsv, producing the reference set of LINE1 source loci (e.g. the 23 elements) that downstream methylation and rearrangement analyses are anchored to. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Identifies and annotates the genomic source elements of LINE1 3' transductions from somatic mobile element insertions detected by nanomonsv, producing the reference set of LINE1 source loci (e.g. the 23 elements) that downstream methylation and rearrangement analyses are anchored to.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When both breakpoints of an SV lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions — the Single breakend SV module cannot detect SVs where both breakpoints are in areas where reference genomes are not well-characterized When the event is a long repeat expansion (VNTR/microsatellite) rather than a LINE1 insertion — the reference-genome-based framework may not capture long repeat expansion events When only short-read tumor/control data is available and full-length inserted sequences cannot be recovered, since tracing 3' transductions to source sites requires full-length insert sequence

skills.description: Use when nanomonsv has produced insertion calls (nanomonsv.result.txt) with full inserted sequences from paired tumor/control long-read data and you need to classify them as LINE1/Alu/SVA or identify LINE1 3' transduction source sites.
skills.name: line1-transduction-source-inference
skills.search_text: line1-transduction-source-inference Use when nanomonsv has produced insertion calls (nanomonsv.result.txt) with full inserted sequences from paired tumor/control long-read data and you need to classify them as LINE1/Alu/SVA or identify LINE1 3' transduction source sites. The goal is somatic copy-number or balanced rearrangement detection rather than insertion classification — use the nanomonsv Canonical SV or Single breakend SV modules instead. Insertions are present in only a minority of cells (subclonal) at modest sequencing depth — the paper notes detection of such subclonal MEIs remains challenging. The event is a long VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion — the paper states the reference-genome-based framework may not appropriately capture long repeat expansion events. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Classifies somatic mobile element insertions detected by nanomonsv into LINE1, Alu, and SVA classes and traces 3' transduction events (partnered vs orphan) back to putative LINE1 source elements, using full-length inserted sequences recovered from tumor/control paired long-read data. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Classifies somatic mobile element insertions detected by nanomonsv into LINE1, Alu, and SVA classes and traces 3' transduction events (partnered vs orphan) back to putative LINE1 source elements, using full-length inserted sequences recovered from tumor/control paired long-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is somatic copy-number or balanced rearrangement detection rather than insertion classification — use the nanomonsv Canonical SV or Single breakend SV modules instead. Insertions are present in only a minority of cells (subclonal) at modest sequencing depth — the paper notes detection of such subclonal MEIs remains challenging. The event is a long VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion — the paper states the reference-genome-based framework may not appropriately capture long repeat expansion events.

skills.description: Use when ONT direct RNA sequencing feature tables (mismatch/insertion/deletion frequencies, per-base quality) are available for a wild-type sample plus matched fully-modified and unmodified references, and per-site modification fraction estimates are needed.
skills.name: linear-regression-stoichiometry-estimation
skills.search_text: linear-regression-stoichiometry-estimation Use when ONT direct RNA sequencing feature tables (mismatch/insertion/deletion frequencies, per-base quality) are available for a wild-type sample plus matched fully-modified and unmodified references, and per-site modification fraction estimates are needed. Only a single sample is available with no matched modified/unmodified references — EpiNano error-based approaches are recommended in paired mode (WT vs KO/KD) Single-read (per-molecule) modification calling is required — EpiNano aggregates information across all reads at a site and lacks per-read resolution The modification type is unknown — EpiNano does not distinguish between different modification types (e.g., m1A vs m6A) http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Estimates per-site m6A modification stoichiometry by linearly regressing wild-type mismatch frequencies at known m6A sites onto two reference endpoints: a 100%-modified in vitro sample and a 0%-modified (ime4Δ-derived) unmodified reference, using EpiNano-extracted base-calling error features from ONT direct RNA sequencing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Estimates per-site m6A modification stoichiometry by linearly regressing wild-type mismatch frequencies at known m6A sites onto two reference endpoints: a 100%-modified in vitro sample and a 0%-modified (ime4Δ-derived) unmodified reference, using EpiNano-extracted base-calling error features from ONT direct RNA sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single sample is available with no matched modified/unmodified references — EpiNano error-based approaches are recommended in paired mode (WT vs KO/KD) Single-read (per-molecule) modification calling is required — EpiNano aggregates information across all reads at a site and lacks per-read resolution The modification type is unknown — EpiNano does not distinguish between different modification types (e.g., m1A vs m6A)

skills.description: Use when working with linked-read (10x Chromium, TELL-Seq, stLFR) BAM data where orphan contigs from unaligned reads must be linked to molecule barcodes before targeted reassembly of non-reference insertions.
skills.name: linked-read-barcode-extraction
skills.search_text: linked-read-barcode-extraction Use when working with linked-read (10x Chromium, TELL-Seq, stLFR) BAM data where orphan contigs from unaligned reads must be linked to molecule barcodes before targeted reassembly of non-reference insertions. Input data lacks synthetic long-read barcode information (plain short-read or long-read data without linked-read barcodes) — barcode recruitment is impossible The goal is whole-genome de novo assembly; Novel-X's barcode-guided local reassembly is explicitly designed to avoid that Detecting insertions small enough that few distinct barcodes associate with them (the authors note small insertions usually have insufficient barcode coverage for anchor assembly) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts the set of 10x/stLFR/TELL-Seq synthetic long-read barcodes associated with candidate non-reference insertion contigs, by aligning unaligned-end reads to orphan contigs and collecting the barcodes of supporting reads. This barcode recruitment step is what lets Novel-X reassemble insertion anchors locally without whole-genome de novo assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Extracts the set of 10x/stLFR/TELL-Seq synthetic long-read barcodes associated with candidate non-reference insertion contigs, by aligning unaligned-end reads to orphan contigs and collecting the barcodes of supporting reads. This barcode recruitment step is what lets Novel-X reassemble insertion anchors locally without whole-genome de novo assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks synthetic long-read barcode information (plain short-read or long-read data without linked-read barcodes) — barcode recruitment is impossible The goal is whole-genome de novo assembly; Novel-X's barcode-guided local reassembly is explicitly designed to avoid that Detecting insertions small enough that few distinct barcodes associate with them (the authors note small insertions usually have insufficient barcode coverage for anchor assembly)

skills.description: Use when you have a LongRanger/stLFR/TELL-Seq aligned BAM of synthetic long reads and need to discover and place novel insertions longer than 300 bp that short-read callers miss, without running a whole-genome assembler like SuperNova.
skills.name: linked-read-novel-insertion-detection
skills.search_text: linked-read-novel-insertion-detection Use when you have a LongRanger/stLFR/TELL-Seq aligned BAM of synthetic long reads and need to discover and place novel insertions longer than 300 bp that short-read callers miss, without running a whole-genome assembler like SuperNova. Insertions are small (<300 bp) — Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes per insertion, and small insertions usually lack sufficient coverage for anchor assembly A whole-genome diploid assembly is already available or desired — SuperNova-based placement may be preferable, though it is computationally far more expensive and offers no user control over assembler parameters Input is short-read data without linked-read barcodes — use short-read NRS methods like NovelSeq, MindTheGap, PopIns2 or Pamir instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 A four-step Snakemake pipeline (Novel-X) that detects and genotypes non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions >300 bp in 10x Genomics linked-read data by combining alignment signatures (unmapped/MQ<10/>20% soft-clipped reads) with barcode-guided local reassembly, avoiding whole-genome de novo assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: A four-step Snakemake pipeline (Novel-X) that detects and genotypes non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions >300 bp in 10x Genomics linked-read data by combining alignment signatures (unmapped/MQ<10/>20% soft-clipped reads) with barcode-guided local reassembly, avoiding whole-genome de novo assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Insertions are small (<300 bp) — Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes per insertion, and small insertions usually lack sufficient coverage for anchor assembly A whole-genome diploid assembly is already available or desired — SuperNova-based placement may be preferable, though it is computationally far more expensive and offers no user control over assembler parameters Input is short-read data without linked-read barcodes — use short-read NRS methods like NovelSeq, MindTheGap, PopIns2 or Pamir instead

skills.description: Use when evaluating coverage sensitivity of linked-read insertion/SV callers: you have one high-coverage simulated linked-read BAM plus a ground-truth callset and need matched lower-coverage test datasets.
skills.name: linked-read-read-downsampling
skills.search_text: linked-read-read-downsampling Use when evaluating coverage sensitivity of linked-read insertion/SV callers: you have one high-coverage simulated linked-read BAM plus a ground-truth callset and need matched lower-coverage test datasets. You need sensitivity on real (non-simulated) haploid/diploid genomes such as CHM1, CHM13, NA12878 or HG002 — this skill is specifically the simulated downsampling workflow The question is caller performance vs. platform (10x Genomics, TELL-Seq, stLFR) rather than vs. read coverage Insertions of interest are <300 bp; the benchmarked callsets and comparison restrict to insertions >300 bp with >300 bp of total anchor length http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Downsampling of a high-coverage synthetic (linked) long-read WGS dataset to a series of lower-coverage versions (65x down to 13x via 80/60/40/20% read removal) to benchmark how NRS-insertion callers degrade with coverage, mirroring the Novel-X paper's Supplementary Table S1. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Downsampling of a high-coverage synthetic (linked) long-read WGS dataset to a series of lower-coverage versions (65x down to 13x via 80/60/40/20% read removal) to benchmark how NRS-insertion callers degrade with coverage, mirroring the Novel-X paper's Supplementary Table S1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need sensitivity on real (non-simulated) haploid/diploid genomes such as CHM1, CHM13, NA12878 or HG002 — this skill is specifically the simulated downsampling workflow The question is caller performance vs. platform (10x Genomics, TELL-Seq, stLFR) rather than vs. read coverage Insertions of interest are <300 bp; the benchmarked callsets and comparison restrict to insertions >300 bp with >300 bp of total anchor length

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare NRS insertion callers on linked-read data where no truth set exists, by simulating a ground-truth genome with known insertions and scoring calls.
skills.name: linked-read-simulation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: linked-read-simulation-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively compare NRS insertion callers on linked-read data where no truth set exists, by simulating a ground-truth genome with known insertions and scoring calls. You have a real (non-simulated) cohort with an independent truth set (e.g. GIAB HG002 or T2T CHM13) — benchmark directly against that instead of simulating. The caller under test cannot consume barcoded linked-reads and you have no means to generate matched short-read data (as ART does for Pamir). You only care about insertions shorter than 300 bp — the Novel-X analysis explicitly restricts to insertions longer than 300 bp with anchor sums exceeding 300 bp, so small-insertion recall will be structurally limited. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Simulate barcoded synthetic long-read (linked-read) benchmarks with planted non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions and compute precision/recall for insertion callers such as Novel-X, NUI, PopIns2, and Pamir, including size-bin breakdowns. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Simulate barcoded synthetic long-read (linked-read) benchmarks with planted non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions and compute precision/recall for insertion callers such as Novel-X, NUI, PopIns2, and Pamir, including size-bin breakdowns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a real (non-simulated) cohort with an independent truth set (e.g. GIAB HG002 or T2T CHM13) — benchmark directly against that instead of simulating. The caller under test cannot consume barcoded linked-reads and you have no means to generate matched short-read data (as ART does for Pamir). You only care about insertions shorter than 300 bp — the Novel-X analysis explicitly restricts to insertions longer than 300 bp with anchor sums exceeding 300 bp, so small-insertion recall will be structurally limited.

skills.description: Use when quantifying depletion or enrichment efficiency of a live RISER run from basecalled, mapped reads split between deplete (even-numbered channels) and control channels, expressed as percent change in read and nt counts per RNA biotype.
skills.name: live-run-depletion-efficiency-analysis
skills.search_text: live-run-depletion-efficiency-analysis Use when quantifying depletion or enrichment efficiency of a live RISER run from basecalled, mapped reads split between deplete (even-numbered channels) and control channels, expressed as percent change in read and nt counts per RNA biotype. Input is a non-RISER control run with no decisions CSV — condition assignment must instead come from randomly split channels for the null comparison, not RISER channel labels Analysis targets globin mRNA depletion in whole blood, which is validated against a different benchmark (>90% globin decrease, ~16% non-globin increase) rather than the mRNA/mtRNA HEK293 metrics Goal is RISER model training/testing or real-time signal classification, not post-sequencing quantification of depletion efficiency http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how much live RISER read-until depletion of mRNA and mtRNA changes per-transcript read and nucleotide counts in a split-flow-cell MinION direct RNA sequencing run, and validates the aggregate depletion against reported benchmarks (~86%/85% read depletion). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Quantifies how much live RISER read-until depletion of mRNA and mtRNA changes per-transcript read and nucleotide counts in a split-flow-cell MinION direct RNA sequencing run, and validates the aggregate depletion against reported benchmarks (~86%/85% read depletion).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a non-RISER control run with no decisions CSV — condition assignment must instead come from randomly split channels for the null comparison, not RISER channel labels Analysis targets globin mRNA depletion in whole blood, which is validated against a different benchmark (>90% globin decrease, ~16% non-globin increase) rather than the mRNA/mtRNA HEK293 metrics Goal is RISER model training/testing or real-time signal classification, not post-sequencing quantification of depletion efficiency

skills.description: Use when a genome-guided transcriptome assembly (StringTie GTF from hybrid PacBio/Illumina RNA-seq) must be split into coding and lncRNA classes with a reconciled, annotated GTF output.
skills.name: lncrna-coding-potential-classification
skills.search_text: lncrna-coding-potential-classification Use when a genome-guided transcriptome assembly (StringTie GTF from hybrid PacBio/Illumina RNA-seq) must be split into coding and lncRNA classes with a reconciled, annotated GTF output. The organism lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI-available annotation in GTF format — the article explicitly restricts the pipeline to such organisms Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a genome-guided assembled GTF — reads must first be aligned (minimap2/HISAT2) and assembled with StringTie De novo transcriptome assembly without a reference genome — the pipeline is genome-guided and requires a genome FASTA as a guide http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Classifies assembled transcripts as coding versus long non-coding RNAs by reconciling the StringTie GTF against existing annotations, running GAWN/Blastx against Swissprot, training the FEELnc lncRNA classifier with known coding RNAs, and using TransDecoder to recover coding regions in remaining unclassified transcripts. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Classifies assembled transcripts as coding versus long non-coding RNAs by reconciling the StringTie GTF against existing annotations, running GAWN/Blastx against Swissprot, training the FEELnc lncRNA classifier with known coding RNAs, and using TransDecoder to recover coding regions in remaining unclassified transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism lacks an assembled genome and an NCBI-available annotation in GTF format — the article explicitly restricts the pipeline to such organisms Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a genome-guided assembled GTF — reads must first be aligned (minimap2/HISAT2) and assembled with StringTie De novo transcriptome assembly without a reference genome — the pipeline is genome-guided and requires a genome FASTA as a guide

skills.description: Use when calling medium-size structural variants (50–10,000 bp) from position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR bams (optionally plus low-coverage long reads) where a full whole-genome assembly is unnecessary or too expensive.
skills.name: local-assembly-with-modified-spades
skills.search_text: local-assembly-with-modified-spades Use when calling medium-size structural variants (50–10,000 bp) from position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR bams (optionally plus low-coverage long reads) where a full whole-genome assembly is unnecessary or too expensive. Input is short-read-only data without SLR barcode tags (BX) — Blackbird relies on encoded SLR barcode information Goal is a whole-genome assembly; Blackbird explicitly avoids whole-genome assembly and only assembles small segments for SV calling The event of interest is shorter than 50 bp — reliable calls are emitted only for indels longer than 50 bp in out_50.vcf http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly of synthetic long-read (SLR) datasets for structural variant detection, implemented in Blackbird with a barcode- and long-read-aware SPAdes fork. Segments the BWA-indexed reference into 50 kbp overlapping windows, collects barcode-linked reads per segment, and assembles each segment locally to call insertions and deletions in the 50–10,000 bp range. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly of synthetic long-read (SLR) datasets for structural variant detection, implemented in Blackbird with a barcode- and long-read-aware SPAdes fork. Segments the BWA-indexed reference into 50 kbp overlapping windows, collects barcode-linked reads per segment, and assembles each segment locally to call insertions and deletions in the 50–10,000 bp range.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read-only data without SLR barcode tags (BX) — Blackbird relies on encoded SLR barcode information Goal is a whole-genome assembly; Blackbird explicitly avoids whole-genome assembly and only assembles small segments for SV calling The event of interest is shorter than 50 bp — reliable calls are emitted only for indels longer than 50 bp in out_50.vcf

skills.description: Use when windowed MSA consensus sequences still carry residual substitution/indel errors, or when a raw long-read assembly (e.g., Flye output) must be polished with ONT or PacBio reads.
skills.name: local-de-bruijn-graph-polishing
skills.search_text: local-de-bruijn-graph-polishing Use when windowed MSA consensus sequences still carry residual substitution/indel errors, or when a raw long-read assembly (e.g., Flye output) must be polished with ONT or PacBio reads. skills.search_text: long-read-compressed-representation Use when assembling large genomes (e.g., 3 Gbp H. sapiens) from long erroneous 3GS reads (PacBio/MinION) plus accurate short-read contigs, and base-level all-vs-all long-read overlap is computationally prohibitive. When only long reads are available with no accurate short-read contigs — the compression step depends on NGS contig anchors When short-read assemblies have been gap-closed or scaffolded — README warns this yields poor final results due to errors from short-read assembly heuristics When a polished, base-level-accurate assembly is the immediate deliverable — this skill covers overlap/layout only; consensus/polishing (BLASR + Sparc/pbdagcon) is a separate step consuming ~90% of runtime http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compact representation of erroneous long 3GS reads by encoding each PacBio read as an ordered list of matched short-read contig anchors (k-mer matches), enabling fast overlap/layout without base-level alignment of raw long reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Compact representation of erroneous long 3GS reads by encoding each PacBio read as an ordered list of matched short-read contig anchors (k-mer matches), enabling fast overlap/layout without base-level alignment of raw long reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only long reads are available with no accurate short-read contigs — the compression step depends on NGS contig anchors When short-read assemblies have been gap-closed or scaffolded — README warns this yields poor final results due to errors from short-read assembly heuristics When a polished, base-level-accurate assembly is the immediate deliverable — this skill covers overlap/layout only; consensus/polishing (BLASR + Sparc/pbdagcon) is a separate step consuming ~90% of runtime

skills.description: Use when hybrid-assembling genomes with DBG2OLC: raw long 3GS reads must be converted to compact contig-identifier lists using accurate short-read DBG contigs before overlap, layout, and consensus.
skills.name: long-read-compression-via-kmer-anchoring
skills.search_text: long-read-compression-via-kmer-anchoring Use when hybrid-assembling genomes with DBG2OLC: raw long 3GS reads must be converted to compact contig-identifier lists using accurate short-read DBG contigs before overlap, layout, and consensus. The contigs are polished, gap-closed, or scaffolded rather than raw DBG contigs — the README warns this yields poor final results due to heuristics introduced by short-read assembly pipelines Only NGS short reads are available and no long reads exist to compress — the non-hybrid NGS assembly mode applies instead Long reads are already base-corrected or replaced by error-corrected overlaps (e.g., PacBioToCA/ECTools/MHAP/HGAP/Falcon correction pipelines) — DBG2OLC's design explicitly skips base-level errors, so pre-correction is unnecessary and the pipeline should not be mixed with other correction tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compress erroneous 3GS long reads (e.g., 20x PacBio FASTA) into ordered lists of contig identifiers by k-mer anchoring against preassembled NGS contigs, giving roughly a threefold read-length reduction that enables fast overlap/layout in DBG2OLC. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Compress erroneous 3GS long reads (e.g., 20x PacBio FASTA) into ordered lists of contig identifiers by k-mer anchoring against preassembled NGS contigs, giving roughly a threefold read-length reduction that enables fast overlap/layout in DBG2OLC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The contigs are polished, gap-closed, or scaffolded rather than raw DBG contigs — the README warns this yields poor final results due to heuristics introduced by short-read assembly pipelines Only NGS short reads are available and no long reads exist to compress — the non-hybrid NGS assembly mode applies instead Long reads are already base-corrected or replaced by error-corrected overlaps (e.g., PacBioToCA/ECTools/MHAP/HGAP/Falcon correction pipelines) — DBG2OLC's design explicitly skips base-level errors, so pre-correction is unnecessary and the pipeline should not be mixed with other correction tools

skills.description: Use when evaluating consensus-sequence quality of third-generation long reads — specifically when raw ONT/PacBio read error rates must be compared against SPOA/POA consensus error rates to compute a percentage error reduction.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-error-quantification
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-error-quantification Use when evaluating consensus-sequence quality of third-generation long reads — specifically when raw ONT/PacBio read error rates must be compared against SPOA/POA consensus error rates to compute a percentage error reduction. Input reads are already high-accuracy (e.g., Illumina or HiFi reads) — the skill targets error-prone third-generation reads where POA consensus yields substantial error reduction The goal is tandem repeat variant calling itself rather than benchmarking the consensus step's error reduction Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions such as centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Quantifies how much the POA-based (SPOA) consensus computation in TRiCoLOR's REFER module reduces per-base sequencing error of error-prone long reads, benchmarked against simulated ONT and PacBio data where reductions of ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) are reported. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Quantifies how much the POA-based (SPOA) consensus computation in TRiCoLOR's REFER module reduces per-base sequencing error of error-prone long reads, benchmarked against simulated ONT and PacBio data where reductions of ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) are reported.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already high-accuracy (e.g., Illumina or HiFi reads) — the skill targets error-prone third-generation reads where POA consensus yields substantial error reduction The goal is tandem repeat variant calling itself rather than benchmarking the consensus step's error reduction Repeats lie in unassembled genomic regions such as centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify

skills.description: Use when error-prone ONT/PacBio reads spanning candidate repetitive regions must be collapsed into haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences, e.g. as input to TR profiling or genotyping from haplotype-resolved BAMs.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-generation
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-generation Use when error-prone ONT/PacBio reads spanning candidate repetitive regions must be collapsed into haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences, e.g. as input to TR profiling or genotyping from haplotype-resolved BAMs. The target region lies in an unassembled part of the genome (e.g., human centromeres or telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats Input alignments are not haplotype-resolved, so haplotype-specific consensus sequences cannot be separated No reads entirely span the candidate region, leaving an insufficient read set for partial order alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates haplotype-specific, low-error consensus sequences from error-prone third-generation long reads (ONT/PacBio) by trimming reads that span a candidate region and applying SIMD-accelerated partial order alignment (POA) via SPOA, as done in TRiCoLOR's REFER module. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Generates haplotype-specific, low-error consensus sequences from error-prone third-generation long reads (ONT/PacBio) by trimming reads that span a candidate region and applying SIMD-accelerated partial order alignment (POA) via SPOA, as done in TRiCoLOR's REFER module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target region lies in an unassembled part of the genome (e.g., human centromeres or telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats Input alignments are not haplotype-resolved, so haplotype-specific consensus sequences cannot be separated No reads entirely span the candidate region, leaving an insufficient read set for partial order alignment

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore amplicon reads (2D or 1D2) from mock or mixed microbial communities are too error-prone (~15% raw error) and a de novo, reference-free full-length 16S consensus with ~99.5% accuracy is the analysis goal.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-generation
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-generation Use when raw nanopore amplicon reads (2D or 1D2) from mock or mixed microbial communities are too error-prone (~15% raw error) and a de novo, reference-free full-length 16S consensus with ~99.5% accuracy is the analysis goal. Input reads are short-read amplicon data (e.g., Illumina MiSeq, Ion Torrent PGM), whose short lengths make rolling-circle INC-Seq concatemer building inapplicable The goal is reference-based classification of raw long reads only — the article notes such approaches are limited in differentiating closely related sequences and risk false detections Reads are already high-quality consensus sequences or a processed OTU/feature table, so consensus generation would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates high-accuracy full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences from noisy ONT MinION amplicon reads using the NanoAmpli-Seq chain: INC-Seq rolling-circle consensus (>=3 concatemers), chopSeq fragmentation/orientation correction, and nanoClust partitioned de novo clustering with within-cluster consensus calling. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Generates high-accuracy full-length 16S rRNA gene consensus sequences from noisy ONT MinION amplicon reads using the NanoAmpli-Seq chain: INC-Seq rolling-circle consensus (>=3 concatemers), chopSeq fragmentation/orientation correction, and nanoClust partitioned de novo clustering with within-cluster consensus calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short-read amplicon data (e.g., Illumina MiSeq, Ion Torrent PGM), whose short lengths make rolling-circle INC-Seq concatemer building inapplicable The goal is reference-based classification of raw long reads only — the article notes such approaches are limited in differentiating closely related sequences and risk false detections Reads are already high-quality consensus sequences or a processed OTU/feature table, so consensus generation would be redundant

skills.description: Use when error-prone haplotype-resolved long-read alignments (BAM) over candidate repetitive regions must be condensed into accurate per-haplotype consensus sequences before motif/multiplicity profiling or downstream comparison to GRCh38.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-generation-via-partial-order-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-generation-via-partial-order-alignment Use when error-prone haplotype-resolved long-read alignments (BAM) over candidate repetitive regions must be condensed into accurate per-haplotype consensus sequences before motif/multiplicity profiling or downstream comparison to GRCh38. Input is raw unassembled FASTQ without prior haplotype-resolved alignment to a reference — TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved BAM input Target regions are in unassembled parts of the genome (centromeres, telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats Data are polyploid or from haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y), which TRiCoLOR does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Compute haplotype-specific, low-error consensus sequences from error-prone ONT or PacBio long reads aligned to repetitive loci, using partial order alignment (SPOA) as implemented inside the TRiCoLOR pipeline, reducing raw read error by ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) before motif resolution. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Compute haplotype-specific, low-error consensus sequences from error-prone ONT or PacBio long reads aligned to repetitive loci, using partial order alignment (SPOA) as implemented inside the TRiCoLOR pipeline, reducing raw read error by ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) before motif resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unassembled FASTQ without prior haplotype-resolved alignment to a reference — TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved BAM input Target regions are in unassembled parts of the genome (centromeres, telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats Data are polyploid or from haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y), which TRiCoLOR does not support

skills.description: Use when you have basecalled nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads for a small genome (e.g. Phage Lambda, E. coli, M. tuberculosis) and need a de novo assembly whose error rate quantifies basecaller quality against a known reference.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-polishing
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-polishing Use when you have basecalled nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads for a small genome (e.g. Phage Lambda, E. coli, M. tuberculosis) and need a de novo assembly whose error rate quantifies basecaller quality against a known reference. Input is Illumina short-read data — the draft layout step relies on pairwise alignment of overlapping long reads No reference genome exists for the organism, since the error-rate quantification step requires aligning the polished assembly to a reference with graphmap The goal is read-level basecalling accuracy (identity to reference reads) rather than assembly-level error rate — Chiron reports read-level accuracy separately using graphmap alignment of reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds de novo draft genomes from long nanopore basecalled reads with Minimap2/Miniasm, then iteratively polishes the consensus with 10 rounds of Racon using the same basecalled reads, and quantifies assembly error rate by aligning the polished assembly to a reference with graphmap. This is the workflow the Chiron paper used to convert basecaller accuracy differences into assembly error-rate comparisons. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: Builds de novo draft genomes from long nanopore basecalled reads with Minimap2/Miniasm, then iteratively polishes the consensus with 10 rounds of Racon using the same basecalled reads, and quantifies assembly error rate by aligning the polished assembly to a reference with graphmap. This is the workflow the Chiron paper used to convert basecaller accuracy differences into assembly error-rate comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Illumina short-read data — the draft layout step relies on pairwise alignment of overlapping long reads No reference genome exists for the organism, since the error-rate quantification step requires aligning the polished assembly to a reference with graphmap The goal is read-level basecalling accuracy (identity to reference reads) rather than assembly-level error rate — Chiron reports read-level accuracy separately using graphmap alignment of reads

skills.description: Use when a long-read (nanopore) genome assembly shows consensus-level base errors — e.g. low BUSCO completeness (3.0% complete / 92.9% missing in the uncorrected eel scaffolds) — and Illumina paired-end data from the same species is available for polishing.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-polishing
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-polishing Use when a long-read (nanopore) genome assembly shows consensus-level base errors — e.g. low BUSCO completeness (3.0% complete / 92.9% missing in the uncorrected eel scaffolds) — and Illumina paired-end data from the same species is available for polishing. The assembly already has near-complete BUSCO scores or no Illumina data from the species is available, so Racon-against-nanopore-only is the only option (the article notes nanopore-only consensus 'cannot be resolved by taking a consensus of nanopore data only') The input is raw reads rather than an assembled scaffold/contig set — assembly (e.g. with TULIP or Canu) must precede polishing Only short reads are available and no long-read assembly exists; this skill corrects long-read assemblies, not short-read-only drafts http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Post-assembly error correction pipeline in which a nanopore-based de novo assembly is first consensus-corrected with Racon against long reads, then polished with Pilon using quality-trimmed Illumina reads, with each stage assessed by BUSCO completeness against the vertebrata_odb9 lineage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Post-assembly error correction pipeline in which a nanopore-based de novo assembly is first consensus-corrected with Racon against long reads, then polished with Pilon using quality-trimmed Illumina reads, with each stage assessed by BUSCO completeness against the vertebrata_odb9 lineage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly already has near-complete BUSCO scores or no Illumina data from the species is available, so Racon-against-nanopore-only is the only option (the article notes nanopore-only consensus 'cannot be resolved by taking a consensus of nanopore data only') The input is raw reads rather than an assembled scaffold/contig set — assembly (e.g. with TULIP or Canu) must precede polishing Only short reads are available and no long-read assembly exists; this skill corrects long-read assemblies, not short-read-only drafts

skills.description: Use when a DBG2OLC (or similar) hybrid assembly backbone has been produced and base-level errors from high-error-rate third-generation reads (up to ~40% ONT MinION error) must be corrected before final assembly evaluation.
skills.name: long-read-consensus-polishing
skills.search_text: long-read-consensus-polishing Use when a DBG2OLC (or similar) hybrid assembly backbone has been produced and base-level errors from high-error-rate third-generation reads (up to ~40% ONT MinION error) must be corrected before final assembly evaluation. The backbone N50 from backbone_raw.fasta is unsatisfactory — the README says to keep tuning DBG2OLC parameters (AdaptiveTh, KmerCovTh, MinOverlap) and not proceed to consensus. The input is only short-read Illumina data with no long reads; this polishing step requires raw 3GS reads aligned to the backbone. The DBG contigs were produced with scaffolding or gap-closing (non-raw contigs), which the README warns introduces errors and degrades the final assembly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A consensus/polishing step for DBG2OLC hybrid assemblies in which BLASR aligns all raw long reads (e.g. Oxford Nanopore MinION or PacBio) to the backbone_raw.fasta and the Sparc sparsity-based consensus module corrects the backbone, reducing error rates from tens of percent down to ~0.23% on the polished E. coli MinION assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: A consensus/polishing step for DBG2OLC hybrid assemblies in which BLASR aligns all raw long reads (e.g. Oxford Nanopore MinION or PacBio) to the backbone_raw.fasta and the Sparc sparsity-based consensus module corrects the backbone, reducing error rates from tens of percent down to ~0.23% on the polished E. coli MinION assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The backbone N50 from backbone_raw.fasta is unsatisfactory — the README says to keep tuning DBG2OLC parameters (AdaptiveTh, KmerCovTh, MinOverlap) and not proceed to consensus. The input is only short-read Illumina data with no long reads; this polishing step requires raw 3GS reads aligned to the backbone. The DBG contigs were produced with scaffolding or gap-closing (non-raw contigs), which the README warns introduces errors and degrades the final assembly.

skills.description: Use when you need to scaffold/assemble a genome from high-error long reads (e.g. ONT MinION up to ~40% error, PacBio) by combining them with accurate Illumina DBG contigs, producing a backbone for later consensus polishing.
skills.name: long-read-contig-anchoring-and-layout
skills.search_text: long-read-contig-anchoring-and-layout Use when you need to scaffold/assemble a genome from high-error long reads (e.g. ONT MinION up to ~40% error, PacBio) by combining them with accurate Illumina DBG contigs, producing a backbone for later consensus polishing. The input contigs are already scaffolded or gap-closed — the README warns this introduces errors from short-read assembly heuristics and yields poor final results You want to interleave DBG2OLC with other assemblers or error-correction tools — the README states combining DBG2OLC with other software may produce worse results because many such tools introduce errors Base-level accuracy of the long reads is the target and no accurate short-read contigs are available — this skill skips base-level errors and requires DBG contigs as anchors; polishing is a separate Sparc/BLASR consensus step http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compress noisy third-generation long reads (PacBio/ONT MinION) by anchoring accurate de Bruijn graph contigs to them via k-mer matching, then overlap-layout the compressed reads to build an assembly backbone, as implemented in DBG2OLC. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Compress noisy third-generation long reads (PacBio/ONT MinION) by anchoring accurate de Bruijn graph contigs to them via k-mer matching, then overlap-layout the compressed reads to build an assembly backbone, as implemented in DBG2OLC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input contigs are already scaffolded or gap-closed — the README warns this introduces errors from short-read assembly heuristics and yields poor final results You want to interleave DBG2OLC with other assemblers or error-correction tools — the README states combining DBG2OLC with other software may produce worse results because many such tools introduce errors Base-level accuracy of the long reads is the target and no accurate short-read contigs are available — this skill skips base-level errors and requires DBG contigs as anchors; polishing is a separate Sparc/BLASR consensus step

skills.description: Use when you need to independently verify that assembled SV haplotype consensus contigs are real by aligning them to a finished diploid assembly and checking locus/orientation concordance.
skills.name: long-read-contig-to-assembly-mapping
skills.search_text: long-read-contig-to-assembly-mapping Use when you need to independently verify that assembled SV haplotype consensus contigs are real by aligning them to a finished diploid assembly and checking locus/orientation concordance. Input contigs were not assembled from mapped HiFi reads by sawfish (e.g. de novo whole-genome assemblies), since the expectation check depends on sawfish candidate breakpoint loci and breakend orientations Only a GRCh38 reference is available and no independent diploid assembly exists — mapping contigs back to the same reference used for discovery is circular and would not provide orthogonal validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Validates locally assembled SV haplotype contigs from sawfish by aligning them with pbmm2 to an independent diploid assembly (T2T-HG002-Q100v1.1) and computing the fraction that map back to the expected locus and breakend orientation, serving as an orthogonal precision check on SV calls. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Validates locally assembled SV haplotype contigs from sawfish by aligning them with pbmm2 to an independent diploid assembly (T2T-HG002-Q100v1.1) and computing the fraction that map back to the expected locus and breakend orientation, serving as an orthogonal precision check on SV calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs were not assembled from mapped HiFi reads by sawfish (e.g. de novo whole-genome assemblies), since the expectation check depends on sawfish candidate breakpoint loci and breakend orientations Only a GRCh38 reference is available and no independent diploid assembly exists — mapping contigs back to the same reference used for discovery is circular and would not provide orthogonal validation

skills.description: Use when evaluating how a long-read corrector's performance changes with input error rate or ploidy, e.g., simulated PacBio CLR triploid E. coli reads at 15% vs. 5% error.
skills.name: long-read-corrector-benchmarking
skills.search_text: long-read-corrector-benchmarking Use when evaluating how a long-read corrector's performance changes with input error rate or ploidy, e.g., simulated PacBio CLR triploid E. coli reads at 15% vs. 5% error. You need to evaluate computational resource usage — the paper notes VeChat 'does not win the competition in terms of computational resources', with longer runtimes and higher peak memory on large datasets You are optimizing preprocessing/error-correction/assembly pipeline combinations for polyploid, cancer, or metagenomic settings — the article states this exploration is beyond the study's scope and requires further efforts http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmarks long-read error correction (e.g., VeChat on simulated PacBio CLR reads from diploid/triploid/tetraploid genomes) by correcting raw read sets under varying sequencing error rates, realigning corrected reads with minimap2, and computing corrected-read error rates to quantify performance. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Benchmarks long-read error correction (e.g., VeChat on simulated PacBio CLR reads from diploid/triploid/tetraploid genomes) by correcting raw read sets under varying sequencing error rates, realigning corrected reads with minimap2, and computing corrected-read error rates to quantify performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to evaluate computational resource usage — the paper notes VeChat 'does not win the competition in terms of computational resources', with longer runtimes and higher peak memory on large datasets You are optimizing preprocessing/error-correction/assembly pipeline combinations for polyploid, cancer, or metagenomic settings — the article states this exploration is beyond the study's scope and requires further efforts

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how much long-read coverage an SV caller needs to match recall/precision, by comparing caller F1 against a GIAB truth set across a downsampled HiFi coverage series.
skills.name: long-read-coverage-downsampling
skills.search_text: long-read-coverage-downsampling Use when you must quantify how much long-read coverage an SV caller needs to match recall/precision, by comparing caller F1 against a GIAB truth set across a downsampled HiFi coverage series. Only a single full-coverage long-read callset is available and the goal is one-shot SV calling rather than coverage-saturation benchmarking The variant classes of interest are outside the 50-10,000 bp medium-size range that Blackbird targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Downsample PacBio HiFi long reads to a coverage ladder (5x, 10x, 20x, 34x) and benchmark SV callers (Blackbird hybrid mode vs Sniffles2 and PBSV) to identify the coverage at which F1-scores saturate on the HG002 GIAB benchmark. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Downsample PacBio HiFi long reads to a coverage ladder (5x, 10x, 20x, 34x) and benchmark SV callers (Blackbird hybrid mode vs Sniffles2 and PBSV) to identify the coverage at which F1-scores saturate on the HG002 GIAB benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single full-coverage long-read callset is available and the goal is one-shot SV calling rather than coverage-saturation benchmarking The variant classes of interest are outside the 50-10,000 bp medium-size range that Blackbird targets

skills.description: Use when you have a deep long-read dataset (e.g., PacBio) plus matching short reads and need to determine at what coverage an assembler's contiguity (NGA50) plateaus or improves most.
skills.name: long-read-coverage-subsampling
skills.search_text: long-read-coverage-subsampling Use when you have a deep long-read dataset (e.g., PacBio) plus matching short reads and need to determine at what coverage an assembler's contiguity (NGA50) plateaus or improves most. The long-read dataset is already at or below the target coverage, so subsampling would discard data without producing a meaningful depth comparison The goal is a single best-quality assembly at full available coverage rather than a sensitivity/benchmarking analysis across depths The input is ultra-long Oxford Nanopore reads, which HASLR does not yet support Short reads are absent, since the hybrid assembler requires both long reads and Illumina-style short reads from the same sample http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Systematically subsample a long-read FASTQ/FASTA (e.g., PacBio reads) to a ladder of target coverage depths using a longest-reads-first selection (HASLR's --cov-lr strategy), then run the hybrid assembler at each depth to quantify how assembly contiguity metrics such as NGA50 and genome fraction depend on long-read coverage. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Systematically subsample a long-read FASTQ/FASTA (e.g., PacBio reads) to a ladder of target coverage depths using a longest-reads-first selection (HASLR's --cov-lr strategy), then run the hybrid assembler at each depth to quantify how assembly contiguity metrics such as NGA50 and genome fraction depend on long-read coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long-read dataset is already at or below the target coverage, so subsampling would discard data without producing a meaningful depth comparison The goal is a single best-quality assembly at full available coverage rather than a sensitivity/benchmarking analysis across depths The input is ultra-long Oxford Nanopore reads, which HASLR does not yet support Short reads are absent, since the hybrid assembler requires both long reads and Illumina-style short reads from the same sample

skills.description: Use when assessing whether an SV caller retains recall/precision/F1 and genotype accuracy as long-read coverage drops, e.g. subsampling HG002 Hifi/CLR/ONT BAMs to 10x to compare against assembly-based baselines.
skills.name: long-read-coverage-subsampling
skills.search_text: long-read-coverage-subsampling Use when assessing whether an SV caller retains recall/precision/F1 and genotype accuracy as long-read coverage drops, e.g. subsampling HG002 Hifi/CLR/ONT BAMs to 10x to compare against assembly-based baselines. The goal is absolute SV detection accuracy at native coverage rather than sensitivity to depth — run each caller on the full BAMs instead. Applying VolcanoSV to sex chromosomes: the pipeline is designed only for autosomes because haplotype phasing differs for sex chromosomes. Evaluating small indel calling on ONT data, where assembly-based small indel detection was ineffective for all three tools (low precision). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Downsamples HG002 long-read BAMs (Hifi_L1-L5, CLR_L1-L3, ONT_L1-L6) with rasusa to graded coverage levels (40x, 30x, 20x, 10x, 5x) and benchmarks assembly-based SV callers (VolcanoSV, PAV, SVIM-asm, Dipcall) against the GIAB HG002 gold standard with Truvari to quantify robustness at low depth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Downsamples HG002 long-read BAMs (Hifi_L1-L5, CLR_L1-L3, ONT_L1-L6) with rasusa to graded coverage levels (40x, 30x, 20x, 10x, 5x) and benchmarks assembly-based SV callers (VolcanoSV, PAV, SVIM-asm, Dipcall) against the GIAB HG002 gold standard with Truvari to quantify robustness at low depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is absolute SV detection accuracy at native coverage rather than sensitivity to depth — run each caller on the full BAMs instead. Applying VolcanoSV to sex chromosomes: the pipeline is designed only for autosomes because haplotype phasing differs for sex chromosomes. Evaluating small indel calling on ONT data, where assembly-based small indel detection was ineffective for all three tools (low precision).

skills.description: Use when the input is a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR bam (e.g. 10X HG002 GRCh37) optionally paired with PacBio HiFi bam/FASTQ, and the goal is indel/SV (>50 bp) calling or runtime/memory benchmarking against long-read SV callers.
skills.name: long-read-dataset-handling
skills.search_text: long-read-dataset-handling Use when the input is a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR bam (e.g. 10X HG002 GRCh37) optionally paired with PacBio HiFi bam/FASTQ, and the goal is indel/SV (>50 bp) calling or runtime/memory benchmarking against long-read SV callers. The input is short-read-only data without BX barcode tags — Blackbird requires barcode information encoded in SLR reads The task needs whole-genome assembly — Blackbird deliberately avoids whole-genome assembly in favor of barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly Only long-read data are available and no SLR bam exists — Sniffles2 or PBSV alone are the appropriate long-read callers in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run Blackbird on synthetic long-read (SLR) datasets and hybrid SLR+long-read datasets for structural variant (50–10,000 bp) detection, and benchmark its runtime and memory against long-read callers such as Sniffles2 and PBSV on HG002. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Run Blackbird on synthetic long-read (SLR) datasets and hybrid SLR+long-read datasets for structural variant (50–10,000 bp) detection, and benchmark its runtime and memory against long-read callers such as Sniffles2 and PBSV on HG002.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read-only data without BX barcode tags — Blackbird requires barcode information encoded in SLR reads The task needs whole-genome assembly — Blackbird deliberately avoids whole-genome assembly in favor of barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly Only long-read data are available and no SLR bam exists — Sniffles2 or PBSV alone are the appropriate long-read callers in that setting

skills.description: Use when raw PacBio CLR or ONT long reads (FASTA/FASTQ, gzip allowed) from diploid, polyploid, or metagenomic mixed samples need error correction that preserves low-frequency haplotype variants prior to assembly or QV benchmarking.
skills.name: long-read-error-correction
skills.search_text: long-read-error-correction Use when raw PacBio CLR or ONT long reads (FASTA/FASTQ, gzip allowed) from diploid, polyploid, or metagenomic mixed samples need error correction that preserves low-frequency haplotype variants prior to assembly or QV benchmarking. The task is short-read error correction or polishing of an existing assembly with Illumina data — VeChat targets raw third-generation long reads. Runtime/peak memory are the primary constraints: on large datasets VeChat has longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competing correctors. Reads are already error-corrected or the goal is consensus polishing of contigs rather than haplotype-aware correction of raw reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Haplotype-aware error correction of noisy long reads (PacBio CLR, ONT) using variation graphs via VeChat, which prunes error-induced nodes/edges from POA-constructed graphs using frequent-itemset-based Support/Confidence thresholds instead of consensus-sequence templates that mask low-frequency haplotype variants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Haplotype-aware error correction of noisy long reads (PacBio CLR, ONT) using variation graphs via VeChat, which prunes error-induced nodes/edges from POA-constructed graphs using frequent-itemset-based Support/Confidence thresholds instead of consensus-sequence templates that mask low-frequency haplotype variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is short-read error correction or polishing of an existing assembly with Illumina data — VeChat targets raw third-generation long reads. Runtime/peak memory are the primary constraints: on large datasets VeChat has longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competing correctors. Reads are already error-corrected or the goal is consensus polishing of contigs rather than haplotype-aware correction of raw reads.

skills.description: Use when correcting raw Nanopore R9/R10 or PacBio CLR diploid long reads prior to assembly and heterozygous alleles (rather than only consensus accuracy) must be preserved.
skills.name: long-read-error-correction
skills.search_text: long-read-error-correction Use when correcting raw Nanopore R9/R10 or PacBio CLR diploid long reads prior to assembly and heterozygous alleles (rather than only consensus accuracy) must be preserved. Input is Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi reads, where the article reports PECAT achieves only mediocre correction/assembly performance The goal is maximum single-haplotype consensus accuracy regardless of heterozygote retention (e.g. a haploid reference polish), where standard POA consensus tools suffice Very low heterozygosity-rate regions are the focus, since the method cannot reliably distinguish small sequencing errors from heterozygote alleles there http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Haplotype-aware error correction of long noisy reads using a POA-graph method that scores supporting reads for same-haplotype membership so heterozygote alleles are retained while sequencing errors (typical of Nanopore R9/R10 and PacBio CLR data) are corrected. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Haplotype-aware error correction of long noisy reads using a POA-graph method that scores supporting reads for same-haplotype membership so heterozygote alleles are retained while sequencing errors (typical of Nanopore R9/R10 and PacBio CLR data) are corrected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi reads, where the article reports PECAT achieves only mediocre correction/assembly performance The goal is maximum single-haplotype consensus accuracy regardless of heterozygote retention (e.g. a haploid reference polish), where standard POA consensus tools suffice Very low heterozygosity-rate regions are the focus, since the method cannot reliably distinguish small sequencing errors from heterozygote alleles there

skills.description: Use when long nanopore reads or RCA-derived consensus sequences must be mapped to a reference genome (e.g. hg19) to identify back-splice junctions and full-length circRNA isoforms from isoCirc data.
skills.name: long-read-genome-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-alignment Use when long nanopore reads or RCA-derived consensus sequences must be mapped to a reference genome (e.g. hg19) to identify back-splice junctions and full-length circRNA isoforms from isoCirc data. Input is short-read RNA-seq (the article's motivation is that short-read RNA-seq does not experimentally determine full-length circRNA sequences); use short-read spliced alignment instead The aim is raw long-read alignment only (genomic ONT/PacBio reads) without isoCirc circRNA consensus filtering — use minimap2 directly with its standard presets (map-ont, splice) rather than via the isoCirc wrapper Sequences have not passed the TRF consensus-calling and min-copy 2.0 filtering steps; unfiltered RCA repeats will inflate false-positive BSJ calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aligns long nanopore reads or isoCirc consensus sequences to a reference genome using minimap2 with splice-aware, quality-tuned settings so back-splice junctions and full-length circRNA isoforms can be placed on genomic coordinates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Aligns long nanopore reads or isoCirc consensus sequences to a reference genome using minimap2 with splice-aware, quality-tuned settings so back-splice junctions and full-length circRNA isoforms can be placed on genomic coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq (the article's motivation is that short-read RNA-seq does not experimentally determine full-length circRNA sequences); use short-read spliced alignment instead The aim is raw long-read alignment only (genomic ONT/PacBio reads) without isoCirc circRNA consensus filtering — use minimap2 directly with its standard presets (map-ont, splice) rather than via the isoCirc wrapper Sequences have not passed the TRF consensus-calling and min-copy 2.0 filtering steps; unfiltered RCA repeats will inflate false-positive BSJ calls

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore long-read FASTQ/BAM data must be aligned to a reference genome before variant calling, and the analysis goal is SV/CNV detection where aligner choice affects call sets.
skills.name: long-read-genome-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-alignment Use when raw nanopore long-read FASTQ/BAM data must be aligned to a reference genome before variant calling, and the analysis goal is SV/CNV detection where aligner choice affects call sets. Input is short-read (Illumina) sequencing data — this skill is specific to long nanopore reads and long-read aligners (lra, minimap2, NGMLR) The task is coverage-based filtering of already-called SVs (deletions/duplications) — use disCoverage instead, which needs putative SV positions as input and is not an aligner or caller Reference build choice is already fixed and only one aligner is required — running the three-aligner comparison adds cost without benefit when the pipeline combination has already been decided http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns whole-genome nanopore (PromethION) reads against a human reference genome (hg38) with multiple long-read aligners — lra, minimap2, and NGMLR — producing one BAM per aligner as the basis for downstream SV calling. Aligner choice and reference build directly determine the sensitivity of large (>50 kb) CNV detection. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Aligns whole-genome nanopore (PromethION) reads against a human reference genome (hg38) with multiple long-read aligners — lra, minimap2, and NGMLR — producing one BAM per aligner as the basis for downstream SV calling. Aligner choice and reference build directly determine the sensitivity of large (>50 kb) CNV detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina) sequencing data — this skill is specific to long nanopore reads and long-read aligners (lra, minimap2, NGMLR) The task is coverage-based filtering of already-called SVs (deletions/duplications) — use disCoverage instead, which needs putative SV positions as input and is not an aligner or caller Reference build choice is already fixed and only one aligner is required — running the three-aligner comparison adds cost without benefit when the pipeline combination has already been decided

skills.description: Use when PacBio long-read (Iso-Seq style) RNA-seq reads must be mapped to a reference genome as the long-read half of a hybrid assembly, prior to merging with short-read alignments.
skills.name: long-read-genome-alignment-minimap2
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-alignment-minimap2 Use when PacBio long-read (Iso-Seq style) RNA-seq reads must be mapped to a reference genome as the long-read half of a hybrid assembly, prior to merging with short-read alignments. Input reads are short Illumina reads — the article aligns those with HISAT2 after fastp trimming, not minimap2 No assembled reference genome exists — the method requires a reference genome as a guide Goal is de novo transcriptome assembly without a reference; StringTie here is run in genome-guided mode on aligned BAMs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align PacBio long-read RNA-seq reads against a reference genome using minimap2 to produce a coordinate-sorted BAM suitable for downstream hybrid transcriptome assembly. In the chicken SCO workflow, minimap2 alignment of PacBio reads achieved ~34x read depth against galGal6. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Align PacBio long-read RNA-seq reads against a reference genome using minimap2 to produce a coordinate-sorted BAM suitable for downstream hybrid transcriptome assembly. In the chicken SCO workflow, minimap2 alignment of PacBio reads achieved ~34x read depth against galGal6.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads — the article aligns those with HISAT2 after fastp trimming, not minimap2 No assembled reference genome exists — the method requires a reference genome as a guide Goal is de novo transcriptome assembly without a reference; StringTie here is run in genome-guided mode on aligned BAMs

skills.description: Use when raw or corrected PacBio/ONT long reads and a reference genome are available and genome assemblies must be generated and compared across correction methods, or when polishing raw long-read assemblies is required.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly Use when raw or corrected PacBio/ONT long reads and a reference genome are available and genome assemblies must be generated and compared across correction methods, or when polishing raw long-read assemblies is required.
