Input is already an assembly or feature table rather than raw/corrected long reads — correction and assembly are not applicable Only short reads (Illumina) are available — the skill targets third-generation PacBio/ONT long reads The goal is de novo assembly without any reference genome — QUAST-LG evaluation and NGA50/NGA75 comparison against a reference cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Assemble long-read datasets (PacBio/ONT FASTA/FASTQ) using the Minimap2+Miniasm overlap-layout-consensus pipeline, with Flye for the H. sapiens chromosome 1 benchmark, then evaluate assemblies against a reference with QUAST-LG (contig counts, NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, errors per 100 kbp, misassemblies). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Assemble long-read datasets (PacBio/ONT FASTA/FASTQ) using the Minimap2+Miniasm overlap-layout-consensus pipeline, with Flye for the H. sapiens chromosome 1 benchmark, then evaluate assemblies against a reference with QUAST-LG (contig counts, NGA50, NGA75, genome coverage, errors per 100 kbp, misassemblies).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembly or feature table rather than raw/corrected long reads — correction and assembly are not applicable Only short reads (Illumina) are available — the skill targets third-generation PacBio/ONT long reads The goal is de novo assembly without any reference genome — QUAST-LG evaluation and NGA50/NGA75 comparison against a reference cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when assembling a diploid genome from long noisy reads (PacBio CLR or Nanopore R9/R10 FASTQ/FASTA) and haplotype-resolved, haplotype-specific contigs are needed without parental/trio data.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly Use when assembling a diploid genome from long noisy reads (PacBio CLR or Nanopore R9/R10 FASTQ/FASTA) and haplotype-resolved, haplotype-specific contigs are needed without parental/trio data. Input reads are high-accuracy PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — the article reports PECAT achieves 'mediocre performance' there and tools like Hifiasm are better suited The genome is haploid or non-diploid — the haplotype-aware correction and two-round phasing pipeline is designed for diploid genomes Data coverage is low and no additional coverage can be obtained — PECAT 'needs higher coverage of data' for high-quality phased assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 De novo diploid genome assembly from long noisy reads (PacBio CLR, Nanopore R9/R10) using PECAT, which combines haplotype-aware error correction that retains heterozygote alleles with a two-round string-graph assembly that removes inconsistent overlaps. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: De novo diploid genome assembly from long noisy reads (PacBio CLR, Nanopore R9/R10) using PECAT, which combines haplotype-aware error correction that retains heterozygote alleles with a two-round string-graph assembly that removes inconsistent overlaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are high-accuracy PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — the article reports PECAT achieves 'mediocre performance' there and tools like Hifiasm are better suited The genome is haploid or non-diploid — the haplotype-aware correction and two-round phasing pipeline is designed for diploid genomes Data coverage is low and no additional coverage can be obtained — PECAT 'needs higher coverage of data' for high-quality phased assembly

skills.description: Use when assembling low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads de novo and a high-quality reference genome (e.g., CHM13 v2.0) is available to partition reads chromosome-by-chromosome before assembly.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly Use when assembling low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads de novo and a high-quality reference genome (e.g., CHM13 v2.0) is available to partition reads chromosome-by-chromosome before assembly. Input is high-coverage (>~25-30x) HiFi data where hifiasm alone already resolves the genome without reference-guided binning. No high-quality, closely related reference genome is available — HiFiCCL is exclusively reference-guided and relies on mapping reads to a reference to partition chromosomes. The goal is chromosome-level scaffolding that must preserve true SVs: RagTag scaffolding overlooked true SVs (only 62.5% of inversion SVs detected), and Hi-C/nanopore integration is not yet implemented. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reference-guided, chromosome-by-chromosome de novo assembly of low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads using HiFiCCL combined with hifiasm, which partitions whole-genome reads into chromosomal bins with a high-quality reference and assembles each bin de novo to reduce misassembled contig length relative to hifiasm alone. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Reference-guided, chromosome-by-chromosome de novo assembly of low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads using HiFiCCL combined with hifiasm, which partitions whole-genome reads into chromosomal bins with a high-quality reference and assembles each bin de novo to reduce misassembled contig length relative to hifiasm alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is high-coverage (>~25-30x) HiFi data where hifiasm alone already resolves the genome without reference-guided binning. No high-quality, closely related reference genome is available — HiFiCCL is exclusively reference-guided and relies on mapping reads to a reference to partition chromosomes. The goal is chromosome-level scaffolding that must preserve true SVs: RagTag scaffolding overlooked true SVs (only 62.5% of inversion SVs detected), and Hi-C/nanopore integration is not yet implemented.

skills.description: Use when you have long-read FASTQ/FASTA datasets (e.g. HG002 PacBio HiFi or CycloneSEQ G400-ER) and need a de novo whole-genome assembly benchmarked on contiguity and accuracy against a reference.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly Use when you have long-read FASTQ/FASTA datasets (e.g. HG002 PacBio HiFi or CycloneSEQ G400-ER) and need a de novo whole-genome assembly benchmarked on contiguity and accuracy against a reference. You only need overlap detection or benchmarking of overlap quality (use Fedrann directly, not a full assembly pipeline) Input reads are short-read (Illumina) data; the overlap-layout-consensus workflow here targets long-read datasets A reference-guided assembly or variant calling against an existing reference is the goal rather than de novo reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 De novo assembly of whole genomes from long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi, ONT, BGI CycloneSEQ) via the overlap-layout-consensus paradigm, using Fedrann's k-mer feature extraction, IDF weighting, and sparse random projection with NNDescent to generate overlaps that feed Shasta assembly stages. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: De novo assembly of whole genomes from long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi, ONT, BGI CycloneSEQ) via the overlap-layout-consensus paradigm, using Fedrann's k-mer feature extraction, IDF weighting, and sparse random projection with NNDescent to generate overlaps that feed Shasta assembly stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need overlap detection or benchmarking of overlap quality (use Fedrann directly, not a full assembly pipeline) Input reads are short-read (Illumina) data; the overlap-layout-consensus workflow here targets long-read datasets A reference-guided assembly or variant calling against an existing reference is the goal rather than de novo reconstruction

skills.description: Use when you have HG002-style long-read BAM inputs (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) and need to run a phased diploid assembly pipeline and quantify its computational resource usage (memory, walltime, CPU hours) versus hifiasm or Flye+HapDup.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly-pipeline-execution Use when you have HG002-style long-read BAM inputs (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) and need to run a phased diploid assembly pipeline and quantify its computational resource usage (memory, walltime, CPU hours) versus hifiasm or Flye+HapDup. The sample is homozygous (e.g. CHM13 from a complete hydatidiform mole) — the phasing module is unsuitable, as the authors excluded VolcanoSV-asm for CHM13 diploid assembly Targeting sex chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes is very different You only need SV calls from an existing assembly — use VolcanoSV-vc on a pre-built assembly instead of re-running the assembly pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Execute chromosome-wise long-read diploid assembly with VolcanoSV-asm (volcanosv-asm.py), selecting the appropriate integrated assembler (hifiasm for HiFi, Flye for CLR/ONT) per data type, and record runtime and peak memory to benchmark against alternative assembly pipelines. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Execute chromosome-wise long-read diploid assembly with VolcanoSV-asm (volcanosv-asm.py), selecting the appropriate integrated assembler (hifiasm for HiFi, Flye for CLR/ONT) per data type, and record runtime and peak memory to benchmark against alternative assembly pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is homozygous (e.g. CHM13 from a complete hydatidiform mole) — the phasing module is unsuitable, as the authors excluded VolcanoSV-asm for CHM13 diploid assembly Targeting sex chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes is very different You only need SV calls from an existing assembly — use VolcanoSV-vc on a pre-built assembly instead of re-running the assembly pipeline

skills.description: Use when a set of corrected long reads (e.g., HECIL output LongRead_Corrected.fasta) must be benchmarked against baselines using assembly-based metrics (N50 via QUAST, dnadiff accuracy) plus k-mer and alignment metrics.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly-quality-assessment Use when a set of corrected long reads (e.g., HECIL output LongRead_Corrected.fasta) must be benchmarked against baselines using assembly-based metrics (N50 via QUAST, dnadiff accuracy) plus k-mer and alignment metrics. Input is raw, uncorrected PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads — this skill scores corrected read sets, so run a hybrid corrector (e.g., HECIL) first No reference genome is available for the organism, since the BLASR identity metrics and MUMmer dnadiff accuracy assessment both require aligning reads/assemblies to a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmarks error-corrected long-read sets by assembling them with Canu and scoring assembly quality (QUAST N50) and accuracy (MUMmer dnadiff), complemented by alignment-based metrics from Jellyfish unique k-mer counts and BLASR. Used in HECIL to show corrected reads outperform LSC, PacBioToCA, LoRDEC, proovread, and CoLoRMap. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Benchmarks error-corrected long-read sets by assembling them with Canu and scoring assembly quality (QUAST N50) and accuracy (MUMmer dnadiff), complemented by alignment-based metrics from Jellyfish unique k-mer counts and BLASR. Used in HECIL to show corrected reads outperform LSC, PacBioToCA, LoRDEC, proovread, and CoLoRMap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, uncorrected PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads — this skill scores corrected read sets, so run a hybrid corrector (e.g., HECIL) first No reference genome is available for the organism, since the BLASR identity metrics and MUMmer dnadiff accuracy assessment both require aligning reads/assemblies to a reference

skills.description: Use when a draft assembly (FASTA contigs) needs improved contiguity and matching long reads (e.g. ONT FASTQ such as SRR10028109) are available to provide mapping-supported contig joins.
skills.name: long-read-genome-scaffolding
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-scaffolding Use when a draft assembly (FASTA contigs) needs improved contiguity and matching long reads (e.g. ONT FASTQ such as SRR10028109) are available to provide mapping-supported contig joins. The draft assembly is already highly contiguous and long-read assemblers (e.g. Flye) have fully exhausted the long-range evidence — ntLink targets leftover join opportunities Only short paired-end reads are available and no long-read library exists for the sample, since ntLink scaffolding relies on long-read minimizer mappings The goal is misassembly correction rather than scaffolding — use ntLink mappings with Tigmint-long (Alternate Protocol 2) instead of the scaffold mode http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scaffold a draft genome assembly (e.g. a Flye contig FASTA) using long-read sequencing data with ntLink, a lightweight minimizer-based scaffolder that infers contig ordering/orientation from minimizer mappings rather than read alignments, optionally with overlap detection, gap-filling, or multiple in-code scaffolding rounds. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Scaffold a draft genome assembly (e.g. a Flye contig FASTA) using long-read sequencing data with ntLink, a lightweight minimizer-based scaffolder that infers contig ordering/orientation from minimizer mappings rather than read alignments, optionally with overlap detection, gap-filling, or multiple in-code scaffolding rounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The draft assembly is already highly contiguous and long-read assemblers (e.g. Flye) have fully exhausted the long-range evidence — ntLink targets leftover join opportunities Only short paired-end reads are available and no long-read library exists for the sample, since ntLink scaffolding relies on long-read minimizer mappings The goal is misassembly correction rather than scaffolding — use ntLink mappings with Tigmint-long (Alternate Protocol 2) instead of the scaffold mode

skills.description: Use when an unresolved rare-disease case is suspected to harbor a large-scale structural rearrangement and you have long-read sequencing data (ONT or PacBio) already aligned to a reference genome in BAM format.
skills.name: long-read-genomic-rearrangement-analysis
skills.search_text: long-read-genomic-rearrangement-analysis Use when an unresolved rare-disease case is suspected to harbor a large-scale structural rearrangement and you have long-read sequencing data (ONT or PacBio) already aligned to a reference genome in BAM format. The pathogenic variant is already resolved by short-read data or is an SNV/small indel, which short-read workflows detect well Input is raw long-read signal or unaligned reads — the skill requires an indexed BAM of alignments produced by a long-read-specific aligner A fully automated, no-user-verification SV caller output is required, since AgileStructure emphasizes user-guided exploration of breakpoint-spanning reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Detect and annotate large-scale genomic rearrangements from aligned long-read (PacBio or ONT) data using AgileStructure, a desktop application that identifies breakpoint-spanning split reads and supports user-guided interpretation of complex structural variant events. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Detect and annotate large-scale genomic rearrangements from aligned long-read (PacBio or ONT) data using AgileStructure, a desktop application that identifies breakpoint-spanning split reads and supports user-guided interpretation of complex structural variant events.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathogenic variant is already resolved by short-read data or is an SNV/small indel, which short-read workflows detect well Input is raw long-read signal or unaligned reads — the skill requires an indexed BAM of alignments produced by a long-read-specific aligner A fully automated, no-user-verification SV caller output is required, since AgileStructure emphasizes user-guided exploration of breakpoint-spanning reads

skills.description: Use when two long-read methylation/modification callers must be compared on the same aligned HiFi BAMs, with per-CpG read-level predictions scored against BS-seq labels to produce accuracy/sensitivity/specificity/AUC tables.
skills.name: long-read-genomics-benchmarking
skills.search_text: long-read-genomics-benchmarking Use when two long-read methylation/modification callers must be compared on the same aligned HiFi BAMs, with per-CpG read-level predictions scored against BS-seq labels to produce accuracy/sensitivity/specificity/AUC tables. The modification of interest is not 5mCpG — the models consider symmetric CpG methylation only and cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA Site-level (aggregate) methylation benchmarking is the goal — this skill targets single-molecule read-level evaluation; site-level comparisons use different models and correlation-to-BS-seq metrics Input reads are nanopore or short-read — the ccsmeth/primrose comparison is specific to PacBio CCS kinetics (IPD/PW) and HiFi reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking skill for head-to-head evaluation of long-read methylation callers (ccsmeth vs primrose) on PacBio HiFi/CCS reads, scoring read-level 5mCpG predictions against bisulfite-sequencing ground truth with accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC AUC. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for head-to-head evaluation of long-read methylation callers (ccsmeth vs primrose) on PacBio HiFi/CCS reads, scoring read-level 5mCpG predictions against bisulfite-sequencing ground truth with accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC AUC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modification of interest is not 5mCpG — the models consider symmetric CpG methylation only and cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs, non-CpG 5mCs, or other modifications such as 6mA Site-level (aggregate) methylation benchmarking is the goal — this skill targets single-molecule read-level evaluation; site-level comparisons use different models and correlation-to-BS-seq metrics Input reads are nanopore or short-read — the ccsmeth/primrose comparison is specific to PacBio CCS kinetics (IPD/PW) and HiFi reads

skills.description: Use when you have a long-read bam/cram plus its reference genome and a fasta of insertion sequences (e.g. Alu, L1, SVA, HERV) and need to call non-reference TE insertions with haplotype/genotype support in VCF.
skills.name: long-read-genotyping
skills.search_text: long-read-genotyping Use when you have a long-read bam/cram plus its reference genome and a fasta of insertion sequences (e.g. Alu, L1, SVA, HERV) and need to call non-reference TE insertions with haplotype/genotype support in VCF. Input is short-read data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data such as PacBio or ONT You need only reference-known TE calls from an annotated reference rather than non-reference insertion detection Coverage exceeds the --maxreads cap (default 100); calls in regions exceeding given coverage are avoided, so re-tune parameters or use a different caller http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Detect and genotype non-reference transposable element insertions from long-read (PacBio/ONT) data using sTELLeR, which clusters split-read insertion signatures, aligns candidate insertions to a TE fasta with minimap2, and emits haplotype-aware VCF calls. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Detect and genotype non-reference transposable element insertions from long-read (PacBio/ONT) data using sTELLeR, which clusters split-read insertion signatures, aligns candidate insertions to a TE fasta with minimap2, and emits haplotype-aware VCF calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data such as PacBio or ONT You need only reference-known TE calls from an annotated reference rather than non-reference insertion detection Coverage exceeds the --maxreads cap (default 100); calls in regions exceeding given coverage are avoided, so re-tune parameters or use a different caller

skills.description: Use when ONT long reads carry methylation tags (MM/ML) and existing SNV-only phase blocks from HapCUT2 or WhatsHap need to be joined into longer autosomal phase blocks.
skills.name: long-read-haplotype-phasing
skills.search_text: long-read-haplotype-phasing Use when ONT long reads carry methylation tags (MM/ML) and existing SNV-only phase blocks from HapCUT2 or WhatsHap need to be joined into longer autosomal phase blocks. Phasing sex chromosomes (X/Y) — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent methylation haplotype patterns; restrict to autosomes Coverage below ~30X ONT, since SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage A BAM containing secondary or supplementary alignments, which triggers a pysam MM tag reading error — filter with `samtools view -bF 2304` first http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Chain SNV-based phase blocks into chromosome-scale blocks using allele-specific CpG methylation from ONT MM/ML tags (MethPhaser), applied after HapCUT2/WhatsHap SNV phasing. Extends phase-block N50 by 78%-151% on ONT R9/R10 data with only a minimal switch-error cost. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Chain SNV-based phase blocks into chromosome-scale blocks using allele-specific CpG methylation from ONT MM/ML tags (MethPhaser), applied after HapCUT2/WhatsHap SNV phasing. Extends phase-block N50 by 78%-151% on ONT R9/R10 data with only a minimal switch-error cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Phasing sex chromosomes (X/Y) — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent methylation haplotype patterns; restrict to autosomes Coverage below ~30X ONT, since SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage A BAM containing secondary or supplementary alignments, which triggers a pysam MM tag reading error — filter with `samtools view -bF 2304` first

skills.description: Use when you must identify heterozygous SNP sites from Nanopore/PacBio long reads aligned to haplotype-collapsed contigs (e.g., to phase reads or flag inconsistent overlaps in a diploid string-graph assembly).
skills.name: long-read-heterozygous-snp-calling
skills.search_text: long-read-heterozygous-snp-calling Use when you must identify heterozygous SNP sites from Nanopore/PacBio long reads aligned to haplotype-collapsed contigs (e.g., to phase reads or flag inconsistent overlaps in a diploid string-graph assembly). Input reads are PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — PECAT achieves only mediocre performance there, and Hifiasm-style corrected-read SNP calling suffices for HiFi Heterozygosity is very low (<0.0005): PECAT's error correction may not distinguish small sequencing errors from heterozygote alleles, so corrected-read SNP calls alone are unreliable You already have a trusted diploid de novo assembly and only need SV comparison — use hapdiff instead of re-calling SNPs from reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Call heterozygous SNP sites from long noisy reads mapped to a haplotype-collapsed assembly, combining a corrected-read SNP caller (base-frequency/second-most-common-base criteria) with a raw-read caller (Clair3 for Nanopore) so SNP alleles can drive inconsistent-overlap identification in PECAT's diploid assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Call heterozygous SNP sites from long noisy reads mapped to a haplotype-collapsed assembly, combining a corrected-read SNP caller (base-frequency/second-most-common-base criteria) with a raw-read caller (Clair3 for Nanopore) so SNP alleles can drive inconsistent-overlap identification in PECAT's diploid assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — PECAT achieves only mediocre performance there, and Hifiasm-style corrected-read SNP calling suffices for HiFi Heterozygosity is very low (<0.0005): PECAT's error correction may not distinguish small sequencing errors from heterozygote alleles, so corrected-read SNP calls alone are unreliable You already have a trusted diploid de novo assembly and only need SV comparison — use hapdiff instead of re-calling SNPs from reads

skills.description: Use when you have long-read WGS FASTQ data (ONT PromethION or PacBio HiFi) from a sample with unknown HLA type and need group-level HLA-I/II predictions using a single Unix pipeline command.
skills.name: long-read-hla-typing
skills.search_text: long-read-hla-typing Use when you have long-read WGS FASTQ data (ONT PromethION or PacBio HiFi) from a sample with unknown HLA type and need group-level HLA-I/II predictions using a single Unix pipeline command. Input is short Illumina-sized reads — use HPTASR (targeted assembly) mode instead; BEST SHORT READ RESULTS ARE OBTAINED WITH HPTASR WITH READS 100bp AND UP The analysis requires full allele-level (4-digit) resolution validated clinically rather than group-level predictions — HPRA streaming reports group-level and top-scoring allele predictions that may be ambiguous Only bulky SAM/alignment files are wanted as persistent outputs — the streaming approach deliberately avoids writing .sam to disk http://edamontology.org/topic_3930 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Predicts HLA class I and II allele groups from whole-genome shotgun long-read (ONT/PacBio) sequencing data by streaming minimap2 SAM alignments directly into HLAminer (HPRA mode), avoiding storage of bulky alignment files on disk. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Predicts HLA class I and II allele groups from whole-genome shotgun long-read (ONT/PacBio) sequencing data by streaming minimap2 SAM alignments directly into HLAminer (HPRA mode), avoiding storage of bulky alignment files on disk.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short Illumina-sized reads — use HPTASR (targeted assembly) mode instead; BEST SHORT READ RESULTS ARE OBTAINED WITH HPTASR WITH READS 100bp AND UP The analysis requires full allele-level (4-digit) resolution validated clinically rather than group-level predictions — HPRA streaming reports group-level and top-scoring allele predictions that may be ambiguous Only bulky SAM/alignment files are wanted as persistent outputs — the streaming approach deliberately avoids writing .sam to disk

skills.description: Use when choosing a host-assignment strategy (e.g., Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, MEGAN-LR, minimap2 variants, read-overlapping) for ARG-carrying long reads and you need quantitative misclassification benchmarks before deployment.
skills.name: long-read-host-identification-evaluation
skills.search_text: long-read-host-identification-evaluation Use when choosing a host-assignment strategy (e.g., Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, MEGAN-LR, minimap2 variants, read-overlapping) for ARG-carrying long reads and you need quantitative misclassification benchmarks before deployment. When the goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited When reads fall below ~1x genome copy coverage, since inadequate read overlaps make clustering unstable and host classification unreliable When the target species is absent from the reference database, since all strategies here (including read-overlapping) are inherently reference-based and may misclassify unseen species http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A simulation-based benchmark skill for quantifying how accurately different taxonomic assignment strategies identify the hosts of ARG-carrying long reads, by computing per-species and overall misclassification rates in simulated high-quality (HQ) and low-quality (LQ) metagenomes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: A simulation-based benchmark skill for quantifying how accurately different taxonomic assignment strategies identify the hosts of ARG-carrying long reads, by computing per-species and overall misclassification rates in simulated high-quality (HQ) and low-quality (LQ) metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited When reads fall below ~1x genome copy coverage, since inadequate read overlaps make clustering unstable and host classification unreliable When the target species is absent from the reference database, since all strategies here (including read-overlapping) are inherently reference-based and may misclassify unseen species

skills.description: Use when noisy long reads (e.g. PacBio E. coli, S. cerevisiae, or heterozygous A. funestus flowcell data) must be corrected with matched Illumina short reads, and alignment/assembly-based correction quality metrics are needed.
skills.name: long-read-hybrid-error-correction
skills.search_text: long-read-hybrid-error-correction Use when noisy long reads (e.g. PacBio E. coli, S. cerevisiae, or heterozygous A. funestus flowcell data) must be corrected with matched Illumina short reads, and alignment/assembly-based correction quality metrics are needed. No matching short reads are available — HECIL is a hybrid corrector requiring aligned Illumina reads (self-correcting methods like HGAP are a different approach) The long reads are already high quality or have been corrected (e.g. Canu-corrected reads are only further improved as a downstream assembly-refinement option) The goal is de novo assembly only without correction — assembly alone with Canu does not substitute for correction and evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Hybrid error correction of noisy third-generation long reads (PacBio/Sequel, Oxford Nanopore) using high-quality Illumina short reads, implemented as HECIL: quick consensus correction plus optimization-based correction, optionally enhanced by an iterative learning loop that realigns and re-corrects across iterations. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Hybrid error correction of noisy third-generation long reads (PacBio/Sequel, Oxford Nanopore) using high-quality Illumina short reads, implemented as HECIL: quick consensus correction plus optimization-based correction, optionally enhanced by an iterative learning loop that realigns and re-corrects across iterations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matching short reads are available — HECIL is a hybrid corrector requiring aligned Illumina reads (self-correcting methods like HGAP are a different approach) The long reads are already high quality or have been corrected (e.g. Canu-corrected reads are only further improved as a downstream assembly-refinement option) The goal is de novo assembly only without correction — assembly alone with Canu does not substitute for correction and evaluation

skills.description: Use when long-read alignments (BAM) must be genotyped for a predefined panel of InDel sites supplied as a BED configure file, applying homopolymer (default length 4) and Q15 base-quality filters, or when benchmarking InDel calls against DeepVariant at targeted loci.
skills.name: long-read-indel-genotyping
skills.search_text: long-read-indel-genotyping Use when long-read alignments (BAM) must be genotyped for a predefined panel of InDel sites supplied as a BED configure file, applying homopolymer (default length 4) and Q15 base-quality filters, or when benchmarking InDel calls against DeepVariant at targeted loci. Reads are raw BAM/FASTQ not yet aligned, sorted, and indexed — preprocess first with MH_umi_dedup_map_pipe.sh (BAM to fastq, QC, UMI analysis, read-reference alignment) The goal is genome-wide discovery of novel InDels rather than genotyping a predefined targeted panel — MacroHapCaller only reports sites listed in the BED configure file InDels of interest lie inside homopolymer regions (homopolymerLen default 4) — candidates inside homopolymers are deliberately skipped by the caller http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Genotyping of targeted InDel loci from long-read (e.g. PacBio HiFi) BAM alignments using MacroHapCaller, which scans CIGAR I/D operations at BED-configured 0-based sites and filters candidates by homopolymer exclusion and Phred Q15 insert quality. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Genotyping of targeted InDel loci from long-read (e.g. PacBio HiFi) BAM alignments using MacroHapCaller, which scans CIGAR I/D operations at BED-configured 0-based sites and filters candidates by homopolymer exclusion and Phred Q15 insert quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are raw BAM/FASTQ not yet aligned, sorted, and indexed — preprocess first with MH_umi_dedup_map_pipe.sh (BAM to fastq, QC, UMI analysis, read-reference alignment) The goal is genome-wide discovery of novel InDels rather than genotyping a predefined targeted panel — MacroHapCaller only reports sites listed in the BED configure file InDels of interest lie inside homopolymer regions (homopolymerLen default 4) — candidates inside homopolymers are deliberately skipped by the caller

skills.description: Use when tumor/control paired long-read (ONT or PacBio) data contain somatic insertion calls whose full-length inserted sequences must be classified by mobile element type and characterized for truncation, inversion, transduction, and source-element properties.
skills.name: long-read-insertion-sequence-characterization
skills.search_text: long-read-insertion-sequence-characterization Use when tumor/control paired long-read (ONT or PacBio) data contain somatic insertion calls whose full-length inserted sequences must be classified by mobile element type and characterized for truncation, inversion, transduction, and source-element properties. Detecting somatic VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion events — the article notes the reference-genome-based framework may not capture long repeat expansion events because the reference is unreliable at susceptible loci SVs where both breakpoints lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions such as centromeres — the Single breakend module cannot detect these Subclonal MEIs present in a minority of cells — detection is challenging at modest sequencing depth http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 A nanomonsv-based workflow that classifies somatic mobile element insertions (LINE1, Alu, SVA, processed pseudogenes) from full-length inserted sequences recovered by paired tumor/control long-read sequencing, and annotates properties such as 5' truncations, internal inversions, polyA tails, target site duplications, and LINE1 3' transduction source sites. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: A nanomonsv-based workflow that classifies somatic mobile element insertions (LINE1, Alu, SVA, processed pseudogenes) from full-length inserted sequences recovered by paired tumor/control long-read sequencing, and annotates properties such as 5' truncations, internal inversions, polyA tails, target site duplications, and LINE1 3' transduction source sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Detecting somatic VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion events — the article notes the reference-genome-based framework may not capture long repeat expansion events because the reference is unreliable at susceptible loci SVs where both breakpoints lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions such as centromeres — the Single breakend module cannot detect these Subclonal MEIs present in a minority of cells — detection is challenging at modest sequencing depth

skills.description: Use when molecule consensus BAMs from Nanopore scRNA-seq must be assigned to annotated Gencode isoforms and the resulting isoform-level UMI count matrices need verification against reported assignment rates and per-cell medians.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-assignment-quality-verification
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-assignment-quality-verification Use when molecule consensus BAMs from Nanopore scRNA-seq must be assigned to annotated Gencode isoforms and the resulting isoform-level UMI count matrices need verification against reported assignment rates and per-cell medians. Input is raw Nanopore FASTQ rather than UMI-consensus molecules — the full-match isoform assignment requires consensus sequences per UMI (Step 4b), not raw noisy reads The goal is novel isoform discovery or unannotated transcript models — IsoformMatrix STRICT mode only assigns UMIs whose exon structure fully matches annotated Gencode transcripts Working with short-read 10x data alone, which lacks full-length transcript information needed for isoform-level assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Verifies that UMI consensus molecules from Nanopore long-read single-cell data are correctly assigned to known Gencode transcript isoforms by full exonic-structure matching, using Sicelore's IsoformMatrix with STRICT method, and validates the resulting gene-/isoform-level count matrices against expected assignment rates and per-cell yields. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Verifies that UMI consensus molecules from Nanopore long-read single-cell data are correctly assigned to known Gencode transcript isoforms by full exonic-structure matching, using Sicelore's IsoformMatrix with STRICT method, and validates the resulting gene-/isoform-level count matrices against expected assignment rates and per-cell yields.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Nanopore FASTQ rather than UMI-consensus molecules — the full-match isoform assignment requires consensus sequences per UMI (Step 4b), not raw noisy reads The goal is novel isoform discovery or unannotated transcript models — IsoformMatrix STRICT mode only assigns UMIs whose exon structure fully matches annotated Gencode transcripts Working with short-read 10x data alone, which lacks full-length transcript information needed for isoform-level assignment

skills.description: Use when you have isocirc.out records from isoCirc long-read circRNA catalogs (12 human tissues + HEK293) and need to recover exact exonic compositions and count internal alternative splicing events within circRNAs.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-block-structure-parsing
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-block-structure-parsing Use when you have isocirc.out records from isoCirc long-read circRNA catalogs (12 human tissues + HEK293) and need to recover exact exonic compositions and count internal alternative splicing events within circRNAs. Input is short-read RNA-seq data (e.g., RNase R-treated libraries) — short reads do not determine full-length circRNA sequences or internal splicing events Input is a circRNA catalog lacking per-isoform block structure (e.g., BSJ-only records from circBase/MiOncoCirc) — internal event classification requires blockType/blockStarts/blockSize The goal is BSJ discovery rather than internal isoform composition — use the upstream isocirc pipeline BSJ-calling step instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Parses full-length circRNA isoform records from isoCirc's isocirc.out (blockType, blockStarts, blockSize fields) to reconstruct each isoform's exact exonic composition and classify internal alternative splicing events (skipped exon, alt 5' splice site, alt 3' splice site, retained intron) within circRNAs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Parses full-length circRNA isoform records from isoCirc's isocirc.out (blockType, blockStarts, blockSize fields) to reconstruct each isoform's exact exonic composition and classify internal alternative splicing events (skipped exon, alt 5' splice site, alt 3' splice site, retained intron) within circRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data (e.g., RNase R-treated libraries) — short reads do not determine full-length circRNA sequences or internal splicing events Input is a circRNA catalog lacking per-isoform block structure (e.g., BSJ-only records from circBase/MiOncoCirc) — internal event classification requires blockType/blockStarts/blockSize The goal is BSJ discovery rather than internal isoform composition — use the upstream isocirc pipeline BSJ-calling step instead

skills.description: Use when you have a populated isoSeQL SQLite database (isoform, counts, isoform_ends, ends_counts, sampleData, exp tables) and need to compare isoforms, counts, or splice junction ends across multiple Iso-Seq samples.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-database-querying
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-database-querying Use when you have a populated isoSeQL SQLite database (isoform, counts, isoform_ends, ends_counts, sampleData, exp tables) and need to compare isoforms, counts, or splice junction ends across multiple Iso-Seq samples. Input is raw subreads or unannotated HiFi reads — the upstream phase (i) database population (isoseq > minimap2/pbmm2 > cDNA_Cupcake > SQANTI3 + sqanti3_RulesFilter.py) must run first Only a single sample exists with no cross-sample comparison needed — the mismatched PB.X.Y identifier problem and intersection plots only matter across multiple datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Phase (ii) of isoSeQL usage: query a consolidated SQLite database built from SQANTI3-filtered classification files to extract sample metadata, isoform-by-sample count matrices, structural-category plots, cross-sample UpSet plots, and start/end read distributions, or write custom SQL queries against the database. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: Phase (ii) of isoSeQL usage: query a consolidated SQLite database built from SQANTI3-filtered classification files to extract sample metadata, isoform-by-sample count matrices, structural-category plots, cross-sample UpSet plots, and start/end read distributions, or write custom SQL queries against the database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw subreads or unannotated HiFi reads — the upstream phase (i) database population (isoseq > minimap2/pbmm2 > cDNA_Cupcake > SQANTI3 + sqanti3_RulesFilter.py) must run first Only a single sample exists with no cross-sample comparison needed — the mismatched PB.X.Y identifier problem and intersection plots only matter across multiple datasets

skills.description: Use when you have a collapsed representative isoform FASTA from long-read single-cell isoform sequencing (e.g., HIT-scISOseq) and need SQANTI3 structural classification plus rules filtering to quantify retained isoforms per sample.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-quality-control
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-quality-control Use when you have a collapsed representative isoform FASTA from long-read single-cell isoform sequencing (e.g., HIT-scISOseq) and need SQANTI3 structural classification plus rules filtering to quantify retained isoforms per sample. Input is still raw CCS or FLNC reads that have not yet been collapsed into non-redundant isoforms — collapse first (e.g., cDNA_Cupcake collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py or isoseq3 collapse) Goal is demultiplexing HIT-scISOseq concatenated reads into single-cell cDNA reads — use scISA-Tools instead Reference annotation/genome for the sample's species are unavailable, since SQANTI3 QC classification against ref.genes.gtf/ref.genome.fa is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Characterize, quality-control, and structurally classify non-redundant long-read isoforms with SQANTI3, tallying structural categories (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, antisense, genic) and applying filters to obtain the final retained isoform set per sample. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Characterize, quality-control, and structurally classify non-redundant long-read isoforms with SQANTI3, tallying structural categories (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, antisense, genic) and applying filters to obtain the final retained isoform set per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw CCS or FLNC reads that have not yet been collapsed into non-redundant isoforms — collapse first (e.g., cDNA_Cupcake collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py or isoseq3 collapse) Goal is demultiplexing HIT-scISOseq concatenated reads into single-cell cDNA reads — use scISA-Tools instead Reference annotation/genome for the sample's species are unavailable, since SQANTI3 QC classification against ref.genes.gtf/ref.genome.fa is required

skills.description: Use when you have SQANTI3 classification.txt output for multiple Iso-Seq samples whose PB.X.Y isoform IDs cannot be matched across samples, and you need a cross-sample isoform/read-count database that can absorb new samples on later runs.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-read-count-tracking
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-read-count-tracking Use when you have SQANTI3 classification.txt output for multiple Iso-Seq samples whose PB.X.Y isoform IDs cannot be matched across samples, and you need a cross-sample isoform/read-count database that can absorb new samples on later runs. You have only a single sample and no need to match isoform IDs across runs — per-sample SQANTI3 output is sufficient Input transcripts have not yet been annotated/filtered through SQANTI3 (e.g. raw cluster BAMs or cDNA_Cupcake collapse output) — run sqanti3_RulesFilter.py first Your goal is raw Iso-Seq read processing (ccs, lima, isoseq refine/cluster2) rather than cross-sample isoform comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Populates an updatable SQLite database (isoseql.db) from per-sample SQANTI3 RulesFilter-filtered classification.txt files, defining isoforms by intron chain so cross-sample PB.X.Y IDs are consolidated into stable common-junction isoform IDs with a separate start/end coordinate (isoform_ends/ends_counts) table. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: Populates an updatable SQLite database (isoseql.db) from per-sample SQANTI3 RulesFilter-filtered classification.txt files, defining isoforms by intron chain so cross-sample PB.X.Y IDs are consolidated into stable common-junction isoform IDs with a separate start/end coordinate (isoform_ends/ends_counts) table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single sample and no need to match isoform IDs across runs — per-sample SQANTI3 output is sufficient Input transcripts have not yet been annotated/filtered through SQANTI3 (e.g. raw cluster BAMs or cDNA_Cupcake collapse output) — run sqanti3_RulesFilter.py first Your goal is raw Iso-Seq read processing (ccs, lima, isoseq refine/cluster2) rather than cross-sample isoform comparison

skills.description: Use when deciding how a collapsing/merging tool (isoseq collapse, gffcompare) treats transcripts with identical intron chains but variable 5'/3' ends, e.g., when variable ends across samples risk being discarded into a single full-length isoform entry.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-variable-end-analysis
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-variable-end-analysis Use when deciding how a collapsing/merging tool (isoseq collapse, gffcompare) treats transcripts with identical intron chains but variable 5'/3' ends, e.g., when variable ends across samples risk being discarded into a single full-length isoform entry. Input transcripts differ in intron chain, not just in 5'/3' end coordinates — the skill specifically probes variable ends on a shared intron chain. The goal is cross-sample isoform comparison by matched IDs (PB.X.Y), which isoSeQL addresses rather than collapse-behavior benchmarking. Only one collapsing tool is of interest and no tool-to-tool asymmetry comparison is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmark-style skill for testing how transcript collapsing/merging tools handle 5'/3' end variability when transcripts share an intron chain: synthetic truncated variants of a reference isoform (e.g., LPAR3 ENST00000440086.1) are collapsed with isoseq collapse and merged with gffcompare, and their outputs are compared to determine whether start/end coordinate variability is retained. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: A benchmark-style skill for testing how transcript collapsing/merging tools handle 5'/3' end variability when transcripts share an intron chain: synthetic truncated variants of a reference isoform (e.g., LPAR3 ENST00000440086.1) are collapsed with isoseq collapse and merged with gffcompare, and their outputs are compared to determine whether start/end coordinate variability is retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transcripts differ in intron chain, not just in 5'/3' end coordinates — the skill specifically probes variable ends on a shared intron chain. The goal is cross-sample isoform comparison by matched IDs (PB.X.Y), which isoSeQL addresses rather than collapse-behavior benchmarking. Only one collapsing tool is of interest and no tool-to-tool asymmetry comparison is needed.

skills.description: Use when input is a long-read (e.g., PacBio HiFi) read-reference BAM and targeted STR/SNP/InDel configure files, and you need read-backed phased multi-allelic macrohaplotypes — including variants (private mutations) not listed in the configure files.
skills.name: long-read-macrohaplotype-calling
skills.search_text: long-read-macrohaplotype-calling Use when input is a long-read (e.g., PacBio HiFi) read-reference BAM and targeted STR/SNP/InDel configure files, and you need read-backed phased multi-allelic macrohaplotypes — including variants (private mutations) not listed in the configure files. The analysis goal is short-read (NGS) phasing — MacroHapCaller is designed for long reads such as PacBio HiFi. You need a validated tool for untargeted whole-genome variant discovery: MacroHapCaller genotypes targeted STR/SNP/InDel loci defined by configure files, not de novo discovery across the genome. Output haplotypes only need STR allele sizing/comparison without phased SNP/InDel/STR combinations — USAT handles post-hoc haplotype comparison instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Genotype and phase targeted STR, SNP, and InDel variants into macrohaplotype strings from long PacBio HiFi reads using MacroHapCaller, including an extension to retain private variants absent from the user-supplied configure files (which stock MacroHapCaller discards). genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Genotype and phase targeted STR, SNP, and InDel variants into macrohaplotype strings from long PacBio HiFi reads using MacroHapCaller, including an extension to retain private variants absent from the user-supplied configure files (which stock MacroHapCaller discards).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is short-read (NGS) phasing — MacroHapCaller is designed for long reads such as PacBio HiFi. You need a validated tool for untargeted whole-genome variant discovery: MacroHapCaller genotypes targeted STR/SNP/InDel loci defined by configure files, not de novo discovery across the genome. Output haplotypes only need STR allele sizing/comparison without phased SNP/InDel/STR combinations — USAT handles post-hoc haplotype comparison instead.

skills.description: Use when evaluating how many k-mers and synthetic mate-pair read pairs from raw or Lordec-corrected long reads are recovered against an Illumina assembly, e.g. benchmarking alignment-free library extraction.

skills.search_text: long-read-recall-assessment-against-assembly Use when evaluating how many k-mers and synthetic mate-pair read pairs from raw or Lordec-corrected long reads are recovered against an Illumina assembly, e.g. benchmarking alignment-free library extraction. The goal is de novo hybrid assembly of large genomes (e.g. NA12878, Arabidopsis) rather than benchmarking library-extraction recall against an existing assembly. The long reads already come from true long-range mate-pair technologies (10X Genomics, DOVETAIL genomics) where insert sizes and pair orientation vary, making recall against a synthetic-library ground truth ill-defined. The reference assembly is not from the same organism/sample as the long reads, so recovered k-mers and pairs are not meaningful recall. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies how faithfully Fast-SG extracts synthetic mate-pair libraries from raw versus hybrid error-corrected ONT (R9.2) and PacBio Sequel long reads, by computing k-mer recall, synthetic mate-pair read recall, and outlier-pair percentage against an Illumina reference assembly (E. coli K12). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Quantifies how faithfully Fast-SG extracts synthetic mate-pair libraries from raw versus hybrid error-corrected ONT (R9.2) and PacBio Sequel long reads, by computing k-mer recall, synthetic mate-pair read recall, and outlier-pair percentage against an Illumina reference assembly (E. coli K12).

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA/FASTQ long reads (PacBio or ONT) with raw per-base error rates (e.g. ~12%) and need corrected reads as input for assembly or downstream variant/coverage analyses.
skills.name: long-read-self-correction
skills.search_text: long-read-self-correction Use when you have FASTA/FASTQ long reads (PacBio or ONT) with raw per-base error rates (e.g. ~12%) and need corrected reads as input for assembly or downstream variant/coverage analyses. Your goal is to fix consensus-level assembly errors rather than per-read errors — use CONSENT-polish on contigs instead of CONSENT-correct on reads. The input is already-corrected reads or short reads; CONSENT is a self-correction method designed for raw PacBio/ONT long reads, not short-read polishing. You need very fast correction of short/easy datasets at the expense of output volume — other tools may outpace CONSENT whose correction-step runtime tends to be higher than some state-of-the-art methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Self-correct long reads (PacBio or ONT) with CONSENT, which computes overlapping-read alignment piles, splits them into windows, derives per-window MSA consensuses, polishes them with local de Bruijn graphs, and locally realigns the polished consensus back to each read. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Self-correct long reads (PacBio or ONT) with CONSENT, which computes overlapping-read alignment piles, splits them into windows, derives per-window MSA consensuses, polishes them with local de Bruijn graphs, and locally realigns the polished consensus back to each read.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to fix consensus-level assembly errors rather than per-read errors — use CONSENT-polish on contigs instead of CONSENT-correct on reads. The input is already-corrected reads or short reads; CONSENT is a self-correction method designed for raw PacBio/ONT long reads, not short-read polishing. skills.search_text: long-read-sequencing-pipeline-execution Use when PacBio Iso-Seq subread BAM inputs must be converted into full-length transcript isoform annotations (e.g., a merged BED12 genome annotation) via the reproducible nf-core/isoseq workflow rather than ad-hoc per-tool scripts. skills.summary: Executes the nf-core/isoseq Nextflow pipeline end to end on PacBio Iso-Seq long-read data — from subread preprocessing (CCS, LIMA, isoseq3 refine) through FLNC mapping (minimap2/uLTRA) to alignment post-processing (TAMA collapse/merge) — producing per-sample merged genome annotation files.

skills.summary: Implements the nanoEM preprocessing step: bismark-like base conversion of both the nanopore FASTQ reads and the reference genome so that EMseq-converted reads (unmethylated C read as T) can be aligned correctly, producing paired *_CT.fq.gz and *_GA.fq.gz read sets and a C-to-T / G-to-A converted reference FASTA.

skills.search_text: long-read-snv-calling Use when PacBio HiFi/CCS reads (e.g. hifi BAM or ccsmeth modBAM) must be converted to a phased variant layer so reads can be haplotagged for allele-specific methylation analysis. Input reads are Illumina short reads or nanopore data — Clair3's HiFi model and this pipeline target PacBio HiFi/CCS reads only. The goal is methylation calling itself — use ccsmeth read-level/site-level models; SNV calling is only the intermediate haplotyping layer of ccsmethphase. High-confidence external VCFs (e.g. GIAB truth sets) are available for phasing — WhatsHap can phase against those directly without de novo Clair3 calling. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calls single-nucleotide variants from haplotype-aware long-read alignments within the ccsmethphase pipeline: Clair3 is applied to pbmm2-merged ccsmeth modBAMs using its HiFi model, and only PASS SNVs are retained for subsequent WhatsHap phasing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are Illumina short reads or nanopore data — Clair3's HiFi model and this pipeline target PacBio HiFi/CCS reads only. skills.description: Use when input is a sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM of long error-prone reads (PacBio or ONT) aligned to an indexed reference FASTA and you need phased, diploid SNV calls with precision/recall evaluation against GIAB truth sets.
skills.name: long-read-snv-variant-calling
skills.search_text: long-read-snv-variant-calling Use when input is a sorted, indexed BAM/CRAM of long error-prone reads (PacBio or ONT) aligned to an indexed reference FASTA and you need phased, diploid SNV calls with precision/recall evaluation against GIAB truth sets. The input is short-read Illumina data — the paper shows short-read callers like FreeBayes (GQ cutoff fixed at 50) are the appropriate choice, though they under-call in segmental duplications with >=95-99% identity The goal is short indel discovery from SMS reads — Longshot only calls SNVs (it can genotype indels only if given in an input VCF), and accurate indel calling from SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate The target is structural-variant calling — use an SV method (e.g., Delly or SMRT-SV) rather than this SNV-calling skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calling and phasing SNVs from error-prone single-molecule sequencing (SMS) long reads (PacBio SMRT, Oxford Nanopore) using Longshot, which combines pileup-based candidate SNV detection with haplotype-informed genotyping. It enables accurate heterozygous SNV calls in diploid genomes, including segmental duplications inaccessible to short reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Calling and phasing SNVs from error-prone single-molecule sequencing (SMS) long reads (PacBio SMRT, Oxford Nanopore) using Longshot, which combines pileup-based candidate SNV detection with haplotype-informed genotyping. It enables accurate heterozygous SNV calls in diploid genomes, including segmental duplications inaccessible to short reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read Illumina data — the paper shows short-read callers like FreeBayes (GQ cutoff fixed at 50) are the appropriate choice, though they under-call in segmental duplications with >=95-99% identity The goal is short indel discovery from SMS reads — Longshot only calls SNVs (it can genotype indels only if given in an input VCF), and accurate indel calling from SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate The target is structural-variant calling — use an SV method (e.g., Delly or SMRT-SV) rather than this SNV-calling skill

skills.description: Use when paired tumor/matched-control long-read sequencing data (ONT PromethION FASTQ/BAM or PacBio) must be mined for somatic SVs at single-base resolution, especially single breakend calls such as HBV/viral integrations, LINE1-mediated rearrangements, or centromeric events.
skills.name: long-read-somatic-sv-detection
skills.search_text: long-read-somatic-sv-detection Use when paired tumor/matched-control long-read sequencing data (ONT PromethION FASTQ/BAM or PacBio) must be mined for somatic SVs at single-base resolution, especially single breakend calls such as HBV/viral integrations, LINE1-mediated rearrangements, or centromeric events. Detecting long repeat expansion events (VNTR/microsatellite expansions): the reference-genome-based framework is not reliable at susceptible loci, per the authors' discussion. Detecting SVs where both breakpoints are located in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions — the Single breakend SV module requires one breakpoint anchored to a characterized reference locus. skills.description: Use when quality-controlled ARG-containing long reads (Nanopore or PacBio) need candidate species assignments and alignment scores against a GTDB-derived reference, as the host-collection step of an ARG profiling pipeline.
skills.name: long-read-taxonomic-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-taxonomic-alignment Use when quality-controlled ARG-containing long reads (Nanopore or PacBio) need candidate species assignments and alignment scores against a GTDB-derived reference, as the host-collection step of an ARG profiling pipeline. Short-read data: this skill relies on minimap2's map-ont preset and long-read overlapping; second-generation short-read surveillance methods linking ARGs to hosts are explicitly noted as limited De novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments: reference-dependent alignment cannot classify unseen species or novel plasmid syntenies — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited ARGs originating from point mutations: read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors, so such ARGs are excluded from the database and will not be resolved http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Collects host information for ARG-containing long reads by mapping them with minimap2 base-level alignment against an ARG-tailored GTDB reference (up to 10,000 bp ARG-containing genomic regions), retaining abundant secondary alignments so per-read candidate species labels and alignment scores can be aggregated downstream. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Collects host information for ARG-containing long reads by mapping them with minimap2 base-level alignment against an ARG-tailored GTDB reference (up to 10,000 bp ARG-containing genomic regions), retaining abundant secondary alignments so per-read candidate species labels and alignment scores can be aggregated downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short-read data: this skill relies on minimap2's map-ont preset and long-read overlapping; second-generation short-read surveillance methods linking ARGs to hosts are explicitly noted as limited De novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments: reference-dependent alignment cannot classify unseen species or novel plasmid syntenies — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods may be better suited ARGs originating from point mutations: read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors, so such ARGs are excluded from the database and will not be resolved

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read Illumina data only — the skill is for long-read (ONT/PacBio) reads from intermediate single-cell cDNA libraries Input is bulk TCR/BCR repertoire data without 10x cell barcodes and UMIs — per-cell assignment is not possible Target loci are not near the 5′ end or transcripts exceed ~4 kB — outside nanoranger's defined optimal target space

skills.search_text: long-read-telomere-sequencing-table-parsing Use when you have demultiplexed telomap TSV output from WGS or telobait-captured long-read data and need per-patient mean telomere length metrics for group-level statistics such as age correlation. skills.summary: Parses per-sample telomap output tables (sample.telomap.tsv) from PacBio HiFi long-read telomere sequencing, extracting read-level TELOMERE_LEN and RAW_TELOMERE_LEN columns and aggregating them into per-patient summary statistics for downstream correlation analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ/BAM long-read data that has not yet been processed by telomap — run telomap first to generate sample.telomap.tsv Reads lack a called telomeric region (no TELOMERE_START from at least two consecutive TTAGGG repeats), so TELOMERE_LEN/RAW_TELOMERE_LEN are undefined Analyzing ALT cell telomere length, since very long ALT telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi read length and are not reliably measured with this method

skills.description: Use when corrected long reads must be mapped to haplotype-collapsed contigs to obtain pileup-based heterozygous SNP sites for read grouping and inconsistent-overlap detection.

The reads are raw (uncorrected) and the goal is read-overlap detection — PECAT instead uses minimap2 'ava-pb' all-against-all overlaps for raw reads The input is PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex data, where PECAT is reported to achieve only mediocre performance A reference-based SNP caller is appropriate — corrected reads alone are insufficient for accurate SNP calling (unlike Hifiasm with HiFi reads), and PECAT falls back to Clair3/Medaka for Nanopore polishing http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns long noisy reads (corrected PacBio CLR or Nanopore reads) back to a haplotype-collapsed first-round assembly using minimap2, producing the base-level alignments needed for downstream SNP calling and read phasing in PECAT's second diploid assembly round. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Aligns long noisy reads (corrected PacBio CLR or Nanopore reads) back to a haplotype-collapsed first-round assembly using minimap2, producing the base-level alignments needed for downstream SNP calling and read phasing in PECAT's second diploid assembly round.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are raw (uncorrected) and the goal is read-overlap detection — PECAT instead uses minimap2 'ava-pb' all-against-all overlaps for raw reads The input is PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex data, where PECAT is reported to achieve only mediocre performance A reference-based SNP caller is appropriate — corrected reads alone are insufficient for accurate SNP calling (unlike Hifiasm with HiFi reads), and PECAT falls back to Clair3/Medaka for Nanopore polishing

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered long-read isoform database (e.g., IsoPops DB with per-isoform read counts) and need to quantify how each gene's expression is distributed across its isoforms or rank genes by isoform diversity.
skills.name: long-read-transcript-catalog-analysis
skills.search_text: long-read-transcript-catalog-analysis Use when you have a filtered long-read isoform database (e.g., IsoPops DB with per-isoform read counts) and need to quantify how each gene's expression is distributed across its isoforms or rank genes by isoform diversity. The input is short-read RNA-seq data alone: typical RNA-seq read lengths are <200 bp and cannot resolve full-length sequences of multi-kilobase transcripts, so Shannon diversity from full-length isoform portfolios cannot be computed. The database has not been filtered (rawDB from compile_raw_db without process_db/filter_db/filter_truncations): unfiltered off-target and truncated transcripts will distort per-gene abundance profiles. The goal is cataloging rare or very short (<4.5 kb) isoforms: the size-selection step of library preparation may have caused some to evade detection. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Method for quantifying and rank-ordering isoform diversity from a PacBio lrCaptureSeq transcript catalog using the IsoPops R package, including Shannon diversity indexing of per-gene isoform portfolios and abundance ranking of individual isoforms. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Method for quantifying and rank-ordering isoform diversity from a PacBio lrCaptureSeq transcript catalog using the IsoPops R package, including Shannon diversity indexing of per-gene isoform portfolios and abundance ranking of individual isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read RNA-seq data alone: typical RNA-seq read lengths are <200 bp and cannot resolve full-length sequences of multi-kilobase transcripts, so Shannon diversity from full-length isoform portfolios cannot be computed. The database has not been filtered (rawDB from compile_raw_db without process_db/filter_db/filter_truncations): unfiltered off-target and truncated transcripts will distort per-gene abundance profiles. The goal is cataloging rare or very short (<4.5 kb) isoforms: the size-selection step of library preparation may have caused some to evade detection.

skills.description: Use when long noisy reads from targeted PacBio Iso-Seq (or ONT/R2C2 CCS-style) sequencing of highly similar gene copies or amplicons must be error-corrected and collapsed into finished consensus transcripts, including isoform-capture versus sequencing-depth analysis.
skills.name: long-read-transcript-error-correction
skills.search_text: long-read-transcript-error-correction Use when long noisy reads from targeted PacBio Iso-Seq (or ONT/R2C2 CCS-style) sequencing of highly similar gene copies or amplicons must be error-corrected and collapsed into finished consensus transcripts, including isoform-capture versus sequencing-depth analysis. The input consists of short reads (e.g., Illumina) or reads that do not span the region of interest end-to-end — IsoCon requires reads spanning the full transcript/amplicon for iterative clustering to converge. The goal is to assign transcripts to individual gene copies or determine gene family copy number from transcriptome-only data — the article explicitly states IsoCon does not allow conclusive gene-copy assignment and downstream analysis is needed. A reference-based transcriptome reconstruction (e.g., with a complete reference genome) is available and sufficient; IsoCon is designed for de novo reconstruction of highly similar copies without a reference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 De novo error correction and redundancy removal of PacBio CCS Iso-Seq reads with IsoCon to reconstruct end-to-end transcripts from highly similar multigene family copies (e.g., TSPY, HSFY, DAZ) at nucleotide-level precision, without a reference genome. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: De novo error correction and redundancy removal of PacBio CCS Iso-Seq reads with IsoCon to reconstruct end-to-end transcripts from highly similar multigene family copies (e.g., TSPY, HSFY, DAZ) at nucleotide-level precision, without a reference genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input consists of short reads (e.g., Illumina) or reads that do not span the region of interest end-to-end — IsoCon requires reads spanning the full transcript/amplicon for iterative clustering to converge. The goal is to assign transcripts to individual gene copies or determine gene family copy number from transcriptome-only data — the article explicitly states IsoCon does not allow conclusive gene-copy assignment and downstream analysis is needed. A reference-based transcriptome reconstruction (e.g., with a complete reference genome) is available and sufficient; IsoCon is designed for de novo reconstruction of highly similar copies without a reference.

skills.description: Use when you need isoform-level expression estimates from ONT direct-RNA (RNA004) reads aligned to a transcriptome, or when validating a nanopore simulator by comparing ESPRESSO-estimated isoform abundances to ground-truth transcript abundances.

skills.search_text: long-read-transcript-isoform-quantification Use when you need isoform-level expression estimates from ONT direct-RNA (RNA004) reads aligned to a transcriptome, or when validating a nanopore simulator by comparing ESPRESSO-estimated isoform abundances to ground-truth transcript abundances. skills.summary: Quantifies transcript isoform abundances from long-read (ONT direct-RNA) sequencing data by aligning basecalled reads to a transcriptome reference with minimap2 and running ESPRESSO, then validating quantification fidelity via Pearson correlation against known abundances (target ~0.996 for NanoSimFormer-simulated HG002 RNA004 reads).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina) RNA-seq data — ESPRESSO-based isoform quantification here is designed for ONT long reads. Input is already a gene/isoform count matrix — apply the correlation comparison instead of re-quantifying. The goal is genomic DNA variant calling or metagenomic abundance only without a transcriptome quantification component.

skills.summary: Annotate a genome-guided StringTie transcriptome assembly built from hybrid PacBio/Illumina RNA-seq using the annotate_my_genomes pipeline, which reconciles the assembly against an NCBI GTF reference, classifies coding vs long non-coding RNAs (TransDecoder, FEELnc, GAWN/Blastx), and reports novel candidate genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism has no assembled genome or no NCBI-available annotation in GTF format, since the pipeline requires both as reference inputs Input is raw reads rather than a genome-guided GTF assembly; upstream alignment (minimap2 for PacBio, fastp/HISAT2 for Illumina) and StringTie assembly must be done first The goal is de novo gene prediction without a transcript assembly; annotation pipelines like BRAKER1/2 or MAKER are the appropriate alternatives

skills.description: Use when raw LRTS bam files (aligned full-length transcripts, e.g. PacBio SequelII IsoSeq data) need QC assessment, filter tagging, or when a saturation/depth analysis is needed to decide if rare transcripts (e.g. 1 TPM) are reliably observed.
skills.name: long-read-transcriptome-sequencing-qc
skills.search_text: long-read-transcriptome-sequencing-qc Use when raw LRTS bam files (aligned full-length transcripts, e.g. PacBio SequelII IsoSeq data) need QC assessment, filter tagging, or when a saturation/depth analysis is needed to decide if rare transcripts (e.g. 1 TPM) are reliably observed. skills.summary: A skill for quality-controlling Long Read Transcriptome Sequencing (LRTS) data using IsoTools, a Python module for LRTS analysis. It covers computing QC metrics on imported PacBio/SequelII bam alignments, filtering suspect reads (e.g. FRAGMENTS not using a reference TSS or PAS), and using IsoTools' negative-binomial saturation analysis to judge whether sequencing depth suffices for transcript discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than full-length long-read transcriptome sequencing alignments — IsoTools is designed for LRTS bam import of full length transcripts.
