skills.name: long-read-transposable-element-calling
skills.search_text: long-read-transposable-element-calling Use when you have a long-read BAM/CRAM aligned to a reference genome and need to detect non-reference TE insertions, or when benchmarking sTELLeR against TLDR/xTEA on PacBio data. Input is short-read sequencing data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for PacBio/ONT long reads; use short-read TE callers such as RetroSeq or MELT2 instead No reference-aligned long-read BAM/CRAM is available or the reference used for alignment cannot be provided — sTELLeR requires both the read file and the exact reference it was aligned to Only reference-resident TE annotation is needed — sTELLeR detects non-reference insertions, not reference TE genotyping against a reference callset alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Detect non-reference transposable element insertions (Alu, L1, HERV, SVA) in long-read (PacBio/ONT) genomes using sTELLeR, a fast, haplotype-aware caller that outputs VCF records (INS:ME) compatible with merging against other TE callers such as TLDR and xTEA. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Detect non-reference transposable element insertions (Alu, L1, HERV, SVA) in long-read (PacBio/ONT) genomes using sTELLeR, a fast, haplotype-aware caller that outputs VCF records (INS:ME) compatible with merging against other TE callers such as TLDR and xTEA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read sequencing data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for PacBio/ONT long reads; use short-read TE callers such as RetroSeq or MELT2 instead No reference-aligned long-read BAM/CRAM is available or the reference used for alignment cannot be provided — sTELLeR requires both the read file and the exact reference it was aligned to Only reference-resident TE annotation is needed — sTELLeR detects non-reference insertions, not reference TE genotyping against a reference callset alone

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from ONT long-read BAM alignments where low-quality candidate loci must be resolved via haplotype-aware consensus sequences, or when phased, haplotagged alignments are needed to build per-haplotype local assemblies.
skills.name: long-read-variant-phasing-haplotagging
skills.search_text: long-read-variant-phasing-haplotagging Use when calling SNVs from ONT long-read BAM alignments where low-quality candidate loci must be resolved via haplotype-aware consensus sequences, or when phased, haplotagged alignments are needed to build per-haplotype local assemblies. Input is short-read Illumina data — the method relies on long ONT reads spanning multiple variants for phasing and haplotagging All candidate loci are already classified high-quality and confidently genotyped by the binomial model, so haplotype-aware consensus generation adds no information The goal is structural variant or indel calling — the pipeline targets SNVs only http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Phase heterozygous SNVs from ONT long reads with WhatsHap and haplotag alignments so that haplotype-specific read subsets can be used for consensus generation and haplotype-aware genotyping, as done in the miniSNV pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: Phase heterozygous SNVs from ONT long reads with WhatsHap and haplotag alignments so that haplotype-specific read subsets can be used for consensus generation and haplotype-aware genotyping, as done in the miniSNV pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read Illumina data — the method relies on long ONT reads spanning multiple variants for phasing and haplotagging All candidate loci are already classified high-quality and confidently genotyped by the binomial model, so haplotype-aware consensus generation adds no information The goal is structural variant or indel calling — the pipeline targets SNVs only

skills.description: Use when a long-read study reports isoforms for a complex, multi-isoform gene locus and you need to test whether per-cell short-read Illumina assembly recovers those same isoforms or produces contigs absent from the long-read set.
skills.name: long-read-vs-short-read-isoform-benchmarking
skills.search_text: long-read-vs-short-read-isoform-benchmarking Use when a long-read study reports isoforms for a complex, multi-isoform gene locus and you need to test whether per-cell short-read Illumina assembly recovers those same isoforms or produces contigs absent from the long-read set. When the goal is isoform detection itself from ONT data — use the Mandalorion pipeline rather than this benchmarking comparison When the study locus has only a single annotated isoform, since the benchmark targets multi-isoform loci (e.g. CD37) where short-read assembly is expected to fail When comparing long-read technologies (e.g. ONT MinION vs PacBio Sequel) rather than short-read de novo assembly vs long-read isoforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark whether de novo short-read Illumina assembly (Trinity) can recover the complex isoforms identified from ONT MinION long-read RNAseq (via the Mandalorion pipeline), testing the claim that short reads fail to resolve multi-isoform loci such as CD37 in individual B1a cells. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms16027
skills.summary: Benchmark whether de novo short-read Illumina assembly (Trinity) can recover the complex isoforms identified from ONT MinION long-read RNAseq (via the Mandalorion pipeline), testing the claim that short reads fail to resolve multi-isoform loci such as CD37 in individual B1a cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is isoform detection itself from ONT data — use the Mandalorion pipeline rather than this benchmarking comparison When the study locus has only a single annotated isoform, since the benchmark targets multi-isoform loci (e.g. CD37) where short-read assembly is expected to fail When comparing long-read technologies (e.g. ONT MinION vs PacBio Sequel) rather than short-read de novo assembly vs long-read isoforms

skills.description: Use when you have a reconstructed long-read transcriptome (e.g. IsoTools pickle from PacBio LRTS) plus paired short-read RNA-seq, and want to know whether PSI values agree per splicing event category.
skills.name: long-read-vs-short-read-splicing-comparison
skills.search_text: long-read-vs-short-read-splicing-comparison Use when you have a reconstructed long-read transcriptome (e.g. IsoTools pickle from PacBio LRTS) plus paired short-read RNA-seq, and want to know whether PSI values agree per splicing event category. Your goal is de novo transcriptome reconstruction or QC of LRTS reads rather than cross-platform PSI agreement You have only long-read data and no paired short-read RNA-seq, so rMATS quantification for comparison is impossible Your events are mutually exclusive exons and you expect strong concordance — this category showed r=-0.05 in the source study http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Compares PSI values of alternative splicing events defined from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) data with short-read RNA-seq quantification by rMATS, using IsoTools' segment-graph event definition and rMATS-format export. It quantifies per-category agreement (ES, 5AS, 3AS, IR, ME) via Pearson correlation. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Compares PSI values of alternative splicing events defined from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) data with short-read RNA-seq quantification by rMATS, using IsoTools' segment-graph event definition and rMATS-format export. It quantifies per-category agreement (ES, 5AS, 3AS, IR, ME) via Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is de novo transcriptome reconstruction or QC of LRTS reads rather than cross-platform PSI agreement You have only long-read data and no paired short-read RNA-seq, so rMATS quantification for comparison is impossible Your events are mutually exclusive exons and you expect strong concordance — this category showed r=-0.05 in the source study

skills.description: Use when raw long-read whole-genome reads (PacBio HiFi or targeted ONT FASTQ/BAM) from human rare-disease samples must be turned into aligned BAMs, phased variant calls, de novo assemblies and methylation profiles via a containerized Nextflow run.
skills.name: long-read-wgs-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: long-read-wgs-pipeline-execution Use when raw long-read whole-genome reads (PacBio HiFi or targeted ONT FASTQ/BAM) from human rare-disease samples must be turned into aligned BAMs, phased variant calls, de novo assemblies and methylation profiles via a containerized Nextflow run. Input data are short-read or single-cell: Nallo is built for long reads from PacBio and (targeted) ONT data focused on rare-disease The goal is only a single variant-calling subtask on a limited budget: epi2me-labs/wf-human-variation or PacificBiosciences/HiFi-human-WGS-WDL may suffice instead of the full Nallo pipeline including assembly (~344 core hours/sample) Coverage is far below ~30x (e.g. targeted panels below 20x): alternative workflows may terminate or yield unexpected outcomes at low depth http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Executes Nallo, a Nextflow pipeline for comprehensive human long-read genome analysis (PacBio and Oxford Nanopore data), covering alignment, variant detection, phasing, de novo assembly and CpG methylation reporting. The skill includes benchmarked compute expectations (~344 core hours per sample, 5 h 52 min wall-clock for a ~32x PacBio HiFi sample on a 68-node dual Intel Xeon Gold 6248R cluster). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag086
skills.summary: Executes Nallo, a Nextflow pipeline for comprehensive human long-read genome analysis (PacBio and Oxford Nanopore data), covering alignment, variant detection, phasing, de novo assembly and CpG methylation reporting. The skill includes benchmarked compute expectations (~344 core hours per sample, 5 h 52 min wall-clock for a ~32x PacBio HiFi sample on a 68-node dual Intel Xeon Gold 6248R cluster).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are short-read or single-cell: Nallo is built for long reads from PacBio and (targeted) ONT data focused on rare-disease The goal is only a single variant-calling subtask on a limited budget: epi2me-labs/wf-human-variation or PacificBiosciences/HiFi-human-WGS-WDL may suffice instead of the full Nallo pipeline including assembly (~344 core hours/sample) Coverage is far below ~30x (e.g. targeted panels below 20x): alternative workflows may terminate or yield unexpected outcomes at low depth

skills.description: Use when annotating germline SNVs/InDels from a VCF and you need to flag stop_gained/frameshift or canonical splice donor/acceptor variants as LOF, or need to resolve which LOF calls should be downgraded by filter exceptions.
skills.name: loss-of-function-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: loss-of-function-variant-filtering Use when annotating germline SNVs/InDels from a VCF and you need to flag stop_gained/frameshift or canonical splice donor/acceptor variants as LOF, or need to resolve which LOF calls should be downgraded by filter exceptions. Input is a somatic (tumor) VCF — this workflow is designed for germline cancer-predisposition screening; use PCGR instead Input VCF still contains non-PASS records, multi-allelic sites, or mitochondrial (chrM) variants — preprocess first or LOF calls will not be reliable You need raw consequence annotation only, without LOF filtering or ACMG PVS1 evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates and filters putative loss-of-function (LOF) germline variants using VEP's LOFTEE plugin and the CPSR LOF_FILTER tag, applying exceptions (GC>GT at splice donor sites, truncations within the last 5% of coding sequence) and PVS1 decision-tree logic before ACMG classification. genomics/v1 10.1002/ijc.33749
skills.summary: Annotates and filters putative loss-of-function (LOF) germline variants using VEP's LOFTEE plugin and the CPSR LOF_FILTER tag, applying exceptions (GC>GT at splice donor sites, truncations within the last 5% of coding sequence) and PVS1 decision-tree logic before ACMG classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a somatic (tumor) VCF — this workflow is designed for germline cancer-predisposition screening; use PCGR instead Input VCF still contains non-PASS records, multi-allelic sites, or mitochondrial (chrM) variants — preprocess first or LOF calls will not be reliable You need raw consequence annotation only, without LOF filtering or ACMG PVS1 evaluation

skills.description: Use when a NanoSpring-compressed nanopore FASTQ archive must be validated as lossless before reporting compression ratios, e.g. when reproducing Table 2 bits-per-base results or coverage-subsampled compression curves.
skills.name: lossless-compression-verification
skills.search_text: lossless-compression-verification Use when a NanoSpring-compressed nanopore FASTQ archive must be validated as lossless before reporting compression ratios, e.g. when reproducing Table 2 bits-per-base results or coverage-subsampled compression curves. The compression tool stores quality values or read identifiers (e.g. gzip on the raw FASTQ), so comparing only sed '2~4p' sequence lines would not establish full losslessness A lossy or reference-based assessment of compression quality is intended rather than a lossless round-trip check Input is not a FASTQ nanopore read file (NanoSpring requires only a FASTQ file as input and compresses only base sequences) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Verifies that a NanoSpring nanopore read compression round-trip is lossless by decompressing the .NanoSpring archive and byte-comparing the recovered sequences against the original FASTQ sequence lines. Because NanoSpring compresses only base sequences (not identifiers or quality values), verification must strip FASTQ to every 4th line before comparison. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Verifies that a NanoSpring nanopore read compression round-trip is lossless by decompressing the .NanoSpring archive and byte-comparing the recovered sequences against the original FASTQ sequence lines. Because NanoSpring compresses only base sequences (not identifiers or quality values), verification must strip FASTQ to every 4th line before comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compression tool stores quality values or read identifiers (e.g. gzip on the raw FASTQ), so comparing only sed '2~4p' sequence lines would not establish full losslessness A lossy or reference-based assessment of compression quality is intended rather than a lossless round-trip check Input is not a FASTQ nanopore read file (NanoSpring requires only a FASTQ file as input and compresses only base sequences)

skills.description: Use when validating that a compressed-then-decompressed nanopore FASTQ dataset is identical to the original reads, e.g. after benchmarking NanoSpring compression or reproducing compression/decompression timing tables.
skills.name: lossless-roundtrip-verification
skills.search_text: lossless-roundtrip-verification Use when validating that a compressed-then-decompressed nanopore FASTQ dataset is identical to the original reads, e.g. after benchmarking NanoSpring compression or reproducing compression/decompression timing tables. The compressor is intentionally lossy or only stores subset data (e.g., NanoSpring drops quality scores and read identifiers, so full-FASTQ diffing will always fail) Output of an assembly or polishing step where reconstructed reads are expected to differ from input http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Verify that a genomic sequence compressor (e.g., NanoSpring) reconstructs data bit-for-bit by comparing the decompressed output against the original reads, as required to validate lossless FASTQ compression workflows. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Verify that a genomic sequence compressor (e.g., NanoSpring) reconstructs data bit-for-bit by comparing the decompressed output against the original reads, as required to validate lossless FASTQ compression workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compressor is intentionally lossy or only stores subset data (e.g., NanoSpring drops quality scores and read identifiers, so full-FASTQ diffing will always fail) Output of an assembly or polishing step where reconstructed reads are expected to differ from input

skills.description: Use when raw fasta/fastq sRNA libraries must be reduced to high-confidence reads (18–26 nt, abundance ≥5, non-t/rRNA, non-low-complexity) prior to genome mapping and miRNA/tasiRNA annotation in the miRPursuit pipeline.
skills.name: low-complexity-sequence-filtering
skills.search_text: low-complexity-sequence-filtering Use when raw fasta/fastq sRNA libraries must be reduced to high-confidence reads (18–26 nt, abundance ≥5, non-t/rRNA, non-low-complexity) prior to genome mapping and miRNA/tasiRNA annotation in the miRPursuit pipeline. Input reads have not been adaptor-trimmed and the --trim flag has not been applied; adaptor trimming (fastx_clipper) precedes the Wbench Filter in Step 1 The goal is genome-based filtering — that is performed later in Step 2 ('Filter Genome & mirbase') with patman mapping at 0 mismatches, not by the Wbench Filter Sequences already filtered and only being re-analysed downstream from a later pipeline stage (miRPursuit allows restarting from a specific stage onward) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 In the miRPursuit Filtering stage, fasta sRNA sequences are filtered for length, abundance and low complexity, and t/rRNA reads are removed, using the UEA sRNA workbench Filter tool configured via wbench_filter.cfg before genome mapping with patman. genomics/v1 10.1002/1873-3468.12746
skills.summary: In the miRPursuit Filtering stage, fasta sRNA sequences are filtered for length, abundance and low complexity, and t/rRNA reads are removed, using the UEA sRNA workbench Filter tool configured via wbench_filter.cfg before genome mapping with patman.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not been adaptor-trimmed and the --trim flag has not been applied; adaptor trimming (fastx_clipper) precedes the Wbench Filter in Step 1 The goal is genome-based filtering — that is performed later in Step 2 ('Filter Genome & mirbase') with patman mapping at 0 mismatches, not by the Wbench Filter Sequences already filtered and only being re-analysed downstream from a later pipeline stage (miRPursuit allows restarting from a specific stage onward)

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether assemblies from ~5x–8x HiFi reads (e.g. HiFiCCL-Hifiasm primary+alternate, HiFlye, LJA) improve detection of large structural variants (>7000 bp) against GIAB Tier 1 or T2T-HG002-Q100 truth sets.
skills.name: low-coverage-assembly-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: low-coverage-assembly-quality-assessment Use when evaluating whether assemblies from ~5x–8x HiFi reads (e.g. HiFiCCL-Hifiasm primary+alternate, HiFlye, LJA) improve detection of large structural variants (>7000 bp) against GIAB Tier 1 or T2T-HG002-Q100 truth sets. Input is high-coverage (>25x) HiFi data — HiFiCCL and this assessment workflow are designed for low-coverage (~5x–8x) scenarios where de novo assembly alone is challenged Input reads are noisy ONT/CLR reads — the framework targets high-fidelity (HiFi) reads, and the compared assemblers (Hifiasm, HiFlye, LJA) are HiFi-based The goal is read-based SV calling (e.g. Sniffles2-style on BAM/CRAM) rather than assembly-based calling — the article uses Sniffles2 only as a recall comparator (0.3526) for the assembly-based SVIM-asm approach http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A benchmark-driven quality assessment skill for assemblies produced from low-coverage (~5x–8x) PacBio HiFi reads, judging contig quality by misassembled-contig length and large-variant detection power (SVs >7000 bp) against curated truth sets such as GIAB Tier 1 and T2T-HG002-Q100. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: A benchmark-driven quality assessment skill for assemblies produced from low-coverage (~5x–8x) PacBio HiFi reads, judging contig quality by misassembled-contig length and large-variant detection power (SVs >7000 bp) against curated truth sets such as GIAB Tier 1 and T2T-HG002-Q100.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is high-coverage (>25x) HiFi data — HiFiCCL and this assessment workflow are designed for low-coverage (~5x–8x) scenarios where de novo assembly alone is challenged Input reads are noisy ONT/CLR reads — the framework targets high-fidelity (HiFi) reads, and the compared assemblers (Hifiasm, HiFlye, LJA) are HiFi-based The goal is read-based SV calling (e.g. Sniffles2-style on BAM/CRAM) rather than assembly-based calling — the article uses Sniffles2 only as a recall comparator (0.3526) for the assembly-based SVIM-asm approach

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires standardized low-coverage HiFi inputs: full-coverage human or plant HiFi FASTQ/FASTA reads must be reduced to ~5x before assembly comparison.
skills.name: low-coverage-hifi-read-downsampling
skills.search_text: low-coverage-hifi-read-downsampling Use when a benchmark requires standardized low-coverage HiFi inputs: full-coverage human or plant HiFi FASTQ/FASTA reads must be reduced to ~5x before assembly comparison. The input reads are already at ~5x or lower coverage — further downsampling would deepen the completeness gaps the paper itself notes ('many genomic regions remain missing' at 5x) The data are noisy long reads (ONT, PacBio CLR) rather than high-fidelity reads — HiFiCCL and this evaluation design target specifically low-coverage HiFi data The goal is assembly at native/high coverage for maximal contiguity rather than a controlled low-coverage benchmark comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Subsample full-coverage PacBio HiFi read sets to ~5x coverage with seqtk (1.3-r106) to create standardized low-coverage inputs for benchmarking HiFiCCL-Hifiasm against hifiasm alone. This controls read depth so assembly-quality differences reflect the framework, not coverage variation. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Subsample full-coverage PacBio HiFi read sets to ~5x coverage with seqtk (1.3-r106) to create standardized low-coverage inputs for benchmarking HiFiCCL-Hifiasm against hifiasm alone. This controls read depth so assembly-quality differences reflect the framework, not coverage variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are already at ~5x or lower coverage — further downsampling would deepen the completeness gaps the paper itself notes ('many genomic regions remain missing' at 5x) The data are noisy long reads (ONT, PacBio CLR) rather than high-fidelity reads — HiFiCCL and this evaluation design target specifically low-coverage HiFi data The goal is assembly at native/high coverage for maximal contiguity rather than a controlled low-coverage benchmark comparison

skills.description: Use when building a consensus genome from nanopore reads mapped to a reference and Medaka cannot fit a matching basecaller model, so that positions below a minimum depth of 20 or with less than 70% nucleotide proportion are masked as N.
skills.name: low-coverage-position-masking
skills.search_text: low-coverage-position-masking Use when building a consensus genome from nanopore reads mapped to a reference and Medaka cannot fit a matching basecaller model, so that positions below a minimum depth of 20 or with less than 70% nucleotide proportion are masked as N. A matching Medaka basecaller model is available for the data — then polish with Medaka instead of the Samtools fallback consensus The input is de novo contigs rather than reads mapped to a reference — ViMOP's de novo assembly step does not use consensus masking The sample is a large DNA virus with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) — the README warns such assemblies may be inaccurate draft genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Masks positions in a Nanopore-derived consensus genome as Ns when coverage or base-support thresholds are not met, ensuring only well-supported bases are reported. This skill reproduces the Samtools-consensus fallback path in the ViMOP pipeline for reference-guided viral genome reconstruction. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Masks positions in a Nanopore-derived consensus genome as Ns when coverage or base-support thresholds are not met, ensuring only well-supported bases are reported. This skill reproduces the Samtools-consensus fallback path in the ViMOP pipeline for reference-guided viral genome reconstruction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A matching Medaka basecaller model is available for the data — then polish with Medaka instead of the Samtools fallback consensus The input is de novo contigs rather than reads mapped to a reference — ViMOP's de novo assembly step does not use consensus masking The sample is a large DNA virus with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) — the README warns such assemblies may be inaccurate draft genomes

skills.description: Use when computing Pearson correlations or accuracy metrics over per-site methylation frequencies from DeepMod2/Dorado calls (BED files), where low-coverage CpGs would otherwise distort agreement between RRMS, whole-genome ONT, and short-read datasets.
skills.name: low-coverage-site-filtering
skills.search_text: low-coverage-site-filtering Use when computing Pearson correlations or accuracy metrics over per-site methylation frequencies from DeepMod2/Dorado calls (BED files), where low-coverage CpGs would otherwise distort agreement between RRMS, whole-genome ONT, and short-read datasets. skills.summary: Filters CpG sites with insufficient Oxford Nanopore coverage (<10X) and low-coverage/inconclusive ground-truth sites before comparing per-site methylation frequencies between RRMS and whole-genome Nanopore sequencing of HG002 or against short-read ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is inherently low coverage — the article notes filtering intermediate predictions and sites 'can lead to lower statistical power in downstream analyses, especially for low coverage samples' Per-read (rather than per-site) F1 evaluation is the goal — per-read ground truth uses ≥90%/<10% methylation labels on the read level, not a site-coverage filter Sites in the 20–80% intermediate methylation range are the target of interest, since EpiQC reported poor concordance there and this skill excludes them from evaluation

skills.name: lrts-bam-alignment-transcript-reconstruction
skills.search_text: lrts-bam-alignment-transcript-reconstruction Use when you have LRTS BAM alignments (e.g. PacBio SequelII full-length reads) plus a gff3/gtf reference annotation and need to reconstruct and quantify transcripts, comparing tool-dependent or filter-dependent transcript recovery. Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than long-read alignments of full-length transcripts — IsoTools is a module for LRTS analysis You only need alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing between sample groups rather than transcriptome reconstruction and tool comparison You lack a reference annotation in gff3/gtf format and cannot supply one, since annotation and classification of novel transcripts depend on it http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstruct transcriptomes from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) BAM alignments using IsoTools, a Python framework that imports aligned full-length transcripts plus gff3/gtf reference annotation and performs transcriptome reconstruction with configurable filtering (e.g. permissive vs. balanced configurations) to control novel transcript recovery. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Reconstruct transcriptomes from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) BAM alignments using IsoTools, a Python framework that imports aligned full-length transcripts plus gff3/gtf reference annotation and performs transcriptome reconstruction with configurable filtering (e.g. permissive vs. balanced configurations) to control novel transcript recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than long-read alignments of full-length transcripts — IsoTools is a module for LRTS analysis You only need alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing between sample groups rather than transcriptome reconstruction and tool comparison You lack a reference annotation in gff3/gtf format and cannot supply one, since annotation and classification of novel transcripts depend on it

skills.description: Use when encoding nanopore FASTQ reads into per-contig streams after approximate assembly and those streams must be packed into a lossless, high-ratio compressed archive.
skills.name: lzma2-bsc-stream-compression
skills.search_text: lzma2-bsc-stream-compression Use when encoding nanopore FASTQ reads into per-contig streams after approximate assembly and those streams must be packed into a lossless, high-ratio compressed archive. The goal is to compress read identifiers or quality values — NanoSpring only compresses base sequences in the FASTQ file and ignores the rest. The input is short, low-error sequencing reads (e.g., Illumina); existing compressors like SPRING or PgRC assume short reads and this assembly-based approach targets long, error-prone ONT reads. A general-purpose compressor is sufficient and ratio is not critical; gzip is simpler, though 3-6x worse on recent basecaller outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compresses the ordered streams produced by NanoSpring's approximate-assembly encoding (consensus sequence, start/error position, error type, erroneous base, reverse-complement flag, read index, and lone reads) using LZMA2 (fast-lzma2) and BSC (libbsc), then bundles the compressed streams into a single tar archive with the .NanoSpring extension. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Compresses the ordered streams produced by NanoSpring's approximate-assembly encoding (consensus sequence, start/error position, error type, erroneous base, reverse-complement flag, read index, and lone reads) using LZMA2 (fast-lzma2) and BSC (libbsc), then bundles the compressed streams into a single tar archive with the .NanoSpring extension.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compress read identifiers or quality values — NanoSpring only compresses base sequences in the FASTQ file and ignores the rest. The input is short, low-error sequencing reads (e.g., Illumina); existing compressors like SPRING or PgRC assume short reads and this assembly-based approach targets long, error-prone ONT reads. A general-purpose compressor is sufficient and ratio is not critical; gzip is simpler, though 3-6x worse on recent basecaller outputs.

skills.search_text: m6a-call-coordinate-binning Use when you have per-tool m6A site BED files from multiple dRNA-seq detection tools and need a coordinate-level pairwise concordance matrix over a binned query space (e.g. oligos, yeast, mouse, human NanOlympicsMod outputs). skills.summary: Quantify concordance between m6A site calls from different dRNA-seq detection tools by partitioning the query space into fixed-size genomic bins, labeling each bin m6A-positive per tool, and computing pairwise overlap matrices with NanOlympicsMod's R post-processing scripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is precision/recall benchmarking of tools against gold-standard or orthogonal reference m6A peak sets rather than inter-tool concordance When input is per-read modification probability data (e.g. FAST5 slot values) rather than aggregated per-tool site BED coordinates When only a single tool's calls are available — pairwise overlap matrices require at least two callers

skills.search_text: m6a-deep-learning-model-training Use when you have RedNano-extracted comb_basecall_raw features (k-mer, 65-signal window, qual/mis/ins/dele) from modified and unmodified Nanopore DRS FAST5s and need a trained m6A site classifier. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a trained checkpoint and you only need site-level m6A probabilities — use scripts/predict.py with a pre-trained model such as mil_allspecies_model_states.pt instead You lack modified/unmodified labeled training data and only have unannotated DRS reads — supervised training requires binary labels appended to feature rows You need the cross-dataset generalization benchmark rather than a custom model — RedNano ships a pre-trained all-species DRACH model for prediction-only use

skills.search_text: m6a-detection-tool-benchmarking Use when comparing m6A detection tools on Nanopore direct RNA-seq data, tuning 'default' vs 'relaxed' thresholds, or assessing whether sequencing depth (e.g. 25/50/75% subsampling) saturates m6A hit discovery. skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is short-read m6A-seq (e.g. MeRIP-seq/miCLIP) rather than Nanopore direct RNA-seq signal-based data — NanOlympicsMod tools operate on FAST5/dRNA inputs A single pre-validated tool with a fixed threshold is all that is needed, with no cross-tool comparison or precision-recall tuning required Only synthetic oligo results matter and in vivo confounders are irrelevant — the article shows tools perform far better on synthetic oligos than on yeast/mouse/human data, so oligo-only benchmarking overestimates in vivo performance

The analysis targets a single tool or needs absolute m6A site quantification rather than comparative benchmarking against gold-standard peaks No orthogonal reference m6A peak set (bed file) exists for the organism, since the biological datasets lack a ground truth and rely on short-read-derived reference sets Input is raw signal only without basecalled FAST5 data, which the pipeline's --fast5_slot handling requires http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Benchmark dRNA-seq m6A detection tools against gold-standard peak bed files using the NanOlympicsMod Nextflow pipeline, sweeping stringency cut-offs to build precision-recall curves and AUPRC estimates with 95% confidence intervals, and testing whether bin-set restrictions (RRACH motifs, exclusion zones, high coverage) improve performance. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: Benchmark dRNA-seq m6A detection tools against gold-standard peak bed files using the NanOlympicsMod Nextflow pipeline, sweeping stringency cut-offs to build precision-recall curves and AUPRC estimates with 95% confidence intervals, and testing whether bin-set restrictions (RRACH motifs, exclusion zones, high coverage) improve performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets a single tool or needs absolute m6A site quantification rather than comparative benchmarking against gold-standard peaks No orthogonal reference m6A peak set (bed file) exists for the organism, since the biological datasets lack a ground truth and rely on short-read-derived reference sets Input is raw signal only without basecalled FAST5 data, which the pipeline's --fast5_slot handling requires

skills.description: Use when dRNA-seq replicates were analyzed both as separate samples and merged, and you need to quantify per-tool overlap of called m6A bins between the two configurations.
skills.name: m6a-hit-overlap-computation
skills.search_text: m6a-hit-overlap-computation Use when dRNA-seq replicates were analyzed both as separate samples and merged, and you need to quantify per-tool overlap of called m6A bins between the two configurations. Tools that cannot process multiple samples (single-sample tools), since merging vs separating replicates is not meaningful for them Datasets without biological replicates, where a separate-vs-merged comparison cannot be constructed Comparing hits across different genomes/annotations or threshold sets, since overlap is only interpretable when pipeline.conf settings are identical between runs http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes per-tool pairwise overlap of m6A hit bins between two configurations of replicate-capable dRNA-seq m6A detection tools (separate replicates vs merged replicates), using NanOlympicsMod's R post-processing scripts and Jaccard-style bin overlap to quantify how much the two configurations agree. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: Computes per-tool pairwise overlap of m6A hit bins between two configurations of replicate-capable dRNA-seq m6A detection tools (separate replicates vs merged replicates), using NanOlympicsMod's R post-processing scripts and Jaccard-style bin overlap to quantify how much the two configurations agree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tools that cannot process multiple samples (single-sample tools), since merging vs separating replicates is not meaningful for them Datasets without biological replicates, where a separate-vs-merged comparison cannot be constructed Comparing hits across different genomes/annotations or threshold sets, since overlap is only interpretable when pipeline.conf settings are identical between runs

skills.description: Use when you have a bed file of predicted m6A site stoichiometries (e.g. mAFiA.sites.bed with modRatio) and an orthogonal reference such as GLORI_chrX.bed, and need to compute and compare site-level correlation benchmarks.
skills.name: m6a-method-benchmarking-against-glori
skills.search_text: m6a-method-benchmarking-against-glori Use when you have a bed file of predicted m6A site stoichiometries (e.g. mAFiA.sites.bed with modRatio) and an orthogonal reference such as GLORI_chrX.bed, and need to compute and compare site-level correlation benchmarks. Sites with dRNA-Seq coverage below the minimum threshold of 50 — the paper explicitly requires a minimum coverage of 50 for comparison against GLORI measurements Benchmarking read-level modification probabilities rather than site-level stoichiometry — this skill operates on aggregated mAFiA.sites.bed output, not single-read P(m6A) values Comparing Ψ or other RNA modifications against GLORI — GLORI measures m6A only; Ψ benchmarks use PRAISE http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks site-level m6A stoichiometry predictions from dRNA-Seq methods (mAFiA, CHEUI, m6Anet) against GLORI chemical-measurement stoichiometry by matching sites on genomic coordinates and computing Pearson/Spearman correlations. Reproduces the paper's headline result of mAFiA vs GLORI correlation 0.86 on 5925 HEK293 WT transcriptome sites. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47661-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks site-level m6A stoichiometry predictions from dRNA-Seq methods (mAFiA, CHEUI, m6Anet) against GLORI chemical-measurement stoichiometry by matching sites on genomic coordinates and computing Pearson/Spearman correlations. Reproduces the paper's headline result of mAFiA vs GLORI correlation 0.86 on 5925 HEK293 WT transcriptome sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sites with dRNA-Seq coverage below the minimum threshold of 50 — the paper explicitly requires a minimum coverage of 50 for comparison against GLORI measurements Benchmarking read-level modification probabilities rather than site-level stoichiometry — this skill operates on aggregated mAFiA.sites.bed output, not single-read P(m6A) values Comparing Ψ or other RNA modifications against GLORI — GLORI measures m6A only; Ψ benchmarks use PRAISE

skills.description: Use when you have ONT fast5/fastq data (basecalled with Albacore or a basecaller retaining event data), a reference assembly, and need per-read and per-position m6A calls at known or suspected methyltransferase motifs.

skills.search_text: m6a-methylation-calling-from-current-deviations Use when you have ONT fast5/fastq data (basecalled with Albacore or a basecaller retaining event data), a reference assembly, and need per-read and per-position m6A calls at known or suspected methyltransferase motifs. skills.summary: Detect N6-methyladenine (m6A) in Oxford Nanopore data with mCaller by classifying deviations between measured and expected ionic current as adenine passes through the pore, then summarize per-read calls into per-position methylation predictions.

skills.summary: Predicts per-site m6A modification probabilities on Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) data using RedNano, a deep-learning model that combines raw current signals with basecalling errors. Running the pre-trained checkpoint on a coverage-filtered, site-aggregated feature table yields per-site probabilities usable for ROC AUC / AUPR evaluation, including cross-species validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still read-level feature output (test.features.sort.tsv) that has not been aggregated with aggre_features_to_site_level.py — aggregation and coverage filtering must come first Sites have fewer than 20 supporting signals — the awk $4>=20 filter must be applied before prediction, otherwise the site-level features are too sparse for the multiple instance learning approach You need single-read-level modification calling rather than site-level probability prediction — this skill uses the multi instance learning (site-level) pathway

skills.description: Use when ONT direct RNA sequencing base-called data contains known m6A sites and you need per-site fractional modification levels (0–100%), not just binary modified/unmodified calls.
skills.name: m6a-site-stoichiometry-quantification
skills.search_text: m6a-site-stoichiometry-quantification Use when ONT direct RNA sequencing base-called data contains known m6A sites and you need per-site fractional modification levels (0–100%), not just binary modified/unmodified calls. You need single-read (per-molecule) modification calls — EpiNano aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and has no per-read resolution You only have one sample with no matched modified/unmodified references — the regression requires both 100%-modified and 0%-modified endpoints (a matched control such as KO/KD is highly recommended) Your goal is binary modified-site detection rather than fractional quantification — EpiNano-SVM with pre-trained m6A models is the more direct choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Estimates per-site m6A modification stoichiometry in direct RNA sequencing data by fitting a linear regression that maps wild-type base-calling mismatch frequencies at known m6A sites onto fully modified (100%) and unmodified (0%, e.g. ime4Δ) reference endpoints, as demonstrated for yeast where the median wt stoichiometry was 12–30%. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Estimates per-site m6A modification stoichiometry in direct RNA sequencing data by fitting a linear regression that maps wild-type base-calling mismatch frequencies at known m6A sites onto fully modified (100%) and unmodified (0%, e.g. ime4Δ) reference endpoints, as demonstrated for yeast where the median wt stoichiometry was 12–30%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need single-read (per-molecule) modification calls — EpiNano aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and has no per-read resolution You only have one sample with no matched modified/unmodified references — the regression requires both 100%-modified and 0%-modified endpoints (a matched control such as KO/KD is highly recommended) Your goal is binary modified-site detection rather than fractional quantification — EpiNano-SVM with pre-trained m6A models is the more direct choice

skills.description: Use when you have raw nanopore fast5 dRNA-Seq reads and need per-site m6A stoichiometry estimates (modRatio), either to correlate against a chemical-assay reference such as GLORI or to call differential modification between strains.
skills.name: m6a-stoichiometry-quantification
skills.search_text: m6a-stoichiometry-quantification Use when you have raw nanopore fast5 dRNA-Seq reads and need per-site m6A stoichiometry estimates (modRatio), either to correlate against a chemical-assay reference such as GLORI or to call differential modification between strains. You need predictions at m6A or Ψ motif classes not covered by the original mAFiA classifiers — use the successor psi-co-mAFiA, which covers all 18 m6A DRACH motifs plus 16 high-frequency Ψ motifs. Sites with dRNA-Seq coverage below the minimum threshold of 50 reads — modRatio estimates there are out of scope for comparison against GLORI and below the recommended precision settings. skills.summary: Quantify site-level m6A stoichiometry from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA-Seq (dRNA-Seq) data using mAFiA: RODAN-based feature extraction plus logistic regression classifiers yield per-read modification probabilities that are aggregated into per-site modRatio values, which can be benchmarked against GLORI or compared across conditions (e.g. col0 vs vir1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need predictions at m6A or Ψ motif classes not covered by the original mAFiA classifiers — use the successor psi-co-mAFiA, which covers all 18 m6A DRACH motifs plus 16 high-frequency Ψ motifs. Sites with dRNA-Seq coverage below the minimum threshold of 50 reads — modRatio estimates there are out of scope for comparison against GLORI and below the recommended precision settings. The input is short-read sequencing or already-processed modification calls from a different chemistry (e.g. existing CHEUI/m6Anet outputs) — this skill requires raw fast5 dRNA-Seq input.

skills.summary: Concatenates per-read SNP, InDel, and STR allele calls from targeted long-read (PacBio HiFi) alignments into a single ';'-separated macrohaplotype string, clusters identical strings, and filters/ranks clusters by read support using read-backed phasing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina) data or read lengths too short to span multiple targeted variant loci — read-backed phasing needs long reads such as PacBio HiFi Goal is de novo genome-wide variant discovery rather than genotyping a pre-specified panel of targeted STR/SNP/InDel loci defined in the configure files Only a single variant class is of interest and phased multi-locus strings are unnecessary — HipSTR or DeepVar may suffice (MacroHapCaller is built for simultaneous STR+SNP+InDel macrohaplotyping)

skills.description: Use when MinION nanopore reads (FASTA/FASTQ) must be mapped to a target genome/reference and alignments need to be exported in MAF format with split-read handling for rearrangements or chimeric sequences.
skills.name: maf-alignment-file-generation
skills.search_text: maf-alignment-file-generation Use when MinION nanopore reads (FASTA/FASTQ) must be mapped to a target genome/reference and alignments need to be exported in MAF format with split-read handling for rearrangements or chimeric sequences. The task is metagenomics analysis of mixed-community reads — NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics and its implementation was only planned per the discussion. The input is already an alignment file or the goal is consensus/polymorphism calling rather than read-to-target mapping — those are downstream NanoPipe stages with their own filter steps. A non-MAF alignment format (e.g., BAM/SAM) is strictly required without format conversion — this skill natively produces MAF output from lastal/last-split. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates MAF-format alignments of MinION sequencing reads against a target genome using the LAST aligner (version 946) with MinION-trained parameters, piping lastal output through last-split to resolve split best-scoring alignments. This is the mapping stage of the NanoPipe pipeline that feeds downstream consensus and polymorphism analysis. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Generates MAF-format alignments of MinION sequencing reads against a target genome using the LAST aligner (version 946) with MinION-trained parameters, piping lastal output through last-split to resolve split best-scoring alignments. This is the mapping stage of the NanoPipe pipeline that feeds downstream consensus and polymorphism analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is metagenomics analysis of mixed-community reads — NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics and its implementation was only planned per the discussion. The input is already an alignment file or the goal is consensus/polymorphism calling rather than read-to-target mapping — those are downstream NanoPipe stages with their own filter steps. skills.search_text: majority-vote-consensus-label-correction Use when HiFi reads mapped to a linear reference (e.g., CHM13 v2.0) at low coverage leave misclassified or unclassified ('None') chromosome labels, and chromosome-wise de novo assembly requires corrected per-read classes. When a full alignment path or start position on the reference is required — collapsing to a 1-D cost array forfeits backtracking, so only the end position is recoverable. When memory is not a constraint and a full M×N sDTW matrix implementation with traceback is already acceptable, since the reduction trades recoverable alignment information for memory. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Collapses the full O(M×N) subsequence DTW (sDTW) cost matrix into a 1-D cost array of size M+1 so raw nanopore signal reads can be aligned to reference expected signal levels with O(M) memory, keeping only the running minimum score and its reference end position for Read Until decisions. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Collapses the full O(M×N) subsequence DTW (sDTW) cost matrix into a 1-D cost array of size M+1 so raw nanopore signal reads can be aligned to reference expected signal levels with O(M) memory, keeping only the running minimum score and its reference end position for Read Until decisions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a full alignment path or start position on the reference is required — collapsing to a 1-D cost array forfeits backtracking, so only the end position is recoverable. When memory is not a constraint and a full M×N sDTW matrix implementation with traceback is already acceptable, since the reduction trades recoverable alignment information for memory.

skills.description: Use when comparing SNV variant callers on parent-offspring trio data (e.g., GIAB HG002/HG003/HG004) and a genotyping-consistency metric such as Mendelian Consistency Rate is needed to complement per-sample F1/precision/recall benchmarks.
skills.name: mendelian-consistency-analysis
skills.search_text: mendelian-consistency-analysis Use when comparing SNV variant callers on parent-offspring trio data (e.g., GIAB HG002/HG003/HG004) and a genotyping-consistency metric such as Mendelian Consistency Rate is needed to complement per-sample F1/precision/recall benchmarks. Input data is not a parent-offspring trio (no parental genotypes available to check child genotypes against). VCFs contain indels or multiallelic variants only — this skill is defined on biallelic SNV genotypes. You need site-level accuracy against a truth set (use GIAB benchmarking with stratifications such as GIAB v3.3 difficult/low-complexity regions instead of trio consistency). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Evaluates trio SNV callers by computing the Mendelian Consistency Rate (MCR): the fraction of child biallelic SNV genotypes (0/0, 0/1, 1/1) consistent with parental genotypes under Mendelian inheritance rules. Used to benchmark miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot on the GIAB Ashkenazi Trio (HG002/HG003/HG004) ONT sup-datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: Evaluates trio SNV callers by computing the Mendelian Consistency Rate (MCR): the fraction of child biallelic SNV genotypes (0/0, 0/1, 1/1) consistent with parental genotypes under Mendelian inheritance rules. Used to benchmark miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot on the GIAB Ashkenazi Trio (HG002/HG003/HG004) ONT sup-datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not a parent-offspring trio (no parental genotypes available to check child genotypes against). VCFs contain indels or multiallelic variants only — this skill is defined on biallelic SNV genotypes. You need site-level accuracy against a truth set (use GIAB benchmarking with stratifications such as GIAB v3.3 difficult/low-complexity regions instead of trio consistency).

skills.description: Use when genotyping tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments in a trio/pedigree and you need to classify each TR call as Mendelian consistent or inconsistent, or estimate the overall consistency fraction.
skills.name: mendelian-inheritance-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: mendelian-inheritance-consistency-checking Use when genotyping tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments in a trio/pedigree and you need to classify each TR call as Mendelian consistent or inconsistent, or estimate the overall consistency fraction. Input lacks trio/pedigree structure (no both parents sequenced) — Mendelian consistency cannot be traced Repeats lie in unassembled regions such as centromeres or telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify Samples are polyploid or on haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Trace Mendelian consistency of tandem repeat genotypes across a trio (e.g., the Puerto Rican PB trio HG00731/HG00732/HG00733) using TRiCoLOR SAGE's --mendel parameter, which flags each TR as Mendelian consistent or inconsistent given inferred parental genotypes. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Trace Mendelian consistency of tandem repeat genotypes across a trio (e.g., the Puerto Rican PB trio HG00731/HG00732/HG00733) using TRiCoLOR SAGE's --mendel parameter, which flags each TR as Mendelian consistent or inconsistent given inferred parental genotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks trio/pedigree structure (no both parents sequenced) — Mendelian consistency cannot be traced Repeats lie in unassembled regions such as centromeres or telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify Samples are polyploid or on haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support

skills.description: Use when setting up MR simulation scenarios in simmrd that require explicit parameter choices such as GWAS sample sizes, SNP counts, sample overlap, weak-instrument regimes, or UHP/CHP horizontal pleiotropy before data generation.
skills.name: mendelian-randomization-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: mendelian-randomization-parameter-configuration Use when setting up MR simulation scenarios in simmrd that require explicit parameter choices such as GWAS sample sizes, SNP counts, sample overlap, weak-instrument regimes, or UHP/CHP horizontal pleiotropy before data generation. The goal is to fit or evaluate MR estimators on real GWAS summary statistics rather than to generate simulated data — simmrd is a simulation tool for evaluating MR method performance. You need multiple simulation replicates driven from a YAML parameter file at scale — the CLI in the cli/ repo with pixi is designed for multi-iteration Monte Carlo runs, whereas set_params()/generate_*() produce a single replicate per call. The simulation scenario matches a paper preset exactly and needs no customization beyond set_params()/load_preset() defaults with no explicit configuration required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Configure simulation parameters for Mendelian randomization data generation using simmrd's set_params(), which builds a validated parameter list where only non-default values (e.g., type, sample_size_Xs, number_of_causal_SNPs, prop_gwas_overlap_Xs_and_Y, pleiotropy settings) need to be specified before passing it to generate_summary() or generate_individual(). genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Configure simulation parameters for Mendelian randomization data generation using simmrd's set_params(), which builds a validated parameter list where only non-default values (e.g., type, sample_size_Xs, number_of_causal_SNPs, prop_gwas_overlap_Xs_and_Y, pleiotropy settings) need to be specified before passing it to generate_summary() or generate_individual().
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to fit or evaluate MR estimators on real GWAS summary statistics rather than to generate simulated data — simmrd is a simulation tool for evaluating MR method performance. You need multiple simulation replicates driven from a YAML parameter file at scale — the CLI in the cli/ repo with pixi is designed for multi-iteration Monte Carlo runs, whereas set_params()/generate_*() produce a single replicate per call. The simulation scenario matches a paper preset exactly and needs no customization beyond set_params()/load_preset() defaults with no explicit configuration required.

skills.description: Use when a task requires simulating GWAS summary or individual-level data for UVMR/MVMR under weak instruments, sample overlap, UHP/CHP, correlated IVs, or winner's curse, or when reproducing named scenarios from the simmrd paper.
skills.name: mendelian-randomization-simulation-execution
skills.search_text: mendelian-randomization-simulation-execution Use when a task requires simulating GWAS summary or individual-level data for UVMR/MVMR under weak instruments, sample overlap, UHP/CHP, correlated IVs, or winner's curse, or when reproducing named scenarios from the simmrd paper. The task needs real, observed GWAS data — simmrd generates only simulated data intended to evaluate statistical properties of MR methods Individual-level confounding must be set directly and generate_summary()'s faster summary-level path is used instead of generate_individual() The prior tool MR_predictor is assumed sufficient — it cannot accommodate horizontal pleiotropy, sample overlap, multiple exposures, weak instruments, correlated IVs, imprecise LD estimation, or winner's curse http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Execute Mendelian randomization simulation replicates with the simmrd R package: build a validated parameter list via set_params() (or load_preset()), generate summary-level or individual-level GWAS data with generate_summary()/generate_individual(), and optionally visualise with plot_simdata(). This replaces ad-hoc, unreliable hand-rolled MR simulation scripts with a standard, open-source framework. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Execute Mendelian randomization simulation replicates with the simmrd R package: build a validated parameter list via set_params() (or load_preset()), generate summary-level or individual-level GWAS data with generate_summary()/generate_individual(), and optionally visualise with plot_simdata(). This replaces ad-hoc, unreliable hand-rolled MR simulation scripts with a standard, open-source framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task needs real, observed GWAS data — simmrd generates only simulated data intended to evaluate statistical properties of MR methods Individual-level confounding must be set directly and generate_summary()'s faster summary-level path is used instead of generate_individual() The prior tool MR_predictor is assumed sufficient — it cannot accommodate horizontal pleiotropy, sample overlap, multiple exposures, weak instruments, correlated IVs, imprecise LD estimation, or winner's curse

skills.description: Use when you have InDel genotype calls for two parents and their F1 progeny (e.g., 2 parents + 20 progeny from InDelGT genotyping) and need to retain only markers following Mendelian segregation before linkage mapping.
skills.name: mendelian-segregation-ratio-testing
skills.search_text: mendelian-segregation-ratio-testing Use when you have InDel genotype calls for two parents and their F1 progeny (e.g., 2 parents + 20 progeny from InDelGT genotyping) and need to retain only markers following Mendelian segregation before linkage mapping. Input genotypes were not called with InDelGT's genotyping step or lack the parental/progeny structure needed for segregation-ratio expectation (e.g., unrelated individuals or a single sample). You intend to keep segregation-distorted markers (e.g., for distortion analysis) rather than filtering them out for linkage map construction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Statistical filter (step 3 of InDelGT) that tests each cataloged InDel site's observed parental/progeny genotype counts against expected Mendelian segregation ratios for cross-pollination (CP) populations, retaining only sites with P-value >= 0.01 and classifying them into seven segregation-type output files. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Statistical filter (step 3 of InDelGT) that tests each cataloged InDel site's observed parental/progeny genotype counts against expected Mendelian segregation ratios for cross-pollination (CP) populations, retaining only sites with P-value >= 0.01 and classifying them into seven segregation-type output files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genotypes were not called with InDelGT's genotyping step or lack the parental/progeny structure needed for segregation-ratio expectation (e.g., unrelated individuals or a single sample). You intend to keep segregation-distorted markers (e.g., for distortion analysis) rather than filtering them out for linkage map construction.

skills.description: Use when evaluating contig-level assemblies from low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads — e.g., HiFiCCL-Hifiasm vs Hifiasm outputs — and you need reference-free completeness and QV estimates alongside QUAST/BUSCO metrics.
skills.name: merqury-kmer-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: merqury-kmer-quality-evaluation Use when evaluating contig-level assemblies from low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads — e.g., HiFiCCL-Hifiasm vs Hifiasm outputs — and you need reference-free completeness and QV estimates alongside QUAST/BUSCO metrics. Input is a high-coverage (>~25x) HiFi dataset where the base assembler alone (e.g., Hifiasm 0.19.5-r592 --primary) already produces high-quality contigs and the reference-guided chromosome-binning pipeline offers no benefit The reads are noisy long reads (ONT) rather than high-fidelity HiFi reads — HiFiCCL and its evaluation workflow are specifically designed for low-coverage high-fidelity reads You only need SV detection on a pangenome graph rather than assembly completeness/QV evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Use Merqury k-mer-based analysis to assess assembly completeness and consensus quality value (QV) for low-coverage HiFi assemblies produced by HiFiCCL-Hifiasm versus Hifiasm alone, as part of the HiFiCCL evaluation pipeline on human (~5x) and plant datasets. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Use Merqury k-mer-based analysis to assess assembly completeness and consensus quality value (QV) for low-coverage HiFi assemblies produced by HiFiCCL-Hifiasm versus Hifiasm alone, as part of the HiFiCCL evaluation pipeline on human (~5x) and plant datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a high-coverage (>~25x) HiFi dataset where the base assembler alone (e.g., Hifiasm 0.19.5-r592 --primary) already produces high-quality contigs and the reference-guided chromosome-binning pipeline offers no benefit The reads are noisy long reads (ONT) rather than high-fidelity HiFi reads — HiFiCCL and its evaluation workflow are specifically designed for low-coverage high-fidelity reads You only need SV detection on a pangenome graph rather than assembly completeness/QV evaluation

skills.search_text: meta-domain-construction-from-protein-domain-annotations Use when building per-family aggregates of Pfam domain annotations from a positional mapping database (e.g. PostgreSQL 'interpro_domains' table) to define homologous-domain groups for variant-tolerance aggregation. Pfam families with only a single homologous domain instance in the human proteome — these cannot form a meta-domain since aggregation requires at least two homologs Aggregation of variation outside annotated protein domains, where no Pfam consensus positions exist to project variants onto http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Constructs Pfam meta-domains by grouping every Pfam family with two or more homologous domain instances across the human proteome and aligning all domain-instance sequences to the family HMM, enabling aggregation of variation data over homologous domains. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798

skills.name: meta-domain-variant-aggregation
skills.search_text: meta-domain-variant-aggregation Use when a task asks to reproduce a gene/domain case study (e.g., CDK13 ENST00000181839.4 with Pkinase PF00069, consensus codon 714), count ClinVar pathogenic SNVs inside a domain, or compute gnomAD missense variant counts and mean allele frequencies across homologous domain positions. Only transcripts mapped to a Swiss-Prot protein can be used in the analysis — a transcript lacking a Swiss-Prot mapping (displayed in gray in the web server) cannot support meta-domain aggregation Sequences that do not start with a start codon (ATG) or end with a stop codon, or whose cDNA translation does not match the GENCODE translation via Biopython's translate function, are excluded from the mapping You need haplotype context or protein-protein interaction information: aggregating variation via meta-domains loses such specific context and only encapsulates general biological or molecular functions attributed to the domain http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Aggregate genetic variation (gnomAD population variants and ClinVar pathogenic mutations) across homologous Pfam protein domains into meta-domains, projecting variation onto Pfam domain consensus positions via a PostgreSQL mapping database. skills.description: Use when mock-community or bulk-sample amplicon FASTQ reads have been demultiplexed and you need per-taxon read counts, taxon-recovery percentages, or fold-change bias statistics (e.g. Levene's test) to compare sequencing platforms' quantitative fidelity.

Input reads are raw, undemultiplexed Nanopore output — run MiniBar demultiplexing (dual-index barcode + primer identification) before counting taxa Input is already a per-taxon count or feature table — skip straight to fold-change computation and Levene's test Assessing Nanopore consensus-sequence error profiles or phylogenetic resolution rather than community composition and quantitative recovery bias http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Counts recovered reads per taxon from demultiplexed metabarcoding FASTQ files (Nanopore long-amplicon rDNA vs Illumina 18S), computes per-taxon fold change between known input DNA amount and recovered reads, and quantifies qualitative recovery (percentage of input taxa recovered) to expose platform-specific abundance bias in mock arthropod communities. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are raw, undemultiplexed Nanopore output — run MiniBar demultiplexing (dual-index barcode + primer identification) before counting taxa Input is already a per-taxon count or feature table — skip straight to fold-change computation and Levene's test Assessing Nanopore consensus-sequence error profiles or phylogenetic resolution rather than community composition and quantitative recovery bias

skills.description: Use when a kinetic-rate inference pipeline (e.g. nano-ID/Nanodynamo) must be validated against a simulated metabolic-labelling benchmark before applying it to experimental 4sU-labelled Nanopore data.
skills.name: metabolic-labelling-rna-species-modeling
skills.search_text: metabolic-labelling-rna-species-modeling Use when a kinetic-rate inference pipeline (e.g. nano-ID/Nanodynamo) must be validated against a simulated metabolic-labelling benchmark before applying it to experimental 4sU-labelled Nanopore data. The goal is to infer rates from experimental (not simulated) metabolic-labelling data — use the experimentalDataAnalysis.R / mainModelingResults.R workflow instead. The target method is INSPEcT quantification of synthesis/processing/degradation rates on its own (INSPEcTAnalysisAllGenes.R), rather than Nanodynamo simulation-based benchmarking. The study lacks RNA metabolic labelling data and only requires accuracy assessment of the nano-ID classifier itself (nanoIDAccuracy.R). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulate RNA-species expression datasets for metabolic-labelling experiments with Nanodynamo — sampling synthesis, processing, export and degradation rates from gaussian distributions anchored to INSPEcT 3T9 medians (1000 genes, 2 replicates, 20-min labelling, CV=5 noise) — then fit the nano-ID model to validate rate inference against ground truth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Simulate RNA-species expression datasets for metabolic-labelling experiments with Nanodynamo — sampling synthesis, processing, export and degradation rates from gaussian distributions anchored to INSPEcT 3T9 medians (1000 genes, 2 replicates, 20-min labelling, CV=5 noise) — then fit the nano-ID model to validate rate inference against ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer rates from experimental (not simulated) metabolic-labelling data — use the experimentalDataAnalysis.R / mainModelingResults.R workflow instead. The target method is INSPEcT quantification of synthesis/processing/degradation rates on its own (INSPEcTAnalysisAllGenes.R), rather than Nanodynamo simulation-based benchmarking. The study lacks RNA metabolic labelling data and only requires accuracy assessment of the nano-ID classifier itself (nanoIDAccuracy.R).

skills.description: Use when long Nanopore (or PacBio) metagenomic reads at moderate-to-high coverage (≥8×) should be assembled into contigs and binned into MAGs so ARGs can be linked to de novo-reconstructed hosts rather than classified read-by-read.
skills.name: metagenome-binning-and-mag-taxonomic-assignment
skills.search_text: metagenome-binning-and-mag-taxonomic-assignment Use when long Nanopore (or PacBio) metagenomic reads at moderate-to-high coverage (≥8×) should be assembled into contigs and binned into MAGs so ARGs can be linked to de novo-reconstructed hosts rather than classified read-by-read. Sample coverage is ≤8× for assembly-based (or ≤32× for binning-based) detection accuracy targets — at 1–2× these approaches stay at or below 0.5 F1 while read-based Argo already achieves type-level F1 of 0.811–0.935 Input reads are short second-generation reads — this workflow depends on long reads for metaFlye '--nano-raw' assembly and SemiBin2 '--sequencing-type=long_read' binning Goal is per-read or per-cluster taxonomic classification without de novo reconstruction — Argo's read-overlapping profiler avoids assembly entirely and classifies ARGs at species level directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Profiles ARG-carrying species from long Nanopore metagenomes by assembling reads with metaFlye, classifying contigs with Kraken2, binning contigs into MAGs with SemiBin2, and labeling MAGs with GTDB-Tk — the binning-based alternative benchmarked against Argo's read-based profiling across 1×–32× coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Profiles ARG-carrying species from long Nanopore metagenomes by assembling reads with metaFlye, classifying contigs with Kraken2, binning contigs into MAGs with SemiBin2, and labeling MAGs with GTDB-Tk — the binning-based alternative benchmarked against Argo's read-based profiling across 1×–32× coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample coverage is ≤8× for assembly-based (or ≤32× for binning-based) detection accuracy targets — at 1–2× these approaches stay at or below 0.5 F1 while read-based Argo already achieves type-level F1 of 0.811–0.935 Input reads are short second-generation reads — this workflow depends on long reads for metaFlye '--nano-raw' assembly and SemiBin2 '--sequencing-type=long_read' binning Goal is per-read or per-cluster taxonomic classification without de novo reconstruction — Argo's read-overlapping profiler avoids assembly entirely and classifies ARGs at species level directly

skills.description: Use when a merged or pooled metagenomic contig set (e.g. from MeGAMerge) must be quality-checked against raw reads and known reference genomes to confirm contig reduction, coverage maintenance, chimera counts, and removal of unmapped contigs.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-quality-validation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-quality-validation Use when a merged or pooled metagenomic contig set (e.g. from MeGAMerge) must be quality-checked against raw reads and known reference genomes to confirm contig reduction, coverage maintenance, chimera counts, and removal of unmapped contigs. You have only a single-assembler contig set with no reference genomes available — reference coverage and chimera validation cannot be computed You are still choosing between assemblers rather than validating a merged/pooled contig set — the article instead recommends comparing assembly metrics via read mapping and gene prediction per assembly Your goal is to judge assembly quality by total assembly size or N50/N90 alone — the paper states these metrics 'are not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates a merged (MeGAMerged) metagenomic contig set by mapping reads back with BWA/SAMtools, aligning contigs to references with Nucmer for coverage, and flagging chimeras — confirming that merging reduces contig count and unmapped contigs while maintaining reference genome coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Validates a merged (MeGAMerged) metagenomic contig set by mapping reads back with BWA/SAMtools, aligning contigs to references with Nucmer for coverage, and flagging chimeras — confirming that merging reduces contig count and unmapped contigs while maintaining reference genome coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single-assembler contig set with no reference genomes available — reference coverage and chimera validation cannot be computed You are still choosing between assemblers rather than validating a merged/pooled contig set — the article instead recommends comparing assembly metrics via read mapping and gene prediction per assembly Your goal is to judge assembly quality by total assembly size or N50/N90 alone — the paper states these metrics 'are not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance'
