skills.description: Use when a post-assembly contig set (e.g., MergedContigs.fasta from MeGAMerge) contains very large contigs (hundreds of kb) whose contiguity must be confirmed by whole-contig colinear alignment to a single reference genome, such as Supplementary Figures S4-S5 validation.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-colinearity-analysis
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-colinearity-analysis Use when a post-assembly contig set (e.g., MergedContigs.fasta from MeGAMerge) contains very large contigs (hundreds of kb) whose contiguity must be confirmed by whole-contig colinear alignment to a single reference genome, such as Supplementary Figures S4-S5 validation. The goal is de novo assembly or contig merging rather than validation of already-produced contigs (use MeGAMerge itself, not a colinearity check). Contigs are short (<2 kb) fragments where full-length colinear alignment to a single reference is not the relevant validity criterion; the paper removes very small contigs before analysis. No reference genome of sufficient similarity is available, so nucmer alignment would yield no meaningful hits and colinearity cannot be judged. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates the contiguity and validity of large metagenomic assembly contigs (e.g., the 342.5 kb and 472.5 kb largest MeGAMerge contigs from HMP sample SRS022071) by aligning them colinearly against a known reference genome with Nucmer/MUMmer, as done against the Bacteroides helcogenes P 36-108 chromosome in Scholz et al. 2014 (Scientific Reports 4, 6480). genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Validates the contiguity and validity of large metagenomic assembly contigs (e.g., the 342.5 kb and 472.5 kb largest MeGAMerge contigs from HMP sample SRS022071) by aligning them colinearly against a known reference genome with Nucmer/MUMmer, as done against the Bacteroides helcogenes P 36-108 chromosome in Scholz et al. 2014 (Scientific Reports 4, 6480).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo assembly or contig merging rather than validation of already-produced contigs (use MeGAMerge itself, not a colinearity check). Contigs are short (<2 kb) fragments where full-length colinear alignment to a single reference is not the relevant validity criterion; the paper removes very small contigs before analysis. No reference genome of sufficient similarity is available, so nucmer alignment would yield no meaningful hits and colinearity cannot be judged.

skills.description: Use when multiple assembled metagenome contig FASTA files (e.g. from SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, Velvet, Newbler) must be pooled and deduplicated prior to OLC-based merging, and exact duplicates, reverse complements, or subsequences must be eliminated first.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-dereplication
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-dereplication Use when multiple assembled metagenome contig FASTA files (e.g. from SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, Velvet, Newbler) must be pooled and deduplicated prior to OLC-based merging, and exact duplicates, reverse complements, or subsequences must be eliminated first. When you have raw reads rather than assembled contig Multi-FASTA files — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process and does not assemble reads itself When contigs are already deduplicated and you only need to re-run a single assembler rather than merge multiple assemblies When single-genome (not metagenomic) input is expected to need very different Newbler auto-options — use -single_genome=1 only for single-genome inputs, not mixed metagenomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Dereplicate pooled contig Multi-FASTA files from multiple metagenomic assemblies (removing exact duplicates, reverse complements, and subsequences) with MeGAMerge's custom Perl dereplication step before size-based binning and OLC-based merging, so the merged contig set contains no replicated data. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Dereplicate pooled contig Multi-FASTA files from multiple metagenomic assemblies (removing exact duplicates, reverse complements, and subsequences) with MeGAMerge's custom Perl dereplication step before size-based binning and OLC-based merging, so the merged contig set contains no replicated data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you have raw reads rather than assembled contig Multi-FASTA files — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process and does not assemble reads itself When contigs are already deduplicated and you only need to re-run a single assembler rather than merge multiple assemblies When single-genome (not metagenomic) input is expected to need very different Newbler auto-options — use -single_genome=1 only for single-genome inputs, not mixed metagenomes

skills.description: Use when you have multiple FASTA files of assembled contigs from different assemblers (e.g., Velvet, SOAPdenovo, IDBA, Ray, CLC Bio) or related metagenome samples and want a single improved, more contiguous merged contig set.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-set-merging
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-set-merging Use when you have multiple FASTA files of assembled contigs from different assemblers (e.g., Velvet, SOAPdenovo, IDBA, Ray, CLC Bio) or related metagenome samples and want a single improved, more contiguous merged contig set. When you only have raw sequencing reads and no existing contig assemblies — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process and requires already-assembled contigs as input When comparing total assembly size or N50/N90 as primary metrics — the article notes removal of small contigs impacts these metrics and they are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' When the input dataset is extremely large — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 MeGAMerge is a post-assembly pipeline that pools contigs from multiple metagenomic assemblies (or multiple samples), dereplicates them, bins contigs at a 2.0 kb cutoff, reassembles smaller contigs with Newbler, and merges everything with Minimus2 to produce an improved, more contiguous contig set without data replication. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: MeGAMerge is a post-assembly pipeline that pools contigs from multiple metagenomic assemblies (or multiple samples), dereplicates them, bins contigs at a 2.0 kb cutoff, reassembles smaller contigs with Newbler, and merges everything with Minimus2 to produce an improved, more contiguous contig set without data replication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only have raw sequencing reads and no existing contig assemblies — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process and requires already-assembled contigs as input When comparing total assembly size or N50/N90 as primary metrics — the article notes removal of small contigs impacts these metrics and they are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' When the input dataset is extremely large — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size

skills.description: Use when metagenomic Illumina (or 454) reads are available, multiple de novo assemblies (e.g. different kmer values or assemblers) have been generated, and improved contiguity (larger contigs, more genes) is needed beyond any single assembler run.
skills.name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
skills.search_text: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly Use when metagenomic Illumina (or 454) reads are available, multiple de novo assemblies (e.g. different kmer values or assemblers) have been generated, and improved contiguity (larger contigs, more genes) is needed beyond any single assembler run. When only a single assembler and kmer choice is available — there is nothing to dereplicate and merge, so the OLC merging step cannot improve contiguity When the input dataset is extremely large, since overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size When the analysis goal is a gene/feature table or taxonomy profile rather than an improved contig set — assembly metrics like N50/N90 and total assembly size are not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance in that context http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A post-assembly metagenomic assembly improvement strategy (MeGAMerge) that pools contigs from multiple de novo assemblers (Velvet, SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, IDBA, Ray) and merges them via overlap-layout-consensus to produce fewer, larger contigs with more predicted genes than any single assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: A post-assembly metagenomic assembly improvement strategy (MeGAMerge) that pools contigs from multiple de novo assemblers (Velvet, SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, IDBA, Ray) and merges them via overlap-layout-consensus to produce fewer, larger contigs with more predicted genes than any single assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single assembler and kmer choice is available — there is nothing to dereplicate and merge, so the OLC merging step cannot improve contiguity When the input dataset is extremely large, since overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size When the analysis goal is a gene/feature table or taxonomy profile rather than an improved contig set — assembly metrics like N50/N90 and total assembly size are not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance in that context

skills.description: Use when comparing merged (MeGAMerge) vs individual metagenomic assemblies by predicted gene counts and coding density, or when annotating contigs >=2 kb without a reference genome.
skills.name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-gene-prediction Use when comparing merged (MeGAMerge) vs individual metagenomic assemblies by predicted gene counts and coding density, or when annotating contigs >=2 kb without a reference genome. When the input is raw reads rather than assembled Multi-FASTA contigs — gene prediction here operates on assembled contigs only When the goal is assembly merging itself (use the MeGAMerge/Minimus2 pipeline, not gene prediction) When contigs <2 kb must be annotated, since the paper's protocol removes contigs smaller than 2 kb prior to Prodigal http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predict protein-coding genes on metagenomic assemblies (e.g., MeGAMerge merged vs. individual Kmer assemblies) with Prodigal in anonymous/metagenomic mode, then quantify predicted gene counts and coding density to compare assembly quality. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Predict protein-coding genes on metagenomic assemblies (e.g., MeGAMerge merged vs. individual Kmer assemblies) with Prodigal in anonymous/metagenomic mode, then quantify predicted gene counts and coding density to compare assembly quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw reads rather than assembled Multi-FASTA contigs — gene prediction here operates on assembled contigs only When the goal is assembly merging itself (use the MeGAMerge/Minimus2 pipeline, not gene prediction) When contigs <2 kb must be annotated, since the paper's protocol removes contigs smaller than 2 kb prior to Prodigal

skills.description: Use when you have metagenomic short-read samples from multiple environments and want to bin contigs across samples jointly (multi-sample mode), comparing or replacing single-sample binners like VAMB.
skills.name: metagenomic-multi-sample-contig-binning
skills.search_text: metagenomic-multi-sample-contig-binning Use when you have metagenomic short-read samples from multiple environments and want to bin contigs across samples jointly (multi-sample mode), comparing or replacing single-sample binners like VAMB. Single-sample data: use SemiBin2's single_easy_bin instead; multi_easy_bin requires the combined contig file from several samples plus BAM files You plan to use prebuilt taxonomic models — these cannot be used in multi-sample mode; self-supervised mode is required Input is already a set of finished bins or MAGs rather than raw reads/contigs needing binning http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Multi-sample metagenomic binning workflow that concatenates per-sample contigs from several environments, maps all reads against the combined FASTA, and bins with SemiBin2's self-supervised contrastive learning (multi_easy_bin) to recover more high-quality genera/species/strains than VAMB. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209
skills.summary: Multi-sample metagenomic binning workflow that concatenates per-sample contigs from several environments, maps all reads against the combined FASTA, and bins with SemiBin2's self-supervised contrastive learning (multi_easy_bin) to recover more high-quality genera/species/strains than VAMB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-sample data: use SemiBin2's single_easy_bin instead; multi_easy_bin requires the combined contig file from several samples plus BAM files You plan to use prebuilt taxonomic models — these cannot be used in multi-sample mode; self-supervised mode is required Input is already a set of finished bins or MAGs rather than raw reads/contigs needing binning

skills.description: Use when untargeted Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical or animal samples contain host (e.g. human, mouse, mastomys), reagent, or bacterial contamination that must be removed before viral de novo assembly.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-decontamination
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-decontamination Use when untargeted Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical or animal samples contain host (e.g. human, mouse, mastomys), reagent, or bacterial contamination that must be removed before viral de novo assembly. Deactivate the centrifuge filter with --centrifuge_do_filter false when Centrifuge's limited accuracy would risk removing true viral reads as false positives Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox): decontamination alone does not fix assembly inaccuracies; outputs should be treated as draft genomes Do not apply the non-viral read filter to contigs — the centrifuge classification of contigs is only for overview, filtering applies to reads (not contigs) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Two-stage removal of non-viral reads from untargeted nanopore FASTQ data: Centrifuge taxonomic classification filters reads classified as non-viral with score >= 150, then minimap2 mapping against host/reagent reference sets (contamination.yaml) extracts and discards remaining contaminant reads, yielding a cleaned read set for downstream assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Two-stage removal of non-viral reads from untargeted nanopore FASTQ data: Centrifuge taxonomic classification filters reads classified as non-viral with score >= 150, then minimap2 mapping against host/reagent reference sets (contamination.yaml) extracts and discards remaining contaminant reads, yielding a cleaned read set for downstream assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Deactivate the centrifuge filter with --centrifuge_do_filter false when Centrifuge's limited accuracy would risk removing true viral reads as false positives Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox): decontamination alone does not fix assembly inaccuracies; outputs should be treated as draft genomes Do not apply the non-viral read filter to contigs — the centrifuge classification of contigs is only for overview, filtering applies to reads (not contigs)

skills.description: Use when you need to judge assembly quality by read support: you have assembled contig FASTA files (individual or merged) and matching trimmed reads, and want per-contig base-coverage percentages.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-contigs
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-contigs Use when you need to judge assembly quality by read support: you have assembled contig FASTA files (individual or merged) and matching trimmed reads, and want per-contig base-coverage percentages. Input is raw reads without assembled contigs — this skill validates assemblies, it does not perform de novo assembly The reference genomes (not contigs) are the alignment target — use Nucmer-based contig-to-reference alignment for reference genome coverage instead You only need assembly length metrics (total size, N50/N90), which the article notes are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates metagenomic assemblies (individual assembler outputs and MeGAMerged contig sets such as MergedContigs.fasta) by mapping trimmed sequencing reads back to contigs with BWA and computing per-contig/per-assembly coverage statistics with SAMtools, reproducing comparisons like the CLC bio oil-spill (~85% coverage) vs MeGAMerge-without-CLC-bio (~99% coverage) analysis. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Validates metagenomic assemblies (individual assembler outputs and MeGAMerged contig sets such as MergedContigs.fasta) by mapping trimmed sequencing reads back to contigs with BWA and computing per-contig/per-assembly coverage statistics with SAMtools, reproducing comparisons like the CLC bio oil-spill (~85% coverage) vs MeGAMerge-without-CLC-bio (~99% coverage) analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads without assembled contigs — this skill validates assemblies, it does not perform de novo assembly The reference genomes (not contigs) are the alignment target — use Nucmer-based contig-to-reference alignment for reference genome coverage instead You only need assembly length metrics (total size, N50/N90), which the article notes are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance'

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore read data (FASTQ, FAST5, or POD5, optionally gzipped) from a suspected viral sample must be assigned a taxonomic identity as part of a virus surveillance workflow.
skills.name: metagenomic-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-taxonomic-classification Use when raw nanopore read data (FASTQ, FAST5, or POD5, optionally gzipped) from a suspected viral sample must be assigned a taxonomic identity as part of a virus surveillance workflow. The goal is de novo taxonomic profiling of complex metagenomes beyond virus detection — VirDetector is a targeted virus-surveillance pipeline, not a general-purpose classifier. Samples are already assembled consensus genomes in FASTA form and only phylogenetic placement is needed — these enter the pipeline from the alignment step onwards, not classification. The sequencing platform is not Oxford Nanopore — the pipeline is designed for nanopore sequencing data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Taxonomic classification of nanopore sequencing samples as implemented in the VirDetector pipeline, which classifies each sample taxonomically after preprocessing and uses the detected virus identity to drive downstream consensus genome reconstruction and phylogenetic analyses. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Taxonomic classification of nanopore sequencing samples as implemented in the VirDetector pipeline, which classifies each sample taxonomically after preprocessing and uses the detected virus identity to drive downstream consensus genome reconstruction and phylogenetic analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo taxonomic profiling of complex metagenomes beyond virus detection — VirDetector is a targeted virus-surveillance pipeline, not a general-purpose classifier. Samples are already assembled consensus genomes in FASTA form and only phylogenetic placement is needed — these enter the pipeline from the alignment step onwards, not classification. The sequencing platform is not Oxford Nanopore — the pipeline is designed for nanopore sequencing data.

skills.description: Use when nanopore long-read metagenomic FASTQ reads need per-read taxonomic classification and an interactive visual summary of community composition in a Galaxy-based (NanoGalaxy) workflow.
skills.name: metagenomic-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-taxonomic-classification Use when nanopore long-read metagenomic FASTQ reads need per-read taxonomic classification and an interactive visual summary of community composition in a Galaxy-based (NanoGalaxy) workflow. Input is genomic or plasmid sequence data intended for de novo genome assembly rather than metagenomic taxonomic profiling. Short-read (150-300 bp) sequencing data where a dedicated short-read classification pipeline is preferred — this skill is grounded in ONT long-read data that the integrated tools were intensively tested for. The user already has a Kraken2 report or feature/taxonomy table — in that case go straight to visualization, not re-classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies nanopore long-read metagenomic FASTQ reads taxonomically using Kraken2 (exact k-mer matches against a pre-indexed database) within NanoGalaxy/Galaxy, then renders the clade-ranked report as an interactive Krona HTML pie chart so users can inspect sample composition without coding. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: Classifies nanopore long-read metagenomic FASTQ reads taxonomically using Kraken2 (exact k-mer matches against a pre-indexed database) within NanoGalaxy/Galaxy, then renders the clade-ranked report as an interactive Krona HTML pie chart so users can inspect sample composition without coding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is genomic or plasmid sequence data intended for de novo genome assembly rather than metagenomic taxonomic profiling. Short-read (150-300 bp) sequencing data where a dedicated short-read classification pipeline is preferred — this skill is grounded in ONT long-read data that the integrated tools were intensively tested for. Input is a gene-level expression matrix or a bulk RNA-seq dataset rather than a single-cell, isoform-level percentile correlation matrix Modules from dynamicTreeCut are already distinct with low inter-cluster metatranscript correlation — merging would incorrectly collapse genuinely different expression modalities The goal is transcriptome reconstruction or isoform functional annotation (SQANTI3/IsoAnnotLite/tappAS territory), not co-expression module definition http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A module-refinement step in the acorde isoform co-expression clustering pipeline in which candidate isoform clusters are merged based on the correlation between their cluster metatranscripts (aggregate expression profiles), yielding non-redundant co-expression modules across cell types. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w

skills.description: Use when evaluating a methylation caller on PacBio HiFi reads with known ground-truth methylation states (PCR-treated unmethylated vs. M.SssI-methylated controls), e.g., to reproduce ccsmeth vs. HK model read-level accuracies or tune an ambiguous-call filter.
skills.name: methylation-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: methylation-accuracy-benchmarking Use when evaluating a methylation caller on PacBio HiFi reads with known ground-truth methylation states (PCR-treated unmethylated vs. M.SssI-methylated controls), e.g., to reproduce ccsmeth vs. HK model read-level accuracies or tune an ambiguous-call filter. The dataset lacks ground-truth methylation states (e.g., native human samples without paired PCR-treated and M.SssI-methylated control DNA), so read-level accuracy cannot be computed. The goal is haplotype-aware methylation phasing or allele-specific methylation detection rather than caller accuracy benchmarking — use the ccsmethphase pipeline instead. Detecting non-CpG 5mCs, hemimethylated CpGs, or other modifications such as 6mA — the article states these methods are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs and cannot be applied to non-CpG 5mC or 6mA. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark read-level DNA 5mCpG detection accuracy of PacBio CCS deep-learning callers (e.g., ccsmeth vs. the HK model) on M.SssI-methylated/PCR-treated control read pairs, and quantify the accuracy gain from discarding ambiguous calls at a ∆p = 0.33 confidence threshold. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Benchmark read-level DNA 5mCpG detection accuracy of PacBio CCS deep-learning callers (e.g., ccsmeth vs. the HK model) on M.SssI-methylated/PCR-treated control read pairs, and quantify the accuracy gain from discarding ambiguous calls at a ∆p = 0.33 confidence threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks ground-truth methylation states (e.g., native human samples without paired PCR-treated and M.SssI-methylated control DNA), so read-level accuracy cannot be computed. The goal is haplotype-aware methylation phasing or allele-specific methylation detection rather than caller accuracy benchmarking — use the ccsmethphase pipeline instead. Detecting non-CpG 5mCs, hemimethylated CpGs, or other modifications such as 6mA — the article states these methods are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs and cannot be applied to non-CpG 5mC or 6mA.

skills.description: Use when ONT reads with MM/ML methylation tags have been SNV-phased (HapCUT2) and WhatsHap-haplotagged, but many reads remain untagged and SNV phase blocks need to be chained across homozygous gaps.
skills.name: methylation-based-read-haplotagging
skills.search_text: methylation-based-read-haplotagging Use when ONT reads with MM/ML methylation tags have been SNV-phased (HapCUT2) and WhatsHap-haplotagged, but many reads remain untagged and SNV phase blocks need to be chained across homozygous gaps. Data are from sex chromosomes: random X inactivation in females gives inconsistent methylation-haplotype patterns, so MethPhaser is autosomes-only. Coverage is below ~30X, where the underlying SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) do not work reasonably. The BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors unless filtered first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Iteratively assign haplotype labels to unphased ONT reads using allele-specific CpG methylation signals, then bridge SNV phase blocks to produce an extended phased VCF and methylation-haplotagged BAM (MethPhaser). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Iteratively assign haplotype labels to unphased ONT reads using allele-specific CpG methylation signals, then bridge SNV phase blocks to produce an extended phased VCF and methylation-haplotagged BAM (MethPhaser).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from sex chromosomes: random X inactivation in females gives inconsistent methylation-haplotype patterns, so MethPhaser is autosomes-only. Coverage is below ~30X, where the underlying SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) do not work reasonably. The BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors unless filtered first.

skills.summary: Trains METEORE's consensus models — an optimized random forest (n_estimators=10, max_depth=3) and a RidgeCV multiple linear regression — on matched per-read methylation scores from Megalodon and DeepSignal, then applies them to held-out mixture data to produce per-site CpG methylation frequencies that are more accurate than either individual tool.

skills.search_text: methylation-motif-concordance-comparison Use when a de novo methylation motif set from ONT sequencing data must be validated against a published reference methylome motif set (e.g. PacBio-derived H. pylori J99 motifs from Krebes et al. 2014) to quantify concordance. Input is raw ONT signal (fast5 files) rather than an already-detected motif set — resquiggle with Tombo and run Snapper first The reference motif set is not from the same strain or is not sequence-comparable (different genome or modified-base context), making exact-sequence identity matching meaningless Motifs are to be compared at modified-base or methyltransferase-gene level rather than as sequence motifs http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Compares a de novo methylation motif set detected from Oxford Nanopore data (e.g. by Snapper) against a reference motif set derived from an orthogonal technology such as PacBio, by exact sequence matching including ambiguous-base notation, and reports matched and discordant motifs in a concordance table. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Compares a de novo methylation motif set detected from Oxford Nanopore data (e.g. by Snapper) against a reference motif set derived from an orthogonal technology such as PacBio, by exact sequence matching including ambiguous-base notation, and reports matched and discordant motifs in a concordance table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ONT signal (fast5 files) rather than an already-detected motif set — resquiggle with Tombo and run Snapper first The reference motif set is not from the same strain or is not sequence-comparable (different genome or modified-base context), making exact-sequence identity matching meaningless Motifs are to be compared at modified-base or methyltransferase-gene level rather than as sequence motifs

skills.description: Use when you have paired native and WGA-control ONT FAST5 read sets plus a reference genome and need to discover methylated sequence motifs de novo, without prior knowledge of methyltransferase specificity.
skills.name: methylation-motif-de-novo-detection
skills.search_text: methylation-motif-de-novo-detection Use when you have paired native and WGA-control ONT FAST5 read sets plus a reference genome and need to discover methylated sequence motifs de novo, without prior knowledge of methyltransferase specificity. You need per-read modified-base calls at individual positions rather than enriched motif sequences — Tombo's modified-base detection or Remora is the alternative The dataset lacks a matched WGA control read set, since Snapper's statistics rely on sample-versus-control signal-level k-mer comparisons You expect highly similar motifs that may collide: Nanodisco's fully automated mode was shown to merge H.pylori J99 motifs CATG and GCGC into GCRYG, so beware of degenerate-collision artifacts when motifs share k-mer context http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 De novo detection of bacterial methylation motifs from Oxford Nanopore sequencing by comparing native versus WGA-control read signal at k-mer level using Snapper's greedy position-specific motif enrichment algorithm, replacing manual, iterative workflows like MEME+Nanodisco. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: De novo detection of bacterial methylation motifs from Oxford Nanopore sequencing by comparing native versus WGA-control read signal at k-mer level using Snapper's greedy position-specific motif enrichment algorithm, replacing manual, iterative workflows like MEME+Nanodisco.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-read modified-base calls at individual positions rather than enriched motif sequences — Tombo's modified-base detection or Remora is the alternative The dataset lacks a matched WGA control read set, since Snapper's statistics rely on sample-versus-control signal-level k-mer comparisons You expect highly similar motifs that may collide: Nanodisco's fully automated mode was shown to merge H.pylori J99 motifs CATG and GCGC into GCRYG, so beware of degenerate-collision artifacts when motifs share k-mer context

skills.description: Use when you have resquiggled multi-fast5 ONT reads for a native sample and a matched WGA control plus a reference genome FASTA, and you need to discover methylated sequence motifs de novo rather than test known motifs.
skills.name: methylation-motif-sequence-analysis
skills.search_text: methylation-motif-sequence-analysis Use when you have resquiggled multi-fast5 ONT reads for a native sample and a matched WGA control plus a reference genome FASTA, and you need to discover methylated sequence motifs de novo rather than test known motifs. You only need per-read/per-site methylation calling at known motifs (e.g. dam/dcm) rather than de novo motif discovery — Tombo's alternative-model detection may suffice Input fast5 files are not resquiggled or are in single-read format — Tombo resquiggling and ont_fast5_api multi-fast5 conversion are prerequisites No matched WGA control sample exists — the KS-test comparison of native vs WGA signal distributions depends on the control http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 De novo detection of methylation motifs from Oxford Nanopore sequencing data using Snapper's high-sensitive greedy position-specific motif-enrichment algorithm, which compares native vs WGA control k-mer signal distributions and iteratively extracts over-represented motifs via chi-squared statistics. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: De novo detection of methylation motifs from Oxford Nanopore sequencing data using Snapper's high-sensitive greedy position-specific motif-enrichment algorithm, which compares native vs WGA control k-mer signal distributions and iteratively extracts over-represented motifs via chi-squared statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need per-read/per-site methylation calling at known motifs (e.g. dam/dcm) rather than de novo motif discovery — Tombo's alternative-model detection may suffice Input fast5 files are not resquiggled or are in single-read format — Tombo resquiggling and ont_fast5_api multi-fast5 conversion are prerequisites No matched WGA control sample exists — the KS-test comparison of native vs WGA signal distributions depends on the control

skills.description: Use when per-read methylation scores exist from a controlled mixture of methylated/unmethylated nanopore reads and default tool cutoffs show high dispersion against expected per-site methylation frequencies.
skills.name: methylation-score-threshold-optimization
skills.search_text: methylation-score-threshold-optimization Use when per-read methylation scores exist from a controlled mixture of methylated/unmethylated nanopore reads and default tool cutoffs show high dispersion against expected per-site methylation frequencies. Only per-site aggregated methylation frequencies are available and no per-read score files exist, since ROC-based cutoff derivation requires individual read scores from fully methylated and fully unmethylated controls The data are not controlled mixtures with known methylation proportions, so expected methylation frequencies for RMSE/correlation validation cannot be established The target modification or platform is not 5mC at CpG sites from R9.4.1 nanopore reads scored by these tools http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Optimizes per-read score cutoffs for nanopore CpG methylation tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Megalodon) by scanning score distributions from controlled mixtures of fully methylated and fully unmethylated reads, deriving single and double cutoffs that outperform default thresholds and reduce RMSE of per-site methylation frequency predictions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Optimizes per-read score cutoffs for nanopore CpG methylation tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Megalodon) by scanning score distributions from controlled mixtures of fully methylated and fully unmethylated reads, deriving single and double cutoffs that outperform default thresholds and reduce RMSE of per-site methylation frequency predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only per-site aggregated methylation frequencies are available and no per-read score files exist, since ROC-based cutoff derivation requires individual read scores from fully methylated and fully unmethylated controls The data are not controlled mixtures with known methylation proportions, so expected methylation frequencies for RMSE/correlation validation cannot be established The target modification or platform is not 5mC at CpG sites from R9.4.1 nanopore reads scored by these tools

skills.description: Use when comparing modification-calling tools on nanopore eventalign data where true-positive regions (e.g. ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) and a matched control (non-specific IgG) allow efficiency-vs-noise benchmarking across score thresholds.
skills.name: methylation-threshold-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: methylation-threshold-sweep-analysis Use when comparing modification-calling tools on nanopore eventalign data where true-positive regions (e.g. ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) and a matched control (non-specific IgG) allow efficiency-vs-noise benchmarking across score thresholds. Input lacks a matched negative-control dataset (e.g. non-specific IgG eventalign), so background noise rates cannot be estimated and the efficiency-to-noise metric is undefined. The goal is per-CpG methylation calling (mCG mode) rather than 6mA-containing region calling; use nanoHiMe's mCG module with its 1.5/-1.5 LLR thresholds instead. Reads are not nanopolish eventaligned or were basecalled with a different Guppy model version, making LLR scores incomparable with the trained nanoHiMe model. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark nanopore 6mA/modification callers (nanoHiMe vs Megalodon) by sweeping their score thresholds (LLR for nanoHiMe, probability for Megalodon) and comparing discovery efficiency against non-specific IgG background noise on nanoHiMe-seq HepG2 H3K27me3 data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Benchmark nanopore 6mA/modification callers (nanoHiMe vs Megalodon) by sweeping their score thresholds (LLR for nanoHiMe, probability for Megalodon) and comparing discovery efficiency against non-specific IgG background noise on nanoHiMe-seq HepG2 H3K27me3 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a matched negative-control dataset (e.g. non-specific IgG eventalign), so background noise rates cannot be estimated and the efficiency-to-noise metric is undefined. The goal is per-CpG methylation calling (mCG mode) rather than 6mA-containing region calling; use nanoHiMe's mCG module with its 1.5/-1.5 LLR thresholds instead. Reads are not nanopolish eventaligned or were basecalled with a different Guppy model version, making LLR scores incomparable with the trained nanoHiMe model.

skills.description: Use when comparing methylation motif callers (Nanodisco, Snapper, MEME+Tombo) on ONT sample/WGA-control fast5 pairs against a PacBio-validated methylome, or when reproducing known tool failure modes like motif merging.
skills.name: methylome-tool-benchmarking
skills.search_text: methylome-tool-benchmarking Use when comparing methylation motif callers (Nanodisco, Snapper, MEME+Tombo) on ONT sample/WGA-control fast5 pairs against a PacBio-validated methylome, or when reproducing known tool failure modes like motif merging. The goal is de novo characterization of a novel strain's methylome rather than tool comparison — apply Snapper directly (it requires no manual control during enrichment) instead of running benchmark rounds Input reads lack a matched WGA control fast5 set, since the tools here rely on sample-versus-control signal-level k-mer comparisons Motifs are already known and curated, so no de novo discovery or collision/merging behavior is being evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarks de novo methylation motif detection tools on Oxford Nanopore data against a known ground-truth methylome (H. pylori J99, previously characterized by PacBio), exposing failure modes such as Nanodisco's automated-mode motif collisions that merge CATG and GCGC into GCRYG. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Benchmarks de novo methylation motif detection tools on Oxford Nanopore data against a known ground-truth methylome (H. pylori J99, previously characterized by PacBio), exposing failure modes such as Nanodisco's automated-mode motif collisions that merge CATG and GCGC into GCRYG.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo characterization of a novel strain's methylome rather than tool comparison — apply Snapper directly (it requires no manual control during enrichment) instead of running benchmark rounds Input reads lack a matched WGA control fast5 set, since the tools here rely on sample-versus-control signal-level k-mer comparisons Motifs are already known and curated, so no de novo discovery or collision/merging behavior is being evaluated

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq reads are available for methyltransferase-deficient mutant strains plus several clonal wild-type isolates of the same bacterium, and the goal is to identify genes differentially expressed due to loss of a specific methylation motif.
skills.name: methyltransferase-mutant-transcriptome-comparison
skills.search_text: methyltransferase-mutant-transcriptome-comparison Use when RNA-seq reads are available for methyltransferase-deficient mutant strains plus several clonal wild-type isolates of the same bacterium, and the goal is to identify genes differentially expressed due to loss of a specific methylation motif. Input is single-molecule SMRT methylation data (aligned_reads.cmph5) rather than RNA-seq reads — use SMALR's SMsn/SMp protocols instead There are no clonal wild-type control isolates, so a mutant-vs-wild-type GLM contrast cannot be fit The aim is consensus-level methylome/motif discovery rather than quantifying methylation-loss effects on transcription http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A differential-expression workflow that quantifies how a genome-wide loss of a specific DNA methylation motif (e.g., 5'-GWCAY or 5'-TCAN6TRG/5'-CYAN6TGA in H. pylori J99) alters gene expression, by testing RNA-seq count data from methyltransferase mutants against multiple clonal wild-type isolates with edgeR's negative-binomial GLM framework. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: A differential-expression workflow that quantifies how a genome-wide loss of a specific DNA methylation motif (e.g., 5'-GWCAY or 5'-TCAN6TRG/5'-CYAN6TGA in H. pylori J99) alters gene expression, by testing RNA-seq count data from methyltransferase mutants against multiple clonal wild-type isolates with edgeR's negative-binomial GLM framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-molecule SMRT methylation data (aligned_reads.cmph5) rather than RNA-seq reads — use SMALR's SMsn/SMp protocols instead There are no clonal wild-type control isolates, so a mutant-vs-wild-type GLM contrast cannot be fit The aim is consensus-level methylome/motif discovery rather than quantifying methylation-loss effects on transcription

skills.description: Reference for preparing a noChr6 GRCh38 reference augmented with HLA-I/II genomic alleles for long-read (PacBio HiFi, ONT) WGS alignment prior to HLAminer HPRA prediction.
skills.name: mhc-reference-genome-preparation
skills.search_text: mhc-reference-genome-preparation Reference for preparing a noChr6 GRCh38 reference augmented with HLA-I/II genomic alleles for long-read (PacBio HiFi, ONT) WGS alignment prior to HLAminer HPRA prediction. Input is Illumina-sized short reads, where the HPTASR targeted-assembly route (TASR k-mer recruitment, de novo assembly, reciprocal BLASTN) is preferred over read alignment to this reference The reference must retain a full, unmasked chr6 HLA locus, which would collapse allelic HLA reads onto the single reference haplotype instead of resolving alleles The goal is transcriptome-only HLA typing (e.g., MCF-7 PacBio RNA-seq demo) rather than WGS long-read genomic alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Prepares a GRCh38-based (GCA_000001405.15) reference FASTA in which chr6 is excluded (or HLA-masked) and replaced with HLA class I/II genomic allele sequences from IMGT/HLA, so that long-read alignments stream directly into HLAminer for HLA-I/II prediction. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Prepares a GRCh38-based (GCA_000001405.15) reference FASTA in which chr6 is excluded (or HLA-masked) and replaced with HLA class I/II genomic allele sequences from IMGT/HLA, so that long-read alignments stream directly into HLAminer for HLA-I/II prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Illumina-sized short reads, where the HPTASR targeted-assembly route (TASR k-mer recruitment, de novo assembly, reciprocal BLASTN) is preferred over read alignment to this reference The reference must retain a full, unmasked chr6 HLA locus, which would collapse allelic HLA reads onto the single reference haplotype instead of resolving alleles The goal is transcriptome-only HLA typing (e.g., MCF-7 PacBio RNA-seq demo) rather than WGS long-read genomic alignment

skills.description: Use when log-phase microarray expression data are available for paired strains that differ by a known duplication genotype, and the goal is to test whether genes within the duplicated region show induced expression relative to the non-duplicated clonal counterpart.
skills.name: microarray-expression-normalization
skills.search_text: microarray-expression-normalization Use when log-phase microarray expression data are available for paired strains that differ by a known duplication genotype, and the goal is to test whether genes within the duplicated region show induced expression relative to the non-duplicated clonal counterpart. The expression data are not paired duplicated/non-duplicated strains from the same clonal population (e.g. unpaired samples or different genetic backgrounds), since the design compares a duplicated to a non-duplicated strain within the same clonal population. The data are RNA-seq or long-read expression measurements rather than the deposited DNA microarray data, for which this microarray-based workflow was designed. The question concerns genes outside the duplicated regions or genome-wide differential expression across many strain contrasts rather than induction of genes contained within known duplications. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Compares DNA-microarray transcript expression between paired S. pombe strains (duplicated vs non-duplicated members of the same clonal population, dataset E-MTAB-4019) to quantify induction of genes inside duplications and its relationship to copy number. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Compares DNA-microarray transcript expression between paired S. pombe strains (duplicated vs non-duplicated members of the same clonal population, dataset E-MTAB-4019) to quantify induction of genes inside duplications and its relationship to copy number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are not paired duplicated/non-duplicated strains from the same clonal population (e.g. unpaired samples or different genetic backgrounds), since the design compares a duplicated to a non-duplicated strain within the same clonal population. The data are RNA-seq or long-read expression measurements rather than the deposited DNA microarray data, for which this microarray-based workflow was designed. The question concerns genes outside the duplicated regions or genome-wide differential expression across many strain contrasts rather than induction of genes contained within known duplications.

skills.description: Use when a Visium HD full-resolution tissue image from Space Ranger must be converted to a fixed microns-per-pixel scale (e.g. mpp=0.5) before StarDist segmentation or downstream bin2cell plotting.
skills.name: microns-per-pixel-image-scale-conversion
skills.search_text: microns-per-pixel-image-scale-conversion Use when a Visium HD full-resolution tissue image from Space Ranger must be converted to a fixed microns-per-pixel scale (e.g. mpp=0.5) before StarDist segmentation or downstream bin2cell plotting. The morphology image is already at the desired mpp or has been rescaled by a prior bin2cell.scaled_he_image/scaled_if_image call — rescaling again would degrade or distort it The goal is expression-level processing (destriping, bin-to-cell grouping) rather than preparing a segmentation input — use bin2cell.destripe or bin2cell.bin_to_cell instead Working with non-Visium-HD imagery whose physical pixel size is unknown, since mpp cannot be set correctly without Space Ranger scale factors http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Rescales a Visium HD Space Ranger morphology image (H&E or IF) to a controlled microns-per-pixel (mpp) resolution using bin2cell's scaled_he_image/scaled_if_image, producing a consistent-resolution reference image for segmentation. This is needed because StarDist segmentation performance is highly dependent on input image resolution. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546
skills.summary: Rescales a Visium HD Space Ranger morphology image (H&E or IF) to a controlled microns-per-pixel (mpp) resolution using bin2cell's scaled_he_image/scaled_if_image, producing a consistent-resolution reference image for segmentation. This is needed because StarDist segmentation performance is highly dependent on input image resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The morphology image is already at the desired mpp or has been rescaled by a prior bin2cell.scaled_he_image/scaled_if_image call — rescaling again would degrade or distort it The goal is expression-level processing (destriping, bin-to-cell grouping) rather than preparing a segmentation input — use bin2cell.destripe or bin2cell.bin_to_cell instead Working with non-Visium-HD imagery whose physical pixel size is unknown, since mpp cannot be set correctly without Space Ranger scale factors

skills.description: Use when de novo profiling tandem repeats in error-prone long-read (ONT or PacBio) alignments: after consensus generation, to assign each discovered TR its motif (≤6 bp), multiplicity (≥5 perfect repeats), and coordinates.
skills.name: microsatellite-motif-parameterization
skills.search_text: microsatellite-motif-parameterization Use when de novo profiling tandem repeats in error-prone long-read (ONT or PacBio) alignments: after consensus generation, to assign each discovered TR its motif (≤6 bp), multiplicity (≥5 perfect repeats), and coordinates. Detecting repeats in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres and telomeres — TRiCoLOR cannot identify TRs there Profiling tandem repeats in polyploid species or haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome) — not supported Profiling mini-satellites (larger repeat units) — parameter values have only been extensively validated for micro-satellites http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Resolves the repeat motif and multiplicity of tandem repeats discovered in haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences using a fast regular expression (RegEx)-based approximate string-matching algorithm, as implemented in the TRiCoLOR REFER module. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Resolves the repeat motif and multiplicity of tandem repeats discovered in haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences using a fast regular expression (RegEx)-based approximate string-matching algorithm, as implemented in the TRiCoLOR REFER module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Detecting repeats in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres and telomeres — TRiCoLOR cannot identify TRs there Profiling tandem repeats in polyploid species or haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome) — not supported Profiling mini-satellites (larger repeat units) — parameter values have only been extensively validated for micro-satellites

skills.search_text: microscopy-calibration-measurement-extraction Use when reproducing or benchmarking slide-loader microscope workflows and you need the published calibration precision (slide-reload displacement) and imaging/detection throughput figures from this paper. You need calibration values for a different microscope platform or slide loader (e.g., a non-Prior PL-200 system) — these figures are instrument-specific to the Prior PL-200 slide loader, Zeiss Axioplan 2, Nikon DSLR D5100 setup You want software changelog or versioning metadata — the paper explicitly reports no changelog and no stated version number for OpenHiCAMM Extracts stage-calibration and acquisition-speed benchmark values reported for the OpenHiCAMM two-phase imaging workflow and structures them into a per-measurement CSV for reuse in method benchmarking. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017

skills.description: Use when a paper reports an autonomous imaging demonstration with per-phase metrics (slide counts, pass durations, per-slide rates, object-detection ranges, re-imaging yields) scattered across supplemental methods text that must be compiled into a verifiable table.
skills.name: microscopy-workflow-results-extraction
skills.search_text: microscopy-workflow-results-extraction Use when a paper reports an autonomous imaging demonstration with per-phase metrics (slide counts, pass durations, per-slide rates, object-detection ranges, re-imaging yields) scattered across supplemental methods text that must be compiled into a verifiable table. The article reports no quantitative demonstration metrics (e.g., the OpenHiCAMM discussion section is qualitative only: 'robust, flexible, easily adapted') — there is nothing to extract. The metrics you need are raw instrument logs or image files from your own run rather than reported figures in published text. The reported workflow is a single-pass acquisition with no phase decomposition, so per-phase duration/object-yield tabulation does not apply. Extracts quantified performance metrics from a demonstrated autonomous microscopy/HCS run (e.g., OpenHiCAMM's two-pass 95-slide Drosophila embryo screen) out of the paper's Transparent Methods supplemental text and assembles them into a structured tabular (CSV) record for reuse or verification. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Extracts quantified performance metrics from a demonstrated autonomous microscopy/HCS run (e.g., OpenHiCAMM's two-pass 95-slide Drosophila embryo screen) out of the paper's Transparent Methods supplemental text and assembles them into a structured tabular (CSV) record for reuse or verification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article reports no quantitative demonstration metrics (e.g., the OpenHiCAMM discussion section is qualitative only: 'robust, flexible, easily adapted') — there is nothing to extract. The metrics you need are raw instrument logs or image files from your own run rather than reported figures in published text. The reported workflow is a single-pass acquisition with no phase decomposition, so per-phase duration/object-yield tabulation does not apply.

skills.description: Use when a ntLink mapping run (ntLink map with paf=True) has produced a labelled PAF file of long-read-to-contig mappings and you must reproduce the mapping statistics of Table 5 (total mappings, average block length, average mappings per contig).
skills.name: miller-command-line-data-aggregation
skills.search_text: miller-command-line-data-aggregation Use when a ntLink mapping run (ntLink map with paf=True) has produced a labelled PAF file of long-read-to-contig mappings and you must reproduce the mapping statistics of Table 5 (total mappings, average block length, average mappings per contig). The file is not a PAF mapping output from ntLink's mapping mode (e.g. it is a scaffolded assembly FASTA or a Tigmint-long correction report) — these statistics are defined only over read-to-contig mapping records You need alignment-quality assessment of long-read mappings (identity, MAPQ, misassemblies) rather than counts and block-length summaries; the article directs those use cases to other protocols (e.g. Tigmint-long correction) or tools like QUAST http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Use Miller (mlr), the awk/sed-like tool for delimited data, to compute summary statistics from ntLink's labelled PAF read-to-contig mapping file — total mappings, average mapping block length, and average mappings per draft contig — as the quality assessment of Alternate Protocol 1. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Use Miller (mlr), the awk/sed-like tool for delimited data, to compute summary statistics from ntLink's labelled PAF read-to-contig mapping file — total mappings, average mapping block length, and average mappings per draft contig — as the quality assessment of Alternate Protocol 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The file is not a PAF mapping output from ntLink's mapping mode (e.g. it is a scaffolded assembly FASTA or a Tigmint-long correction report) — these statistics are defined only over read-to-contig mapping records You need alignment-quality assessment of long-read mappings (identity, MAPQ, misassemblies) rather than counts and block-length summaries; the article directs those use cases to other protocols (e.g. Tigmint-long correction) or tools like QUAST

skills.description: Use when building contigs or consensus sequences from long, error-prone nanopore reads without a reference — e.g., to find candidate overlapping reads for greedy contig extension, or to parameterize read overlap search in NanoSpring-style compression.
skills.name: minhash-overlap-detection
skills.search_text: minhash-overlap-detection Use when building contigs or consensus sequences from long, error-prone nanopore reads without a reference — e.g., to find candidate overlapping reads for greedy contig extension, or to parameterize read overlap search in NanoSpring-style compression. Input is short, low-error Illumina-style read data — NanoSpring's MinHash overlap approach targets long ONT reads, and compressors like SPRING or PgRC assume short reads instead. The goal is read-level overlap for de novo assembly of a published genome rather than compression — NanoSpring's consensus graph is an intermediate for lossless sequence compression, not a polished assembly. You need to compress quality values or read identifiers — NanoSpring compresses only base sequences from the FASTQ. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Detects overlapping nanopore reads by sketching sequences with MinHash and querying a MinHash index for candidates that overlap a growing consensus, as done in NanoSpring's approximate-assembly compression pipeline. Candidate overlaps are then confirmed with minimap2 alignment before insertion into a consensus graph. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Detects overlapping nanopore reads by sketching sequences with MinHash and querying a MinHash index for candidates that overlap a growing consensus, as done in NanoSpring's approximate-assembly compression pipeline. Candidate overlaps are then confirmed with minimap2 alignment before insertion into a consensus graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short, low-error Illumina-style read data — NanoSpring's MinHash overlap approach targets long ONT reads, and compressors like SPRING or PgRC assume short reads instead. The goal is read-level overlap for de novo assembly of a published genome rather than compression — NanoSpring's consensus graph is an intermediate for lossless sequence compression, not a polished assembly. You need to compress quality values or read identifiers — NanoSpring compresses only base sequences from the FASTQ.

skills.description: Use when you need to identify nanopore reads that overlap a query sequence using k-mer MinHash sketches — e.g., to reproduce or extend NanoSpring's overlap-finding stage for approximate-assembly-based compression of long, error-prone ONT reads.
skills.name: minhash-sketching-of-sequencing-reads
skills.search_text: minhash-sketching-of-sequencing-reads Use when you need to identify nanopore reads that overlap a query sequence using k-mer MinHash sketches — e.g., to reproduce or extend NanoSpring's overlap-finding stage for approximate-assembly-based compression of long, error-prone ONT reads. Reads are short and low-error (e.g., Illumina-style) — tools like SPRING and PgRC assume short reads and the minhash overlap approach targets long nanopore reads. You need reference-based compression — NanoSpring's minhash indexing is part of its reference-free approximate assembly approach. You need to compress read identifiers or quality values — NanoSpring only compresses the base sequences in the FASTQ file. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Index nanopore FASTQ read sequences by computing MinHash sketches over k-mers (default k=23, n=60 hash functions in NanoSpring) and building static lookup tables so that reads overlapping a query sequence can be found by matching at least t (default 6) of the n sketch values. This enables the approximate-assembly overlap step of NanoSpring's reference-free compression. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Index nanopore FASTQ read sequences by computing MinHash sketches over k-mers (default k=23, n=60 hash functions in NanoSpring) and building static lookup tables so that reads overlapping a query sequence can be found by matching at least t (default 6) of the n sketch values.
