skills.name: minimizer-based-long-read-scaffolding
skills.search_text: minimizer-based-long-read-scaffolding Use when a draft assembly (e.g. from Flye or another long-read assembler) has fragmented contigs and long reads (FASTQ, e.g. ONT SRR10028109) are available to infer contig ordering, orientation, joins, and gap-filling. The input is already a set of long-read-to-contig alignments rather than raw reads plus a draft assembly — instead use ntLink as a standalone mapping tool (Alternate Protocol 1) or Tigmint-long correction (Alternate Protocol 2) The goal is correcting misassemblies rather than ordering/orienting contigs — use the Tigmint-long correction workflow built on ntLink mappings No long-read data are available, since ntLink infers joins from long-read mapping evidence http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scaffold a draft genome assembly using ntLink's lightweight minimizer-based long-read mappings rather than full read alignments, optionally with overlap detection, gap-filling, and in-code scaffolding iterations, to produce highly contiguous scaffolds while remaining computationally efficient. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Scaffold a draft genome assembly using ntLink's lightweight minimizer-based long-read mappings rather than full read alignments, optionally with overlap detection, gap-filling, and in-code scaffolding iterations, to produce highly contiguous scaffolds while remaining computationally efficient.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a set of long-read-to-contig alignments rather than raw reads plus a draft assembly — instead use ntLink as a standalone mapping tool (Alternate Protocol 1) or Tigmint-long correction (Alternate Protocol 2) The goal is correcting misassemblies rather than ordering/orienting contigs — use the Tigmint-long correction workflow built on ntLink mappings No long-read data are available, since ntLink infers joins from long-read mapping evidence

skills.description: Use when a ntLink mapping-mode PAF file of long-read to contig mappings (emitted with paf=True) must be assessed numerically, e.g. reproducing the Table 5 statistics: total mappings, average block length, and average mappings per contig.
skills.name: minimizer-based-mapping-block-length-computation
skills.search_text: minimizer-based-mapping-block-length-computation Use when a ntLink mapping-mode PAF file of long-read to contig mappings (emitted with paf=True) must be assessed numerically, e.g. reproducing the Table 5 statistics: total mappings, average block length, and average mappings per contig. The goal is scaffolding or correction itself (Basic Protocols 1-3, or Alternate Protocol 2 with Tigmint-long) rather than numerically assessing the mapping output. The mapping file is a standard minimap2 SAM/BAM or an unlabelled PAF rather than ntLink's labelled PAF output, so the mlr workflow over named delimited fields does not apply. Base-level alignment quality or identity metrics are required; minimizer-based PAF block lengths do not encode alignment scores. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies ntLink's minimizer-based long-read mappings by computing the total number of mappings, the average mapping block length from PAF start-end coordinates, and the average number of read mappings per draft contig using Miller (mlr), so that Alternate Protocol 1 mapping output can be validated against Table 5. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Quantifies ntLink's minimizer-based long-read mappings by computing the total number of mappings, the average mapping block length from PAF start-end coordinates, and the average number of read mappings per draft contig using Miller (mlr), so that Alternate Protocol 1 mapping output can be validated against Table 5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scaffolding or correction itself (Basic Protocols 1-3, or Alternate Protocol 2 with Tigmint-long) rather than numerically assessing the mapping output. The mapping file is a standard minimap2 SAM/BAM or an unlabelled PAF rather than ntLink's labelled PAF output, so the mlr workflow over named delimited fields does not apply. Base-level alignment quality or identity metrics are required; minimizer-based PAF block lengths do not encode alignment scores.

skills.description: Use when you have a draft assembly FASTA (e.g. celegans-abyss.fa) and long reads (e.g. SRR10028109 FASTQ.GZ) and need read-to-contig mappings faster than minimap2 alignments, in PAF format, for scaffolding or correction.
skills.name: minimizer-based-read-mapping
skills.search_text: minimizer-based-read-mapping Use when you have a draft assembly FASTA (e.g. celegans-abyss.fa) and long reads (e.g. SRR10028109 FASTQ.GZ) and need read-to-contig mappings faster than minimap2 alignments, in PAF format, for scaffolding or correction. You need base-level alignment detail (CIGAR strings, per-base alignment scores) rather than minimizer-based contig-level mappings Your goal is scaffolding itself rather than standalone mappings — run the full ntLink scaffold pipeline instead of pair/mapping mode The read or assembly data are not present in the current working directory, which ntLink requires (use soft links) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Use ntLink's lightweight minimizer-based mapping mode (Alternate Protocol 1) to align long reads to draft assembly contigs without full read alignments, outputting PAF-like mappings that can power scaffolding, misassembly detection (Tigmint-long), or other downstream applications. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Use ntLink's lightweight minimizer-based mapping mode (Alternate Protocol 1) to align long reads to draft assembly contigs without full read alignments, outputting PAF-like mappings that can power scaffolding, misassembly detection (Tigmint-long), or other downstream applications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need base-level alignment detail (CIGAR strings, per-base alignment scores) rather than minimizer-based contig-level mappings Your goal is scaffolding itself rather than standalone mappings — run the full ntLink scaffold pipeline instead of pair/mapping mode The read or assembly data are not present in the current working directory, which ntLink requires (use soft links)

skills.description: Use when mapping long, noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads to a large reference genome and you need fast seed lookup plus detection of inversion SVs via anchor chaining.
skills.name: minimizer-hash-table-genome-indexing
skills.search_text: minimizer-hash-table-genome-indexing Use when mapping long, noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads to a large reference genome and you need fast seed lookup plus detection of inversion SVs via anchor chaining. The task is short-read mapping without structural-variant detection — invMap targets long noisy reads spanning SV breakpoints. The reference genome or read set exceeds available memory — invMap requires a minimum of 16G of RAM for large reference genomes. Input files are not in FASTA or FASTQ format and cannot be converted. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Index a reference genome as a minimizer hash-table so that seeds for each long noisy read can be retrieved rapidly, as done by the invMap mapper to anchor PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads and expose inversion structural variants. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Index a reference genome as a minimizer hash-table so that seeds for each long noisy read can be retrieved rapidly, as done by the invMap mapper to anchor PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads and expose inversion structural variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is short-read mapping without structural-variant detection — invMap targets long noisy reads spanning SV breakpoints. The reference genome or read set exceeds available memory — invMap requires a minimum of 16G of RAM for large reference genomes. Input files are not in FASTA or FASTQ format and cannot be converted.

skills.description: Use when you have a draft genome assembly FASTA plus long-read sequencing data and need fast, alignment-free read-to-contig mappings (PAF-like) to infer contig ordering/orientation, gap sizes, or misassemblies.
skills.name: minimizer-sketch-computation
skills.search_text: minimizer-sketch-computation Use when you have a draft genome assembly FASTA plus long-read sequencing data and need fast, alignment-free read-to-contig mappings (PAF-like) to infer contig ordering/orientation, gap sizes, or misassemblies. You already have accurate full read alignments (e.g. minimap2 PAF/BAM) and alignment-based scaffolding evidence is acceptable — minimizer mappings are a lightweight substitute, not a richer signal Input is short-read sequencing data — the method's joins rely on long reads spanning multiple contigs You need base-level alignment detail (e.g. variant calling) rather than contig-level mapping evidence http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Compute ordered minimizer sketches of a target draft assembly (FASTA) and long reads (FASTA/FASTQ) and use them to produce lightweight minimizer-based read-to-contig mappings, as implemented in ntLink with btllib ntHash2-style recursive spaced-seed hashing. These mappings replace read alignments as the evidence for scaffolding joins, gap estimates, and downstream applications such as misassembly detection. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Compute ordered minimizer sketches of a target draft assembly (FASTA) and long reads (FASTA/FASTQ) and use them to produce lightweight minimizer-based read-to-contig mappings, as implemented in ntLink with btllib ntHash2-style recursive spaced-seed hashing. These mappings replace read alignments as the evidence for scaffolding joins, gap estimates, and downstream applications such as misassembly detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have accurate full read alignments (e.g. minimap2 PAF/BAM) and alignment-based scaffolding evidence is acceptable — minimizer mappings are a lightweight substitute, not a richer signal Input is short-read sequencing data — the method's joins rely on long reads spanning multiple contigs You need base-level alignment detail (e.g. variant calling) rather than contig-level mapping evidence

skills.description: Use when a downstream application (e.g. Tigmint-long correction or misassembly detection) needs long-read-to-contig mappings from a draft FASTA and long-read FASTQ, and alignment-based mapping (e.g. minimap2) is unnecessary or too heavyweight.
skills.name: minimizer-sketch-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: minimizer-sketch-parameter-configuration Use when a downstream application (e.g. Tigmint-long correction or misassembly detection) needs long-read-to-contig mappings from a draft FASTA and long-read FASTQ, and alignment-based mapping (e.g. minimap2) is unnecessary or too heavyweight. The goal is de novo scaffolding with overlap detection, gap-filling, or in-code iterations (Basic Protocols 1-3) rather than producing standalone read-to-contig mappings. The assembly draft needs correction with Tigmint-long but no ntLink mapping file has been generated yet — Alternate Protocol 2 consumes these mappings rather than producing them. Short paired-end read data is the input; ntLink's mapping/scaffolding modes are designed for long-read sequencing data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Configure and run ntLink's minimizer-based mapping mode so that ordered minimizer sketches of a draft assembly and long reads are computed and used to map reads to contigs without full read alignment, emitting standard PAF-formatted mappings. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Configure and run ntLink's minimizer-based mapping mode so that ordered minimizer sketches of a draft assembly and long reads are computed and used to map reads to contigs without full read alignment, emitting standard PAF-formatted mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo scaffolding with overlap detection, gap-filling, or in-code iterations (Basic Protocols 1-3) rather than producing standalone read-to-contig mappings. The assembly draft needs correction with Tigmint-long but no ntLink mapping file has been generated yet — Alternate Protocol 2 consumes these mappings rather than producing them. Short paired-end read data is the input; ntLink's mapping/scaffolding modes are designed for long-read sequencing data.

skills.description: Use when building or updating a NanoPipe target whose alignments against MinION reads should use MinION-adjusted scoring, e.g. before running lastal with a trained parameters file via the -p option.
skills.name: minion-error-model-calibration
skills.search_text: minion-error-model-calibration Use when building or updating a NanoPipe target whose alignments against MinION reads should use MinION-adjusted scoring, e.g. before running lastal with a trained parameters file via the -p option. Input reads are not MinION nanopore data — the trained parameters are specifically adjusted to MinION sequencing specifics and would mis-score other platforms A precompiled NanoPipe target already ships with last-train-derived parameters and the target/reference has not changed The task is alignment analysis or consensus/SNP calling (e.g. 20% alternate coverage SNP candidates, majority-rule consensus) rather than producing the scoring parameters themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Trains LAST alignment scoring parameters (substitution matrix with per-nucleotide-pair mismatch costs plus insertion/deletion rates) on a sample of MinION reads so that downstream alignment in NanoPipe reflects the error profile of Oxford Nanopore sequencing rather than a generic scoring scheme. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Trains LAST alignment scoring parameters (substitution matrix with per-nucleotide-pair mismatch costs plus insertion/deletion rates) on a sample of MinION reads so that downstream alignment in NanoPipe reflects the error profile of Oxford Nanopore sequencing rather than a generic scoring scheme.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not MinION nanopore data — the trained parameters are specifically adjusted to MinION sequencing specifics and would mis-score other platforms A precompiled NanoPipe target already ships with last-train-derived parameters and the target/reference has not changed The task is alignment analysis or consensus/SNP calling (e.g. 20% alternate coverage SNP candidates, majority-rule consensus) rather than producing the scoring parameters themselves

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample demultiplexed Nanopore FASTQ files of multi-kilobase rDNA amplicons and need to discard low-quality/short reads before consensus calling or downstream barcode analysis.
skills.name: minion-long-read-qc-thresholding
skills.search_text: minion-long-read-qc-thresholding Use when you have per-sample demultiplexed Nanopore FASTQ files of multi-kilobase rDNA amplicons and need to discard low-quality/short reads before consensus calling or downstream barcode analysis. Input FASTQ has not yet been demultiplexed by MiniBar — filter per-sample only after dual-index binning, not on the raw combined MinION read file Sequencing short amplicons (e.g. COI barcodes or Illumina short reads) — the 3000 bp minimum length cutoff would discard all reads, since it is sized for multi-kilobase rDNA amplicons Reads still carry barcode and primer sequences at their ends and you have not run MiniBar -T trimming — filtering untrimmed reads will not match the reference yield http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quality- and length-filters MiniBar-demultiplexed Nanopore long rDNA amplicon reads with NanoFilt, using a minimum average Phred quality of 13 and a minimum read length of 3000 bp, yielding ~245,433 filtered reads for the main run. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Quality- and length-filters MiniBar-demultiplexed Nanopore long rDNA amplicon reads with NanoFilt, using a minimum average Phred quality of 13 and a minimum read length of 3000 bp, yielding ~245,433 filtered reads for the main run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input FASTQ has not yet been demultiplexed by MiniBar — filter per-sample only after dual-index binning, not on the raw combined MinION read file Sequencing short amplicons (e.g. COI barcodes or Illumina short reads) — the 3000 bp minimum length cutoff would discard all reads, since it is sized for multi-kilobase rDNA amplicons Reads still carry barcode and primer sequences at their ends and you have not run MiniBar -T trimming — filtering untrimmed reads will not match the reference yield

skills.description: Use when analyzing Oxford Nanopore MinION reads (FASTA/FASTQ) aligned against a target sequence to detect and rank SNP candidates, and you need error-aware polymorphism probabilities instead of naive majority-rule consensus calls.
skills.name: minion-sequencing-error-aware-polymorphism-analysis
skills.search_text: minion-sequencing-error-aware-polymorphism-analysis Use when analyzing Oxford Nanopore MinION reads (FASTA/FASTQ) aligned against a target sequence to detect and rank SNP candidates, and you need error-aware polymorphism probabilities instead of naive majority-rule consensus calls. You need sophisticated SNP statistics or variant calling beyond NanoPipe's current scoring — the authors state more sophisticated statistics for SNP detection and evaluation are planned future work Your task is metagenomics analysis — NanoPipe does not yet support it (implementation planned) Positions have read coverage below 10 reads — a gap is assigned rather than a nucleotide/consensus call, so polymorphism scoring is inappropriate there http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detects SNP candidates from MinION nanopore reads aligned to a target by combining coverage filters (20% alternate coverage, 30% of maximum contig coverage), transition/transversion-weighted probability scoring, and p-error-based alignment quality assessment, producing a ranked polymorphisms table. This is NanoPipe's core polymorphism-analysis approach, adjusted to the specifics of MinION sequencing technology. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Detects SNP candidates from MinION nanopore reads aligned to a target by combining coverage filters (20% alternate coverage, 30% of maximum contig coverage), transition/transversion-weighted probability scoring, and p-error-based alignment quality assessment, producing a ranked polymorphisms table. This is NanoPipe's core polymorphism-analysis approach, adjusted to the specifics of MinION sequencing technology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need sophisticated SNP statistics or variant calling beyond NanoPipe's current scoring — the authors state more sophisticated statistics for SNP detection and evaluation are planned future work Your task is metagenomics analysis — NanoPipe does not yet support it (implementation planned) Positions have read coverage below 10 reads — a gap is assigned rather than a nucleotide/consensus call, so polymorphism scoring is inappropriate there

skills.description: Use when raw MinION/ONT sequencing reads (FASTA/FASTQ) have been mapped to a target reference and a per-target consensus sequence must be computed while handling nanopore error via read-count and IUPAC ambiguity thresholds.
skills.name: minion-sequencing-error-handling
skills.search_text: minion-sequencing-error-handling Use when raw MinION/ONT sequencing reads (FASTA/FASTQ) have been mapped to a target reference and a per-target consensus sequence must be computed while handling nanopore error via read-count and IUPAC ambiguity thresholds. Data are not from Oxford Nanopore MinION devices or were not aligned to a target with LAST — the consensus thresholds are tuned to MinION error specifics Metagenomics analysis is required — NanoPipe does not yet support it (implementation planned) Sophisticated SNP detection/evaluation statistics are required — current SNP detection statistics are basic and are planned future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates a majority-rule consensus sequence per target chromosome/region from MinION read-to-target alignments (LAST v946 MAF) as implemented in NanoPipe, using coverage and ambiguity thresholds to control nanopore sequencing error. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Generates a majority-rule consensus sequence per target chromosome/region from MinION read-to-target alignments (LAST v946 MAF) as implemented in NanoPipe, using coverage and ambiguity thresholds to control nanopore sequencing error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not from Oxford Nanopore MinION devices or were not aligned to a target with LAST — the consensus thresholds are tuned to MinION error specifics Metagenomics analysis is required — NanoPipe does not yet support it (implementation planned) Sophisticated SNP detection/evaluation statistics are required — current SNP detection statistics are basic and are planned future work

skills.description: Use when MinION nanopore amplicon or targeted reads (FASTA/FASTQ) must be aligned to a reference target and expected mutations/SNPs identified, e.g. EGFR exons 17-22 from cell line H1975 against hg38.
skills.name: minion-snp-variant-detection
skills.search_text: minion-snp-variant-detection Use when MinION nanopore amplicon or targeted reads (FASTA/FASTQ) must be aligned to a reference target and expected mutations/SNPs identified, e.g. EGFR exons 17-22 from cell line H1975 against hg38. Metagenomics analysis — NanoPipe does not yet support it; the authors state implementation of a metagenomics option is planned Analysis requiring sophisticated SNP statistics beyond the current pipeline — the authors note 'more sophisticated statistics for SNP detection and evaluation' are planned future work Reads too short for reliable mapping — set a read length limit (e.g. 200 nucleotides) or the result is 'noise' from too-short read alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Detect SNP variants from Oxford Nanopore MinION amplicon reads using NanoPipe: align FASTA/FASTQ reads against a target database with LAST (version 946, MinION-trained parameters), then call polymorphisms with nanopipe_calc_polymorphism.py using coverage- and probability-based filters. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Detect SNP variants from Oxford Nanopore MinION amplicon reads using NanoPipe: align FASTA/FASTQ reads against a target database with LAST (version 946, MinION-trained parameters), then call polymorphisms with nanopipe_calc_polymorphism.py using coverage- and probability-based filters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metagenomics analysis — NanoPipe does not yet support it; the authors state implementation of a metagenomics option is planned Analysis requiring sophisticated SNP statistics beyond the current pipeline — the authors note 'more sophisticated statistics for SNP detection and evaluation' are planned future work Reads too short for reliable mapping — set a read length limit (e.g. 200 nucleotides) or the result is 'noise' from too-short read alignments

skills.description: Use when aligning MinION nanopore reads (FASTA/FASTQ) against a target genome and you need MinION-trained LAST scoring parameters plus split-alignment handling for chimeric or rearranged reads.
skills.name: minion-trained-alignment-parameter-application
skills.search_text: minion-trained-alignment-parameter-application Use when aligning MinION nanopore reads (FASTA/FASTQ) against a target genome and you need MinION-trained LAST scoring parameters plus split-alignment handling for chimeric or rearranged reads. The input is not Oxford Nanopore/MinION data — the parameters are last-train-derived for MinION technology specifics and are not transferable to Illumina or PacBio reads The target sequence database has not been created/indexed with lastdb — NanoPipe requires a prepared target before alignment Metagenomic analysis is the goal — the article states metagenomics analysis is not yet supported and implementation is planned http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Maps MinION sequencing reads to a target genome using the LAST aligner (version 946) with last-train-derived, MinION-adjusted scoring parameters and a substitution matrix, then resolves split alignments with last-split. This is the mapping stage of the NanoPipe pipeline, tuned to the error profile of Oxford Nanopore data. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Maps MinION sequencing reads to a target genome using the LAST aligner (version 946) with last-train-derived, MinION-adjusted scoring parameters and a substitution matrix, then resolves split alignments with last-split. This is the mapping stage of the NanoPipe pipeline, tuned to the error profile of Oxford Nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not Oxford Nanopore/MinION data — the parameters are last-train-derived for MinION technology specifics and are not transferable to Illumina or PacBio reads The target sequence database has not been created/indexed with lastdb — NanoPipe requires a prepared target before alignment Metagenomic analysis is the goal — the article states metagenomics analysis is not yet supported and implementation is planned

skills.description: Use when the analysis goal is de novo identification and genotyping of tandem repeats with motif length ≥7 bp (mini-satellites) from haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio BAM alignments, requiring overriding TRiCoLOR's default motif-length parameter.
skills.name: minisatellite-motif-size-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: minisatellite-motif-size-parameter-tuning Use when the analysis goal is de novo identification and genotyping of tandem repeats with motif length ≥7 bp (mini-satellites) from haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio BAM alignments, requiring overriding TRiCoLOR's default motif-length parameter. The target regions are unassembled parts of the genome (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats The sample is polyploid or contains haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support Default micro-satellite profiling (motifs ≤6 bp) suffices — in that case run TRiCoLOR with its default motif-length setting instead of tuning '--size' http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Parameterizes TRiCoLOR (via the '--size' option of the REFER module) so its RegEx-based matcher detects motifs longer than the default ≤6 bp micro-satellite setting, enabling de novo mini-satellite profiling from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Parameterizes TRiCoLOR (via the '--size' option of the REFER module) so its RegEx-based matcher detects motifs longer than the default ≤6 bp micro-satellite setting, enabling de novo mini-satellite profiling from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target regions are unassembled parts of the genome (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats The sample is polyploid or contains haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support Default micro-satellite profiling (motifs ≤6 bp) suffices — in that case run TRiCoLOR with its default motif-length setting instead of tuning '--size'

skills.description: Use when a consensus DE isoform set must be pruned before co-usage/coDIU analysis so that low-contribution (minor) isoforms and single-DE-isoform genes do not enter downstream isoform co-expression modeling.
skills.name: minor-isoform-expression-filtering
skills.search_text: minor-isoform-expression-filtering Use when a consensus DE isoform set must be pruned before co-usage/coDIU analysis so that low-contribution (minor) isoforms and single-DE-isoform genes do not enter downstream isoform co-expression modeling. When the goal is gene-level DE rather than isoform co-usage — the 10% minor-isoform cutoff and single-DE-isoform-gene removal would discard valid gene-level signals. When the input is an unfiltered isoform quantification matrix that has not yet gone through consensus DIU significance selection; filtering must follow DE isoform selection. When isoform proportions cannot be reliably computed (e.g. transcriptome without isoform-to-gene relationships or per-isoform expression estimates). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A post-DIU-selection filtering step from the acorde pipeline that removes isoforms whose expression is <10% of their gene's total expression, followed by exclusion of genes left with only a single DE isoform, to isolate genes with meaningful isoform co-usage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: A post-DIU-selection filtering step from the acorde pipeline that removes isoforms whose expression is <10% of their gene's total expression, followed by exclusion of genes left with only a single DE isoform, to isolate genes with meaningful isoform co-usage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is gene-level DE rather than isoform co-usage — the 10% minor-isoform cutoff and single-DE-isoform-gene removal would discard valid gene-level signals. When the input is an unfiltered isoform quantification matrix that has not yet gone through consensus DIU significance selection; filtering must follow DE isoform selection. When isoform proportions cannot be reliably computed (e.g. transcriptome without isoform-to-gene relationships or per-isoform expression estimates).

skills.description: Use when comparing host-identification accuracy of taxonomic classifiers (e.g., Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, MEGAN-LR, minimap2 variants) on ARG-containing long reads in simulated metagenomes with known ground truth.
skills.name: misclassification-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: misclassification-rate-quantification Use when comparing host-identification accuracy of taxonomic classifiers (e.g., Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, MEGAN-LR, minimap2 variants) on ARG-containing long reads in simulated metagenomes with known ground truth. Reads have no simulated or known ground-truth host labels — misclassification rate cannot be computed without a species-level truth set The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in understudied environments, where assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods are better suited Evaluating short-read classifiers — this benchmark is specific to ARG-carrying long (ONT-style) reads and NanoSim error models http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 Quantifies per-species and overall misclassification rates of taxonomic assignment strategies applied to ARG-carrying long reads, as used in the Argo benchmark where minimap2+RO achieved 0.19% (HQ) and 0.09% (LQ) overall misclassification versus up to 16.63% for Kraken2 (M. tuberculosis, HQ). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Quantifies per-species and overall misclassification rates of taxonomic assignment strategies applied to ARG-carrying long reads, as used in the Argo benchmark where minimap2+RO achieved 0.19% (HQ) and 0.09% (LQ) overall misclassification versus up to 16.63% for Kraken2 (M. tuberculosis, HQ).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have no simulated or known ground-truth host labels — misclassification rate cannot be computed without a species-level truth set The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in understudied environments, where assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) methods are better suited Evaluating short-read classifiers — this benchmark is specific to ARG-carrying long (ONT-style) reads and NanoSim error models

skills.description: Use when analyzing ONT direct RNA sequencing FASTQ/BAM data to detect m6A (or other RNA modifications such as pseudouridine) from base-called 'error' signatures, or to build feature tables for stoichiometry estimation.
skills.name: mismatch-frequency-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: mismatch-frequency-feature-extraction Use when analyzing ONT direct RNA sequencing FASTQ/BAM data to detect m6A (or other RNA modifications such as pseudouridine) from base-called 'error' signatures, or to build feature tables for stoichiometry estimation. When per-read, single-molecule modification resolution is required — EpiNano aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and does not predict modifications in individual RNA molecules When a specific modification type must be distinguished (e.g. m1A vs m6A) — the algorithm does not distinguish between different modification types When data was base-called with a base-caller version for which no pre-trained SVM model exists (e.g. non-Guppy 3.1.5 data with EpiNano-SVM); in that case use EpiNano-Error pairwise mode or retrain http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Extract per-site (per-base and per-k-mer) base-calling error features — mismatch frequency, deletion frequency, insertion frequency, and per-base quality — from ONT direct RNA sequencing reads with EpiNano, as the basis for detecting and quantifying m6A RNA modifications. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Extract per-site (per-base and per-k-mer) base-calling error features — mismatch frequency, deletion frequency, insertion frequency, and per-base quality — from ONT direct RNA sequencing reads with EpiNano, as the basis for detecting and quantifying m6A RNA modifications.

skills.search_text: mixed-model-gwas-association-testing Use when testing genotype variants (SVs with minor allele counts ≥5, SNPs or indels) against quantitative trait measurements across related strains or individuals, where population structure requires a mixed-model GWAS with family-wise error control. The goal is heritability estimation rather than association testing — use the separate mixed-model analysis estimating total proportion of variance explained by additive genomic variants. Variants have minor allele counts <5, which were explicitly excluded from the GWAS in this study. SVs were not curated first — the pipeline prioritized high specificity (consensus of Delly, Lumpy, Pindel and cn.MOPs calls, filtering, manual vetting) before genotyping, so uncurated raw SV calls should not be fed directly into association testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Runs mixed-model genome-wide association studies of structural variants (and SNPs/indels) against quantitative traits in a strain panel, using permutation-derived trait-specific significance thresholds. Used in the S. pombe study to show that 19 of 68 SVs (28%) were significantly trait-associated. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061

skills.description: Use when quantitative trait measurements and multiple variant classes (SNPs, indels, CNVs, rearrangements) are available and you need to partition trait variance per variant class rather than run SNP-only GWA.
skills.name: mixed-model-heritability-estimation
skills.search_text: mixed-model-heritability-estimation Use when quantitative trait measurements and multiple variant classes (SNPs, indels, CNVs, rearrangements) are available and you need to partition trait variance per variant class rather than run SNP-only GWA. Traits are binary/case-control rather than quantitative — the method here was calibrated on 228 quantitative trait values, not discrete phenotypes Structural variant genotypes are unreliable for the variant class of interest — the authors did not re-examine translocations and inversions because they were 'more challenging to accurately genotype' Only one variant class is available (e.g. SNPs alone) — a composite multi-kinship partition cannot be performed and only the SNP-only model applies http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Estimate narrow-sense heritability for 228 quantitative traits in S. pombe using LDAK mixed models, comparing a SNP-only kinship against a composite model with separate kinship matrices for SNPs, CNVs and rearrangements. This partitions trait variance across variant classes that are weakly linked to SNPs and would otherwise inflate SNP-only estimates. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Estimate narrow-sense heritability for 228 quantitative traits in S. pombe using LDAK mixed models, comparing a SNP-only kinship against a composite model with separate kinship matrices for SNPs, CNVs and rearrangements. This partitions trait variance across variant classes that are weakly linked to SNPs and would otherwise inflate SNP-only estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Traits are binary/case-control rather than quantitative — the method here was calibrated on 228 quantitative trait values, not discrete phenotypes Structural variant genotypes are unreliable for the variant class of interest — the authors did not re-examine translocations and inversions because they were 'more challenging to accurately genotype' Only one variant class is available (e.g. SNPs alone) — a composite multi-kinship partition cannot be performed and only the SNP-only model applies

skills.summary: Benchmark nanopore 5mC methylation-calling tools by applying optimized single and double per-read score cutoffs to controlled methylation mixtures and scoring per-site methylation frequencies against known expected frequencies via RMSE and correlation.

skills.search_text: mlp-base-modification-model-training Use when you have filtered PacBio CCS BAMs with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) and need to train a supervised k-mer MLP to classify modified-vs-canonical reads or call Z/A at single-nucleotide resolution. Input BAMs lack kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) or fail the Median_PW/Median_IPD and >=3-pass quality filters, so no reliable training features exist The goal is detecting modification types whose kinetic signatures are not represented in training data (e.g. hybrid reads with diluted signatures for the SVM read classifier, which is optimized for fully substituted dZ-genomes) No labeled ground-truth modified/canonical training reads are available — supervised MLP training is the wrong choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Train PyTorch multi-layer perceptron (MLP) classifiers on PacBio CCS kinetic features (pulse width and inter-pulse duration over k-mer contexts) to discriminate modified (dZ/Z) from canonical (dA/A) bases and reads, exporting TorchScript checkpoints for downstream base calling with Z-Calling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8

skills.description: Use when raw Oxford Nanopore MinION full-length 16S rRNA amplicon reads from mixed microbial communities need de novo consensus OTU calling without reference-based mapping, and benchmark accuracy against mock-community references is required.

skills.description: Use when you have an aligned modBAM from nanopore reads (direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA basecalled with Dorado) and need per-site modification calls with coverage/frequency filtering to reduce false positives.

skills.search_text: modbam-modification-extraction Use when you have an aligned modBAM from nanopore reads (direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA basecalled with Dorado) and need per-site modification calls with coverage/frequency filtering to reduce false positives. The morphology image is already at the target mpp (≈0.3, within 0.2–0.5) matched to the StarDist model — rescaling again is unnecessary.

skills.search_text: morris-pratt-failure-function-analysis Use when enumerating candidate repeat-unit substrings of a DNA string for tandem repeat decomposition and you must filter out substrings whose proper suffix matches a prefix (self-overlapping candidates). The input is not a DNA string but raw sequencing reads that still need preprocessing, clustering, or basecalling before unit enumeration The goal is annotation of an existing tandem repeat pattern (e.g., variant-unit output) rather than de novo candidate unit enumeration Representative units longer than 20 nt are already known and should be supplied via -u (use mTR for long units) rather than re-derived by enumeration http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes the Morris-Pratt failure-function array OLi for each suffix position of a DNA string, as used inside uTR's Algorithm 2 to certify that candidate repeat units are non-self-overlapping. Combined with the suffix-array-based LEN test, this enables O(n^2) enumeration of repetitive, non-self-overlapping substring candidates. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185

skills.description: Use when long-read (e.g. PacBio HiFi) sequences are suspected to contain mosaic tandem repeats with multiple repeat units that must be annotated with an exact decomposition pattern and mismatch statistics.
skills.name: mosaic-tr-pattern-annotation
skills.search_text: mosaic-tr-pattern-annotation Use when long-read (e.g. PacBio HiFi) sequences are suspected to contain mosaic tandem repeats with multiple repeat units that must be annotated with an exact decomposition pattern and mismatch statistics. When the analysis goal is counting sample variants or haplotypes rather than decomposing the pattern — use cTR, which clusters reads with a maximum Levenshtein distance of 0.01 times average read length When precise per-unit variant strings are needed downstream of an already-estimated pattern — use vTR, which outputs variant units instead of the concise pattern When input strings are short or contain no tandem repeat structure; -r will suppress output entirely if the mismatch ratio exceeds the default threshold of 0.3 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Annotates DNA strings from long reads with mosaic tandem repeat (TR) patterns composed of different repeat units using uTR, which decomposes each read via optimal partial matching against inferred unit strings. It outputs annotations like '#Pat <CAG>19<CCG>38' with dissimilarity information. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Annotates DNA strings from long reads with mosaic tandem repeat (TR) patterns composed of different repeat units using uTR, which decomposes each read via optimal partial matching against inferred unit strings. It outputs annotations like '#Pat <CAG>19<CCG>38' with dissimilarity information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is counting sample variants or haplotypes rather than decomposing the pattern — use cTR, which clusters reads with a maximum Levenshtein distance of 0.01 times average read length When precise per-unit variant strings are needed downstream of an already-estimated pattern — use vTR, which outputs variant units instead of the concise pattern When input strings are short or contain no tandem repeat structure; -r will suppress output entirely if the mismatch ratio exceeds the default threshold of 0.3

skills.description: Use when running Snapper de novo motif discovery on native vs WGA nanopore FAST5 pairs and you need to validate recovered motifs against known REBASE reference methylation motifs for the strain.
skills.name: motif-benchmarking-against-rebase-references
skills.search_text: motif-benchmarking-against-rebase-references Use when running Snapper de novo motif discovery on native vs WGA nanopore FAST5 pairs and you need to validate recovered motifs against known REBASE reference methylation motifs for the strain. Input data are not Oxford Nanopore reads with a matched native/WGA pair — Snapper's greedy motif enrichment requires sample and control FAST5 directories plus a reference genome. The goal is single-base modification calling at specific positions rather than de novo motif discovery — Tombo-style per-site detection or alternative model approaches are the wrong scope. The strain has no REBASE reference (or expected motif set) available — benchmarking against REBASE references cannot be the acceptance criterion. http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark de novo methylation motifs called by Snapper on ONT native/WGA read pairs against REBASE reference methyltransferase specificities, as demonstrated on the four external SRP219538 strains (T. phaeum, N. gonorrhoeae, M. hungatei, C. perfringens). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Benchmark de novo methylation motifs called by Snapper on ONT native/WGA read pairs against REBASE reference methyltransferase specificities, as demonstrated on the four external SRP219538 strains (T. phaeum, N. gonorrhoeae, M. hungatei, C. perfringens).

skills.name: motif-site-m6a-quantification

skills.description: Use when preparing SMALR SMsn or SMp runs against SMRT cmp.h5/BAM alignments: the methyltransferase motif is known, a reference FASTA for the strain is available, and per-molecule methylation scoring needs the complete forward- and reverse-strand motif site coordinates.
skills.name: motif-site-mapping-on-reference
skills.search_text: motif-site-mapping-on-reference Use when preparing SMALR SMsn or SMp runs against SMRT cmp.h5/BAM alignments: the methyltransferase motif is known, a reference FASTA for the strain is available, and per-molecule methylation scoring needs the complete forward- and reverse-strand motif site coordinates. The methylation motif is unknown and must be discovered de novo — SMALR requires the motif and modified-base position to be supplied via --motif and --mod_pos and does not perform de novo motif discovery from the reference. The analysis target is not SMRT sequencing kinetics (e.g. no native-vs-WGA IPD data) — mapping motif sites alone provides no methylation information without the IPD comparison. The target modifications create kinetic signatures extending into surrounding bases that require more sophisticated algorithms beyond SMALR's per-motif-position scoring scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Exhaustively scans a bacterial reference FASTA to locate all occurrences of a target methylation motif (e.g. 5'-GATC, 5'-RGATCY, 5'-GWCAY) on both forward and reverse strands of each contig, assigning each site a strand-relative modified-base position (--mod_pos) prior to SMALR SMsn or SMp kinetic scoring. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: Exhaustively scans a bacterial reference FASTA to locate all occurrences of a target methylation motif (e.g. 5'-GATC, 5'-RGATCY, 5'-GWCAY) on both forward and reverse strands of each contig, assigning each site a strand-relative modified-base position (--mod_pos) prior to SMALR SMsn or SMp kinetic scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The methylation motif is unknown and must be discovered de novo — SMALR requires the motif and modified-base position to be supplied via --motif and --mod_pos and does not perform de novo motif discovery from the reference. The analysis target is not SMRT sequencing kinetics (e.g. no native-vs-WGA IPD data) — mapping motif sites alone provides no methylation information without the IPD comparison. The target modifications create kinetic signatures extending into surrounding bases that require more sophisticated algorithms beyond SMALR's per-motif-position scoring scope.

skills.description: Use when you must quantify the fraction of PacBio-predicted motif sites (e.g. GATC) called methylated by mCaller per-position ONT predictions across multiple strains, to reproduce a species-by-motif enrichment table like the paper's fig3a_species_motif_percent_methylated.csv.
skills.name: motif-site-methylation-fraction-summary
skills.search_text: motif-site-methylation-fraction-summary Use when you must quantify the fraction of PacBio-predicted motif sites (e.g. GATC) called methylated by mCaller per-position ONT predictions across multiple strains, to reproduce a species-by-motif enrichment table like the paper's fig3a_species_motif_percent_methylated.csv. You need the per-read classification itself (mCaller.py on the eventalign TSV) rather than a downstream per-site fraction summary — this skill operates on mCaller output, not raw fast5/fastq. The target sequence context was not part of the E. coli training set — the paper warns training biases can decrease accuracy at contexts dissimilar to the training examples, so fraction summaries there are unreliable. You need de novo motif discovery or methylation-type assignment (e.g. the GATCGVNY motif in S. aureus) — this skill only quantifies methylation at pre-defined PacBio-predicted motif sites and cannot distinguish methylation types. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Summarizes mCaller per-read m6A predictions into per-position methylation calls (make_bed.py with a -d read-depth floor and -t 0.5 mod_threshold), then computes the fraction of PacBio-predicted methyltransferase target motif sites called methylated per Zymo strain and motif, yielding a species-by-motif percentage table that cross-confirms motif identification. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Summarizes mCaller per-read m6A predictions into per-position methylation calls (make_bed.py with a -d read-depth floor and -t 0.5 mod_threshold), then computes the fraction of PacBio-predicted methyltransferase target motif sites called methylated per Zymo strain and motif, yielding a species-by-motif percentage table that cross-confirms motif identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the per-read classification itself (mCaller.py on the eventalign TSV) rather than a downstream per-site fraction summary — this skill operates on mCaller output, not raw fast5/fastq. The target sequence context was not part of the E. coli training set — the paper warns training biases can decrease accuracy at contexts dissimilar to the training examples, so fraction summaries there are unreliable. You need de novo motif discovery or methylation-type assignment (e.g. the GATCGVNY motif in S. aureus) — this skill only quantifies methylation at pre-defined PacBio-predicted motif sites and cannot distinguish methylation types.

skills.description: Use when short-insert (~250bp) PacBio SMRT library preps provide multiple passes over each motif site per molecule, and single-molecule, single-nucleotide methylation calls (rather than population-level consensus) are the analysis goal.
skills.name: motif-site-position-scoring
skills.search_text: motif-site-position-scoring Use when short-insert (~250bp) PacBio SMRT library preps provide multiple passes over each motif site per molecule, and single-molecule, single-nucleotide methylation calls (rather than population-level consensus) are the analysis goal. Library preps are long (10Kb+) so each subread spans many distinct motif sites — use the SMp motif-pooled protocol instead, which assesses molecule-wide methylation status Only population-level consensus methylation calls across the whole sample are needed and single-cell/molecule epigenetic heterogeneity is not of interest No matched WGA control reads exist for kinetics comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Scores each motif site on each individual sequencing molecule for methylation status by comparing native PacBio SMRT kinetics against matched WGA controls using the SMALR SMsn protocol, enabling single-molecule resolution methylome analysis without subjective thresholds. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: Scores each motif site on each individual sequencing molecule for methylation status by comparing native PacBio SMRT kinetics against matched WGA controls using the SMALR SMsn protocol, enabling single-molecule resolution methylome analysis without subjective thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Library preps are long (10Kb+) so each subread spans many distinct motif sites — use the SMp motif-pooled protocol instead, which assesses molecule-wide methylation status Only population-level consensus methylation calls across the whole sample are needed and single-cell/molecule epigenetic heterogeneity is not of interest No matched WGA control reads exist for kinetics comparison

skills.description: Use when building a binary RNA-class classifier from raw nanopore DRS signals and you need biotype-verified labels, removal of ambiguous transcripts (e.g. pseudogenes), and a 50/50 class balance from an imbalanced read pool.
skills.name: mrna-biotype-dataset-curation-and-class-balancing
skills.search_text: mrna-biotype-dataset-curation-and-class-balancing Use when building a binary RNA-class classifier from raw nanopore DRS signals and you need biotype-verified labels, removal of ambiguous transcripts (e.g. pseudogenes), and a 50/50 class balance from an imbalanced read pool. The input reads are not direct RNA sequencing data with a 3'-end anchored signal (the class signal lives at the start of the DRS read) You need labels for RNA classes other than mRNA vs non-mRNA without rethinking pseudogene and low-expression handling, e.g. lncRNAs, whose accurate 3'-end identification the authors report as still challenging The dataset is already class-balanced and biotype-filtered; re-undersampling would discard majority-class data unnecessarily http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Curates a balanced mRNA vs non-mRNA training/testing dataset for direct RNA sequencing (DRS) signal classifiers by basecalling and mapping MinION fast5 reads to GENCODE, labeling by biotype, balancing classes by undersampling, and trimming adapter/poly(A) so only the first 4 s of transcript signal remains. This yields the clean, class-balanced signal set on which models like RISER's CNN are trained. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Curates a balanced mRNA vs non-mRNA training/testing dataset for direct RNA sequencing (DRS) signal classifiers by basecalling and mapping MinION fast5 reads to GENCODE, labeling by biotype, balancing classes by undersampling, and trimming adapter/poly(A) so only the first 4 s of transcript signal remains. This yields the clean, class-balanced signal set on which models like RISER's CNN are trained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are not direct RNA sequencing data with a 3'-end anchored signal (the class signal lives at the start of the DRS read) You need labels for RNA classes other than mRNA vs non-mRNA without rethinking pseudogene and low-expression handling, e.g. lncRNAs, whose accurate 3'-end identification the authors report as still challenging The dataset is already class-balanced and biotype-filtered; re-undersampling would discard majority-class data unnecessarily

skills.summary: Generate haplotype consensus sequences at candidate SNV loci by extracting overlapping reads and building either an abPOA-based multiple sequence alignment or a de Bruijn-graph local assembly, then realigning the resulting consensus sequences to the local reference to derive alternative alleles for low-quality loci in miniSNV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus was already classified as high-quality (known variant with R_alt > 0.3 or unknown variant with R_alt > 0.7 and no other candidate within 10 bp) — these are genotyped directly with the binomial model and bypass consensus generation Data is short-read or non-ONT, since the skill's spanning-read and overlap-ratio decision points (70% spanning, overlap > 0.6/0.4) are calibrated for long nanopore reads Only single-consensus output is needed — FMAlign/HAlign-style MSA that cannot produce multiple consensus sequences at heterozygous sites cannot replace this diploid-aware step

skills.search_text: msa-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing MSA tools on ultralong (>=100,000 bp up to multi-Mbp) nucleotide sequences and you need success/failure outcomes plus wall-clock runtime per method and per sequence length. Sequences are short (well under 100,000 bp) or few in number — standard MSA tools handle these directly without the ultralong benchmarking harness Input molecules are proteins — FMAlign2 is a multiple *nucleotide* sequence alignment method The goal is accuracy benchmarking on reference alignments rather than success/failure and runtime scaling on ultralong inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark multiple sequence alignment methods on ultralong nucleotide datasets by timing success/failure across truncated human Y chromosome inputs (10,000 bp to 15 Mbp), with FMAlign2 wrapping backends like MAFFT, Clustal Omega, HAlign3, and HAlign4. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae014
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple sequence alignment methods on ultralong nucleotide datasets by timing success/failure across truncated human Y chromosome inputs (10,000 bp to 15 Mbp), with FMAlign2 wrapping backends like MAFFT, Clustal Omega, HAlign3, and HAlign4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are short (well under 100,000 bp) or few in number — standard MSA tools handle these directly without the ultralong benchmarking harness Input molecules are proteins — FMAlign2 is a multiple *nucleotide* sequence alignment method The goal is accuracy benchmarking on reference alignments rather than success/failure and runtime scaling on ultralong inputs

skills.search_text: multi-assembler-contig-generation Use when you have a metagenomic shotgun read set (e.g. Illumina FASTQ, trimmed) and want to maximize contig diversity and quality by assembling with several assemblers/Kmers (51–71) before post-assembly merging. skills.summary: Generate a diverse pool of de novo contigs from the same metagenomic read set by running multiple assemblers (SOAPdenovo, Velvet, IDBA, Ray, and optionally CLC Bio) independently, then pooling and dereplicating the results so they can be merged into an improved consensus set via the MeGAMerge OLC-based pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single assembler run and no additional assemblies to merge — the OLC-based merge has little to combine and overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with input dataset size Input is already assembled contigs with no underlying reads available for independent re-assembly (in that case run MeGAMerge directly on the existing Multi-FASTA files instead) Total assembly size and N50/N90 are the primary metrics of interest — removing contigs < 2.0 kb explicitly trades these metrics for contig quality
