skills.name: multi-caller-sv-callset-merging
skills.search_text: multi-caller-sv-callset-merging Use when you hold filtered VCF call sets from several nanopore SV callers run on the same lra/minimap2/NGMLR alignment and need one consensus SV call set per aligner plus a summary type-distribution table. When the goal is coverage-based validation of insertions or inversions — coverage analysis such as disCoverage can only be applied to deletions and duplications When 'disCoverage' alone is expected to produce the call set — it is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions obtained from another technique or multi-sample analysis When input is a single caller's already-merged or raw VCF with no cross-caller call sets to consensus on — no merging signal exists http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Combines structural variant call sets produced by multiple long-read variant callers (Sniffles, CuteSV, SVIM, NanoVar) on the same nanopore BAM into one consensus VCF per aligner, then tabulates SV counts and DEL/DUP/INS distribution. It counters the paper's finding that single callers report incomplete variant sets containing erroneous calls. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Combines structural variant call sets produced by multiple long-read variant callers (Sniffles, CuteSV, SVIM, NanoVar) on the same nanopore BAM into one consensus VCF per aligner, then tabulates SV counts and DEL/DUP/INS distribution. It counters the paper's finding that single callers report incomplete variant sets containing erroneous calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is coverage-based validation of insertions or inversions — coverage analysis such as disCoverage can only be applied to deletions and duplications When 'disCoverage' alone is expected to produce the call set — it is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions obtained from another technique or multi-sample analysis When input is a single caller's already-merged or raw VCF with no cross-caller call sets to consensus on — no merging signal exists

skills.description: Use when comparing SNV caller performance on trio nanopore data, e.g. replicating Mendelian Consistency Rate benchmarks across miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot VCFs on GIAB sup-datasets.
skills.name: multi-caller-variant-call-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-caller-variant-call-comparison Use when comparing SNV caller performance on trio nanopore data, e.g. replicating Mendelian Consistency Rate benchmarks across miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot VCFs on GIAB sup-datasets. Input is raw ONT signal/FASTQ rather than called variant VCFs — run the callers (miniSNV, Clair3, Longshot) first via their own pipelines The datasets are not a parent–child trio (e.g. single-sample HG002 k12-data with Guppy basecalls) — Mendelian Consistency Rate cannot be computed without parental genotypes Evaluating indels or structural variants — this skill is restricted to biallelic SNV genotype comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 Benchmark multiple SNV callers (miniSNV, Clair3, Longshot) on the same ONT long-read datasets by regenerating per-caller variant calls and computing Mendelian Consistency Rate on the GIAB Ashkenazi Trio (HG002/HG003/HG004) to assess caller accuracy beyond F1-score. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple SNV callers (miniSNV, Clair3, Longshot) on the same ONT long-read datasets by regenerating per-caller variant calls and computing Mendelian Consistency Rate on the GIAB Ashkenazi Trio (HG002/HG003/HG004) to assess caller accuracy beyond F1-score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ONT signal/FASTQ rather than called variant VCFs — run the callers (miniSNV, Clair3, Longshot) first via their own pipelines The datasets are not a parent–child trio (e.g. single-sample HG002 k12-data with Guppy basecalls) — Mendelian Consistency Rate cannot be computed without parental genotypes Evaluating indels or structural variants — this skill is restricted to biallelic SNV genotype comparison

skills.description: Use when starting a consensus SV-calling workflow from ONT fastq.gz samples and you need per-caller candidate VCFs before pre-filtering and CNN-based consensus; triggered by headerless sample CSVs of fastq.gz paths for HGSVC-style samples.
skills.name: multi-caller-vcf-collection
skills.search_text: multi-caller-vcf-collection Use when starting a consensus SV-calling workflow from ONT fastq.gz samples and you need per-caller candidate VCFs before pre-filtering and CNN-based consensus; triggered by headerless sample CSVs of fastq.gz paths for HGSVC-style samples. Your input is already a set of caller VCFs — this skill only covers alignment and raw candidate generation, not consensus or CNN filtering Your reads are Illumina or PacBio short-read data; the pipeline targets fastq.gz Oxford Nanopore long-read samples You need per-sample variants for a single caller only — the pipeline runs all six callers as a set http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Generates one structural-variant candidate VCF per SV caller per ONT sample by running CuteSV, Sniffles, Dysgu, SVIM, PBSV and Nanovar on per-sample long-read alignments (minimap2 for the first five, pbmm2 for PBSV) inside the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow pipeline, producing 18 VCFs for three HGSVC samples (HG00733, HG00514, NA19240) that feed downstream consensus. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Generates one structural-variant candidate VCF per SV caller per ONT sample by running CuteSV, Sniffles, Dysgu, SVIM, PBSV and Nanovar on per-sample long-read alignments (minimap2 for the first five, pbmm2 for PBSV) inside the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow pipeline, producing 18 VCFs for three HGSVC samples (HG00733, HG00514, NA19240) that feed downstream consensus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a set of caller VCFs — this skill only covers alignment and raw candidate generation, not consensus or CNN filtering Your reads are Illumina or PacBio short-read data; the pipeline targets fastq.gz Oxford Nanopore long-read samples You need per-sample variants for a single caller only — the pipeline runs all six callers as a set

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a nanopore methylation caller's performance generalizes across diverse datasets (e.g., human cell lines and plant species) by comparing its methylation frequencies against a bisulfite-sequencing ground truth at controlled coverage depths.
skills.name: multi-dataset-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-dataset-benchmark-comparison Use when evaluating whether a nanopore methylation caller's performance generalizes across diverse datasets (e.g., human cell lines and plant species) by comparing its methylation frequencies against a bisulfite-sequencing ground truth at controlled coverage depths. The task is single-molecule per-read methylation calling accuracy (AUROC/F1 evaluation) rather than genome-wide frequency-level comparison against BS-seq The caller being evaluated is trained specifically for plant species only (e.g., DeepSignal-plant), so cross-kingdom benchmarking against human datasets is out of scope Input data is from an older pore chemistry (pre-R10.4); the article notes only a small number of tools including DeepMod2 and Dorado are compatible with R10.4 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark a methylation caller (e.g., DeepBAM vs Dorado) across heterogeneous human and plant nanopore R10.4 datasets by down-sampling BAMs to 10x-30x coverage, computing genome-wide CpG methylation frequencies, and correlating them against matched BS-seq tracks to expose dataset-dependent performance differences. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Benchmark a methylation caller (e.g., DeepBAM vs Dorado) across heterogeneous human and plant nanopore R10.4 datasets by down-sampling BAMs to 10x-30x coverage, computing genome-wide CpG methylation frequencies, and correlating them against matched BS-seq tracks to expose dataset-dependent performance differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-molecule per-read methylation calling accuracy (AUROC/F1 evaluation) rather than genome-wide frequency-level comparison against BS-seq The caller being evaluated is trained specifically for plant species only (e.g., DeepSignal-plant), so cross-kingdom benchmarking against human datasets is out of scope Input data is from an older pore chemistry (pre-R10.4); the article notes only a small number of tools including DeepMod2 and Dorado are compatible with R10.4

skills.description: Use when Illumina metagenomic reads (e.g., HMP or Horizon oil-spill samples) have been quality-trimmed and the goal is an improved assembly beyond what any single assembler/kmer run achieves, by merging multiple individual assemblies.
skills.name: multi-kmer-assembly-optimization
skills.search_text: multi-kmer-assembly-optimization Use when Illumina metagenomic reads (e.g., HMP or Horizon oil-spill samples) have been quality-trimmed and the goal is an improved assembly beyond what any single assembler/kmer run achieves, by merging multiple individual assemblies. You have a single small dataset where one assembler/kmer run already meets contiguity needs — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with input dataset size You need an unchimeric assembly: the merging process introduces new chimeras even though MeGAMerge reduces total input chimeras Total assembly size or N50/N90 are the primary metrics of interest — the removal of small contigs affects these, and they are described as not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Optimizes metagenomic de novo assembly by running multiple assemblers (Velvet, SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, IDBA, Ray) at both small (21-31) and large (85-105) kmer ranges, then merging all contig sets with MeGAMerge — a post-assembly OLC-based pipeline using Newbler and Minimus2 — to yield fewer, larger, more contiguous contigs. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Optimizes metagenomic de novo assembly by running multiple assemblers (Velvet, SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, IDBA, Ray) at both small (21-31) and large (85-105) kmer ranges, then merging all contig sets with MeGAMerge — a post-assembly OLC-based pipeline using Newbler and Minimus2 — to yield fewer, larger, more contiguous contigs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single small dataset where one assembler/kmer run already meets contiguity needs — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with input dataset size You need an unchimeric assembly: the merging process introduces new chimeras even though MeGAMerge reduces total input chimeras Total assembly size or N50/N90 are the primary metrics of interest — the removal of small contigs affects these, and they are described as not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance

skills.description: Use when mapping quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed sRNA-seq reads to a tRNA-enriched (artificial-chromosome) genome index and ambiguous multi-locus alignment would otherwise inflate tncRNA counts or confuse subtype assignment.
skills.name: multi-mapped-read-filtering
skills.search_text: multi-mapped-read-filtering Use when mapping quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed sRNA-seq reads to a tRNA-enriched (artificial-chromosome) genome index and ambiguous multi-locus alignment would otherwise inflate tncRNA counts or confuse subtype assignment. When the goal is to quantify multi-copy repeat-derived small RNAs where multi-mapping signal is biologically meaningful and fractional assignment (e.g. EM-based multi-mappers) is preferable When reads come from long RNA-seq or paired-end data with splice-aware mapping requirements — this Bowtie1-based small-RNA workflow assumes short single-end sRNA reads When the user needs base-modification-aware alignment of tRNAs (conventional RNA-seq suffers from tRNA modification biases; tRNA-seq is recommended instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Suppress and discard reads that align to too many genomic loci when profiling tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs, using Bowtie1's -m option (default: discard alignments occurring more than 50 times) so that tncRNA calls and quantification (RPM) are not inflated by ambiguously mapped small RNAs. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Suppress and discard reads that align to too many genomic loci when profiling tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs, using Bowtie1's -m option (default: discard alignments occurring more than 50 times) so that tncRNA calls and quantification (RPM) are not inflated by ambiguously mapped small RNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to quantify multi-copy repeat-derived small RNAs where multi-mapping signal is biologically meaningful and fractional assignment (e.g. EM-based multi-mappers) is preferable When reads come from long RNA-seq or paired-end data with splice-aware mapping requirements — this Bowtie1-based small-RNA workflow assumes short single-end sRNA reads When the user needs base-modification-aware alignment of tRNAs (conventional RNA-seq suffers from tRNA modification biases; tRNA-seq is recommended instead)

skills.description: Use when nanopore DRS reads aligned with minimap2 map to multiple transcript isoforms and you need probabilistic EM-based multi-mapping disambiguation for transcript-level abundance quantification.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-disambiguation
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-disambiguation Use when nanopore DRS reads aligned with minimap2 map to multiple transcript isoforms and you need probabilistic EM-based multi-mapping disambiguation for transcript-level abundance quantification. Reads were aligned to a whole genome rather than a transcriptome with retained secondary mappings — the EM compatibility index requires multi-mapping read-to-transcript alignments The goal is novel isoform discovery/annotation rather than abundance estimation of annotated transcripts (pair NanoCount with FLAIR for discovery of novel isoforms) Data is short-read RNA-seq or already has a resolved count matrix — use Salmon/tximport-style downstream tools instead of DRS-specific filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Resolves reads that map to multiple transcript isoforms in Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) by applying DRS-specific alignment filters and an expectation-maximisation algorithm (NanoCount) to estimate per-transcript abundances. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1129
skills.summary: Resolves reads that map to multiple transcript isoforms in Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) by applying DRS-specific alignment filters and an expectation-maximisation algorithm (NanoCount) to estimate per-transcript abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads were aligned to a whole genome rather than a transcriptome with retained secondary mappings — the EM compatibility index requires multi-mapping read-to-transcript alignments The goal is novel isoform discovery/annotation rather than abundance estimation of annotated transcripts (pair NanoCount with FLAIR for discovery of novel isoforms) Data is short-read RNA-seq or already has a resolved count matrix — use Salmon/tximport-style downstream tools instead of DRS-specific filtering

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a phylogeny from long (~3.5-4.2 kb) multi-marker rDNA alignments spanning divergent eukaryotes, and deposited reference Newick trees are available for topology validation.
skills.name: multi-marker-ribosomal-dna-phylogenetics
skills.search_text: multi-marker-ribosomal-dna-phylogenetics Use when building or reproducing a phylogeny from long (~3.5-4.2 kb) multi-marker rDNA alignments spanning divergent eukaryotes, and deposited reference Newick trees are available for topology validation. Input is not ribosomal DNA (e.g. mitochondrial COI barcodes) — the paper compared rDNA resolution against COI, and this skill is specific to the rRNA cluster You need quantitative (as opposed to qualitative) topology comparison — the source validation only assessed agreement against deposited reference trees without a topological metric The goal is bulk-sample metabarcoding abundance estimation — the article found long rDNA amplicon metabarcoding recovers highly skewed diversity estimates and is not yet reliable for bulk sample analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Reconstructs Bayesian phylogenies from multi-marker ribosomal DNA alignments (concatenated 18S/5.8S/28S, optionally retaining ITS1/ITS2) by combining MAFFT alignment, PartitionFinder partition/model selection, and MrBayes inference, as demonstrated on the 117-taxon 3,656 bp and 83-spider 4,214 bp rDNA datasets from Krehenwinkel et al. (2019, GigaScience). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Reconstructs Bayesian phylogenies from multi-marker ribosomal DNA alignments (concatenated 18S/5.8S/28S, optionally retaining ITS1/ITS2) by combining MAFFT alignment, PartitionFinder partition/model selection, and MrBayes inference, as demonstrated on the 117-taxon 3,656 bp and 83-spider 4,214 bp rDNA datasets from Krehenwinkel et al. (2019, GigaScience).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not ribosomal DNA (e.g. mitochondrial COI barcodes) — the paper compared rDNA resolution against COI, and this skill is specific to the rRNA cluster You need quantitative (as opposed to qualitative) topology comparison — the source validation only assessed agreement against deposited reference trees without a topological metric The goal is bulk-sample metabarcoding abundance estimation — the article found long rDNA amplicon metabarcoding recovers highly skewed diversity estimates and is not yet reliable for bulk sample analysis

skills.description: Use when comparing a cell-type annotation method against statistical-metric-based (SingleR, scmap, SciBet), tree-based (CHETAH, scClassify) and machine-learning-based (scPred, SingleCellNet, scID, CaSTLe, SVMrejection) competitors on many paired reference-query tests.
skills.name: multi-method-rank-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-method-rank-aggregation Use when comparing a cell-type annotation method against statistical-metric-based (SingleR, scmap, SciBet), tree-based (CHETAH, scClassify) and machine-learning-based (scPred, SingleCellNet, scID, CaSTLe, SVMrejection) competitors on many paired reference-query tests. You only need a single annotation of one query dataset, not a systematic multi-method benchmark across many reference-query pairs The query dataset has no paired, well-annotated reference and no atlas (MCA/HCL) is applicable, so RBC methods cannot be compared fairly Competing methods lack configurable 'optimal parameter settings' or cannot accept Seurat-preprocessed expression matrices, making a fair rank comparison infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark one target method (scMAGIC) against 13 competing reference-based classification (RBC) methods across 86 paired reference-query scRNA-seq tests spanning three RBC situations, then aggregate per-test accuracy, balanced accuracy and cluster accuracy into median ranks per method. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Benchmark one target method (scMAGIC) against 13 competing reference-based classification (RBC) methods across 86 paired reference-query scRNA-seq tests spanning three RBC situations, then aggregate per-test accuracy, balanced accuracy and cluster accuracy into median ranks per method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single annotation of one query dataset, not a systematic multi-method benchmark across many reference-query pairs The query dataset has no paired, well-annotated reference and no atlas (MCA/HCL) is applicable, so RBC methods cannot be compared fairly Competing methods lack configurable 'optimal parameter settings' or cannot accept Seurat-preprocessed expression matrices, making a fair rank comparison infeasible

skills.description: Use when calling deletion structural variants from third-generation sequencing alignments and you have both generated deletion-region images and CIGAR-framed encoded base sequences that must be fused for classification.
skills.name: multi-modal-feature-attention-weighting
skills.search_text: multi-modal-feature-attention-weighting Use when calling deletion structural variants from third-generation sequencing alignments and you have both generated deletion-region images and CIGAR-framed encoded base sequences that must be fused for classification. The task requires insertion or base substitution calling — the article states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling'. Only raw read alignments without the upstream pre-processing outputs (100x100 images and zero-padded 100-length encoded sequences) are available. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fuses 100x100-pixel deletion-region alignment images with encoded base sequences (A/C/T/G as 2/3/4/5, deletions as 9, zero-padded to 100) via a dual attention mechanism — spatial attention over images and GAP/GMP channel attention over sequence features — feeding a ResNet backbone for deletion variant calling (DASV). genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: Fuses 100x100-pixel deletion-region alignment images with encoded base sequences (A/C/T/G as 2/3/4/5, deletions as 9, zero-padded to 100) via a dual attention mechanism — spatial attention over images and GAP/GMP channel attention over sequence features — feeding a ResNet backbone for deletion variant calling (DASV).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires insertion or base substitution calling — the article states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling'. Only raw read alignments without the upstream pre-processing outputs (100x100 images and zero-padded 100-length encoded sequences) are available.

skills.description: Use when comparing how the same structural variant locus is encoded visually across sequencing platforms, e.g. verifying that short-read (Illumina) encodings show coverage loss rather than the split-read-style deletion signal of long reads.
skills.name: multi-platform-alignment-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-platform-alignment-comparison Use when comparing how the same structural variant locus is encoded visually across sequencing platforms, e.g. verifying that short-read (Illumina) encodings show coverage loss rather than the split-read-style deletion signal of long reads. Input data is short-read only and the goal is de novo SV calling rather than cross-platform encoding comparison (Illumina cannot produce the long-read split-read-style deletion encoding) Variant calls are needed for whole-genome samples rather than inspection of specific pre-identified deletion loci http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Reproduces the cross-platform (PacBio, Illumina, ONT) image encoding comparison of two example deletions (Fig. 2 of ConsensuSV-ONT), showing how structural variant signal differs between short-read and long-read technologies in 50x50x3 CNN input images. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Reproduces the cross-platform (PacBio, Illumina, ONT) image encoding comparison of two example deletions (Fig. 2 of ConsensuSV-ONT), showing how structural variant signal differs between short-read and long-read technologies in 50x50x3 CNN input images.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is short-read only and the goal is de novo SV calling rather than cross-platform encoding comparison (Illumina cannot produce the long-read split-read-style deletion encoding) Variant calls are needed for whole-genome samples rather than inspection of specific pre-identified deletion loci

skills.description: Use when you have CNV calls from several related samples (e.g., trio or cohort .pytor files) and need to produce a unified joint call set with sample membership and per-sample genotypes rather than per-sample call lists.
skills.name: multi-sample-cnv-call-merging
skills.search_text: multi-sample-cnv-call-merging Use when you have CNV calls from several related samples (e.g., trio or cohort .pytor files) and need to produce a unified joint call set with sample membership and per-sample genotypes rather than per-sample call lists. You need single-sample CNV calling from raw BAMs — this skill operates on already-called .pytor files in view mode, not on the -rd/-his/-partition/-call pipeline itself You need somatic CNA detection between tumor-normal pairs — the article notes the somatic CNA caller is only a functional prototype, distinct from multi-sample merged_calls Your samples' calls do not co-occur at reciprocal overlap >50%, in which case calls will simply not cluster into joint regions http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Merges CNV calls from multiple samples (e.g., a CEPH trio of .pytor files) into joint calls by clustering regions with reciprocal overlap >50% in CNVpytor viewer mode, optionally followed by per-sample genotyping of the merged regions. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Merges CNV calls from multiple samples (e.g., a CEPH trio of .pytor files) into joint calls by clustering regions with reciprocal overlap >50% in CNVpytor viewer mode, optionally followed by per-sample genotyping of the merged regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need single-sample CNV calling from raw BAMs — this skill operates on already-called .pytor files in view mode, not on the -rd/-his/-partition/-call pipeline itself You need somatic CNA detection between tumor-normal pairs — the article notes the somatic CNA caller is only a functional prototype, distinct from multi-sample merged_calls Your samples' calls do not co-occur at reciprocal overlap >50%, in which case calls will simply not cluster into joint regions

skills.description: Use when reconstructing MAGs from dozens of short-read metagenomic samples (e.g., human gut, dog gut, ocean, soil projects with 82–129 samples) for which assembled contigs and sorted BAM files are available and joint binning is desired.
skills.name: multi-sample-short-read-binning-workflow
skills.search_text: multi-sample-short-read-binning-workflow Use when reconstructing MAGs from dozens of short-read metagenomic samples (e.g., human gut, dog gut, ocean, soil projects with 82–129 samples) for which assembled contigs and sorted BAM files are available and joint binning is desired. Only one sample is being binned — the paper prescribes `single_easy_bin` for that case instead of the combined multi-sample inputs Input is long-read data — SemiBin2 instead uses its ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering path for long reads, a separate workflow from multi_easy_bin short-read binning Bins already exist and the goal is only taxonomic annotation or quality re-assessment rather than de novo binning http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs metagenome-assembled genomes from many short-read samples in one joint SemiBin2 run, using cross-sample co-abundance features (multi_easy_bin, self-supervised mode). It is the paper's core short-read benchmarking path that yielded 8.3–21.5% more high-quality bins than SemiBin1 at 25% of the runtime and 11% of the peak memory. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209
skills.summary: Reconstructs metagenome-assembled genomes from many short-read samples in one joint SemiBin2 run, using cross-sample co-abundance features (multi_easy_bin, self-supervised mode). It is the paper's core short-read benchmarking path that yielded 8.3–21.5% more high-quality bins than SemiBin1 at 25% of the runtime and 11% of the peak memory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one sample is being binned — the paper prescribes `single_easy_bin` for that case instead of the combined multi-sample inputs Input is long-read data — SemiBin2 instead uses its ensemble-based DBSCAN clustering path for long reads, a separate workflow from multi_easy_bin short-read binning Bins already exist and the goal is only taxonomic annotation or quality re-assessment rather than de novo binning

skills.description: Use when reconstructing transcripts from aligned full-length LRTS BAM files (e.g. PacBio hepatocyte CTL/VPA data) and you need to choose a filtering stringency by comparing permissive, balanced, and strict add_filter outcomes.

skills.search_text: multi-strategy-transcript-filtering Use when reconstructing transcripts from aligned full-length LRTS BAM files (e.g. PacBio hepatocyte CTL/VPA data) and you need to choose a filtering stringency by comparing permissive, balanced, and strict add_filter outcomes. Input data are short-read RNA-seq libraries rather than aligned full-length LRTS BAM files The goal is alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing analysis rather than choosing a transcript filtering stringency Only one filtering strategy is required and no cross-strategy comparison of counts or novel-transcript fractions is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A skill for running IsoTools transcriptome reconstruction of long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) data under multiple filtering stringencies (permissive, balanced, strict) using the DEFAULT_GENE_FILTER, DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_FILTER, and DEFAULT_REF_TRANSCRIPT_FILTER constants, then comparing gene/transcript counts and GENCODE-novel fractions across strategies. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364

skills.description: Use when comparing variant-calling accuracy across Illumina, PacBio, and ONT reads and the input BAM/FASTQ alignments need to be harmonized (coverage downsampled, reads re-aligned to a decoy reference) before calling.
skills.name: multi-technology-alignment-preprocessing
skills.search_text: multi-technology-alignment-preprocessing Use when comparing variant-calling accuracy across Illumina, PacBio, and ONT reads and the input BAM/FASTQ alignments need to be harmonized (coverage downsampled, reads re-aligned to a decoy reference) before calling. The input is already a set of consistently aligned BAMs at matched coverage — re-alignment would only add variance The target is somatic/trio variant calling or multi-allelic variants, which the Clairvoyante pipeline does not support The sequencing technology is novel and lacks a high-quality GIAB-style training dataset on standard samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Prepare BAM alignments from Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore whole-genome data so that downstream variant callers (e.g., Clairvoyante) can be evaluated comparably across sequencing technologies, following the Clairvoyante HG001 workflow. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Prepare BAM alignments from Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore whole-genome data so that downstream variant callers (e.g., Clairvoyante) can be evaluated comparably across sequencing technologies, following the Clairvoyante HG001 workflow.

skills.description: Use when a new mapping or analysis tool must be validated against established alternatives on the same datasets, e.g. comparing runtimes or SV-calling accuracy across coverage levels.
skills.name: multi-tool-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-tool-comparison-analysis Use when a new mapping or analysis tool must be validated against established alternatives on the same datasets, e.g. comparing runtimes or SV-calling accuracy across coverage levels. The goal is a single tool's alignment quality on one dataset rather than a controlled head-to-head comparison across tools Read data are short Illumina reads — the compared mappers are designed for long PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads Compute resources (threads, RAM) cannot be held constant across tools, making runtime comparisons invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks competing long-read mapping tools (invMap, minimap2, Winnowmap2, lra, NGMLR) side-by-side under identical conditions to quantify accuracy and runtime differences, as done in the invMap SV benchmarking study on simulated PacBio CLR datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Benchmarks competing long-read mapping tools (invMap, minimap2, Winnowmap2, lra, NGMLR) side-by-side under identical conditions to quantify accuracy and runtime differences, as done in the invMap SV benchmarking study on simulated PacBio CLR datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single tool's alignment quality on one dataset rather than a controlled head-to-head comparison across tools Read data are short Illumina reads — the compared mappers are designed for long PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads Compute resources (threads, RAM) cannot be held constant across tools, making runtime comparisons invalid

skills.description: Use when benchmarking several overlap-detection or sequence-search tools on the same read sets and you need a unified comparison table of error rate, mean overlap size, #COC, #CC, runtime, and peak memory per tool-dataset pair.
skills.name: multi-tool-results-tabulation
skills.search_text: multi-tool-results-tabulation Use when benchmarking several overlap-detection or sequence-search tools on the same read sets and you need a unified comparison table of error rate, mean overlap size, #COC, #CC, runtime, and peak memory per tool-dataset pair. You have only a single tool's output on a single dataset — a per-tool report, not a cross-tool tabulation, is appropriate The tools produce incomparable output types with no shared ground-truth alignment evaluation against the same reference assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Aggregate overlap-detection quality and efficiency metrics from multiple tools (Fedrann, minimap2, MECAT2, MHAP, wtdbg2, xRead, BLEND) across datasets into a single CSV with one row per tool-dataset pair, enabling direct accuracy and runtime comparison. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Aggregate overlap-detection quality and efficiency metrics from multiple tools (Fedrann, minimap2, MECAT2, MHAP, wtdbg2, xRead, BLEND) across datasets into a single CSV with one row per tool-dataset pair, enabling direct accuracy and runtime comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single tool's output on a single dataset — a per-tool report, not a cross-tool tabulation, is appropriate The tools produce incomparable output types with no shared ground-truth alignment evaluation against the same reference assembly

skills.description: Use when comparing transcriptome reconstruction output from multiple LRTS tools (TALON, FLAIR, IsoQuant, Bambu, IsoTools) on the same BAM alignment, especially to assess how filtering criteria affect uniquely identified transcripts.
skills.name: multi-tool-transcript-overlap-set-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-tool-transcript-overlap-set-analysis Use when comparing transcriptome reconstruction output from multiple LRTS tools (TALON, FLAIR, IsoQuant, Bambu, IsoTools) on the same BAM alignment, especially to assess how filtering criteria affect uniquely identified transcripts. The input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than aligned full-length long-read transcripts — IsoTools is defined as a python module for Long Read Transcriptome Sequencing (LRTS) analysis The goal is alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing analysis rather than cross-tool transcriptome reconstruction comparison Only a single tool's transcript set is available, so no multi-way overlap can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill that reconstructs transcriptomes from a shared long-read RNA-seq (LRTS) BAM alignment using five tools (TALON, FLAIR, IsoQuant, Bambu, IsoTools) and computes multi-way transcript overlap sets to quantify shared and tool-unique transcript recovery. It exposes how filtering stringency — e.g. IsoTools permissive vs balanced filters — changes the number of uniquely recovered transcripts. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that reconstructs transcriptomes from a shared long-read RNA-seq (LRTS) BAM alignment using five tools (TALON, FLAIR, IsoQuant, Bambu, IsoTools) and computes multi-way transcript overlap sets to quantify shared and tool-unique transcript recovery. It exposes how filtering stringency — e.g. IsoTools permissive vs balanced filters — changes the number of uniquely recovered transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than aligned full-length long-read transcripts — IsoTools is defined as a python module for Long Read Transcriptome Sequencing (LRTS) analysis The goal is alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing analysis rather than cross-tool transcriptome reconstruction comparison Only a single tool's transcript set is available, so no multi-way overlap can be computed

skills.description: Use when comparing TE insertion callers on the same long-read (PacBio/ONT) BAMs — e.g. HG002/HG01071 — and you need per-caller true-positive counts scored against an assembly-based callset.
skills.name: multi-tool-vcf-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-tool-vcf-comparison Use when comparing TE insertion callers on the same long-read (PacBio/ONT) BAMs — e.g. HG002/HG01071 — and you need per-caller true-positive counts scored against an assembly-based callset. Input is short-read data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data (PacBio or ONT) The comparison target is a reference-presence callset rather than non-reference TE insertions — sTELLeR detects non-reference TE insertions You only have a single caller's VCF with no truth callset — true-positive scoring against the assembly-based callset is not possible http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Benchmark transposable element insertion (TEI) callers (sTELLeR, TLDR, xTEA) by intersecting each caller's INS:ME VCF records against an assembly-based truth callset, producing per-caller true-positive counts for reproducibility (e.g. Table 3). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Benchmark transposable element insertion (TEI) callers (sTELLeR, TLDR, xTEA) by intersecting each caller's INS:ME VCF records against an assembly-based truth callset, producing per-caller true-positive counts for reproducibility (e.g. Table 3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data (PacBio or ONT) The comparison target is a reference-presence callset rather than non-reference TE insertions — sTELLeR detects non-reference TE insertions You only have a single caller's VCF with no truth callset — true-positive scoring against the assembly-based callset is not possible

skills.description: Use when contig sets from multiple assemblies or related samples are being pooled into Multi-FASTA files and must be deduplicated (duplicates, reverse complements, subsequences) prior to overlap-layout-consensus merging.
skills.name: multifasta-contig-dereplication
skills.search_text: multifasta-contig-dereplication Use when contig sets from multiple assemblies or related samples are being pooled into Multi-FASTA files and must be deduplicated (duplicates, reverse complements, subsequences) prior to overlap-layout-consensus merging. Input is a single assembly whose contigs are already unique — dereplication and OLC merging add no value and overlap-based tools' run-times increase exponentially with input size The goal is total assembly size or N50/N90 comparison — the article notes removal of small contigs impacts these metrics and they are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' Only raw reads (not assembled contigs) are available — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process requiring Multi-FASTA contig inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Dereplicate pooled Multi-FASTA contig sets (e.g., from multiple metagenome assemblies) using MeGAMerge's custom Perl script, which removes exact duplicates, reverse complements, and subsequences before OLC-based merging. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Dereplicate pooled Multi-FASTA contig sets (e.g., from multiple metagenome assemblies) using MeGAMerge's custom Perl script, which removes exact duplicates, reverse complements, and subsequences before OLC-based merging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single assembly whose contigs are already unique — dereplication and OLC merging add no value and overlap-based tools' run-times increase exponentially with input size The goal is total assembly size or N50/N90 comparison — the article notes removal of small contigs impacts these metrics and they are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' Only raw reads (not assembled contigs) are available — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process requiring Multi-FASTA contig inputs

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth simulated long-read transcript data from highly similar gene copies to evaluate de novo error-correction or isoform reconstruction tools at varying read depths and abundance profiles.
skills.name: multigene-family-transcript-simulation
skills.search_text: multigene-family-transcript-simulation Use when you need ground-truth simulated long-read transcript data from highly similar gene copies to evaluate de novo error-correction or isoform reconstruction tools at varying read depths and abundance profiles. The reads are short Illumina reads rather than long PacBio Iso-Seq reads spanning the transcript end-to-end — error correction approaches for short reads cannot leverage the linked variant structure IsoCon relies on The goal is reference-based isoform quantification rather than de novo reconstruction evaluation without a reference genome A real experimental dataset with no ground-truth isoform set is used — precision/recall against simulated truth is not computable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Simulates PacBio Iso-Seq read sets for highly similar multigene family transcripts (e.g., TSPY13P, HSFY2, DAZ2) with controlled isoform counts, unequal abundances, mutation rates, and read depths, to benchmark transcript reconstruction methods like IsoCon against ICE using nucleotide-level precision and recall. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Simulates PacBio Iso-Seq read sets for highly similar multigene family transcripts (e.g., TSPY13P, HSFY2, DAZ2) with controlled isoform counts, unequal abundances, mutation rates, and read depths, to benchmark transcript reconstruction methods like IsoCon against ICE using nucleotide-level precision and recall.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are short Illumina reads rather than long PacBio Iso-Seq reads spanning the transcript end-to-end — error correction approaches for short reads cannot leverage the linked variant structure IsoCon relies on The goal is reference-based isoform quantification rather than de novo reconstruction evaluation without a reference genome A real experimental dataset with no ground-truth isoform set is used — precision/recall against simulated truth is not computable

skills.description: Use when assigning per-read chromosome classes to low-coverage (~5x) HiFi reads via reference alignment, where multi-mapping reads must aggregate every hit chromosome and unmapped reads must be retained as 'None' rather than discarded.
skills.name: multimapping-chromosome-class-aggregation
skills.search_text: multimapping-chromosome-class-aggregation Use when assigning per-read chromosome classes to low-coverage (~5x) HiFi reads via reference alignment, where multi-mapping reads must aggregate every hit chromosome and unmapped reads must be retained as 'None' rather than discarded. Reads are high-coverage enough for fully de novo assembly without reference guidance, or no reference genome exists for the organism Input is short or noisy long reads — minimap2's map-hifi preset targets PacBio HiFi/CCS reads, so short-read or ONT data would need a different preset/skill The goal is de novo class correction of already-classified reads (the ALG-based heuristic or translocation correction steps), not initial reference-derived class assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 HiFiCCL's reference-guided chromosome classification stage: every low-coverage PacBio HiFi read is aligned to a linear reference (e.g., CHM13 v2.0) with minimap2 '-ax map-hifi', and each read's class is set by aggregating all chromosome classes when it maps to multiple chromosomes, with unaligned reads labeled 'None' (optionally resolved later via pangenome-graph DFS). genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: HiFiCCL's reference-guided chromosome classification stage: every low-coverage PacBio HiFi read is aligned to a linear reference (e.g., CHM13 v2.0) with minimap2 '-ax map-hifi', and each read's class is set by aggregating all chromosome classes when it maps to multiple chromosomes, with unaligned reads labeled 'None' (optionally resolved later via pangenome-graph DFS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are high-coverage enough for fully de novo assembly without reference guidance, or no reference genome exists for the organism Input is short or noisy long reads — minimap2's map-hifi preset targets PacBio HiFi/CCS reads, so short-read or ONT data would need a different preset/skill The goal is de novo class correction of already-classified reads (the ALG-based heuristic or translocation correction steps), not initial reference-derived class assignment

skills.description: Use when building per-cell gene/isoform count tables from droplet-barcoded long-read alignments and reads must be assigned to reconstructed (known or novel) transcript models despite gene- or isoform-level multimapping ambiguity.
skills.name: multimapping-read-weighting
skills.search_text: multimapping-read-weighting Use when building per-cell gene/isoform count tables from droplet-barcoded long-read alignments and reads must be assigned to reconstructed (known or novel) transcript models despite gene- or isoform-level multimapping ambiguity. Input is short-read single-cell data or lacks droplet cell barcodes — scywalker targets 10x-style long-read (ONT/PacBio) full-length cDNA Only bulk-level abundance is needed and no per-cell/per-droplet counting is required — weighting across cells adds overhead without benefit The reference contains organelle sequences not excluded via the refdir organelles configuration, since the IsoQuant-based code often hangs or crashes on organelle data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 scywalker's counting scheme for per-droplet gene and isoform tables from long-read single-cell data, in which reads mapping to multiple genes are fractionated (a read mapping to N genes contributes 1/N to each) and complemented by unique and strict count variants. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: scywalker's counting scheme for per-droplet gene and isoform tables from long-read single-cell data, in which reads mapping to multiple genes are fractionated (a read mapping to N genes contributes 1/N to each) and complemented by unique and strict count variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read single-cell data or lacks droplet cell barcodes — scywalker targets 10x-style long-read (ONT/PacBio) full-length cDNA Only bulk-level abundance is needed and no per-cell/per-droplet counting is required — weighting across cells adds overhead without benefit The reference contains organelle sequences not excluded via the refdir organelles configuration, since the IsoQuant-based code often hangs or crashes on organelle data

skills.description: Use when the task requires retrieving or reproducing counts, gene-level omics profiles (e.g., METTL3 CNV deletion frequency or CNV-vs-RNA-expression correlation), or disease-gene/drug-disease statistics from the GutUDB release.
skills.name: multiomics-database-querying
skills.search_text: multiomics-database-querying Use when the task requires retrieving or reproducing counts, gene-level omics profiles (e.g., METTL3 CNV deletion frequency or CNV-vs-RNA-expression correlation), or disease-gene/drug-disease statistics from the GutUDB release. The question concerns an intestinal-disease omics resource other than GutUDB — its counts (58,970 genes, 56 diseases, 6 species) are specific to this release. You need raw sequencing data or novel analysis beyond the pre-computed profiles GutUDB ships (e.g., de novo variant calling from FASTQs). The analysis targets non-intestinal tissues/diseases outside GutUDB's 56 intestinal diseases and 6 species scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Query and reproduce aggregate statistics and gene-level analyses from GutUDB, a multiomics database for intestinal diseases that bundles ~9 million profiles across eight omics types (genomics, RNA-seq transcriptomics, m6A, microbe-metabolite relationships) with 58,970 genes and 260,790 disease-gene associations. genomics/v1 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Query and reproduce aggregate statistics and gene-level analyses from GutUDB, a multiomics database for intestinal diseases that bundles ~9 million profiles across eight omics types (genomics, RNA-seq transcriptomics, m6A, microbe-metabolite relationships) with 58,970 genes and 260,790 disease-gene associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns an intestinal-disease omics resource other than GutUDB — its counts (58,970 genes, 56 diseases, 6 species) are specific to this release. You need raw sequencing data or novel analysis beyond the pre-computed profiles GutUDB ships (e.g., de novo variant calling from FASTQs). The analysis targets non-intestinal tissues/diseases outside GutUDB's 56 intestinal diseases and 6 species scope.

skills.description: Use when read-level feature rows or read-level modification probabilities must be collapsed into per-site (transcript, pos, strand) methylation probabilities from Nanopore DRS data, provided site coverage is sufficient.
skills.name: multiple-instance-learning-read-aggregation
skills.search_text: multiple-instance-learning-read-aggregation Use when read-level feature rows or read-level modification probabilities must be collapsed into per-site (transcript, pos, strand) methylation probabilities from Nanopore DRS data, provided site coverage is sufficient. When only single-read-level evaluation is desired (e.g. read-level ACC/SEN/SPE/AUC benchmarking against nanom6A) — no site aggregation is needed When a candidate site has fewer than 20 supporting reads, as the coverage filter ($4>=20) would exclude it and site-level probabilities would be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Aggregate RedNano read-level m6A predictions into transcriptome-level site probabilities using a multiple-instance-learning approach, grouping read-level features by transcript position and retaining only sites with >= 20 reads of coverage. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae375
skills.summary: Aggregate RedNano read-level m6A predictions into transcriptome-level site probabilities using a multiple-instance-learning approach, grouping read-level features by transcript position and retaining only sites with >= 20 reads of coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only single-read-level evaluation is desired (e.g. read-level ACC/SEN/SPE/AUC benchmarking against nanom6A) — no site aggregation is needed When a candidate site has fewer than 20 supporting reads, as the coverage filter ($4>=20) would exclude it and site-level probabilities would be unreliable

skills.description: Use when raw MAFFT/MUSCLE multiple alignments of consensus genomes plus reference sequences must be cleaned of poorly aligned regions before phylogenetic tree inference.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-cleaning
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-cleaning Use when raw MAFFT/MUSCLE multiple alignments of consensus genomes plus reference sequences must be cleaned of poorly aligned regions before phylogenetic tree inference. Input is still raw reads or unaligned FASTQ/FASTA/POD5 samples — alignment and cleaning happen only after consensus genome reconstruction (FASTA input enters the pipeline at the alignment step). Only two sequences (e.g. one consensus plus one reference) are available — a multiple alignment with CIAlign cleaning and tree inference is not meaningful. The analysis goal is basecalling, taxonomic classification, or structural variant detection rather than phylogenetic preparation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Clean raw multiple-sequence alignments built from reconstructed viral consensus genomes and database reference sequences (aligned with MAFFT or MUSCLE) using CIAlign, then convert the edited alignment to NEXUS with seqmagick for downstream maximum-likelihood (IQ-TREE2) and Bayesian (MrBayes) tree inference in VirDetector. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Clean raw multiple-sequence alignments built from reconstructed viral consensus genomes and database reference sequences (aligned with MAFFT or MUSCLE) using CIAlign, then convert the edited alignment to NEXUS with seqmagick for downstream maximum-likelihood (IQ-TREE2) and Bayesian (MrBayes) tree inference in VirDetector.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw reads or unaligned FASTQ/FASTA/POD5 samples — alignment and cleaning happen only after consensus genome reconstruction (FASTA input enters the pipeline at the alignment step). Only two sequences (e.g. one consensus plus one reference) are available — a multiple alignment with CIAlign cleaning and tree inference is not meaningful. The analysis goal is basecalling, taxonomic classification, or structural variant detection rather than phylogenetic preparation.

skills.description: Use when Nanopore long reads already carry BC, U8 and GE tags (Step 3 output BAM) and per-UMI consensus cDNA molecules are needed for downstream isoform/matrix building in Step 4.b.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-consensus-calling
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-consensus-calling Use when Nanopore long reads already carry BC, U8 and GE tags (Step 3 output BAM) and per-UMI consensus cDNA molecules are needed for downstream isoform/matrix building in Step 4.b. Input SAM records lack the BC, U8 or GE tags (Step 3 UMI assignment has not been run) — ComputeConsensus would have no molecules to group. The goal is a gene/isoform matrix directly from annotated long-reads — Step 4.a (IsoformMatrixReads) is the correct path, not UMI-guided consensus generation. Reads are already high-accuracy consensus molecules — re-running consensus would not improve accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates a single error-corrected consensus cDNA per UMI from Nanopore long-read alignments in the ScNaUmi-seq workflow, using Sicelore's ComputeConsensus with partial-order alignment (spoa) polished by racon to convert noisy Oxford Nanopore reads into high-accuracy molecule sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Generates a single error-corrected consensus cDNA per UMI from Nanopore long-read alignments in the ScNaUmi-seq workflow, using Sicelore's ComputeConsensus with partial-order alignment (spoa) polished by racon to convert noisy Oxford Nanopore reads into high-accuracy molecule sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input SAM records lack the BC, U8 or GE tags (Step 3 UMI assignment has not been run) — ComputeConsensus would have no molecules to group. The goal is a gene/isoform matrix directly from annotated long-reads — Step 4.a (IsoformMatrixReads) is the correct path, not UMI-guided consensus generation. Reads are already high-accuracy consensus molecules — re-running consensus would not improve accuracy.

skills.description: Use when self-correcting long reads (PacBio or ONT) by deriving per-window consensus from overlapping read piles, or when ultra-long reads (up to 1.5 Mbp) break alignment-based correctors.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-consensus-generation
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-consensus-generation Use when self-correcting long reads (PacBio or ONT) by deriving per-window consensus from overlapping read piles, or when ultra-long reads (up to 1.5 Mbp) break alignment-based correctors. The task is assembly polishing rather than read self-correction — use CONSENT-polish (--contigs/--reads) instead of CONSENT-correct When correcting repeated regions that grow very long: the strategy of selecting only the N highest-identity overlaps per alignment pile may be inefficient in that regime When disk space is limited: the overlaps file alone requires ~5 TB of external storage for a full human ONT dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Generate corrected long-read consensus sequences by computing multiple sequence alignments (MSA) over windows of overlapping PacBio/ONT reads and polishing each window consensus with a local de Bruijn graph, as implemented in CONSENT. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Generate corrected long-read consensus sequences by computing multiple sequence alignments (MSA) over windows of overlapping PacBio/ONT reads and polishing each window consensus with a local de Bruijn graph, as implemented in CONSENT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is assembly polishing rather than read self-correction — use CONSENT-polish (--contigs/--reads) instead of CONSENT-correct When correcting repeated regions that grow very long: the strategy of selecting only the N highest-identity overlaps per alignment pile may be inefficient in that regime When disk space is limited: the overlaps file alone requires ~5 TB of external storage for a full human ONT dataset

skills.description: Use when a functional enrichment scan (e.g. tappAS partially-overlapping-samples z-test over positional features and GO terms) returns many unadjusted p-values that must be corrected for multiple testing before calling significant features.
skills.name: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction Use when a functional enrichment scan (e.g. tappAS partially-overlapping-samples z-test over positional features and GO terms) returns many unadjusted p-values that must be corrected for multiple testing before calling significant features. Only a single hypothesis is being tested (no family of enrichment p-values to correct) The enrichment tool already reports FDR-adjusted values, so a second correction would double-shrink significance The goal is genome-wide DE gene correction rather than correcting across functional feature/GO term tests in tappAS http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate procedure to the family of p-values produced by a tappAS functional enrichment comparison of coDIU vs DIU genes, retaining features significant at FDR < 0.05 before downstream redundancy filtering (Revigo). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Apply the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate procedure to the family of p-values produced by a tappAS functional enrichment comparison of coDIU vs DIU genes, retaining features significant at FDR < 0.05 before downstream redundancy filtering (Revigo).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single hypothesis is being tested (no family of enrichment p-values to correct) The enrichment tool already reports FDR-adjusted values, so a second correction would double-shrink significance The goal is genome-wide DE gene correction rather than correcting across functional feature/GO term tests in tappAS

skills.description: Use when many p-values from per-event statistical tests (e.g. beta-binomial likelihood-ratio tests of PSI differences between sample groups) must be corrected for multiple comparisons before thresholding at an FDR level.
skills.name: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction Use when many p-values from per-event statistical tests (e.g. beta-binomial likelihood-ratio tests of PSI differences between sample groups) must be corrected for multiple comparisons before thresholding at an FDR level. When only a single hypothesis is tested (no family-wise multiplicity), where a raw p-value suffices When raw p-values are not calibrated (e.g. fail uniformity on simulated nulls with KS test p <= 0.05), which invalidates BH's control assumptions When the goal is genome-wide transcript-level differential expression rather than per-event alternative splicing calls from LRTS segment graphs http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across alternative splicing events to control the expected fraction of false positives when testing thousands of events (e.g. IsoTools beta-binomial differential splicing tests) simultaneously. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across alternative splicing events to control the expected fraction of false positives when testing thousands of events (e.g. IsoTools beta-binomial differential splicing tests) simultaneously.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single hypothesis is tested (no family-wise multiplicity), where a raw p-value suffices When raw p-values are not calibrated (e.g. fail uniformity on simulated nulls with KS test p <= 0.05), which invalidates BH's control assumptions When the goal is genome-wide transcript-level differential expression rather than per-event alternative splicing calls from LRTS segment graphs

skills.description: Use when a tncRNA or gene count matrix (control vs stress conditions, ≥3 biological replicates each) is tested for differential expression and raw per-feature p-values must be FDR-controlled before calling up/down-regulation.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction Use when a tncRNA or gene count matrix (control vs stress conditions, ≥3 biological replicates each) is tested for differential expression and raw per-feature p-values must be FDR-controlled before calling up/down-regulation. Input is raw small RNA-seq FASTQ that has not yet been adapter-trimmed (Trim Galore) and quantified into a tncRNA count matrix — use tncRNA identification/quantification first Comparison has fewer than three biological replicates per condition — the source workflow explicitly retains only such sample sets before DE testing Input is already a table of adjusted p-values or DE results — no re-correction is needed; proceed directly to significance filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini–Hochberg multiple-testing correction to differential expression testing of tncRNAs (via DESeq2's Wald test), so that stress-responsive tncRNA calls (adjusted p < 0.05) control the false discovery rate across thousands of simultaneous tests. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini–Hochberg multiple-testing correction to differential expression testing of tncRNAs (via DESeq2's Wald test), so that stress-responsive tncRNA calls (adjusted p < 0.05) control the false discovery rate across thousands of simultaneous tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw small RNA-seq FASTQ that has not yet been adapter-trimmed (Trim Galore) and quantified into a tncRNA count matrix — use tncRNA identification/quantification first Comparison has fewer than three biological replicates per condition — the source workflow explicitly retains only such sample sets before DE testing Input is already a table of adjusted p-values or DE results — no re-correction is needed; proceed directly to significance filtering

skills.description: Use when calling modified transcriptomic sites (m6A/m5C k-mers) from nanopore direct RNA predictions across a large number of sites, and per-site significance or probability must be corrected at alpha = 0.05, 0.01, or 0.001.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction-thresholding
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction-thresholding Use when calling modified transcriptomic sites (m6A/m5C k-mers) from nanopore direct RNA predictions across a large number of sites, and per-site significance or probability must be corrected at alpha = 0.05, 0.01, or 0.001. Only a handful of pre-specified candidate sites are being tested, so the multiple-testing burden is negligible and strict transcriptome-wide cut-offs would unnecessarily reduce sensitivity The goal is single-read (per-molecule) modification prediction rather than site-level significance testing across many transcriptomic sites Input is raw FAST5/nanopolish eventalign signal that has not yet been scored by a modification caller — thresholding applies downstream of prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies multiple-testing correction and probability/score thresholds to control the expected FDR when calling RNA modifications (m6A, m5C) from nanopore direct RNA data across thousands of transcriptomic sites, as used to benchmark CHEUI against Xpore, Nanocompore, Epinano, NanoRMS and Tombo. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Applies multiple-testing correction and probability/score thresholds to control the expected FDR when calling RNA modifications (m6A, m5C) from nanopore direct RNA data across thousands of transcriptomic sites, as used to benchmark CHEUI against Xpore, Nanocompore, Epinano, NanoRMS and Tombo.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a handful of pre-specified candidate sites are being tested, so the multiple-testing burden is negligible and strict transcriptome-wide cut-offs would unnecessarily reduce sensitivity The goal is single-read (per-molecule) modification prediction rather than site-level significance testing across many transcriptomic sites Input is raw FAST5/nanopolish eventalign signal that has not yet been scored by a modification caller — thresholding applies downstream of prediction

skills.name: multiplex-imaging-feature-histogram-estimation

Data are pixel-level OME-TIFF images rather than a single-cell feature table — pixel-level normalization requires nucleus/cell segmentation masks and a different pipeline branch Data are mIHC (chromogenic) samples — linear shift/scale normalization factors are unsuitable due to non-linear enzyme-catalyzed signal amplification The input is already a normalized feature matrix or the goal is batch correction by mean division/Z score/ComBat rather than distribution alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 First stage of UniFORM's feature-level normalization: compute per-marker histogram distributions of log-transformed single-cell mean intensities over a shared global range so that distributions from different MTI batches are directly comparable before functional data registration. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172
skills.summary: First stage of UniFORM's feature-level normalization: compute per-marker histogram distributions of log-transformed single-cell mean intensities over a shared global range so that distributions from different MTI batches are directly comparable before functional data registration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are pixel-level OME-TIFF images rather than a single-cell feature table — pixel-level normalization requires nucleus/cell segmentation masks and a different pipeline branch Data are mIHC (chromogenic) samples — linear shift/scale normalization factors are unsuitable due to non-linear enzyme-catalyzed signal amplification The input is already a normalized feature matrix or the goal is batch correction by mean division/Z score/ComBat rather than distribution alignment

skills.description: Use when integrating single-cell or pixel-level MTI data (CyCIF, ORION, COMET platforms) across batches with right-skewed, heterogeneous marker distributions that violate Z score/ComBat assumptions.
skills.name: multiplex-imaging-intensity-normalization
skills.search_text: multiplex-imaging-intensity-normalization Use when integrating single-cell or pixel-level MTI data (CyCIF, ORION, COMET platforms) across batches with right-skewed, heterogeneous marker distributions that violate Z score/ComBat assumptions. Data are mIHC (multiplex immunohistochemistry) samples: chromogenic detection produces non-linear signal intensities due to enzyme-catalyzed colorimetric amplification, for which linear normalization factors are unsuitable Input is already normalized, or the goal is analysis of normalized data without cross-batch intensity alignment (e.g., pure downstream clustering on a single batch) Signals come from extracellular regions or compromised datasets/segmentation masks — UniFORM is optimized for within-cell normalization and cannot recover compromised signals http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Normalizes multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) marker intensities across samples and batches at both feature (single-cell) and pixel levels by aligning biologically invariant negative populations with automatic rigid-landmark functional registration, preserving distribution shape and positive-population proportions. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172
skills.summary: Normalizes multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) marker intensities across samples and batches at both feature (single-cell) and pixel levels by aligning biologically invariant negative populations with automatic rigid-landmark functional registration, preserving distribution shape and positive-population proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are mIHC (multiplex immunohistochemistry) samples: chromogenic detection produces non-linear signal intensities due to enzyme-catalyzed colorimetric amplification, for which linear normalization factors are unsuitable Input is already normalized, or the goal is analysis of normalized data without cross-batch intensity alignment (e.g., pure downstream clustering on a single batch) Signals come from extracellular regions or compromised datasets/segmentation masks — UniFORM is optimized for within-cell normalization and cannot recover compromised signals

skills.description: Use when segmenting individual cells in multiplexed immunofluorescence (e.g., colorectal adenoma) or MIBI breast carcinoma tissue images where columnar epithelial cells have incomplete membranes and nuclear-dilation or Voronoi methods undersegment.
skills.name: multiplexed-image-cell-segmentation
skills.search_text: multiplexed-image-cell-segmentation Use when segmenting individual cells in multiplexed immunofluorescence (e.g., colorectal adenoma) or MIBI breast carcinoma tissue images where columnar epithelial cells have incomplete membranes and nuclear-dilation or Voronoi methods undersegment. The goal is comparison against deep-learning segmentation on non-epithelial tissues — Mesmer was trained on normal mouse small intestine, normal human colon, and colorectal cancer but not colorectal adenomas, so cross-method conclusions are tissue-specific Input images are single-channel or lack membrane markers (e.g., NaKATPase) — excluding membrane markers and DAPI from pixel classification decreased similarity to manually annotated borders The task is cell clustering or population discovery rather than segmentation — t-SNE shape analysis in this study did not reveal discernible cellular populations or clear patterns in marker expression MIRIAM-style segmentation of single cells in multiplexed tissue imaging: random-forest (Ilastik) pixel classification to define nucleus/membrane/cytoplasm compartments, followed by detection and 'connects the dots' resegmentation of cells with internal aberrant membranes. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: MIRIAM-style segmentation of single cells in multiplexed tissue imaging: random-forest (Ilastik) pixel classification to define nucleus/membrane/cytoplasm compartments, followed by detection and 'connects the dots' resegmentation of cells with internal aberrant membranes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comparison against deep-learning segmentation on non-epithelial tissues — Mesmer was trained on normal mouse small intestine, normal human colon, and colorectal cancer but not colorectal adenomas, so cross-method conclusions are tissue-specific Input images are single-channel or lack membrane markers (e.g., NaKATPase) — excluding membrane markers and DAPI from pixel classification decreased similarity to manually annotated borders The task is cell clustering or population discovery rather than segmentation — t-SNE shape analysis in this study did not reveal discernible cellular populations or clear patterns in marker expression

skills.description: Use when input is a multi-marker (e.g., 36-marker MIBI or multiplexed immunofluorescence) tissue image stack needing pixel-level compartment labels (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm/other) before single-cell segmentation and per-cell marker quantification.

skills.search_text: multiplexed-image-pixel-classification Use when input is a multi-marker (e.g., 36-marker MIBI or multiplexed immunofluorescence) tissue image stack needing pixel-level compartment labels (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm/other) before single-cell segmentation and per-cell marker quantification. Input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table or segmentation mask — pixel classification is upstream and unnecessary The imaging data is single-channel or non-multiplexed histology where marker-based compartment definitions (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm) cannot be learned The goal is a deep-learning pretrained segmentation (e.g., Mesmer) rather than a trained-on-your-data random forest classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Random-forest-based machine learning pixel classification of multiplexed tissue imaging data (e.g., MIBI or multiplexed immunofluorescence) to label nuclei, membranes, and other intracellular structures, serving as the input to downstream cell segmentation and per-compartment quantification as in the MIRIAM pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Random-forest-based machine learning pixel classification of multiplexed tissue imaging data (e.g., MIBI or multiplexed immunofluorescence) to label nuclei, membranes, and other intracellular structures, serving as the input to downstream cell segmentation and per-compartment quantification as in the MIRIAM pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table or segmentation mask — pixel classification is upstream and unnecessary The imaging data is single-channel or non-multiplexed histology where marker-based compartment definitions (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm) cannot be learned The goal is a deep-learning pretrained segmentation (e.g., Mesmer) rather than a trained-on-your-data random forest classifier

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell autoencoder latent shape vectors and compartment-quantified marker intensities from multiplexed imaging, and want to test whether shape-space structure predicts molecular phenotypes.
skills.name: multiplexed-imaging-single-cell-quantification
skills.search_text: multiplexed-imaging-single-cell-quantification Use when you have per-cell autoencoder latent shape vectors and compartment-quantified marker intensities from multiplexed imaging, and want to test whether shape-space structure predicts molecular phenotypes. When the goal is marker-expression-based clustering itself — use t-SNE directly on marker intensities (Figure 3A), not on shape latent vectors When latent vectors include cells used to train the autoencoder — the embedding would reflect training data and not generalize to held-out cells When the data are not single-cell outputs from a multiplexed imaging segmentation/quantification pipeline (e.g., already-aggregated bulk features) http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Applies t-SNE (Rtsne) to autoencoder-derived cell shape latent vectors from the MIRIAM pipeline on held-out colonic adenoma cells, then overlays per-cell marker intensities (e.g., p-ERK) to test whether shape-space clusters correspond to marker-expression patterns. Reproduces the shape-based t-SNE panel of Figure 3 and the negative result of Supplemental Figure 5. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Applies t-SNE (Rtsne) to autoencoder-derived cell shape latent vectors from the MIRIAM pipeline on held-out colonic adenoma cells, then overlays per-cell marker intensities (e.g., p-ERK) to test whether shape-space clusters correspond to marker-expression patterns. Reproduces the shape-based t-SNE panel of Figure 3 and the negative result of Supplemental Figure 5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is marker-expression-based clustering itself — use t-SNE directly on marker intensities (Figure 3A), not on shape latent vectors When latent vectors include cells used to train the autoencoder — the embedding would reflect training data and not generalize to held-out cells When the data are not single-cell outputs from a multiplexed imaging segmentation/quantification pipeline (e.g., already-aggregated bulk features)

skills.description: Use when per-sample VCFs and sample_info.txt files exist for all members of a trio (e.g. NA12878/NA12891/NA12892) and a joint multisample VCF plus pedigree file is needed for downstream family-based annotation, scoring, and prioritization.
skills.name: multisample-joint-genotyping-trio
skills.search_text: multisample-joint-genotyping-trio Use when per-sample VCFs and sample_info.txt files exist for all members of a trio (e.g. NA12878/NA12891/NA12892) and a joint multisample VCF plus pedigree file is needed for downstream family-based annotation, scoring, and prioritization. Only a single sample needs processing — eDiVA-Predict alone (eDiVA-Predict.nf) suffices; joint calling requires all family members' calls Variants are already annotated and ranked (e.g. combined.variants.supplement.ranked.csv exists) — proceed to eDiVA-Prioritize instead of regenotyping http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Regenotypes every variant position harboring an SNV or small indel in at least one trio member to build a joint multisample VCF matrix, using eDiVA_prepare_for_annotation.nf after individual sample variant calling.
