skills.description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing Clairvoyante's five-layer CNN architecture for variant calling from SMS reads, or when building a multitask DNN that predicts variant type, zygosity, alternative allele and indel length from alignment tensors.
skills.name: multitask-convolutional-network-implementation
skills.search_text: multitask-convolutional-network-implementation Use when reconstructing or reimplementing Clairvoyante's five-layer CNN architecture for variant calling from SMS reads, or when building a multitask DNN that predicts variant type, zygosity, alternative allele and indel length from alignment tensors. Variants with two or more alternative alleles — the current Clairvoyante design ignores multi-allelic variants and multi-allelic SNPs are excluded from training Indels longer than 4 bp when an exact alternative allele is needed — due to rareness of long indel training samples, the exact alternative allele is only provided for indels ≤4 bp Somatic or trio-sample-based variant calling — not supported by this implementation (planned future work) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implement Clairvoyante, a multi-task five-layer convolutional neural network (three conv layers plus two fully connected layers with four prediction heads) for variant calling on single-molecule sequencing reads, built on TensorFlow. The network jointly predicts variant type (SNP or indel), zygosity, alternative allele, and indel length from encoded read-alignment tensors. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Implement Clairvoyante, a multi-task five-layer convolutional neural network (three conv layers plus two fully connected layers with four prediction heads) for variant calling on single-molecule sequencing reads, built on TensorFlow. The network jointly predicts variant type (SNP or indel), zygosity, alternative allele, and indel length from encoded read-alignment tensors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants with two or more alternative alleles — the current Clairvoyante design ignores multi-allelic variants and multi-allelic SNPs are excluded from training Indels longer than 4 bp when an exact alternative allele is needed — due to rareness of long indel training samples, the exact alternative allele is only provided for indels ≤4 bp Somatic or trio-sample-based variant calling — not supported by this implementation (planned future work)

skills.description: Use when comparing runtime and memory footprint of nanopore read compressors/decompressors on FASTQ benchmarks, especially multi-threaded (>4 thread) decompression speed comparisons like NanoSpring vs CoLoRd.
skills.name: multithreaded-compressor-execution
skills.search_text: multithreaded-compressor-execution Use when comparing runtime and memory footprint of nanopore read compressors/decompressors on FASTQ benchmarks, especially multi-threaded (>4 thread) decompression speed comparisons like NanoSpring vs CoLoRd. When the goal is compression ratio (bits per base) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking — NanoSpring only compresses base sequences, not identifiers or quality scores When reads are short, low-error Illumina reads — specialized tools like SPRING and PgRC assume short reads and this nanopore workflow does not apply When only a single-thread or <=4-thread regime is of interest — the paper's key speed advantage (e.g. >4x faster decompression) is measured with 20 threads http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark NanoSpring and competing FASTQ compressors (gzip, ENANO, CoLoRd) by running compression and decompression with 20 threads, recording wall-clock time and peak memory to reproduce the paper's Tables 3-4 resource-usage comparison. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Benchmark NanoSpring and competing FASTQ compressors (gzip, ENANO, CoLoRd) by running compression and decompression with 20 threads, recording wall-clock time and peak memory to reproduce the paper's Tables 3-4 resource-usage comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is compression ratio (bits per base) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking — NanoSpring only compresses base sequences, not identifiers or quality scores When reads are short, low-error Illumina reads — specialized tools like SPRING and PgRC assume short reads and this nanopore workflow does not apply When only a single-thread or <=4-thread regime is of interest — the paper's key speed advantage (e.g. >4x faster decompression) is measured with 20 threads

skills.description: Use when you need to validate that large de novo contigs align colinearly to a known reference genome, e.g. checking that ~342.5 kb and ~472.5 kb MeGAMerge contigs from HMP sample SRS022071 match the B. helcogenes chromosome.
skills.name: mummer-alignment-coordinates-extraction
skills.search_text: mummer-alignment-coordinates-extraction Use when you need to validate that large de novo contigs align colinearly to a known reference genome, e.g. checking that ~342.5 kb and ~472.5 kb MeGAMerge contigs from HMP sample SRS022071 match the B. helcogenes chromosome. When the goal is de novo assembly or merging of contigs — use the MeGAMerge/Minimus2 pipeline itself; nucmer alignment is only the downstream validation step When no reference genome is available — colinearity validation against a reference cannot be performed, and the article instead relies on read mapping, gene prediction, and similarity searches When contigs are expected to be chimeric — nucmer colinearity alone will not flag contigs that do not contiguously align to a single reference genome as chimeric without additional chimera-flagging analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Validates contiguity of large merged metagenomic contigs (e.g., MeGAMerge output) by aligning them with nucmer to a reference genome, filtering to the best collinear alignments with delta-filter, and extracting tabular query/reference coordinates with show-coords to confirm colinearity. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Validates contiguity of large merged metagenomic contigs (e.g., MeGAMerge output) by aligning them with nucmer to a reference genome, filtering to the best collinear alignments with delta-filter, and extracting tabular query/reference coordinates with show-coords to confirm colinearity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo assembly or merging of contigs — use the MeGAMerge/Minimus2 pipeline itself; nucmer alignment is only the downstream validation step When no reference genome is available — colinearity validation against a reference cannot be performed, and the article instead relies on read mapping, gene prediction, and similarity searches When contigs are expected to be chimeric — nucmer colinearity alone will not flag contigs that do not contiguously align to a single reference genome as chimeric without additional chimera-flagging analysis

skills.description: Use when assembled scaffolds or contigs (e.g., DFS hybrid NA12878 scaffolds) must be structurally validated against a reference genome and compared to competing assemblies (Canu, MaSuRCA, 10X, DOVETAIL) via whole-genome alignment statistics.
skills.name: mummer-nucmer-whole-genome-alignment
skills.search_text: mummer-nucmer-whole-genome-alignment Use when assembled scaffolds or contigs (e.g., DFS hybrid NA12878 scaffolds) must be structurally validated against a reference genome and compared to competing assemblies (Canu, MaSuRCA, 10X, DOVETAIL) via whole-genome alignment statistics. Input is unassembled reads rather than finished scaffolds/contigs — this skill evaluates assembly accuracy and cannot itself scaffold; use Fast-SG to construct the scaffolding graph and produce the DFS scaffolds first. No reference genome or comparison assemblies are available — the Gage structural-error classification (misjoins, relocations, translocations, inversions) is defined relative to the reference whole-genome alignment. The goal is k-mer counting or scaffolding-graph construction rather than assembly evaluation — use KMC/Fast-SG, which Fast-SG relies on via its alignment-free algorithm. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Structural-accuracy evaluation of genome assemblies (e.g., the Fast-SG/DFS hybrid assembly of NA12878) by whole-genome Nucmer alignment against the human reference, followed by Gage computation of N50, alignment identity, and structural-error percentages (misjoins, relocations, translocations, inversions). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Structural-accuracy evaluation of genome assemblies (e.g., the Fast-SG/DFS hybrid assembly of NA12878) by whole-genome Nucmer alignment against the human reference, followed by Gage computation of N50, alignment identity, and structural-error percentages (misjoins, relocations, translocations, inversions).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unassembled reads rather than finished scaffolds/contigs — this skill evaluates assembly accuracy and cannot itself scaffold; use Fast-SG to construct the scaffolding graph and produce the DFS scaffolds first. No reference genome or comparison assemblies are available — the Gage structural-error classification (misjoins, relocations, translocations, inversions) is defined relative to the reference whole-genome alignment. The goal is k-mer counting or scaffolding-graph construction rather than assembly evaluation — use KMC/Fast-SG, which Fast-SG relies on via its alignment-free algorithm.

skills.description: Use when comparing two genome assemblies (FASTA sets) to test bidirectional completeness: whether one assembly contains sequence missing from the other, and to visualize syntenic layout as in the Fig. 5a eel comparison.
skills.name: mummer-synteny-dotplot-generation
skills.search_text: mummer-synteny-dotplot-generation Use when comparing two genome assemblies (FASTA sets) to test bidirectional completeness: whether one assembly contains sequence missing from the other, and to visualize syntenic layout as in the Fig. 5a eel comparison. When only read-level validation (not whole-assembly structural comparison) is needed, e.g. checking consensus accuracy with Racon/Pilon — this skill compares finished scaffold sets only When a high-quality reference genome exists for structural validation — the article notes no such reference was available, and this skill only gives reciprocal assembly-vs-assembly agreement, not ground truth When quantifying base-level accuracy rather than presence/absence and layout of large syntenic blocks http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A MUMmer-based whole-genome alignment and synteny visualization workflow that aligns an assembly (e.g. the TULIP nanopore eel scaffolds) against a reference draft (AZBK01) with nucmer, filters to reciprocal-best 1-to-1 alignments, and renders an ordered scaffold-vs-contig dot plot to detect sequence present in one assembly but absent from the other. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: A MUMmer-based whole-genome alignment and synteny visualization workflow that aligns an assembly (e.g. the TULIP nanopore eel scaffolds) against a reference draft (AZBK01) with nucmer, filters to reciprocal-best 1-to-1 alignments, and renders an ordered scaffold-vs-contig dot plot to detect sequence present in one assembly but absent from the other.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only read-level validation (not whole-assembly structural comparison) is needed, e.g. checking consensus accuracy with Racon/Pilon — this skill compares finished scaffold sets only When a high-quality reference genome exists for structural validation — the article notes no such reference was available, and this skill only gives reciprocal assembly-vs-assembly agreement, not ground truth When quantifying base-level accuracy rather than presence/absence and layout of large syntenic blocks

skills.description: Use when building a benchmark with known ground-truth variants: a reference FASTA must be mutated (e.g. insertions/deletions of 100 bp–4 kbp) so real reads can be aligned and SV calls scored against the induced event list.
skills.name: mutant-reference-generation-with-mutatrix
skills.search_text: mutant-reference-generation-with-mutatrix Use when building a benchmark with known ground-truth variants: a reference FASTA must be mutated (e.g. insertions/deletions of 100 bp–4 kbp) so real reads can be aligned and SV calls scored against the induced event list. You need realistic biological variation or allele frequencies drawn from real population data — Mutatrix draws alleles from a simulated zeta-distribution power-law spectrum, not observed variants. Your mappers are being benchmarked on SNVs only in the original reference — no mutated reference is needed since no truth set must be constructed. When signatures are unknown and must be extracted de novo from the mutation count matrix — use the denovoNMF 5-step framework (Dirichlet resampling, k-means initialization, silhouette-based K selection) instead of fixing P and running InverseNMF. When the input is already a normalized signature contribution/abundance matrix rather than raw per-sample somatic mutation records (MAF/VCF). http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Estimate per-sample contributions to a fixed, user-defined mutational signature (e.g., COSMIC SBS1*, the age signature) using the RNMF InverseNMF approach, then stratify samples (e.g., by TP53 R342* status) and compare group median contributions to link a gene mutation to signature activity. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Estimate per-sample contributions to a fixed, user-defined mutational signature (e.g., COSMIC SBS1*, the age signature) using the RNMF InverseNMF approach, then stratify samples (e.g., by TP53 R342* status) and compare group median contributions to link a gene mutation to signature activity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When signatures are unknown and must be extracted de novo from the mutation count matrix — use the denovoNMF 5-step framework (Dirichlet resampling, k-means initialization, silhouette-based K selection) instead of fixing P and running InverseNMF. skills.summary: Computes gene-level cumulative contribution abundance (CCA) using the RNMF R package to quantify and visualize the association between mutational signatures (COSMIC SBS/DBS/ID or de novo NMF) and individual genes from a MAF file plus P and S signature matrices.

skills.description: Use when you have a non-silent mutation MAF file plus RNMF P/S signature matrices for an ESCC cohort and need per-signature gene CCA matrices as image inputs for survival-outcome classification.
skills.name: mutational-signature-gene-cca-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: mutational-signature-gene-cca-matrix-generation Use when you have a non-silent mutation MAF file plus RNMF P/S signature matrices for an ESCC cohort and need per-signature gene CCA matrices as image inputs for survival-outcome classification. You only need de novo signature extraction — use denovoNMF directly; CCA matrix generation requires pre-computed P and S signature matrices. Your mutation set includes silent mutations — the workflow operates on the non-silent MAF input intersected with the 717 genes list. skills.summary: Generates gene-level cumulative contribution abundance (CCA) matrices from RNMF signature results and non-silent MAF mutation data, then renders them as ordered N x N images (resized to 500x500) that serve as image features for deep-learning prognostic classification (e.g., DenseNet-121 G2 vs G4 ESCC survival discrimination).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need de novo signature extraction — use denovoNMF directly; CCA matrix generation requires pre-computed P and S signature matrices. You need population-scale prognostic modeling with complete clinical covariates — the article notes incomplete clinical information (treatment, medication, follow-up) and a relatively small cohort limit model learning.

skills.description: Use when you have a somatic mutation catalog (MAF/VCF) for one or few tumor samples and a predefined COSMIC signature set, and you need per-sample signature contribution scores rather than de novo signature discovery.
skills.name: mutational-signature-refitting
skills.search_text: mutational-signature-refitting Use when you have a somatic mutation catalog (MAF/VCF) for one or few tumor samples and a predefined COSMIC signature set, and you need per-sample signature contribution scores rather than de novo signature discovery. You need to discover novel signatures rather than quantify known COSMIC signatures — use RNMF's denovoNMF 5-step framework instead Input is already a refitted contribution matrix S or a gene-level association result (e.g. CCA matrix) rather than raw somatic variant calls http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Refit a fixed, user-defined COSMIC signature matrix P onto an observed tumor mutation count matrix V using the RNMF package's InverseNMF procedure, estimating the per-sample contribution matrix S. skills.summary: Refit a fixed, user-defined COSMIC signature matrix P onto an observed tumor mutation count matrix V using the RNMF package's InverseNMF procedure, estimating the per-sample contribution matrix S. skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to discover novel signatures rather than quantify known COSMIC signatures — use RNMF's denovoNMF 5-step framework instead Input is already a refitted contribution matrix S or a gene-level association result (e.g. CCA matrix) rather than raw somatic variant calls

skills.description: Use when you have nanopolish eventalign output from nanopore reads (e.g., nanoHiMe-seq HepG2 H3K27me3 data) and need to identify 6mA-containing genomic windows, optionally limited to ChIP-seq/CUT&Tag peak regions.
skills.name: nanopore-6ma-region-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-6ma-region-calling Use when you have nanopolish eventalign output from nanopore reads (e.g., nanoHiMe-seq HepG2 H3K27me3 data) and need to identify 6mA-containing genomic windows, optionally limited to ChIP-seq/CUT&Tag peak regions. skills.summary: Calls 6mA-containing regions (50 bp windows, 25 bp step) from nanopolish eventalign nanopore reads using the nanoHiMe hidden Markov model, optionally restricting calling to peak regions (e.g., ENCODE H3K27me3 peaks) and scoring each window by a log likelihood ratio for 6mA methylation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-CpG 5-methylcytosine calls rather than 6mA-containing regions — use nanoHiMe mCG-calling mode instead. A precompiled NanoPipe target already exists — it already ships with best-fitting last-train-derived alignment parameters and substitution matrices The analysis goal is metagenomics analysis — the paper states metagenomics is not yet supported and only planned future work The downstream goal is SNP detection polishing rather than target preparation — use the filter steps (e.g., 20% alternate coverage, 30% of maximum contig coverage) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Constructs a LAST alignment target database (via lastdb) and derives MinION-adjusted alignment scoring parameters (via last-train) so NanoPipe can align Oxford Nanopore MinION reads to a user-supplied target genome. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Constructs a LAST alignment target database (via lastdb) and derives MinION-adjusted alignment scoring parameters (via last-train) so NanoPipe can align Oxford Nanopore MinION reads to a user-supplied target genome.

skills.description: Use when an ONT- (or PacBio-) sequenced 10x Genomics 5' cDNA or targeted TCR amplicon FASTQ must be converted into per-cell-barcode TCR calls and a TCR-positive cell count comparable to Illumina-based 10x V(DJ) results.
skills.name: nanopore-amplicon-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: nanopore-amplicon-pipeline-execution Use when an ONT- (or PacBio-) sequenced 10x Genomics 5' cDNA or targeted TCR amplicon FASTQ must be converted into per-cell-barcode TCR calls and a TCR-positive cell count comparable to Illumina-based 10x V(DJ) results. Input is Illumina short-read data — nanoranger is built for long reads from ONT or Pacific Biosciences devices, and short reads cannot resolve the full-length targeted amplicons Input is a raw 10x whole-transcriptome FASTQ with no targeted amplification of the locus of interest — nanoranger defines optimal targets as loci near the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcripts shorter than 4 kB; unsuitable loci hit the genotyping ceiling The analysis goal is standard gene-expression quantification (count matrix / clustering) rather than lineage-defining features such as TCR sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3304 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Run the nanoranger long-read workflow in 5p10X_XCR mode to align ONT-sequenced 10x Genomics TCR amplicon reads and call TCR sequences per cell barcode, then aggregate per-cell calls to a total TCR-positive cell count. This converts targeted-amplification long-read FASTQ into a quantitative, Illumina-comparable per-cell TCR detection result. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Run the nanoranger long-read workflow in 5p10X_XCR mode to align ONT-sequenced 10x Genomics TCR amplicon reads and call TCR sequences per cell barcode, then aggregate per-cell calls to a total TCR-positive cell count. This converts targeted-amplification long-read FASTQ into a quantitative, Illumina-comparable per-cell TCR detection result.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Illumina short-read data — nanoranger is built for long reads from ONT or Pacific Biosciences devices, and short reads cannot resolve the full-length targeted amplicons Input is a raw 10x whole-transcriptome FASTQ with no targeted amplification of the locus of interest — nanoranger defines optimal targets as loci near the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcripts shorter than 4 kB; unsuitable loci hit the genotyping ceiling The analysis goal is standard gene-expression quantification (count matrix / clustering) rather than lineage-defining features such as TCR sequences

skills.description: Decision support for choosing how many ONT MinION reads (2D or 1D2) to allocate per OTU when constructing de novo 16S rRNA consensus sequences, or when validating that a consensus depth yields sufficient accuracy.
skills.name: nanopore-amplicon-read-subsampling
skills.search_text: nanopore-amplicon-read-subsampling Decision support for choosing how many ONT MinION reads (2D or 1D2) to allocate per OTU when constructing de novo 16S rRNA consensus sequences, or when validating that a consensus depth yields sufficient accuracy. Analysis already has >=50 reads per OTU and only needs a point estimate of consensus accuracy rather than a depth-accuracy curve Input is short-read amplicon data (e.g., Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM) rather than ONT nanopore 2D/1D2 reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A benchmarking skill that subsamples nanopore amplicon reads at varying per-OTU depths (5-100) and quantifies how read count affects nanoClust consensus sequence accuracy, establishing that >99% accuracy is reached above 5 reads, plateaus at 10-15 reads, and is only reliably high at >=50 reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that subsamples nanopore amplicon reads at varying per-OTU depths (5-100) and quantifies how read count affects nanoClust consensus sequence accuracy, establishing that >99% accuracy is reached above 5 reads, plateaus at 10-15 reads, and is only reliably high at >=50 reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis already has >=50 reads per OTU and only needs a point estimate of consensus accuracy rather than a depth-accuracy curve Input is short-read amplicon data (e.g., Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM) rather than ONT nanopore 2D/1D2 reads

skills.description: Use when putative DEL/DUP SV calls (from Sniffles, CuteSV, SVIM, NanoVar on nanopore WGS alignments) must be profiled by per-base coverage across each SV interval plus 1-Mb up- and downstream flanks before coverage-based filtering or truth-set validation.
skills.name: nanopore-bam-coverage-profiling
skills.search_text: nanopore-bam-coverage-profiling Use when putative DEL/DUP SV calls (from Sniffles, CuteSV, SVIM, NanoVar on nanopore WGS alignments) must be profiled by per-base coverage across each SV interval plus 1-Mb up- and downstream flanks before coverage-based filtering or truth-set validation. The SV calls are insertions, inversions, or other non-DEL/DUP types — coverage analysis 'can only be applied to some types, namely deletions and duplications' No putative SV coordinates exist — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs positions from another technique or multi-sample analysis The candidate SV is very large (>10 Mb) and encompasses other SVs or centromeres — such calls were treated as probable artifacts, not true variants http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Profiles per-base read depth from nanopore alignment BAMs over putative DEL/DUP structural variants and their 1-Mb flanking sequence, using disCoverage which internally invokes mosdepth. This coverage profile is the raw material disCoverage needs to statistically test whether called SVs agree with observed DNA copy number. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012

This coverage profile is the raw material disCoverage needs to statistically test whether called SVs agree with observed DNA copy number.

skills.description: Use when Nanopore FASTQ reads need demultiplexing or barcode attachment auditing (rapid or native kits like SQK-RBK114-96/SQK-NBD114-96), or when detecting complex/fused barcode configurations that simpler demultiplexers mis-handle.
skills.name: nanopore-barcode-annotation
skills.search_text: nanopore-barcode-annotation Use when Nanopore FASTQ reads need demultiplexing or barcode attachment auditing (rapid or native kits like SQK-RBK114-96/SQK-NBD114-96), or when detecting complex/fused barcode configurations that simpler demultiplexers mis-handle. Input is not Nanopore barcode data (e.g. already-demultiplexed FASTQ or a feature/count table) — there are no barcodes to annotate A simple kit demultiplex alone suffices and runtime matters greatly — --use-extended is ~3x slower and only needed for fusion-point/artefact searches or consensus-grade quality Screening contamination at loci requiring exact-match semantics rather than approximate edit-distance matching, where Sassy-based fuzzy search could yield random Fflank false positives http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Pattern-aware annotation of Nanopore barcode/flank attachments using Barbell's Sassy-based edit-distance search, producing a per-read TSV (anno.tsv) of barcode labels, match types, flank/barcode costs, strands, and cut coordinates for downstream inspect/filter/trim steps. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Pattern-aware annotation of Nanopore barcode/flank attachments using Barbell's Sassy-based edit-distance search, producing a per-read TSV (anno.tsv) of barcode labels, match types, flank/barcode costs, strands, and cut coordinates for downstream inspect/filter/trim steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not Nanopore barcode data (e.g. already-demultiplexed FASTQ or a feature/count table) — there are no barcodes to annotate A simple kit demultiplex alone suffices and runtime matters greatly — --use-extended is ~3x slower and only needed for fusion-point/artefact searches or consensus-grade quality Screening contamination at loci requiring exact-match semantics rather than approximate edit-distance matching, where Sassy-based fuzzy search could yield random Fflank false positives

skills.description: Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads with Barbell and you need to reproduce, verify, or tune barcode acceptance scoring: e.g., validating that reads are assigned their synthetically embedded barcode under the >=20%-of-perfect-score and >=10%-separation default thresholds.
skills.name: nanopore-barcode-assignment-threshold-tuning
skills.search_text: nanopore-barcode-assignment-threshold-tuning Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads with Barbell and you need to reproduce, verify, or tune barcode acceptance scoring: e.g., validating that reads are assigned their synthetically embedded barcode under the >=20%-of-perfect-score and >=10%-separation default thresholds. Input reads carry no barcode constructs and the goal is basecalling or assembly rather than demultiplexing. An annotation TSV already exists and the task is only pattern summarization or trimming (`barbell inspect` / `barbell trim`), not threshold reconstruction or validation. Input is RNA or Twist Nanopore kit data, which the README notes are exceptions to the built-in kit presets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs and validates Barbell's subsequence-based barcode scoring scheme, which derives per-read scores from edit-distance alignment CIGARs rewarding long contiguous exact-match runs, and applies the default acceptance thresholds (score >=20% of the perfect-match score with >=10% separation from the second-best barcode) to demultiplex Nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Reconstructs and validates Barbell's subsequence-based barcode scoring scheme, which derives per-read scores from edit-distance alignment CIGARs rewarding long contiguous exact-match runs, and applies the default acceptance thresholds (score >=20% of the perfect-match score with >=10% separation from the second-best barcode) to demultiplex Nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads carry no barcode constructs and the goal is basecalling or assembly rather than demultiplexing. An annotation TSV already exists and the task is only pattern summarization or trimming (`barbell inspect` / `barbell trim`), not threshold reconstruction or validation. Input is RNA or Twist Nanopore kit data, which the README notes are exceptions to the built-in kit presets.

skills.description: Use when designing or expanding a DNA barcode kit for nanopore sequencing at a fixed barcode length (e.g., 24 bp) and error tolerance (e.g., 2 edit errors), or when comparing a generated kit's demultiplexing accuracy to official ONT kits.
skills.name: nanopore-barcode-kit-generation
skills.search_text: nanopore-barcode-kit-generation Use when designing or expanding a DNA barcode kit for nanopore sequencing at a fixed barcode length (e.g., 24 bp) and error tolerance (e.g., 2 edit errors), or when comparing a generated kit's demultiplexing accuracy to official ONT kits. PacBio sequencing data: the article states 'no tests on PacBio data have been performed yet', so kit designs are only validated on ONT data. The goal is demultiplexing existing official ONT kit reads without generating a new kit — use the demultiplexing mode alone rather than this generation-and-benchmark skill. Barcodes of unequal length: the NP-complete formulation and probability-divergence design assume all candidate sequences have the same length. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generate error-tolerant DNA barcode kits for ONT nanopore sequencing using PRO's farthest-point sampling under probability divergence, then benchmark demultiplexing accuracy (with PRO and Guppy 6.5.7) against official ONT kits via simulated library preparation and sequencing. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
skills.summary: Generate error-tolerant DNA barcode kits for ONT nanopore sequencing using PRO's farthest-point sampling under probability divergence, then benchmark demultiplexing accuracy (with PRO and Guppy 6.5.7) against official ONT kits via simulated library preparation and sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: PacBio sequencing data: the article states 'no tests on PacBio data have been performed yet', so kit designs are only validated on ONT data. The goal is demultiplexing existing official ONT kit reads without generating a new kit — use the demultiplexing mode alone rather than this generation-and-benchmark skill. Barcodes of unequal length: the NP-complete formulation and probability-divergence design assume all candidate sequences have the same length.

skills.description: Use when validating whether submitted GenBank/NCBI assemblies (e.g. CP131573.1, CP165501.1) carry detectable Nanopore rapid-barcode artefacts from kits like SQK-RBK114-96.
skills.name: nanopore-barcode-sequence-search
skills.search_text: nanopore-barcode-sequence-search Use when validating whether submitted GenBank/NCBI assemblies (e.g. CP131573.1, CP165501.1) carry detectable Nanopore rapid-barcode artefacts from kits like SQK-RBK114-96. The input is Nanopore reads requiring demultiplexing/trimming rather than assembled reference sequences — use the Barbell annotate/filter/trim workflow instead. You need exact string matching with zero errors only; the method relies on edit-distance approximate matching with a flank error tolerance and will report imperfect matches. The barcode kit is not covered by a Barbell preset or supported_kits.txt (RNA and Twist kits are exceptions to the tested DNA kits). http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Searches public NCBI/GenBank nucleotide assemblies for residual Nanopore rapid-barcode and flank sequences using edit-distance approximate matching (Sassy) with kit presets extracted via Barbell, to document barcode contamination in submitted genomes. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Searches public NCBI/GenBank nucleotide assemblies for residual Nanopore rapid-barcode and flank sequences using edit-distance approximate matching (Sassy) with kit presets extracted via Barbell, to document barcode contamination in submitted genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is Nanopore reads requiring demultiplexing/trimming rather than assembled reference sequences — use the Barbell annotate/filter/trim workflow instead. You need exact string matching with zero errors only; the method relies on edit-distance approximate matching with a flank error tolerance and will report imperfect matches. The barcode kit is not covered by a Barbell preset or supported_kits.txt (RNA and Twist kits are exceptions to the tested DNA kits).

skills.description: Use when quantifying per-site m6A stoichiometry from ONT direct RNA reads that have wt, fully modified, and unmodified (knockout-derived) counterparts, using base-called error features rather than raw current intensity.
skills.name: nanopore-basecalling-error-feature-analysis
skills.search_text: nanopore-basecalling-error-feature-analysis Use when quantifying per-site m6A stoichiometry from ONT direct RNA reads that have wt, fully modified, and unmodified (knockout-derived) counterparts, using base-called error features rather than raw current intensity. When single-read (per-molecule) modification detection is required — the algorithm aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and cannot call modifications per read When you need to distinguish between modification types (e.g., m1A vs m6A) — the base-calling error signature does not discriminate modification identity When no matched unmodified control (e.g., ime4Δ/KO or demethylase-treated sample) exists — direct RNA base-calling is error-rich in unmodified sequences and error patterns alone are noisy http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Estimate per-site m6A modification stoichiometry from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing by regressing wild-type base-calling mismatch frequencies (extracted with EpiNano) against 100%-modified in vitro and 0%-modified ime4Δ reference endpoints, as done for yeast (median stoichiometry 12–30%). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Estimate per-site m6A modification stoichiometry from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing by regressing wild-type base-calling mismatch frequencies (extracted with EpiNano) against 100%-modified in vitro and 0%-modified ime4Δ reference endpoints, as done for yeast (median stoichiometry 12–30%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When single-read (per-molecule) modification detection is required — the algorithm aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and cannot call modifications per read When you need to distinguish between modification types (e.g., m1A vs m6A) — the base-calling error signature does not discriminate modification identity When no matched unmodified control (e.g., ime4Δ/KO or demethylase-treated sample) exists — direct RNA base-calling is error-rich in unmodified sequences and error patterns alone are noisy

skills.description: Use when the starting point is a folder of ONT POD5 files (direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA) that must be basecalled, optionally with modified bases, into a single unmapped BAM before alignment or modkit analysis.
skills.name: nanopore-basecalling-with-dorado
skills.search_text: nanopore-basecalling-with-dorado Use when the starting point is a folder of ONT POD5 files (direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA) that must be basecalled, optionally with modified bases, into a single unmapped BAM before alignment or modkit analysis. Input is already a merged unmapped BAM or mapped BAM — use the standalone kallisto, remap, or annotateRNA entry points instead of re-running basecalling Input is an existing CDNA FASTQ — use the fastq CDNA workflow, which creates an unmapped BAM without re-basecalling POD5 Reads are not Oxford Nanopore POD5 data (e.g. Illumina FASTQ or PacBio data) — Dorado is specific to ONT reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Automates the basecalling layer of Oxford Nanopore reprocessing with Dogme/Nextflow: Dorado models are downloaded, each POD5 input is basecalled into a per-file BAM, and the per-POD5 BAMs are merged into a single unmapped BAM for downstream mapping and modification calling. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Automates the basecalling layer of Oxford Nanopore reprocessing with Dogme/Nextflow: Dorado models are downloaded, each POD5 input is basecalled into a per-file BAM, and the per-POD5 BAMs are merged into a single unmapped BAM for downstream mapping and modification calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a merged unmapped BAM or mapped BAM — use the standalone kallisto, remap, or annotateRNA entry points instead of re-running basecalling Input is an existing CDNA FASTQ — use the fastq CDNA workflow, which creates an unmapped BAM without re-basecalling POD5 Reads are not Oxford Nanopore POD5 data (e.g. Illumina FASTQ or PacBio data) — Dorado is specific to ONT reads

skills.description: Use when analyzing 10x Oxford Nanopore long-read single-cell cDNA (or PacBio with an appropriate index) and reads must be aligned to a genome for downstream isoform reconstruction and gene quantification.
skills.name: nanopore-cdna-alignment-with-minimap2-splice
skills.search_text: nanopore-cdna-alignment-with-minimap2-splice Use when analyzing 10x Oxford Nanopore long-read single-cell cDNA (or PacBio with an appropriate index) and reads must be aligned to a genome for downstream isoform reconstruction and gene quantification. The input is short-read data (e.g. Cell Ranger/short-read UMI quantification), which should instead serve as the comparison baseline, not be aligned with minimap2 splice. No genome reference directory is available and only transcript-level quantification is needed — scywalker alignment is genome-based via minimap2_splice. The dataset's organelle chromosomes are not specified at reference-building time; the isoquant-based code can hang or crash on the very different organelle data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Align full-length Oxford Nanopore single-cell cDNA reads to a reference genome using minimap2 with the splice preset, the default aligner inside scywalker's end-to-end pipeline, to support isoform/gene reconstruction and per-cell quantification. Splice-aware alignment preserves exon boundaries, which is essential for IsoQuant-based transcript discovery downstream. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Align full-length Oxford Nanopore single-cell cDNA reads to a reference genome using minimap2 with the splice preset, the default aligner inside scywalker's end-to-end pipeline, to support isoform/gene reconstruction and per-cell quantification. Splice-aware alignment preserves exon boundaries, which is essential for IsoQuant-based transcript discovery downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read data (e.g. Cell Ranger/short-read UMI quantification), which should instead serve as the comparison baseline, not be aligned with minimap2 splice. No genome reference directory is available and only transcript-level quantification is needed — scywalker alignment is genome-based via minimap2_splice. The dataset's organelle chromosomes are not specified at reference-building time; the isoquant-based code can hang or crash on the very different organelle data.

skills.description: Use when FASTA consensus reads from a nanopore amplicon workflow (INC-Seq / chopSeq / nanoClust) must be error-profiled against 16S references, e.g. to test whether remaining errors are homopolymer deletions.
skills.name: nanopore-consensus-error-attribution
skills.search_text: nanopore-consensus-error-attribution Use when FASTA consensus reads from a nanopore amplicon workflow (INC-Seq / chopSeq / nanoClust) must be error-profiled against 16S references, e.g. to test whether remaining errors are homopolymer deletions. When the input is raw noisy nanopore reads rather than corrected consensus sequences (INC-Seq, chopSeq, or nanoClust output) — this skill characterizes residual consensus error, not raw-read error rates When a reference database is unavailable or the goal is fully de novo consensus accuracy assessment, since the attribution depends on blastn alignment to 16S references http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Attributes residual errors in Nanopore amplicon consensus reads (INC-Seq, chopSeq, nanoClust stages) by comparing read-to-reference blastn alignment length ratios and mapping mismatches/indels to homopolymer tracts. This distinguishes deletion-dominated base-calling error from other error classes in ONT MinION data. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Attributes residual errors in Nanopore amplicon consensus reads (INC-Seq, chopSeq, nanoClust stages) by comparing read-to-reference blastn alignment length ratios and mapping mismatches/indels to homopolymer tracts. This distinguishes deletion-dominated base-calling error from other error classes in ONT MinION data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw noisy nanopore reads rather than corrected consensus sequences (INC-Seq, chopSeq, or nanoClust output) — this skill characterizes residual consensus error, not raw-read error rates When a reference database is unavailable or the goal is fully de novo consensus accuracy assessment, since the attribution depends on blastn alignment to 16S references

skills.description: Use when a nanopore virus-surveillance workflow has already reconstructed viral consensus genomes (reference-based or hybrid assembly) and you need to identify structural variants relative to the reference as an optional downstream analysis.
skills.name: nanopore-consensus-genome-variant-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-consensus-genome-variant-calling Use when a nanopore virus-surveillance workflow has already reconstructed viral consensus genomes (reference-based or hybrid assembly) and you need to identify structural variants relative to the reference as an optional downstream analysis. Input is raw FASTQ/FAST5/POD5 nanopore data that has not yet been preprocessed, classified, or assembled into a consensus genome — variant calling in this skill operates on consensus sequences, not reads. You only need taxonomic classification or phylogenetic tree inference (maximum likelihood / Bayesian) without structural-variant analysis. The workflow is run with the structural-variant step disabled (variant calling is optional; disabling steps leaves samples only preprocessed and trimmed). http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 An optional downstream step of the VirDetector nanopore-sequencing pipeline in which structural variants are detected in the assembled viral genomes: Sniffles2 is applied to the consensus genome sequence reconstructed for each sample and the detected variants are written to a per-sample variant record (VCF-style) file. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: An optional downstream step of the VirDetector nanopore-sequencing pipeline in which structural variants are detected in the assembled viral genomes: Sniffles2 is applied to the consensus genome sequence reconstructed for each sample and the detected variants are written to a per-sample variant record (VCF-style) file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ/FAST5/POD5 nanopore data that has not yet been preprocessed, classified, or assembled into a consensus genome — variant calling in this skill operates on consensus sequences, not reads. You only need taxonomic classification or phylogenetic tree inference (maximum likelihood / Bayesian) without structural-variant analysis. The workflow is run with the structural-variant step disabled (variant calling is optional; disabling steps leaves samples only preprocessed and trimmed).

skills.description: Use when reconstructing a consensus genome for a known virus from untargeted nanopore reads after a reference genome has been identified, and a polished reference-guided consensus (not de novo contigs) is the deliverable.
skills.name: nanopore-consensus-polishing
skills.search_text: nanopore-consensus-polishing Use when reconstructing a consensus genome for a known virus from untargeted nanopore reads after a reference genome has been identified, and a polished reference-guided consensus (not de novo contigs) is the deliverable. The goal is a finished genome for a large DNA virus with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) — ViMOP output should then only be regarded as a draft genome No fitting reference genome can be identified in the virus reference database, since this skill is reference-guided consensus assembly, not de novo assembly Reads are not Oxford Nanopore data (e.g. Illumina), as the polishing path depends on nanopore-specific Medaka models http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 ViMOP's reference-guided consensus assembly: after a BLAST-selected reference is chosen, nanopore reads are mapped, Sniffles2 large indels are merged into the reference with BCFtools consensus, and Medaka (or a Samtools fallback with depth ≥20 and ≥70% base proportion, N-masking below-threshold positions) produces the final consensus FASTA. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: ViMOP's reference-guided consensus assembly: after a BLAST-selected reference is chosen, nanopore reads are mapped, Sniffles2 large indels are merged into the reference with BCFtools consensus, and Medaka (or a Samtools fallback with depth ≥20 and ≥70% base proportion, N-masking below-threshold positions) produces the final consensus FASTA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a finished genome for a large DNA virus with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) — ViMOP output should then only be regarded as a draft genome No fitting reference genome can be identified in the virus reference database, since this skill is reference-guided consensus assembly, not de novo assembly Reads are not Oxford Nanopore data (e.g. Illumina), as the polishing path depends on nanopore-specific Medaka models

skills.description: Use when handling INC-Seq consensus reads from ONT MinION amplicon sequencing (2D or 1D2 chemistry) that require fragmentation and orientation correction with chopSeq before downstream analysis.
skills.name: nanopore-consensus-read-processing
skills.search_text: nanopore-consensus-read-processing Use when handling INC-Seq consensus reads from ONT MinION amplicon sequencing (2D or 1D2 chemistry) that require fragmentation and orientation correction with chopSeq before downstream analysis. Input is raw, noisy nanopore reads rather than INC-Seq consensus reads — those require the upstream clustering/consensus-calling steps (e.g. nanoClust) of NanoAmpli-Seq first. Reads are from short-read platforms such as Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM, whose short read lengths are the limitation this nanopore workflow addresses. The goal is reference-based mapping of noisy reads; the paper's rationale is to avoid reference dependence because incorrect mapping is likely due to high raw nanopore read error rates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Post-processing of INC-Seq consensus reads produced on the ONT MinION platform, using chopSeq to fragment and orientation-correct consensus reads before downstream analyses such as tandem repeat characterization of 2D and 1D2 nanopore runs. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Post-processing of INC-Seq consensus reads produced on the ONT MinION platform, using chopSeq to fragment and orientation-correct consensus reads before downstream analyses such as tandem repeat characterization of 2D and 1D2 nanopore runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, noisy nanopore reads rather than INC-Seq consensus reads — those require the upstream clustering/consensus-calling steps (e.g. nanoClust) of NanoAmpli-Seq first. Reads are from short-read platforms such as Illumina MiSeq or Ion Torrent PGM, whose short read lengths are the limitation this nanopore workflow addresses. The goal is reference-based mapping of noisy reads; the paper's rationale is to avoid reference dependence because incorrect mapping is likely due to high raw nanopore read error rates.

skills.description: Use when nanopore FAST5/FASTQ data needs per-read CpG (5mC) methylation calls, especially alongside 6mA detection, or when comparing nanoHiMe vs nanopolish vs Megalodon accuracy.
skills.name: nanopore-cpg-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-cpg-methylation-calling Use when nanopore FAST5/FASTQ data needs per-read CpG (5mC) methylation calls, especially alongside 6mA detection, or when comparing nanoHiMe vs nanopolish vs Megalodon accuracy. When the goal is calling 6mA-containing regions genome-wide — use nanoHiMe 6mA mode instead, since genome-wide mCG-style calls will not localize modified-adenine windows When reads are not aligned to k-mer-level events (no nanopolish eventalign file) — nanoHiMe requires event-level alignments, not just FASTQ When DNA carries modifications outside the trained model space (e.g. 5-hmC, 5-fC, 4-mC, GpC methylation) — no unified calling model exists yet http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call CpG methylation from nanopore reads using nanoHiMe's hidden Markov model on nanopolish eventalign files, benchmarking against nanopolish and Megalodon with AUCs against enzymatic-treatment ground truth and Pearson correlations with WGBS. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Call CpG methylation from nanopore reads using nanoHiMe's hidden Markov model on nanopolish eventalign files, benchmarking against nanopolish and Megalodon with AUCs against enzymatic-treatment ground truth and Pearson correlations with WGBS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is calling 6mA-containing regions genome-wide — use nanoHiMe 6mA mode instead, since genome-wide mCG-style calls will not localize modified-adenine windows When reads are not aligned to k-mer-level events (no nanopolish eventalign file) — nanoHiMe requires event-level alignments, not just FASTQ When DNA carries modifications outside the trained model space (e.g. 5-hmC, 5-fC, 4-mC, GpC methylation) — no unified calling model exists yet

skills.search_text: nanopore-direct-rna-m6a-model-training Use when you have RedNano-extracted read-level features (k_signals_rect, qual, mis, ins, dele columns) from modified and unmodified Nanopore DRS samples and need to train a species- or dataset-specific m6A detection model instead of using a pre-trained one. skills.description: Use when input is Oxford Nanopore direct-RNA FASTQ reads plus a transcriptome FASTA and the goal is to produce BAM alignments that preserve secondary mappings for EM-based isoform quantification (NanoCount, Salmon, LIQA).
skills.name: nanopore-drs-transcriptome-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-drs-transcriptome-alignment Use when input is Oxford Nanopore direct-RNA FASTQ reads plus a transcriptome FASTA and the goal is to produce BAM alignments that preserve secondary mappings for EM-based isoform quantification (NanoCount, Salmon, LIQA). The goal is spliced whole-genome alignment of DRS reads rather than transcript-level assignment — minimap2's splice preset (-ax splice -uf -k14 for noisy Nanopore direct RNA) would be the appropriate mode instead of map-ont against a transcriptome. Downstream quantification needs only a single best alignment per read — retaining -N secondary mappings and -p 0 would inflate the alignment file unnecessarily. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) reads to a reference transcriptome with minimap2 (map-ont preset), deliberately retaining multiple secondary mappings (-p 0, -N 10 or higher) and converting to BAM with samtools, because downstream EM-based transcript quantification (e.g. NanoCount) needs the full multi-mapping compatibility set per read. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1129
skills.summary: Aligns Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) reads to a reference transcriptome with minimap2 (map-ont preset), deliberately retaining multiple secondary mappings (-p 0, -N 10 or higher) and converting to BAM with samtools, because downstream EM-based transcript quantification (e.g. NanoCount) needs the full multi-mapping compatibility set per read.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spliced whole-genome alignment of DRS reads rather than transcript-level assignment — minimap2's splice preset (-ax splice -uf -k14 for noisy Nanopore direct RNA) would be the appropriate mode instead of map-ont against a transcriptome. Downstream quantification needs only a single best alignment per read — retaining -N secondary mappings and -p 0 would inflate the alignment file unnecessarily.

Input reads are already filtered FASTQ (post-FastP output) — re-filtering would discard additional reads and distort per-batch QC totals The goal is taxonomic classification or BLAST validation itself — those are handled by the separate Kraken2 classification and BLAST validation steps that run after this filtering stage Data are not Oxford Nanopore FASTQ batches (e.g. short-read or non-FASTQ formats) — the nanometanf pipeline is specific to Oxford Nanopore long-read data http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs the initial read-filtering stage of the Nanometa Live workflow, in which each newly generated nanopore FASTQ batch is passed through FastP (the 'Quality control (FASTP)' process of the nanometanf Nextflow pipeline) before downstream Kraken2 taxonomic classification. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae108

skills.description: Use when assembling a large (hundreds of Mbp to multi-Gbp) eukaryotic genome from uncorrected nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads on modest hardware, and existing de novo assemblers such as Canu are computationally prohibitive (tens of thousands of CPU hours).
skills.name: nanopore-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: nanopore-genome-assembly Use when assembling a large (hundreds of Mbp to multi-Gbp) eukaryotic genome from uncorrected nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads on modest hardware, and existing de novo assemblers such as Canu are computationally prohibitive (tens of thousands of CPU hours). The task is polishing or correcting an existing long-read assembly with Illumina data — use the separate Racon/Pilon polishing step instead (TULIP deliberately skips per-read correction). You require a single monolithic de novo assembler run on small genomes where Canu-style assembly is affordable — TULIP's value is in chunking very large genomes. Seeds contain highly repetitive sequence or violate the strict requirements (nonzero unique numeric identifiers, exactly equal lengths), which slows graph untangling and can invalidate the layout. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 De novo assembly of large eukaryotic genomes from uncorrected Oxford Nanopore long reads using TULIP (The Uncorrected Long-read Integration Process), demonstrated by assembling the 860 Mbp European eel (Anguilla anguilla) genome in two days on a single CPU. TULIP splits large assembly problems into manageable subsets of long reads anchored on sparse short 'seed' alignments, replacing quadratic scaling with nearly linear behaviour. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: De novo assembly of large eukaryotic genomes from uncorrected Oxford Nanopore long reads using TULIP (The Uncorrected Long-read Integration Process), demonstrated by assembling the 860 Mbp European eel (Anguilla anguilla) genome in two days on a single CPU. TULIP splits large assembly problems into manageable subsets of long reads anchored on sparse short 'seed' alignments, replacing quadratic scaling with nearly linear behaviour.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is polishing or correcting an existing long-read assembly with Illumina data — use the separate Racon/Pilon polishing step instead (TULIP deliberately skips per-read correction). You require a single monolithic de novo assembler run on small genomes where Canu-style assembly is affordable — TULIP's value is in chunking very large genomes. Seeds contain highly repetitive sequence or violate the strict requirements (nonzero unique numeric identifiers, exactly equal lengths), which slows graph untangling and can invalidate the layout.

skills.description: Use when demultiplexed MinION long-amplicon (e.g. rDNA) reads must be converted into a per-specimen consensus sequence of sufficient accuracy to compare against an Illumina short-read reference, with a minimum per-position coverage cutoff.
skills.name: nanopore-long-amplicon-consensus-assembly
skills.search_text: nanopore-long-amplicon-consensus-assembly Use when demultiplexed MinION long-amplicon (e.g. rDNA) reads must be converted into a per-specimen consensus sequence of sufficient accuracy to compare against an Illumina short-read reference, with a minimum per-position coverage cutoff. Input is already assembled consensus sequences — this skill covers read-level demultiplexing, assembly, and polishing, not consensus-vs-consensus comparison alone Reads are Illumina short reads; the workflow is built around Nanopore long rDNA amplicons with dual barcode indexes and primer trimming A specimen lacks ≥30 reads per position in the alignment; the coverage threshold cannot be enforced and the consensus would not be validated http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assembles accurate per-specimen consensus sequences from dual-indexed Nanopore long rDNA amplicon reads by demultiplexing with MiniBar, building a consensus with a minimum 30-reads-per-position coverage threshold, and polishing with Racon so the Nanopore consensus can be benchmarked against Illumina-based consensus sequences. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Assembles accurate per-specimen consensus sequences from dual-indexed Nanopore long rDNA amplicon reads by demultiplexing with MiniBar, building a consensus with a minimum 30-reads-per-position coverage threshold, and polishing with Racon so the Nanopore consensus can be benchmarked against Illumina-based consensus sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled consensus sequences — this skill covers read-level demultiplexing, assembly, and polishing, not consensus-vs-consensus comparison alone Reads are Illumina short reads; the workflow is built around Nanopore long rDNA amplicons with dual barcode indexes and primer trimming A specimen lacks ≥30 reads per position in the alignment; the coverage threshold cannot be enforced and the consensus would not be validated

skills.description: Use when long nanopore FASTQ reads from targeted (e.g. FUDGE-enriched) sequencing must be aligned to a human reference to support downstream SV/fusion calling with NanoSV, Sniffles or NanoFG.
skills.name: nanopore-long-read-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-long-read-alignment Use when long nanopore FASTQ reads from targeted (e.g. FUDGE-enriched) sequencing must be aligned to a human reference to support downstream SV/fusion calling with NanoSV, Sniffles or NanoFG. Input consists of short Illumina paired-end reads — minimap2's 'sr' preset exists, but the NanoFG fusion-detection workflow requires long nanopore reads to span fusion breakpoints DNA is fragmented (e.g. FFPE material), where the article notes short read lengths will fail to comprehensively identify fusion genes The analysis goal is de novo genome assembly rather than reference-guided variant/fusion calling http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps enriched Oxford Nanopore long reads against the GRCh37 human reference genome with minimap2 (v2.6) and indexes/sorts the resulting BAM with Samtools, producing the alignment file that NanoSV/Sniffles screen for structural variants and NanoFG refines into fusion-gene calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: Maps enriched Oxford Nanopore long reads against the GRCh37 human reference genome with minimap2 (v2.6) and indexes/sorts the resulting BAM with Samtools, producing the alignment file that NanoSV/Sniffles screen for structural variants and NanoFG refines into fusion-gene calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of short Illumina paired-end reads — minimap2's 'sr' preset exists, but the NanoFG fusion-detection workflow requires long nanopore reads to span fusion breakpoints DNA is fragmented (e.g. FFPE material), where the article notes short read lengths will fail to comprehensively identify fusion genes The analysis goal is de novo genome assembly rather than reference-guided variant/fusion calling

skills.description: Use when the input is Oxford Nanopore long-read FASTQ data (genomic, metagenomic, or plasmid) and a quick de novo assembly with error-corrected consensus is needed without command-line skills.
skills.name: nanopore-long-read-assembly
skills.search_text: nanopore-long-read-assembly Use when the input is Oxford Nanopore long-read FASTQ data (genomic, metagenomic, or plasmid) and a quick de novo assembly with error-corrected consensus is needed without command-line skills. Input consists of short reads (150–300 bp), which the article notes complicate assembly of repetitive regions — use a short-read workflow instead Input is already an assembled set of contigs requiring only classification (e.g. only PlasFlow/Krona steps are needed) The platform is Pacific Biosciences data and validated performance is required — the article states PacBio tools 'should also work' but were not intensively tested for ONT alternatives http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Rapid de novo assembly of Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing data within the Galaxy (NanoGalaxy) environment, chaining minimap2 overlap detection, miniasm string-graph assembly, and Racon polishing. It packages best-practice long-read tools behind Galaxy's GUI so non-bioinformaticians can assemble genomic, metagenomic, or plasmid reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: Rapid de novo assembly of Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing data within the Galaxy (NanoGalaxy) environment, chaining minimap2 overlap detection, miniasm string-graph assembly, and Racon polishing. It packages best-practice long-read tools behind Galaxy's GUI so non-bioinformaticians can assemble genomic, metagenomic, or plasmid reads.
