skills.name: nanopore-long-read-locus-subsetting
skills.search_text: nanopore-long-read-locus-subsetting Use when you need locus-restricted RNA editing or SNV rates from ScNaUmi-seq error-corrected consensus molecules, e.g. measuring A-to-I editing at two linked sites like Gria2 Q/R and R/G and testing whether editing at one site influences the other. Input is raw Nanopore reads rather than UMI-corrected consensus molecules (molecules.GE.tags.bam); per-read base errors will swamp true editing signals The variant of interest spans transcripts across different chromosomes, since locus subsetting by a single samtools region assumes one contiguous range http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Extract error-corrected molecule BAM records (Sicelore step 4.b.5 consensus output) at a defined genomic locus with samtools, then run Sicelore SNPMatrix to compute per-site and joint two-site editing/SNV fractions from molecule counts. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Extract error-corrected molecule BAM records (Sicelore step 4.b.5 consensus output) at a defined genomic locus with samtools, then run Sicelore SNPMatrix to compute per-site and joint two-site editing/SNV fractions from molecule counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Nanopore reads rather than UMI-corrected consensus molecules (molecules.GE.tags.bam); per-read base errors will swamp true editing signals The variant of interest spans transcripts across different chromosomes, since locus subsetting by a single samtools region assumes one contiguous range

skills.description: Use when analyzing EMseq/nanoEM base-converted Oxford Nanopore long reads to quantify per-CpG methylation genome-wide, or when reproducing methylation rates and CpG coverage versus WGBS, EMseq, and nanopolish.
skills.name: nanopore-long-read-methylation-pipeline
skills.search_text: nanopore-long-read-methylation-pipeline Use when analyzing EMseq/nanoEM base-converted Oxford Nanopore long reads to quantify per-CpG methylation genome-wide, or when reproducing methylation rates and CpG coverage versus WGBS, EMseq, and nanopolish. Input is short-read bisulfite or EMseq data (WGBS/EMseq) — use conventional short-read aligners (e.g. Trim Galore + Bismark) rather than this long-read CT/GA dual-mapping pipeline You need to distinguish 5-methylcytosine from 5-hydroxymethylcytosine on the same molecule — nanoEM cannot separate mC from hmC; use direct nanopore WGS signal calling instead You are running nanopolish methylation calling on R10.4 flowcells — nanopolish does not support R10.4 for variant/methylation calling http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A bioinformatics pipeline (nanoEM) that calls per-CpG methylation from enzymatically base-converted (C-to-T) long nanopore reads by dual CT/GA strand-conversion mapping with minimap2, best-alignment selection, and sambamba mpileup-based methylation calling. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: A bioinformatics pipeline (nanoEM) that calls per-CpG methylation from enzymatically base-converted (C-to-T) long nanopore reads by dual CT/GA strand-conversion mapping with minimap2, best-alignment selection, and sambamba mpileup-based methylation calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read bisulfite or EMseq data (WGBS/EMseq) — use conventional short-read aligners (e.g. Trim Galore + Bismark) rather than this long-read CT/GA dual-mapping pipeline You need to distinguish 5-methylcytosine from 5-hydroxymethylcytosine on the same molecule — nanoEM cannot separate mC from hmC; use direct nanopore WGS signal calling instead You are running nanopolish methylation calling on R10.4 flowcells — nanopolish does not support R10.4 for variant/methylation calling

skills.description: Use when a SPAdes short-read draft assembly needs finishing with nanopore long reads, especially when streaming MinION data in real time or when minimizing long-read coverage (e.g. ~30-fold for E. coli, ~14-fold for Kpn2146 plasmids).
skills.name: nanopore-long-read-scaffolding-realtime
skills.search_text: nanopore-long-read-scaffolding-realtime Use when a SPAdes short-read draft assembly needs finishing with nanopore long reads, especially when streaming MinION data in real time or when minimizing long-read coverage (e.g. ~30-fold for E. coli, ~14-fold for Kpn2146 plasmids). The input long reads are already error-corrected and intended for a de novo long-read assembler (e.g. Celera Assembler) rather than scaffolding a short-read draft Only short-read data are available and no nanopore long reads can be generated or streamed npScarf is unmaintained and a modern streaming assembler is required — the README directs users to npGraph as the replacement http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scaffold and complete a short-read draft assembly in real time using streaming Oxford Nanopore long reads with npScarf (jsa.np.npscarf), reporting assembly metrics during the sequencing run so the run can be terminated once sufficient quality is reached. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Scaffold and complete a short-read draft assembly in real time using streaming Oxford Nanopore long reads with npScarf (jsa.np.npscarf), reporting assembly metrics during the sequencing run so the run can be terminated once sufficient quality is reached.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input long reads are already error-corrected and intended for a de novo long-read assembler (e.g. Celera Assembler) rather than scaffolding a short-read draft Only short-read data are available and no nanopore long reads can be generated or streamed npScarf is unmaintained and a modern streaming assembler is required — the README directs users to npGraph as the replacement

skills.description: Use when ONT fastq/fast5 reads (Albacore-basecalled, R9/R9.4/R9.5) need per-read m6A probability calls at known motif or positions-file sites, using nanopolish eventalign TSVs with --scale-events and a trained model like r95_twobase_model_NN_6_m6A.pkl.
skills.name: nanopore-m6a-per-read-classification
skills.search_text: nanopore-m6a-per-read-classification Use when ONT fastq/fast5 reads (Albacore-basecalled, R9/R9.4/R9.5) need per-read m6A probability calls at known motif or positions-file sites, using nanopolish eventalign TSVs with --scale-events and a trained model like r95_twobase_model_NN_6_m6A.pkl. Data from R10.4 flowcells: nanopolish does not support R10.4 variant/methylation calling, so the eventalign-based input pipeline is unavailable Motifs where both m6A and m4C are possible (e.g. the GATCGVNY motif in S. aureus): single-molecule methods fail to distinguish methylation types Sequence contexts very dissimilar to the E. coli-trained model contexts: training biases can decrease mCaller accuracy at untrained motifs (e.g. it lost to Tombo at the untrained E. coli AAGANNNNNCTC motif, 0.71 vs 0.86 PR-AUC) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Per-read m6A classification on Oxford Nanopore data using mCaller, a scikit-learn neural network that scores deviations between measured and expected currents at adenine positions. It complements Tombo and is designed for microbial reference materials with motif-confirmed methylated/unmethylated sites. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Per-read m6A classification on Oxford Nanopore data using mCaller, a scikit-learn neural network that scores deviations between measured and expected currents at adenine positions. It complements Tombo and is designed for microbial reference materials with motif-confirmed methylated/unmethylated sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data from R10.4 flowcells: nanopolish does not support R10.4 variant/methylation calling, so the eventalign-based input pipeline is unavailable Motifs where both m6A and m4C are possible (e.g. the GATCGVNY motif in S. aureus): single-molecule methods fail to distinguish methylation types Sequence contexts very dissimilar to the E. coli-trained model contexts: training biases can decrease mCaller accuracy at untrained motifs (e.g. it lost to Tombo at the untrained E. coli AAGANNNNNCTC motif, 0.71 vs 0.86 PR-AUC)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an ARG profiler (e.g., Argo) against assembly/metaFlye+Kraken2 or binning/SemiBin2+GTDB-Tk pipelines and ground-truth ARG abundances at controlled sequencing coverages are needed.
skills.name: nanopore-metagenome-read-simulation
skills.search_text: nanopore-metagenome-read-simulation Use when benchmarking an ARG profiler (e.g., Argo) against assembly/metaFlye+Kraken2 or binning/SemiBin2+GTDB-Tk pipelines and ground-truth ARG abundances at controlled sequencing coverages are needed. When the goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — the article notes assembly- and binning-based methods may be better suited there When real, externally validated metagenomic samples are required (e.g., the 329-sample human and non-human primate fecal validation dataset) rather than simulated ground-truth data When the input is already sequenced real Nanopore data with no truth set — simulation-based benchmarking presupposes controllable coverage and known expected abundances http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Simulate Nanopore metagenomic reads with NanoSim and downsample to a graded coverage grid (1×–32×) to benchmark read-based, assembly-based, and binning-based ARG profiling methods against known ground truth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Simulate Nanopore metagenomic reads with NanoSim and downsample to a graded coverage grid (1×–32×) to benchmark read-based, assembly-based, and binning-based ARG profiling methods against known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — the article notes assembly- and binning-based methods may be better suited there When real, externally validated metagenomic samples are required (e.g., the 329-sample human and non-human primate fecal validation dataset) rather than simulated ground-truth data When the input is already sequenced real Nanopore data with no truth set — simulation-based benchmarking presupposes controllable coverage and known expected abundances

skills.description: Use when a real-time Oxford Nanopore (MinION/Flongle) metagenomic run has been classified with Kraken2 and hits to user-defined species of interest or pathogens need secondary confirmation before alerting.
skills.name: nanopore-metagenomic-classification-verification
skills.search_text: nanopore-metagenomic-classification-verification Use when a real-time Oxford Nanopore (MinION/Flongle) metagenomic run has been classified with Kraken2 and hits to user-defined species of interest or pathogens need secondary confirmation before alerting. The goal is initial taxonomic profiling of all reads, not confirmation of specific flagged species — Kraken2 classification alone is the correct step No species-of-interest watchlist is defined and no taxids have been flagged, so there is nothing to validate with BLAST Reads are short-read (Illumina) metagenomic data; the skill's pipeline and QC thresholds are calibrated for Oxford Nanopore long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Verification of Kraken2 taxonomic assignments of Oxford Nanopore metagenomic reads against a user-defined species-of-interest watchlist by extracting flagged reads and validating them with BLAST (blastn) searches against user-selected reference genomes, as implemented in the Nanometa Live / nanometanf workflow. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae108
skills.summary: Verification of Kraken2 taxonomic assignments of Oxford Nanopore metagenomic reads against a user-defined species-of-interest watchlist by extracting flagged reads and validating them with BLAST (blastn) searches against user-selected reference genomes, as implemented in the Nanometa Live / nanometanf workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is initial taxonomic profiling of all reads, not confirmation of specific flagged species — Kraken2 classification alone is the correct step No species-of-interest watchlist is defined and no taxids have been flagged, so there is nothing to validate with BLAST Reads are short-read (Illumina) metagenomic data; the skill's pipeline and QC thresholds are calibrated for Oxford Nanopore long reads

skills.description: Use when evaluating methylation-calling accuracy of a Nanopore 5mC caller against short-read bisulfite ground truth at per-read and per-site granularity, needing stratified F1 scores with explicit methylation-frequency filters.
skills.name: nanopore-methylation-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: nanopore-methylation-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating methylation-calling accuracy of a Nanopore 5mC caller against short-read bisulfite ground truth at per-read and per-site granularity, needing stratified F1 scores with explicit methylation-frequency filters. The task is to generate methylation calls rather than evaluate them — DeepMod2 detection is a separate step; this skill assumes existing per-read/per-site outputs Evaluation requires sites with intermediate 20–80% methylation — EpiQC reported poor concordance there between ONT and short-read methods, so F1 on such sites is not a reliable signal Non-5mC modifications (e.g., 5hmC) are of interest — DeepMod2 models cover only 5mCpG methylation and no 5hmC was detected in GIAB cell lines HG001-HG007 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Benchmark 5mC methylation calls from a Nanopore methylation caller (e.g., DeepMod2) against bisulfite short-read ground truth (EpiQC, GSE186383), computing per-read (~95% expected) and per-site (~99% expected) precision, recall, and F1-score on HG002-class human datasets across R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 flowcells. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Benchmark 5mC methylation calls from a Nanopore methylation caller (e.g., DeepMod2) against bisulfite short-read ground truth (EpiQC, GSE186383), computing per-read (~95% expected) and per-site (~99% expected) precision, recall, and F1-score on HG002-class human datasets across R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 flowcells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to generate methylation calls rather than evaluate them — DeepMod2 detection is a separate step; this skill assumes existing per-read/per-site outputs Evaluation requires sites with intermediate 20–80% methylation — EpiQC reported poor concordance there between ONT and short-read methods, so F1 on such sites is not a reliable signal Non-5mC modifications (e.g., 5hmC) are of interest — DeepMod2 models cover only 5mCpG methylation and no 5hmC was detected in GIAB cell lines HG001-HG007

skills.description: Use when calling 5mC methylation from ONT R10.4 POD5/BAM plant nanopore data in CpG, CHG, or CHH contexts, or when needing per-site methylation rates comparable to BS-seq across species.
skills.name: nanopore-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-methylation-calling Use when calling 5mC methylation from ONT R10.4 POD5/BAM plant nanopore data in CpG, CHG, or CHH contexts, or when needing per-site methylation rates comparable to BS-seq across species. Data are from the older R9.4 FlowCell — tools like Tombo, Megalodon, and DeepSignal-Plant developed for R9.4 cannot be directly applied to R10.4, and this skill's models are R10.4-specific The goal is CpG/CHG-only methylation profiling where Dorado's default performance is already sufficient and computational runtime is the binding constraint Input is already aggregated methylation frequency data rather than raw nanopore signal/read alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect 5-methylcytosine (5mC) modifications in plant genomes from Oxford Nanopore R10.4 sequencing data using DeepPlant (Bi-LSTM + Transformer), benchmarking against Dorado, and refine methylation calls with an adaptive score-threshold selection method before computing genome-wide methylation frequency correlations with BS-seq. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Detect 5-methylcytosine (5mC) modifications in plant genomes from Oxford Nanopore R10.4 sequencing data using DeepPlant (Bi-LSTM + Transformer), benchmarking against Dorado, and refine methylation calls with an adaptive score-threshold selection method before computing genome-wide methylation frequency correlations with BS-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from the older R9.4 FlowCell — tools like Tombo, Megalodon, and DeepSignal-Plant developed for R9.4 cannot be directly applied to R10.4, and this skill's models are R10.4-specific The goal is CpG/CHG-only methylation profiling where Dorado's default performance is already sufficient and computational runtime is the binding constraint Input is already aggregated methylation frequency data rather than raw nanopore signal/read alignments

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore fast5 files must be converted to per-read 5mC CpG calls or per-site methylation frequencies, especially to benchmark or combine tool predictions on R9.4.1 flowcell data.
skills.name: nanopore-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-methylation-calling Use when raw nanopore fast5 files must be converted to per-read 5mC CpG calls or per-site methylation frequencies, especially to benchmark or combine tool predictions on R9.4.1 flowcell data. Input is already per-read score TSVs or per-site BED files — go directly to consensus/evaluation rather than re-running callers Data are from flowcells/chemistries other than R9.4.1 (e.g. R10.4), where the cited configs, Remora model dna_r9.4.1_e8 hac 0.0.0, and trained models do not apply Production modified basecalling is the goal on current ONT hardware — Megalodon is deprecated in favor of Dorado/modkit per the tool README http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A benchmarked workflow for calling CpG 5-methylcytosine (5mC) from Oxford Nanopore fast5 files using six tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, DeepMod), producing per-read scores and per-site methylation frequencies in augmented BED format for downstream accuracy assessment. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: A benchmarked workflow for calling CpG 5-methylcytosine (5mC) from Oxford Nanopore fast5 files using six tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, DeepMod), producing per-read scores and per-site methylation frequencies in augmented BED format for downstream accuracy assessment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already per-read score TSVs or per-site BED files — go directly to consensus/evaluation rather than re-running callers Data are from flowcells/chemistries other than R9.4.1 (e.g. R10.4), where the cited configs, Remora model dna_r9.4.1_e8 hac 0.0.0, and trained models do not apply Production modified basecalling is the goal on current ONT hardware — Megalodon is deprecated in favor of Dorado/modkit per the tool README

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore FAST5 signals must be turned into balanced, denoised training samples for 5mC detection (e.g. building DeepSignal-plant training sets with CpG/CHG/CHH motifs from re-squiggled reads).
skills.name: nanopore-methylation-feature-handling
skills.search_text: nanopore-methylation-feature-handling Use when raw Nanopore FAST5 signals must be turned into balanced, denoised training samples for 5mC detection (e.g. building DeepSignal-plant training sets with CpG/CHG/CHH motifs from re-squiggled reads). Input is bisulfite sequencing data rather than native Nanopore signal — this skill builds features from raw electrical signals, not converted reads Goal is per-site methylation frequency reporting from an existing call_mods output (use call_freq instead of re-extracting and denoising features) A pretrained 5mC checkpoint already exists (e.g. model.dp2.CNN.arabnrice2-1_120m_R9.4plus_tem.bn13_sn16.both_bilstm.epoch6.ckpt) and no retraining is needed Preparation of raw Nanopore signal features for plant 5mC model training: re-squiggled signals are converted into 13-mer sequence plus 13x16 signal features per targeted cytosine, balanced per k-mer motif, and iteratively denoised by two-fold cross-prediction before training DeepSignal-plant. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Preparation of raw Nanopore signal features for plant 5mC model training: re-squiggled signals are converted into 13-mer sequence plus 13x16 signal features per targeted cytosine, balanced per k-mer motif, and iteratively denoised by two-fold cross-prediction before training DeepSignal-plant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bisulfite sequencing data rather than native Nanopore signal — this skill builds features from raw electrical signals, not converted reads Goal is per-site methylation frequency reporting from an existing call_mods output (use call_freq instead of re-extracting and denoising features) A pretrained 5mC checkpoint already exists (e.g. model.dp2.CNN.arabnrice2-1_120m_R9.4plus_tem.bn13_sn16.both_bilstm.epoch6.ckpt) and no retraining is needed

skills.description: Use when you need to de novo discover DNA methylation motifs (6mA, 5mC, 4mC) from native vs WGA nanopore signal data of a bacterium, and benchmark recovery against REBASE reference motifs.
skills.name: nanopore-methylation-motif-enrichment
skills.search_text: nanopore-methylation-motif-enrichment Use when you need to de novo discover DNA methylation motifs (6mA, 5mC, 4mC) from native vs WGA nanopore signal data of a bacterium, and benchmark recovery against REBASE reference motifs. When methylation motifs are already known and the goal is typing/fine-mapping of candidate motifs with the pretrained Nanoident model (best_model/Nanoident.pt) rather than de novo discovery When input is modBAM/bedMethyl data intended for ONT modkit pileup-style workflows instead of raw nanopore signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A de novo methylation motif enrichment workflow for bacterial nanopore data that extends nanodisco preprocessing with four additional signal features (std, time, reference-base proportion, quality score) and compares enriched motifs against REBASE references. It enables recovery of more reference motifs than nanodisco's automatic mode. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf397
skills.summary: A de novo methylation motif enrichment workflow for bacterial nanopore data that extends nanodisco preprocessing with four additional signal features (std, time, reference-base proportion, quality score) and compares enriched motifs against REBASE references. It enables recovery of more reference motifs than nanodisco's automatic mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When methylation motifs are already known and the goal is typing/fine-mapping of candidate motifs with the pretrained Nanoident model (best_model/Nanoident.pt) rather than de novo discovery When input is modBAM/bedMethyl data intended for ONT modkit pileup-style workflows instead of raw nanopore signal

skills.description: Use when assessing whether direct 97% VSEARCH clustering of full-length post-chopSeq nanopore amplicon reads gives accurate OTU richness for mock communities, or when justifying a partition-based clustering step by quantifying singleton-driven OTU inflation.
skills.name: nanopore-mock-community-diversity-analysis
skills.search_text: nanopore-mock-community-diversity-analysis Use when assessing whether direct 97% VSEARCH clustering of full-length post-chopSeq nanopore amplicon reads gives accurate OTU richness for mock communities, or when justifying a partition-based clustering step by quantifying singleton-driven OTU inflation. When the goal is accurate de novo OTU estimation itself — the article shows direct full-length clustering fails here; use the partition-based nanoClust approach instead When reads have not been fragmented and orientation-corrected with chopSeq and size-selected, since the skill is defined on post-chopSeq, size-selected full-length reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarks de novo OTU richness estimation of nanopore amplicon mock communities by directly clustering post-chopSeq, size-selected full-length reads with VSEARCH at 97% identity, quantifying how grossly OTU counts (817/1301/2122/2725 OTUs) inflate relative to theoretical mock richness and thereby motivating partition-based nanoClust. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Benchmarks de novo OTU richness estimation of nanopore amplicon mock communities by directly clustering post-chopSeq, size-selected full-length reads with VSEARCH at 97% identity, quantifying how grossly OTU counts (817/1301/2122/2725 OTUs) inflate relative to theoretical mock richness and thereby motivating partition-based nanoClust.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accurate de novo OTU estimation itself — the article shows direct full-length clustering fails here; use the partition-based nanoClust approach instead When reads have not been fragmented and orientation-corrected with chopSeq and size-selected, since the skill is defined on post-chopSeq, size-selected full-length reads

skills.description: Use when nanopore R10.4 FASTQ/BAM/POD5 data need CpG methylation calling and per-site modification rates, especially when Dorado's methylation model shows inconsistent performance across heterogeneous human or plant datasets.
skills.name: nanopore-modification-calling-with-deepbam
skills.search_text: nanopore-modification-calling-with-deepbam Use when nanopore R10.4 FASTQ/BAM/POD5 data need CpG methylation calling and per-site modification rates, especially when Dorado's methylation model shows inconsistent performance across heterogeneous human or plant datasets. Data are from older nanopore chemistries: DeepBAM targets the R10.4 flowcell, and only a small number of tools (DeepMod2, Dorado) support newer R10.4 data. Methylation types other than CpG/5mC are the target, as the model and workflows here (motif_type=CG) are built for CpG methylation detection. A pre-trained model suffices and no new training is needed — do not run extract_hc_sites/train_lstm.py unless retraining on new high-confidence bisulfite data is the goal. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 A skill for calling CpG methylation states at single-molecule resolution from Oxford Nanopore R10.4 data using DeepBAM, a deep neural network tool that outperforms Dorado in accuracy and cross-dataset robustness on human and plant datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: A skill for calling CpG methylation states at single-molecule resolution from Oxford Nanopore R10.4 data using DeepBAM, a deep neural network tool that outperforms Dorado in accuracy and cross-dataset robustness on human and plant datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from older nanopore chemistries: DeepBAM targets the R10.4 flowcell, and only a small number of tools (DeepMod2, Dorado) support newer R10.4 data. Methylation types other than CpG/5mC are the target, as the model and workflows here (motif_type=CG) are built for CpG methylation detection. A pre-trained model suffices and no new training is needed — do not run extract_hc_sites/train_lstm.py unless retraining on new high-confidence bisulfite data is the goal.

skills.description: Use when you have an aligned nanopore modBAM with MM/ML base-modification tags from direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA reads and need high-confidence per-site modification calls filtered by coverage and modification frequency.
skills.name: nanopore-modification-frequency-filtering
skills.search_text: nanopore-modification-frequency-filtering Use when you have an aligned nanopore modBAM with MM/ML base-modification tags from direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA reads and need high-confidence per-site modification calls filtered by coverage and modification frequency. The input is not a modBAM with MM/ML base-modification tags — modkit pileup cannot extract modification frequencies without these tags You need transcript isoform quantification rather than modification site detection — for RNA and cDNA, Dogme runs kallisto on an extracted FASTQ instead Coverage is uniformly below the minimum threshold (fewer than 3 reads per site) — the filter will discard nearly all sites and the output will be uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extracts per-site RNA and DNA modification counts from nanopore modBAMs using modkit, then applies the Dogme custom filter — retaining only sites with at least 3 supporting reads and a modification frequency of at least 5% — to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Extracts per-site RNA and DNA modification counts from nanopore modBAMs using modkit, then applies the Dogme custom filter — retaining only sites with at least 3 supporting reads and a modification frequency of at least 5% — to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a modBAM with MM/ML base-modification tags — modkit pileup cannot extract modification frequencies without these tags You need transcript isoform quantification rather than modification site detection — for RNA and cDNA, Dogme runs kallisto on an extracted FASTQ instead Coverage is uniformly below the minimum threshold (fewer than 3 reads per site) — the filter will discard nearly all sites and the output will be uninformative

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore fast5 single-read files must be converted into per-read or per-site CpG 5mC methylation calls, or when comparing methylation-calling tools against a WGBS/truth reference.
skills.name: nanopore-modified-basecalling
skills.search_text: nanopore-modified-basecalling Use when raw Nanopore fast5 single-read files must be converted into per-read or per-site CpG 5mC methylation calls, or when comparing methylation-calling tools against a WGBS/truth reference. Input is already per-site methylation frequency data (e.g., WGBS CpG tables) — this skill calls methylation from raw fast5 signal, not from bisulfite or pre-aggregated data. Running times without GPU support are prohibitive — combining multiple tools (e.g., Megalodon plus DeepMod) may be impractical for routine analyses, per the discussion. Targeting RNA modifications or non-CpG (e.g., 6mA) contexts without adapting the tool configs — the pipelines here target 5-methylcytosine at CG dinucleotides specifically. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Detect 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites from Oxford Nanopore fast5 reads using the six benchmarked methylation-calling tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, DeepMod) orchestrated via METEORE Snakemake pipelines, and optionally combine their per-read predictions into a higher-accuracy METEORE consensus. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Detect 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites from Oxford Nanopore fast5 reads using the six benchmarked methylation-calling tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, DeepMod) orchestrated via METEORE Snakemake pipelines, and optionally combine their per-read predictions into a higher-accuracy METEORE consensus.

skills.description: Use when you have native RNA Nanopore reads from a subcellular fraction (e.g. chromatin, nucleoplasm, cytoplasm) and need per-read premature vs. mature labels to estimate processing-state fractions.
skills.name: nanopore-native-rna-read-classification
skills.search_text: nanopore-native-rna-read-classification Use when you have native RNA Nanopore reads from a subcellular fraction (e.g. chromatin, nucleoplasm, cytoplasm) and need per-read premature vs. mature labels to estimate processing-state fractions. Reads come from PCR-cDNA or amplified Nanopore libraries rather than native RNA sequencing — the modification-probability signal the classifier thresholds on is generated by the native-RNA chemistry The goal is to quantify synthesis/processing/degradation kinetic rates rather than to classify individual reads — use the nano-ID model fitting (nanoIDMain.R) instead Input reads are already labeled by metabolic-labeling ground truth (4sU/s4U labeling status known), so classification is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Classify individual native Nanopore dRNA-seq reads as premature or mature using Nanodynamo's fractionsReadsClassification-style thresholding of nano-ID modification-probability scores against labeled/unlabeled training distributions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Classify individual native Nanopore dRNA-seq reads as premature or mature using Nanodynamo's fractionsReadsClassification-style thresholding of nano-ID modification-probability scores against labeled/unlabeled training distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads come from PCR-cDNA or amplified Nanopore libraries rather than native RNA sequencing — the modification-probability signal the classifier thresholds on is generated by the native-RNA chemistry The goal is to quantify synthesis/processing/degradation kinetic rates rather than to classify individual reads — use the nano-ID model fitting (nanoIDMain.R) instead Input reads are already labeled by metabolic-labeling ground truth (4sU/s4U labeling status known), so classification is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you have CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read probability distributions grouped by transcript site and need site-level m6A/m5C modification probability and stoichiometry in a single condition without a knock-out/control sample.

skills.search_text: nanopore-probability-distribution-modeling Use when you have CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read probability distributions grouped by transcript site and need site-level m6A/m5C modification probability and stoichiometry in a single condition without a knock-out/control sample. When the goal is single-read (single-molecule) modification calls rather than transcript-site-level prediction — that is CHEUI-solo Model 1's role When detecting differential methylation between two conditions — use CHEUI-diff instead When the signal variability between modified and non-modified reads is expected to be comparable to variation among non-modified reads (e.g. densely modified rRNA with signal interference at distances <5 nt), site-level accuracy will be limited http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Second-stage modeling in CHEUI that classifies transcript-site methylation (m6A, m5C) by feeding a CNN binary classifier with the per-site distribution of Model 1 per-read modification probabilities from nanopore direct RNA sequencing, yielding site-level probabilities, stoichiometry, and controlled false-positive rates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Second-stage modeling in CHEUI that classifies transcript-site methylation (m6A, m5C) by feeding a CNN binary classifier with the per-site distribution of Model 1 per-read modification probabilities from nanopore direct RNA sequencing, yielding site-level probabilities, stoichiometry, and controlled false-positive rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is single-read (single-molecule) modification calls rather than transcript-site-level prediction — that is CHEUI-solo Model 1's role When detecting differential methylation between two conditions — use CHEUI-diff instead When the signal variability between modified and non-modified reads is expected to be comparable to variation among non-modified reads (e.g. densely modified rRNA with signal interference at distances <5 nt), site-level accuracy will be limited

skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-data-file-parsing Use when you need to enumerate every read stored in a POD5 file and extract each read's read_id, e.g. to build a read inventory, feed a filter list, or verify the number of reads a viewer reports. The input is already a read-ID text list rather than a POD5 file — in that case pod5Viewer's `File > Filter reads...` window can load IDs directly. The input is not POD5 format (e.g. FAST5 or basecalled FASTQ), which this pod5-based parsing path does not address. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parses nanopore POD5 raw signal files to enumerate all contained reads and expose their read IDs, mirroring how pod5Viewer lists files and reads in its navigator panel. skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-alignment Use when performing signal-domain mapping of raw nanopore reads (BLOW5/FAST5) against a reference FASTA for selective sequencing (Read Until) or when benchmarking sDTW alignment throughput on CPU vs FPGA hardware. Input is already basecalled sequence (FASTQ) intended for sequence-domain aligners such as Minimap2 No FPGA/MPSoC hardware is available and real-time Read Until latency is required — the CPU-only sigfish-cpu path (~12.52 reads/s Python, ~162 reads/s optimized C on a 10-core desktop) may be too slow Signal values are scaled above 128 in fixed-point mode, where sDTW data overflow degrades mapping accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Maps ONT nanopore raw signal (squiggles) directly to a reference genome using subsequence DTW (sDTW), bypassing basecalling, optionally accelerated by the HARU FPGA accelerator on a Xilinx Kria KV260 MPSoC for real-time Read Until. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore fast5 files must be translated into basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) with a deep learning basecaller, either with a pretrained model (DNA_default/RNA_default) or a custom-trained model, and accuracy should rival Albacore v2.0.1.
skills.name: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling
skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling Use when raw nanopore fast5 files must be translated into basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) with a deep learning basecaller, either with a pretrained model (DNA_default/RNA_default) or a custom-trained model, and accuracy should rival Albacore v2.0.1. The input is already basecalled (FASTQ/FASTA) reads — alignment or assembly tools, not a basecaller, are needed. Segregated-event or k-mer-segmentation-based basecallers (nanonet, Albacore pre-v2.0.1, DeepNano, BasecRAWller) are required for legacy two-stage pipeline compatibility. Only a CPU is available and large-scale throughput is required — Chiron runs at only ~21 bp/s greedy on CPU vs 1652 bp/s on a K80 GPU, and is substantially more computationally expensive than Albacore. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 End-to-end basecalling of Oxford Nanopore raw signal (fast5) directly into nucleotide sequence using Chiron's CNN+RNN+CTC deep learning architecture, bypassing the error-prone segmentation step used by prior two-stage basecallers. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: End-to-end basecalling of Oxford Nanopore raw signal (fast5) directly into nucleotide sequence using Chiron's CNN+RNN+CTC deep learning architecture, bypassing the error-prone segmentation step used by prior two-stage basecallers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already basecalled (FASTQ/FASTA) reads — alignment or assembly tools, not a basecaller, are needed. Segregated-event or k-mer-segmentation-based basecallers (nanonet, Albacore pre-v2.0.1, DeepNano, BasecRAWller) are required for legacy two-stage pipeline compatibility. Only a CPU is available and large-scale throughput is required — Chiron runs at only ~21 bp/s greedy on CPU vs 1652 bp/s on a K80 GPU, and is substantially more computationally expensive than Albacore.

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore signal reads (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 BLOW5 from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7314838) must be converted into per-read event sequences—event detection, prefix trimming, z-score normalization, and scaling—before squiggle mapping or sDTW-based Read Until on R9.4 chemistry.
skills.name: nanopore-raw-signal-event-detection
skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-event-detection Use when raw nanopore signal reads (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 BLOW5 from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7314838) must be converted into per-read event sequences—event detection, prefix trimming, z-score normalization, and scaling—before squiggle mapping or sDTW-based Read Until on R9.4 chemistry. Reads are already basecalled and the pipeline operates in the base domain (base-domain Read Until uses Minimap2-style mapping, not signal event detection). The nanopore chemistry is not R9.4 — the ~250-events-per-read budget and R9.4 pore model from RUscripts-R9 would not apply. Input is a FASTA/FASTQ reference or base sequence rather than raw signal reads (BLOW5); event detection requires the raw squiggle. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Adaptive event detection and preprocessing of raw ONT nanopore signal reads (BLOW5) into ~250-event normalized, fixed-point arrays ready for sDTW squiggle alignment in the HARU Read Until pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Adaptive event detection and preprocessing of raw ONT nanopore signal reads (BLOW5) into ~250-event normalized, fixed-point arrays ready for sDTW squiggle alignment in the HARU Read Until pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already basecalled and the pipeline operates in the base domain (base-domain Read Until uses Minimap2-style mapping, not signal event detection). The nanopore chemistry is not R9.4 — the ~250-events-per-read budget and R9.4 pore model from RUscripts-R9 would not apply. Input is a FASTA/FASTQ reference or base sequence rather than raw signal reads (BLOW5); event detection requires the raw squiggle.

skills.description: Use when resquiggled Nanopore DRS FAST5 signals and basecall alignments are available and per-read k-mer/signal/error features must be encoded and pooled into site-level m6A probabilities.
skills.name: nanopore-raw-signal-kmer-feature-encoding
skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-kmer-feature-encoding Use when resquiggled Nanopore DRS FAST5 signals and basecall alignments are available and per-read k-mer/signal/error features must be encoded and pooled into site-level m6A probabilities. Input is already an aggregated site-level file (test.features.sort.aggre.tsv); rerunning extraction or read-level feature sorting is redundant Only basecalled FASTQ/sequence data are available without raw FAST5 signals or quality/error features — RedNano's dual-branch design requires both k_signals_rect and qual/mis/ins/dele features Target sites have fewer than 20 aligned reads, since the site-level aggregation workflow filters them out with the $4>=20 awk criterion Extracts combined per-read features for RedNano m6A detection from Nanopore direct RNA sequencing: a 5-mer sequence channel, a 65-sample rectified raw-current signal window, and basecalling-error features (qual, mis, ins, dele), then feeds them into dual-ResNet encoders with a sigmoid read-level head. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae375
skills.summary: Extracts combined per-read features for RedNano m6A detection from Nanopore direct RNA sequencing: a 5-mer sequence channel, a 65-sample rectified raw-current signal window, and basecalling-error features (qual, mis, ins, dele), then feeds them into dual-ResNet encoders with a sigmoid read-level head.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated site-level file (test.features.sort.aggre.tsv); rerunning extraction or read-level feature sorting is redundant Only basecalled FASTQ/sequence data are available without raw FAST5 signals or quality/error features — RedNano's dual-branch design requires both k_signals_rect and qual/mis/ins/dele features Target sites have fewer than 20 aligned reads, since the site-level aggregation workflow filters them out with the $4>=20 awk criterion

skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-resquiggling Use when preparing Nanopore DRS FAST5 reads for RedNano feature extraction: after guppy basecalling (--fast5_out) and before extracting k-mer raw signals, the signals must be resquiggled against a reference transcript FASTA. skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a genome reference FASTA is available and no transcriptome FASTA can be built — tombo resquiggle requires the reference gene/transcript fasta, not a genome file The input is already a RedNano feature table (chrom/pos/k_mer/k_signals_rect/qual/mis/ins/dele rows) — resquiggling is upstream of feature extraction Working with Illumina or other non-nanopore short-read data — resquiggling only applies to Nanopore raw signal FAST5 files

skills.description: Use when aligning Oxford Nanopore MinION 1d/2d reads (or PacBio reads) to a reference genome with high sensitivity despite high error rates, or when downstream SV/SNV calling requires gapped alignments that span 100 bp–4 kbp insertion/deletion events directly.
skills.name: nanopore-read-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-alignment Use when aligning Oxford Nanopore MinION 1d/2d reads (or PacBio reads) to a reference genome with high sensitivity despite high error rates, or when downstream SV/SNV calling requires gapped alignments that span 100 bp–4 kbp insertion/deletion events directly. Input reads are short Illumina reads on a small genome — the paper's advantage targets long, error-prone reads; short-read mappers may suffice. Alignment of RNA-seq spliced reads is required and the experimental spliced-alignment mode is not yet stable — the paper notes this mode is 'under way'. Reference is a very large genome (e.g. human) on a memory-limited machine — GraphMap's hash index needs ~14x reference size (~42 GB peak for human) and the FM-index reduction was 'currently under implementation'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Align long, error-prone Oxford Nanopore MinION reads to a reference using GraphMap, a mapper built on gapped spaced seeds, graph-based seed processing, and LCSk anchor chaining that achieves >95% precision and 10–80% higher mapping sensitivity than BWA-MEM, LAST, BLASR, and DALIGNER on nanopore data. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Align long, error-prone Oxford Nanopore MinION reads to a reference using GraphMap, a mapper built on gapped spaced seeds, graph-based seed processing, and LCSk anchor chaining that achieves >95% precision and 10–80% higher mapping sensitivity than BWA-MEM, LAST, BLASR, and DALIGNER on nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads on a small genome — the paper's advantage targets long, error-prone reads; short-read mappers may suffice. Alignment of RNA-seq spliced reads is required and the experimental spliced-alignment mode is not yet stable — the paper notes this mode is 'under way'. Reference is a very large genome (e.g. human) on a memory-limited machine — GraphMap's hash index needs ~14x reference size (~42 GB peak for human) and the FM-index reduction was 'currently under implementation'.

skills.search_text: nanopore-read-alignment-and-preprocessing Use when raw ONT reads must be converted into methylation-annotated primary-alignment BAMs (MM/ML tags) plus SNV-phased, haplotagged BAM/VCF inputs for methylation-based phasing of ~30X human autosomes. The target is sex chromosomes (X/Y) — MethPhaser cannot improve phasing there because random X inactivation in females yields an inconsistent haplotype pattern Coverage is well below ~30X — HapCUT2 and WhatsHap only work reasonably above that coverage, so the haplotagged input would be unreliable The reads carry no base-modification information (no MM/ML tags), so methylation-based read phasing cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Turns raw ~30X Oxford Nanopore reads into the methylation-annotated, primary-only, haplotagged inputs MethPhaser requires: Dorado/Bonito/Guppy basecalling with methylation, minimap2 v2.24 alignment preserving MM/ML tags, primary-alignment filtering, Clair3 variant calling with AF > 0.25 filtering in GIAB high-confidence regions, HapCUT2 SNV phasing, and WhatsHap haplotagging. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Turns raw ~30X Oxford Nanopore reads into the methylation-annotated, primary-only, haplotagged inputs MethPhaser requires: Dorado/Bonito/Guppy basecalling with methylation, minimap2 v2.24 alignment preserving MM/ML tags, primary-alignment filtering, Clair3 variant calling with AF > 0.25 filtering in GIAB high-confidence regions, HapCUT2 SNV phasing, and WhatsHap haplotagging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target is sex chromosomes (X/Y) — MethPhaser cannot improve phasing there because random X inactivation in females yields an inconsistent haplotype pattern Coverage is well below ~30X — HapCUT2 and WhatsHap only work reasonably above that coverage, so the haplotagged input would be unreliable The reads carry no base-modification information (no MM/ML tags), so methylation-based read phasing cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when Dorado sup-basecalled ONT reads (kit v14, R10.4.1) from samples such as HG002/HG003/HG004 must be placed on GRCh38 as sorted, indexed BAMs before variant calling.
skills.name: nanopore-read-alignment-to-grch38
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-alignment-to-grch38 Use when Dorado sup-basecalled ONT reads (kit v14, R10.4.1) from samples such as HG002/HG003/HG004 must be placed on GRCh38 as sorted, indexed BAMs before variant calling. Input reads are short reads (Illumina/PacBio) — the alignment strategy and downstream callers (miniSNV, Longshot) are optimized for ONT long-read error profiles The sample is the kit v12 HG002 Guppy-basecalled dataset (k12-data) — that benchmark uses a different chemistry and basecaller and separate evaluation The goal is variant calling itself rather than producing the aligned BAM input — use the miniSNV/Clair3/Longshot calling skill instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps ONT (kit v14, R10.4.1, Dorado sup-basecalled) nanopore reads onto the GRCh38 reference (GCA_000001405.15) to produce sorted, samtools-indexed BAM files that serve as the input for SNV callers such as miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot in the GIAB Ashkenazi trio benchmark. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: Maps ONT (kit v14, R10.4.1, Dorado sup-basecalled) nanopore reads onto the GRCh38 reference (GCA_000001405.15) to produce sorted, samtools-indexed BAM files that serve as the input for SNV callers such as miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot in the GIAB Ashkenazi trio benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short reads (Illumina/PacBio) — the alignment strategy and downstream callers (miniSNV, Longshot) are optimized for ONT long-read error profiles The sample is the kit v12 HG002 Guppy-basecalled dataset (k12-data) — that benchmark uses a different chemistry and basecaller and separate evaluation The goal is variant calling itself rather than producing the aligned BAM input — use the miniSNV/Clair3/Longshot calling skill instead

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore PASS reads (e.g. PCR-amplified or M.SssI-treated E. coli K12 samples in fast5/fastq) must be mapped to a reference such as ecoli_k12_mg1655.fasta before methylation-calling or coverage filtering.
skills.name: nanopore-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-alignment-to-reference-genome Use when raw nanopore PASS reads (e.g. PCR-amplified or M.SssI-treated E. coli K12 samples in fast5/fastq) must be mapped to a reference such as ecoli_k12_mg1655.fasta before methylation-calling or coverage filtering. Input reads are already aligned — an indexed BAM exists, so re-alignment adds no information before methylation calling. The sequencing platform is short-read (Illumina WGBS); Minimap2 nanopore presets and this long-read pipeline are inappropriate for such data. No reference genome is available or the target genome differs substantially from the provided ecoli_k12_mg1655.fasta without a valid substitute. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Aligns Oxford Nanopore long reads to a reference genome with Minimap2 and processes the resulting BAM with samtools, forming the foundational coordinate anchor for downstream methylation calling in the METEORE benchmarking pipelines. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Aligns Oxford Nanopore long reads to a reference genome with Minimap2 and processes the resulting BAM with samtools, forming the foundational coordinate anchor for downstream methylation calling in the METEORE benchmarking pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already aligned — an indexed BAM exists, so re-alignment adds no information before methylation calling. The sequencing platform is short-read (Illumina WGBS); Minimap2 nanopore presets and this long-read pipeline are inappropriate for such data. No reference genome is available or the target genome differs substantially from the provided ecoli_k12_mg1655.fasta without a valid substitute.

skills.description: Use when a pipeline must convert coarse seed-hit clusters from a seeding stage into precise read/reference coordinate anchors prior to anchor chaining (LCSk), specifically for MinION nanopore or other long error-prone reads.
skills.name: nanopore-read-anchor-detection
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-anchor-detection Use when a pipeline must convert coarse seed-hit clusters from a seeding stage into precise read/reference coordinate anchors prior to anchor chaining (LCSk), specifically for MinION nanopore or other long error-prone reads. Reads are short Illumina reads — GraphMap's five-stage funnel and graph traversal target long, error-prone third-generation reads even though defaults can handle Illumina The task is full end-to-end alignment/variant calling rather than producing intermediate anchors — downstream stages (LCSk chaining, alignment) are needed Reference-scale memory is unavailable — index construction peaks around ~42 GB for a human genome (~14 x reference size final index), so very constrained-memory environments are unsuitable http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs GraphMap's stage II, which refines stage I clustered seed hits via graph-based vertex-centric seed processing (k-mer mapping graph with l=9 outbound edges per vertex) to construct alignment anchors for long, error-prone nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Reconstructs GraphMap's stage II, which refines stage I clustered seed hits via graph-based vertex-centric seed processing (k-mer mapping graph with l=9 outbound edges per vertex) to construct alignment anchors for long, error-prone nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are short Illumina reads — GraphMap's five-stage funnel and graph traversal target long, error-prone third-generation reads even though defaults can handle Illumina The task is full end-to-end alignment/variant calling rather than producing intermediate anchors — downstream stages (LCSk chaining, alignment) are needed Reference-scale memory is unavailable — index construction peaks around ~42 GB for a human genome (~14 x reference size final index), so very constrained-memory environments are unsuitable

skills.description: Use when a POD5 nanopore file's per-read metadata must be fully enumerated and flattened — e.g. to inspect nested attributes of a selected read ID or export them to per-read JSON files.
skills.name: nanopore-read-attribute-parsing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-attribute-parsing Use when a POD5 nanopore file's per-read metadata must be fully enumerated and flattened — e.g. to inspect nested attributes of a selected read ID or export them to per-read JSON files. The goal is to inspect or export the raw current measurements (signal data) rather than the read's metadata — use pod5Viewer's `View signal` or `Export signal` workflows instead The input is not a POD5 file but an already-extracted JSON/CSV of read attributes — re-parsing would duplicate existing work Recursively extracts all attributes stored for a single read in a POD5 file as key-value pairs, expanding nested groups (e.g. context or run-info sub-structures) down to every leaf value, mirroring pod5Viewer's data view panel and `File > Export all info` behaviour. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae665
skills.summary: Recursively extracts all attributes stored for a single read in a POD5 file as key-value pairs, expanding nested groups (e.g. context or run-info sub-structures) down to every leaf value, mirroring pod5Viewer's data view panel and `File > Export all info` behaviour.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to inspect or export the raw current measurements (signal data) rather than the read's metadata — use pod5Viewer's `View signal` or `Export signal` workflows instead The input is not a POD5 file but an already-extracted JSON/CSV of read attributes — re-parsing would duplicate existing work

skills.name: nanopore-read-basecalling
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-basecalling Use when raw nanopore signals simulated from a reference (e.g. BLOW5/POD5 from seq2squiggle, squigulator, or DeepSimulator under R9.4.1 or R10.4.1 chemistry) must be turned into basecalled reads for variant-detection benchmarking. In the seq2squiggle paper this step bridges signal simulation (seq2squiggle, squigulator, DeepSimulator) to read-based evaluation with minimap2, Clair3, and RTGtools. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744

skills.search_text: nanopore-read-basecalling-and-resquiggling Use when starting from raw single-read FAST5 Nanopore files (e.g. R9.4 plant reads) that need basecalls and raw-signal-to-reference alignment before deep-learning methylation detection. Input is already basecalled, re-squiggled FAST5 with a populated RawGenomeCorrected_000 group (skip straight to deepsignal_plant call_mods) Data is R10.4.1 POD5/BAM from Dorado rather than R9.4 FAST5 + Guppy + Tombo, where the Tombo-based re-squiggle path does not apply Goal is methylation calling with statistical methods (e.g. Tombo detect_mods) rather than preparing inputs for DeepSignal-plant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Preprocess raw Oxford Nanopore FAST5 reads for methylation calling by basecalling with Guppy and re-squiggling raw signals to the genome reference with Tombo, producing signal-to-base aligned reads ready for DeepSignal-plant per-read 5mC probability calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already basecalled, re-squiggled FAST5 with a populated RawGenomeCorrected_000 group (skip straight to deepsignal_plant call_mods) Data is R10.4.1 POD5/BAM from Dorado rather than R9.4 FAST5 + Guppy + Tombo, where the Tombo-based re-squiggle path does not apply Goal is methylation calling with statistical methods (e.g. Tombo detect_mods) rather than preparing inputs for DeepSignal-plant

skills.name: nanopore-read-basecalling-orchestration
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-basecalling-orchestration Use when raw nanopore signal files (FAST5, .fast5.gz, POD5, .pod5.gz) or already-basecalled FASTQ (.fastq, .fq, .fastq.gz, .fq.gz) must enter VirDetector's preprocessing before taxonomic classification.
