skills.description: Use when assembling untargeted (metagenomic) Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical samples where uneven viral genome abundance (e.g., co-infections) may prevent a single Canu run from recovering low-abundance virus genomes.
skills.name: nanopore-read-de-novo-assembly
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-de-novo-assembly Use when assembling untargeted (metagenomic) Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical samples where uneven viral genome abundance (e.g., co-infections) may prevent a single Canu run from recovering low-abundance virus genomes. Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g., mpox), where assemblies may contain inaccuracies and should only be regarded as draft genomes Reads already reduced to a single high-abundance target where a single Canu run suffices and iterative re-assembly would only add runtime Reads that have not passed adapter/primer trimming, Centrifuge non-viral filtering, and host/contaminant removal — assembling unfiltered reads will waste Canu resources on non-viral content http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Iterative de novo assembly of untargeted viral nanopore reads with Canu in ViMOP: reads mapping to newly generated contigs are removed and Canu is re-run on the remainder, with a cd-hit-est pre-clustering fallback when a target-filtered read set yields no contigs. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Iterative de novo assembly of untargeted viral nanopore reads with Canu in ViMOP: reads mapping to newly generated contigs are removed and Canu is re-run on the remainder, with a cd-hit-est pre-clustering fallback when a target-filtered read set yields no contigs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g., mpox), where assemblies may contain inaccuracies and should only be regarded as draft genomes Reads already reduced to a single high-abundance target where a single Canu run suffices and iterative re-assembly would only add runtime Reads that have not passed adapter/primer trimming, Centrifuge non-viral filtering, and host/contaminant removal — assembling unfiltered reads will waste Canu resources on non-viral content

skills.description: Use when you have dual-indexed MinION FASTA/FASTQ amplicon reads (e.g. long rDNA amplicons) plus a barcode/index combination file and need to assign each read to a specimen by matching forward/reverse barcodes and primers.
skills.name: nanopore-read-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-demultiplexing Use when you have dual-indexed MinION FASTA/FASTQ amplicon reads (e.g. long rDNA amplicons) plus a barcode/index combination file and need to assign each read to a specimen by matching forward/reverse barcodes and primers. Input reads are already demultiplexed or single-indexed without dual barcodes and primers at both read ends — MiniBar's search logic expects dual indexes plus primers at the start and end of each MinION read Input is a post-clustering OTU/ASV table or per-sample read-count matrix — no demultiplexing remains to be done Downstream processing that requires fully trimmed, consensus-called sequences is the goal without needing sample assignment — use the trimming/consensus steps of the pipeline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Demultiplex dual-indexed Oxford Nanopore MinION rDNA amplicon reads with MiniBar (minibar.py, Python 2.7/3 with Edlib), matching dual barcode indexes and primers at the sequence ends and appending per-read sample IDs to record headers. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Demultiplex dual-indexed Oxford Nanopore MinION rDNA amplicon reads with MiniBar (minibar.py, Python 2.7/3 with Edlib), matching dual barcode indexes and primers at the sequence ends and appending per-read sample IDs to record headers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already demultiplexed or single-indexed without dual barcodes and primers at both read ends — MiniBar's search logic expects dual indexes plus primers at the start and end of each MinION read Input is a post-clustering OTU/ASV table or per-sample read-count matrix — no demultiplexing remains to be done Downstream processing that requires fully trimmed, consensus-called sequences is the goal without needing sample assignment — use the trimming/consensus steps of the pipeline instead

skills.description: Use when nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads have been ligated with a PRO-designed barcode kit and each read must be assigned to its source barcode, especially when comparing accuracy against Guppy or edit-distance assignment.
skills.name: nanopore-read-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-demultiplexing Use when nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads have been ligated with a PRO-designed barcode kit and each read must be assigned to its source barcode, especially when comparing accuracy against Guppy or edit-distance assignment. Reads were barcoded with official ONT kits B1 (EXP-NBD104), B2 (SQK-16S024), or B3 (EXP-PBC096) whose flanking sequences resemble the barcodes — PRO may underperform Guppy because similar flanking sequences prevent accurate barcode extraction Data are PacBio reads — PRO has not been tested on PacBio data The goal is generating or selecting a new barcode set rather than assigning reads to existing barcodes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Demultiplex corrupted DNA barcodes from simulated or real nanopore reads using PRO's PRO-dex strategy, which extracts corrupted barcodes via edlib alignment of flanking sequences and assigns them by probability divergence, outperforming Guppy's edit-distance-based demultiplexing on large PRO-designed barcode kits. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
skills.summary: Demultiplex corrupted DNA barcodes from simulated or real nanopore reads using PRO's PRO-dex strategy, which extracts corrupted barcodes via edlib alignment of flanking sequences and assigns them by probability divergence, outperforming Guppy's edit-distance-based demultiplexing on large PRO-designed barcode kits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads were barcoded with official ONT kits B1 (EXP-NBD104), B2 (SQK-16S024), or B3 (EXP-PBC096) whose flanking sequences resemble the barcodes — PRO may underperform Guppy because similar flanking sequences prevent accurate barcode extraction Data are PacBio reads — PRO has not been tested on PacBio data The goal is generating or selecting a new barcode set rather than assigning reads to existing barcodes

skills.description: Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads from barcoding kits (e.g. SQK-RBK114-96 rapid or SQK-NBD114-96 native barcoding), especially when reads show complex barcode attachments, partially trimmed adapter contamination, or custom barcode patterns.
skills.name: nanopore-read-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-demultiplexing Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads from barcoding kits (e.g. SQK-RBK114-96 rapid or SQK-NBD114-96 native barcoding), especially when reads show complex barcode attachments, partially trimmed adapter contamination, or custom barcode patterns. Input is already demultiplexed/trimmed sequence data with no barcode constructs to resolve Reads come from RNA or Twist kits, which are exceptions to Barbell's tested DNA kit presets Ultra-strict barcode configuration is required and reads must not be maximally retained (consider whether the --maximize flag is appropriate) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Pattern-aware demultiplexing and trimming of Oxford Nanopore reads with Barbell, executed as four fixed steps (annotate → inspect → filter → trim) that detect complex barcode configurations (dual-end, concatenated, artefact attachments) that Dorado and Flexiplex miss. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Pattern-aware demultiplexing and trimming of Oxford Nanopore reads with Barbell, executed as four fixed steps (annotate → inspect → filter → trim) that detect complex barcode configurations (dual-end, concatenated, artefact attachments) that Dorado and Flexiplex miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already demultiplexed/trimmed sequence data with no barcode constructs to resolve Reads come from RNA or Twist kits, which are exceptions to Barbell's tested DNA kit presets Ultra-strict barcode configuration is required and reads must not be maximally retained (consider whether the --maximize flag is appropriate)

skills.description: Use when comparing methylation callers or basecalling models on nanopore data and you need standardized, depth-matched BAM inputs (e.g., 10x and 30x coverage) from high-coverage R10.4 datasets.
skills.name: nanopore-read-downsampling
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-downsampling Use when comparing methylation callers or basecalling models on nanopore data and you need standardized, depth-matched BAM inputs (e.g., 10x and 30x coverage) from high-coverage R10.4 datasets. The input BAM is already at or below the target depth — further sampling would erode coverage and bias frequency estimates The analysis goal is single-molecule per-read methylation accuracy benchmarking against ground-truth labels, where down-sampling frequency estimates to genome-wide tracks is not the target Reference genomes or matched BS-seq tracks are unavailable, so depth-controlled downstream correlation cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Down-samples ONT nanopore BAM alignments to controlled sequencing depths (10x and 30x in the DeepBAM study) using samtools view -s, enabling depth-controlled benchmarking of methylation callers against BS-seq. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Down-samples ONT nanopore BAM alignments to controlled sequencing depths (10x and 30x in the DeepBAM study) using samtools view -s, enabling depth-controlled benchmarking of methylation callers against BS-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAM is already at or below the target depth — further sampling would erode coverage and bias frequency estimates The analysis goal is single-molecule per-read methylation accuracy benchmarking against ground-truth labels, where down-sampling frequency estimates to genome-wide tracks is not the target Reference genomes or matched BS-seq tracks are unavailable, so depth-controlled downstream correlation cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when raw Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads contain PCR/tiling primer and adapter sequences at read ends and a fixed-length trim of both ends is needed before downstream classification or assembly.
skills.name: nanopore-read-end-trimming
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-end-trimming Use when raw Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads contain PCR/tiling primer and adapter sequences at read ends and a fixed-length trim of both ends is needed before downstream classification or assembly. Input reads are already primer- and adapter-trimmed (e.g. ONT basecaller output with adapters removed) — a fixed-length double-end trim would unnecessarily remove biological sequence Primer positions vary per read (e.g. heterogeneous tiling schemes) so a fixed --trim_length cut from both ends is inappropriate and coordinate-aware primer trimming is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Primer/adapter end trimming for untargeted nanopore FASTQ reads as implemented at the start of the ViMOP pipeline, using seqtk to cut a user-defined number of bases from both the 3' and 5' ends of every read. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Primer/adapter end trimming for untargeted nanopore FASTQ reads as implemented at the start of the ViMOP pipeline, using seqtk to cut a user-defined number of bases from both the 3' and 5' ends of every read.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already primer- and adapter-trimmed (e.g. ONT basecaller output with adapters removed) — a fixed-length double-end trim would unnecessarily remove biological sequence Primer positions vary per read (e.g. heterogeneous tiling schemes) so a fixed --trim_length cut from both ends is inappropriate and coordinate-aware primer trimming is required

skills.description: Reference for generating or verifying per-sample output tables (reads.tsv, consensus.tsv, contigs.tsv) and HTML report sections summarizing read filtering statistics from a ViMOP Nextflow run.
skills.name: nanopore-read-filtering-statistics-summarization
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-filtering-statistics-summarization Reference for generating or verifying per-sample output tables (reads.tsv, consensus.tsv, contigs.tsv) and HTML report sections summarizing read filtering statistics from a ViMOP Nextflow run. The input is raw FASTQ before any ViMOP run — this skill summarizes completed run outputs, it does not perform filtering itself. The pipeline was run with --centrifuge_do_classify false, so no classification/Krona content is available for the report's contig section. The goal is genome reconstruction quality assessment rather than per-sample reporting; consult the alignment .bam files directly instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstruct ViMOP's per-sample summarization of read filtering statistics into tab-delimited tables and a three-section HTML report, so that read trimming, Centrifuge classification, and host/contaminant removal results are reproducibly reported per barcode. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Reconstruct ViMOP's per-sample summarization of read filtering statistics into tab-delimited tables and a three-section HTML report, so that read trimming, Centrifuge classification, and host/contaminant removal results are reproducibly reported per barcode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ before any ViMOP run — this skill summarizes completed run outputs, it does not perform filtering itself. The pipeline was run with --centrifuge_do_classify false, so no classification/Krona content is available for the report's contig section. The goal is genome reconstruction quality assessment rather than per-sample reporting; consult the alignment .bam files directly instead.

skills.description: Use when long nanopore reads must be assigned to a parental haplotype using trio-phased heterozygous SNPs, e.g. to phase SVs or determine parental origin of de novo breakpoint junctions.
skills.name: nanopore-read-haplotype-phasing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-haplotype-phasing Use when long nanopore reads must be assigned to a parental haplotype using trio-phased heterozygous SNPs, e.g. to phase SVs or determine parental origin of de novo breakpoint junctions. When only short-read (Illumina) data are available — the method requires long MinION reads spanning multiple heterozygous SNPs to assign haplotype per read When no trio-phased (GATK PBT) heterozygous SNP ground truth exists to anchor the haplotypes When the goal is de novo genome assembly rather than read-level phasing — the authors did not attempt assembly due to insufficient coverage (11–16×) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Assign individual MinION nanopore reads to paternal or maternal haplotypes by summing SNP allele log-likelihoods (incorporating base and mapping qualities) over trio-phased (GATK PBT) heterozygous SNPs overlapped by each read, enabling read-based phasing of SVs and determination of the parental origin of de novo chromothripsis breakpoints. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Assign individual MinION nanopore reads to paternal or maternal haplotypes by summing SNP allele log-likelihoods (incorporating base and mapping qualities) over trio-phased (GATK PBT) heterozygous SNPs overlapped by each read, enabling read-based phasing of SVs and determination of the parental origin of de novo chromothripsis breakpoints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only short-read (Illumina) data are available — the method requires long MinION reads spanning multiple heterozygous SNPs to assign haplotype per read When no trio-phased (GATK PBT) heterozygous SNP ground truth exists to anchor the haplotypes When the goal is de novo genome assembly rather than read-level phasing — the authors did not attempt assembly due to insufficient coverage (11–16×)

skills.description: Use when ONT nanopore reads (e.g., an HG002 R10.4 alignment BAM) must be partitioned into paternal/maternal haplotype read sets for allele-specific methylation analysis and a phased VCF of heterozygous variants is available.
skills.name: nanopore-read-haplotype-tagging
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-haplotype-tagging Use when ONT nanopore reads (e.g., an HG002 R10.4 alignment BAM) must be partitioned into paternal/maternal haplotype read sets for allele-specific methylation analysis and a phased VCF of heterozygous variants is available. No phased VCF of heterozygous variants exists for the sample — haplotag has no informative variants to assign HP:i:1/HP:i:2 tags from. The BAM is already haplotype-tagged; only the split/filter step (extracting hp1.bam and hp2.bam) is needed, not re-tagging. The goal is single-molecule CpG methylation calling itself (e.g., running DeepBAM or Dorado on R10.4 POD5/BAM data) rather than assigning reads to haplotypes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Assigns Oxford Nanopore reads to paternal or maternal haplotypes by tagging them with whatshap haplotag against GIAB phased variants (HP:i:1 / HP:i:2), as done for HG002 R10.4 data in DeepBAM to enable allele-specific methylation analysis at ~80% assignment rate. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Assigns Oxford Nanopore reads to paternal or maternal haplotypes by tagging them with whatshap haplotag against GIAB phased variants (HP:i:1 / HP:i:2), as done for HG002 R10.4 data in DeepBAM to enable allele-specific methylation analysis at ~80% assignment rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No phased VCF of heterozygous variants exists for the sample — haplotag has no informative variants to assign HP:i:1/HP:i:2 tags from. The BAM is already haplotype-tagged; only the split/filter step (extracting hp1.bam and hp2.bam) is needed, not re-tagging. The goal is single-molecule CpG methylation calling itself (e.g., running DeepBAM or Dorado on R10.4 POD5/BAM data) rather than assigning reads to haplotypes.

skills.description: Use when compressing or indexing ONT nanopore read sequences from a FASTQ file and a k-mer–based MinHash sketch is needed to find reads overlapping a query sequence.
skills.name: nanopore-read-kmer-extraction
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-kmer-extraction Use when compressing or indexing ONT nanopore read sequences from a FASTQ file and a k-mer–based MinHash sketch is needed to find reads overlapping a query sequence. Input is not a FASTQ base-sequence file — NanoSpring ignores read identifiers and quality scores, so this skill is wrong for quality-score or header compression tasks Reads are short, low-error short-read data — NanoSpring's approximate-assembly approach targets long nanopore reads made feasible by deep-learning basecallers reaching ~5% or better median error rates A reference genome is available and a reference-based compressor (e.g. RENANO) is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extract all k-mers of length k=23 from the base sequences of nanopore FASTQ reads and compute n=60 MinHash hash values per read, as the first stages of NanoSpring's MinHash overlap-detection pipeline used by its approximate-assembly compressor. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Extract all k-mers of length k=23 from the base sequences of nanopore FASTQ reads and compute n=60 MinHash hash values per read, as the first stages of NanoSpring's MinHash overlap-detection pipeline used by its approximate-assembly compressor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a FASTQ base-sequence file — NanoSpring ignores read identifiers and quality scores, so this skill is wrong for quality-score or header compression tasks Reads are short, low-error short-read data — NanoSpring's approximate-assembly approach targets long nanopore reads made feasible by deep-learning basecallers reaching ~5% or better median error rates A reference genome is available and a reference-based compressor (e.g. RENANO) is preferred

skills.description: Use when characterizing a nanopore WGS dataset by read-length statistics and genome-wide coverage at MAPQ ≥ 20 across alternative aligners (e.g., rebuilding the NA19240 control metrics from Table 2).
skills.name: nanopore-read-length-statistics
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-length-statistics Use when characterizing a nanopore WGS dataset by read-length statistics and genome-wide coverage at MAPQ ≥ 20 across alternative aligners (e.g., rebuilding the NA19240 control metrics from Table 2). Input is not whole-genome nanopore data (e.g., targeted panels or short reads) — genome-wide coverage fractions and long-read length statistics will not be comparable to Table 2. The goal is SV calling or coverage-based polishing/filtering of calls (disCoverage) rather than dataset-level QC metrics. Comparing aligner call sets rather than characterizing the underlying read set and alignment coverage — this skill produces only QC/coverage summaries, not variant calls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reproduces baseline nanopore WGS dataset metrics — mean read length via NanoStat on the FASTQ and MAPQ ≥ 20 genome-wide coverage fractions via mosdepth on each aligner BAM — for the NA19240 control dataset, mirroring the Table 2 row (14,565 bp; 93/92/91% for lra/minimap2/NGMLR; median 16/17/15×). genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Reproduces baseline nanopore WGS dataset metrics — mean read length via NanoStat on the FASTQ and MAPQ ≥ 20 genome-wide coverage fractions via mosdepth on each aligner BAM — for the NA19240 control dataset, mirroring the Table 2 row (14,565 bp; 93/92/91% for lra/minimap2/NGMLR; median 16/17/15×).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not whole-genome nanopore data (e.g., targeted panels or short reads) — genome-wide coverage fractions and long-read length statistics will not be comparable to Table 2. The goal is SV calling or coverage-based polishing/filtering of calls (disCoverage) rather than dataset-level QC metrics. Comparing aligner call sets rather than characterizing the underlying read set and alignment coverage — this skill produces only QC/coverage summaries, not variant calls.

skills.description: Use when preparing Fast-SG hybrid scaffolding or assembly runs on raw Nanopore/PacBio long-read FASTA libraries, e.g. shallow ~5X NA12878 ultra-long reads feeding a scaffolding graph built with k-mer size 22.
skills.name: nanopore-read-library-configuration
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-library-configuration Use when preparing Fast-SG hybrid scaffolding or assembly runs on raw Nanopore/PacBio long-read FASTA libraries, e.g. shallow ~5X NA12878 ultra-long reads feeding a scaffolding graph built with k-mer size 22. The input libraries are Illumina paired-end short reads described as separate fwd/rev paths — use the short-read config format '#type libID Path(fwd) Path(rev) SAM(1:single 2:paired)' instead of the long-read 'long' line format Requested insert sizes exceed the actual long-read length, since Fast-SG restricts synthetic insert size to the real read size The scaffolding graph will be built by a read-to-contig aligner (Bowtie/Bowtie2/Bwa-Mem) rather than Fast-SG, which does not consume this configuration file http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Writes the Fast-SG read configuration file that describes Nanopore (or other long-read) libraries — one space-separated line per library with type 'long', library ID, FASTA path, comma-separated insert sizes, and the single-end flag — so FAST-SG.pl can extract alignment-free synthetic mate-pair libraries from uncorrected long reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Writes the Fast-SG read configuration file that describes Nanopore (or other long-read) libraries — one space-separated line per library with type 'long', library ID, FASTA path, comma-separated insert sizes, and the single-end flag — so FAST-SG.pl can extract alignment-free synthetic mate-pair libraries from uncorrected long reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input libraries are Illumina paired-end short reads described as separate fwd/rev paths — use the short-read config format '#type libID Path(fwd) Path(rev) SAM(1:single 2:paired)' instead of the long-read 'long' line format Requested insert sizes exceed the actual long-read length, since Fast-SG restricts synthetic insert size to the real read size The scaffolding graph will be built by a read-to-contig aligner (Bowtie/Bowtie2/Bwa-Mem) rather than Fast-SG, which does not consume this configuration file

skills.description: Use when comparing long-read mapper sensitivity (mapped reads/bases) or consensus accuracy on Oxford Nanopore MinION data against published GraphMap results, or when validating a mapper build on real MinION data sets.
skills.name: nanopore-read-mapping-benchmarking
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-mapping-benchmarking Use when comparing long-read mapper sensitivity (mapped reads/bases) or consensus accuracy on Oxford Nanopore MinION data against published GraphMap results, or when validating a mapper build on real MinION data sets. The task is de novo assembly or read overlapping rather than mapping-to-reference benchmarking (use GraphMap's 'owler' overlapping mode instead) Data are simulated reads only — the sensitivity/consensus validation thresholds here are defined against real MinION data sets from the reproduction bundle Mapping to very large genomes on memory-limited machines — GraphMap's hash index requires ~14x reference size (~100 GB peak for human genome) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark GraphMap against LAST, BWA-MEM, BLASR and DALIGNER on real MinION nanopore read sets by measuring mapped-read/base fractions and whole-genome consensus accuracy, reproducing the paper's Fig. 3 sensitivity and consensus-error claims. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Benchmark GraphMap against LAST, BWA-MEM, BLASR and DALIGNER on real MinION nanopore read sets by measuring mapped-read/base fractions and whole-genome consensus accuracy, reproducing the paper's Fig. 3 sensitivity and consensus-error claims.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is de novo assembly or read overlapping rather than mapping-to-reference benchmarking (use GraphMap's 'owler' overlapping mode instead) Data are simulated reads only — the sensitivity/consensus validation thresholds here are defined against real MinION data sets from the reproduction bundle Mapping to very large genomes on memory-limited machines — GraphMap's hash index requires ~14x reference size (~100 GB peak for human genome)

skills.description: Use when you have a per-read feature table (read_id, mapping-quality ratio, chain-score ratio, mean chain-score ratio) from RawHash2 output and need to reproduce or audit the weighted-sum mapped/unmapped decision.
skills.name: nanopore-read-mapping-decision-scoring
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-mapping-decision-scoring Use when you have a per-read feature table (read_id, mapping-quality ratio, chain-score ratio, mean chain-score ratio) from RawHash2 output and need to reproduce or audit the weighted-sum mapped/unmapped decision. Input is raw FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5 signal files rather than an already-extracted per-read feature table — indexing and mapping/chaining must run first. The goal is reference-free overlap discovery (all-vs-all), which is Rawsamble's task, not the RawHash2 mapping decision. Features or weights are unavailable and cannot be supplied — the threshold mechanism cannot be reproduced without explicit config values. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs RawHash2's weighted mapping decision mechanism (Section 2.4): a per-read weighted sum over mapping-quality and chain-score ratios is compared against a configurable threshold to emit a mapped/unmapped call, replacing RawHash's fixed conditional checks. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Reconstructs RawHash2's weighted mapping decision mechanism (Section 2.4): a per-read weighted sum over mapping-quality and chain-score ratios is compared against a configurable threshold to emit a mapped/unmapped call, replacing RawHash's fixed conditional checks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5 signal files rather than an already-extracted per-read feature table — indexing and mapping/chaining must run first. The goal is reference-free overlap discovery (all-vs-all), which is Rawsamble's task, not the RawHash2 mapping decision. Features or weights are unavailable and cannot be supplied — the threshold mechanism cannot be reproduced without explicit config values.

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore DRS fast5 signals need transcript-level assignment — e.g. before curating training/testing sets for RISER, or before computing per-transcript read/nucleotide counts for enrichment or depletion benchmarks.
skills.name: nanopore-read-mapping-filtering
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-mapping-filtering Use when raw nanopore DRS fast5 signals need transcript-level assignment — e.g. before curating training/testing sets for RISER, or before computing per-transcript read/nucleotide counts for enrichment or depletion benchmarks. Data are cDNA nanopore reads or short-read RNA-seq rather than direct RNA sequencing signals with adapter and poly(A) structure The goal is real-time classification during a live run — RISER classifies raw signals directly without basecalling or a reference, so this offline mapping chain is unnecessary A reference transcriptome is unavailable and de novo or signal-level analysis is intended (RISER works without basecalling or a reference) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A standard nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) analysis chain: trim adapter/poly(A) from raw signals with BoostNano, basecall with Guppy, map to the GENCODE reference transcriptome with minimap2, and retain only high-confidence alignments with samtools. This produces reliable per-read transcript assignments needed for downstream quantification and RISER label curation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: A standard nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) analysis chain: trim adapter/poly(A) from raw signals with BoostNano, basecall with Guppy, map to the GENCODE reference transcriptome with minimap2, and retain only high-confidence alignments with samtools. This produces reliable per-read transcript assignments needed for downstream quantification and RISER label curation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are cDNA nanopore reads or short-read RNA-seq rather than direct RNA sequencing signals with adapter and poly(A) structure The goal is real-time classification during a live run — RISER classifies raw signals directly without basecalling or a reference, so this offline mapping chain is unnecessary A reference transcriptome is unavailable and de novo or signal-level analysis is intended (RISER works without basecalling or a reference)

skills.description: Use when the task requires locating a subset of reads by read ID within one or more POD5 files — e.g. searching read IDs by substring, sorting them lexicographically, or intersecting them with a supplied list of read IDs.
skills.name: nanopore-read-metadata-inspection
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-metadata-inspection Use when the task requires locating a subset of reads by read ID within one or more POD5 files — e.g. searching read IDs by substring, sorting them lexicographically, or intersecting them with a supplied list of read IDs. The input is not a POD5 file but an already-extracted list of read IDs or another format (e.g. FASTQ/BAM), where the pod5 reader library is unnecessary. The goal is to inspect signal values, plot signals, or export reads to JSON/NumPy rather than to select which reads are shown. No read selection is needed — all reads from the POD5 file should be retained, so no search/sort/filter step is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Locates specific reads among those enumerated in a POD5 file's navigator panel by applying live substring search, ascending/descending alphabetical sorting, and set-based read ID filtering, mirroring pod5Viewer's file navigation functions. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae665
skills.summary: Locates specific reads among those enumerated in a POD5 file's navigator panel by applying live substring search, ascending/descending alphabetical sorting, and set-based read ID filtering, mirroring pod5Viewer's file navigation functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a POD5 file but an already-extracted list of read IDs or another format (e.g. FASTQ/BAM), where the pod5 reader library is unnecessary. The goal is to inspect signal values, plot signals, or export reads to JSON/NumPy rather than to select which reads are shown. No read selection is needed — all reads from the POD5 file should be retained, so no search/sort/filter step is required.

skills.description: Use when ONT reads need to be assigned to parental haplotypes to resolve haplotype-specific methylation — e.g. detecting imprinted control regions, parent-of-origin labeling in a trio, or differential methylation between phases.
skills.name: nanopore-read-phasing-with-snp-haplotyping
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-phasing-with-snp-haplotyping Use when ONT reads need to be assigned to parental haplotypes to resolve haplotype-specific methylation — e.g. detecting imprinted control regions, parent-of-origin labeling in a trio, or differential methylation between phases. The target region lies in long runs of homozygosity — read phasing may not be possible there, so haplotype-resolved methylation counts will be unreliable Only bulk per-site methylation frequencies are needed with no haplotype context — run DeepMod2 detect on the unphased aligned BAM instead The modification of interest is not 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides models for 5mCpG due to lack of training data for other modifications http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Phases ONT reads into parental haplotypes via SNP haplotyping (NanoCaller) and then calls haplotype-resolved 5mC methylation with DeepMod2, enabling detection of allele-specific (epihaplotype) methylation such as imprinted control regions in the Ashkenazim trio (HG002/HG003/HG004). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Phases ONT reads into parental haplotypes via SNP haplotyping (NanoCaller) and then calls haplotype-resolved 5mC methylation with DeepMod2, enabling detection of allele-specific (epihaplotype) methylation such as imprinted control regions in the Ashkenazim trio (HG002/HG003/HG004).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target region lies in long runs of homozygosity — read phasing may not be possible there, so haplotype-resolved methylation counts will be unreliable Only bulk per-site methylation frequencies are needed with no haplotype context — run DeepMod2 detect on the unphased aligned BAM instead The modification of interest is not 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides models for 5mCpG due to lack of training data for other modifications

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore sequencing files (FASTQ, .fastq.gz, FAST5, or POD5) must be basecalled, preprocessed, and primer-trimmed before viral genome reconstruction or taxonomic classification in VirDetector.
skills.name: nanopore-read-preprocessing-and-trimming
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-preprocessing-and-trimming Use when raw nanopore sequencing files (FASTQ, .fastq.gz, FAST5, or POD5) must be basecalled, preprocessed, and primer-trimmed before viral genome reconstruction or taxonomic classification in VirDetector. Input is already assembled consensus genomes or clean FASTA sequences — these enter the pipeline at the alignment step, not preprocessing You only need to test pipeline execution without basecalling on raw signal data — run 'nextflow run main.nf' which skips basecalling Data is Illumina or other non-nanopore short-read sequencing — VirDetector is designed for nanopore sequencing http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Preprocess and trim Oxford Nanopore reads (FASTQ/FAST5/POD5) as the first stage of the VirDetector virus-surveillance pipeline, producing per-sample trimmed FASTQ files ready for reference-based or hybrid assembly and taxonomic classification. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Preprocess and trim Oxford Nanopore reads (FASTQ/FAST5/POD5) as the first stage of the VirDetector virus-surveillance pipeline, producing per-sample trimmed FASTQ files ready for reference-based or hybrid assembly and taxonomic classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled consensus genomes or clean FASTA sequences — these enter the pipeline at the alignment step, not preprocessing You only need to test pipeline execution without basecalling on raw signal data — run 'nextflow run main.nf' which skips basecalling Data is Illumina or other non-nanopore short-read sequencing — VirDetector is designed for nanopore sequencing

skills.description: Use when comparing nanopore direct RNA m6A between two conditions (e.g. WT vs knock-out replicates) using per-read modification probabilities to call differentially modified transcriptomic sites.
skills.name: nanopore-read-probability-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-probability-statistical-testing Use when comparing nanopore direct RNA m6A between two conditions (e.g. WT vs knock-out replicates) using per-read modification probabilities to call differentially modified transcriptomic sites. Sites with an absolute stoichiometry difference <0.1 between conditions — CHEUI-diff does not test these Sites lacking >20 aligned reads in both conditions, or sites that are not adenosines Single-condition m6A/m5C discovery without a control condition — use CHEUI-solo site-level prediction instead of the differential test http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detects differential m6A between two conditions by applying a Mann-Whitney U-test to CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read modification probabilities, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, as implemented in CHEUI-diff and benchmarked against Xpore and Nanocompore on HEK293 WT vs METTL3-KO data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Detects differential m6A between two conditions by applying a Mann-Whitney U-test to CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read modification probabilities, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, as implemented in CHEUI-diff and benchmarked against Xpore and Nanocompore on HEK293 WT vs METTL3-KO data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sites with an absolute stoichiometry difference <0.1 between conditions — CHEUI-diff does not test these Sites lacking >20 aligned reads in both conditions, or sites that are not adenosines Single-condition m6A/m5C discovery without a control condition — use CHEUI-solo site-level prediction instead of the differential test

skills.description: Use when you have untargeted metagenomic nanopore FASTQ data (optionally barcode-demultiplexed into barcode01, barcode02, ... subdirectories) from MinION sequencing of clinical or animal samples and need to detect known viral species and reconstruct their consensus genomes.
skills.name: nanopore-read-processing
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-processing Use when you have untargeted metagenomic nanopore FASTQ data (optionally barcode-demultiplexed into barcode01, barcode02, ... subdirectories) from MinION sequencing of clinical or animal samples and need to detect known viral species and reconstruct their consensus genomes. The input is already assembled contigs or consensus genomes rather than raw nanopore FASTQ reads — Centrifuge filtering and Canu assembly operate on reads, not contigs The target is de novo discovery of novel or divergent viruses with no close reference — ViMOP relies on BLAST matches to known viral references in ViMOP_DB The organism is a large DNA virus with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) where only inaccurate draft genomes are expected http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 End-to-end processing of untargeted Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads for viral genome reconstruction, as implemented in ViMOP: read-end trimming (adapter/primer removal), Centrifuge-based taxonomic classification and non-viral read filtering, host/contaminant read removal by mapping, de novo assembly with Canu, iterative re-assembly, BLAST reference identification, and reference-guided consensus generation (samtools/medaka). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: End-to-end processing of untargeted Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads for viral genome reconstruction, as implemented in ViMOP: read-end trimming (adapter/primer removal), Centrifuge-based taxonomic classification and non-viral read filtering, host/contaminant read removal by mapping, de novo assembly with Canu, iterative re-assembly, BLAST reference identification, and reference-guided consensus generation (samtools/medaka).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already assembled contigs or consensus genomes rather than raw nanopore FASTQ reads — Centrifuge filtering and Canu assembly operate on reads, not contigs The target is de novo discovery of novel or divergent viruses with no close reference — ViMOP relies on BLAST matches to known viral references in ViMOP_DB The organism is a large DNA virus with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) where only inaccurate draft genomes are expected

skills.description: Use when running mCaller on ONT eventalign data and read-level noise from low-quality basecalls is degrading per-position methylation accuracy, and you want to restrict classification to reads above an average base-quality threshold.
skills.name: nanopore-read-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-quality-filtering Use when running mCaller on ONT eventalign data and read-level noise from low-quality basecalls is degrading per-position methylation accuracy, and you want to restrict classification to reads above an average base-quality threshold. When low read depth is the limiting factor — filtering to high-quality reads removes observations and can interact with the separate minimum read depth for inclusion parameter When basecalled fastq lacks per-base quality scores or event data (e.g. non-Albacore basecallers that do not save event data), since average quality cannot be computed or eventalign will fail When evaluating accuracy at contexts dissimilar to training examples, where mCaller accuracy is dominated by training bias rather than read quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Restricts mCaller m6A classification to nanopore reads whose average base quality exceeds a cutoff via the -q/qual_thresh option, improving per-position accuracy by excluding noisy reads. For R9 data in this study, the 'NN_hq' variant classified only reads with average base quality > 9. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Restricts mCaller m6A classification to nanopore reads whose average base quality exceeds a cutoff via the -q/qual_thresh option, improving per-position accuracy by excluding noisy reads. For R9 data in this study, the 'NN_hq' variant classified only reads with average base quality > 9.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When low read depth is the limiting factor — filtering to high-quality reads removes observations and can interact with the separate minimum read depth for inclusion parameter When basecalled fastq lacks per-base quality scores or event data (e.g. non-Albacore basecallers that do not save event data), since average quality cannot be computed or eventalign will fail When evaluating accuracy at contexts dissimilar to training examples, where mCaller accuracy is dominated by training bias rather than read quality

skills.description: Use when a viral genome must be reconstructed from nanopore FASTQ reads for which a suitable reference FASTA already exists, e.g. a known virus such as West Nile virus where mapping beats de novo assembly.
skills.name: nanopore-read-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-reference-alignment Use when a viral genome must be reconstructed from nanopore FASTQ reads for which a suitable reference FASTA already exists, e.g. a known virus such as West Nile virus where mapping beats de novo assembly. No suitable reference sequence is available and an automated hybrid assembly approach (e.g. with params.canu_genome_size set) should be used instead. Input is already assembled contigs or FASTA sequences rather than reads — VirDetector accepts FASTA input only from the alignment step onwards. The goal is taxonomic classification of unknown samples rather than reconstruction of a specific known viral genome. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reference-based alignment of filtered nanopore reads against a provided viral reference sequence using minimap2, with samtools-based BAM sorting/indexing, Qualimap coverage reporting, and samtools consensus genome generation — the reference branch of VirDetector's genome reconstruction layer. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Reference-based alignment of filtered nanopore reads against a provided viral reference sequence using minimap2, with samtools-based BAM sorting/indexing, Qualimap coverage reporting, and samtools consensus genome generation — the reference branch of VirDetector's genome reconstruction layer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No suitable reference sequence is available and an automated hybrid assembly approach (e.g. with params.canu_genome_size set) should be used instead. Input is already assembled contigs or FASTA sequences rather than reads — VirDetector accepts FASTA input only from the alignment step onwards. The goal is taxonomic classification of unknown samples rather than reconstruction of a specific known viral genome.

skills.description: Use when evaluating SV-caller sensitivity/specificity (NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles) without wet-lab validation: simulated nanopore reads with a realistic error profile and known ground-truth breakpoints must be generated.
skills.name: nanopore-read-simulation
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-simulation Use when evaluating SV-caller sensitivity/specificity (NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles) without wet-lab validation: simulated nanopore reads with a realistic error profile and known ground-truth breakpoints must be generated. You already have real nanopore data with validated breakpoint junctions (as for Patient 1's known de novo junctions) — benchmark directly rather than simulating Your goal is SNV/short-read variant calling — this skill is specific to long-read SV breakpoint detection with split/gapped alignment evidence Coverage or read-length distribution of the simulation should mimic a platform other than Oxford Nanopore (e.g. Pacific Biosciences SMRT) without retraining the read model on that platform's data Simulate error-profile-matched nanopore long reads from a designed (rearranged) reference to benchmark SV callers: a NanoSim read model trained on real MinION reads is used to generate synthetic reads over 501 simulated chromosome 1 breakpoints, which are then downsampled (1x–44x) and evaluated by recall and false-positive rate. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Simulate error-profile-matched nanopore long reads from a designed (rearranged) reference to benchmark SV callers: a NanoSim read model trained on real MinION reads is used to generate synthetic reads over 501 simulated chromosome 1 breakpoints, which are then downsampled (1x–44x) and evaluated by recall and false-positive rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have real nanopore data with validated breakpoint junctions (as for Patient 1's known de novo junctions) — benchmark directly rather than simulating Your goal is SNV/short-read variant calling — this skill is specific to long-read SV breakpoint detection with split/gapped alignment evidence Coverage or read-length distribution of the simulation should mimic a platform other than Oxford Nanopore (e.g. Pacific Biosciences SMRT) without retraining the read model on that platform's data

skills.description: Use when benchmarking long-read taxonomic classifiers or ARG host-assignment pipelines and realistic simulated ONT metagenomes with controlled error profiles (HQ vs LQ) and known ground-truth species composition are needed.
skills.name: nanopore-read-simulation-error-modeling
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-simulation-error-modeling Use when benchmarking long-read taxonomic classifiers or ARG host-assignment pipelines and realistic simulated ONT metagenomes with controlled error profiles (HQ vs LQ) and known ground-truth species composition are needed. When the goal is to characterize real environmental samples rather than create controlled benchmarks with known ground truth — simulation cannot capture real strain diversity or plasmid-mediated HGT patterns When evaluating short-read (Illumina) pipelines, since the NanoSim models here are trained on ONT error profiles When ARGs of unseen species or novel genomic contexts need assessment — the simulation is restricted to the 25 RefSeq-complete reference genomes used to build the classifier databases http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Train platform-specific NanoSim error models from real Zymo mock-community nanopore reads (HQ from Zymo D6331, LQ from Zymo D6300) and use them to simulate large metagenomic read sets for benchmarking taxonomic host-identification strategies on ARG-carrying long reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Train platform-specific NanoSim error models from real Zymo mock-community nanopore reads (HQ from Zymo D6331, LQ from Zymo D6300) and use them to simulate large metagenomic read sets for benchmarking taxonomic host-identification strategies on ARG-carrying long reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to characterize real environmental samples rather than create controlled benchmarks with known ground truth — simulation cannot capture real strain diversity or plasmid-mediated HGT patterns When evaluating short-read (Illumina) pipelines, since the NanoSim models here are trained on ONT error profiles When ARGs of unseen species or novel genomic contexts need assessment — the simulation is restricted to the 25 RefSeq-complete reference genomes used to build the classifier databases

skills.description: Use when you need to determine how many Nanopore amplicon reads are sufficient for an accurate majority-vote consensus, by sweeping subsample sizes and measuring consensus error against a higher-accuracy reference consensus.
skills.name: nanopore-read-subsampling
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-subsampling Use when you need to determine how many Nanopore amplicon reads are sufficient for an accurate majority-vote consensus, by sweeping subsample sizes and measuring consensus error against a higher-accuracy reference consensus. Your goal is sample demultiplexing or binning of raw MinION reads rather than characterizing consensus accuracy versus depth — use minibar.py's demultiplexing options instead You have no independent higher-accuracy reference (e.g. Illumina-derived consensus) against which to compute edit distance, so subsampled consensus error cannot be calibrated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Randomly subsamples demultiplexed Nanopore long-read FASTQ reads across a range of assembly coverages (10–800 reads) to quantify how consensus sequence error depends on read depth, identifying the coverage at which majority-vote consensus accuracy plateaus. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Randomly subsamples demultiplexed Nanopore long-read FASTQ reads across a range of assembly coverages (10–800 reads) to quantify how consensus sequence error depends on read depth, identifying the coverage at which majority-vote consensus accuracy plateaus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is sample demultiplexing or binning of raw MinION reads rather than characterizing consensus accuracy versus depth — use minibar.py's demultiplexing options instead You have no independent higher-accuracy reference (e.g. Illumina-derived consensus) against which to compute edit distance, so subsampled consensus error cannot be calibrated

skills.description: Use when assessing the minimum nanopore sequencing depth at which nanoHiMe-seq CpG methylation calls remain accurate versus WGBS, e.g. before committing MinION flowcells for a low-coverage epigenomics experiment.
skills.name: nanopore-read-subsampling-coverage-scaling
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-subsampling-coverage-scaling Use when assessing the minimum nanopore sequencing depth at which nanoHiMe-seq CpG methylation calls remain accurate versus WGBS, e.g. before committing MinION flowcells for a low-coverage epigenomics experiment. When the question is histone-modification enrichment (6mA peak calling) rather than CpG methylation accuracy vs WGBS — use nanoHiMe 6mA mode with input.peak.bed instead When comparing methylation callers rather than depths (e.g. benchmarking nanoHiMe vs Megalodon/Guppy accuracy) — subsampling depth scaling does not address that comparison When CpG sites lack >= 20x coverage by both WGBS and nanoHiMe-seq — the correlation analysis is undefined at those sites http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Subsample a basecalled nanoHiMe-seq FASTQ (HepG2) to 5x, 10x, 30x and 50x coverage, then run the full minimap2/nanopolish/nanoHiMe mCG-calling pipeline per depth and compute Pearson correlations vs ENCODE WGBS to establish the minimum depth for accurate CpG methylation measurement. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Subsample a basecalled nanoHiMe-seq FASTQ (HepG2) to 5x, 10x, 30x and 50x coverage, then run the full minimap2/nanopolish/nanoHiMe mCG-calling pipeline per depth and compute Pearson correlations vs ENCODE WGBS to establish the minimum depth for accurate CpG methylation measurement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is histone-modification enrichment (6mA peak calling) rather than CpG methylation accuracy vs WGBS — use nanoHiMe 6mA mode with input.peak.bed instead When comparing methylation callers rather than depths (e.g. benchmarking nanoHiMe vs Megalodon/Guppy accuracy) — subsampling depth scaling does not address that comparison When CpG sites lack >= 20x coverage by both WGBS and nanoHiMe-seq — the correlation analysis is undefined at those sites

skills.description: Use when you have untargeted metagenomic nanopore FASTQ reads (e.g. Lassa, Ebola, Dengue clinical samples) and need to remove non-viral reads based on Centrifuge taxonomic classification confidence before viral genome reconstruction.
skills.name: nanopore-read-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-taxonomic-classification Use when you have untargeted metagenomic nanopore FASTQ reads (e.g. Lassa, Ebola, Dengue clinical samples) and need to remove non-viral reads based on Centrifuge taxonomic classification confidence before viral genome reconstruction. When you expect only viral reads and minimal contamination — Centrifuge has limited accuracy and may remove some false-positive viral reads When processing contigs — the centrifuge filter applies to reads only, not contigs; contig classification is a separate, coarse step When you have deactivated classification with --centrifuge_do_classify false — no classification.tsv or Krona plot will be produced http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classify untargeted Oxford Nanopore reads with Centrifuge against the ViMOP_DB index and remove reads classified as non-viral with a score of at least 150, producing a classification.tsv and a Krona plot. This step reduces bacterial/host background before downstream host/reagent mapping and viral genome assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Classify untargeted Oxford Nanopore reads with Centrifuge against the ViMOP_DB index and remove reads classified as non-viral with a score of at least 150, producing a classification.tsv and a Krona plot. This step reduces bacterial/host background before downstream host/reagent mapping and viral genome assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you expect only viral reads and minimal contamination — Centrifuge has limited accuracy and may remove some false-positive viral reads When processing contigs — the centrifuge filter applies to reads only, not contigs; contig classification is a separate, coarse step When you have deactivated classification with --centrifuge_do_classify false — no classification.tsv or Krona plot will be produced

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA-formatted nanopore reads (e.g. R7.3, R9 1D/2D, R9.4 1D MinION runs) plus a set of pre-selected 'not too repetitive' seed sequences of uniform length, and need read-to-seed alignments to drive a TULIP seed-layout assembly.
skills.name: nanopore-read-to-seed-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-to-seed-alignment Use when you have FASTA-formatted nanopore reads (e.g. R7.3, R9 1D/2D, R9.4 1D MinION runs) plus a set of pre-selected 'not too repetitive' seed sequences of uniform length, and need read-to-seed alignments to drive a TULIP seed-layout assembly. If you are polishing or aligning reads to an existing contig set (e.g. Canu contigs or Illumina data for Pilon), not to sparse 285 bp seed islands — that is a different mapping task with different parameters. If your seed sequences violate TULIP requirements (repetitive seeds, non-numeric or duplicated identifiers including 0, unequal lengths) — the graph untangling becomes prohibitively slow or fails. If your aligner output is not SAM (e.g. DALIGNER output) — TULIP version 0.4 accepts only SAM format. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns Oxford Nanopore long reads to sparse 285 bp seed sequences with BWA MEM using per-chemistry parameters, then condenses the SAM output to its first six fields so TULIP can build a seed graph. This alignment step is the input layer that converts raw MinION reads into seed-link evidence for the eel genome assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Aligns Oxford Nanopore long reads to sparse 285 bp seed sequences with BWA MEM using per-chemistry parameters, then condenses the SAM output to its first six fields so TULIP can build a seed graph. This alignment step is the input layer that converts raw MinION reads into seed-link evidence for the eel genome assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you are polishing or aligning reads to an existing contig set (e.g. Canu contigs or Illumina data for Pilon), not to sparse 285 bp seed islands — that is a different mapping task with different parameters. If your seed sequences violate TULIP requirements (repetitive seeds, non-numeric or duplicated identifiers including 0, unequal lengths) — the graph untangling becomes prohibitively slow or fails. If your aligner output is not SAM (e.g. DALIGNER output) — TULIP version 0.4 accepts only SAM format.

skills.description: Use when reported per-read execution time (ms) and energy (mJ) measurements exist for HARU (Xilinx FPGA + 4-core ARM) and one or more software baselines, and the goal is to derive or verify EDP and platform-level efficiency ratios.
skills.name: nanopore-read-until-platform-comparison
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-until-platform-comparison Use when reported per-read execution time (ms) and energy (mJ) measurements exist for HARU (Xilinx FPGA + 4-core ARM) and one or more software baselines, and the goal is to derive or verify EDP and platform-level efficiency ratios. The sources report only throughput or wall-clock totals without per-read energy measurements — EDP cannot be reconstructed and a latency-only comparison should be used instead The task is to actually run the HARU pipeline (flash PetaLinux image, load haru-dtw-firmware, run sigfish-haru dtw) rather than to analyze or verify its reported benchmark numbers The comparison targets a different workload (e.g. non-SARS-CoV-2 or non-Read-Until benchmark) whose absolute EDP values would not transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs the energy-delay product (EDP = per-read time × per-read energy) comparison of HARU's FPGA-accelerated sDTW Read Until against optimized software-only baselines (4-core ARM, Intel Core-i9, 36-core Xeon Gold), quantifying how much latency and energy an edge accelerator saves over server-class implementations. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Reconstructs the energy-delay product (EDP = per-read time × per-read energy) comparison of HARU's FPGA-accelerated sDTW Read Until against optimized software-only baselines (4-core ARM, Intel Core-i9, 36-core Xeon Gold), quantifying how much latency and energy an edge accelerator saves over server-class implementations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sources report only throughput or wall-clock totals without per-read energy measurements — EDP cannot be reconstructed and a latency-only comparison should be used instead The task is to actually run the HARU pipeline (flash PetaLinux image, load haru-dtw-firmware, run sigfish-haru dtw) rather than to analyze or verify its reported benchmark numbers The comparison targets a different workload (e.g. non-SARS-CoV-2 or non-Read-Until benchmark) whose absolute EDP values would not transfer

skills.description: Use when nanopore reads (e.g. nanoHiMe-seq FASTQ/BAM aligned to hg19) must be assigned to parental alleles — e.g. to compute per-allele phasing rates over H3K4me3/H3K27me3 peaks or CpG islands — and heterozygous variants are available or need calling.
skills.name: nanopore-read-variant-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-variant-calling Use when nanopore reads (e.g. nanoHiMe-seq FASTQ/BAM aligned to hg19) must be assigned to parental alleles — e.g. to compute per-allele phasing rates over H3K4me3/H3K27me3 peaks or CpG islands — and heterozygous variants are available or need calling. The locus has a low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs — phasing of 6mA-containing regions and CpG methylation depends on heterozygous variant density and will be unreliable The analysis does not require allele resolution (e.g. bulk methylation calling or 6mA region detection, which nanoHiMe performs on unphased eventalign input) Input reads are short Illumina reads, whose reported phasing rates (14.1% H3K4me3 CUT&Tag, 16.6% H3K27me3 CUT&Tag, 5.7% WGBS) are far below nanopore and are meant only as comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Calls and phases heterozygous variants directly from nanopore long reads (SNVs and INDELs via PEPPER-Margin-DeepVariant, haplotagging with Margin v2.2, phasing with WhatsHap v1.4) so that individual nanoHiMe-seq reads can be assigned to parental haplotypes for allele-specific epigenetic analysis. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Calls and phases heterozygous variants directly from nanopore long reads (SNVs and INDELs via PEPPER-Margin-DeepVariant, haplotagging with Margin v2.2, phasing with WhatsHap v1.4) so that individual nanoHiMe-seq reads can be assigned to parental haplotypes for allele-specific epigenetic analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus has a low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs — phasing of 6mA-containing regions and CpG methylation depends on heterozygous variant density and will be unreliable The analysis does not require allele resolution (e.g. bulk methylation calling or 6mA region detection, which nanoHiMe performs on unphased eventalign input) Input reads are short Illumina reads, whose reported phasing rates (14.1% H3K4me3 CUT&Tag, 16.6% H3K27me3 CUT&Tag, 5.7% WGBS) are far below nanopore and are meant only as comparisons

skills.description: Use when raw multi-fast5 ONT direct RNA reads must be converted to single-read fast5 and raw current signal aligned (resquiggled) to a reference FASTA before per-position modification detection, especially when tuning alignment/event-detection parameters for rRNA or similar references.
skills.name: nanopore-reference-alignment-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: nanopore-reference-alignment-parameter-tuning Use when raw multi-fast5 ONT direct RNA reads must be converted to single-read fast5 and raw current signal aligned (resquiggled) to a reference FASTA before per-position modification detection, especially when tuning alignment/event-detection parameters for rRNA or similar references. If reads are already single-read fast5 and resquiggled, re-running conversion/resquiggle is unnecessary and risks overwriting with --overwrite When the target requires a trained kmer model for modification identification without an IVT control — the paper notes no such training sets exist and detection here depends on comparison with an IVT control When the goal is basecalling or alignment of cDNA/DNA nanopore reads rather than raw RNA signal-to-sequence alignment for modification detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 A resquiggling/alignment-parameterization recipe for ONT direct RNA nanopore data: converting multi-fast5 files to single-read fast5 and aligning raw ionic-current signal to a reference sequence with Tombo's resquiggle using the paper's validated flag set, so that subsequent modification detection (KS-based sample comparison) operates on correctly signal-to-sequence-aligned reads. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: A resquiggling/alignment-parameterization recipe for ONT direct RNA nanopore data: converting multi-fast5 files to single-read fast5 and aligning raw ionic-current signal to a reference sequence with Tombo's resquiggle using the paper's validated flag set, so that subsequent modification detection (KS-based sample comparison) operates on correctly signal-to-sequence-aligned reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If reads are already single-read fast5 and resquiggled, re-running conversion/resquiggle is unnecessary and risks overwriting with --overwrite When the target requires a trained kmer model for modification identification without an IVT control — the paper notes no such training sets exist and detection here depends on comparison with an IVT control When the goal is basecalling or alignment of cDNA/DNA nanopore reads rather than raw RNA signal-to-sequence alignment for modification detection

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing fast5 files must be assigned transcript identities (e.g., to label RNA classes for model training or quantify transcript abundance) via basecalling, transcriptome mapping, and high-confidence alignment filtering.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-basecalling-and-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-basecalling-and-alignment Use when raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing fast5 files must be assigned transcript identities (e.g., to label RNA classes for model training or quantify transcript abundance) via basecalling, transcriptome mapping, and high-confidence alignment filtering. You need real-time reject decisions during live sequencing — RISER classifies raw signal directly and is faster than GPU-accelerated basecalling and mapping, so basecall-plus-map is the wrong runtime path Reads are intended for a reference-free or de novo analysis where transcriptome mapping would bias the result http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Converts raw nanopore fast5 signals into mapped, high-confidence transcript alignments by basecalling with Guppy, aligning with minimap2 to a GENCODE transcriptome, and filtering with samtools — the labeling backbone used to curate RISER's mRNA/non-mRNA training data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Converts raw nanopore fast5 signals into mapped, high-confidence transcript alignments by basecalling with Guppy, aligning with minimap2 to a GENCODE transcriptome, and filtering with samtools — the labeling backbone used to curate RISER's mRNA/non-mRNA training data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need real-time reject decisions during live sequencing — RISER classifies raw signal directly and is faster than GPU-accelerated basecalling and mapping, so basecall-plus-map is the wrong runtime path Reads are intended for a reference-free or de novo analysis where transcriptome mapping would bias the result

skills.description: Use when a single read's raw nanopore current measurements stored in a POD5 file must be extracted into a .npy Numpy binary or plain-text file for downstream numpy processing without the pod5 API.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-binary-npy-export
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-binary-npy-export Use when a single read's raw nanopore current measurements stored in a POD5 file must be extracted into a .npy Numpy binary or plain-text file for downstream numpy processing without the pod5 API. Input is not a POD5 file (e.g. legacy FAST5 or FASTQ reads) — pod5Viewer is built for inspecting POD5 files. Goal is bulk scripted extraction of many reads' signals — only the all-info JSON export offers an 'All opened reads' option; the signal export targets a given read, so use the pod5 API/scripts instead for batch jobs. Goal is saving the plotted figure — use `Export > Export current view...` for an SVG vector graphic instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Exports the current measurements (signal) of a focused read from a POD5 file via pod5Viewer's `Export signal` menu to a .npy Numpy binary file (or a one-measurement-per-line text file), decoupling downstream analysis from the pod5 API. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae665
skills.summary: Exports the current measurements (signal) of a focused read from a POD5 file via pod5Viewer's `Export signal` menu to a .npy Numpy binary file (or a one-measurement-per-line text file), decoupling downstream analysis from the pod5 API.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a POD5 file (e.g. legacy FAST5 or FASTQ reads) — pod5Viewer is built for inspecting POD5 files. Goal is bulk scripted extraction of many reads' signals — only the all-info JSON export offers an 'All opened reads' option; the signal export targets a given read, so use the pod5 API/scripts instead for batch jobs. Goal is saving the plotted figure — use `Export > Export current view...` for an SVG vector graphic instead.

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore DRS signals (fast5, RNA002 or RNA004 kits) must be classified into RNA classes such as protein_coding mRNA, mtRNA, lncRNA or globin (HBA1/HBA2/HBB) directly from the first few seconds of signal.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-classification
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-classification Use when raw nanopore DRS signals (fast5, RNA002 or RNA004 kits) must be classified into RNA classes such as protein_coding mRNA, mtRNA, lncRNA or globin (HBA1/HBA2/HBB) directly from the first few seconds of signal. Accurate lncRNA-only discrimination is the goal — the paper states accurate lncRNA identification from the 3′ end signal remains challenging and lncRNA cell type-specific expression hinders generalization The task requires full-length sequence output or reference-based alignment of complete reads — RISER classifies from only the first ~70–280 nt of raw signal and does not basecall Input signals are cDNA sequencing or non-RNA002/RNA004 nanopore chemistry not supported by the shipped models http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Classify RNA biotypes (mRNA, mtRNA, globin mRNA) directly from raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing signals using the RISER convolutional neural network, without basecalling or a reference, enabling biochemical-free real-time enrichment or depletion via the read-until system. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Classify RNA biotypes (mRNA, mtRNA, globin mRNA) directly from raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing signals using the RISER convolutional neural network, without basecalling or a reference, enabling biochemical-free real-time enrichment or depletion via the read-until system.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Accurate lncRNA-only discrimination is the goal — the paper states accurate lncRNA identification from the 3′ end signal remains challenging and lncRNA cell type-specific expression hinders generalization The task requires full-length sequence output or reference-based alignment of complete reads — RISER classifies from only the first ~70–280 nt of raw signal and does not basecall Input signals are cDNA sequencing or non-RNA002/RNA004 nanopore chemistry not supported by the shipped models

skills.description: Use when starting from raw nanopore FAST5 files and you need event-level signal-to-reference alignments (test.eventalign.txt) as input for nanoHiMe modification calling or model training.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-event-alignment
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-event-alignment Use when starting from raw nanopore FAST5 files and you need event-level signal-to-reference alignments (test.eventalign.txt) as input for nanoHiMe modification calling or model training. Input is already a nanopolish eventalign table — skip directly to nanoHiMe 6mA/mCG calling or Model_training The target modification caller requires raw signal models directly (e.g. Megalodon v2.5.0 runs on FAST5/BAM with res_dna_r941_min_modbases-all-context_v001.cfg and does not need the nanopolish eventalign step) Reads are not ONT R9.4.1 data (the dna_r9.4.1_450bps_hac.cfg basecalling model and k-mer event alignment are signal chemistry specific) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Pipeline for converting Oxford Nanopore FAST5 signal data into per-event, k-mer-level alignments: Guppy basecalling, nanopolish read-to-signal indexing, minimap2 alignment with MAPQ≥20 filtering, and nanopolish eventalign with --scale-events to produce the eventalign tables that nanoHiMe requires for 6mA and CpG methylation calling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Pipeline for converting Oxford Nanopore FAST5 signal data into per-event, k-mer-level alignments: Guppy basecalling, nanopolish read-to-signal indexing, minimap2 alignment with MAPQ≥20 filtering, and nanopolish eventalign with --scale-events to produce the eventalign tables that nanoHiMe requires for 6mA and CpG methylation calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a nanopolish eventalign table — skip directly to nanoHiMe 6mA/mCG calling or Model_training The target modification caller requires raw signal models directly (e.g. Megalodon v2.5.0 runs on FAST5/BAM with res_dna_r941_min_modbases-all-context_v001.cfg and does not need the nanopolish eventalign step) Reads are not ONT R9.4.1 data (the dna_r9.4.1_450bps_hac.cfg basecalling model and k-mer event alignment are signal chemistry specific)

skills.description: Use when raw ONT fast5 reads must be resquiggled, converted to multi-fast5, and parsed into position-anchored signal events to support k-mer-level comparisons of native vs WGA samples.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-event-extraction
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-event-extraction Use when raw ONT fast5 reads must be resquiggled, converted to multi-fast5, and parsed into position-anchored signal events to support k-mer-level comparisons of native vs WGA samples. Input fast5 files have not been resquiggled with Tombo — raw unanchored signal cannot be keyed by genome position Genome coverage of the native sample or WGA control is below the minimal coverage depth (default 40), making per-k-mer signal samples unreliable The goal is single-read modification calling per site rather than motif-level comparison of native vs WGA signal distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Extract normalized per-read signal events from Tombo-resquiggled multi-fast5 files using h5py/ont-tombo event data, and key each read's signal by genome position and strand so per-k-mer signal distributions can be compared between native and WGA control samples. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Extract normalized per-read signal events from Tombo-resquiggled multi-fast5 files using h5py/ont-tombo event data, and key each read's signal by genome position and strand so per-k-mer signal distributions can be compared between native and WGA control samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input fast5 files have not been resquiggled with Tombo — raw unanchored signal cannot be keyed by genome position Genome coverage of the native sample or WGA control is below the minimal coverage depth (default 40), making per-k-mer signal samples unreliable The goal is single-read modification calling per site rather than motif-level comparison of native vs WGA signal distributions

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore FAST5/POD5 reads have been basecalled and re-squiggled against a genome reference and per-base sequence-context plus raw-signal features are needed to train or run a methylation-calling model on cytosine sites.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-feature-extraction Use when raw Nanopore FAST5/POD5 reads have been basecalled and re-squiggled against a genome reference and per-base sequence-context plus raw-signal features are needed to train or run a methylation-calling model on cytosine sites. skills.description: Use when calling structural variants (deletions, inversions, translocations) from long nanopore reads at medium coverage (11–16×), or when reproducing the NanoSV SV discovery workflow from Cretu Stancu et al. 2017.
skills.name: nanopore-sv-calling
skills.search_text: nanopore-sv-calling Use when calling structural variants (deletions, inversions, translocations) from long nanopore reads at medium coverage (11–16×), or when reproducing the NanoSV SV discovery workflow from Cretu Stancu et al. 2017. Input is short-read Illumina data — NanoSV is designed for long reads (MinION/GridION/PromethION, PacBio RSII/Sequel); many SVs are missed in short-read data Coverage is too low for de novo assembly — the authors explicitly did not attempt a full genome assembly from MinION reads due to insufficient coverage The goal is comprehensive SV discovery in complex repeat regions and segmental duplications, which the authors flag as an unresolved challenge with conservative calling/filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Detect structural variants from Oxford Nanopore MinION long reads using the NanoSV pipeline (LAST mapping + split/gapped-read breakpoint clustering), achieving >95% precision with ~75% estimated sensitivity at 11–16× coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
