When the goal is single-molecule methylation accuracy or F1-score benchmarking rather than region-level coverage of profiled sites When BS-seq data are long-read or region-specific rather than short-read whole-genome, since the coverage advantage being tested depends on BS-seq's short-read limitation in repetitive regions When the species/platform is not plant R10.4 nanopore data, since DeepPlant's Bi-LSTM model and training set target plant CHH methylation on R10.4 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks nanopore-based 5mC methylation calls (e.g., DeepPlant on ONT R10.4 data) against whole-genome BS-seq by computing per-site CHH coverage ratios in hard-to-map regions like centromeres, where short-read BS-seq coverage collapses. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x

skills.search_text: nanopore-vs-bisulfite-cross-platform-comparison Use when comparing CpG site coverage between nanopore modification-call outputs (tsv with read_id, chromosome, pos_in_strand, strand, methylation_rate) and matched BS-seq calls across matched human or plant whole-genome datasets. skills.description: Use when a whole-genome shotgun long-read FASTQ (e.g. Oxford Nanopore PromethION WGS) needs HLA class I/II allele prediction, and disk/time-efficient single-command streaming of aligner output into HLAminer is preferred over writing SAM files to disk.

skills.search_text: nanopore-wgs-read-streaming Use when a whole-genome shotgun long-read FASTQ (e.g. Oxford Nanopore PromethION WGS) needs HLA class I/II allele prediction, and disk/time-efficient single-command streaming of aligner output into HLAminer is preferred over writing SAM files to disk. skills.summary: Stream minimap2 SAM alignments of ONT PromethION whole-genome shotgun reads directly into HLAminer v1.4 via a Unix pipe, eliminating bulky intermediate SAM files while predicting HLA class I and II alleles from ~10x coverage long-read data.

skills.search_text: nanoshape-reactivity-profiling Use when validating nanoSHAPE per-read reactivity (from current or dwell signal) against SHAPE-MaP on an AcIm-modified RNA such as pri-miR-17~92, or when determining how few reads are needed for a stable reactivity profile. skills.search_text: nascent-rna-observation-modeling Use when testing whether ODE kinetic parameters (synthesis, detachment, processing, export, translation, degradation rates) of an RNA life-cycle model are structurally identifiable from nascent RNA profiling observations. skills.description: Use when screening assembled FASTA genomes or contigs (especially NCBI records of Nanopore-derived assemblies) for leftover native barcoding kit barcode/adapters that signal contamination in the deposited sequence.

skills.search_text: native-barcoding-kit-adapter-detection Use when screening assembled FASTA genomes or contigs (especially NCBI records of Nanopore-derived assemblies) for leftover native barcoding kit barcode/adapters that signal contamination in the deposited sequence. Biological sequence features (repeats, integrons) that resemble barcodes only by chance — Fflank matches at random, non-terminal locations indicate spurious hits, not contamination footprints. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Detects remnant Nanopore native barcoding kit barcode sequences (e.g., NB02, NB13) left as contamination footprints in assembled genome records by approximate edit-distance search with Barbell's annotate/inspect commands. skills.description: Use when native Oxford Nanopore fast5 reads and a matched WGA control are available for the same strain and the goal is de novo detection of methylated bases and methylation motifs against a reference genome.

skills.description: Use when you have barcode-aware synthetic long-read data (10x Genomics Chromium, TELL-Seq, or stLFR) aligned to a reference genome such as GRCh38, and the goal is to discover non-reference sequence insertions >300 bp that short-read callers miss.

skills.search_text: novel-insertion-variant-calling Use when you have barcode-aware synthetic long-read data (10x Genomics Chromium, TELL-Seq, or stLFR) aligned to a reference genome such as GRCh38, and the goal is to discover non-reference sequence insertions >300 bp that short-read callers miss. The goal is to call small insertions: Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes per insertion, and for small insertions the number of associated barcodes is usually small and coverage is insufficient for anchor assembly. The data are plain short reads without barcode/linked-read information, since the method fundamentally depends on barcode and long-fragment information encoded in synthetic long reads. A full whole-genome de novo assembly is already available or required; Novel-X is designed to avoid whole-genome de novo assembly and only processes a small fraction of informative linked-reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Detects and genotypes non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions longer than 300 bp in synthetic long-read (linked-read) data using Novel-X, an integrated alignment-based and local assembly-based algorithm that leverages barcode information. It recovers large novel insertions that short-read methods fail to assemble and place, without whole-genome de novo assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Detects and genotypes non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions longer than 300 bp in synthetic long-read (linked-read) data using Novel-X, an integrated alignment-based and local assembly-based algorithm that leverages barcode information. It recovers large novel insertions that short-read methods fail to assemble and place, without whole-genome de novo assembly.

The algorithm is still running in floating point and no quantization parameter needs tuning Output agreement cannot be reduced to an exact-match or tolerance comparison against a float32 baseline (e.g., stochastic or non-deterministic outputs) The numeric range of the data exceeds 16-bit fixed-point representation even at moderate scaling factors (overflow dominates, as above factor 128 in HARU's sDTW) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Sweeps a numerical-precision parameter (fixed-point scaling factor) against float32 ground truth to characterize accuracy degradation, used by HARU to select a 16-bit fixed-point scaling factor of 32 for sDTW squiggle mapping (~99% accuracy). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Sweeps a numerical-precision parameter (fixed-point scaling factor) against float32 ground truth to characterize accuracy degradation, used by HARU to select a 16-bit fixed-point scaling factor of 32 for sDTW squiggle mapping (~99% accuracy).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The algorithm is still running in floating point and no quantization parameter needs tuning Output agreement cannot be reduced to an exact-match or tolerance comparison against a float32 baseline (e.g., stochastic or non-deterministic outputs) The numeric range of the data exceeds 16-bit fixed-point representation even at moderate scaling factors (overflow dominates, as above factor 128 in HARU's sDTW)

skills.description: Use when a per-read raw signal (measurements from a POD5 file) must be persisted as a standalone binary array for further processing in a NumPy environment, without dropping or duplicating any measurements.
skills.name: numpy-array-serialization
skills.search_text: numpy-array-serialization Use when a per-read raw signal (measurements from a POD5 file) must be persisted as a standalone binary array for further processing in a NumPy environment, without dropping or duplicating any measurements. The goal is interactive plotting of the signal rather than persistence — pod5Viewer subplots long signals to a maximum of 10000 measurements per signal via median binning, so do not round-trip through this skill for plotting The signal is already exported as text (one measurement per line) or JSON via pod5Viewer's other export formats and no .npy output is required Serialize a complete numeric signal (e.g. a full nanopore raw current signal read from a POD5 file) into a binary NumPy .npy file, mirroring pod5Viewer's 'Export signal' option. Chunked reading keeps memory bounded and preserves all measurements exactly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae665
skills.summary: Serialize a complete numeric signal (e.g. a full nanopore raw current signal read from a POD5 file) into a binary NumPy .npy file, mirroring pod5Viewer's 'Export signal' option. Chunked reading keeps memory bounded and preserves all measurements exactly.

skills.description: Use when a sorted, indexed BAM alignment of nanopore cDNA or Illumina TruSeq reads against an mRNA vaccine reference must be fractionated into on-target versus off-target RNA contaminant classes with fractional abundances.
skills.name: off-target-read-classification
skills.search_text: off-target-read-classification Use when a sorted, indexed BAM alignment of nanopore cDNA or Illumina TruSeq reads against an mRNA vaccine reference must be fractionated into on-target versus off-target RNA contaminant classes with fractional abundances. Input is raw FASTQ without a sorted, indexed BAM alignment to the mRNA/plasmid reference — barcode removal (Porechop), Q>9 filtering, and Minimap2 alignment must happen first The goal is per-nucleotide error profiles or consensus calling (use pysamstats/bcftools) rather than read-level on/off-target fractionation Analysis targets plasmid template DNA quality attributes rather than RNA contaminant fractions in cDNA libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Classifies aligned sequencing reads from mRNA vaccine (VAX-seq) cDNA libraries into on-target mRNA product versus off-target classes (upstream, downstream, antisense, cryptic TSS-derived, and contaminant reads such as E. coli), and reports the fractional abundance of each class. This quantifies mRNA purity, one of the key quality attributes VAX-seq measures. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Classifies aligned sequencing reads from mRNA vaccine (VAX-seq) cDNA libraries into on-target mRNA product versus off-target classes (upstream, downstream, antisense, cryptic TSS-derived, and contaminant reads such as E. coli), and reports the fractional abundance of each class. This quantifies mRNA purity, one of the key quality attributes VAX-seq measures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ without a sorted, indexed BAM alignment to the mRNA/plasmid reference — barcode removal (Porechop), Q>9 filtering, and Minimap2 alignment must happen first The goal is per-nucleotide error profiles or consensus calling (use pysamstats/bcftools) rather than read-level on/off-target fractionation Analysis targets plasmid template DNA quality attributes rather than RNA contaminant fractions in cDNA libraries

skills.search_text: olc-overlap-assembly-parameter-tuning Use when you have two or more Multi-FASTA files of assembled contigs (from different samples, assemblers, or platforms) and want to merge them into a single improved contig set via OLC assembly. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than already-assembled contigs — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process and expects FASTA contig files, not FASTQ reads Only a single assembly exists and no merging is desired — a single assembler run is the appropriate choice instead Input dataset is extremely large — overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size

skills.description: Use when performing pixel-level normalization on whole-slide MTI data stored as OME-TIFF stacks, where cell/nucleus segmentation masks must restrict analysis to in-cell pixels and output must remain uint16-compatible.
skills.name: ome-tiff-whole-slide-image-io
skills.search_text: ome-tiff-whole-slide-image-io Use when performing pixel-level normalization on whole-slide MTI data stored as OME-TIFF stacks, where cell/nucleus segmentation masks must restrict analysis to in-cell pixels and output must remain uint16-compatible. Input is already a single-cell feature table (cell x marker matrix); UniFORM's feature-level workflow does not need OME-TIFF stack IO. Data are mIHC chromogenic images; linear normalization factors are unsuitable because enzyme-catalyzed colorimetric amplification produces non-linear signal intensities. Normalization targets extracellular (non-cell) regions; UniFORM is currently optimized only for within-cell normalization via segmentation masks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Dask-backed reading of OME-TIFF whole-slide multiplex immunofluorescence stacks with nucleus/cell segmentation masks, and writing of the normalized intensity stack back as an OME-TIFF file, as used in UniFORM's pixel-level normalization pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172
skills.summary: Dask-backed reading of OME-TIFF whole-slide multiplex immunofluorescence stacks with nucleus/cell segmentation masks, and writing of the normalized intensity stack back as an OME-TIFF file, as used in UniFORM's pixel-level normalization pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single-cell feature table (cell x marker matrix); UniFORM's feature-level workflow does not need OME-TIFF stack IO. Data are mIHC chromogenic images; linear normalization factors are unsuitable because enzyme-catalyzed colorimetric amplification produces non-linear signal intensities. Normalization targets extracellular (non-cell) regions; UniFORM is currently optimized only for within-cell normalization via segmentation masks.

skills.name: ont-basecaller-guided-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: ont-basecaller-guided-loss-implementation Use when training a nanopore signal simulator on POD5/BAM-derived training chunks and you need a differentiable basecaller-guided CTC objective alongside signal-level MSE losses. Input is simulated signals already generated by a trained simulator — this skill is the training objective, not the simulate CLI path You only need basecalling of simulated reads into FASTQ/BAM — use the --basecall/--emit-bam options with Dorado instead No resquiggle-derived dwell times (dwells.npy) are available, since the MSE targets require per-base dwell assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements NanoSimFormer's multi-objective training loss, combining MSE terms on per-base mean signal level and noise standard deviation (from resquiggle-derived dwell times) with a CTC negative log-likelihood loss computed through a frozen pre-trained ONT Dorado basecaller. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Implements NanoSimFormer's multi-objective training loss, combining MSE terms on per-base mean signal level and noise standard deviation (from resquiggle-derived dwell times) with a CTC negative log-likelihood loss computed through a frozen pre-trained ONT Dorado basecaller.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated signals already generated by a trained simulator — this skill is the training objective, not the simulate CLI path You only need basecalling of simulated reads into FASTQ/BAM — use the --basecall/--emit-bam options with Dorado instead No resquiggle-derived dwell times (dwells.npy) are available, since the MSE targets require per-base dwell assignments

skills.name: ont-dataset-acquisition
skills.search_text: ont-dataset-acquisition Use when an analysis requires raw ONT long-read WGS FASTQ inputs (e.g., NA24385 guppy v5.0.6 ~67x or dorado kit14-2022-12 ~72x, NA19240 PromethION ~10x) to reproduce or benchmark HLA prediction workflows. The task needs short-read (Illumina-sized) data — HPTASR is the targeted-assembly route for 100-150bp reads, not ONT WGS FASTQ acquisition The analysis requires freshly base-called signal (POD5/FAST5) rather than published FASTQ base-calls The target individual lacks clinically confirmed HLA types, so the acquisition cannot support concordance validation as described Acquire Oxford Nanopore whole-genome shotgun FASTQ datasets (PromethION, clinically typed individuals such as NA19240 and NA24385) from public repositories (ENA/SRA/epi2me) as input for long-read HLA prediction with HLAminer. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Acquire Oxford Nanopore whole-genome shotgun FASTQ datasets (PromethION, clinically typed individuals such as NA19240 and NA24385) from public repositories (ENA/SRA/epi2me) as input for long-read HLA prediction with HLAminer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task needs short-read (Illumina-sized) data — HPTASR is the targeted-assembly route for 100-150bp reads, not ONT WGS FASTQ acquisition The analysis requires freshly base-called signal (POD5/FAST5) rather than published FASTQ base-calls The target individual lacks clinically confirmed HLA types, so the acquisition cannot support concordance validation as described

skills.search_text: ont-fast5-signal-data-processing Use when raw nanopore .fast5 files (single-read format) must be prepared as input for ONT signal-level methylation motif detection, e.g. before running Snapper on H.pylori J99 sample versus WGA-control reads. Input reads are already in multi-read fast5 format and resquiggled — reconverting or re-resquiggling is unnecessary and risks corrupting the signal index Analysis relies on modern basecalling-native POD5/BAM inputs with Remora, since Tombo is deprecated and unsupported by Oxford Nanopore Data is not Oxford Nanopore signal data (e.g. PacBio or Illumina reads), which lack .fast5 raw signal and cannot be resquiggled http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Preprocess Oxford Nanopore raw .fast5 signal data for methylation motif analysis by resquiggling reads against a reference genome with Tombo, then converting to the multi-read fast5 format with ont_fast5_api before running Snapper. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Preprocess Oxford Nanopore raw .fast5 signal data for methylation motif analysis by resquiggling reads against a reference genome with Tombo, then converting to the multi-read fast5 format with ont_fast5_api before running Snapper.

skills.description: Use when FASTQ files from ONT sequencing of 10x Genomics-derived amplicons or cDNA libraries must be converted into per-cell transcript classifications (e.g. CAR+ vs wildtype CD28) that short-read scRNA-seq fails to fully resolve.
skills.name: ont-long-read-fastq-processing
skills.search_text: ont-long-read-fastq-processing Use when FASTQ files from ONT sequencing of 10x Genomics-derived amplicons or cDNA libraries must be converted into per-cell transcript classifications (e.g. CAR+ vs wildtype CD28) that short-read scRNA-seq fails to fully resolve. The input is short-read (Illumina) scRNA-seq data, which the paper notes is suboptimal for long fragments and cannot easily resolve structural variants such as transgenes like CARs The analysis goal is whole-genome or unrestricted transcriptome profiling rather than targeted detection of specific loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes shorter than 4 kB The cDNA library is not 5'-anchored 10x Genomics chemistry, so cell barcodes and UMIs cannot be extracted from the long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Process Oxford Nanopore long-read FASTQ data from targeted amplicons or whole-transcriptome 10x Genomics 5'-anchored cDNA libraries with the nanoranger pipeline to detect cell lineage-defining features such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) transcripts and distinguish them from wildtype (e.g. CD28) transcripts at single-cell resolution. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Process Oxford Nanopore long-read FASTQ data from targeted amplicons or whole-transcriptome 10x Genomics 5'-anchored cDNA libraries with the nanoranger pipeline to detect cell lineage-defining features such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) transcripts and distinguish them from wildtype (e.g. CD28) transcripts at single-cell resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read (Illumina) scRNA-seq data, which the paper notes is suboptimal for long fragments and cannot easily resolve structural variants such as transgenes like CARs The analysis goal is whole-genome or unrestricted transcriptome profiling rather than targeted detection of specific loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes shorter than 4 kB The cDNA library is not 5'-anchored 10x Genomics chemistry, so cell barcodes and UMIs cannot be extracted from the long reads

skills.summary: Generates ONT-like long-read sequencing datasets with Pbsim3 v3.0.4 from reference genomes at controlled depths (e.g. 60x Human chr2, 30x Mouse chr2) to benchmark SNV callers such as miniSNV, Longshot, and Clair3 against known truth variants.

skills.search_text: ont-methylation-caller-benchmarking Use when comparing methylation-caller accuracy (e.g., DeepMod2 vs Guppy/Dorado) on Ashkenazim trio (HG002/HG003/HG004) ONT datasets against short-read ground truth using per-read/per-site F1 and correlation. skills.search_text: ont-read-alignment-realignment Use when ONT (or PacBio) reads are provided as alignments to a different reference (e.g. GRCh38) than the one required by the downstream variant-calling pipeline, or when reproducing the Clairvoyante HG001 chr1 benchmark. skills.description: Use when a draft or gap-filled long-read assembly (e.g., ntLink scaffolds incorporating raw ONT sequence) needs polishing, or when read-to-assembly alignments are required for downstream consensus correction and QUAST evaluation.
skills.name: ont-read-alignment-to-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: ont-read-alignment-to-genome-assembly Use when a draft or gap-filled long-read assembly (e.g., ntLink scaffolds incorporating raw ONT sequence) needs polishing, or when read-to-assembly alignments are required for downstream consensus correction and QUAST evaluation. The assembly is already polished or derived only from corrected reads (no raw long-read sequence was incorporated, e.g., outputs of Basic Protocol 1 overlap detection without gap-filling) The reads are not ONT data — minimap2's map-ont preset and this Racon workflow are specific to Oxford Nanopore reads A different scaffolding step (Tigmint-long correction or ntLink mapping per Alternate Protocols 1–2) is the actual goal rather than polishing http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns ONT long reads to a genome assembly (e.g., ntLink gap-filled scaffolds) with minimap2's map-ont preset and uses the resulting read-to-scaffold alignments as input for Racon consensus polishing to correct errors introduced by raw long-read gap filling. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Aligns ONT long reads to a genome assembly (e.g., ntLink gap-filled scaffolds) with minimap2's map-ont preset and uses the resulting read-to-scaffold alignments as input for Racon consensus polishing to correct errors introduced by raw long-read gap filling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly is already polished or derived only from corrected reads (no raw long-read sequence was incorporated, e.g., outputs of Basic Protocol 1 overlap detection without gap-filling) The reads are not ONT data — minimap2's map-ont preset and this Racon workflow are specific to Oxford Nanopore reads A different scaffolding step (Tigmint-long correction or ntLink mapping per Alternate Protocols 1–2) is the actual goal rather than polishing

skills.description: Use when raw ONT fastq.gz reads (e.g. HGSVC samples HG00733, HG00514, NA19240) must be aligned to a reference genome so that downstream long-read structural variant callers can be run.
skills.name: ont-read-alignment-to-reference
skills.search_text: ont-read-alignment-to-reference Use when raw ONT fastq.gz reads (e.g. HGSVC samples HG00733, HG00514, NA19240) must be aligned to a reference genome so that downstream long-read structural variant callers can be run. Input data is short-read Illumina or PacBio rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read fastq.gz — the pipeline is built for ONT reads You need only final consensus SV calls and already possess per-caller BAMs or VCFs — alignment would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Aligns Oxford Nanopore long-read FASTQ files to the hg38 reference genome with minimap2 (for CuteSV, Sniffles, Dysgu, SVIM, Nanovar) and pbmm2 (for PBSV) as the alignment stage of the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow pipeline, producing per-sample BAMs that feed six SV callers. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Aligns Oxford Nanopore long-read FASTQ files to the hg38 reference genome with minimap2 (for CuteSV, Sniffles, Dysgu, SVIM, Nanovar) and pbmm2 (for PBSV) as the alignment stage of the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow pipeline, producing per-sample BAMs that feed six SV callers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is short-read Illumina or PacBio rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read fastq.gz — the pipeline is built for ONT reads You need only final consensus SV calls and already possess per-caller BAMs or VCFs — alignment would be redundant

skills.description: Use when POD5/FAST5 reads have been basecalled with move tables and an aligned BAM is needed for reference-anchored signal-to-base alignment (e.g. DeepMod2 5mC calling) or per-site methylation frequencies.
skills.name: ont-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
skills.search_text: ont-read-alignment-to-reference-genome Use when POD5/FAST5 reads have been basecalled with move tables and an aligned BAM is needed for reference-anchored signal-to-base alignment (e.g. DeepMod2 5mC calling) or per-site methylation frequencies. Reads are already provided as an aligned BAM (e.g. Guppy/Dorado run with a reference supplied directly) — skip re-alignment and go straight to methylation detection Only de novo assembly or alignment-free analyses are planned and no reference genome is available Downstream methylation calling will run in unaligned/read-level-only mode, where the reference anchor is not used http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Align Dorado/Guppy-basecalled Oxford Nanopore reads to a reference genome (e.g. GRCh38) with minimap2 while preserving move-table tags, producing aligned BAMs that enable reference-anchored methylation detection with DeepMod2. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Align Dorado/Guppy-basecalled Oxford Nanopore reads to a reference genome (e.g. GRCh38) with minimap2 while preserving move-table tags, producing aligned BAMs that enable reference-anchored methylation detection with DeepMod2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already provided as an aligned BAM (e.g. Guppy/Dorado run with a reference supplied directly) — skip re-alignment and go straight to methylation detection Only de novo assembly or alignment-free analyses are planned and no reference genome is available Downstream methylation calling will run in unaligned/read-level-only mode, where the reference anchor is not used

skills.description: Use when benchmarking long-read phasing performance across sequencing depths, e.g., downsampling HG002 R9 ONT reads to 30X/60X/80X to test how methylation-based phasing N50 gains scale with coverage.
skills.name: ont-read-coverage-subsampling
skills.search_text: ont-read-coverage-subsampling Use when benchmarking long-read phasing performance across sequencing depths, e.g., downsampling HG002 R9 ONT reads to 30X/60X/80X to test how methylation-based phasing N50 gains scale with coverage. Phasing human sex chromosomes — MethPhaser does not work there due to random X inactivation, so the sweep must be limited to autosomes Data below ~30X coverage — most SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage, so the SNV baseline is unreliable Samples with very high SNV phasing errors (e.g., very high hamming distance in R9 80X results), where subsampled-depth comparison would negatively impact MethPhaser accuracy and confound the depth-effect estimate http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Subsampling deep ONT reads to controlled coverage levels (e.g., 30X, 60X, 80X) while preserving methylation tags, so that coverage-dependent effects on methylation-based phasing (phase block N50, switch error) can be quantified. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Subsampling deep ONT reads to controlled coverage levels (e.g., 30X, 60X, 80X) while preserving methylation tags, so that coverage-dependent effects on methylation-based phasing (phase block N50, switch error) can be quantified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Phasing human sex chromosomes — MethPhaser does not work there due to random X inactivation, so the sweep must be limited to autosomes Data below ~30X coverage — most SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage, so the SNV baseline is unreliable Samples with very high SNV phasing errors (e.g., very high hamming distance in R9 80X results), where subsampled-depth comparison would negatively impact MethPhaser accuracy and confound the depth-effect estimate

skills.description: Use when ONT long reads (e.g. SQK-LSK109 of a linearised pDNA template, concatenated FASTQ of Q>9 reads) must be partitioned into plasmid-mapped, host-contamination and failed-read fractions as a QC metric.
skills.name: ont-read-fate-fraction-reporting
skills.search_text: ont-read-fate-fraction-reporting Use when ONT long reads (e.g. SQK-LSK109 of a linearised pDNA template, concatenated FASTQ of Q>9 reads) must be partitioned into plasmid-mapped, host-contamination and failed-read fractions as a QC metric. Input reads are short Illumina reads quality-trimmed to Q20 with TrimGalore — this read-fate accounting is defined for ONT map-ont alignments The goal is mRNA product QC (sequence identity, poly(A) tail length, integrity) rather than plasmid template identity and contamination quantification Only per-nucleotide error profiles or variant calling are needed — use pysamstats or bcftools v1.15 instead of the read-fate fractioning http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies the fate fractions of Oxford Nanopore reads from a linearised plasmid DNA template run: the percentage mapping to the plasmid reference, the percentage attributable to E. coli carry-over contamination, and the percentage of failed reads, using Minimap2, SAMtools and Mana. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Quantifies the fate fractions of Oxford Nanopore reads from a linearised plasmid DNA template run: the percentage mapping to the plasmid reference, the percentage attributable to E. coli carry-over contamination, and the percentage of failed reads, using Minimap2, SAMtools and Mana.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads quality-trimmed to Q20 with TrimGalore — this read-fate accounting is defined for ONT map-ont alignments The goal is mRNA product QC (sequence identity, poly(A) tail length, integrity) rather than plasmid template identity and contamination quantification Only per-nucleotide error profiles or variant calling are needed — use pysamstats or bcftools v1.15 instead of the read-fate fractioning

skills.description: Use when you need simulated ONT sequencing data for benchmarking barcode kits or demultiplexing tools — e.g., ligating custom or official ONT kits onto reference genomes and producing FASTQ reads with realistic error profiles.
skills.name: ont-read-simulation-with-deepsimulator
skills.search_text: ont-read-simulation-with-deepsimulator Use when you need simulated ONT sequencing data for benchmarking barcode kits or demultiplexing tools — e.g., ligating custom or official ONT kits onto reference genomes and producing FASTQ reads with realistic error profiles. When real ONT read data are already available — simulation should not replace validation on experimental reads, and PRO's accuracy claims are simulation-based When the target platform is PacBio: the article states no tests on PacBio data have been performed, so simulation parameters are tuned for ONT only http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulates Oxford Nanopore sequencing reads by ligating a barcode kit onto raw DNA sequences (e.g., E. coli WGS and lambda phage reads) via a multisample library-preparation pipeline, then running DeepSimulator 1.5 to generate FASTQ read data for benchmarking demultiplexing tools. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
skills.summary: Simulates Oxford Nanopore sequencing reads by ligating a barcode kit onto raw DNA sequences (e.g., E. coli WGS and lambda phage reads) via a multisample library-preparation pipeline, then running DeepSimulator 1.5 to generate FASTQ read data for benchmarking demultiplexing tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When real ONT read data are already available — simulation should not replace validation on experimental reads, and PRO's accuracy claims are simulation-based When the target platform is PacBio: the article states no tests on PacBio data have been performed, so simulation parameters are tuned for ONT only

skills.description: Use when raw ONT signal data must be converted to basecalled FASTQ and you need to measure how Guppy basecaller mode (fast, hac, sup) affects read error rate and subsequent NanoSpring compression performance.
skills.name: ont-signal-basecalling
skills.search_text: ont-signal-basecalling Use when raw ONT signal data must be converted to basecalled FASTQ and you need to measure how Guppy basecaller mode (fast, hac, sup) affects read error rate and subsequent NanoSpring compression performance. Input is already a basecalled FASTQ with no raw signal available, so Guppy modes cannot be varied The goal requires compressed output that preserves read identifiers or quality values — NanoSpring explicitly does not compress them Basecaller error rates are far above the ~5% regime the approximate-assembly approach relies on (e.g. very old basecallers), where NanoSpring's compression gains are not expected http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Basecalls Oxford Nanopore raw signal data into FASTQ with Guppy in fast, high-accuracy (hac), and super-accurate (sup) modes, and quantifies how basecaller mode changes mean error rate and downstream NanoSpring compression (bits/base) on datasets such as S. aureus. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Basecalls Oxford Nanopore raw signal data into FASTQ with Guppy in fast, high-accuracy (hac), and super-accurate (sup) modes, and quantifies how basecaller mode changes mean error rate and downstream NanoSpring compression (bits/base) on datasets such as S. aureus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a basecalled FASTQ with no raw signal available, so Guppy modes cannot be varied The goal requires compressed output that preserves read identifiers or quality values — NanoSpring explicitly does not compress them Basecaller error rates are far above the ~5% regime the approximate-assembly approach relies on (e.g. very old basecallers), where NanoSpring's compression gains are not expected

skills.description: Use when ONT long-read RNA-seq AISO measurements (Fupfi distributions, upfi/dofi ratios) disagree with short-read results and 5'/3' truncation biases from long-read sequencing or library preparation are suspected.
skills.name: ont-truncation-bias-correction
skills.search_text: ont-truncation-bias-correction Use when ONT long-read RNA-seq AISO measurements (Fupfi distributions, upfi/dofi ratios) disagree with short-read results and 5'/3' truncation biases from long-read sequencing or library preparation are suspected. Data are short reads — truncation bias correction is specific to long-read sequencing and library preparation artifacts and is unnecessary for short-read AISO runs The goal is splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the exon of interest, which only long reads can provide and for which bias correction is not the limiting factor http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Applies Insplico's optional --biascorr module to correct 5' and 3' truncation biases in ONT direct-RNA long reads, so that long-read adjacent-intron splicing-order (AISO) patterns (upfi/dofi ratios) harmonize with the short-read reference distributions. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Applies Insplico's optional --biascorr module to correct 5' and 3' truncation biases in ONT direct-RNA long reads, so that long-read adjacent-intron splicing-order (AISO) patterns (upfi/dofi ratios) harmonize with the short-read reference distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are short reads — truncation bias correction is specific to long-read sequencing and library preparation artifacts and is unnecessary for short-read AISO runs The goal is splicing-order information beyond the introns directly flanking the exon of interest, which only long reads can provide and for which bias correction is not the limiting factor

skills.description: Use when evaluating how much a consensus-generation step (e.g., SPOA partial order alignment) reduces raw read error on error-prone third-generation sequencing data, or when comparing substitution/insertion/deletion error profiles between ONT and PacBio synthetic or real reads.
skills.name: ont-versus-pacbio-error-profile-comparison
skills.search_text: ont-versus-pacbio-error-profile-comparison Use when evaluating how much a consensus-generation step (e.g., SPOA partial order alignment) reduces raw read error on error-prone third-generation sequencing data, or when comparing substitution/insertion/deletion error profiles between ONT and PacBio synthetic or real reads. Input reads are already high-accuracy short reads (Illumina) where consensus correction is unnecessary and the ONT/PB error profiles do not apply The goal is TR genotyping or motif resolution rather than measuring consensus error reduction Reads come from unassembled regions (centromeres, telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies and compares per-base sequencing error rates of ONT versus PacBio long reads before and after POA-based consensus correction, as done in TRiCoLOR's REFER evaluation where consensus computation reduced error by ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Quantifies and compares per-base sequencing error rates of ONT versus PacBio long reads before and after POA-based consensus correction, as done in TRiCoLOR's REFER evaluation where consensus computation reduced error by ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already high-accuracy short reads (Illumina) where consensus correction is unnecessary and the ONT/PB error profiles do not apply The goal is TR genotyping or motif resolution rather than measuring consensus error reduction Reads come from unassembled regions (centromeres, telomeres), where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats

skills.description: Use when starting from an m6A-modification-bearing mapped gDNA modBAM and the goal is to identify accessible (open) chromatin regions as a per-genome BED and BedGraph for browser visualization.
skills.name: open-chromatin-bed-generation
skills.search_text: open-chromatin-bed-generation Use when starting from an m6A-modification-bearing mapped gDNA modBAM and the goal is to identify accessible (open) chromatin regions as a per-genome BED and BedGraph for browser visualization. Input is direct RNA or cDNA data — the open-chromatin workflow targets mapped BAMs with m6A modifications from genomic DNA; RNA/cDNA reads route to the kallisto/LR-Kallisto transcript quantification branch instead. The modBAM lacks m6A modification calls (e.g., unlabeled gDNA or a model without modification tagging) — modkit pileup would yield no accessibility signal. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Generates consolidated open-chromatin calls from m6A-labeled nanopore genomic DNA by running modkit (v0.5+) pileup on the mapped modBAM, filtering high-confidence m6A positions, and exporting a per-genome BED plus BedGraph tracks. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Generates consolidated open-chromatin calls from m6A-labeled nanopore genomic DNA by running modkit (v0.5+) pileup on the mapped modBAM, filtering high-confidence m6A positions, and exporting a per-genome BED plus BedGraph tracks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is direct RNA or cDNA data — the open-chromatin workflow targets mapped BAMs with m6A modifications from genomic DNA; RNA/cDNA reads route to the kallisto/LR-Kallisto transcript quantification branch instead. The modBAM lacks m6A modification calls (e.g., unlabeled gDNA or a model without modification tagging) — modkit pileup would yield no accessibility signal.

skills.description: Use when structural variant candidate regions have been converted to raw read-by-position matrices (rows = reads from a BAM, columns = genomic positions) and a fixed-size CNN input image (50x50x3) is required.
skills.name: opencv-image-resizing
skills.search_text: opencv-image-resizing Use when structural variant candidate regions have been converted to raw read-by-position matrices (rows = reads from a BAM, columns = genomic positions) and a fixed-size CNN input image (50x50x3) is required. Input is already a fixed-shape image (e.g. previously saved 50x50x3 PNG/NPZ) — re-resizing would double-resample the alignment features. The reads have not yet been extracted into a raw read-by-position matrix; this skill resizes matrices, it does not pull alignments from the BAM. Filtering is being done by rule-based VCF criteria rather than the ConsensuSV-ONT CNN, which is the only consumer of the 50x50x3 encoding. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Resizes raw per-variant read-by-position alignment matrices into fixed-shape 50x50x3 images so they can be consumed by the ConsensuSV-ONT convolutional neural network that filters high-quality structural variants from Oxford Nanopore long-read data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Resizes raw per-variant read-by-position alignment matrices into fixed-shape 50x50x3 images so they can be consumed by the ConsensuSV-ONT convolutional neural network that filters high-quality structural variants from Oxford Nanopore long-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fixed-shape image (e.g. previously saved 50x50x3 PNG/NPZ) — re-resizing would double-resample the alignment features. The reads have not yet been extracted into a raw read-by-position matrix; this skill resizes matrices, it does not pull alignments from the BAM. Filtering is being done by rule-based VCF criteria rather than the ConsensuSV-ONT CNN, which is the only consumer of the 50x50x3 encoding.

skills.description: Use when the phenotype is an ordered categorical trait (e.g., disease status undiagnosed/pre-disease/mild/moderate/severe or GOLD stages) coded 1-J with covariates, and a null model without SNP effects is needed for GWAS score testing.
skills.name: ordered-multinomial-model-fitting
skills.search_text: ordered-multinomial-model-fitting Use when the phenotype is an ordered categorical trait (e.g., disease status undiagnosed/pre-disease/mild/moderate/severe or GOLD stages) coded 1-J with covariates, and a null model without SNP effects is needed for GWAS score testing. The trait is continuous or binary — linear regression or logistic regression baselines are the appropriate models, not ordered multinomial regression Categories have no meaningful ordering — use multinomial regression that ignores ordinality instead The proportional odds assumption is heavily violated and a category-specific (non-proportional) model is required; the article notes existing tests for this violation are liberal and verification is difficult http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit an ordered multinomial (proportional odds, e.g. LogitLink) null model to an ordinal trait and covariates using OrdinalMultinomialModels.jl/OrdinalGWAS.jl, the first step of the ordinalgwas workflow before single-SNP score-test scanning. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22276
skills.summary: Fit an ordered multinomial (proportional odds, e.g. LogitLink) null model to an ordinal trait and covariates using OrdinalMultinomialModels.jl/OrdinalGWAS.jl, the first step of the ordinalgwas workflow before single-SNP score-test scanning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trait is continuous or binary — linear regression or logistic regression baselines are the appropriate models, not ordered multinomial regression Categories have no meaningful ordering — use multinomial regression that ignores ordinality instead The proportional odds assumption is heavily violated and a category-specific (non-proportional) model is required; the article notes existing tests for this violation are liberal and verification is difficult

skills.description: Use when you need simulated ordinal-trait GWAS replicates — J ordered categories, genotype dosage, covariates at n≈2500 — to benchmark empirical type I error and power of association tests before real-cohort analyses.
skills.name: ordinal-phenotype-data-simulation
skills.search_text: ordinal-phenotype-data-simulation Use when you need simulated ordinal-trait GWAS replicates — J ordered categories, genotype dosage, covariates at n≈2500 — to benchmark empirical type I error and power of association tests before real-cohort analyses. The trait is continuous/quantitative rather than taking ordered discrete values — linear regression is the appropriate model and the ordinal simulation framing does not apply. Phenotype categories are unordered (nominal) — the ordered multinomial machinery assumes ordered discrete categories. The goal is association testing on real cohort data (e.g., COPDGene or UK Biobank) rather than synthetic type I error/power benchmarking. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Generates synthetic ordinal-trait GWAS datasets (J ordered phenotype categories, SNP dosage, covariates, configurable SNP effect gamma) to estimate empirical type I error and power for ordered multinomial regression against linear, dichotomized-logistic, and multinomial baselines. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22276
skills.summary: Generates synthetic ordinal-trait GWAS datasets (J ordered phenotype categories, SNP dosage, covariates, configurable SNP effect gamma) to estimate empirical type I error and power for ordered multinomial regression against linear, dichotomized-logistic, and multinomial baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trait is continuous/quantitative rather than taking ordered discrete values — linear regression is the appropriate model and the ordinal simulation framing does not apply. Phenotype categories are unordered (nominal) — the ordered multinomial machinery assumes ordered discrete categories. The goal is association testing on real cohort data (e.g., COPDGene or UK Biobank) rather than synthetic type I error/power benchmarking.

skills.description: Use when you have full-length mRNA isoforms (FASTA plus GFF from PacBio lrCaptureSeq-style catalogs) and need to count or extract predicted ORFs/protein sequences per isoform and gene.
skills.name: orf-prediction-with-genomic-correction
skills.search_text: orf-prediction-with-genomic-correction Use when you have full-length mRNA isoforms (FASTA plus GFF from PacBio lrCaptureSeq-style catalogs) and need to count or extract predicted ORFs/protein sequences per isoform and gene. Input is raw short-read RNA-seq: typical read lengths <200 bp cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcripts, so isoform counts and full-length ORFs cannot be determined The isoform catalog has not yet been filtered (off-target transcripts, truncated transcripts, and low-abundance isoforms will corrupt ORF counts) The target genome is not mouse mm10 and no appropriate reference is available for genomic correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Predicts open reading frames (ORFs) from a filtered long-read isoform catalog (lrCaptureSeq of neural cell-surface molecules) using SQANTI v1.2 ORF prediction with genomic correction against the mm10 reference genome, to define predicted coding sequences and protein diversity. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Predicts open reading frames (ORFs) from a filtered long-read isoform catalog (lrCaptureSeq of neural cell-surface molecules) using SQANTI v1.2 ORF prediction with genomic correction against the mm10 reference genome, to define predicted coding sequences and protein diversity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short-read RNA-seq: typical read lengths <200 bp cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcripts, so isoform counts and full-length ORFs cannot be determined The isoform catalog has not yet been filtered (off-target transcripts, truncated transcripts, and low-abundance isoforms will corrupt ORF counts) The target genome is not mouse mm10 and no appropriate reference is available for genomic correction

skills.description: Use when you have predicted ORF peptide/protein FASTA from an isoform catalog and need in-silico trypsin digestion, reference-proteome diffing, or extraction of peptides absent from UniProt for targeted mass spectrometry.
skills.name: orf-protein-sequence-processing
skills.search_text: orf-protein-sequence-processing Use when you have predicted ORF peptide/protein FASTA from an isoform catalog and need in-silico trypsin digestion, reference-proteome diffing, or extraction of peptides absent from UniProt for targeted mass spectrometry. Input is raw transcript/GFF/abundance files rather than processed ORF protein sequences — use IsoPops database compilation and filtering (compile_raw_db/process_db/filter_db) first The goal is peptide identification from raw mass-spectrometry spectra (mzML/RAW) rather than building a predicted peptide reference from ORF sequences Protein sequences already come from a fully annotated reference proteome, so a UniProt-absence diff would be trivially empty http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Process predicted ORF protein sequences from an lrCaptureSeq/PacBio isoform catalog (managed with the IsoPops R package) into an in-silico tryptic peptide reference, and diff it against a reference proteome such as UniProt Mouse to extract unannotated peptides for MS validation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Process predicted ORF protein sequences from an lrCaptureSeq/PacBio isoform catalog (managed with the IsoPops R package) into an in-silico tryptic peptide reference, and diff it against a reference proteome such as UniProt Mouse to extract unannotated peptides for MS validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw transcript/GFF/abundance files rather than processed ORF protein sequences — use IsoPops database compilation and filtering (compile_raw_db/process_db/filter_db) first The goal is peptide identification from raw mass-spectrometry spectra (mzML/RAW) rather than building a predicted peptide reference from ORF sequences Protein sequences already come from a fully annotated reference proteome, so a UniProt-absence diff would be trivially empty

skills.description: Use when a list of predicted m6A sites from nanopore differential analysis needs independent support from antibody-based orthogonal methods, or when comparing tools' agreement rates and false-positive behavior.
skills.name: orthogonal-m6a-site-validation
skills.search_text: orthogonal-m6a-site-validation Use when a list of predicted m6A sites from nanopore differential analysis needs independent support from antibody-based orthogonal methods, or when comparing tools' agreement rates and false-positive behavior. Validating modification types other than m6A (e.g. m5C or pseudouridine) — the m6ACE-seq/miCLIP union covers m6A only Sites with fewer than 20 aligned reads in either condition, or adenosine sites whose absolute stoichiometry difference is <0.1 — CHEUI-diff does not test them Datasets lacking orthogonal antibody-based evidence (m6ACE-seq/miCLIP) for the same cell type; only the KO-only false-positive estimation would be possible http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Validate nanopore-derived differential m6A calls (e.g. CHEUI-diff on HEK293 WT vs METTL3-KO) by intersecting them with a union of m6ACE-seq and miCLIP sites and by estimating per-tool false positives from knock-out-only replicates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Validate nanopore-derived differential m6A calls (e.g. CHEUI-diff on HEK293 WT vs METTL3-KO) by intersecting them with a union of m6ACE-seq and miCLIP sites and by estimating per-tool false positives from knock-out-only replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Validating modification types other than m6A (e.g. m5C or pseudouridine) — the m6ACE-seq/miCLIP union covers m6A only Sites with fewer than 20 aligned reads in either condition, or adenosine sites whose absolute stoichiometry difference is <0.1 — CHEUI-diff does not test them Datasets lacking orthogonal antibody-based evidence (m6ACE-seq/miCLIP) for the same cell type; only the KO-only false-positive estimation would be possible

skills.description: Use when tuning a de novo clustering partition count for long-read 16S amplicon data and you need to quantify the OTU-inflation vs. consensus-accuracy trade-off across partition settings (1–7) on mock or known-composition communities.
skills.name: otu-count-partition-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: otu-count-partition-sensitivity-analysis Use when tuning a de novo clustering partition count for long-read 16S amplicon data and you need to quantify the OTU-inflation vs. consensus-accuracy trade-off across partition settings (1–7) on mock or known-composition communities. Data are raw noisy nanopore reads that have not been processed by chopSeq/INC-Seq consensus generation — the sweep assumes consensus reads as input The community composition is unknown (no reference 16S sequences), so consensus accuracy cannot be computed and only OTU-count trends are assessable The goal is taxonomic classification with a reference database rather than de novo partitioning-based clustering, which the paper argues risks incorrect mapping and discarding of reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A sensitivity-analysis skill that sweeps the nanoClust partition count (1–7 partitions) over chopSeq-processed INC-Seq consensus 16S rRNA reads from ONT MinION mock communities, quantifying how partition length trades off detected OTU count against consensus sequence accuracy. It reproduces the NanoAmpli-Seq Fig. 7 / Table 2 ablation showing that more partitions inflate OTU counts and degrade accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill that sweeps the nanoClust partition count (1–7 partitions) over chopSeq-processed INC-Seq consensus 16S rRNA reads from ONT MinION mock communities, quantifying how partition length trades off detected OTU count against consensus sequence accuracy. It reproduces the NanoAmpli-Seq Fig. 7 / Table 2 ablation showing that more partitions inflate OTU counts and degrade accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw noisy nanopore reads that have not been processed by chopSeq/INC-Seq consensus generation — the sweep assumes consensus reads as input The community composition is unknown (no reference 16S sequences), so consensus accuracy cannot be computed and only OTU-count trends are assessable The goal is taxonomic classification with a reference database rather than de novo partitioning-based clustering, which the paper argues risks incorrect mapping and discarding of reads

skills.description: Use when estimating mate-pair library insert-size mean/SD and read-pair orientation from aligned synthetic read pairs where extreme tail values (very small or very large inferred inserts) would distort the mean and standard deviation.
skills.name: outlier-trimming-statistics
skills.search_text: outlier-trimming-statistics Use when estimating mate-pair library insert-size mean/SD and read-pair orientation from aligned synthetic read pairs where extreme tail values (very small or very large inferred inserts) would distort the mean and standard deviation. The library is a real long-range mate-pair technology (e.g. 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL genomics) where linking information comes from a range of insert sizes and read-pair orientation may be unknown — the paper notes gap-size estimation there is more challenging than with Fast-SG synthetic libraries The input is already a per-library statistics table — no re-trimming or re-estimation is needed The long reads are shorter than the requested insert size, since Fast-SG restricts the insert size to the actual long-read length and no valid pairs can be extracted Estimates per-library mate-pair statistics (mean insert size, standard deviation, FR/RF orientation) by computing them from same-contig aligned synthetic read pairs after symmetrically trimming the lowest and highest 10% of the insert-size distribution as outliers, as done in the Fast-SG hybrid assembly workflow. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Estimates per-library mate-pair statistics (mean insert size, standard deviation, FR/RF orientation) by computing them from same-contig aligned synthetic read pairs after symmetrically trimming the lowest and highest 10% of the insert-size distribution as outliers, as done in the Fast-SG hybrid assembly workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The library is a real long-range mate-pair technology (e.g. 10X Genomics or DOVETAIL genomics) where linking information comes from a range of insert sizes and read-pair orientation may be unknown — the paper notes gap-size estimation there is more challenging than with Fast-SG synthetic libraries The input is already a per-library statistics table — no re-trimming or re-estimation is needed The long reads are shorter than the requested insert size, since Fast-SG restricts the insert size to the actual long-read length and no valid pairs can be extracted

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how sequencing parameters (read length, coverage depth, accuracy) affect overlap graph quality of a long-read overlap detector on simulated data with known ground truth.
skills.name: overlap-detection-benchmarking-on-simulated-reads
skills.search_text: overlap-detection-benchmarking-on-simulated-reads Use when you need to quantify how sequencing parameters (read length, coverage depth, accuracy) affect overlap graph quality of a long-read overlap detector on simulated data with known ground truth. The goal is de novo genome assembly rather than overlap graph quality evaluation — use the full assembler integration (Fedrann-Shasta) instead. Input is real sequencing data without a ground-truth reference alignment (e.g., ONT R9 SRR10028111 or PacBio HiFi HG002); use the real-data benchmarking workflows from kNN-overlap-finder rather than simulation-based error-rate scoring. You need end-to-end assembly quality metrics (BUSCO primates_odb10, contiguity) rather than overlap-level error rates. Benchmark overlap-detection pipelines (e.g., Fedrann) on simulated long-read datasets by sweeping read length, coverage, and sequencing accuracy, then scoring predicted overlaps against minimap2-derived ground truth as overlap graph error rates. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Benchmark overlap-detection pipelines (e.g., Fedrann) on simulated long-read datasets by sweeping read length, coverage, and sequencing accuracy, then scoring predicted overlaps against minimap2-derived ground truth as overlap graph error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo genome assembly rather than overlap graph quality evaluation — use the full assembler integration (Fedrann-Shasta) instead. Input is real sequencing data without a ground-truth reference alignment (e.g., ONT R9 SRR10028111 or PacBio HiFi HG002); use the real-data benchmarking workflows from kNN-overlap-finder rather than simulation-based error-rate scoring. You need end-to-end assembly quality metrics (BUSCO primates_odb10, contiguity) rather than overlap-level error rates.

Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than a candidate overlap set from a detection tool The goal is assembly-quality assessment (e.g. BUSCO/primates_odb10 completeness, contiguity of Fedrann-Shasta assemblies) rather than overlap graph quality The application is a downstream use of overlaps (e.g. metagenomic binning, taxonomic classification) which the authors note lacks empirical validation of these metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Evaluates candidate overlap sets from long-read overlap detection tools (Fedrann, minimap2, MECAT2, MHAP, wtdbg2, xRead, BLEND) by scoring error rate, mean overlap size, #COC, #CC, runtime, and peak memory per tool-dataset pair against reference-based ground-truth alignments. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Evaluates candidate overlap sets from long-read overlap detection tools (Fedrann, minimap2, MECAT2, MHAP, wtdbg2, xRead, BLEND) by scoring error rate, mean overlap size, #COC, #CC, runtime, and peak memory per tool-dataset pair against reference-based ground-truth alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than a candidate overlap set from a detection tool The goal is assembly-quality assessment (e.g. BUSCO/primates_odb10 completeness, contiguity of Fedrann-Shasta assemblies) rather than overlap graph quality The application is a downstream use of overlaps (e.g. metagenomic binning, taxonomic classification) which the authors note lacks empirical validation of these metrics

skills.description: Use when a candidate overlap graph from an overlap detection tool must be judged against truth/reference overlaps on long-read datasets, e.g. comparing Fedrann weighting x metric configurations or tools like minimap2 and MECAT2.
skills.name: overlap-graph-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: overlap-graph-quality-assessment Use when a candidate overlap graph from an overlap detection tool must be judged against truth/reference overlaps on long-read datasets, e.g. comparing Fedrann weighting x metric configurations or tools like minimap2 and MECAT2. Input is a feature matrix or dimensionality-reduced embedding rather than a set of candidate overlaps — evaluation requires a concrete overlap graph No reference truth overlaps are available (e.g. unassembled novel sample with no ground-truth mapping), so error rates cannot be computed The goal is end-to-end assembly quality (contiguity, BUSCO) rather than overlap graph accuracy — use assembler-level metrics instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scores overlap graphs (e.g. Fedrann's overlaps.tsv) against reference truth overlaps by applying alignment filters (>= 100 matched bases, >= 10% identity) and computing overlap error rates, enabling benchmark comparison across tool or parameter configurations. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Scores overlap graphs (e.g. Fedrann's overlaps.tsv) against reference truth overlaps by applying alignment filters (>= 100 matched bases, >= 10% identity) and computing overlap error rates, enabling benchmark comparison across tool or parameter configurations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature matrix or dimensionality-reduced embedding rather than a set of candidate overlaps — evaluation requires a concrete overlap graph No reference truth overlaps are available (e.g. unassembled novel sample with no ground-truth mapping), so error rates cannot be computed The goal is end-to-end assembly quality (contiguity, BUSCO) rather than overlap graph accuracy — use assembler-level metrics instead

skills.description: Use when you have pooled Multi-FASTA contig files from several assemblies (e.g. SOAPdenovo, Velvet, IDBA, Ray across Kmers 51-71) and need one improved contig set without re-sequencing data replication.
skills.name: overlap-layout-consensus-contig-merging
skills.search_text: overlap-layout-consensus-contig-merging Use when you have pooled Multi-FASTA contig files from several assemblies (e.g. SOAPdenovo, Velvet, IDBA, Ray across Kmers 51-71) and need one improved contig set without re-sequencing data replication. Input is already a single, final contig set with no alternative assemblies to merge — dereplication and OLC merging would add little and may introduce new chimeras The dataset is very large: overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size The input is raw reads or FASTQ data rather than already-assembled contig FASTAs — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Merges contigs from multiple independent metagenomic assemblies (different assemblers and/or Kmers) into an improved, non-replicated contig set via MeGAMerge, a Perl wrapper that dereplicates inputs, bins contigs at a 2.0 kb cutoff, reassembles small contigs with Newbler, and merges everything with Minimus2 (OLC-based, AMOS toolbox). genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Merges contigs from multiple independent metagenomic assemblies (different assemblers and/or Kmers) into an improved, non-replicated contig set via MeGAMerge, a Perl wrapper that dereplicates inputs, bins contigs at a 2.0 kb cutoff, reassembles small contigs with Newbler, and merges everything with Minimus2 (OLC-based, AMOS toolbox).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single, final contig set with no alternative assemblies to merge — dereplication and OLC merging would add little and may introduce new chimeras The dataset is very large: overlap-based consensus tools' run-times increase exponentially with increasing input dataset size The input is raw reads or FASTQ data rather than already-assembled contig FASTAs — MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process

skills.description: Use when you have raw fast5-derived basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) for a small genome and need a de novo draft assembly whose error rate will be compared across basecallers.
skills.name: overlap-layout-consensus-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: overlap-layout-consensus-genome-assembly Use when you have raw fast5-derived basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) for a small genome and need a de novo draft assembly whose error rate will be compared across basecallers. The goal is read-level basecalling accuracy comparison rather than assembly-level error comparison (align reads to the reference with graphmap instead) Input is already an assembled genome with no underlying basecalled reads available for Racon polishing The genome is large/human-scale — the paper's workflow was applied to bacterial and viral genomes (Lambda, E. coli, M. tuberculosis), not large eukaryotic assemblies http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 De novo assembly of nanopore basecalled reads via an overlap-layout-consensus pipeline: build a draft genome by aligning overlapping reads with Minimap2 and laying out the assembly with Miniasm, then polish with 10 rounds of Racon before evaluating assembly error against a reference. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: De novo assembly of nanopore basecalled reads via an overlap-layout-consensus pipeline: build a draft genome by aligning overlapping reads with Minimap2 and laying out the assembly with Miniasm, then polish with 10 rounds of Racon before evaluating assembly error against a reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is read-level basecalling accuracy comparison rather than assembly-level error comparison (align reads to the reference with graphmap instead) Input is already an assembled genome with no underlying basecalled reads available for Racon polishing The genome is large/human-scale — the paper's workflow was applied to bacterial and viral genomes (Lambda, E. coli, M. tuberculosis), not large eukaryotic assemblies

skills.description: Use when self-correcting PacBio or ONT long reads from a FASTA/FASTQ input without external short-read or reference data, or when benchmarking MSA segmentation strategies on high-error-rate (e.g. 12%) simulated read sets.
skills.name: overlap-multiple-sequence-alignment
skills.search_text: overlap-multiple-sequence-alignment Use when self-correcting PacBio or ONT long reads from a FASTA/FASTQ input without external short-read or reference data, or when benchmarking MSA segmentation strategies on high-error-rate (e.g. 12%) simulated read sets. The goal is polishing an existing assembly rather than correcting reads — use CONSENT-polish instead (CONSENT-polish --contigs ... --reads ... --out ...). Only N-highest-identity overlap selection may be inefficient when repeated regions are very long, so accuracy on long repeats should not be assumed from this skill alone. Correction of organisms far larger/ more complex than those benchmarked (e.g. full human datasets require ~10 days and ~5 TB disk for the overlaps file) — resource-constrained settings should not attempt this blindly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Compute windowed multiple sequence alignments (MSA) over overlapping regions of long reads to derive consensus sequences for self-correction, using CONSENT's k-mer-chaining segmentation strategy to shrink each MSA instance. This is the core correction mechanism of CONSENT, combining overlap piles, windowed MSA consensus, and local de Bruijn graph polishing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Compute windowed multiple sequence alignments (MSA) over overlapping regions of long reads to derive consensus sequences for self-correction, using CONSENT's k-mer-chaining segmentation strategy to shrink each MSA instance. This is the core correction mechanism of CONSENT, combining overlap piles, windowed MSA consensus, and local de Bruijn graph polishing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is polishing an existing assembly rather than correcting reads — use CONSENT-polish instead (CONSENT-polish --contigs ... --reads ... --out ...). Only N-highest-identity overlap selection may be inefficient when repeated regions are very long, so accuracy on long repeats should not be assumed from this skill alone. Correction of organisms far larger/ more complex than those benchmarked (e.g. full human datasets require ~10 days and ~5 TB disk for the overlaps file) — resource-constrained settings should not attempt this blindly.

skills.description: Use when comparing TE insertion callers on PacBio long-read BAMs and you need per-caller true-positive counts scored against an assembly-based callset, e.g. reproducing Table 3 on HG002/HG01071.
skills.name: pacbio-bam-variant-calling-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pacbio-bam-variant-calling-benchmarking Use when comparing TE insertion callers on PacBio long-read BAMs and you need per-caller true-positive counts scored against an assembly-based callset, e.g. reproducing Table 3 on HG002/HG01071. Input reads are short-read (Illumina) rather than PacBio/ONT long reads — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data The goal is calling arbitrary non-TE variants rather than transposable element insertions, and no TE sequence FASTA is available No assembly-based truth callset exists to score true positives against http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark transposable element insertion (TEI) callers (sTELLeR, TLDR, xTEA) on GRCh38-realigned PacBio BAMs by counting true positives against an assembly-based truth callset, as done for HG002 and HG01071 in the sTELLeR paper (Table 3). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Benchmark transposable element insertion (TEI) callers (sTELLeR, TLDR, xTEA) on GRCh38-realigned PacBio BAMs by counting true positives against an assembly-based truth callset, as done for HG002 and HG01071 in the sTELLeR paper (Table 3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short-read (Illumina) rather than PacBio/ONT long reads — sTELLeR is designed and tested for long-read data The goal is calling arbitrary non-TE variants rather than transposable element insertions, and no TE sequence FASTA is available No assembly-based truth callset exists to score true positives against

skills.description: Use when you have aligned PacBio HiFi/CCS BAMs and need per-read, single-molecule CpG methylation probabilities using native kinetics (IPD/PW) features, or when benchmarking ccsmeth vs primrose read-level 5mC calling.
skills.name: pacbio-ccs-kinetics-feature-inference
skills.search_text: pacbio-ccs-kinetics-feature-inference Use when you have aligned PacBio HiFi/CCS BAMs and need per-read, single-molecule CpG methylation probabilities using native kinetics (IPD/PW) features, or when benchmarking ccsmeth vs primrose read-level 5mC calling. Detection of non-CpG 5mC or other DNA modifications such as 6mA — the article states ccsmeth 'cannot be applied for 5mC detection in non-CpGs or the detection of other DNA modifications (such as 6mA)' Detection of hemimethylated CpGs — the models only consider symmetric methylation Site-level (pooled) methylation frequencies rather than single-molecule read-level calls — use the site-level ccsmeth model or aligned_bam_to_cpg_scores instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Deep-learning read-level 5mCpG detection on PacBio circular consensus sequencing (HiFi) reads using kinetic features (IPDs and pulse widths) via ccsmeth's pre-trained model, benchmarked against primrose on long (≥10 Kb) reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Deep-learning read-level 5mCpG detection on PacBio circular consensus sequencing (HiFi) reads using kinetic features (IPDs and pulse widths) via ccsmeth's pre-trained model, benchmarked against primrose on long (≥10 Kb) reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Detection of non-CpG 5mC or other DNA modifications such as 6mA — the article states ccsmeth 'cannot be applied for 5mC detection in non-CpGs or the detection of other DNA modifications (such as 6mA)' Detection of hemimethylated CpGs — the models only consider symmetric methylation Site-level (pooled) methylation frequencies rather than single-molecule read-level calls — use the site-level ccsmeth model or aligned_bam_to_cpg_scores instead

skills.description: Use when you need to estimate nucleotide-level error rates of de novo transcript consensus sequences from PacBio Iso-Seq data, using independent Illumina short-read validation (≥2 agreeing reads per position).
skills.name: pacbio-ccs-read-error-assessment
skills.search_text: pacbio-ccs-read-error-assessment Use when you need to estimate nucleotide-level error rates of de novo transcript consensus sequences from PacBio Iso-Seq data, using independent Illumina short-read validation (≥2 agreeing reads per position). When no matching Illumina library exists for a primer pair-sample combination, since the ≥2-agreeing-read criterion cannot be evaluated for those transcripts When the goal is assigning transcripts to individual gene copies — the paper states IsoCon/transcriptome-only sequencing 'does not allow us to conclusively assign each transcript to a gene copy' When reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline to remove primers, barcodes, and chimeras, since the methods assume cleaned FLNC input http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies nucleotide-level accuracy of predicted Iso-Seq transcript consensus sequences (IsoCon, ICE, Illumina-corrected CCS, and original CCS reads) by counting positions supported by at least two agreeing Illumina reads. This reproduces the Fig. 3 validation from the IsoCon paper comparing error rates across the four transcript-calling approaches. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
