This reproduces the Fig. 3 validation from the IsoCon paper comparing error rates across the four transcript-calling approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no matching Illumina library exists for a primer pair-sample combination, since the ≥2-agreeing-read criterion cannot be evaluated for those transcripts When the goal is assigning transcripts to individual gene copies — the paper states IsoCon/transcriptome-only sequencing 'does not allow us to conclusively assign each transcript to a gene copy' When reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline to remove primers, barcodes, and chimeras, since the methods assume cleaned FLNC input

skills.description: Use when calling 5mCpG methylation states at single-molecule (per-read) resolution from long (≥10 Kb) PacBio CCS/HiFi reads (subreads.bam or hifi.bam), or when benchmarking read-level 5mC classifiers on M.SssI-methylated vs PCR-treated control datasets.
skills.name: pacbio-ccs-read-level-5mc-classification
skills.search_text: pacbio-ccs-read-level-5mc-classification Use when calling 5mCpG methylation states at single-molecule (per-read) resolution from long (≥10 Kb) PacBio CCS/HiFi reads (subreads.bam or hifi.bam), or when benchmarking read-level 5mC classifiers on M.SssI-methylated vs PCR-treated control datasets. The goal is detection of hemimethylated CpGs — ccsmeth and similar methods only consider symmetric methylation and are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs The target is 5mC at non-CpG contexts or other DNA modifications such as 6mA — ccsmeth's read-level model is designed for 5mCpG only Only genome-wide aggregated site-level methylation frequencies (e.g. bedmethyl) are needed — a site-level model or pileup tool is more appropriate than per-read classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Detect 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites (5mCpG) per single read using a deep-learning model (ccsmeth) trained on kinetics features (IPDs and PWs) of PacBio circular consensus sequencing (CCS) reads, benchmarked against CNN-based baselines such as the HK model and primrose. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Detect 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites (5mCpG) per single read using a deep-learning model (ccsmeth) trained on kinetics features (IPDs and PWs) of PacBio circular consensus sequencing (CCS) reads, benchmarked against CNN-based baselines such as the HK model and primrose.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detection of hemimethylated CpGs — ccsmeth and similar methods only consider symmetric methylation and are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs The target is 5mC at non-CpG contexts or other DNA modifications such as 6mA — ccsmeth's read-level model is designed for 5mCpG only Only genome-wide aggregated site-level methylation frequencies (e.g. bedmethyl) are needed — a site-level model or pileup tool is more appropriate than per-read classification

skills.description: Use when input is PacBio Iso-seq CCS read FASTA from long-read transcriptome sequencing and it must be prepared/filtered before TAGET alignment, annotation, or fusion detection.
skills.name: pacbio-ccs-read-processing
skills.search_text: pacbio-ccs-read-processing Use when input is PacBio Iso-seq CCS read FASTA from long-read transcriptome sequencing and it must be prepared/filtered before TAGET alignment, annotation, or fusion detection. Input is short-read RNA-seq (e.g., Illumina FASTQ) rather than PacBio Iso-seq CCS reads — the cluster filtering logic does not apply The analysis goal is to maximize gene detection at low coverage: filtering single-read CCS clusters discards ~80% of reads, many from true expressed isoforms, so alternative tools that use these reads may be preferable The data are already full-length transcript FASTA post-filtering and only alignment/annotation (TransAnnot.py) is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Handles PacBio Iso-seq CCS reads as input to TAGET, including the quality-motivated filtering of circular-consensus-sequence read clusters that contain only a single read, which feeds TAGET's transcript alignment, annotation, and gene fusion detection. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Handles PacBio Iso-seq CCS reads as input to TAGET, including the quality-motivated filtering of circular-consensus-sequence read clusters that contain only a single read, which feeds TAGET's transcript alignment, annotation, and gene fusion detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq (e.g., Illumina FASTQ) rather than PacBio Iso-seq CCS reads — the cluster filtering logic does not apply The analysis goal is to maximize gene detection at low coverage: filtering single-read CCS clusters discards ~80% of reads, many from true expressed isoforms, so alternative tools that use these reads may be preferable The data are already full-length transcript FASTA post-filtering and only alignment/annotation (TransAnnot.py) is needed

skills.description: Use when running IsoCon's statistical filtering (stat_filter) on targeted Iso-Seq FLNC reads in fastq/fasta and per-read error probabilities must be extracted from Phred quality values to compute candidate-significance p-values.
skills.name: pacbio-iso-seq-read-quality-parsing
skills.search_text: pacbio-iso-seq-read-quality-parsing Use when running IsoCon's statistical filtering (stat_filter) on targeted Iso-Seq FLNC reads in fastq/fasta and per-read error probabilities must be extracted from Phred quality values to compute candidate-significance p-values. Reads are raw, unprocessed PacBio output that has not gone through the Iso-Seq pipeline for primer/barcode removal and chimera filtering — IsoCon assumes pre-processed FLNC reads. Reads do not span the region of interest end-to-end (e.g., fragmented or short reads), since the weighted-support statistic requires reads spanning variant positions across the transcript. The goal is general transcript quantification or reference-based isoform annotation rather than de novo resolution of highly similar gene-copy transcripts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Parses per-read base error probabilities from PacBio Iso-Seq FLNC read quality strings (Phred scores) and log-normalizes them to feed IsoCon's weighted-support statistic T = prod(1/p_i^{s_i}) used in candidate hypothesis testing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Parses per-read base error probabilities from PacBio Iso-Seq FLNC read quality strings (Phred scores) and log-normalizes them to feed IsoCon's weighted-support statistic T = prod(1/p_i^{s_i}) used in candidate hypothesis testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are raw, unprocessed PacBio output that has not gone through the Iso-Seq pipeline for primer/barcode removal and chimera filtering — IsoCon assumes pre-processed FLNC reads. Reads do not span the region of interest end-to-end (e.g., fragmented or short reads), since the weighted-support statistic requires reads spanning variant positions across the transcript. The goal is general transcript quantification or reference-based isoform annotation rather than de novo resolution of highly similar gene-copy transcripts.

skills.description: Use when input is a raw PacBio CCS BAM with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) that must be quality-filtered before Z-Calling base calling, SVM read classification, or metagenome dZ-source detection.
skills.name: pacbio-kinetic-read-filtering
skills.search_text: pacbio-kinetic-read-filtering Use when input is a raw PacBio CCS BAM with kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) that must be quality-filtered before Z-Calling base calling, SVM read classification, or metagenome dZ-source detection. Input reads lack the kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) — e.g. CCS BAMs generated without the '--keep-kinetics' option — since filtering and all Z-Calling models depend on PW/IPD signals Input is short-read (Illumina/ONT) data rather than PacBio CCS HiFi reads, where PW/IPD kinetics do not exist The goal is site-specific A/Z calling on already-filtered BAMs — re-filtering could discard reads needed for per-site Z-frequency aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Pre-processing step of the Z-Calling pipeline that removes PacBio CCS reads lacking kinetic tags, poor Median_PW/Median_IPD signal quality, or insufficient polymerase passes, so that downstream dZ-DNA base calling and read classification operate on reliable kinetic signals. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: Pre-processing step of the Z-Calling pipeline that removes PacBio CCS reads lacking kinetic tags, poor Median_PW/Median_IPD signal quality, or insufficient polymerase passes, so that downstream dZ-DNA base calling and read classification operate on reliable kinetic signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack the kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) — e.g. CCS BAMs generated without the '--keep-kinetics' option — since filtering and all Z-Calling models depend on PW/IPD signals Input is short-read (Illumina/ONT) data rather than PacBio CCS HiFi reads, where PW/IPD kinetics do not exist The goal is site-specific A/Z calling on already-filtered BAMs — re-filtering could discard reads needed for per-site Z-frequency aggregation

skills.description: Use when PacBio CCS BAM files contain kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) and the goal is per-base PW/IPD feature extraction around A/Z target bases for dZ-DNA detection or kinetic shift analysis.
skills.name: pacbio-kinetic-signal-extraction
skills.search_text: pacbio-kinetic-signal-extraction Use when PacBio CCS BAM files contain kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) and the goal is per-base PW/IPD feature extraction around A/Z target bases for dZ-DNA detection or kinetic shift analysis. Input reads lack kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) or CCS BAMs were produced without '--keep-kinetics', since PW/IPD signals are absent The goal is ONT ionic-current analysis rather than PacBio polymerase kinetics — the article notes ONT relies on ionic-current perturbations, a different signal modality You only need read-level dZ-DNA vs canonical classification — the SVM read classifier (z-calling-read, min_len >= 500, intervals = 100) is the appropriate tool instead of per-base k-mer extraction Extract pulse width (PW) and inter-pulse duration (IPD) kinetic signals from PacBio HiFi/CCS BAMs, filter reads by kinetic quality (fi/ri/fp/rp tags, Median_PW/Median_IPD ≥ 0.3 and ≤ 99th percentile, fn/rn ≥ 3), and build single-A/Z 21-mer context k-mer feature tables for Z/A discrimination and downstream modeling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: Extract pulse width (PW) and inter-pulse duration (IPD) kinetic signals from PacBio HiFi/CCS BAMs, filter reads by kinetic quality (fi/ri/fp/rp tags, Median_PW/Median_IPD ≥ 0.3 and ≤ 99th percentile, fn/rn ≥ 3), and build single-A/Z 21-mer context k-mer feature tables for Z/A discrimination and downstream modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack kinetic tags (fi, ri, fp, rp) or CCS BAMs were produced without '--keep-kinetics', since PW/IPD signals are absent The goal is ONT ionic-current analysis rather than PacBio polymerase kinetics — the article notes ONT relies on ionic-current perturbations, a different signal modality You only need read-level dZ-DNA vs canonical classification — the SVM read classifier (z-calling-read, min_len >= 500, intervals = 100) is the appropriate tool instead of per-base k-mer extraction

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth-controlled hybrid sequencing data (short + long reads) to benchmark genome assemblers on misassemblies, NGA50, genome fraction, runtime, and memory.
skills.name: pacbio-long-read-simulation
skills.search_text: pacbio-long-read-simulation Use when you need ground-truth-controlled hybrid sequencing data (short + long reads) to benchmark genome assemblers on misassemblies, NGA50, genome fraction, runtime, and memory. You need to benchmark on real, previously published sequencing data — use the paper's real datasets (e.g., E. coli Loman lab ultra-long Nanopore reads with Illumina MiSeq, yeast ERX1725434/ERX1725435/ERX1725441 PacBio with ERX1943903 Illumina, C. elegans DevNet PacBio with SRR065390, CHM1 SRP044331 PacBio with SRX652547) instead of simulation The goal is phased assembly of diploid genomes — the paper states the current HASLR version does not generate phased assemblies Reads are high-fidelity (e.g., PacBio HiFi/CCS) rather than error-prone long reads — HASLR is designed for error-prone PacBio/ONT long reads combined with Illumina short reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Simulate 50x paired-end Illumina short reads (ART) and 50x PacBio long reads (PBSIM) from reference genomes (E. coli, yeast, C. elegans, human) to build controlled benchmark datasets for comparing hybrid assemblers such as HASLR against alternatives using QUAST metrics. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: Simulate 50x paired-end Illumina short reads (ART) and 50x PacBio long reads (PBSIM) from reference genomes (E. coli, yeast, C. elegans, human) to build controlled benchmark datasets for comparing hybrid assemblers such as HASLR against alternatives using QUAST metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to benchmark on real, previously published sequencing data — use the paper's real datasets (e.g., E. coli Loman lab ultra-long Nanopore reads with Illumina MiSeq, yeast ERX1725434/ERX1725435/ERX1725441 PacBio with ERX1943903 Illumina, C. elegans DevNet PacBio with SRR065390, CHM1 SRP044331 PacBio with SRX652547) instead of simulation The goal is phased assembly of diploid genomes — the paper states the current HASLR version does not generate phased assemblies Reads are high-fidelity (e.g., PacBio HiFi/CCS) rather than error-prone long reads — HASLR is designed for error-prone PacBio/ONT long reads combined with Illumina short reads

skills.description: Use when raw PacBio CLR (or ONT) FASTQ/FASTA reads from mixed samples such as metagenomes or polyploid genomes must be error-corrected without masking true low-frequency haplotype variants.
skills.name: pacbio-metagenome-read-correction
skills.search_text: pacbio-metagenome-read-correction Use when raw PacBio CLR (or ONT) FASTQ/FASTA reads from mixed samples such as metagenomes or polyploid genomes must be error-corrected without masking true low-frequency haplotype variants. When consensus-sequence-based correction is sufficient, e.g. clonal haploid samples where masking of low-frequency variants is not a concern When runtime and peak memory are the binding constraints — VeChat experiences longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competing tools, particularly on large datasets When reads are short or already high-accuracy (e.g. PacBio HiFi/CCS or Illumina), since VeChat targets noisy long TGS reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Haplotype-aware self-correction of noisy PacBio CLR metagenomic reads using VeChat's two-cycle variation-graph workflow, which preserves low-frequency haplotype variants that consensus-sequence templates mistakenly mask as errors. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Haplotype-aware self-correction of noisy PacBio CLR metagenomic reads using VeChat's two-cycle variation-graph workflow, which preserves low-frequency haplotype variants that consensus-sequence templates mistakenly mask as errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When consensus-sequence-based correction is sufficient, e.g. clonal haploid samples where masking of low-frequency variants is not a concern When runtime and peak memory are the binding constraints — VeChat experiences longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competing tools, particularly on large datasets When reads are short or already high-accuracy (e.g. PacBio HiFi/CCS or Illumina), since VeChat targets noisy long TGS reads

skills.description: Use when you need labeled methylated/unmethylated positions from PacBio-validated motif sites (e.g., E. coli GATC) to train or score ONT nanopore m6A classifiers on current-deviation features.
skills.name: pacbio-orthogonal-methylation-label-construction
skills.search_text: pacbio-orthogonal-methylation-label-construction Use when you need labeled methylated/unmethylated positions from PacBio-validated motif sites (e.g., E. coli GATC) to train or score ONT nanopore m6A classifiers on current-deviation features. You already have a trained .pkl model and only need per-read calling (use mCaller.py without --train, e.g., -m GATC -b A). The target context has no PacBio-confirmed motif sites — training labels cannot be constructed, and mCaller accuracy decreases at contexts dissimilar to training examples. The organism's motifs cannot be confidently assigned (e.g., C. neoformans and S. cerevisiae, where sites were not consistently detected across PacBio, nanopore, and MeDIP-seq). http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Builds ground-truth labels (chromosome, position, strand, methylated/unmethylated) from orthogonal PacBio SMRT calls at known methyltransferase motifs, so binary classifiers like mCaller's neural network can be trained and evaluated on nanopore current-deviation features. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Builds ground-truth labels (chromosome, position, strand, methylated/unmethylated) from orthogonal PacBio SMRT calls at known methyltransferase motifs, so binary classifiers like mCaller's neural network can be trained and evaluated on nanopore current-deviation features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a trained .pkl model and only need per-read calling (use mCaller.py without --train, e.g., -m GATC -b A). The target context has no PacBio-confirmed motif sites — training labels cannot be constructed, and mCaller accuracy decreases at contexts dissimilar to training examples. The organism's motifs cannot be confidently assigned (e.g., C. neoformans and S. cerevisiae, where sites were not consistently detected across PacBio, nanopore, and MeDIP-seq).

skills.description: Use when raw PacBio or ONT long reads (FASTA/FASTQ) contain sequencing errors that must be reduced via self-correction before assembly, mapping, or downstream benchmarking, without short-read or reference-based correction.
skills.name: pacbio-read-error-correction
skills.search_text: pacbio-read-error-correction Use when raw PacBio or ONT long reads (FASTA/FASTQ) contain sequencing errors that must be reduced via self-correction before assembly, mapping, or downstream benchmarking, without short-read or reference-based correction. The input is already-corrected reads or a polished assembly — CONSENT-polish, not self-correction, is the appropriate mode for raw assemblies. The goal is to correct reads using a reference genome or short reads (hybrid/reference-based correction, e.g. CoLoRMAP/HECiL style) rather than self-correction from the long reads alone. The dataset exceeds the scale that alignment-pile-based correctors like Canu or Daccord can handle (e.g. C. elegans / full human) and you need an alternative memory-lean strategy — although this is exactly where CONSENT is preferred, correction of larger and more complex organisms than human has not been performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Self-correction of PacBio (and ONT) long reads using CONSENT, which computes multiple sequence alignments between overlapping read regions, derives per-window consensus sequences, and polishes them with local de Bruijn graphs to lower the final error rate. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Self-correction of PacBio (and ONT) long reads using CONSENT, which computes multiple sequence alignments between overlapping read regions, derives per-window consensus sequences, and polishes them with local de Bruijn graphs to lower the final error rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already-corrected reads or a polished assembly — CONSENT-polish, not self-correction, is the appropriate mode for raw assemblies. The goal is to correct reads using a reference genome or short reads (hybrid/reference-based correction, e.g. CoLoRMAP/HECiL style) rather than self-correction from the long reads alone. The dataset exceeds the scale that alignment-pile-based correctors like Canu or Daccord can handle (e.g. C. elegans / full human) and you need an alternative memory-lean strategy — although this is exactly where CONSENT is preferred, correction of larger and more complex organisms than human has not been performed.

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from error-prone PacBio SMRT (or ONT) whole-genome BAM alignments, where candidate variants must be detected from a read pileup and read-level allele observations must be extracted for haplotype-informed genotyping.
skills.name: pacbio-read-pileup-allelotyping
skills.search_text: pacbio-read-pileup-allelotyping Use when calling SNVs from error-prone PacBio SMRT (or ONT) whole-genome BAM alignments, where candidate variants must be detected from a read pileup and read-level allele observations must be extracted for haplotype-informed genotyping. The input is short-read data (e.g. Illumina aligned with BWA-MEM) — short-read callers such as GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the intended tools for that regime The goal is de novo calling of short indels or structural variants — Longshot only calls SNVs (it can genotype indels only when provided in an input VCF, and SVs >50 bp are unsupported) The BAM lacks accurate alignments in highly similar segmental duplications, where correctly mapping PacBio reads remains a challenge and pileup-based allelotyping may be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Identifies candidate SNVs from a pileup of aligned PacBio long reads by computing genotype likelihoods (as in Samtools) and then performs sensitive allelotyping of reads at those sites, feeding haplotype-informed phased genotyping as implemented in Longshot. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Identifies candidate SNVs from a pileup of aligned PacBio long reads by computing genotype likelihoods (as in Samtools) and then performs sensitive allelotyping of reads at those sites, feeding haplotype-informed phased genotyping as implemented in Longshot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read data (e.g. Illumina aligned with BWA-MEM) — short-read callers such as GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the intended tools for that regime The goal is de novo calling of short indels or structural variants — Longshot only calls SNVs (it can genotype indels only when provided in an input VCF, and SVs >50 bp are unsupported) The BAM lacks accurate alignments in highly similar segmental duplications, where correctly mapping PacBio reads remains a challenge and pileup-based allelotyping may be unreliable

skills.description: Use when validating de novo methylation motifs detected from ONT data (e.g. Snapper output final_motifs_[strand]_[contig].fasta) against an established PacBio methylome reference for the same strain.
skills.name: pacbio-reference-motif-curation
skills.search_text: pacbio-reference-motif-curation Use when validating de novo methylation motifs detected from ONT data (e.g. Snapper output final_motifs_[strand]_[contig].fasta) against an established PacBio methylome reference for the same strain. The strain has no previously characterized PacBio methylome, so no reference motif set exists for exact-sequence matching. You need de novo motif discovery itself from raw nanopore signal — use Snapper (with Tombo resquiggling and multi-fast5 conversion) instead of this comparison step. The motifs of interest require methylation-type assignment or modification-site-level mapping rather than motif sequence concordance. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Curates a PacBio-derived reference set of methylation motifs (e.g. H. pylori J99 motifs from Krebes et al. 2014) and matches it against de novo motifs detected by Snapper on Oxford Nanopore reads to build a concordance table of matched and discordant motifs. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Curates a PacBio-derived reference set of methylation motifs (e.g. H. pylori J99 motifs from Krebes et al. 2014) and matches it against de novo motifs detected by Snapper on Oxford Nanopore reads to build a concordance table of matched and discordant motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The strain has no previously characterized PacBio methylome, so no reference motif set exists for exact-sequence matching. You need de novo motif discovery itself from raw nanopore signal — use Snapper (with Tombo resquiggling and multi-fast5 conversion) instead of this comparison step. The motifs of interest require methylation-type assignment or modification-site-level mapping rather than motif sequence concordance.

Input is already a CCS BAM or FLNC BAM file — proceed directly to LIMA/isoseq3 refine instead of regenerating CCS Data are short-read Illumina FASTQ rather than PacBio subread BAMs, since CCS generation is specific to circularly sequenced PacBio molecules http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Generates Circular Consensus Sequences (CCS) from PacBio subread BAM inputs, the first stage of the nf-core/isoseq read-processing workflow that feeds downstream LIMA primer removal and isoseq3 refine chimera filtering. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: Generates Circular Consensus Sequences (CCS) from PacBio subread BAM inputs, the first stage of the nf-core/isoseq read-processing workflow that feeds downstream LIMA primer removal and isoseq3 refine chimera filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a CCS BAM or FLNC BAM file — proceed directly to LIMA/isoseq3 refine instead of regenerating CCS Data are short-read Illumina FASTQ rather than PacBio subread BAMs, since CCS generation is specific to circularly sequenced PacBio molecules

skills.description: Use when preparing PacBio (or other long-read) alignments for deep-learning-based small variant calling: the raw vendor BAM must be extracted and realigned to GRCh37 decoy v5 with NGMLR v0.2.3 before tensor generation and calling against GIAB HG001 v3.3.2 truth.
skills.name: pacific-biosciences-alignment-handling-grch37
skills.search_text: pacific-biosciences-alignment-handling-grch37 Use when preparing PacBio (or other long-read) alignments for deep-learning-based small variant calling: the raw vendor BAM must be extracted and realigned to GRCh37 decoy v5 with NGMLR v0.2.3 before tensor generation and calling against GIAB HG001 v3.3.2 truth. The input is Illumina short-read data — Clairvoyante's Illumina pipeline does not use the NGMLR realignment step, and GATK UnifiedGenotyper is the comparator on Illumina. Multi-allelic variants or indels >4 bp must be reported with exact alternative alleles — Clairvoyante's network version 3 cannot provide these. The task is somatic or trio-based variant calling — these modes are not yet supported by Clairvoyante. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Re-align long PacBio sequencing reads (e.g. the 44x HG001/NA12878 BAM) to the GRCh37 decoy version 5 reference using NGMLR v0.2.3, producing the alignment that Clairvoyante tensor extraction and variant calling consume for single-molecule sequencing variant calling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Re-align long PacBio sequencing reads (e.g. the 44x HG001/NA12878 BAM) to the GRCh37 decoy version 5 reference using NGMLR v0.2.3, producing the alignment that Clairvoyante tensor extraction and variant calling consume for single-molecule sequencing variant calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is Illumina short-read data — Clairvoyante's Illumina pipeline does not use the NGMLR realignment step, and GATK UnifiedGenotyper is the comparator on Illumina. Multi-allelic variants or indels >4 bp must be reported with exact alternative alleles — Clairvoyante's network version 3 cannot provide these. The task is somatic or trio-based variant calling — these modes are not yet supported by Clairvoyante.

skills.description: Use when long reads must be mapped to draft assembly contigs in PAF format via minimizer sketches instead of a full read aligner, e.g. as input for Tigmint-long correction or misassembly detection.
skills.name: paf-alignment-format-handling
skills.search_text: paf-alignment-format-handling Use when long reads must be mapped to draft assembly contigs in PAF format via minimizer sketches instead of a full read aligner, e.g. as input for Tigmint-long correction or misassembly detection. The goal is full scaffolding (scaffold graph, ordering/orientation of contigs) rather than standalone read-to-contig mappings — use ntLink's basic scaffolding protocols instead. You need base-level aligned alignments with mismatch/CIGAR detail rather than minimizer-based mappings — an aligner like minimap2 is more appropriate. Input assemblies or reads are not present in the current working directory, since ntLink's pair/mapping stage expects both target and reads locally. Generating and handling PAF-format long-read to contig mappings using ntLink's standalone minimizer-based mapping mode (Alternate Protocol 1), which reuses the scaffolder's lightweight mapping machinery without full alignment. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Generating and handling PAF-format long-read to contig mappings using ntLink's standalone minimizer-based mapping mode (Alternate Protocol 1), which reuses the scaffolder's lightweight mapping machinery without full alignment.

skills.description: Use when comparing raw nanopore signal read-mapping tools whose outputs are in PAF format and you need precision/recall/F1 against a sequence-based ground truth such as minimap2 alignments of basecalled reads.
skills.name: paf-mapping-accuracy-scoring-precision-recall
skills.search_text: paf-mapping-accuracy-scoring-precision-recall Use when comparing raw nanopore signal read-mapping tools whose outputs are in PAF format and you need precision/recall/F1 against a sequence-based ground truth such as minimap2 alignments of basecalled reads. Inputs are basecalled sequence reads (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than raw-signal mapper PAF outputs — use standard sequence-alignment benchmarking instead No trusted ground-truth alignment exists for the dataset — pafstats requires a reference PAF to score against Evaluating overlap-based all-vs-all tasks (Rawsamble) where no reference genome ground truth is defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scores raw-signal mapper PAF outputs (e.g., RawHash2, RawHash, UNCALLED) against minimap2-based ground-truth PAF alignments using UNCALLED's pafstats to compute per-dataset precision, recall, and F1, as done in the RawHash2 evaluation where RawHash2 improves F1 over RawHash by 10.57% on average (up to 20.25%). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478

skills.description: Use when a labelled PAF file of long-read to contig mappings generated by ntLink with paf=True needs to be counted, aggregated per target contig, or validated against published mapping statistics.
skills.name: paf-mapping-file-parsing
skills.search_text: paf-mapping-file-parsing Use when a labelled PAF file of long-read to contig mappings generated by ntLink with paf=True needs to be counted, aggregated per target contig, or validated against published mapping statistics. The input is a raw, unlabelled PAF from a different mapper (e.g. minimap2) whose column semantics were not produced by ntLink's paf=True output — field positions and labels differ. The goal is scaffolding (Basic Protocols 1–3) or Tigmint-long correction (Alternate Protocol 2), where mappings are consumed by ntLink itself rather than being summarized. Quality-filtering or misassembly detection is the goal; this skill only counts and averages, it does not filter or correct. Parses and summarizes the labelled PAF file produced by ntLink's mapping mode (Alternate Protocol 1), using Miller (mlr) to compute total mappings, average mapping block length, and average mappings per draft contig as reported in Table 5 of the ntLink Current Protocols article. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Parses and summarizes the labelled PAF file produced by ntLink's mapping mode (Alternate Protocol 1), using Miller (mlr) to compute total mappings, average mapping block length, and average mappings per draft contig as reported in Table 5 of the ntLink Current Protocols article.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw, unlabelled PAF from a different mapper (e.g. minimap2) whose column semantics were not produced by ntLink's paf=True output — field positions and labels differ. skills.description: Use when raw-signal mapper outputs are in the UNCALLED-style modified PAF format and you need to extract mapped read positions, throughput (mapped bases/sec), or bases/chunks processed before the mapping decision.
skills.name: paf-mapping-output-parsing
skills.search_text: paf-mapping-output-parsing Use when raw-signal mapper outputs are in the UNCALLED-style modified PAF format and you need to extract mapped read positions, throughput (mapped bases/sec), or bases/chunks processed before the mapping decision. The mapping output is a standard 12-column minimap2 PAF without the UNCALLED-style mapping-decision tags — the bases/chunks-parsed fields will not exist The goal is base-level alignment quality (CIGAR/identity), which the raw-signal mappers' PAF output does not provide without a downstream signal-alignment step (DTW as in RawAlign) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parse and interpret PAF-format mapping outputs produced by raw nanopore signal mappers (RawHash2, RawHash, UNCALLED, Sigmap), which follow the UNCALLED-style modified PAF template that records mapping decisions and early-termination information. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478

skills.description: Use when you need per-read allele likelihoods (p_ref vs p_alt) at candidate SNVs in long error-prone SMS reads (PacBio/ONT), e.g. as the allelotyping stage before haplotype-informed genotyping.
skills.name: pair-hmm-forward-read-realignment
skills.search_text: pair-hmm-forward-read-realignment Use when you need per-read allele likelihoods (p_ref vs p_alt) at candidate SNVs in long error-prone SMS reads (PacBio/ONT), e.g. as the allelotyping stage before haplotype-informed genotyping. Your reads are short Illumina reads — the paper positions Longshot as a method leveraging long SMS reads where haplotype information is present The variant is a structural variant longer than 50 bp — Longshot does not support SVs (only SNVs; indels are genotyped only if given in an input VCF) You need a single best alignment per read rather than likelihoods averaged over all alignments — the -x/--max_alignment flag switches away from the pair-HMM forward algorithm, indicating the pair-HMM is not the right default for max-scoring alignment use cases http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Allelotyping of individual long reads at candidate biallelic SNV sites by realigning each read to reference and alternate windows using a pair-HMM forward algorithm, yielding per-read allele assignments and phred-scaled allele quality scores. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Allelotyping of individual long reads at candidate biallelic SNV sites by realigning each read to reference and alternate windows using a pair-HMM forward algorithm, yielding per-read allele assignments and phred-scaled allele quality scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your reads are short Illumina reads — the paper positions Longshot as a method leveraging long SMS reads where haplotype information is present The variant is a structural variant longer than 50 bp — Longshot does not support SVs (only SNVs; indels are genotyped only if given in an input VCF) You need a single best alignment per read rather than likelihoods averaged over all alignments — the -x/--max_alignment flag switches away from the pair-HMM forward algorithm, indicating the pair-HMM is not the right default for max-scoring alignment use cases

Input is long-read data (PacBio/ONT) — use dysgu's 'call' with --mode presets (e.g. nanopore-r10, pacbio-revio) instead of the PE run pipeline Sample is somatic/tumor with copy-number changes or poly-clonality where events have low allelic fraction — the default diploid model underperforms; use --diploid False Goal is resolving full-length insertion sequences or multi-allelic sites from PE data — the paper notes dysgu lacks a de novo assembly stage and these remain unresolved http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call structural variants (deletions, insertions) from Illumina paired-end sequencing data using dysgu in paired-end mode, benchmarked against PE callers such as manta, delly, and lumpy on GIAB HG002 Tier 1 SVs. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Call structural variants (deletions, insertions) from Illumina paired-end sequencing data using dysgu in paired-end mode, benchmarked against PE callers such as manta, delly, and lumpy on GIAB HG002 Tier 1 SVs.

skills.description: Use when a consensus VCF of SV calls (merged across callers with SURVIVOR) must be down-filtered before manual curation — e.g. dropping calls with low paired-end support or breakpoints in low-complexity or annotated LTR regions.
skills.name: paired-end-support-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: paired-end-support-threshold-filtering Use when a consensus VCF of SV calls (merged across callers with SURVIVOR) must be down-filtered before manual curation — e.g. dropping calls with low paired-end support or breakpoints in low-complexity or annotated LTR regions. The input is raw caller output rather than a merged consensus set — the article filters the post-SURVIVOR-merge set (SVs detected by at least two callers), not individual caller VCFs. The goal is maximum SV sensitivity rather than specificity — the authors explicitly prioritized high specificity over detecting all SVs, so this aggressive filtering will drop true calls. The variants are translocations or inversions requiring genotyping re-examination — the article excluded these from re-examination because they were more challenging to accurately genotype. http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Down-filters a consensus structural variant (SV) call set — here the 315-call fission yeast set accepted by at least two callers — by removing calls with low paired-end support, breakpoints in MQ=0 regions, and overlaps with annotated long terminal repeats, prior to manual read-alignment inspection. Implemented with the SURVIVOR filter module from the Jeffares et al. (2017) S. pombe SV pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Down-filters a consensus structural variant (SV) call set — here the 315-call fission yeast set accepted by at least two callers — by removing calls with low paired-end support, breakpoints in MQ=0 regions, and overlaps with annotated long terminal repeats, prior to manual read-alignment inspection. Implemented with the SURVIVOR filter module from the Jeffares et al. (2017) S. pombe SV pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw caller output rather than a merged consensus set — the article filters the post-SURVIVOR-merge set (SVs detected by at least two callers), not individual caller VCFs. The goal is maximum SV sensitivity rather than specificity — the authors explicitly prioritized high specificity over detecting all SVs, so this aggressive filtering will drop true calls. The variants are translocations or inversions requiring genotyping re-examination — the article excluded these from re-examination because they were more challenging to accurately genotype.

skills.description: Use when paired-end Illumina read pairs overlap and must be converted into single merged fragments before downstream k-mer counting or seed construction, e.g. to derive 'not too repetitive' seeds for TULIP.
skills.name: paired-read-merging-with-overlap-detection
skills.search_text: paired-read-merging-with-overlap-detection Use when paired-end Illumina read pairs overlap and must be converted into single merged fragments before downstream k-mer counting or seed construction, e.g. to derive 'not too repetitive' seeds for TULIP. Mate pairs do not overlap (no shared sequence between R1 and R2), so merging cannot join them The goal is direct de novo assembly of the read pairs rather than constructing short seeds for a long-read scaffolding pipeline like TULIP Input reads are already single-end or already merged; re-merging adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Merges overlapping paired-end Illumina read mates into single contiguous fragments using FLASh with a minimum mate overlap of 15 nt, producing merged fragments that serve as raw material for k-mer-counting seed selection in the TULIP assembly of the European eel genome. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Merges overlapping paired-end Illumina read mates into single contiguous fragments using FLASh with a minimum mate overlap of 15 nt, producing merged fragments that serve as raw material for k-mer-counting seed selection in the TULIP assembly of the European eel genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mate pairs do not overlap (no shared sequence between R1 and R2), so merging cannot join them The goal is direct de novo assembly of the read pairs rather than constructing short seeds for a long-read scaffolding pipeline like TULIP Input reads are already single-end or already merged; re-merging adds no information

skills.description: Use when you have expression data from strains that carry a duplication paired with a non-duplicated strain of the same clonal population, and you need to test whether duplicated-region genes are induced and whether induction tracks copy number.
skills.name: paired-strain-differential-expression
skills.search_text: paired-strain-differential-expression Use when you have expression data from strains that carry a duplication paired with a non-duplicated strain of the same clonal population, and you need to test whether duplicated-region genes are induced and whether induction tracks copy number. Expression comparisons are not clonally paired (duplicated and non-duplicated strains come from different clonal populations), so genetic background confounds the induction estimate The variant of interest is not a duplication/CNV (e.g. translocations or inversions, which the authors excluded from genotyping re-examination because they were more challenging to accurately genotype) The data are RNA-seq rather than the deposited DNA microarray expression data, requiring a different quantification pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Tests whether genes inside naturally occurring duplications are induced in expression, by comparing log-phase microarray transcript levels of each duplicated S. pombe strain against a non-duplicated strain from the same clonal population, and correlating induction with duplication copy number across the eight strain pairs. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Tests whether genes inside naturally occurring duplications are induced in expression, by comparing log-phase microarray transcript levels of each duplicated S. pombe strain against a non-duplicated strain from the same clonal population, and correlating induction with duplication copy number across the eight strain pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression comparisons are not clonally paired (duplicated and non-duplicated strains come from different clonal populations), so genetic background confounds the induction estimate The variant of interest is not a duplication/CNV (e.g. translocations or inversions, which the authors excluded from genotyping re-examination because they were more challenging to accurately genotype) The data are RNA-seq rather than the deposited DNA microarray expression data, requiring a different quantification pipeline

skills.description: Use when quantifying real-time depletion effects (e.g., RISER globin mRNA depletion in whole blood) and a null-comparison is needed against per-transcript percent changes arising from random splitting of an independent control run.
skills.name: paired-wilcoxon-significance-testing
skills.search_text: paired-wilcoxon-significance-testing Use when quantifying real-time depletion effects (e.g., RISER globin mRNA depletion in whole blood) and a null-comparison is needed against per-transcript percent changes arising from random splitting of an independent control run. Input data are unpaired or come from different samples/conditions with no natural pairing (e.g., comparing two independent flow-cell runs without matched transcripts) — use an unpaired test instead Percent-change distributions are already known to differ trivially (e.g., comparing against a zero-null when the effect size, >90% globin depletion, is the reported claim) without a matched control split The transcript set has fewer than the required minimum counts (≥30 reads in both conditions), making per-transcript percent changes unstable and the paired test underpowered http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Non-parametric paired significance testing used as a control analysis in the RISER globin-depletion study: per-transcript percent changes computed between two randomly split halves of an independent non-RISER run are compared against RISER-mediated changes to confirm the observed depletion/increase effects exceed random run-to-run variation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Non-parametric paired significance testing used as a control analysis in the RISER globin-depletion study: per-transcript percent changes computed between two randomly split halves of an independent non-RISER run are compared against RISER-mediated changes to confirm the observed depletion/increase effects exceed random run-to-run variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are unpaired or come from different samples/conditions with no natural pairing (e.g., comparing two independent flow-cell runs without matched transcripts) — use an unpaired test instead Percent-change distributions are already known to differ trivially (e.g., comparing against a zero-null when the effect size, >90% globin depletion, is the reported claim) without a matched control split The transcript set has fewer than the required minimum counts (≥30 reads in both conditions), making per-transcript percent changes unstable and the paired test underpowered

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA consensus sequences per specimen/marker (e.g. Nanopore rDNA consensus and Illumina reference consensus, or COI barcodes vs rDNA regions) and need a pairwise distance matrix partitioned into intra- vs interspecific classes.
skills.name: pairwise-genetic-distance-calculation
skills.search_text: pairwise-genetic-distance-calculation Use when you have FASTA consensus sequences per specimen/marker (e.g. Nanopore rDNA consensus and Illumina reference consensus, or COI barcodes vs rDNA regions) and need a pairwise distance matrix partitioned into intra- vs interspecific classes. Input is raw Nanopore reads rather than polished consensus sequences — raw reads carry high error rates and must first be demultiplexed with MiniBar, consensus-called (e.g. Allele Wrangler with 30 reads-per-position coverage) and polished (RACON) The goal is phylogenetic tree inference or community composition (metabarcoding abundance) analysis rather than specimen-level pairwise distance quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes pairwise genetic (edit/alignment) distances between consensus sequences — e.g. Nanopore rDNA consensus vs Illumina-based consensus, or COI vs rDNA distance matrices across specimens — to quantify consensus accuracy or compare taxonomic resolution between markers. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Computes pairwise genetic (edit/alignment) distances between consensus sequences — e.g. Nanopore rDNA consensus vs Illumina-based consensus, or COI vs rDNA distance matrices across specimens — to quantify consensus accuracy or compare taxonomic resolution between markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Nanopore reads rather than polished consensus sequences — raw reads carry high error rates and must first be demultiplexed with MiniBar, consensus-called (e.g. Allele Wrangler with 30 reads-per-position coverage) and polished (RACON) The goal is phylogenetic tree inference or community composition (metabarcoding abundance) analysis rather than specimen-level pairwise distance quantification

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to tRNA loci and you need to define the exact read-end/tRNA cleavage interface, classify tRNA halves vs tRF-5/tRF-3, or verify a conserved cleavage motif.
skills.name: pairwise-sequence-alignment-of-derived-fragments
skills.search_text: pairwise-sequence-alignment-of-derived-fragments Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to tRNA loci and you need to define the exact read-end/tRNA cleavage interface, classify tRNA halves vs tRF-5/tRF-3, or verify a conserved cleavage motif. When the question is tncRNA discovery/annotation from raw sRNA-seq rather than characterizing cleavage interfaces of already-mapped tncRNAs (use the full tncRNA Toolkit pipeline instead) When reads are not uniquely mappable to a single tRNA locus (multi-mapped reads aligned > 50 times are discarded by the upstream bowtie '-m 50' step), so cleavage position is ambiguous When studying non-tRNA-derived small RNAs such as miRNAs or piRNAs — the AG::TGG interface motif and anticodon-loop window are specific to tRNA cleavage http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 Locally aligns tRNA-derived small RNA reads (tncRNAs) to their progenitor mature tRNA sequences to pinpoint the cleavage interface and detect the conserved tRF-5::tRNA motif (AG::TGG), demonstrating that plant tRNA cleavage is codon-dependent and specific rather than random degradation. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Locally aligns tRNA-derived small RNA reads (tncRNAs) to their progenitor mature tRNA sequences to pinpoint the cleavage interface and detect the conserved tRF-5::tRNA motif (AG::TGG), demonstrating that plant tRNA cleavage is codon-dependent and specific rather than random degradation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is tncRNA discovery/annotation from raw sRNA-seq rather than characterizing cleavage interfaces of already-mapped tncRNAs (use the full tncRNA Toolkit pipeline instead) When reads are not uniquely mappable to a single tRNA locus (multi-mapped reads aligned > 50 times are discarded by the upstream bowtie '-m 50' step), so cleavage position is ambiguous When studying non-tRNA-derived small RNAs such as miRNAs or piRNAs — the AG::TGG interface motif and anticodon-loop window are specific to tRNA cleavage

skills.description: Use when you have error-corrected long-read transcript sequences from highly similar gene copies and need to detect pairs whose differences consist only of large indels (exon-level differences) rather than point substitutions or small indels.
skills.name: pairwise-transcript-alignment-comparison
skills.search_text: pairwise-transcript-alignment-comparison Use when you have error-corrected long-read transcript sequences from highly similar gene copies and need to detect pairs whose differences consist only of large indels (exon-level differences) rather than point substitutions or small indels. Transcripts from a well-annotated reference genome where a reference-based isoform comparison (e.g., exon-coordinate overlap) is available instead of de novo pairwise alignment Alignment of highly divergent sequences where differences are not limited to large indels — grouping by cliques would merge unrelated transcripts Uncorrected or error-prone long reads (e.g., raw PacBio CCS inputs) — the comparison assumes transcripts already error-corrected by IsoCon so that only true exon-level differences remain http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes pairwise alignments between reconstructed transcripts (e.g., IsoCon final_candidates.fa output) using parasail, and inspects alignment differences to determine whether two transcripts differ only by large indels (exon-level differences), enabling grouping of highly similar transcripts from multigene family Iso-Seq data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Computes pairwise alignments between reconstructed transcripts (e.g., IsoCon final_candidates.fa output) using parasail, and inspects alignment differences to determine whether two transcripts differ only by large indels (exon-level differences), enabling grouping of highly similar transcripts from multigene family Iso-Seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Transcripts from a well-annotated reference genome where a reference-based isoform comparison (e.g., exon-coordinate overlap) is available instead of de novo pairwise alignment Alignment of highly divergent sequences where differences are not limited to large indels — grouping by cliques would merge unrelated transcripts Uncorrected or error-prone long reads (e.g., raw PacBio CCS inputs) — the comparison assumes transcripts already error-corrected by IsoCon so that only true exon-level differences remain

skills.description: Use when designing strand-specific CRISPR-Cas9 crRNAs (e.g., FUDGE fusion-gene enrichment) against known driver exon loci such as BRAF Exon 10, EWSR1 Exon 7, or SS18 Exon 9, where guides must orient Cas9 cutting toward an unknown fusion partner.
skills.name: pam-proximal-protospacer-extraction
skills.search_text: pam-proximal-protospacer-extraction Use when designing strand-specific CRISPR-Cas9 crRNAs (e.g., FUDGE fusion-gene enrichment) against known driver exon loci such as BRAF Exon 10, EWSR1 Exon 7, or SS18 Exon 9, where guides must orient Cas9 cutting toward an unknown fusion partner. The input DNA is fragmented FFPE material — the FUDGE crRNA protocol applied to degraded DNA will most likely fail to comprehensively identify fusion genes The fusion partner's identity and breakpoint are already known and the goal is re-sequencing a known junction rather than partner-independent discovery Only one candidate PAM exists per target and no guide on the strand that orients sequencing toward the unknown partner can be found — no valid strand-directed guide can be produced http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scans target-locus reference sequences for NGG PAM motifs and extracts the 20-nt protospacer immediately 5' of each PAM to generate candidate FUDGE crRNAs for strand-directed fusion-gene enrichment prior to nanopore sequencing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: Scans target-locus reference sequences for NGG PAM motifs and extracts the 20-nt protospacer immediately 5' of each PAM to generate candidate FUDGE crRNAs for strand-directed fusion-gene enrichment prior to nanopore sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input DNA is fragmented FFPE material — the FUDGE crRNA protocol applied to degraded DNA will most likely fail to comprehensively identify fusion genes The fusion partner's identity and breakpoint are already known and the goal is re-sequencing a known junction rather than partner-independent discovery Only one candidate PAM exists per target and no guide on the strand that orients sequencing toward the unknown partner can be found — no valid strand-directed guide can be produced
