skills.description: Use when you need to build a pangenome graph from a collection of de novo assemblies (GFA/FASTA) or evaluate whether one set of assemblies yields a more accurate graph (precision/recall of bubbles) than another.
skills.name: pangenome-graph-construction
skills.search_text: pangenome-graph-construction Use when you need to build a pangenome graph from a collection of de novo assemblies (GFA/FASTA) or evaluate whether one set of assemblies yields a more accurate graph (precision/recall of bubbles) than another. Input is a single reference genome without multiple per-sample assemblies — a pangenome graph requires a collection of haplotype/assembly sequences Your goal is short-read variant calling against an existing graph rather than building or benchmarking a new graph from assemblies Graph nodes/paths lack chromosome annotations needed for reference-guided classification (e.g., constructing the Pangenome Label Graph is a separate skill) http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Constructs pangenome graphs with minigraph from multiple genome assemblies (e.g., CHM13 plus 45 per-sample HiFiCCL-Hifiasm assemblies at ~5x coverage) using GRCh38 as the reference, then extracts bubble regions with gfatools to benchmark graph accuracy against an HPRC-derived reference graph. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Constructs pangenome graphs with minigraph from multiple genome assemblies (e.g., CHM13 plus 45 per-sample HiFiCCL-Hifiasm assemblies at ~5x coverage) using GRCh38 as the reference, then extracts bubble regions with gfatools to benchmark graph accuracy against an HPRC-derived reference graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single reference genome without multiple per-sample assemblies — a pangenome graph requires a collection of haplotype/assembly sequences Your goal is short-read variant calling against an existing graph rather than building or benchmarking a new graph from assemblies Graph nodes/paths lack chromosome annotations needed for reference-guided classification (e.g., constructing the Pangenome Label Graph is a separate skill)

skills.description: Use when the input is a folder of raw Oxford Nanopore POD5 files (direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA) and the goal is GPU-parallel Dorado basecalling with modified-base tags, consolidated into a single unmapped BAM for downstream modkit/minimap2 steps.
skills.name: parallel-basecalling-of-pod5-batches
skills.search_text: parallel-basecalling-of-pod5-batches Use when the input is a folder of raw Oxford Nanopore POD5 files (direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA) and the goal is GPU-parallel Dorado basecalling with modified-base tags, consolidated into a single unmapped BAM for downstream modkit/minimap2 steps. Input is already basecalled (FASTQ or unmapped BAM) — use the Dogme 'remap' or 'kallisto' entry points instead of re-running basecalling Input is barcoded reads needing classification/demultiplexing as the primary goal — use Dogme's optional Dorado demultiplexing (kitName) workflow rather than plain parallel basecalling The data are not Oxford Nanopore POD5 files (e.g., Illumina FASTQ or PacBio data) — Dorado basecalling is specific to ONT reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Automates the basecalling layer of ONT reprocessing in Dogme: download the latest Dorado models, basecall each POD5 file with Dorado in parallel to produce one BAM per POD5, then merge the per-POD5 BAMs into a single unmapped BAM for downstream mapping with minimap2. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Automates the basecalling layer of ONT reprocessing in Dogme: download the latest Dorado models, basecall each POD5 file with Dorado in parallel to produce one BAM per POD5, then merge the per-POD5 BAMs into a single unmapped BAM for downstream mapping with minimap2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already basecalled (FASTQ or unmapped BAM) — use the Dogme 'remap' or 'kallisto' entry points instead of re-running basecalling Input is barcoded reads needing classification/demultiplexing as the primary goal — use Dogme's optional Dorado demultiplexing (kitName) workflow rather than plain parallel basecalling The data are not Oxford Nanopore POD5 files (e.g., Illumina FASTQ or PacBio data) — Dorado basecalling is specific to ONT reads

skills.description: Use when modeling a detector process whose quanta split or fork into parallel paths (e.g., K-fluorescence escape in CsI or charge trapping in a-Se) and signal/noise must be recombined with correct cross-spectral terms before computing MTF/NNPS.
skills.name: parallel-cascade-cross-spectral-term-computation
skills.search_text: parallel-cascade-cross-spectral-term-computation Use when modeling a detector process whose quanta split or fork into parallel paths (e.g., K-fluorescence escape in CsI or charge trapping in a-Se) and signal/noise must be recombined with correct cross-spectral terms before computing MTF/NNPS. The process is strictly serial with no branching (e.g., pure pixel integration) — apply it as a single serial cascade block instead Fano noise or photoconductor discharge gain variability must be modeled — these are not explicitly handled in CASYMIR's current parallel cascade Photon-counting detectors with adaptive binning — such architectures are not yet included in CASYMIR Combines the branching stages of a cascaded linear-systems x-ray detector model (e.g., K-fluorescence reabsorption in CsI) using CASYMIR Path/Node objects and apply_parallel_process, computing pairwise cross-spectral terms so that MTF and NPS can be evaluated at any stage of the cascade. genomics/v1 10.1002/mp.18079
skills.summary: Combines the branching stages of a cascaded linear-systems x-ray detector model (e.g., K-fluorescence reabsorption in CsI) using CASYMIR Path/Node objects and apply_parallel_process, computing pairwise cross-spectral terms so that MTF and NPS can be evaluated at any stage of the cascade.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The process is strictly serial with no branching (e.g., pure pixel integration) — apply it as a single serial cascade block instead Fano noise or photoconductor discharge gain variability must be modeled — these are not explicitly handled in CASYMIR's current parallel cascade Photon-counting detectors with adaptive binning — such architectures are not yet included in CASYMIR

skills.description: Use when modeling an x-ray detector whose cascade splits into parallel pathways — e.g., the Kim architecture where scintillator-transmitted x rays convert within the photodiode — and you need combined MTF/NNPS with cross-spectral noise terms.
skills.name: parallel-cascade-modeling
skills.search_text: parallel-cascade-modeling Use when modeling an x-ray detector whose cascade splits into parallel pathways — e.g., the Kim architecture where scintillator-transmitted x rays convert within the photodiode — and you need combined MTF/NNPS with cross-spectral noise terms. The detector cascade is purely serial with no branching — use CASYMIR's standard serial process blocks instead of constructing parallel Paths The detector is a photon-counting system with adaptive binning, or temporal effects such as detector lag and ghosting must be modeled — these are not included in CASYMIR Per-energy-bin propagation or input-labeled (input-quantum-limited) formulations are required — CASYMIR does not propagate signal and noise quantities on a per-energy-bin basis http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Constructs parallel cascades within CASYMIR by defining custom Path/Node branches (e.g., a Kim-style photodiode-conversion pathway alongside the standard scintillation path) and combining them with apply_parallel_process, which accounts for pairwise cross-spectral noise terms at the summation point before computing MTF and NNPS. genomics/v1 10.1002/mp.18079
skills.summary: Constructs parallel cascades within CASYMIR by defining custom Path/Node branches (e.g., a Kim-style photodiode-conversion pathway alongside the standard scintillation path) and combining them with apply_parallel_process, which accounts for pairwise cross-spectral noise terms at the summation point before computing MTF and NNPS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The detector cascade is purely serial with no branching — use CASYMIR's standard serial process blocks instead of constructing parallel Paths The detector is a photon-counting system with adaptive binning, or temporal effects such as detector lag and ghosting must be modeled — these are not included in CASYMIR Per-energy-bin propagation or input-labeled (input-quantum-limited) formulations are required — CASYMIR does not propagate signal and noise quantities on a per-energy-bin basis

skills.description: Use when modeling an x-ray imaging detector (e.g., a-Se direct conversion or CsI indirect conversion) whose resolution/noise behavior must be predicted from system YAML configurations and acquisition parameters.
skills.name: parallel-cascade-signal-propagation
skills.search_text: parallel-cascade-signal-propagation Use when modeling an x-ray imaging detector (e.g., a-Se direct conversion or CsI indirect conversion) whose resolution/noise behavior must be predicted from system YAML configurations and acquisition parameters. Modeling photon-counting detectors or adaptive-binning processes, which are not yet included in CASYMIR Systems where temporal effects such as detector lag and ghosting, or depth-dependent effects (Lubberts effect, optical Swank noise, Fano noise, photoconductor discharge), dominate noise propagation—these are not explicitly modeled Analyses requiring per-energy-bin propagation of signal and noise quantities or input-quantum-limited (input-labeled) formulations http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Propagate x-ray signal and noise through a detector modeled as cascaded gain, blur, sampling, and aliasing process blocks—serial or in parallel—using CASYMIR to compute the MTF and NNPS of direct- or indirect-conversion detectors. genomics/v1 10.1002/mp.18079
skills.summary: Propagate x-ray signal and noise through a detector modeled as cascaded gain, blur, sampling, and aliasing process blocks—serial or in parallel—using CASYMIR to compute the MTF and NNPS of direct- or indirect-conversion detectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modeling photon-counting detectors or adaptive-binning processes, which are not yet included in CASYMIR Systems where temporal effects such as detector lag and ghosting, or depth-dependent effects (Lubberts effect, optical Swank noise, Fano noise, photoconductor discharge), dominate noise propagation—these are not explicitly modeled Analyses requiring per-energy-bin propagation of signal and noise quantities or input-quantum-limited (input-labeled) formulations

skills.description: Use when building or querying an in-memory barcode-indexed store of poorly aligned reads from a BX-tagged SLR BAM, e.g. to let barcode-aware sliding-window assembly skip badly aligned read pairs.
skills.name: parallel-hash-map-barcode-indexing
skills.search_text: parallel-hash-map-barcode-indexing Use when building or querying an in-memory barcode-indexed store of poorly aligned reads from a BX-tagged SLR BAM, e.g. to let barcode-aware sliding-window assembly skip badly aligned read pairs. Running Blackbird with the hidden `-n` flag, which explicitly disables collection of poorly aligned reads Input reads lack BX barcode tags or the BAM is not position-sorted/indexed, so barcode-keyed queries cannot be built The analysis does not involve SLR/hybrid SV calling with barcode-aware local assembly, where badly aligned reads would never be re-queried http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements Blackbird's read map M: a parallel flat hash map that stores the badly aligned read set R from a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAM file, keyed so that M(B) — the reads sharing any barcode in a list B — can be efficiently retrieved during barcode-based local assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Implements Blackbird's read map M: a parallel flat hash map that stores the badly aligned read set R from a position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAM file, keyed so that M(B) — the reads sharing any barcode in a list B — can be efficiently retrieved during barcode-based local assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running Blackbird with the hidden `-n` flag, which explicitly disables collection of poorly aligned reads Input reads lack BX barcode tags or the BAM is not position-sorted/indexed, so barcode-keyed queries cannot be built The analysis does not involve SLR/hybrid SV calling with barcode-aware local assembly, where badly aligned reads would never be re-queried

skills.description: Use when blastp hits for novel predicted coding genes show multiple high-identity matches and you must decide whether the query is a missing single-copy gene, a paralog, or a novel homolog based on genomic coordinates.
skills.name: paralog-classification-by-genomic-loci
skills.search_text: paralog-classification-by-genomic-loci Use when blastp hits for novel predicted coding genes show multiple high-identity matches and you must decide whether the query is a missing single-copy gene, a paralog, or a novel homolog based on genomic coordinates. Input transcripts are already present in the NCBI reference annotation (GTF reconciliation handles them; the homology/paralog scheme targets genes absent from reference annotations) Hits have <90% homology or are on different loci — they do not meet the paralog criterion and would be misclassified The organism lacks an assembled genome or NCBI GTF annotation, since genomic locus positions cannot be compared http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A homology-based classification step, from the annotate_my_genomes workflow, that distinguishes single-copy homologs from paralogs among blastp hits of novel predicted proteins against the UniProt Gallus gallus proteome by checking whether 90-100% identity matches map to the same genomic locus (<0.5 Mb apart). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: A homology-based classification step, from the annotate_my_genomes workflow, that distinguishes single-copy homologs from paralogs among blastp hits of novel predicted proteins against the UniProt Gallus gallus proteome by checking whether 90-100% identity matches map to the same genomic locus (<0.5 Mb apart).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transcripts are already present in the NCBI reference annotation (GTF reconciliation handles them; the homology/paralog scheme targets genes absent from reference annotations) Hits have <90% homology or are on different loci — they do not meet the paralog criterion and would be misclassified The organism lacks an assembled genome or NCBI GTF annotation, since genomic locus positions cannot be compared

skills.description: Use when simulating sequencing reads or other stochastic quantities that must follow a realistic empirical length/size distribution, and the sampled output needs numerical validation against that target distribution.
skills.name: parametric-distribution-fitting-and-comparison
skills.search_text: parametric-distribution-fitting-and-comparison Use when simulating sequencing reads or other stochastic quantities that must follow a realistic empirical length/size distribution, and the sampled output needs numerical validation against that target distribution. Input is already a set of pre-existing reads (use seq2squiggle's --read-input mode, which simulates signals directly without additional fragmentation) The goal is to model signal-level noise or dwell-time variation rather than read-length sampling (use the noise/duration samplers or static normal distributions for amplitude and event durations instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Draw and validate simulated quantities (e.g. nanopore read lengths) from parametric distributions — exponential, beta, or a mixed/two-gamma mixture inherited from DeepSimulator — and numerically verify that the empirical histogram of generated samples matches the target distribution. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Draw and validate simulated quantities (e.g. nanopore read lengths) from parametric distributions — exponential, beta, or a mixed/two-gamma mixture inherited from DeepSimulator — and numerically verify that the empirical histogram of generated samples matches the target distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of pre-existing reads (use seq2squiggle's --read-input mode, which simulates signals directly without additional fragmentation) The goal is to model signal-level noise or dwell-time variation rather than read-length sampling (use the noise/duration samplers or static normal distributions for amplitude and event durations instead)

skills.description: Use when you have trio (e.g. Ashkenazim HG002/HG003/HG004) Oxford Nanopore POD5/BAM data and need to detect imprinted regions or assign parent-of-origin to haplotype-specific (epihaplotype) methylation patterns.
skills.name: parent-of-origin-epihaplotype-classification
skills.search_text: parent-of-origin-epihaplotype-classification Use when you have trio (e.g. Ashkenazim HG002/HG003/HG004) Oxford Nanopore POD5/BAM data and need to detect imprinted regions or assign parent-of-origin to haplotype-specific (epihaplotype) methylation patterns. Samples lacking trio/parent-offspring structure or phased variant calls — haplotype phasing and parent-of-origin assignment cannot be determined Imprinted regions falling in long runs of homozygosity, where read phasing may not be possible and phased methylation counts alone are unreliable Modifications other than 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides models for 5mCpG due to lack of training data for other methylation types http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Classifies parent-of-origin methylation states (epihaplotypes) at imprinting control regions by combining haplotype-phased reads with phased per-site methylation calls from DeepMod2 on ONT data. Enables trio-based assignment of methylated vs unmethylated parental alleles at known ICRs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Classifies parent-of-origin methylation states (epihaplotypes) at imprinting control regions by combining haplotype-phased reads with phased per-site methylation calls from DeepMod2 on ONT data. Enables trio-based assignment of methylated vs unmethylated parental alleles at known ICRs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lacking trio/parent-offspring structure or phased variant calls — haplotype phasing and parent-of-origin assignment cannot be determined Imprinted regions falling in long runs of homozygosity, where read phasing may not be possible and phased methylation counts alone are unreliable Modifications other than 5mCpG — DeepMod2 currently only provides models for 5mCpG due to lack of training data for other methylation types

skills.description: Use when comparing error correctors on trio-classified diploid long-read datasets and you need to measure, per parental haplotype, which parent-specific k-mers survive correction in the 40X longest corrected reads.
skills.name: parent-specific-kmer-completeness-assessment
skills.search_text: parent-specific-kmer-completeness-assessment Use when comparing error correctors on trio-classified diploid long-read datasets and you need to measure, per parental haplotype, which parent-specific k-mers survive correction in the 40X longest corrected reads. Data without trio classification or parent-specific k-mer annotations — the kp/km consistency and completeness metrics cannot be defined Evaluating correctors on Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi reads, where PECAT itself achieves only mediocre performance Assessing polished assembly base accuracy against a reference (use reference-based tools like Pomoxis instead of k-mer retention) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Evaluates haplotype-specific k-mer consistency and completeness of corrected long reads on trio-classified diploid datasets, to quantify how well an error corrector (e.g., PECAT vs Canu, FALCON, MECAT2, NECAT) retains heterozygote alleles from each parental haplotype. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Evaluates haplotype-specific k-mer consistency and completeness of corrected long reads on trio-classified diploid datasets, to quantify how well an error corrector (e.g., PECAT vs Canu, FALCON, MECAT2, NECAT) retains heterozygote alleles from each parental haplotype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data without trio classification or parent-specific k-mer annotations — the kp/km consistency and completeness metrics cannot be defined Evaluating correctors on Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi reads, where PECAT itself achieves only mediocre performance Assessing polished assembly base accuracy against a reference (use reference-based tools like Pomoxis instead of k-mer retention)

skills.description: Use when you have genotype-resolved variant calls (SNP VCFs, SV/rearrangement/CNV call sets) for parent strains plus cross-level hybrid offspring viability measurements, and want to test which variant classes correlate with reproductive isolation.
skills.name: parental-genetic-distance-computation-from-variant-calls
skills.search_text: parental-genetic-distance-computation-from-variant-calls Use when you have genotype-resolved variant calls (SNP VCFs, SV/rearrangement/CNV call sets) for parent strains plus cross-level hybrid offspring viability measurements, and want to test which variant classes correlate with reproductive isolation. The goal is trait association within strains (mixed-model GWAS on 68 SVs / SNPs with permutation thresholds), not between-strain distance-vs-hybrid-fitness correlation. Variants cannot be reliably genotyped in both parents — in the source study translocations and inversions were not re-examined because they were 'more challenging to accurately genotype'. No cross-level phenotype (hybrid spore viability) exists for the parent pairs, leaving only per-strain trait data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Computes pairwise parental genetic distances as the number of unshared variants between S. pombe parent strains for each variant class (SNPs, all SVs, rearrangements only, CNVs only) from genotyped variant calls, then tests each class against hybrid spore viability using Kendall tau rank correlations and partial correlations. Used to disentangle which variant classes contribute to intrinsic reproductive isolation. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Computes pairwise parental genetic distances as the number of unshared variants between S. pombe parent strains for each variant class (SNPs, all SVs, rearrangements only, CNVs only) from genotyped variant calls, then tests each class against hybrid spore viability using Kendall tau rank correlations and partial correlations. Used to disentangle which variant classes contribute to intrinsic reproductive isolation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is trait association within strains (mixed-model GWAS on 68 SVs / SNPs with permutation thresholds), not between-strain distance-vs-hybrid-fitness correlation. Variants cannot be reliably genotyped in both parents — in the source study translocations and inversions were not re-examined because they were 'more challenging to accurately genotype'. No cross-level phenotype (hybrid spore viability) exists for the parent pairs, leaving only per-strain trait data.

skills.description: Use when you need to build a catalog of indel sites segregating between two parents (e.g., P. deltoides × P. simonii) from parental paired-end FASTQ reads, as the first step before calling indel genotypes across a hybrid population.
skills.name: parental-indel-catalog-generation
skills.search_text: parental-indel-catalog-generation Use when you need to build a catalog of indel sites segregating between two parents (e.g., P. deltoides × P. simonii) from parental paired-end FASTQ reads, as the first step before calling indel genotypes across a hybrid population. The parental indel catalog already exists (parent.cls from a previous run) — skip this step with the --nocatalog flag to go directly to genotype calling. The goal is calling indel genotypes across the progeny or testing Mendelian segregation — those are steps 2 and 3 of InDelGT, not catalog generation. Input data are not paired-end reads from two parents plus a reference genome aligned to restriction sites (e.g., whole-genome variant calls from other tools). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Generate the parental indel catalog (parent.cls) by aligning the two parental RAD-seq FASTQ files to a reference genome with BWA and calling indels at restriction-site loci with SAMtools/BCFtools — step 1 of the InDelGT pipeline. This catalog defines the indel marker set used for downstream genotyping of the hybrid progeny. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Generate the parental indel catalog (parent.cls) by aligning the two parental RAD-seq FASTQ files to a reference genome with BWA and calling indels at restriction-site loci with SAMtools/BCFtools — step 1 of the InDelGT pipeline. This catalog defines the indel marker set used for downstream genotyping of the hybrid progeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The parental indel catalog already exists (parent.cls from a previous run) — skip this step with the --nocatalog flag to go directly to genotype calling. The goal is calling indel genotypes across the progeny or testing Mendelian segregation — those are steps 2 and 3 of InDelGT, not catalog generation. Input data are not paired-end reads from two parents plus a reference genome aligned to restriction sites (e.g., whole-genome variant calls from other tools).

skills.description: Use when running the miRPursuit novel-miRNA branch (Step 4, miRCat) on a large reference genome such as TAIR10 on a machine with limited RAM, requiring genome-part execution and result merging.
skills.name: part-based-genome-result-merging
skills.search_text: part-based-genome-result-merging Use when running the miRPursuit novel-miRNA branch (Step 4, miRCat) on a large reference genome such as TAIR10 on a machine with limited RAM, requiring genome-part execution and result merging. When sufficient RAM is available to run miRCat against the whole genome in one pass — the README states to set GENOME_MIRCAT=${GENOME} if you don't need to run various parts When the goal is conserved miRNA quantification (miRProf against miRBase) rather than novel miRNA prediction from non-conserved reads When the analysis target is tasiRNA prediction (Step 3, ta-si predictor) rather than Step 4 miRCat http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Handles RAM-limited novel miRNA prediction in miRPursuit by running miRCat against split genome part files (e.g. GENOME_MIRCAT=${GENOME/.fa/part-1.fa}) instead of the full genome, merging the part-based prediction sets, and filtering merged hits by the max_genome_hits threshold in wbench_mircat.cfg. genomics/v1 10.1002/1873-3468.12746
skills.summary: Handles RAM-limited novel miRNA prediction in miRPursuit by running miRCat against split genome part files (e.g. GENOME_MIRCAT=${GENOME/.fa/part-1.fa}) instead of the full genome, merging the part-based prediction sets, and filtering merged hits by the max_genome_hits threshold in wbench_mircat.cfg.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sufficient RAM is available to run miRCat against the whole genome in one pass — the README states to set GENOME_MIRCAT=${GENOME} if you don't need to run various parts When the goal is conserved miRNA quantification (miRProf against miRBase) rather than novel miRNA prediction from non-conserved reads When the analysis target is tasiRNA prediction (Step 3, ta-si predictor) rather than Step 4 miRCat

skills.description: Use when evaluating how robustly a long-read transcript annotation or reconstruction tool recovers known splice junctions when the supplied reference annotation is incomplete, i.e. sensitivity/precision as a function of annotation completeness.
skills.name: partial-annotation-deletion-benchmarking
skills.search_text: partial-annotation-deletion-benchmarking Use when evaluating how robustly a long-read transcript annotation or reconstruction tool recovers known splice junctions when the supplied reference annotation is incomplete, i.e. sensitivity/precision as a function of annotation completeness. Input transcripts are short-read RNA-seq reads rather than full-length Iso-seq (PacBio HiFi) transcripts, since this benchmark is designed for Iso-seq full-length transcript FASTA The goal is de novo junction discovery with a complete, trusted reference annotation rather than stress-testing recovery under annotation incompleteness The organism lacks a curated GTF annotation, so genes cannot be systematically deleted from a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3574 Benchmark splice-junction recovery sensitivity and precision of transcript annotation tools (TAGET vs SQANTI, IsoQuant, StringTie2, FLAIR) by systematically deleting 5-50% of genes from the hg38.ensembl.gtf reference and measuring how much of the removed annotation each tool recovers from Iso-seq data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Benchmark splice-junction recovery sensitivity and precision of transcript annotation tools (TAGET vs SQANTI, IsoQuant, StringTie2, FLAIR) by systematically deleting 5-50% of genes from the hg38.ensembl.gtf reference and measuring how much of the removed annotation each tool recovers from Iso-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transcripts are short-read RNA-seq reads rather than full-length Iso-seq (PacBio HiFi) transcripts, since this benchmark is designed for Iso-seq full-length transcript FASTA The goal is de novo junction discovery with a complete, trusted reference annotation rather than stress-testing recovery under annotation incompleteness The organism lacks a curated GTF annotation, so genes cannot be systematically deleted from a reference

skills.description: Use when two variant classes (e.g. SNPs vs rearrangements) both correlate with an outcome such as offspring viability and you must estimate each factor's influence alone via partial correlations on unshared-variant distances.
skills.name: partial-correlation-confounder-control
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-confounder-control Use when two variant classes (e.g. SNPs vs rearrangements) both correlate with an outcome such as offspring viability and you must estimate each factor's influence alone via partial correlations on unshared-variant distances. Input is per-strain GWAS genotype/phenotype data rather than paired parental distances and cross-level spore-viability measurements — use mixed-model GWAS instead The candidate predictors are near-perfectly collinear, so partial correlations are unstable and cannot separate the factors' influence The variant classes of interest were not reliably genotyped (the authors did not re-examine translocations and inversions because they were challenging to accurately genotype) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies whether two correlated genetic-distance predictors (e.g. parental SNP-distance and rearrangement-distance) each independently explain hybrid spore viability, by computing Kendall tau rank correlations per variant class and then partial correlations that control for the other class. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Quantifies whether two correlated genetic-distance predictors (e.g. parental SNP-distance and rearrangement-distance) each independently explain hybrid spore viability, by computing Kendall tau rank correlations per variant class and then partial correlations that control for the other class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is per-strain GWAS genotype/phenotype data rather than paired parental distances and cross-level spore-viability measurements — use mixed-model GWAS instead The candidate predictors are near-perfectly collinear, so partial correlations are unstable and cannot separate the factors' influence The variant classes of interest were not reliably genotyped (the authors did not re-examine translocations and inversions because they were challenging to accurately genotype)

skills.description: Use when error-prone ONT or PacBio long reads must be converted into accurate per-haplotype consensus sequences for candidate repetitive regions (e.g., BED-defined [S,E] intervals) before motif profiling.
skills.name: partial-order-alignment-consensus
skills.search_text: partial-order-alignment-consensus Use when error-prone ONT or PacBio long reads must be converted into accurate per-haplotype consensus sequences for candidate repetitive regions (e.g., BED-defined [S,E] intervals) before motif profiling. The goal is de novo discovery of repetitive regions from raw reads — use the upstream SENSoR Shannon-entropy stage (20 bp windows, entropy threshold 1.23) instead of consensus generation Repeats lie in unassembled regions of the genome (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify Reads do not entirely span the region of interest; partially spanning reads are not fetched for POA consensus http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Generates haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences for candidate repetitive regions by trimming haplotype-resolved long reads to a region of interest and running SIMD-accelerated partial order alignment (SPOA), as used in the TRiCoLOR REFER stage. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Generates haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences for candidate repetitive regions by trimming haplotype-resolved long reads to a region of interest and running SIMD-accelerated partial order alignment (SPOA), as used in the TRiCoLOR REFER stage.

skills.description: Use when two gene sets being compared for functional feature annotation share a substantial fraction of members (e.g. coDIU and DIU gene sets from an acorde analysis), so a standard proportion test assuming independence is inappropriate.

skills.search_text: partially-overlapping-samples-z-test Use when two gene sets being compared for functional feature annotation share a substantial fraction of members (e.g. coDIU and DIU gene sets from an acorde analysis), so a standard proportion test assuming independence is inappropriate. The gene sets being compared are fully disjoint, so a standard two-proportion enrichment test suffices and the partially-overlapping correction is unnecessary The transcriptome is de novo rather than a pre-annotated reference compatible with IsoAnnotLite/tappAS, since functional features cannot be transferred to the isoform models The goal is gene-level differential expression or DIU testing rather than functional annotation enrichment A tappAS statistical test for functional enrichment that compares the proportion of annotated genes between partially overlapping gene sets — used in the acorde study to identify positional functional features and GO terms enriched in coDIU versus DIU genes in mouse neural single-cell isoform data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w

skills.summary: Selects a best-fit partitioning scheme and substitution models for multi-marker nucleotide alignments (e.g. concatenated 18S/5.8S/28S rDNA or full-amplicon rDNA with ITS regions) using PartitionFinder, so that downstream Bayesian inference in MrBayes runs under an appropriate model per partition rather than a single global model.

skills.name: pbmc-marker-gene-curation
skills.search_text: pbmc-marker-gene-curation Use when processing long-read single-cell (10x) FASTQ data, e.g. PacBio or Oxford Nanopore PBMC runs, and you need marker-based cell-type assignments plus pseudobulk per-cell-type counts from scywalker. Input is already a cell-by-gene or cell-by-isoform count matrix from another pipeline — scywalker's typing runs end-to-end from FASTQ within its own workflow No cell-type marker file is available and sctype's internal tissue database does not cover the sample's tissue — scsorter/sctype celltyping is skipped and only counts are produced Limited test data (e.g. chromosome-17-restricted scywalker_test dataset) — the included markers_chr17.tsv are explicitly 'not good markers, they are just made to allow celltyping to at least run' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Curate a PBMC cell-type marker file (with 'marker' and 'celltype' columns) and use it with scywalker's cell filtering and typing module (scsorter, optionally sctype) to assign canonical PBMC populations — T cells, B cells, monocytes, NK cells — from long-read single-cell data such as the PacBio PBMC dataset shown in Supplementary Fig. S16. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549

skills.summary: Final grouping step of the bin2cell pipeline in which 2 μm Visium HD bins are assigned to reconstructed cell labels produced by StarDist segmentation and label expansion, using PCA transcriptional similarity to resolve equidistant bins.

skills.description: Use when per-sample species/genera-resolved ARG abundance tables (cpg values from Argo) must be compared across sample groups (e.g., CN, KR, SG, DE, US human vs NH non-human primate) by composition rather than total abundance.
skills.name: pcoa-permanova-beta-diversity-analysis
skills.search_text: pcoa-permanova-beta-diversity-analysis Use when per-sample species/genera-resolved ARG abundance tables (cpg values from Argo) must be compared across sample groups (e.g., CN, KR, SG, DE, US human vs NH non-human primate) by composition rather than total abundance. Input is raw long reads or unprocessed Argo output files rather than aggregated per-sample abundance matrices The question concerns differences in total ARG abundance (cpg) per group — use Kruskal–Wallis with pairwise Mann–Whitney (Bonferroni-corrected) tests instead of ordination-based testing Reads are short reads or abundance data without species/genera resolution, since Argo's species-resolved cpg outputs are the expected basis for the dissimilarity matrix Decomposes ARG abundance profiles (e.g., genera-level or ARG-type compositions in copies-per-genome from Argo outputs) into beta-diversity structure using principal coordinate analysis and tests group differences with PERMANOVA, as applied to compare human versus non-human primate fecal ARG profiles. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Decomposes ARG abundance profiles (e.g., genera-level or ARG-type compositions in copies-per-genome from Argo outputs) into beta-diversity structure using principal coordinate analysis and tests group differences with PERMANOVA, as applied to compare human versus non-human primate fecal ARG profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long reads or unprocessed Argo output files rather than aggregated per-sample abundance matrices The question concerns differences in total ARG abundance (cpg) per group — use Kruskal–Wallis with pairwise Mann–Whitney (Bonferroni-corrected) tests instead of ordination-based testing Reads are short reads or abundance data without species/genera resolution, since Argo's species-resolved cpg outputs are the expected basis for the dissimilarity matrix

skills.search_text: pcr-primer-design-breakpoint-spanning Use when a NanoFG (or similar SV-caller) breakpoint VCF contains a called fusion gene whose junction must be validated by breakpoint PCR, and flanking reference sequence is available from GRCh37. Starting material is fragmented FFPE DNA, which the article notes will most likely fail FUDGE/NanoFG fusion identification and thus cannot supply reliable breakpoints for primer design. The goal is de novo assembly or SV discovery rather than validating an already-called fusion breakpoint. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Designs PCR primer pairs that span a detected fusion gene breakpoint by running Primer3 on reference sequence flanking the NanoFG-called breakpoint (GRCh37), enabling experimental validation of fusion calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: Designs PCR primer pairs that span a detected fusion gene breakpoint by running Primer3 on reference sequence flanking the NanoFG-called breakpoint (GRCh37), enabling experimental validation of fusion calls.

The goal is de novo assembly or SV discovery rather than validating an already-called fusion breakpoint.

skills.summary: Quantify concordance between HIT-scISOseq (PacBio Sequel II long-read) and Illumina short-read NGS single-cell UMI/gene count matrices, and between HIT-scISOseq biological replicates, by computing Pearson correlation coefficients on aggregated UMI counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrices come from different cells/samples without shared cell barcodes or gene identifiers, so paired correlation is undefined The goal is isoform-level (not gene/UMI-level) comparison, which requires the scIsoform_matrix output and SQANTI3-filtered isoform set rather than UMI totals Raw CCS/FLNC read data still needs demultiplexing — run scISA-Tools (classify_by_primer, cellBC_UMI_corrector) before any correlation

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether simulated nanopore reads (DNA metagenomic or direct-RNA) preserve known strain or transcript-isoform relative abundances and when comparing fidelity against other simulators.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-against-simulator-baselines
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-benchmark-against-simulator-baselines Use when evaluating whether simulated nanopore reads (DNA metagenomic or direct-RNA) preserve known strain or transcript-isoform relative abundances and when comparing fidelity against other simulators. Input is real experimental sequencing data rather than simulator output — there is no simulator baseline to benchmark and correlation against ground truth is trivially the data itself. The reference abundances of the community/transcripts are unknown, making a correlation between estimated and known abundances undefined. The analysis goal is basecalling accuracy or variant-calling fidelity (SNP/indel F1), not abundance preservation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantify how faithfully simulator-generated nanopore reads preserve known relative abundances by computing Pearson correlations between estimated and ground-truth abundances, and benchmarking against baseline simulators (seq2squiggle, Squigulator). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Quantify how faithfully simulator-generated nanopore reads preserve known relative abundances by computing Pearson correlations between estimated and ground-truth abundances, and benchmarking against baseline simulators (seq2squiggle, Squigulator).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental sequencing data rather than simulator output — there is no simulator baseline to benchmark and correlation against ground truth is trivially the data itself. The reference abundances of the community/transcripts are unknown, making a correlation between estimated and known abundances undefined. The analysis goal is basecalling accuracy or variant-calling fidelity (SNP/indel F1), not abundance preservation.

skills.description: Use when you have per-site methylation frequencies from a Nanopore caller (e.g., output.per_site.aggregated from DeepMod2) plus matched short-read WGBS or methylation microarray ground truth, and need a genome-wide correlation benchmark per sample and flowcell.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-computation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-benchmark-computation Use when you have per-site methylation frequencies from a Nanopore caller (e.g., output.per_site.aggregated from DeepMod2) plus matched short-read WGBS or methylation microarray ground truth, and need a genome-wide correlation benchmark per sample and flowcell. Evaluating per-read (not per-site) methylation accuracy — use per-read F1-score against binary ground truth (sites ≥90% or <10% methylated, ≥10X coverage) instead of frequency correlation Ground-truth sites with intermediate methylation (20–80%) should be excluded, as EpiQC reported poor concordance between ONT and short-read methods in that range Non-CpG methylation (e.g., 5hmC or non-CpG contexts) — DeepMod2 only provides models for 5mCpG methylation http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Compute genome-wide Pearson correlation coefficients between a Nanopore methylation caller's per-site CpG methylation frequencies (e.g., DeepMod2 output.per_site.aggregated) and short-read bisulfite sequencing or methylation microarray ground truth, benchmarking against the reported r > 0.95 for DeepMod2 on the Ashkenazim trio R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 datasets. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Compute genome-wide Pearson correlation coefficients between a Nanopore methylation caller's per-site CpG methylation frequencies (e.g., DeepMod2 output.per_site.aggregated) and short-read bisulfite sequencing or methylation microarray ground truth, benchmarking against the reported r > 0.95 for DeepMod2 on the Ashkenazim trio R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating per-read (not per-site) methylation accuracy — use per-read F1-score against binary ground truth (sites ≥90% or <10% methylated, ≥10X coverage) instead of frequency correlation Ground-truth sites with intermediate methylation (20–80%) should be excluded, as EpiQC reported poor concordance between ONT and short-read methods in that range Non-CpG methylation (e.g., 5hmC or non-CpG contexts) — DeepMod2 only provides models for 5mCpG methylation

skills.description: Use when a regression model's continuous predictions (e.g. ΔΨ per variant) must be scored against held-out experimental values on an independent test set, as in CAGI-style blind challenges.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-benchmark-evaluation Use when a regression model's continuous predictions (e.g. ΔΨ per variant) must be scored against held-out experimental values on an independent test set, as in CAGI-style blind challenges. skills.search_text: per-cell-snv-genotyping-matrix-construction Use when you have long-read (ONT/PacBio) amplicon reads from 10x Genomics 5' scRNA-seq cDNA libraries targeting known somatic mutations and need per-cell genotype calls and genotyping rates keyed by cell barcode.
