skills.summary: Constructs a per-cell single-nucleotide-variant genotyping matrix from long-read single-cell amplicon data by collapsing nanoranger variant calls to 10x Genomics cell barcodes, enabling quantification of per-mutation genotyping rates as demonstrated for AML1022 mutations (DNMT3AR882H, RUNX1I177S, SF3B1K700E).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target loci are far from the 5' end of lowly expressed genes with transcripts longer than 4 kB — nanoranger performs best for loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcript lengths shorter than 4 kB Input is short-read Illumina data requiring whole-gene primer panels — existing Illumina-based single-cell genotyping requires large numbers of primers and is suboptimal for long fragments You need to detect private or rarely mutated somatic mutations beyond the primed targets — increasing genotyped features per sample to such mutations remains future work

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation quality between two representations of Visium HD data (e.g. bin2cell cells vs 8 μm bins) and you need per-cell-type tallies of median confidence and mean genes detected.
skills.name: per-cell-type-confidence-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-confidence-aggregation Use when comparing cell-type annotation quality between two representations of Visium HD data (e.g. bin2cell cells vs 8 μm bins) and you need per-cell-type tallies of median confidence and mean genes detected. Input is a single AnnData representation with no matched comparison object (e.g. only b2c cells or only 8 μm bins) — no comparison table can be built. The CellTypist model was not trained on a matching species/tissue atlas (e.g. a human atlas applied to mouse brain data) — confidence scores would not be interpretable across 113 mouse brain cell types. Expression matrices are raw counts without library-size normalization and log1p — gene detection counts would not be comparable across representations. Aggregate CellTypist annotation confidence and gene detection per cell type to compare two Visium HD representations (bin2cell-reconstructed cells vs default 8 μm bins), quantifying how many of the 113 Yao et al. 2023 atlas cell types favor each representation. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546
skills.summary: Aggregate CellTypist annotation confidence and gene detection per cell type to compare two Visium HD representations (bin2cell-reconstructed cells vs default 8 μm bins), quantifying how many of the 113 Yao et al. 2023 atlas cell types favor each representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single AnnData representation with no matched comparison object (e.g. only b2c cells or only 8 μm bins) — no comparison table can be built. The CellTypist model was not trained on a matching species/tissue atlas (e.g. a human atlas applied to mouse brain data) — confidence scores would not be interpretable across 113 mouse brain cell types. Expression matrices are raw counts without library-size normalization and log1p — gene detection counts would not be comparable across representations.

skills.description: Use when you have a long-read WGS BAM (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) from a diploid sample and need a phased, per-chromosome diploid assembly as input for SV calling or resource benchmarking.
skills.name: per-chromosome-phased-assembly
skills.search_text: per-chromosome-phased-assembly Use when you have a long-read WGS BAM (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) from a diploid sample and need a phased, per-chromosome diploid assembly as input for SV calling or resource benchmarking. The sample is haploid or homozygous (e.g. CHM13): phasing is unsuitable, as the paper did not use VolcanoSV-asm for the CHM13 diploid assembly You need sex chromosome assemblies: VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since sex-chromosome phasing differs Input is short-read data or unaligned FASTQ without a reference — the pipeline is a hybrid method requiring read alignments to a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Runs VolcanoSV-asm, which assembles each autosome independently with a platform-appropriate assembler (hifiasm for HiFi, Flye for CLR/ONT) and phasing/local-assembly modules to produce a haplotype-resolved diploid contig set from long-read BAMs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Runs VolcanoSV-asm, which assembles each autosome independently with a platform-appropriate assembler (hifiasm for HiFi, Flye for CLR/ONT) and phasing/local-assembly modules to produce a haplotype-resolved diploid contig set from long-read BAMs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is haploid or homozygous (e.g. CHM13): phasing is unsuitable, as the paper did not use VolcanoSV-asm for the CHM13 diploid assembly You need sex chromosome assemblies: VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes since sex-chromosome phasing differs Input is short-read data or unaligned FASTQ without a reference — the pipeline is a hybrid method requiring read alignments to a reference

skills.description: Use when a labelled ntLink PAF mapping file (produced with paf=True) must be summarised into counts and per-contig averages, e.g. to reproduce or validate the mapping statistics of Table 5.
skills.name: per-contig-mapping-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-contig-mapping-count-aggregation Use when a labelled ntLink PAF mapping file (produced with paf=True) must be summarised into counts and per-contig averages, e.g. to reproduce or validate the mapping statistics of Table 5. The input is a raw minimizer sketch or scaffold graph rather than a completed PAF mapping file — the aggregation operates on PAF records only The goal is assembly correction or scaffolding; use Tigmint-long (Alternate Protocol 2) or ntLink's scaffolding modes instead of just counting mappings Quality/identity assessment of individual alignments is needed (e.g. via minimap2 alignment scores) — this skill only aggregates counts and coordinate-derived lengths http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Summarise an ntLink PAF mapping file (long-read-to-contig mappings from Alternate Protocol 1) into table-level statistics — total mappings, average mapping block length, and average mappings per draft contig — using Miller (mlr) delimited-data operations, for validation against Table 5 of the ntLink protocols paper. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.733
skills.summary: Summarise an ntLink PAF mapping file (long-read-to-contig mappings from Alternate Protocol 1) into table-level statistics — total mappings, average mapping block length, and average mappings per draft contig — using Miller (mlr) delimited-data operations, for validation against Table 5 of the ntLink protocols paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw minimizer sketch or scaffold graph rather than a completed PAF mapping file — the aggregation operates on PAF records only The goal is assembly correction or scaffolding; use Tigmint-long (Alternate Protocol 2) or ntLink's scaffolding modes instead of just counting mappings Quality/identity assessment of individual alignments is needed (e.g. via minimap2 alignment scores) — this skill only aggregates counts and coordinate-derived lengths

skills.description: Use when validating metagenome assemblies by measuring what fraction of contig bases are covered by mapped reads — e.g. to detect poorly covered assembler outputs like the CLC bio Horizon oil-spill assembly (~85% coverage vs ~99% for MeGAMerge).
skills.name: per-contig-read-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: per-contig-read-coverage-quantification Use when validating metagenome assemblies by measuring what fraction of contig bases are covered by mapped reads — e.g. to detect poorly covered assembler outputs like the CLC bio Horizon oil-spill assembly (~85% coverage vs ~99% for MeGAMerge). Input is raw unassembled reads with no contig FASTA to map against — coverage validation presupposes existing assemblies Reads are untrimmed low-quality data — the article's coverage statistics assume reads trimmed with a sliding window protocol at minimum quality score 2 The goal is reference-genome coverage assessment rather than read-based contig coverage — that requires aligning contigs to genomes with Nucmer instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies the percentage of bases on each assembled contig (individual assembler output or MeGAMerge MergedContigs.fasta) covered by trimmed sample reads, using BWA mapping parsed with SAMtools, to validate assembly quality and expose assembler-specific coverage deficits. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Quantifies the percentage of bases on each assembled contig (individual assembler output or MeGAMerge MergedContigs.fasta) covered by trimmed sample reads, using BWA mapping parsed with SAMtools, to validate assembly quality and expose assembler-specific coverage deficits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unassembled reads with no contig FASTA to map against — coverage validation presupposes existing assemblies Reads are untrimmed low-quality data — the article's coverage statistics assume reads trimmed with a sliding window protocol at minimum quality score 2 The goal is reference-genome coverage assessment rather than read-based contig coverage — that requires aligning contigs to genomes with Nucmer instead

skills.description: Use when you have barcoded long-read alignments to a reference genome and need per-cell/per-droplet gene and isoform count matrices, including novel isoforms, with explicit handling of multimapping reads.
skills.name: per-droplet-isoform-and-gene-quantification
skills.search_text: per-droplet-isoform-and-gene-quantification Use when you have barcoded long-read alignments to a reference genome and need per-cell/per-droplet gene and isoform count matrices, including novel isoforms, with explicit handling of multimapping reads. Input is bulk long-read data without 10x droplet barcodes and no per-cell quantification is required — IsoQuant alone can quantify without the per-droplet machinery Reads are unaligned FASTQ — alignment (minimap2_splice) and transcript reconstruction must run first http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 scywalker assigns barcoded long reads to IsoQuant-reconstructed transcript models and generates per-droplet (per-cell) isoform and gene count tables in weighted, unique, strict, polyA-restricted, and nicount variants, in _raw and _filtered versions. This turns full-length nanopore/PacBio alignments into single-cell quantification comparable to short-read count matrices. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: scywalker assigns barcoded long reads to IsoQuant-reconstructed transcript models and generates per-droplet (per-cell) isoform and gene count tables in weighted, unique, strict, polyA-restricted, and nicount variants, in _raw and _filtered versions. This turns full-length nanopore/PacBio alignments into single-cell quantification comparable to short-read count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk long-read data without 10x droplet barcodes and no per-cell quantification is required — IsoQuant alone can quantify without the per-droplet machinery Reads are unaligned FASTQ — alignment (minimap2_splice) and transcript reconstruction must run first

skills.description: Use when two-pass imaging timing data (per-slide acquisition time, detected-object counts, full-slide image counts) must be converted into per-sample cost and a speedup factor to benchmark against a reported figure.
skills.name: per-embryo-cost-normalization
skills.search_text: per-embryo-cost-normalization Use when two-pass imaging timing data (per-slide acquisition time, detected-object counts, full-slide image counts) must be converted into per-sample cost and a speedup factor to benchmark against a reported figure. The imaging dataset lacks per-slide timing or detected-object counts, so per-embryo normalization cannot be computed The screen uses single-pass acquisition or well-based (e.g., cell culture plate) samples rather than slide-based two-pass imaging, so the full-slide 20x baseline comparison is invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Derives the per-embryo high-resolution imaging cost from the OpenHiCAMM two-pass (Phase 1/Phase 2) timing data by normalizing per-slide acquisition time by the ~300 embryos imaged per slide, then validates the computed >10x speedup against full-slide 20x imaging baselines. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Derives the per-embryo high-resolution imaging cost from the OpenHiCAMM two-pass (Phase 1/Phase 2) timing data by normalizing per-slide acquisition time by the ~300 embryos imaged per slide, then validates the computed >10x speedup against full-slide 20x imaging baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The imaging dataset lacks per-slide timing or detected-object counts, so per-embryo normalization cannot be computed The screen uses single-pass acquisition or well-based (e.g., cell culture plate) samples rather than slide-based two-pass imaging, so the full-slide 20x baseline comparison is invalid

skills.description: Use when you have per-read internal non-A residue calls (position, count, tail length) from PAIso-seq CCS reads and need transcript/gene-level non-A fractions comparable to Fig. 2c of the PAIso-seq paper.
skills.name: per-gene-non-a-ratio-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-gene-non-a-ratio-aggregation Use when you have per-read internal non-A residue calls (position, count, tail length) from PAIso-seq CCS reads and need transcript/gene-level non-A fractions comparable to Fig. 2c of the PAIso-seq paper. The goal is quantifying non-A modifications at the very last 3'-end base of the poly(A) tail — PAIso-seq cannot accurately quantify terminal non-A residues because terminal G/C/U pair to the adaptor and are lost. Input data are short-read or non-PacBio (e.g., Illumina/TAIL-seq) where internal poly(A) tail bases are not directly read and per-read non-A positions cannot be called. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Aggregates U/G/C residues detected inside poly(A) tail bodies (called by the PAIso-seq pipeline) into per-transcript and per-gene non-A ratios across mouse GV oocyte sequencing replicates, so that the fraction of mRNAs harboring internal non-A residues can be validated against the paper's 17% benchmark and per-gene ratios checked for replicate correlation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Aggregates U/G/C residues detected inside poly(A) tail bodies (called by the PAIso-seq pipeline) into per-transcript and per-gene non-A ratios across mouse GV oocyte sequencing replicates, so that the fraction of mRNAs harboring internal non-A residues can be validated against the paper's 17% benchmark and per-gene ratios checked for replicate correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantifying non-A modifications at the very last 3'-end base of the poly(A) tail — PAIso-seq cannot accurately quantify terminal non-A residues because terminal G/C/U pair to the adaptor and are lost. Input data are short-read or non-PacBio (e.g., Illumina/TAIL-seq) where internal poly(A) tail bases are not directly read and per-read non-A positions cannot be called.

skills.description: Use when ONT nanopolish call-methylation TSVs exist for tumor and matched control and the goal is per-locus hypomethylation P-values at LINE1 3' transduction source elements, combined across positions.
skills.name: per-locus-fisher-exact-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: per-locus-fisher-exact-hypothesis-testing Use when ONT nanopolish call-methylation TSVs exist for tumor and matched control and the goal is per-locus hypomethylation P-values at LINE1 3' transduction source elements, combined across positions. The goal is detecting or classifying somatic SVs or mobile element insertions themselves — use the nanomonsv Canonical SV or Single breakend SV modules instead; this skill only tests methylation at already-inferred source loci. Only basecalled reads/alignments are available without the original fast5 signal files — 'nanopolish index' and 'call-methylation' cannot run from BAM/FASTQ alone. Need an aggregate methylation comparison across the whole genome or broad regions rather than per-locus tests at specific LINE1 source elements. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Per-locus one-sided Fisher's exact tests on nanopolish-derived per-position methylation frequencies, with P-values combined per LINE1 3' transduction source element using the harmonicmeanp package, to test tumor-vs-matched-control hypomethylation from ONT raw signal-level methylation calls. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Per-locus one-sided Fisher's exact tests on nanopolish-derived per-position methylation frequencies, with P-values combined per LINE1 3' transduction source element using the harmonicmeanp package, to test tumor-vs-matched-control hypomethylation from ONT raw signal-level methylation calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting or classifying somatic SVs or mobile element insertions themselves — use the nanomonsv Canonical SV or Single breakend SV modules instead; this skill only tests methylation at already-inferred source loci. Only basecalled reads/alignments are available without the original fast5 signal files — 'nanopolish index' and 'call-methylation' cannot run from BAM/FASTQ alone. Need an aggregate methylation comparison across the whole genome or broad regions rather than per-locus tests at specific LINE1 source elements.

skills.description: Use when nanopore reads (cDNA SQK-PCS111 or direct RNA SQK-RNA002) have been aligned to a plasmid or mRNA reference and you need per-position mismatch/insertion/deletion counts or per-read mean error rates against the reference.
skills.name: per-nucleotide-error-profiling
skills.search_text: per-nucleotide-error-profiling Use when nanopore reads (cDNA SQK-PCS111 or direct RNA SQK-RNA002) have been aligned to a plasmid or mRNA reference and you need per-position mismatch/insertion/deletion counts or per-read mean error rates against the reference. Reads have not yet been aligned to a reference — pysamstats pileup-based statistics require a SAM/BAM alignment against a reference FASTA The goal is short-read (Illumina) error profiling, which in this workflow is trimmed to Q20 with TrimGalore and analysed separately, not with this ONT error profile Secondary or non-primary alignments should be included — the workflow explicitly filters with 'SAMtools view -F 2048' before profiling http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3569 Determines the per-nucleotide error profile (mismatches, insertions, deletions) of mapped ONT nanopore reads against a reference sequence using pysamstats, decomposing the observed error rate into error-type classes. Used in the VAX-seq mRNA vaccine QC workflow to quantify sequencing error rates, including elevated deletion rates in the poly(A) tail. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Determines the per-nucleotide error profile (mismatches, insertions, deletions) of mapped ONT nanopore reads against a reference sequence using pysamstats, decomposing the observed error rate into error-type classes. Used in the VAX-seq mRNA vaccine QC workflow to quantify sequencing error rates, including elevated deletion rates in the poly(A) tail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not yet been aligned to a reference — pysamstats pileup-based statistics require a SAM/BAM alignment against a reference FASTA The goal is short-read (Illumina) error profiling, which in this workflow is trimmed to Q20 with TrimGalore and analysed separately, not with this ONT error profile Secondary or non-primary alignments should be included — the workflow explicitly filters with 'SAMtools view -F 2048' before profiling

skills.description: Use when direct RNA nanopore reads aligned to a reference transcript (sorted/indexed BAM) must be scanned for position-specific error enrichment — e.g. elevated mismatch/deletion rates marking N1-methylpseudouridine sites in mRNA vaccines.
skills.name: per-nucleotide-error-statistics-interpretation
skills.search_text: per-nucleotide-error-statistics-interpretation Use when direct RNA nanopore reads aligned to a reference transcript (sorted/indexed BAM) must be scanned for position-specific error enrichment — e.g. elevated mismatch/deletion rates marking N1-methylpseudouridine sites in mRNA vaccines. Data are nanopore cDNA sequencing rather than direct RNA — the authors found cDNA sequencing more reliable, so error-based modification signatures at specific nucleosides are not the expected signal Input is raw FASTQ without a BAM alignment to a reference transcript — Mana analyses ONT alignments (.BAM), not unassembled reads Goal is general run/sample quality (read length N50, quality scores) rather than position-specific error signature — NanoPlot-style QC is the wrong lens here http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Interprets the per-nucleotide error profile (mismatches, deletions, insertions) from direct RNA ONT alignments (.BAM) to detect chemically modified nucleosides such as N1-methylpseudouridine in synthetic mRNA, using Mana's QC reports (built on Pysam/pysamstats). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Interprets the per-nucleotide error profile (mismatches, deletions, insertions) from direct RNA ONT alignments (.BAM) to detect chemically modified nucleosides such as N1-methylpseudouridine in synthetic mRNA, using Mana's QC reports (built on Pysam/pysamstats).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are nanopore cDNA sequencing rather than direct RNA — the authors found cDNA sequencing more reliable, so error-based modification signatures at specific nucleosides are not the expected signal Input is raw FASTQ without a BAM alignment to a reference transcript — Mana analyses ONT alignments (.BAM), not unassembled reads Goal is general run/sample quality (read length N50, quality scores) rather than position-specific error signature — NanoPlot-style QC is the wrong lens here

skills.description: Use when telomeric long reads have already been chromosome-end-assigned (e.g., Chr 7q in sample.telomap.tsv) and the goal is to profile, cluster, and compare sample-specific TVS distribution signatures across the telomeric repeat region.
skills.name: per-nucleotide-motif-frequency-profiling
skills.search_text: per-nucleotide-motif-frequency-profiling Use when telomeric long reads have already been chromosome-end-assigned (e.g., Chr 7q in sample.telomap.tsv) and the goal is to profile, cluster, and compare sample-specific TVS distribution signatures across the telomeric repeat region. The goal is telomere length distribution (TELOMERE_LEN histograms) rather than positional TVS variant-sequence signature comparison Input reads lack unambiguous subtelomeric anchor assignment to a specific chromosome end (e.g., subtelomeric regions too short against T2T-CHM13 after RsaI/HinfI trimming) Data are from ALT cells whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity, so full telomere tracts are not captured in reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the per-nucleotide frequency of non-canonical telomeric variant sequences (TVS) across the first 3 kb of individual chromosome-end telomeres from PacBio HiFi reads processed by telomap, yielding a dispersed TVS signature that is patient/sample-specific and evaluated by pairwise Euclidean-distance correlation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Quantifies the per-nucleotide frequency of non-canonical telomeric variant sequences (TVS) across the first 3 kb of individual chromosome-end telomeres from PacBio HiFi reads processed by telomap, yielding a dispersed TVS signature that is patient/sample-specific and evaluated by pairwise Euclidean-distance correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is telomere length distribution (TELOMERE_LEN histograms) rather than positional TVS variant-sequence signature comparison Input reads lack unambiguous subtelomeric anchor assignment to a specific chromosome end (e.g., subtelomeric regions too short against T2T-CHM13 after RsaI/HinfI trimming) Data are from ALT cells whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity, so full telomere tracts are not captured in reads

skills.description: Use when dZ-positive reads in a mixed metagenome must be traced to their organism of origin, i.e. a per-read Z-Calling SVM TSV exists and reads are aligned to a multi-organism reference and you need per-species LR+ evidence of dZ-DNA presence.
skills.name: per-organism-likelihood-ratio-source-assignment
skills.search_text: per-organism-likelihood-ratio-source-assignment Use when dZ-positive reads in a mixed metagenome must be traced to their organism of origin, i.e. a per-read Z-Calling SVM TSV exists and reads are aligned to a multi-organism reference and you need per-species LR+ evidence of dZ-DNA presence. The goal is single-nucleotide Z/A site calling or Z-frequency profiling (z-bam2txt/zfreq) rather than assigning reads to source organisms Reads cannot be mapped to a multi-organism reference with high fidelity (dv:f >= 0.05), so the LR+ denominator would be unreliable The sample consists of fully substituted dZ-genome only (no mixed metagenome), where the simpler read classifier alone suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 A downstream Z-Calling pipeline that identifies the taxonomic sources of dZ-DNA reads in mixed metagenomes by joining per-read SVM '+'/'-' classifications with primary read-to-reference-contig alignments and computing per-organism positive likelihood ratios (LR+). It enables dZ-positive organisms to be pinpointed while the SVM read classifier enforces zero false positive discovery. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: A downstream Z-Calling pipeline that identifies the taxonomic sources of dZ-DNA reads in mixed metagenomes by joining per-read SVM '+'/'-' classifications with primary read-to-reference-contig alignments and computing per-organism positive likelihood ratios (LR+). It enables dZ-positive organisms to be pinpointed while the SVM read classifier enforces zero false positive discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-nucleotide Z/A site calling or Z-frequency profiling (z-bam2txt/zfreq) rather than assigning reads to source organisms Reads cannot be mapped to a multi-organism reference with high fidelity (dv:f >= 0.05), so the LR+ denominator would be unreliable The sample consists of fully substituted dZ-genome only (no mixed metagenome), where the simpler read classifier alone suffices

skills.description: Use when you have per-read telomap TSV output for multiple barcoded patient PBL samples and need read-to-patient aggregation (mean telomere length, mean raw telomere length) followed by a Pearson correlation of those summaries against patient age.
skills.name: per-patient-summary-statistics-computation
skills.search_text: per-patient-summary-statistics-computation Use when you have per-read telomap TSV output for multiple barcoded patient PBL samples and need read-to-patient aggregation (mean telomere length, mean raw telomere length) followed by a Pearson correlation of those summaries against patient age. Input is read-level data that has not yet been processed by telomap (no TELOMERE_LEN/RAW_TELOMERE_LEN columns exist yet) The association of interest is non-linear or the goal is per-chromosome-end analysis rather than a single per-patient mean summary Samples are ALT cells or very long telomeres that exceed PacBio HiFi read length, where telomap lengths are not reliable http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Aggregates read-level telomere length measurements from per-sample telomap output tables into per-patient summary statistics (mean TELOMERE_LEN and mean RAW_TELOMERE_LEN), then tests their association with clinical covariates such as age via Pearson correlation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Aggregates read-level telomere length measurements from per-sample telomap output tables into per-patient summary statistics (mean TELOMERE_LEN and mean RAW_TELOMERE_LEN), then tests their association with clinical covariates such as age via Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is read-level data that has not yet been processed by telomap (no TELOMERE_LEN/RAW_TELOMERE_LEN columns exist yet) The association of interest is non-linear or the goal is per-chromosome-end analysis rather than a single per-patient mean summary Samples are ALT cells or very long telomeres that exceed PacBio HiFi read length, where telomap lengths are not reliable

skills.description: Use when consensus sequences must be derived directly from read alignments (SAM/BAM/CRAM, possibly unsorted or streamed from a mapper) and you need fast, memory-efficient per-position base and insertion tallies rather than sorted pileups.
skills.name: per-position-base-insertion-count-tallying
skills.search_text: per-position-base-insertion-count-tallying Use when consensus sequences must be derived directly from read alignments (SAM/BAM/CRAM, possibly unsorted or streamed from a mapper) and you need fast, memory-efficient per-position base and insertion tallies rather than sorted pileups. Ultra-long reference genomes (e.g. human chromosomes), since memory consumption scales linearly with reference genome length and may require prohibitively large amounts of memory Workflows that require sorted, indexed BAM pileups or per-read variant evidence rather than a single most-frequent-base consensus http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Stream unsorted SAM/BAM/CRAM read alignments one record at a time and increment in-memory base counts at each reference-genome position and insertion counts before each position, so consensus calling can happen on-the-fly without sorting or intermediate pileup files. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Stream unsorted SAM/BAM/CRAM read alignments one record at a time and increment in-memory base counts at each reference-genome position and insertion counts before each position, so consensus calling can happen on-the-fly without sorting or intermediate pileup files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ultra-long reference genomes (e.g. human chromosomes), since memory consumption scales linearly with reference genome length and may require prohibitively large amounts of memory Workflows that require sorted, indexed BAM pileups or per-read variant evidence rather than a single most-frequent-base consensus

skills.description: Use when you have MAPQ/flag-filtered read alignments (BAM) and need per-base counts of soft/hard-clipped reads alongside total coverage to locate candidate assembly-error breakpoints or heterozygous positions.
skills.name: per-position-coverage-tabulation
skills.search_text: per-position-coverage-tabulation Use when you have MAPQ/flag-filtered read alignments (BAM) and need per-base counts of soft/hard-clipped reads alongside total coverage to locate candidate assembly-error breakpoints or heterozygous positions. Alignments are unfiltered raw mapping output — clipping tallies on low-MAPQ, secondary, or duplicate records inflate false clip positions; apply the '-F 1796 -q 20' filter first You need final CRE/CSE error calls or AQI scores rather than the intermediate per-position clipping/coverage tables — this skill produces only the position-level clip counts and coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Tabulates, for every genomic position in filtered NGS and SMS BAM alignments, the number of clipped reads (CIGAR S/H operations) and the total mapped-read coverage, producing CRAQ's SR_clip.coverRate- and LR_clip.coverRate-style tables. This per-position clipping/coverage tally is the first CRAQ step toward separating assembly error breakpoints from heterozygous loci. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Tabulates, for every genomic position in filtered NGS and SMS BAM alignments, the number of clipped reads (CIGAR S/H operations) and the total mapped-read coverage, producing CRAQ's SR_clip.coverRate- and LR_clip.coverRate-style tables. This per-position clipping/coverage tally is the first CRAQ step toward separating assembly error breakpoints from heterozygous loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Alignments are unfiltered raw mapping output — clipping tallies on low-MAPQ, secondary, or duplicate records inflate false clip positions; apply the '-F 1796 -q 20' filter first You need final CRE/CSE error calls or AQI scores rather than the intermediate per-position clipping/coverage tables — this skill produces only the position-level clip counts and coverage

skills.description: Use when ONT eventalign TSVs have been classified with trained mCaller models and you must quantify per-position detection accuracy against orthogonal methylated/unmethylated position labels.
skills.name: per-position-methylation-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: per-position-methylation-accuracy-benchmarking Use when ONT eventalign TSVs have been classified with trained mCaller models and you must quantify per-position detection accuracy against orthogonal methylated/unmethylated position labels. Classifying sequence contexts on which the model has not been trained — training biases can decrease accuracy at dissimilar contexts Comparing against R10.4 flowcell data — nanopolish eventalign does not currently support R10 Validating non-motif methylation calls, which may be method-specific false positives reflecting different noise sources between nanopore current deviations and PacBio IPD ratios http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark m6A methylation classifiers on nanopore data by aggregating per-read calls to per-position methylation fractions and computing per-position accuracy against orthogonal labels (e.g. PacBio motif calls), as done for NN, RF, NBC, and LR classifiers in mCaller on E. coli R9 data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-08289-9
skills.summary: Benchmark m6A methylation classifiers on nanopore data by aggregating per-read calls to per-position methylation fractions and computing per-position accuracy against orthogonal labels (e.g. PacBio motif calls), as done for NN, RF, NBC, and LR classifiers in mCaller on E. coli R9 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Classifying sequence contexts on which the model has not been trained — training biases can decrease accuracy at dissimilar contexts Comparing against R10.4 flowcell data — nanopolish eventalign does not currently support R10 Validating non-motif methylation calls, which may be method-specific false positives reflecting different noise sources between nanopore current deviations and PacBio IPD ratios

skills.description: Use when MinION reads have been mapped to target sequences (e.g., via LAST) and a per-target consensus in FASTA format is needed, with explicit coverage and ambiguity handling per position.
skills.name: per-position-nucleotide-counting
skills.search_text: per-position-nucleotide-counting Use when MinION reads have been mapped to target sequences (e.g., via LAST) and a per-target consensus in FASTA format is needed, with explicit coverage and ambiguity handling per position. The goal is metagenomics analysis — the article states NanoPipe does not yet support it (implementation is planned), so multi-species mixtures are out of scope. Positions need statistically evaluated SNP calls with sophisticated scoring — the article notes current SNP detection statistics are not yet sophisticated; use the consensus module only for majority-rule bases, not formal SNP calling. Input is already a consensus or variant table — this skill operates on per-read alignments and would add nothing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds a majority-rule consensus sequence for each target chromosome/region by aggregating nucleotide counts from MinION read-to-target alignments (MAF output of LAST 946), emitting gaps where support is insufficient and IUPAC ambiguity codes where two nucleotides are nearly tied. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Builds a majority-rule consensus sequence for each target chromosome/region by aggregating nucleotide counts from MinION read-to-target alignments (MAF output of LAST 946), emitting gaps where support is insufficient and IUPAC ambiguity codes where two nucleotides are nearly tied.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is metagenomics analysis — the article states NanoPipe does not yet support it (implementation is planned), so multi-species mixtures are out of scope. Positions need statistically evaluated SNP calls with sophisticated scoring — the article notes current SNP detection statistics are not yet sophisticated; use the consensus module only for majority-rule bases, not formal SNP calling. Input is already a consensus or variant table — this skill operates on per-read alignments and would add nothing.

skills.description: Use when a long-read metagenomics pipeline must flag ARG-carrying reads and emit per-read records (hit coordinates, plasmid status, lineage) that feed Argo's read-overlap clustering and host-assignment steps.
skills.name: per-read-annotation-generation
skills.search_text: per-read-annotation-generation Use when a long-read metagenomics pipeline must flag ARG-carrying reads and emit per-read records (hit coordinates, plasmid status, lineage) that feed Argo's read-overlap clustering and host-assignment steps. Input is short-read data — Argo's overlapping-based screening (and this per-read annotation step) is designed for long reads; use a short-read profiler such as Lynx instead The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) approaches may be better suited Accurate ORF-level annotation or detailed sequence typing of highly similar ARGs (e.g., distinguishing blaOXA-1 from blaOXA-1042) is required — Argo clusters similar ARGs, lowering resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates a per-read ARG annotation structure (e.g., Argo's example.sarg JSON) by screening quality-controlled long reads with DIAMOND frameshift-aware blastx against the SARG+ protein database, recording each flagged read's ARG hits, plasmid flag, and lineage for downstream species-resolved ARG profiling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Generates a per-read ARG annotation structure (e.g., Argo's example.sarg JSON) by screening quality-controlled long reads with DIAMOND frameshift-aware blastx against the SARG+ protein database, recording each flagged read's ARG hits, plasmid flag, and lineage for downstream species-resolved ARG profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — Argo's overlapping-based screening (and this per-read annotation step) is designed for long reads; use a short-read profiler such as Lynx instead The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in new, understudied environments — assembly-based (metaFlye + Kraken2) or binning-based (SemiBin2 + GTDB-Tk) approaches may be better suited Accurate ORF-level annotation or detailed sequence typing of highly similar ARGs (e.g., distinguishing blaOXA-1 from blaOXA-1042) is required — Argo clusters similar ARGs, lowering resolution

skills.description: Use when benchmarking nanopore signal simulators or basecallers on DNA/RNA reads: you have POD5/FASTQ read sets plus a reference and need per-read accuracy, Q-score, error-type breakdowns, and DTW signal distances aggregated to medians.
skills.name: per-read-error-profile-analysis
skills.search_text: per-read-error-profile-analysis Use when benchmarking nanopore signal simulators or basecallers on DNA/RNA reads: you have POD5/FASTQ read sets plus a reference and need per-read accuracy, Q-score, error-type breakdowns, and DTW signal distances aggregated to medians. Input is raw signal without a reference or basecalled reads — alignment-based per-read accuracy cannot be computed without minimap2 alignments against a reference. Comparing assembly consensus quality rather than per-read basecalling fidelity — use variant-calling F1 or consensus error-rate benchmarks instead. Evaluating methylation or modified-base calling performance — Dorado/Remora mod-calling workflows, not identity-based error profiling, are required. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify per-read basecalling accuracy and error structure (mismatch, insertion, deletion rates, Q-scores, and DTW signal distances) of simulated or real nanopore reads against their reference, as used to benchmark NanoSimFormer against seq2squiggle and Squigulator on ONT R10.4.1 DNA and RNA004 data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Quantify per-read basecalling accuracy and error structure (mismatch, insertion, deletion rates, Q-scores, and DTW signal distances) of simulated or real nanopore reads against their reference, as used to benchmark NanoSimFormer against seq2squiggle and Squigulator on ONT R10.4.1 DNA and RNA004 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw signal without a reference or basecalled reads — alignment-based per-read accuracy cannot be computed without minimap2 alignments against a reference. Comparing assembly consensus quality rather than per-read basecalling fidelity — use variant-calling F1 or consensus error-rate benchmarks instead. Evaluating methylation or modified-base calling performance — Dorado/Remora mod-calling workflows, not identity-based error profiling, are required.

skills.description: Use when tombo-resquiggled single fast5 files for a MODIFIED or UNMODIFIED direct RNA nanopore sample must be stacked into a 2D (num_reads x target_rna_length) signal array for per-read modification analysis.
skills.name: per-read-event-alignment-to-reference
skills.search_text: per-read-event-alignment-to-reference Use when tombo-resquiggled single fast5 files for a MODIFIED or UNMODIFIED direct RNA nanopore sample must be stacked into a 2D (num_reads x target_rna_length) signal array for per-read modification analysis. Input is still multi-read fast5 files — these must first be converted with multi_to_single_fast5 and resquiggled with tombo before per-read arrays can be extracted The goal is population-level modification detection statistics rather than per-read single-molecule signal arrays — use 'tombo detect_modifications model_sample_compare' directly The reads have not been resquiggled against the reference FASTA, so raw signal events are not yet aligned to reference positions http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts tombo-resquiggled single-read fast5 files into a per-read by position numpy array of raw-signal features (pore current, dwell time, or current standard deviation) aligned to a target RNA's reference positions, enabling single-molecule RNA modification visualization and plotting. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: Converts tombo-resquiggled single-read fast5 files into a per-read by position numpy array of raw-signal features (pore current, dwell time, or current standard deviation) aligned to a target RNA's reference positions, enabling single-molecule RNA modification visualization and plotting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still multi-read fast5 files — these must first be converted with multi_to_single_fast5 and resquiggled with tombo before per-read arrays can be extracted The goal is population-level modification detection statistics rather than per-read single-molecule signal arrays — use 'tombo detect_modifications model_sample_compare' directly The reads have not been resquiggled against the reference FASTA, so raw signal events are not yet aligned to reference positions

skills.description: Use when you have a per-read feature table from raw nanopore signal mapping (read_id, mapping-quality ratio, chain-score ratio, mean chain-score ratio) and need to classify reads as mapped or unmapped with a weighted threshold rule.
skills.name: per-read-mapping-quality-analysis
skills.search_text: per-read-mapping-quality-analysis Use when you have a per-read feature table from raw nanopore signal mapping (read_id, mapping-quality ratio, chain-score ratio, mean chain-score ratio) and need to classify reads as mapped or unmapped with a weighted threshold rule. Input is already a mapping decision file or PAF alignment output rather than a per-read feature ratio table You need RawHash's legacy fixed conditional checks rather than RawHash2's weighted-sum threshold mechanism Feature weights or the decision threshold cannot be supplied explicitly, since no default values are prescribed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs RawHash2's weighted mapping decision mechanism: each read's mapping-quality ratio and best/mean chain-score ratios are combined into a weighted sum that is compared against a predefined threshold to emit a mapped/unmapped decision, replacing RawHash's fixed conditional checks. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Reconstructs RawHash2's weighted mapping decision mechanism: each read's mapping-quality ratio and best/mean chain-score ratios are combined into a weighted sum that is compared against a predefined threshold to emit a mapped/unmapped decision, replacing RawHash's fixed conditional checks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a mapping decision file or PAF alignment output rather than a per-read feature ratio table You need RawHash's legacy fixed conditional checks rather than RawHash2's weighted-sum threshold mechanism Feature weights or the decision threshold cannot be supplied explicitly, since no default values are prescribed

skills.description: Use when you have CHEUI Model 1 read-level m6A/m5C predictions from pooled nanopore direct RNA replicates and need to define significantly modified sites, filter transcript/site coverage, and compute single-molecule modification statistics such as co-occurrence.
skills.name: per-read-methylation-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-read-methylation-aggregation Use when you have CHEUI Model 1 read-level m6A/m5C predictions from pooled nanopore direct RNA replicates and need to define significantly modified sites, filter transcript/site coverage, and compute single-molecule modification statistics such as co-occurrence. Sites or molecules in ribosomal RNA, which are highly and densely modified and where signal interference at distances <5 nt exacerbates per-read prediction errors Differential methylation between two conditions — use CHEUI-diff instead of aggregating per-read states When the input is raw FAST5 signal with no basecalling/alignment/eventalign preprocessing; CHEUI preprocessing requires Guppy-basecalled, minimap2-aligned, nanopolish-eventaligned data first http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregates CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read m6A/m5C probabilities with Model 2 site-level modification probabilities (threshold >0.9999) to identify significantly modified sites and quantify read-level co-occurrence of two modification types on the same mRNA molecules in nanopore direct RNA data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Aggregates CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read m6A/m5C probabilities with Model 2 site-level modification probabilities (threshold >0.9999) to identify significantly modified sites and quantify read-level co-occurrence of two modification types on the same mRNA molecules in nanopore direct RNA data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sites or molecules in ribosomal RNA, which are highly and densely modified and where signal interference at distances <5 nt exacerbates per-read prediction errors Differential methylation between two conditions — use CHEUI-diff instead of aggregating per-read states When the input is raw FAST5 signal with no basecalling/alignment/eventalign preprocessing; CHEUI preprocessing requires Guppy-basecalled, minimap2-aligned, nanopolish-eventaligned data first

skills.description: Use when benchmarking per-read 5mC methylation calling accuracy of ONT callers (DeepMod2, Guppy, Dorado) on HG002/HG003/HG004 data against short-read bisulfite ground truth (GSE186383).
skills.name: per-read-methylation-f1-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-read-methylation-f1-evaluation Use when benchmarking per-read 5mC methylation calling accuracy of ONT callers (DeepMod2, Guppy, Dorado) on HG002/HG003/HG004 data against short-read bisulfite ground truth (GSE186383). Per-site (methylation frequency) accuracy is the target — per-site ground truth uses different filters (≥80%/<20% methylation, ≥50% frequency cutoff) and modkit aggregation The modification of interest is not 5mCpG — DeepMod2 only provides models for 5mCpG methylation Evaluating methylation at 20–80% intermediate methylation levels, which EpiQC showed have poor concordance even among short-read methods http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Evaluates Nanopore methylation callers (DeepMod2, Guppy, Dorado) at the per-read level by binarizing 5mC probability calls at a 0.5 threshold and computing precision/recall/F1 against EpiQC short-read bisulfite ground truth, reproducing the ~95% per-read F1 reported for DeepMod2 on human cell lines. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Evaluates Nanopore methylation callers (DeepMod2, Guppy, Dorado) at the per-read level by binarizing 5mC probability calls at a 0.5 threshold and computing precision/recall/F1 against EpiQC short-read bisulfite ground truth, reproducing the ~95% per-read F1 reported for DeepMod2 on human cell lines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-site (methylation frequency) accuracy is the target — per-site ground truth uses different filters (≥80%/<20% methylation, ≥50% frequency cutoff) and modkit aggregation The modification of interest is not 5mCpG — DeepMod2 only provides models for 5mCpG methylation Evaluating methylation at 20–80% intermediate methylation levels, which EpiQC showed have poor concordance even among short-read methods

skills.description: Use when you have per-read methylation scores (TSV with ID/Chr/Pos/Strand/Score columns) from one or more nanopore 5mC-calling tools and control reads of known methylation status (0%/100% sets), and need to quantify per-read detection accuracy via ROC/AUC and precision-recall curves.
skills.name: per-read-methylation-score-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-read-methylation-score-evaluation Use when you have per-read methylation scores (TSV with ID/Chr/Pos/Strand/Score columns) from one or more nanopore 5mC-calling tools and control reads of known methylation status (0%/100% sets), and need to quantify per-read detection accuracy via ROC/AUC and precision-recall curves. Your goal is per-site methylation frequency accuracy (dispersion against expected mixture frequency, RMSE) rather than single-molecule classification — use the METEORE consensus/evaluation workflow instead Your reads come from biological samples without control-derived ground truth (e.g. WGBS or Cas9-targeted comparisons), where binary per-read labels cannot be assigned from 0%/100% mixtures Scores come from tools not in the benchmark (e.g. DeepMod was excluded from the per-site augmented BED output and consensus comparisons) without re-verifying score semantics Benchmarking of per-read CpG (5mC) methylation detection tools (Nanopolish, Megalodon, DeepSignal, Guppy, Tombo) from nanopore fast5 data by ranking per-read scores against binary ground truth from 0% and 100% methylated control sets, quantified with ROC curves, AUC, precision-recall curves and AUCPR. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Benchmarking of per-read CpG (5mC) methylation detection tools (Nanopolish, Megalodon, DeepSignal, Guppy, Tombo) from nanopore fast5 data by ranking per-read scores against binary ground truth from 0% and 100% methylated control sets, quantified with ROC curves, AUC, precision-recall curves and AUCPR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is per-site methylation frequency accuracy (dispersion against expected mixture frequency, RMSE) rather than single-molecule classification — use the METEORE consensus/evaluation workflow instead Your reads come from biological samples without control-derived ground truth (e.g. WGBS or Cas9-targeted comparisons), where binary per-read labels cannot be assigned from 0%/100% mixtures Scores come from tools not in the benchmark (e.g. DeepMod was excluded from the per-site augmented BED output and consensus comparisons) without re-verifying score semantics

skills.description: Use when nanopore direct RNA sequencing reads have been classified per-read by CHEUI-solo Model 1 and transcriptome-wide site-level methylation probabilities and stoichiometry estimates are needed for individual experimental conditions.
skills.name: per-read-probability-aggregation-stoichiometry
skills.search_text: per-read-probability-aggregation-stoichiometry Use when nanopore direct RNA sequencing reads have been classified per-read by CHEUI-solo Model 1 and transcriptome-wide site-level methylation probabilities and stoichiometry estimates are needed for individual experimental conditions. When the goal is differential methylation between two conditions — CHEUI-diff, not CHEUI-solo Model 2 aggregation, is the appropriate mode When reads have not yet been processed through CHEUI-solo Model 1 to produce per-read probability distributions (the aggregation requires these as input) When a more permissive sensitivity-oriented site call is needed: the article notes strict cutoffs reduce CHEUI sensitivity, and many sites found by orthogonal methods had high probabilities below the set thresholds http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Aggregates CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read m6A/m5C modification probabilities into site-level modification probabilities and stoichiometry estimates using CHEUI-solo Model 2 (a CNN classifier over per-read probability distributions), with a significance cutoff of prediction probability > 0.9999. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Aggregates CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read m6A/m5C modification probabilities into site-level modification probabilities and stoichiometry estimates using CHEUI-solo Model 2 (a CNN classifier over per-read probability distributions), with a significance cutoff of prediction probability > 0.9999.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential methylation between two conditions — CHEUI-diff, not CHEUI-solo Model 2 aggregation, is the appropriate mode When reads have not yet been processed through CHEUI-solo Model 1 to produce per-read probability distributions (the aggregation requires these as input) When a more permissive sensitivity-oriented site call is needed: the article notes strict cutoffs reduce CHEUI sensitivity, and many sites found by orthogonal methods had high probabilities below the set thresholds

skills.description: Use when per-read methylation score files (ID, Chr, Pos, Strand, Score) from multiple nanopore methylation callers are available and single-tool predictions show poor agreement with expected methylation frequencies.
skills.name: per-read-score-consensus-modeling
skills.search_text: per-read-score-consensus-modeling Use when per-read methylation score files (ID, Chr, Pos, Strand, Score) from multiple nanopore methylation callers are available and single-tool predictions show poor agreement with expected methylation frequencies. When only a single tool's per-read scores are available — the consensus requires predictions from two or more tools When time is constrained and no GPU is available, since combining tools is 'impractical for routine analyses, due to the running times for some methods without GPU support' Combines per-read 5mC methylation predictions from multiple nanopore tools (e.g. Megalodon and DeepSignal) into a consensus score using METEORE's random-forest or regression models, improving accuracy over any single tool for CpG methylation detection. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Combines per-read 5mC methylation predictions from multiple nanopore tools (e.g. Megalodon and DeepSignal) into a consensus score using METEORE's random-forest or regression models, improving accuracy over any single tool for CpG methylation detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single tool's per-read scores are available — the consensus requires predictions from two or more tools When time is constrained and no GPU is available, since combining tools is 'impractical for routine analyses, due to the running times for some methods without GPU support'

skills.description: Use when per-read methylation predictions from multiple nanopore methylation callers must be merged into a common format before training or applying METEORE's random forest or multiple linear regression combination models.
skills.name: per-read-score-file-formatting
skills.search_text: per-read-score-file-formatting Use when per-read methylation predictions from multiple nanopore methylation callers must be merged into a common format before training or applying METEORE's random forest or multiple linear regression combination models. Only one tool's predictions are needed and no consensus/combination model will be applied Input is already a per-read score TSV in METEORE format The goal is per-site aggregation only, with no per-read tool comparison (a simple per-site summary suffices) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reformat heterogeneous per-read methylation scores from Nanopore 5mC calling tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, DeepMod) into METEORE's unified per-read TSV format (ID, Chr, Pos, Strand, Score) so tool outputs can be combined by consensus models. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Reformat heterogeneous per-read methylation scores from Nanopore 5mC calling tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, DeepMod) into METEORE's unified per-read TSV format (ID, Chr, Pos, Strand, Score) so tool outputs can be combined by consensus models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one tool's predictions are needed and no consensus/combination model will be applied Input is already a per-read score TSV in METEORE format The goal is per-site aggregation only, with no per-read tool comparison (a simple per-site summary suffices)

skills.description: Use when PAIso-seq clean CCS reads have been aligned with minimap2 -x splice to mm10/GRCm38 and per-read poly(A) tail lengths must be called from terminal clipped sequences under explicit length/purity thresholds.
skills.name: per-read-tail-table-generation
skills.search_text: per-read-tail-table-generation Use when PAIso-seq clean CCS reads have been aligned with minimap2 -x splice to mm10/GRCm38 and per-read poly(A) tail lengths must be called from terminal clipped sequences under explicit length/purity thresholds. Input alignments are chimeric or carry a supplementary alignment tag, since such alignments are explicitly ignored by the pipeline The task is 3' end poly(A) site annotation or APA analysis (handled by the TAPIS/run_tapis.py pipeline with GMAP), not per-read tail-length measurement Clipped candidates shorter than 15 nt or lacking five continuous adenosines exist and no candidate tail can satisfy the filter — no tail should be forced onto such reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extracts the terminal soft-clipped sequence from minimap2 (v2.15-r905, -x splice) alignments of clean CCS reads, applies the PAIso-seq four-criterion poly(A) tail filter, and writes per-read tail lengths (e.g. polya_tail_lengths.csv) used for downstream non-A residue and tail-length analysis. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Extracts the terminal soft-clipped sequence from minimap2 (v2.15-r905, -x splice) alignments of clean CCS reads, applies the PAIso-seq four-criterion poly(A) tail filter, and writes per-read tail lengths (e.g. polya_tail_lengths.csv) used for downstream non-A residue and tail-length analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments are chimeric or carry a supplementary alignment tag, since such alignments are explicitly ignored by the pipeline The task is 3' end poly(A) site annotation or APA analysis (handled by the TAPIS/run_tapis.py pipeline with GMAP), not per-read tail-length measurement Clipped candidates shorter than 15 nt or lacking five continuous adenosines exist and no candidate tail can satisfy the filter — no tail should be forced onto such reads

skills.description: Use when comparing taxonomic classifiers for host identification of ARG-carrying long reads, or when quantifying misclassification rates (true-positive, false-positive, unclassified) of metagenomic profilers against known ground truth.
skills.name: per-read-taxonomic-benchmarking
skills.search_text: per-read-taxonomic-benchmarking Use when comparing taxonomic classifiers for host identification of ARG-carrying long reads, or when quantifying misclassification rates (true-positive, false-positive, unclassified) of metagenomic profilers against known ground truth. The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in novel, understudied environments where reference-based classification is unreliable (Argo is inherently reference-based and may misclassify unseen species or novel plasmid syntenies) Reads contain point-mutation-derived ARGs that cannot be distinguished from sequencing errors, since these are excluded from the SARG+ database Only one classifier is being evaluated without a shared reference catalog — the misclassification benchmark requires a like-for-like comparison across strategies on identical simulated ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A simulation-based benchmark that quantifies how accurately different taxonomic assignment strategies (e.g., minimap2+RO, Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, MEGAN-LR) identify the true species hosts of ARG-carrying long reads, using per-species and overall misclassification rates as the metric. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: A simulation-based benchmark that quantifies how accurately different taxonomic assignment strategies (e.g., minimap2+RO, Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, MEGAN-LR) identify the true species hosts of ARG-carrying long reads, using per-species and overall misclassification rates as the metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo identification of ARG genomic contexts and hosts in novel, understudied environments where reference-based classification is unreliable (Argo is inherently reference-based and may misclassify unseen species or novel plasmid syntenies) Reads contain point-mutation-derived ARGs that cannot be distinguished from sequencing errors, since these are excluded from the SARG+ database Only one classifier is being evaluated without a shared reference catalog — the misclassification benchmark requires a like-for-like comparison across strategies on identical simulated ground truth

skills.description: Use when you have a telomap main output table (sample.telomap.tsv) and need to extract per-read telomeric regions for specific barcodes or chromosome ends to compute raw vs canonical telomere lengths or motif binding-site densities.
skills.name: per-read-telomap-table-filtering
skills.search_text: per-read-telomap-table-filtering Use when you have a telomap main output table (sample.telomap.tsv) and need to extract per-read telomeric regions for specific barcodes or chromosome ends to compute raw vs canonical telomere lengths or motif binding-site densities. Input is raw long-read FASTQ/BAM rather than telomap output — run telomap (wgs or telobait mode) first to generate sample.telomap.tsv Telomeres are from ALT cells with very long telomeres that exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity — telomap-based per-read measurement is incompatible The subtelomeric anchor region is too short for unambiguous chromosome-end identification against T2T-CHM13 (e.g. after RsaI/HinfI trimming), making CHROM assignments unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Filters and interprets the per-read telomap output table (sample.telomap.tsv) to isolate telomeric reads for a given sample barcode and chromosome end, using columns such as CHROM, BARCODE, TELOMERE_START, TELOMERE_END, RAW_TELOMERE_LEN, and TELOMERE_LEN for downstream telomere-length and motif-density comparisons. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Filters and interprets the per-read telomap output table (sample.telomap.tsv) to isolate telomeric reads for a given sample barcode and chromosome end, using columns such as CHROM, BARCODE, TELOMERE_START, TELOMERE_END, RAW_TELOMERE_LEN, and TELOMERE_LEN for downstream telomere-length and motif-density comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long-read FASTQ/BAM rather than telomap output — run telomap (wgs or telobait mode) first to generate sample.telomap.tsv Telomeres are from ALT cells with very long telomeres that exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity — telomap-based per-read measurement is incompatible The subtelomeric anchor region is too short for unambiguous chromosome-end identification against T2T-CHM13 (e.g. after RsaI/HinfI trimming), making CHROM assignments unreliable

skills.name: per-region-count-tabulation
skills.search_text: per-region-count-tabulation Use when you have variant-calling results (e.g. VCF-style call sets from two simulators on R10.4. You only need genome-wide aggregate precision/recall with no stratification by genomic context — a single confusion matrix suffices The call set has not yet been resolved into true-positive vs false-positive calls (run the upstream variant-calling/truth-comparison task first) Regions of interest are defined by something other than sequence-context classes (e.g. gene bodies or GC bins), for which this three-class scheme does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Tabulates true-positive and false-positive variant calls per genomic region class (homopolymer runs >=5 identical bases, TRF tandem repeats, or neither) for each simulator, quantifying where call accuracy degrades. It converts a flat VCF-style call set into a per-region TP/FP contingency table that exposes context-dependent simulator error. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Tabulates true-positive and false-positive variant calls per genomic region class (homopolymer runs >=5 identical bases, TRF tandem repeats, or neither) for each simulator, quantifying where call accuracy degrades. It converts a flat VCF-style call set into a per-region TP/FP contingency table that exposes context-dependent simulator error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need genome-wide aggregate precision/recall with no stratification by genomic context — a single confusion matrix suffices The call set has not yet been resolved into true-positive vs false-positive calls (run the upstream variant-calling/truth-comparison task first) Regions of interest are defined by something other than sequence-context classes (e.g. gene bodies or GC bins), for which this three-class scheme does not apply

skills.name: per-sample-read-count-tabulation
skills.search_text: per-sample-read-count-tabulation Use when you have MiniBar-demultiplexed Nanopore FASTA/FASTQ records with sample IDs in header comments and need per-specimen read tallies, e.g. to quantify assignment yield across barcode edit-distance settings (-e 2/3/4). skills.search_text: per-sample-variant-count-benchmarking Use when reproducing or validating a published WGS/WES pipeline's variant yield: public SRA FASTQ samples are given with accession IDs (PRJNA/SRR) and expected total variant counts per project to compare against. The goal is variant interpretation or clinical genotyping rather than validating reported variant yield — use the JWES visualization/annotation modules or dedicated clinical pipelines instead The input is raw sequencing data from non-human organisms — the pipeline aligns against the hg38 human reference genome and its variant counts are only comparable for human WGS/WES samples Only a single sample with no published reference count exists — per-sample benchmarking against reported values requires published figures to compare against http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking skill that reproduces the per-project variant counts reported by the JWES WGS/WES pipeline (e.g. 1,793,959 for PRJNA624223; 43,685 for PRJNA657985) by running the full FastQC→Trimmomatic→BWA(hg38)→GATK→snpEff workflow on public SRA samples and tabulating total variants per project accession. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that reproduces the per-project variant counts reported by the JWES WGS/WES pipeline (e.g. 1,793,959 for PRJNA624223; 43,685 for PRJNA657985) by running the full FastQC→Trimmomatic→BWA(hg38)→GATK→snpEff workflow on public SRA samples and tabulating total variants per project accession.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is variant interpretation or clinical genotyping rather than validating reported variant yield — use the JWES visualization/annotation modules or dedicated clinical pipelines instead The input is raw sequencing data from non-human organisms — the pipeline aligns against the hg38 human reference genome and its variant counts are only comparable for human WGS/WES samples Only a single sample with no published reference count exists — per-sample benchmarking against reported values requires published figures to compare against

skills.description: Use when you have base-called ONT direct RNA reads (FASTQ/FAST5, Albacore or Guppy) aligned to a transcriptome and need per-site error/quality features for RNA modification classification with EpiNano-SVM or EpiNano-Error.
skills.name: per-site-base-quality-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-site-base-quality-aggregation Use when you have base-called ONT direct RNA reads (FASTQ/FAST5, Albacore or Guppy) aligned to a transcriptome and need per-site error/quality features for RNA modification classification with EpiNano-SVM or EpiNano-Error. Input is already a per-site feature/error table — feature extraction would be redundant; proceed directly to SVM classification or pairwise error comparison Single-read (per-molecule) modification detection is required — EpiNano aggregates information from all reads at a site and explicitly lacks per-read resolution A specific modification type must be distinguished (e.g., m1A vs m6A) — the error features do not discriminate between modification types http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts per-site base-called features (mean per-base quality, mismatch, insertion, and deletion frequencies) from ONT direct RNA sequencing alignments, organized over the 5-mer positions (−2, −1, 0, +1, +2) surrounding each transcriptomic site. These error-rich features are the inputs EpiNano uses to detect m6A as systematic base-calling errors and decreased base-calling qualities. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Extracts per-site base-called features (mean per-base quality, mismatch, insertion, and deletion frequencies) from ONT direct RNA sequencing alignments, organized over the 5-mer positions (−2, −1, 0, +1, +2) surrounding each transcriptomic site. These error-rich features are the inputs EpiNano uses to detect m6A as systematic base-calling errors and decreased base-calling qualities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-site feature/error table — feature extraction would be redundant; proceed directly to SVM classification or pairwise error comparison Single-read (per-molecule) modification detection is required — EpiNano aggregates information from all reads at a site and explicitly lacks per-read resolution A specific modification type must be distinguished (e.g., m1A vs m6A) — the error features do not discriminate between modification types

Per-read modification states are the deliverable — use the call_mods per-read output directly instead of aggregating. Input is already a per-site methylation table (e.g., bisulfite-derived bedMethyl) — there are no Nanopore per-read calls left to aggregate. Raw FAST5s have not yet been basecalled and re-squiggled (Guppy + tombo resquiggle into RawGenomeCorrected_000) — call_freq has no call_mods file to consume. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Collapse DeepSignal-plant's per-read 5mC probability calls (the call_mods output) into per-cytosine methylation frequencies with call_freq, optionally emitting sorted bedMethyl, then split by CG/CHG/CHH context so Nanopore methylation levels can be compared directly against bisulfite sequencing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Collapse DeepSignal-plant's per-read 5mC probability calls (the call_mods output) into per-cytosine methylation frequencies with call_freq, optionally emitting sorted bedMethyl, then split by CG/CHG/CHH context so Nanopore methylation levels can be compared directly against bisulfite sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-read modification states are the deliverable — use the call_mods per-read output directly instead of aggregating. Input is already a per-site methylation table (e.g., bisulfite-derived bedMethyl) — there are no Nanopore per-read calls left to aggregate. skills.description: Use when preparing per-read (output.per_read) or per-site (output.per_site) methylation predictions for binarized benchmarking against discrete bisulfite ground-truth labels.
skills.name: per-site-methylation-frequency-binarization
skills.search_text: per-site-methylation-frequency-binarization Use when preparing per-read (output.per_read) or per-site (output.per_site) methylation predictions for binarized benchmarking against discrete bisulfite ground-truth labels. Sites with 20–80% methylation frequency, which EpiQC reported to have poor concordance between ONT and short-read methods and should be excluded from evaluation Low-coverage sites (<10X for HG002-4 ground truth, <5X for NIH3T3), where binarized labels are unreliable Intermediate probability per-read predictions where the user wishes to retain continuous confidence rather than a binary call http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Binarizes 5mC methylation calls from Oxford Nanopore methylation callers (e.g., DeepMod2) by applying a 0.5 probability-score threshold to per-read predictions and a ≥50% methylation-frequency cutoff to per-site predictions, enabling F1-score evaluation against short-read bisulfite ground truth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Binarizes 5mC methylation calls from Oxford Nanopore methylation callers (e.g., DeepMod2) by applying a 0.5 probability-score threshold to per-read predictions and a ≥50% methylation-frequency cutoff to per-site predictions, enabling F1-score evaluation against short-read bisulfite ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sites with 20–80% methylation frequency, which EpiQC reported to have poor concordance between ONT and short-read methods and should be excluded from evaluation Low-coverage sites (<10X for HG002-4 ground truth, <5X for NIH3T3), where binarized labels are unreliable Intermediate probability per-read predictions where the user wishes to retain continuous confidence rather than a binary call
