skills.description: Use when you have a split-flow-cell live RISER run (deplete vs control channels) with basecalled, mapped reads and a RISER decisions CSV, and you need per-transcript read/nt count percent changes per biotype.
skills.name: per-transcript-percent-change-computation
skills.search_text: per-transcript-percent-change-computation Use when you have a split-flow-cell live RISER run (deplete vs control channels) with basecalled, mapped reads and a RISER decisions CSV, and you need per-transcript read/nt count percent changes per biotype. Data comes from a non-RISER run with randomly split channels rather than a live RISER deplete/control split — such splits serve as the negative-control background in the Wilcoxon test, not the effect being quantified. Transcripts fail the filters (not in the top 95% of control-condition reads, or fewer than 30 read counts in both conditions), or are lncRNAs overlapping protein-coding exons — their percent changes are excluded from the summary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes per-transcript percent changes in read counts and nucleotide (nt) counts between RISER-deplete (even-numbered channels) and control (remaining channels) conditions from a live HEK293 MinION direct RNA sequencing run, to quantify RISER-mediated mRNA/mtRNA depletion and lncRNA enrichment. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Computes per-transcript percent changes in read counts and nucleotide (nt) counts between RISER-deplete (even-numbered channels) and control (remaining channels) conditions from a live HEK293 MinION direct RNA sequencing run, to quantify RISER-mediated mRNA/mtRNA depletion and lncRNA enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data comes from a non-RISER run with randomly split channels rather than a live RISER deplete/control split — such splits serve as the negative-control background in the Wilcoxon test, not the effect being quantified. Transcripts fail the filters (not in the top 95% of control-condition reads, or fewer than 30 read counts in both conditions), or are lncRNAs overlapping protein-coding exons — their percent changes are excluded from the summary.

skills.description: Use when comparing per-transcript read or nucleotide abundance between two sequencing conditions (e.g., RISER-deplete vs control channels) to quantify percent change per transcript, as for globin mRNA depletion in whole blood.
skills.name: per-transcript-read-count-quantification
skills.search_text: per-transcript-read-count-quantification Use when comparing per-transcript read or nucleotide abundance between two sequencing conditions (e.g., RISER-deplete vs control channels) to quantify percent change per transcript, as for globin mRNA depletion in whole blood. The comparison is between independent sequencing runs without a shared channel/split-flow-cell design — random read splitting alone cannot separate RISER effects from run-to-run variation without the described randomization control. The goal is whole-sample gene-level abundance (e.g., a count matrix for differential expression) rather than measuring depletion/enrichment percent change of targeted transcripts. Reads are not high-confidence alignments (e.g., secondary/supplementary/unmapped mappings not removed with samtools -F 2324), so per-transcript counts would be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Quantify per-transcript read and nucleotide counts from nanopore direct RNA sequencing BAM alignments under two conditions (e.g., RISER globin-deplete vs control split-flow-cell) and compute per-transcript percent changes to measure depletion efficiency. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48673-8
skills.summary: Quantify per-transcript read and nucleotide counts from nanopore direct RNA sequencing BAM alignments under two conditions (e.g., RISER globin-deplete vs control split-flow-cell) and compute per-transcript percent changes to measure depletion efficiency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison is between independent sequencing runs without a shared channel/split-flow-cell design — random read splitting alone cannot separate RISER effects from run-to-run variation without the described randomization control. The goal is whole-sample gene-level abundance (e.g., a count matrix for differential expression) rather than measuring depletion/enrichment percent change of targeted transcripts. Reads are not high-confidence alignments (e.g., secondary/supplementary/unmapped mappings not removed with samtools -F 2324), so per-transcript counts would be unreliable.

You have only short-read (Illumina) data — npScarf requires long nanopore reads aligned to the draft assembly, and the paper notes the pipeline still requires short read data as input You need a finished assembly rather than positional annotation of mobile elements — use standard batch scaffolding or a successor tool such as npGraph, since npScarf is no longer maintained Batch analysis after sequencing has finished — the real-time annotation value (stopping once genes are confirmed) is lost; use batch bwa mem | jsa.np.npscarf mode instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Real-time annotation of plasmid origins of replication and AMR genes as npScarf scaffolds an assembly with streaming nanopore reads, allowing plasmid-borne resistance determinants (e.g. 18 of 27 AMR genes in K. pneumoniae Kpn2146) to be confirmed with as little as 83 Mb (~14-fold) of long-read data. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Real-time annotation of plasmid origins of replication and AMR genes as npScarf scaffolds an assembly with streaming nanopore reads, allowing plasmid-borne resistance determinants (e.g. 18 of 27 AMR genes in K. pneumoniae Kpn2146) to be confirmed with as little as 83 Mb (~14-fold) of long-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only short-read (Illumina) data — npScarf requires long nanopore reads aligned to the draft assembly, and the paper notes the pipeline still requires short read data as input You need a finished assembly rather than positional annotation of mobile elements — use standard batch scaffolding or a successor tool such as npGraph, since npScarf is no longer maintained Batch analysis after sequencing has finished — the real-time annotation value (stopping once genes are confirmed) is lost; use batch bwa mem | jsa.np.npscarf mode instead

skills.description: Use when ONT FASTQ reads from a linearised pDNA template (e.g. SQK-LSK109) need read-fate fractions against a plasmid reference, including E. coli carry-over and failed-read fractions.
skills.name: plasmid-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: plasmid-reference-mapping Use when ONT FASTQ reads from a linearised pDNA template (e.g. SQK-LSK109) need read-fate fractions against a plasmid reference, including E. coli carry-over and failed-read fractions. Input reads are Illumina short reads (the article uses TrimGalore Q20 trimming and a different short-read workflow, not Minimap2 -ax map-ont) The sample is final mRNA product rather than a plasmid DNA template — use the mRNA/cDNA sequencing arm of VAX-seq instead of pDNA reference mapping Reads have not passed the quality filter (Q>9) so read-fate fractions would be skewed by low-quality reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantifies the fate of ONT long reads from a linearised plasmid DNA (pDNA) template by aligning Nanopore reads to the plasmid reference with Minimap2, sorting/indexing BAMs with SAMtools, and computing read-fate fractions (plasmid-aligned, E. coli contamination, failed reads) via Mana. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Quantifies the fate of ONT long reads from a linearised plasmid DNA (pDNA) template by aligning Nanopore reads to the plasmid reference with Minimap2, sorting/indexing BAMs with SAMtools, and computing read-fate fractions (plasmid-aligned, E. coli contamination, failed reads) via Mana.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are Illumina short reads (the article uses TrimGalore Q20 trimming and a different short-read workflow, not Minimap2 -ax map-ont) The sample is final mRNA product rather than a plasmid DNA template — use the mRNA/cDNA sequencing arm of VAX-seq instead of pDNA reference mapping Reads have not passed the quality filter (Q>9) so read-fate fractions would be skewed by low-quality reads

skills.description: Use when MinION-targeted amplicon reads (e.g., P. falciparum drug-resistance loci) have been mapped to a target with LAST via NanoPipe and the per-position polymorphisms need to be called and annotated against PlasmoDB SNP data.
skills.name: plasmodium-snp-database-annotation
skills.search_text: plasmodium-snp-database-annotation Use when MinION-targeted amplicon reads (e.g., P. falciparum drug-resistance loci) have been mapped to a target with LAST via NanoPipe and the per-position polymorphisms need to be called and annotated against PlasmoDB SNP data. The input is metagenomic or mixed-species MinION data — NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics analysis; it is designed for targeted read-to-reference alignment and SNP detection Positions have fewer than 10 reads — the consensus assigns a gap below this minimum, so polymorphism calls would be unreliable The reads are not aligned against a target database yet (no calc.lastalign.maf/calc.bam) — this skill operates downstream of the lastal/last-split mapping step http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes per-position nucleotide counts and majority-rule consensus from MinION amplicon alignments (NanoPipe/LAST), calls SNP candidates under NanoPipe's coverage and transition/transversion filters, and annotates them against a local PlasmoDB P. falciparum 3D7 SNP database using nanopipe_calc_polymorphism.py with -s plasf. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Computes per-position nucleotide counts and majority-rule consensus from MinION amplicon alignments (NanoPipe/LAST), calls SNP candidates under NanoPipe's coverage and transition/transversion filters, and annotates them against a local PlasmoDB P. falciparum 3D7 SNP database using nanopipe_calc_polymorphism.py with -s plasf.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is metagenomic or mixed-species MinION data — NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics analysis; it is designed for targeted read-to-reference alignment and SNP detection Positions have fewer than 10 reads — the consensus assigns a gap below this minimum, so polymorphism calls would be unreliable The reads are not aligned against a target database yet (no calc.lastalign.maf/calc.bam) — this skill operates downstream of the lastal/last-split mapping step

skills.description: Use when a benchmark or analysis contains per-replicate consensus error measurements from both ONT and Illumina read sets (e.g. simulated SARS-CoV-2 reads at 30x/40x/50x) and the goal is to test whether ONT reconstruction error exceeds Illumina error at equal coverage.
skills.name: platform-error-comparison-ont-illumina
skills.search_text: platform-error-comparison-ont-illumina Use when a benchmark or analysis contains per-replicate consensus error measurements from both ONT and Illumina read sets (e.g. simulated SARS-CoV-2 reads at 30x/40x/50x) and the goal is to test whether ONT reconstruction error exceeds Illumina error at equal coverage. The dataset contains only one sequencing platform — there is no ONT/Illumina contrast to compute, so a within-platform coverage-trend analysis alone is more appropriate. The consensus caller or error metric differs from the ViralConsensus accuracy benchmark design (e.g. variant-calling pipelines like CoVpipe2 rather than direct consensus error rates), making fold-change comparisons non-comparable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Quantifies and compares viral consensus sequence reconstruction error between Oxford Nanopore (ONT) and Illumina sequencing platforms using ViralConsensus, benchmarked on simulated SARS-CoV-2 reads at matched coverage depths (30x, 40x, 50x). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Quantifies and compares viral consensus sequence reconstruction error between Oxford Nanopore (ONT) and Illumina sequencing platforms using ViralConsensus, benchmarked on simulated SARS-CoV-2 reads at matched coverage depths (30x, 40x, 50x).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains only one sequencing platform — there is no ONT/Illumina contrast to compute, so a within-platform coverage-trend analysis alone is more appropriate. The consensus caller or error metric differs from the ViralConsensus accuracy benchmark design (e.g. variant-calling pipelines like CoVpipe2 rather than direct consensus error rates), making fold-change comparisons non-comparable.

skills.description: Use when comparing per-site methylation discrepancies between nanopore tools and WGBS and you need to test whether sequence context (e.g. AT-rich NNNCGNNN 8-mers) drives tool-specific error.
skills.name: plogo-sequence-motif-visualization
skills.search_text: plogo-sequence-motif-visualization Use when comparing per-site methylation discrepancies between nanopore tools and WGBS and you need to test whether sequence context (e.g. AT-rich NNNCGNNN 8-mers) drives tool-specific error. Input is single-read (per-read) methylation scores rather than aggregated per-site methylation frequencies, since the analysis groups discrepancies per CpG site The goal is methylation calling itself — this skill only visualizes and tests sequence-context bias in already-produced per-site calls The methylation system is not CpG (e.g. dam/dcm GATC contexts), since the 8-mer extraction is centered on NNNCGNNN http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 A skill for visualizing sequence-context bias in nanopore CpG methylation calls by comparing flanking-sequence motifs (pLogos) between low- and high-discrepancy CpG sites and ranking NNNCGNNN 8-mers by mean nanopore-vs-WGBS discrepancy per tool. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: A skill for visualizing sequence-context bias in nanopore CpG methylation calls by comparing flanking-sequence motifs (pLogos) between low- and high-discrepancy CpG sites and ranking NNNCGNNN 8-mers by mean nanopore-vs-WGBS discrepancy per tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-read (per-read) methylation scores rather than aggregated per-site methylation frequencies, since the analysis groups discrepancies per CpG site The goal is methylation calling itself — this skill only visualizes and tests sequence-context bias in already-produced per-site calls The methylation system is not CpG (e.g. dam/dcm GATC contexts), since the 8-mer extraction is centered on NNNCGNNN

skills.description: Use when evaluating error-correction or assembly tools on long reads (PacBio CLR/ONT) from polyploid genomes or metagenomes, where per-haplotype accuracy (QV, switch error, haplotype coverage) must be quantified against reference haplotypes.
skills.name: ploidy-aware-haplotype-evaluation
skills.search_text: ploidy-aware-haplotype-evaluation Use when evaluating error-correction or assembly tools on long reads (PacBio CLR/ONT) from polyploid genomes or metagenomes, where per-haplotype accuracy (QV, switch error, haplotype coverage) must be quantified against reference haplotypes. The input is short-read (Illumina) data or already-high-accuracy reads (HiFi/CCS), where haplotype-aware long-read self-correction benchmarks do not apply The sample is a single-haploid/clonal genome with no low-frequency haplotypes, where consensus-template correction biases are not at issue You need only a speed/resource benchmark and do not have reference haplotypes — ploidy-aware QV/HC computation requires aligning corrected reads or assemblies back to known references http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark long-read error correction and assembly quality in mixed samples by evaluating haplotype-aware metrics — residual error rate (QV), switch error, and haplotype coverage (HC) — across diploid, triploid, tetraploid, and metagenomic datasets, rather than consensus-only accuracy, because consensus-template methods mask low-frequency haplotype variants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read error correction and assembly quality in mixed samples by evaluating haplotype-aware metrics — residual error rate (QV), switch error, and haplotype coverage (HC) — across diploid, triploid, tetraploid, and metagenomic datasets, rather than consensus-only accuracy, because consensus-template methods mask low-frequency haplotype variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read (Illumina) data or already-high-accuracy reads (HiFi/CCS), where haplotype-aware long-read self-correction benchmarks do not apply The sample is a single-haploid/clonal genome with no low-frequency haplotypes, where consensus-template correction biases are not at issue You need only a speed/resource benchmark and do not have reference haplotypes — ploidy-aware QV/HC computation requires aligning corrected reads or assemblies back to known references

skills.description: Use when you need to verify or reproduce the error-reduction benefit of POA-computed haplotype-specific consensus sequences from ONT or PacBio simulated reads before TR profiling.
skills.name: poa-consensus-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: poa-consensus-quality-evaluation Use when you need to verify or reproduce the error-reduction benefit of POA-computed haplotype-specific consensus sequences from ONT or PacBio simulated reads before TR profiling. You need to profile tandem repeats themselves rather than quantify consensus accuracy — use TRiCoLOR's SENSoR/REFER TR-calling workflow instead Input reads are already high-accuracy (e.g., Illumina) where the POA consensus error-reduction benefit for error-prone third-generation reads does not apply Reads come from unassembled genomic regions (centromeres, telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats in http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Quantifies how much TRiCoLOR's SPOA-based partial order alignment consensus step reduces per-base sequencing error of error-prone long reads, benchmarked against the reported ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PacBio) error reductions from Supplementary Note S3. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Quantifies how much TRiCoLOR's SPOA-based partial order alignment consensus step reduces per-base sequencing error of error-prone long reads, benchmarked against the reported ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PacBio) error reductions from Supplementary Note S3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to profile tandem repeats themselves rather than quantify consensus accuracy — use TRiCoLOR's SENSoR/REFER TR-calling workflow instead Input reads are already high-accuracy (e.g., Illumina) where the POA consensus error-reduction benefit for error-prone third-generation reads does not apply Reads come from unassembled genomic regions (centromeres, telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats in

skills.description: Use when you have haplotype-resolved long-read BAM alignments (ONT or PacBio) over candidate repetitive regions and need low-error haplotype-specific consensus sequences before repeat motif calling.
skills.name: poa-consensus-sequence-generation
skills.search_text: poa-consensus-sequence-generation Use when you have haplotype-resolved long-read BAM alignments (ONT or PacBio) over candidate repetitive regions and need low-error haplotype-specific consensus sequences before repeat motif calling. Input reads are short Illumina reads with low error rates, where POA-based error correction is unnecessary Candidate regions lack sufficient spanning read support in the haplotype-resolved BAM, yielding unreliable consensus Repeats lie in unassembled regions such as centromeres or telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Builds haplotype-specific, low-error consensus sequences from error-prone ONT/PacBio long reads spanning candidate tandem repeat regions using partial order alignment (POA), as implemented by SPOA inside the TRiCoLOR REFER module. The consensus step approximates error reduction of ~77% for ONT and ~88% for PB reads, making motif detection by the downstream RegEx string matcher feasible. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Builds haplotype-specific, low-error consensus sequences from error-prone ONT/PacBio long reads spanning candidate tandem repeat regions using partial order alignment (POA), as implemented by SPOA inside the TRiCoLOR REFER module. The consensus step approximates error reduction of ~77% for ONT and ~88% for PB reads, making motif detection by the downstream RegEx string matcher feasible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads with low error rates, where POA-based error correction is unnecessary Candidate regions lack sufficient spanning read support in the haplotype-resolved BAM, yielding unreliable consensus Repeats lie in unassembled regions such as centromeres or telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify

skills.description: Use when you need to compare two or more genome polishing pipelines on HiFi (or T2T) assemblies and must quantify both correction gains and overcorrection harm, rather than relying on a single QV number.
skills.name: polishing-tool-benchmarking
skills.search_text: polishing-tool-benchmarking Use when you need to compare two or more genome polishing pipelines on HiFi (or T2T) assemblies and must quantify both correction gains and overcorrection harm, rather than relying on a single QV number. The assembly is from noisy long reads alone and no high-coverage short reads (>=60X) exist — NextPolish2-style k-mer benchmarking relies heavily on short reads to judge whether a K-mer contains errors The goal is de novo assembly quality assessment (completeness/contiguity, e.g. yak inspect for completeness) rather than comparing polishing-tool error correction and overcorrection behavior Only a single polishing pipeline is being applied with no comparison tool — benchmarking metrics such as fold-change ratios require at least two pipelines on identical inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A multi-pronged benchmarking strategy for comparing genome polishing tools (e.g. NextPolish2 vs Racon+Merfin pipelines) on HiFi-assembled genomes, using Merqury/k-mer QV, k-mer overcorrection counts, TE identity ratios, and pseudo-long-read alignment-based accuracy as complementary evaluation axes. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: A multi-pronged benchmarking strategy for comparing genome polishing tools (e.g. NextPolish2 vs Racon+Merfin pipelines) on HiFi-assembled genomes, using Merqury/k-mer QV, k-mer overcorrection counts, TE identity ratios, and pseudo-long-read alignment-based accuracy as complementary evaluation axes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly is from noisy long reads alone and no high-coverage short reads (>=60X) exist — NextPolish2-style k-mer benchmarking relies heavily on short reads to judge whether a K-mer contains errors The goal is de novo assembly quality assessment (completeness/contiguity, e.g. yak inspect for completeness) rather than comparing polishing-tool error correction and overcorrection behavior Only a single polishing pipeline is being applied with no comparison tool — benchmarking metrics such as fold-change ratios require at least two pipelines on identical inputs

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already basecalled FASTQ/BAM sequence data rather than raw fast5 signal — trimming is a signal-space preprocessing step Signals have already been trimmed in a previous BoostNano pass (re-running would re-segment and the transcript signal has been replaced in the Signal slot) The analysis targets adapter or poly(A) tail properties themselves (e.g., tail-length estimation) rather than the transcript body signal

skills.description: Use when PacBio PAIso-seq CCS reads must be converted into per-read/per-gene poly(A) tail-length measurements, including spike-in accuracy validation or isoform-level tail-length comparisons.

skills.search_text: polya-tail-length-quantification Use when PacBio PAIso-seq CCS reads must be converted into per-read/per-gene poly(A) tail-length measurements, including spike-in accuracy validation or isoform-level tail-length comparisons. The input is short-read Illumina or TAIL-seq/PAL-seq data — TAIL-seq cannot handle tails larger than 231 nt and PAL-seq requires the discontinued Illumina Genome Analyzer II, whereas this skill depends on full-length PacBio CCS reads The goal is annotating poly(A) sites rather than measuring tail lengths — use the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py) with GMAP alignments and PolyASite GRCm38-96 clusters instead Reads fail QC: fewer than 10 ccs passes, or a clipped tail shorter than 15 nt without five continuous adenosines — such reads must be discarded, not force-called http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify per-read and per-transcript poly(A) tail lengths from PAIso-seq data by extracting terminal soft-clipped sequences from minimap2 splice alignments of clean CCS reads and applying the paper's four-criterion tail-acceptance filter before recording tail length. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Quantify per-read and per-transcript poly(A) tail lengths from PAIso-seq data by extracting terminal soft-clipped sequences from minimap2 splice alignments of clean CCS reads and applying the paper's four-criterion tail-acceptance filter before recording tail length.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read Illumina or TAIL-seq/PAL-seq data — TAIL-seq cannot handle tails larger than 231 nt and PAL-seq requires the discontinued Illumina Genome Analyzer II, whereas this skill depends on full-length PacBio CCS reads The goal is annotating poly(A) sites rather than measuring tail lengths — use the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py) with GMAP alignments and PolyASite GRCm38-96 clusters instead Reads fail QC: fewer than 10 ccs passes, or a clipped tail shorter than 15 nt without five continuous adenosines — such reads must be discarded, not force-called

skills.search_text: polya-tail-misalignment-quantification Use when comparing short-read (Illumina TruSeq) vs long-read (ONT cDNA) alignment behaviour at a template-encoded 3' poly(A) tail, to quantify short-read misalignment errors and the resulting consensus accuracy drop. skills.summary: Quantifies how short-read Illumina TruSeq sequencing misaligns at the low-complexity 3' poly(A) tail of an eGFP mRNA relative to long-read ONT cDNA sequencing, by running the Mana --mrna pipeline on both alignment BAMs and comparing per-nucleotide coverage, error profiles, and consensus accuracy against the reference-encoded poly(A) sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is overall mRNA quality attributes (sequence identity, integrity, poly(A) tail length, contamination) rather than a focused comparison of alignment accuracy at the poly(A) tail — use the broader VAX-seq/Mana QC reporting instead. skills.description: Use when PacBio CCS reads (BAM/FASTQ) from HIT-scISOseq or 10x-compatible scIso-Seq libraries must be classified as full-length by primer orientation and have polyA tails, barcodes, and UMIs trimmed before genome mapping.

skills.search_text: polya-tail-trimming Use when PacBio CCS reads (BAM/FASTQ) from HIT-scISOseq or 10x-compatible scIso-Seq libraries must be classified as full-length by primer orientation and have polyA tails, barcodes, and UMIs trimmed before genome mapping. Input reads are already FLNC transcript FASTQs that have been primer-, barcode-, UMI-, and polyA-trimmed (proceed directly to minimap2 splice alignment). The library was not built with the PacBio original scIso-Seq or BGI HIT-scISOseq 10x-compatible primer scheme, so primer_F/primer_S sequences would not be present at read termini. Reads are raw subreads rather than CCS consensus reads — FLNC classification relies on high-accuracy CCS sequence. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect and extract full-length non-concatemer (FLNC) reads from HIT-scISOseq CCS reads by BLAST-mapping 5'/3' primer sequences and trimming poly(A) tails, cell barcodes, and UMIs with scISA-Tools' classify_by_primer. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Detect and extract full-length non-concatemer (FLNC) reads from HIT-scISOseq CCS reads by BLAST-mapping 5'/3' primer sequences and trimming poly(A) tails, cell barcodes, and UMIs with scISA-Tools' classify_by_primer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already FLNC transcript FASTQs that have been primer-, barcode-, UMI-, and polyA-trimmed (proceed directly to minimap2 splice alignment). skills.search_text: polya-tail-trimming-flnc-reads Use when FLNC reads have already passed LIMA primer removal and isoseq3 refine chimera filtering, and residual polyA tails must be detected and trimmed before mapping reads on the genome with minimap2 or uLTRA. Input is raw subread BAM or unrefined CCS reads — primer removal (LIMA) and chimeric read removal (isoseq3 refine) must happen first Input is already BAM-format FLNC reads that have not been converted to FASTA by bamtools convert Goal is polyA tail detection in aligned transcriptome data rather than trimming of unaligned FLNC reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Detect and trim polyA tails from selected FLNC reads in the nf-core/isoseq subread preprocessing stage using the TAMA cleanup module (gstama_polyacleanup), yielding chunked polyA-tail-free FLNC FASTA files ready for splice-aware genome alignment. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: Detect and trim polyA tails from selected FLNC reads in the nf-core/isoseq subread preprocessing stage using the TAMA cleanup module (gstama_polyacleanup), yielding chunked polyA-tail-free FLNC FASTA files ready for splice-aware genome alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw subread BAM or unrefined CCS reads — primer removal (LIMA) and chimeric read removal (isoseq3 refine) must happen first Input is already BAM-format FLNC reads that have not been converted to FASTA by bamtools convert Goal is polyA tail detection in aligned transcriptome data rather than trimming of unaligned FLNC reads

skills.description: Use when full-length PacBio CCS reads (PAIso−seq or similar) must be analyzed for alternative polyadenylation: counting distinct poly(A) sites per gene and reporting per-gene APA site-count distributions.
skills.name: polyadenylation-site-detection-tapis
skills.search_text: polyadenylation-site-detection-tapis Use when full-length PacBio CCS reads (PAIso−seq or similar) must be analyzed for alternative polyadenylation: counting distinct poly(A) sites per gene and reporting per-gene APA site-count distributions. Input reads are short Illumina reads rather than full-length PacBio CCS reads, since poly(A) tails must be captured within the same molecule as the cDNA The goal is quantifying non-A residues within poly(A) tail bodies rather than detecting APA sites (use the tail-composition skill instead) The organism/reference is not mouse GRCm38/mm10 and no equivalent Ensembl annotation is available for gene assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Detects per-read polyadenylation (APA) sites from full-length PAIso−seq CCS reads by aligning tail-trimmed reads to mm10 with GMAP, extracting qualifying 3' poly(A) tail clips, and running the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py) to count distinct poly(A) sites per gene against Ensembl GRCm38 release 92 annotation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Detects per-read polyadenylation (APA) sites from full-length PAIso−seq CCS reads by aligning tail-trimmed reads to mm10 with GMAP, extracting qualifying 3' poly(A) tail clips, and running the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py) to count distinct poly(A) sites per gene against Ensembl GRCm38 release 92 annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads rather than full-length PacBio CCS reads, since poly(A) tails must be captured within the same molecule as the cDNA The goal is quantifying non-A residues within poly(A) tail bodies rather than detecting APA sites (use the tail-composition skill instead) The organism/reference is not mouse GRCm38/mm10 and no equivalent Ensembl annotation is available for gene assignment

skills.description: Use when teaching or demonstrating quantitative-genetic responses to selection on a polygenic trait — specifically when the goal is to render an animated sequence of phenotypic distributions that shift under directional selection from standing genetic variation only.

skills.search_text: polygenic-trait-distribution-animation Use when teaching or demonstrating quantitative-genetic responses to selection on a polygenic trait — specifically when the goal is to render an animated sequence of phenotypic distributions that shift under directional selection from standing genetic variation only. A static single-generation plot suffices and animation or frame-by-frame export is unnecessary overhead. skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns allele-frequency change at one or a few loci under deterministic or stochastic processes rather than the distribution of a quantitative polygenic trait — use the package's gene-frequency simulation functions instead. The user cannot run R and only needs a conceptual demonstration — the article notes web interfaces exist for functions, but this animation workflow requires an R session.

skills.description: Use when separating true SNPs from sequencing/mapping artifacts in MinION read alignments — e.g. per-position nucleotide counts from NanoPipe must be filtered with the ≥10-read minimum, ≥20% alternate coverage, and p-error quality checks before calling polymorphisms.
skills.name: polymorphism-artifact-filtering
skills.search_text: polymorphism-artifact-filtering Use when separating true SNPs from sequencing/mapping artifacts in MinION read alignments — e.g. per-position nucleotide counts from NanoPipe must be filtered with the ≥10-read minimum, ≥20% alternate coverage, and p-error quality checks before calling polymorphisms. The goal is metagenomics analysis — the article states NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics and only plans this option Positions failing the thresholds (alternate coverage <20% of reads, position coverage <10 reads, or <30% of maximum contig coverage) — these are artifacts/gaps by definition, not reportable SNPs High-confidence variant calling from mature, orchestrated variant-caller stacks is needed — the authors note current NanoPipe SNP detection statistics 'are not yet sophisticated' and plan more sophisticated statistics as future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Applies NanoPipe's majority-rule consensus and SNP-candidate filtering criteria to per-position nucleotide counts from aligned Oxford Nanopore MinION reads, suppressing sequencing/mapping noise (e.g. short-read mismapping) before calling polymorphisms with dbSNP annotation. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Applies NanoPipe's majority-rule consensus and SNP-candidate filtering criteria to per-position nucleotide counts from aligned Oxford Nanopore MinION reads, suppressing sequencing/mapping noise (e.g. short-read mismapping) before calling polymorphisms with dbSNP annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is metagenomics analysis — the article states NanoPipe does not yet support metagenomics and only plans this option Positions failing the thresholds (alternate coverage <20% of reads, position coverage <10 reads, or <30% of maximum contig coverage) — these are artifacts/gaps by definition, not reportable SNPs High-confidence variant calling from mature, orchestrated variant-caller stacks is needed — the authors note current NanoPipe SNP detection statistics 'are not yet sophisticated' and plan more sophisticated statistics as future work

skills.description: Use when long reads (PacBio CLR or ONT) come from mixed samples — triploid/tetraploid genomes, metagenomes, or virus mixtures — and consensus-template correction would mask low-frequency haplotype variants.
skills.name: polyploid-haplotype-variant-recovery
skills.search_text: polyploid-haplotype-variant-recovery Use when long reads (PacBio CLR or ONT) come from mixed samples — triploid/tetraploid genomes, metagenomes, or virus mixtures — and consensus-template correction would mask low-frequency haplotype variants. Reads are from a single-haploid/clonal sample where a simple consensus template suffices — the graph-based haplotype machinery is unnecessary overhead (VeChat has longer runtimes and higher peak memory on large datasets). Input is already-corrected or high-accuracy data (e.g., PacBio HiFi/CCS); VeChat is a self-correction method for noisy raw TGS long reads. The goal is only assembly polishing of contigs rather than recovering haplotype variants in a mixed sample (e.g., Racon-style consensus polishing is the wrong-and-right tool mismatch). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Haplotype-aware error correction of long reads from polyploid (>diploid) samples using variation graphs (VeChat), so that true variants of lower-frequency haplotypes are not mistakenly masked as sequencing errors by consensus-induced biases. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Haplotype-aware error correction of long reads from polyploid (>diploid) samples using variation graphs (VeChat), so that true variants of lower-frequency haplotypes are not mistakenly masked as sequencing errors by consensus-induced biases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are from a single-haploid/clonal sample where a simple consensus template suffices — the graph-based haplotype machinery is unnecessary overhead (VeChat has longer runtimes and higher peak memory on large datasets). Input is already-corrected or high-accuracy data (e.g., PacBio HiFi/CCS); VeChat is a self-correction method for noisy raw TGS long reads. The goal is only assembly polishing of contigs rather than recovering haplotype variants in a mixed sample (e.g., Racon-style consensus polishing is the wrong-and-right tool mismatch).

skills.description: Use when assembling long TGS reads (PacBio or ONT) from diploid/polyploid or mixed samples where standard assemblers mask true low-frequency haplotype variants, and haplotype coverage must be quantified.
skills.name: polyploid-long-read-assembly
skills.search_text: polyploid-long-read-assembly Use when assembling long TGS reads (PacBio or ONT) from diploid/polyploid or mixed samples where standard assemblers mask true low-frequency haplotype variants, and haplotype coverage must be quantified. The input is a haploid/clonal sample with no haplotype structure — consensus-based correction is sufficient and VeChat adds runtime/memory overhead The analysis goal is exploring optimal preprocessing/error-correction/assembly pipeline combinations for polyploid, cancer or metagenomic settings, which the authors state is beyond the scope of this study and requires further efforts Only short Illumina reads are available — VeChat is designed for long TGS reads, and existing short-read error correction tools are the appropriate class http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assemble haplotype-aware genomes from long reads by first correcting reads with VeChat (variation graph-based error correction) and then running haplotype-aware and standard assemblers (HiCanu/Canu, Flye), followed by QUAST evaluation of haplotype coverage and error rates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Assemble haplotype-aware genomes from long reads by first correcting reads with VeChat (variation graph-based error correction) and then running haplotype-aware and standard assemblers (HiCanu/Canu, Flye), followed by QUAST evaluation of haplotype coverage and error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a haploid/clonal sample with no haplotype structure — consensus-based correction is sufficient and VeChat adds runtime/memory overhead The analysis goal is exploring optimal preprocessing/error-correction/assembly pipeline combinations for polyploid, cancer or metagenomic settings, which the authors state is beyond the scope of this study and requires further efforts Only short Illumina reads are available — VeChat is designed for long TGS reads, and existing short-read error correction tools are the appropriate class

skills.description: Use when benchmarking haplotype-aware long-read error correction on polyploid/poly-ploid mixtures (ploidy > 2) and you need simulated noisy PacBio CLR reads at controlled input error rates and per-haplotype coverage.
skills.name: polyploid-reference-read-generation
skills.search_text: polyploid-reference-read-generation Use when benchmarking haplotype-aware long-read error correction on polyploid/poly-ploid mixtures (ploidy > 2) and you need simulated noisy PacBio CLR reads at controlled input error rates and per-haplotype coverage. The reference is haploid or diploid — standard single/diploid simulation suffices and polyploid-aware ground truth is unnecessary Real sequencing data are already available; simulation is only needed to establish ground truth and controlled error rates The data are high-accuracy PacBio HiFi or ONT Q20 reads, where the noisy CLR simulation model (up to ~15% error) does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates simulated PacBio CLR long reads from a polyploid reference (e.g. a triploid genome built from three E. coli strains) at controlled sequencing error rates (15% and 5%) and ~30x coverage per haplotype, using PBSIM2, to benchmark haplotype-aware error correction such as VeChat. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Generates simulated PacBio CLR long reads from a polyploid reference (e.g. a triploid genome built from three E. coli strains) at controlled sequencing error rates (15% and 5%) and ~30x coverage per haplotype, using PBSIM2, to benchmark haplotype-aware error correction such as VeChat.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference is haploid or diploid — standard single/diploid simulation suffices and polyploid-aware ground truth is unnecessary Real sequencing data are already available; simulation is only needed to establish ground truth and controlled error rates The data are high-accuracy PacBio HiFi or ONT Q20 reads, where the noisy CLR simulation model (up to ~15% error) does not apply

skills.description: Use when pooled WGS reads must be mapped to exon sequences predicted from a de novo transcriptome (no reference genome) to call genotypable exonic SNPs, e.g. retrospective validation against known SNPs.
skills.name: pooled-genomic-read-mapping-to-predicted-exons
skills.search_text: pooled-genomic-read-mapping-to-predicted-exons Use when pooled WGS reads must be mapped to exon sequences predicted from a de novo transcriptome (no reference genome) to call genotypable exonic SNPs, e.g. retrospective validation against known SNPs. A reference genome and annotation exist and a splice-aware aligner such as GMAP can extract IEB coordinates directly — the EXFI route is for organisms where genomic references are not available or not reliable The input transcriptome is of poor quality or assembled from a single tissue, so lowly expressed transcripts are fragmented or missing (the herring case where EXFI was less accurate) SNPs of interest are non-exonic, since predicted exons cover only transcriptome-overlapping genomic k-mers http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps pooled raw whole-genome sequencing reads onto exon sequences predicted by EXFI (from a de novo transcriptome) with Bowtie2, then calls variants with BCFTools to recover genotypable exonic SNPs when no reference genome is available. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Maps pooled raw whole-genome sequencing reads onto exon sequences predicted by EXFI (from a de novo transcriptome) with Bowtie2, then calls variants with BCFTools to recover genotypable exonic SNPs when no reference genome is available.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome and annotation exist and a splice-aware aligner such as GMAP can extract IEB coordinates directly — the EXFI route is for organisms where genomic references are not available or not reliable The input transcriptome is of poor quality or assembled from a single tissue, so lowly expressed transcripts are fragmented or missing (the herring case where EXFI was less accurate) SNPs of interest are non-exonic, since predicted exons cover only transcriptome-overlapping genomic k-mers

skills.description: Use when running miniSNV's candidate-finder on nanopore BAM alignments and you need the prebuilt known-variant index (from a 1000 Genomes population VCF) to classify pileup candidate loci as high- or low-quality before genotyping.
skills.name: population-variant-frequency-indexing
skills.search_text: population-variant-frequency-indexing Use when running miniSNV's candidate-finder on nanopore BAM alignments and you need the prebuilt known-variant index (from a 1000 Genomes population VCF) to classify pileup candidate loci as high- or low-quality before genotyping. skills.search_text: pore-model-current-level-binning Use when nanopore signal-to-read or signal-to-reference alignments (e.g. move-table based plots from reads.blow5 + move tables) need a precise base shift, or when validating a k-mer pore model's per-base current-level separation. The signal alignment boundaries are already refined and validated (e.g. by f5c eventalign), so no base shift correction is needed. No k-mer pore model or move-table alignment exists for the chemistry — the binning requires either a pore model file or a read–signal alignment. You only need interactive visualisation of an already-aligned read (use squigualiser plot/plot_pileup directly instead of offset calculation). Derives a chemistry-specific k-mer-to-base shift correction by binning k-mer current levels into A/C/G/T density plots per candidate base index, identifying the most significant base, and sweeping sig_move_offset to find where base-specific current-level separation emerges. This corrects the systematic offset between signal events and single bases that existing nanopore signal alignment methods leave uncorrected. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae501

This corrects the systematic offset between signal events and single bases that existing nanopore signal alignment methods leave uncorrected.

skills.summary: Benchmark protocol that quantifies alignment precision and recall of read-to-contig linking information (as used for scaffolding graphs) against truth from simulated reads, alongside wall-clock runtime, across competing aligners and k-mer sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real reads with unknown truth — precision/recall of linking information cannot be computed without simulated ground truth Evaluation goals unrelated to scaffolding-graph linking information (e.g. base-level alignment accuracy of alignments themselves) Long-read aligner benchmarking — this protocol targets short-read aligners (Bowtie, Bowtie2, Bwa, Bwa-Mem) and Fast-SG

skills.description: Use when you have reads with per-read ground-truth modification labels (e.g. synthetic oligos where even-cycle GGACU positions are known modified) and need to compare modification callers by read-level precision-recall curves and PR AUC.
skills.name: precision-recall-evaluation-of-modification-callers
skills.search_text: precision-recall-evaluation-of-modification-callers Use when you have reads with per-read ground-truth modification labels (e.g. synthetic oligos where even-cycle GGACU positions are known modified) and need to compare modification callers by read-level precision-recall curves and PR AUC. The benchmark exposes only ensemble-level modification status with no per-read ground truth (e.g. natural mRNA with approximate labels), so read-level PR AUC cannot be computed Input reads have already been filtered/aligned or modification probabilities have already been computed — proceed directly to the thresholding and PR calculation step Evaluation target is site-level stoichiometry accuracy (e.g. comparison against GLORI measurements with min coverage 50), not single-molecule caller discrimination Benchmark dRNA-Seq m6A detection methods (mAFiA, CHEUI, m6Anet) at single-read resolution by computing precision-recall curves and PR AUC against known true-positive modifications on the TEST2 periodic-repeat synthetic benchmark, where reads carry a phase-shifted m6A pattern invisible at the aggregate site level. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47661-2
skills.summary: Benchmark dRNA-Seq m6A detection methods (mAFiA, CHEUI, m6Anet) at single-read resolution by computing precision-recall curves and PR AUC against known true-positive modifications on the TEST2 periodic-repeat synthetic benchmark, where reads carry a phase-shifted m6A pattern invisible at the aggregate site level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmark exposes only ensemble-level modification status with no per-read ground truth (e.g. natural mRNA with approximate labels), so read-level PR AUC cannot be computed Input reads have already been filtered/aligned or modification probabilities have already been computed — proceed directly to the thresholding and PR calculation step Evaluation target is site-level stoichiometry accuracy (e.g. comparison against GLORI measurements with min coverage 50), not single-molecule caller discrimination

skills.search_text: precision-recall-evaluation-of-variant-callers Use when a newly generated SV call set (e.g., from tumor/control long-read data) must be quantified as true/false positives against a published high-confidence somatic SV truth set to report precision and recall. The caller output is germline-only or single-sample, with no matched control — the somatic truth-set comparison does not model germline contamination. The truth set is not high-confidence or contains events ≤100 bp that were not filtered, since short indels are excluded from both benchmarks by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks somatic SV caller output against curated high-confidence truth sets by breakpoint overlap to compute precision and recall, as done for nanomonsv on COLO829 against the Arora and Valle-Inclan somatic SV benchmarks. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Benchmarks somatic SV caller output against curated high-confidence truth sets by breakpoint overlap to compute precision and recall, as done for nanomonsv on COLO829 against the Arora and Valle-Inclan somatic SV benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The caller output is germline-only or single-sample, with no matched control — the somatic truth-set comparison does not model germline contamination. The truth set is not high-confidence or contains events ≤100 bp that were not filtered, since short indels are excluded from both benchmarks by design.

skills.search_text: precision-recall-f1-computation Use when benchmarking SV callers whose outputs are VCFs against a simulated or GIAB truth set, and you need per-SV-type (insertion vs deletion) recall, precision, and F1 to rank methods. skills.summary: Computes recall, precision, and F1 score for structural variant callers (e.g. Blackbird, LongRanger, Manta, SvABA, LEVIATHAN) by matching each caller's VCF insertions/deletions longer than 50 bp against a truth set, enabling head-to-head benchmarking on the same BAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The caller outputs have not been filtered to the common size range (>50 bp insertions/deletions), so metrics would not be comparable across callers. There is no truth set available; recall/precision/F1 cannot be computed without a benchmark reference.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a variant caller's VCF output against a GIAB HG001 truth set and you need whole-genome or per-chromosome precision, recall, and F1-score to compare callers or verify reported metrics.
skills.name: precision-recall-f1-computation
skills.search_text: precision-recall-f1-computation Use when benchmarking a variant caller's VCF output against a GIAB HG001 truth set and you need whole-genome or per-chromosome precision, recall, and F1-score to compare callers or verify reported metrics. You are calling somatic variants or need trio-based analysis — Clairvoyante's evaluation pipeline here targets germline small variants only against a GIAB truth set The callset includes multi-allelic SNPs or indels >4 bp — these are excluded or only approximately typed in the Clairvoyante design, so F1 against them is not meaningful You need performance on a completely novel sequencing technology/chemistry for which no GIAB-style training/truth dataset exists http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Compute precision, recall, and F1-score for germline variant callsets by comparing caller VCFs against the Genome-in-a-Bottle v3.3.2 HG001 truth dataset with RTG vcfeval's haplotype-aware genotype matching, then extracting TP/FP/FN counts from the vcfeval output. This is the standard benchmarking step for evaluating variant callers such as Clairvoyante and DeepVariant across Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Compute precision, recall, and F1-score for germline variant callsets by comparing caller VCFs against the Genome-in-a-Bottle v3.3.2 HG001 truth dataset with RTG vcfeval's haplotype-aware genotype matching, then extracting TP/FP/FN counts from the vcfeval output. This is the standard benchmarking step for evaluating variant callers such as Clairvoyante and DeepVariant across Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are calling somatic variants or need trio-based analysis — Clairvoyante's evaluation pipeline here targets germline small variants only against a GIAB truth set The callset includes multi-allelic SNPs or indels >4 bp — these are excluded or only approximately typed in the Clairvoyante design, so F1 against them is not meaningful You need performance on a completely novel sequencing technology/chemistry for which no GIAB-style training/truth dataset exists

skills.description: Use when you have variant/insertion callsets (VCF) and a curated truth set (e.g., 5,630 HGSVC TE insertions) and need to quantify detection performance as precision/recall/F1, or compare tools head-to-head.

skills.search_text: precision-recall-f1-evaluation Use when you have variant/insertion callsets (VCF) and a curated truth set (e.g., 5,630 HGSVC TE insertions) and need to quantify detection performance as precision/recall/F1, or compare tools head-to-head. You lack a curated truth set — precision and recall cannot be computed and only consistency checks across callsets are possible Insertion coordinates come from different reference assemblies or unaligned representations, making SURVIVOR's positional distance-margin matching invalid The goal is genotyping accuracy (e.g., concordance with HGSV2 genotypes) rather than insertion detection performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark TE insertion detection callsets by matching predictions against a truth set with SURVIVOR at 100 bp (and a permissive 500 bp) distance margin, then computing precision, recall, and F1-score per tool or caller combination, as done to evaluate RetroInspector against the HGSVC 5,630-insertion truth set. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Benchmark TE insertion detection callsets by matching predictions against a truth set with SURVIVOR at 100 bp (and a permissive 500 bp) distance margin, then computing precision, recall, and F1-score per tool or caller combination, as done to evaluate RetroInspector against the HGSVC 5,630-insertion truth set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack a curated truth set — precision and recall cannot be computed and only consistency checks across callsets are possible Insertion coordinates come from different reference assemblies or unaligned representations, making SURVIVOR's positional distance-margin matching invalid The goal is genotyping accuracy (e.g., concordance with HGSV2 genotypes) rather than insertion detection performance

skills.name: primer-ccs-read-classification
skills.search_text: primer-ccs-read-classification Use when starting from a PacBio CCS BAM produced by HIT-scISOseq or 10x-coupled PacBio scIsoSeq libraries and you need to identify FLNC reads and extract CellBC/UMI/polyA-trimmed transcript sequences via primer orientation. Input is raw subreads BAM rather than CCS reads — run the ccs step first (SMRTlink 8.0+) Libraries whose primer sequences differ from the PacBio scIsoSeq / HIT-scISOseq 10x primer set, since primer_F/primer_S sequences and orientation semantics are hard-coded to that convention Reads already classified as FLNC by PacBio official isoseq3 software — the cDNA_Cupcake README notes many functions now have official isoseq equivalents http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Classifies PacBio CCS reads as full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) by BLAST-mapping them against 5' and 3' primer sequences and running scISA-Tools' classify_by_primer, which extracts cell barcodes, UMIs, and polyA-trimmed transcripts. It is the FLNC-detection step of the HIT-scISOseq/scISA-Tools pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Classifies PacBio CCS reads as full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) by BLAST-mapping them against 5' and 3' primer sequences and running scISA-Tools' classify_by_primer, which extracts cell barcodes, UMIs, and polyA-trimmed transcripts. It is the FLNC-detection step of the HIT-scISOseq/scISA-Tools pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw subreads BAM rather than CCS reads — run the ccs step first (SMRTlink 8.0+) Libraries whose primer sequences differ from the PacBio scIsoSeq / HIT-scISOseq 10x primer set, since primer_F/primer_S sequences and orientation semantics are hard-coded to that convention Reads already classified as FLNC by PacBio official isoseq3 software — the cDNA_Cupcake README notes many functions now have official isoseq equivalents

skills.description: Use when PacBio subread BAM files must be converted into primer-trimmed, chimeric-free FLNC reads before polyA trimming, alignment, or isoform annotation in an Iso-Seq workflow.
skills.name: primer-pair-selection-and-trimming
skills.search_text: primer-pair-selection-and-trimming Use when PacBio subread BAM files must be converted into primer-trimmed, chimeric-free FLNC reads before polyA trimming, alignment, or isoform annotation in an Iso-Seq workflow. Input is already FLNC reads with primers removed and chimeras discarded — re-running LIMA would find no primer pairs to select. Data is short-read or not PacBio single-molecule sequencing data — the ccs/LIMA/isoseq3 refine chain is specific to PacBio Iso-Seq libraries. The goal is demultiplexing barcodes from pooled samples without Iso-Seq library structure, where primer-pair selection does not apply as the primary operation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A PacBio Iso-Seq subread preprocessing skill in which LIMA selects CCS reads containing valid pairs of primers and removes the primer sequences, followed by chimera detection, producing clean full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) reads for downstream polyA trimming. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: A PacBio Iso-Seq subread preprocessing skill in which LIMA selects CCS reads containing valid pairs of primers and removes the primer sequences, followed by chimera detection, producing clean full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) reads for downstream polyA trimming.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already FLNC reads with primers removed and chimeras discarded — re-running LIMA would find no primer pairs to select. Data is short-read or not PacBio single-molecule sequencing data — the ccs/LIMA/isoseq3 refine chain is specific to PacBio Iso-Seq libraries. The goal is demultiplexing barcodes from pooled samples without Iso-Seq library structure, where primer-pair selection does not apply as the primary operation.

skills.description: Use when fusion breakpoints (e.g., from a NanoFG VCF) need PCR validation primers whose amplicon spans the fusion junction and must reproduce published validation primer sequences.
skills.name: primer-sequence-validation-against-published-primers
skills.search_text: primer-sequence-validation-against-published-primers Use when fusion breakpoints (e.g., from a NanoFG VCF) need PCR validation primers whose amplicon spans the fusion junction and must reproduce published validation primer sequences. Input is raw nanopore FASTQ reads that have not yet been processed by NanoFG — no breakpoint coordinates exist to flank with primers Starting material is fragmented FFPE DNA, where the article warns the FUDGE/crRNA approach and its validation strategy will most likely fail The goal is de novo primer design for arbitrary loci with no published primers to validate against — this skill specifically checks reproducibility of reported primers http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Designs fusion-junction-spanning PCR primer pairs with Primer3 from breakpoint-flanking reference sequence of fusion genes called by NanoFG, then validates the design by comparing it against published validation primers (e.g., Table 2 SS18 primers). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: Designs fusion-junction-spanning PCR primer pairs with Primer3 from breakpoint-flanking reference sequence of fusion genes called by NanoFG, then validates the design by comparing it against published validation primers (e.g., Table 2 SS18 primers).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore FASTQ reads that have not yet been processed by NanoFG — no breakpoint coordinates exist to flank with primers Starting material is fragmented FFPE DNA, where the article warns the FUDGE/crRNA approach and its validation strategy will most likely fail The goal is de novo primer design for arbitrary loci with no published primers to validate against — this skill specifically checks reproducibility of reported primers

skills.description: Use when a fusion gene has been called (e.g., a fusion breakpoint VCF from NanoFG/FUDGE) and PCR primers spanning the fusion junction are needed for validation.
skills.name: primer3-amplicon-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: primer3-amplicon-parameter-configuration Use when a fusion gene has been called (e.g., a fusion breakpoint VCF from NanoFG/FUDGE) and PCR primers spanning the fusion junction are needed for validation. Input DNA is fragmented/FFPE material, where the FUDGE/NanoFG assay most likely fails to comprehensively identify fusion genes and thus provides no reliable breakpoints to design against The structural variant has not been flagged as a candidate fusion (both SV ends must be in different genes and on the same strand with a continuous transcript) Only one fusion-spanning read supports the call and the plan is no-validation reporting (NanoFG's cutoff requires at least two fusion-spanning reads for validation-free detection) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Designs breakpoint-spanning PCR primer pairs with Primer3 for validation of fusion genes called by the NanoFG pipeline, extracting 200-400 bp of GRCh37 reference sequence flanking each fusion breakpoint and writing designed primers to primer_pairs.tsv. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: Designs breakpoint-spanning PCR primer pairs with Primer3 for validation of fusion genes called by the NanoFG pipeline, extracting 200-400 bp of GRCh37 reference sequence flanking each fusion breakpoint and writing designed primers to primer_pairs.tsv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input DNA is fragmented/FFPE material, where the FUDGE/NanoFG assay most likely fails to comprehensively identify fusion genes and thus provides no reliable breakpoints to design against The structural variant has not been flagged as a candidate fusion (both SV ends must be in different genes and on the same strand with a continuous transcript) Only one fusion-spanning read supports the call and the plan is no-validation reporting (NanoFG's cutoff requires at least two fusion-spanning reads for validation-free detection)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a phenotype-based gene prioritizer and you suspect certain genes recur at high positions across many cases; count top-N gene occurrences per ranked case output to expose such bias.

skills.search_text: prioritization-bias-analysis Use when benchmarking a phenotype-based gene prioritizer and you suspect certain genes recur at high positions across many cases; count top-N gene occurrences per ranked case output to expose such bias. The tool output is unranked or already collapsed into a single gene set rather than per-case ranked gene lists The goal is overall ranking accuracy (e.g., rank-of-causal-gene distributions, recall at rank 20) rather than detecting recurring over-represented genes Analysis targets structural variants or variant-level filtering (allele frequency, pathogenicity) rather than gene-prioritization output http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3325 Quantifies over-representation of specific genes in the top-ranked positions of a gene prioritization tool's per-case output lists, as done for MECP2 (NCBI 4204) and KMT2D (NCBI 8085) in the VIBE benchmark of 305 rare-disease patient cases. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Quantifies over-representation of specific genes in the top-ranked positions of a gene prioritization tool's per-case output lists, as done for MECP2 (NCBI 4204) and KMT2D (NCBI 8085) in the VIBE benchmark of 305 rare-disease patient cases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tool output is unranked or already collapsed into a single gene set rather than per-case ranked gene lists The goal is overall ranking accuracy (e.g., rank-of-causal-gene distributions, recall at rank 20) rather than detecting recurring over-represented genes Analysis targets structural variants or variant-level filtering (allele frequency, pathogenicity) rather than gene-prioritization output

skills.description: Use when you need to index the unique k-mer content of reference contigs for fast k-mer look-up in reads (e.g. scaffolding-graph construction), especially for k-mer sizes in the 12–256 range and memory-frugal probabilistic storage.
skills.name: probabilistic-kmer-dictionary-construction
skills.search_text: probabilistic-kmer-dictionary-construction Use when you need to index the unique k-mer content of reference contigs for fast k-mer look-up in reads (e.g. scaffolding-graph construction), especially for k-mer sizes in the 12–256 range and memory-frugal probabilistic storage. When exact (zero false-positive) k-mer look-up is required — quasi_dictionary returns values for non-indexed keys at a rate below 1/2^fingerprint_size, so it is unsuitable where any false positive is intolerable. When k-mer size outside the supported 12–256 range is needed, or when the dictionary would be better served by an exact hash map for a small reference. When you need base-level alignments rather than alignment-free k-mer linking — this index supports Fast-SG's scaffolding-graph construction, not read alignment/variant calling. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Builds a light-weight, alignment-free k-mer dictionary over contig sequences by counting k-mers with KMC3 and storing the unique set in a BBHash minimal perfect hash wrapped in a quasi_dictionary probabilistic membership structure, as used by Fast-SG to enable ultrafast scaffolding-graph construction. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Builds a light-weight, alignment-free k-mer dictionary over contig sequences by counting k-mers with KMC3 and storing the unique set in a BBHash minimal perfect hash wrapped in a quasi_dictionary probabilistic membership structure, as used by Fast-SG to enable ultrafast scaffolding-graph construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When exact (zero false-positive) k-mer look-up is required — quasi_dictionary returns values for non-indexed keys at a rate below 1/2^fingerprint_size, so it is unsuitable where any false positive is intolerable. When k-mer size outside the supported 12–256 range is needed, or when the dictionary would be better served by an exact hash map for a small reference. When you need base-level alignments rather than alignment-free k-mer linking — this index supports Fast-SG's scaffolding-graph construction, not read alignment/variant calling.

skills.description: Use when you have per-site nanopore methylation calls with a continuous score (e.g., methylation_rate from Dorado call_mods output) and need a data-driven confidence cutoff before aggregating methylation frequency for benchmarking against BS-seq.
skills.name: probability-distribution-binning
skills.search_text: probability-distribution-binning Use when you have per-site nanopore methylation calls with a continuous score (e.g., methylation_rate from Dorado call_mods output) and need a data-driven confidence cutoff before aggregating methylation frequency for benchmarking against BS-seq. Methylation calls already carry a validated fixed confidence threshold from the tool vendor and re-tuning is out of scope The score distribution over 0.2-0.9 is unimodal with no discernible trough, making the minimum-population bin an unstable threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Selects an adaptive methylation score confidence threshold (P_th) by binning per-site methylation_rate values into a probability histogram and picking the trough (minimum-population bin) as the decision boundary. Borrowed from DeepPlant, it minimizes the sum of false-positive and false-negative methylation calls and was shown to improve Dorado's site-level methylation correlations with BS-seq (the Dorado* condition). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Selects an adaptive methylation score confidence threshold (P_th) by binning per-site methylation_rate values into a probability histogram and picking the trough (minimum-population bin) as the decision boundary. Borrowed from DeepPlant, it minimizes the sum of false-positive and false-negative methylation calls and was shown to improve Dorado's site-level methylation correlations with BS-seq (the Dorado* condition).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Methylation calls already carry a validated fixed confidence threshold from the tool vendor and re-tuning is out of scope The score distribution over 0.2-0.9 is unimodal with no discernible trough, making the minimum-population bin an unstable threshold

skills.description: Use when nanopore (ONT) FASTQ/FASTA reads contain barcodes embedded in adapter-flanking-barcode-flanking-insert library structures and you must assign reads to samples despite ONT-level insertion/deletion/substitution errors.
skills.name: probability-divergence-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: probability-divergence-demultiplexing Use when nanopore (ONT) FASTQ/FASTA reads contain barcodes embedded in adapter-flanking-barcode-flanking-insert library structures and you must assign reads to samples despite ONT-level insertion/deletion/substitution errors. PacBio sequencing data — the authors note PRO 'can be employed for both ONT and PacBio sequencing data; however, no tests on PacBio data have been performed yet' Barcode kits whose flanking sequences are similar to the barcodes themselves (as with ONT kits B1–B3), where PRO cannot accurately extract the corrupted barcode and Guppy performs better Reads lacking the expected adapters-flanking-barcode-flanking-insert library structure with known flanking sequences, since barcode extraction depends on edlib alignment of the flanking sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Demultiplex corrupted DNA barcodes from high-error-rate nanopore reads using PRO's two-stage approach: extract the noisy barcode by aligning flanking sequences with edlib, then assign each barcode by maximum probability divergence (PRO-dex), a probabilistic divergence measure that outperformed Guppy by 4.31% on large PRO-designed kits. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
skills.summary: Demultiplex corrupted DNA barcodes from high-error-rate nanopore reads using PRO's two-stage approach: extract the noisy barcode by aligning flanking sequences with edlib, then assign each barcode by maximum probability divergence (PRO-dex), a probabilistic divergence measure that outperformed Guppy by 4.31% on large PRO-designed kits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: PacBio sequencing data — the authors note PRO 'can be employed for both ONT and PacBio sequencing data; however, no tests on PacBio data have been performed yet' Barcode kits whose flanking sequences are similar to the barcodes themselves (as with ONT kits B1–B3), where PRO cannot accurately extract the corrupted barcode and Guppy performs better Reads lacking the expected adapters-flanking-barcode-flanking-insert library structure with known flanking sequences, since barcode extraction depends on edlib alignment of the flanking sequences

skills.name: probability-divergence-sequence-scoring
skills.search_text: probability-divergence-sequence-scoring Use when comparing short DNA barcode sequences under nanopore-style error models (substitutions, insertions, deletions) — e. Reads whose flanking sequences are similar to the barcode itself — PRO cannot accurately extract the corrupted barcode and underperforms Guppy in that case Barcodes of unequal length or non-ONT error profiles where the pm/pd/ps/pi decomposition does not apply PacBio sequencing data — PRO is proposed for both ONT and PacBio but no PacBio tests have been performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Scores dissimilarity between two short, equal-length DNA sequences using PRO's probability divergence, ProDiv(X,Y)=pm^m·pd^d·(1/3·ps)^s·(1/4·pi)^i, a probabilistic alternative to edit distance for selecting distinguishable barcodes and demultiplexing corrupted nanopore barcode reads. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
