skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads whose flanking sequences are similar to the barcode itself — PRO cannot accurately extract the corrupted barcode and underperforms Guppy in that case Barcodes of unequal length or non-ONT error profiles where the pm/pd/ps/pi decomposition does not apply PacBio sequencing data — PRO is proposed for both ONT and PacBio but no PacBio tests have been performed

skills.description: Use when generating a PRO barcode kit and you must translate a target edit-error tolerance (e.g., 2 errors in a 24-mer) into the probability-divergence threshold t that governs candidate removal and barcode selection.
skills.name: probability-divergence-threshold-calibration
skills.search_text: probability-divergence-threshold-calibration Use when generating a PRO barcode kit and you must translate a target edit-error tolerance (e.g., 2 errors in a 24-mer) into the probability-divergence threshold t that governs candidate removal and barcode selection. The task is demultiplexing already-sequenced reads with Guppy official configs (barcode_arrs_nb12.cfg, barcode_arrs_16s.cfg, barcode_arrs_pcr96.cfg) — no PRO threshold calibration is involved. The candidate set has not been preprocessed (64-bit hashing and flanking-similarity removal with edlib, edit distance <= 1), so the threshold would be applied over an unnecessarily large 4^n space. The platform is PacBio — the article states no tests on PacBio data have been performed, so the ONT-calibrated threshold may not transfer. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calibrates PRO's probability-divergence threshold t used during barcode generation by converting the number of edit errors a 24 bp barcode must tolerate (e.g., -th 2 at sequencing accuracy -a 0.88) into ProDiv units, then filtering the candidate k-mer space accordingly before farthest-point sampling. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.fmre.2024.04.014
skills.summary: Calibrates PRO's probability-divergence threshold t used during barcode generation by converting the number of edit errors a 24 bp barcode must tolerate (e.g., -th 2 at sequencing accuracy -a 0.88) into ProDiv units, then filtering the candidate k-mer space accordingly before farthest-point sampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is demultiplexing already-sequenced reads with Guppy official configs (barcode_arrs_nb12.cfg, barcode_arrs_16s.cfg, barcode_arrs_pcr96.cfg) — no PRO threshold calibration is involved. The candidate set has not been preprocessed (64-bit hashing and flanking-similarity removal with edlib, edit distance <= 1), so the threshold would be applied over an unnecessarily large 4^n space. The platform is PacBio — the article states no tests on PacBio data have been performed, so the ONT-calibrated threshold may not transfer.

skills.description: Use when you have per-read per-CpG methylation probabilities (e.g., ccsmeth 5mCpG calls on PacBio HiFi reads) with ground truth, and need to trade call coverage for accuracy via a confidence threshold.
skills.name: probability-margin-threshold-evaluation
skills.search_text: probability-margin-threshold-evaluation Use when you have per-read per-CpG methylation probabilities (e.g., ccsmeth 5mCpG calls on PacBio HiFi reads) with ground truth, and need to trade call coverage for accuracy via a confidence threshold. The modification is not CpG-context 5mC (e.g., non-CpG 5mC, 6mA, or hemimethylated CpGs) — ccsmeth models cannot detect these, so probability calls would not exist to filter No ground truth (methylated/unmethylated control DNA) is available, since the skill requires computing accuracy before vs. after filtering The downstream step is site-level aggregation at very low coverage, where discarding 8.9–12.8% of reads may further degrade per-site estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Filters ambiguous per-read methylation calls by a probability-margin threshold ∆p = |Pr − P'r| (P'r = 1 − Pr), quantifying the accuracy gain against the fraction of calls discarded. Applied to ccsmeth read-level 5mCpG calls, ∆p ≥ 0.33 lifts read-level accuracy by 3.5–4.2 percentage points at the cost of dropping 8.9–12.8% of calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Filters ambiguous per-read methylation calls by a probability-margin threshold ∆p = |Pr − P'r| (P'r = 1 − Pr), quantifying the accuracy gain against the fraction of calls discarded. Applied to ccsmeth read-level 5mCpG calls, ∆p ≥ 0.33 lifts read-level accuracy by 3.5–4.2 percentage points at the cost of dropping 8.9–12.8% of calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modification is not CpG-context 5mC (e.g., non-CpG 5mC, 6mA, or hemimethylated CpGs) — ccsmeth models cannot detect these, so probability calls would not exist to filter No ground truth (methylated/unmethylated control DNA) is available, since the skill requires computing accuracy before vs. after filtering The downstream step is site-level aggregation at very low coverage, where discarding 8.9–12.8% of reads may further degrade per-site estimates

skills.description: Use when nanomonsv insert_classify returns somatic insertion sequences from tumor/control paired long-read data and some inserted sequences match annotated transcripts, requiring separation of processed pseudogene insertions from LINE1/Alu/SVA mobile element insertions.
skills.name: processed-pseudogene-transcript-matching
skills.search_text: processed-pseudogene-transcript-matching Use when nanomonsv insert_classify returns somatic insertion sequences from tumor/control paired long-read data and some inserted sequences match annotated transcripts, requiring separation of processed pseudogene insertions from LINE1/Alu/SVA mobile element insertions. Input is germline or single-sample long-read data without a matched control — nanomonsv's somatic calling and this classification workflow assume tumor/control paired data Detecting subclonal MEIs present in a minority of cells, which the article notes remains challenging at modest sequencing depth Long repeat expansion events (e.g. VNTR/microsatellite expansions), which the reference-genome-based framework may not capture reliably http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Within the nanomonsv mobile element insertion (MEI) classification workflow, inserted sequences whose sequence significantly matches a Gencode transcript are re-labeled as processed pseudogenes before RepeatMasker-based LINE1/Alu/SVA annotation, so retrotransposition counts are not inflated by pseudogene insertions. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Within the nanomonsv mobile element insertion (MEI) classification workflow, inserted sequences whose sequence significantly matches a Gencode transcript are re-labeled as processed pseudogenes before RepeatMasker-based LINE1/Alu/SVA annotation, so retrotransposition counts are not inflated by pseudogene insertions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is germline or single-sample long-read data without a matched control — nanomonsv's somatic calling and this classification workflow assume tumor/control paired data Detecting subclonal MEIs present in a minority of cells, which the article notes remains challenging at modest sequencing depth Long repeat expansion events (e.g. VNTR/microsatellite expansions), which the reference-genome-based framework may not capture reliably

skills.description: Use when a concatenated multi-view protein feature vector (e.g. 3240-D DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) contains noisy/redundant features and you need ranked feature importance plus an optimal subset before SVM classification.
skills.name: protein-dna-binding-feature-importance-analysis
skills.search_text: protein-dna-binding-feature-importance-analysis Use when a concatenated multi-view protein feature vector (e.g. 3240-D DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) contains noisy/redundant features and you need ranked feature importance plus an optimal subset before SVM classification. Input is already a small, non-redundant feature table where SVM-RFE+CBR ranking would add cost without benefit The task is raw sequence annotation rather than feature-space analysis — feature extraction (DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) must happen first Only the independent-test dataset (PDB186) is available without a training set to drive the recursive feature elimination http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Ranks multi-view protein features and extracts the optimal discriminating subset for DNA-binding protein (DBP) prediction using SVM-RFE+CBR, as in iDBP-DEP, which reduces the 3240-dimension DDE/PSSM-DBT/PSSM-DWT/NMBAC vector to a 424-feature optimum. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small, non-redundant feature table where SVM-RFE+CBR ranking would add cost without benefit The task is raw sequence annotation rather than feature-space analysis — feature extraction (DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) must happen first Only the independent-test dataset (PDB186) is available without a training set to drive the recursive feature elimination

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a protein-domain inventory over a curated FASTA set (e.g. Swiss-Prot sequences matched to GENCODE Basic translations) so that residues can later be projected onto Pfam domain consensus positions for meta-domain variant aggregation.
skills.name: protein-domain-annotation-with-interproscan
skills.search_text: protein-domain-annotation-with-interproscan Use when building or reproducing a protein-domain inventory over a curated FASTA set (e.g. Swiss-Prot sequences matched to GENCODE Basic translations) so that residues can later be projected onto Pfam domain consensus positions for meta-domain variant aggregation. You only need the finished mapping database rather than a fresh domain annotation — download the prebuilt release (e.g. MetaDome_v2.0_GRCh38.p14_..._Pfam-37.4_prebuild-mapping-database.csv.gz from Zenodo record 19376150) instead of re-annotating Your input is raw GENCODE transcript translations that have not yet been filtered and BLAST-matched to Swiss-Prot sequences — run the GENCODE-to-Swiss-Prot Protein–Protein BLAST mapping step first You need non-Pfam domain resources or Gene Ontology annotation the paper does not describe as loaded into MetaDome's 'interpro_domains' table Annotates protein domain instances on matched Swiss-Prot sequences by running InterProScan v5.20-59.0 with the Pfam-A v30.0 library, then loading each domain annotation into the 'interpro_domains' table of the MetaDome PostgreSQL mapping database. This establishes the Pfam domain inventory (71,419 domains on 30,406 Swiss-Prot sequences) that MetaDome's meta-domain aggregation depends on. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Annotates protein domain instances on matched Swiss-Prot sequences by running InterProScan v5.20-59.0 with the Pfam-A v30.0 library, then loading each domain annotation into the 'interpro_domains' table of the MetaDome PostgreSQL mapping database. This establishes the Pfam domain inventory (71,419 domains on 30,406 Swiss-Prot sequences) that MetaDome's meta-domain aggregation depends on.

skills.name: protein-feature-vector-construction
skills.search_text: protein-feature-vector-construction Use when starting from raw FASTA protein sequences and you need a fixed-length dipeptide-composition feature matrix (400 dimensions per protein) to feed downstream feature selection or SVM classification. Input is already a computed feature matrix or workspace .mat file (e.g. feature_NMBAC_594.mat) — re-encoding would be redundant Sequences are shorter than 50 residues or contain 'X' ambiguous residues, which the iDBP-DEP pipeline excludes The goal is PSSM-based evolutionary encoding (PSSM-DBT/PSSM-DWT), which requires PSI-BLAST profiles rather than raw sequence dipeptide statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Constructs per-protein numeric feature vectors for DNA-binding protein prediction by encoding dipeptide composition as the Dipeptide Deviation from Expected Mean (DDE) descriptor, the first encoding step of the iDBP-DEP multi-view feature pipeline before PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT and NMBAC encoding. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Constructs per-protein numeric feature vectors for DNA-binding protein prediction by encoding dipeptide composition as the Dipeptide Deviation from Expected Mean (DDE) descriptor, the first encoding step of the iDBP-DEP multi-view feature pipeline before PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT and NMBAC encoding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a computed feature matrix or workspace .mat file (e.g. feature_NMBAC_594.mat) — re-encoding would be redundant Sequences are shorter than 50 residues or contain 'X' ambiguous residues, which the iDBP-DEP pipeline excludes The goal is PSSM-based evolutionary encoding (PSSM-DBT/PSSM-DWT), which requires PSI-BLAST profiles rather than raw sequence dipeptide statistics

skills.description: Use when coding genes predicted from an assembled transcriptome are absent from reference annotations (e.g. NCBI/Ensembl GTF) and their identity must be recovered by protein-level homology against a same-species UniProt proteome.
skills.name: protein-homology-identification-blastp
skills.search_text: protein-homology-identification-blastp Use when coding genes predicted from an assembled transcriptome are absent from reference annotations (e.g. NCBI/Ensembl GTF) and their identity must be recovered by protein-level homology against a same-species UniProt proteome. The organism has no assembled genome or no NCBI GTF annotation available, since the pipeline requires both to define which genes are missing Coding genes are already present in the reference annotation (NCBI or Ensembl), so no novel proteins need homology assignment Only nucleotide-level (not protein-level) homology is needed — the method uses blastp on deduced proteins, not blastn http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 A method for recovering genes missing from a reference genome annotation by blasting novel predicted protein sequences (e.g. from a StringTie SCO transcriptome assembly) against the species' UniProt proteome and classifying hits as homologs or paralogs using genomic position and percent identity criteria. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: A method for recovering genes missing from a reference genome annotation by blasting novel predicted protein sequences (e.g. from a StringTie SCO transcriptome assembly) against the species' UniProt proteome and classifying hits as homologs or paralogs using genomic position and percent identity criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism has no assembled genome or no NCBI GTF annotation available, since the pipeline requires both to define which genes are missing Coding genes are already present in the reference annotation (NCBI or Ensembl), so no novel proteins need homology assignment Only nucleotide-level (not protein-level) homology is needed — the method uses blastp on deduced proteins, not blastn

skills.description: Use when encoding protein sequences for classification (e.g. DBP vs non-DBP) requires combining evolutionary-profile, dipeptide-composition and physicochemical-property views into one fixed-length vector for downstream feature selection.
skills.name: protein-multiview-feature-vector-concatenation
skills.search_text: protein-multiview-feature-vector-concatenation Use when encoding protein sequences for classification (e.g. DBP vs non-DBP) requires combining evolutionary-profile, dipeptide-composition and physicochemical-property views into one fixed-length vector for downstream feature selection. Input is already a reduced/optimal feature table from a prior feature-selection run — re-concatenating raw descriptor blocks would reintroduce the noisy and redundant features the selection was meant to remove No PSSM profiles are available (or no PSI-BLAST run against nr is feasible) — the PSSM-DBT and PSSM-DWT blocks cannot be computed, so the 3240-dim scheme does not apply The task requires interpreting individual descriptor importance rather than producing a single classification-ready matrix — per-descriptor analysis is a different sub-task http://edamontology.org/topic_3510 Concatenate heterogeneous protein descriptors — DDE (dipeptide deviation), PSSM-DBT (Distance-Bigram Transformation), PSSM-DWT (Discrete Wavelet Transformation) and NMBAC (Normalized Moreau-Broto Autocorrelation) — into a single 3240-dimension feature vector per sequence, which is then pruned by SVM-RFE+CBR feature selection before SVM classification. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Concatenate heterogeneous protein descriptors — DDE (dipeptide deviation), PSSM-DBT (Distance-Bigram Transformation), PSSM-DWT (Discrete Wavelet Transformation) and NMBAC (Normalized Moreau-Broto Autocorrelation) — into a single 3240-dimension feature vector per sequence, which is then pruned by SVM-RFE+CBR feature selection before SVM classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced/optimal feature table from a prior feature-selection run — re-concatenating raw descriptor blocks would reintroduce the noisy and redundant features the selection was meant to remove No PSSM profiles are available (or no PSI-BLAST run against nr is feasible) — the PSSM-DBT and PSSM-DWT blocks cannot be computed, so the 3240-dim scheme does not apply The task requires interpreting individual descriptor importance rather than producing a single classification-ready matrix — per-descriptor analysis is a different sub-task

skills.description: Use when encoding raw protein sequences (e.g. from PDB1075/PDB594 FASTA sets) into physicochemical-property autocorrelation features plus amino acid composition for a DNA-binding-protein classifier.
skills.name: protein-sequence-amino-acid-composition-calculation
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-amino-acid-composition-calculation Use when encoding raw protein sequences (e.g. from PDB1075/PDB594 FASTA sets) into physicochemical-property autocorrelation features plus amino acid composition for a DNA-binding-protein classifier. Input is already an extracted feature table or .mat feature matrix (e.g. feature_NMBAC_594.mat) — recomputing the descriptor would be redundant The target descriptor is PSSM-based (PSSM-DBT or PSSM-DWT) — those skills operate on PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles, not raw sequences and phy_6.mat properties Sequences contain non-standard or ambiguous amino acid residues — the descriptor standardizes only the 20 natural amino acids defined in phy_6.mat http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes the Normalized Moreau-Broto Autocorrelation (NMBAC) descriptor from protein sequences in the iDBP-DEP pipeline: 6 physicochemical properties autocorrelated at lags 1-30 plus amino acid frequencies, yielding a 200-dimension vector per protein. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Computes the Normalized Moreau-Broto Autocorrelation (NMBAC) descriptor from protein sequences in the iDBP-DEP pipeline: 6 physicochemical properties autocorrelated at lags 1-30 plus amino acid frequencies, yielding a 200-dimension vector per protein.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an extracted feature table or .mat feature matrix (e.g. feature_NMBAC_594.mat) — recomputing the descriptor would be redundant The target descriptor is PSSM-based (PSSM-DBT or PSSM-DWT) — those skills operate on PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles, not raw sequences and phy_6.mat properties Sequences contain non-standard or ambiguous amino acid residues — the descriptor standardizes only the 20 natural amino acids defined in phy_6.mat

skills.description: Use when merging heterogeneous protein reference databases (e.g., CARD, NDARO, SARG, RefSeq homologs) and redundant near-identical sequences must be collapsed into a consistent type/subtype hierarchy before read mapping.
skills.name: protein-sequence-clustering-deduplication
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-clustering-deduplication Use when merging heterogeneous protein reference databases (e.g., CARD, NDARO, SARG, RefSeq homologs) and redundant near-identical sequences must be collapsed into a consistent type/subtype hierarchy before read mapping. Applications requiring ORF-based annotation or detailed sequence typing, since clustering highly similar ARGs (e.g., blaOXA-1 with blaOXA-1042) intentionally lowers resolution Analyses targeting point-mutation-derived ARG variants, which are excluded from the database because read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Deduplicate and organize large protein reference sets into non-redundant clusters with strict sequence-identity thresholds, as done to curate the SARG+ ARG database (104,529 sequences) for species-level read-based antibiotic resistance surveillance. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Deduplicate and organize large protein reference sets into non-redundant clusters with strict sequence-identity thresholds, as done to curate the SARG+ ARG database (104,529 sequences) for species-level read-based antibiotic resistance surveillance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Applications requiring ORF-based annotation or detailed sequence typing, since clustering highly similar ARGs (e.g., blaOXA-1 with blaOXA-1042) intentionally lowers resolution Analyses targeting point-mutation-derived ARG variants, which are excluded from the database because read-based profiling cannot reliably distinguish SNPs from sequencing errors

skills.description: Use when you need per-descriptor protein feature matrices (.mat workspaces for DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) from FASTA sequences plus PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles, e.g. for ablation or downstream SVM-RFE+CBR selection.
skills.name: protein-sequence-descriptor-extraction
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-descriptor-extraction Use when you need per-descriptor protein feature matrices (.mat workspaces for DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) from FASTA sequences plus PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles, e.g. for ablation or downstream SVM-RFE+CBR selection. The per-descriptor .mat feature tables already exist in the repository's Data/*/Feature Data directories — load them instead of re-extracting You only have raw sequences without PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles and cannot run PSI-BLAST against nr, since PSSM-DBT and PSSM-DWT require evolutionary profiles The goal is classifier training or evaluation (before_FS.m, train_1075.m) rather than descriptor generation http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Encode protein sequences into the four multi-view descriptor spaces used by iDBP-DEP — DDE (dipeptide deviation from expected mean), PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT and NMBAC — which together yield 3240-dimension feature vectors for DNA-binding protein prediction and per-descriptor ablation. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Encode protein sequences into the four multi-view descriptor spaces used by iDBP-DEP — DDE (dipeptide deviation from expected mean), PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT and NMBAC — which together yield 3240-dimension feature vectors for DNA-binding protein prediction and per-descriptor ablation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The per-descriptor .mat feature tables already exist in the repository's Data/*/Feature Data directories — load them instead of re-extracting You only have raw sequences without PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles and cannot run PSI-BLAST against nr, since PSSM-DBT and PSSM-DWT require evolutionary profiles The goal is classifier training or evaluation (before_FS.m, train_1075.m) rather than descriptor generation

skills.description: Use when raw protein sequences (e.g. FASTA from PDB1075, PDB594, PDB186) must be converted into fixed-length dipeptide-composition feature vectors for machine-learning classification of DNA-binding proteins.
skills.name: protein-sequence-dipeptide-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-dipeptide-feature-extraction Use when raw protein sequences (e.g. FASTA from PDB1075, PDB594, PDB186) must be converted into fixed-length dipeptide-composition feature vectors for machine-learning classification of DNA-binding proteins. The input is already a numeric feature matrix or a precomputed DDE workspace (.mat) file rather than raw sequences The target descriptor is the PSSM-based feature (PSSM-DBT/PSSM-DWT) or the physicochemical NMBAC descriptor, which require PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles or amino-acid physicochemical property tables instead of bare sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3510 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes the Dipeptide Deviation from Expected Mean (DDE) descriptor, a 400-dimension encoding of protein dipeptide composition, as used as the first feature-extraction step of the iDBP-DEP DNA-binding protein predictor. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Computes the Dipeptide Deviation from Expected Mean (DDE) descriptor, a 400-dimension encoding of protein dipeptide composition, as used as the first feature-extraction step of the iDBP-DEP DNA-binding protein predictor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a numeric feature matrix or a precomputed DDE workspace (.mat) file rather than raw sequences The target descriptor is the PSSM-based feature (PSSM-DBT/PSSM-DWT) or the physicochemical NMBAC descriptor, which require PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles or amino-acid physicochemical property tables instead of bare sequences

skills.description: Use when raw protein sequences (PDB1075/PDB594/PDB186 style FASTA) must be turned into fixed-length numeric descriptors before machine-learning classification, and PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles plus physicochemical properties are available.
skills.name: protein-sequence-feature-vectorization
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-feature-vectorization Use when raw protein sequences (PDB1075/PDB594/PDB186 style FASTA) must be turned into fixed-length numeric descriptors before machine-learning classification, and PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles plus physicochemical properties are available. Input is already a per-protein feature matrix (e.g. the ~/Data/*/Feature Data .mat files) — re-vectorization would duplicate the encoding step No PSI-BLAST PSSM profile can be generated (e.g. no nr database access) — PSSM-DBT and PSSM-DWT descriptors cannot be computed, only DDE and NMBAC apply The downstream task requires residue-level rather than sequence-level fixed-length representations http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encode protein sequences into fixed-length numeric feature vectors using multiple descriptors from the iDBP-DEP pipeline: DDE (dipeptide composition), PSSM-DBT (Distance-Bigram Transformation, 1600-d), PSSM-DWT (Discrete Wavelet Transform, 1040-d), and NMBAC (Normalized Moreau-Broto Autocorrelation, 200-d), concatenated into a 3240-dimension vector per protein for DNA-binding protein prediction. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Encode protein sequences into fixed-length numeric feature vectors using multiple descriptors from the iDBP-DEP pipeline: DDE (dipeptide composition), PSSM-DBT (Distance-Bigram Transformation, 1600-d), PSSM-DWT (Discrete Wavelet Transform, 1040-d), and NMBAC (Normalized Moreau-Broto Autocorrelation, 200-d), concatenated into a 3240-dimension vector per protein for DNA-binding protein prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-protein feature matrix (e.g. the ~/Data/*/Feature Data .mat files) — re-vectorization would duplicate the encoding step No PSI-BLAST PSSM profile can be generated (e.g. no nr database access) — PSSM-DBT and PSSM-DWT descriptors cannot be computed, only DDE and NMBAC apply The downstream task requires residue-level rather than sequence-level fixed-length representations

skills.description: Use when validating that deduced proteins from an assembled transcriptome (e.g. GAWN/TransDecoder prot.fa outputs) match known homologs, or when confirming identity of a reconstructed protein like chicken SSPO against AJ866919.
skills.name: protein-sequence-homology-blast-verification
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-homology-blast-verification Use when validating that deduced proteins from an assembled transcriptome (e.g. GAWN/TransDecoder prot.fa outputs) match known homologs, or when confirming identity of a reconstructed protein like chicken SSPO against AJ866919. When the organism has no assembled genome or NCBI GTF annotation available — the upstream pipeline this verification depends on is explicitly restricted to such cases When transcripts are predicted as long non-coding RNAs by FEELnc and have no deduced protein product to blast When the goal is comprehensive homolog discovery rather than single-best-hit verification — forcing -max_hsps 1 -max_target_seqs 1 discards secondary hits http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Verifies assembled transcript-derived proteins by BLAST homology against reference databases, using constrained blastx/blastp settings (e.g. -max_hsps 1 -max_target_seqs 1) to recover a single top hit and quantify identity to a known protein such as the chicken SSPO reference AJ866919. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Verifies assembled transcript-derived proteins by BLAST homology against reference databases, using constrained blastx/blastp settings (e.g. -max_hsps 1 -max_target_seqs 1) to recover a single top hit and quantify identity to a known protein such as the chicken SSPO reference AJ866919.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the organism has no assembled genome or NCBI GTF annotation available — the upstream pipeline this verification depends on is explicitly restricted to such cases When transcripts are predicted as long non-coding RNAs by FEELnc and have no deduced protein product to blast When the goal is comprehensive homolog discovery rather than single-best-hit verification — forcing -max_hsps 1 -max_target_seqs 1 discards secondary hits

skills.description: Use when testing whether per-gene poly(A) tail lengths (e.g., PAIso-seq GV oocyte measurements) correlate with protein abundance by splitting genes into detected vs non-detected proteome classes.
skills.name: proteome-abundance-based-transcript-classification
skills.search_text: proteome-abundance-based-transcript-classification Use when testing whether per-gene poly(A) tail lengths (e.g., PAIso-seq GV oocyte measurements) correlate with protein abundance by splitting genes into detected vs non-detected proteome classes. Input is single-mRNA data (e.g., individualReporter-based translational control experiments) rather than transcriptome-wide per-gene tail lengths Proteome list lacks gene identifiers matching the tail-length table's gene keys, so the join by gene identifier would fail silently http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Classify maternal transcripts into high vs low protein abundance groups by joining per-gene geometric-mean poly(A) tail lengths from PAIso-seq GV oocyte data with a GV oocyte mass-spectrometry proteome gene list, then test whether the positive tail-length–translation association holds transcriptome-wide. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Classify maternal transcripts into high vs low protein abundance groups by joining per-gene geometric-mean poly(A) tail lengths from PAIso-seq GV oocyte data with a GV oocyte mass-spectrometry proteome gene list, then test whether the positive tail-length–translation association holds transcriptome-wide.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-mRNA data (e.g., individualReporter-based translational control experiments) rather than transcriptome-wide per-gene tail lengths Proteome list lacks gene identifiers matching the tail-length table's gene keys, so the join by gene identifier would fail silently

skills.description: Use when determining which Pfam domain families have ≥2 homologous domain instances across the human proteome, or when computing the fraction of proteome positions covered by annotated homologous domains.
skills.name: proteome-domain-position-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: proteome-domain-position-coverage-quantification Use when determining which Pfam domain families have ≥2 homologous domain instances across the human proteome, or when computing the fraction of proteome positions covered by annotated homologous domains. When haplotype context or protein-protein interaction information must be preserved — the article notes that aggregation via meta-domains loses such specific context When only one homologous domain instance exists for a Pfam family — single-instance families are not suitable for meta-domain construction When the input is raw variant data (VCF) rather than a populated mapping database; domain-position coverage cannot be computed without the mapping-database annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies how much of a proteome's protein positions fall inside annotated homologous domains and identifies Pfam families with two or more homologous domain occurrences as candidates for meta-domain construction, as done in MetaDome (3,334 meta-domains covering 43.6% of mapping-database positions). genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Quantifies how much of a proteome's protein positions fall inside annotated homologous domains and identifies Pfam families with two or more homologous domain occurrences as candidates for meta-domain construction, as done in MetaDome (3,334 meta-domains covering 43.6% of mapping-database positions).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When haplotype context or protein-protein interaction information must be preserved — the article notes that aggregation via meta-domains loses such specific context When only one homologous domain instance exists for a Pfam family — single-instance families are not suitable for meta-domain construction When the input is raw variant data (VCF) rather than a populated mapping database; domain-position coverage cannot be computed without the mapping-database annotations

skills.description: Use when you need a ground-truth-based accuracy comparison of two or more genome assemblies (original vs polished variants) and lack sequencing reads, by simulating long reads from a trusted reference such as CHM13 T2T.
skills.name: pseudo-read-fragmentation-from-reference-genome
skills.search_text: pseudo-read-fragmentation-from-reference-genome Use when you need a ground-truth-based accuracy comparison of two or more genome assemblies (original vs polished variants) and lack sequencing reads, by simulating long reads from a trusted reference such as CHM13 T2T. You have real sequencing reads (e.g. PacBio HiFi) or short reads available — use k-mer-based QV evaluation (Merqury/yak) instead of simulated pseudo-reads The reference itself is unverified — error correction performance estimates will only be as good as the ground-truth assembly Assemblies are from a different species/individual than the reference, since divergent haplotypes will masquerade as low alignment identity http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Fragments a trusted reference genome (e.g. the corrected CHM13 T2T assembly) into fixed-size pseudo-long reads (6250 reads × 500 kb) so the reference can be aligned back against candidate polished assemblies to measure alignment-identity-based consensus accuracy (QV). genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Fragments a trusted reference genome (e.g. the corrected CHM13 T2T assembly) into fixed-size pseudo-long reads (6250 reads × 500 kb) so the reference can be aligned back against candidate polished assemblies to measure alignment-identity-based consensus accuracy (QV).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have real sequencing reads (e.g. PacBio HiFi) or short reads available — use k-mer-based QV evaluation (Merqury/yak) instead of simulated pseudo-reads The reference itself is unverified — error correction performance estimates will only be as good as the ground-truth assembly Assemblies are from a different species/individual than the reference, since divergent haplotypes will masquerade as low alignment identity

skills.description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Tasic SMART-seq, 1727 mouse primary visual cortex cells) must be collapsed into per-cell-type expression profiles before testing which genes are up-regulated in each reference cell type.
skills.name: pseudobulk-aggregation-by-cell-label
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-aggregation-by-cell-label Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Tasic SMART-seq, 1727 mouse primary visual cortex cells) must be collapsed into per-cell-type expression profiles before testing which genes are up-regulated in each reference cell type. The reference dataset has no cell type labels, so profiles cannot be aggregated per type (use the atlas-only scMAGIC_atlas mode instead) The analysis requires single-cell resolution expression (e.g. direct expression profile correlation of individual query cells), where aggregation would erase per-cell information Input is already bulk RNA-seq or already pseudo-bulk reference data — no aggregation step is needed before limma http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Aggregates a single-cell count matrix by known cell type labels into pseudo-bulk profiles per reference cell type, reducing sparsity so downstream differential-expression testing (limma) can identify cell type-specific marker genes, as done in scMAGIC's first-round marker-gene module. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Aggregates a single-cell count matrix by known cell type labels into pseudo-bulk profiles per reference cell type, reducing sparsity so downstream differential-expression testing (limma) can identify cell type-specific marker genes, as done in scMAGIC's first-round marker-gene module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference dataset has no cell type labels, so profiles cannot be aggregated per type (use the atlas-only scMAGIC_atlas mode instead) The analysis requires single-cell resolution expression (e.g. direct expression profile correlation of individual query cells), where aggregation would erase per-cell information Input is already bulk RNA-seq or already pseudo-bulk reference data — no aggregation step is needed before limma

skills.description: Use when long-read single-cell (10x nanopore or PacBio) counts must be converted into per-cell-type pseudobulk gene and isoform count tables for cross-sample comparison, given per-cell counts and cell-type annotations.
skills.name: pseudobulk-count-aggregation-per-cell-type
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-count-aggregation-per-cell-type Use when long-read single-cell (10x nanopore or PacBio) counts must be converted into per-cell-type pseudobulk gene and isoform count tables for cross-sample comparison, given per-cell counts and cell-type annotations. No cell-specific markersets are available (-cellmarkerfile not given): scsorter will not be used to determine celltypes and pseudobulk files will not be made Input is already bulk or pseudobulk count data — no per-cell barcode-level counts exist to aggregate Cells have not passed emptydrops filtering (is_cell flag) — only emptydrops-approved cells should enter the pseudobulk tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregates scywalker per-cell gene and isoform counts into pseudobulk (per cell-type) gene and isoform count tables for each sample, enabling cell-type-specific and cross-sample comparison of isoform expression, including novel isoforms. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Aggregates scywalker per-cell gene and isoform counts into pseudobulk (per cell-type) gene and isoform count tables for each sample, enabling cell-type-specific and cross-sample comparison of isoform expression, including novel isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-specific markersets are available (-cellmarkerfile not given): scsorter will not be used to determine celltypes and pseudobulk files will not be made Input is already bulk or pseudobulk count data — no per-cell barcode-level counts exist to aggregate Cells have not passed emptydrops filtering (is_cell flag) — only emptydrops-approved cells should enter the pseudobulk tables

skills.description: Use when long-read (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) 10x single-cell FASTQs must be converted into per-cell-type pseudobulk isoform counts, e.g. to compare neuronal vs glial groups or feed DRIMSeq/stageR DTU testing.
skills.name: pseudobulk-isoform-count-analysis
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-isoform-count-analysis Use when long-read (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) 10x single-cell FASTQs must be converted into per-cell-type pseudobulk isoform counts, e.g. to compare neuronal vs glial groups or feed DRIMSeq/stageR DTU testing. No cell-specific markerset is available (scsorter will not run, so no cell types or pseudobulk files are generated) — only per-cell/bulk counts are produced Data are short-read single-cell rather than full-length long-read cDNA (scywalker targets 10x Oxford Nanopore and PacBio long-read data) Only empty-drop rejected barcodes/noise cells are of interest — the _filtered files exclude cells not approved by emptydrops http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate per-cell-type (pseudobulk) isoform and gene count matrices from long-read single-cell data with scywalker, by supplying cell-specific markersets so scsorter/sctype assign cell types, then aggregate per-cell isoform counts (weighed, unique, or strict) into per-group counts for cross-sample comparison and downstream DTU testing. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Generate per-cell-type (pseudobulk) isoform and gene count matrices from long-read single-cell data with scywalker, by supplying cell-specific markersets so scsorter/sctype assign cell types, then aggregate per-cell isoform counts (weighed, unique, or strict) into per-group counts for cross-sample comparison and downstream DTU testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-specific markerset is available (scsorter will not run, so no cell types or pseudobulk files are generated) — only per-cell/bulk counts are produced Data are short-read single-cell rather than full-length long-read cDNA (scywalker targets 10x Oxford Nanopore and PacBio long-read data) Only empty-drop rejected barcodes/noise cells are of interest — the _filtered files exclude cells not approved by emptydrops

skills.description: Use when you have an IsoTools Transcriptome object built from PacBio LRTS bam files and need per-condition PSI values for a specific alternative splicing event (e.g., FN1 exon 32 EDA or SLC39A14 exon 4A/4B) in defined sample groups.
skills.name: psi-computation-from-transcript-support-counts
skills.search_text: psi-computation-from-transcript-support-counts Use when you have an IsoTools Transcriptome object built from PacBio LRTS bam files and need per-condition PSI values for a specific alternative splicing event (e.g., FN1 exon 32 EDA or SLC39A14 exon 4A/4B) in defined sample groups. Input genotypes have not been filtered and curated — calls must already have passed consensus identification (SURVIVOR), filtering (at least two callers, breakpoints not in low-complexity regions or annotated LTRs) and manual inspection; this skill is not an SV-calling skill SVs have minor allele counts <5 (only 68 of 113 curated SVs qualified); very rare SVs cannot be tested with this mixed-model design The question is estimating narrow-sense heritability of traits rather than testing individual SV–trait associations http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Estimates the additive effect of structural variations (SVs) on quantitative traits by running mixed-model GWAS in LDAK across an S. pombe strain panel, with trait-specific significance set by permutation. Quantifies how much SVs contribute to trait variance beyond SNPs and indels. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Estimates the additive effect of structural variations (SVs) on quantitative traits by running mixed-model GWAS in LDAK across an S. pombe strain panel, with trait-specific significance set by permutation. Quantifies how much SVs contribute to trait variance beyond SNPs and indels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genotypes have not been filtered and curated — calls must already have passed consensus identification (SURVIVOR), filtering (at least two callers, breakpoints not in low-complexity regions or annotated LTRs) and manual inspection; this skill is not an SV-calling skill SVs have minor allele counts <5 (only 68 of 113 curated SVs qualified); very rare SVs cannot be tested with this mixed-model design The question is estimating narrow-sense heritability of traits rather than testing individual SV–trait associations

skills.description: Use when reimplementing, testing, or validating RawHash2-style adaptive quantization of raw nanopore signals (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5), or when verifying that quantized-value buckets are dynamically sized from the normalized signal distribution rather than fixed-width.
skills.name: quantization-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: quantization-distribution-analysis Use when reimplementing, testing, or validating RawHash2-style adaptive quantization of raw nanopore signals (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5), or when verifying that quantized-value buckets are dynamically sized from the normalized signal distribution rather than fixed-width. The goal is uniform fixed-width quantization (RawHash-style); this skill specifically validates the adaptive, distribution-dependent bucket layout, and a uniform layout fails the check Input signals are already sequenced basecalls or basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than raw current-level signal data The task concerns later RawHash2 stages (hash-based seeding, chaining, DTW signal alignment) rather than the quantization step itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Reconstructs and validates RawHash2's adaptive quantization of normalized nanopore signal values, where bucket sizes are dynamically arranged from the normalized signal distribution (fine range bounded by fmin/fmax with resolution fr, coarser buckets outside it with cr=(1−fr)×0.5, per Equation 1). This quantization underpins hash-based seeding and drove RawHash2's accuracy and performance gains over RawHash. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Reconstructs and validates RawHash2's adaptive quantization of normalized nanopore signal values, where bucket sizes are dynamically arranged from the normalized signal distribution (fine range bounded by fmin/fmax with resolution fr, coarser buckets outside it with cr=(1−fr)×0.5, per Equation 1). This quantization underpins hash-based seeding and drove RawHash2's accuracy and performance gains over RawHash.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is uniform fixed-width quantization (RawHash-style); this skill specifically validates the adaptive, distribution-dependent bucket layout, and a uniform layout fails the check Input signals are already sequenced basecalls or basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than raw current-level signal data The task concerns later RawHash2 stages (hash-based seeding, chaining, DTW signal alignment) rather than the quantization step itself

skills.description: Use when a detector cascade forks one quantum path into two parallel branches (gain/blur stages on each) that are summed downstream, and the combined NPS must include cross-terms W_ab between branches per Equation 6.
skills.name: quantum-fork-cross-spectral-term-calculation
skills.search_text: quantum-fork-cross-spectral-term-calculation Use when a detector cascade forks one quantum path into two parallel branches (gain/blur stages on each) that are summed downstream, and the combined NPS must include cross-terms W_ab between branches per Equation 6. The cascade is purely serial (no fork and recombination), so there are no branch-pair cross-spectral terms to compute — a single chain of process blocks suffices Signal and noise must be propagated on a per-energy-bin basis, or the detector is photon-counting with adaptive binning — CASYMIR does not propagate per energy bin and does not include photon-counting processes The target physics is dominated by depth-dependent effects such as the Lubberts effect or optical Swank noise, which CASYMIR does not account for http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Computes the pairwise cross-spectral noise terms that arise when CASYMIR parallel cascade branches (e.g., a quantum fork splitting scintillator-transmitted quanta into a Kim photodiode-conversion path alongside the standard scintillation path) are recombined at a summation point, so that the NNPS of the combined Signal is physically correct. genomics/v1 10.1002/mp.18079
skills.summary: Computes the pairwise cross-spectral noise terms that arise when CASYMIR parallel cascade branches (e.g., a quantum fork splitting scintillator-transmitted quanta into a Kim photodiode-conversion path alongside the standard scintillation path) are recombined at a summation point, so that the NNPS of the combined Signal is physically correct.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cascade is purely serial (no fork and recombination), so there are no branch-pair cross-spectral terms to compute — a single chain of process blocks suffices Signal and noise must be propagated on a per-energy-bin basis, or the detector is photon-counting with adaptive binning — CASYMIR does not propagate per energy bin and does not include photon-counting processes The target physics is dominated by depth-dependent effects such as the Lubberts effect or optical Swank noise, which CASYMIR does not account for

Typhi H58). genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515

skills.search_text: r-package-data-processing Use when working with PacBio lrCaptureSeq-derived full-length isoform catalogs (transcript, abundance, GFF, ORF files) that need compilation into a structured R database, filtering, or downstream isoform-level analysis in R. Input data is short-read RNA-seq reads (<200 bp) rather than full-length isoform sequences — such reads cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcripts The goal is de novo isoform discovery without targeted CaptureSeq pull-down data; IsoPops processes curated isoform catalogs rather than raw PacBio subreads A simple one-off script would suffice and no isoform-specific database filtering, k-mer analysis, or Lorenz-style visualization is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Process and analyze long-read mRNA isoform datasets using the IsoPops R package: compile raw isoform databases from transcript, abundance, GFF, and ORF files; filter by exon count, abundance, and truncation; and support downstream visualization/analysis with tidyverse packages. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7

skills.description: Use when a paper claims an R package or script outperforms a manual workflow in time, and you must reproduce the runtime claim on the paper's own reference inputs (e.g. plastid genomes AB086179 or AY178864.1).
skills.name: r-package-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: r-package-runtime-benchmarking Use when a paper claims an R package or script outperforms a manual workflow in time, and you must reproduce the runtime claim on the paper's own reference inputs (e.g. plastid genomes AB086179 or AY178864.1). The goal is to predict the full set of RNA editing sites from RNA-Seq data — ReFernment is explicitly not intended to predict every RNA editing site like RNA-Seq-based packages. The GFF3 input was created in Sequin — ReFernment has a known error producing no annotations for Sequin files, so any timing would be meaningless (files exported from Geneious still work). You want a runtime comparison across many plastomes in one call — ReFernment can take several minutes for a large number of plastomes, so the per-genome sub-minute criterion does not apply to that aggregate run. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of an R scientific package on a defined reference input to quantify speedup over a manual alternative. Here, ReFernment's full RNA-editing annotation of a fern or hornwort plastid genome is timed and must complete in under 60 seconds versus hours of manual annotation. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.1216
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of an R scientific package on a defined reference input to quantify speedup over a manual alternative. Here, ReFernment's full RNA-editing annotation of a fern or hornwort plastid genome is timed and must complete in under 60 seconds versus hours of manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to predict the full set of RNA editing sites from RNA-Seq data — ReFernment is explicitly not intended to predict every RNA editing site like RNA-Seq-based packages. The GFF3 input was created in Sequin — ReFernment has a known error producing no annotations for Sequin files, so any timing would be meaningless (files exported from Geneious still work). You want a runtime comparison across many plastomes in one call — ReFernment can take several minutes for a large number of plastomes, so the per-genome sub-minute criterion does not apply to that aggregate run.

skills.description: Use when read-level PAIso-seq poly(A) tail lengths with isoform assignments need per-group summaries, t-tests of tail-length differences between isoforms (e.g., Ccnb1 APA1/APA2/APA3, Wee2, Tcl1), or R/Bioconductor enrichment analyses.
skills.name: r-statistical-scripting
skills.search_text: r-statistical-scripting Use when read-level PAIso-seq poly(A) tail lengths with isoform assignments need per-group summaries, t-tests of tail-length differences between isoforms (e.g., Ccnb1 APA1/APA2/APA3, Wee2, Tcl1), or R/Bioconductor enrichment analyses. Reads have not passed the PAIso-seq QC filters (pass number <10, tail <15 nt or <5 continuous adenosines, non-A residues >=50% or >=20) — statistics on unfiltered tails will be biased Reads cannot be unambiguously assigned to a single gene/isoform (CCSs assigned to multiple genes or ambiguous sample assignment are discarded upstream) The goal is poly(A) site detection or alignment itself — that is handled upstream by minimap2/GMAP and the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py), not the R statistical layer http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 R-based statistical analysis and scripting layer of the PAIso-seq pipeline (R 3.5.1 in the GV_oocyte_PAIsoSeqAnalysis repo), used to compute per-isoform poly(A) tail-length summaries, apply Student's t-tests between isoforms (e.g., Ccnb1 APA1/APA2 vs APA3, p=0.0067; Wee2 APA isoforms, p=3.9e-12; Tcl1 splice isoforms a/b/c/e, p=0.038 and p=0.014), and run R/Bioconductor enrichment via clusterProfiler. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: R-based statistical analysis and scripting layer of the PAIso-seq pipeline (R 3.5.1 in the GV_oocyte_PAIsoSeqAnalysis repo), used to compute per-isoform poly(A) tail-length summaries, apply Student's t-tests between isoforms (e.g., Ccnb1 APA1/APA2 vs APA3, p=0.0067; Wee2 APA isoforms, p=3.9e-12; Tcl1 splice isoforms a/b/c/e, p=0.038 and p=0.014), and run R/Bioconductor enrichment via clusterProfiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not passed the PAIso-seq QC filters (pass number <10, tail <15 nt or <5 continuous adenosines, non-A residues >=50% or >=20) — statistics on unfiltered tails will be biased Reads cannot be unambiguously assigned to a single gene/isoform (CCSs assigned to multiple genes or ambiguous sample assignment are discarded upstream) The goal is poly(A) site detection or alignment itself — that is handled upstream by minimap2/GMAP and the TAPIS pipeline (run_tapis.py), not the R statistical layer

skills.name: r10-flowcell-preset-selection
skills.search_text: r10-flowcell-preset-selection Use when input raw signals come from an R10.4/R10.4.1 Oxford Nanopore flow cell (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5) and must be mapped with RawHash2, or when comparing R10.4 versus R9.4 mapping accuracy. Input signals are legacy r9.4.1 data — use the standard R9.4 Sigmap segmentation parameters/preset instead; UNCALLED itself only supports legacy r9.4.1 data The goal is reference-free all-vs-all overlap detection between raw signals — use the Rawsamble mechanism rather than the reference-guided R10.4 mapping preset A base-level read mapper on basecalled FASTQ/POD5 basecalls is sufficient — minimap2 on sequences, not RawHash2 on raw signals, is the right tool Select the correct RawHash2 k-mer model and mapping preset when mapping raw nanopore signals from the newer R10.4 flow cell, using the UNCALLED4 R10.4.1 k-mer model for indexing and the --r10 flag plus a genome-size preset for mapping, because R10.4 signals require different segmentation/scoring parameters than legacy R9.4 data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478

skills.description: Use when you have an assembled Nanopore long-amplicon consensus (e.g. an rDNA consensus built with Allele Wrangler from MiniBar-demultiplexed MinION reads) and need to lower its residual error rate against an Illumina reference.
skills.name: racon-read-error-correction
skills.search_text: racon-read-error-correction Use when you have an assembled Nanopore long-amplicon consensus (e.g. an rDNA consensus built with Allele Wrangler from MiniBar-demultiplexed MinION reads) and need to lower its residual error rate against an Illumina reference. The input is already an Illumina short-read consensus (reference quality) rather than a noisy Nanopore draft consensus — polishing targets raw-read errors in long-amplicon ONT data Only raw MinION reads are available with no assembled draft consensus — Racon requires a pre-assembled consensus to correct The goal is bulk-sample metabarcoding abundance analysis — the article states further research into the observed bias is required before long rDNA amplicon sequencing can be used reliably for bulk samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Polishes per-specimen Nanopore rDNA consensus sequences with Racon to reduce residual raw-read errors before comparing them against Illumina-based consensus references, as in the Peperomia long-amplicon MinION barcoding workflow. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz006
skills.summary: Polishes per-specimen Nanopore rDNA consensus sequences with Racon to reduce residual raw-read errors before comparing them against Illumina-based consensus references, as in the Peperomia long-amplicon MinION barcoding workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an Illumina short-read consensus (reference quality) rather than a noisy Nanopore draft consensus — polishing targets raw-read errors in long-amplicon ONT data Only raw MinION reads are available with no assembled draft consensus — Racon requires a pre-assembled consensus to correct The goal is bulk-sample metabarcoding abundance analysis — the article states further research into the observed bias is required before long rDNA amplicon sequencing can be used reliably for bulk samples

skills.search_text: rad-seq-poplar-data-processing Use when starting an InDelGT run on parental RAD-seq FASTQ files of two parents of a hybrid population and you need the merged parental indel catalog (parent.cls) before genotype calling. The parental InDel catalog (parent.cls) already exists from a prior run — skip this step with the --nocatalog flag Input reads are long-read sequencing rather than paired-end RAD-seq reads mapped to a reference genome with BWA The goal is calling InDel genotypes across progeny or testing segregation — those are InDelGT steps 2 and 3, run after this catalog exists http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Generates the merged parental InDel catalog (parent.cls) by aligning two parents' RAD-seq paired-end FASTQ reads to the P. trichocarpa v4.0 reference with BWA and calling indels at parental restriction-site loci with SAMtools/BCFtools via InDelGT. This is the first of InDelGT's three steps and produced 50,532 indel sites in the Populus case study. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499

skills.when_to_use_negative: The parental InDel catalog (parent.cls) already exists from a prior run — skip this step with the --nocatalog flag Input reads are long-read sequencing rather than paired-end RAD-seq reads mapped to a reference genome with BWA The goal is calling InDel genotypes across progeny or testing segregation — those are InDelGT steps 2 and 3, run after this catalog exists

skills.description: Use when segmenting single cells from multiplexed imaging data (e.g., MIBI or multiplexed immunofluorescence tissue images such as colorectal adenoma or breast carcinoma TMA stacks) where membranes are incomplete and per-cell compartment intensities are needed.
skills.name: random-forest-cell-compartment-segmentation
skills.search_text: random-forest-cell-compartment-segmentation Use when segmenting single cells from multiplexed imaging data (e.g., MIBI or multiplexed immunofluorescence tissue images such as colorectal adenoma or breast carcinoma TMA stacks) where membranes are incomplete and per-cell compartment intensities are needed. Input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table and no image segmentation is required Images lack multiple markers or compartmental structure (e.g., single-channel images without membrane staining), where the full-marker random-forest compartment classification cannot be trained A fully automated deep-learning-only segmentation is preferred and training annotations/labels for the pixel classifier cannot be provided Train a random-forest-based pixel classifier on all markers of multiplexed tissue images to define nuclei, membranes, and other intracellular compartments, then use those compartment masks to drive MIRIAM's internal-membrane cell separation and per-compartment marker quantification. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Train a random-forest-based pixel classifier on all markers of multiplexed tissue images to define nuclei, membranes, and other intracellular compartments, then use those compartment masks to drive MIRIAM's internal-membrane cell separation and per-compartment marker quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table and no image segmentation is required Images lack multiple markers or compartmental structure (e.g., single-channel images without membrane staining), where the full-marker random-forest compartment classification cannot be trained A fully automated deep-learning-only segmentation is preferred and training annotations/labels for the pixel classifier cannot be provided

skills.search_text: random-forest-classifier-training Use when you have aligned PacBio CCS reads with kinetic tags and need a baseline supervised classifier to test whether kinetic signals discriminate two base states and to rank feature contributions. skills.summary: Trains Random Forest classifiers on PacBio kinetic features (PW and IPD) extracted from 21-mer context k-mers to discriminate Z from A bases, and exports a feature-importance matrix that quantifies which kinetic signals drive A/Z discrimination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-nucleotide Z calling on production reads — use Z-Calling's MLP base-calling module (k11-mixed-AZ model) instead of the RFC baseline Context k-mers contain adjacent A/Z bases or fewer than 10 observations in one condition, violating the one-target-base and minimum-observation filters Comparing architectures (MLP, CNN, BiLSTM, GCN) rather than establishing the RFC kinetic baseline

skills.description: Use when you have a raw NanoSV (or similar long-read) SV call set with per-call features and an independent benchmark truth set (e.g. 1KG or PB SV sites) and need a principled, stringent post-calling filter instead of hand-tuned cutoffs.
skills.name: random-forest-classifier-training
skills.search_text: random-forest-classifier-training Use when you have a raw NanoSV (or similar long-read) SV call set with per-call features and an independent benchmark truth set (e.g. 1KG or PB SV sites) and need a principled, stringent post-calling filter instead of hand-tuned cutoffs. You only need a discovery-grade call set without a precision benchmark — the paper's pipeline deliberately uses extremely stringent filtering that costs sensitivity (~75%), which is wrong for maximizing variant recovery No labeled benchmark truth set (1KG or PB SV sites) exists for your genome/sample, since the classifier is supervised and requires TP/FP labels Input reads are short reads (e.g. Illumina); NanoSV is designed for long reads from MinION/GridION/PromethION or PacBio RSII/Sequel instruments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Train a supervised random forest classifier (scikit-learn) on labeled NanoSV structural-variant calls to replace ad-hoc post-calling filtering, raising precision far above the ~54% baseline while retaining ~75% sensitivity. Calls are labeled true/false positives against 1KG and Pacific Biosciences benchmark SV sites and described by 12 NanoSV-derived features (VAF, PID, CIPOS/CIEND, plength, MAPQ, local coverage, etc.). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Train a supervised random forest classifier (scikit-learn) on labeled NanoSV structural-variant calls to replace ad-hoc post-calling filtering, raising precision far above the ~54% baseline while retaining ~75% sensitivity. Calls are labeled true/false positives against 1KG and Pacific Biosciences benchmark SV sites and described by 12 NanoSV-derived features (VAF, PID, CIPOS/CIEND, plength, MAPQ, local coverage, etc.).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a discovery-grade call set without a precision benchmark — the paper's pipeline deliberately uses extremely stringent filtering that costs sensitivity (~75%), which is wrong for maximizing variant recovery No labeled benchmark truth set (1KG or PB SV sites) exists for your genome/sample, since the classifier is supervised and requires TP/FP labels Input reads are short reads (e.g. Illumina); NanoSV is designed for long reads from MinION/GridION/PromethION or PacBio RSII/Sequel instruments

skills.description: Use when you have per-read methylation score files (ID/Chr/Pos/Strand/Score columns) from two or more nanopore CpG methylation tools run on the same reads, and need a consensus per-read methylation probability more accurate than either tool alone.
skills.name: random-forest-consensus-model-training
skills.search_text: random-forest-consensus-model-training Use when you have per-read methylation score files (ID/Chr/Pos/Strand/Score columns) from two or more nanopore CpG methylation tools run on the same reads, and need a consensus per-read methylation probability more accurate than either tool alone. You only have per-read scores from a single methylation tool — the consensus model requires outputs from two or more tools to ameliorate individual method deficiencies Your goal is per-site methylation frequency directly from one tool's output (e.g. Megalodon alone already gave the best single-tool performance); the consensus adds substantial compute (DeepSignal + Megalodon require GPUs for efficiency) Your training and evaluation data come from the same controlled mixture — the reported RMSE improvement must be demonstrated on an independent dataset (mixture dataset 2) http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train METEORE's random forest consensus model that combines per-read 5mC methylation predictions from multiple nanopore methylation callers (e.g. Megalodon and DeepSignal) into a single consensus score with higher accuracy than any individual tool. The optimised model uses n_estimators=10 and max_depth=3. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Train METEORE's random forest consensus model that combines per-read 5mC methylation predictions from multiple nanopore methylation callers (e.g. Megalodon and DeepSignal) into a single consensus score with higher accuracy than any individual tool. The optimised model uses n_estimators=10 and max_depth=3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have per-read scores from a single methylation tool — the consensus model requires outputs from two or more tools to ameliorate individual method deficiencies Your goal is per-site methylation frequency directly from one tool's output (e.g. Megalodon alone already gave the best single-tool performance); the consensus adds substantial compute (DeepSignal + Megalodon require GPUs for efficiency) Your training and evaluation data come from the same controlled mixture — the reported RMSE improvement must be demonstrated on an independent dataset (mixture dataset 2)

skills.search_text: random-forest-pixel-classification Use when segmenting cells from multiplexed imaging data (e.g., multiplexed immunofluorescence colorectal adenoma images or MIBI breast carcinoma images) and you need pixel-level classification of cellular compartments to seed membrane-based resegmentation. When nuclei-only inputs are available and no membrane markers were imaged — the article shows omitting membrane markers plus DAPI markedly decreased similarity to annotated cell borders. When a deep-learning segmentation tool such as Mesmer is preferred and training-on-annotation infrastructure is unavailable; note MIRIAM outperformed Mesmer on the manually annotated colorectal adenoma data but Mesmer requires no per-project classifier training. skills.summary: Random forest-based machine learning pixel classification (trained in Ilastik) that defines intracellular compartments — nucleus, membrane, and cytoplasm — from multiplexed immunofluorescence tissue images, providing the input to MIRIAM's membrane-based cell segmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When nuclei-only inputs are available and no membrane markers were imaged — the article shows omitting membrane markers plus DAPI markedly decreased similarity to annotated cell borders. skills.description: Use when a raw genome-wide NanoSV VCF call set from MinION nanopore reads must be reduced to a high-confidence SV set, and a repeat filter has already (or will) produced the intermediate filtered call set the classifier is trained to score.
skills.name: random-forest-variant-classification
skills.search_text: random-forest-variant-classification Use when a raw genome-wide NanoSV VCF call set from MinION nanopore reads must be reduced to a high-confidence SV set, and a repeat filter has already (or will) produced the intermediate filtered call set the classifier is trained to score. The input is a raw NanoSV call set that has not yet passed the homopolymer/simple-repeat filter — the random forest is the second stage of the cascade and expects repeat-filtered records The data are short-read (Illumina) variant calls — the classifier was trained on NA12878 nanopore SV features and NanoSV's split-read/gapped-alignment statistics, not short-read evidence Maximum sensitivity is the priority rather than precision — this filter is explicitly stringent and drops an estimated ~25% of true SVs http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Second-stage post-calling filter for NanoSV structural variant calls: after homopolymer/simple-repeat filtering, each remaining SV is scored by an ancillary random forest classifier trained on the NA12878 nanopore genome, and only SVs passing the classifier probability threshold (set via NanoSV's config.ini) are retained as high-confidence calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Second-stage post-calling filter for NanoSV structural variant calls: after homopolymer/simple-repeat filtering, each remaining SV is scored by an ancillary random forest classifier trained on the NA12878 nanopore genome, and only SVs passing the classifier probability threshold (set via NanoSV's config.ini) are retained as high-confidence calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw NanoSV call set that has not yet passed the homopolymer/simple-repeat filter — the random forest is the second stage of the cascade and expects repeat-filtered records The data are short-read (Illumina) variant calls — the classifier was trained on NA12878 nanopore SV features and NanoSV's split-read/gapped-alignment statistics, not short-read evidence Maximum sensitivity is the priority rather than precision — this filter is explicitly stringent and drops an estimated ~25% of true SVs

skills.description: Use when testing whether a set of circular RNA BSJs (or any splice-site pairs) is enriched for a genomic feature (e.g. inverted Alu repeats) and you need a matched non-BSJ control set sampled from the same annotation.
skills.name: random-splice-site-control-sampling
skills.search_text: random-splice-site-control-sampling Use when testing whether a set of circular RNA BSJs (or any splice-site pairs) is enriched for a genomic feature (e.g. inverted Alu repeats) and you need a matched non-BSJ control set sampled from the same annotation. The goal is reconstructing full-length circRNA isoform sequences rather than testing genomic-feature enrichment of BSJs No gene annotation or RepeatMasker Alu BED is available for the reference genome, so matched control sampling or the window scan cannot be performed The hypothesis concerns Alu orientation effects in a specific locus rather than genome-wide enrichment, where a global sampling control is underpowered or mis-specified http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a matched negative-control set of splice-site pairs by randomly sampling 10,000 non-BSJ splice-site pairs from the same gene annotation, then applies the identical flanking-intron Alu window scan used for isoCirc-derived known and novel back-splice junctions (BSJs), enabling Fisher's exact tests of inverted-Alu enrichment with a two-sided design. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Builds a matched negative-control set of splice-site pairs by randomly sampling 10,000 non-BSJ splice-site pairs from the same gene annotation, then applies the identical flanking-intron Alu window scan used for isoCirc-derived known and novel back-splice junctions (BSJs), enabling Fisher's exact tests of inverted-Alu enrichment with a two-sided design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is reconstructing full-length circRNA isoform sequences rather than testing genomic-feature enrichment of BSJs No gene annotation or RepeatMasker Alu BED is available for the reference genome, so matched control sampling or the window scan cannot be performed The hypothesis concerns Alu orientation effects in a specific locus rather than genome-wide enrichment, where a global sampling control is underpowered or mis-specified

skills.description: Use when reproducing the VIBE benchmark (305 patient cases / 308 causal genes) or any gene-prioritization benchmark where the causal gene may be missing from tool output and its rank must be randomly assigned, requiring outlier-robust per-case rank aggregation.
skills.name: rank-stabilization-median-permutation
skills.search_text: rank-stabilization-median-permutation Use when reproducing the VIBE benchmark (305 patient cases / 308 causal genes) or any gene-prioritization benchmark where the causal gene may be missing from tool output and its rank must be randomly assigned, requiring outlier-robust per-case rank aggregation. When the causal gene is always present in every tool's returned list, so no random-rank assignment (and hence no permutation stabilization) is needed When analyzing the VIBE tool's actual runtime behavior rather than reproducing the benchmark figures — use the standard VIBE workflow with the HDT database and HPO.owl instead A benchmark post-processing technique from the VIBE paper that stabilizes a tool's causal-gene rank by taking the median rank over 25 permutations, compensating for outliers introduced when genes absent from a tool's output must be assigned a random rank positioned after the returned genes. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: A benchmark post-processing technique from the VIBE paper that stabilizes a tool's causal-gene rank by taking the median rank over 25 permutations, compensating for outliers introduced when genes absent from a tool's output must be assigned a random rank positioned after the returned genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the causal gene is always present in every tool's returned list, so no random-rank assignment (and hence no permutation stabilization) is needed When analyzing the VIBE tool's actual runtime behavior rather than reproducing the benchmark figures — use the standard VIBE workflow with the HDT database and HPO.owl instead

skills.search_text: ranked-gene-list-parsing Use when you have ranked gene lists from a prioritization tool (tab-delimited, ordered by score) and need to quantify over-representation of specific genes (e.g. MECP2, KMT2D) at top ranks across many cases. skills.when_to_use_negative: The tool output is not ranked (e.g. unsorted candidate gene sets) — top-N position counting requires a defined ordering such as descending highest GDA score You need per-case rank-of-causal-gene statistics (rank distributions, recall curves) rather than aggregate occurrence counts of specific genes Ontology traversal was enabled (e.g. -n children/distance options), so counts would not reproduce the paper's default-settings over-representation values

skills.search_text: raw-fast5-signal-processing Use when you have ONT direct RNA raw FAST5 files and need signal-level re-alignment (resquiggling) of current intensities to a reference transcriptome to detect m6A sites, e.g., to benchmark against a base-called-feature method like EpiNano. Your analysis plan is the EpiNano strategy, which explicitly identifies RNA modifications from base-called features 'without the need of squiggling realignments or manipulation of raw current intensity data sets' Your data is not ONT direct RNA raw signal data (e.g., you already have FASTQ-only base-called feature tables and no FAST5 signal) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Process ONT direct RNA raw FAST5 files by base-calling them and re-squiggling each read's raw current-intensity signal against an expected signal derived from basecalls and a reference transcriptome (as done with Tombo on yeast WT/ime4Δ data), providing a signal-level baseline for detecting RNA modifications. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
