skills.description: Use when building or reimplementing the signal-representation step of RawHash2/Rawsamble: normalized raw nanopore signal values (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5) must be assigned to quantized buckets before hash-based seeding, and bucket sizes should follow the signal's normalized distribution.
skills.name: raw-signal-adaptive-quantization
skills.search_text: raw-signal-adaptive-quantization Use when building or reimplementing the signal-representation step of RawHash2/Rawsamble: normalized raw nanopore signal values (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5) must be assigned to quantized buckets before hash-based seeding, and bucket sizes should follow the signal's normalized distribution. Input signals are basecalled sequences (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than raw electrical current values — quantization operates on raw signals. A uniform (fixed-width) bucket layout is required, since the validation explicitly rejects uniform layouts as inconsistent with RawHash2's adaptive mechanism. Signal values have not been normalized first — Equation (1) operates on normalized values using R9.4 segmentation parameters. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Implements RawHash2's adaptive quantization, which maps normalized nanopore signal values to quantized buckets using a bifurcated fine/coarse range scheme (fine range bounded by fmin/fmax at resolution fr, coarse buckets sized by cr=(1−fr)×0.5), so denser signal regions receive finer buckets. This improves hashing accuracy and throughput over RawHash's fixed quantization. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Implements RawHash2's adaptive quantization, which maps normalized nanopore signal values to quantized buckets using a bifurcated fine/coarse range scheme (fine range bounded by fmin/fmax at resolution fr, coarse buckets sized by cr=(1−fr)×0.5), so denser signal regions receive finer buckets. This improves hashing accuracy and throughput over RawHash's fixed quantization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input signals are basecalled sequences (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than raw electrical current values — quantization operates on raw signals. A uniform (fixed-width) bucket layout is required, since the validation explicitly rejects uniform layouts as inconsistent with RawHash2's adaptive mechanism. Signal values have not been normalized first — Equation (1) operates on normalized values using R9.4 segmentation parameters.

skills.search_text: raw-signal-file-format-conversion Decision support for choosing or converting a raw nanopore signal storage format (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5/BLOW5) when mapping raw signals with RawHash/RawHash2 and read- or file-reading overhead dominates total run time. skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about mapping accuracy (F1) or algorithmic seeding/quantization performance rather than file-reading/compression overhead — use the RawHash2 accuracy or throughput benchmarks instead The signal files are in a format RawHash does not support; RawHash reads FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, or BLOW5 only Reads are already basecalled sequences — use a sequence mapper such as minimap2 with map-ont, not raw-signal format benchmarking

skills.search_text: raw-signal-read-until-scoring Use when raw nanopore signal reads (BLOW5) must be mapped to expected signal levels of a reference genome in real time for selective sequencing, and only the alignment end position and normalized sDTW score are required rather than a full alignment path. skills.name: rca-copy-number-stratified-analysis
skills.search_text: rca-copy-number-stratified-analysis Use when isoCirc raw nanopore reads and TRF-called consensus sequences are available and you need to verify consensus error-rate reduction stratified by RCA copy number, or to report average copy number and read-length statistics. You need to identify high-confidence BSJs or full-length circRNA isoforms from raw data — use the full isoCirc pipeline with its stringent false-positive filtering instead of this error-rate stratification Input consensus sequences were not called from RCA-derived tandem-repeat reads (e.g. single-pass long reads without rolling circle amplification), so copy number inferred as floor(raw length / consensus length) is meaningless You want splice-aware mapping of reads to the reference genome rather than read-to-consensus alignment for error-rate computation http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantifies how consensus sequences called from isoCirc rolling-circle-amplified nanopore reads reduce error rate as a function of RCA copy number, by aligning each HEK293 raw read to its TRF-called consensus with minimap2 and binning per-base error rates (1 - identity) by inferred copy number (floor(raw length / consensus length)). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Quantifies how consensus sequences called from isoCirc rolling-circle-amplified nanopore reads reduce error rate as a function of RCA copy number, by aligning each HEK293 raw read to its TRF-called consensus with minimap2 and binning per-base error rates (1 - identity) by inferred copy number (floor(raw length / consensus length)).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to identify high-confidence BSJs or full-length circRNA isoforms from raw data — use the full isoCirc pipeline with its stringent false-positive filtering instead of this error-rate stratification Input consensus sequences were not called from RCA-derived tandem-repeat reads (e.g. single-pass long reads without rolling circle amplification), so copy number inferred as floor(raw length / consensus length) is meaningless You want splice-aware mapping of reads to the reference genome rather than read-to-consensus alignment for error-rate computation

skills.description: Use when you need to assign a copy-number genotype to a specific genomic region (e.g. 12:11396601-11436500) from an existing CNVpytor .pytor file, rather than calling CNVs genome-wide.
skills.name: rd-normalization-to-autosomal-baseline
skills.search_text: rd-normalization-to-autosomal-baseline Use when you need to assign a copy-number genotype to a specific genomic region (e.g. 12:11396601-11436500) from an existing CNVpytor .pytor file, rather than calling CNVs genome-wide. You want genome-wide CNV discovery/calling rather than genotyping a pre-specified region — use the -rd/-his/-partition/-call workflow instead. No .pytor archive with RD signal exists yet; RD must first be parsed from the BAM with cnvpytor -root file.pytor -rd file.bam. The region is on a non-autosomal contig — normalization divides by mean autosomal RD, so sex-chromosome or mitochondrial regions need a different baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Genotypes the copy number of a user-supplied genomic region in CNVpytor by computing the mean read depth within the region, dividing it by the mean autosomal read depth, and scaling by 2, with optional extended statistics (e-value, q0, pN, BAF level, homozygous/heterozygous counts, BAF P-value) and P-mask-filtered RD signal. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Genotypes the copy number of a user-supplied genomic region in CNVpytor by computing the mean read depth within the region, dividing it by the mean autosomal read depth, and scaling by 2, with optional extended statistics (e-value, q0, pN, BAF level, homozygous/heterozygous counts, BAF P-value) and P-mask-filtered RD signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want genome-wide CNV discovery/calling rather than genotyping a pre-specified region — use the -rd/-his/-partition/-call workflow instead. No .pytor archive with RD signal exists yet; RD must first be parsed from the BAM with cnvpytor -root file.pytor -rd file.bam. The region is on a non-autosomal contig — normalization divides by mean autosomal RD, so sex-chromosome or mitochondrial regions need a different baseline.

skills.description: Use when patient symptoms are encoded as HPO codes (e.g. HP:0002996, HP:0001377) and must be translated into disease/concept identifiers (CUIs) via an RDF knowledge base to enable downstream gene prioritization.
skills.name: rdf-knowledge-graph-branch-querying
skills.search_text: rdf-knowledge-graph-branch-querying Use when patient symptoms are encoded as HPO codes (e.g. HP:0002996, HP:0001377) and must be translated into disease/concept identifiers (CUIs) via an RDF knowledge base to enable downstream gene prioritization. Input phenotypes are free text rather than HPO codes — the module expects HPO IDs already normalized against a specific HPO release (v2018-03-08 in the benchmark). The analysis does not need ontology-backed phenotype-to-disease translation (e.g. variants already filtered and prioritized by other evidence types). The RDF triple store has not been built — running the branch query without the TDB constructed by Apache Jena v3.12.0 from the DisGeNET/SIO/HOOM sources will fail. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0634 Maps HPO phenotype codes to UMLS CUIs by executing a single optimized SPARQL query against an Apache Jena TDB triple store that branches into three matching paths (UMLS Metathesaurus, HOOM HPO-ORDO, and DisGeNET PDAs), then unions the returned CUIs so phenotype-to-concept coverage is maximized. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Maps HPO phenotype codes to UMLS CUIs by executing a single optimized SPARQL query against an Apache Jena TDB triple store that branches into three matching paths (UMLS Metathesaurus, HOOM HPO-ORDO, and DisGeNET PDAs), then unions the returned CUIs so phenotype-to-concept coverage is maximized.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input phenotypes are free text rather than HPO codes — the module expects HPO IDs already normalized against a specific HPO release (v2018-03-08 in the benchmark). The analysis does not need ontology-backed phenotype-to-disease translation (e.g. variants already filtered and prioritized by other evidence types). The RDF triple store has not been built — running the branch query without the TDB constructed by Apache Jena v3.12.0 from the DisGeNET/SIO/HOOM sources will fail.

skills.description: Use when patient symptoms encoded as HPO codes must be translated to UMLS CUIs and used to retrieve and rank gene-disease associations from a local RDF/SPARQL knowledge base.
skills.name: rdf-triple-store-querying
skills.search_text: rdf-triple-store-querying Use when patient symptoms encoded as HPO codes must be translated to UMLS CUIs and used to retrieve and rank gene-disease associations from a local RDF/SPARQL knowledge base. The task requires structural variant prioritization or data sources beyond SNV/indel variant-gene evidence — the article notes phenotype-gene matching embedded in variant prioritization only applies to SNVs and indels The knowledge base must be queried through an external web service — VIBE's design goal is local, offline installation precisely because external services' privacy and availability are not guaranteed No RDF/SPARQL triple store exists and building one is out of scope — this skill presumes a prebuilt Jena TDB/HDT database http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds a local RDF triple store from combined knowledge sources (DisGeNET-RDF, SIO, HOOM) and queries it with SPARQL to map patient HPO terms to CUIs and retrieve gene-disease associations, as done in VIBE for phenotype-based gene prioritization. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Builds a local RDF triple store from combined knowledge sources (DisGeNET-RDF, SIO, HOOM) and queries it with SPARQL to map patient HPO terms to CUIs and retrieve gene-disease associations, as done in VIBE for phenotype-based gene prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires structural variant prioritization or data sources beyond SNV/indel variant-gene evidence — the article notes phenotype-gene matching embedded in variant prioritization only applies to SNVs and indels The knowledge base must be queried through an external web service — VIBE's design goal is local, offline installation precisely because external services' privacy and availability are not guaranteed No RDF/SPARQL triple store exists and building one is out of scope — this skill presumes a prebuilt Jena TDB/HDT database

skills.description: Use when you have long-read sequencing data (e.g. PBSIM3-simulated PacBio RS II reads or real ONT/PacBio reads) plus a reference genome FASTA and need a sorted BAM as input for insertion/variant calling.
skills.name: read-alignment-and-bam-manipulation
skills.search_text: read-alignment-and-bam-manipulation Use when you have long-read sequencing data (e.g. PBSIM3-simulated PacBio RS II reads or real ONT/PacBio reads) plus a reference genome FASTA and need a sorted BAM as input for insertion/variant calling. Input is already an aligned, sorted, indexed BAM or CRAM — proceed directly to sTELLeR instead of re-aligning. Input is short Illumina reads, since sTELLeR and this workflow are designed and tested for long-read (PacBio/ONT) data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns long reads (PacBio or ONT) to a reference genome with minimap2 and produces a sorted, indexed BAM with samtools, yielding the caller-ready alignment file required by sTELLeR for TE insertion detection. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Aligns long reads (PacBio or ONT) to a reference genome with minimap2 and produces a sorted, indexed BAM with samtools, yielding the caller-ready alignment file required by sTELLeR for TE insertion detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned, sorted, indexed BAM or CRAM — proceed directly to sTELLeR instead of re-aligning. Input is short Illumina reads, since sTELLeR and this workflow are designed and tested for long-read (PacBio/ONT) data.

skills.description: Use when you have predicted exon sequences (e.g., from EXFI, ChopStitch, or GMAP) and a reference genome, and need to quantify how usable those exons are for downstream SNP genotyping or read recruitment analysis.
skills.name: read-alignment-mappability-assessment
skills.search_text: read-alignment-mappability-assessment Use when you have predicted exon sequences (e.g., from EXFI, ChopStitch, or GMAP) and a reference genome, and need to quantify how usable those exons are for downstream SNP genotyping or read recruitment analysis. No reference genome is available — the exon predictions themselves are reference-free (EXFI), so mappability cannot be computed; use precision/recall against an annotation instead The comparison target is exon-boundary accuracy rather than downstream usability — high mappability is more optimistic than exon precision and does not indicate correct IEB prediction Input is raw WGS reads rather than predicted exon sequences — mappability here is defined for predicted exon sequences aligned to the reference, not raw reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assesses the mappability of predicted exon sequences by aligning them to a genomic reference with BWA MEM and computing the fraction of mapped exons and the fraction with a perfect CIGAR string (all matches or small indels, no base clipping). genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Assesses the mappability of predicted exon sequences by aligning them to a genomic reference with BWA MEM and computing the fraction of mapped exons and the fraction with a perfect CIGAR string (all matches or small indels, no base clipping).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available — the exon predictions themselves are reference-free (EXFI), so mappability cannot be computed; use precision/recall against an annotation instead The comparison target is exon-boundary accuracy rather than downstream usability — high mappability is more optimistic than exon precision and does not indicate correct IEB prediction Input is raw WGS reads rather than predicted exon sequences — mappability here is defined for predicted exon sequences aligned to the reference, not raw reads

skills.description: Use when you have corrected or raw long reads (FASTA/FASTQ) and a reference genome and need quantitative correction-quality metrics such as aligned fraction, alignment identity, and read N50.
skills.name: read-alignment-statistics-computation
skills.search_text: read-alignment-statistics-computation Use when you have corrected or raw long reads (FASTA/FASTQ) and a reference genome and need quantitative correction-quality metrics such as aligned fraction, alignment identity, and read N50. When the goal is assembly-level evaluation (contig coverage of the reference, unaligned contigs) rather than per-read alignment statistics — the paper notes CONSENT's own assembly covers a smaller reference proportion and that analysis is separate. When polishing assemblies rather than correcting reads; CONSENT-polish output should be evaluated with assembly-level metrics instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Compute alignment-based quality statistics (fraction of aligned reads, alignment identity, corrected-read N50) by mapping corrected long reads back to a reference genome with minimap2, as done to validate CONSENT-corrected ONT reads against Table 5 of the paper. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Compute alignment-based quality statistics (fraction of aligned reads, alignment identity, corrected-read N50) by mapping corrected long reads back to a reference genome with minimap2, as done to validate CONSENT-corrected ONT reads against Table 5 of the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is assembly-level evaluation (contig coverage of the reference, unaligned contigs) rather than per-read alignment statistics — the paper notes CONSENT's own assembly covers a smaller reference proportion and that analysis is separate. When polishing assemblies rather than correcting reads; CONSENT-polish output should be evaluated with assembly-level metrics instead.

skills.search_text: read-alignment-subsampling-benchmarking Use when comparing runtime and memory scaling of consensus-calling or similar per-read tools across sequencing depths, by generating controlled read-count subsamples from a BAM and profiling each run. Reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. human chromosomes), where ViralConsensus memory consumption scales linearly with reference length and may be prohibitively large You need to benchmark end-to-end read preprocessing pipelines rather than comparing consensus-calling time/memory scaling A benchmarking skill that subsamples sorted/aligned amplicon reads (e.g. SARS-CoV-2) to controlled mapped-read depths and profiles wall-clock runtime and peak RSS of consensus-calling tools, as done to show ViralConsensus orders of magnitude faster and more memory-efficient than the iVar pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that subsamples sorted/aligned amplicon reads (e.g. SARS-CoV-2) to controlled mapped-read depths and profiles wall-clock runtime and peak RSS of consensus-calling tools, as done to show ViralConsensus orders of magnitude faster and more memory-efficient than the iVar pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. human chromosomes), where ViralConsensus memory consumption scales linearly with reference length and may be prohibitively large You need to benchmark end-to-end read preprocessing pipelines rather than comparing consensus-calling time/memory scaling

skills.description: Use when you have basecalled Nanopore direct RNA FASTQ reads (e.g., test.fastq from Guppy) and need them mapped to a reference transcript FASTA for downstream signal-to-sequence feature extraction.
skills.name: read-alignment-to-reference-transcriptome
skills.search_text: read-alignment-to-reference-transcriptome Use when you have basecalled Nanopore direct RNA FASTQ reads (e.g., test.fastq from Guppy) and need them mapped to a reference transcript FASTA for downstream signal-to-sequence feature extraction. Reads have not yet been basecalled — basecalling with guppy_basecaller (rna_r9.4.1_70bps_hac.cfg) must precede alignment The only available reference is a genome FASTA rather than a transcript/gene FASTA — RedNano's resquiggle and alignment steps expect the reference gene fasta, not a genome file http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Align basecalled Nanopore DRS reads to a reference transcriptome using minimap2, sort/index the BAM with samtools, and optionally convert to TSV via jvarkit sam2tsv — a prerequisite step in RedNano's preprocessing so raw signals can be re-squiggled to transcript coordinates. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae375
skills.summary: Align basecalled Nanopore DRS reads to a reference transcriptome using minimap2, sort/index the BAM with samtools, and optionally convert to TSV via jvarkit sam2tsv — a prerequisite step in RedNano's preprocessing so raw signals can be re-squiggled to transcript coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not yet been basecalled — basecalling with guppy_basecaller (rna_r9.4.1_70bps_hac.cfg) must precede alignment The only available reference is a genome FASTA rather than a transcript/gene FASTA — RedNano's resquiggle and alignment steps expect the reference gene fasta, not a genome file

skills.description: Use when long-read SAM/BAM alignments must be converted into fixed-size RGB images (100x100) encoding CIGAR deletion features, e.g., as image-modality input for a dual-attention structural-variant-calling model.
skills.name: read-alignment-to-rgb-image-encoding
skills.search_text: read-alignment-to-rgb-image-encoding Use when long-read SAM/BAM alignments must be converted into fixed-size RGB images (100x100) encoding CIGAR deletion features, e.g., as image-modality input for a dual-attention structural-variant-calling model. The goal is insertion or base substitution variant calling — the paper states it 'currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling'. Input is raw FASTQ/basecalled reads without an existing alignment (SAM/BAM) and CIGAR fields. A schema-preserving numeric feature representation is required rather than a rasterized image modality (e.g., for non-vision models). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A skill for converting quality-controlled SAM/BAM read alignments (e.g., HG002 from GIAB AshkenazimTrio) into 100x100 RGB images whose pixels encode CIGAR operation states (D, M, S, I), so that deletion-variant features are spatially mapped onto image regions for local feature perception in DASV. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: A skill for converting quality-controlled SAM/BAM read alignments (e.g., HG002 from GIAB AshkenazimTrio) into 100x100 RGB images whose pixels encode CIGAR operation states (D, M, S, I), so that deletion-variant features are spatially mapped onto image regions for local feature perception in DASV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is insertion or base substitution variant calling — the paper states it 'currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling'. Input is raw FASTQ/basecalled reads without an existing alignment (SAM/BAM) and CIGAR fields. A schema-preserving numeric feature representation is required rather than a rasterized image modality (e.g., for non-vision models).

skills.search_text: read-alignment-to-synthetic-reference Use when basecalled nanopore dRNA reads must be mapped onto synthetic RNA reference sequences (random-ligation or splint-ligation oligo constructs) before per-read m6A prediction, and mapq-filtered BAMs are required. Input is already a sorted, indexed, quality-filtered BAM from a prior alignment run Reads are raw fast5 signal files that still need RODAN basecalling before any alignment is possible The task is ensemble-level quantification against a transcriptome where ambiguous multi-mapping is acceptable rather than to be excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align RODAN-basecalled direct RNA reads to synthetic oligo reference sequences (e.g., the TEST1 heteropolymer references containing all possible random combinations of constituent oligos) with minimap2.22 under splice-aware, primary-only settings, then filter to high mapping quality with samtools so downstream m6A detection (mAFiA) operates on confidently placed reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47661-2
skills.summary: Align RODAN-basecalled direct RNA reads to synthetic oligo reference sequences (e.g., the TEST1 heteropolymer references containing all possible random combinations of constituent oligos) with minimap2.22 under splice-aware, primary-only settings, then filter to high mapping quality with samtools so downstream m6A detection (mAFiA) operates on confidently placed reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a sorted, indexed, quality-filtered BAM from a prior alignment run Reads are raw fast5 signal files that still need RODAN basecalling before any alignment is possible The task is ensemble-level quantification against a transcriptome where ambiguous multi-mapping is acceptable rather than to be excluded

skills.name: read-alignment-with-minimap2
skills.search_text: read-alignment-with-minimap2 Use when per-read accuracy, median Q-score, or per-read mismatch/insertion/deletion rates must be computed from basecalled ONT reads by mapping them to a known reference genome (e.g., HG002 chr22, bacterial genomes) or transcriptome. Input is raw POD5 signal that has not yet been basecalled — Dorado basecalling must precede alignment The analysis goal is signal-level fidelity (Dynamic Time Warping distances between simulated and real signal chunks) rather than sequence-level accuracy — alignment accuracy metrics do not capture signal fidelity The simulator output has no known reference against which per-read identity can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Align Dorado-basecalled nanopore reads (from real data or NanoSimFormer/seq2squiggle/Squigulator simulated POD5 signals) to their reference genomes or transcriptomes with minimap2, yielding the per-read alignments required to compute per-read accuracies, Q-scores, and mismatch/insertion/deletion error profiles in the simulator benchmark. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Align Dorado-basecalled nanopore reads (from real data or NanoSimFormer/seq2squiggle/Squigulator simulated POD5 signals) to their reference genomes or transcriptomes with minimap2, yielding the per-read alignments required to compute per-read accuracies, Q-scores, and mismatch/insertion/deletion error profiles in the simulator benchmark.

skills.description: Use when long reads (e.g., PacBio HiFi BAM alignments) span targeted STR/SNP/InDel loci and you need phased macrohaplotypes rather than per-locus genotypes, e.g., for forensics, polyploids, or DNA mixtures.
skills.name: read-backed-haplotype-phasing
skills.search_text: read-backed-haplotype-phasing Use when long reads (e.g., PacBio HiFi BAM alignments) span targeted STR/SNP/InDel loci and you need phased macrohaplotypes rather than per-locus genotypes, e.g., for forensics, polyploids, or DNA mixtures. Variants (private mutations) absent from the user-supplied STR/InDel/SNP configure files — the current version discards them, so the skill cannot report untargeted alleles Short-read NGS data where reads do not span multiple targeted loci, since physical read-backed phasing requires a single read to carry the co-located alleles Haplotype comparison, alignment, or allele-size conversion tasks — use USAT downstream, which consumes the macrohaplotype output rather than producing it http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 Phase targeted STR, SNP, and InDel alleles called from individual PacBio HiFi long reads into macrohaplotype strings using physical (read-backed) phasing, enabling multi-allelic haplotype detection in diploid, polyploid, and mixed DNA samples. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Phase targeted STR, SNP, and InDel alleles called from individual PacBio HiFi long reads into macrohaplotype strings using physical (read-backed) phasing, enabling multi-allelic haplotype detection in diploid, polyploid, and mixed DNA samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants (private mutations) absent from the user-supplied STR/InDel/SNP configure files — the current version discards them, so the skill cannot report untargeted alleles Short-read NGS data where reads do not span multiple targeted loci, since physical read-backed phasing requires a single read to carry the co-located alleles Haplotype comparison, alignment, or allele-size conversion tasks — use USAT downstream, which consumes the macrohaplotype output rather than producing it

skills.description: Use when you need per-variant image inputs for CNN filtering of ONT structural variants: given a consensus VCF of candidate SVs and a Chaisson et al. minimap2 BAM, build one alignment image per candidate.
skills.name: read-by-position-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: read-by-position-matrix-construction Use when you need per-variant image inputs for CNN filtering of ONT structural variants: given a consensus VCF of candidate SVs and a Chaisson et al. minimap2 BAM, build one alignment image per candidate. Input is already the consensus VCF-free output of individual SV callers without consensus coordinates — the matrix construction is anchored on per-candidate coordinates from the consensus list Sequencing data is short-read (Illumina) rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read data; the pipeline targets ONT long-read SV detection You need per-position variant statistics or genotype calls rather than image-encoded candidates for CNN filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Encodes each structural variant candidate from ConsensuSV-ONT as a raw read-by-position alignment matrix — one row per quality-passing read, one column per genomic position — which is resized with OpenCV into the fixed 50x50x3 image consumed by the CNN-based high-quality variant filter. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Encodes each structural variant candidate from ConsensuSV-ONT as a raw read-by-position alignment matrix — one row per quality-passing read, one column per genomic position — which is resized with OpenCV into the fixed 50x50x3 image consumed by the CNN-based high-quality variant filter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already the consensus VCF-free output of individual SV callers without consensus coordinates — the matrix construction is anchored on per-candidate coordinates from the consensus list Sequencing data is short-read (Illumina) rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read data; the pipeline targets ONT long-read SV detection You need per-position variant statistics or genotype calls rather than image-encoded candidates for CNN filtering

skills.description: Use when low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads must be partitioned into chromosomal bins prior to per-chromosome de novo assembly, especially when translocations cause reads to span two chromosomes and naive reference alignment would misclassify them.
skills.name: read-chromosome-classification
skills.search_text: read-chromosome-classification Use when low-coverage (~5x) PacBio HiFi reads must be partitioned into chromosomal bins prior to per-chromosome de novo assembly, especially when translocations cause reads to span two chromosomes and naive reference alignment would misclassify them. Input reads are ONT/noisy reads — HiFiCCL is designed specifically for low-coverage high-fidelity (HiFi) reads The goal is reference-based scaffolding of existing assemblies rather than partitioning raw reads for de novo assembly — RagTag scaffolding is a separate, lossier approach that may overlook true SVs Coverage is high (e.g., 41x HiFi as for HG00438 standard pipelines) — the framework targets low-coverage cost-sensitive scenarios http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns individual HiFi reads to chromosome classes in HiFiCCL, using split-alignment translocation signals (SigBND) to correctly label breakpoint-spanning reads that reference-based clustering would otherwise assign to the wrong chromosome. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Assigns individual HiFi reads to chromosome classes in HiFiCCL, using split-alignment translocation signals (SigBND) to correctly label breakpoint-spanning reads that reference-based clustering would otherwise assign to the wrong chromosome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are ONT/noisy reads — HiFiCCL is designed specifically for low-coverage high-fidelity (HiFi) reads The goal is reference-based scaffolding of existing assemblies rather than partitioning raw reads for de novo assembly — RagTag scaffolding is a separate, lossier approach that may overlook true SVs Coverage is high (e.g., 41x HiFi as for HG00438 standard pipelines) — the framework targets low-coverage cost-sensitive scenarios

skills.search_text: read-coverage-based-binning Use when benchmarking m6A detection on dRNA-seq requires restricting per-bin calls to motif-containing, exclusion-zone-free, or high-coverage bins to test whether such filters improve precision-recall performance. Input is a synthetic oligos dataset, where in vivo bin restriction (motifs, exclusion zones, coverage) is not meaningful The analysis goal is raw tool benchmarking on the unfiltered bin baseline rather than testing the effect of bin-set restrictions Bins lack read-count or sequence information, so the three flags cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Annotates fixed genome bins from dRNA-seq alignments with coverage counts and binary flags (RRACH motif presence, distance from 100-nt exon-end exclusion zones) so that m6A tool calls restricted to RRACH-containing, exclusion-zone-free, or highly expressed (>100 read counts) bins can be re-scored for precision and recall. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: Annotates fixed genome bins from dRNA-seq alignments with coverage counts and binary flags (RRACH motif presence, distance from 100-nt exon-end exclusion zones) so that m6A tool calls restricted to RRACH-containing, exclusion-zone-free, or highly expressed (>100 read counts) bins can be re-scored for precision and recall.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a synthetic oligos dataset, where in vivo bin restriction (motifs, exclusion zones, coverage) is not meaningful The analysis goal is raw tool benchmarking on the unfiltered bin baseline rather than testing the effect of bin-set restrictions Bins lack read-count or sequence information, so the three flags cannot be computed

Long-read scaffolding evaluation (PacBio/Nanopore) where the comparison target is Links-style hybrid scaffolding rather than short-read aligner coverage agreement When only final scaffold sequences are available without the underlying scaffolding graphs, since per-contig read-coverage cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes average contig read-coverage for scaffolding graphs built by short-read aligners and derives pairwise Pearson correlations against Fast-SG's coverage values, to quantify agreement between alignment-free and alignment-based graph construction. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048

skills.description: Use when planning nanopore amplicon experiments or consensus calling where you must decide how many reads per OTU are needed, e.g. to verify >99% accuracy above 5 reads and stability at >=50 reads.
skills.name: read-depth-accuracy-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: read-depth-accuracy-curve-visualization Use when planning nanopore amplicon experiments or consensus calling where you must decide how many reads per OTU are needed, e.g. to verify >99% accuracy above 5 reads and stability at >=50 reads. Your goal is mock-community diversity estimation rather than characterizing read-depth requirements for consensus accuracy. Your input is a reference-based pipeline (e.g. mapping raw reads to SILVA); the skill targets nanoClust's de novo clustering approach, which was motivated because reference-based mapping of noisy nanopore reads is unreliable. Reads are short reads (Illumina MiSeq, Ion Torrent PGM) rather than long nanopore amplicon reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Characterizes how many nanopore reads must feed consensus construction for accurate full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences by subsampling per-OTU read depth, running nanoClust de novo clustering and consensus calling at each depth, and plotting consensus accuracy (sequence identity vs a SILVA reference) as a function of read count. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Characterizes how many nanopore reads must feed consensus construction for accurate full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences by subsampling per-OTU read depth, running nanoClust de novo clustering and consensus calling at each depth, and plotting consensus accuracy (sequence identity vs a SILVA reference) as a function of read count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is mock-community diversity estimation rather than characterizing read-depth requirements for consensus accuracy. Your input is a reference-based pipeline (e.g. mapping raw reads to SILVA); the skill targets nanoClust's de novo clustering approach, which was motivated because reference-based mapping of noisy nanopore reads is unreliable. Reads are short reads (Illumina MiSeq, Ion Torrent PGM) rather than long nanopore amplicon reads.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a paired tumor/control long-read SV caller's robustness across variable sequencing yield and tumor purity, requiring a simulated truth set of somatic SVs.
skills.name: read-depth-and-purity-subsampling
skills.search_text: read-depth-and-purity-subsampling Use when evaluating a paired tumor/control long-read SV caller's robustness across variable sequencing yield and tumor purity, requiring a simulated truth set of somatic SVs. Input is real (non-simulated) tumor/control sequencing data with no truth set — precision/recall cannot be computed, so the depth/purity grid has no ground truth to score against. Evaluating germline SV calling where tumor purity sub-sampling is irrelevant to the caller's design. Short-read-based SV calling, where ONT-specific NanoSim read simulation and the sub-sampling grid do not model the platform error profile. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Benchmarking skill that stress-tests somatic SV callers by sub-sampling simulated tumor/control long-read BAM alignments to a grid of sequencing depths and tumor purities, then scoring precision/recall against a simulated truth set. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that stress-tests somatic SV callers by sub-sampling simulated tumor/control long-read BAM alignments to a grid of sequencing depths and tumor purities, then scoring precision/recall against a simulated truth set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) tumor/control sequencing data with no truth set — precision/recall cannot be computed, so the depth/purity grid has no ground truth to score against. Evaluating germline SV calling where tumor purity sub-sampling is irrelevant to the caller's design. Short-read-based SV calling, where ONT-specific NanoSim read simulation and the sub-sampling grid do not model the platform error profile.

skills.description: Use when you need a per-region copy-number estimate from WGS read depth stored in a .pytor archive, e.g. to genotype a specific interval like 12:11396601-11436500 in CNVpytor.
skills.name: read-depth-based-cnv-genotyping
skills.search_text: read-depth-based-cnv-genotyping Use when you need a per-region copy-number estimate from WGS read depth stored in a .pytor archive, e.g. to genotype a specific interval like 12:11396601-11436500 in CNVpytor. You want de novo CNV discovery across the genome — use the -rd/-his/-partition/-call workflow instead of region genotyping. No .pytor archive exists yet; RD must first be binned into the archive with -rd file.bam before genotyping. The somatic/mosaic CNA setting calling for the joint caller prototype, which the article describes as still under development rather than a genotyping substitute. http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Genotype a user-supplied genomic region with CNVpytor by computing copy number as the mean read depth within the region divided by the mean autosomal read depth, scaled by 2, optionally enriched with BAF likelihood evidence (e-value, q0, pN, maximum-likelihood BAF level) from imported SNP VCF data. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Genotype a user-supplied genomic region with CNVpytor by computing copy number as the mean read depth within the region divided by the mean autosomal read depth, scaled by 2, optionally enriched with BAF likelihood evidence (e-value, q0, pN, maximum-likelihood BAF level) from imported SNP VCF data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want de novo CNV discovery across the genome — use the -rd/-his/-partition/-call workflow instead of region genotyping. No .pytor archive exists yet; RD must first be binned into the archive with -rd file.bam before genotyping. The somatic/mosaic CNA setting calling for the joint caller prototype, which the article describes as still under development rather than a genotyping substitute.

skills.name: read-depth-benchmarking
skills.search_text: read-depth-benchmarking Use when you need to empirically validate performance claims for read-depth CNV callers by measuring parse wall-time and intermediate file sizes per sample on the same BAM inputs. The goal is CNV calling accuracy or concordance of called regions rather than parse-time and file-size benchmarking (use CNVpytor's -call workflow instead; note CNVnator and CNVpytor calls overlap by >99%) The inputs are not whole-genome alignment (BAM) files, e.g. only VCF SNP data is available — the speedup claim applies specifically to parsing alignment files You need the somatic CNA caller for cancer/mosaic CNAs, which exists only as a prototype and is not what this benchmark exercises http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarks CNVpytor against its predecessor CNVnator on read-depth parsing of whole-genome alignment files, quantifying the reported 2–20x parse speedup and 20–50x smaller intermediate (.pytor vs ROOT) file footprint on the CEPH trio example dataset. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Benchmarks CNVpytor against its predecessor CNVnator on read-depth parsing of whole-genome alignment files, quantifying the reported 2–20x parse speedup and 20–50x smaller intermediate (.pytor vs ROOT) file footprint on the CEPH trio example dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is CNV calling accuracy or concordance of called regions rather than parse-time and file-size benchmarking (use CNVpytor's -call workflow instead; note CNVnator and CNVpytor calls overlap by >99%) The inputs are not whole-genome alignment (BAM) files, e.g. only VCF SNP data is available — the speedup claim applies specifically to parsing alignment files You need the somatic CNA caller for cancer/mosaic CNAs, which exists only as a prototype and is not what this benchmark exercises

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from error-prone long-read (PacBio CLR/ONT) BAM alignments where locally elevated read depth from segmental duplications or copy-number amplification would otherwise produce false-positive variant calls.
skills.name: read-depth-coverage-filtering
skills.search_text: read-depth-coverage-filtering Use when calling SNVs from error-prone long-read (PacBio CLR/ONT) BAM alignments where locally elevated read depth from segmental duplications or copy-number amplification would otherwise produce false-positive variant calls. When genotyping a pre-specified VCF of candidate variants with -v, where the goal is joint genotyping rather than de novo candidate discovery and coverage gating may drop true amplified-region alleles When the dataset is uniformly very low coverage (below the min_cov 6 default), since the filter will eliminate nearly all candidate positions rather than correcting for amplification For structural-variant discovery (e.g., Delly CNV calling), where read depth is the signal of interest rather than a nuisance to filter out http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 A coverage-based candidate-SNV filtering strategy from Longshot: positions are considered only if read depth falls between a minimum coverage and a maximum set as d + 5*sqrt(d) (median depth d), which suppresses false SNVs arising from copy-number amplifications in PacBio/ONT long-read alignments. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: A coverage-based candidate-SNV filtering strategy from Longshot: positions are considered only if read depth falls between a minimum coverage and a maximum set as d + 5*sqrt(d) (median depth d), which suppresses false SNVs arising from copy-number amplifications in PacBio/ONT long-read alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When genotyping a pre-specified VCF of candidate variants with -v, where the goal is joint genotyping rather than de novo candidate discovery and coverage gating may drop true amplified-region alleles When the dataset is uniformly very low coverage (below the min_cov 6 default), since the filter will eliminate nearly all candidate positions rather than correcting for amplification For structural-variant discovery (e.g., Delly CNV calling), where read depth is the signal of interest rather than a nuisance to filter out

skills.description: Use when testing how far SMRT read depth can be reduced before single-molecule SMSN methylation detection (sensitivity/specificity) degrades, e.g. to probe reference-free de novo motif discovery at low coverage.
skills.name: read-depth-downsampling
skills.search_text: read-depth-downsampling Use when testing how far SMRT read depth can be reduced before single-molecule SMSN methylation detection (sensitivity/specificity) degrades, e.g. to probe reference-free de novo motif discovery at low coverage. Library prep is long (10Kb+) with single long subreads spanning many distinct motif sites — use the SMp motif-pooled protocol instead, whose reliability scales with number of distinct motif sites per subread. Goal is population-level consensus methylation calling rather than single-molecule, single-nucleotide methylation status. Modification has kinetic signatures extending into surrounding bases — beyond the scope of SMALR's current per-position approach. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Downsample native and WGA SMRT alignments (cmp.h5/BAM) to reduced genomic coverage with samtools, then run SMALR SMsn to determine the single-molecule coverage floor at which SMSN-based 6mA detection retains accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438
skills.summary: Downsample native and WGA SMRT alignments (cmp.h5/BAM) to reduced genomic coverage with samtools, then run SMALR SMsn to determine the single-molecule coverage floor at which SMSN-based 6mA detection retains accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Library prep is long (10Kb+) with single long subreads spanning many distinct motif sites — use the SMp motif-pooled protocol instead, whose reliability scales with number of distinct motif sites per subread. Goal is population-level consensus methylation calling rather than single-molecule, single-nucleotide methylation status. Modification has kinetic signatures extending into surrounding bases — beyond the scope of SMALR's current per-position approach.

skills.search_text: read-depth-gc-bias-correction Use when correcting binned read depth signal for GC-content-dependent bias during CNV/CNA discovery with CNVpytor, especially on GRCh37/GRCh38 where GC content per 100-bp bin is pre-calculated as packaged resource data. skills.when_to_use_negative: Working with a non-human reference genome for which CNVpytor does not ship a pre-calculated GC/AT per-100-bp-bin resource — the packaged-resource approach described here is specific to GRCh37 (hg19) and GRCh38 The goal is detecting CNVs from allele imbalance/B-allele frequency rather than read depth — this skill only corrects the RD signal, not SNP/BAF likelihood data

skills.description: Use when nanopore long reads (e.g. nanoHiMe-seq from HepG2) must be assigned to paternal/maternal haplotypes at feature regions such as H3K4me3 peaks, H3K27me3 peaks or CpG islands for allele-specific epigenetics.
skills.name: read-haplotagging-allele-assignment
skills.search_text: read-haplotagging-allele-assignment Use when nanopore long reads (e.g. nanoHiMe-seq from HepG2) must be assigned to paternal/maternal haplotypes at feature regions such as H3K4me3 peaks, H3K27me3 peaks or CpG islands for allele-specific epigenetics. Loci with a low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs, where phasing depends on variant density and haplotype assignment is unreliable Regions with read coverage <20, which the article excludes from allele-specific analysis Short-read data where read length does not span multiple heterozygous sites — Illumina phasing rates (5.7–16.6%) are far below nanopore rates and this skill's advantage does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Assigns individual nanopore nanoHiMe-seq reads to parental haplotypes by haplotagging heterozygous SNV/INDEL variants with Margin and phasing with WhatsHap, enabling allele-specific epigenetic analysis. Long single-molecule reads spanning multiple heterozygous sites allow far higher allele-assignment rates than short Illumina reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: Assigns individual nanopore nanoHiMe-seq reads to parental haplotypes by haplotagging heterozygous SNV/INDEL variants with Margin and phasing with WhatsHap, enabling allele-specific epigenetic analysis. Long single-molecule reads spanning multiple heterozygous sites allow far higher allele-assignment rates than short Illumina reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci with a low density of heterozygous SNVs/INDELs, where phasing depends on variant density and haplotype assignment is unreliable Regions with read coverage <20, which the article excludes from allele-specific analysis Short-read data where read length does not span multiple heterozygous sites — Illumina phasing rates (5.7–16.6%) are far below nanopore rates and this skill's advantage does not apply

skills.summary: PECAT's divide-then-combine bisecting k-means method clusters long reads into haplotype groups using SNP-allele vectors extracted from corrected reads aligned to haplotype-collapsed first-round contigs, verifying and correcting assigned SNP alleles to identify inconsistent overlaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — PECAT achieves mediocre phased-assembly performance on these high-accuracy read types Input is only raw reads without corrected reads or a first-round haplotype-collapsed assembly — the SNP-allele vectors require corrected reads aligned to collapsed contigs Genomic regions with very low heterozygosity rate — SNP calling accuracy is too low to support reliable haplotype clustering

skills.description: Use when a task requires locating or narrowing a subset of reads enumerated from POD5 nanopore files by substring search, lexicographic sorting, or intersection with a supplied list of read IDs (mirroring pod5Viewer's navigator search and File > Filter reads workflow).
skills.name: read-id-subset-intersection-filtering
skills.search_text: read-id-subset-intersection-filtering Use when a task requires locating or narrowing a subset of reads enumerated from POD5 nanopore files by substring search, lexicographic sorting, or intersection with a supplied list of read IDs (mirroring pod5Viewer's navigator search and File > Filter reads workflow). Input data is not in POD5 format (e.g. FAST5 or FASTQ) — this skill replicates pod5Viewer's POD5-specific navigator and filter behavior Filtering requires signal-level criteria (e.g. length or signal value cutoffs) rather than membership in a supplied read-ID set — pod5Viewer filtering only retains reads found in the given ID set A GUI inspection session is sufficient — opening the pod5Viewer and using `File > Filter reads...` directly is simpler than reproducing the workflow in a script http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Implements the pod5Viewer read-filtering behavior programmatically: enumerate read IDs from POD5 files with the pod5 reader library (v0.3.10), apply live-style substring search and ascending/descending lexicographic sorting, then intersect with a filter text file containing one read ID per line to retain only reads in the submitted set. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae665
skills.summary: Implements the pod5Viewer read-filtering behavior programmatically: enumerate read IDs from POD5 files with the pod5 reader library (v0.3.10), apply live-style substring search and ascending/descending lexicographic sorting, then intersect with a filter text file containing one read ID per line to retain only reads in the submitted set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not in POD5 format (e.g. FAST5 or FASTQ) — this skill replicates pod5Viewer's POD5-specific navigator and filter behavior Filtering requires signal-level criteria (e.g. length or signal value cutoffs) rather than membership in a supplied read-ID set — pod5Viewer filtering only retains reads found in the given ID set A GUI inspection session is sufficient — opening the pod5Viewer and using `File > Filter reads...` directly is simpler than reproducing the workflow in a script

skills.summary: Locates specific nanopore reads among those enumerated from POD5 files by combining live substring search over read IDs, lexicographic sorting, and set-based filtering against a submitted read-ID list, mirroring the pod5Viewer file navigator panel's search, sort, and filter functions.
