skills.description: Reference for building QC panels that assess Oxford Nanopore (or PacBio) full-length single-cell cDNA read quality: you have a minimap2_splice BAM and per-cell counts from a scywalker run and need read-length histograms plus alignment metrics in a report.
skills.name: read-length-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: read-length-distribution-analysis Reference for building QC panels that assess Oxford Nanopore (or PacBio) full-length single-cell cDNA read quality: you have a minimap2_splice BAM and per-cell counts from a scywalker run and need read-length histograms plus alignment metrics in a report. Input is short-read scRNA-seq data — the read-length vs exon-count relationship inspected here is specific to full-length long-read cDNA (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) You only need cell calling/QC (knee plot, emptydrops filtering) and not alignment/read-quality metrics — no BAM or cramino metrics required http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates read-length distribution QC plots (overall read-length histogram and read length versus number of exons per read) with cramino-derived alignment metrics, as part of scywalker's interactive HTML QC report for long-read single-cell/nuclei data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Generates read-length distribution QC plots (overall read-length histogram and read length versus number of exons per read) with cramino-derived alignment metrics, as part of scywalker's interactive HTML QC report for long-read single-cell/nuclei data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read scRNA-seq data — the read-length vs exon-count relationship inspected here is specific to full-length long-read cDNA (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) You only need cell calling/QC (knee plot, emptydrops filtering) and not alignment/read-quality metrics — no BAM or cramino metrics required

skills.description: Use when generating synthetic nanopore reads from a reference FASTA and you need realistic read-length heterogeneity rather than fixed-length reads, e.g. before seq2squiggle signal simulation.
skills.name: read-length-distribution-sampling
skills.search_text: read-length-distribution-sampling Use when generating synthetic nanopore reads from a reference FASTA and you need realistic read-length heterogeneity rather than fixed-length reads, e.g. before seq2squiggle signal simulation. Input is already a FASTA/FASTQ of pre-existing reads — use seq2squiggle's --read-input mode, which simulates one signal per input read without additional fragmentation A uniform or fixed read length is explicitly required by the downstream benchmark design The goal is basecalling or read modification rather than de novo synthetic read generation from a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Sample synthetic nanopore read lengths from one of three distributions inherited from DeepSimulator — an exponential, a beta, or a mixed (two-gamma) distribution — so that simulated reads mimic experimental ONT read-length profiles before signal simulation with seq2squiggle. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Sample synthetic nanopore read lengths from one of three distributions inherited from DeepSimulator — an exponential, a beta, or a mixed (two-gamma) distribution — so that simulated reads mimic experimental ONT read-length profiles before signal simulation with seq2squiggle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a FASTA/FASTQ of pre-existing reads — use seq2squiggle's --read-input mode, which simulates one signal per input read without additional fragmentation A uniform or fixed read length is explicitly required by the downstream benchmark design The goal is basecalling or read modification rather than de novo synthetic read generation from a reference

skills.description: Use when you have aligned PacBio CCS/HiFi BAMs and need per-read 5mCpG methylation probabilities (not just site-level frequencies), e.g. for read-level accuracy evaluation against BS-seq ground truth.
skills.name: read-level-5mcpg-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: read-level-5mcpg-methylation-calling Use when you have aligned PacBio CCS/HiFi BAMs and need per-read 5mCpG methylation probabilities (not just site-level frequencies), e.g. for read-level accuracy evaluation against BS-seq ground truth. You need hemimethylated CpG detection — the methods only consider symmetric methylation and are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs You need 5mC detection in non-CpG contexts or other DNA modifications such as 6mA — ccsmeth/primrose cannot be applied for these Input reads are nanopore reads rather than PacBio CCS/HiFi — use nanopore-specific callers (e.g. deepsignal2, Megalodon) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Detect 5mCpG methylation states at single-molecule (per-read) resolution from PacBio HiFi/CCS reads using the deep-learning tool ccsmeth, which exploits kinetics features (IPD and pulse width) and a pre-trained read-level model, and benchmark it against PacBio's CNN-based primrose caller. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Detect 5mCpG methylation states at single-molecule (per-read) resolution from PacBio HiFi/CCS reads using the deep-learning tool ccsmeth, which exploits kinetics features (IPD and pulse width) and a pre-trained read-level model, and benchmark it against PacBio's CNN-based primrose caller.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need hemimethylated CpG detection — the methods only consider symmetric methylation and are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs You need 5mC detection in non-CpG contexts or other DNA modifications such as 6mA — ccsmeth/primrose cannot be applied for these Input reads are nanopore reads rather than PacBio CCS/HiFi — use nanopore-specific callers (e.g. deepsignal2, Megalodon) instead

skills.description: Use when basecalled reads from a nanopore basecaller (e.g. Chiron FASTQ/FASTA output) need a per-read accuracy score against a reference genome, especially to compare model variants or basecallers.
skills.name: read-level-basecalling-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: read-level-basecalling-accuracy-evaluation Use when basecalled reads from a nanopore basecaller (e.g. Chiron FASTQ/FASTA output) need a per-read accuracy score against a reference genome, especially to compare model variants or basecallers. The goal is consensus/assembly quality rather than per-read basecalling accuracy — the paper evaluates read-level accuracy separately from Minimap2/Miniasm assembly with Racon polishing. The basecaller output has no reference genome to align against, so accuracy cannot be computed (e.g. truly novel de novo samples). You are benchmarking raw inference throughput (bases/second) rather than accuracy — use the decoder speed comparison path instead. Quantifies basecaller quality by aligning basecalled nanopore reads to a reference genome with graphmap (default parameters) and computing read-level accuracy, enabling side-by-side comparison of basecalling models such as full CNN+RNN+CTC Chiron versus ablated CNN-only or RNN-only variants. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: Quantifies basecaller quality by aligning basecalled nanopore reads to a reference genome with graphmap (default parameters) and computing read-level accuracy, enabling side-by-side comparison of basecalling models such as full CNN+RNN+CTC Chiron versus ablated CNN-only or RNN-only variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is consensus/assembly quality rather than per-read basecalling accuracy — the paper evaluates read-level accuracy separately from Minimap2/Miniasm assembly with Racon polishing. The basecaller output has no reference genome to align against, so accuracy cannot be computed (e.g. truly novel de novo samples). You are benchmarking raw inference throughput (bases/second) rather than accuracy — use the decoder speed comparison path instead.

skills.description: Use when per-read 5mC calls from Nanopore data (e.g., DeepSignal-plant vs Megalodon) must be validated against bisulfite sequencing across CG/CHG/CHH contexts using Pearson correlation, RMSE, and read-level accuracy.
skills.name: read-level-classification-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: read-level-classification-accuracy-assessment Use when per-read 5mC calls from Nanopore data (e.g., DeepSignal-plant vs Megalodon) must be validated against bisulfite sequencing across CG/CHG/CHH contexts using Pearson correlation, RMSE, and read-level accuracy. Only bisulfite sequencing data is available with no native Nanopore reads — there are no per-read modification calls to assess against the gold standard. The goal is only to profile methylation frequencies, not to benchmark a caller's per-read classification against bisulfite. Cytosines of interest are covered by fewer than 5 Nanopore reads or fewer than 10 bisulfite reads — these are excluded by the evaluation filter and cannot support the metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assess per-read 5mC classification accuracy of Nanopore modification callers (DeepSignal-plant vs Megalodon) against a bisulfite-sequencing gold standard, computing per-context (CG/CHG/CHH) Pearson correlation, RMSE, and read-level accuracy in plants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Assess per-read 5mC classification accuracy of Nanopore modification callers (DeepSignal-plant vs Megalodon) against a bisulfite-sequencing gold standard, computing per-context (CG/CHG/CHH) Pearson correlation, RMSE, and read-level accuracy in plants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only bisulfite sequencing data is available with no native Nanopore reads — there are no per-read modification calls to assess against the gold standard. The goal is only to profile methylation frequencies, not to benchmark a caller's per-read classification against bisulfite. Cytosines of interest are covered by fewer than 5 Nanopore reads or fewer than 10 bisulfite reads — these are excluded by the evaluation filter and cannot support the metrics.

skills.description: Use when you have per-read per-CpG methylation probabilities (e.g. ccsmeth 5mCpG scores on PacBio HiFi reads) and need higher read-level accuracy at the cost of dropping 8.9-12.8% of ambiguous calls.
skills.name: read-level-methylation-confidence-filtering
skills.search_text: read-level-methylation-confidence-filtering Use when you have per-read per-CpG methylation probabilities (e.g. ccsmeth 5mCpG scores on PacBio HiFi reads) and need higher read-level accuracy at the cost of dropping 8.9-12.8% of ambiguous calls. You need to keep every call or detect hemimethylated CpGs — filtering removes 8.9-12.8% of calls and these methods cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs The target modification is non-CpG 5mC or another modification such as 6mA — ccsmeth's design covers CpG 5mC detection only You are working at the genome-wide site level rather than the read level — site-level aggregation of calls is a different model/task http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A confidence-margin filter for per-read 5mCpG methylation calls: discard ambiguous calls whose delta-p = |Pr − (1 − Pr)| falls below a 0.33 threshold to raise ccsmeth read-level accuracy, trading away a small fraction of calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: A confidence-margin filter for per-read 5mCpG methylation calls: discard ambiguous calls whose delta-p = |Pr − (1 − Pr)| falls below a 0.33 threshold to raise ccsmeth read-level accuracy, trading away a small fraction of calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to keep every call or detect hemimethylated CpGs — filtering removes 8.9-12.8% of calls and these methods cannot detect hemimethylated CpGs The target modification is non-CpG 5mC or another modification such as 6mA — ccsmeth's design covers CpG 5mC detection only You are working at the genome-wide site level rather than the read level — site-level aggregation of calls is a different model/task

skills.description: Use when per-read (single-molecule) m6A or m5C modification probabilities are needed from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA data, e.g. to reproduce CHEUI-solo Model 1 accuracy/precision/recall/AUC on IVT test sets.
skills.name: read-level-rna-modification-classification
skills.search_text: read-level-rna-modification-classification Use when per-read (single-molecule) m6A or m5C modification probabilities are needed from Oxford Nanopore direct RNA data, e.g. to reproduce CHEUI-solo Model 1 accuracy/precision/recall/AUC on IVT test sets. Data were produced with the RNA004 chemistry or you need pseudouridine predictions — use SWARM, which CHEUI's authors state improves accuracy and adds a pseudouridine model The goal is transcript-site stoichiometry or differential methylation between two conditions — that requires CHEUI Model 2 or CHEUI-diff, not read-level Model 1 alone Input is not nanopore direct RNA sequencing signal (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or antibody-based m6A/miCLIP data) — CHEUI operates on ionic current signals http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Classify individual nanopore direct RNA reads as m6A- or m5C-modified by feeding resquiggled ionic-current signals through CHEUI-solo Model 1 CNNs (Keras/TensorFlow), yielding a posterior modification probability per read for benchmarking model accuracy and recall. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Classify individual nanopore direct RNA reads as m6A- or m5C-modified by feeding resquiggled ionic-current signals through CHEUI-solo Model 1 CNNs (Keras/TensorFlow), yielding a posterior modification probability per read for benchmarking model accuracy and recall.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were produced with the RNA004 chemistry or you need pseudouridine predictions — use SWARM, which CHEUI's authors state improves accuracy and adds a pseudouridine model The goal is transcript-site stoichiometry or differential methylation between two conditions — that requires CHEUI Model 2 or CHEUI-diff, not read-level Model 1 alone Input is not nanopore direct RNA sequencing signal (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or antibody-based m6A/miCLIP data) — CHEUI operates on ionic current signals

skills.description: Use when raw NGS short reads (Illumina) or SMS long reads (PacBio HiFi/CLR, ONT) are being mapped to a draft genome assembly as input for clipped-read-based error calling (CRE/CSE) and AQI computation.
skills.name: read-mapping-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: read-mapping-quality-filtering Use when raw NGS short reads (Illumina) or SMS long reads (PacBio HiFi/CLR, ONT) are being mapped to a draft genome assembly as input for clipped-read-based error calling (CRE/CSE) and AQI computation. The alignments are already the filtered BAMs consumed by CRAQ — re-filtering could discard legitimate clipped reads and bias clipping-ratio cutoffs. The quality-assessment goal is completeness- or k-mer-based (e.g. BUSCO, Merqury, LAI) and involves no read mapping to the draft assembly. Only a single read type is available and clipping-based error classification (CRE/CSE), which integrates both NGS and SMS mapping, cannot be performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A cleanup step in the CRAQ assembly-assessment pipeline that maps raw sequencing reads back to a draft assembly with Minimap2 and then removes low-confidence alignments with 'samtools view -F 1796 -q 20' so that only high-quality clipped signals feed error and heterozygosity classification. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: A cleanup step in the CRAQ assembly-assessment pipeline that maps raw sequencing reads back to a draft assembly with Minimap2 and then removes low-confidence alignments with 'samtools view -F 1796 -q 20' so that only high-quality clipped signals feed error and heterozygosity classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The alignments are already the filtered BAMs consumed by CRAQ — re-filtering could discard legitimate clipped reads and bias clipping-ratio cutoffs. The quality-assessment goal is completeness- or k-mer-based (e.g. BUSCO, Merqury, LAI) and involves no read mapping to the draft assembly. Only a single read type is available and clipping-based error classification (CRE/CSE), which integrates both NGS and SMS mapping, cannot be performed.

skills.description: Use when constructing a viral sequencing pipeline where a read mapper (e.g. minimap2 with -t 1 -a -x sr) produces alignment records and you want to reduce disk I/O and wall-clock time by streaming records to consensus calling without writing an intermediary SAM/BAM file.
skills.name: read-mapping-stream-piping
skills.search_text: read-mapping-stream-piping Use when constructing a viral sequencing pipeline where a read mapper (e.g. minimap2 with -t 1 -a -x sr) produces alignment records and you want to reduce disk I/O and wall-clock time by streaming records to consensus calling without writing an intermediary SAM/BAM file. Your reconstruction requires multiple reference sequences — ViralConsensus builds consensus from a single reference sequence The reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. a human chromosome) and you lack large-memory capacity, since memory consumption scales linearly with reference genome length You need to inspect or reprocess the full alignment records downstream (e.g. variant-level analysis with sorted, indexed BAMs) rather than just call the consensus http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Pipe the read mapper's SAM output stream directly into ViralConsensus via standard input so consensus calling happens on-the-fly, eliminating the intermediate SAM file on disk that two-step alignment-then-consensus workflows require. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Pipe the read mapper's SAM output stream directly into ViralConsensus via standard input so consensus calling happens on-the-fly, eliminating the intermediate SAM file on disk that two-step alignment-then-consensus workflows require.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your reconstruction requires multiple reference sequences — ViralConsensus builds consensus from a single reference sequence The reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. a human chromosome) and you lack large-memory capacity, since memory consumption scales linearly with reference genome length You need to inspect or reprocess the full alignment records downstream (e.g. variant-level analysis with sorted, indexed BAMs) rather than just call the consensus

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare nanopore signal simulators' output quality on R10.4.1 chemistry — e.g. comparing simulated-read basecalling accuracy (match rate, PHRED) between seq2squiggle and k-mer-model tools like squigulator.
skills.name: read-mode-vs-genome-mode-simulation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: read-mode-vs-genome-mode-simulation-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively compare nanopore signal simulators' output quality on R10.4.1 chemistry — e.g. comparing simulated-read basecalling accuracy (match rate, PHRED) between seq2squiggle and k-mer-model tools like squigulator. You need biological downstream validity of simulated reads (variant calling, assembly benchmarks) rather than basecalling-accuracy metrics — this skill only measures match rate/PHRED of basecalled simulated signals. Your data uses non-R10.4.1 chemistry (e.g. R9.4.1) without a compatible pretrained model; seq2squiggle requires matching model weights for predictions. You want to evaluate simulator signal fidelity directly (e.g. per-k-mer amplitude/dwell distributions) rather than through a basecalling/alignment round-trip. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 A benchmarking skill that compares nanopore read simulators (seq2squiggle vs squigulator) in Read-mode and Genome-mode on R10.4.1 datasets by basecalling simulated signals with dorado, aligning them with minimap2, and reporting median match rate and median PHRED score. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that compares nanopore read simulators (seq2squiggle vs squigulator) in Read-mode and Genome-mode on R10.4.1 datasets by basecalling simulated signals with dorado, aligning them with minimap2, and reporting median match rate and median PHRED score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need biological downstream validity of simulated reads (variant calling, assembly benchmarks) rather than basecalling-accuracy metrics — this skill only measures match rate/PHRED of basecalled simulated signals. Your data uses non-R10.4.1 chemistry (e.g. R9.4.1) without a compatible pretrained model; seq2squiggle requires matching model weights for predictions. You want to evaluate simulator signal fidelity directly (e.g. per-k-mer amplitude/dwell distributions) rather than through a basecalling/alignment round-trip.

skills.description: Use when running DBG2OLC overlap-layout on hybrid data — an accurate DBG contig set (e.g., SparseAssembler Contigs.txt, N50 ~29-32 kbp) plus 10x-100x error-prone PacBio/ONT FASTA reads — and a backbone_raw.fasta must be produced before consensus.
skills.name: read-overlap-graph-construction
skills.search_text: read-overlap-graph-construction Use when running DBG2OLC overlap-layout on hybrid data — an accurate DBG contig set (e.g., SparseAssembler Contigs.txt, N50 ~29-32 kbp) plus 10x-100x error-prone PacBio/ONT FASTA reads — and a backbone_raw.fasta must be produced before consensus. You are already past layout and hold backbone_raw.fasta plus DBG2OLC_Consensus_info.txt — the next skill is BLASR-based consensus (Sparc/pbdagcon), not overlap graph construction. Your DBG contigs come from a short-read pipeline that applied repeat resolving such as gap closing or scaffolding — the README warns these heuristics introduce errors and yield poor final results. You are assembling short reads alone without long reads — this is the hybrid overlap-layout skill, not the non-hybrid NGS assembly commands. Construct DBG2OLC's best overlap graph from long erroneous reads compressed into DBG-contig anchors: round 1 removes contained nodes, round 2 finds suffix-prefix overlaps by aligning compressed reads via matching 17-mers, then tips are pruned and bubbles merged to yield backbone_raw.fasta. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Construct DBG2OLC's best overlap graph from long erroneous reads compressed into DBG-contig anchors: round 1 removes contained nodes, round 2 finds suffix-prefix overlaps by aligning compressed reads via matching 17-mers, then tips are pruned and bubbles merged to yield backbone_raw.fasta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are already past layout and hold backbone_raw.fasta plus DBG2OLC_Consensus_info.txt — the next skill is BLASR-based consensus (Sparc/pbdagcon), not overlap graph construction. Your DBG contigs come from a short-read pipeline that applied repeat resolving such as gap closing or scaffolding — the README warns these heuristics introduce errors and yield poor final results. You are assembling short reads alone without long reads — this is the hybrid overlap-layout skill, not the non-hybrid NGS assembly commands.

skills.description: Use when building an overlap graph or string graph from long noisy reads (Nanopore R9/R10, PacBio CLR) and partial overlaps with long unaligned overhangs would otherwise create spurious edges.
skills.name: read-overlap-overhang-filtering
skills.search_text: read-overlap-overhang-filtering Use when building an overlap graph or string graph from long noisy reads (Nanopore R9/R10, PacBio CLR) and partial overlaps with long unaligned overhangs would otherwise create spurious edges. Input reads are already high-accuracy (PacBio HiFi, Nanopore duplex) — the paper reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on these, where simpler assemblers like Hifiasm suffice Reads are short (Illumina-style) — minimap2 overlap presets '-x ava-pb'/'-x ava-ont' are tuned for long noisy reads with error rates up to ~15% The goal is reference-based mapping or polishing rather than de novo overlap graph construction Detects candidate read-to-read overlaps with minimap2, extends partial alignments to read ends using the diff (edit-distance) algorithm, and filters overlaps that still retain long overhangs before string graph construction in PECAT. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Detects candidate read-to-read overlaps with minimap2, extends partial alignments to read ends using the diff (edit-distance) algorithm, and filters overlaps that still retain long overhangs before string graph construction in PECAT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already high-accuracy (PacBio HiFi, Nanopore duplex) — the paper reports PECAT achieves only mediocre performance on these, where simpler assemblers like Hifiasm suffice Reads are short (Illumina-style) — minimap2 overlap presets '-x ava-pb'/'-x ava-ont' are tuned for long noisy reads with error rates up to ~15% The goal is reference-based mapping or polishing rather than de novo overlap graph construction

skills.description: Use when building or querying a read-overlap index for nanopore FASTQ reads without a reference, e.g. to find reads that overlap a query sequence via MinHash sketches and a match threshold.
skills.name: read-overlap-threshold-querying
skills.search_text: read-overlap-threshold-querying Use when building or querying a read-overlap index for nanopore FASTQ reads without a reference, e.g. to find reads that overlap a query sequence via MinHash sketches and a match threshold. The input is not read base sequences but quality values or read identifiers — NanoSpring does not compress or index those The goal is reference-based overlap detection with high-accuracy alignment (e.g. minimap2 mapping) rather than fast approximate MinHash matching Reads are short and low-error (e.g. Illumina) — NanoSpring and its overlap approach target long, higher-error nanopore reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs NanoSpring's MinHash-based read-overlap index: k-mer extraction (k=23), n=60 hash-function sketches, BBHash minimal-perfect-hash lookup tables, and threshold queries returning reads matching at least t=6 of 60 sketch values. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs NanoSpring's MinHash-based read-overlap index: k-mer extraction (k=23), n=60 hash-function sketches, BBHash minimal-perfect-hash lookup tables, and threshold queries returning reads matching at least t=6 of 60 sketch values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not read base sequences but quality values or read identifiers — NanoSpring does not compress or index those The goal is reference-based overlap detection with high-accuracy alignment (e.g. minimap2 mapping) rather than fast approximate MinHash matching Reads are short and low-error (e.g. Illumina) — NanoSpring and its overlap approach target long, higher-error nanopore reads

skills.description: Use when constructing a scaffolding graph from Illumina mate-pair (or long) reads without a traditional aligner, and you need to score k-mer hits against contigs and rescue weakly-placed mates before writing pair locations as SAM.
skills.name: read-pair-scoring-and-rescue
skills.search_text: read-pair-scoring-and-rescue Use when constructing a scaffolding graph from Illumina mate-pair (or long) reads without a traditional aligner, and you need to score k-mer hits against contigs and rescue weakly-placed mates before writing pair locations as SAM. Input is raw unlinked long reads where insert size matters: synthetic-library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size, so gap-size estimation differs from 10X/DOVETAIL-style mate-pair data You need full base-level alignments with mismatches/CIGAR strings — Fast-SG is alignment-free and only reports pair locations, not alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fast-SG's alignment-free placement of read pairs: ntHash rolling-hash k-mer look-ups against a unique k-mer index fill per-read hit vectors, windowed scoring localizes each mate, and a rescue step (score thresholds 3/5/4) retains pairs whose individual placement is weak but joint placement is consistent, emitting pair locations in SAM format. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Fast-SG's alignment-free placement of read pairs: ntHash rolling-hash k-mer look-ups against a unique k-mer index fill per-read hit vectors, windowed scoring localizes each mate, and a rescue step (score thresholds 3/5/4) retains pairs whose individual placement is weak but joint placement is consistent, emitting pair locations in SAM format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unlinked long reads where insert size matters: synthetic-library insert size is restricted to the actual long-read size, so gap-size estimation differs from 10X/DOVETAIL-style mate-pair data You need full base-level alignments with mismatches/CIGAR strings — Fast-SG is alignment-free and only reports pair locations, not alignments

skills.description: Use when preprocessing raw nanopore output (FASTQ .fastq/.fq/.fastq.gz/.fq.gz, FAST5, or POD5) that requires per-sample read filtering plus comparative quality visualisations before taxonomic classification or genome reconstruction.
skills.name: read-quality-visualisation-nanopore-data
skills.search_text: read-quality-visualisation-nanopore-data Use when preprocessing raw nanopore output (FASTQ .fastq/.fq/.fastq.gz/.fq.gz, FAST5, or POD5) that requires per-sample read filtering plus comparative quality visualisations before taxonomic classification or genome reconstruction. Input consists only of FASTA files (.fasta, .fas, .fsa, .fna, .fa), which VirDetector uses from the alignment step onwards and do not enter the basecalling/quality-filtering stage Samples have already been basecalled and quality-filtered and only downstream steps (classification, consensus reconstruction, phylogeny) are needed All pipeline steps are disabled — samples will only be preprocessed and trimmed, so no downstream quality comparison is produced http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Filter Oxford Nanopore reads with NanoFilt after optional basecalling and use NanoComp to generate quality plots comparing unfiltered and filtered FASTQ reads, as done in VirDetector's preprocessing stage (section 2.1). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Filter Oxford Nanopore reads with NanoFilt after optional basecalling and use NanoComp to generate quality plots comparing unfiltered and filtered FASTQ reads, as done in VirDetector's preprocessing stage (section 2.1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists only of FASTA files (.fasta, .fas, .fsa, .fna, .fa), which VirDetector uses from the alignment step onwards and do not enter the basecalling/quality-filtering stage Samples have already been basecalled and quality-filtered and only downstream steps (classification, consensus reconstruction, phylogeny) are needed All pipeline steps are disabled — samples will only be preprocessed and trimmed, so no downstream quality comparison is produced

skills.description: Use when generating synthetic nanopore read sets from a reference genome/contigs in FASTA format, matching a specified coverage, read count, or empirical read-length distribution.
skills.name: read-sampling-from-reference-genome
skills.search_text: read-sampling-from-reference-genome Use when generating synthetic nanopore read sets from a reference genome/contigs in FASTA format, matching a specified coverage, read count, or empirical read-length distribution. Input is already a FASTA/FASTQ of pre-existing reads — use seq2squiggle's --read-input mode instead of sampling fresh reads from a reference The goal is only to simulate signals for existing reads without additional fragmentation, not to synthesize new read sequences Amplicon- or transcript-based read structures are required where uniform random sampling over the reference would be inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Simulates synthetic nanopore reads by uniformly sampling start positions on a FASTA reference genome or contigs, drawing read lengths from user-selected target distributions (e.g. the exponential, beta, and mixed-gamma distributions adopted from DeepSimulator), and emitting a FASTA/FASTQ read set that can be fed to signal simulation with seq2squiggle. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Simulates synthetic nanopore reads by uniformly sampling start positions on a FASTA reference genome or contigs, drawing read lengths from user-selected target distributions (e.g. the exponential, beta, and mixed-gamma distributions adopted from DeepSimulator), and emitting a FASTA/FASTQ read set that can be fed to signal simulation with seq2squiggle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a FASTA/FASTQ of pre-existing reads — use seq2squiggle's --read-input mode instead of sampling fresh reads from a reference The goal is only to simulate signals for existing reads without additional fragmentation, not to synthesize new read sequences Amplicon- or transcript-based read structures are required where uniform random sampling over the reference would be inappropriate

skills.description: Use when planning or validating nanoSHAPE experiments on ONT direct RNA data and you need to know the minimum read count at which per-read KS-derived reactivity correlations (current or dwell) plateau.
skills.name: read-subsampling-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: read-subsampling-curve-analysis Use when planning or validating nanoSHAPE experiments on ONT direct RNA data and you need to know the minimum read count at which per-read KS-derived reactivity correlations (current or dwell) plateau. Fewer than 100 reads are available in modified or control condition, below the --minimum-test-reads threshold tombo needs for in vitro sample comparison The goal is modification identification from trained kmer models rather than sample-comparison reactivity profiling against an unmodified control No SHAPE-MaP reactivity reference exists for the target, so the subsampled correlations cannot be anchored to an orthogonal profile Assesses how many nanopore reads are needed for a stable nanoSHAPE reactivity profile by subsampling 1 to N reads and plotting Spearman correlation of the KS-derived per-read signal against the AcIm SHAPE-MaP reactivity profile. Establishes read-depth sufficiency (95% of maximum correlation at ~200 reads) for single-molecule structure probing. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: Assesses how many nanopore reads are needed for a stable nanoSHAPE reactivity profile by subsampling 1 to N reads and plotting Spearman correlation of the KS-derived per-read signal against the AcIm SHAPE-MaP reactivity profile. Establishes read-depth sufficiency (95% of maximum correlation at ~200 reads) for single-molecule structure probing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fewer than 100 reads are available in modified or control condition, below the --minimum-test-reads threshold tombo needs for in vitro sample comparison The goal is modification identification from trained kmer models rather than sample-comparison reactivity profiling against an unmodified control No SHAPE-MaP reactivity reference exists for the target, so the subsampled correlations cannot be anchored to an orthogonal profile

skills.description: Use when you need to characterize how site-level m6A detection performance degrades as the fraction of modified reads per site drops — e.g., benchmarking EpiNano-SVM on heterogeneous or partial-methylation samples.
skills.name: read-subsampling-mixture-simulation
skills.search_text: read-subsampling-mixture-simulation Use when you need to characterize how site-level m6A detection performance degrades as the fraction of modified reads per site drops — e.g., benchmarking EpiNano-SVM on heterogeneous or partial-methylation samples. You need per-read (single-molecule) modification calls — the algorithm explicitly aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and cannot resolve individual molecules You are trying to distinguish modification types (e.g., m1A vs m6A) — the trained m6A models do not discriminate between different modification species The sample is fully modified or fully unmodified with no stoichiometry variation — a simple pairwise (WT vs KO) EpiNano-Error analysis is more appropriate than mixture simulation Generates in-silico partial-methylation read pools by subsampling m6A-modified and unmodified direct RNA sequencing reads at defined proportions, then scores sites with the trained EpiNano combined-features SVM to quantify how detection performance (ROC AUC) depends on methylation stoichiometry. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Generates in-silico partial-methylation read pools by subsampling m6A-modified and unmodified direct RNA sequencing reads at defined proportions, then scores sites with the trained EpiNano combined-features SVM to quantify how detection performance (ROC AUC) depends on methylation stoichiometry.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-read (single-molecule) modification calls — the algorithm explicitly aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and cannot resolve individual molecules You are trying to distinguish modification types (e.g., m1A vs m6A) — the trained m6A models do not discriminate between different modification species The sample is fully modified or fully unmodified with no stoichiometry variation — a simple pairwise (WT vs KO) EpiNano-Error analysis is more appropriate than mixture simulation

skills.description: Use when simulating Iso-Seq reads of multigene-family transcripts (e.g., TSPY, HSFY) and you need to determine, per isoform and per depth, whether IsoCon captured it, removed it in statistical filtering, or failed to converge it during error correction.
skills.name: read-to-candidate-assignment-parsing
skills.search_text: read-to-candidate-assignment-parsing Use when simulating Iso-Seq reads of multigene-family transcripts (e.g., TSPY, HSFY) and you need to determine, per isoform and per depth, whether IsoCon captured it, removed it in statistical filtering, or failed to converge it during error correction. IsoCon has not been run and no cluster_info.tsv, final_candidates.fa, or not_converged.fa exist — assignment parsing requires the converged clustering output Reads come from real (not simulated) data without isoform truth labels — fate classification per simulated isoform cannot be computed The goal is to distinguish transcripts from different gene copies post-reconstruction — IsoCon does not provide definitive gene-copy assignment ('further downstream analysis would be needed') http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Parses IsoCon's per-read clustering output (cluster_info.tsv) together with final_candidates.fa and not_converged.fa to classify each simulated isoform's fate — captured, filtered in the statistical step, or lost in error correction — as a function of per-isoform read depth. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Parses IsoCon's per-read clustering output (cluster_info.tsv) together with final_candidates.fa and not_converged.fa to classify each simulated isoform's fate — captured, filtered in the statistical step, or lost in error correction — as a function of per-isoform read depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: IsoCon has not been run and no cluster_info.tsv, final_candidates.fa, or not_converged.fa exist — assignment parsing requires the converged clustering output Reads come from real (not simulated) data without isoform truth labels — fate classification per simulated isoform cannot be computed The goal is to distinguish transcripts from different gene copies post-reconstruction — IsoCon does not provide definitive gene-copy assignment ('further downstream analysis would be needed')

skills.description: Use when comparing basecaller accuracy: you have basecalled FASTQ reads from one or more basecallers and the corresponding reference genome, and you need per-read identity/error-rate metrics.
skills.name: read-to-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: read-to-reference-alignment Use when comparing basecaller accuracy: you have basecalled FASTQ reads from one or more basecallers and the corresponding reference genome, and you need per-read identity/error-rate metrics. No reference genome exists for the sample — use the de novo route (Minimap2/Miniasm draft + 10 rounds of Racon polishing) instead of read-to-reference alignment Input is raw fast5 signal rather than basecalled reads — basecall first (e.g. Chiron dna-pre preset) before aligning Reads have already been aligned and error rates extracted — re-running graphmap alignment would duplicate the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns basecalled nanopore reads (FASTQ/FASTA from Chiron, Albacore, Metrichor, or BasecRAWller) to a known reference genome with graphmap using default parameters, then parses alignment CIGAR/MD strings to derive per-read identity, insertion, deletion, and mismatch rates for basecaller benchmarking. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy037
skills.summary: Aligns basecalled nanopore reads (FASTQ/FASTA from Chiron, Albacore, Metrichor, or BasecRAWller) to a known reference genome with graphmap using default parameters, then parses alignment CIGAR/MD strings to derive per-read identity, insertion, deletion, and mismatch rates for basecaller benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome exists for the sample — use the de novo route (Minimap2/Miniasm draft + 10 rounds of Racon polishing) instead of read-to-reference alignment Input is raw fast5 signal rather than basecalled reads — basecall first (e.g. Chiron dna-pre preset) before aligning Reads have already been aligned and error rates extracted — re-running graphmap alignment would duplicate the analysis

skills.description: Use when input is FLNC CCS reads (FASTQ/FASTA) from targeted Iso-Seq of a multigene family and each read must be assigned to its originating transcript/cluster despite near-identical copy sequences.
skills.name: read-to-transcript-cluster-assignment
skills.search_text: read-to-transcript-cluster-assignment Use when input is FLNC CCS reads (FASTQ/FASTA) from targeted Iso-Seq of a multigene family and each read must be assigned to its originating transcript/cluster despite near-identical copy sequences. Reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline (primers, barcodes, and chimeras still present) — IsoCon assumes clean FLNC input Reads do not span the region of interest end-to-end (e.g. shotgun transcriptome or genomic reads rather than targeted Iso-Seq/amplicon reads spanning the transcript) The goal is to definitively distinguish alleles from distinct gene copies or determine gene family size — IsoCon provides only hypothetical assignment and further downstream analysis would be needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Assigns pre-processed FLNC PacBio CCS reads to consensus transcript clusters for highly similar gene copies, via iterative nearest-neighbor graph clustering, center-based error correction, and greedy closest-neighbor candidate assignment with pairwise hypothesis testing (as implemented in IsoCon). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Assigns pre-processed FLNC PacBio CCS reads to consensus transcript clusters for highly similar gene copies, via iterative nearest-neighbor graph clustering, center-based error correction, and greedy closest-neighbor candidate assignment with pairwise hypothesis testing (as implemented in IsoCon).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline (primers, barcodes, and chimeras still present) — IsoCon assumes clean FLNC input Reads do not span the region of interest end-to-end (e.g. shotgun transcriptome or genomic reads rather than targeted Iso-Seq/amplicon reads spanning the transcript) The goal is to definitively distinguish alleles from distinct gene copies or determine gene family size — IsoCon provides only hypothetical assignment and further downstream analysis would be needed

skills.description: Use when benchmarking software signal-alignment (sDTW) runtimes against reference length, or when needing quantitative evidence that CPU squiggle mapping becomes a computational bottleneck for Read Until and justifies FPGA acceleration.
skills.name: read-until-alignment-profiling
skills.search_text: read-until-alignment-profiling Use when benchmarking software signal-alignment (sDTW) runtimes against reference length, or when needing quantitative evidence that CPU squiggle mapping becomes a computational bottleneck for Read Until and justifies FPGA acceleration. The goal is to measure the HARU FPGA-accelerated sDTW itself rather than the software baseline — this skill deliberately times sigfish-cpu only Input reads are already basecalled and alignment is in base space (e.g., Minimap2); this skill profiles raw-signal-domain sDTW squiggle mapping Only a single reference length is available, since power-law exponent fitting requires multiple increasing reference lengths http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Profile the single-thread CPU execution time of the sigfish sDTW (subsequence dynamic time warping) squiggle-mapping step as reference sequence length increases, establishing the empirical superlinear (quadratic O(MN)) scaling that motivates hardware acceleration with HARU. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Profile the single-thread CPU execution time of the sigfish sDTW (subsequence dynamic time warping) squiggle-mapping step as reference sequence length increases, establishing the empirical superlinear (quadratic O(MN)) scaling that motivates hardware acceleration with HARU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to measure the HARU FPGA-accelerated sDTW itself rather than the software baseline — this skill deliberately times sigfish-cpu only Input reads are already basecalled and alignment is in base space (e.g., Minimap2); this skill profiles raw-signal-domain sDTW squiggle mapping Only a single reference length is available, since power-law exponent fitting requires multiple increasing reference lengths

skills.description: Use when comparing raw-signal mapping tools (e.g., RawHash2 vs. RawHash vs. UNCALLED) on the same FAST5 datasets and you need precision/recall/F1 against a minimap2-derived ground truth.
skills.name: readmapper-benchmark-f1-comparison
skills.search_text: readmapper-benchmark-f1-comparison Use when comparing raw-signal mapping tools (e.g., RawHash2 vs. RawHash vs. UNCALLED) on the same FAST5 datasets and you need precision/recall/F1 against a minimap2-derived ground truth. When evaluating basecalled-read mappers directly (minimap2 itself is the ground-truth generator here, not a benchmark subject). When no trusted basecalling/reference is available to produce minimap2 ground truth, since all F1 scores are relative to that standard. For overlap/assembly quality assessment (Rawsamble all-vs-all overlapping outputs are not scored by this precision/recall/F1 workflow). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark raw-signal nanopore read mappers by scoring their PAF outputs against minimap2-based ground-truth alignments using UNCALLED's pafstats to compute per-dataset precision, recall, and F1, as done to show RawHash2 improves F1 over RawHash by 10.57% on average (up to 20.25%). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Benchmark raw-signal nanopore read mappers by scoring their PAF outputs against minimap2-based ground-truth alignments using UNCALLED's pafstats to compute per-dataset precision, recall, and F1, as done to show RawHash2 improves F1 over RawHash by 10.57% on average (up to 20.25%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When evaluating basecalled-read mappers directly (minimap2 itself is the ground-truth generator here, not a benchmark subject). When no trusted basecalling/reference is available to produce minimap2 ground truth, since all F1 scores are relative to that standard. For overlap/assembly quality assessment (Rawsamble all-vs-all overlapping outputs are not scored by this precision/recall/F1 workflow).

skills.description: Use when comparing early-termination behavior of real-time raw signal mappers (RawHash/RawHash2) on FAST5 test datasets and you need per-dataset mean bases/chunks processed before the mapping decision from PAF outputs.
skills.name: real-time-prefix-mapping-length-quantification
skills.search_text: real-time-prefix-mapping-length-quantification Use when comparing early-termination behavior of real-time raw signal mappers (RawHash/RawHash2) on FAST5 test datasets and you need per-dataset mean bases/chunks processed before the mapping decision from PAF outputs. PAF outputs come from base-level mappers (e.g., minimap2) that lack the UNCALLED-template mapping-decision records with prefix lengths and chunk counts The analysis goal is F1 mapping accuracy or throughput comparison rather than early-termination sequencing length before the mapping decision Signals were not analyzed in real time / early termination was disabled, so no prefix-based mapping decision exists in the output http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies how much signal each raw nanopore signal mapper processes before halting — bases and chunks of the read prefix consumed prior to the mapping decision — by parsing modified PAF mapping outputs (UNCALLED-style template) from RawHash and RawHash2. Used to show that RawHash2 reduces average sequencing length before the mapping decision by ~1.9× over RawHash. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478
skills.summary: Quantifies how much signal each raw nanopore signal mapper processes before halting — bases and chunks of the read prefix consumed prior to the mapping decision — by parsing modified PAF mapping outputs (UNCALLED-style template) from RawHash and RawHash2. Used to show that RawHash2 reduces average sequencing length before the mapping decision by ~1.9× over RawHash.
skills.when_to_use_negative: PAF outputs come from base-level mappers (e.g., minimap2) that lack the UNCALLED-template mapping-decision records with prefix lengths and chunk counts The analysis goal is F1 mapping accuracy or throughput comparison rather than early-termination sequencing length before the mapping decision Signals were not analyzed in real time / early termination was disabled, so no prefix-based mapping decision exists in the output

skills.description: Use when nanopore reads arrive incrementally during a MinION run and you want to merge SPAdes/Illumina contigs into completed scaffolds on-the-fly, using streaming bwa mem alignments piped into jsa.np.npscarf -realtime.
skills.name: real-time-streaming-scaffolding
skills.search_text: real-time-streaming-scaffolding Use when nanopore reads arrive incrementally during a MinION run and you want to merge SPAdes/Illumina contigs into completed scaffolds on-the-fly, using streaming bwa mem alignments piped into jsa.np.npscarf -realtime. The long-read data are already fully sequenced and base-called and you do not need incremental assembly metrics — use npScarf in batch mode (same bwa mem parameters, no -realtime) instead The draft assembly consists of long-read-only contigs or the input is already a finished/scaffolded assembly — npScarf scaffolds short-read draft assemblies from SPAdes-style contigs npScarf is unmaintained and you are starting a new pipeline rather than reproducing this method — the README points to npGraph (github.com/hsnguyen/assembly) as the replacement http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scaffold and complete a short-read draft genome assembly using Oxford Nanopore long reads streamed during an ongoing sequencing run, via npScarf (jsa.np.npscarf), so assembly metrics are reported in real time and the run can be terminated once sufficient quality is reached. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Scaffold and complete a short-read draft genome assembly using Oxford Nanopore long reads streamed during an ongoing sequencing run, via npScarf (jsa.np.npscarf), so assembly metrics are reported in real time and the run can be terminated once sufficient quality is reached.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long-read data are already fully sequenced and base-called and you do not need incremental assembly metrics — use npScarf in batch mode (same bwa mem parameters, no -realtime) instead The draft assembly consists of long-read-only contigs or the input is already a finished/scaffolded assembly — npScarf scaffolds short-read draft assemblies from SPAdes-style contigs npScarf is unmaintained and you are starting a new pipeline rather than reproducing this method — the README points to npGraph (github.com/hsnguyen/assembly) as the replacement

skills.description: Use when base-called nanopore reads are arriving during an active run (or emulated stream) and you need a hybrid SPAdes+npScarf scaffolded assembly with live metrics to decide when to stop sequencing.
skills.name: realtime-streaming-assembly-pipelining
skills.search_text: realtime-streaming-assembly-pipelining Use when base-called nanopore reads are arriving during an active run (or emulated stream) and you need a hybrid SPAdes+npScarf scaffolded assembly with live metrics to decide when to stop sequencing. The nanopore data are already fully base-called and you want the fastest/best final assembly rather than in-run scaffolding and termination decisions — batch mode or a dedicated long-read assembler (npScarf is unmaintained; npGraph is its successor) is more appropriate. There are no short-read data and none can be generated — the pipeline scaffolds a short-read draft assembly and cannot work from long reads alone. Millisecond-level real-time updates on every added base are required — the pipeline is real-time only at minute-level temporal resolution and depends on base-caller latency. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run npScarf (Japsa) to scaffold and complete a short-read draft assembly while a nanopore run is still in progress, streaming base-called long reads block-wise through BWA-MEM and merging contigs as bridge scores cross threshold. Reports assembly metrics (contigs, N50) in real-time so sequencing can be terminated once sufficient quality is reached. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Run npScarf (Japsa) to scaffold and complete a short-read draft assembly while a nanopore run is still in progress, streaming base-called long reads block-wise through BWA-MEM and merging contigs as bridge scores cross threshold. Reports assembly metrics (contigs, N50) in real-time so sequencing can be terminated once sufficient quality is reached.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The nanopore data are already fully base-called and you want the fastest/best final assembly rather than in-run scaffolding and termination decisions — batch mode or a dedicated long-read assembler (npScarf is unmaintained; npGraph is its successor) is more appropriate. There are no short-read data and none can be generated — the pipeline scaffolds a short-read draft assembly and cannot work from long reads alone. Millisecond-level real-time updates on every added base are required — the pipeline is real-time only at minute-level temporal resolution and depends on base-caller latency.

skills.description: Use when you have de novo enriched methylation motifs (from Nanoident_enrich.sh or nanodisco automatic mode) for bacteria with known REBASE motif references and need to quantify motif recovery and compare methods.
skills.name: rebase-motif-reference-comparison
skills.search_text: rebase-motif-reference-comparison Use when you have de novo enriched methylation motifs (from Nanoident_enrich.sh or nanodisco automatic mode) for bacteria with known REBASE motif references and need to quantify motif recovery and compare methods. When no REBASE reference motifs exist for the strain, so agreement cannot be scored When inputs are already typed/mapped motifs rather than de novo enriched motif sets needing reference matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Matches de novo discovered methylation motifs from Nanoident's optimized enrichment module against REBASE reference motifs for each bacterium, providing a ground-truth-based comparison with nanodisco's automatic discovery mode. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf397
skills.summary: Matches de novo discovered methylation motifs from Nanoident's optimized enrichment module against REBASE reference motifs for each bacterium, providing a ground-truth-based comparison with nanodisco's automatic discovery mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no REBASE reference motifs exist for the strain, so agreement cannot be scored When inputs are already typed/mapped motifs rather than de novo enriched motif sets needing reference matching

skills.description: Use when evaluating a candidate-variant shortlist from a prioritization run where ground-truth causal variants are known (e.g. semisynthetic spiked-in ClinVar variants), to quantify recall and false positives per inheritance mode.
skills.name: recall-false-positive-metric-computation
skills.search_text: recall-false-positive-metric-computation Use when evaluating a candidate-variant shortlist from a prioritization run where ground-truth causal variants are known (e.g. semisynthetic spiked-in ClinVar variants), to quantify recall and false positives per inheritance mode. Input is a real disease cohort without known ground-truth causal variants — recall cannot be computed without spiked-in or resolved causal variants The task is variant calling accuracy (e.g. SNV/indel sensitivity of eDiVA-Predict) rather than candidate shortlist prioritization quality You need formal precision (1 - FP/(TP+FP)) rather than the average-false-positives proxy used when shortlists vary in length http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3325 Compute recall and average false positives as a precision proxy when benchmarking a variant prioritization tool across inheritance modes, as done for eDiVA-Prioritize on 6,811 semisynthetic parent-child trios built from ClinVar pathogenic variants spiked into the 1000 Genomes CEPH trio. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772
skills.summary: Compute recall and average false positives as a precision proxy when benchmarking a variant prioritization tool across inheritance modes, as done for eDiVA-Prioritize on 6,811 semisynthetic parent-child trios built from ClinVar pathogenic variants spiked into the 1000 Genomes CEPH trio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a real disease cohort without known ground-truth causal variants — recall cannot be computed without spiked-in or resolved causal variants The task is variant calling accuracy (e.g. SNV/indel sensitivity of eDiVA-Predict) rather than candidate shortlist prioritization quality You need formal precision (1 - FP/(TP+FP)) rather than the average-false-positives proxy used when shortlists vary in length

skills.description: Use when a structural-variant caller must cluster SV candidate reads (discordant pairs, split reads, cigar-derived deletions/insertions, breakends) into signature nodes on an alignment graph and connect compatible signatures without pairwise sequence alignment.
skills.name: reciprocal-overlap-edge-annotation
skills.search_text: reciprocal-overlap-edge-annotation Use when a structural-variant caller must cluster SV candidate reads (discordant pairs, split reads, cigar-derived deletions/insertions, breakends) into signature nodes on an alignment graph and connect compatible signatures without pairwise sequence alignment. Input is raw unaligned reads or an unfiltered VCF of finished calls rather than candidate read alignments — the skill operates on the clustering stage between read fetching and SV calling The goal is genotype refinement or ML quality scoring of already-called SVs; dysgu applies a gradient boosting classifier downstream for that purpose A de novo assembly stage is required to resolve multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences, which the authors state dysgu's clustering stage does not do http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A graph-clustering skill from dysgu that converts SV candidate reads into enumerated SV-signature nodes ('discordant', 'split', 'deletion', 'insertion', 'breakend') and links compatible signatures with black edges using a reciprocal-overlap threshold of 0.1 plus a span position distance (SPD) threshold of 0.3, so soft-clipped reads can be clustered without pairwise sequence alignment. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: A graph-clustering skill from dysgu that converts SV candidate reads into enumerated SV-signature nodes ('discordant', 'split', 'deletion', 'insertion', 'breakend') and links compatible signatures with black edges using a reciprocal-overlap threshold of 0.1 plus a span position distance (SPD) threshold of 0.3, so soft-clipped reads can be clustered without pairwise sequence alignment.

skills.name: reference-genome-alignment
skills.search_text: reference-genome-alignment Use when raw or Trimmomatic-trimmed FASTQ reads from WGS/WES samples (e.g. SRA projects PRJNA624223, PRJEB39632) must be aligned to a reference genome before variant calling with GATK HaplotypeCaller. Input is raw untrimmed FASTQ that has not passed the FastQC/Trimmomatic QC stage — the JWES chain requires QC and trimming before mapping Non-human or non-hg38 reference genomes — the article grounds this workflow in mapping against the reference human genome (hg38) Downstream analysis needing only variant counts from already-annotated VCFs (e.g. parsing with JWES-DB) — no re-alignment is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Maps quality-trimmed FASTQ reads against the human reference genome hg38 with BWA as the alignment stage of the JWES pipeline, then sorts, deduplicates, and indexes the resulting SAM file to prepare a clean BAM for GATK variant calling. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261
skills.summary: Maps quality-trimmed FASTQ reads against the human reference genome hg38 with BWA as the alignment stage of the JWES pipeline, then sorts, deduplicates, and indexes the resulting SAM file to prepare a clean BAM for GATK variant calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw untrimmed FASTQ that has not passed the FastQC/Trimmomatic QC stage — the JWES chain requires QC and trimming before mapping Non-human or non-hg38 reference genomes — the article grounds this workflow in mapping against the reference human genome (hg38) Downstream analysis needing only variant counts from already-annotated VCFs (e.g. parsing with JWES-DB) — no re-alignment is required

skills.description: Use when consensus subtelomeric anchor sequences (e.g., from a sample.telomap.anchors.tsv cluster table) must be assigned to unique chromosomal ends against the T2T-CHM13 reference for chromosome-end-specific telomere analysis.
skills.name: reference-genome-assembly-handling
skills.search_text: reference-genome-assembly-handling Use when consensus subtelomeric anchor sequences (e.g., from a sample.telomap.anchors.tsv cluster table) must be assigned to unique chromosomal ends against the T2T-CHM13 reference for chromosome-end-specific telomere analysis. Subtelomeric regions are too short for unambiguous chromosome-end identification (e.g., after RsaI/HinfI trimming), so most anchors would be labeled 'U' Input reads are not yet clustered into consensus subtelomeric anchors — run the subtelomeric clustering step first Using a non-telomere-to-telomere reference lacking complete subtelomeric sequence, since chromosome-end mapping is based on the T2T-CHM13 assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Assigns consensus subtelomeric anchor sequences to specific chromosome ends by aligning them against the T2T-CHM13 telomere-to-telomere human assembly, enabling chromosome-end-specific telomere analyses (e.g., Chr. 7q) in the telomap workflow. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Assigns consensus subtelomeric anchor sequences to specific chromosome ends by aligning them against the T2T-CHM13 telomere-to-telomere human assembly, enabling chromosome-end-specific telomere analyses (e.g., Chr. 7q) in the telomap workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Subtelomeric regions are too short for unambiguous chromosome-end identification (e.g., after RsaI/HinfI trimming), so most anchors would be labeled 'U' Input reads are not yet clustered into consensus subtelomeric anchors — run the subtelomeric clustering step first Using a non-telomere-to-telomere reference lacking complete subtelomeric sequence, since chromosome-end mapping is based on the T2T-CHM13 assembly

skills.search_text: reference-genome-base-conversion Use when building the nanoEM pipeline's first step: base-converted long reads (from EMseq/APOBEC treatment) must be mapped against a reference that mirrors their C-to-T and G-to-A substitutions. The downstream alignment target for unconverted reads (e.g. methylation calling against 'ref' in sambamba mpileup, or nanopolish-style signal calling) — those steps need the original, unconverted reference Aligning ordinary, non-base-converted reads where C positions must be scored against cytosines directly Preparing a bisulfite-style reference for short-read aligners such as bismark — this conversion is tailored to the nanoEM minimap2 map-ont workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Generates a methylation-conversion-aware reference for the nanoEM pipeline by replacing every C with T and every G with A in a whole-genome FASTA (e.g. GRCh38.p12) using Python3 and pysam, so that C-to-T/G-to-A converted nanopore reads can align to it. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397

skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream alignment target for unconverted reads (e.g. methylation calling against 'ref' in sambamba mpileup, or nanopolish-style signal calling) — those steps need the original, unconverted reference Aligning ordinary, non-base-converted reads where C positions must be scored against cytosines directly Preparing a bisulfite-style reference for short-read aligners such as bismark — this conversion is tailored to the nanoEM minimap2 map-ont workflow

skills.description: Use when validating a long-read ARG profiler on sequenced mock communities: supplier reference genomes with known ARG content are available and a per-ARG expected abundance (cpg) profile is needed for precision/recall/Pearson evaluation.
skills.name: reference-genome-based-expected-abundance-computation
skills.search_text: reference-genome-based-expected-abundance-computation Use when validating a long-read ARG profiler on sequenced mock communities: supplier reference genomes with known ARG content are available and a per-ARG expected abundance (cpg) profile is needed for precision/recall/Pearson evaluation. Profiling unknown environmental or clinical metagenomes where no curated reference genomes exist — use the profiler (e.g., Argo) directly instead of building an expected profile When ARG content must be discovered de novo (novel genes, point-mutation-derived ARGs), since this workflow only counts occurrences of known SARG+ reference entries http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Computes the expected (ground-truth) ARG abundance profile of a mock community by aligning supplier reference genomes against the SARG+ database with DIAMOND blastx, then filtering HSPs and counting ARG occurrences. Provides the reference profile against which Argo's estimated ARG abundances (cpg values) are validated. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Computes the expected (ground-truth) ARG abundance profile of a mock community by aligning supplier reference genomes against the SARG+ database with DIAMOND blastx, then filtering HSPs and counting ARG occurrences. Provides the reference profile against which Argo's estimated ARG abundances (cpg values) are validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Profiling unknown environmental or clinical metagenomes where no curated reference genomes exist — use the profiler (e.g., Argo) directly instead of building an expected profile When ARG content must be discovered de novo (novel genes, point-mutation-derived ARGs), since this workflow only counts occurrences of known SARG+ reference entries

skills.description: Use when a merged or post-assembly contig set must be validated against reference genomes — e.g., checking that merging maintains reference coverage while reducing contig count and unmapped contigs.
skills.name: reference-genome-coverage-alignment
skills.search_text: reference-genome-coverage-alignment Use when a merged or post-assembly contig set must be validated against reference genomes — e.g., checking that merging maintains reference coverage while reducing contig count and unmapped contigs. The metagenome sample has no reference genomes available, so coverage cannot be computed and only ab initio metrics (gene prediction, similarity searches) apply The goal is de novo assembly quality assessment of a single isolate where total assembly size and N50/N90 suffice — the article notes these are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' but coverage-based validation targets mixed communities Input is raw reads rather than an assembled/merged contig set; this skill validates post-assembly output, it does not assemble http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validate a merged metagenome assembly (e.g., MeGAMerged contigs) by aligning contigs to known reference genomes with Nucmer to compute reference genome coverage, and by mapping reads back with BWA/SAMtools to count unmapped contigs and flag chimeras. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Validate a merged metagenome assembly (e.g., MeGAMerged contigs) by aligning contigs to known reference genomes with Nucmer to compute reference genome coverage, and by mapping reads back with BWA/SAMtools to count unmapped contigs and flag chimeras.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metagenome sample has no reference genomes available, so coverage cannot be computed and only ab initio metrics (gene prediction, similarity searches) apply The goal is de novo assembly quality assessment of a single isolate where total assembly size and N50/N90 suffice — the article notes these are 'not very useful for comparing metagenome assembly performance' but coverage-based validation targets mixed communities Input is raw reads rather than an assembled/merged contig set; this skill validates post-assembly output, it does not assemble

skills.description: Use when starting an ONT SNV-calling benchmark or analysis and you need indexed reference assemblies (e.g. GRCh38, GRCm39, TAIR10, BDGP6) plus a miniSNV population-variant index.
skills.name: reference-genome-preparation
skills.search_text: reference-genome-preparation Use when starting an ONT SNV-calling benchmark or analysis and you need indexed reference assemblies (e.g. GRCh38, GRCm39, TAIR10, BDGP6) plus a miniSNV population-variant index. The analysis target is not SNV calling against a reference (e.g. de novo assembly or reference-free variant discovery), since miniSNV's pipeline is reference- and population-VCF-dependent Only indels or structural variants are of interest — miniSNV and this preparation workflow target SNV genotyping The input BAM is not aligned to the same assembly/contig naming as the reference FASTA (mismatched contig names will break chunked processing) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Prepare species-appropriate reference genome FASTAs and the auxiliary indexes (samtools FASTA index, BAM index, and the miniSNV prebuilt known-variants index from 1000 Genomes population VCFs) required before SNV calling on ONT data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: Prepare species-appropriate reference genome FASTAs and the auxiliary indexes (samtools FASTA index, BAM index, and the miniSNV prebuilt known-variants index from 1000 Genomes population VCFs) required before SNV calling on ONT data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is not SNV calling against a reference (e.g. de novo assembly or reference-free variant discovery), since miniSNV's pipeline is reference- and population-VCF-dependent Only indels or structural variants are of interest — miniSNV and this preparation workflow target SNV genotyping The input BAM is not aligned to the same assembly/contig naming as the reference FASTA (mismatched contig names will break chunked processing)

skills.description: Use when preparing to align long-read (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) whole-genome shotgun data for HLA typing with HLAminer, and a combined human+HLA-allele reference must be built and indexed before streaming minimap2 alignments.
skills.name: reference-genome-preparation-hla-augmented
skills.search_text: reference-genome-preparation-hla-augmented Use when preparing to align long-read (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio) whole-genome shotgun data for HLA typing with HLAminer, and a combined human+HLA-allele reference must be built and indexed before streaming minimap2 alignments. The analysis targets short Illumina reads — HLAminer's HPTASR targeted-assembly route with a k-mer hash table (not the long-read augmented reference) is the intended path for 100–150 bp reads The goal is routine whole-genome variant calling where a standard reference including chr6 is correct; stripping chr6 would lose that locus The HLA database must remain frozen at an older IPD-IMGT/HLA release for reproducibility and no updated-allele augmentation is wanted http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Prepare a combined long-read alignment reference consisting of GRCh38 (GCA_000001405.15, chromosome-only with chr6 excluded) augmented with HLA class I and II allele sequences downloaded from the IMGT/HLA repository, then index it for minimap2 so that HLA reads map to the allele targets rather than being suppressed by the alt/chr6 reference locus. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Prepare a combined long-read alignment reference consisting of GRCh38 (GCA_000001405.15, chromosome-only with chr6 excluded) augmented with HLA class I and II allele sequences downloaded from the IMGT/HLA repository, then index it for minimap2 so that HLA reads map to the allele targets rather than being suppressed by the alt/chr6 reference locus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets short Illumina reads — HLAminer's HPTASR targeted-assembly route with a k-mer hash table (not the long-read augmented reference) is the intended path for 100–150 bp reads The goal is routine whole-genome variant calling where a standard reference including chr6 is correct; stripping chr6 would lose that locus The HLA database must remain frozen at an older IPD-IMGT/HLA release for reproducibility and no updated-allele augmentation is wanted

skills.description: Use when building a simulated long-read benchmark where ground-truth overlaps must come from aligning reads back to a known reference chromosome with defined accuracy, coverage, and read-length grid conditions.
skills.name: reference-genome-read-extraction
skills.search_text: reference-genome-read-extraction Use when building a simulated long-read benchmark where ground-truth overlaps must come from aligning reads back to a known reference chromosome with defined accuracy, coverage, and read-length grid conditions. The dataset consists of real sequencing reads where ground-truth overlaps cannot be derived by aligning to a known reference (use real-data benchmarks like the GIAB HG002 PacBio HiFi or ONT SRR datasets instead). The analysis goal is assembly quality assessment (BUSCO/contiguity on Shasta assemblies) rather than overlap graph error rate benchmarking. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Extracts a reference sequence (e.g., chromosome 22 from the human T2T-CHM13 v2.0 assembly) to serve as ground truth for PBSIM3 long-read simulation, enabling controlled benchmarking of overlap detection against known alignment-derived overlaps. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giag048
skills.summary: Extracts a reference sequence (e.g., chromosome 22 from the human T2T-CHM13 v2.0 assembly) to serve as ground truth for PBSIM3 long-read simulation, enabling controlled benchmarking of overlap detection against known alignment-derived overlaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset consists of real sequencing reads where ground-truth overlaps cannot be derived by aligning to a known reference (use real-data benchmarks like the GIAB HG002 PacBio HiFi or ONT SRR datasets instead). The analysis goal is assembly quality assessment (BUSCO/contiguity on Shasta assemblies) rather than overlap graph error rate benchmarking.

skills.description: Use when you have a coordinate-indexed variant list (e.g. CHROM/POS from a GIAB/1KGp3 truth VCF) and need the surrounding reference bases from GRCh37 or GRCh38 to classify sequence context such as homopolymer runs (>=4 identical bases) or STRs (>=3 units of a 1-6 bp motif).
skills.name: reference-genome-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: reference-genome-sequence-extraction Use when you have a coordinate-indexed variant list (e.g. CHROM/POS from a GIAB/1KGp3 truth VCF) and need the surrounding reference bases from GRCh37 or GRCh38 to classify sequence context such as homopolymer runs (>=4 identical bases) or STRs (>=3 units of a 1-6 bp motif). The input is already an annotated sequence-context table and the goal is downstream statistics rather than sequence retrieval The reference genome build does not match the truth-variant coordinate build — extracted flanks would come from the wrong alleles/coordinates and inflate context mislabeling You need caller-level error modeling (e.g. Clairvoyante tensor extraction from BAMs) rather than static reference-sequence context classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts downstream reference sequence flanking each variant coordinate from a FASTA-indexed reference genome (GRCh37/GRCh38) so that sequence context — homopolymer runs and short tandem repeats — can be classified for undetected variant sets. This is the sequence-retrieval step that underpins context-based explanations of why SMS variant callers miss known truth variants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Extracts downstream reference sequence flanking each variant coordinate from a FASTA-indexed reference genome (GRCh37/GRCh38) so that sequence context — homopolymer runs and short tandem repeats — can be classified for undetected variant sets. This is the sequence-retrieval step that underpins context-based explanations of why SMS variant callers miss known truth variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an annotated sequence-context table and the goal is downstream statistics rather than sequence retrieval The reference genome build does not match the truth-variant coordinate build — extracted flanks would come from the wrong alleles/coordinates and inflate context mislabeling You need caller-level error modeling (e.g. Clairvoyante tensor extraction from BAMs) rather than static reference-sequence context classification
