skills.description: Use when paired-end Illumina RAD-seq reads (e.g., EcoRI-site reads from Populus parents) must be mapped to a reference genome to enable indel calling at restriction-site loci.
skills.name: reference-guided-read-alignment
skills.search_text: reference-guided-read-alignment Use when paired-end Illumina RAD-seq reads (e.g., EcoRI-site reads from Populus parents) must be mapped to a reference genome to enable indel calling at restriction-site loci. Input reads are long-read (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) data — BWA-MEM is intended for Illumina-type short reads and the article workflow uses parental RAD-seq paired-end reads No reference genome is available — reference-guided alignment is inapplicable; a de novo approach would be required The parental indel catalog already exists and the goal is genotyping only — InDelGT supports '--nocatalog' to skip this alignment/catalog step http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns parental paired-end RAD-seq FASTQ reads to the P. trichocarpa v4.0 reference genome using BWA 0.7.17, then processes alignments with SAMtools 1.9/BCFtools 1.9, as the first underlying step of InDelGT's parental InDel catalog generation. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Aligns parental paired-end RAD-seq FASTQ reads to the P. trichocarpa v4.0 reference genome using BWA 0.7.17, then processes alignments with SAMtools 1.9/BCFtools 1.9, as the first underlying step of InDelGT's parental InDel catalog generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are long-read (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) data — BWA-MEM is intended for Illumina-type short reads and the article workflow uses parental RAD-seq paired-end reads No reference genome is available — reference-guided alignment is inapplicable; a de novo approach would be required The parental indel catalog already exists and the goal is genotyping only — InDelGT supports '--nocatalog' to skip this alignment/catalog step

skills.description: Use when nanopore reads from an untargeted viral sequencing run have been trimmed, filtered, and de novo assembled, and a -scoring reference genome from a BLAST search in the virus reference database is available to guide consensus construction.
skills.name: reference-guided-viral-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: reference-guided-viral-genome-assembly Use when nanopore reads from an untargeted viral sequencing run have been trimmed, filtered, and de novo assembled, and a -scoring reference genome from a BLAST search in the virus reference database is available to guide consensus construction. No suitable reference can be identified — de novo contigs do not match any entry in the reference database or only partially The sample targets large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox), where the pipeline itself warns assemblies 'may contain inaccuracies and should be regarded as draft genomes' Reads have not been adapter/primer-trimmed or filtered for host/contaminant/non-viral content, so mapping against the reference would include off-target reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs consensus viral genomes from untargeted nanopore reads by mapping trimmed reads against a BLAST-selected reference, integrating Sniffles2-called indels into a BCFtools consensus draft, and polishing the final sequence with Medaka or Samtools. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Reconstructs consensus viral genomes from untargeted nanopore reads by mapping trimmed reads against a BLAST-selected reference, integrating Sniffles2-called indels into a BCFtools consensus draft, and polishing the final sequence with Medaka or Samtools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No suitable reference can be identified — de novo contigs do not match any entry in the reference database or only partially The sample targets large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox), where the pipeline itself warns assemblies 'may contain inaccuracies and should be regarded as draft genomes' Reads have not been adapter/primer-trimmed or filtered for host/contaminant/non-viral content, so mapping against the reference would include off-target reads

skills.description: Use when validating that a long-read (Oxford Nanopore) plasmid assembly pipeline recovers known plasmids from a reference set, or when benchmarking an assembly against published plasmid recovery results.
skills.name: reference-plasmid-identity-comparison
skills.search_text: reference-plasmid-identity-comparison Use when validating that a long-read (Oxford Nanopore) plasmid assembly pipeline recovers known plasmids from a reference set, or when benchmarking an assembly against published plasmid recovery results. The input is short-read (150-300 bp) sequencing data rather than Nanopore long reads — the skill and its underlying tools were intensively tested only for ONT data The goal is de novo plasmid discovery without any reference plasmid set to compare against No polished assembly is available yet — run minimap2/miniasm and Racon first before the identity comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Compares de novo-assembled Nanopore plasmid contigs against a published reference plasmid set, recording the number of plasmids recovered and their mean sequence identity (e.g. the Li et al. benchmark: 19 of 21 plasmids at 97.76% mean identity) to validate a long-read assembly workflow. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: Compares de novo-assembled Nanopore plasmid contigs against a published reference plasmid set, recording the number of plasmids recovered and their mean sequence identity (e.g. the Li et al. benchmark: 19 of 21 plasmids at 97.76% mean identity) to validate a long-read assembly workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read (150-300 bp) sequencing data rather than Nanopore long reads — the skill and its underlying tools were intensively tested only for ONT data The goal is de novo plasmid discovery without any reference plasmid set to compare against No polished assembly is available yet — run minimap2/miniasm and Racon first before the identity comparison

skills.description: Use when a PacBio long-read isoform catalog (e.g., IsoPops-filtered .db) must be benchmarked against RefSeq or UCSC Genes GTF annotations to report per-database isoform recovery fractions like 53.9% (RefSeq) or 72.3% (UCSC).
skills.name: refseq-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: refseq-annotation-matching Use when a PacBio long-read isoform catalog (e.g., IsoPops-filtered .db) must be benchmarked against RefSeq or UCSC Genes GTF annotations to report per-database isoform recovery fractions like 53.9% (RefSeq) or 72.3% (UCSC). The transcript evidence is short-read RNA-seq only — typical read lengths <200 bp cannot resolve full-length sequences of multi-kilobase transcripts, so full-splice-match classification of complete isoforms is not meaningful. The isoform catalog has not yet been filtered (e.g., with filter_db/filer_truncations for exon count ≥4 and truncation removal) — matching unfiltered or truncated transcripts inflates apparent recovery statistics. The goal is novel isoform discovery rather than annotation benchmarking — use catalog novelty classification instead of database recovery comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies a PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoform catalog against public RefSeq and UCSC Genes mm10 annotations by intron-chain matching under SQANTI full-splice-match criteria, quantifying what fraction of each database's annotated isoforms the targeted long-read catalog recovers. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Classifies a PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoform catalog against public RefSeq and UCSC Genes mm10 annotations by intron-chain matching under SQANTI full-splice-match criteria, quantifying what fraction of each database's annotated isoforms the targeted long-read catalog recovers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The transcript evidence is short-read RNA-seq only — typical read lengths <200 bp cannot resolve full-length sequences of multi-kilobase transcripts, so full-splice-match classification of complete isoforms is not meaningful. The isoform catalog has not yet been filtered (e.g., with filter_db/filer_truncations for exon count ≥4 and truncation removal) — matching unfiltered or truncated transcripts inflates apparent recovery statistics. The goal is novel isoform discovery rather than annotation benchmarking — use catalog novelty classification instead of database recovery comparison.

skills.description: Use when profiling tandem repeats de novo from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments (ONT or PacBio BAM), or when re-tuning TRiCoLOR REFER via '--size' to detect longer motifs such as mini-satellites beyond the default micro-satellite settings.
skills.name: regex-approximate-string-matching-repeat-motif-calling
skills.search_text: regex-approximate-string-matching-repeat-motif-calling Use when profiling tandem repeats de novo from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments (ONT or PacBio BAM), or when re-tuning TRiCoLOR REFER via '--size' to detect longer motifs such as mini-satellites beyond the default micro-satellite settings. The goal is to call repeats in unassembled genomic regions such as centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot access Input is a haploid chromosome (e.g., human Y) or a polyploid genome, since the tool assumes diploid haplotype resolution A validated ground-truth mini-satellite call set is required for benchmarking: the tool has been extensively applied only to micro-satellites, and mini-satellite parameterizations are unvalidated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Two-stage RegEx-based repeat resolution within TRiCoLOR's REFER module: first identify motifs perfectly repeated (default length ≤6 bp, ≥5 repeats) in haplotype-specific consensus sequences, then match approximate repetitions up to an edit distance ≤1 and resolve overlapping predictions with an N-gram model favoring the most frequent perfect repeat motif. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Two-stage RegEx-based repeat resolution within TRiCoLOR's REFER module: first identify motifs perfectly repeated (default length ≤6 bp, ≥5 repeats) in haplotype-specific consensus sequences, then match approximate repetitions up to an edit distance ≤1 and resolve overlapping predictions with an N-gram model favoring the most frequent perfect repeat motif.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to call repeats in unassembled genomic regions such as centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot access Input is a haploid chromosome (e.g., human Y) or a polyploid genome, since the tool assumes diploid haplotype resolution A validated ground-truth mini-satellite call set is required for benchmarking: the tool has been extensively applied only to micro-satellites, and mini-satellite parameterizations are unvalidated

skills.description: Use when genotyping tandem repeats de novo from error-prone long-read (ONT/PacBio) alignments: once haplotype-specific POA consensus sequences exist and candidate low-entropy regions must be decomposed into motif + multiplicity.
skills.name: regex-based-tandem-repeat-motif-discovery
skills.search_text: regex-based-tandem-repeat-motif-discovery Use when genotyping tandem repeats de novo from error-prone long-read (ONT/PacBio) alignments: once haplotype-specific POA consensus sequences exist and candidate low-entropy regions must be decomposed into motif + multiplicity. Target repeats in unassembled regions of the genome (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres) — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there Profiling mini-satellites or polyploid/haploid (e.g., human Y chromosome) data — parameters validated only for micro-satellites and diploid genomes Short reads or non-haplotype-resolved alignments — the method requires haplotype-resolved long-read alignments as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Resolves the repeat motif and multiplicity of tandem repeats from haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences using a fast regular expression (RegEx)-based approximate string-matching algorithm, as implemented in the TRiCoLOR REFER module. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Resolves the repeat motif and multiplicity of tandem repeats from haplotype-specific low-error consensus sequences using a fast regular expression (RegEx)-based approximate string-matching algorithm, as implemented in the TRiCoLOR REFER module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target repeats in unassembled regions of the genome (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres) — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there Profiling mini-satellites or polyploid/haploid (e.g., human Y chromosome) data — parameters validated only for micro-satellites and diploid genomes Short reads or non-haplotype-resolved alignments — the method requires haplotype-resolved long-read alignments as input

skills.description: Use when chaining alignment anchors for long, error-prone (e.g., Oxford Nanopore MinION) reads and you must rank or prune candidate mapping regions before final gapped alignment.
skills.name: region-quality-scoring
skills.search_text: region-quality-scoring Use when chaining alignment anchors for long, error-prone (e.g., Oxford Nanopore MinION) reads and you must rank or prune candidate mapping regions before final gapped alignment. Short-read mapping where a BWT/FM-index mapper (e.g., BWA-MEM) suffices — GraphMap's hash index is ~14x the reference size (~42 GB peak for human) and the FM-index memory reduction was only 'currently under implementation' Already-aligned inputs — the funnel assumes raw seed hits and anchors, not a SAM/BAM alignment Use cases requiring minimal-memory large-genome indexing; the article notes GraphMap requires large-memory machines (~100 GB for the human genome) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 GraphMap's candidate-region scoring step (stage IV of its five-stage read funnel), where chained anchor paths from the LCSk chaining stage are refined by L1 linear regression, filtered to a ±3-sigma residual band, and ranked with the paper's region quality scoring formulae (Eqs. 4–7) to select the best mapping locations on nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: GraphMap's candidate-region scoring step (stage IV of its five-stage read funnel), where chained anchor paths from the LCSk chaining stage are refined by L1 linear regression, filtered to a ±3-sigma residual band, and ranked with the paper's region quality scoring formulae (Eqs. 4–7) to select the best mapping locations on nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short-read mapping where a BWT/FM-index mapper (e.g., BWA-MEM) suffices — GraphMap's hash index is ~14x the reference size (~42 GB peak for human) and the FM-index memory reduction was only 'currently under implementation' Already-aligned inputs — the funnel assumes raw seed hits and anchors, not a SAM/BAM alignment Use cases requiring minimal-memory large-genome indexing; the article notes GraphMap requires large-memory machines (~100 GB for the human genome)

skills.description: Use when fitting simulated or real scRNA-seq counts under alternative model specifications (e.g., no ZI, intercept-only ZI, covariate-inclusive ZI) and you need a unified per-gene table of coefficient estimates and standard errors for comparison.
skills.name: regression-coefficient-tabulation
skills.search_text: regression-coefficient-tabulation Use when fitting simulated or real scRNA-seq counts under alternative model specifications (e.g., no ZI, intercept-only ZI, covariate-inclusive ZI) and you need a unified per-gene table of coefficient estimates and standard errors for comparison. When the goal is gene set testing or set-level enrichment—the adhoc procedure and per-gene coefficient tabulation are not recommended there because geneset testing requires a common gene-level null across genes When the analysis goal is hypothesis testing of a covariate via likelihood ratio test rather than tabulating coefficient estimates—use lr.twosigma / lr.twosigma_custom instead When random-effect variance components need to be formally tested—use test.vc.twosigma rather than comparing fixed-effect tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tabulates per-gene fixed-effect coefficient estimates and standard errors from alternative model specifications—in this context, zero-inflated negative binomial fits from glmmTMB via the twosigma R package—into a single comparison table so conditional-mean estimates can be compared side by side. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Tabulates per-gene fixed-effect coefficient estimates and standard errors from alternative model specifications—in this context, zero-inflated negative binomial fits from glmmTMB via the twosigma R package—into a single comparison table so conditional-mean estimates can be compared side by side.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is gene set testing or set-level enrichment—the adhoc procedure and per-gene coefficient tabulation are not recommended there because geneset testing requires a common gene-level null across genes When the analysis goal is hypothesis testing of a covariate via likelihood ratio test rather than tabulating coefficient estimates—use lr.twosigma / lr.twosigma_custom instead When random-effect variance components need to be formally tested—use test.vc.twosigma rather than comparing fixed-effect tables

skills.description: Use when domain-instance homology counts, Pfam family groupings, or position-level domain coverage must be derived from a prebuilt protein-to-genome mapping database rather than recomputed from raw FASTA/BLAST output.
skills.name: relational-database-domain-annotation-querying
skills.search_text: relational-database-domain-annotation-querying Use when domain-instance homology counts, Pfam family groupings, or position-level domain coverage must be derived from a prebuilt protein-to-genome mapping database rather than recomputed from raw FASTA/BLAST output. When the mapping database has not been populated — the query needs the loaded PostgreSQL table, not raw GENCODE/UniProt/Pfam downloads, which the application does not read directly When a Pfam family has only a single homologous domain instance in the human proteome — it fails the ≥2-homolog threshold and cannot form a meta-domain When the goal is to create transcript-to-Swiss-Prot mappings themselves (Protein–Protein BLAST v2.2.31+ against GENCODE Basic translations), which is an upstream mapping-database construction step http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Query a PostgreSQL mapping database that links genomic positions, protein residues, and Pfam domain annotations to group homologous domain instances by Pfam family, the basis for constructing MetaDome meta-domains (3,334 families with ≥2 homologs covering 43.6% of domain positions). genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Query a PostgreSQL mapping database that links genomic positions, protein residues, and Pfam domain annotations to group homologous domain instances by Pfam family, the basis for constructing MetaDome meta-domains (3,334 families with ≥2 homologs covering 43.6% of domain positions).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the mapping database has not been populated — the query needs the loaded PostgreSQL table, not raw GENCODE/UniProt/Pfam downloads, which the application does not read directly When a Pfam family has only a single homologous domain instance in the human proteome — it fails the ≥2-homolog threshold and cannot form a meta-domain When the goal is to create transcript-to-Swiss-Prot mappings themselves (Protein–Protein BLAST v2.2.31+ against GENCODE Basic translations), which is an upstream mapping-database construction step

skills.description: Use when annotated variant output (VCF/snpEff-annotated records) from a variant-calling pipeline must be persisted into a relational database with a modeled schema for downstream querying and dump/export.
skills.name: relational-database-schema-design
skills.search_text: relational-database-schema-design Use when annotated variant output (VCF/snpEff-annotated records) from a variant-calling pipeline must be persisted into a relational database with a modeled schema for downstream querying and dump/export. Input is already a structured database dump or a feature table loaded in persistent storage rather than raw annotated variant records The goal is upstream data processing (QC, trimming, alignment, variant calling) rather than variant-data storage/loading — use the JWES data-processing module instead The variant data must remain in VCF text form for tools that consume VCF directly and no relational persistence is required Designs a relational schema for storing annotated VCF variant records as the JWES-DB (JWES-ETL) storage module, organizing parsed variant data into Variant, Info, and Sample tables and loading them into a MySQL RDBMS via an ETL routine. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261
skills.summary: Designs a relational schema for storing annotated VCF variant records as the JWES-DB (JWES-ETL) storage module, organizing parsed variant data into Variant, Info, and Sample tables and loading them into a MySQL RDBMS via an ETL routine.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a structured database dump or a feature table loaded in persistent storage rather than raw annotated variant records The goal is upstream data processing (QC, trimming, alignment, variant calling) rather than variant-data storage/loading — use the JWES data-processing module instead The variant data must remain in VCF text form for tools that consume VCF directly and no relational persistence is required

skills.description: Use when building or populating a relational mapping database that links genomic positions to protein residues (e.g., GENCODE transcripts to Swiss-Prot canonical/isoform sequences) with indexed lookup fields for downstream variant aggregation.
skills.name: relational-database-schema-population
skills.search_text: relational-database-schema-population Use when building or populating a relational mapping database that links genomic positions to protein residues (e.g., GENCODE transcripts to Swiss-Prot canonical/isoform sequences) with indexed lookup fields for downstream variant aggregation. Downstream analyses such as tolerance landscapes, meta-domain construction or meta-domain variant annotation — these consume the already-populated mapping database rather than populating it. Input is a VCF of gnomAD/ClinVar variants to be annotated — the populated database is a prerequisite for that annotation step, not the target of this skill. The released mapping CSV has already been loaded and verified against the committed quality-control reports — re-populating from scratch is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs and loads a PostgreSQL relational mapping database that links every coding genomic position to a GENCODE transcript, a Swiss-Prot protein residue and, where applicable, a Pfam domain consensus position. This indexed mapping database is the substrate on which all MetaDome variant aggregation and tolerance analyses run. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23798
skills.summary: Constructs and loads a PostgreSQL relational mapping database that links every coding genomic position to a GENCODE transcript, a Swiss-Prot protein residue and, where applicable, a Pfam domain consensus position. This indexed mapping database is the substrate on which all MetaDome variant aggregation and tolerance analyses run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Downstream analyses such as tolerance landscapes, meta-domain construction or meta-domain variant annotation — these consume the already-populated mapping database rather than populating it. Input is a VCF of gnomAD/ClinVar variants to be annotated — the populated database is a prerequisite for that annotation step, not the target of this skill. The released mapping CSV has already been loaded and verified against the committed quality-control reports — re-populating from scratch is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when simulating evolutionary game dynamics in R where two behavioral strategies interact at their current frequencies and relative fitnesses derived from a payoff matrix must update those frequencies each generation.
skills.name: relative-fitness-frequency-update-implementation
skills.search_text: relative-fitness-frequency-update-implementation Use when simulating evolutionary game dynamics in R where two behavioral strategies interact at their current frequencies and relative fitnesses derived from a payoff matrix must update those frequencies each generation. The question concerns deterministic or stochastic allele-frequency change under selection or drift rather than frequency-dependent game-theoretic strategies A ready-made learnPopGen function suffices and reimplementing the update loop is unnecessary Students less adept in R would be better served by one of the package's web interfaces http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Implements the frequency-dependent dynamics of the learnPopGen hawk-dove game model: each generation, strategy payoffs from a user-specified matrix are normalized into relative fitnesses and multiplied by current strategy frequencies to evolve hawk-dove proportions through time. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412
skills.summary: Implements the frequency-dependent dynamics of the learnPopGen hawk-dove game model: each generation, strategy payoffs from a user-specified matrix are normalized into relative fitnesses and multiplied by current strategy frequencies to evolve hawk-dove proportions through time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns deterministic or stochastic allele-frequency change under selection or drift rather than frequency-dependent game-theoretic strategies A ready-made learnPopGen function suffices and reimplementing the update loop is unnecessary Students less adept in R would be better served by one of the package's web interfaces

skills.description: Use when comparing INC-Seq consensus read sets from different ONT chemistries (2D vs 1D2) or aligners and you need to test whether tandem repeat prevalence or repeat length distributions differ between them.
skills.name: repeat-length-distribution-comparison-across-runs
skills.search_text: repeat-length-distribution-comparison-across-runs Use when comparing INC-Seq consensus read sets from different ONT chemistries (2D vs 1D2) or aligners and you need to test whether tandem repeat prevalence or repeat length distributions differ between them. Input data are raw noisy nanopore reads rather than chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads, since the prevalence range and distribution shapes were established on consensus sequences. The goal is homopolymer error characterization or residual deletion analysis rather than tandem repeat structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantify and compare tandem repeat prevalence and repeat length distributions across nanopore INC-Seq consensus runs to test whether these features depend on aligner choice or sequencing chemistry (2D vs 1D2). genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Quantify and compare tandem repeat prevalence and repeat length distributions across nanopore INC-Seq consensus runs to test whether these features depend on aligner choice or sequencing chemistry (2D vs 1D2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw noisy nanopore reads rather than chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads, since the prevalence range and distribution shapes were established on consensus sequences. The goal is homopolymer error characterization or residual deletion analysis rather than tandem repeat structure.

skills.description: Use when preparing a repeat library for graph-genome-based TE detection (e.g. GraffiTE with the 'pangenie' graph method), starting from a Dfam release that must be converted to the tool's required format.
skills.name: repeat-library-conversion-for-graph-genomes
skills.search_text: repeat-library-conversion-for-graph-genomes Use when preparing a repeat library for graph-genome-based TE detection (e.g. GraffiTE with the 'pangenie' graph method), starting from a Dfam release that must be converted to the tool's required format. The downstream TE-calling tool is RetroInspector's Snakemake pipeline, which aligns reads with minimap2 against GRCh38 and calls variants with cuteSV+Sniffles2 rather than consuming a graph-genome repeat library The analysis targets short-read TE detection with tools like MELT or xTea, which do not use the FamDB/Dfam graph-genome library path You only need repeat annotation (RepeatMasker-style) and no graph-genome TE caller, in which case curated consensus (cc) FamDB components can be used directly without a GraffiTE-specific conversion http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts a complete Dfam transposable-element release into the graph-genome repeat-library format consumed by GraffiTE using the FamDB toolkit, extracting species-specific (human and ancestor) repeat families for TE insertion detection on nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Converts a complete Dfam transposable-element release into the graph-genome repeat-library format consumed by GraffiTE using the FamDB toolkit, extracting species-specific (human and ancestor) repeat families for TE insertion detection on nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream TE-calling tool is RetroInspector's Snakemake pipeline, which aligns reads with minimap2 against GRCh38 and calls variants with cuteSV+Sniffles2 rather than consuming a graph-genome repeat library The analysis targets short-read TE detection with tools like MELT or xTea, which do not use the FamDB/Dfam graph-genome library path You only need repeat annotation (RepeatMasker-style) and no graph-genome TE caller, in which case curated consensus (cc) FamDB components can be used directly without a GraffiTE-specific conversion

skills.description: Use when you have DeepSignal-plant per-site methylation frequency tables for two homologous/repeat regions (or two samples) and need to identify cytosine-level and region-level differential methylation between paired repeats in plant genomes.
skills.name: repeat-pair-differential-methylation-classification
skills.search_text: repeat-pair-differential-methylation-classification Use when you have DeepSignal-plant per-site methylation frequency tables for two homologous/repeat regions (or two samples) and need to identify cytosine-level and region-level differential methylation between paired repeats in plant genomes. If methylation calls come from short-read bisulfite sequencing — the article notes bisulfite cannot profile 5mCs in repetitive genome regions, invalidating repeat-pair methylation comparisons If the regions lack the repeat-pair criteria (length >100, identity score >0.99, at least one cytosine) — thresholds lose meaning for non-homologous or cytosine-free regions http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies pre-computed repeat pairs (length >100 bp, identity score >0.99, at least one cytosine) as differentially methylated by comparing per-site methylation frequencies from DeepSignal-plant call_freq tables between the two regions of each pair, quantifying the fraction of differentially methylated repeat pairs per species and per sequence context. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Classifies pre-computed repeat pairs (length >100 bp, identity score >0.99, at least one cytosine) as differentially methylated by comparing per-site methylation frequencies from DeepSignal-plant call_freq tables between the two regions of each pair, quantifying the fraction of differentially methylated repeat pairs per species and per sequence context.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If methylation calls come from short-read bisulfite sequencing — the article notes bisulfite cannot profile 5mCs in repetitive genome regions, invalidating repeat-pair methylation comparisons If the regions lack the repeat-pair criteria (length >100, identity score >0.99, at least one cytosine) — thresholds lose meaning for non-homologous or cytosine-free regions

skills.description: Use when comparing methylation states between paralogous duplicated regions of a genome: input is a reference FASTA (e.g. TAIR10 or IRGSP-1.0) and the goal is paired regions suitable for differential-methylation analysis.
skills.name: repeat-pair-identification
skills.search_text: repeat-pair-identification Use when comparing methylation states between paralogous duplicated regions of a genome: input is a reference FASTA (e.g. TAIR10 or IRGSP-1.0) and the goal is paired regions suitable for differential-methylation analysis. The goal is de novo repeat-family annotation or transposable-element classification rather than paired segmental duplications for methylation comparison The genome reference is not yet available or not self-aligned with MUMmer — no alignment output exists to filter Analyzing methylation at single sites without a duplicated-region comparator; this skill only produces paired regions for differential-methylation testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Identifies segmental-duplication repeat pairs by whole-genome self-alignment with MUMmer, retaining aligned region pairs with length >100 and identity score >0.99 that contain at least one cytosine, for downstream differential-methylation analysis in the DeepSignal-plant pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Identifies segmental-duplication repeat pairs by whole-genome self-alignment with MUMmer, retaining aligned region pairs with length >100 and identity score >0.99 that contain at least one cytosine, for downstream differential-methylation analysis in the DeepSignal-plant pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo repeat-family annotation or transposable-element classification rather than paired segmental duplications for methylation comparison The genome reference is not yet available or not self-aligned with MUMmer — no alignment output exists to filter Analyzing methylation at single sites without a duplicated-region comparator; this skill only produces paired regions for differential-methylation testing

skills.description: Use when a set of novel-insertion breakpoint coordinates (e.g. from a Novel-X VCF) needs classification by whether the surrounding reference sequence is repetitive, to characterize detection sensitivity in repeat-rich loci.
skills.name: repeat-region-annotation-with-repeatmasker
skills.search_text: repeat-region-annotation-with-repeatmasker Use when a set of novel-insertion breakpoint coordinates (e.g. from a Novel-X VCF) needs classification by whether the surrounding reference sequence is repetitive, to characterize detection sensitivity in repeat-rich loci. Input is raw linked-read FASTQ or BAM — RepeatMasker here applies only to extracted flanking sequences of already-called insertion breakpoints, not to reads or assemblies The insertion set is not from Novel-X's >300 bp anchor-sum-filtered VCF; this skill was characterized only on Novel-X output records meeting those thresholds The goal is de novo discovery of repeat consensus sequences rather than binary repeat/non-repeat annotation of known reference coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Screens the 300 bp sequences flanking each non-reference insertion breakpoint (reported in VCF by Novel-X on GRCh38) for repetitive reference sequence using RepeatMasker, to quantify how many detected insertions land in repeat regions of the reference genome. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Screens the 300 bp sequences flanking each non-reference insertion breakpoint (reported in VCF by Novel-X on GRCh38) for repetitive reference sequence using RepeatMasker, to quantify how many detected insertions land in repeat regions of the reference genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw linked-read FASTQ or BAM — RepeatMasker here applies only to extracted flanking sequences of already-called insertion breakpoints, not to reads or assemblies The insertion set is not from Novel-X's >300 bp anchor-sum-filtered VCF; this skill was characterized only on Novel-X output records meeting those thresholds The goal is de novo discovery of repeat consensus sequences rather than binary repeat/non-repeat annotation of known reference coordinates

skills.description: Use when a trio DNV candidate list (e.g., from GLnexus joint-genotyped VCFs passing Mendelian, depth, and dual-caller filters) must be pruned of variants falling in repeats, low-complexity sequence, or centromeres before emitting final calls.
skills.name: repeat-region-blacklist-masking
skills.search_text: repeat-region-blacklist-masking Use when a trio DNV candidate list (e.g., from GLnexus joint-genotyped VCFs passing Mendelian, depth, and dual-caller filters) must be pruned of variants falling in repeats, low-complexity sequence, or centromeres before emitting final calls. Input is raw aligned reads (BAM/CRAM) with no joint-genotyped trio VCF — use the Hare or Tortoise variant-calling workflow first You only have existing multi-sample VCFs without BAM/CRAM access and want drop-in trio DNV detection — HAT-FLEX is the caller-agnostic alternative The reference region set already excludes repeats/centromeres (e.g., exome targets restricted to high-confidence regions), making a second blacklist pass redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Excludes candidate de novo variants that overlap a BED-style blacklist of repeat, low-complexity, and centromeric regions, a step in HAT's custom _de novo_ variant filter applied after GLnexus family-level joint genotyping. Masking these error-prone intervals removes false DNVs driven by aligner/variant-caller artifacts. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775
skills.summary: Excludes candidate de novo variants that overlap a BED-style blacklist of repeat, low-complexity, and centromeric regions, a step in HAT's custom _de novo_ variant filter applied after GLnexus family-level joint genotyping. Masking these error-prone intervals removes false DNVs driven by aligner/variant-caller artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw aligned reads (BAM/CRAM) with no joint-genotyped trio VCF — use the Hare or Tortoise variant-calling workflow first You only have existing multi-sample VCFs without BAM/CRAM access and want drop-in trio DNV detection — HAT-FLEX is the caller-agnostic alternative The reference region set already excludes repeats/centromeres (e.g., exome targets restricted to high-confidence regions), making a second blacklist pass redundant

skills.description: Use when you need CpG coverage/phasing counts or methylation-state detection rates in repetitive genomic regions (RepeatMasker, segmental duplications, cenSat annotations) from PacBio HiFi/CCS modbam and bedmethyl data aligned to T2T-CHM13.
skills.name: repeat-region-methylation-annotation
skills.search_text: repeat-region-methylation-annotation Use when you need CpG coverage/phasing counts or methylation-state detection rates in repetitive genomic regions (RepeatMasker, segmental duplications, cenSat annotations) from PacBio HiFi/CCS modbam and bedmethyl data aligned to T2T-CHM13. The goal is detection of hemimethylated CpGs — CCS-based methods like ccsmeth consider only symmetric methylation and are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs. The target modification is non-CpG 5mC or another DNA modification such as 6mA — the models and CpG-intersection workflow do not apply. Only primary chromosomes chr1-22,X,Y matter and speed is preferred — running with include_all_ctgs=true is unnecessary overhead compared to the default false. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantifies how many CpGs genome-wide — and specifically in repetitive regions (RepeatMasker repeats, segmental duplications, cenSats) — are covered and haplotype-phased by PacBio CCS/HiFi methylation calls, by intersecting per-haplotype bedmethyl outputs from ccsmethphase with T2T-CHM13 repeat annotations. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how many CpGs genome-wide — and specifically in repetitive regions (RepeatMasker repeats, segmental duplications, cenSats) — are covered and haplotype-phased by PacBio CCS/HiFi methylation calls, by intersecting per-haplotype bedmethyl outputs from ccsmethphase with T2T-CHM13 repeat annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detection of hemimethylated CpGs — CCS-based methods like ccsmeth consider only symmetric methylation and are incapable of detecting hemimethylated CpGs. The target modification is non-CpG 5mC or another DNA modification such as 6mA — the models and CpG-intersection workflow do not apply. Only primary chromosomes chr1-22,X,Y matter and speed is preferred — running with include_all_ctgs=true is unnecessary overhead compared to the default false.

skills.description: Use when a consensus SV call set (e.g. a merged VCF such as the 315-call set accepted by at least two callers) must be reduced by dropping calls whose breakpoints overlap repeats, low complexity regions, or annotated LTRs before manual inspection.
skills.name: repeat-region-overlap-filtering
skills.search_text: repeat-region-overlap-filtering Use when a consensus SV call set (e.g. a merged VCF such as the 315-call set accepted by at least two callers) must be reduced by dropping calls whose breakpoints overlap repeats, low complexity regions, or annotated LTRs before manual inspection. Input is raw per-caller SV predictions before the SURVIVOR merge step has produced the consensus set — the merge (at-least-two-callers) step comes first The next step is manual vetting by visual inspection of read alignments — this filtering only precedes, and does not replace, that curation The goal is maximizing sensitivity to detect all SVs — this study explicitly prioritized high specificity over high sensitivity, so filtering removes true but unreliable calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Removes structural variant calls whose breakpoints fall in low complexity regions or previously annotated long terminal repeats (LTRs), as applied to the 315-call consensus SV set in the fission yeast S. pombe study prior to manual curation. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Removes structural variant calls whose breakpoints fall in low complexity regions or previously annotated long terminal repeats (LTRs), as applied to the 315-call consensus SV set in the fission yeast S. pombe study prior to manual curation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw per-caller SV predictions before the SURVIVOR merge step has produced the consensus set — the merge (at-least-two-callers) step comes first The next step is manual vetting by visual inspection of read alignments — this filtering only precedes, and does not replace, that curation The goal is maximizing sensitivity to detect all SVs — this study explicitly prioritized high specificity over high sensitivity, so filtering removes true but unreliable calls

skills.description: Use when a NanoSV-generated SV call set in VCF format (e.g. 36,959 or 36,321 initial genome-wide calls, or 3957 NA12878 chr1 calls) must be reduced by removing breakpoints overlapping homopolymer/simple-repeat regions before downstream classification.
skills.name: repeat-region-sv-annotation
skills.search_text: repeat-region-sv-annotation Use when a NanoSV-generated SV call set in VCF format (e.g. 36,959 or 36,321 initial genome-wide calls, or 3957 NA12878 chr1 calls) must be reduced by removing breakpoints overlapping homopolymer/simple-repeat regions before downstream classification. Input is raw nanopore BAM/FASTQ that has not yet been called with NanoSV — SV calling must precede repeat-region filtering The goal is discovery of retrotransposon insertions or other repeat-associated novel SVs, which this filter deliberately discards The call set has already passed the repeat/homopolymer filter stage — re-running would double-filter and reduce counts below the reported 657/654 or 8578/6791 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Intersects NanoSV structural-variant breakpoint positions with homopolymer and simple/tandem-repeat region annotations to discard SV calls whose breakpoints fall inside such repeats, producing the intermediate call sets (e.g. 8578 and 6791 SVs for Patient 1 and 2) that precede random-forest high-confidence filtering. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Intersects NanoSV structural-variant breakpoint positions with homopolymer and simple/tandem-repeat region annotations to discard SV calls whose breakpoints fall inside such repeats, producing the intermediate call sets (e.g. 8578 and 6791 SVs for Patient 1 and 2) that precede random-forest high-confidence filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore BAM/FASTQ that has not yet been called with NanoSV — SV calling must precede repeat-region filtering The goal is discovery of retrotransposon insertions or other repeat-associated novel SVs, which this filter deliberately discards The call set has already passed the repeat/homopolymer filter stage — re-running would double-filter and reduce counts below the reported 657/654 or 8578/6791

skills.description: Use when tumor/control long-read data has yielded full-length inserted sequences (nanomonsv.result.txt) and you must classify each insertion by mobile element class and characterize its structural properties (inversion, transduction source, TSD).
skills.name: repeatmasker-annotation-quantification
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-annotation-quantification Use when tumor/control long-read data has yielded full-length inserted sequences (nanomonsv.result.txt) and you must classify each insertion by mobile element class and characterize its structural properties (inversion, transduction source, TSD). When the inserted sequence significantly matches a Gencode transcript — those insertions should be classified as processed pseudogenes, not RepeatMasker element classes For long repeat expansion events (VNTR/microsatellite expansions) — the article notes the reference-genome-based framework may not capture them reliably When only one breakpoint is detectable and the other lies in a highly repetitive region — this is the Single breakend SV module's problem, not MEI classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Classifies somatic mobile element insertions (LINE1, Alu, SVA) from nanomonsv's full-length inserted sequences by applying RepeatMasker annotation plus Gencode transcript matching, and quantifies 5' truncations, internal inversions, polyA/polyT tails, target site duplications, and LINE1 3' transductions. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Classifies somatic mobile element insertions (LINE1, Alu, SVA) from nanomonsv's full-length inserted sequences by applying RepeatMasker annotation plus Gencode transcript matching, and quantifies 5' truncations, internal inversions, polyA/polyT tails, target site duplications, and LINE1 3' transductions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the inserted sequence significantly matches a Gencode transcript — those insertions should be classified as processed pseudogenes, not RepeatMasker element classes For long repeat expansion events (VNTR/microsatellite expansions) — the article notes the reference-genome-based framework may not capture them reliably When only one breakpoint is detectable and the other lies in a highly repetitive region — this is the Single breakend SV module's problem, not MEI classification

skills.description: Use when benchmarking uTR (or another mosaic tandem repeat decomposer) against RepeatMasker on simulated mosaic TR fasta datasets, or when collecting RepeatMasker wall-clock execution times for a runtime comparison table.
skills.name: repeatmasker-command-line-execution
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-command-line-execution Use when benchmarking uTR (or another mosaic tandem repeat decomposer) against RepeatMasker on simulated mosaic TR fasta datasets, or when collecting RepeatMasker wall-clock execution times for a runtime comparison table. The goal is to decompose mosaic TRs themselves — RepeatMasker is only a baseline comparator and, per the paper, often fails to properly decompose mosaic TRs The input is real long-read data without a correct answer pattern, where the test_public accuracy-checking workflow (check_RepeatMasker) does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Runs RepeatMasker as a baseline tandem repeat annotator on simulated mosaic tandem repeat (TR) datasets from the uTR benchmark, using the paper's exact HMMER-based invocation, and parses/checks its output for accuracy and runtime comparison against uTR and TRF. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Runs RepeatMasker as a baseline tandem repeat annotator on simulated mosaic tandem repeat (TR) datasets from the uTR benchmark, using the paper's exact HMMER-based invocation, and parses/checks its output for accuracy and runtime comparison against uTR and TRF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to decompose mosaic TRs themselves — RepeatMasker is only a baseline comparator and, per the paper, often fails to properly decompose mosaic TRs The input is real long-read data without a correct answer pattern, where the test_public accuracy-checking workflow (check_RepeatMasker) does not apply

skills.description: Use when RepeatMasker has been run on simulated tandem repeat FASTA files (e.g. with 'repeatmasker -e hmmer -noint -pa 4 -div 0 -xsmall $TR_file') and the raw predictions must be converted to pattern-level counts scored against known mosaic TR ground truth.
skills.name: repeatmasker-output-parsing
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-output-parsing Use when RepeatMasker has been run on simulated tandem repeat FASTA files (e.g. with 'repeatmasker -e hmmer -noint -pa 4 -div 0 -xsmall $TR_file') and the raw predictions must be converted to pattern-level counts scored against known mosaic TR ground truth. The goal is to score uTR's own decompositions — use check_uTR instead of parse_RepeatMasker/check_RepeatMasker The RepeatMasker run was executed with parameters other than the benchmark settings ('-e hmmer -noint -pa 4 -div 0 -xsmall'), since the checker's allowances were calibrated for this configuration http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parse the raw output of RepeatMasker runs on simulated mosaic tandem repeat FASTA datasets and score the parsed predictions against ground-truth patterns, enabling benchmarking of RepeatMasker's prediction accuracy against uTR in the uTR test_public pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Parse the raw output of RepeatMasker runs on simulated mosaic tandem repeat FASTA datasets and score the parsed predictions against ground-truth patterns, enabling benchmarking of RepeatMasker's prediction accuracy against uTR in the uTR test_public pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to score uTR's own decompositions — use check_uTR instead of parse_RepeatMasker/check_RepeatMasker The RepeatMasker run was executed with parameters other than the benchmark settings ('-e hmmer -noint -pa 4 -div 0 -xsmall'), since the checker's allowances were calibrated for this configuration

skills.description: Use when nanomonsv's Single breakend SV module has produced PASS single breakend calls and each breakpoint's distal side must be characterized as satellite- or simple-repeat-bound (e.g., centromeric rearrangements).
skills.name: repeatmasker-satellite-annotation
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-satellite-annotation Use when nanomonsv's Single breakend SV module has produced PASS single breakend calls and each breakpoint's distal side must be characterized as satellite- or simple-repeat-bound (e.g., centromeric rearrangements). Both breakpoints of the SV are already resolved by the Canonical SV module — RepeatMasker contig annotation is only needed for single breakends where one side is unresolvable Both breakpoints lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive reference regions — the Single breakend SV module itself cannot detect such events The question is long repeat expansion detection (VNTR/microsatellite expansions) — the reference-genome-based framework is not appropriate for those http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies nanomonsv single breakend SVs by realigning the assembled contig sequence after the breakpoint to the reference genome and annotating it with RepeatMasker to label events bound to alpha satellite, human satellite, or simple repeat sequences. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Classifies nanomonsv single breakend SVs by realigning the assembled contig sequence after the breakpoint to the reference genome and annotating it with RepeatMasker to label events bound to alpha satellite, human satellite, or simple repeat sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Both breakpoints of the SV are already resolved by the Canonical SV module — RepeatMasker contig annotation is only needed for single breakends where one side is unresolvable Both breakpoints lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive reference regions — the Single breakend SV module itself cannot detect such events The question is long repeat expansion detection (VNTR/microsatellite expansions) — the reference-genome-based framework is not appropriate for those

skills.description: Use when generating or curating a truth callset of non-reference transposable element insertions from long-read assemblies or read-level candidate insertions, and per-family TE labels with divergence/length filtering are needed for benchmarking.
skills.name: repeatmasker-te-annotation
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-te-annotation Use when generating or curating a truth callset of non-reference transposable element insertions from long-read assemblies or read-level candidate insertions, and per-family TE labels with divergence/length filtering are needed for benchmarking. The goal is de novo TE insertion detection from long reads rather than annotating/labeling already-extracted candidate insertions — use a caller like sTELLeR directly (it takes --bam, --ref, --TE_fasta and outputs a VCF). The analysis targets ancient/divergent TE insertions, since the <15% consensus-divergence filter is designed specifically to enrich for recent, intact insertions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Annotate candidate insertion sequences with RepeatMasker by aligning them against TE consensus sequences to assign TE family labels (Alu, L1, HERV, SVA), then filter for recent intact insertions using a divergence and family-specific length thresholds. This is the approach used to build assembly-based truth callsets for benchmarking long-read TE callers like sTELLeR. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Annotate candidate insertion sequences with RepeatMasker by aligning them against TE consensus sequences to assign TE family labels (Alu, L1, HERV, SVA), then filter for recent intact insertions using a divergence and family-specific length thresholds. This is the approach used to build assembly-based truth callsets for benchmarking long-read TE callers like sTELLeR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo TE insertion detection from long reads rather than annotating/labeling already-extracted candidate insertions — use a caller like sTELLeR directly (it takes --bam, --ref, --TE_fasta and outputs a VCF). The analysis targets ancient/divergent TE insertions, since the <15% consensus-divergence filter is designed specifically to enrich for recent, intact insertions.

skills.description: Use when you have a long-read (e.g., MinION NanoSV) SV VCF plus matched short-read call sets and want to characterize which novel SVs overlap repeats or retrotransposon insertions.
skills.name: repetitive-element-annotation-of-sv-breakpoints
skills.search_text: repetitive-element-annotation-of-sv-breakpoints Use when you have a long-read (e.g., MinION NanoSV) SV VCF plus matched short-read call sets and want to characterize which novel SVs overlap repeats or retrotransposon insertions. The input call set is already intersected with short-read calls, so a novelty comparison would double-count shared variants The sequencing data are not human patient genomes with matched short-read data from the same individuals, since the shared-vs-specific classification requires both call sets on the same reference genome The goal is de novo complex rearrangement (e.g., chromothripsis) breakpoint resolution, which requires read-based phasing rather than repeat-content annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates nanopore-derived structural variant call sets with repeat content from UCSC RepeatMasker and DFAM to flag retrotransposon/LINE insertions, and contrasts GC content and size distributions of nanopore-specific versus shared SVs. This distinguishes novel long-read-only variants—largely retrotransposon insertions—from those detectable by short-read Illumina calling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Annotates nanopore-derived structural variant call sets with repeat content from UCSC RepeatMasker and DFAM to flag retrotransposon/LINE insertions, and contrasts GC content and size distributions of nanopore-specific versus shared SVs. This distinguishes novel long-read-only variants—largely retrotransposon insertions—from those detectable by short-read Illumina calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input call set is already intersected with short-read calls, so a novelty comparison would double-count shared variants The sequencing data are not human patient genomes with matched short-read data from the same individuals, since the shared-vs-specific classification requires both call sets on the same reference genome The goal is de novo complex rearrangement (e.g., chromothripsis) breakpoint resolution, which requires read-based phasing rather than repeat-content annotation

skills.description: Use when nanopore R10.4 reads have been methylation-called and you need per-read or haplotype-resolved CpG methylation plots over transposable-element/repetitive loci (L1HS, AluYa5) or imprinted regions.
skills.name: repetitive-element-methylation-visualization
skills.search_text: repetitive-element-methylation-visualization Use when nanopore R10.4 reads have been methylation-called and you need per-read or haplotype-resolved CpG methylation plots over transposable-element/repetitive loci (L1HS, AluYa5) or imprinted regions. Input is short-read BS-seq or array methylation data — this skill requires single-molecule nanopore signal, not converted reads Methylation motifs other than CpG (DeepBAM is a CpG-specific caller with motif CG) Allele-specific visualization on unphased reads lacking haplotype tags — haplotype-level tracks cannot be built http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Visualize allele-specific CpG methylation patterns at repetitive elements (e.g., L1HS LINE-1 and AluYa5 SINE) using single-molecule methylation calls from DeepBAM on Oxford Nanopore R10.4 reads, optionally split by parental haplotype. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Visualize allele-specific CpG methylation patterns at repetitive elements (e.g., L1HS LINE-1 and AluYa5 SINE) using single-molecule methylation calls from DeepBAM on Oxford Nanopore R10.4 reads, optionally split by parental haplotype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read BS-seq or array methylation data — this skill requires single-molecule nanopore signal, not converted reads Methylation motifs other than CpG (DeepBAM is a CpG-specific caller with motif CG) Allele-specific visualization on unphased reads lacking haplotype tags — haplotype-level tracks cannot be built

skills.description: Use when preparing HiFi read alignments against a repetitive draft assembly (e.g., a T2T or HiFiasm primary assembly) for NextPolish2 polishing, where you need winnowmap's -W repetitive k-mer list instead of plain minimap2 masking.
skills.name: repetitive-kmer-identification
skills.search_text: repetitive-kmer-identification Use when preparing HiFi read alignments against a repetitive draft assembly (e.g., a T2T or HiFiasm primary assembly) for NextPolish2 polishing, where you need winnowmap's -W repetitive k-mer list instead of plain minimap2 masking. The reference is low in segmental duplications or tandem repeats — minimap2 alone (-ax map-hifi/-ax map-pb) suffices and avoids the meryl counting step You are using meryl databases built with canu 1.8 or earlier — the rewritten meryl is not compatible with old .mcdat/.mcidx formats You need a k-mer set for quality-value (QV) estimation or Merqury/yak-based evaluation rather than for mapping — those workflows use yak k-mer datasets (k21/k31), not the winnowmap -W list http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Identifies highly repetitive k-mers in a HiFi-derived draft assembly using meryl (k=15, distinct>0.9998) and supplies them to winnowmap via -W so that repetitive references — centromeric satellites, segmental duplications, large tandem repeats — are seeded correctly during HiFi read alignment for polishing. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Identifies highly repetitive k-mers in a HiFi-derived draft assembly using meryl (k=15, distinct>0.9998) and supplies them to winnowmap via -W so that repetitive references — centromeric satellites, segmental duplications, large tandem repeats — are seeded correctly during HiFi read alignment for polishing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference is low in segmental duplications or tandem repeats — minimap2 alone (-ax map-hifi/-ax map-pb) suffices and avoids the meryl counting step You are using meryl databases built with canu 1.8 or earlier — the rewritten meryl is not compatible with old .mcdat/.mcidx formats You need a k-mer set for quality-value (QV) estimation or Merqury/yak-based evaluation rather than for mapping — those workflows use yak k-mer datasets (k21/k31), not the winnowmap -W list

skills.description: Use when a plant genome (e.g., A. thaliana TAIR10.1 or O. sativa IRGSP-1.0) has Nanopore-derived per-cytosine methylation frequencies and you must quantify 5mC in highly repetitive regions where short-read bisulfite sequencing fails to map reads.
skills.name: repetitive-region-methylation-analysis
skills.search_text: repetitive-region-methylation-analysis Use when a plant genome (e.g., A. thaliana TAIR10.1 or O. sativa IRGSP-1.0) has Nanopore-derived per-cytosine methylation frequencies and you must quantify 5mC in highly repetitive regions where short-read bisulfite sequencing fails to map reads. Your goal is single-base 5mC calling from raw Nanopore signals rather than comparing methylation between duplicated regions — use DeepSignal-plant call_mods/call_freq directly instead. The genome has few segmental duplications under the 100 bp / 0.99 identity threshold, so the repeat-pair table would be too sparse for pair-level statistics. You lack per-cytosine methylation frequencies from both technologies being compared; repeat pairs alone cannot support the |rmet1 - rmet2| >= 0.5 differential call. http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Identifies segmental-duplication repeat pairs by whole-genome self-alignment with MUMmer (length >= 100, identity >= 0.99, containing cytosines), then tests cytosine methylation differences between paired regions to compare Nanopore-based 5mC profiling (via DeepSignal-plant) against bisulfite sequencing in repetitive genome regions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-26278-9
skills.summary: Identifies segmental-duplication repeat pairs by whole-genome self-alignment with MUMmer (length >= 100, identity >= 0.99, containing cytosines), then tests cytosine methylation differences between paired regions to compare Nanopore-based 5mC profiling (via DeepSignal-plant) against bisulfite sequencing in repetitive genome regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is single-base 5mC calling from raw Nanopore signals rather than comparing methylation between duplicated regions — use DeepSignal-plant call_mods/call_freq directly instead. The genome has few segmental duplications under the 100 bp / 0.99 identity threshold, so the repeat-pair table would be too sparse for pair-level statistics. You lack per-cytosine methylation frequencies from both technologies being compared; repeat pairs alone cannot support the |rmet1 - rmet2| >= 0.5 differential call.

skills.description: Use when PAIso-seq CCS reads have been tail-called per transcript and you need per-gene non-A ratios across replicates plus a replicate-correlation check (Fig. 2c) to validate the 17% internal non-A finding.
skills.name: replicate-correlation-of-polya-composition
skills.search_text: replicate-correlation-of-polya-composition Use when PAIso-seq CCS reads have been tail-called per transcript and you need per-gene non-A ratios across replicates plus a replicate-correlation check (Fig. 2c) to validate the 17% internal non-A finding. Estimating the frequency of non-A residues at the very last 3′-end base of the tail — PAIso-seq cannot accurately quantify terminal non-A modifications because terminal G/C/U pair to the adaptor and are lost Short-read poly(A) tail data (e.g. TAIL-seq-style or Illumina PAL-seq) that cannot resolve tail bodies or tails longer than ~231–250 nt Datasets without multiple biological replicates (e.g. a single oocyte library), where per-gene ratio correlation cannot be assessed http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates internally detected U/G/C residues in PAIso-seq poly(A) tails to per-gene non-A ratios across sequencing replicates of mouse GV oocytes, and assesses replicate correlation (Fig. 2c) to validate the reported 17% of mRNAs harboring internal non-A residues. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Aggregates internally detected U/G/C residues in PAIso-seq poly(A) tails to per-gene non-A ratios across sequencing replicates of mouse GV oocytes, and assesses replicate correlation (Fig. 2c) to validate the reported 17% of mRNAs harboring internal non-A residues.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Estimating the frequency of non-A residues at the very last 3′-end base of the tail — PAIso-seq cannot accurately quantify terminal non-A modifications because terminal G/C/U pair to the adaptor and are lost Short-read poly(A) tail data (e.g. TAIL-seq-style or Illumina PAL-seq) that cannot resolve tail bodies or tails longer than ~231–250 nt Datasets without multiple biological replicates (e.g. a single oocyte library), where per-gene ratio correlation cannot be assessed

skills.description: Use when quantifying how many DNVs survive and what fraction of a full-coverage DNV callset is recovered as sequencing depth is reduced, e.g. 10x/20x/30x downsampling of BAM/CRAM trios.
skills.name: replicate-count-aggregation-across-coverage-depths
skills.search_text: replicate-count-aggregation-across-coverage-depths Use when quantifying how many DNVs survive and what fraction of a full-coverage DNV callset is recovered as sequencing depth is reduced, e.g. 10x/20x/30x downsampling of BAM/CRAM trios. Input is already a full-coverage callset and the goal is DNV characterization rather than depth sensitivity — use acorn directly instead Only existing VCFs are available with no BAM/CRAM access — downsampled reruns require aligned reads; use HAT-FLEX for VCF-only trios The data are not from a parent-child trio or not from highly accurate reads (Illumina short-read or PacBio HiFi) Aggregates de novo variant (DNV) counts and confirmation rates across seeded downsampling replicates of a PacBio HiFi trio at multiple depths (10x, 20x, 30x) to determine the minimum per-sample coverage needed for reliable DNV calling with HAT/Tortoise. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775
skills.summary: Aggregates de novo variant (DNV) counts and confirmation rates across seeded downsampling replicates of a PacBio HiFi trio at multiple depths (10x, 20x, 30x) to determine the minimum per-sample coverage needed for reliable DNV calling with HAT/Tortoise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a full-coverage callset and the goal is DNV characterization rather than depth sensitivity — use acorn directly instead Only existing VCFs are available with no BAM/CRAM access — downsampled reruns require aligned reads; use HAT-FLEX for VCF-only trios The data are not from a parent-child trio or not from highly accurate reads (Illumina short-read or PacBio HiFi)

skills.description: Use when several nanopore dRNA replicates have been processed through Dogme and you need per-replicate modkit BED counts merged across plus/minus strands, averaged per modification type, and checked against reported values.
skills.name: replicate-count-aggregation-and-reproducibility-checking
skills.search_text: replicate-count-aggregation-and-reproducibility-checking Use when several nanopore dRNA replicates have been processed through Dogme and you need per-replicate modkit BED counts merged across plus/minus strands, averaged per modification type, and checked against reported values. When you only have a single sample/run and no replicates to compare — the aggregation and cross-replicate reproducibility check has no basis When modification sites have not yet been extracted and filtered with modkit (raw modBAMs, unfiltered BEDs, or basecalled-only FASTQs are the wrong inputs) When the goal is transcript quantification (kallisto/LR-Kallisto outputs) rather than modification site counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregates per-replicate RNA modification site counts (m6A, m5C, inosine, pseudouridine, Nm) from Dogme/modkit BED outputs across ONT direct RNA replicates, computes per-sample averages, and compares them against reported targets to verify reproducibility of the pipeline's modification profiles. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Aggregates per-replicate RNA modification site counts (m6A, m5C, inosine, pseudouridine, Nm) from Dogme/modkit BED outputs across ONT direct RNA replicates, computes per-sample averages, and compares them against reported targets to verify reproducibility of the pipeline's modification profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only have a single sample/run and no replicates to compare — the aggregation and cross-replicate reproducibility check has no basis When modification sites have not yet been extracted and filtered with modkit (raw modBAMs, unfiltered BEDs, or basecalled-only FASTQs are the wrong inputs) When the goal is transcript quantification (kallisto/LR-Kallisto outputs) rather than modification site counts

skills.description: Use when full-length PAIso-seq CCS reads have been mapped and gene-assigned per library, and you need to report mappable transcript counts and gene coverage per replicate for QC or comparison.
skills.name: replicate-count-summarization
skills.search_text: replicate-count-summarization Use when full-length PAIso-seq CCS reads have been mapped and gene-assigned per library, and you need to report mappable transcript counts and gene coverage per replicate for QC or comparison. Input is raw subread BAM or untrimmed CCS BAM that has not been demultiplexed, adapter-trimmed, and gene-assigned by the run.pl pipeline The goal is poly(A) tail length or non-A residue analysis rather than transcript detection counts per replicate http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Tabulates per-replicate detected full-length transcript counts and total genes covered after CCS generation, trimming, concatemer splitting, and gene assignment in PAIso-seq GV oocyte libraries, yielding the summary detection table. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Tabulates per-replicate detected full-length transcript counts and total genes covered after CCS generation, trimming, concatemer splitting, and gene assignment in PAIso-seq GV oocyte libraries, yielding the summary detection table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw subread BAM or untrimmed CCS BAM that has not been demultiplexed, adapter-trimmed, and gene-assigned by the run.pl pipeline The goal is poly(A) tail length or non-A residue analysis rather than transcript detection counts per replicate

skills.description: Use when short-read and long-read BAM alignments of the same mRNA vaccine transcript are available and you need to quantify coverage homogeneity, per-nucleotide error profiles, and consensus accuracy across replicates or chemistries.
skills.name: replicate-coverage-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: replicate-coverage-correlation-analysis Use when short-read and long-read BAM alignments of the same mRNA vaccine transcript are available and you need to quantify coverage homogeneity, per-nucleotide error profiles, and consensus accuracy across replicates or chemistries. You need to measure mRNA chemistry or nucleoside modifications (e.g. N1-methylpseudouridine), which requires direct RNA sequencing rather than alignment-based coverage comparison The alignment BAMs come from plasmid-template sequencing quality checks where the poly(A) tail region is not the target of the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Compares per-nucleotide coverage and error profiles of Illumina TruSeq and ONT cDNA alignments over an mRNA vaccine transcript — especially the low-complexity 3' poly(A) tail — using Mana, and validates coverage homogeneity by checking that replicate Illumina coverage profiles correlate with R2 approximately 0.99. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Compares per-nucleotide coverage and error profiles of Illumina TruSeq and ONT cDNA alignments over an mRNA vaccine transcript — especially the low-complexity 3' poly(A) tail — using Mana, and validates coverage homogeneity by checking that replicate Illumina coverage profiles correlate with R2 approximately 0.99.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to measure mRNA chemistry or nucleoside modifications (e.g. N1-methylpseudouridine), which requires direct RNA sequencing rather than alignment-based coverage comparison The alignment BAMs come from plasmid-template sequencing quality checks where the poly(A) tail region is not the target of the comparison

Input is single-cell or bulk cDNA quantification without replicate structure rather than per-replicate dRNA transcript quantification The goal is modification-site counting (m6A, m5C, inosine, pseudouridine, Nm) rather than transcript isoform classification counts Only one sample is available, so replicate-level concordance cannot be assessed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregate per-replicate transcript detection and classification counts (known, ISM, NIC, NNC) from Dogme/LR-Kallisto outputs on dRNA MinION replicates into a validation-checked table (transcript_class_counts.csv). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Aggregate per-replicate transcript detection and classification counts (known, ISM, NIC, NNC) from Dogme/LR-Kallisto outputs on dRNA MinION replicates into a validation-checked table (transcript_class_counts.csv).
