skills.description: Use when replicate-capable m6A tools (ELIGOS, Yanocomp, DiffErr, Nanocompore, drummer, differr) are run on multi-replicate dRNA-seq data and you need to know whether merging replicates alters the detected m6A site set, or how the two configurations overlap.
skills.name: replicate-merge-configuration-comparison
skills.search_text: replicate-merge-configuration-comparison Use when replicate-capable m6A tools (ELIGOS, Yanocomp, DiffErr, Nanocompore, drummer, differr) are run on multi-replicate dRNA-seq data and you need to know whether merging replicates alters the detected m6A site set, or how the two configurations overlap. The dataset has only a single replicate per condition, so there is no separate-versus-merged choice to compare. The tools of interest are not replicate-capable multi-sample tools (e.g. single-sample tools cannot exploit the replicate configuration difference). You lack the base-called fast5 folder structure and SK1 genome/transcriptome annotation required by the NanOlympicsMod pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 A method for testing how presenting replicate Nanopore dRNA-seq data as separate samples versus a single merged sample changes the m6A hits reported by replicate-capable multi-sample tools, and quantifying the per-tool overlap between the two configurations using the NanOlympicsMod Nextflow pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: A method for testing how presenting replicate Nanopore dRNA-seq data as separate samples versus a single merged sample changes the m6A hits reported by replicate-capable multi-sample tools, and quantifying the per-tool overlap between the two configurations using the NanOlympicsMod Nextflow pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has only a single replicate per condition, so there is no separate-versus-merged choice to compare. The tools of interest are not replicate-capable multi-sample tools (e.g. single-sample tools cannot exploit the replicate configuration difference). You lack the base-called fast5 folder structure and SK1 genome/transcriptome annotation required by the NanOlympicsMod pipeline.

skills.description: Use when you have per-replicate modkit-extracted modification BED tables from >=2 (typically 3) nanopore dRNA replicates and need to count sites/genes conserved across all replicates per modification type.
skills.name: replicate-modification-site-intersection
skills.search_text: replicate-modification-site-intersection Use when you have per-replicate modkit-extracted modification BED tables from >=2 (typically 3) nanopore dRNA replicates and need to count sites/genes conserved across all replicates per modification type. Input is raw POD5 or unfiltered modBAM — the site tables must first be produced by the Dogme/modkit extract-and-filter steps (params.minCov, params.perMod thresholds via filterbed.py). The goal is a statistical differential-modification test between conditions rather than strict three-replicate conservation counting of the same genomic site coordinates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies reproducibility of nanopore RNA modification calls by strictly intersecting per-replicate modkit BED site coordinates across three biological replicates (e.g. the three mouse C2C12 dRNA replicates of ENCSR160HKZ) and counting shared sites per modification type (m6A, m5C, inosine, pseudouridine, Nm). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Quantifies reproducibility of nanopore RNA modification calls by strictly intersecting per-replicate modkit BED site coordinates across three biological replicates (e.g. the three mouse C2C12 dRNA replicates of ENCSR160HKZ) and counting shared sites per modification type (m6A, m5C, inosine, pseudouridine, Nm).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw POD5 or unfiltered modBAM — the site tables must first be produced by the Dogme/modkit extract-and-filter steps (params.minCov, params.perMod thresholds via filterbed.py). The goal is a statistical differential-modification test between conditions rather than strict three-replicate conservation counting of the same genomic site coordinates.

skills.name: replicate-number-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: replicate-number-sensitivity-analysis Decision support for planning Nanodynamo or similar RNA-kinetics experiments: when you must choose how many sequencing replicates suffice for reliable rate inference before committing wet-lab budget. Input is real experimental data rather than simulated data — this skill quantifies the in silico relationship between replicate count and rate-inference correlation, not accuracy on an existing experimental dataset. The question is nascent-RA read depth/saturation rather than replicate count — use the nascentSaturation.R analysis (Figure S3) instead. You need per-gene coupling or post-transcriptional processing analyses (couplings.R, fractionsReadsClassification.R), not experimental-design optimisation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Empirical replicate-count optimisation for Nanodynamo kinetic inference: simulate in silico metabolic-labelling datasets at a fixed 20-minute labelling time with 1–5 replicates, fit the kinetic model to each setting, and quantify the plateau in correlation between inferred and real synthesis/processing/degradation rates. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Empirical replicate-count optimisation for Nanodynamo kinetic inference: simulate in silico metabolic-labelling datasets at a fixed 20-minute labelling time with 1–5 replicates, fit the kinetic model to each setting, and quantify the plateau in correlation between inferred and real synthesis/processing/degradation rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental data rather than simulated data — this skill quantifies the in silico relationship between replicate count and rate-inference correlation, not accuracy on an existing experimental dataset. The question is nascent-RA read depth/saturation rather than replicate count — use the nascentSaturation.R analysis (Figure S3) instead. You need per-gene coupling or post-transcriptional processing analyses (couplings.R, fractionsReadsClassification.R), not experimental-design optimisation.

skills.search_text: reported-fraction-verification Use when validating reported percentages of undetected known variants located in homopolymer runs or STRs, where undetected sets are defined by combinations of Illumina, PacBio, and ONT caller failures against a truth VCF. Input is raw caller VCF output that has not yet been intersected with the GIAB/1KGp3 truth set to define the undetected-variant classes The reference genome build does not match the truth-set build (e.g., GRCh37 truth variants queried against GRCh38), since flank extraction would be misaligned The goal is de novo variant discovery rather than characterizing why known truth variants were missed http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Recomputes the fractions of known (GIAB/1KGp3 truth) variants undetected by Illumina, PacBio, and/or Oxford Nanopore variant callers that lie in homopolymer runs or short tandem repeats, and checks the recomputed percentages against the reported values (26.67% homopolymer / 29.45% STR of 12,331 variants missed by all three technologies; 57.67% / 18.54% of 178,331 missed by PacBio+ONT). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Recomputes the fractions of known (GIAB/1KGp3 truth) variants undetected by Illumina, PacBio, and/or Oxford Nanopore variant callers that lie in homopolymer runs or short tandem repeats, and checks the recomputed percentages against the reported values (26.67% homopolymer / 29.45% STR of 12,331 variants missed by all three technologies; 57.67% / 18.54% of 178,331 missed by PacBio+ONT).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw caller VCF output that has not yet been intersected with the GIAB/1KGp3 truth set to define the undetected-variant classes The reference genome build does not match the truth-set build (e.g., GRCh37 truth variants queried against GRCh38), since flank extraction would be misaligned The goal is de novo variant discovery rather than characterizing why known truth variants were missed

skills.search_text: rna-modification-co-occurrence-analysis Use when you have per-read modification predictions for two modification types (e.g. CHEUI-solo m6A and m5C calls) on the same direct RNA reads and want to test single-molecule co-occurrence at pairs of modified sites 1–15 nt apart. The input is only site-level (stoichiometry) data with no per-read modification calls — single-molecule co-occurrence cannot be computed without read-level state at both sites. Transcripts carry only one tested modification site — pairs at 1–15 nt distance cannot be formed, so co-occurrence is undefined. skills.search_text: rna-secondary-structure-prediction Use when single-molecule SHAPE reactivity profiles (nanoSHAPE or SHAPE-MaP) for a specific RNA are available and the goal is to test whether constrained folding recovers expected structural elements (e.g., miRNA hairpins). Input is already a folded structure model or base-pair set — use structure comparison/PPV tools directly instead of refolding No experimental probing data and no unmodified control exists — a nanoSHAPE/SHAPE-MaP sample-compare constraint cannot be derived; an NPD fold alone is the only option The target is a short RNA far shorter than needed for nanopore reads — short-read SHAPE-MaP approaches may be sufficient and simpler http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Generate secondary structure models for a target RNA by folding its sequence with SHAPE-derived pseudo-free energy constraints — comparing nanoSHAPE- and SHAPE-MaP-constrained predictions against no-probing-data (NPD) folds to quantify how probing data shifts the structural ensemble. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: Generate secondary structure models for a target RNA by folding its sequence with SHAPE-derived pseudo-free energy constraints — comparing nanoSHAPE- and SHAPE-MaP-constrained predictions against no-probing-data (NPD) folds to quantify how probing data shifts the structural ensemble.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a folded structure model or base-pair set — use structure comparison/PPV tools directly instead of refolding No experimental probing data and no unmodified control exists — a nanoSHAPE/SHAPE-MaP sample-compare constraint cannot be derived; an NPD fold alone is the only option The target is a short RNA far shorter than needed for nanopore reads — short-read SHAPE-MaP approaches may be sufficient and simpler

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires a ground-truth RNA-Seq dataset with known transcript provenance, so assembler completeness (95%-assembled genes/isoforms), accuracy (misassemblies), and duplication ratio can be evaluated against a reference transcriptome.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-simulation-with-rsem
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-simulation-with-rsem Use when a benchmark requires a ground-truth RNA-Seq dataset with known transcript provenance, so assembler completeness (95%-assembled genes/isoforms), accuracy (misassemblies), and duplication ratio can be evaluated against a reference transcriptome. The goal is to benchmark on real data where transcript provenance is unknown — the article uses real datasets (SRR5133163, SRR1957703/SRR1957706, SRX648736, SRR1560107, SRR1588569, SRR5344669/SRR5344670) separately from the simulated ones The application is metatranscriptome assembly — the article states the approach 'was initially designed for RNA-Seq data obtained from a single organism' and that metatranscriptomic quality evaluation is future work Only assembly contiguity or reference-free quality is of interest — the article warns that 'high database coverage or nucleotide recall can be achieved by a very fragmented assembly (or even raw reads)' Generates synthetic RNA-Seq read sets with the RSEM read simulator using the exact command lines from Supplementary Section S3, producing controlled benchmark inputs (e.g., the Human simulated dataset) for de novo transcriptome assembler comparison. Simulated reads allow assembler output to be scored against a known reference transcriptome with rnaQUAST metrics such as 95%-assembled genes/isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, and duplication ratio. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Generates synthetic RNA-Seq read sets with the RSEM read simulator using the exact command lines from Supplementary Section S3, producing controlled benchmark inputs (e.g., the Human simulated dataset) for de novo transcriptome assembler comparison. Simulated reads allow assembler output to be scored against a known reference transcriptome with rnaQUAST metrics such as 95%-assembled genes/isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, and duplication ratio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark on real data where transcript provenance is unknown — the article uses real datasets (SRR5133163, SRR1957703/SRR1957706, SRX648736, SRR1560107, SRR1588569, SRR5344669/SRR5344670) separately from the simulated ones The application is metatranscriptome assembly — the article states the approach 'was initially designed for RNA-Seq data obtained from a single organism' and that metatranscriptomic quality evaluation is future work Only assembly contiguity or reference-free quality is of interest — the article warns that 'high database coverage or nucleotide recall can be achieved by a very fragmented assembly (or even raw reads)'

skills.description: Use when the starting point is NCBI SRA accession numbers (SRR/SRX) for the paper's single-organism RNA-Seq datasets and paired-end FASTQ files are needed to launch rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, or other transcriptome assemblers.
skills.name: rna-seq-sra-read-acquisition
skills.search_text: rna-seq-sra-read-acquisition Use when the starting point is NCBI SRA accession numbers (SRR/SRX) for the paper's single-organism RNA-Seq datasets and paired-end FASTQ files are needed to launch rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, or other transcriptome assemblers. If the reads are already local FASTQ files — acquisition is unnecessary and assembly/evaluation should start directly. If the data are Oxford Nanopore or PacBio long reads: the article notes their high error rate prevents using output reads directly as complete transcripts, and SPAdes is primarily developed for Illumina data. If the target is metatranscriptome assembly — the paper explicitly states the approach was initially designed for RNA-Seq data obtained from a single organism and only potentially applicable to metatranscriptomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Retrieves the paired-end RNA-Seq FASTQ reads used in the rnaSPAdes benchmarking (Human large SRR1957703/SRR1957706, Arabidopsis SRR5344669/SRR5344670, plus Human SRR5133163, Mouse SRX648736, Worm SRR1560107, Corn SRR1588569) from NCBI SRA so the compared assemblers can be run and timed on the paper's datasets. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Retrieves the paired-end RNA-Seq FASTQ reads used in the rnaSPAdes benchmarking (Human large SRR1957703/SRR1957706, Arabidopsis SRR5344669/SRR5344670, plus Human SRR5133163, Mouse SRX648736, Worm SRR1560107, Corn SRR1588569) from NCBI SRA so the compared assemblers can be run and timed on the paper's datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the reads are already local FASTQ files — acquisition is unnecessary and assembly/evaluation should start directly. If the data are Oxford Nanopore or PacBio long reads: the article notes their high error rate prevents using output reads directly as complete transcripts, and SPAdes is primarily developed for Illumina data. If the target is metatranscriptome assembly — the paper explicitly states the approach was initially designed for RNA-Seq data obtained from a single organism and only potentially applicable to metatranscriptomes.

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblers across datasets with different gene-detection depths, especially when raw counts of assembled genes are unfair and a Kallisto-normalized fraction of 95%-assembled genes is needed for cross-dataset ranking.
skills.name: rna-seq-transcriptome-assembly-benchmarking
skills.search_text: rna-seq-transcriptome-assembly-benchmarking Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblers across datasets with different gene-detection depths, especially when raw counts of assembled genes are unfair and a Kallisto-normalized fraction of 95%-assembled genes is needed for cross-dataset ranking. Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the article notes the approach was designed for RNA-Seq from a single organism and that an appropriate metatranscriptomic quality-evaluation pipeline is future work Ranking assemblers by contiguity-only metrics such as database coverage or nucleotide recall — the article warns these can be achieved by very fragmented assemblies or even raw reads Datasets lacking a reference genome and gene annotations, since rnaQUAST-based 95%-assembled gene counting is reference-dependent http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks de novo transcriptome assemblers (rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) across multiple real RNA-Seq datasets by combining rnaQUAST assembly-completeness counts (95%-assembled genes) with Kallisto-based gene detection, yielding a detection-normalized fraction that is comparable across datasets and assemblers. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Benchmarks de novo transcriptome assemblers (rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) across multiple real RNA-Seq datasets by combining rnaQUAST assembly-completeness counts (95%-assembled genes) with Kallisto-based gene detection, yielding a detection-normalized fraction that is comparable across datasets and assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the article notes the approach was designed for RNA-Seq from a single organism and that an appropriate metatranscriptomic quality-evaluation pipeline is future work Ranking assemblers by contiguity-only metrics such as database coverage or nucleotide recall — the article warns these can be achieved by very fragmented assemblies or even raw reads Datasets lacking a reference genome and gene annotations, since rnaQUAST-based 95%-assembled gene counting is reference-dependent

skills.description: Use when aligned ONT direct RNA reads (BAM) against an mRNA reference are available and you need a total error rate plus mismatch/deletion/insertion decomposition, or to compare dRNA-specific per-nucleotide error biases against matched plasmid/cDNA sequencing.
skills.name: rna-sequence-error-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-error-rate-quantification Use when aligned ONT direct RNA reads (BAM) against an mRNA reference are available and you need a total error rate plus mismatch/deletion/insertion decomposition, or to compare dRNA-specific per-nucleotide error biases against matched plasmid/cDNA sequencing. The goal is consensus sequence identity confirmation rather than error-rate estimation — the authors found cDNA sequencing more reliable than direct RNA sequencing for identity calls Only short-read Illumina data is available, since this skill is grounded in ONT alignment analysis via Mana and pysamstats You need an error rate including the poly(A) tail — this method explicitly excludes the poly(A) region, where dRNA shows deletion of low-quality nucleotides http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify the mean per-nucleotide sequencing error rate of Oxford Nanopore direct RNA reads (e.g. SQK-RNA002 on an eGFP mRNA vaccine) and decompose it into mismatch, deletion and insertion classes using Minimap2, SAMtools, Mana and pysamstats, while excluding the poly(A) tail. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Quantify the mean per-nucleotide sequencing error rate of Oxford Nanopore direct RNA reads (e.g. SQK-RNA002 on an eGFP mRNA vaccine) and decompose it into mismatch, deletion and insertion classes using Minimap2, SAMtools, Mana and pysamstats, while excluding the poly(A) tail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is consensus sequence identity confirmation rather than error-rate estimation — the authors found cDNA sequencing more reliable than direct RNA sequencing for identity calls Only short-read Illumina data is available, since this skill is grounded in ONT alignment analysis via Mana and pysamstats You need an error rate including the poly(A) tail — this method explicitly excludes the poly(A) region, where dRNA shows deletion of low-quality nucleotides

skills.description: Use when per-tool TP/FP/FN bin classifications from an m6A dRNA-seq benchmark need to be explained by sequence context (motif variant, GC, structure, entropy).
skills.name: rna-sequence-feature-computation
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-feature-computation Use when per-tool TP/FP/FN bin classifications from an m6A dRNA-seq benchmark need to be explained by sequence context (motif variant, GC, structure, entropy). When no TP/FP/FN bin classifications from a benchmark run exist yet — features must be computed on already-classified bins When the goal is generic motif scanning of a transcriptome rather than explaining classifier error classes from the m6A benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Characterizes m6A benchmarking bins (true-positive, false-positive, false-negative) by sequence features — RRACH motif variant, GC content, RNAfold minimum free energy, and Shannon entropy — plus de novo motif discovery on FPs, to explain which sequence contexts make m6A easier or harder to detect with dRNA-seq tools. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: Characterizes m6A benchmarking bins (true-positive, false-positive, false-negative) by sequence features — RRACH motif variant, GC content, RNAfold minimum free energy, and Shannon entropy — plus de novo motif discovery on FPs, to explain which sequence contexts make m6A easier or harder to detect with dRNA-seq tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no TP/FP/FN bin classifications from a benchmark run exist yet — features must be computed on already-classified bins When the goal is generic motif scanning of a transcriptome rather than explaining classifier error classes from the m6A benchmark

skills.description: Use when simulating ONT direct-RNA (RNA004) nanopore signals from a transcriptome where per-transcript abundance and truncation profiles must be honored, e.g. reproducing HG002-RNA004 experiments.
skills.name: rna-transcript-abundance-simulation
skills.search_text: rna-transcript-abundance-simulation Use when simulating ONT direct-RNA (RNA004) nanopore signals from a transcriptome where per-transcript abundance and truncation profiles must be honored, e.g. reproducing HG002-RNA004 experiments. Input is DNA genomic data — use the ont_r1041_dna_5khz preset workflow instead of the RNA004 preset and transcript profile Simulating from already-basecalled reads rather than a transcriptome reference — use Read mode without the abundance TSV The analysis does not require transcript abundance/truncation fidelity and uniform read sampling is acceptable — omit --trans-profile rather than supplying a fabricated profile http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulate direct-RNA nanopore signals (RNA004) with transcript-specific abundance and truncation using NanoSimFormer's --trans-profile 3-column TSV and the ont_rna004_4khz preset, enabling abundance-faithful synthetic transcriptomic signal data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Simulate direct-RNA nanopore signals (RNA004) with transcript-specific abundance and truncation using NanoSimFormer's --trans-profile 3-column TSV and the ont_rna004_4khz preset, enabling abundance-faithful synthetic transcriptomic signal data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is DNA genomic data — use the ont_r1041_dna_5khz preset workflow instead of the RNA004 preset and transcript profile Simulating from already-basecalled reads rather than a transcriptome reference — use Read mode without the abundance TSV The analysis does not require transcript abundance/truncation fidelity and uniform read sampling is acceptable — omit --trans-profile rather than supplying a fabricated profile

skills.description: Use when benchmarking de novo transcriptome assemblers (e.g., rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) on real RNA-Seq datasets and you need a completeness metric comparable across organisms and datasets.
skills.name: rnaquast-95-percent-assembled-gene-metric-computation
skills.search_text: rnaquast-95-percent-assembled-gene-metric-computation Use when benchmarking de novo transcriptome assemblers (e.g., rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) on real RNA-Seq datasets and you need a completeness metric comparable across organisms and datasets. The goal is contiguity assessment alone — high database coverage or nucleotide recall can be achieved by very fragmented assemblies (or even raw reads), so this completeness metric must not be used as a proxy for assembly contiguity No reference gene annotations are available — rnaQUAST-based 95%-assembled gene counting is a reference-based evaluation Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the approach was designed for RNA-Seq data from a single organism, and metatranscriptomic quality evaluation remains future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes the fraction of 95%-assembled genes for each de novo transcriptome assembly using rnaQUAST against reference gene annotations, then normalizes per dataset by the number of Kallisto-detected genes (nucleotide coverage > 5) to enable fair cross-dataset assembler comparison. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Computes the fraction of 95%-assembled genes for each de novo transcriptome assembly using rnaQUAST against reference gene annotations, then normalizes per dataset by the number of Kallisto-detected genes (nucleotide coverage > 5) to enable fair cross-dataset assembler comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is contiguity assessment alone — high database coverage or nucleotide recall can be achieved by very fragmented assemblies (or even raw reads), so this completeness metric must not be used as a proxy for assembly contiguity No reference gene annotations are available — rnaQUAST-based 95%-assembled gene counting is a reference-based evaluation Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the approach was designed for RNA-Seq data from a single organism, and metatranscriptomic quality evaluation remains future work

skills.description: Use when you have de novo transcriptome contigs (e.g. rnaSPAdes/Trinity output) plus a reference annotation and need quality metrics such as 95%-assembled genes, isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, or duplication ratio.
skills.name: rnaquast-assembly-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: rnaquast-assembly-quality-evaluation Use when you have de novo transcriptome contigs (e.g. rnaSPAdes/Trinity output) plus a reference annotation and need quality metrics such as 95%-assembled genes, isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, or duplication ratio. Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the paper states no appropriate quality-evaluation pipeline for metatranscriptomic assemblies was designed and designing one is future work Judging assembly contiguity from database coverage or nucleotide recall alone, since these metrics can be maximized by very fragmented assemblies or raw reads Comparing against Detonate scores expecting perfect agreement — the absence of a mapped-fraction cutoff in rnaQUAST means the two metrics do not perfectly correlate http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Evaluate de novo transcriptome assemblies with rnaQUAST against a reference transcriptome, extracting 95%-assembled genes/isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, and duplication ratio. This is the benchmarking approach used to rank rnaSPAdes against Trinity, RNA-Bloom, Trans-ABySS and other assemblers in the rnaSPAdes paper. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Evaluate de novo transcriptome assemblies with rnaQUAST against a reference transcriptome, extracting 95%-assembled genes/isoforms, database coverage, misassemblies, and duplication ratio. This is the benchmarking approach used to rank rnaSPAdes against Trinity, RNA-Bloom, Trans-ABySS and other assemblers in the rnaSPAdes paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating metatranscriptome assemblies — the paper states no appropriate quality-evaluation pipeline for metatranscriptomic assemblies was designed and designing one is future work Judging assembly contiguity from database coverage or nucleotide recall alone, since these metrics can be maximized by very fragmented assemblies or raw reads Comparing against Detonate scores expecting perfect agreement — the absence of a mapped-fraction cutoff in rnaQUAST means the two metrics do not perfectly correlate

skills.description: Use when starting from FASTQ RNA-Seq reads (single-organism Illumina data, e.g. NCBI SRA accessions like SRR5133163) and a de novo transcriptome assembly with metrics such as 95%-assembled genes/isoforms is required.
skills.name: rnaseq-de-novo-transcriptome-assembly
skills.search_text: rnaseq-de-novo-transcriptome-assembly Use when starting from FASTQ RNA-Seq reads (single-organism Illumina data, e.g. NCBI SRA accessions like SRR5133163) and a de novo transcriptome assembly with metrics such as 95%-assembled genes/isoforms is required. Input is metatranscriptomic data — the approach was initially designed for RNA-Seq from a single organism and metatranscriptome assembly quality evaluation remains unaddressed Input is raw long RNA reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) alone — their high error rate prevents using output reads directly as complete transcripts; long reads are only suitable as supplementary data in hybrid mode Goal is short-read-only analysis with zero duplication — SPAdes/rnaSPAdes output carries duplicated sequences (mean duplication ratio 32% for rnaSPAdes vs 2% for SPAdes) that can harm downstream gene annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 De novo assembly of Illumina RNA-Seq reads into transcript contigs using rnaSPAdes, a de Bruijn graph assembler built on SPAdes that handles non-uniform coverage via iterative multi-k construction, and subsequent quality evaluation with rnaQUAST. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: De novo assembly of Illumina RNA-Seq reads into transcript contigs using rnaSPAdes, a de Bruijn graph assembler built on SPAdes that handles non-uniform coverage via iterative multi-k construction, and subsequent quality evaluation with rnaQUAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is metatranscriptomic data — the approach was initially designed for RNA-Seq from a single organism and metatranscriptome assembly quality evaluation remains unaddressed Input is raw long RNA reads (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) alone — their high error rate prevents using output reads directly as complete transcripts; long reads are only suitable as supplementary data in hybrid mode Goal is short-read-only analysis with zero duplication — SPAdes/rnaSPAdes output carries duplicated sequences (mean duplication ratio 32% for rnaSPAdes vs 2% for SPAdes) that can harm downstream gene annotation

skills.description: Use when you have PacBio IsoSeq and Illumina RNA-seq reads from the same organism and a reference genome, and need to compare IsoSeq-only, merged, and Illumina-only transcriptome assemblies.
skills.name: rnaseq-read-alignment-hybrid-assembly
skills.search_text: rnaseq-read-alignment-hybrid-assembly Use when you have PacBio IsoSeq and Illumina RNA-seq reads from the same organism and a reference genome, and need to compare IsoSeq-only, merged, and Illumina-only transcriptome assemblies. The organism lacks an assembled reference genome and an NCBI annotation in GTF format, since the genome-guided assembly and annotation strategy cannot be applied. The goal is annotation of predicted proteins or coding/lncRNA classification of assembled transcripts — that is handled downstream by the annotate_my_genomes pipeline, not by this alignment/assembly step. Only de novo (reference-free) assembly is possible because no reference genome is available for the reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Generates a genome-guided hybrid transcriptome assembly by aligning PacBio IsoSeq and trimmed Illumina reads to a reference genome (galGal6), merging the alignments into a single BAM, and assembling transcripts with StringTie for downstream Ex90N50 and BUSCO (aves_odb10) comparison. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Generates a genome-guided hybrid transcriptome assembly by aligning PacBio IsoSeq and trimmed Illumina reads to a reference genome (galGal6), merging the alignments into a single BAM, and assembling transcripts with StringTie for downstream Ex90N50 and BUSCO (aves_odb10) comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism lacks an assembled reference genome and an NCBI annotation in GTF format, since the genome-guided assembly and annotation strategy cannot be applied. The goal is annotation of predicted proteins or coding/lncRNA classification of assembled transcripts — that is handled downstream by the annotate_my_genomes pipeline, not by this alignment/assembly step. Only de novo (reference-free) assembly is possible because no reference genome is available for the reads.

skills.description: Use when Illumina short-read FASTQ files (e.g. ENA PRJEB36584) must be adapter- and quality-trimmed prior to genome-guided spliced alignment with HISAT2 in a hybrid long-read/short-read transcriptome assembly workflow.
skills.name: rnaseq-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: rnaseq-read-quality-trimming Use when Illumina short-read FASTQ files (e.g. ENA PRJEB36584) must be adapter- and quality-trimmed prior to genome-guided spliced alignment with HISAT2 in a hybrid long-read/short-read transcriptome assembly workflow. Long PacBio reads (ENA PRJEB36569) — these are aligned directly with minimap2, not trimmed with fastp Reads already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered by upstream processing Assemblies or BAM files rather than raw reads — trimming only applies to FASTQ input http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quality-trim Illumina short reads with fastp before genome alignment, as done in the chicken SCO hybrid RNA-seq workflow where fastp-trimmed reads were aligned to galGal6 with HISAT2 to build the merged PacBio+Illumina BAM assembly input. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Quality-trim Illumina short reads with fastp before genome alignment, as done in the chicken SCO hybrid RNA-seq workflow where fastp-trimmed reads were aligned to galGal6 with HISAT2 to build the merged PacBio+Illumina BAM assembly input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Long PacBio reads (ENA PRJEB36569) — these are aligned directly with minimap2, not trimmed with fastp Reads already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered by upstream processing Assemblies or BAM files rather than raw reads — trimming only applies to FASTQ input

skills.description: Use when comparing binary variant classifiers (pathogenic vs benign) on labeled ClinVar or HGMD variant sets and you need ROC curves and AUC values per method per test subset.
skills.name: roc-auc-computation
skills.search_text: roc-auc-computation Use when comparing binary variant classifiers (pathogenic vs benign) on labeled ClinVar or HGMD variant sets and you need ROC curves and AUC values per method per test subset. The task is variant calling, annotation, or prioritization rather than benchmarking a pathogenicity classifier (use the eDiVA-Predict/Annotate/Prioritize pipeline instead) Variant labels lack binary TP/TN definitions (e.g. no 'pathogenic' vs 'benign' ClinVar labels or HGMD DM/DM? categories), since ROC/AUC is undefined without class labels Only a single classifier is scored without competing methods, making ROC comparison across tools pointless Computes receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) to benchmark variant pathogenicity classifiers such as eDiVA-Score against CADD, DANN, Eigen, Revel, M-CAP, and MetaLR on ClinVar/HGMD test sets with defined TP/TN subsets. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772
skills.summary: Computes receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) to benchmark variant pathogenicity classifiers such as eDiVA-Score against CADD, DANN, Eigen, Revel, M-CAP, and MetaLR on ClinVar/HGMD test sets with defined TP/TN subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is variant calling, annotation, or prioritization rather than benchmarking a pathogenicity classifier (use the eDiVA-Predict/Annotate/Prioritize pipeline instead) Variant labels lack binary TP/TN definitions (e.g. no 'pathogenic' vs 'benign' ClinVar labels or HGMD DM/DM? categories), since ROC/AUC is undefined without class labels Only a single classifier is scored without competing methods, making ROC comparison across tools pointless

skills.description: Use when you have per-read posterior modification probabilities from a binary RNA-modification classifier (e.g. CHEUI Model 1 on IVT reads) and need to report accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC-AUC to validate or benchmark the model.
skills.name: roc-auc-evaluation
skills.search_text: roc-auc-evaluation Use when you have per-read posterior modification probabilities from a binary RNA-modification classifier (e.g. CHEUI Model 1 on IVT reads) and need to report accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC-AUC to validate or benchmark the model. Evaluating site-level stoichiometry or differential methylation (CHEUI Model 2 or CHEUI-diff outputs), where read-level AUC is not the appropriate metric Classifying 9-mer contexts with multiple modifiable bases (multiple A's or C's), which are excluded from the IVT test design Benchmarking tools that only output site-level calls without per-read probabilities, since ROC-AUC cannot be computed without score distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Compute per-read classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, and AUC) from posterior modification probabilities produced by CHEUI-solo Model 1 on in-vitro transcript (IVT) test sets, to benchmark single-molecule m6A and m5C prediction performance against reported figures. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Compute per-read classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, and AUC) from posterior modification probabilities produced by CHEUI-solo Model 1 on in-vitro transcript (IVT) test sets, to benchmark single-molecule m6A and m5C prediction performance against reported figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating site-level stoichiometry or differential methylation (CHEUI Model 2 or CHEUI-diff outputs), where read-level AUC is not the appropriate metric Classifying 9-mer contexts with multiple modifiable bases (multiple A's or C's), which are excluded from the IVT test design Benchmarking tools that only output site-level calls without per-read probabilities, since ROC-AUC cannot be computed without score distributions

skills.description: Use when a held-out independent test set (e.g. PDB186, 93 DBPs + 93 non-DBPs) must be scored by a pre-trained SVM and its Acc/Sn/Sp/MCC/AUC benchmarked against published predictor comparisons.
skills.name: roc-auc-performance-comparison-across-predictors
skills.search_text: roc-auc-performance-comparison-across-predictors Use when a held-out independent test set (e.g. PDB186, 93 DBPs + 93 non-DBPs) must be scored by a pre-trained SVM and its Acc/Sn/Sp/MCC/AUC benchmarked against published predictor comparisons. The goal is cross-validated performance on the training benchmarks (Jackknife test on PDB1075/PDB594) rather than an independent test — use the train_1075 workflow instead of Independent_test.m Input sequences lack precomputed PSSM profiles or feature workspace .mat files, so the 3240-dimension multi-view feature space (DDE, PSSM-DBT with T=3, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC with nlag=30) cannot be assembled http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reproduces an independent-validation benchmark of iDBP-DEP on PDB186: train the RBF-kernel SVM (C=1, gamma=0.03125) on PDB1075 top-424 feature vectors, predict PDB186 labels, compute Acc/Sn/Sp/MCC/AUC, and compare against alternative predictors (Local-DPP, DBPPred, etc.) as in Table 8. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Reproduces an independent-validation benchmark of iDBP-DEP on PDB186: train the RBF-kernel SVM (C=1, gamma=0.03125) on PDB1075 top-424 feature vectors, predict PDB186 labels, compute Acc/Sn/Sp/MCC/AUC, and compare against alternative predictors (Local-DPP, DBPPred, etc.) as in Table 8.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cross-validated performance on the training benchmarks (Jackknife test on PDB1075/PDB594) rather than an independent test — use the train_1075 workflow instead of Independent_test.m Input sequences lack precomputed PSSM profiles or feature workspace .mat files, so the 3240-dimension multi-view feature space (DDE, PSSM-DBT with T=3, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC with nlag=30) cannot be assembled

skills.description: Use when you have native (modified) and IVT (unmodified) direct RNA nanopore fast5 datasets for a transcript with known modification annotations (e.g. rRNA Nm, Ψ, base sites) and need to call/localize modification positions from raw-signal KS statistics.
skills.name: rrna-modification-site-annotation
skills.search_text: rrna-modification-site-annotation Use when you have native (modified) and IVT (unmodified) direct RNA nanopore fast5 datasets for a transcript with known modification annotations (e.g. rRNA Nm, Ψ, base sites) and need to call/localize modification positions from raw-signal KS statistics. You have no IVT/unmodified control sample — the paper notes identification without an IVT comparison would require training sets of known modifications in all possible kmer sequence contexts, which do not yet exist. Your goal is de novo modification classification independent of prior annotation rather than localizing sites to a known rRNA modification map. Input is already a per-position statistics table requiring no raw-signal processing (use downstream profiling/correlation skills instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Localizes RNA modification sites by comparing per-position Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics of nanopore ionic-current and dwell-time distributions between native and IVT-control direct RNA reads, then tabulating called KS-peak positions against annotated E. coli / S. cerevisiae rRNA modification maps. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: Localizes RNA modification sites by comparing per-position Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics of nanopore ionic-current and dwell-time distributions between native and IVT-control direct RNA reads, then tabulating called KS-peak positions against annotated E. coli / S. cerevisiae rRNA modification maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no IVT/unmodified control sample — the paper notes identification without an IVT comparison would require training sets of known modifications in all possible kmer sequence contexts, which do not yet exist. Your goal is de novo modification classification independent of prior annotation rather than localizing sites to a known rRNA modification map. Input is already a per-position statistics table requiring no raw-signal processing (use downstream profiling/correlation skills instead).

skills.description: Use when executing or reproducing a published pipeline (e.g. streamed minimap2-to-HLAminer HLA typing) and you need to verify that wall-clock runtime scales as reported for a given dataset, such as ~40 minutes for 10x ONT WGS.

The goal is per-read alignment speed of minimap2 alone (e.g. aligner benchmarking), rather than end-to-end runtime of the piped alignment-into-prediction protocol. The pipeline is short-read Illumina-based HPTASR assembly, whose runtime profile and stages differ from the streamed long-read HPRA workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Measure wall-clock runtime and resource usage of a multi-stage bioinformatics protocol (e.g. streaming minimap2 alignments into HLAminer) using /usr/bin/time -v, so runtimes can be compared against published expectations and dataset coverage. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Measure wall-clock runtime and resource usage of a multi-stage bioinformatics protocol (e.g. streaming minimap2 alignments into HLAminer) using /usr/bin/time -v, so runtimes can be compared against published expectations and dataset coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has drastically different coverage or read chemistry (e.g. PacBio HiFi instead of older-chemistry ONT), so published runtimes like ~40 minutes at 10x are not comparable baselines. The pipeline is short-read Illumina-based HPTASR assembly, whose runtime profile and stages differ from the streamed long-read HPRA workflow.

The goal is calling insertion or base-substitution variants — the source study only covers deletion variant calling, and the downstream DASV model is deletion-specific Input data are already filtered call sets (e.g. VCF deletion calls) rather than read-level SAM/BAM alignments — re-filtering has no effect on variant-level output Working with short-read NGS data where paired-end mapping or depth-based callers (e.g. ReadDepth, BreakDancer) rather than CIGAR-based long-read deletion calling is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quality-control step that removes poorly aligned or multimapped sequenced fragments from SAM/BAM alignment files before downstream structural-variant feature extraction. In the DASV deletion-calling pipeline this filtering is the precondition for reliable CIGAR-based deletion feature framing. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: Quality-control step that removes poorly aligned or multimapped sequenced fragments from SAM/BAM alignment files before downstream structural-variant feature extraction. In the DASV deletion-calling pipeline this filtering is the precondition for reliable CIGAR-based deletion feature framing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling insertion or base-substitution variants — the source study only covers deletion variant calling, and the downstream DASV model is deletion-specific Input data are already filtered call sets (e.g. VCF deletion calls) rather than read-level SAM/BAM alignments — re-filtering has no effect on variant-level output Working with short-read NGS data where paired-end mapping or depth-based callers (e.g. ReadDepth, BreakDancer) rather than CIGAR-based long-read deletion calling is intended

skills.description: Use when mapped FLNC SAM alignments (e.g. isoseq_flnc.Transcript.sam) must be position-sorted before cDNA_Cupcake collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py can collapse redundant isoforms.
skills.name: sam-coordinate-sorting
skills.search_text: sam-coordinate-sorting Use when mapped FLNC SAM alignments (e.g. isoseq_flnc.Transcript.sam) must be position-sorted before cDNA_Cupcake collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py can collapse redundant isoforms. Input alignments are already position-sorted (e.g. minimap2 output piped through samtools sort) and the downstream tool accepts sorted or coordinate-grouped input directly The task is splice-junction annotation comparison (gffcompare/filter.tmap.pl) rather than isoform collapsing — that step uses the unsorted SAM converted to GFF via sam2gff.pl http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Sort the SAM file of mapped HIT-scISOseq FLNC alignments by chromosome and start coordinate so that the cDNA_Cupcake collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py script can merge reads with matching splice junctions into nonredundant isoform models. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Sort the SAM file of mapped HIT-scISOseq FLNC alignments by chromosome and start coordinate so that the cDNA_Cupcake collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py script can merge reads with matching splice junctions into nonredundant isoform models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments are already position-sorted (e.g. minimap2 output piped through samtools sort) and the downstream tool accepts sorted or coordinate-grouped input directly The task is splice-junction annotation comparison (gffcompare/filter.tmap.pl) rather than isoform collapsing — that step uses the unsorted SAM converted to GFF via sam2gff.pl

skills.description: Reference for interpreting SAM alignment flags and auxiliary tags when scanning synthetic long-read (SLR) BAMs to identify badly aligned read pairs or group reads by BX barcodes.
skills.name: sam-flag-and-tag-parsing
skills.search_text: sam-flag-and-tag-parsing Reference for interpreting SAM alignment flags and auxiliary tags when scanning synthetic long-read (SLR) BAMs to identify badly aligned read pairs or group reads by BX barcodes. Input is not an indexed SLR BAM with BX tags — Blackbird's -b input requires position-sorted and indexed reads with barcode tags The goal is to keep all reads for assembly, e.g. when invoking Blackbird with the -n option which skips collecting poorly aligned reads The reads are plain short reads without barcode information, where barcode-aware retrieval M(B) has no meaning http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parses SAM/BAM alignment flags and auxiliary tags (AM, BX) to flag badly aligned read pairs in position-sorted SLR BAM files and to key barcoded reads into Blackbird's read map M for later barcode-based retrieval. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Parses SAM/BAM alignment flags and auxiliary tags (AM, BX) to flag badly aligned read pairs in position-sorted SLR BAM files and to key barcoded reads into Blackbird's read map M for later barcode-based retrieval.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not an indexed SLR BAM with BX tags — Blackbird's -b input requires position-sorted and indexed reads with barcode tags The goal is to keep all reads for assembly, e.g. when invoking Blackbird with the -n option which skips collecting poorly aligned reads The reads are plain short reads without barcode information, where barcode-aware retrieval M(B) has no meaning

skills.description: Use when a scaffolding-graph pipeline must convert alignment-free read-to-contig placements into standard SAM pair records that short-read scaffolders can consume, or when validating Fast-SG's -p output.
skills.name: sam-format-pair-location-output
skills.search_text: sam-format-pair-location-output Use when a scaffolding-graph pipeline must convert alignment-free read-to-contig placements into standard SAM pair records that short-read scaffolders can consume, or when validating Fast-SG's -p output. You need full base-level alignments with mapping quality and CIGAR strings — Fast-SG reports only pair locations, not alignments. Linking information comes from long-range technologies with unknown read-pair orientation and mixed insert sizes (e.g. 10X Genomics, DOVETAIL), where gap-size estimation from these SAM pairs is documented as challenging. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Emits Fast-SG's alignment-free read placement results as a SAM-format file of pair locations under the -p output prefix, using SAM flags to distinguish single (1) versus paired (2) read configurations so downstream scaffolders can build the scaffolding graph. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Emits Fast-SG's alignment-free read placement results as a SAM-format file of pair locations under the -p output prefix, using SAM flags to distinguish single (1) versus paired (2) read configurations so downstream scaffolders can build the scaffolding graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need full base-level alignments with mapping quality and CIGAR strings — Fast-SG reports only pair locations, not alignments. Linking information comes from long-range technologies with unknown read-pair orientation and mixed insert sizes (e.g. 10X Genomics, DOVETAIL), where gap-size estimation from these SAM pairs is documented as challenging.

skills.description: Use when a long-read (nanopore/PacBio) WGS FASTQ must be typed for HLA class I and II alleles and the aligner output is SAM with MD tags — e.g., substituting a non-minimap2 aligner in the HLAminer streaming protocol.
skills.name: sam-md-tag-alignment-annotation
skills.search_text: sam-md-tag-alignment-annotation Use when a long-read (nanopore/PacBio) WGS FASTQ must be typed for HLA class I and II alleles and the aligner output is SAM with MD tags — e.g., substituting a non-minimap2 aligner in the HLAminer streaming protocol. Short Illumina-sized reads — the HPTASR targeted-assembly mode (reads ≥100 bp, ideally 150 bp) is the recommended route, not SAM streaming from long-read aligners The input is already a completed SAM/BAM alignment without MD tags — MD tags are required for the streaming protocol; re-alignment or re-tagging is needed first A bulky intermediate alignment file must be archived anyway — this skill's rationale (in-memory piping) is moot if the SAM must be stored, though it still functions http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Streams SAM-formatted long-read alignments (with MD tags) directly from any SAM-compatible read aligner into HLAminer v1.4 to predict HLA-I and -II allele groups, avoiding intermediate SAM files on disk. Enables aligner-agnostic HLA typing from ONT PromethION or PacBio whole-genome shotgun data via a single Unix pipe. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Streams SAM-formatted long-read alignments (with MD tags) directly from any SAM-compatible read aligner into HLAminer v1.4 to predict HLA-I and -II allele groups, avoiding intermediate SAM files on disk. Enables aligner-agnostic HLA typing from ONT PromethION or PacBio whole-genome shotgun data via a single Unix pipe.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short Illumina-sized reads — the HPTASR targeted-assembly mode (reads ≥100 bp, ideally 150 bp) is the recommended route, not SAM streaming from long-read aligners The input is already a completed SAM/BAM alignment without MD tags — MD tags are required for the streaming protocol; re-alignment or re-tagging is needed first A bulky intermediate alignment file must be archived anyway — this skill's rationale (in-memory piping) is moot if the SAM must be stored, though it still functions

skills.description: Use when hybrid-correcting long reads and you need per-base questionable-position calls derived from a BWA-MEM alignment of short reads, so downstream consensus or optimization-based correction only touches flagged positions.
skills.name: sam-mismatch-and-indel-detection
skills.search_text: sam-mismatch-and-indel-detection Use when hybrid-correcting long reads and you need per-base questionable-position calls derived from a BWA-MEM alignment of short reads, so downstream consensus or optimization-based correction only touches flagged positions. When there are no aligned short reads (i.e. self-correction such as HGAP-style multiple alignments) — this skill requires a short-read SAM/BAM alignment When positions are already annotated as questionable by a prior HECIL iteration (realign-and-remarking is an iterative step, not a re-parse of raw data) When the goal is de novo assembly of corrected reads (Canu/QUAST evaluation), not base-level questionable-position detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Parses a BWA-MEM SAM/BAM alignment of Illumina short reads against long reads to mark, per long read, every position of disagreement (mismatch, insertion, deletion) as questionable — the prerequisite step in HECIL that feeds the Quick Correction (η = 0.9 consensus) and Optimization-Based Correction stages. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Parses a BWA-MEM SAM/BAM alignment of Illumina short reads against long reads to mark, per long read, every position of disagreement (mismatch, insertion, deletion) as questionable — the prerequisite step in HECIL that feeds the Quick Correction (η = 0.9 consensus) and Optimization-Based Correction stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there are no aligned short reads (i.e. self-correction such as HGAP-style multiple alignments) — this skill requires a short-read SAM/BAM alignment When positions are already annotated as questionable by a prior HECIL iteration (realign-and-remarking is an iterative step, not a re-parse of raw data) When the goal is de novo assembly of corrected reads (Canu/QUAST evaluation), not base-level questionable-position detection

skills.description: Use when running long-read WGS (e.g. ONT PromethION) alignments with minimap2 and you need immediate downstream prediction (HLA typing) without storing large intermediate SAM files.
skills.name: sam-streaming-bioinformatics-pipelines
skills.search_text: sam-streaming-bioinformatics-pipelines Use when running long-read WGS (e.g. ONT PromethION) alignments with minimap2 and you need immediate downstream prediction (HLA typing) without storing large intermediate SAM files. Input reads are short Illumina-sized reads better handled by HLAminer's targeted-assembly HPTASR mode You need to retain or re-examine the raw alignments afterwards — stream mode discards the SAM, so write alignments to disk instead Data are already assembled contigs or an existing alignment file rather than raw sequencing reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3542 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Streams a read aligner's SAM output directly into a downstream analysis tool (HLAminer) via a Unix pipe, avoiding writing bulky .sam files to disk. Used here to derive HLA class I/II predictions from long-read (ONT/PacBio) WGS alignments in a single command. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Streams a read aligner's SAM output directly into a downstream analysis tool (HLAminer) via a Unix pipe, avoiding writing bulky .sam files to disk. Used here to derive HLA class I/II predictions from long-read (ONT/PacBio) WGS alignments in a single command.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina-sized reads better handled by HLAminer's targeted-assembly HPTASR mode You need to retain or re-examine the raw alignments afterwards — stream mode discards the SAM, so write alignments to disk instead Data are already assembled contigs or an existing alignment file rather than raw sequencing reads

skills.description: Use when HLA-I/II allele predictions are needed from long-read WGS data (PacBio HiFi or ONT PromethION) with clinically confirmed HLA types available for validation, and disk space or runtime favors streaming over writing SAM files.
skills.name: sam-streaming-hla-prediction
skills.search_text: sam-streaming-hla-prediction Use when HLA-I/II allele predictions are needed from long-read WGS data (PacBio HiFi or ONT PromethION) with clinically confirmed HLA types available for validation, and disk space or runtime favors streaming over writing SAM files. Input is short Illumina-sized reads — the HPTASR targeted-assembly mode (reads 100bp+, ideally 150bp) is the recommended route for short reads, not streamed long-read HPRA Only HLA class I alleles are needed from targeted RNA-seq or exome capture data with low depth — the original HPTASR or direct-alignment short-read workflows may be more appropriate No HLA reference database update or chr6-masked GRCh38 reference is available and one cannot be prepared, since alignments to endogenous chr6 would confound scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_3534 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Predicts HLA class I and II alleles from whole-genome shotgun long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi or ONT) by streaming minimap2 SAM alignment output directly into HLAminer v1.4 (HPRA mode), avoiding bulky intermediate SAM files on disk. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Predicts HLA class I and II alleles from whole-genome shotgun long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi or ONT) by streaming minimap2 SAM alignment output directly into HLAminer v1.4 (HPRA mode), avoiding bulky intermediate SAM files on disk.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short Illumina-sized reads — the HPTASR targeted-assembly mode (reads 100bp+, ideally 150bp) is the recommended route for short reads, not streamed long-read HPRA Only HLA class I alleles are needed from targeted RNA-seq or exome capture data with low depth — the original HPTASR or direct-alignment short-read workflows may be more appropriate No HLA reference database update or chr6-masked GRCh38 reference is available and one cannot be prepared, since alignments to endogenous chr6 would confound scoring

skills.description: Use when long ONT/PacBio reads have been aligned with Minimap2 (e.g. -ax map-ont --secondary=no) and the downstream tool (AgileStructure) requires a sorted, indexed BAM input.
skills.name: sam-to-bam-conversion-and-indexing
skills.search_text: sam-to-bam-conversion-and-indexing Use when long ONT/PacBio reads have been aligned with Minimap2 (e.g. -ax map-ont --secondary=no) and the downstream tool (AgileStructure) requires a sorted, indexed BAM input. The alignment is still in PAF format from minimap2 without CIGAR/SAM output — convert or re-run with -a first The downstream tool accepts SAM or CRAM directly, making sorting/indexing redundant overhead Short-read data is being processed for SNV/small-indel calling, where this long-read SV workflow does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts Minimap2 long-read SAM alignments to coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM so that desktop SV callers such as AgileStructure can load and browse breakpoint-spanning reads for structural rearrangement annotation. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Converts Minimap2 long-read SAM alignments to coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM so that desktop SV callers such as AgileStructure can load and browse breakpoint-spanning reads for structural rearrangement annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The alignment is still in PAF format from minimap2 without CIGAR/SAM output — convert or re-run with -a first The downstream tool accepts SAM or CRAM directly, making sorting/indexing redundant overhead Short-read data is being processed for SNV/small-indel calling, where this long-read SV workflow does not apply

skills.description: Use when _align.py has emitted per-strand SAM files (output_CT.sam, output_GA.sam) from nanoEM C-to-T and G-to-A alignments and they must become sorted, indexed BAMs for methylation calling.
skills.name: sam-to-bam-conversion-paired-strand-alignments
skills.search_text: sam-to-bam-conversion-paired-strand-alignments Use when _align.py has emitted per-strand SAM files (output_CT.sam, output_GA.sam) from nanoEM C-to-T and G-to-A alignments and they must become sorted, indexed BAMs for methylation calling. Input files are already sorted, indexed BAMs (1.sorted.bam / 2.sorted.bam from minimap2) — these are best_align.py inputs, not its SAM outputs, and must not be re-sorted. You are still at the read-conversion stage with only *_CT.fq.gz / *_GA.fq.gz FASTQs — mapping with minimap2 must happen before this conversion step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Converts the best-alignment SAM outputs of the nanoEM best_align.py step (output_CT.sam and output_GA.sam, one per C-to-T / G-to-A strand) into coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM files so they can feed sambamba mpileup methylation calling and IGV bisulfite visualization. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: Converts the best-alignment SAM outputs of the nanoEM best_align.py step (output_CT.sam and output_GA.sam, one per C-to-T / G-to-A strand) into coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM files so they can feed sambamba mpileup methylation calling and IGV bisulfite visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are already sorted, indexed BAMs (1.sorted.bam / 2.sorted.bam from minimap2) — these are best_align.py inputs, not its SAM outputs, and must not be re-sorted. You are still at the read-conversion stage with only *_CT.fq.gz / *_GA.fq.gz FASTQs — mapping with minimap2 must happen before this conversion step.

skills.description: Use when SAM alignments of PacBio FLNC single-cell reads must be converted to GFF so that gffcompare can compare them against a reference annotation GTF.
skills.name: sam-to-gff-format-conversion
skills.search_text: sam-to-gff-format-conversion Use when SAM alignments of PacBio FLNC single-cell reads must be converted to GFF so that gffcompare can compare them against a reference annotation GTF. Alignments are not from full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) transcript reads or were not produced by splice-aware minimap2 settings — the GFF transcript reconstruction assumes splice-aligned transcript reads Downstream step needs per-read SAM records (e.g. read-level quality or coordinate inspection) rather than collapsed GFF transcript features http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts minimap2 splice-mode SAM alignments of FLNC single-cell reads into GFF format with the sam2gff.pl script (from gpertea/gscripts), a prerequisite for gffcompare-based assignment of FLNC transcripts to annotated genes in the scISA-Tools HIT-scISOseq pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Converts minimap2 splice-mode SAM alignments of FLNC single-cell reads into GFF format with the sam2gff.pl script (from gpertea/gscripts), a prerequisite for gffcompare-based assignment of FLNC transcripts to annotated genes in the scISA-Tools HIT-scISOseq pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Alignments are not from full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) transcript reads or were not produced by splice-aware minimap2 settings — the GFF transcript reconstruction assumes splice-aligned transcript reads Downstream step needs per-read SAM records (e.g. read-level quality or coordinate inspection) rather than collapsed GFF transcript features

skills.description: Use when you need base-level pileup counts at CpG positions from base-converted nanopore BAM alignments (CT and GA strands) as input for CpG methylation frequency calling.
skills.name: sambamba-mpileup-base-counting-at-cpg-sites
skills.search_text: sambamba-mpileup-base-counting-at-cpg-sites Use when you need base-level pileup counts at CpG positions from base-converted nanopore BAM alignments (CT and GA strands) as input for CpG methylation frequency calling. Native (unconverted) nanopore reads where methylation should be called directly from signal, e.g. with nanopolish call-methylation — pileup-based counting of converted bases does not apply. Short-read EMseq/bisulfite data processed with standard short-read aligners; the nanoEM pileup step depends on long-read minimap2 map-ont alignments of converted reads. Whole-genome variant calling at all positions — this setup is deliberately restricted to CpG positions via cpg_sites.bed, not genome-wide. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Restricts sambamba mpileup (v0.7.1, default parameters) to reference-genome CpG sites via a BED file to count bases from the C-to-T and G-to-A converted, best-aligned nanoEM reads, producing per-CpG pileup tables for downstream methylation calling. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab397
skills.summary: Restricts sambamba mpileup (v0.7.1, default parameters) to reference-genome CpG sites via a BED file to count bases from the C-to-T and G-to-A converted, best-aligned nanoEM reads, producing per-CpG pileup tables for downstream methylation calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Native (unconverted) nanopore reads where methylation should be called directly from signal, e.g. with nanopolish call-methylation — pileup-based counting of converted bases does not apply. Short-read EMseq/bisulfite data processed with standard short-read aligners; the nanoEM pileup step depends on long-read minimap2 map-ont alignments of converted reads. Whole-genome variant calling at all positions — this setup is deliberately restricted to CpG positions via cpg_sites.bed, not genome-wide.

skills.description: Use when isoform co-expression clusters (from percentile-correlation clustering) are available and the goal is to detect genes whose isoforms co-vary across cell types (coDIU) beyond gene-level differential usage.
skills.name: same-gene-isoform-pair-selection-from-clusters
skills.search_text: same-gene-isoform-pair-selection-from-clusters Use when isoform co-expression clusters (from percentile-correlation clustering) are available and the goal is to detect genes whose isoforms co-vary across cell types (coDIU) beyond gene-level differential usage. No isoform cluster assignments exist yet — run acorde's percentile-correlation clustering first, since candidate pairs are selected from clusters The input matrix is gene-level rather than isoform-level, so same-gene isoform pairs cannot be formed The aim is plain gene-level differential expression/DIU without testing isoform co-usage coordination http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Screens isoform co-expression clusters for candidate pairs containing at least two same-gene isoforms, then tests them with negative-binomial GLMs (cluster*cell-type vs. gene*cell-type terms) to identify genes with co-differential isoform usage (coDIU) that is not visible at the gene level. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Screens isoform co-expression clusters for candidate pairs containing at least two same-gene isoforms, then tests them with negative-binomial GLMs (cluster*cell-type vs. gene*cell-type terms) to identify genes with co-differential isoform usage (coDIU) that is not visible at the gene level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No isoform cluster assignments exist yet — run acorde's percentile-correlation clustering first, since candidate pairs are selected from clusters The input matrix is gene-level rather than isoform-level, so same-gene isoform pairs cannot be formed The aim is plain gene-level differential expression/DIU without testing isoform co-usage coordination

skills.description: Use when converting aligned Iso-Seq SAM/BAM alignments (from uLTRA or minimap2 mapping of FLNC reads) into a non-redundant per-sample genome annotation in BED12 format.
skills.name: sample-level-transcript-annotation-merging
skills.search_text: sample-level-transcript-annotation-merging Use when converting aligned Iso-Seq SAM/BAM alignments (from uLTRA or minimap2 mapping of FLNC reads) into a non-redundant per-sample genome annotation in BED12 format. Input reads have not yet been mapped to the genome — the pipeline stage expects SAM alignments from uLTRA/minimap2, not raw FLNC FASTA/BAM The goal is a multi-sample consensus annotation rather than a per-sample one — TAMA merge in this workflow combines chunks within a sample, not across samples Only primer/chimera/polyA cleanup is needed (LIMA, isoseq3 refine, TAMA polyA cleanup) — those are upstream filtering steps, not annotation collapsing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Collapse splice-consistent long-read alignments into non-redundant transcript models with TAMA collapse, then merge chunk-level collapsed BED12 annotations into a single per-sample annotation using TAMA merge, as done in the nf-core/isoseq pipeline after uLTRA/minimap2 genome mapping. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: Collapse splice-consistent long-read alignments into non-redundant transcript models with TAMA collapse, then merge chunk-level collapsed BED12 annotations into a single per-sample annotation using TAMA merge, as done in the nf-core/isoseq pipeline after uLTRA/minimap2 genome mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been mapped to the genome — the pipeline stage expects SAM alignments from uLTRA/minimap2, not raw FLNC FASTA/BAM The goal is a multi-sample consensus annotation rather than a per-sample one — TAMA merge in this workflow combines chunks within a sample, not across samples Only primer/chimera/polyA cleanup is needed (LIMA, isoseq3 refine, TAMA polyA cleanup) — those are upstream filtering steps, not annotation collapsing

skills.description: Use when compiling multiple long-read Iso-Seq runs (per-sample SQANTI3 RulesFilter classification.txt files) into a shared, updatable isoSeQL database and each sample's source material and analysis provenance must be captured for cross-sample comparability.
skills.name: sample-metadata-curation
skills.search_text: sample-metadata-curation Use when compiling multiple long-read Iso-Seq runs (per-sample SQANTI3 RulesFilter classification.txt files) into a shared, updatable isoSeQL database and each sample's source material and analysis provenance must be captured for cross-sample comparability. Input is a single sample with no intention of cross-sample comparison — per-sample PB.X.Y IDs and the SQANTI3 classification file alone suffice, so a shared metadata database adds overhead Reads have not yet passed the isoseq > minimap2 > collapse > SQANTI3 RulesFilter pipeline — there are no high-quality filtered isoforms or counts to which sample metadata can be linked The analysis is short-read transcriptomics or de novo assembly without SQANTI3 output — isoSeQL was built specifically to work with SQANTI2/SQANTI3 output http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Curates and records per-sample provenance metadata—cell line/tissue source material, software and reference versions, experiment date, and single-cell barcodes/cell types—into the sampleData, exp, and single-cell tables of an isoSeQL SQLite database (isoseql.db) as SQANTI3-filtered Iso-Seq samples are compiled. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf680
skills.summary: Curates and records per-sample provenance metadata—cell line/tissue source material, software and reference versions, experiment date, and single-cell barcodes/cell types—into the sampleData, exp, and single-cell tables of an isoSeQL SQLite database (isoseql.db) as SQANTI3-filtered Iso-Seq samples are compiled.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single sample with no intention of cross-sample comparison — per-sample PB.X.Y IDs and the SQANTI3 classification file alone suffice, so a shared metadata database adds overhead Reads have not yet passed the isoseq > minimap2 > collapse > SQANTI3 RulesFilter pipeline — there are no high-quality filtered isoforms or counts to which sample metadata can be linked The analysis is short-read transcriptomics or de novo assembly without SQANTI3 output — isoSeQL was built specifically to work with SQANTI2/SQANTI3 output

skills.description: Use when you have matched ONT fast5 datasets from a native (methylated) sample and a WGA (unmethylated) control, resquiggled against a reference genome, and want to de novo identify modified-base motifs from raw signal differences.
skills.name: sample-vs-wga-control-signal-comparison
skills.search_text: sample-vs-wga-control-signal-comparison Use when you have matched ONT fast5 datasets from a native (methylated) sample and a WGA (unmethylated) control, resquiggled against a reference genome, and want to de novo identify modified-base motifs from raw signal differences. You have only a native sample with no WGA control — Snapper's sample comparison requires -control_fast5dir and cannot be applied Reads are not ONT raw-signal fast5 files (e.g. basecalled FASTQ or PacBio data) — the signal-level k-mer comparison depends on resquiggled nanopore signal The goal is per-read per-base modification calling rather than de novo motif discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Detects methylated motifs by comparing raw Oxford Nanopore signal-level k-mer statistics between native (methylated) sample reads and whole-genome-amplified (WGA) control reads, where methylated positions show signal shifts absent in the WGA control. This sample-versus-control comparison underlies both Tombo's sample-comparison mode and Snapper's greedy motif enrichment. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad702
skills.summary: Detects methylated motifs by comparing raw Oxford Nanopore signal-level k-mer statistics between native (methylated) sample reads and whole-genome-amplified (WGA) control reads, where methylated positions show signal shifts absent in the WGA control. This sample-versus-control comparison underlies both Tombo's sample-comparison mode and Snapper's greedy motif enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a native sample with no WGA control — Snapper's sample comparison requires -control_fast5dir and cannot be applied Reads are not ONT raw-signal fast5 files (e.g. basecalled FASTQ or PacBio data) — the signal-level k-mer comparison depends on resquiggled nanopore signal The goal is per-read per-base modification calling rather than de novo motif discovery

skills.search_text: scaling-factor-estimation Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (general or sparse Matrix, e.g. dgCMatrix) exhibit technical biases from sequencing depth, capture efficiency, or dropout, and per-cell scaling factors plus normalized counts are needed without linear count-depth or distributional assumptions. The input is not raw single-cell RNA-seq counts (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, already-normalized expression values, or a feature/summary table) — LocASN expects a count matrix. A method-specific distributional or count-depth assumption is deliberately desired (e.g. reproducing SCnorm or sctransform behavior for comparison); scKWARN's design specifically avoids restrictive model/distribution assumptions, so results are not interchangeable.
