skills.search_text: sequencing-platform-parameter-configuration Use when running VeChat (or its Minimap2 overlap step) on raw long reads and the input platform (PacBio PB or ONT) must be declared so platform-appropriate alignment presets and error models are applied. Input reads are already corrected or are short Illumina reads — VeChat is a self-correction method for noisy long TGS reads (PacBio/ONT) The analysis goal is polishing an assembly rather than correcting raw long reads — Racon is the consensus/polishing module in this toolchain A fixed reference genome exists for correction — VeChat performs haplotype-aware self-correction against ad-hoc variation graphs built from the reads themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Configure sequencing-platform-specific parameters (PacBio vs Oxford Nanopore) when running VeChat's two-cycle long-read error-correction workflow and its Minimap2 overlap stage, since read chemistry and error profiles determine preset choices such as --platform and ava-pb/ava-ont overlap modes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Configure sequencing-platform-specific parameters (PacBio vs Oxford Nanopore) when running VeChat's two-cycle long-read error-correction workflow and its Minimap2 overlap stage, since read chemistry and error profiles determine preset choices such as --platform and ava-pb/ava-ont overlap modes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already corrected or are short Illumina reads — VeChat is a self-correction method for noisy long TGS reads (PacBio/ONT) The analysis goal is polishing an assembly rather than correcting raw long reads — Racon is the consensus/polishing module in this toolchain A fixed reference genome exists for correction — VeChat performs haplotype-aware self-correction against ad-hoc variation graphs built from the reads themselves

skills.description: Use when the same single-cell cDNA libraries (e.g., 10x Genomics corneal limbus samples) have been measured on two sequencing platforms or as independent replicates, and you need numeric concordance statistics to validate reproducibility.
skills.name: sequencing-replicate-reproducibility-assessment
skills.search_text: sequencing-replicate-reproducibility-assessment Use when the same single-cell cDNA libraries (e.g., 10x Genomics corneal limbus samples) have been measured on two sequencing platforms or as independent replicates, and you need numeric concordance statistics to validate reproducibility. The datasets being compared are from different biological samples or different single-cell capture runs, so barcode-level or gene-level correlations would conflate biological with technical variation You need isoform-level concordance rather than gene/UMI count-level agreement; this skill operates on cellBC and gene UMI totals only Count matrices have not been demultiplexed and corrected (e.g., with cellBC_UMI_corrector using the whitelist posterior probability threshold >0.975), so per-cell counts are unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify concordance between HIT-scISOseq (PacBio Sequel II) and Illumina short-read NGS measurements, and between biological replicates, by computing Pearson correlations of UMI counts per cell barcode, per gene, and across replicate count matrices. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Quantify concordance between HIT-scISOseq (PacBio Sequel II) and Illumina short-read NGS measurements, and between biological replicates, by computing Pearson correlations of UMI counts per cell barcode, per gene, and across replicate count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets being compared are from different biological samples or different single-cell capture runs, so barcode-level or gene-level correlations would conflate biological with technical variation You need isoform-level concordance rather than gene/UMI count-level agreement; this skill operates on cellBC and gene UMI totals only Count matrices have not been demultiplexed and corrected (e.g., with cellBC_UMI_corrector using the whitelist posterior probability threshold >0.975), so per-cell counts are unreliable

skills.description: Use when a paper reports per-sample sequencing metrics (read counts, lengths, FLNC/artifact fractions) and the deposited subreads BAM files plus stated processing parameters are available to independently reproduce the table.
skills.name: sequencing-summary-table-reproduction
skills.search_text: sequencing-summary-table-reproduction Use when a paper reports per-sample sequencing metrics (read counts, lengths, FLNC/artifact fractions) and the deposited subreads BAM files plus stated processing parameters are available to independently reproduce the table. The paper does not deposit raw subreads BAM files, so CCS generation cannot be re-run and only summary statistics are available The downstream goal is isoform characterization or quantification (use collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py / SQANTI3 workflows instead of table reproduction) The sequencing platform is not PacBio CCS-based (e.g. Nanopore PromethION reads, where barcode demultiplex efficiency is limited by error rate and the ccs pipeline does not apply) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A benchmarking skill for recomputing the per-sample read-processing metrics reported in a sequencing paper's summary table (e.g. Table 1: CCS read counts, mean CCS read lengths, FLNC counts, artifact cDNA percentages) directly from the deposited raw data using the authors' stated parameters. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for recomputing the per-sample read-processing metrics reported in a sequencing paper's summary table (e.g. Table 1: CCS read counts, mean CCS read lengths, FLNC counts, artifact cDNA percentages) directly from the deposited raw data using the authors' stated parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The paper does not deposit raw subreads BAM files, so CCS generation cannot be re-run and only summary statistics are available The downstream goal is isoform characterization or quantification (use collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py / SQANTI3 workflows instead of table reproduction) The sequencing platform is not PacBio CCS-based (e.g. Nanopore PromethION reads, where barcode demultiplex efficiency is limited by error rate and the ccs pipeline does not apply)

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered IsoPops database of full-length PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoforms with per-isoform abundances and need to quantify and rank which genes express the most diverse isoform portfolios.
skills.name: shannon-diversity-index-calculation
skills.search_text: shannon-diversity-index-calculation Use when you have a filtered IsoPops database of full-length PacBio lrCaptureSeq isoforms with per-isoform abundances and need to quantify and rank which genes express the most diverse isoform portfolios. The goal is kmer-based isoform clustering or dimensionality reduction (use get_kmer_counts with kmer_PCA / kmer_tSNE / cluster_isoforms instead of abundance-based diversity ranking) Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than a full-length lrCaptureSeq isoform database, since reads <200 bp cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcript sequences Only overall gene-level expression is needed and no isoform-level abundance partition is available http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Rank-order genes from an lrCaptureSeq/PacBio isoform catalog by Shannon diversity index computed from per-gene isoform relative abundances, so that isoform-diverse targets (e.g., Nrxn3) can be identified and Lorenz-style jellyfish plots contextualized. Uses the IsoPops R package database and the vegan package's diversity metric. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Rank-order genes from an lrCaptureSeq/PacBio isoform catalog by Shannon diversity index computed from per-gene isoform relative abundances, so that isoform-diverse targets (e.g., Nrxn3) can be identified and Lorenz-style jellyfish plots contextualized. Uses the IsoPops R package database and the vegan package's diversity metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is kmer-based isoform clustering or dimensionality reduction (use get_kmer_counts with kmer_PCA / kmer_tSNE / cluster_isoforms instead of abundance-based diversity ranking) Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than a full-length lrCaptureSeq isoform database, since reads <200 bp cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcript sequences Only overall gene-level expression is needed and no isoform-level abundance partition is available

skills.description: Use when you need to de novo identify candidate tandem repeat regions from haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio whole-genome long-read BAM alignments (e.g., HGSVC data) with no prior motif or locus annotation.
skills.name: shannon-entropy-repetitive-region-detection
skills.search_text: shannon-entropy-repetitive-region-detection Use when you need to de novo identify candidate tandem repeat regions from haplotype-resolved ONT or PacBio whole-genome long-read BAM alignments (e.g., HGSVC data) with no prior motif or locus annotation. The target repeats lie in unassembled genome regions (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify The genome is polyploid or haploid (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not yet support You already have an annotated TR locus and only want genotyping of a known motif rather than de novo region discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Scan haplotype-resolved long-read (ONT/PacBio) BAM alignments with TRiCoLOR SENSoR, which uses the Shannon entropy of DNA sequences in sliding windows to flag candidate repetitive regions de novo, without prior knowledge of motifs or locations. The output BED anchors the downstream TRiCoLOR REFER genotyping step. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Scan haplotype-resolved long-read (ONT/PacBio) BAM alignments with TRiCoLOR SENSoR, which uses the Shannon entropy of DNA sequences in sliding windows to flag candidate repetitive regions de novo, without prior knowledge of motifs or locations. The output BED anchors the downstream TRiCoLOR REFER genotyping step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target repeats lie in unassembled genome regions (e.g., human centromeres and telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify The genome is polyploid or haploid (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not yet support You already have an annotated TR locus and only want genotyping of a known motif rather than de novo region discovery

skills.description: Use when starting from haplotype-resolved long-read BAM alignments and needing de novo discovery of candidate repetitive/tandem-repeat regions without any prior knowledge of motifs or repeat locations.
skills.name: shannon-entropy-sequence-scanning
skills.search_text: shannon-entropy-sequence-scanning Use when starting from haplotype-resolved long-read BAM alignments and needing de novo discovery of candidate repetitive/tandem-repeat regions without any prior knowledge of motifs or repeat locations. Input lacks haplotype-resolved long-read alignments — TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved BAM files as input, so short-read or non-phased BAMs are out of scope. Goal is to detect repeats in unassembled regions such as human centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify. Input is polyploid species or haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. You already have an annotated tandem-repeat catalog or known motifs — REFER profiling of specific loci may be more appropriate than de novo entropy scanning. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs the SENSoR module of TRiCoLOR, which scans haplotype-resolved ONT long-read alignments with a Shannon-entropy test on 20 bp non-overlapping windows to identify candidate repetitive regions de novo, emitting a sorted 3-column BED file. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Reconstructs the SENSoR module of TRiCoLOR, which scans haplotype-resolved ONT long-read alignments with a Shannon-entropy test on 20 bp non-overlapping windows to identify candidate repetitive regions de novo, emitting a sorted 3-column BED file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks haplotype-resolved long-read alignments — TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved BAM files as input, so short-read or non-phased BAMs are out of scope. Goal is to detect repeats in unassembled regions such as human centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify. Input is polyploid species or haploid chromosomes (e.g., human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. You already have an annotated tandem-repeat catalog or known motifs — REFER profiling of specific loci may be more appropriate than de novo entropy scanning.

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized per-nucleotide SHAPE/SHAPE-MaP reactivity profile for an RNA and need a secondary structure model that incorporates that probing data, plus a benchmark of whether constraints improve folding.
skills.name: shape-reactivity-constrained-rna-folding
skills.search_text: shape-reactivity-constrained-rna-folding Use when you have a normalized per-nucleotide SHAPE/SHAPE-MaP reactivity profile for an RNA and need a secondary structure model that incorporates that probing data, plus a benchmark of whether constraints improve folding. No experimental reactivity data exist for the target RNA — a no-probing-data fold is then the baseline, not the constrained model The goal is de novo modification detection on raw nanopore signal rather than structure modeling from already-derived reactivities Reactivities are unreliable (e.g., the article notes poor nanoSHAPE resolution at the 5' ends of long RNAs); constraints derived from such regions can mislead the fold http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Converts SHAPE reactivity profiles (e.g., nanoSHAPE-derived from nanopore direct RNA sequencing, or SHAPE-MaP) into pseudo-free-energy soft constraints to fold an RNA with RNAstructure or RNAfold, and benchmarks the constrained models against no-probing-data (NPD) folds by PPV/sensitivity and recovery of expected structural motifs. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: Converts SHAPE reactivity profiles (e.g., nanoSHAPE-derived from nanopore direct RNA sequencing, or SHAPE-MaP) into pseudo-free-energy soft constraints to fold an RNA with RNAstructure or RNAfold, and benchmarks the constrained models against no-probing-data (NPD) folds by PPV/sensitivity and recovery of expected structural motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No experimental reactivity data exist for the target RNA — a no-probing-data fold is then the baseline, not the constrained model The goal is de novo modification detection on raw nanopore signal rather than structure modeling from already-derived reactivities Reactivities are unreliable (e.g., the article notes poor nanoSHAPE resolution at the 5' ends of long RNAs); constraints derived from such regions can mislead the fold

skills.description: Use when wrapping an R simulation or analysis function (e.g. a population-genetic routine from learnPopGen) in a browser-based interface so that students can explore how changing argument values reactively recomputes and replots the result without knowing R.
skills.name: shiny-reactive-app-development
skills.search_text: shiny-reactive-app-development Use when wrapping an R simulation or analysis function (e.g. a population-genetic routine from learnPopGen) in a browser-based interface so that students can explore how changing argument values reactively recomputes and replots the result without knowing R. The goal is an animated graphic (e.g. an exported video or animation of trait change under selection) — web-interface graphics cannot be animated; export animations from R instead The target audience is comfortable in an interactive R session and can call the package functions directly, making a browser interface unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build a Shiny web interface for an R analysis function (here, learnPopGen's selection.drift) in which slider inputs for each numeric argument trigger automatic recomputation and re-plotting of the analysis output. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412
skills.summary: Build a Shiny web interface for an R analysis function (here, learnPopGen's selection.drift) in which slider inputs for each numeric argument trigger automatic recomputation and re-plotting of the analysis output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is an animated graphic (e.g. an exported video or animation of trait change under selection) — web-interface graphics cannot be animated; export animations from R instead The target audience is comfortable in an interactive R session and can call the package functions directly, making a browser interface unnecessary

skills.description: Use when long-read FASTQ reads from a split hybrid LR-SR scRNA-seq library must have their 10x barcode-adjacent segment located and extracted, via adapter alignment with edit-distance scoring.
skills.name: short-read-adapter-glocal-alignment
skills.search_text: short-read-adapter-glocal-alignment Use when long-read FASTQ reads from a split hybrid LR-SR scRNA-seq library must have their 10x barcode-adjacent segment located and extracted, via adapter alignment with edit-distance scoring. The long-read library template lacks a fixed sequence adjacent to the cellular barcode — non-10x platform support is only possible if the LR template includes some fixed sequence next to the barcode The goal is matching barcodes between SR and LR reads (this skill only extracts LR segments; matching is the separate match_trie step) Extracting short-read barcodes from a Cell Ranger BAM — use the extract_sr_bc step instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Locates the cellular barcode segment within each long read by glocal-aligning the fixed Illumina short-read adapter sequence (default CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT) to every long read with edlib, then extracting the bases immediately downstream of the adapter alignment. This is the extract_lr_bc stage of scTagger that produces candidate barcode segments for downstream trie matching. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104530
skills.summary: Locates the cellular barcode segment within each long read by glocal-aligning the fixed Illumina short-read adapter sequence (default CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT) to every long read with edlib, then extracting the bases immediately downstream of the adapter alignment. This is the extract_lr_bc stage of scTagger that produces candidate barcode segments for downstream trie matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long-read library template lacks a fixed sequence adjacent to the cellular barcode — non-10x platform support is only possible if the LR template includes some fixed sequence next to the barcode The goal is matching barcodes between SR and LR reads (this skill only extracts LR segments; matching is the separate match_trie step) Extracting short-read barcodes from a Cell Ranger BAM — use the extract_sr_bc step instead

skills.description: Use when the goal is to quantify how an alignment-free scaffolding-graph builder compares with Bowtie/Bowtie2/Bwa/Bwa-Mem on short-read data, via precision/recall of link recovery and wall-clock runtime per k-mer size.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-benchmarking
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-benchmarking Use when the goal is to quantify how an alignment-free scaffolding-graph builder compares with Bowtie/Bowtie2/Bwa/Bwa-Mem on short-read data, via precision/recall of link recovery and wall-clock runtime per k-mer size. The goal is scaffolder output quality (F-score/error counts against a reference) rather than aligner precision/recall/runtime of link recovery The input is long reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) — Fast-SG can extract synthetic libraries from raw or error-corrected long reads, but the short-read aligners benchmarked here are not the right comparators Only one graph-construction method is of interest with no aligner baseline — there is nothing to benchmark against http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks Fast-SG's alignment-free scaffolding-graph construction against state-of-the-art short-read aligners (Bowtie, Bowtie2 global/local, Bwa, Bwa-Mem) on identical read sets, comparing precision, recall, and runtime of the recovered linking information. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Benchmarks Fast-SG's alignment-free scaffolding-graph construction against state-of-the-art short-read aligners (Bowtie, Bowtie2 global/local, Bwa, Bwa-Mem) on identical read sets, comparing precision, recall, and runtime of the recovered linking information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scaffolder output quality (F-score/error counts against a reference) rather than aligner precision/recall/runtime of link recovery The input is long reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) — Fast-SG can extract synthetic libraries from raw or error-corrected long reads, but the short-read aligners benchmarked here are not the right comparators Only one graph-construction method is of interest with no aligner baseline — there is nothing to benchmark against

skills.description: Use when you need to map Illumina paired-end reads to a reference genome and recover split-read signal to support structural variation prediction across many strains.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-reference
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-reference Use when you need to map Illumina paired-end reads to a reference genome and recover split-read signal to support structural variation prediction across many strains. If the goal is exhaustive (high-sensitivity) SV discovery — this study deliberately prioritized high specificity (correctness of inferred SVs), so not all SVs will be detected If reads are long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — the pipeline relies on paired-end soft-clipping and split-read recovery with NextGenMap/YAHA, not long-read alignment If SV calls are already produced and only downstream genotyping/curation is needed (e.g. re-examining CNV read coverage in clonal populations) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A read-mapping and split-read recovery pipeline for predicting structural variations from Illumina paired-end short reads of 161 S. pombe strains against the ASM294v2.22 reference, feeding a consensus SV-calling workflow (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPs merged with SURVIVOR). genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: A read-mapping and split-read recovery pipeline for predicting structural variations from Illumina paired-end short reads of 161 S. pombe strains against the ASM294v2.22 reference, feeding a consensus SV-calling workflow (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPs merged with SURVIVOR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is exhaustive (high-sensitivity) SV discovery — this study deliberately prioritized high specificity (correctness of inferred SVs), so not all SVs will be detected If reads are long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — the pipeline relies on paired-end soft-clipping and split-read recovery with NextGenMap/YAHA, not long-read alignment If SV calls are already produced and only downstream genotyping/curation is needed (e.g. re-examining CNV read coverage in clonal populations)

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ/FASTA reads from WGS or WES samples must be aligned to a reference genome (e.g., hg38) to prepare sorted, duplicate-marked, indexed BAM files for variant calling.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome Use when raw FASTQ/FASTA reads from WGS or WES samples must be aligned to a reference genome (e.g., hg38) to prepare sorted, duplicate-marked, indexed BAM files for variant calling. Input is already a sorted, duplicate-marked, indexed BAM — the alignment step would only duplicate work Input is a VCF or annotated variant file (e.g., a JWES-DB parse target) rather than sequence reads The task is de novo assembly rather than mapping to a known reference genome http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps processed WGS/WES reads against the human reference genome hg38 using BWA within the JWES pipeline, then converts, sorts, deduplicates, and indexes the alignment to produce an analysis-ready BAM for downstream GATK variant calling. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261
skills.summary: Maps processed WGS/WES reads against the human reference genome hg38 using BWA within the JWES pipeline, then converts, sorts, deduplicates, and indexes the alignment to produce an analysis-ready BAM for downstream GATK variant calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a sorted, duplicate-marked, indexed BAM — the alignment step would only duplicate work Input is a VCF or annotated variant file (e.g., a JWES-DB parse target) rather than sequence reads The task is de novo assembly rather than mapping to a known reference genome

skills.description: Use when short sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. single-end HiSeq or ONT-derived reads) must be aligned to one known viral reference genome (FASTA) as the step preceding consensus sequence reconstruction or variant analysis.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-with-minimap2
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-with-minimap2 Use when short sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. single-end HiSeq or ONT-derived reads) must be aligned to one known viral reference genome (FASTA) as the step preceding consensus sequence reconstruction or variant analysis. When reads are long or noisy native ONT/pacbio reads requiring a different minimap2 preset (the -x sr preset is specifically for short reads) When the reference is an ultra-long genome (e.g. human chromosomes) where memory consumption for downstream consensus calling scales linearly with reference length and may be prohibitive When multiple distinct reference sequences must be handled jointly, since ViralConsensus-based consensus reconstruction requires a single reference sequence http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Map simulated or real short reads (e.g. Illumina HiSeq 2000) to a single viral reference genome with minimap2 in short-read mode, producing SAM/BAM alignments suitable for direct downstream consensus calling with ViralConsensus. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Map simulated or real short reads (e.g. Illumina HiSeq 2000) to a single viral reference genome with minimap2 in short-read mode, producing SAM/BAM alignments suitable for direct downstream consensus calling with ViralConsensus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are long or noisy native ONT/pacbio reads requiring a different minimap2 preset (the -x sr preset is specifically for short reads) When the reference is an ultra-long genome (e.g. human chromosomes) where memory consumption for downstream consensus calling scales linearly with reference length and may be prohibitive When multiple distinct reference sequences must be handled jointly, since ViralConsensus-based consensus reconstruction requires a single reference sequence

skills.description: Use when a draft de novo assembly (FASTA/contigs) needs quality assessment at single-nucleotide resolution, and matched short-read (Illumina) plus long-read (PacBio HiFi, PacBio CLR, or ONT) sequencing data are available to remap onto it.
skills.name: short-read-and-long-read-genome-mapping
skills.search_text: short-read-and-long-read-genome-mapping Use when a draft de novo assembly (FASTA/contigs) needs quality assessment at single-nucleotide resolution, and matched short-read (Illumina) plus long-read (PacBio HiFi, PacBio CLR, or ONT) sequencing data are available to remap onto it. Only one read type is available (NGS-only or SMS-only), since CRAQ integrates coverage and clipping signals from both NGS and SMS mapping to classify errors versus heterozygous variants The genome has ploidy above diploid, where CRAQ's accuracy has not been benchmarked and heterozygous/error classification may be unreliable The goal is assembly completeness (gene content) assessment rather than error detection — use BUSCO instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Map NGS short reads and SMS long reads back to a draft genome assembly with Minimap2 ('-ax sr' for Illumina, '-ax map-hifi/map-pb/map-ont' for PacBio HiFi/CLR/ONT), then filter alignments with SAMtools to feed CRAQ's clipping-based error detection. Dual-read-type mapping is the prerequisite step for single-nucleotide-resolution assembly error and heterozygous locus identification. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Map NGS short reads and SMS long reads back to a draft genome assembly with Minimap2 ('-ax sr' for Illumina, '-ax map-hifi/map-pb/map-ont' for PacBio HiFi/CLR/ONT), then filter alignments with SAMtools to feed CRAQ's clipping-based error detection. Dual-read-type mapping is the prerequisite step for single-nucleotide-resolution assembly error and heterozygous locus identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one read type is available (NGS-only or SMS-only), since CRAQ integrates coverage and clipping signals from both NGS and SMS mapping to classify errors versus heterozygous variants The genome has ploidy above diploid, where CRAQ's accuracy has not been benchmarked and heterozygous/error classification may be unreliable The goal is assembly completeness (gene content) assessment rather than error detection — use BUSCO instead

skills.description: Use when you have a 10x Genomics short-read BAM (from Cell Ranger mapping/filtering/UMI counting) and need a compact whitelist of the most frequent cellular barcodes that cover the bulk of short reads before barcode matching to long reads.
skills.name: short-read-barcode-frequency-filtering
skills.search_text: short-read-barcode-frequency-filtering Use when you have a 10x Genomics short-read BAM (from Cell Ranger mapping/filtering/UMI counting) and need a compact whitelist of the most frequent cellular barcodes that cover the bulk of short reads before barcode matching to long reads. You want to avoid short reads entirely — use the extract_sr_bc_from_lr module instead, which builds a barcode whitelist directly from long-read segments against the 10x Genomics barcode whitelist (e.g. 3M-february-2018.txt.gz). The experiment is not 10x Genomics scRNA-seq; the article notes scTagger in its current form is specific for 10x Genomics scRNA-seq (other platforms only work if the LR template has a fixed sequence next to the barcode). The number of relevant barcodes is much larger than tens of thousands — the article states scTagger's current design is not expected to scale well in that regime. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the top short-read cellular barcodes (10x Genomics Chromium) that cumulatively cover most SR reads, stopping when an additional 1,000-barcodes batch adds less than t% (default 0.5%) of total SRs. This is scTagger's extract_sr_bc stage, which builds a tractable SR barcode list for later trie-based matching against LR barcode segments. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104530
skills.summary: Selects the top short-read cellular barcodes (10x Genomics Chromium) that cumulatively cover most SR reads, stopping when an additional 1,000-barcodes batch adds less than t% (default 0.5%) of total SRs. This is scTagger's extract_sr_bc stage, which builds a tractable SR barcode list for later trie-based matching against LR barcode segments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to avoid short reads entirely — use the extract_sr_bc_from_lr module instead, which builds a barcode whitelist directly from long-read segments against the 10x Genomics barcode whitelist (e.g. 3M-february-2018.txt.gz). The experiment is not 10x Genomics scRNA-seq; the article notes scTagger in its current form is specific for 10x Genomics scRNA-seq (other platforms only work if the LR template has a fixed sequence next to the barcode). The number of relevant barcodes is much larger than tens of thousands — the article states scTagger's current design is not expected to scale well in that regime.

skills.description: Use when sequencing cDNA libraries of an in vitro-transcribed mRNA product (Illumina TruSeq short reads or ONT long reads) and you need to compute the fraction of reads attributable to the intended mRNA versus off-target RNAs and bacterial contamination.
skills.name: short-read-contamination-quantification
skills.search_text: short-read-contamination-quantification Use when sequencing cDNA libraries of an in vitro-transcribed mRNA product (Illumina TruSeq short reads or ONT long reads) and you need to compute the fraction of reads attributable to the intended mRNA versus off-target RNAs and bacterial contamination. Input is still raw ONT FASTQ from plasmid DNA template sequencing — use the plasmid mapping/fate-fraction workflow (Minimap2 -ax map-ont) instead, not mRNA read classification. The goal is per-nucleotide error profiles or consensus generation (pysamstats/bcftools), not read-class fraction quantification. Reads have not been adapter/barcode processed (Porechop for ONT, TrimGalore Q20 for Illumina), so fractions would be biased by technical artefacts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the fractional abundance of on-target versus off-target RNA in VAX-seq cDNA libraries of synthetic mRNA (e.g. eGFP mRNA), classifying reads as on-target mRNA, upstream, downstream, antisense, cryptic TSS-derived, or contaminant (e.g. E. coli) using SAMtools/bedtools/Pysam-based alignment classification and Mana. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41354-y
skills.summary: Quantifies the fractional abundance of on-target versus off-target RNA in VAX-seq cDNA libraries of synthetic mRNA (e.g. eGFP mRNA), classifying reads as on-target mRNA, upstream, downstream, antisense, cryptic TSS-derived, or contaminant (e.g. E. coli) using SAMtools/bedtools/Pysam-based alignment classification and Mana.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw ONT FASTQ from plasmid DNA template sequencing — use the plasmid mapping/fate-fraction workflow (Minimap2 -ax map-ont) instead, not mRNA read classification. The goal is per-nucleotide error profiles or consensus generation (pysamstats/bcftools), not read-class fraction quantification. Reads have not been adapter/barcode processed (Porechop for ONT, TrimGalore Q20 for Illumina), so fractions would be biased by technical artefacts.

skills.description: Use when ~50x Illumina FASTQ reads are available and accurate short contigs are needed as the contig input for a DBG2OLC hybrid assembly or similar long-read scaffolding pipeline.
skills.name: short-read-de-novo-contig-assembly
skills.search_text: short-read-de-novo-contig-assembly Use when ~50x Illumina FASTQ reads are available and accurate short contigs are needed as the contig input for a DBG2OLC hybrid assembly or similar long-read scaffolding pipeline. When the goal is a standalone finished short-read assembly — these raw contigs deliberately skip gap closing and scaffolding and are meant only as input to long-read hybrid assembly When only long reads (PacBio/ONT) are available and no Illumina contig file can be produced When a previously scaffolded or gap-closed short-read assembly is all that exists — the README warns this 'may have poor final results due to the errors introduced by the heuristics' http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Preassemble ~50x Illumina short reads into short but accurate raw de Bruijn graph (DBG) contigs with SparseAssembler, e.g. k 51, g 15, NodeCovTh 1, EdgeCovTh 0, GS 12000000 on the S.cer w303 dataset, to serve as high-quality anchors for long-read hybrid assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/srep31900
skills.summary: Preassemble ~50x Illumina short reads into short but accurate raw de Bruijn graph (DBG) contigs with SparseAssembler, e.g. k 51, g 15, NodeCovTh 1, EdgeCovTh 0, GS 12000000 on the S.cer w303 dataset, to serve as high-quality anchors for long-read hybrid assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a standalone finished short-read assembly — these raw contigs deliberately skip gap closing and scaffolding and are meant only as input to long-read hybrid assembly When only long reads (PacBio/ONT) are available and no Illumina contig file can be produced When a previously scaffolded or gap-closed short-read assembly is all that exists — the README warns this 'may have poor final results due to the errors introduced by the heuristics'

skills.description: Use when short-read FASTQ data must be assembled de novo and the resulting contigs need to be checked against a long-read-defined isoform set to assess whether complex/multi-isoform loci are recovered.
skills.name: short-read-de-novo-transcriptome-assembly
skills.search_text: short-read-de-novo-transcriptome-assembly Use when short-read FASTQ data must be assembled de novo and the resulting contigs need to be checked against a long-read-defined isoform set to assess whether complex/multi-isoform loci are recovered. The input reads are ONT long reads — Mandalorion is intended for R2C2/C3POa or PacBio ccs/lima consensus data and 'is not tested for use with regular ONT reads'; a different pipeline is required. The goal is gene-level expression quantification rather than isoform structure recovery — ONT RNAseq alone quantifies known genes with high correlation to Illumina, so no assembly step is needed. The locus is known to express a single simple isoform — the skill targets multi-isoform surface receptor loci such as CD37, where assembly failure is expected. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Assembles per-cell Illumina RNAseq reads de novo with Trinity to test whether short-read assembly can recover complex isoforms (e.g. the multi-isoform CD37 locus) identified by ONT long-read RNAseq, then aligns Trinity contigs against the ONT isoform set for concordance checking. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms16027
skills.summary: Assembles per-cell Illumina RNAseq reads de novo with Trinity to test whether short-read assembly can recover complex isoforms (e.g. the multi-isoform CD37 locus) identified by ONT long-read RNAseq, then aligns Trinity contigs against the ONT isoform set for concordance checking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are ONT long reads — Mandalorion is intended for R2C2/C3POa or PacBio ccs/lima consensus data and 'is not tested for use with regular ONT reads'; a different pipeline is required. The goal is gene-level expression quantification rather than isoform structure recovery — ONT RNAseq alone quantifies known genes with high correlation to Illumina, so no assembly step is needed. The locus is known to express a single simple isoform — the skill targets multi-isoform surface receptor loci such as CD37, where assembly failure is expected.

skills.description: Use when starting a hybrid assembly from Illumina MiSeq paired-end FASTQ (e.g. ERR654977, Kp2146_paired_*.fastq.gz) that will subsequently be completed with long nanopore reads via npScarf.
skills.name: short-read-genome-assembly-spades
skills.search_text: short-read-genome-assembly-spades Use when starting a hybrid assembly from Illumina MiSeq paired-end FASTQ (e.g. ERR654977, Kp2146_paired_*.fastq.gz) that will subsequently be completed with long nanopore reads via npScarf. When the goal is a pure long-read assembly — the paper instead compares against assemblers 'designed for long and accurate reads such as Celera Assembler' for corrected long reads When reads are untrimmed raw MiSeq output — the pipeline requires adapter- and quality-trimmed input before SPAdes When the target is npGraph-based streaming assembly — npScarf's README states it 'is not on maintenance anymore' and npGraph is the replacement http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Assemble trimmed Illumina MiSeq paired-end reads into a draft contig set with SPAdes, then length-sort contigs and build a BWA index so the draft can serve as the backbone for npScarf's real-time nanopore scaffolding. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Assemble trimmed Illumina MiSeq paired-end reads into a draft contig set with SPAdes, then length-sort contigs and build a BWA index so the draft can serve as the backbone for npScarf's real-time nanopore scaffolding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a pure long-read assembly — the paper instead compares against assemblers 'designed for long and accurate reads such as Celera Assembler' for corrected long reads When reads are untrimmed raw MiSeq output — the pipeline requires adapter- and quality-trimmed input before SPAdes When the target is npGraph-based streaming assembly — npScarf's README states it 'is not on maintenance anymore' and npGraph is the replacement

skills.description: Use when assembling de novo transcriptomes from Illumina RNA-Seq FASTQ reads and the goal is a condensed de Bruijn graph whose branching vertices preserve multiple paths through shared k-mers (alternative isoforms) rather than collapsing them.
skills.name: short-read-graph-assembly
skills.search_text: short-read-graph-assembly Use when assembling de novo transcriptomes from Illumina RNA-Seq FASTQ reads and the goal is a condensed de Bruijn graph whose branching vertices preserve multiple paths through shared k-mers (alternative isoforms) rather than collapsing them. The goal is reconstructing a single linear genomic sequence rather than multiple alternative isoform paths — unmodified genome-oriented SPAdes lacks an isoform detection step and collapses alternative isoforms (on the simulated Mouse dataset it produced the same number of 95%-assembled genes and isoforms) Input reads are high-error-rate long reads (Oxford Nanopore/PacBio) meant to be used directly as complete transcripts — the pipeline is designed for accurate short Illumina reads The data is metatranscriptomic — the approach was designed for RNA-Seq from a single organism and repetitive patterns in homologous genes and extreme mRNA quantity differences are unaddressed challenges http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstruct a condensed de Bruijn assembly graph from short RNA-Seq reads (as rnaSPAdes does on top of the SPAdes framework), selecting k-mer sizes from read length, condensing non-branching paths into edges while retaining every branching vertex so alternatively spliced isoform paths are not collapsed. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Reconstruct a condensed de Bruijn assembly graph from short RNA-Seq reads (as rnaSPAdes does on top of the SPAdes framework), selecting k-mer sizes from read length, condensing non-branching paths into edges while retaining every branching vertex so alternatively spliced isoform paths are not collapsed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is reconstructing a single linear genomic sequence rather than multiple alternative isoform paths — unmodified genome-oriented SPAdes lacks an isoform detection step and collapses alternative isoforms (on the simulated Mouse dataset it produced the same number of 95%-assembled genes and isoforms) Input reads are high-error-rate long reads (Oxford Nanopore/PacBio) meant to be used directly as complete transcripts — the pipeline is designed for accurate short Illumina reads The data is metatranscriptomic — the approach was designed for RNA-Seq from a single organism and repetitive patterns in homologous genes and extreme mRNA quantity differences are unaddressed challenges

skills.description: Use when you have parental paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. EcoRI RAD-seq) and a reference FASTA, and need a catalog of indel sites between two parents of a mapping population for downstream genotyping.
skills.name: short-read-indel-variant-calling
skills.search_text: short-read-indel-variant-calling Use when you have parental paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. EcoRI RAD-seq) and a reference FASTA, and need a catalog of indel sites between two parents of a mapping population for downstream genotyping. The goal is SNP calling or whole-genome deep-coverage variant discovery rather than indel genotyping at restriction-site loci for linkage mapping You only have a single sample rather than two parents of a segregating (BC1, BC2, F2, or CP hybrid) population A parental indel catalog already exists and only downstream genotyping is needed (use the --nocatalog option to skip this step) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Call indel variants between two parents from paired-end RAD-seq reads aligned to a reference genome using the InDelGT pipeline (BWA 0.7.17 + SAMtools 1.9/BCFtools 1.9), producing a merged parental indel catalog (parent.cls), e.g. 50,532 indel sites between P. deltoides and P. simonii against the P. trichocarpa v4.0 reference. genomics/v1 10.1002/aps3.11499
skills.summary: Call indel variants between two parents from paired-end RAD-seq reads aligned to a reference genome using the InDelGT pipeline (BWA 0.7.17 + SAMtools 1.9/BCFtools 1.9), producing a merged parental indel catalog (parent.cls), e.g. 50,532 indel sites between P. deltoides and P. simonii against the P. trichocarpa v4.0 reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is SNP calling or whole-genome deep-coverage variant discovery rather than indel genotyping at restriction-site loci for linkage mapping You only have a single sample rather than two parents of a segregating (BC1, BC2, F2, or CP hybrid) population A parental indel catalog already exists and only downstream genotyping is needed (use the --nocatalog option to skip this step)

skills.description: Use when you have matched long-read (MinION/nanopore) and short-read (Illumina) SV call sets from the same genomes and need to determine which SVs are long-read-specific and characterize their size, GC, and repeat content.
skills.name: short-read-long-read-sv-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: short-read-long-read-sv-concordance-analysis Use when you have matched long-read (MinION/nanopore) and short-read (Illumina) SV call sets from the same genomes and need to determine which SVs are long-read-specific and characterize their size, GC, and repeat content. When there is no matched short-read call set from the same genome — the intersection defining 'nanopore-specific' requires the Illumina comparator data When the goal is de novo complex SV breakpoint detection or phasing of chromothripsis rather than genome-wide inherited SV concordance — use the NanoSV calling/phasing pipeline directly instead When reads have not been basecalled and mapped (BAM must be coordinate-sorted and indexed before NanoSV calling) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 A comparison workflow that intersects nanopore NanoSV call sets from MinION-sequenced patient genomes against short-read Illumina SV calls from six variant callers and 1KG variant sites, to quantify and characterize nanopore-specific structural variants missed by short reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: A comparison workflow that intersects nanopore NanoSV call sets from MinION-sequenced patient genomes against short-read Illumina SV calls from six variant callers and 1KG variant sites, to quantify and characterize nanopore-specific structural variants missed by short reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there is no matched short-read call set from the same genome — the intersection defining 'nanopore-specific' requires the Illumina comparator data When the goal is de novo complex SV breakpoint detection or phasing of chromothripsis rather than genome-wide inherited SV concordance — use the NanoSV calling/phasing pipeline directly instead When reads have not been basecalled and mapped (BAM must be coordinate-sorted and indexed before NanoSV calling)

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing Nanopore 5mC methylation callers against short-read ground truth: you have per-read modBAM/TSV calls plus a short-read methylation reference (e.g. EpiQC, GSE186383) and need per-site F1 and frequency correlation.
skills.name: short-read-methylation-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: short-read-methylation-correlation-analysis Use when evaluating or comparing Nanopore 5mC methylation callers against short-read ground truth: you have per-read modBAM/TSV calls plus a short-read methylation reference (e.g. EpiQC, GSE186383) and need per-site F1 and frequency correlation. Evaluating per-read (not per-site) performance — the per-read ground truth uses the stricter ≥90%/<10% methylation with ≥10X filter instead No short-read or microarray ground truth is available — correlation/F1 scoring cannot be computed Calling modifications other than 5mCpG — DeepMod2 provides models only for 5mCpG and no 5hmC was detected in GIAB cell lines HG001-HG007 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Benchmark ONT per-site methylation calls (DeepMod2, Guppy, Dorado) against short-read sequencing ground truth by computing per-site F1 and correlation of methylation frequencies on the Ashkenazim trio (HG002, HG003, HG004) datasets, as done in the DeepMod2 paper. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-45778-y
skills.summary: Benchmark ONT per-site methylation calls (DeepMod2, Guppy, Dorado) against short-read sequencing ground truth by computing per-site F1 and correlation of methylation frequencies on the Ashkenazim trio (HG002, HG003, HG004) datasets, as done in the DeepMod2 paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating per-read (not per-site) performance — the per-read ground truth uses the stricter ≥90%/<10% methylation with ≥10X filter instead No short-read or microarray ground truth is available — correlation/F1 scoring cannot be computed Calling modifications other than 5mCpG — DeepMod2 provides models only for 5mCpG and no 5hmC was detected in GIAB cell lines HG001-HG007

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina FASTQ reads have heterogeneous lengths or trailing low-quality bases that would distort k-mer spectra, and the downstream goal is k-mer histogram generation for genome size, repeat, and heterozygosity estimation.
skills.name: short-read-preprocessing
skills.search_text: short-read-preprocessing Use when raw Illumina FASTQ reads have heterogeneous lengths or trailing low-quality bases that would distort k-mer spectra, and the downstream goal is k-mer histogram generation for genome size, repeat, and heterozygosity estimation. The downstream task is long-read (nanopore) assembly with TULIP/Canu, where reads must remain full-length and adaptive trimming of the 3'-end would discard signal Input reads are already uniform-length and quality-trimmed, so re-truncation only discards data Polishing a genome with Pilon using the Illumina reads, where maximum read length and full pairing may improve base correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Uniformize short-read (Illumina) input prior to k-mer-based genome profiling by quality/length trimming or truncation (e.g. truncating SRR5235521 reads to 76 nt), so that k-mer counts computed by Jellyfish across k=19–25 are of consistent quality before GenomeScope model fitting. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Uniformize short-read (Illumina) input prior to k-mer-based genome profiling by quality/length trimming or truncation (e.g. truncating SRR5235521 reads to 76 nt), so that k-mer counts computed by Jellyfish across k=19–25 are of consistent quality before GenomeScope model fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream task is long-read (nanopore) assembly with TULIP/Canu, where reads must remain full-length and adaptive trimming of the 3'-end would discard signal Input reads are already uniform-length and quality-trimmed, so re-truncation only discards data Polishing a genome with Pilon using the Illumina reads, where maximum read length and full pairing may improve base correction

skills.description: Use when preparing Illumina/short-read data as input to yak k-mer counting for NextPolish2 polishing or Merqury/yak QV evaluation, and reads need adapter removal, quality trimming, and filtering.
skills.name: short-read-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: short-read-quality-filtering Use when preparing Illumina/short-read data as input to yak k-mer counting for NextPolish2 polishing or Merqury/yak QV evaluation, and reads need adapter removal, quality trimming, and filtering. Input is already a polished assembly or long-read HiFi FASTQ — fastp QC here targets short reads only. Short-read coverage is well below the recommended >=60X, since NextPolish2 performance relies heavily on short reads and singletons would be discarded by yak -b 37. The goal is polishing without k-mer evaluation (e.g., only Racon-based long-read polishing), where short-read QC adds no value. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quality-control short-read data with fastp prior to k-mer dataset construction (yak) for genome polishing and QV evaluation, applying adapter removal, quality trimming, and read filtering so that polishing and Merqury-style metrics rely on reliable k-mers. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Quality-control short-read data with fastp prior to k-mer dataset construction (yak) for genome polishing and QV evaluation, applying adapter removal, quality trimming, and read filtering so that polishing and Merqury-style metrics rely on reliable k-mers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a polished assembly or long-read HiFi FASTQ — fastp QC here targets short reads only. Short-read coverage is well below the recommended >=60X, since NextPolish2 performance relies heavily on short reads and singletons would be discarded by yak -b 37. The goal is polishing without k-mer evaluation (e.g., only Racon-based long-read polishing), where short-read QC adds no value.

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina FASTQ and/or Nanopore long-read FASTQ (e.g. plasmid datasets from GigaDB) must be trimmed before assembly with Unicycler, Filtlong, or Bandage graph inspection.
skills.name: short-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: short-read-quality-trimming Use when raw Illumina FASTQ and/or Nanopore long-read FASTQ (e.g. plasmid datasets from GigaDB) must be trimmed before assembly with Unicycler, Filtlong, or Bandage graph inspection. Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed and the goal is only assembly or Bandage graph rendering Input is not sequencing read data (e.g. already-assembled contigs or an AMR analysis use case) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quality- and adapter-trim Illumina short reads and adapter-trim Nanopore long reads within the NanoGalaxy hybrid assembly workflow, so that downstream short-only, long-only, and Unicycler hybrid assemblies of plasmid data start from clean reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa105
skills.summary: Quality- and adapter-trim Illumina short reads and adapter-trim Nanopore long reads within the NanoGalaxy hybrid assembly workflow, so that downstream short-only, long-only, and Unicycler hybrid assemblies of plasmid data start from clean reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed and the goal is only assembly or Bandage graph rendering Input is not sequencing read data (e.g. already-assembled contigs or an AMR analysis use case)

skills.description: Use when short-read Illumina RNA-seq data (e.g. ENA PRJEB36584) must be aligned to a reference genome as part of a hybrid (PacBio + Illumina) genome-guided transcriptome assembly.
skills.name: short-read-rnaseq-alignment-hisat2
skills.search_text: short-read-rnaseq-alignment-hisat2 Use when short-read Illumina RNA-seq data (e.g. ENA PRJEB36584) must be aligned to a reference genome as part of a hybrid (PacBio + Illumina) genome-guided transcriptome assembly. No assembled reference genome is available — the pipeline is genome-guided and requires a reference genome as a guide Only PacBio long-read data is available — use a PacBio-only pipeline such as IsoSeq/IsoCon instead of hybrid alignment Input alignment BAMs already exist and only transcript assembly is needed — proceed directly to StringTie http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Trim paired-end Illumina RNA-seq reads with fastp and align them to a reference genome (galGal6, GCA_000002315.5) using HISAT2, producing a BAM file that is merged with a minimap2-aligned PacBio BAM for downstream StringTie transcript assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac099
skills.summary: Trim paired-end Illumina RNA-seq reads with fastp and align them to a reference genome (galGal6, GCA_000002315.5) using HISAT2, producing a BAM file that is merged with a minimap2-aligned PacBio BAM for downstream StringTie transcript assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No assembled reference genome is available — the pipeline is genome-guided and requires a reference genome as a guide Only PacBio long-read data is available — use a PacBio-only pipeline such as IsoSeq/IsoCon instead of hybrid alignment Input alignment BAMs already exist and only transcript assembly is needed — proceed directly to StringTie

skills.description: Use when Illumina short-read RNA-seq (FASTQ) needs BSJ-spanning read counts per library to quantify circRNA back-splice junction proportions, e.g. as the comparator arm of an isoCirc enrichment analysis.
skills.name: short-read-rnaseq-bsj-read-mapping
skills.search_text: short-read-rnaseq-bsj-read-mapping Use when Illumina short-read RNA-seq (FASTQ) needs BSJ-spanning read counts per library to quantify circRNA back-splice junction proportions, e.g. as the comparator arm of an isoCirc enrichment analysis. Input data are isoCirc long-read (RCA + nanopore) reads — those are processed by the isoCirc pipeline, not short-read BSJ counting The goal is full-length circRNA isoform reconstruction; short-read RNA-seq cannot determine full-length circRNA sequences or internal alternative splicing BSJs already have adequate long-read support and no short-read comparator library is available http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aligns short-read Illumina RNA-seq libraries (RNase R-treated and poly(A)-selected) to a reference genome and counts reads spanning circRNA back-splice junctions (BSJs), establishing the short-read baseline that isoCirc long-read BSJ enrichment is benchmarked against. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Aligns short-read Illumina RNA-seq libraries (RNase R-treated and poly(A)-selected) to a reference genome and counts reads spanning circRNA back-splice junctions (BSJs), establishing the short-read baseline that isoCirc long-read BSJ enrichment is benchmarked against.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are isoCirc long-read (RCA + nanopore) reads — those are processed by the isoCirc pipeline, not short-read BSJ counting The goal is full-length circRNA isoform reconstruction; short-read RNA-seq cannot determine full-length circRNA sequences or internal alternative splicing BSJs already have adequate long-read support and no short-read comparator library is available

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an NRS/insertion detection method against baselines that require ordinary paired-end short reads, and ground-truth insertions (e.g. 2000 sequences of 50-6000 bp inserted into GRCh38) must be tested at matched coverage.
skills.name: short-read-simulation-for-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: short-read-simulation-for-baseline-comparison Use when benchmarking an NRS/insertion detection method against baselines that require ordinary paired-end short reads, and ground-truth insertions (e.g. 2000 sequences of 50-6000 bp inserted into GRCh38) must be tested at matched coverage. The baseline method natively accepts barcoded linked-reads (e.g. Novel-X, NUI, PopIns2) — use the LRSIM linked-read BAM with LongRanger alignment instead. The goal is to assess real-sample performance rather than a controlled simulation — use real datasets such as the Polaris PGx cohort, NA12878, or haploid CHM1/CHM13 genomes. Insertions of interest are < 300 bp, where Novel-X's own analysis and coverage-based limitations apply differently. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulate matched standard short-read data with ART at the same coverage as a linked-read benchmark so that baseline tools that cannot consume linked-reads (e.g. Pamir) can be compared on equal footing against synthetic-long-read methods like Novel-X, NUI, and PopIns2. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Simulate matched standard short-read data with ART at the same coverage as a linked-read benchmark so that baseline tools that cannot consume linked-reads (e.g. Pamir) can be compared on equal footing against synthetic-long-read methods like Novel-X, NUI, and PopIns2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The baseline method natively accepts barcoded linked-reads (e.g. Novel-X, NUI, PopIns2) — use the LRSIM linked-read BAM with LongRanger alignment instead. The goal is to assess real-sample performance rather than a controlled simulation — use real datasets such as the Polaris PGx cohort, NA12878, or haploid CHM1/CHM13 genomes. Insertions of interest are < 300 bp, where Novel-X's own analysis and coverage-based limitations apply differently.

skills.description: Use when an lrCaptureSeq (PacBio) isoform catalog needs independent validation: short-read RNA-seq (GSE101986, GSE79416) can confirm splice junctions, and CAGE-seq (DRA002410) can confirm 5' transcription start sites.
skills.name: short-read-splice-aware-alignment
skills.search_text: short-read-splice-aware-alignment Use when an lrCaptureSeq (PacBio) isoform catalog needs independent validation: short-read RNA-seq (GSE101986, GSE79416) can confirm splice junctions, and CAGE-seq (DRA002410) can confirm 5' transcription start sites. The goal is to discover novel full-length isoform sequences de novo — typical RNA-seq read lengths are <200 bp and cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcripts, so long-read lrCaptureSeq is required instead. The long-read isoform catalog has not yet been filtered (no 4+ exon, truncation-removed, 95% abundance filtering), since aligning against an unfiltered GFF propagates truncated or low-confidence junctions. Validating isoforms that differ only at 3' ends in single-cell data, where 3' bias makes junction-based validation inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Splice-aware alignment of independent short-read RNA-seq or CAGE-seq reads against the mouse genome, guided by long-read-defined isoform annotations, to validate lrCaptureSeq splice junctions and transcription start sites. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Splice-aware alignment of independent short-read RNA-seq or CAGE-seq reads against the mouse genome, guided by long-read-defined isoform annotations, to validate lrCaptureSeq splice junctions and transcription start sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to discover novel full-length isoform sequences de novo — typical RNA-seq read lengths are <200 bp and cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcripts, so long-read lrCaptureSeq is required instead. The long-read isoform catalog has not yet been filtered (no 4+ exon, truncation-removed, 95% abundance filtering), since aligning against an unfiltered GFF propagates truncated or low-confidence junctions. Validating isoforms that differ only at 3' ends in single-cell data, where 3' bias makes junction-based validation inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when a hybrid error-correction task requires mapping short reads (e.g. Illumina FASTQ) onto long reads (e.g. PacBio/Sequel FASTA) to localize questionable bases before consensus- or optimization-based correction.
skills.name: short-read-to-long-read-alignment
skills.search_text: short-read-to-long-read-alignment Use when a hybrid error-correction task requires mapping short reads (e.g. Illumina FASTQ) onto long reads (e.g. PacBio/Sequel FASTA) to localize questionable bases before consensus- or optimization-based correction. The long reads are already high quality or the goal is self-correction without short-read data (e.g. HGAP-style self-correcting approaches) — this skill is specifically hybrid correction driven by aligned short reads Input short reads are not from a second-generation technology with per-base quality (e.g. 454 pyro-sequencing output), since HECIL's correction weights depend on PHRED-derived quality and mapping identity of the aligned short reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns high-accuracy Illumina short reads onto noisy third-generation long reads with BWA-MEM and marks mismatch, insertion, and deletion positions on the long reads as questionable, providing the evidence layer that HECIL's correction stages consume. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-28364-3
skills.summary: Aligns high-accuracy Illumina short reads onto noisy third-generation long reads with BWA-MEM and marks mismatch, insertion, and deletion positions on the long reads as questionable, providing the evidence layer that HECIL's correction stages consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The long reads are already high quality or the goal is self-correction without short-read data (e.g. HGAP-style self-correcting approaches) — this skill is specifically hybrid correction driven by aligned short reads Input short reads are not from a second-generation technology with per-base quality (e.g. 454 pyro-sequencing output), since HECIL's correction weights depend on PHRED-derived quality and mapping identity of the aligned short reads

skills.description: Use when a long-read (e.g. Oxford Nanopore) assembly has high raw error rates and paired Illumina reads are available to raise base-level accuracy, and when the improvement must be quantified per polishing stage.
skills.name: short-read-variant-based-assembly-polishing
skills.search_text: short-read-variant-based-assembly-polishing Use when a long-read (e.g. Oxford Nanopore) assembly has high raw error rates and paired Illumina reads are available to raise base-level accuracy, and when the improvement must be quantified per polishing stage. The assembly was built from short reads only and is already at base-level accuracy, so nanopore-specific Racon consensus correction is unnecessary No independent Illumina data are available, in which case Pilon variant-based polishing cannot be performed and Racon alone cannot resolve errors the article notes 'cannot be resolved by taking a consensus of nanopore data only' The goal is structural/long-range validation (e.g. misjoins or scaffold merging) rather than base-level error correction — the article points to optical mapping for that purpose http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Improves a nanopore-derived de novo assembly by rounds of Racon consensus correction followed by Illumina short-read variant-based polishing with Pilon, then quantifies the effect with BUSCO completeness assessments against the vertebrata_odb9 lineage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-07650-6
skills.summary: Improves a nanopore-derived de novo assembly by rounds of Racon consensus correction followed by Illumina short-read variant-based polishing with Pilon, then quantifies the effect with BUSCO completeness assessments against the vertebrata_odb9 lineage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly was built from short reads only and is already at base-level accuracy, so nanopore-specific Racon consensus correction is unnecessary No independent Illumina data are available, in which case Pilon variant-based polishing cannot be performed and Racon alone cannot resolve errors the article notes 'cannot be resolved by taking a consensus of nanopore data only' The goal is structural/long-range validation (e.g. misjoins or scaffold merging) rather than base-level error correction — the article points to optical mapping for that purpose

skills.description: Use when you have basecalled nanopore reads aligned to hg38 and need to detect SNVs/indels, especially when comparing variant-detection performance across read simulators on chr22 (NA12878) data.
skills.name: short-read-variant-calling-with-clair3
skills.search_text: short-read-variant-calling-with-clair3 Use when you have basecalled nanopore reads aligned to hg38 and need to detect SNVs/indels, especially when comparing variant-detection performance across read simulators on chr22 (NA12878) data.
