skills.search_text: simulation-based-variant-caller-benchmarking Use when comparing SNV calling accuracy between short-read-based (e.g. GATK, FreeBayes) and SMS read-based (e.g. Longshot) callers, and no unbiased truth set exists — simulation provides ground-truth variants for precision/recall quantification. Input is real (non-simulated) data intended for downstream biological interpretation — simulation output is only a benchmark, not usable variant calls Assessing indel or structural variant calling — Longshot calls SNVs only (indels must be supplied in an input VCF for genotyping, and SVs >50 bp are unsupported) A mature, unbiased high-confidence truth set exists (e.g. GIAB) — though note the article warns GIAB/Platinum Genomes sets are biased toward short-read technologies http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark SNV calling accuracy by simulating a diploid genome with known heterozygous variants and generating synthetic short-read (Illumina) and long-read (PacBio SMS) datasets, then comparing caller output against ground-truth VCFs at matched coverages (20–60×). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Benchmark SNV calling accuracy by simulating a diploid genome with known heterozygous variants and generating synthetic short-read (Illumina) and long-read (PacBio SMS) datasets, then comparing caller output against ground-truth VCFs at matched coverages (20–60×).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) data intended for downstream biological interpretation — simulation output is only a benchmark, not usable variant calls Assessing indel or structural variant calling — Longshot calls SNVs only (indels must be supplied in an input VCF for genotyping, and SVs >50 bp are unsupported) A mature, unbiased high-confidence truth set exists (e.g. GIAB) — though note the article warns GIAB/Platinum Genomes sets are biased toward short-read technologies

skills.description: Use when validating a kinetic-rate inference pipeline on synthetic data: you need a simulated RNA-life-cycle benchmark with known ground-truth synthesis/processing/export/degradation rates and corresponding benchmark figures.
skills.name: simulation-benchmark-figure-generation
skills.search_text: simulation-benchmark-figure-generation Use when validating a kinetic-rate inference pipeline on synthetic data: you need a simulated RNA-life-cycle benchmark with known ground-truth synthesis/processing/export/degradation rates and corresponding benchmark figures. The goal is analysing real Nanodynamo experimental data (untreated, Pladienolide B, Leptomycin B, Harringtonine conditions) rather than benchmarking inference — use experimentalDataAnalysis.R / mainModelingResults.R instead. The aim is to quantify RNA dynamics in samples without ground-truth kinetic rates; simulation is only a validation exercise, not a measurement method. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Generates and analyzes a simulated Nanodynamo benchmark dataset (1000 genes, 2 replicates, 20-min 4U metabolic labelling) with rates sampled from gaussian distributions anchored to INSPEcT 3T9 fibroblast medians (CV=5), to validate kinetic-rate inference and reproduce Figures 1D, 1E, S4-5. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Generates and analyzes a simulated Nanodynamo benchmark dataset (1000 genes, 2 replicates, 20-min 4U metabolic labelling) with rates sampled from gaussian distributions anchored to INSPEcT 3T9 fibroblast medians (CV=5), to validate kinetic-rate inference and reproduce Figures 1D, 1E, S4-5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is analysing real Nanodynamo experimental data (untreated, Pladienolide B, Leptomycin B, Harringtonine conditions) rather than benchmarking inference — use experimentalDataAnalysis.R / mainModelingResults.R instead. The aim is to quantify RNA dynamics in samples without ground-truth kinetic rates; simulation is only a validation exercise, not a measurement method.

skills.description: Use when a simulation study consumes simmrd::generate_summary() output and you must verify, before analysis, that every documented named-list component is present and structurally correct (e.g. bx is m x p, IVtype labels are 'valid'/'UHP'/'CHP').
skills.name: simulation-list-schema-checking
skills.search_text: simulation-list-schema-checking Use when a simulation study consumes simmrd::generate_summary() output and you must verify, before analysis, that every documented named-list component is present and structurally correct (e.g. bx is m x p, IVtype labels are 'valid'/'UHP'/'CHP'). You need individual-level genotype and phenotype data with directly set confounding — the generate_individual() workflow is slower but lets you set confounding directly, so schema validation should target that path instead You want to compare simulation scenarios against the paper's named settings — use load_preset()/list_presets() to reproduce named scenarios rather than relying on set_params() defaults The goal is visualization of simulated GWAS results rather than schema verification — plot_simdata() is the appropriate step http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Validates that a simmrd simulation replicate returned by generate_summary() (run under set_params() defaults) contains the full named-list schema — the ten documented components bx, bxse, by, byse, RhoME, LDMatrix, LDhatMatrix, theta, IVtype, and the unstandardized bx/by variants — so downstream MR method evaluation consumes structurally complete data. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Validates that a simmrd simulation replicate returned by generate_summary() (run under set_params() defaults) contains the full named-list schema — the ten documented components bx, bxse, by, byse, RhoME, LDMatrix, LDhatMatrix, theta, IVtype, and the unstandardized bx/by variants — so downstream MR method evaluation consumes structurally complete data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need individual-level genotype and phenotype data with directly set confounding — the generate_individual() workflow is slower but lets you set confounding directly, so schema validation should target that path instead You want to compare simulation scenarios against the paper's named settings — use load_preset()/list_presets() to reproduce named scenarios rather than relying on set_params() defaults The goal is visualization of simulated GWAS results rather than schema verification — plot_simdata() is the appropriate step

skills.description: Use when you need an exact replicate of the TWO-SIGMA paper's simulated ZINB random-effect dataset for benchmarking, type-I error/power studies, or validating the twosigma package against the published simulation design.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-configuration Use when you need an exact replicate of the TWO-SIGMA paper's simulated ZINB random-effect dataset for benchmarking, type-I error/power studies, or validating the twosigma package against the published simulation design. When the goal is to fit TWO-SIGMA to real scRNA-seq counts rather than generate a synthetic benchmark dataset — use the twosigma()/lr.twosigma() fitting functions instead When you need a simulation design with different covariates, sample sizes, or effect sizes than the paper's example — those require newly chosen parameters, not this fixed configuration When you need normalized or transformed expression values — the simulator produces non-negative integer counts only (no normalization is done) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the TWO-SIGMA paper's example zero-inflated negative binomial random-effect simulation by calling simulate_zero_inflated_nb_random_effect_data with the paper's exact parameters (nind=10, ncellsper=1000, sigma.a=sigma.b=0.1, alpha=(-1,0,-0.5,-2), beta=(2,0,-0.1,0.6), phi=0.1) over 10,000 genes. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Reproduces the TWO-SIGMA paper's example zero-inflated negative binomial random-effect simulation by calling simulate_zero_inflated_nb_random_effect_data with the paper's exact parameters (nind=10, ncellsper=1000, sigma.a=sigma.b=0.1, alpha=(-1,0,-0.5,-2), beta=(2,0,-0.1,0.6), phi=0.1) over 10,000 genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to fit TWO-SIGMA to real scRNA-seq counts rather than generate a synthetic benchmark dataset — use the twosigma()/lr.twosigma() fitting functions instead When you need a simulation design with different covariates, sample sizes, or effect sizes than the paper's example — those require newly chosen parameters, not this fixed configuration When you need normalized or transformed expression values — the simulator produces non-negative integer counts only (no normalization is done)

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating the runtime performance claims of simmrd's summary-level GWAS data generator, or when establishing that a simulation pipeline can produce GWAS summary statistics and select IVs within a 0.1 s budget.
skills.name: simulation-pipeline-performance-validation
skills.search_text: simulation-pipeline-performance-validation Use when reproducing or validating the runtime performance claims of simmrd's summary-level GWAS data generator, or when establishing that a simulation pipeline can produce GWAS summary statistics and select IVs within a 0.1 s budget. When benchmarking generate_individual(), which builds individual-level genotype and phenotype data before running GWAS and is explicitly slower — its runtime is not covered by the ≤ 0.1 s summary-level bound When the goal is to validate the statistical correctness (bias, power, Type I error) of MR estimators on simulated data rather than the computational performance of the data-generation pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime of simmrd's generate_summary() function across the paper's five default simulation scenarios (CHP, UHP, UHP+CHP, weak IVs, UHP+CHP+weak IVs) to verify it meets the Table 1 performance bound of ≤ 0.1 s per replicate. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime of simmrd's generate_summary() function across the paper's five default simulation scenarios (CHP, UHP, UHP+CHP, weak IVs, UHP+CHP+weak IVs) to verify it meets the Table 1 performance bound of ≤ 0.1 s per replicate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When benchmarking generate_individual(), which builds individual-level genotype and phenotype data before running GWAS and is explicitly slower — its runtime is not covered by the ≤ 0.1 s summary-level bound When the goal is to validate the statistical correctness (bias, power, Type I error) of MR estimators on simulated data rather than the computational performance of the data-generation pipeline

skills.description: Use when the task requires simulating allele-frequency change over generations under combined deterministic and stochastic forces (e.g., selection and drift) and producing time-series trajectories plus plots from a biallelic population-genetic model.
skills.name: simulation-trajectory-visualization
skills.search_text: simulation-trajectory-visualization Use when the task requires simulating allele-frequency change over generations under combined deterministic and stochastic forces (e.g., selection and drift) and producing time-series trajectories plus plots from a biallelic population-genetic model. The goal is purely deterministic analysis with no stochastic (drift) component — use a deterministic selection or frequency-function tool instead The trait is quantitative/phenotypic rather than a biallelic gene frequency — learnPopGen handles phenotypic trait changes under selection via other functions The user cannot use R and needs a result without any R session — the article recommends web interfaces for those 'less adept in the R environment', which may be a better route than scripting this simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Simulate allele-frequency trajectories under deterministic and stochastic evolutionary processes (e.g., selection plus genetic drift at a biallelic locus) using learnPopGen's Wright–Fisher-style simulation functions, then export and visualize the generation-by-generation trajectories as plots/graphics. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412
skills.summary: Simulate allele-frequency trajectories under deterministic and stochastic evolutionary processes (e.g., selection plus genetic drift at a biallelic locus) using learnPopGen's Wright–Fisher-style simulation functions, then export and visualize the generation-by-generation trajectories as plots/graphics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is purely deterministic analysis with no stochastic (drift) component — use a deterministic selection or frequency-function tool instead The trait is quantitative/phenotypic rather than a biallelic gene frequency — learnPopGen handles phenotypic trait changes under selection via other functions The user cannot use R and needs a result without any R session — the article recommends web interfaces for those 'less adept in the R environment', which may be a better route than scripting this simulation

skills.description: Use when comparing nanopore signal simulators (e.g. seq2squiggle vs squigulator) on similarity of simulated raw signals to real experimental reads, via DTW distance on a fixed read set.
skills.name: simulator-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: simulator-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing nanopore signal simulators (e.g. seq2squiggle vs squigulator) on similarity of simulated raw signals to real experimental reads, via DTW distance on a fixed read set. The goal is to generate synthetic reads from a reference genome rather than compare simulators on existing reads — use seq2squiggle's default Reference mode instead of Read-mode evaluation Only basecalled sequences are available with no real raw signal data to serve as the ground-truth comparison set Evaluating sequence-level fidelity (base accuracy) rather than raw signal-level similarity to experimental reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark nanopore signal simulators by measuring how closely their simulated raw signals resemble real experimental reads, using length-normalized dynamic-time-warping (DTW) distances. This is the evaluation strategy the seq2squiggle paper used to show transformer-based simulation outperforms static k-mer-model simulators (median DTW ≈ 9.78 vs ≈ 10.01 on R10.4.1 data). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Benchmark nanopore signal simulators by measuring how closely their simulated raw signals resemble real experimental reads, using length-normalized dynamic-time-warping (DTW) distances. This is the evaluation strategy the seq2squiggle paper used to show transformer-based simulation outperforms static k-mer-model simulators (median DTW ≈ 9.78 vs ≈ 10.01 on R10.4.1 data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to generate synthetic reads from a reference genome rather than compare simulators on existing reads — use seq2squiggle's default Reference mode instead of Read-mode evaluation Only basecalled sequences are available with no real raw signal data to serve as the ground-truth comparison set Evaluating sequence-level fidelity (base accuracy) rather than raw signal-level similarity to experimental reads

skills.description: Use when nanomonsv single breakend results contain contigs from highly repetitive centromeric sequences that need to be subset for high-order repeat (HOR) consistency analysis with HORmon monomers and StringDecomposer.
skills.name: single-breakend-contig-repeat-annotation-filtering
skills.search_text: single-breakend-contig-repeat-annotation-filtering Use when nanomonsv single breakend results contain contigs from highly repetitive centromeric sequences that need to be subset for high-order repeat (HOR) consistency analysis with HORmon monomers and StringDecomposer. Single breakend SVs whose breakpoints lie in poorly characterized repetitive regions where the reference genome is unreliable and RepeatMasker gives no informative annotation (e.g. both breakpoints in uncharacterized repeats) Canonical (two-breakend) somatic SVs from the nanomonsv Canonical SV module, which are assessed by short-read-compatible precision/recall rather than centromeric HOR consistency Non-centromeric repeats (e.g. LINE1-mediated insertions, viral integrations) where HORmon monomer decomposition is not the appropriate analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Selects contigs from the nanomonsv Single breakend SV module results that derive from highly repetitive centromeric regions, by filtering on the single breakend result file's Contig column and RepeatMasker 'Satellite/centr' annotations, so that downstream HOR match scoring is applied to the right contig set. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Selects contigs from the nanomonsv Single breakend SV module results that derive from highly repetitive centromeric regions, by filtering on the single breakend result file's Contig column and RepeatMasker 'Satellite/centr' annotations, so that downstream HOR match scoring is applied to the right contig set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single breakend SVs whose breakpoints lie in poorly characterized repetitive regions where the reference genome is unreliable and RepeatMasker gives no informative annotation (e.g. both breakpoints in uncharacterized repeats) Canonical (two-breakend) somatic SVs from the nanomonsv Canonical SV module, which are assessed by short-read-compatible precision/recall rather than centromeric HOR consistency Non-centromeric repeats (e.g. LINE1-mediated insertions, viral integrations) where HORmon monomer decomposition is not the appropriate analysis

skills.description: Use when paired tumor and matched-control ONT (or PacBio) long-read data must be scanned for somatic SVs with only one resolvable breakpoint, e.g., centromeric/satellite rearrangements, LINE1-mediated events, or viral integrations that short-read callers miss.
skills.name: single-breakend-sv-detection
skills.search_text: single-breakend-sv-detection Use when paired tumor and matched-control ONT (or PacBio) long-read data must be scanned for somatic SVs with only one resolvable breakpoint, e.g., centromeric/satellite rearrangements, LINE1-mediated events, or viral integrations that short-read callers miss. Both breakpoints of the SV of interest lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions where the reference genome is unreliable — the Single breakend SV module cannot detect such events The goal is to capture long repeat expansion events (VNTR/microsatellite expansions) — a reference-genome-based framework is not appropriate for these Only short-read data are available — single breakend SVs of this complexity are identifiable only by long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Use nanomonsv's Single breakend SV module to detect somatic SVs in which only one breakpoint can be identified — typically because the other end falls in poorly characterized repetitive regions such as centromeric satellite sequences, LINE1-mediated rearrangements, or viral (e.g., HBV) integration sites — from tumor/control paired long-read data. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Use nanomonsv's Single breakend SV module to detect somatic SVs in which only one breakpoint can be identified — typically because the other end falls in poorly characterized repetitive regions such as centromeric satellite sequences, LINE1-mediated rearrangements, or viral (e.g., HBV) integration sites — from tumor/control paired long-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Both breakpoints of the SV of interest lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions where the reference genome is unreliable — the Single breakend SV module cannot detect such events The goal is to capture long repeat expansion events (VNTR/microsatellite expansions) — a reference-genome-based framework is not appropriate for these Only short-read data are available — single breakend SVs of this complexity are identifiable only by long reads

skills.description: Use when query scRNA-seq datasets have known ground-truth cell-type labels and you need to quantify or compare annotation accuracy of reference-based classifiers, including atlas-referenced settings where some query types are absent from the reference.
skills.name: single-cell-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-accuracy-benchmarking Use when query scRNA-seq datasets have known ground-truth cell-type labels and you need to quantify or compare annotation accuracy of reference-based classifiers, including atlas-referenced settings where some query types are absent from the reference. Query datasets lack credible ground-truth cell-type labels, so accuracy cannot be tabulated You need a single-method annotation result rather than a comparative benchmark across methods Query cell types are completely covered by a well-matched specific reference, where the exploratory atlas-referenced setting (and its labeled-accuracy caveats) does not apply Benchmark single-cell annotation accuracy by running a query classifier (e.g. scMAGIC, scMCA, scHCL) against datasets with known true cell-type labels and comparing per-method accuracy and labeled balanced accuracy across matched method-dataset pairs. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell annotation accuracy by running a query classifier (e.g. scMAGIC, scMCA, scHCL) against datasets with known true cell-type labels and comparing per-method accuracy and labeled balanced accuracy across matched method-dataset pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query datasets lack credible ground-truth cell-type labels, so accuracy cannot be tabulated You need a single-method annotation result rather than a comparative benchmark across methods Query cell types are completely covered by a well-matched specific reference, where the exploratory atlas-referenced setting (and its labeled-accuracy caveats) does not apply

skills.description: Use when processing concatenated long-read single-cell cDNA data (PacBio MAS-Seq/MAS-ISO-seq or ONT) with nanoranger and a protocol-specific adapter barcode pattern (e.g., TruSeq adapter) must be configured to segment reads and recover cell barcodes/UMIs.
skills.name: single-cell-barcode-search-configuration
skills.search_text: single-cell-barcode-search-configuration Use when processing concatenated long-read single-cell cDNA data (PacBio MAS-Seq/MAS-ISO-seq or ONT) with nanoranger and a protocol-specific adapter barcode pattern (e.g., TruSeq adapter) must be configured to segment reads and recover cell barcodes/UMIs. Input is short-read scRNA-seq data with whitelisted 10x Genomics barcodes — nanoranger's barcode search targets concatenated long reads from intermediate single-cell cDNA libraries Reads are already deconcatenated into individual molecules with barcodes assigned, so no adapter-barcode-driven segmentation is needed Genomic (non-cDNA) long reads without single-cell barcode structure, where segment demultiplexing by adapter barcode is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configure the nanoranger workflow's barcode search (e.g., the TruSeq-adapter barcode search for PacBio MAS-Seq/MAS-ISO-seq runs) so concatenated long reads from single-cell cDNA libraries are correctly split into per-cell segments with cell barcodes and UMIs assigned before quantification. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Configure the nanoranger workflow's barcode search (e.g., the TruSeq-adapter barcode search for PacBio MAS-Seq/MAS-ISO-seq runs) so concatenated long reads from single-cell cDNA libraries are correctly split into per-cell segments with cell barcodes and UMIs assigned before quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read scRNA-seq data with whitelisted 10x Genomics barcodes — nanoranger's barcode search targets concatenated long reads from intermediate single-cell cDNA libraries Reads are already deconcatenated into individual molecules with barcodes assigned, so no adapter-barcode-driven segmentation is needed Genomic (non-cDNA) long reads without single-cell barcode structure, where segment demultiplexing by adapter barcode is not applicable

skills.description: Use when processing long-read FASTQ from 10x Genomics 5'-anchored whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries or targeted amplicons and you need per-cell, per-UMI assignment of reads before calling SNVs, fusions, isoforms, or CAR/TCR sequences.
skills.name: single-cell-barcode-umi-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-barcode-umi-annotation Use when processing long-read FASTQ from 10x Genomics 5'-anchored whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries or targeted amplicons and you need per-cell, per-UMI assignment of reads before calling SNVs, fusions, isoforms, or CAR/TCR sequences. Input is bulk (non-single-cell) amplicon or short-read Illumina data without 10x cell barcodes and UMIs embedded in reads — there is nothing to demultiplex per cell The transcript/locus of interest is far from the 5' end or longer than ~4 kB, where nanoranger's 5'-anchored capture is suboptimal Standard short-read scRNA-seq expression quantification is sufficient and no lineage-defining variant (SNV, fusion, isoform, CAR/TCR) is being genotyped http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts and annotates 10x Genomics cell barcodes (CBs) and unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) from long-read (ONT/PacBio) single-cell sequencing data, then error-corrects UMIs and calls cells so reads can be assigned per-cell to variants such as SNVs, fusion genes, CAR/TCR sequences, and isoforms. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Extracts and annotates 10x Genomics cell barcodes (CBs) and unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) from long-read (ONT/PacBio) single-cell sequencing data, then error-corrects UMIs and calls cells so reads can be assigned per-cell to variants such as SNVs, fusion genes, CAR/TCR sequences, and isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk (non-single-cell) amplicon or short-read Illumina data without 10x cell barcodes and UMIs embedded in reads — there is nothing to demultiplex per cell The transcript/locus of interest is far from the 5' end or longer than ~4 kB, where nanoranger's 5'-anchored capture is suboptimal Standard short-read scRNA-seq expression quantification is sufficient and no lineage-defining variant (SNV, fusion, isoform, CAR/TCR) is being genotyped

skills.description: Use when input FASTQ/BAM reads come from 10x Genomics whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries or targeted amplicons sequenced on ONT or Pacific Biosciences devices and need nanoranger processing, including multimer deconcatenation.
skills.name: single-cell-cdna-library-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: single-cell-cdna-library-pipeline-execution Use when input FASTQ/BAM reads come from 10x Genomics whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries or targeted amplicons sequenced on ONT or Pacific Biosciences devices and need nanoranger processing, including multimer deconcatenation. Input is short-read (e.g., Illumina) single-cell data — the workflow is designed for long-read ONT/PacBio reads, as short reads cannot resolve structural transcriptomic variants like fusions and isoforms Input is bulk (non-single-cell) sequencing data without 10x cell barcodes/UMIs — nanoranger starts from intermediate single-cell cDNA libraries Target loci are far from the 5' end of poorly expressed genes or transcripts longer than ~4 kB — the paper defines optimal nanoranger targets as loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcripts shorter than 4 kB http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Execute the nanoranger long-read single-cell pipeline on 5'-anchored 10x Genomics scRNA-seq cDNA libraries, including deconcatenation of multimer reads (e.g., PacBio 15-mer MAS-seq arrays) into subreads before alignment and barcode/UMI-aware processing. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Execute the nanoranger long-read single-cell pipeline on 5'-anchored 10x Genomics scRNA-seq cDNA libraries, including deconcatenation of multimer reads (e.g., PacBio 15-mer MAS-seq arrays) into subreads before alignment and barcode/UMI-aware processing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (e.g., Illumina) single-cell data — the workflow is designed for long-read ONT/PacBio reads, as short reads cannot resolve structural transcriptomic variants like fusions and isoforms Input is bulk (non-single-cell) sequencing data without 10x cell barcodes/UMIs — nanoranger starts from intermediate single-cell cDNA libraries Target loci are far from the 5' end of poorly expressed genes or transcripts longer than ~4 kB — the paper defines optimal nanoranger targets as loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcripts shorter than 4 kB

skills.description: Use when pseudobulk per-cell-type isoform counts from long-read single-cell data are available for two cell groups and the goal is to find genes with differential transcript usage (gDTU) and per-transcript significance.
skills.name: single-cell-celltype-group-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-celltype-group-comparison Use when pseudobulk per-cell-type isoform counts from long-read single-cell data are available for two cell groups and the goal is to find genes with differential transcript usage (gDTU) and per-transcript significance. No cell-type markerset was supplied, so scywalker did not run scsorter and no pseudobulk per-cell-type counts exist to compare The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than differential transcript/isoform usage (DTU) More than two groups must be contrasted simultaneously without a pairwise design, since the procedure is built around a two-group comparison design matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compares assigned cell-type groups (e.g. neuronal vs glial) using scywalker pseudobulk isoform counts and a two-stage DRIMSeq/stageR Dirichlet-multinomial DTU analysis, yielding genes with differential transcript usage (gDTU) at FDR < 0.05 with per-transcript tFDR values. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Compares assigned cell-type groups (e.g. neuronal vs glial) using scywalker pseudobulk isoform counts and a two-stage DRIMSeq/stageR Dirichlet-multinomial DTU analysis, yielding genes with differential transcript usage (gDTU) at FDR < 0.05 with per-transcript tFDR values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-type markerset was supplied, so scywalker did not run scsorter and no pseudobulk per-cell-type counts exist to compare The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than differential transcript/isoform usage (DTU) More than two groups must be contrasted simultaneously without a pairwise design, since the procedure is built around a two-group comparison design matrix

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with known variance-component structure (random intercepts in mean and/or zero-inflation components) to evaluate type-I error or power of mixed-effects DE tests.
skills.name: single-cell-count-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-data-simulation Use when you need synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with known variance-component structure (random intercepts in mean and/or zero-inflation components) to evaluate type-I error or power of mixed-effects DE tests. The goal is analysis of a real scRNA-seq dataset — simulation is only for benchmarking type-I error/power, not for producing biological findings You need normalized expression values or log-transformed data — the twosigma count_matrix input must be non-negative integer counts with no normalization performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulates zero-inflated negative binomial single-cell count data with random effects using the simulate_zero_inflated_nb_random_effect_data function of the twosigma R package, to benchmark model-based association tests such as TWO-SIGMA variance-component likelihood ratio tests. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Simulates zero-inflated negative binomial single-cell count data with random effects using the simulate_zero_inflated_nb_random_effect_data function of the twosigma R package, to benchmark model-based association tests such as TWO-SIGMA variance-component likelihood ratio tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is analysis of a real scRNA-seq dataset — simulation is only for benchmarking type-I error/power, not for producing biological findings You need normalized expression values or log-transformed data — the twosigma count_matrix input must be non-negative integer counts with no normalization performed

skills.description: Use when a long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) single-cell count matrix (e.g. Sicelore PREFIX_genematrix.txt) must be benchmarked against a same-sample Illumina Cell Ranger matrix to quantify agreement.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-comparison Use when a long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) single-cell count matrix (e.g. Sicelore PREFIX_genematrix.txt) must be benchmarked against a same-sample Illumina Cell Ranger matrix to quantify agreement. The two count matrices come from different biological samples or incompatible barcode whitelists, since barcode intersection would be meaningless The long-read matrix was produced by a short-read-free workflow (e.g. Sicelore 2.1) without a same-sample Illumina counterpart to validate against The goal is isoform, SNP, or fusion-level comparison rather than gene/UMI count concordance, which these matrices do not directly capture http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Cross-platform validation of Nanopore single-cell gene/UMI count matrices against Illumina Cell Ranger matrices by computing per-cell gene/UMI totals and Pearson correlations, verifying that the long-read dataset faithfully represents the 10x Genomics transcriptome. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Cross-platform validation of Nanopore single-cell gene/UMI count matrices against Illumina Cell Ranger matrices by computing per-cell gene/UMI totals and Pearson correlations, verifying that the long-read dataset faithfully represents the 10x Genomics transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two count matrices come from different biological samples or incompatible barcode whitelists, since barcode intersection would be meaningless The long-read matrix was produced by a short-read-free workflow (e.g. Sicelore 2.1) without a same-sample Illumina counterpart to validate against The goal is isoform, SNP, or fusion-level comparison rather than gene/UMI count concordance, which these matrices do not directly capture

skills.description: Use when HIT-scISOseq PacBio HiFi reads (post cellBC/UMI correction) must be converted into cell-by-gene or cell-by-isoform count matrices, or when cross-platform agreement with 10x Genomics/NGS counts on the same cDNA needs to be measured.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-processing Use when HIT-scISOseq PacBio HiFi reads (post cellBC/UMI correction) must be converted into cell-by-gene or cell-by-isoform count matrices, or when cross-platform agreement with 10x Genomics/NGS counts on the same cDNA needs to be measured. Input is raw CCS/subreads BAM that has not yet been classified by primer or barcode-corrected — scGene_matrix requires FLNC reads with valid cellBC/UMI The goal is isoform structural characterization or QC classification (SQANTI3/filter.tmap.pl territory), not building expression count matrices Data derive from platforms other than 10x Genomics — compatibility is claimed but not demonstrated in the study http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Build and validate single-cell UMI/gene count matrices from HIT-scISOseq long reads using the scISA-Tools scGene_matrix and scIsoform_matrix utilities, then quantify platform concordance against Illumina short-read NGS via Pearson correlations on cell-barcode and gene-aggregated UMI counts. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Build and validate single-cell UMI/gene count matrices from HIT-scISOseq long reads using the scISA-Tools scGene_matrix and scIsoform_matrix utilities, then quantify platform concordance against Illumina short-read NGS via Pearson correlations on cell-barcode and gene-aggregated UMI counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw CCS/subreads BAM that has not yet been classified by primer or barcode-corrected — scGene_matrix requires FLNC reads with valid cellBC/UMI The goal is isoform structural characterization or QC classification (SQANTI3/filter.tmap.pl territory), not building expression count matrices Data derive from platforms other than 10x Genomics — compatibility is claimed but not demonstrated in the study

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic scRNA-seq counts with known co-expression modules (ground-truth cluster labels) to benchmark correlation metrics or clustering pipelines.
skills.name: single-cell-count-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-simulation Use when you need synthetic scRNA-seq counts with known co-expression modules (ground-truth cluster labels) to benchmark correlation metrics or clustering pipelines. Input is already real scRNA-seq data with no recoverable ground truth — simulation is only needed when benchmarking against known cluster structure The goal is downstream biological analysis of actual expression data rather than controlled evaluation of co-expression metrics You need long-read transcriptome definition or functional annotation — the acorde package explicitly excludes these steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulate single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with known co-expression cluster structure using the SymSim R package, so that co-expression metrics (percentile, Pearson, Spearman, zero-inflated Kendall, rho proportionality) can be benchmarked against ground truth. Used in the acorde study to validate that percentile correlations recover co-expression modules in sparse single-cell data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Simulate single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with known co-expression cluster structure using the SymSim R package, so that co-expression metrics (percentile, Pearson, Spearman, zero-inflated Kendall, rho proportionality) can be benchmarked against ground truth. Used in the acorde study to validate that percentile correlations recover co-expression modules in sparse single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already real scRNA-seq data with no recoverable ground truth — simulation is only needed when benchmarking against known cluster structure The goal is downstream biological analysis of actual expression data rather than controlled evaluation of co-expression metrics You need long-read transcriptome definition or functional annotation — the acorde package explicitly excludes these steps

skills.description: Use when analyzing scywalker long-read single-cell (10x Oxford nanopore or PacBio) data and you need expression-based cell groups, cell-type assignments, and per-cell-type pseudobulk gene/isoform count tables per sample.
skills.name: single-cell-expression-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-expression-clustering Use when analyzing scywalker long-read single-cell (10x Oxford nanopore or PacBio) data and you need expression-based cell groups, cell-type assignments, and per-cell-type pseudobulk gene/isoform count tables per sample. No cell-specific markersets are available and scSorter-based typing/pseudobulk is required without falling back to ScType only Data are not single-cell long-read cDNA (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or short-read-only data); scywalker targets 10x Oxford nanopore (or PacBio with -pacbioindex) data Only empty droplets/background barcodes are of interest — use the _raw counts instead of filtered cell-type pseudobulk outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 In scywalker, single-cell expression clustering retains only EmptyDrops-approved cells, groups them with Seurat clustering (resolution 0.5), assigns cell types via ScType (internal tissue database) and scSorter (marker tsv), then aggregates filtered per-cell gene/isoform counts into per-cell-type pseudobulk tables. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: In scywalker, single-cell expression clustering retains only EmptyDrops-approved cells, groups them with Seurat clustering (resolution 0.5), assigns cell types via ScType (internal tissue database) and scSorter (marker tsv), then aggregates filtered per-cell gene/isoform counts into per-cell-type pseudobulk tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-specific markersets are available and scSorter-based typing/pseudobulk is required without falling back to ScType only Data are not single-cell long-read cDNA (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or short-read-only data); scywalker targets 10x Oxford nanopore (or PacBio with -pacbioindex) data Only empty droplets/background barcodes are of interest — use the _raw counts instead of filtered cell-type pseudobulk outputs

The goal is isoform-level rather than gene-level quantification — use scIsoform_matrix instead The tmap still contains multi-mapping FLNC transcripts (filter.tmap.pl has not been run), since the matrix must be built exclusively from uniquely mapped reads Cell barcodes and UMIs have not yet been corrected (no cellBC_UMI_correction.xls output from cellBC_UMI_corrector) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates the per-sample single-cell gene expression quantity table from uniquely mapped FLNC reads in the scISA-Tools/HIT-scISOseq pipeline, using the scGene_matrix utility downstream of gffcompare-based gene assignment and cellBC/UMI correction. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Generates the per-sample single-cell gene expression quantity table from uniquely mapped FLNC reads in the scISA-Tools/HIT-scISOseq pipeline, using the scGene_matrix utility downstream of gffcompare-based gene assignment and cellBC/UMI correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is isoform-level rather than gene-level quantification — use scIsoform_matrix instead The tmap still contains multi-mapping FLNC transcripts (filter.tmap.pl has not been run), since the matrix must be built exclusively from uniquely mapped reads Cell barcodes and UMIs have not yet been corrected (no cellBC_UMI_correction.xls output from cellBC_UMI_corrector)

skills.description: Use when a reference-based classifier (e.g. scMAGIC first round) has produced candidate labels per query cell and you must separate confidently validated cells from low-confidence negative controls before retraining or reclassification.
skills.name: single-cell-identity-validation
skills.search_text: single-cell-identity-validation Use when a reference-based classifier (e.g. scMAGIC first round) has produced candidate labels per query cell and you must separate confidently validated cells from low-confidence negative controls before retraining or reclassification. The query cell types are already fully covered by a high-quality reference and no batch effects exist between reference and query datasets You only need a first-round annotation and do not intend to run a second-round RBC with validated query cells as the new reference Any candidate local reference cell label is supported by fewer than min_cell validated query cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates first-round candidate cell labels in scMAGIC (Module 3) by scoring each query cell with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on the candidate reference cell type's marker genes, decomposing confidence-score densities with mclust, and using confidently validated cells to build the local reference and per-label negative control expression matrices consumed by the second-round RBC. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Validates first-round candidate cell labels in scMAGIC (Module 3) by scoring each query cell with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on the candidate reference cell type's marker genes, decomposing confidence-score densities with mclust, and using confidently validated cells to build the local reference and per-label negative control expression matrices consumed by the second-round RBC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query cell types are already fully covered by a high-quality reference and no batch effects exist between reference and query datasets You only need a first-round annotation and do not intend to run a second-round RBC with validated query cells as the new reference Any candidate local reference cell label is supported by fewer than min_cell validated query cells

skills.description: Use when the input is a filtered isoform-level single-cell count matrix (e.g. 6794 isoforms from Tasic et al. Smart-Seq2 data) with cell type labels, and sparse cell-level counts make direct cell-to-cell correlations too noisy for co-expression estimation.
skills.name: single-cell-isoform-count-summarization
skills.search_text: single-cell-isoform-count-summarization Use when the input is a filtered isoform-level single-cell count matrix (e.g. 6794 isoforms from Tasic et al. Smart-Seq2 data) with cell type labels, and sparse cell-level counts make direct cell-to-cell correlations too noisy for co-expression estimation. Input is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated to cell-type/group-level expression, where direct correlations suffice and percentile summarization of single-cell sparsity is unnecessary The goal is functional (tappAS/isoAnnotLite) annotation analysis or DIU/coDIU testing rather than co-expression estimation, since acorde handles those as separate analysis blocks The count matrix has not been DE-filtered, so the isoform set has not been reduced to isoforms with detectable expression signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Summarizes sparse single-cell isoform count values into cell-type-level percentile profiles (10 deciles) before computing correlations, as implemented in acorde's percentile correlation method for isoform co-expression estimation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Summarizes sparse single-cell isoform count values into cell-type-level percentile profiles (10 deciles) before computing correlations, as implemented in acorde's percentile correlation method for isoform co-expression estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated to cell-type/group-level expression, where direct correlations suffice and percentile summarization of single-cell sparsity is unnecessary The goal is functional (tappAS/isoAnnotLite) annotation analysis or DIU/coDIU testing rather than co-expression estimation, since acorde handles those as separate analysis blocks The count matrix has not been DE-filtered, so the isoform set has not been reduced to isoforms with detectable expression signal

skills.description: Use when a collapsed long-read single-cell isoform FASTA (e.g. all.collapsed.rep.fa from cDNA_Cupcake) must be classified with SQANTI3 and the resulting per-sample retained isoform counts and structural-category distribution (FSM/ISM/NIC/NNC) need validation against reported values.
skills.name: single-cell-isoform-count-verification
skills.search_text: single-cell-isoform-count-verification Use when a collapsed long-read single-cell isoform FASTA (e.g. all.collapsed.rep.fa from cDNA_Cupcake) must be classified with SQANTI3 and the resulting per-sample retained isoform counts and structural-category distribution (FSM/ISM/NIC/NNC) need validation against reported values. Input is raw CCS/FLNC reads that have not yet been collapsed to nonredundant isoforms — run collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py first The goal is gene-level single-cell quantification (scGene_matrix / scIsoform_matrix UMI counting), not transcript structural classification Data derive from short-read scRNA-Seq (e.g. 10x 3' gene expression), where structural categories like FSM/NIC are not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Verifies the characterization and filtering step of the HIT-scISOseq single-cell isoform pipeline by running SQANTI3 QC on collapsed isoforms and checking that retained isoform counts and the dominant isoform class reproduce the reported results (29,392 isoforms for sample s1, 31,793 for s2, FSM most abundant). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Verifies the characterization and filtering step of the HIT-scISOseq single-cell isoform pipeline by running SQANTI3 QC on collapsed isoforms and checking that retained isoform counts and the dominant isoform class reproduce the reported results (29,392 isoforms for sample s1, 31,793 for s2, FSM most abundant).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw CCS/FLNC reads that have not yet been collapsed to nonredundant isoforms — run collapse_isoforms_by_sam.py first The goal is gene-level single-cell quantification (scGene_matrix / scIsoform_matrix UMI counting), not transcript structural classification Data derive from short-read scRNA-Seq (e.g. 10x 3' gene expression), where structural categories like FSM/NIC are not applicable

skills.description: Use when you must assess how stable isoform-level DE/DIU calls are to random cell sampling in single-cell isoform count matrices, e.g. before trusting multi-group DESeq2/edgeR DIU results on Tasic-style neural Smart-Seq2 data.
skills.name: single-cell-isoform-downsampling-robustness-testing
skills.search_text: single-cell-isoform-downsampling-robustness-testing Use when you must assess how stable isoform-level DE/DIU calls are to random cell sampling in single-cell isoform count matrices, e.g. before trusting multi-group DESeq2/edgeR DIU results on Tasic-style neural Smart-Seq2 data. Input is a gene-level (not isoform-level) expression matrix — acorde's DIU testing requires isoform quantification. The goal is bulk RNA-seq differential expression where per-cell sampling variability and zero inflation are not relevant, so downsampling robustness estimation is unnecessary. You need long-read transcriptome building or functional annotation of isoforms — the acorde R package explicitly excludes these external steps. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking workflow that quantifies the reproducibility of multi-group differential isoform usage (DIU) calls by repeating random downsampling of scRNA-seq cells, running DESeq2 and edgeR on each replicate, and summarizing per-method DE counts and within-method Jaccard indices against published benchmarks. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: A benchmarking workflow that quantifies the reproducibility of multi-group differential isoform usage (DIU) calls by repeating random downsampling of scRNA-seq cells, running DESeq2 and edgeR on each replicate, and summarizing per-method DE counts and within-method Jaccard indices against published benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a gene-level (not isoform-level) expression matrix — acorde's DIU testing requires isoform quantification. The goal is bulk RNA-seq differential expression where per-cell sampling variability and zero inflation are not relevant, so downsampling robustness estimation is unnecessary. You need long-read transcriptome building or functional annotation of isoforms — the acorde R package explicitly excludes these external steps.

skills.description: Use when long-read single-cell Nanopore data with 10x cell barcodes and UMIs must be quantified against known transcript annotations to produce per-cell isoform and gene count matrices.
skills.name: single-cell-isoform-quantification-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: single-cell-isoform-quantification-matrix-generation Use when long-read single-cell Nanopore data with 10x cell barcodes and UMIs must be quantified against known transcript annotations to produce per-cell isoform and gene count matrices. Input is raw Nanopore FASTQ without cell barcode/UMI annotation or prior UMI-guided consensus generation — run Sicelore Steps 1–4b (NanoporeBC_UMI_finder, mapping, UMI assignment, ComputeConsensus) first. The goal is novel isoform discovery from unannotated splicing; STRICT IsoformMatrix assignment only counts UMIs matching known Gencode transcript structures. Data are short-read scRNA-seq (e.g. Illumina-only 10x data) without full-length long reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates gene-, isoform- and junction-level UMI count matrices per cell by requiring a full exonic-structure match between UMI consensus reads and annotated Gencode transcripts, using Sicelore-2.1 IsoformMatrix on molecule BAMs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Generates gene-, isoform- and junction-level UMI count matrices per cell by requiring a full exonic-structure match between UMI consensus reads and annotated Gencode transcripts, using Sicelore-2.1 IsoformMatrix on molecule BAMs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Nanopore FASTQ without cell barcode/UMI annotation or prior UMI-guided consensus generation — run Sicelore Steps 1–4b (NanoporeBC_UMI_finder, mapping, UMI assignment, ComputeConsensus) first. The goal is novel isoform discovery from unannotated splicing; STRICT IsoformMatrix assignment only counts UMIs matching known Gencode transcript structures. Data are short-read scRNA-seq (e.g. Illumina-only 10x data) without full-length long reads.

skills.description: Use when analyzing 10x single-cell/nuclei Oxford nanopore (or PacBio) long-read cDNA and you need to call real cells via knee-plot thresholds plus emptydrops, or to build/interpret the scywalker HTML QC report.
skills.name: single-cell-knee-plot-qc-filtering
skills.search_text: single-cell-knee-plot-qc-filtering Use when analyzing 10x single-cell/nuclei Oxford nanopore (or PacBio) long-read cDNA and you need to call real cells via knee-plot thresholds plus emptydrops, or to build/interpret the scywalker HTML QC report. Input is bulk long-read RNA-seq without cell barcodes — emptydrops-based cell calling and knee plots are not applicable You only need pseudobulk per-cell-type isoform counts; the knee-plot QC step concerns per-cell (droplet) quality assessment, not pseudobulk aggregation Short-read scRNA-seq data is available and a matched short-read pipeline is preferred — scywalker is designed to analyse 10x nanopore data without matching short reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes knee-plot thresholds and applies emptydrops-based cell QC to distinguish real cells from empty droplets in scywalker's long-read single-cell analysis, then visualizes the approved cells in the interactive HTML QC report alongside read-length, genes-per-cell and UMAP panels. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Computes knee-plot thresholds and applies emptydrops-based cell QC to distinguish real cells from empty droplets in scywalker's long-read single-cell analysis, then visualizes the approved cells in the interactive HTML QC report alongside read-length, genes-per-cell and UMAP panels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk long-read RNA-seq without cell barcodes — emptydrops-based cell calling and knee plots are not applicable You only need pseudobulk per-cell-type isoform counts; the knee-plot QC step concerns per-cell (droplet) quality assessment, not pseudobulk aggregation Short-read scRNA-seq data is available and a matched short-read pipeline is preferred — scywalker is designed to analyse 10x nanopore data without matching short reads

skills.search_text: single-cell-long-read-pipeline-qc-metrics Use when deposited subreads BAM files from a 10x Genomics + PacBio single-cell isoform experiment must be reprocessed through CCS and FLNC classification to verify reported per-sample QC metrics. Input is already demultiplexed FLNC fastq or HiFi reads — no CCS or primer-classification step is needed The goal is isoform-level characterization (gffcompare, SQANTI3 filtering, isoform count matrices) rather than Table 1 read-processing metrics Libraries were not constructed via the 10x Genomics ScISOr-Seq/Linked-scISOseq/HIT-scISOseq primer structure (classify_by_primer detects full-length transcripts specifically for these protocols) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce the Table 1 read-processing QC metrics (CCS read counts/lengths, FLNC counts, artifact cDNA percentages) for ScISOr-Seq, Linked-scISOseq, and HIT-scISOseq from deposited PacBio subreads BAMs using the paper's stated CCS and FLNC-filtering parameters. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already demultiplexed FLNC fastq or HiFi reads — no CCS or primer-classification step is needed The goal is isoform-level characterization (gffcompare, SQANTI3 filtering, isoform count matrices) rather than Table 1 read-processing metrics Libraries were not constructed via the 10x Genomics ScISOr-Seq/Linked-scISOseq/HIT-scISOseq primer structure (classify_by_primer detects full-length transcripts specifically for these protocols)

skills.description: Use when processing raw PacBio subreads from single-cell PAIso-seq libraries and you need quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed CCS reads with reliable poly(A) tail calls before isoform or tail-length analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-pacbio-read-qc-filtering
skills.search_text: single-cell-pacbio-read-qc-filtering Use when processing raw PacBio subreads from single-cell PAIso-seq libraries and you need quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed CCS reads with reliable poly(A) tail calls before isoform or tail-length analysis. The input is short-read Illumina data or bulk (non-single-cell) RNA-seq — the QC thresholds and library structure (TSO/barcode/adapter layout) are specific to PAIso-seq PacBio single-oocyte libraries. You only need genome annotation or isoform clustering rather than per-read poly(A) tail QC — use IsoSeq3 clustering tools or TAPIS instead. Reads fail the paper's QC criteria (pass number <10, tail <15 nt or lacking 5 continuous adenosines) and cannot be rescued; filtering further is not meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply the PAIso-seq per-read QC filters for single mouse GV oocyte PacBio data: generate CCS reads, demultiplex/trim barcodes and adapters, and retain only reads with pass number >=10, clipped tail >=15 nt with >=5 continuous adenosines, and non-A residues <50% and <20 in number. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Apply the PAIso-seq per-read QC filters for single mouse GV oocyte PacBio data: generate CCS reads, demultiplex/trim barcodes and adapters, and retain only reads with pass number >=10, clipped tail >=15 nt with >=5 continuous adenosines, and non-A residues <50% and <20 in number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read Illumina data or bulk (non-single-cell) RNA-seq — the QC thresholds and library structure (TSO/barcode/adapter layout) are specific to PAIso-seq PacBio single-oocyte libraries. You only need genome annotation or isoform clustering rather than per-read poly(A) tail QC — use IsoSeq3 clustering tools or TAPIS instead. Reads fail the paper's QC criteria (pass number <10, tail <15 nt or lacking 5 continuous adenosines) and cannot be rescued; filtering further is not meaningful.

skills.description: Use when demultiplexing HIT-scISOseq or 10x Genomics-based long-read scRNA-seq FLNC reads requires correcting sequencing-error-derived cellBCs and merging UMI duplicates per gene/cell.

skills.search_text: single-cell-read-deduplication Use when demultiplexing HIT-scISOseq or 10x Genomics-based long-read scRNA-seq FLNC reads requires correcting sequencing-error-derived cellBCs and merging UMI duplicates per gene/cell. Input reads carry no cell barcodes or UMIs (e.g. bulk Iso-Seq or TSO-artifact reads lacking barcode structure) A short-read 10x scRNA-seq dataset is available that CellRanger can process natively; cellBC_UMI_corrector instead wraps CellRanger logic for long-read data without short-read guidance Barcode structure follows a non-10x design not represented in the 3M-february-2018 whitelist http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Correct single-cell barcodes against a whitelist and collapse UMI duplicates from long-read single-cell RNA-seq data using scISA-Tools' cellBC_UMI_corrector, which wraps CellRanger's cellBC/UMI correction logic for HIT-scISOseq FLNC reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-38324-9
skills.summary: Correct single-cell barcodes against a whitelist and collapse UMI duplicates from long-read single-cell RNA-seq data using scISA-Tools' cellBC_UMI_corrector, which wraps CellRanger's cellBC/UMI correction logic for HIT-scISOseq FLNC reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads carry no cell barcodes or UMIs (e.g. bulk Iso-Seq or TSO-artifact reads lacking barcode structure) A short-read 10x scRNA-seq dataset is available that CellRanger can process natively; cellBC_UMI_corrector instead wraps CellRanger logic for long-read data without short-read guidance Barcode structure follows a non-10x design not represented in the 3M-february-2018 whitelist

skills.description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset needs automated cell-type labels against a labeled scRNA-seq/bulk reference, especially when query cell types may not be fully covered by the reference or significant batch effects separate reference and query (e.g. SMART-seq reference vs Drop-seq query).
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset needs automated cell-type labels against a labeled scRNA-seq/bulk reference, especially when query cell types may not be fully covered by the reference or significant batch effects separate reference and query (e.g. SMART-seq reference vs Drop-seq query). The query dataset is bulk RNA-seq or non-expression data (e.g. ATAC, CITE-seq ADT) where expression-profile correlation and marker gene scoring are not applicable as designed No labeled reference expression matrix exists and no atlas (MCA/HCL) matches the organism — scMAGIC_atlas cannot produce reliable annotations without an atlas reference Cell labels already exist and are trusted; re-classification with RBC would be redundant rather than informative http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate query scRNA-seq cells against a well-annotated reference using scMAGIC, which identifies a candidate reference cell type by expression-profile correlation, validates identity via reference cell-type marker genes, and runs a second-round RBC using confidently validated query cells as a new reference to eliminate reference-query batch effects. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1275
skills.summary: Annotate query scRNA-seq cells against a well-annotated reference using scMAGIC, which identifies a candidate reference cell type by expression-profile correlation, validates identity via reference cell-type marker genes, and runs a second-round RBC using confidently validated query cells as a new reference to eliminate reference-query batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset is bulk RNA-seq or non-expression data (e.g. ATAC, CITE-seq ADT) where expression-profile correlation and marker gene scoring are not applicable as designed No labeled reference expression matrix exists and no atlas (MCA/HCL) matches the organism — scMAGIC_atlas cannot produce reliable annotations without an atlas reference Cell labels already exist and are trusted; re-classification with RBC would be redundant rather than informative

skills.description: Use when you have a raw single-cell count matrix (cells nested within individuals) and need gene-level covariate association inference that controls for drop-out (zero inflation), overdispersion, and within-sample correlation.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-count-modeling Use when you have a raw single-cell count matrix (cells nested within individuals) and need gene-level covariate association inference that controls for drop-out (zero inflation), overdispersion, and within-sample correlation. The ad hoc procedure is not recommended for use in gene set testing: when some genes have random effects and others do not, the common gene-level null required by twosigmag is not clearly met. Input is already normalized or log-transformed data — twosigma models observed counts directly (like a ZINB, unlike MAST's log-scale hurdle model) and performs no normalization. skills.search_text: single-molecule-methylation-calling Use when you have matched native and WGA PacBio SMRT cmp.h5 alignments for a bacterial genome and need per-molecule, per-motif-site methylation calls (e.g., quantifying methylated vs non-methylated fractions of a motif like 5'-CTGCAG). You only have population-level kinetics and want a consensus methylome call with no native/WGA pair available — SMsn requires matched WGA alignments for the score difference. The modification type creates kinetic signatures extending into surrounding bases — the paper states detection of such modifications is beyond the scope of the current work. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3656 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 SMALR's SMsn protocol calls methylation status at each motif site on each individual SMRT sequencing molecule by comparing subread-normalized ln(IPD) kinetics of native DNA against a whole-genome-amplified (WGA) control, yielding a single-molecule score rather than a population-level consensus. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms8438

skills.name: slr-barcode-aware-local-assembly

Calls shorter than 50 bp are the target — out_50.vcf only contains indels >50 bp, and other calls in out.vcf are explicitly unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run Blackbird, an integrated alignment- and local-assembly-based SV caller that exploits BX barcode information in synthetic long reads (SLR) and optional low-coverage long reads, to sensitively detect medium-size insertions and deletions (50–10,000 bp) without whole-genome assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151

skills.when_to_use_negative: Whole-genome de novo assembly output is required — Blackbird deliberately assembles only small sliding-window segments, not the full genome. skills.search_text: small-indel-size-thresholding Use when a NanoSV VCF from long-read (MinION nanopore) data contains indel calls and you must exclude sub-40 bp indels that are not genuine split-alignment structural variants. When calling short indels (<40 bp) themselves — this skill removes them by design, since they are not typically split-aligned; use a dedicated small-variant caller instead. When the input is not a long-read (MinION/PacBio) NanoSV-style call set — split-alignment-based size thresholds are not calibrated for short-read indel callers such as those applied to Illumina data. When a downstream analysis specifically targets small indel events; this filter intentionally discards them as out of SV scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 A post-calling filter that removes indel calls smaller than a 40 base pair threshold from a NanoSV structural-variant call set, because indels below this size typically do not produce split-read alignments and therefore fall outside NanoSV's SV detection regime. Applied after repeat-region filtering, it reduced the NA12878 chromosome 1 call set from 657 to 654 SVs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: A post-calling filter that removes indel calls smaller than a 40 base pair threshold from a NanoSV structural-variant call set, because indels below this size typically do not produce split-read alignments and therefore fall outside NanoSV's SV detection regime. Applied after repeat-region filtering, it reduced the NA12878 chromosome 1 call set from 657 to 654 SVs.

skills.search_text: smith-waterman-local-alignment Use when reconstructing FMAlign2's MEMs-filtering and partial-chain-formation step: after MEMs are found and filtered, similar substrings must be recovered in sequences lacking MEMs via local alignment before segmentation. skills.search_text: snp-quality-and-boundary-proximity-filtering Use when you have called SNPs (e.g. BCFTools on reads mapped to predicted exons) and need to derive genotypable regions before comparing against a validated SNP reference set. The goal is exon/splice graph prediction or read filtering (biobloomcategorizer, cascading Bloom filter) — those are upstream EXFI steps, not SNP post-filtering.
