skills.description: Use when haplotype-resolved methylation or allele-specific methylation must be derived from PacBio HiFi/CCS modBAMs: per-read 5mCpG calls exist but reads are not yet haplotagged and no phased SNV VCF is available.
skills.name: snv-calling-and-haplotype-phasing
skills.search_text: snv-calling-and-haplotype-phasing Use when haplotype-resolved methylation or allele-specific methylation must be derived from PacBio HiFi/CCS modBAMs: per-read 5mCpG calls exist but reads are not yet haplotagged and no phased SNV VCF is available. Input reads are nanopore or Illumina rather than PacBio CCS/HiFi — Clair3 must run with the hifi model and the pipeline is designed for CCS kinetics-derived modBAMs. The modBAMs already carry haplotype tags and a phased SNV VCF exists — re-running calling/phasing would be redundant. The goal is read-level 5mC detection without haplotype resolution — ccsmeth alone suffices, no SNV calling/phasing needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Calls SNVs from ccsmeth-generated modified-base BAMs with Clair3 (hifi model) and phases PASS SNVs and reads with WhatsHap to produce haplotype-resolved VCFs and haplotagged modBAMs, enabling haplotype-aware methylation detection from PacBio CCS reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-39784-9
skills.summary: Calls SNVs from ccsmeth-generated modified-base BAMs with Clair3 (hifi model) and phases PASS SNVs and reads with WhatsHap to produce haplotype-resolved VCFs and haplotagged modBAMs, enabling haplotype-aware methylation detection from PacBio CCS reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are nanopore or Illumina rather than PacBio CCS/HiFi — Clair3 must run with the hifi model and the pipeline is designed for CCS kinetics-derived modBAMs. The modBAMs already carry haplotype tags and a phased SNV VCF exists — re-running calling/phasing would be redundant. The goal is read-level 5mC detection without haplotype resolution — ccsmeth alone suffices, no SNV calling/phasing needed.

skills.description: Use when you have minimap2-aligned ONT (or PacBio SMRT) whole-genome BAM/CRAM reads plus an indexed GRCh38/hg38 FASTA and need accurate, phased diploid SNV calls benchmarked against GIAB high-confidence sets.
skills.name: snv-calling-from-ont-long-reads
skills.search_text: snv-calling-from-ont-long-reads Use when you have minimap2-aligned ONT (or PacBio SMRT) whole-genome BAM/CRAM reads plus an indexed GRCh38/hg38 FASTA and need accurate, phased diploid SNV calls benchmarked against GIAB high-confidence sets. You need to call indels de novo — Longshot only calls SNVs; it can genotype indels only if supplied in an input VCF, and accurate short indel calling from SMS reads is limited by high insertion/deletion error rates. Structural variants > 50 bp are needed — they are not supported by Longshot and require SV-specific callers. Input is short-read sequencing data — the haplotype-informed genotyping model is designed for long, error-prone SMS reads, not Illumina data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call and phase diploid SNVs from Oxford Nanopore (or PacBio) long, error-prone reads using Longshot, which combines pileup-based allelotyping, pair-HMM local realignment, and haplotype-informed genotyping via HapCUT2. On NA12878 37x whole-genome ONT data this reproduces best F1 0.967 against GIAB high-confidence calls in ~5h13m on one core. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Call and phase diploid SNVs from Oxford Nanopore (or PacBio) long, error-prone reads using Longshot, which combines pileup-based allelotyping, pair-HMM local realignment, and haplotype-informed genotyping via HapCUT2. On NA12878 37x whole-genome ONT data this reproduces best F1 0.967 against GIAB high-confidence calls in ~5h13m on one core.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to call indels de novo — Longshot only calls SNVs; it can genotype indels only if supplied in an input VCF, and accurate short indel calling from SMS reads is limited by high insertion/deletion error rates. Structural variants > 50 bp are needed — they are not supported by Longshot and require SV-specific callers. Input is short-read sequencing data — the haplotype-informed genotyping model is designed for long, error-prone SMS reads, not Illumina data.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking long-read SNV calls against GIAB truth sets and you need to characterize error sequence contexts (indel-proximate FPs, homopolymer FNs) or evaluate an indel-proximity filter for FP reduction.
skills.name: snv-false-positive-context-annotation
skills.search_text: snv-false-positive-context-annotation Use when benchmarking long-read SNV calls against GIAB truth sets and you need to characterize error sequence contexts (indel-proximate FPs, homopolymer FNs) or evaluate an indel-proximity filter for FP reduction. Longshot cannot call indels de novo — it only calls SNVs and can genotype indels only if supplied via a --potential_variants VCF, so this skill will not recover indel variants themselves Truth-set comparison is meaningless where the reference truth panel itself is incomplete; GIAB/Platinum Genomes sets are biased in favor of short-read technologies, so some Longshot FPs may actually be truth-set FNs Structural variants >50 bp are unsupported by Longshot (--potential_variants explicitly excludes them), so this annotation approach cannot be applied to SV calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Classify long-read SNV calls (Longshot) against GIAB high-confidence truth sets, annotate false positives by proximity to known indels and false negatives by homopolymer context, and quantify FP reduction from filtering calls near known common indels (Mills + 1000 Genomes Gold Standard Indels). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Classify long-read SNV calls (Longshot) against GIAB high-confidence truth sets, annotate false positives by proximity to known indels and false negatives by homopolymer context, and quantify FP reduction from filtering calls near known common indels (Mills + 1000 Genomes Gold Standard Indels).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Longshot cannot call indels de novo — it only calls SNVs and can genotype indels only if supplied via a --potential_variants VCF, so this skill will not recover indel variants themselves Truth-set comparison is meaningless where the reference truth panel itself is incomplete; GIAB/Platinum Genomes sets are biased in favor of short-read technologies, so some Longshot FPs may actually be truth-set FNs Structural variants >50 bp are unsupported by Longshot (--potential_variants explicitly excludes them), so this annotation approach cannot be applied to SV calls

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify accuracy of germline SNV/indel calls (VCF) against a GIAB truth set, e.g. comparing a variant caller's performance on HG001/NA12878 using genotype-aware TP/FP/FN classification.
skills.name: snv-indel-precision-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: snv-indel-precision-recall-evaluation Use when you need to quantify accuracy of germline SNV/indel calls (VCF) against a GIAB truth set, e.g. comparing a variant caller's performance on HG001/NA12878 using genotype-aware TP/FP/FN classification. Evaluating whole-genome performance rather than 1KGP3 common variant sites — the paper reports separate whole-genome F1-scores (98.65/92.57/87.26%) and they differ substantially from common-site scores Indel-heavy ONT benchmarking where the method itself admits limits — the paper notes Indel F1-score remains around 50% for ONT data Somatic or trio-sample variant calling, which Clairvoyante does not yet support and for which this GIAB germline truth-set protocol is not appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Genotype-aware benchmarking of SNV and small-indel variant calls using RTG vcfeval against the GIAB v3.3.2 HG001 truth dataset, computing FPR, FNR, precision, and F1-score at 1KGP3 common variant sites. This is the evaluation scheme the Clairvoyante paper uses to report its best Illumina configuration. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Genotype-aware benchmarking of SNV and small-indel variant calls using RTG vcfeval against the GIAB v3.3.2 HG001 truth dataset, computing FPR, FNR, precision, and F1-score at 1KGP3 common variant sites. This is the evaluation scheme the Clairvoyante paper uses to report its best Illumina configuration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating whole-genome performance rather than 1KGP3 common variant sites — the paper reports separate whole-genome F1-scores (98.65/92.57/87.26%) and they differ substantially from common-site scores Indel-heavy ONT benchmarking where the method itself admits limits — the paper notes Indel F1-score remains around 50% for ONT data Somatic or trio-sample variant calling, which Clairvoyante does not yet support and for which this GIAB germline truth-set protocol is not appropriate

skills.description: Use when ONT reads with MM/ML methylation tags have already been SNV-phased (HapCUT2/WhatsHap) into fragmented phase blocks and you need to bridge adjacent blocks using allele-specific methylation.
skills.name: snv-phase-block-chaining
skills.search_text: snv-phase-block-chaining Use when ONT reads with MM/ML methylation tags have already been SNV-phased (HapCUT2/WhatsHap) into fragmented phase blocks and you need to bridge adjacent blocks using allele-specific methylation. Data include sex chromosomes — MethPhaser cannot improve phasing there because random X inactivation in females yields inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns; restrict to autosomes Coverage is well below 30X or reads are short — SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) and methylation voting need at least ~30X ONT coverage and adequate read length Input BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors instead of being usable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Chains disconnected SNV phase blocks into larger blocks by leveraging haplotype-specific CpG methylation signals from ONT reads, using majority voting over methylation-haplotagged reads to infer neighbor block relationships and merge them. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Chains disconnected SNV phase blocks into larger blocks by leveraging haplotype-specific CpG methylation signals from ONT reads, using majority voting over methylation-haplotagged reads to infer neighbor block relationships and merge them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data include sex chromosomes — MethPhaser cannot improve phasing there because random X inactivation in females yields inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns; restrict to autosomes Coverage is well below 30X or reads are short — SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) and methylation voting need at least ~30X ONT coverage and adequate read length Input BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors instead of being usable

skills.description: Reference for benchmarking haplotype phasing accuracy when a method (e.g., MethPhaser) joins SNV phase blocks and you must validate each connection against a trio-phased truth VCF before reporting N50 or switch-error improvements.
skills.name: snv-phase-block-connection-verification
skills.search_text: snv-phase-block-connection-verification Reference for benchmarking haplotype phasing accuracy when a method (e.g., MethPhaser) joins SNV phase blocks and you must validate each connection against a trio-phased truth VCF before reporting N50 or switch-error improvements. Phasing sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype patterns, and the README states MethPhaser 'won't work on sex chromosomes' Samples lacking a trio-phased truth set — per-connection verification against GIAB trio-phased VCF is not possible for non-benchmark genomes Coverage below 30X ONT — SNV phasing methods like HapCUT2 and WhatsHap only work reasonably above that coverage, so the baseline being verified is unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Verify the correctness of SNV phase block connections established by a phasing method (e.g., MethPhaser) by comparing each block connection against the GIAB trio-phased truth VCF for HG002, then compute corrected phase block N50 and switch-error metrics. This is how the MethPhaser paper separates genuine phasing gains from incorrectly joined blocks. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Verify the correctness of SNV phase block connections established by a phasing method (e.g., MethPhaser) by comparing each block connection against the GIAB trio-phased truth VCF for HG002, then compute corrected phase block N50 and switch-error metrics. This is how the MethPhaser paper separates genuine phasing gains from incorrectly joined blocks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Phasing sex chromosomes — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype patterns, and the README states MethPhaser 'won't work on sex chromosomes' Samples lacking a trio-phased truth set — per-connection verification against GIAB trio-phased VCF is not possible for non-benchmark genomes Coverage below 30X ONT — SNV phasing methods like HapCUT2 and WhatsHap only work reasonably above that coverage, so the baseline being verified is unreliable

skills.name: snv-variant-calling-benchmarking
skills.search_text: snv-variant-calling-benchmarking Use when comparing single nucleotide variant caller performance on ONT long-read data (e.g., Dorado hac/sup-basecalled GIAB trio BAMs or Pbsim3-simulated reads) and per-caller precision, recall, and F1-score metrics are needed. skills.description: Use when generating or auditing consensus contigs at SV breakpoints from split/discordant/soft-clipped reads, or when verifying that low-quality clipped bases are trimmed before contig remapping.
skills.name: soft-clip-quality-trimming-at-breakpoints
skills.search_text: soft-clip-quality-trimming-at-breakpoints Use when generating or auditing consensus contigs at SV breakpoints from split/discordant/soft-clipped reads, or when verifying that low-quality clipped bases are trimmed before contig remapping. The input is a final VCF of SV calls rather than raw SV-associated alignments — this skill operates on the pre-calling consensus-generation stage, not on filtering or merging calls. A full de novo assembly stage is required (e.g. resolving multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences in PE data) — the article notes dysgu lacks such a stage and consensus-based insertion sizes are expected to be less accurate than assembly-based callers such as manta and gatk. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs dysgu's linear-time consensus sequence generator for structural variant breakpoints: base-tuple graph vertices weighted by summed base quality, longest-path back-tracing to emit per-breakpoint consensus contigs, and trimming of soft-clipped bases where path quality P_q < 0.5. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Reconstructs dysgu's linear-time consensus sequence generator for structural variant breakpoints: base-tuple graph vertices weighted by summed base quality, longest-path back-tracing to emit per-breakpoint consensus contigs, and trimming of soft-clipped bases where path quality P_q < 0.5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a final VCF of SV calls rather than raw SV-associated alignments — this skill operates on the pre-calling consensus-generation stage, not on filtering or merging calls. A full de novo assembly stage is required (e.g. resolving multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences in PE data) — the article notes dysgu lacks such a stage and consensus-based insertion sizes are expected to be less accurate than assembly-based callers such as manta and gatk.

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a graph-based SV-calling clustering stage (as in dysgu) where soft-clipped reads must be grouped by sequence similarity cheaply, or when enumerating SV-signature nodes from discordant/split/deletion/insertion/breakend evidence.
skills.name: soft-clip-sequence-clustering
skills.search_text: soft-clip-sequence-clustering Use when building or reproducing a graph-based SV-calling clustering stage (as in dysgu) where soft-clipped reads must be grouped by sequence similarity cheaply, or when enumerating SV-signature nodes from discordant/split/deletion/insertion/breakend evidence. Input is a VCF of already-called SVs — clustering of raw soft-clipped signatures is a pre-call stage, not a post-call merge/filter step You need full break-end sequence resolution or multi-allelic site resolution: the paper notes no de novo assembly stage is incorporated, so full-length insertions in PE data remain unresolved Reads are not SV-associated (no soft-clip >= 15 bp, no split/discordant/supplementary mapping) — dysgu's fetch stage will simply not emit them http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Clusters soft-clipped read sequences from SV candidate alignments without pairwise sequence alignment, using dysgu's unique-set minimizer sketch (kmer length 6, window 12) compared through hashmap queries, alongside graph-based SV-signature clustering with reciprocal-overlap and span-position-distance thresholds. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Clusters soft-clipped read sequences from SV candidate alignments without pairwise sequence alignment, using dysgu's unique-set minimizer sketch (kmer length 6, window 12) compared through hashmap queries, alongside graph-based SV-signature clustering with reciprocal-overlap and span-position-distance thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a VCF of already-called SVs — clustering of raw soft-clipped signatures is a pre-call stage, not a post-call merge/filter step You need full break-end sequence resolution or multi-allelic site resolution: the paper notes no de novo assembly stage is incorporated, so full-length insertions in PE data remain unresolved Reads are not SV-associated (no soft-clip >= 15 bp, no split/discordant/supplementary mapping) — dysgu's fetch stage will simply not emit them

skills.description: Use when paired-end short reads aligned to a reference (e.g. ASM294v2.22) need split-read evidence recovered at SV breakpoints, and the primary aligner soft-clips breakpoint-spanning reads instead of aligning them contiguously.
skills.name: soft-clipped-read-extraction
skills.search_text: soft-clipped-read-extraction Use when paired-end short reads aligned to a reference (e.g. ASM294v2.22) need split-read evidence recovered at SV breakpoints, and the primary aligner soft-clips breakpoint-spanning reads instead of aligning them contiguously. Long-read data are available and direct split-read or read-pair evidence can be obtained without clip-and-realign rescue Only read-pair (discordant-pair) SV evidence is targeted and soft-clip signal is not needed Input alignments were produced by an aligner that already reports split/chimeric alignments (e.g. no soft-clipped breakpoint reads to rescue) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Extracts reads with soft-clipped segments (≥20 bp) from NextGenMap alignments of Illumina paired-end S. pombe reads and re-aligns them with YAHA to recover split-read signal across structural-variant breakpoints, merging results back into a 40x-normalized BAM. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Extracts reads with soft-clipped segments (≥20 bp) from NextGenMap alignments of Illumina paired-end S. pombe reads and re-aligns them with YAHA to recover split-read signal across structural-variant breakpoints, merging results back into a 40x-normalized BAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Long-read data are available and direct split-read or read-pair evidence can be obtained without clip-and-realign rescue Only read-pair (discordant-pair) SV evidence is targeted and soft-clip signal is not needed Input alignments were produced by an aligner that already reports split/chimeric alignments (e.g. no soft-clipped breakpoint reads to rescue)

skills.description: Use when a paper or package claims a runtime bound for a simulation/generation function and you need to reproduce or verify that timing claim across named scenarios with R's system.time().
skills.name: software-runtime-benchmarking-in-r
skills.search_text: software-runtime-benchmarking-in-r Use when a paper or package claims a runtime bound for a simulation/generation function and you need to reproduce or verify that timing claim across named scenarios with R's system.time(). You need individual-level genotype/phenotype simulation timing — generate_individual() is the slower path and is not covered by the summary-level runtime bound You want statistical performance of MR estimators (bias, power, Type I error) rather than software wall-clock runtime The target function requires multi-iteration Monte Carlo throughput measurement rather than a single-call per-scenario timing http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of an R package function (here simmrd::generate_summary()) across its documented scenario presets to verify it meets a stated performance bound (≤ 0.1 s per call), producing a reproducible timing table. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of an R package function (here simmrd::generate_summary()) across its documented scenario presets to verify it meets a stated performance bound (≤ 0.1 s per call), producing a reproducible timing table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need individual-level genotype/phenotype simulation timing — generate_individual() is the slower path and is not covered by the summary-level runtime bound You want statistical performance of MR estimators (bias, power, Type I error) rather than software wall-clock runtime The target function requires multi-iteration Monte Carlo throughput measurement rather than a single-call per-scenario timing

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the per-stage runtime share of a nanopore Read Until / squiggle-mapping pipeline (e.g. to verify that sDTW dominates software execution before investing in FPGA acceleration).
skills.name: software-runtime-profiling-per-stage-decomposition
skills.search_text: software-runtime-profiling-per-stage-decomposition Use when you need to quantify the per-stage runtime share of a nanopore Read Until / squiggle-mapping pipeline (e.g. to verify that sDTW dominates software execution before investing in FPGA acceleration). When profiling the hardware-accelerated (HARU/FPGA) pipeline — the goal there is to show the reduced sDTW share (<64%), not the software bottleneck When the input reads are not raw nanopore signal in BLOW5 format or lack a matched reference FASTA for squiggle mapping When a coarse end-to-end timing comparison against the 36-core Intel Xeon server baseline is sufficient and per-stage decomposition is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Profiles the software-only Read Until pipeline by timing each stage (sDTW alignment, signal preprocessing, file I/O) on the SARS-CoV-2 nanopore dataset to quantify what fraction of total runtime the sDTW computation occupies, establishing the >98% bottleneck baseline that motivates hardware acceleration with HARU. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Profiles the software-only Read Until pipeline by timing each stage (sDTW alignment, signal preprocessing, file I/O) on the SARS-CoV-2 nanopore dataset to quantify what fraction of total runtime the sDTW computation occupies, establishing the >98% bottleneck baseline that motivates hardware acceleration with HARU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When profiling the hardware-accelerated (HARU/FPGA) pipeline — the goal there is to show the reduced sDTW share (<64%), not the software bottleneck When the input reads are not raw nanopore signal in BLOW5 format or lack a matched reference FASTA for squiggle mapping When a coarse end-to-end timing comparison against the 36-core Intel Xeon server baseline is sufficient and per-stage decomposition is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you need a CPU-only software baseline throughput (reads/s) for raw-signal squiggle mapping to quantify how much a hardware accelerator like HARU improves on software-only Read Until alignment.
skills.name: software-throughput-benchmarking
skills.search_text: software-throughput-benchmarking Use when you need a CPU-only software baseline throughput (reads/s) for raw-signal squiggle mapping to quantify how much a hardware accelerator like HARU improves on software-only Read Until alignment. You are evaluating the HARU hardware-accelerated path itself — this skill covers only the software-only (sigfish-cpu / RUscripts-R9 Python) baselines, not sigfish-haru runs on the Kria FPGA. Your dataset is not raw nanopore signal in BLOW5/FAST5 with R9.4 chemistry — RUscripts-R9 was specifically modified for BLOW5 format and ONT's R9.4 chemistry. You need base-level alignment (e.g., Minimap2 on basecalled FASTQ) rather than raw-signal-domain squiggle mapping via sDTW. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Measures signal mapping throughput (reads/s) of pure software baselines — the RUscripts-R9 Python pipeline and the optimized sigfish-cpu sDTW binary — over the 1.382M-read SARS-CoV-2 dataset, establishing the CPU-only reference points against which the HARU FPGA accelerator is compared. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giad046
skills.summary: Measures signal mapping throughput (reads/s) of pure software baselines — the RUscripts-R9 Python pipeline and the optimized sigfish-cpu sDTW binary — over the 1.382M-read SARS-CoV-2 dataset, establishing the CPU-only reference points against which the HARU FPGA accelerator is compared.

You lack a matched control sample — the joint tumor/control comparison (control filtering, control panel subtraction) is the core of the method and separate detection-then-subtraction is known to produce false positives from germline SVs. The variant of interest is a somatic VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion — the authors state the reference-genome-based framework 'may not be appropriate to capture long repeat expansion events'. Both breakpoints of the SV lie in poorly characterized highly repetitive regions (e.g. some centromeric sequences) — the Single breakend SV module cannot detect SVs where both breakpoints are in areas where the reference genome is not well characterized. You only have short-read data — this skill is for ONT/PacBio long-read tumor/control pairs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Detect somatic structural variants (SVs) with single-base resolution by jointly analyzing tumor and matched-control long-read (ONT/PacBio) data with nanomonsv, using its Canonical SV and Single breakend SV modules rather than separate detection-then-subtraction. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether a monotonic relationship exists between an ordinal/dosage variable (e.g. duplication copy number across strain pairs) and a continuous outcome (e.g. log2 expression induction), without assuming linearity or normality.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-statistics
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-statistics Use when you need to test whether a monotonic relationship exists between an ordinal/dosage variable (e.g. duplication copy number across strain pairs) and a continuous outcome (e.g. log2 expression induction), without assuming linearity or normality. When the goal is to estimate the independent effect of one variant class (e.g. rearrangements) controlling for another (SNPs) — the paper uses partial correlations for that, not rank correlation When observations are not meaningfully pairable or the relationship is expected to be non-monotonic; rank correlation will miss sign changes across the range When a fully parametric effect-size estimate (e.g. variance explained by mixed models, as in the paper's 24%/7%/4% decomposition) is required rather than a monotonic association test http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Non-parametric rank-correlation analysis used in this study to quantify monotonic associations between structural-variation dosage and continuous genomic measurements — e.g. Spearman ρ=0.22 (P=0.041) between CNV copy number and nearby SNP variation, and per-pair testing of duplication copy number versus expression induction of genes within duplications. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Non-parametric rank-correlation analysis used in this study to quantify monotonic associations between structural-variation dosage and continuous genomic measurements — e.g. Spearman ρ=0.22 (P=0.041) between CNV copy number and nearby SNP variation, and per-pair testing of duplication copy number versus expression induction of genes within duplications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to estimate the independent effect of one variant class (e.g. rearrangements) controlling for another (SNPs) — the paper uses partial correlations for that, not rank correlation When observations are not meaningfully pairable or the relationship is expected to be non-monotonic; rank correlation will miss sign changes across the range When a fully parametric effect-size estimate (e.g. variance explained by mixed models, as in the paper's 24%/7%/4% decomposition) is required rather than a monotonic association test

skills.search_text: splice-junction-chain-matching-to-annotation Use when minimap2-spliced nanopore BAMs (direct RNA or cDNA) contain full-length reads whose isoforms must be labeled known/ISM/NIC/NNC against a reference transcript annotation, e.g., testing isoform-class reproducibility across C2C12 dRNA replicates. The goal is modified-base calling or filtering (Dorado/modkit on RNA or DNA POD5), not isoform structure annotation — use the modkit workflow instead. Input is still unmapped POD5/FASTQ and only basecalling or remapping is needed — use the basecall or remap entry points rather than annotateRNA. Reads are short reads or otherwise lack full-length splice junction chains, so ISM/NIC/NNC junction-chain rules cannot be meaningfully applied. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies full-length nanopore transcripts detected in dRNA or cDNA runs against a reference GTF by matching their splice junction chains, labeling each transcript as a known isoform, ISM, NIC, or NNC. In the Dogme pipeline this is the step that turns LR-Kallisto-detected isoforms into a per-replicate isoform-class table. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag066
skills.summary: Classifies full-length nanopore transcripts detected in dRNA or cDNA runs against a reference GTF by matching their splice junction chains, labeling each transcript as a known isoform, ISM, NIC, or NNC. In the Dogme pipeline this is the step that turns LR-Kallisto-detected isoforms into a per-replicate isoform-class table.

The reference annotation is complete and the goal is de novo transcript reconstruction rather than junction-recovery benchmarking against partially deleted references Input data is short-read RNA-seq rather than PacBio Iso-seq full-length transcript FASTA, since TAGET's TransAnnot is designed for Iso-seq full-length reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking skill that measures how well transcript-annotation tools (TAGET, SQANTI, StringTie2, FLAIR, IsoQuant) recover splice junctions when a known fraction (5–50%) of genes is deleted from the hg38 Ensembl reference, computing junction-recovery sensitivity and precision per tool per deletion level as in TAGET's Supplementary Fig. 5. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0

skills.description: Use when you have long-read Iso-seq splice junction predictions from multiple aligners plus matched short-read RNA-seq data and need to quantify what fraction of predicted junctions (especially novel ones) are independently supported.
skills.name: splice-junction-support-validation
skills.search_text: splice-junction-support-validation Use when you have long-read Iso-seq splice junction predictions from multiple aligners plus matched short-read RNA-seq data and need to quantify what fraction of predicted junctions (especially novel ones) are independently supported. You only have short-read RNA-seq and no long-read Iso-seq junction predictions to validate The goal is transcript quantification or DIU analysis rather than junction precision benchmarking (use TAGET's TransAnnotMerge/expression_V1.py workflow instead) No matched short-read data or reference annotation exists, so support cannot be assessed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Validates splice junctions predicted from long-read Iso-seq alignments (TAGET, minimap2, GMAP) by counting how many matched short-read RNA-seq reads span each junction, computing overall and novel-only support fractions against a reference annotation. This benchmarks the precision of novel junction discovery across aligners. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-41649-0
skills.summary: Validates splice junctions predicted from long-read Iso-seq alignments (TAGET, minimap2, GMAP) by counting how many matched short-read RNA-seq reads span each junction, computing overall and novel-only support fractions against a reference annotation. This benchmarks the precision of novel junction discovery across aligners.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have short-read RNA-seq and no long-read Iso-seq junction predictions to validate The goal is transcript quantification or DIU analysis rather than junction precision benchmarking (use TAGET's TransAnnotMerge/expression_V1.py workflow instead) No matched short-read data or reference annotation exists, so support cannot be assessed

skills.description: Use when you have IsoCon final_candidates.fa transcripts from targeted PacBio Iso-Seq sequencing of the nine Y chromosome ampliconic gene families and need to tally coding/non-coding counts per family and classify novel transcripts vs novel splice variants against NCBI nr/nt.
skills.name: splice-variant-novelty-counting
skills.search_text: splice-variant-novelty-counting Use when you have IsoCon final_candidates.fa transcripts from targeted PacBio Iso-Seq sequencing of the nine Y chromosome ampliconic gene families and need to tally coding/non-coding counts per family and classify novel transcripts vs novel splice variants against NCBI nr/nt. The input reads are raw PacBio CCS/Iso-Seq reads that have not yet been run through IsoCon — run IsoCon first to obtain final_candidates.fa before grouping or novelty counting. The goal is a definitive determination of gene family size or definitive assignment of each transcript to an individual gene copy — the paper states transcriptome-only sequencing 'does not provide a definitive answer' for either. The goal is distinguishing alleles from distinct gene copies — IsoCon output requires further downstream analysis for this, so this counting skill alone is insufficient. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reproduces the paper's post-IsoCon novelty accounting: transcripts shared between testis samples are grouped by exon-level (large-indel) differences, classified as coding vs non-coding, and screened against NCBI nr/nt to count novel transcripts separately from novel splice variants (Table 3: 72 coding, 49 non-coding, 51 groups, 38 coding groups, 94 novel transcripts, 38 novel splice variants). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: Reproduces the paper's post-IsoCon novelty accounting: transcripts shared between testis samples are grouped by exon-level (large-indel) differences, classified as coding vs non-coding, and screened against NCBI nr/nt to count novel transcripts separately from novel splice variants (Table 3: 72 coding, 49 non-coding, 51 groups, 38 coding groups, 94 novel transcripts, 38 novel splice variants).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are raw PacBio CCS/Iso-Seq reads that have not yet been run through IsoCon — run IsoCon first to obtain final_candidates.fa before grouping or novelty counting. The goal is a definitive determination of gene family size or definitive assignment of each transcript to an individual gene copy — the paper states transcriptome-only sequencing 'does not provide a definitive answer' for either. The goal is distinguishing alleles from distinct gene copies — IsoCon output requires further downstream analysis for this, so this counting skill alone is insufficient.

When only one sequencing technology is available — a single Fupfi histogram cannot distinguish biological AISO patterns from technology-specific bias When the goal is differential splicing (PSI/DSU) between conditions rather than splicing-order (AISO) quantification around exons of interest When exons exceed the maximum length quantifiable by short reads (read/fragment-size limited), as short-read Fupfi counts will be biased toward short exons http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Quantifies and visualizes adjacent intron splicing order (AISO) biases between sequencing technologies by computing per-exon upfi/dofi count ratios and plotting genome-wide Fupfi histograms from Insplico output, revealing that long-read (ONT) and short-read (Illumina) protocols yield discrepant AISO patterns (upfi/dofi ≈ 0.41 vs ≈ 1.41). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Quantifies and visualizes adjacent intron splicing order (AISO) biases between sequencing technologies by computing per-exon upfi/dofi count ratios and plotting genome-wide Fupfi histograms from Insplico output, revealing that long-read (ONT) and short-read (Illumina) protocols yield discrepant AISO patterns (upfi/dofi ≈ 0.41 vs ≈ 1.41).

skills.search_text: splicing-feature-computation-from-exon-sequence Use when you have variant calls (VCF) near splice sites with hg19 exon annotations and need per-variant splicing feature vectors to feed a delta-PSI regression model such as PredPSI-SVR. skills.search_text: splicing-order-quantification-accuracy-benchmarking Use when validating an AISO/Fupfi quantification tool with simulated short RNA-seq reads carrying known UPFI/DOFI copy numbers, or when assessing whether exon and flanking intron lengths bias splicing-order quantification. The goal is quantifying real biological AISO patterns from actual RNA-seq data rather than validating quantification accuracy with known ground truth. Long-read sequencing data is the target — the article's short-read simulation cannot emulate the 5'/3' long-read biases that Insplico corrects with its optional module. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark the accuracy of Insplico's Fupfi/Fdofi quantification and exon-detection limits by simulating RNA-seq reads (polyester, 75/150-nt, SE and PE 250/500) from synthetic UPFI/DOFI transcript pairs with known copy numbers, then comparing STAR-aligned results against ground truth (Figure 2 of the Insplico paper). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy of Insplico's Fupfi/Fdofi quantification and exon-detection limits by simulating RNA-seq reads (polyester, 75/150-nt, SE and PE 250/500) from synthetic UPFI/DOFI transcript pairs with known copy numbers, then comparing STAR-aligned results against ground truth (Figure 2 of the Insplico paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantifying real biological AISO patterns from actual RNA-seq data rather than validating quantification accuracy with known ground truth. Long-read sequencing data is the target — the article's short-read simulation cannot emulate the 5'/3' long-read biases that Insplico corrects with its optional module.

skills.description: Use when you have contig-to-reference BAM alignments (e.g. Hifi_L2_hg19_minimap2_chr10.bam from the VolcanoSV Zenodo test data) and need to harvest large indel SV signatures into a signatures.tsv before VCF generation.
skills.name: split-alignment-signature-extraction
skills.search_text: split-alignment-signature-extraction Use when you have contig-to-reference BAM alignments (e.g. Hifi_L2_hg19_minimap2_chr10.bam from the VolcanoSV Zenodo test data) and need to harvest large indel SV signatures into a signatures.tsv before VCF generation. The goal is complex SV calling (translocations, duplications, inversions) — those require the VolcanoSV-vc Complex_SV module with WGS read BAM support, not split-alignment signatures from a single chromosome The input is read-to-reference alignments rather than assembly contig-to-reference alignments — this signature extraction is defined on the diploid assembly output The target is sex chromosomes — VolcanoSV is designed only for autosome chromosomes because the phasing procedure for sex chromosomes differs http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts large insertion/deletion (50 bp–several kb) structural variant signatures from contig-to-reference alignments of a diploid assembly, as implemented in the VolcanoSV-vc Large INDEL module, by parsing primary and supplementary (split) alignment blocks and classifying consecutive-block discrepancies as INS or DEL signatures. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0

skills.description: Use when HiFi reads aligned with minimap2 '-ax map-hifi' produce split alignment records whose segments map to different chromosomes, and you must extract SigBND translocation signals to recover correct chromosome labels for breakpoint-spanning reads.
skills.name: split-alignment-translocation-signal-extraction
skills.search_text: split-alignment-translocation-signal-extraction Use when HiFi reads aligned with minimap2 '-ax map-hifi' produce split alignment records whose segments map to different chromosomes, and you must extract SigBND translocation signals to recover correct chromosome labels for breakpoint-spanning reads. Reads produce single-segment (non-split) alignments mapping entirely to one chromosome — no translocation signal can be extracted and de novo class correction alone suffices Split segments map to different chromosomes but are separated by 100 bp or more on the read — the signal does not meet the <100 bp read-gap criterion for a SigBND event Signal clusters fall below the predefined support threshold and must be discarded rather than propagated as breakpoint labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extracts translocation (BND) variant signals from split alignments of PacBio HiFi reads against a linear reference, following a CuteSV-style breakpoint formulation, as the first stage of HiFiCCL's translocation class correction. It enables breakpoint-spanning reads to be labeled with their correct chromosome despite reference-based misclassification. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Extracts translocation (BND) variant signals from split alignments of PacBio HiFi reads against a linear reference, following a CuteSV-style breakpoint formulation, as the first stage of HiFiCCL's translocation class correction. It enables breakpoint-spanning reads to be labeled with their correct chromosome despite reference-based misclassification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads produce single-segment (non-split) alignments mapping entirely to one chromosome — no translocation signal can be extracted and de novo class correction alone suffices Split segments map to different chromosomes but are separated by 100 bp or more on the read — the signal does not meet the <100 bp read-gap criterion for a SigBND event Signal clusters fall below the predefined support threshold and must be discarded rather than propagated as breakpoint labels

skills.description: Use when you have Minimap2-aligned long-read (PacBio/ONT) BAMs spanning putative rearrangements and need to label each event simple vs complex from the number of split-read alignment columns.
skills.name: split-read-alignment-pattern-classification
skills.search_text: split-read-alignment-pattern-classification Use when you have Minimap2-aligned long-read (PacBio/ONT) BAMs spanning putative rearrangements and need to label each event simple vs complex from the number of split-read alignment columns. skills.search_text: srna-library-file-partitioning Use when sRNA sequencing reads have already been genome-mapped with PatMan (0 mismatches) and you must split each library into miRBase-conserved vs non-conserved read files before novel miRNA or ta-siRNA prediction. Input reads have not yet been filtered and mapped to the genome with PatMan (0 mismatches) — the Filtering stage must run first The goal is novel miRNA discovery itself rather than separating conserved from non-conserved reads — use miRCat on the non-conserved fraction instead Conserved miRNAs should be identified against a custom reference other than miRBase mature sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Partitions the genome-mapped reads of each sRNA library into a conserved fraction (reads matching the miRBase mature database) and a non-conserved fraction using miRProf in the miRPursuit Annotation stage, so downstream novel miRNA (miRCat) and ta-siRNA prediction operate only on non-conserved reads. genomics/v1 10.1002/1873-3468.12746
skills.summary: Partitions the genome-mapped reads of each sRNA library into a conserved fraction (reads matching the miRBase mature database) and a non-conserved fraction using miRProf in the miRPursuit Annotation stage, so downstream novel miRNA (miRCat) and ta-siRNA prediction operate only on non-conserved reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been filtered and mapped to the genome with PatMan (0 mismatches) — the Filtering stage must run first The goal is novel miRNA discovery itself rather than separating conserved from non-conserved reads — use miRCat on the non-conserved fraction instead Conserved miRNAs should be identified against a custom reference other than miRBase mature sequences

skills.description: Use when processing plant sRNA-seq FASTQ/FASTA libraries and you need reproducible, parameterized read filtering plus genome-mapped reads before conserved miRNA (miRBase) or novel miRNA/tasiRNA analysis.
skills.name: srna-pipeline-filtering
skills.search_text: srna-pipeline-filtering Use when processing plant sRNA-seq FASTQ/FASTA libraries and you need reproducible, parameterized read filtering plus genome-mapped reads before conserved miRNA (miRBase) or novel miRNA/tasiRNA analysis. When the goal is strict genome-based read removal — wbench_filter.cfg sets filter_genome_hits=false, so this stage does NOT discard reads based on genome hits When reads should be mapped to the genome with mismatches or gaps allowed — patman_genome.cfg fixes EDITS=0 and GAPS=0, so this skill only supports exact 0-mismatch mapping When the aim is quality control of raw reads — fastqc is not yet implemented in miRPursuit http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Filters plant small-RNA (sRNA) sequencing reads in the miRPursuit Filtering stage: adaptor trimming, Wbench filtering (length 18–26, abundance ≥5, low-complexity, t/rRNA removal), then mapping reads to the reference genome with PatMaN at 0 mismatches/0 gaps. genomics/v1 10.1002/1873-3468.12746
skills.summary: Filters plant small-RNA (sRNA) sequencing reads in the miRPursuit Filtering stage: adaptor trimming, Wbench filtering (length 18–26, abundance ≥5, low-complexity, t/rRNA removal), then mapping reads to the reference genome with PatMaN at 0 mismatches/0 gaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is strict genome-based read removal — wbench_filter.cfg sets filter_genome_hits=false, so this stage does NOT discard reads based on genome hits When reads should be mapped to the genome with mismatches or gaps allowed — patman_genome.cfg fixes EDITS=0 and GAPS=0, so this skill only supports exact 0-mismatch mapping When the aim is quality control of raw reads — fastqc is not yet implemented in miRPursuit

skills.description: Use when short-read RNA-seq from SRRM4 perturbation (e.g. GSE207459 HEK293 GFP vs 3xFlag-SRRM4) must be classified into SRRM4-dependent microexons and compared for downstream-intron-first vs upstream-intron-first AISO fractions.
skills.name: srrm4-microexon-psi-threshold-classification
skills.search_text: srrm4-microexon-psi-threshold-classification Use when short-read RNA-seq from SRRM4 perturbation (e.g. GSE207459 HEK293 GFP vs 3xFlag-SRRM4) must be classified into SRRM4-dependent microexons and compared for downstream-intron-first vs upstream-intron-first AISO fractions. The analysis targets genome-wide AISO patterns across tissues or species rather than classification of microexons around a single trans-acting factor perturbation Only long-read RNA-seq is available without correction for 5'/3' biases, which Insplico's correction module must harmonize with short-read results The exon of interest exceeds the length quantifiable by short reads, which is limited by read length and paired-end fragment size http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Classifies microexons as SRRM4-dependent versus matched controls and stratifies them by adjacent-intron splicing order (upfi/dofi) using PSI/PIR and upfi/dofi/bus/bos counts estimated with Insplico from STAR-aligned HEK293 GFP vs 3xFlag-SRRM4 RNA-seq (GSE207459). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad244
skills.summary: Classifies microexons as SRRM4-dependent versus matched controls and stratifies them by adjacent-intron splicing order (upfi/dofi) using PSI/PIR and upfi/dofi/bus/bos counts estimated with Insplico from STAR-aligned HEK293 GFP vs 3xFlag-SRRM4 RNA-seq (GSE207459).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets genome-wide AISO patterns across tissues or species rather than classification of microexons around a single trans-acting factor perturbation Only long-read RNA-seq is available without correction for 5'/3' biases, which Insplico's correction module must harmonize with short-read results The exon of interest exceeds the length quantifiable by short reads, which is limited by read length and paired-end fragment size

skills.description: Use when a workflow must convert basecaller move tables (e.g. mv:B:c auxiliary fields in SAM/BAM) into compact ss-string signal alignments, or parse such ss strings back into matches/insertions/deletions for nanopore signal-alignment statistics.
skills.name: ss-tag-encoding-and-decoding
skills.search_text: ss-tag-encoding-and-decoding Use when a workflow must convert basecaller move tables (e.g. mv:B:c auxiliary fields in SAM/BAM) into compact ss-string signal alignments, or parse such ss strings back into matches/insertions/deletions for nanopore signal-alignment statistics. Signal-to-reference alignments are already produced by f5c eventalign or nanopolish with their own event-alignment output — use those alignments directly rather than re-encoding from move tables Input has no basecaller move table (e.g. signal alignment via nanopolish signal projection or squigualiser signal simulation without moves) The goal is visualisation only (plot, plot_pileup, plot_tracks) rather than alignment encoding or statistic computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Encodes and decodes nanopore signal-to-sequence alignments as the f5c-style 'ss' auxiliary tag (the move-table-to-ss-string 'reform' conversion in Squigualiser), enabling signal alignments to be carried in BAM/PAF files and parsed for alignment statistics via the 'metric' sub-tool. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae501
skills.summary: Encodes and decodes nanopore signal-to-sequence alignments as the f5c-style 'ss' auxiliary tag (the move-table-to-ss-string 'reform' conversion in Squigualiser), enabling signal alignments to be carried in BAM/PAF files and parsed for alignment statistics via the 'metric' sub-tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Signal-to-reference alignments are already produced by f5c eventalign or nanopolish with their own event-alignment output — use those alignments directly rather than re-encoding from move tables Input has no basecaller move table (e.g. signal alignment via nanopolish signal projection or squigualiser signal simulation without moves) The goal is visualisation only (plot, plot_pileup, plot_tracks) rather than alignment encoding or statistic computation

skills.description: Use when de novo error correction (e.g. on targeted Iso-Seq FLNC CCS reads) has produced multiple candidate transcript variants and you must decide, statistically, which candidates are distinct isoforms versus redundant low-support splits.
skills.name: statistical-transcript-candidate-filtering
skills.search_text: statistical-transcript-candidate-filtering Use when de novo error correction (e.g. on targeted Iso-Seq FLNC CCS reads) has produced multiple candidate transcript variants and you must decide, statistically, which candidates are distinct isoforms versus redundant low-support splits. Candidates differ by more than the default threshold of 10 variant positions — these are not statistically evaluated and instead retained directly Input reads are FASTA without quality values — the weighted-support test requires per-read Phred error probabilities Reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline (primers, barcodes, chimeras still present) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 IsoCon's second-stage candidate filtering: a weighted-support Bernoulli-style hypothesis test (with a Chernoff-type bound) decides which candidate transcripts from error correction are statistically redundant, so only well-supported distinct transcripts survive. It prevents overcalling isoforms among highly similar gene copies in PacBio Iso-Seq data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-06910-x
skills.summary: IsoCon's second-stage candidate filtering: a weighted-support Bernoulli-style hypothesis test (with a Chernoff-type bound) decides which candidate transcripts from error correction are statistically redundant, so only well-supported distinct transcripts survive. It prevents overcalling isoforms among highly similar gene copies in PacBio Iso-Seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidates differ by more than the default threshold of 10 variant positions — these are not statistically evaluated and instead retained directly Input reads are FASTA without quality values — the weighted-support test requires per-read Phred error probabilities Reads have not been pre-processed with the Iso-Seq pipeline (primers, barcodes, chimeras still present)

skills.description: Use when the goal is to simulate or demonstrate allele-frequency trajectories at a biallelic locus under both deterministic natural selection and stochastic genetic drift, e.g. for teaching population genetics.
skills.name: stochastic-drift-and-selection-modeling
skills.search_text: stochastic-drift-and-selection-modeling Use when the goal is to simulate or demonstrate allele-frequency trajectories at a biallelic locus under both deterministic natural selection and stochastic genetic drift, e.g. for teaching population genetics. When only deterministic processes are needed (selection or drift alone) — learnPopGen provides separate functions for individual deterministic and stochastic processes rather than the combined drift.selection model When the locus is multiallelic — drift.selection is defined for a biallelic locus When the user cannot run R and only needs a quick demonstration — a browser-based web interface for the function may be more appropriate than a local R session http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulates the simultaneous effects of natural selection and genetic drift at a biallelic locus using the drift.selection function of the learnPopGen R package, which performs Wright–Fisher-style binomial sampling of allele frequencies each generation modulated by a deterministic selection step defined by genotype fitnesses. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.5412
skills.summary: Simulates the simultaneous effects of natural selection and genetic drift at a biallelic locus using the drift.selection function of the learnPopGen R package, which performs Wright–Fisher-style binomial sampling of allele frequencies each generation modulated by a deterministic selection step defined by genotype fitnesses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only deterministic processes are needed (selection or drift alone) — learnPopGen provides separate functions for individual deterministic and stochastic processes rather than the combined drift.selection model When the locus is multiallelic — drift.selection is defined for a biallelic locus When the user cannot run R and only needs a quick demonstration — a browser-based web interface for the function may be more appropriate than a local R session

skills.description: Use when benchmarking site-wise modification stoichiometry estimation from nanopore direct RNA reads against ground-truth IVT stoichiometry mixtures (20-100%), or when reproducing the CHEUI vs competing-tools accuracy comparison.
skills.name: stoichiometry-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: stoichiometry-correlation-analysis Use when benchmarking site-wise modification stoichiometry estimation from nanopore direct RNA reads against ground-truth IVT stoichiometry mixtures (20-100%), or when reproducing the CHEUI vs competing-tools accuracy comparison. Goal is differential modification detection between two biological conditions rather than absolute stoichiometry (CHEUI-diff / sample-comparison mode is the appropriate path) Data are not Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reads with ionic-current signals (e.g., short-read or amplicon data have no signal level for CHEUI/signal-based tools) Target modification is not m6A or m5C; the CHEUI trained models are specific to these modifications (pseudouridine/other mods require alternative models, e.g. SWARM) Benchmark of site-wise RNA modification stoichiometry prediction (m6A, m5C) from nanopore direct RNA data, comparing CHEUI-solo against Xpore, Nanocompore, Epinano, NanoRMS and Tombo on controlled IVT mixtures by Pearson correlation with expected stoichiometry. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47953-7
skills.summary: Benchmark of site-wise RNA modification stoichiometry prediction (m6A, m5C) from nanopore direct RNA data, comparing CHEUI-solo against Xpore, Nanocompore, Epinano, NanoRMS and Tombo on controlled IVT mixtures by Pearson correlation with expected stoichiometry.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is differential modification detection between two biological conditions rather than absolute stoichiometry (CHEUI-diff / sample-comparison mode is the appropriate path) Data are not Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reads with ionic-current signals (e.g., short-read or amplicon data have no signal level for CHEUI/signal-based tools) Target modification is not m6A or m5C; the CHEUI trained models are specific to these modifications (pseudouridine/other mods require alternative models, e.g. SWARM)

skills.description: Use when analyzing PacBio HiFi or other long reads of targeted amplicons (e.g. ~8-kb forensic STR loci) to genotype STR/SNP/InDel alleles and produce read-backed phased macrohaplotypes per locus.
skills.name: str-allele-genotyping
skills.search_text: str-allele-genotyping Use when analyzing PacBio HiFi or other long reads of targeted amplicons (e.g. ~8-kb forensic STR loci) to genotype STR/SNP/InDel alleles and produce read-backed phased macrohaplotypes per locus. Short NGS reads where read length cannot span the targeted STR and flanking SNPs/InDels — MacroHapCaller targets long reads such as PacBio HiFi Unaligned raw reads — reads must first be aligned, sorted, and indexed to the reference (via MH_umi_dedup_map_pipe.sh or equivalent) before calling The goal is downstream haplotype sequence comparison/visualization rather than genotyping — USAT is the companion tool that takes haplotype output for alignment, plotting, and allele-size calculation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Genotypes targeted STR/SNP/InDel alleles from long sequencing reads (e.g. PacBio HiFi) by calling each variant class per read, concatenating them into macrohaplotype strings, clustering by string identity, and filtering noisy calls with MinReadCount/MinReadProportion thresholds. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Genotypes targeted STR/SNP/InDel alleles from long sequencing reads (e.g. PacBio HiFi) by calling each variant class per read, concatenating them into macrohaplotype strings, clustering by string identity, and filtering noisy calls with MinReadCount/MinReadProportion thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short NGS reads where read length cannot span the targeted STR and flanking SNPs/InDels — MacroHapCaller targets long reads such as PacBio HiFi Unaligned raw reads — reads must first be aligned, sorted, and indexed to the reference (via MH_umi_dedup_map_pipe.sh or equivalent) before calling The goal is downstream haplotype sequence comparison/visualization rather than genotyping — USAT is the companion tool that takes haplotype output for alignment, plotting, and allele-size calculation

skills.description: Use when genotyping targeted STR/TR loci (e.g., forensic CODIS markers) from long PacBio HiFi reads in a BAM and you need anchor-guided boundary detection plus motif-validated allele calling rather than de novo TR discovery.
skills.name: str-anchor-edit-distance-matching
skills.search_text: str-anchor-edit-distance-matching Use when genotyping targeted STR/TR loci (e.g., forensic CODIS markers) from long PacBio HiFi reads in a BAM and you need anchor-guided boundary detection plus motif-validated allele calling rather than de novo TR discovery. Input is raw PacBio HiFi BAM or fastq reads that have not yet been aligned, sorted, and indexed to a reference genome — run the MH_umi_dedup_map_pipe.sh preprocessing pipeline first The goal is de novo discovery of unknown tandem repeat loci — the algorithm requires pre-configured anchor coordinates and Motif_must_present repeat units per targeted locus Targeted variant classes are only SNPs or InDels without an STR component — use the SNP panel (-n) or InDel BED (-d) configure files instead of the STR anchor workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Anchored tandem-repeat (STR) allele calling in MacroHapCaller: for each targeted STR locus in a read-reference BAM, flanking chunk sequences are screened for left/right anchor matches by edit distance, the inter-anchor read sequence is extracted and validated against the configured repeat motif, and read support is tallied into a macrohaplotype table. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Anchored tandem-repeat (STR) allele calling in MacroHapCaller: for each targeted STR locus in a read-reference BAM, flanking chunk sequences are screened for left/right anchor matches by edit distance, the inter-anchor read sequence is extracted and validated against the configured repeat motif, and read support is tallied into a macrohaplotype table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw PacBio HiFi BAM or fastq reads that have not yet been aligned, sorted, and indexed to a reference genome — run the MH_umi_dedup_map_pipe.sh preprocessing pipeline first The goal is de novo discovery of unknown tandem repeat loci — the algorithm requires pre-configured anchor coordinates and Motif_must_present repeat units per targeted locus Targeted variant classes are only SNPs or InDels without an STR component — use the SNP panel (-n) or InDel BED (-d) configure files instead of the STR anchor workflow

skills.description: Use when preparing, checking, or supplying the '-a/--strAnchorFile' anchor configuration for MacroHapCaller targeted STR genotyping from PacBio HiFi BAM alignments, e.g. for forensic CODIS loci on GRCh38.
skills.name: str-loci-configure-file-parsing
skills.search_text: str-loci-configure-file-parsing Use when preparing, checking, or supplying the '-a/--strAnchorFile' anchor configuration for MacroHapCaller targeted STR genotyping from PacBio HiFi BAM alignments, e.g. for forensic CODIS loci on GRCh38. If the locus file is a USAT-style BED file (columns Chrom, ChromStart, ChromEnd, Name, Left_offset, Right_offset, Basic_motif_period, Ref_hap_length, Motif, Ref_allele, Inner_offset, Min_stutter_threshold) — that format serves USAT haplotype comparison, not MacroHapCaller anchor calling If the goal is SNP (-n snpPanelPosFile) or InDel (-d inDelBedFile) configuration parsing — those use different file formats specified separately If reads are short paired-end NGS rather than long PacBio HiFi reads; MacroHapCaller is designed for long-read macrohaplotype calling http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Parses and validates MacroHapCaller's tab-separated STR anchor configure file (one fixed headline, 11 columns per STR locus, e.g. the CODIS example CODISSTR_anchor.XW.config_v0.2.txt) so targeted STR loci can be genotyped with anchor-based calling. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Parses and validates MacroHapCaller's tab-separated STR anchor configure file (one fixed headline, 11 columns per STR locus, e.g. the CODIS example CODISSTR_anchor.XW.config_v0.2.txt) so targeted STR loci can be genotyped with anchor-based calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the locus file is a USAT-style BED file (columns Chrom, ChromStart, ChromEnd, Name, Left_offset, Right_offset, Basic_motif_period, Ref_hap_length, Motif, Ref_allele, Inner_offset, Min_stutter_threshold) — that format serves USAT haplotype comparison, not MacroHapCaller anchor calling If the goal is SNP (-n snpPanelPosFile) or InDel (-d inDelBedFile) configuration parsing — those use different file formats specified separately If reads are short paired-end NGS rather than long PacBio HiFi reads; MacroHapCaller is designed for long-read macrohaplotype calling

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from single-molecule long reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) with Longshot and you need to remove false variant sites where observed alleles are over-represented on one sequencing strand.
skills.name: strand-bias-fishers-exact-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: strand-bias-fishers-exact-variant-filtering Use when calling SNVs from single-molecule long reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) with Longshot and you need to remove false variant sites where observed alleles are over-represented on one sequencing strand. Calling short indels with SMS reads — the paper notes accurate short indel calling is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate, and Longshot only calls SNVs de novo Processing short-read data (Illumina) where tools like GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the appropriate callers Genotyping a pre-specified VCF with -v where the paper warns that excessive false potential variants can lead to inaccurate results and every input variant is used regardless of filters http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A Longshot default filter that discards candidate SNVs whose allele observations are strand-biased, using a two-tailed Fisher's exact test at p < 0.01, which is especially important for error-prone Oxford Nanopore reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: A Longshot default filter that discards candidate SNVs whose allele observations are strand-biased, using a two-tailed Fisher's exact test at p < 0.01, which is especially important for error-prone Oxford Nanopore reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling short indels with SMS reads — the paper notes accurate short indel calling is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate, and Longshot only calls SNVs de novo Processing short-read data (Illumina) where tools like GATK HaplotypeCaller or FreeBayes are the appropriate callers Genotyping a pre-specified VCF with -v where the paper warns that excessive false potential variants can lead to inaccurate results and every input variant is used regardless of filters

skills.description: Use when calling SNVs from error-prone Oxford Nanopore or PacBio SMRT reads and candidate variants show alleles over-represented on one read strand; the filter runs on the allelotyped candidate list prior to haplotype assembly.
skills.name: strand-bias-statistical-filtering
skills.search_text: strand-bias-statistical-filtering Use when calling SNVs from error-prone Oxford Nanopore or PacBio SMRT reads and candidate variants show alleles over-represented on one read strand; the filter runs on the allelotyped candidate list prior to haplotype assembly. Input is short-read data — the article positions this filter for SMS reads; short-read variant calling uses tools like GATK HaplotyperCaller and FreeBayes Calling variant classes other than SNVs — Longshot currently only calls single nucleotide variants (indels can only be genotyped if supplied in an input VCF) All candidate variants must be retained regardless of strand skew (e.g. with --potential_variants, since 'Every variant is used and only the allele fields are considered') — filtering would discard intended input sites http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A candidate-SNV filtering step from Longshot that removes potential variants whose allele observations show significant strand bias, judged by a two-tailed Fisher's exact test p-value < 0.01. It counters context-specific, strand-dependent sequencing errors in error-prone single-molecule sequencing (SMS) reads before haplotype-informed genotyping. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: A candidate-SNV filtering step from Longshot that removes potential variants whose allele observations show significant strand bias, judged by a two-tailed Fisher's exact test p-value < 0.01. It counters context-specific, strand-dependent sequencing errors in error-prone single-molecule sequencing (SMS) reads before haplotype-informed genotyping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — the article positions this filter for SMS reads; short-read variant calling uses tools like GATK HaplotyperCaller and FreeBayes Calling variant classes other than SNVs — Longshot currently only calls single nucleotide variants (indels can only be genotyped if supplied in an input VCF) All candidate variants must be retained regardless of strand skew (e.g. with --potential_variants, since 'Every variant is used and only the allele fields are considered') — filtering would discard intended input sites

skills.description: Use when nanopore per-site methylation outputs from multiple tools must be harmonized into a single strand-merged BED table per CpG site for downstream correlation, coverage-threshold filtering, or WGBS comparison.
skills.name: strand-merged-methylation-site-aggregation
skills.search_text: strand-merged-methylation-site-aggregation Use when nanopore per-site methylation outputs from multiple tools must be harmonized into a single strand-merged BED table per CpG site for downstream correlation, coverage-threshold filtering, or WGBS comparison. When per-strand methylation information must be preserved, e.g. strand-sensitive analyses of asymmetric methylation — the merged table averages both strands and drops the strand field When the methylation caller is DeepMod, whose per-site output is not yet in the METEORE augmented BED format and cannot be strand-merged with this procedure When single-read (per-read) methylation scores are the target, e.g. for training METEORE combined models, which use per-read score files rather than aggregated per-site tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates per-site CpG methylation calls from nanopore methylation-calling tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, METEORE) into combined-strand BED-format tables by averaging methylation frequencies across both strands and summing read coverage, enabling direct comparison with strand-agnostic WGBS methylation frequencies. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Aggregates per-site CpG methylation calls from nanopore methylation-calling tools (Nanopolish, DeepSignal, Tombo, Guppy, Megalodon, METEORE) into combined-strand BED-format tables by averaging methylation frequencies across both strands and summing read coverage, enabling direct comparison with strand-agnostic WGBS methylation frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When per-strand methylation information must be preserved, e.g. strand-sensitive analyses of asymmetric methylation — the merged table averages both strands and drops the strand field When the methylation caller is DeepMod, whose per-site output is not yet in the METEORE augmented BED format and cannot be strand-merged with this procedure When single-read (per-read) methylation scores are the target, e.g. for training METEORE combined models, which use per-read score files rather than aggregated per-site tables

skills.description: Use when designing enrichment guides for a known fusion-gene driver locus whose fusion partner gene and breakpoint are unknown, and long reads must be directed outward from the crRNA cut site into the uncharacterized partner.
skills.name: strand-specific-guide-orientation-selection
skills.search_text: strand-specific-guide-orientation-selection Use when designing enrichment guides for a known fusion-gene driver locus whose fusion partner gene and breakpoint are unknown, and long reads must be directed outward from the crRNA cut site into the uncharacterized partner. The fusion partner gene and breakpoint location are already known (no strand-directional enrichment is needed; standard two-sided guide design suffices) Input DNA is degraded/fragmented FFPE material, where the FUDGE crRNA protocol 'will most likely fail to comprehensively identify fusion genes' Only a single guide per locus is needed regardless of orientation, e.g., for non-directional target enrichment rather than partner discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A crRNA design procedure used in the FUDGE assay in which only CRISPR-Cas9 guides on the strand that orients nanopore reads from the known fusion-gene driver (e.g., BRAF exon 10, EWSR1 exon 7, SS18 exon 9) toward the unknown 5' or 3' fusion partner are retained, enabling partner- and breakpoint-independent fusion detection. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: A crRNA design procedure used in the FUDGE assay in which only CRISPR-Cas9 guides on the strand that orients nanopore reads from the known fusion-gene driver (e.g., BRAF exon 10, EWSR1 exon 7, SS18 exon 9) toward the unknown 5' or 3' fusion partner are retained, enabling partner- and breakpoint-independent fusion detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The fusion partner gene and breakpoint location are already known (no strand-directional enrichment is needed; standard two-sided guide design suffices) Input DNA is degraded/fragmented FFPE material, where the FUDGE crRNA protocol 'will most likely fail to comprehensively identify fusion genes' Only a single guide per locus is needed regardless of orientation, e.g., for non-directional target enrichment rather than partner discovery

skills.description: Use when per-site methylation calls (read_id, chromosome, pos_in_reference, strand, methylation_rate) from nanopore 5mC detection need to be intersected with element annotations (TE classes, gene regions) to test for strand-biased methylation in a specific context such as CHH.
skills.name: strand-specific-methylation-bias-analysis
skills.search_text: strand-specific-methylation-bias-analysis Use when per-site methylation calls (read_id, chromosome, pos_in_reference, strand, methylation_rate) from nanopore 5mC detection need to be intersected with element annotations (TE classes, gene regions) to test for strand-biased methylation in a specific context such as CHH. Input is raw POD5/BAM data without methylation calls — run DeepPlant's extract_and_call_mods first to produce the per-site TSV Methylation calls were produced by a tool without validated plant CHH performance (e.g., default Dorado models) — DeepPlant improves whole-genome CHH correlation with BS-seq by 23.4–117.6% over Dorado The question requires absolute methylation levels across species rather than within-genome strand-bias comparisons; DeepPlant's CHH model was trained on species screened for abundant high-methylation CHH sites and may not capture full pattern diversity across all plants http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies strand-specific CHH methylation frequency within annotated genomic elements (e.g., centromeric transposon types and protein-coding controls) using per-read methylation calls from DeepPlant, revealing element-specific forward/reverse methylation bias in plant genomes. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-58576-x
skills.summary: Quantifies strand-specific CHH methylation frequency within annotated genomic elements (e.g., centromeric transposon types and protein-coding controls) using per-read methylation calls from DeepPlant, revealing element-specific forward/reverse methylation bias in plant genomes.
