skills.description: Use when assembling a supervised quality-score model for structural variant calls from labelled positive/negative feature vectors (e.g. GIAB HG001/HG002, svclassify, NanoVar gold sets) and you need feature selection plus hyperparameter tuning before serializing the model.
skills.name: stratified-cross-validation-grid-search
skills.search_text: stratified-cross-validation-grid-search Use when assembling a supervised quality-score model for structural variant calls from labelled positive/negative feature vectors (e.g. GIAB HG001/HG002, svclassify, NanoVar gold sets) and you need feature selection plus hyperparameter tuning before serializing the model. You only need to score/filter existing calls with a trained model — use dysgu filter with model-probability thresholds (≥0.5 for PacBio, ≥0.35 for ONT) instead of retraining Only simulated training data are available — the dysgu authors specifically avoided simulated datasets, considering non-simulated training to enhance performance The input is already a fitted model pickle; re-running feature elimination and grid search is unnecessary for inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Trains dysgu's SV quality-score classifier by combining recursive feature elimination with a 5-fold stratified cross-validated grid search over hyperparameters of a LightGBM 'dart' gradient-boosting model, using non-simulated gold-set labelled SVs as training data. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Trains dysgu's SV quality-score classifier by combining recursive feature elimination with a 5-fold stratified cross-validated grid search over hyperparameters of a LightGBM 'dart' gradient-boosting model, using non-simulated gold-set labelled SVs as training data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to score/filter existing calls with a trained model — use dysgu filter with model-probability thresholds (≥0.5 for PacBio, ≥0.35 for ONT) instead of retraining Only simulated training data are available — the dysgu authors specifically avoided simulated datasets, considering non-simulated training to enhance performance The input is already a fitted model pickle; re-running feature elimination and grid search is unnecessary for inference

skills.description: Use when nanopore long reads arrive incrementally during an ongoing MinION run and must be aligned block-wise to a pre-assembled draft (e.g. SPAdes contigs) to update a real-time npScarf scaffold.
skills.name: streaming-bwa-mem-alignment-pipeline
skills.search_text: streaming-bwa-mem-alignment-pipeline Use when nanopore long reads arrive incrementally during an ongoing MinION run and must be aligned block-wise to a pre-assembled draft (e.g. SPAdes contigs) to update a real-time npScarf scaffold. All nanopore reads are already available and no real-time scaffolding is needed — a plain batch bwa mem + scaffolder run is simpler. Input is short-read (Illumina) data rather than long nanopore reads — the k11/-L0 parameters are tuned for long, error-prone reads and the draft is the BWA target. npScarf scaffolding itself is not the goal (e.g. polishing or base-calling) — this pipeline produces scaffolds, not corrected reads or consensus. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Streams nanopore reads (live or emulated) through BWA-MEM with a fixed long-read-tuned parameter set (-k11 -W20 -r10 -A1 -B1 -O1 -E1 -L0 -a -Y) and pipes the SAM output into jsa.np.npscarf for real-time scaffolding of a short-read draft assembly. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14515
skills.summary: Streams nanopore reads (live or emulated) through BWA-MEM with a fixed long-read-tuned parameter set (-k11 -W20 -r10 -A1 -B1 -O1 -E1 -L0 -a -Y) and pipes the SAM output into jsa.np.npscarf for real-time scaffolding of a short-read draft assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All nanopore reads are already available and no real-time scaffolding is needed — a plain batch bwa mem + scaffolder run is simpler. Input is short-read (Illumina) data rather than long nanopore reads — the k11/-L0 parameters are tuned for long, error-prone reads and the draft is the BWA target. npScarf scaffolding itself is not the goal (e.g. polishing or base-calling) — this pipeline produces scaffolds, not corrected reads or consensus.

skills.description: Use when assembling diploid genomes from long noisy reads (Nanopore R9/R10, PacBio CLR) where overlap-graph construction and phasing of haplotype-specific contigs is the goal.
skills.name: string-graph-assembly
skills.search_text: string-graph-assembly Use when assembling diploid genomes from long noisy reads (Nanopore R9/R10, PacBio CLR) where overlap-graph construction and phasing of haplotype-specific contigs is the goal. Input reads are PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — PECAT achieves mediocre performance on these highly accurate read types Input is short-read data or the goal is reference-based variant calling rather than de novo diploid assembly Dataset has very low heterozygosity rate — SNP calling accuracy is low in such regions, undermining inconsistent-overlap removal Build and traverse a string graph from long-read overlaps to assemble haplotype-collapsed and phased diploid contigs, as implemented in PECAT with minimap2 candidate overlaps and Myers' transitive-edge reduction. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Build and traverse a string graph from long-read overlaps to assemble haplotype-collapsed and phased diploid contigs, as implemented in PECAT with minimap2 candidate overlaps and Myers' transitive-edge reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are PacBio HiFi or Nanopore duplex — PECAT achieves mediocre performance on these highly accurate read types Input is short-read data or the goal is reference-based variant calling rather than de novo diploid assembly Dataset has very low heterozygosity rate — SNP calling accuracy is low in such regions, undermining inconsistent-overlap removal

skills.name: stringdecomposer-output-parsing
skills.search_text: stringdecomposer-output-parsing Use when nanomonsv single breakend SVs are classified as 'High Repeat single breakend SVs' and RepeatMasker annotates them 'Satellite/centr', and you must quantify how consistently each contig matches centromeric HORs. SVs where both breakpoints lie in poorly characterized repetitive regions — the nanomonsv Single breakend SV module cannot detect these, so no contig is available to score Long repeat expansion events (VNTR/microsatellite) where the reference genome is unreliable and a reference-genome-based decomposition would be inappropriate Contigs already decomposed against monomer sets from a different chromosome than the one whose HOR definitions (cen*_hors.tsv) are used for consistency checking http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes a per-contig HOR match score (0–1) for centromeric single breakend contigs by parsing StringDecomposer (v1.1.2) final_decomposition.tsv output line by line against HORmon-curated HOR definitions, then normalizing summed monomer concordance by contig length. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Computes a per-contig HOR match score (0–1) for centromeric single breakend contigs by parsing StringDecomposer (v1.1.2) final_decomposition.tsv output line by line against HORmon-curated HOR definitions, then normalizing summed monomer concordance by contig length.

skills.description: Use when a mechanistic ODE model's kinetic parameters (e.g. RNA synthesis, processing, export, degradation rates) must be shown to be uniquely recoverable from a given set of measurable outputs before fitting rates to experimental data.
skills.name: structural-identifiability-analysis-of-ode-models
skills.search_text: structural-identifiability-analysis-of-ode-models Use when a mechanistic ODE model's kinetic parameters (e.g. RNA synthesis, processing, export, degradation rates) must be shown to be uniquely recoverable from a given set of measurable outputs before fitting rates to experimental data. The model parameters have already been fitted and you only need goodness-of-fit or uncertainty estimates rather than a structural (algebraic) uniqueness guarantee. Your observation model cannot include nascent RNA measurements — the identifiability guarantee here rests specifically on declaring nascent RNA species as measurable outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Assess whether every kinetic rate (k1-k9) of a 9-rate ODE model of RNA life-cycle dynamics is globally structurally identifiable by running a differential-algebra SIAN analysis on the ODE system with nascent RNA species declared as measurable observation functions. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51917-2
skills.summary: Assess whether every kinetic rate (k1-k9) of a 9-rate ODE model of RNA life-cycle dynamics is globally structurally identifiable by running a differential-algebra SIAN analysis on the ODE system with nascent RNA species declared as measurable observation functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model parameters have already been fitted and you only need goodness-of-fit or uncertainty estimates rather than a structural (algebraic) uniqueness guarantee. Your observation model cannot include nascent RNA measurements — the identifiability guarantee here rests specifically on declaring nascent RNA species as measurable outputs.

skills.search_text: structural-misassembly-error-detection Use when a candidate assembly (FASTA scaffolds) must be checked for structural errors against a reference genome or compared head-to-head with other assemblies using alignment-based Gage statistics. Input is raw long or short reads rather than an assembled scaffold FASTA — use the Fast-SG scaffolding-graph construction step instead of Gage evaluation The goal is insert/gap-size estimation with 10X or DOVETAIL long-range mate-pair technologies, which the article notes is challenging because linking information spans a range of insert sizes with possibly unknown read-pair orientation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies structural accuracy of genome assemblies (e.g., the Fast-SG DFS hybrid assembly of NA12878) by whole-genome Nucmer alignment against a reference and Gage statistics (N50, identity, misjoins, relocations, translocations, inversions), benchmarking against public Canu, MaSuRCA, 10X, and DOVETAIL assemblies. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long or short reads rather than an assembled scaffold FASTA — use the Fast-SG scaffolding-graph construction step instead of Gage evaluation The goal is insert/gap-size estimation with 10X or DOVETAIL long-range mate-pair technologies, which the article notes is challenging because linking information spans a range of insert sizes with possibly unknown read-pair orientation

skills.name: structural-variant-anchor-evidence-assembly
skills.search_text: structural-variant-anchor-evidence-assembly Use when you have invMap SAM/inversion-call outputs plus competing mapper call sets and need to isolate and tabulate novel inversion calls missed by all baselines, e.g. invMap-only calls on NA12878. The goal is general SV discovery from scratch rather than assembling evidence for candidate calls already produced by invMap and baselines. Input reads are short reads rather than long noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads that can span inversion breakpoints. No competing-mapper call sets are available, so invMap-only calls cannot be isolated by interval overlap. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Assembles evidence tables for inversion structural-variant calls by comparing invMap calls against competing long-read mappers (Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, lra) via interval overlap on reference coordinates, isolating invMap-only discoveries such as the novel 231 bp inversion on the NA12878 real human genome dataset. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Assembles evidence tables for inversion structural-variant calls by comparing invMap calls against competing long-read mappers (Winnowmap2, minimap2, NGMLR, lra) via interval overlap on reference coordinates, isolating invMap-only discoveries such as the novel 231 bp inversion on the NA12878 real human genome dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is general SV discovery from scratch rather than assembling evidence for candidate calls already produced by invMap and baselines. Input reads are short reads rather than long noisy PacBio or Oxford Nanopore reads that can span inversion breakpoints. skills.description: Use when ONT or PacBio long reads are aligned to a reference genome and a suspected large-scale rearrangement (translocation, deletion, inversion) needs breakpoint-level annotation, e.g. reproducing a published t(chr6;chr8) breakpoint from SRA reads.
skills.name: structural-variant-annotation
skills.search_text: structural-variant-annotation Use when ONT or PacBio long reads are aligned to a reference genome and a suspected large-scale rearrangement (translocation, deletion, inversion) needs breakpoint-level annotation, e.g. reproducing a published t(chr6;chr8) breakpoint from SRA reads. The underlying variant is expected to be a SNV or small indel resolvable by short-read sequencing; AgileStructure targets large-scale structural rearrangements that short-read data misses. Only short-read Illumina data is available — breakpoint-spanning split reads from long reads are required to call junctions. You need fully automated, unsupervised SV discovery rather than user-guided interpretation of specific candidate breakpoints. http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Locate and annotate large-scale genomic structural rearrangements (e.g. translocations) from aligned long-read sequencing data using AgileStructure, a desktop application that supports user-guided exploration of breakpoint-spanning split reads and consensus per-read variant annotation. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Locate and annotate large-scale genomic structural rearrangements (e.g. translocations) from aligned long-read sequencing data using AgileStructure, a desktop application that supports user-guided exploration of breakpoint-spanning split reads and consensus per-read variant annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying variant is expected to be a SNV or small indel resolvable by short-read sequencing; AgileStructure targets large-scale structural rearrangements that short-read data misses. Only short-read Illumina data is available — breakpoint-spanning split reads from long reads are required to call junctions. You need fully automated, unsupervised SV discovery rather than user-guided interpretation of specific candidate breakpoints.

skills.description: Use when preparing medium-size (50–10,000 bp) insertion/deletion SV calls from position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAMs (optionally with paired long-read BAM/FASTQ) and a BWA-indexed reference genome.
skills.name: structural-variant-assembly-preprocessing
skills.search_text: structural-variant-assembly-preprocessing Use when preparing medium-size (50–10,000 bp) insertion/deletion SV calls from position-sorted, BX-tagged SLR BAMs (optionally with paired long-read BAM/FASTQ) and a BWA-indexed reference genome. Whole-genome assembly is desired — Blackbird explicitly avoids computationally expensive whole-genome assembly in favor of local segment assembly Target SVs are shorter than 50 bp — Blackbird's primary output out_50.vcf contains only insertion/deletion calls longer than 50 bp, and shorter calls in out.vcf are described as not reliable The SLR bam lacks position-sorted, indexed BX tags or the reference is not BWA-indexed — required input assumptions are violated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Segment a BWA-indexed reference genome into overlapping 50 kbp sliding windows and build barcode-aware local-assembly read sets for structural variant calling, as implemented in Blackbird for synthetic long read (SLR) and hybrid SLR+long-read SV detection. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Segment a BWA-indexed reference genome into overlapping 50 kbp sliding windows and build barcode-aware local-assembly read sets for structural variant calling, as implemented in Blackbird for synthetic long read (SLR) and hybrid SLR+long-read SV detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Whole-genome assembly is desired — Blackbird explicitly avoids computationally expensive whole-genome assembly in favor of local segment assembly Target SVs are shorter than 50 bp — Blackbird's primary output out_50.vcf contains only insertion/deletion calls longer than 50 bp, and shorter calls in out.vcf are described as not reliable The SLR bam lacks position-sorted, indexed BX tags or the reference is not BWA-indexed — required input assumptions are violated

skills.description: Use when comparing insertion/deletion (>50 bp) SV callsets against GIAB HG002 or simulated ground truth across coverage levels to quantify caller recall, precision, F1, and long-read coverage saturation.
skills.name: structural-variant-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: structural-variant-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing insertion/deletion (>50 bp) SV callsets against GIAB HG002 or simulated ground truth across coverage levels to quantify caller recall, precision, F1, and long-read coverage saturation. Calling variants in a single sample without any benchmark/ground-truth SV set or competing caller — the skill is about comparison and evaluation, not detection itself Detecting SVs from short-read data alone — the article notes most SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short-read sequencing Variant sizes below 50 bp — Blackbird's reliable output (out_50.vcf) and the benchmark scope are restricted to events longer than 50 bp http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark structural variant callers (Blackbird, PBSV, Sniffles2, SvABA, Manta) by comparing their VCF callsets to a ground-truth SV set with Truvari, computing per-SV-type recall, precision, and F1 across long-read coverage levels. Used to show Blackbird hybrid mode needs only 5× PacBio HiFi coverage to match PBSV/Sniffles2 at 10×. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant callers (Blackbird, PBSV, Sniffles2, SvABA, Manta) by comparing their VCF callsets to a ground-truth SV set with Truvari, computing per-SV-type recall, precision, and F1 across long-read coverage levels. Used to show Blackbird hybrid mode needs only 5× PacBio HiFi coverage to match PBSV/Sniffles2 at 10×.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling variants in a single sample without any benchmark/ground-truth SV set or competing caller — the skill is about comparison and evaluation, not detection itself Detecting SVs from short-read data alone — the article notes most SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short-read sequencing Variant sizes below 50 bp — Blackbird's reliable output (out_50.vcf) and the benchmark scope are restricted to events longer than 50 bp

skills.description: Use when comparing SV caller accuracy on HiFi WGS callsets against a GIAB SV truth set and you need an independent second evaluator (hap-eval) to confirm rankings previously established with Truvari.
skills.name: structural-variant-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: structural-variant-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing SV caller accuracy on HiFi WGS callsets against a GIAB SV truth set and you need an independent second evaluator (hap-eval) to confirm rankings previously established with Truvari. The truth set is the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark (HG002_GRCh38_CMRG_SV_v1.00), which per the article is assessed with 'truvari bench' alone rather than the hap-eval T2T workflow The assessment must include sex chromosomes chrX/chrY, since the confident-region BED is deliberately restricted to autosomes with 'grep -v chr[XY]' The callset is not a structural-variant VCF from a long-read HiFi caller (e.g., short-read variant VCFs or read-level data) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Independently benchmark long-read SV caller outputs (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) against the GIAB draft T2T-HG002-Q100 SV benchmark using Sentieon hap-eval as a second assessment method beyond Truvari, extracting per-caller precision, recall, and F1 to confirm accuracy rankings cross-method. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Independently benchmark long-read SV caller outputs (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) against the GIAB draft T2T-HG002-Q100 SV benchmark using Sentieon hap-eval as a second assessment method beyond Truvari, extracting per-caller precision, recall, and F1 to confirm accuracy rankings cross-method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The truth set is the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark (HG002_GRCh38_CMRG_SV_v1.00), which per the article is assessed with 'truvari bench' alone rather than the hap-eval T2T workflow The assessment must include sex chromosomes chrX/chrY, since the confident-region BED is deliberately restricted to autosomes with 'grep -v chr[XY]' The callset is not a structural-variant VCF from a long-read HiFi caller (e.g., short-read variant VCFs or read-level data)

skills.description: Use when SV calls in VCF format (single-technology or merged callsets from dysgu 'merge') must be evaluated against the GIAB HG002 benchmark, reporting precision/recall per SV type for All-regions vs Tier 1 regions.

skills.search_text: structural-variant-benchmark-evaluation-against-giab-truth-set Use when SV calls in VCF format (single-technology or merged callsets from dysgu 'merge') must be evaluated against the GIAB HG002 benchmark, reporting precision/recall per SV type for All-regions vs Tier 1 regions. Truth set is not GIAB HG002-compatible (e.g. syndip/CHM1-CHM13 assemblies call for a different benchmarking setup) Calls have not been merged/filtered yet and the question is single-caller performance, not recall gains from merging Small variant (<30 bp indel/SNV) calling accuracy is the target; svbench defaults apply a --min-size-query of 30 suited to SVs ≥50 bp http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark structural variant callsets (e.g. dysgu VCFs from paired-end Illumina, PacBio, or ONT reads, or merged PE+LR callsets) against the Genome in a Bottle HG002 Ashkenazi son truth set using svbench, computing precision and recall per SV type to quantify recall gains from call merging. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant callsets (e.g. dysgu VCFs from paired-end Illumina, PacBio, or ONT reads, or merged PE+LR callsets) against the Genome in a Bottle HG002 Ashkenazi son truth set using svbench, computing precision and recall per SV type to quantify recall gains from call merging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Truth set is not GIAB HG002-compatible (e.g. syndip/CHM1-CHM13 assemblies call for a different benchmarking setup) Calls have not been merged/filtered yet and the question is single-caller performance, not recall gains from merging Small variant (<30 bp indel/SNV) calling accuracy is the target; svbench defaults apply a --min-size-query of 30 suited to SVs ≥50 bp

skills.description: Use when a per-sample collapsed consensus VCF from the ConsensuSV-ONT pipeline (e.g. HG00733, HG00514) needs TP/FP labels against an HGSVC ground truth to train or evaluate a CNN SV quality filter.

skills.search_text: structural-variant-benchmarking Use when a per-sample collapsed consensus VCF from the ConsensuSV-ONT pipeline (e.g. HG00733, HG00514) needs TP/FP labels against an HGSVC ground truth to train or evaluate a CNN SV quality filter. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input VCFs come from the individual SV callers rather than the collapsed consensus set — this skill labels only the consensus candidates No HGSVC benchmark VCF exists for the sample's genome, so no ground-truth counterparts can be defined Goal is calling SVs de novo from FASTQ rather than labelling existing consensus calls against a benchmark

skills.description: Use when a LongRanger-aligned 10x (or TELL-Seq/stLFR) BAM is available and the goal is to discover and genotype non-reference insertions longer than 300 bp that short-read methods fail to assemble and place.
skills.name: structural-variant-breakpoint-alignment
skills.search_text: structural-variant-breakpoint-alignment Use when a LongRanger-aligned 10x (or TELL-Seq/stLFR) BAM is available and the goal is to discover and genotype non-reference insertions longer than 300 bp that short-read methods fail to assemble and place. The goal requires assembling full genomes or SV classes other than NRS insertions — Novel-X targets NRS insertion discovery and does not perform whole-genome de novo assembly nor assembly of other complex SV classes. Insertions are small (<300 bp): Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes, and for small insertions the number of associated barcodes is usually small and coverage insufficient for anchor assembly. Input is raw FASTQ without barcode-aware alignment — the pipeline expects a LongRanger-aligned BAM as its starting point. http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Detects and places non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions >300 bp from 10x Genomics linked-read data via Novel-X's four-step pipeline: orphan contig assembly, barcode extraction, barcode-guided reassembly with SPAdes, and Minimap2 anchor alignment to the reference, without whole-genome de novo assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Detects and places non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions >300 bp from 10x Genomics linked-read data via Novel-X's four-step pipeline: orphan contig assembly, barcode extraction, barcode-guided reassembly with SPAdes, and Minimap2 anchor alignment to the reference, without whole-genome de novo assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal requires assembling full genomes or SV classes other than NRS insertions — Novel-X targets NRS insertion discovery and does not perform whole-genome de novo assembly nor assembly of other complex SV classes. Insertions are small (<300 bp): Novel-X needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes, and for small insertions the number of associated barcodes is usually small and coverage insufficient for anchor assembly. Input is raw FASTQ without barcode-aware alignment — the pipeline expects a LongRanger-aligned BAM as its starting point.

skills.description: Use when assembling low-coverage HiFi reads with reference-guided chromosome binning and reads spanning translocation breakpoints risk being assigned to the wrong chromosome class.
skills.name: structural-variant-breakpoint-clustering
skills.search_text: structural-variant-breakpoint-clustering Use when assembling low-coverage HiFi reads with reference-guided chromosome binning and reads spanning translocation breakpoints risk being assigned to the wrong chromosome class. Input reads are high-coverage and will be assembled with a purely de novo assembler such as hifiasm alone — the translocation correction module is specific to reference-guided chromosome-by-chromosome binning The analysis targets structural variants smaller than the workflow's scope (large germline SVs larger than 10,000 bp detected downstream) rather than chromosome-class correction of reads No reference genome is available, since split-alignment SigBND extraction against a linear reference is the basis of the signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reconstructs HiFiCCL's translocation class correction: extracting split-alignment translocation signals (SigBND), clustering breakpoints by genomic-coordinate distance, and reassigning breakpoint-spanning reads to the correct chromosome so they are not misclassified during reference-guided clustering. genomics/v1 10.1002/advs.202515308
skills.summary: Reconstructs HiFiCCL's translocation class correction: extracting split-alignment translocation signals (SigBND), clustering breakpoints by genomic-coordinate distance, and reassigning breakpoint-spanning reads to the correct chromosome so they are not misclassified during reference-guided clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are high-coverage and will be assembled with a purely de novo assembler such as hifiasm alone — the translocation correction module is specific to reference-guided chromosome-by-chromosome binning The analysis targets structural variants smaller than the workflow's scope (large germline SVs larger than 10,000 bp detected downstream) rather than chromosome-class correction of reads No reference genome is available, since split-alignment SigBND extraction against a linear reference is the basis of the signal

skills.description: Use when an indexed long-read BAM (ONT reads aligned with minimap2 '-ax map-ont --secondary=no') must be screened for structural rearrangement breakpoints and classified as simple (2 columns of split reads; 3 for insertions) or complex (3 or 4 columns).
skills.name: structural-variant-breakpoint-detection
skills.search_text: structural-variant-breakpoint-detection Use when an indexed long-read BAM (ONT reads aligned with minimap2 '-ax map-ont --secondary=no') must be screened for structural rearrangement breakpoints and classified as simple (2 columns of split reads; 3 for insertions) or complex (3 or 4 columns). Input reads are short-read (Illumina) alignments, which are stated to fail to resolve the underlying pathogenic variant in approximately 50% of rare-disease patients The BAM lacks linked secondary alignments for split reads (e.g. aligned without split-read or primary/secondary linking information), so primary/secondary junction positions cannot be extracted The goal is small variant calling (SNVs or small indels) rather than large-scale structural rearrangement detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Detects and annotates large-scale genomic rearrangements (deletions, insertions, inversions, duplications, translocations, ring chromosomes, complex insertion-deletion events) from aligned long-read BAM data using AgileStructure's split-read junction clustering and two-panel user-guided annotation interface. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Detects and annotates large-scale genomic rearrangements (deletions, insertions, inversions, duplications, translocations, ring chromosomes, complex insertion-deletion events) from aligned long-read BAM data using AgileStructure's split-read junction clustering and two-panel user-guided annotation interface.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short-read (Illumina) alignments, which are stated to fail to resolve the underlying pathogenic variant in approximately 50% of rare-disease patients The BAM lacks linked secondary alignments for split reads (e.g. aligned without split-read or primary/secondary linking information), so primary/secondary junction positions cannot be extracted The goal is small variant calling (SNVs or small indels) rather than large-scale structural rearrangement detection

skills.description: Use when mapped long-read (HiFi) alignments must be scanned for SV breakpoint evidence and clustered into candidates as the discovery stage of sawfish SV/CNV calling on GRCh38.
skills.name: structural-variant-breakpoint-evidence-clustering
skills.search_text: structural-variant-breakpoint-evidence-clustering Use when mapped long-read (HiFi) alignments must be scanned for SV breakpoint evidence and clustered into candidates as the discovery stage of sawfish SV/CNV calling on GRCh38. The input is raw unaligned reads — evidence scanning requires a coordinate-sorted mapped BAM, so alignment with pbmm2 must precede this step The goal is short-read SV calling — the article scopes sawfish to mapped HiFi sequencing reads Per-sample discover output already exists — discover is run once per sample, and multi-sample merging/genotyping is handled by the sawfish joint-call step instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Clusters per-read breakpoint evidence from mapped HiFi alignments into candidate breakpoint clusters, refines each cluster into SV haplotype contigs via POA assembly (spoa) and wavefront realignment (WFA2-lib), and discards noise so sawfish discover produces basepair-resolution candidate SVs ready for joint genotyping. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Clusters per-read breakpoint evidence from mapped HiFi alignments into candidate breakpoint clusters, refines each cluster into SV haplotype contigs via POA assembly (spoa) and wavefront realignment (WFA2-lib), and discards noise so sawfish discover produces basepair-resolution candidate SVs ready for joint genotyping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw unaligned reads — evidence scanning requires a coordinate-sorted mapped BAM, so alignment with pbmm2 must precede this step The goal is short-read SV calling — the article scopes sawfish to mapped HiFi sequencing reads Per-sample discover output already exists — discover is run once per sample, and multi-sample merging/genotyping is handled by the sawfish joint-call step instead

skills.description: Use when comparing the accuracy of long-read mappers for locating aligned regions or detecting inversion SVs on simulated PacBio CCS/CLR or ONT reads across reference genomes of different sizes.
skills.name: structural-variant-breakpoint-mapping-evaluation
skills.search_text: structural-variant-breakpoint-mapping-evaluation Use when comparing the accuracy of long-read mappers for locating aligned regions or detecting inversion SVs on simulated PacBio CCS/CLR or ONT reads across reference genomes of different sizes. The goal is real-data variant discovery rather than mapper benchmarking — e.g. finding candidate inversion variant calls on a real dataset such as NA12878 (a separate downstream analysis). Input reads are short reads or already accurately aligned with trusted ground-truth coordinates, where location-accuracy benchmarking adds no information. The reference genome or read set is much larger than chromosome-scale assemblies used here — invMap requires a minimum of 16 GB RAM for mapping to large reference genomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmark long-read mapping accuracy and inversion structural-variant (SV) calling for invMap against minimap2, Winnowmap2, lra, and NGMLR using PBSIM/PBSIM2-simulated PacBio CCS, CLR, and ONT reads, computing location accuracy as the fraction of reads whose aligned region matches the true simulated origin. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read mapping accuracy and inversion structural-variant (SV) calling for invMap against minimap2, Winnowmap2, lra, and NGMLR using PBSIM/PBSIM2-simulated PacBio CCS, CLR, and ONT reads, computing location accuracy as the fraction of reads whose aligned region matches the true simulated origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is real-data variant discovery rather than mapper benchmarking — e.g. finding candidate inversion variant calls on a real dataset such as NA12878 (a separate downstream analysis). Input reads are short reads or already accurately aligned with trusted ground-truth coordinates, where location-accuracy benchmarking adds no information. The reference genome or read set is much larger than chromosome-scale assemblies used here — invMap requires a minimum of 16 GB RAM for mapping to large reference genomes.

skills.description: Use when locally assembled contigs (e.g. from Blackbird's barcode-aware sliding-window SPAdes assembly) have been aligned to a reference with minimap2 and raw CIGAR-derived indel events must be deduplicated and filtered into a reliable VCF.
skills.name: structural-variant-call-deduplication
skills.search_text: structural-variant-call-deduplication Use when locally assembled contigs (e.g. from Blackbird's barcode-aware sliding-window SPAdes assembly) have been aligned to a reference with minimap2 and raw CIGAR-derived indel events must be deduplicated and filtered into a reliable VCF. The goal is whole-genome-assembly-based SV calling — Blackbird deliberately uses a barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly instead of a whole-genome assembly Only short-read sequencing data are available without SLR barcodes or long reads — most SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short reads Variants shorter than 50 bp are the target — they are routed to out.vcf, which Blackbird reports as not reliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Deduplicates insertion and deletion calls produced by Blackbird's SV identification stage by collapsing variants sharing an identical breakpoint and event length, then filters to indels longer than 50 bp and writes a position-sorted VCF. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Deduplicates insertion and deletion calls produced by Blackbird's SV identification stage by collapsing variants sharing an identical breakpoint and event length, then filters to indels longer than 50 bp and writes a position-sorted VCF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is whole-genome-assembly-based SV calling — Blackbird deliberately uses a barcode-aware sliding-window local assembly instead of a whole-genome assembly Only short-read sequencing data are available without SLR barcodes or long reads — most SVs in the 50–10,000 bp range cannot be resolved with short reads Variants shorter than 50 bp are the target — they are routed to out.vcf, which Blackbird reports as not reliable

skills.description: Use when two assemblies of the same organism exist (e.g., Canu >500k contigs vs CaSM scaffolds) and you need SV coordinates to benchmark reference-free error calls like CRAQ CREs/CSEs against.
skills.name: structural-variant-calling-from-assemblies
skills.search_text: structural-variant-calling-from-assemblies Use when two assemblies of the same organism exist (e.g., Canu >500k contigs vs CaSM scaffolds) and you need SV coordinates to benchmark reference-free error calls like CRAQ CREs/CSEs against. Only one assembly is available and no second assembly or reference exists to define structural differences — CRAQ alone is the reference-free option The goal is small variant calling (SNPs/indels) rather than assembly-vs-assembly SVs; SyRI parameters here deliberately ignore SNPs, HDRs, INSs, and DELs < 40 bp The genome is polyploid — the article states evaluation accuracy 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases' for higher ploidy levels http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call structural variants between two de novo assemblies (e.g., SyRI with a Canu assembly as query against a CaSM assembly as reference) and quantify their overlap with CRAQ-detected assembly errors to distinguish true assembly errors from genuine haplotype/structural divergence. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-42336-w
skills.summary: Call structural variants between two de novo assemblies (e.g., SyRI with a Canu assembly as query against a CaSM assembly as reference) and quantify their overlap with CRAQ-detected assembly errors to distinguish true assembly errors from genuine haplotype/structural divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one assembly is available and no second assembly or reference exists to define structural differences — CRAQ alone is the reference-free option The goal is small variant calling (SNPs/indels) rather than assembly-vs-assembly SVs; SyRI parameters here deliberately ignore SNPs, HDRs, INSs, and DELs < 40 bp The genome is polyploid — the article states evaluation accuracy 'may not be as accurate as the benchmarked cases' for higher ploidy levels

skills.description: Use when you have long-read nanopore BAM alignments against GRCh37 and need a filtered SV VCF as input for downstream gene-fusion annotation or breakpoint refinement.
skills.name: structural-variant-calling-from-bam
skills.search_text: structural-variant-calling-from-bam Use when you have long-read nanopore BAM alignments against GRCh37 and need a filtered SV VCF as input for downstream gene-fusion annotation or breakpoint refinement. Input reads are short paired-end or already a curated VCF of final fusion calls rather than long-read BAM alignments DNA is fragmented (e.g. FFPE material), where short read lengths prevent comprehensive SV/fusion identification The goal is small-variant (SNV/indel) calling rather than gross structural variants and gene fusions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Call structural variants from long-read nanopore BAM alignments to the GRCh37 human reference using NanoSV (v.1.2.4) or Sniffles (v.1.0.9), then filter the resulting VCF as the first stage of the NanoFG fusion-gene pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16641-7
skills.summary: Call structural variants from long-read nanopore BAM alignments to the GRCh37 human reference using NanoSV (v.1.2.4) or Sniffles (v.1.0.9), then filter the resulting VCF as the first stage of the NanoFG fusion-gene pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short paired-end or already a curated VCF of final fusion calls rather than long-read BAM alignments DNA is fragmented (e.g. FFPE material), where short read lengths prevent comprehensive SV/fusion identification The goal is small-variant (SNV/indel) calling rather than gross structural variants and gene fusions

skills.description: Use when calling deletion structural variants (>50 bp) from long-read alignments (SAM/BAM) of third-generation sequencing data and benchmarking caller performance against a truth set.
skills.name: structural-variant-calling-from-long-read-sequencing
skills.search_text: structural-variant-calling-from-long-read-sequencing Use when calling deletion structural variants (>50 bp) from long-read alignments (SAM/BAM) of third-generation sequencing data and benchmarking caller performance against a truth set. The goal is insertion or base substitution (SNV) variant calling — the paper states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling' Input data are short NGS reads (e.g. Illumina ~250–300 bp) rather than third-generation long reads A versioned, production-ready caller is required — the authors note they 'aim to further develop and package this technology into user-friendly software' (future work) Reproduce the DASV deletion-calling workflow on third-generation sequencing (CLR/CCS) data: quality-filter aligned SAM/BAM files, extract deletions from CIGAR fields, encode sequences to 100x100-pixel images, run the dual-attention multi-scale ResNet caller, and benchmark F1/precision/recall against cuteSV, SVIM, Sniffles and PBSV on HG002. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: Reproduce the DASV deletion-calling workflow on third-generation sequencing (CLR/CCS) data: quality-filter aligned SAM/BAM files, extract deletions from CIGAR fields, encode sequences to 100x100-pixel images, run the dual-attention multi-scale ResNet caller, and benchmark F1/precision/recall against cuteSV, SVIM, Sniffles and PBSV on HG002.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is insertion or base substitution (SNV) variant calling — the paper states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling' Input data are short NGS reads (e.g. Illumina ~250–300 bp) rather than third-generation long reads A versioned, production-ready caller is required — the authors note they 'aim to further develop and package this technology into user-friendly software' (future work)

skills.description: Use when detecting inversion structural variants from long noisy reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) mapped to a reference genome, especially when implanted or known inversion truth sets (e.g., SURVIVOR VCF) must be evaluated per mapper.
skills.name: structural-variant-calling-from-long-reads
skills.search_text: structural-variant-calling-from-long-reads Use when detecting inversion structural variants from long noisy reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) mapped to a reference genome, especially when implanted or known inversion truth sets (e.g., SURVIVOR VCF) must be evaluated per mapper. Input reads are short reads (Illumina); the article's method targets longer PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads that frequently span SV breakpoints The analysis goal is SNV/small-indel calling rather than inversion structural variant detection No reference genome or truth VCF is available, so sensitivity/precision against implanted inversions cannot be evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Call inversion structural variants from PacBio/ONT long-read alignments using the invMap mapper followed by SVision, then benchmark sensitivity/precision against a SURVIVOR-derived truth set. This captures the invMap-SVision pipeline that the article shows recovers inversions better than minimap2-, NGMLR-, Winnowmap2- or lra-based pipelines. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Call inversion structural variants from PacBio/ONT long-read alignments using the invMap mapper followed by SVision, then benchmark sensitivity/precision against a SURVIVOR-derived truth set. This captures the invMap-SVision pipeline that the article shows recovers inversions better than minimap2-, NGMLR-, Winnowmap2- or lra-based pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short reads (Illumina); the article's method targets longer PacBio/Oxford Nanopore reads that frequently span SV breakpoints The analysis goal is SNV/small-indel calling rather than inversion structural variant detection No reference genome or truth VCF is available, so sensitivity/precision against implanted inversions cannot be evaluated

skills.description: Use when nanopore/long-read FASTQ or FASTA data must be turned into TE insertion/deletion callsets, or when caller combinations and supporting-read thresholds must be compared against a truth set.
skills.name: structural-variant-calling-long-reads
skills.search_text: structural-variant-calling-long-reads Use when nanopore/long-read FASTQ or FASTA data must be turned into TE insertion/deletion callsets, or when caller combinations and supporting-read thresholds must be compared against a truth set. Input is short-read sequencing data — tools like MELT or xTea cover short-read TE detection; this skill relies on long-read SV callers (cuteSV, Sniffles2, SVIM) The goal is annotation or enrichment of already-called TE insertions rather than detection — RetroInspector's annotation/enrichment stages, not SV calling, are the relevant step A single caller suffices and no benchmarking is needed — the strict-criterion value here comes from intersecting two callers, which discards single-caller-only calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Detect transposable element (TE) insertions and deletions from basecalled nanopore reads by aligning to GRCh38 with minimap2, calling structural variants with multiple SV callers (cuteSV, Sniffles2, optionally SVIM), and filtering the callsets by supporting-read thresholds under strict (intersection) or lax criteria before benchmarking against a truth set. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Detect transposable element (TE) insertions and deletions from basecalled nanopore reads by aligning to GRCh38 with minimap2, calling structural variants with multiple SV callers (cuteSV, Sniffles2, optionally SVIM), and filtering the callsets by supporting-read thresholds under strict (intersection) or lax criteria before benchmarking against a truth set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read sequencing data — tools like MELT or xTea cover short-read TE detection; this skill relies on long-read SV callers (cuteSV, Sniffles2, SVIM) The goal is annotation or enrichment of already-called TE insertions rather than detection — RetroInspector's annotation/enrichment stages, not SV calling, are the relevant step A single caller suffices and no benchmarking is needed — the strict-criterion value here comes from intersecting two callers, which discards single-caller-only calls

skills.description: Use when you have a long-read (nanopore) SV VCF plus matched short-read SV callsets for the same genomes and need to quantify which SVs are missed by short reads or absent from 1KG, including their size/GC/repeat properties.
skills.name: structural-variant-callset-intersection
skills.search_text: structural-variant-callset-intersection Use when you have a long-read (nanopore) SV VCF plus matched short-read SV callsets for the same genomes and need to quantify which SVs are missed by short reads or absent from 1KG, including their size/GC/repeat properties. Calling de novo chromothripsis rearrangement breakpoints or phasing them by haplotype - that is a different task in this paper, not callset intersection Only one callset (no matched short-read or population data) exists, so shared-versus-novel classification cannot be computed Attempting a full de novo human genome assembly from MinION reads - the authors did not attempt this due to insufficient coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Intersects NanoSV structural-variant callsets from MinION nanopore sequencing of patient genomes against SV calls from six Illumina short-read callers (Pindel, Manta, Delly, FREEC, Mobster, GATK HaplotypeCaller) and 1KG variant sites to define nanopore-specific (novel) SVs, then profiles their class, size, GC, and repeat/LINE composition. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Intersects NanoSV structural-variant callsets from MinION nanopore sequencing of patient genomes against SV calls from six Illumina short-read callers (Pindel, Manta, Delly, FREEC, Mobster, GATK HaplotypeCaller) and 1KG variant sites to define nanopore-specific (novel) SVs, then profiles their class, size, GC, and repeat/LINE composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling de novo chromothripsis rearrangement breakpoints or phasing them by haplotype - that is a different task in this paper, not callset intersection Only one callset (no matched short-read or population data) exists, so shared-versus-novel classification cannot be computed Attempting a full de novo human genome assembly from MinION reads - the authors did not attempt this due to insufficient coverage

skills.description: Use when you have a VCF of predicted non-reference sequence insertions and need precision/recall against a PacBio validation callset, or a confirmation rate against a T2T-assembly-derived insertion benchmark.
skills.name: structural-variant-callset-matching
skills.search_text: structural-variant-callset-matching Use when you have a VCF of predicted non-reference sequence insertions and need precision/recall against a PacBio validation callset, or a confirmation rate against a T2T-assembly-derived insertion benchmark. You need de novo comparison of two assemblies rather than matching a callset to a trusted benchmark — this skill presumes one side is treated as ground truth Insertions are shorter than 300 bp: Novel-X output filters and the paper's analysis are restricted to insertions longer than 300 bp Only raw read alignments exist and no benchmark insertion set (PacBio callset or T2T assembly) can be constructed for the sample http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Benchmark a predicted insertion/SV callset (e.g. Novel-X VCFs) against an independent validation set (PacBio long-read calls or a T2T assembly-derived insertion set) using paired breakpoint/length tolerance matching, then compute precision, recall, or confirmation rate. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Benchmark a predicted insertion/SV callset (e.g. Novel-X VCFs) against an independent validation set (PacBio long-read calls or a T2T assembly-derived insertion set) using paired breakpoint/length tolerance matching, then compute precision, recall, or confirmation rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need de novo comparison of two assemblies rather than matching a callset to a trusted benchmark — this skill presumes one side is treated as ground truth Insertions are shorter than 300 bp: Novel-X output filters and the paper's analysis are restricted to insertions longer than 300 bp Only raw read alignments exist and no benchmark insertion set (PacBio callset or T2T assembly) can be constructed for the sample

skills.description: Use when merging insertion variant calls from per-sample callsets (e.g., from cuteSV and Sniffles2 VCFs) where coordinate-only merging would collapse distinct near-coordinate events that carry different inserted sequences.
skills.name: structural-variant-callset-merging
skills.search_text: structural-variant-callset-merging Use when merging insertion variant calls from per-sample callsets (e.g., from cuteSV and Sniffles2 VCFs) where coordinate-only merging would collapse distinct near-coordinate events that carry different inserted sequences. When a standardized, coordinate-only SV merge is sufficient and sequence identity between insertions is not of interest — SURVIVOR with its own distance limits is the baseline for this case When variants are not insertions (e.g., deletions or inversions), since the Levenshtein comparison relies on reassembled inserted sequences When supporting reads for an insertion are so variable that the 15% length filter excludes most reads, leaving no reliable consensus for sequence comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A sequence-aware method for merging insertion calls from multiple structural variant callsets, used in RetroInspector to combine cuteSV and Sniffles2 insertion records within and across samples using coordinates, insertion length, and Levenshtein distance on reassembled inserted sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: A sequence-aware method for merging insertion calls from multiple structural variant callsets, used in RetroInspector to combine cuteSV and Sniffles2 insertion records within and across samples using coordinates, insertion length, and Levenshtein distance on reassembled inserted sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a standardized, coordinate-only SV merge is sufficient and sequence identity between insertions is not of interest — SURVIVOR with its own distance limits is the baseline for this case When variants are not insertions (e.g., deletions or inversions), since the Levenshtein comparison relies on reassembled inserted sequences When supporting reads for an insertion are so variable that the 15% length filter excludes most reads, leaving no reliable consensus for sequence comparison

skills.description: Use when a task requires obtaining the published curated SV catalogue (genotypes and copy numbers) for S. pombe strains and checking per-class counts against the paper's reported composition.
skills.name: structural-variant-callset-retrieval
skills.search_text: structural-variant-callset-retrieval Use when a task requires obtaining the published curated SV catalogue (genotypes and copy numbers) for S. pombe strains and checking per-class counts against the paper's reported composition. Input is a raw set of SV predictions from a single caller (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel or cn.MOPS) rather than the deposited curated callset — the consensus/filtering pipeline would need to be rerun instead The task requires de novo SV discovery or genotyping of translocations/inversions; the paper explicitly did not re-examine genotypes of translocations and inversions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Retrieve the deposited curated structural-variant callset for the worldwide S. pombe strain collection from the Figshare project (fission yeast structural variation, project 15798) and verify it reproduces the reported catalogue of 113 SVs (23 deletions, 64 duplications, 11 inversions, 15 translocations). genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Retrieve the deposited curated structural-variant callset for the worldwide S. pombe strain collection from the Figshare project (fission yeast structural variation, project 15798) and verify it reproduces the reported catalogue of 113 SVs (23 deletions, 64 duplications, 11 inversions, 15 translocations).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw set of SV predictions from a single caller (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel or cn.MOPS) rather than the deposited curated callset — the consensus/filtering pipeline would need to be rerun instead The task requires de novo SV discovery or genotyping of translocations/inversions; the paper explicitly did not re-examine genotypes of translocations and inversions

skills.description: Use when you have a sorted, indexed .bam/.cram (bwa-mem paired-end or minimap2/ngmlr long reads) and need to partition reads carrying SV signals (soft-clips >=15 bp, discordant pairs, supplementary mappings, cigar gaps) before SV calling.
skills.name: structural-variant-candidate-detection
skills.search_text: structural-variant-candidate-detection Use when you have a sorted, indexed .bam/.cram (bwa-mem paired-end or minimap2/ngmlr long reads) and need to partition reads carrying SV signals (soft-clips >=15 bp, discordant pairs, supplementary mappings, cigar gaps) before SV calling. You already have a filtered SV VCF and want post-calling filtering — use 'dysgu filter' instead of re-running fetch. Input reads are unaligned FASTQ with no BAM/CRAM — fetch operates on sorted, indexed alignments, so an aligner (bwa-mem, minimap2, ngmlr) must be run first. You need full-length insertion resolution or multi-allelic site resolution in PE data — the README notes dysgu lacks a de novo assembly stage for this. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Isolate SV-associated reads (split, discordant, soft-clipped, cigar-gap reads) from a sorted/indexed BAM or CRAM using dysgu's 'fetch' stage, producing a temporary dysgu_reads BAM that feeds the 'call' stage of dysgu's PE/LR structural variant calling pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Isolate SV-associated reads (split, discordant, soft-clipped, cigar-gap reads) from a sorted/indexed BAM or CRAM using dysgu's 'fetch' stage, producing a temporary dysgu_reads BAM that feeds the 'call' stage of dysgu's PE/LR structural variant calling pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a filtered SV VCF and want post-calling filtering — use 'dysgu filter' instead of re-running fetch. Input reads are unaligned FASTQ with no BAM/CRAM — fetch operates on sorted, indexed alignments, so an aligner (bwa-mem, minimap2, ngmlr) must be run first. You need full-length insertion resolution or multi-allelic site resolution in PE data — the README notes dysgu lacks a de novo assembly stage for this.

skills.description: Use when SV calls (VCF or coordinate lists from a variant caller or external technique) must be reformatted into BED for coverage-based validation with disCoverage/mosdepth, retaining only deletions and duplications.
skills.name: structural-variant-coordinate-bed-encoding
skills.search_text: structural-variant-coordinate-bed-encoding Use when SV calls (VCF or coordinate lists from a variant caller or external technique) must be reformatted into BED for coverage-based validation with disCoverage/mosdepth, retaining only deletions and duplications. The SV set contains types other than deletions and duplications (e.g., insertions, inversions, translocations) — disCoverage can only check DEL/DUP No putative SV coordinates exist yet — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs positions supplied from another technique or multi-sample analysis The goal is de novo SV discovery from coverage alone rather than validation or filtering of already-called coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Encodes putative SV calls as a 4-column BED (chromosome, start, end, SV type) so disCoverage can invoke mosdepth and compute per-base coverage over each SV interval plus 1-Mb up- and downstream flanks, the prerequisite for its coverage-based statistics. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Encodes putative SV calls as a 4-column BED (chromosome, start, end, SV type) so disCoverage can invoke mosdepth and compute per-base coverage over each SV interval plus 1-Mb up- and downstream flanks, the prerequisite for its coverage-based statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV set contains types other than deletions and duplications (e.g., insertions, inversions, translocations) — disCoverage can only check DEL/DUP No putative SV coordinates exist yet — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs positions supplied from another technique or multi-sample analysis The goal is de novo SV discovery from coverage alone rather than validation or filtering of already-called coordinates

Input is short-read Illumina data only — the paper's phasing depends on reads long enough to span multiple heterozygous SNPs and SV breakpoints; Illumina data even missed many of these SVs entirely. No trio (or other externally phased) heterozygous SNP ground truth exists for the sample — the benchmark and the haplotype anchoring both require trio-phased SNPs. Goal is de novo genome assembly from the nanopore reads — the authors did not attempt this 'primarily due to insufficient coverage' (11–16×). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Phases MinION nanopore reads against trio-phased (GATK PBT) heterozygous SNPs by read-level allele log-likelihood, then uses haplotype-assigned reads flanking SV breakpoints to phase Manta/NanoSV calls and benchmark phasing accuracy against the trio ground truth. This is the mechanism the paper used to show all 40 de novo chromothripsis breakpoint junctions in Patient 1 are paternal and to achieve 1909/2389 SVs phased at 98.5% concordance. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4

You only need per-variant read counts or genotype confidence scores rather than spatial alignment-feature images for CNN filtering Input reads are short-read (Illumina) alignments, since this encoding is built around long-read ONT alignments and split reads You lack the alignment BAM and only hold VCF summaries — the encoding requires per-read, per-position alignment features http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Encodes each consensus structural variant candidate from ConsensuSV-ONT into a fixed 50x50x3 image by extracting quality-passing long-read alignments around the variant and resizing the read-by-position matrix, so the CNN filter can score high-quality variants. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Encodes each consensus structural variant candidate from ConsensuSV-ONT into a fixed 50x50x3 image by extracting quality-passing long-read alignments around the variant and resizing the read-by-position matrix, so the CNN filter can score high-quality variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need per-variant read counts or genotype confidence scores rather than spatial alignment-feature images for CNN filtering Input reads are short-read (Illumina) alignments, since this encoding is built around long-read ONT alignments and split reads You lack the alignment BAM and only hold VCF summaries — the encoding requires per-read, per-position alignment features

skills.description: Use when reproducing or re-implementing dysgu's SV clustering: you have per-read SV signatures from split/discordant/supplementary alignments plus soft-clipped sequences and need to build a signature graph and quotient-graph partitions.
skills.name: structural-variant-signature-graph-construction
skills.search_text: structural-variant-signature-graph-construction Use when reproducing or re-implementing dysgu's SV clustering: you have per-read SV signatures from split/discordant/supplementary alignments plus soft-clipped sequences and need to build a signature graph and quotient-graph partitions. Input is a finalized VCF of SV calls rather than per-read signature data — downstream filtering (e.g. model probability >= 0.5 PacBio / >= 0.35 ONT) applies instead The analysis requires de novo assembly to resolve multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences in PE data, which the signature graph does not address Pairwise sequence alignment of soft-clip sequences is explicitly required; dysgu's design goal is to avoid it via minimizer sketches http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs dysgu's graph-based SV clustering stage: candidate read alignments are converted into enumerated SV-signature nodes ('discordant', 'split', 'deletion', 'insertion', 'breakend'), linked with black edges under reciprocal-overlap and span-position-distance thresholds, and unlinked soft-clipped reads are clustered via a unique-set minimizer sketch instead of pairwise alignment. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Reconstructs dysgu's graph-based SV clustering stage: candidate read alignments are converted into enumerated SV-signature nodes ('discordant', 'split', 'deletion', 'insertion', 'breakend'), linked with black edges under reciprocal-overlap and span-position-distance thresholds, and unlinked soft-clipped reads are clustered via a unique-set minimizer sketch instead of pairwise alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a finalized VCF of SV calls rather than per-read signature data — downstream filtering (e.g. model probability >= 0.5 PacBio / >= 0.35 ONT) applies instead The analysis requires de novo assembly to resolve multi-allelic sites or full-length insertion sequences in PE data, which the signature graph does not address Pairwise sequence alignment of soft-clip sequences is explicitly required; dysgu's design goal is to avoid it via minimizer sketches

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real sequencing data (e.g. GIAB HG002 PacBio reads) where mapper accuracy should be measured against experimentally implanted or curated truth sets rather than simulated reads You need to evaluate mapper alignment speed or base-level mapping quality rather than downstream SV-calling accuracy against known ground truth The question concerns SV types other than inversions and indels (e.g. duplications, translocations) that the described simulateSV setup does not cover

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a deletion SV caller needs known-truth simulated long-read data across homozygous/heterozygous groups and multiple coverage depths, requiring SURVIVOR parameter files plus PaSS PacBio read simulation and NGMLR alignment.
skills.name: structural-variant-simulation-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: structural-variant-simulation-parameter-configuration Use when benchmarking a deletion SV caller needs known-truth simulated long-read data across homozygous/heterozygous groups and multiple coverage depths, requiring SURVIVOR parameter files plus PaSS PacBio read simulation and NGMLR alignment. The goal is real-sample validation rather than a controlled truth-set benchmark — the article's real data (GIAB Ashkenazim Trio HG002/HG003/HG004, NIST RM 8392, Arabidopsis thaliana F1 hybrid) do not require simulated parameter files The SV caller under test must handle insertions or base substitutions — the article's simulation setup covers deletion variants only Only a single coverage depth or a single zygosity condition is needed, in which case the 4-depth x 2-group factorial simulation design is over-specified http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Configure and run a long-read structural-variant simulation benchmark for deletion calling: generate SURVIVOR simulation parameter files specifying homozygous/heterozygous deletion lengths (50-1000 bp and 1000-5000 bp), simulate PacBio SMRT reads with PaSS at four coverage depths (90x, 65x, 45x, 20x), and align them with NGMLR to produce BAM inputs for benchmarking DASV against cuteSV, SVIM, Sniffles and PBSV. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: Configure and run a long-read structural-variant simulation benchmark for deletion calling: generate SURVIVOR simulation parameter files specifying homozygous/heterozygous deletion lengths (50-1000 bp and 1000-5000 bp), simulate PacBio SMRT reads with PaSS at four coverage depths (90x, 65x, 45x, 20x), and align them with NGMLR to produce BAM inputs for benchmarking DASV against cuteSV, SVIM, Sniffles and PBSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is real-sample validation rather than a controlled truth-set benchmark — the article's real data (GIAB Ashkenazim Trio HG002/HG003/HG004, NIST RM 8392, Arabidopsis thaliana F1 hybrid) do not require simulated parameter files The SV caller under test must handle insertions or base substitutions — the article's simulation setup covers deletion variants only Only a single coverage depth or a single zygosity condition is needed, in which case the 4-depth x 2-group factorial simulation design is over-specified

skills.description: Use when Truvari bench/refine ga4gh VCFs from a long-read SV caller comparison are available and you need to know whether a caller's F1 advantage holds within specific SV length bins, not just genome-wide.
skills.name: structural-variant-size-stratification
skills.search_text: structural-variant-size-stratification Use when Truvari bench/refine ga4gh VCFs from a long-read SV caller comparison are available and you need to know whether a caller's F1 advantage holds within specific SV length bins, not just genome-wide. Input is a raw caller VCF rather than Truvari ga4gh-annotated truth/query VCFs with TP/FP/FN decision annotations — no per-stratum F1 can be computed without benchmark decisions The goal is a genome-wide (aggregate) accuracy comparison only; stratification is unnecessary and adds size-binning bookkeeping The comparison uses a benchmark engine other than the paper's bench/refine consolidation (e.g. hap-eval), whose match semantics differ from Truvari 4.2.2 decisions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark SV caller accuracy as a function of variant size by binning Truvari-benchmarked TP, FP, and FN calls into 50-499 bp, 500-4999 bp, and >=5000 bp strata and computing per-stratum precision, recall, and F1 to reveal whether a caller (e.g. sawfish) leads across all size groups rather than only in aggregate. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Benchmark SV caller accuracy as a function of variant size by binning Truvari-benchmarked TP, FP, and FN calls into 50-499 bp, 500-4999 bp, and >=5000 bp strata and computing per-stratum precision, recall, and F1 to reveal whether a caller (e.g. sawfish) leads across all size groups rather than only in aggregate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw caller VCF rather than Truvari ga4gh-annotated truth/query VCFs with TP/FP/FN decision annotations — no per-stratum F1 can be computed without benchmark decisions The goal is a genome-wide (aggregate) accuracy comparison only; stratification is unnecessary and adds size-binning bookkeeping The comparison uses a benchmark engine other than the paper's bench/refine consolidation (e.g. hap-eval), whose match semantics differ from Truvari 4.2.2 decisions

skills.description: Use when you have merged SV or TE insertion VCF callsets and a curated truth set, and need precision/recall trade-off numbers to compare caller combinations or filtering criteria (strict vs lax).
skills.name: structural-variant-truth-set-benchmarking
skills.search_text: structural-variant-truth-set-benchmarking Use when you have merged SV or TE insertion VCF callsets and a curated truth set, and need precision/recall trade-off numbers to compare caller combinations or filtering criteria (strict vs lax). No curated truth set exists for the samples/variant classes under study — precision and recall cannot be computed meaningfully Callsets are raw single-caller outputs that have not been merged and filtered by the read-evidence threshold, making the strict/lax comparison ill-defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmarks structural-variant/TE insertion callsets against a curated truth set (e.g. the HGSVC 5,630-insertion TE set) using SURVIVOR with a 100 bp distance margin to compute precision, recall, and F1 for comparing filtering criteria. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks structural-variant/TE insertion callsets against a curated truth set (e.g. the HGSVC 5,630-insertion TE set) using SURVIVOR with a 100 bp distance margin to compute precision, recall, and F1 for comparing filtering criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No curated truth set exists for the samples/variant classes under study — precision and recall cannot be computed meaningfully Callsets are raw single-caller outputs that have not been merged and filtered by the read-evidence threshold, making the strict/lax comparison ill-defined

skills.description: Use when a reproduced nanopore variant-calling pipeline (VCFs from Sniffles/CuteSV/SVIM/NanoVar on minimap2/NGMLR/lra alignments) must be benchmarked against a published gold-standard SV set, split by SV type and size.
skills.name: structural-variant-truth-set-recall-analysis
skills.search_text: structural-variant-truth-set-recall-analysis Use when a reproduced nanopore variant-calling pipeline (VCFs from Sniffles/CuteSV/SVIM/NanoVar on minimap2/NGMLR/lra alignments) must be benchmarked against a published gold-standard SV set, split by SV type and size. The SVs of interest are not deletions or duplications — disCoverage can only check DEL/DUP, so coverage-support against a truth set cannot be applied to other SV types No established truth set or external reference variant set exists for the sample, so recall cannot be computed and only internal filtering (e.g., aCGH comparison in patients) is possible A standalone variant caller is needed — disCoverage is not a variant caller and requires putative SV positions supplied as input http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies how much of an external SV/CNV truth set (e.g., the Chaisson et al. 2019 high-confidence set for NA19240) is recovered by a nanopore SV-calling pipeline, using disCoverage coverage-support checks and per-aligner, per-SV-type recall metrics. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Quantifies how much of an external SV/CNV truth set (e.g., the Chaisson et al. 2019 high-confidence set for NA19240) is recovered by a nanopore SV-calling pipeline, using disCoverage coverage-support checks and per-aligner, per-SV-type recall metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SVs of interest are not deletions or duplications — disCoverage can only check DEL/DUP, so coverage-support against a truth set cannot be applied to other SV types No established truth set or external reference variant set exists for the sample, so recall cannot be computed and only internal filtering (e.g., aCGH comparison in patients) is possible A standalone variant caller is needed — disCoverage is not a variant caller and requires putative SV positions supplied as input

skills.description: Use when multiple per-caller structural variant VCFs exist for the same ONT sample and a single non-overlapping consensus SV candidate set is needed before consensus filtering.
skills.name: structural-variant-vcf-merging
skills.search_text: structural-variant-vcf-merging Use when multiple per-caller structural variant VCFs exist for the same ONT sample and a single non-overlapping consensus SV candidate set is needed before consensus filtering. When only a single caller's VCF is available — there is nothing to merge and collapse across callers. When the goal is final high-quality variant selection — that is handled by the downstream convolutional neural network filtering step, not by Truvari merge/collapse. For short-read (Illumina) variant consensus; ConsensuSV-ONT targets Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing data. Consolidates the VCF callsets produced by the six independent long-read SV callers into one non-redundant candidate set, using the Truvari merge module to combine records and the Truvari collapse module to remove overlapping variants inside the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow/Docker pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Consolidates the VCF callsets produced by the six independent long-read SV callers into one non-redundant candidate set, using the Truvari merge module to combine records and the Truvari collapse module to remove overlapping variants inside the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow/Docker pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single caller's VCF is available — there is nothing to merge and collapse across callers. When the goal is final high-quality variant selection — that is handled by the downstream convolutional neural network filtering step, not by Truvari merge/collapse. For short-read (Illumina) variant consensus; ConsensuSV-ONT targets Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing data.

skills.description: Use when you have a long-read SV caller's VCF (e.g., VolcanoSV VCF from Zenodo test data) and need to inspect, filter, or re-type records — specifically to recover DUP calls hidden among INS records.

skills.search_text: structural-variant-vcf-parsing Use when you have a long-read SV caller's VCF (e.g., VolcanoSV VCF from Zenodo test data) and need to inspect, filter, or re-type records — specifically to recover DUP calls hidden among INS records. The input callset already contains DUP calls that match the ground truth — no INS-to-DUP recovery is needed Sex chromosomes (chrX/chrY) are in scope: VolcanoSV is designed only for autosomes because its phasing differs for sex chromosomes The analysis is a plain Truvari benchmark of an existing callset rather than recovery of mislabeled insertion calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A method-level procedure for parsing long-read SV callset VCFs (e.g., VolcanoSV output on hg19), extracting INS inserted sequences, realigning them to the reference, and post-hoc relabeling self-aligning insertions as DUP calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0

skills.description: Use when you have a reactivity profile (e.g. nanoSHAPE or SHAPE-MaP) plus the same RNA folded without probing data, and need to quantify constrained-structure accuracy by base-pair set comparison (PPV/sensitivity) against the NPD reference.
skills.name: structure-accuracy-ppv-sensitivity-evaluation
skills.search_text: structure-accuracy-ppv-sensitivity-evaluation Use when you have a reactivity profile (e.g. nanoSHAPE or SHAPE-MaP) plus the same RNA folded without probing data, and need to quantify constrained-structure accuracy by base-pair set comparison (PPV/sensitivity) against the NPD reference. The goal is modification detection/localization from nanopore signal rather than judging secondary structure prediction accuracy — use tombo detect_modifications instead of base-pair set comparison. There is no reactivity profile available and no NPD reference fold, so neither constrained-vs-NPD comparison nor PPV/sensitivity can be computed. The reactivity profile has poor resolution (e.g. the 5' ends of long RNAs), so converting it to pseudo-free-energy constraints would mislead the fold rather than refine it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmark for judging whether probing-data-constrained RNA secondary structure predictions (nanoSHAPE, SHAPE-MaP) outperform unconstrained no-probing-data (NPD) folds, using positive predictive value (PPV), sensitivity, and recovery of known miRNA hairpins in pri-miR-17~92. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100097
skills.summary: Benchmark for judging whether probing-data-constrained RNA secondary structure predictions (nanoSHAPE, SHAPE-MaP) outperform unconstrained no-probing-data (NPD) folds, using positive predictive value (PPV), sensitivity, and recovery of known miRNA hairpins in pri-miR-17~92.
