There is no reactivity profile available and no NPD reference fold, so neither constrained-vs-NPD comparison nor PPV/sensitivity can be computed. The reactivity profile has poor resolution (e.g. the 5' ends of long RNAs), so converting it to pseudo-free-energy constraints would mislead the fold rather than refine it.

skills.description: Use when read-level metadata and nested key-value structures from a POD5 (nanopore) file must be flattened and persisted as JSON per read ID, e.g. for programmatic downstream use.
skills.name: structured-export
skills.search_text: structured-export Use when read-level metadata and nested key-value structures from a POD5 (nanopore) file must be flattened and persisted as JSON per read ID, e.g. for programmatic downstream use. You only need the raw current measurements of a read — use pod5Viewer's `Export signal` menu to write a .npy Numpy file or a plain text file (one measurement per line) instead. You want to visualize or plot signal data rather than capture metadata — use `View > Plot signal...` / `View > Plot pA signal...`. The metadata is already available as flat, machine-readable key-value JSON for the target reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Exports all attributes stored for a POD5 read — including nested groups such as context and run-info structures — into one JSON file per read, mirroring pod5Viewer's `File > Export all info` behaviour. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae665
skills.summary: Exports all attributes stored for a POD5 read — including nested groups such as context and run-info structures — into one JSON file per read, mirroring pod5Viewer's `File > Export all info` behaviour.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the raw current measurements of a read — use pod5Viewer's `Export signal` menu to write a .npy Numpy file or a plain text file (one measurement per line) instead. You want to visualize or plot signal data rather than capture metadata — use `View > Plot signal...` / `View > Plot pA signal...`. The metadata is already available as flat, machine-readable key-value JSON for the target reads.

skills.description: Use when per-read poly(A) tail lengths are already assigned to transcript isoforms (APA or splice isoforms) and you need to test, gene by gene, whether two or more isoforms have significantly different tail-length distributions.
skills.name: students-t-test-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: students-t-test-hypothesis-testing Use when per-read poly(A) tail lengths are already assigned to transcript isoforms (APA or splice isoforms) and you need to test, gene by gene, whether two or more isoforms have significantly different tail-length distributions. Input is raw PacBio subreads or untrimmed CCS reads — tail lengths must first be computed with the PAIso-seq pipeline (ccs, trim.py, run.pl, minimap2) Comparing tail lengths between different genes or between biological conditions rather than between isoforms of the same gene Tail-length data violate the QC criteria (pass number <10, tails <15 nt, >=20 non-A residues) — the published comparison was made only on reads passing these filters http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Student's t-tests in R to compare per-isoform poly(A) tail-length distributions (e.g. Ccnb1 APA1/APA2/APA3, Wee2 APA isoforms, Tcl1 splice isoforms) from PAIso-seq per-read tail measurements in mouse GV oocytes, testing whether isoforms of the same gene carry different tails. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Apply Student's t-tests in R to compare per-isoform poly(A) tail-length distributions (e.g. Ccnb1 APA1/APA2/APA3, Wee2 APA isoforms, Tcl1 splice isoforms) from PAIso-seq per-read tail measurements in mouse GV oocytes, testing whether isoforms of the same gene carry different tails.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw PacBio subreads or untrimmed CCS reads — tail lengths must first be computed with the PAIso-seq pipeline (ccs, trim.py, run.pl, minimap2) Comparing tail lengths between different genes or between biological conditions rather than between isoforms of the same gene Tail-length data violate the QC criteria (pass number <10, tails <15 nt, >=20 non-A residues) — the published comparison was made only on reads passing these filters

skills.search_text: subcellular-fraction-read-annotation Use when native RNA Nanopore reads from subcellular fractions need gene assignment and mature vs premature classification (e.g., inputs are BAM alignments plus a matching GTF) before quantifying fraction-specific transcript populations. skills.search_text: subtelomeric-anchor-sequence-alignment Use when consensus subtelomeric anchor clusters (sample.telomap.anchors.tsv from telomap) need to be assigned to specific T2T-CHM13 chromosome ends for chromosome-end-specific telomere length or TVS analyses. skills.summary: Maps telomap's consensus subtelomeric anchor sequences to chromosome ends using the T2T-CHM13 human genome assembly, enabling chromosome-end-specific (e.g., Chr. 7q) telomere analyses per sample.

skills.description: Use when telomeric reads from telomap must be assigned to specific chromosome ends so per-end analyses such as TVS signature plots can be built, by clustering their 5' subtelomeric segments into anchor groups.
skills.name: subtelomeric-segment-clustering
skills.search_text: subtelomeric-segment-clustering Use when telomeric reads from telomap must be assigned to specific chromosome ends so per-end analyses such as TVS signature plots can be built, by clustering their 5' subtelomeric segments into anchor groups. The subtelomeric region extracted from the HiFi read is too short (e.g. after aggressive RsaI/HinfI trimming) for unambiguous identification of specific chromosome ends against T2T-CHM13. Input is raw WGS or telobait reads that have not yet passed telomap's telomere-identification step — the clustering step requires telomeric reads, not raw long reads. The goal is measuring telomere length of ALT cells, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi read length and are incompatible with this workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Clusters the non-telomeric 5' subtelomeric segments of telomeric long reads (from telomap) to group reads by chromosome end, building a 100 bp per-cluster consensus anchor that supports chromosome-end mapping and per-end TVS signature plots. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Clusters the non-telomeric 5' subtelomeric segments of telomeric long reads (from telomap) to group reads by chromosome end, building a 100 bp per-cluster consensus anchor that supports chromosome-end mapping and per-end TVS signature plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The subtelomeric region extracted from the HiFi read is too short (e.g. after aggressive RsaI/HinfI trimming) for unambiguous identification of specific chromosome ends against T2T-CHM13. Input is raw WGS or telobait reads that have not yet passed telomap's telomere-identification step — the clustering step requires telomeric reads, not raw long reads. The goal is measuring telomere length of ALT cells, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi read length and are incompatible with this workflow.

skills.description: Use when you need to extract all maximal exact matches (MEMs) shared across multiple ultra-long nucleotide sequences, e.g. to seed segmentation for an MSA pipeline on sequences reaching billions of bases.
skills.name: suffix-array-construction-gsacak
skills.search_text: suffix-array-construction-gsacak Use when you need to extract all maximal exact matches (MEMs) shared across multiple ultra-long nucleotide sequences, e.g. to seed segmentation for an MSA pipeline on sequences reaching billions of bases. Input is a protein alignment or non-nucleotide sequence data — FMAlign2 Step 1 is designed for nucleotide sequences Sequences share only very short common substrings — MEMs shorter than the -l threshold (default 30) are discarded; the README advises lowering -l if too few MEMs are found, but if none exist above any reasonable threshold the MEM-finding module yields nothing useful You need global chains of common seeds rather than partial-chain MEM segmentation — that is FMAlign's approach, which FMAlign2 explicitly redefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstructs the MEMs-finding module of FMAlign2 Step 1 by concatenating input nucleotide sequences with unique separators, building the suffix and LCP arrays with the linear-time gSACA-K algorithm, and traversing LCP intervals to emit maximal exact matches of length at least lmin (default 30). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae014
skills.summary: Reconstructs the MEMs-finding module of FMAlign2 Step 1 by concatenating input nucleotide sequences with unique separators, building the suffix and LCP arrays with the linear-time gSACA-K algorithm, and traversing LCP intervals to emit maximal exact matches of length at least lmin (default 30).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a protein alignment or non-nucleotide sequence data — FMAlign2 Step 1 is designed for nucleotide sequences Sequences share only very short common substrings — MEMs shorter than the -l threshold (default 30) are discarded; the README advises lowering -l if too few MEMs are found, but if none exist above any reasonable threshold the MEM-finding module yields nothing useful You need global chains of common seeds rather than partial-chain MEM segmentation — that is FMAlign's approach, which FMAlign2 explicitly redefined

skills.description: Use when an MSA output FASTA from FMAlign2 or its backends must be quality-checked or compared across methods (e.g., Y-chromosome truncation or mtDB 20x/50x/100x benchmarks) via an SP score.
skills.name: sum-of-pairs-alignment-scoring
skills.search_text: sum-of-pairs-alignment-scoring Use when an MSA output FASTA from FMAlign2 or its backends must be quality-checked or compared across methods (e.g., Y-chromosome truncation or mtDB 20x/50x/100x benchmarks) via an SP score. The alignment file is not a valid FASTA MSA (e.g., raw unaligned input.fasta) — sp.py expects aligned sequences of equal length. A different scoring scheme is required by the study design; the documented scheme (match 0, mismatch 1, gap1 2, gap2 2) must be kept fixed for cross-method comparability. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Score multiple nucleotide sequence alignments produced by FMAlign2 (or its MAFFT/Clustal Omega/HAlign3/HAlign4 backends) using the sp.py script, which computes the Sum-of-Pairs (SP) score under a match 0 / mismatch 1 / gap1 2 / gap2 2 scheme to verify alignment quality in benchmark comparisons. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae014
skills.summary: Score multiple nucleotide sequence alignments produced by FMAlign2 (or its MAFFT/Clustal Omega/HAlign3/HAlign4 backends) using the sp.py script, which computes the Sum-of-Pairs (SP) score under a match 0 / mismatch 1 / gap1 2 / gap2 2 scheme to verify alignment quality in benchmark comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The alignment file is not a valid FASTA MSA (e.g., raw unaligned input.fasta) — sp.py expects aligned sequences of equal length. A different scoring scheme is required by the study design; the documented scheme (match 0, mismatch 1, gap1 2, gap2 2) must be kept fixed for cross-method comparability.

skills.description: Use when you have IV–exposure associations (bx, bxse) and IV–outcome associations (by, byse) from GWAS summary data — e.g., a simmrd generate_summary() replicate — and need causal effect estimates from one or more summary-level MR estimators.
skills.name: summary-level-mr-estimation
skills.search_text: summary-level-mr-estimation Use when you have IV–exposure associations (bx, bxse) and IV–outcome associations (by, byse) from GWAS summary data — e.g., a simmrd generate_summary() replicate — and need causal effect estimates from one or more summary-level MR estimators. You only have individual-level genotype/phenotype data (from generate_individual()) and want two-sample summary MR — construct summary statistics first or use individual-level MR methods instead You need to simulate or generate the GWAS summary data itself — that is the role of simmrd's set_params()/generate_summary(), not of the MR estimation step You require estimators (e.g., LD-aware or robust variance methods) not implemented in the MendelianRandomization package http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Fit competing summary-data Mendelian Randomization estimators (e.g., IVW, MR-Egger) with the MendelianRandomization R package on GWAS summary statistics (bx, bxse, by, byse) generated by simmrd's generate_summary(), and compare the estimated causal effects against the true effects (theta). genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Fit competing summary-data Mendelian Randomization estimators (e.g., IVW, MR-Egger) with the MendelianRandomization R package on GWAS summary statistics (bx, bxse, by, byse) generated by simmrd's generate_summary(), and compare the estimated causal effects against the true effects (theta).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have individual-level genotype/phenotype data (from generate_individual()) and want two-sample summary MR — construct summary statistics first or use individual-level MR methods instead You need to simulate or generate the GWAS summary data itself — that is the role of simmrd's set_params()/generate_summary(), not of the MR estimation step You require estimators (e.g., LD-aware or robust variance methods) not implemented in the MendelianRandomization package

skills.description: Use when an article claim (e.g. 'the 192-sample Nallo run completed in 34 hours') is backed by a deposited supplementary file, and the claim must be independently verified from the file's raw contents.
skills.name: supplementary-file-retrieval
skills.search_text: supplementary-file-retrieval Use when an article claim (e.g. 'the 192-sample Nallo run completed in 34 hours') is backed by a deposited supplementary file, and the claim must be independently verified from the file's raw contents. No supplementary workflow report or execution trace is deposited alongside the article, so the claim cannot be independently parsed. The question concerns biological/variant-call outputs of the pipeline rather than execution resource-use metrics. The run reported is single-sample or small-scale rather than the multi-node (68-node) cohort execution the trace aggregation assumes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Retrieve and parse a supplementary file (here, the Nextflow workflow report deposited as data File 1 in Bioinformatics online) to extract quantitative evidence — e.g. total wall-clock run duration — that corroborates a claim made in the article text. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag086
skills.summary: Retrieve and parse a supplementary file (here, the Nextflow workflow report deposited as data File 1 in Bioinformatics online) to extract quantitative evidence — e.g. total wall-clock run duration — that corroborates a claim made in the article text.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No supplementary workflow report or execution trace is deposited alongside the article, so the claim cannot be independently parsed. The question concerns biological/variant-call outputs of the pipeline rather than execution resource-use metrics. The run reported is single-sample or small-scale rather than the multi-node (68-node) cohort execution the trace aggregation assumes.

skills.description: Use when a computed call set (e.g. invMap inversion calls on the NA12878 dataset) must be labeled as ground-truth vs non-ground-truth using the paper's supplementary tables/figures, or when published summary statistics must be reproduced.
skills.name: supplementary-table-cross-referencing
skills.search_text: supplementary-table-cross-referencing Use when a computed call set (e.g. invMap inversion calls on the NA12878 dataset) must be labeled as ground-truth vs non-ground-truth using the paper's supplementary tables/figures, or when published summary statistics must be reproduced. The variant calls are already labeled against ground truth, so supplementary cross-referencing would duplicate existing annotations. The analysis targets structural-variant types (e.g. deletions, duplications) not covered by the paper's supplementary inversion tables S5 and Figures S3-S4. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Cross-references predicted variant/alignment calls against the paper's supplementary tables and figures to label each call as ground-truth-matching or novel, and to recover published summary statistics (e.g. mean identity of non-ground-truth invMap-only inversion calls, 81.95%). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Cross-references predicted variant/alignment calls against the paper's supplementary tables and figures to label each call as ground-truth-matching or novel, and to recover published summary statistics (e.g. mean identity of non-ground-truth invMap-only inversion calls, 81.95%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant calls are already labeled against ground truth, so supplementary cross-referencing would duplicate existing annotations. The analysis targets structural-variant types (e.g. deletions, duplications) not covered by the paper's supplementary inversion tables S5 and Figures S3-S4.

skills.description: Use when predicting ΔΨ caused by genetic variants from a VCF with wild-type Ψ available, and when you need to train or reproduce an SVR model on vex-seq-style splicing features (TR957/TS1098) and report Pearson correlation coefficients.
skills.name: support-vector-regression-model-training
skills.search_text: support-vector-regression-model-training Use when predicting ΔΨ caused by genetic variants from a VCF with wild-type Ψ available, and when you need to train or reproduce an SVR model on vex-seq-style splicing features (TR957/TS1098) and report Pearson correlation coefficients. Wild-type Ψ of the exons is not available — use the PredPSI-SVR-noPSI variant (./main.sh without '-p'), which trades about 0.1 PCC for independence from experimental Ψ Variants lie in intergenic regions or more than 200 bp from splice sites — the pipeline's ANNOVAR-based filter removes them, so an SVR prediction will not be returned for those variants You need branch-point sequence or effective pre-mRNA secondary-structure features, or tissue-specific Ψ prediction — PredPSI-SVR omits these due to the small sample size http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Train an ε-SVR (LIBSVM, RBF kernel) to predict variant-induced ΔΨ using 42 splicing-related features extracted from the exon and flanking regions of the CAGI-5 vex-seq TR957 training set, with grid-searched C/γ under 10-fold cross-validation and greedy forward feature selection that peaks at 8 features (PCC 0.570). genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Train an ε-SVR (LIBSVM, RBF kernel) to predict variant-induced ΔΨ using 42 splicing-related features extracted from the exon and flanking regions of the CAGI-5 vex-seq TR957 training set, with grid-searched C/γ under 10-fold cross-validation and greedy forward feature selection that peaks at 8 features (PCC 0.570).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Wild-type Ψ of the exons is not available — use the PredPSI-SVR-noPSI variant (./main.sh without '-p'), which trades about 0.1 PCC for independence from experimental Ψ Variants lie in intergenic regions or more than 200 bp from splice sites — the pipeline's ANNOVAR-based filter removes them, so an SVR prediction will not be returned for those variants You need branch-point sequence or effective pre-mRNA secondary-structure features, or tissue-specific Ψ prediction — PredPSI-SVR omits these due to the small sample size

skills.description: Use when annotating and quantifying full-length complex isoforms at surface receptor gene loci from R2C2 ONT single-cell RNAseq, e.g. checking whether CD19, CD20 (Ms4a1), IGH, Ptprc, CD2, CD79b or CD37 express multiple isoforms across cells.
skills.name: surface-receptor-isoform-annotation
skills.search_text: surface-receptor-isoform-annotation Use when annotating and quantifying full-length complex isoforms at surface receptor gene loci from R2C2 ONT single-cell RNAseq, e.g. checking whether CD19, CD20 (Ms4a1), IGH, Ptprc, CD2, CD79b or CD37 express multiple isoforms across cells. Input is regular (non-R2C2) ONT reads — the Mandalorion README states it is 'not tested for use with regular ONT reads. I recommend using FLAIR instead for those.' Input is short-read Illumina data — the paper's Trinity comparison (task_008) shows short-read assembly largely failed to reproduce ONT-identified CD37 isoforms Target transcripts are under 500 bp, which were not captured due to stringent size selection during library preparation and the -I 500 isoform length filter http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Identifies and quantifies full-length complex isoforms (alternative TSS/TES plus alternative splice sites) at B cell surface receptor loci by running the Mandalorion pipeline on R2C2 ONT reads from individual murine B1a cells, then testing differential isoform usage across cells. This reproduces the paper's finding that loci such as CD19, Ms4a1 (CD20), IGH, Ptprc (CD45), CD2, CD79b and CD37 express multiple complex isoforms. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms16027
skills.summary: Identifies and quantifies full-length complex isoforms (alternative TSS/TES plus alternative splice sites) at B cell surface receptor loci by running the Mandalorion pipeline on R2C2 ONT reads from individual murine B1a cells, then testing differential isoform usage across cells. This reproduces the paper's finding that loci such as CD19, Ms4a1 (CD20), IGH, Ptprc (CD45), CD2, CD79b and CD37 express multiple complex isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is regular (non-R2C2) ONT reads — the Mandalorion README states it is 'not tested for use with regular ONT reads. I recommend using FLAIR instead for those.' Input is short-read Illumina data — the paper's Trinity comparison (task_008) shows short-read assembly largely failed to reproduce ONT-identified CD37 isoforms Target transcripts are under 500 bp, which were not captured due to stringent size selection during library preparation and the -I 500 isoform length filter

skills.description: Use when a per-sample binary mutation status (e.g. TP53 R248Q from a MAF) must be combined with survival group annotations (e.g. G2/G4) into one covariate table for multivariate Cox regression of prognosis.
skills.name: survival-covariate-table-construction
skills.search_text: survival-covariate-table-construction Use when a per-sample binary mutation status (e.g. TP53 R248Q from a MAF) must be combined with survival group annotations (e.g. G2/G4) into one covariate table for multivariate Cox regression of prognosis. When only aggregate gene-by-signature association statistics (samFisherSigs/samPerMutSigs outputs with Mutfreq=0.04, threshold=0.06, Qvalue=0.1) are needed rather than per-sample prognostic modeling When no survival/group annotation exists for the samples, since the Cox covariates require the Groupfile labels When the question is de novo mutational signature extraction (denovoNMF) rather than testing a specific mutation's prognostic independence Constructs a per-sample covariate table that merges a gene hotspot mutation indicator (e.g. TP53 R248Q extracted from an RNMF MAF file keyed on Tumor_Sample_Barcode/Hugo_Symbol) with survival group labels from a Groupfile, so a multivariate Cox proportional hazards model can test whether the mutation is an independent prognosticator. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Constructs a per-sample covariate table that merges a gene hotspot mutation indicator (e.g. TP53 R248Q extracted from an RNMF MAF file keyed on Tumor_Sample_Barcode/Hugo_Symbol) with survival group labels from a Groupfile, so a multivariate Cox proportional hazards model can test whether the mutation is an independent prognosticator.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only aggregate gene-by-signature association statistics (samFisherSigs/samPerMutSigs outputs with Mutfreq=0.04, threshold=0.06, Qvalue=0.1) are needed rather than per-sample prognostic modeling When no survival/group annotation exists for the samples, since the Cox covariates require the Groupfile labels When the question is de novo mutational signature extraction (denovoNMF) rather than testing a specific mutation's prognostic independence

skills.search_text: survival-outcome-image-classification Use when non-image tabular data (gene-by-signature CCA matrices from RNMF) must be converted to N x N images and a deep CNN should be evaluated for binary survival-outcome discrimination. When the goal is de novo extraction of mutational signatures from raw mutation data rather than survival prediction from precomputed CCA matrices (use denovoNMF instead). When clinical information such as treatment methods, medication, or follow-up time is required for a robust prognostic model — the article notes such information was incomplete and the cohort relatively small for model learning. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Trains a DenseNet-121 convolutional classifier (PyTorch) on gene cumulative contribution abundance (CCA) matrix images rendered at 500x500 pixels to preliminarily discriminate shortened (G4) versus longer (G2) survival outcome in ESCC. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Trains a DenseNet-121 convolutional classifier (PyTorch) on gene cumulative contribution abundance (CCA) matrix images rendered at 500x500 pixels to preliminarily discriminate shortened (G4) versus longer (G2) survival outcome in ESCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo extraction of mutational signatures from raw mutation data rather than survival prediction from precomputed CCA matrices (use denovoNMF instead). skills.search_text: sv-benchmark-evaluation-with-truvari Use when query VCFs from SV callers must be assessed against GIAB benchmark SV sets (T2T-HG002-Q100 stvar or CMRG v1.00) to produce per-caller TP/FP/FN, precision, recall, and F1 metrics. Benchmarking small variants or SNVs — truvari bench targets structural variants and will not score SNV/small-indel accuracy Comparing two caller VCFs directly without a GIAB truth set and confident-region BED — bench requires a benchmark VCF and --includebed to restrict assessment Assessing calls that include non-PASS records when using --passonly, since these are excluded from scoring by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Benchmark long-read SV caller output (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) against GIAB truth sets using truvari 4.2.2 bench (and bench+refine with MAFFT for the T2T set), computing precision, recall, and F1 for caller comparison. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136

skills.search_text: sv-breakpoint-gene-annotation Use when nanopore reads from targeted fusion-gene enrichment need fusion partner and breakpoint identification, i.e. mapping long reads to GRCh37, calling SVs, and annotating SV breakpoints with genes to nominate fusions. skills.search_text: sv-call-accuracy-evaluation-against-truth-set Use when you need to quantify how accurately different long-read mappers detect implanted or known inversions by calling SVs from each mapper's alignments and comparing them to a truth VCF. No truth set exists (e.g. purely exploratory real-data SV discovery, as in the NA12878 candidate-variant-calling analysis rather than accuracy benchmarking) The question is short-read variant calling or SNV/indel accuracy — this skill is specific to long-read inversion structural variant detection Evaluating a single mapper with no baselines — the skill's value is the cross-mapper accuracy comparison on identical inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark long-read mapper accuracy for inversion detection by comparing mapper-specific SV calls against a SURVIVOR-implanted inversion truth set, as done for invMap vs. minimap2, NGMLR, Winnowmap2, and lra on the GIAB HG002 PacBio real-read benchmark. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read mapper accuracy for inversion detection by comparing mapper-specific SV calls against a SURVIVOR-implanted inversion truth set, as done for invMap vs. minimap2, NGMLR, Winnowmap2, and lra on the GIAB HG002 PacBio real-read benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No truth set exists (e.g. purely exploratory real-data SV discovery, as in the NA12878 candidate-variant-calling analysis rather than accuracy benchmarking) The question is short-read variant calling or SNV/indel accuracy — this skill is specific to long-read inversion structural variant detection Evaluating a single mapper with no baselines — the skill's value is the cross-mapper accuracy comparison on identical inputs

skills.description: Use when evaluating deletion SV calling performance on third-generation sequencing data with a known truth set, or when reproducing precision/recall/F1 comparisons across multiple callers on HG002 GIAB samples.
skills.name: sv-call-benchmarking-against-nist-truth-set
skills.search_text: sv-call-benchmarking-against-nist-truth-set Use when evaluating deletion SV calling performance on third-generation sequencing data with a known truth set, or when reproducing precision/recall/F1 comparisons across multiple callers on HG002 GIAB samples. The goal is insertion or base substitution calling — the article states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling'. No truth set (e.g. NIST RM 8392) is available, so precision/recall/F1 cannot be computed against a benchmark. Input data are short-read (Illumina-style NGS) rather than third-generation long reads, which the evaluated callers were designed for. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark structural-variant deletion callers (DASV, cuteSV, SVIM, Sniffles, PBSV) on real GIAB HG002 long-read data by comparing each tool's deletion calls against the NIST Reference Material 8392 benchmark and computing precision, recall and F1 across coverage depths and CLR/CCS platforms. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae269
skills.summary: Benchmark structural-variant deletion callers (DASV, cuteSV, SVIM, Sniffles, PBSV) on real GIAB HG002 long-read data by comparing each tool's deletion calls against the NIST Reference Material 8392 benchmark and computing precision, recall and F1 across coverage depths and CLR/CCS platforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is insertion or base substitution calling — the article states 'This study currently focuses exclusively on experiments related to deletion variants calling'. No truth set (e.g. NIST RM 8392) is available, so precision/recall/F1 cannot be computed against a benchmark. Input data are short-read (Illumina-style NGS) rather than third-generation long reads, which the evaluated callers were designed for.

skills.description: Use when validating a somatic SV caller against published cell-line benchmarks (COLO829, H2009, HCC1954 tumor/control ONT pairs) and you need exact PASS call counts comparable to a reported result.
skills.name: sv-call-count-reproduction
skills.search_text: sv-call-count-reproduction Use when validating a somatic SV caller against published cell-line benchmarks (COLO829, H2009, HCC1954 tumor/control ONT pairs) and you need exact PASS call counts comparable to a reported result. Goal is detecting single breakend SVs or complex SVs where both breakpoints fall in poorly characterized repetitive regions (e.g. centromeres) — the canonical count only covers canonical SVs and the module cannot detect both-breakpoint-repeat events Detecting somatic VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion events — the reference-genome-based framework may not capture long repeat expansion events The caller under evaluation is a separate-detect-then-subtract design — the paper notes such approaches generate false positives like germline SVs passing threshold in tumor but narrowly missing it in the matched control http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Reproduce the canonical somatic SV call counts (49/724/748 for COLO829/H2009/HCC1954) reported by the nanomonsv paper by running the full tumor/control paired ONT detection pipeline, including the 39 single-breakend-rescued canonical SVs. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad526
skills.summary: Reproduce the canonical somatic SV call counts (49/724/748 for COLO829/H2009/HCC1954) reported by the nanomonsv paper by running the full tumor/control paired ONT detection pipeline, including the 39 single-breakend-rescued canonical SVs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is detecting single breakend SVs or complex SVs where both breakpoints fall in poorly characterized repetitive regions (e.g. centromeres) — the canonical count only covers canonical SVs and the module cannot detect both-breakpoint-repeat events Detecting somatic VNTR/microsatellite repeat expansion events — the reference-genome-based framework may not capture long repeat expansion events The caller under evaluation is a separate-detect-then-subtract design — the paper notes such approaches generate false positives like germline SVs passing threshold in tumor but narrowly missing it in the matched control

skills.description: Use when you have raw SV calls from ≥2 independent callers (e.g. VCFs from Delly, Lumpy, Pindel) on the same aligned BAMs and need a high-specificity consensus call set by requiring multi-caller support.
skills.name: sv-call-filtering-by-caller-support
skills.search_text: sv-call-filtering-by-caller-support Use when you have raw SV calls from ≥2 independent callers (e.g. VCFs from Delly, Lumpy, Pindel) on the same aligned BAMs and need a high-specificity consensus call set by requiring multi-caller support. Sensitivity matters more than specificity — the study explicitly focused on high specificity rather than detecting all SVs, so multi-caller consensus will drop real events seen by only one caller Calls cannot be converted to VCF with consistent coordinates and SV type annotations — SURVIVOR's merge operates on VCF-formatted SV calls SVs were called by a single algorithm only and no second caller can be run on the data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Consensus structural-variant calling by merging preliminary SV predictions from multiple callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel; cn.MOPs for CNVs) with SURVIVOR, retaining only SVs detected by at least two callers. In the S. pombe strain-panel study this reduced the initial prediction set to 315 preliminary variant calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Consensus structural-variant calling by merging preliminary SV predictions from multiple callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel; cn.MOPs for CNVs) with SURVIVOR, retaining only SVs detected by at least two callers. In the S. pombe strain-panel study this reduced the initial prediction set to 315 preliminary variant calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sensitivity matters more than specificity — the study explicitly focused on high specificity rather than detecting all SVs, so multi-caller consensus will drop real events seen by only one caller Calls cannot be converted to VCF with consistent coordinates and SV type annotations — SURVIVOR's merge operates on VCF-formatted SV calls SVs were called by a single algorithm only and no second caller can be run on the data

skills.description: Use when building per-caller SV candidate VCFs from ONT fastq.gz reads (e.g. HG00733, HG00514, NA19240) and preparing them for downstream consensus in ConsensuSV-ONT.
skills.name: sv-call-pre-filtering
skills.search_text: sv-call-pre-filtering Use when building per-caller SV candidate VCFs from ONT fastq.gz reads (e.g. HG00733, HG00514, NA19240) and preparing them for downstream consensus in ConsensuSV-ONT. Input is already a set of filtered or consensus SV VCFs rather than raw per-caller candidate calls from the six supported callers Reads are short-read (Illumina) or PacBio HiFi rather than ONT fastq.gz long reads, since the pipeline and its caller set are tuned for ONT data Generates and pre-filters per-caller structural variant candidate VCFs from ONT long-read alignments in the ConsensuSV-ONT pipeline, so that CuteSV, Sniffles, Dysgu, SVIM, PBSV and Nanovar raw calls are cleaned per caller before CNN-based consensus filtering. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Generates and pre-filters per-caller structural variant candidate VCFs from ONT long-read alignments in the ConsensuSV-ONT pipeline, so that CuteSV, Sniffles, Dysgu, SVIM, PBSV and Nanovar raw calls are cleaned per caller before CNN-based consensus filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of filtered or consensus SV VCFs rather than raw per-caller candidate calls from the six supported callers Reads are short-read (Illumina) or PacBio HiFi rather than ONT fastq.gz long reads, since the pipeline and its caller set are tuned for ONT data

skills.description: Use when finished SV call sets (VCF) from multiple callers must be scored for recall against curated breakpoint-junction truth sets, e.g. validated de novo chromothripsis junctions per patient.
skills.name: sv-call-set-intersection-against-validated-junctions
skills.search_text: sv-call-set-intersection-against-validated-junctions Use when finished SV call sets (VCF) from multiple callers must be scored for recall against curated breakpoint-junction truth sets, e.g. validated de novo chromothripsis junctions per patient. Inputs are raw nanopore reads or unaligned FASTQ/BAM rather than finished SV call sets — run basecalling, LAST mapping, and NanoSV calling first No validated breakpoint-junction truth set exists for the sample, so recall cannot be computed (e.g. genome-wide inherited SV surveillance without curated de novo junctions) The goal is precision or false-discovery estimation rather than recovery of known junctions, which this recall-only intersection does not measure http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Benchmarking step that intersects SV caller outputs (NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles on MinION nanopore data; Manta, Delly on matched Illumina data) with validated de novo chromothripsis breakpoint-junction truth sets to compute per-caller recall, quantifying the paper's claim that nanopore long reads outperform short reads for de novo rearrangement detection. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Benchmarking step that intersects SV caller outputs (NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles on MinION nanopore data; Manta, Delly on matched Illumina data) with validated de novo chromothripsis breakpoint-junction truth sets to compute per-caller recall, quantifying the paper's claim that nanopore long reads outperform short reads for de novo rearrangement detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are raw nanopore reads or unaligned FASTQ/BAM rather than finished SV call sets — run basecalling, LAST mapping, and NanoSV calling first No validated breakpoint-junction truth set exists for the sample, so recall cannot be computed (e.g. genome-wide inherited SV surveillance without curated de novo junctions) The goal is precision or false-discovery estimation rather than recovery of known junctions, which this recall-only intersection does not measure

skills.description: Use when you have SAM/BAM alignments from multiple long-read mappers over a simulated benchmark with a known ground-truth SV set, and need to rank mapper-caller combinations by inversion detection sensitivity and precision.
skills.name: sv-call-vs-truth-matching
skills.search_text: sv-call-vs-truth-matching Use when you have SAM/BAM alignments from multiple long-read mappers over a simulated benchmark with a known ground-truth SV set, and need to rank mapper-caller combinations by inversion detection sensitivity and precision. The dataset is real sequencing data (e.g. NA12878) without a known ground truth — there is no truth set to match against, so sensitivity/precision cannot be computed The analysis goal is raw mapping alignment quality rather than downstream SV calling comparison — use the mapping benchmark metrics instead The variant type of interest is not inversion SVs, since this comparison was designed and validated for inversion detection http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Run an SV caller (SVision) on each mapper's long-read alignments and match the resulting inversion call sets against a SURVIVOR-derived simulated ground truth to compute per-mapper total calls, correct calls, sensitivity, and precision. This is how the invMap paper builds its Table 2 comparison showing invMap-SVision achieves 125 calls with 82 correct and a 2.5%-15.49% sensitivity gain. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Run an SV caller (SVision) on each mapper's long-read alignments and match the resulting inversion call sets against a SURVIVOR-derived simulated ground truth to compute per-mapper total calls, correct calls, sensitivity, and precision. This is how the invMap paper builds its Table 2 comparison showing invMap-SVision achieves 125 calls with 82 correct and a 2.5%-15.49% sensitivity gain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real sequencing data (e.g. NA12878) without a known ground truth — there is no truth set to match against, so sensitivity/precision cannot be computed The analysis goal is raw mapping alignment quality rather than downstream SV calling comparison — use the mapping benchmark metrics instead The variant type of interest is not inversion SVs, since this comparison was designed and validated for inversion detection

skills.description: Use when comparing accuracy of long-read SV callers against a GIAB truth set and you need F1 rankings stratified by SV length (50-499 bp, 500-4999 bp, >=5000 bp).
skills.name: sv-caller-accuracy-ranking-comparison
skills.search_text: sv-caller-accuracy-ranking-comparison Use when comparing accuracy of long-read SV callers against a GIAB truth set and you need F1 rankings stratified by SV length (50-499 bp, 500-4999 bp, >=5000 bp). Evaluating the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark (HG002_GRCh38_CMRG_SV_v1.00), where truvari bench alone is used without the bench/refine/ga4gh consolidation Depth-stratified or joint-genotyping pedigree-concordance comparisons rather than SV size-stratified accuracy Calls outside benchmark-qualified confident regions or BND/translocation records, which have no END-POS length for stratification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Benchmark SV callers (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) on the GIAB T2T HG002 benchmark by computing per-size-stratum precision, recall, and F1 from Truvari ga4gh consolidation outputs, showing sawfish leads in every SV size group. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Benchmark SV callers (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) on the GIAB T2T HG002 benchmark by computing per-size-stratum precision, recall, and F1 from Truvari ga4gh consolidation outputs, showing sawfish leads in every SV size group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark (HG002_GRCh38_CMRG_SV_v1.00), where truvari bench alone is used without the bench/refine/ga4gh consolidation Depth-stratified or joint-genotyping pedigree-concordance comparisons rather than SV size-stratified accuracy Calls outside benchmark-qualified confident regions or BND/translocation records, which have no END-POS length for stratification

skills.description: Use when comparing SV caller accuracy from Truvari GA4GH VCF outputs and you need per-size-stratum (50-499 bp, 500-4999 bp, >=5000 bp) precision/recall/F1 rankings across callers.
skills.name: sv-caller-benchmark-f1-computation
skills.search_text: sv-caller-benchmark-f1-computation Use when comparing SV caller accuracy from Truvari GA4GH VCF outputs and you need per-size-stratum (50-499 bp, 500-4999 bp, >=5000 bp) precision/recall/F1 rankings across callers. The comparison VCFs are raw Truvari bench outputs that have not been consolidated with the refine step — the article specifies using bench AND refine results consolidated into the ga4gh VCFs, so unrefined outputs will not match reported F1 values The input records are BND/translocation calls, which lack END-based lengths and are excluded from the size-stratified computation (only non-BND records are sized) The task is depth-level (10- to 32-fold) accuracy comparison rather than SV size-stratified comparison, which requires a different aggregation dimension http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3574 Computes size-stratified precision, recall, and F1 scores for long-read SV callers (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) by aggregating Truvari bench/refine TP, FP, and FN annotations from consolidated GA4GH VCFs on the GIAB T2T-HG002-Q100 benchmark, reproducing the article's finding that sawfish ranks first in every SV size stratum. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Computes size-stratified precision, recall, and F1 scores for long-read SV callers (sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) by aggregating Truvari bench/refine TP, FP, and FN annotations from consolidated GA4GH VCFs on the GIAB T2T-HG002-Q100 benchmark, reproducing the article's finding that sawfish ranks first in every SV size stratum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison VCFs are raw Truvari bench outputs that have not been consolidated with the refine step — the article specifies using bench AND refine results consolidated into the ga4gh VCFs, so unrefined outputs will not match reported F1 values The input records are BND/translocation calls, which lack END-based lengths and are excluded from the size-stratified computation (only non-BND records are sized) The task is depth-level (10- to 32-fold) accuracy comparison rather than SV size-stratified comparison, which requires a different aggregation dimension

skills.description: Use when comparing insertion-calling tools on simulated linked-read data with a known ground truth, or when reproducing the reported precision/recall values for Novel-X versus NUI, PopIns2 and Pamir at 65x coverage.
skills.name: sv-caller-precision-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: sv-caller-precision-recall-evaluation Use when comparing insertion-calling tools on simulated linked-read data with a known ground truth, or when reproducing the reported precision/recall values for Novel-X versus NUI, PopIns2 and Pamir at 65x coverage. The dataset is real (non-simulated) data without a known insertion ground truth — precision/recall cannot be computed against the 2000 simulated insertions; use independent validation against assemblies (e.g. the T2T CHM13 v2.0 assembly) instead. The caller under test is Pamir and only linked-read data exist — Pamir cannot consume linked-reads, so it must be given separately simulated matched short reads. The analysis targets insertions below 300 bp — Novel-X's output filter (>300 bp with >300 bp anchor sum) and its requirement for many distinct barcodes (t=5) structurally bias evaluation of short insertions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A benchmarking protocol that evaluates non-reference sequence (NRS) insertion callers — Novel-X, NUI, PopIns2 and Pamir — on simulated 65x barcoded linked-read data by matching each tool's calls against 2000 ground-truth GRCh38 insertions and computing precision/recall with size-bin breakdowns. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that evaluates non-reference sequence (NRS) insertion callers — Novel-X, NUI, PopIns2 and Pamir — on simulated 65x barcoded linked-read data by matching each tool's calls against 2000 ground-truth GRCh38 insertions and computing precision/recall with size-bin breakdowns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real (non-simulated) data without a known insertion ground truth — precision/recall cannot be computed against the 2000 simulated insertions; use independent validation against assemblies (e.g. the T2T CHM13 v2.0 assembly) instead. The caller under test is Pamir and only linked-read data exist — Pamir cannot consume linked-reads, so it must be given separately simulated matched short reads. The analysis targets insertions below 300 bp — Novel-X's output filter (>300 bp with >300 bp anchor sum) and its requirement for many distinct barcodes (t=5) structurally bias evaluation of short insertions.

skills.search_text: sv-caller-vcf-conversion-and-normalization Use when raw SV calls from independent tools (e.g. DELLY, Lumpy, Pindel) are in heterogeneous formats and must be unified as VCF records with consistent coordinates and SV type annotations before consensus merging. When a single high-sensitivity caller is sufficient and no cross-caller consensus vote is intended — the study explicitly prioritized specificity over sensitivity and therefore did not detect all SVs When inputs are long-read assemblies or smap/bedpe outputs needing different conversion — SURVIVOR offers smaptovcf/bedpetovcf/convertAssemblytics for those formats instead of caller-output normalization When the goal is copy-number genotyping (CNVs from cn.MOPs) rather than breakpoint-level SV consensus merging http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Converts raw structural variant outputs from multiple callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel) into valid, coordinate- and type-consistent VCF format so they can be merged into a consensus with SURVIVOR. Normalization is the prerequisite for the >=2-caller vote that produced the S. pombe SV catalogue. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Converts raw structural variant outputs from multiple callers (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel) into valid, coordinate- and type-consistent VCF format so they can be merged into a consensus with SURVIVOR. Normalization is the prerequisite for the >=2-caller vote that produced the S. pombe SV catalogue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single high-sensitivity caller is sufficient and no cross-caller consensus vote is intended — the study explicitly prioritized specificity over sensitivity and therefore did not detect all SVs When inputs are long-read assemblies or smap/bedpe outputs needing different conversion — SURVIVOR offers smaptovcf/bedpetovcf/convertAssemblytics for those formats instead of caller-output normalization When the goal is copy-number genotyping (CNVs from cn.MOPs) rather than breakpoint-level SV consensus merging

skills.description: Use when evaluating or reproducing SV caller performance metrics (precision/recall/F1) on simulated or GIAB/Wagner-style truth sets using synthetic long reads, hybrid SLR+long-read data, or low-coverage (e.g. 5x) long-read benchmarks.
skills.name: sv-callset-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sv-callset-benchmarking Use when evaluating or reproducing SV caller performance metrics (precision/recall/F1) on simulated or GIAB/Wagner-style truth sets using synthetic long reads, hybrid SLR+long-read data, or low-coverage (e.g. 5x) long-read benchmarks. The goal is calling or typing variants, not measuring caller performance — use Blackbird directly rather than this benchmarking workflow. Truth set is unavailable or the events of interest are outside the reliable 50-10,000 bp indel range Blackbird reports (out.vcf calls are explicitly unreliable). Input is short-read-only data without SLR barcodes or long reads — Blackbird and its comparison SLR/hybrid callers are not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark structural variant callers (Blackbird in SLR or hybrid mode against LongRanger, Manta, SvABA, LEVIATHAN, PBSV, Sniffles2) by computing precision, recall, and F1 for insertions and deletions longer than 50 bp on curated truth sets such as HG002 GIAB and the Wagner et al. 2022 challenging medically relevant autosomal gene callset. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant callers (Blackbird in SLR or hybrid mode against LongRanger, Manta, SvABA, LEVIATHAN, PBSV, Sniffles2) by computing precision, recall, and F1 for insertions and deletions longer than 50 bp on curated truth sets such as HG002 GIAB and the Wagner et al. 2022 challenging medically relevant autosomal gene callset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling or typing variants, not measuring caller performance — use Blackbird directly rather than this benchmarking workflow. Truth set is unavailable or the events of interest are outside the reliable 50-10,000 bp indel range Blackbird reports (out.vcf calls are explicitly unreliable). Input is short-read-only data without SLR barcodes or long reads — Blackbird and its comparison SLR/hybrid callers are not applicable.

skills.search_text: sv-callset-f1-comparison-across-callers Use when comparing germline SV calling accuracy of multiple long-read callers on HG002 HiFi WGS data against the GIAB draft T2T SV benchmark (GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1_stvar) or the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark, to obtain size-stratified F1-scores and caller rankings. Assessing short-read SV callers or somatic/low-VAF SV calls — this workflow targets germline SVs from mapped HiFi reads, as sawfish is a germline SV/CNV caller for HiFi data When a bench-only comparison is sufficient for the CMRG benchmark — the bench/refine/ga4gh consolidation with MAFFT is specifically required for the T2T SV assessment, not the CMRG assessment which 'uses the truvari bench command alone' Benchmarking against older/GRCh37 truth sets without breakpoint-refinement support, where MAFFT refinement of candidate.refine.bed regions cannot improve match accounting http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmark structural variant callsets (e.g. sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) against a GIAB SV truth benchmark using truvari bench/refine with MAFFT refinement, consolidated via truvari ga4gh, to compute and compare per-caller F1-scores. skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant callsets (e.g. sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) against a GIAB SV truth benchmark using truvari bench/refine with MAFFT refinement, consolidated via truvari ga4gh, to compute and compare per-caller F1-scores.
