skills.description: Use when a filtered SV VCF or BED callset from long-read (MinION/nanopore) calling must be quantified for recall and precision against an established reference SV panel on a defined region such as NA12878 chromosome 1.
skills.name: sv-callset-intersection-with-truth-panels
skills.search_text: sv-callset-intersection-with-truth-panels Use when a filtered SV VCF or BED callset from long-read (MinION/nanopore) calling must be quantified for recall and precision against an established reference SV panel on a defined region such as NA12878 chromosome 1. Input callset has not passed the post-calling filtering step — intersecting raw calls with truth panels produces sensitivity/precision values incomparable with the published benchmarks Truth and query callsets use inconsistent SV type or breakpoint representations (e.g., BND vs. type-specific records), since matching requires agreement on SV type and breakpoint proximity The goal is de novo SV discovery or phasing rather than benchmarking against an established truth panel — the article's novelty assessment (e.g., retrotransposon insertions missed by short reads) falls outside this intersection workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks structural-variant callsets (e.g., NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles VCFs derived from MinION nanopore reads) against public truth panels such as the 1000 Genomes (1KG) Illumina and PacBio (PB) SV call sets by intersecting calls and matching events by SV type and breakpoint proximity, then computing per-caller sensitivity and precision. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks structural-variant callsets (e.g., NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles VCFs derived from MinION nanopore reads) against public truth panels such as the 1000 Genomes (1KG) Illumina and PacBio (PB) SV call sets by intersecting calls and matching events by SV type and breakpoint proximity, then computing per-caller sensitivity and precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input callset has not passed the post-calling filtering step — intersecting raw calls with truth panels produces sensitivity/precision values incomparable with the published benchmarks Truth and query callsets use inconsistent SV type or breakpoint representations (e.g., BND vs. type-specific records), since matching requires agreement on SV type and breakpoint proximity The goal is de novo SV discovery or phasing rather than benchmarking against an established truth panel — the article's novelty assessment (e.g., retrotransposon insertions missed by short reads) falls outside this intersection workflow

skills.description: Use when you have a NanoSV VCF of SV calls from long nanopore reads and need per-call numeric features to train or apply a machine-learning filter (e.g. random forest in scikit-learn) that separates true SVs from false positives beyond baseline precision (~54%).
skills.name: sv-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: sv-feature-extraction Use when you have a NanoSV VCF of SV calls from long nanopore reads and need per-call numeric features to train or apply a machine-learning filter (e.g. random forest in scikit-learn) that separates true SVs from false positives beyond baseline precision (~54%). You need an SV caller itself — use NanoSV (or minimap2/ngmlr + NanoSV) to produce the call set first; feature extraction assumes calls already exist in a VCF. Input alignments are short-read Illumina (e.g. from six short-read variant calling methods); this feature set is derived from long-read NanoSV split/gapped-read breakpoint-junction output. You only need raw call sets without ML-based filtering — NanoSV's own config thresholds (min_mapq 20, min_pid 0.7, cluster_count 2) may suffice without a random forest. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Extract per-call features from NanoSV structural-variant call output — including VAF, PID, CIPOS/CIEND confidence intervals, plength, MAPQ, and local coverage — to build a feature matrix for training a random forest SV filtering classifier. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Extract per-call features from NanoSV structural-variant call output — including VAF, PID, CIPOS/CIEND confidence intervals, plength, MAPQ, and local coverage — to build a feature matrix for training a random forest SV filtering classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need an SV caller itself — use NanoSV (or minimap2/ngmlr + NanoSV) to produce the call set first; feature extraction assumes calls already exist in a VCF. Input alignments are short-read Illumina (e.g. from six short-read variant calling methods); this feature set is derived from long-read NanoSV split/gapped-read breakpoint-junction output. You only need raw call sets without ML-based filtering — NanoSV's own config thresholds (min_mapq 20, min_pid 0.7, cluster_count 2) may suffice without a random forest.

skills.description: Use when you have putative SV calls (VCF/BED from dysgu or gold sets such as GIAB HG001/HG002 or pbsv PacBio calls) and need feature vectors plus quality probabilities for ML-based SV classification.
skills.name: sv-feature-vector-computation
skills.search_text: sv-feature-vector-computation Use when you have putative SV calls (VCF/BED from dysgu or gold sets such as GIAB HG001/HG002 or pbsv PacBio calls) and need feature vectors plus quality probabilities for ML-based SV classification. The task is SV calling itself (signal detection from BAMs) rather than scoring already-detected events — use dysgu's run/fetch/call pipeline instead You need to benchmark SV calls against truth sets rather than compute classification features — use svbench (svbench REFERENCE_VCF QUERY_VCFS...) instead Only read-support filtering is needed without sequence metrics — the --contigs False model strips all sequence-related metrics, making full feature computation unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes per-event structural variant feature vectors (read support, coverage-based metrics such as fold change in coverage (FCC), and sequence/contig metrics) from putative SV calls so they can be scored by dysgu's LightGBM gradient-boosting quality classifier. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Computes per-event structural variant feature vectors (read support, coverage-based metrics such as fold change in coverage (FCC), and sequence/contig metrics) from putative SV calls so they can be scored by dysgu's LightGBM gradient-boosting quality classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is SV calling itself (signal detection from BAMs) rather than scoring already-detected events — use dysgu's run/fetch/call pipeline instead You need to benchmark SV calls against truth sets rather than compute classification features — use svbench (svbench REFERENCE_VCF QUERY_VCFS...) instead Only read-support filtering is needed without sequence metrics — the --contigs False model strips all sequence-related metrics, making full feature computation unnecessary

skills.description: Use when a genotype matrix of SVs (duplications, deletions, translocations) and a table of quantitative trait measurements across a strain panel are both available and the goal is to map SVs to trait variation.
skills.name: sv-genotype-phenotype-mapping
skills.search_text: sv-genotype-phenotype-mapping Use when a genotype matrix of SVs (duplications, deletions, translocations) and a table of quantitative trait measurements across a strain panel are both available and the goal is to map SVs to trait variation. SV calls have not been filtered/validated yet (calls detected by fewer than two callers, breakpoints overlapping low-complexity regions or annotated LTRs) — the input catalogue should already be curated The question is variance-partitioning of trait heritability across variant classes rather than per-SV association testing (use mixed-model heritability estimation instead) Traits are binary or survival-type rather than quantitative; the permutation-threshold mixed-model design described here targets quantitative traits http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Test structural variations (SVs) for association with quantitative traits using mixed-model GWAS with permutation-derived significance thresholds, as done in the S. pombe SV study where 19 of 68 SVs were trait-associated. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Test structural variations (SVs) for association with quantitative traits using mixed-model GWAS with permutation-derived significance thresholds, as done in the S. pombe SV study where 19 of 68 SVs were trait-associated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: SV calls have not been filtered/validated yet (calls detected by fewer than two callers, breakpoints overlapping low-complexity regions or annotated LTRs) — the input catalogue should already be curated The question is variance-partitioning of trait heritability across variant classes rather than per-SV association testing (use mixed-model heritability estimation instead) Traits are binary or survival-type rather than quantitative; the permutation-threshold mixed-model design described here targets quantitative traits

skills.description: Use when a published SV study deposits a curated callset (e.g. on Figshare) and you must reproduce its reported catalogue size and per-class composition from the deposited SV records, genotypes and copy numbers.
skills.name: sv-genotype-table-parsing
skills.search_text: sv-genotype-table-parsing Use when a published SV study deposits a curated callset (e.g. on Figshare) and you must reproduce its reported catalogue size and per-class composition from the deposited SV records, genotypes and copy numbers. The goal is de novo SV discovery from raw short-read alignments — use the four-caller consensus pipeline (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPS + SURVIVOR) instead of parsing a deposited catalogue The deposited table is an unfiltered or intermediate callset (e.g. the 315 two-caller calls) rather than the final manually curated catalogue, so counts will not match the reported 113 The input lacks per-record variant class annotations (SVTYPE), making per-class tallying impossible without re-annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Parses a deposited curated structural-variant catalogue (SV calls, genotypes and copy numbers) and tallies SV counts by class (deletions, duplications, inversions, translocations) to verify the published composition against the 113-SV fission yeast catalogue (23 deletions, 64 duplications, 11 inversions, 15 translocations). genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms14061
skills.summary: Parses a deposited curated structural-variant catalogue (SV calls, genotypes and copy numbers) and tallies SV counts by class (deletions, duplications, inversions, translocations) to verify the published composition against the 113-SV fission yeast catalogue (23 deletions, 64 duplications, 11 inversions, 15 translocations).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo SV discovery from raw short-read alignments — use the four-caller consensus pipeline (Delly, Lumpy, Pindel, cn.MOPS + SURVIVOR) instead of parsing a deposited catalogue The deposited table is an unfiltered or intermediate callset (e.g. the 315 two-caller calls) rather than the final manually curated catalogue, so counts will not match the reported 113 The input lacks per-record variant class annotations (SVTYPE), making per-class tallying impossible without re-annotation

skills.description: Use when an assembly/locus-based SV caller (e.g. sawfish discover) emits per-breakpoint SV haplotype consensus contigs and you need orthogonal, sequence-level evidence that the calls are real and correctly placed.
skills.name: sv-haplotype-contig-alignment
skills.search_text: sv-haplotype-contig-alignment Use when an assembly/locus-based SV caller (e.g. sawfish discover) emits per-breakpoint SV haplotype consensus contigs and you need orthogonal, sequence-level evidence that the calls are real and correctly placed. The goal is variant-level precision/recall benchmarking against a truth VCF — use truvari bench/refine (with MAFFT refinement) or hap-eval instead of contig-to-assembly alignment The caller produces only variant records without assembled haplotype contigs — there is no contig set to realign, so this validation is inapplicable The sample lacks a high-quality diploid assembly or T2T benchmark, leaving no independent reference to distinguish expected from spurious contig placements http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Validates structural variant (SV) caller output by aligning the assembled SV haplotype consensus contigs back to an independent high-quality diploid assembly (T2T-HG002-Q100v1.1) and computing the fraction that map to their called locus and breakend orientation, reproducing the paper's 99.4% expected-alignment rate for HG002 32x data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Validates structural variant (SV) caller output by aligning the assembled SV haplotype consensus contigs back to an independent high-quality diploid assembly (T2T-HG002-Q100v1.1) and computing the fraction that map to their called locus and breakend orientation, reproducing the paper's 99.4% expected-alignment rate for HG002 32x data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is variant-level precision/recall benchmarking against a truth VCF — use truvari bench/refine (with MAFFT refinement) or hap-eval instead of contig-to-assembly alignment The caller produces only variant records without assembled haplotype contigs — there is no contig set to realign, so this validation is inapplicable The sample lacks a high-quality diploid assembly or T2T benchmark, leaving no independent reference to distinguish expected from spurious contig placements

skills.description: Use when calling germline SVs from mapped HiFi reads where breakpoint evidence must be resolved to basepair resolution via local haplotype assembly rather than read-pair heuristics.
skills.name: sv-haplotype-local-assembly-and-poa-consensus
skills.search_text: sv-haplotype-local-assembly-and-poa-consensus Use when calling germline SVs from mapped HiFi reads where breakpoint evidence must be resolved to basepair resolution via local haplotype assembly rather than read-pair heuristics. Input reads are short reads or noisy long reads below HiFi quality — the method is built for mapped HiFi sequencing reads with high gap-compressed identity (>= 0.97 retained). The goal is benchmarking an existing SV callset rather than discovery — use truvari bench/refine or hap-eval instead of re-running local haplotype assembly. Only copy number variation (depth-based) is of interest without breakpoint-level SV resolution — depth segmentation alone may suffice. http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assembles breakpoint-based structural variants as local haplotype contigs from clustered long-read breakpoint evidence using partial order alignment (spoa) and wavefront alignment (WFA2-lib), then realigns the contigs to the reference genome to resolve SVs to basepair resolution with breakpoint homology and insertion detail. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Assembles breakpoint-based structural variants as local haplotype contigs from clustered long-read breakpoint evidence using partial order alignment (spoa) and wavefront alignment (WFA2-lib), then realigns the contigs to the reference genome to resolve SVs to basepair resolution with breakpoint homology and insertion detail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short reads or noisy long reads below HiFi quality — the method is built for mapped HiFi sequencing reads with high gap-compressed identity (>= 0.97 retained). The goal is benchmarking an existing SV callset rather than discovery — use truvari bench/refine or hap-eval instead of re-running local haplotype assembly. Only copy number variation (depth-based) is of interest without breakpoint-level SV resolution — depth segmentation alone may suffice.

skills.description: Use when you have a raw NanoSV (or equivalent long-read) SV VCF and need to remove likely false positives, especially calls anchored in homopolymer or tandem-repeat regions and small indels below the 40 bp SV threshold.
skills.name: sv-post-calling-filtering
skills.search_text: sv-post-calling-filtering Use when you have a raw NanoSV (or equivalent long-read) SV VCF and need to remove likely false positives, especially calls anchored in homopolymer or tandem-repeat regions and small indels below the 40 bp SV threshold. Input is raw nanopore FASTQ or an unaligned BAM — NanoSV SV calling (with LAST/BWA-MEM/minimap2/NGMLR mapping) must run first to produce the VCF to be filtered Goal is detecting small variants or indels <40 bp — this filtering intentionally discards sub-40 bp indels because they rarely produce the split alignments NanoSV relies on Goal is read-based phasing or chromothripsis structure reconstruction — those skills operate on phased SNPs and haplotype-separated reads, not on SV call-set curation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Applies the paper's stringent post-calling filtering cascade to a NanoSV structural-variant call set: first discard SVs whose breakpoints fall in homopolymer/short-tandem-repeat regions, then drop small indels (<40 bp) that typically do not produce split alignments. This conservative filtering trades sensitivity (~75%) for precision (>95%). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Applies the paper's stringent post-calling filtering cascade to a NanoSV structural-variant call set: first discard SVs whose breakpoints fall in homopolymer/short-tandem-repeat regions, then drop small indels (<40 bp) that typically do not produce split alignments. This conservative filtering trades sensitivity (~75%) for precision (>95%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore FASTQ or an unaligned BAM — NanoSV SV calling (with LAST/BWA-MEM/minimap2/NGMLR mapping) must run first to produce the VCF to be filtered Goal is detecting small variants or indels <40 bp — this filtering intentionally discards sub-40 bp indels because they rarely produce the split alignments NanoSV relies on Goal is read-based phasing or chromothripsis structure reconstruction — those skills operate on phased SNPs and haplotype-separated reads, not on SV call-set curation

skills.description: Use when comparing SV-caller outputs (VCFs from dysgu, manta, delly, lumpy, strelka, gatk) against a reference call set (e.g. NIST_SVs_Integration_v0.6) to quantify per-class precision/recall/F1.
skills.name: sv-precision-recall-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sv-precision-recall-benchmarking Use when comparing SV-caller outputs (VCFs from dysgu, manta, delly, lumpy, strelka, gatk) against a reference call set (e.g. NIST_SVs_Integration_v0.6) to quantify per-class precision/recall/F1. Input is a single production sample call set with no truth/benchmark VCF — svbench requires a reference_vcf to compare against Evaluating small-variant (SNP/indel <30 bp) genotyping accuracy with tools like rtg/CHM-eval rather than SV presence/absence calling Benchmarking long-read SV callers where truth sets other than GIAB SV sets (e.g. PacBio HiFi deletion/insertion benchmark) are required http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark structural-variant callers by computing precision, recall and F1 per SV type (deletions, insertions) against a GIAB truth set, using svbench for interval-overlap matching (1000 bp overlap, 15% size similarity). Used to rank callers such as dysgu, manta, delly and lumpy on HG002 Tier 1 regions. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Benchmark structural-variant callers by computing precision, recall and F1 per SV type (deletions, insertions) against a GIAB truth set, using svbench for interval-overlap matching (1000 bp overlap, 15% size similarity). Used to rank callers such as dysgu, manta, delly and lumpy on HG002 Tier 1 regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single production sample call set with no truth/benchmark VCF — svbench requires a reference_vcf to compare against Evaluating small-variant (SNP/indel <30 bp) genotyping accuracy with tools like rtg/CHM-eval rather than SV presence/absence calling Benchmarking long-read SV callers where truth sets other than GIAB SV sets (e.g. PacBio HiFi deletion/insertion benchmark) are required

skills.description: Use when comparing SV caller sensitivity/FPR (e.g., NanoSV vs Lumpy vs Sniffles) from simulated nanopore reads with a known set of rearrangement breakpoints as ground truth.
skills.name: sv-recall-fpr-evaluation
skills.search_text: sv-recall-fpr-evaluation Use when comparing SV caller sensitivity/FPR (e.g., NanoSV vs Lumpy vs Sniffles) from simulated nanopore reads with a known set of rearrangement breakpoints as ground truth. Input is real patient data without a known ground truth — recall/FPR cannot be computed without simulated or validated breakpoint truth sets Short-read (Illumina) SV calling — the benchmark design, read simulation (NanoSim), and NanoSV's split-read clustering are specific to long nanopore reads Estimating novel-variant discovery rates in real genomes, where the article instead reports conservative filtering with ~75% estimated sensitivity and >95% precision http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark structural variant callers on simulated nanopore long reads with known ground-truth breakpoints, computing per-caller recall and false positive rate across downsampled coverage levels (1x to 44x). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant callers on simulated nanopore long reads with known ground-truth breakpoints, computing per-caller recall and false positive rate across downsampled coverage levels (1x to 44x).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real patient data without a known ground truth — recall/FPR cannot be computed without simulated or validated breakpoint truth sets Short-read (Illumina) SV calling — the benchmark design, read simulation (NanoSim), and NanoSV's split-read clustering are specific to long nanopore reads Estimating novel-variant discovery rates in real genomes, where the article instead reports conservative filtering with ~75% estimated sensitivity and >95% precision

skills.description: Use when mining a contig-to-reference BAM (primary + supplementary split blocks) for large INS/DEL signatures with the 30 bp Diff_dis / 3000 bp Diff_olp thresholds of the VolcanoSV-vc large indel module.
skills.name: sv-signature-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: sv-signature-threshold-filtering Use when mining a contig-to-reference BAM (primary + supplementary split blocks) for large INS/DEL signatures with the 30 bp Diff_dis / 3000 bp Diff_olp thresholds of the VolcanoSV-vc large indel module. The input is raw reads with no diploid assembly — this skill operates on contig-to-reference alignments from the VolcanoSV-asm output, not directly on read alignments Calling complex SVs (TRA/INV/DUP) — those require the VolcanoSV-vc Complex_SV module in WGS mode with WGS BAM support; translocation detection 'does not make sense to run on single chromosome level' Small indels — assembly-based small indel detection is a separate VolcanoSV-vc Small_INDEL module and was shown ineffective for ONT data http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extracts large insertion/deletion SV signatures from contig-to-reference alignment blocks using VolcanoSV-vc's distance (Diff_dis, TH_dis=30 bp) and overlap (Diff_olp, TH_olp=3000 bp) thresholds, writing them to a signatures.tsv that feeds the large indel module's phased VCF output. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-51282-0
skills.summary: Extracts large insertion/deletion SV signatures from contig-to-reference alignment blocks using VolcanoSV-vc's distance (Diff_dis, TH_dis=30 bp) and overlap (Diff_olp, TH_olp=3000 bp) thresholds, writing them to a signatures.tsv that feeds the large indel module's phased VCF output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw reads with no diploid assembly — this skill operates on contig-to-reference alignments from the VolcanoSV-asm output, not directly on read alignments Calling complex SVs (TRA/INV/DUP) — those require the VolcanoSV-vc Complex_SV module in WGS mode with WGS BAM support; translocation detection 'does not make sense to run on single chromosome level' Small indels — assembly-based small indel detection is a separate VolcanoSV-vc Small_INDEL module and was shown ineffective for ONT data

skills.description: Use when you have long-read (e.g., nanopore NanoSV VCF) SV call sets plus matched short-read caller outputs and need to classify which calls are novel, then profile their size bins, GC content, and retrotransposon (LINE) enrichment.
skills.name: sv-size-and-class-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: sv-size-and-class-distribution-analysis Use when you have long-read (e.g., nanopore NanoSV VCF) SV call sets plus matched short-read caller outputs and need to classify which calls are novel, then profile their size bins, GC content, and retrotransposon (LINE) enrichment. Input consists only of short-read Illumina SV calls with no long-read call set to compare against — there is no nanopore-specific fraction to define. The goal is de novo complex rearrangement resolution or phasing (e.g., chromothripsis breakpoint phasing) rather than genome-wide novel-SV characterization. Coverage is far below the 11–16× MinION depth used here; size/GC bias contrasts will not be comparable to the published distributions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the fraction of nanopore-specific SVs (not seen in short-read Illumina calls or 1KG sites) and characterizes them by SV class, size, GC content, and repeat/LINE composition, as done with NanoSV calls from MinION-sequenced patient genomes at 11–16× coverage. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01343-4
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of nanopore-specific SVs (not seen in short-read Illumina calls or 1KG sites) and characterizes them by SV class, size, GC content, and repeat/LINE composition, as done with NanoSV calls from MinION-sequenced patient genomes at 11–16× coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists only of short-read Illumina SV calls with no long-read call set to compare against — there is no nanopore-specific fraction to define. The goal is de novo complex rearrangement resolution or phasing (e.g., chromothripsis breakpoint phasing) rather than genome-wide novel-SV characterization. Coverage is far below the 11–16× MinION depth used here; size/GC bias contrasts will not be comparable to the published distributions.

skills.description: Use when you have simulated reads with a known embedded SV set (e.g. 900 SVs from SURVIVOR simulateSV) and need to score mapper/tool SV calls (recall, precision, F1) against the truth set.
skills.name: sv-truth-set-comparison
skills.search_text: sv-truth-set-comparison Use when you have simulated reads with a known embedded SV set (e.g. 900 SVs from SURVIVOR simulateSV) and need to score mapper/tool SV calls (recall, precision, F1) against the truth set. You lack a ground-truth SV set — the comparison requires the SURVIVOR truth set; without it only candidate-call counts (as in the NA12878 real-data analysis) can be reported, not accuracy Your reads are short reads — this workflow is built around long noisy reads from PacBio or Oxford Nanopore sequencers that span SV breakpoints You need per-base alignment accuracy rather than SV discovery accuracy — this skill scores SV call sets, not alignment quality http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmarks long-read structural variant (SV) calls against a SURVIVOR-generated ground-truth set, computing recall, precision, and F1 separately for indels and inversions across coverage levels. This is the evaluation workflow used to show invMap outperforms competing mappers for inversion calling on simulated chr1 data. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad726
skills.summary: Benchmarks long-read structural variant (SV) calls against a SURVIVOR-generated ground-truth set, computing recall, precision, and F1 separately for indels and inversions across coverage levels. This is the evaluation workflow used to show invMap outperforms competing mappers for inversion calling on simulated chr1 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack a ground-truth SV set — the comparison requires the SURVIVOR truth set; without it only candidate-call counts (as in the NA12878 real-data analysis) can be reported, not accuracy Your reads are short reads — this workflow is built around long noisy reads from PacBio or Oxford Nanopore sequencers that span SV breakpoints You need per-base alignment accuracy rather than SV discovery accuracy — this skill scores SV call sets, not alignment quality

skills.description: Use when a sample has multiple SV caller VCFs (e.g. the six callers of ConsensuSV-ONT) that must be merged and deduplicated into one overlapping-variant-free candidate VCF before consensus scoring or CNN filtering.
skills.name: sv-variant-overlap-collapse
skills.search_text: sv-variant-overlap-collapse Use when a sample has multiple SV caller VCFs (e.g. the six callers of ConsensuSV-ONT) that must be merged and deduplicated into one overlapping-variant-free candidate VCF before consensus scoring or CNN filtering. Input is already a single consensus VCF that has been through collapse — re-running would not reduce overlap and could alter records You only have one caller's output and no multi-caller union to consolidate; Truvari merge/collapse addresses redundancy across callers, not within-callset calling errors The task is quality filtering of consensus variants — that is the separate CNN-based filtering step of ConsensuSV-ONT http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Combines the per-caller structural variant VCFs produced by six independent ONT SV callers into a single non-redundant candidate set, using the Truvari merge module followed by the Truvari collapse module, as orchestrated inside the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow pipeline. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Combines the per-caller structural variant VCFs produced by six independent ONT SV callers into a single non-redundant candidate set, using the Truvari merge module followed by the Truvari collapse module, as orchestrated inside the ConsensuSV-ONT Nextflow pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single consensus VCF that has been through collapse — re-running would not reduce overlap and could alter records You only have one caller's output and no multi-caller union to consolidate; Truvari merge/collapse addresses redundancy across callers, not within-callset calling errors The task is quality filtering of consensus variants — that is the separate CNN-based filtering step of ConsensuSV-ONT

skills.description: Use when a nanopore TE callset contains insertions annotated as generic SVA (SVA F) by the RepeatMasker-on-Dfam step and you need to distinguish the newer SVA F1 family, which is absent from Dfam.
skills.name: sva-f1-mast2-thumbprint-detection
skills.search_text: sva-f1-mast2-thumbprint-detection Use when a nanopore TE callset contains insertions annotated as generic SVA (SVA F) by the RepeatMasker-on-Dfam step and you need to distinguish the newer SVA F1 family, which is absent from Dfam. Insertions belong to other TE families (e.g. L1 or Alu) that are already recovered by the RepeatMasker-on-Dfam annotation step — the MAST2 thumbprint check is specific to SVA elements No reassembled inserted sequence is available (the check operates on the reassembled inserted region, not on raw supporting reads alone) The goal is detection of SVA insertions generally rather than sub-family resolution of already-called SVA insertions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 A discrete follow-up step in RetroInspector that resolves SVA insertions not distinguished by Dfam/RepeatMasker: called SVA insertions are screened for the MAST2 thumbprint fragment carried by SVA F1 elements and relabelled SVA F1 when the fragment is found. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: A discrete follow-up step in RetroInspector that resolves SVA insertions not distinguished by Dfam/RepeatMasker: called SVA insertions are screened for the MAST2 thumbprint fragment carried by SVA F1 elements and relabelled SVA F1 when the fragment is found.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Insertions belong to other TE families (e.g. L1 or Alu) that are already recovered by the RepeatMasker-on-Dfam annotation step — the MAST2 thumbprint check is specific to SVA elements No reassembled inserted sequence is available (the check operates on the reassembled inserted region, not on raw supporting reads alone) The goal is detection of SVA insertions generally rather than sub-family resolution of already-called SVA insertions

skills.description: Use when multiple SV caller VCFs (e.g. dysgu PacBio/ONT, SVIM, NanoVar, Sniffles) must be compared on the same HG002 long-read alignments, and per-caller precision/recall/F1 for deletions and insertions is the deliverable.
skills.name: svbench-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: svbench-benchmark-evaluation Use when multiple SV caller VCFs (e.g. dysgu PacBio/ONT, SVIM, NanoVar, Sniffles) must be compared on the same HG002 long-read alignments, and per-caller precision/recall/F1 for deletions and insertions is the deliverable. Short-read (paired-end) caller comparisons against Manta/DELLY/Lumpy — use the paper's PE benchmarking workflow (HG002 Tier 1 at 20x, syndip benchmark) instead Genotype concordance or allele-accuracy evaluation — svbench reports precision/recall/F1; a different evaluator (e.g. rtg-based) is needed The goal is calling SVs rather than benchmarking existing VCFs — run dysgu directly (dysgu run/dysgu call) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark structural variant callers (dysgu, SVIM, NanoVar, Sniffles) on HG002 long-read data by evaluating their VCFs against the GIAB v0.6 HG002 SV truth set with svbench, computing precision, recall and F1 restricted to deletion and insertion event classes (paper Table 5). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Benchmark structural variant callers (dysgu, SVIM, NanoVar, Sniffles) on HG002 long-read data by evaluating their VCFs against the GIAB v0.6 HG002 SV truth set with svbench, computing precision, recall and F1 restricted to deletion and insertion event classes (paper Table 5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Short-read (paired-end) caller comparisons against Manta/DELLY/Lumpy — use the paper's PE benchmarking workflow (HG002 Tier 1 at 20x, syndip benchmark) instead Genotype concordance or allele-accuracy evaluation — svbench reports precision/recall/F1; a different evaluator (e.g. rtg-based) is needed The goal is calling SVs rather than benchmarking existing VCFs — run dysgu directly (dysgu run/dysgu call) instead

The per-site/per-kmer feature table already exists — proceed directly to SVM classification rather than re-extracting features. Per-read (single-molecule) modification calls are required — EpiNano has no per-read resolution; it aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site. skills.description: Use when ONT direct RNA sequencing reads (base-called FASTQ/FAST5) are available and per-site m6A modification calls are needed, restricting candidates to RRACH motif adenosines rather than calling per-molecule.
skills.name: svm-modification-site-scoring
skills.search_text: svm-modification-site-scoring Use when ONT direct RNA sequencing reads (base-called FASTQ/FAST5) are available and per-site m6A modification calls are needed, restricting candidates to RRACH motif adenosines rather than calling per-molecule. Per-read (single-molecule) modification detection is required — EpiNano 'does not predict RNA modifications in individual RNA molecules' and only aggregates reads per site The caller cannot restrict candidates to a known sequence motif (e.g., RRACH) or the modification type is not represented by a pre-trained SVM model — EpiNano-SVM depends on the base-caller version and available pretrained models Distinguishing modification types (m1A vs m6A) is required — the algorithm does not distinguish between them http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Score RRACH motif adenosine sites in ONT direct RNA base-called reads for m6A using the EpiNano SVM, which classifies sites from per-site base-calling error features (per-base qualities, mismatch and deletion frequencies) learned on synthetic m6A-modified/unmodified training sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9

skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-read (single-molecule) modification detection is required — EpiNano 'does not predict RNA modifications in individual RNA molecules' and only aggregates reads per site The caller cannot restrict candidates to a known sequence motif (e.g., RRACH) or the modification type is not represented by a pre-trained SVM model — EpiNano-SVM depends on the base-caller version and available pretrained models Distinguishing modification types (m1A vs m6A) is required — the algorithm does not distinguish between them

skills.description: Use when a concatenated high-dimensional feature vector (e.g. 3240-dimension DDE+PSSM-DBT+PSSM-DWT+NMBAC for PDB1075) contains noisy/redundant descriptors and an SVM classifier needs a compact, bias-reduced feature subset before training.
skills.name: svm-recursive-feature-elimination-feature-selection
skills.search_text: svm-recursive-feature-elimination-feature-selection Use when a concatenated high-dimensional feature vector (e.g. 3240-dimension DDE+PSSM-DBT+PSSM-DWT+NMBAC for PDB1075) contains noisy/redundant descriptors and an SVM classifier needs a compact, bias-reduced feature subset before training. The input is already a small, non-redundant feature table where wrapper-based elimination adds cost without variance reduction The task requires a filter or embedded method independent of a specific SVM classifier (SVM-RFE+CBR weights are tied to the LIBSVM RBF model with C=1, gamma=0.03125) Only individual descriptor spaces are being compared without a concatenated multi-view vector — the 424-dimension optimum was derived for the combined 3240-dimension space http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Ranks features in high-dimensional protein feature spaces by recursively removing lowest-weight SVM features with Correlation Bias Reduction (SVM-RFE+CBR), then selects the top-ranked subset size maximizing Jackknife cross-validation accuracy — in iDBP-DEP this reduces the 3240-dimension multi-view vector (DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) to an optimal 424-dimension subset. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Ranks features in high-dimensional protein feature spaces by recursively removing lowest-weight SVM features with Correlation Bias Reduction (SVM-RFE+CBR), then selects the top-ranked subset size maximizing Jackknife cross-validation accuracy — in iDBP-DEP this reduces the 3240-dimension multi-view vector (DDE, PSSM-DBT, PSSM-DWT, NMBAC) to an optimal 424-dimension subset.

skills.search_text: swissprot-sequence-set-preparation Use when building a genome-to-protein mapping database (e.g. MetaDome prebuild) and you need the filtered Swiss-Prot FASTA subset of GENCODE-matched canonical/isoform sequences as input to domain annotation. skills.search_text: synthetic-long-read-dataset-generation Use when you need ground-truth structural-variant datasets to benchmark a long-read SV detection or annotation tool, e.g. testing whether deletions, inversions, duplications, translocations, or complex insertion-deletion rearrangements are resolved correctly. The synthetic reads contain no background mutations or sequence variants, so the data are unsuitable for benchmarking SNV/small-indel callers or for any use beyond algorithm testing. Do not use this approach when real experimental read characteristics (error profiles, uneven coverage) are required — MakeSVGenome data alternate orientation at fixed length/spacing and are explicitly not real experimental data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Generate in silico long-read test datasets with MakeSVGenome — fixed-length fixed-spacing reads of alternating orientation carrying known structural rearrangements — then align with minimap2 and benchmark annotation accuracy (e.g. of AgileStructure) against the ground-truth variants. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Generate in silico long-read test datasets with MakeSVGenome — fixed-length fixed-spacing reads of alternating orientation carrying known structural rearrangements — then align with minimap2 and benchmark annotation accuracy (e.g. of AgileStructure) against the ground-truth variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The synthetic reads contain no background mutations or sequence variants, so the data are unsuitable for benchmarking SNV/small-indel callers or for any use beyond algorithm testing. Do not use this approach when real experimental read characteristics (error profiles, uneven coverage) are required — MakeSVGenome data alternate orientation at fixed length/spacing and are explicitly not real experimental data.

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing non-reference insertion callers (e.g. Novel-X, PopIns2, NUI) on linked-read data, or when quantifying how coverage level affects NRS detection performance.
skills.name: synthetic-long-read-insertion-detection
skills.search_text: synthetic-long-read-insertion-detection Use when evaluating or comparing non-reference insertion callers (e.g. Novel-X, PopIns2, NUI) on linked-read data, or when quantifying how coverage level affects NRS detection performance. The goal is detection of insertions shorter than 300 bp — Novel-X only outputs insertions longer than 300 bp with anchor lengths exceeding 300 bp, and needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes that small insertions usually lack Input data are ultra-short reads without barcode information — this skill requires linked-reads (10x Genomics, TELL-Seq or stLFR) and barcode-aware callers The goal is whole-genome de novo assembly-based detection — this skill benchmarks targeted/local-assembly callers and does not cover expensive whole-genome assembly approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarking protocol for detecting non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions with linked-read (synthetic long-read) tools, based on the Novel-X paper's coverage-sensitivity assessment: downsample a simulated 65x synthetic long-read dataset to 52x/39x/26x/13x, run competing callers, and score recall/precision against a ground-truth insertion callset. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for detecting non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions with linked-read (synthetic long-read) tools, based on the Novel-X paper's coverage-sensitivity assessment: downsample a simulated 65x synthetic long-read dataset to 52x/39x/26x/13x, run competing callers, and score recall/precision against a ground-truth insertion callset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detection of insertions shorter than 300 bp — Novel-X only outputs insertions longer than 300 bp with anchor lengths exceeding 300 bp, and needs a substantial number of distinct barcodes that small insertions usually lack Input data are ultra-short reads without barcode information — this skill requires linked-reads (10x Genomics, TELL-Seq or stLFR) and barcode-aware callers The goal is whole-genome de novo assembly-based detection — this skill benchmarks targeted/local-assembly callers and does not cover expensive whole-genome assembly approaches

skills.description: Use when input is a position-sorted, indexed SLR BAM with BX barcode tags aligned to a BWA-indexed reference (optionally paired with low-coverage long-read BAM/FASTQ) and the goal is sensitive insertion/deletion calling in the 50–10,000 bp range.
skills.name: synthetic-long-read-structural-variant-calling
skills.search_text: synthetic-long-read-structural-variant-calling Use when input is a position-sorted, indexed SLR BAM with BX barcode tags aligned to a BWA-indexed reference (optionally paired with low-coverage long-read BAM/FASTQ) and the goal is sensitive insertion/deletion calling in the 50–10,000 bp range. The dataset is short-read-only without BX barcode tags — Blackbird depends on SLR barcode information encoded in reads The target events are outside the 50–10,000 bp range or calls shorter than 50 bp are needed — out_50.vcf only reports calls longer than 50 bp and out.vcf calls are 'not reliable' A whole-genome assembly or non-SV variant calling (SNVs, small indels <50 bp) is the goal — Blackbird performs barcode-aware segment assembly for SV detection only http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Call medium-size structural variants (50–10,000 bp insertions and deletions) using synthetic long reads (SLR) with barcode information, optionally augmented with low-coverage PacBio HiFi long reads (hybrid mode), via the barcode-aware sliding-window local assembler Blackbird. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf151
skills.summary: Call medium-size structural variants (50–10,000 bp insertions and deletions) using synthetic long reads (SLR) with barcode information, optionally augmented with low-coverage PacBio HiFi long reads (hybrid mode), via the barcode-aware sliding-window local assembler Blackbird.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is short-read-only without BX barcode tags — Blackbird depends on SLR barcode information encoded in reads The target events are outside the 50–10,000 bp range or calls shorter than 50 bp are needed — out_50.vcf only reports calls longer than 50 bp and out.vcf calls are 'not reliable' A whole-genome assembly or non-SV variant calling (SNVs, small indels <50 bp) is the goal — Blackbird performs barcode-aware segment assembly for SV detection only

skills.description: Use when you have raw or Lordec-corrected long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) plus an Illumina contig assembly in FASTA, and need synthetic mate-pair FASTQ libraries with user-specified insert sizes to drive short-read scaffolders alignment-free.
skills.name: synthetic-mate-pair-library-extraction-from-long-reads
skills.search_text: synthetic-mate-pair-library-extraction-from-long-reads Use when you have raw or Lordec-corrected long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) plus an Illumina contig assembly in FASTA, and need synthetic mate-pair FASTQ libraries with user-specified insert sizes to drive short-read scaffolders alignment-free. The reads are already short Illumina mate-pair libraries — Fast-SG's synthetic extraction targets long-read linking information and is unnecessary You need a long-read-aware scaffolder to consume the original long reads directly (e.g. Links is the baseline for that; Fast-SG synthetic pairs are for short-read scaffolders) Only a raw read set with no contig assembly exists — extraction builds the scaffolding graph against a reference contig set (-r), so no contigs means the skill cannot be applied as described http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extract alignment-free synthetic mate-pair libraries from raw or error-corrected long reads (ONT, PacBio) using Fast-SG, converting long-read linking information into short-read-style mate pairs that reusable short-read scaffolders (Opera-LG, ScaffMatch, Boss) can consume. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy048
skills.summary: Extract alignment-free synthetic mate-pair libraries from raw or error-corrected long reads (ONT, PacBio) using Fast-SG, converting long-read linking information into short-read-style mate pairs that reusable short-read scaffolders (Opera-LG, ScaffMatch, Boss) can consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already short Illumina mate-pair libraries — Fast-SG's synthetic extraction targets long-read linking information and is unnecessary You need a long-read-aware scaffolder to consume the original long reads directly (e.g. Links is the baseline for that; Fast-SG synthetic pairs are for short-read scaffolders) Only a raw read set with no contig assembly exists — extraction builds the scaffolding graph against a reference contig set (-r), so no contigs means the skill cannot be applied as described

skills.description: Use when a controlled benchmark with known reference genomes is required to quantify how a merge/assembly pipeline changes contig counts, unmapped contigs, reference genome coverage, and chimeras.
skills.name: synthetic-metagenomic-read-simulation
skills.search_text: synthetic-metagenomic-read-simulation Use when a controlled benchmark with known reference genomes is required to quantify how a merge/assembly pipeline changes contig counts, unmapped contigs, reference genome coverage, and chimeras. The sample is real (not synthetically derived) metagenomic data with no reference genomes, so unmapped-contig and reference-coverage validation is impossible The goal is to compare read-level QC protocols rather than post-assembly merging, since MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process operating on already-assembled contigs The input is a single assembly whose contigs should not be merged; use the -single_genome=1 mode only when merging long reads/single-genome contigs, not multi-assembler pooling http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Generates a ground-truth synthetic metagenome by simulating shotgun reads (MetaSim, customized Illumina error model with in-house per-base quality assignments) from 1,000 known reference genomes, then trims, assembles per-Kmer (51–71), merges contigs with MeGAMerge, and validates via read mapping (BWA/SAMtools) and reference alignment (Nucmer). genomics/v1 10.1038/srep06480
skills.summary: Generates a ground-truth synthetic metagenome by simulating shotgun reads (MetaSim, customized Illumina error model with in-house per-base quality assignments) from 1,000 known reference genomes, then trims, assembles per-Kmer (51–71), merges contigs with MeGAMerge, and validates via read mapping (BWA/SAMtools) and reference alignment (Nucmer).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is real (not synthetically derived) metagenomic data with no reference genomes, so unmapped-contig and reference-coverage validation is impossible The goal is to compare read-level QC protocols rather than post-assembly merging, since MeGAMerge is a post-assembly process operating on already-assembled contigs The input is a single assembly whose contigs should not be merged; use the -single_genome=1 mode only when merging long reads/single-genome contigs, not multi-assembler pooling

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a read-level RNA modification caller can resolve phase-shifted or patterned modifications hidden in synthetic oligo benchmarks whose aggregate site-level signals are uninformative.
skills.name: synthetic-oligo-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: synthetic-oligo-benchmark-analysis Use when evaluating whether a read-level RNA modification caller can resolve phase-shifted or patterned modifications hidden in synthetic oligo benchmarks whose aggregate site-level signals are uninformative. Data are natural mRNA without per-read ground-truth modification labels — benchmark AUC cannot be computed without known even-cycle true positives The question is site-level stoichiometry in biological samples (e.g., GLORI correlation), not read-level pattern resolution on synthetic oligos Reads cover only a single modification status per site (~0% or ~100%), so any competent read-level caller separates them and the benchmark loses discriminating power http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark single-read m6A detection tools (mAFiA vs CHEUI and m6Anet) on synthetic TEST2 periodic-repeat dRNA-Seq reads, where GGACU sites are indistinguishable (~50% modification) at the aggregate site level, by computing precision-recall AUC against known even-cycle true positives. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47661-2
skills.summary: Benchmark single-read m6A detection tools (mAFiA vs CHEUI and m6Anet) on synthetic TEST2 periodic-repeat dRNA-Seq reads, where GGACU sites are indistinguishable (~50% modification) at the aggregate site level, by computing precision-recall AUC against known even-cycle true positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are natural mRNA without per-read ground-truth modification labels — benchmark AUC cannot be computed without known even-cycle true positives The question is site-level stoichiometry in biological samples (e.g., GLORI correlation), not read-level pattern resolution on synthetic oligos Reads cover only a single modification status per site (~0% or ~100%), so any competent read-level caller separates them and the benchmark loses discriminating power

skills.description: Use when you need labeled m6A/unm6A training examples for base-called-feature classifiers from ONT direct RNA data, e.g. training or reproducing EpiNano SVMs on synthetic RRACH k-mers where ground-truth modification status is known by design.
skills.name: synthetic-oligo-training-data-handling
skills.search_text: synthetic-oligo-training-data-handling Use when you need labeled m6A/unm6A training examples for base-called-feature classifiers from ONT direct RNA data, e.g. training or reproducing EpiNano SVMs on synthetic RRACH k-mers where ground-truth modification status is known by design. In vivo datasets without ground-truth modification labels — the article recommends pairing EpiNano with a matched control (WT vs KO/KD or demethylase-treated) instead of synthetic-oligo supervised training Per-read (single-molecule) modification calling — the algorithm aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and does not predict modifications in individual RNA molecules Analyses requiring manipulation of raw current intensity (squiggle realignment) — EpiNano works on base-called features without touching raw signal data http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares and uses in vitro synthetic RNA oligos with known m6A-modified and unmodified RRACH sites as ground-truth training data for EpiNano's SVM-based m6A classification on Oxford Nanopore direct RNA reads, exploiting base-called 'error' features (mismatch, deletion, base quality) rather than raw current signals. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Prepares and uses in vitro synthetic RNA oligos with known m6A-modified and unmodified RRACH sites as ground-truth training data for EpiNano's SVM-based m6A classification on Oxford Nanopore direct RNA reads, exploiting base-called 'error' features (mismatch, deletion, base quality) rather than raw current signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: In vivo datasets without ground-truth modification labels — the article recommends pairing EpiNano with a matched control (WT vs KO/KD or demethylase-treated) instead of synthetic-oligo supervised training Per-read (single-molecule) modification calling — the algorithm aggregates information from all reads mapping to a site and does not predict modifications in individual RNA molecules Analyses requiring manipulation of raw current intensity (squiggle realignment) — EpiNano works on base-called features without touching raw signal data

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth demultiplexing benchmarks: synthetic FASTQ reads with embedded barcodes at read ends to test scoring, acceptance thresholds, or trimming/demux correctness.
skills.name: synthetic-read-benchmark-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-read-benchmark-generation Use when you need ground-truth demultiplexing benchmarks: synthetic FASTQ reads with embedded barcodes at read ends to test scoring, acceptance thresholds, or trimming/demux correctness. Input is already demultiplexed or reads lack embedded barcode/flank constructs at read ends The goal is kit-level demultiplexing of real data with presets (use `barbell kit` instead of a custom synthetic benchmark) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates synthetic Nanopore-style FASTQ reads with known barcode/flank constructs embedded at read ends so that Barbell's subsequence-based barcode scoring and acceptance thresholds (score >=20% of perfect, >=10% separation from second-best) can be validated against ground-truth labels. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag349
skills.summary: Generates synthetic Nanopore-style FASTQ reads with known barcode/flank constructs embedded at read ends so that Barbell's subsequence-based barcode scoring and acceptance thresholds (score >=20% of perfect, >=10% separation from second-best) can be validated against ground-truth labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already demultiplexed or reads lack embedded barcode/flank constructs at read ends The goal is kit-level demultiplexing of real data with presets (use `barbell kit` instead of a custom synthetic benchmark)

skills.description: Use when validating a consensus/variant-calling pipeline on simulated ONT or PacBio reads, or when reproducing the SPOA partial-order-alignment error reduction of ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) reported in Supplementary Note S3 / Fig. S2.
skills.name: synthetic-read-benchmark-validation
skills.search_text: synthetic-read-benchmark-validation Use when validating a consensus/variant-calling pipeline on simulated ONT or PacBio reads, or when reproducing the SPOA partial-order-alignment error reduction of ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) reported in Supplementary Note S3 / Fig. S2. Input consists of real (non-simulated) long reads where the ground-truth per-base error rate is not known, making the raw-vs-consensus reduction denominator unreliable The goal is TR discovery/genotyping itself (use TRiCoLOR end-to-end) rather than validating the consensus step's error reduction http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark a long-read consensus computation by quantifying per-base error reduction between raw error-prone reads and POA-derived consensus sequences on simulated third-generation sequencing data, reproducing the ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) reduction reported for TRiCoLOR's REFER module. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Benchmark a long-read consensus computation by quantifying per-base error reduction between raw error-prone reads and POA-derived consensus sequences on simulated third-generation sequencing data, reproducing the ~77% (ONT) and ~88% (PB) reduction reported for TRiCoLOR's REFER module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of real (non-simulated) long reads where the ground-truth per-base error rate is not known, making the raw-vs-consensus reduction denominator unreliable The goal is TR discovery/genotyping itself (use TRiCoLOR end-to-end) rather than validating the consensus step's error reduction

skills.description: Use when you need to simulate nanopore raw signals from existing FASTA/FASTQ reads or a reference genome — e.g. to create synthetic R9.4.1/R10.4.1 chemistry data for benchmarking signal-comparison or basecalling pipelines.
skills.name: synthetic-read-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-read-generation Use when you need to simulate nanopore raw signals from existing FASTA/FASTQ reads or a reference genome — e.g. to create synthetic R9.4.1/R10.4.1 chemistry data for benchmarking signal-comparison or basecalling pipelines. You need basecalled sequences or variant-level simulation rather than raw signal squiggles — seq2squiggle outputs signal data, not consensus reads. The goal is to preserve exact read sequences while adding signal variability but splitting reads is required — Read mode samples input reads without splitting them. Static k-mer-model simulation fidelity is explicitly acceptable and a lightweight CPU tool is preferred over a transformer model with model-weight downloads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generate artificial nanopore sequencing signals (raw squiggles in BLOW5/POD5) from nucleotide sequences using seq2squiggle, a transformer-based, non-autoregressive simulator, so that simulated signals can be benchmarked against real experimental reads (e.g. via DTW distance). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Generate artificial nanopore sequencing signals (raw squiggles in BLOW5/POD5) from nucleotide sequences using seq2squiggle, a transformer-based, non-autoregressive simulator, so that simulated signals can be benchmarked against real experimental reads (e.g. via DTW distance).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need basecalled sequences or variant-level simulation rather than raw signal squiggles — seq2squiggle outputs signal data, not consensus reads. The goal is to preserve exact read sequences while adding signal variability but splitting reads is required — Read mode samples input reads without splitting them. Static k-mer-model simulation fidelity is explicitly acceptable and a lightweight CPU tool is preferred over a transformer model with model-weight downloads.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking read mappers (e.g. GraphMap vs BWA-MEM, LAST, BLASR, DALIGNER, BLAST) against ground truth, and you need synthetic long reads spanning diverse error profiles (Illumina, PacBio, ONT 1D/2D) with known true origins.
skills.name: synthetic-read-simulation-error-profiles
skills.search_text: synthetic-read-simulation-error-profiles Use when benchmarking read mappers (e.g. GraphMap vs BWA-MEM, LAST, BLASR, DALIGNER, BLAST) against ground truth, and you need synthetic long reads spanning diverse error profiles (Illumina, PacBio, ONT 1D/2D) with known true origins. When the evaluation question is mapping runtime or sensitivity on real sequencing runs where true read origins are unknown (real-data tests use src/run-realdata.py instead of simulations) When the goal is production mapping of a real sample — simulated error profiles from ART/PBSIM may not reproduce the error spectrum of a specific MinION flow cell, so conclusions should not be transferred directly When only short, low-error Illumina reads with an established mapper benchmark are involved — the mappers compared here (GraphMap, BLASR, DALIGNER) target long, error-prone third-generation reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Generate simulated sequencing reads with known ground-truth origins using ART (Illumina) and PBSIM (PacBio, ONT 1D/2D) so that mapper precision, recall, and per-base alignment accuracy can be measured exactly against simulated truth positions rather than uncertain real-data labels. genomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11307
skills.summary: Generate simulated sequencing reads with known ground-truth origins using ART (Illumina) and PBSIM (PacBio, ONT 1D/2D) so that mapper precision, recall, and per-base alignment accuracy can be measured exactly against simulated truth positions rather than uncertain real-data labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the evaluation question is mapping runtime or sensitivity on real sequencing runs where true read origins are unknown (real-data tests use src/run-realdata.py instead of simulations) When the goal is production mapping of a real sample — simulated error profiles from ART/PBSIM may not reproduce the error spectrum of a specific MinION flow cell, so conclusions should not be transferred directly When only short, low-error Illumina reads with an established mapper benchmark are involved — the mappers compared here (GraphMap, BLASR, DALIGNER) target long, error-prone third-generation reads

skills.description: Use when a single-nucleotide m6A classifier needs read-level ground-truth labels from synthetic RNA oligos whose modification status per nucleotide is precisely controlled, especially for train-on-RL/test-on-SL generalization tests across unseen DRACH contexts.
skills.name: synthetic-rna-oligo-read-labeling
skills.search_text: synthetic-rna-oligo-read-labeling Use when a single-nucleotide m6A classifier needs read-level ground-truth labels from synthetic RNA oligos whose modification status per nucleotide is precisely controlled, especially for train-on-RL/test-on-SL generalization tests across unseen DRACH contexts. Input is natural mRNA without per-nucleotide modification ground truth (approximate labels only, e.g. miCLIP2-style sites) — read-level y=0/y=1 labels cannot be justified The goal is site-level stoichiometry on biological samples (use mAFiA site-level pileup with min_coverage 50 and P(m6A) threshold 0.5 instead of training labels) The target modification is outside m6A in DRACH motifs (e.g. pseudouridine in GUUCN-like motifs — use psi-co-mAFiA motifs instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Generates read-level ground-truth m6A labels by basecalling direct RNA-Seq reads from synthetic UNM/MOD oligo pairs (random-ligation and splint-ligation) with a RODAN backbone, extracting 768-dim features per target-motif nucleotide, and assigning y=0/y=1 labels for classifier training and cross-context validation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47661-2
skills.summary: Generates read-level ground-truth m6A labels by basecalling direct RNA-Seq reads from synthetic UNM/MOD oligo pairs (random-ligation and splint-ligation) with a RODAN backbone, extracting 768-dim features per target-motif nucleotide, and assigning y=0/y=1 labels for classifier training and cross-context validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is natural mRNA without per-nucleotide modification ground truth (approximate labels only, e.g. miCLIP2-style sites) — read-level y=0/y=1 labels cannot be justified The goal is site-level stoichiometry on biological samples (use mAFiA site-level pileup with min_coverage 50 and P(m6A) threshold 0.5 instead of training labels) The target modification is outside m6A in DRACH motifs (e.g. pseudouridine in GUUCN-like motifs — use psi-co-mAFiA motifs instead)

skills.description: Use when synthetic RNA sequences intended for training or benchmarking a base-calling/modification-detection model must be checked for complete k-mer coverage and minimized secondary structure before training.
skills.name: synthetic-sequence-design-validation
skills.search_text: synthetic-sequence-design-validation Use when synthetic RNA sequences intended for training or benchmarking a base-calling/modification-detection model must be checked for complete k-mer coverage and minimized secondary structure before training. Input is already a curated training dataset with documented k-mer coverage — no re-validation needed Goal is per-read modification prediction quality assessment rather than validation of the synthetic training set itself The sequences are natural transcripts (e.g. yeast mRNAs), which cannot be k-mer-complete by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Verify that synthetic training sequences (e.g. the 'curlcake' sequences used to train EpiNano's m6A SVM models) cover the complete k-mer space — all 1024 possible RNA 5-mers — while keeping RNA secondary structure (minimum free energy) minimized, so that an algorithm trained on them is not biased toward specific sequence contexts. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-11713-9
skills.summary: Verify that synthetic training sequences (e.g. the 'curlcake' sequences used to train EpiNano's m6A SVM models) cover the complete k-mer space — all 1024 possible RNA 5-mers — while keeping RNA secondary structure (minimum free energy) minimized, so that an algorithm trained on them is not biased toward specific sequence contexts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated training dataset with documented k-mer coverage — no re-validation needed Goal is per-read modification prediction quality assessment rather than validation of the synthetic training set itself The sequences are natural transcripts (e.g. yeast mRNAs), which cannot be k-mer-complete by design

skills.description: Use when testing a reconstructed CONSENT-style polishing module: you need to confirm that weak-k-mer regions between solid anchors are corrected via local de Bruijn graph paths, and left unchanged otherwise.
skills.name: synthetic-sequence-polishing-validation
skills.search_text: synthetic-sequence-polishing-validation Use when testing a reconstructed CONSENT-style polishing module: you need to confirm that weak-k-mer regions between solid anchors are corrected via local de Bruijn graph paths, and left unchanged otherwise. Input is a full long-read correction job rather than a single-window polishing validation — use the complete CONSENT-correct pipeline instead Sequences contain no detectable weak k-mer regions, so there is nothing to polish and the validation invariant cannot be exercised You need assembly polishing of contigs against reads — use CONSENT-polish on contig/read FASTA files rather than this synthetic validation setup http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Validates a reimplementation of CONSENT's consensus-polishing phase by running the local de Bruijn graph polishing on small synthetic window sequences and checking that weak k-mer regions are replaced only when a solid-anchor-flanked path exists. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Validates a reimplementation of CONSENT's consensus-polishing phase by running the local de Bruijn graph polishing on small synthetic window sequences and checking that weak k-mer regions are replaced only when a solid-anchor-flanked path exists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a full long-read correction job rather than a single-window polishing validation — use the complete CONSENT-correct pipeline instead Sequences contain no detectable weak k-mer regions, so there is nothing to polish and the validation invariant cannot be exercised You need assembly polishing of contigs against reads — use CONSENT-polish on contig/read FASTA files rather than this synthetic validation setup

skills.description: Use when coverage-based significance p-values for candidate structural variants fall below R's smallest representable positive double (2.225074e-308) and would round to zero with normal precision.
skills.name: t-distribution-tail-probability-computation
skills.search_text: t-distribution-tail-probability-computation Use when coverage-based significance p-values for candidate structural variants fall below R's smallest representable positive double (2.225074e-308) and would round to zero with normal precision. p-values lie within the normal double range (> 2.225074e-308), so direct R computation without Rmpfr suffices SVs other than deletions and duplications — disCoverage's coverage analysis 'can only check deletions and duplications' No putative SV positions are available — disCoverage 'is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions, which could be obtained from an additional technique' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Recover two-tailed Welch t-test p-values from disCoverage's coverage significance analysis that underflow R's smallest positive double (2.225074e-308), by evaluating ln(p) = 2*cdf(-|t|, df) in log space and exponentiating with Rmpfr at 100 bits of precision (down to ~1e-13482). genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Recover two-tailed Welch t-test p-values from disCoverage's coverage significance analysis that underflow R's smallest positive double (2.225074e-308), by evaluating ln(p) = 2*cdf(-|t|, df) in log space and exponentiating with Rmpfr at 100 bits of precision (down to ~1e-13482).
skills.when_to_use_negative: p-values lie within the normal double range (> 2.225074e-308), so direct R computation without Rmpfr suffices SVs other than deletions and duplications — disCoverage's coverage analysis 'can only check deletions and duplications' No putative SV positions are available — disCoverage 'is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions, which could be obtained from an additional technique'
