skills.name: t2t-sv-benchmark-preprocessing
skills.search_text: t2t-sv-benchmark-preprocessing Use when benchmarking long-read SV callers (e.g., sawfish, Sniffles2, pbsv) against the GIAB T2T-HG002-Q100 SV benchmark and the raw VCF/BED truth files must be filtered to SV records on autosomes first. The truth set is the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark (HG002_GRCh38_CMRG_SV_v1.00), which in this workflow uses truvari bench alone without the SVTYPE and autosomal filtering steps You need to assess SVs on sex chromosomes, since the confident regions are deliberately restricted to autosomes here Comparing callsets with a different evaluation engine (e.g., hap-eval) that does not require the truvari-specific base/includebed preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Preprocesses the GIAB draft T2T SV benchmark (GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1_stvar) so it can be used with truvari bench: retains only structural-variant records via bcftools and restricts the confident-region BED to autosomes, yielding a clean truth set for HiFi SV caller benchmarking. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf136
skills.summary: Preprocesses the GIAB draft T2T SV benchmark (GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1_stvar) so it can be used with truvari bench: retains only structural-variant records via bcftools and restricts the confident-region BED to autosomes, yielding a clean truth set for HiFi SV caller benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The truth set is the GIAB CMRG SV benchmark (HG002_GRCh38_CMRG_SV_v1.00), which in this workflow uses truvari bench alone without the SVTYPE and autosomal filtering steps You need to assess SVs on sex chromosomes, since the confident regions are deliberately restricted to autosomes here Comparing callsets with a different evaluation engine (e.g., hap-eval) that does not require the truvari-specific base/includebed preprocessing

skills.description: Use when analyzing full-length PacBio Iso-seq/PAIso-seq CCS reads to test whether non-adenosine residues occur inside poly(A) tail bodies, by classifying T30VN RT-primer anchoring as terminal versus internal (non-A) positions.
skills.name: t30vn-internal-priming-anchoring-classification
skills.search_text: t30vn-internal-priming-anchoring-classification Use when analyzing full-length PacBio Iso-seq/PAIso-seq CCS reads to test whether non-adenosine residues occur inside poly(A) tail bodies, by classifying T30VN RT-primer anchoring as terminal versus internal (non-A) positions. Input reads lack CCS pass counts or fail the >=10 passes requirement, since base-calling accuracy of tail non-A residues cannot be trusted The goal is to quantify non-A modifications at the very last 3'-end tail base, which PAIso-seq cannot accurately measure because terminal G/C/U pair to the adaptor and are lost Data are short-read Illumina-based (e.g., PAL-seq on the discontinued Illumina Genome Analyzer II) rather than full-length PacBio cDNA reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classifies PAIso-seq reads by where the T30VN reverse-transcription primer anchored on the poly(A) tail, distinguishing terminal anchoring from internal anchoring on non-adenosine residues within the poly(A) tail body. This validates the existence of non-A residues inside tails in independent datasets such as the pepper Iso-seq data (CRA001412), where ~5% of transcripts show VN base pairing with internal tail nucleotides. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13228-9
skills.summary: Classifies PAIso-seq reads by where the T30VN reverse-transcription primer anchored on the poly(A) tail, distinguishing terminal anchoring from internal anchoring on non-adenosine residues within the poly(A) tail body. This validates the existence of non-A residues inside tails in independent datasets such as the pepper Iso-seq data (CRA001412), where ~5% of transcripts show VN base pairing with internal tail nucleotides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack CCS pass counts or fail the >=10 passes requirement, since base-calling accuracy of tail non-A residues cannot be trusted The goal is to quantify non-A modifications at the very last 3'-end tail base, which PAIso-seq cannot accurately measure because terminal G/C/U pair to the adaptor and are lost Data are short-read Illumina-based (e.g., PAL-seq on the discontinued Illumina Genome Analyzer II) rather than full-length PacBio cDNA reads

skills.description: Use when comparing coverage breadth (unique genomic positions) between two or more platforms — e.g., DeepBAM/Dorado nanopore TSV calls vs BS-seq methylation tables — across multiple matched datasets.
skills.name: tabular-aggregation-across-datasets
skills.search_text: tabular-aggregation-across-datasets Use when comparing coverage breadth (unique genomic positions) between two or more platforms — e.g., DeepBAM/Dorado nanopore TSV calls vs BS-seq methylation tables — across multiple matched datasets. The goal is per-read single-molecule methylation state calling rather than aggregating calls to unique genomic CpG positions The comparison is of methylation frequency correlation with BS-seq (a different skill; DeepBAM targets >0.95 correlation there), not coverage breadth http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Aggregates per-dataset tabular methylation call outputs into a unified CpG coverage comparison table, counting unique CpG sites per platform across human and plant datasets to test whether nanopore resolves more CpGs than BS-seq. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae413
skills.summary: Aggregates per-dataset tabular methylation call outputs into a unified CpG coverage comparison table, counting unique CpG sites per platform across human and plant datasets to test whether nanopore resolves more CpGs than BS-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-read single-molecule methylation state calling rather than aggregating calls to unique genomic CpG positions The comparison is of methylation frequency correlation with BS-seq (a different skill; DeepBAM targets >0.95 correlation there), not coverage breadth

skills.description: Use when a tabular association table (disease-gene pairs from GutUDB's DISEASES module) must be tallied per category and intersected across groups to find shared genes such as STK11, CFTR, APC.
skills.name: tabular-data-aggregation
skills.search_text: tabular-data-aggregation Use when a tabular association table (disease-gene pairs from GutUDB's DISEASES module) must be tallied per category and intersected across groups to find shared genes such as STK11, CFTR, APC. The input is raw omics profiles (e.g., the ~9 million genomics/transcriptomics profiles) rather than curated association tables — other GutUDB modules apply The goal is drug-disease interaction analysis (21,984 THERAPY module interactions), not disease-gene association counting You need statistical association testing (p-values, enrichment) rather than deterministic set operations and counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Aggregate GutUDB's DISEASES module records into per-disease gene-association counts and a shared-gene intersection using pandas, reproducing the article's reported 260,790 disease-gene associations. genomics/v1 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Aggregate GutUDB's DISEASES module records into per-disease gene-association counts and a shared-gene intersection using pandas, reproducing the article's reported 260,790 disease-gene associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw omics profiles (e.g., the ~9 million genomics/transcriptomics profiles) rather than curated association tables — other GutUDB modules apply The goal is drug-disease interaction analysis (21,984 THERAPY module interactions), not disease-gene association counting You need statistical association testing (p-values, enrichment) rather than deterministic set operations and counts

skills.description: Use when producing or validating a VIBE-style ranked gene output: a tab-delimited file ordered by descending highest GDA score carrying gene (NCBI), gene symbol (HGNC) and diseases (UMLS) columns.
skills.name: tabular-output-formatting-for-genome-diagnostics
skills.search_text: tabular-output-formatting-for-genome-diagnostics Use when producing or validating a VIBE-style ranked gene output: a tab-delimited file ordered by descending highest GDA score carrying gene (NCBI), gene symbol (HGNC) and diseases (UMLS) columns. The input is a ranked gene list from another prioritization tool (e.g., Phenomizer, hiPHIVE, GADO benchmark output) that must first be converted from HGNC symbols to NCBI gene IDs via the BenchmarkFileGeneSymbolToIdConverter workflow rather than re-formatted by VIBE. The consumer needs an interactive user interface rather than a file artifact; use the molgenis-app-vibe web application instead of the tabular command-line output. http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Emits VIBE's prioritized gene list as a tab-delimited results file (e.g., results.tsv) in which genes are ordered by descending highest GDA score, so downstream pipeline modules and human curators can consume the ranked candidates reproducibly. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Emits VIBE's prioritized gene list as a tab-delimited results file (e.g., results.tsv) in which genes are ordered by descending highest GDA score, so downstream pipeline modules and human curators can consume the ranked candidates reproducibly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a ranked gene list from another prioritization tool (e.g., Phenomizer, hiPHIVE, GADO benchmark output) that must first be converted from HGNC symbols to NCBI gene IDs via the BenchmarkFileGeneSymbolToIdConverter workflow rather than re-formatted by VIBE. The consumer needs an interactive user interface rather than a file artifact; use the molgenis-app-vibe web application instead of the tabular command-line output.

skills.description: Use when a long-read isoform catalog (e.g. PacBio lrCaptureSeq abundance tables processed with IsoPops) must be reduced to per-gene isoform counts, total distinct isoforms, and per-experiment read totals for export or comparison with public annotations.
skills.name: tabular-summary-export
skills.search_text: tabular-summary-export Use when a long-read isoform catalog (e.g. PacBio lrCaptureSeq abundance tables processed with IsoPops) must be reduced to per-gene isoform counts, total distinct isoforms, and per-experiment read totals for export or comparison with public annotations. The input is short-read RNA-seq data only: typical RNA-seq read lengths (<200 bp) cannot resolve full-length sequences of multi-kilobase transcripts, so per-gene full-length isoform counts cannot be computed this way. You need quantitative isoform expression time/place mapping via single-cell integration rather than a static catalog summary. The database still contains off-target or truncated transcripts and you have not yet run the IsoPots filtering steps (filter_db, filter_truncations) that precede a defensible summary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Summarize the lrCaptureSeq isoform catalog produced by the IsoPops pipeline into a per-gene isoform-count table plus catalog-wide and per-experiment read totals, exported to a CSV (catalog_summary.csv). It quantifies how many mRNA isoforms the 30 targeted genes yield relative to public annotations. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: Summarize the lrCaptureSeq isoform catalog produced by the IsoPops pipeline into a per-gene isoform-count table plus catalog-wide and per-experiment read totals, exported to a CSV (catalog_summary.csv). It quantifies how many mRNA isoforms the 30 targeted genes yield relative to public annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read RNA-seq data only: typical RNA-seq read lengths (<200 bp) cannot resolve full-length sequences of multi-kilobase transcripts, so per-gene full-length isoform counts cannot be computed this way. You need quantitative isoform expression time/place mapping via single-cell integration rather than a static catalog summary. The database still contains off-target or truncated transcripts and you have not yet run the IsoPots filtering steps (filter_db, filter_truncations) that precede a defensible summary.

skills.description: Use when long-read sequencing data are suspected to carry a large tandem duplication (e.g. an unintended duplication in a knock-out line) and split-read or soft-clip evidence in a BAM must be converted into precise breakpoint coordinates.
skills.name: tandem-duplication-annotation
skills.search_text: tandem-duplication-annotation Use when long-read sequencing data are suspected to carry a large tandem duplication (e.g. an unintended duplication in a knock-out line) and split-read or soft-clip evidence in a BAM must be converted into precise breakpoint coordinates. The variant of interest is a small indel or SNV resolvable with short-read sequencing data, rather than a large-scale rearrangement requiring long reads. No sorted, indexed alignment BAM exists and reads have not been aligned with a long-read-specific aligner such as minimap2 or lra. The task is bulk automated SV calling across many samples rather than user-guided inspection and annotation of a specific breakpoint event. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Annotate large-scale tandem duplications from aligned long-read (PacBio/ONT) data by user-guided inspection of split and soft-clipped reads in AgileStructure, then validate the resulting SV coordinates against published breakpoints. Demonstrated on the Agmo knockout mouse dataset (SRR12783028) where AgileStructure recovered chr12:37,206,133_37,300,424dup. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag294
skills.summary: Annotate large-scale tandem duplications from aligned long-read (PacBio/ONT) data by user-guided inspection of split and soft-clipped reads in AgileStructure, then validate the resulting SV coordinates against published breakpoints. Demonstrated on the Agmo knockout mouse dataset (SRR12783028) where AgileStructure recovered chr12:37,206,133_37,300,424dup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant of interest is a small indel or SNV resolvable with short-read sequencing data, rather than a large-scale rearrangement requiring long reads. No sorted, indexed alignment BAM exists and reads have not been aligned with a long-read-specific aligner such as minimap2 or lra. The task is bulk automated SV calling across many samples rather than user-guided inspection and annotation of a specific breakpoint event.

skills.description: Use when processing isoCirc RCA nanopore reads (FASTA/FASTQ) where each read contains tandem copies of a circular RNA template and a per-read consensus sequence must be derived before BSJ and full-length isoform calling.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-consensus-calling
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-consensus-calling Use when processing isoCirc RCA nanopore reads (FASTA/FASTQ) where each read contains tandem copies of a circular RNA template and a per-read consensus sequence must be derived before BSJ and full-length isoform calling. Input reads are not RCA-derived (e.g. direct RNA or linear cDNA long reads) — the tandem-repeat consensus model assumes repeated copies of the same circular template within each read CircRNAs have already been consensus-called and you only need downstream BSJ/isoform filtering — applying TRF again is redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Builds consensus sequences from rolling-circle-amplified (RCA) isoCirc nanopore reads by treating each read's repeated circRNA copies as tandem repeats and calling a consensus with Tandem Repeats Finder, then filtering and mapping the consensus with minimap2. This converts noisy multi-copy long reads into full-length circRNA isoform sequences suitable for BSJ identification. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Builds consensus sequences from rolling-circle-amplified (RCA) isoCirc nanopore reads by treating each read's repeated circRNA copies as tandem repeats and calling a consensus with Tandem Repeats Finder, then filtering and mapping the consensus with minimap2. This converts noisy multi-copy long reads into full-length circRNA isoform sequences suitable for BSJ identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not RCA-derived (e.g. direct RNA or linear cDNA long reads) — the tandem-repeat consensus model assumes repeated copies of the same circular template within each read CircRNAs have already been consensus-called and you only need downstream BSJ/isoform filtering — applying TRF again is redundant

skills.description: Use when long-read FASTA reads are suspected to contain mosaic tandem repeats (e.g. disease-associated STRs like SAMD12 (AAAAT)23 or RFC1 (AAAAG)11) and you need unit-level decomposition plus a TRF comparison.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-decomposition-from-long-reads
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-decomposition-from-long-reads Use when long-read FASTA reads are suspected to contain mosaic tandem repeats (e.g. disease-associated STRs like SAMD12 (AAAAT)23 or RFC1 (AAAAG)11) and you need unit-level decomposition plus a TRF comparison. Tandem repeat units longer than 20 nt need to be estimated: use mTR instead, since uTR without -u only automatically estimates units of length 20 nt or less The goal is a concise pattern for reads already annotated with an estimated mosaic pattern — use vTR, which outputs series of variant units rather than a decomposition Input is not FASTA read data but simulated pattern checks or RepeatMasker parse outputs from the test_public pipeline (use the gendata/check_uTR/parse_RepeatMasker workflow instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reproduces uTR-based decomposition of mosaic tandem repeats (different repeat units mixed in one string) from long-read FASTA data, benchmarking uTR against TRF. Grounded in the SAMD12, RFC1, KAZN and ZNF37A mosaic repeats from realdata/realdata.fasta of the morisUtokyo/uTR repository. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Reproduces uTR-based decomposition of mosaic tandem repeats (different repeat units mixed in one string) from long-read FASTA data, benchmarking uTR against TRF. Grounded in the SAMD12, RFC1, KAZN and ZNF37A mosaic repeats from realdata/realdata.fasta of the morisUtokyo/uTR repository.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tandem repeat units longer than 20 nt need to be estimated: use mTR instead, since uTR without -u only automatically estimates units of length 20 nt or less The goal is a concise pattern for reads already annotated with an estimated mosaic pattern — use vTR, which outputs series of variant units rather than a decomposition Input is not FASTA read data but simulated pattern checks or RepeatMasker parse outputs from the test_public pipeline (use the gendata/check_uTR/parse_RepeatMasker workflow instead)

skills.description: Use when raw or consensus nanopore reads (FASTA from chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq output) need to be scanned for tandem repeats to compare repeat prevalence or length distributions across chemistries (2D vs 1D2) or aligner choices.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-feature-detection
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-feature-detection Use when raw or consensus nanopore reads (FASTA from chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq output) need to be scanned for tandem repeats to compare repeat prevalence or length distributions across chemistries (2D vs 1D2) or aligner choices. Input is raw noisy nanopore reads that have not been through INC-Seq consensus calling and chopSeq orientation correction — repeat calls would be dominated by sequencing noise rather than true tandem repeat features The goal is homopolymer region error analysis rather than tandem repeat feature detection — residual errors in NanoAmpli-Seq sequences originate from homopolymer deletions and need a different assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Detects and characterizes tandem repeat features in chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads from Oxford Nanopore 2D and 1D2 amplicon sequencing using the etandem detector, quantifying repeat prevalence and contrasting unimodal (2D) versus bimodal (1D2) repeat length distributions. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: Detects and characterizes tandem repeat features in chopSeq-corrected INC-Seq consensus reads from Oxford Nanopore 2D and 1D2 amplicon sequencing using the etandem detector, quantifying repeat prevalence and contrasting unimodal (2D) versus bimodal (1D2) repeat length distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw noisy nanopore reads that have not been through INC-Seq consensus calling and chopSeq orientation correction — repeat calls would be dominated by sequencing noise rather than true tandem repeat features The goal is homopolymer region error analysis rather than tandem repeat feature detection — residual errors in NanoAmpli-Seq sequences originate from homopolymer deletions and need a different assessment

skills.description: Use when profiling tandem repeats de novo from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments (ONT or PacBio BAMs) with no annotated motifs or positions, and per-haplotype genotypes are needed.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-genotyping-from-long-reads
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-genotyping-from-long-reads Use when profiling tandem repeats de novo from haplotype-resolved long-read alignments (ONT or PacBio BAMs) with no annotated motifs or positions, and per-haplotype genotypes are needed. Target repeats lie in unassembled regions such as human centromeres or telomeres, where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats. The genome is polyploid or contains haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. The profiled repeats are mini-satellites rather than micro-satellites, since TRiCoLOR has been extensively applied so far only to micro-satellites. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 De novo identification and genotyping of tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved ONT/PacBio long-read BAMs using TRiCoLOR's two modules, SENSoR (Shannon-entropy detection of repetitive regions) and REFER (POA consensus plus RegEx-based motif/multiplicity resolution), producing BCF-compliant TR calls without prior knowledge of motifs or locations. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: De novo identification and genotyping of tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved ONT/PacBio long-read BAMs using TRiCoLOR's two modules, SENSoR (Shannon-entropy detection of repetitive regions) and REFER (POA consensus plus RegEx-based motif/multiplicity resolution), producing BCF-compliant TR calls without prior knowledge of motifs or locations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target repeats lie in unassembled regions such as human centromeres or telomeres, where TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats. The genome is polyploid or contains haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. The profiled repeats are mini-satellites rather than micro-satellites, since TRiCoLOR has been extensively applied so far only to micro-satellites.

skills.description: Use when haplotype-resolved long-read (PacBio or ONT) BAM alignments are available and genome-wide, de novo TR motifs, multiplicities, and genotypes must be called without prior motif or locus annotation.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-motif-genotyping
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-motif-genotyping Use when haplotype-resolved long-read (PacBio or ONT) BAM alignments are available and genome-wide, de novo TR motifs, multiplicities, and genotypes must be called without prior motif or locus annotation. The target repeats lie in unassembled regions such as human centromeres or telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot profile. The organism is polyploid or the target chromosome is haploid (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. Only short-read data are available and no haplotype-resolved long-read alignments exist, since TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved long-read alignments as input. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 De novo identification and haplotype-resolved genotyping of tandem repeats (TRs) from error-prone long-read alignments using TRiCoLOR's SENSoR, REFER, and SAGE modules, with optional Mendelian-consistency tracing in trios. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: De novo identification and haplotype-resolved genotyping of tandem repeats (TRs) from error-prone long-read alignments using TRiCoLOR's SENSoR, REFER, and SAGE modules, with optional Mendelian-consistency tracing in trios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target repeats lie in unassembled regions such as human centromeres or telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot profile. The organism is polyploid or the target chromosome is haploid (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. Only short-read data are available and no haplotype-resolved long-read alignments exist, since TRiCoLOR requires haplotype-resolved long-read alignments as input.

skills.description: Use when you have VCF-style variant call sets from two or more simulators (e.g. seq2squiggle vs squigulator) and need to stratify TP/FP calls by repeat context (homopolymer, TRF, neither) to explain error patterns.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-region-annotation
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-region-annotation Use when you have VCF-style variant call sets from two or more simulators (e.g. seq2squiggle vs squigulator) and need to stratify TP/FP calls by repeat context (homopolymer, TRF, neither) to explain error patterns. Input is raw nanopore signal data (BLOW5/POD5) rather than a processed variant call set — annotation requires called variant positions The reference genome has no TRF annotation available and generating one is out of scope; homopolymer-only stratification would be a simpler alternative Variant calls come from a single simulator, preventing the per-simulator comparison that motivates the classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Annotate variant call positions against tandem repeat (TRF) and homopolymer (runs of >=5 identical bases) regions, then classify true-positive and false-positive SNV/indel calls per region class to evaluate simulator-dependent variant-calling accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Annotate variant call positions against tandem repeat (TRF) and homopolymer (runs of >=5 identical bases) regions, then classify true-positive and false-positive SNV/indel calls per region class to evaluate simulator-dependent variant-calling accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore signal data (BLOW5/POD5) rather than a processed variant call set — annotation requires called variant positions The reference genome has no TRF annotation available and generating one is out of scope; homopolymer-only stratification would be a simpler alternative Variant calls come from a single simulator, preventing the per-simulator comparison that motivates the classification

skills.description: Use when you need to identify and genotype tandem repeats de novo from haplotype-resolved BAM files of error-prone long reads (ONT or PacBio), without prior knowledge of repeat motifs or genomic locations.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-region-profiling
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-region-profiling Use when you need to identify and genotype tandem repeats de novo from haplotype-resolved BAM files of error-prone long reads (ONT or PacBio), without prior knowledge of repeat motifs or genomic locations. You need to detect repeats in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres and telomeres — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there. Your data is from a polyploid species or a haploid chromosome (e.g., the human Y chromosome) — TRiCoLOR assumes diploid haplotype-resolved input. Your input is short-read (Illumina) alignments or non-haplotype-resolved BAMs — the workflow requires haplotype-resolved error-prone long-read alignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 De novo profiling of tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved ONT/PacBio long-read alignments using TRiCoLOR: Shannon-entropy scanning identifies candidate repetitive regions, POA-based consensus sequences correct raw read errors, and a RegEx-based approximate string-matching step resolves repeat motif and multiplicity per haplotype. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: De novo profiling of tandem repeats from haplotype-resolved ONT/PacBio long-read alignments using TRiCoLOR: Shannon-entropy scanning identifies candidate repetitive regions, POA-based consensus sequences correct raw read errors, and a RegEx-based approximate string-matching step resolves repeat motif and multiplicity per haplotype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to detect repeats in unassembled genomic regions such as human centromeres and telomeres — TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats there. Your data is from a polyploid species or a haploid chromosome (e.g., the human Y chromosome) — TRiCoLOR assumes diploid haplotype-resolved input. Your input is short-read (Illumina) alignments or non-haplotype-resolved BAMs — the workflow requires haplotype-resolved error-prone long-read alignments.

skills.description: Use when you need simulated mosaic tandem repeat reads with correct-answer patterns to benchmark TR decomposition tools (uTR vs TRF vs RepeatMasker) for accuracy or runtime across unit-count ranges and error rates.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-sequence-simulation
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-sequence-simulation Use when you need simulated mosaic tandem repeat reads with correct-answer patterns to benchmark TR decomposition tools (uTR vs TRF vs RepeatMasker) for accuracy or runtime across unit-count ranges and error rates. Input is real long-read data (e.g. realdata/realdata.fasta or SAND12 BAFME reads) rather than synthetic benchmarks — run the uTR/mTR/cTR analysis pipeline instead The goal is to decompose reads with repeat units longer than 20 nt — simulation with gendata targets short-unit mosaic TRs; use mTR for long units You only need accuracy evaluation of an already-generated dataset — use check_uTR/check_RepeatMasker rather than re-simulating http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Generate synthetic mosaic tandem repeat datasets with known ground-truth patterns (e.g. (AC)m(AG)n) using gendata from the uTR test_public suite, varying the m/n ranges and sequencing error rate to benchmark tools like uTR, TRF and RepeatMasker. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Generate synthetic mosaic tandem repeat datasets with known ground-truth patterns (e.g. (AC)m(AG)n) using gendata from the uTR test_public suite, varying the m/n ranges and sequencing error rate to benchmark tools like uTR, TRF and RepeatMasker.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real long-read data (e.g. realdata/realdata.fasta or SAND12 BAFME reads) rather than synthetic benchmarks — run the uTR/mTR/cTR analysis pipeline instead The goal is to decompose reads with repeat units longer than 20 nt — simulation with gendata targets short-unit mosaic TRs; use mTR for long units You only need accuracy evaluation of an already-generated dataset — use check_uTR/check_RepeatMasker rather than re-simulating

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth benchmark data for evaluating tandem repeat decomposition tools: simulate mosaic TRs of known patterns with controlled occurrence ranges and substitution error rates.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-synthetic-dataset-generation
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-synthetic-dataset-generation Use when you need ground-truth benchmark data for evaluating tandem repeat decomposition tools: simulate mosaic TRs of known patterns with controlled occurrence ranges and substitution error rates. You need to characterize mosaic TRs in real long reads (use uTR directly, optionally with cTR pre-clustering and mTR for long units) rather than benchmark decomposition accuracy Input data already has ground-truth repeat decomposition (use check_uTR/check_RepeatMasker scoring instead of generating new simulations) http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates synthetic mosaic tandem repeat benchmark datasets using the gendata utility from the uTR repository, producing FASTA files of simulated strings built from known mosaic TR patterns (e.g. (AC)i(AG)j) with injected substitution errors, to provide ground truth for evaluating decomposition tools like uTR, TRF, and RepeatMasker. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Generates synthetic mosaic tandem repeat benchmark datasets using the gendata utility from the uTR repository, producing FASTA files of simulated strings built from known mosaic TR patterns (e.g. (AC)i(AG)j) with injected substitution errors, to provide ground truth for evaluating decomposition tools like uTR, TRF, and RepeatMasker.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to characterize mosaic TRs in real long reads (use uTR directly, optionally with cTR pre-clustering and mTR for long units) rather than benchmark decomposition accuracy Input data already has ground-truth repeat decomposition (use check_uTR/check_RepeatMasker scoring instead of generating new simulations)

skills.description: Use when long-read (e.g. PacBio) FASTA sequences contain mosaic tandem repeats with multiple different repeat units that standard tools like TRF or RepeatMasker fail to decompose correctly.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-unit-decomposition
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-unit-decomposition Use when long-read (e.g. PacBio) FASTA sequences contain mosaic tandem repeats with multiple different repeat units that standard tools like TRF or RepeatMasker fail to decompose correctly. Input is a single simple (non-mosaic) tandem repeat with one unit — TRF or RepeatMasker suffice and mosaic-unit selection is unnecessary The mismatch ratio between the representative unit and the tandem repeat exceeds the -r threshold (default 0.3) — uTR outputs no tandem repeat at all The goal is inspecting per-unit substitutions/indels in a known decomposition rather than computing it — vTR, not uTR, outputs variant units from an already-estimated pattern http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A skill for decomposing DNA strings into mosaic tandem repeats composed of different repeat units using the uTR algorithm, which greedily selects repeat units and then computes an optimal partial-match decomposition. It outperforms TRF and RepeatMasker, especially on complex mosaic TRs with three or more series of units. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: A skill for decomposing DNA strings into mosaic tandem repeats composed of different repeat units using the uTR algorithm, which greedily selects repeat units and then computes an optimal partial-match decomposition. It outperforms TRF and RepeatMasker, especially on complex mosaic TRs with three or more series of units.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single simple (non-mosaic) tandem repeat with one unit — TRF or RepeatMasker suffice and mosaic-unit selection is unnecessary The mismatch ratio between the representative unit and the tandem repeat exceeds the -r threshold (default 0.3) — uTR outputs no tandem repeat at all The goal is inspecting per-unit substitutions/indels in a known decomposition rather than computing it — vTR, not uTR, outputs variant units from an already-estimated pattern

skills.description: Use when a DNA read (e.g. S=ACCGACCGACCG) must be decomposed into mosaic tandem repeat units and you need a principled, penalty-driven criterion for choosing which unit strings to include in the decomposition.
skills.name: tandem-repeat-unit-selection
skills.search_text: tandem-repeat-unit-selection Use when a DNA read (e.g. S=ACCGACCGACCG) must be decomposed into mosaic tandem repeat units and you need a principled, penalty-driven criterion for choosing which unit strings to include in the decomposition. When units longer than 20 nt are needed — uTR auto-estimates units of length 20 nt or less only; use mTR for long units When the input already has a known representative unit — pass it via uTR's -u flag instead of re-running greedy selection http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Selects repeat-unit strings for mosaic tandem repeat decomposition by first enumerating candidate substrings that are simultaneously repetitive (suffix-array LEN test) and non-self-overlapping (Morris-Pratt OLi test), then running uTR's greedy loop that iteratively adds the unit minimizing an extended penalty until no candidate reduces it. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Selects repeat-unit strings for mosaic tandem repeat decomposition by first enumerating candidate substrings that are simultaneously repetitive (suffix-array LEN test) and non-self-overlapping (Morris-Pratt OLi test), then running uTR's greedy loop that iteratively adds the unit minimizing an extended penalty until no candidate reduces it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When units longer than 20 nt are needed — uTR auto-estimates units of length 20 nt or less only; use mTR for long units When the input already has a known representative unit — pass it via uTR's -u flag instead of re-running greedy selection

skills.description: Use when a .NanoSpring (or similar tar-structured) compressed output must be decomposed into its constituent compressed streams to attribute total compressed size to individual algorithmic components.
skills.name: tar-archive-stream-extraction
skills.search_text: tar-archive-stream-extraction Use when a .NanoSpring (or similar tar-structured) compressed output must be decomposed into its constituent compressed streams to attribute total compressed size to individual algorithmic components. Input is a plain FASTQ or a general-purpose compressed file (gzip/lzma), not a .NanoSpring tar archive of streams The goal is total compressed size or compression ratio rather than per-stream attribution NanoSpring output was produced with modified stream structure or a different compressor whose archive layout differs http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Untar a NanoSpring .NanoSpring compressed archive — which is a tar of separate compressed streams — and measure the byte size of each stream (consensus, error, lone-read) so per-stream bits-per-base contributions to total compressed size can be computed across FASTQ datasets. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Untar a NanoSpring .NanoSpring compressed archive — which is a tar of separate compressed streams — and measure the byte size of each stream (consensus, error, lone-read) so per-stream bits-per-base contributions to total compressed size can be computed across FASTQ datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a plain FASTQ or a general-purpose compressed file (gzip/lzma), not a .NanoSpring tar archive of streams The goal is total compressed size or compression ratio rather than per-stream attribution NanoSpring output was produced with modified stream structure or a different compressor whose archive layout differs

skills.description: Use when a NanoPipe analysis must align MinION reads against a user-supplied (custom or downloaded) target FASTA instead of a precompiled target, requiring lastdb index construction.
skills.name: target-genome-fasta-preparation
skills.search_text: target-genome-fasta-preparation Use when a NanoPipe analysis must align MinION reads against a user-supplied (custom or downloaded) target FASTA instead of a precompiled target, requiring lastdb index construction. A precompiled target for the species of interest already ships with NanoPipe and no custom sequence is needed The alignment backend is not LAST/NanoPipe (e.g., metagenomics analysis, which NanoPipe does not yet support) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Prepares a custom alignment target for NanoPipe by placing a target genome FASTA in NANOPIPE/targets and building a LAST index with lastdb, so that the pipeline's lastal alignment stage can map MinION reads against it. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169
skills.summary: Prepares a custom alignment target for NanoPipe by placing a target genome FASTA in NANOPIPE/targets and building a LAST index with lastdb, so that the pipeline's lastal alignment stage can map MinION reads against it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A precompiled target for the species of interest already ships with NanoPipe and no custom sequence is needed The alignment backend is not LAST/NanoPipe (e.g., metagenomics analysis, which NanoPipe does not yet support)

skills.description: Use when you have FASTQ files from targeted amplification of a transgene/wildtype locus from a 10x Genomics 5' cDNA library sequenced on ONT, and need per-cell CAR+ vs wildtype transcript classification with UMI collapsing.
skills.name: targeted-amplicon-quantification-per-cell
skills.search_text: targeted-amplicon-quantification-per-cell Use when you have FASTQ files from targeted amplification of a transgene/wildtype locus from a 10x Genomics 5' cDNA library sequenced on ONT, and need per-cell CAR+ vs wildtype transcript classification with UMI collapsing. You only need standard whole-transcriptome gene-expression counts from unenriched 10x libraries without transgene/wildtype discrimination — nanoranger's targeted 5p10XGEX mode is for locus-level genotyping, not full GEX. The target locus is far from the 5' end or the transcript exceeds ~4 kB, since optimal nanoranger targets are loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcript lengths shorter than 4 kB. Input data are short Illumina reads without an intermediate single-cell cDNA library — barcode/UMI extraction from long reads is the basis of the workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Quantifies targeted long-read amplicons per single cell by running nanoranger in 5p10XGEX mode on ONT-sequenced amplicons from intermediate 10x Genomics 5'-anchored cDNA libraries, assigning each read to a transgene (e.g. CD19 CAR) versus its wildtype counterpart (endogenous CD28) and collapsing UMIs per cell barcode. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Quantifies targeted long-read amplicons per single cell by running nanoranger in 5p10XGEX mode on ONT-sequenced amplicons from intermediate 10x Genomics 5'-anchored cDNA libraries, assigning each read to a transgene (e.g. CD19 CAR) versus its wildtype counterpart (endogenous CD28) and collapsing UMIs per cell barcode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need standard whole-transcriptome gene-expression counts from unenriched 10x libraries without transgene/wildtype discrimination — nanoranger's targeted 5p10XGEX mode is for locus-level genotyping, not full GEX. The target locus is far from the 5' end or the transcript exceeds ~4 kB, since optimal nanoranger targets are loci close to the 5' end of highly expressed genes with transcript lengths shorter than 4 kB. Input data are short Illumina reads without an intermediate single-cell cDNA library — barcode/UMI extraction from long reads is the basis of the workflow.

skills.description: Use when a HASLR draft hybrid assembly shows elevated mismatch/indel error rates versus other assemblers and you want parity via polishing, without polishing the entire assembly.
skills.name: targeted-assembly-polishing-between-unique-contigs
skills.search_text: targeted-assembly-polishing-between-unique-contigs Use when a HASLR draft hybrid assembly shows elevated mismatch/indel error rates versus other assemblers and you want parity via polishing, without polishing the entire assembly. When the assembler already includes a polishing step and its mismatch/indel rates are at parity — the deficiency this skill targets is specific to HASLR's lack of a polishing module When the errors of interest are misassemblies, genome fraction, or NGA50 rather than small local mismatch/indel errors — polishing fixes small local assembly mistakes, not structural issues When no corresponding high-quality short reads (e.g. Illumina) are available and long-read-only Racon polishing cannot achieve the required correction depth http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A single round of targeted polishing (Racon and/or Pilon) applied only to the SPOA-derived regions of a HASLR hybrid assembly that lie between unique short-read contigs, to bring HASLR's elevated mismatch and indel rates (per 100 kbp) to parity with other assemblers. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101389
skills.summary: A single round of targeted polishing (Racon and/or Pilon) applied only to the SPOA-derived regions of a HASLR hybrid assembly that lie between unique short-read contigs, to bring HASLR's elevated mismatch and indel rates (per 100 kbp) to parity with other assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the assembler already includes a polishing step and its mismatch/indel rates are at parity — the deficiency this skill targets is specific to HASLR's lack of a polishing module When the errors of interest are misassemblies, genome fraction, or NGA50 rather than small local mismatch/indel errors — polishing fixes small local assembly mistakes, not structural issues When no corresponding high-quality short reads (e.g. Illumina) are available and long-read-only Racon polishing cannot achieve the required correction depth

skills.description: Use when a workflow is defined as nodes (hardware tasks like microscope acquisition, software tasks like image analysis) with dependency edges, and you must produce an execution schedule plus resumable persisted state after interruption.
skills.name: task-dependency-topological-scheduling
skills.search_text: task-dependency-topological-scheduling Use when a workflow is defined as nodes (hardware tasks like microscope acquisition, software tasks like image analysis) with dependency edges, and you must produce an execution schedule plus resumable persisted state after interruption. The workflow is a single-pass linear pipeline with no hardware/software interleaving, e.g. commercial automated microscopes that 'imaging is done in a single pass' No interruption/recovery semantics are needed and a plain sequential script suffices The tasks have no explicit dependency edges, so topological ordering is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Resolves a task-dependency graph from OpenHiCAMM's workflow engine into a topologically ordered schedule where microscope-dependent hardware tasks (e.g. slide loader, acquisition) run sequentially and computational image-analysis modules run in parallel, with SQL-backed persistence so interrupted workflows resume from persisted task states. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2018.03.017
skills.summary: Resolves a task-dependency graph from OpenHiCAMM's workflow engine into a topologically ordered schedule where microscope-dependent hardware tasks (e.g. slide loader, acquisition) run sequentially and computational image-analysis modules run in parallel, with SQL-backed persistence so interrupted workflows resume from persisted task states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The workflow is a single-pass linear pipeline with no hardware/software interleaving, e.g. commercial automated microscopes that 'imaging is done in a single pass' No interruption/recovery semantics are needed and a plain sequential script suffices The tasks have no explicit dependency edges, so topological ordering is undefined

skills.description: Use when benchmarking multiple taxonomic classifiers (e.g., Kraken2 vs Centrifuger vs minimap2-based strategies) on the same sample and you need reference-matched, version-pinned databases to make misclassification rates comparable.
skills.name: taxonomic-classifier-database-construction
skills.search_text: taxonomic-classifier-database-construction Use when benchmarking multiple taxonomic classifiers (e.g., Kraken2 vs Centrifuger vs minimap2-based strategies) on the same sample and you need reference-matched, version-pinned databases to make misclassification rates comparable. The analysis goal is ARG detection itself rather than host-identification benchmarking — use Argo with its SARG+/GTDB Zenodo database instead of rebuilding classifier databases from RefSeq The classifiers being compared intentionally use different reference databases (e.g., GTDB vs RefSeq), where reference-matched construction would erase the effect under study http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Constructs taxonomic classifier databases for benchmarking host identification of ARG-carrying long reads, rebuilding Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, and a shared minimap2 map-ont index exclusively from NCBI RefSeq complete genomes (2024-05-10) so all methods are compared on identical reference content. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-025-57088-y
skills.summary: Constructs taxonomic classifier databases for benchmarking host identification of ARG-carrying long reads, rebuilding Kraken2, Centrifuger, MetaMaps, and a shared minimap2 map-ont index exclusively from NCBI RefSeq complete genomes (2024-05-10) so all methods are compared on identical reference content.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is ARG detection itself rather than host-identification benchmarking — use Argo with its SARG+/GTDB Zenodo database instead of rebuilding classifier databases from RefSeq The classifiers being compared intentionally use different reference databases (e.g., GTDB vs RefSeq), where reference-matched construction would erase the effect under study

skills.description: Use when tab-separated Kraken2 kreport2 files are available and the goal is interactive exploration of read distribution across taxonomic ranks (Sankey/Sunburst/species table) for one or more barcoded samples.
skills.name: taxonomic-hierarchy-sunburst-rendering
skills.search_text: taxonomic-hierarchy-sunburst-rendering Use when tab-separated Kraken2 kreport2 files are available and the goal is interactive exploration of read distribution across taxonomic ranks (Sankey/Sunburst/species table) for one or more barcoded samples. Input is raw FASTQ or unclassified Kraken2 output rather than kreport2 report files — classification must already be done (delegated to the nanometanf pipeline). A static publication figure is needed rather than an interactive dashboard view; the Sankey/Sunburst are Dash callback-driven components, not print exports. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Render Kraken2 per-sample classification reports as interactive taxonomic visualizations — a Sankey diagram of read flow across ranks, a click-to-explore Sunburst, and a most-abundant-species table — inside the Nanometa Live Dash GUI so users can explore a sample's taxonomic composition in real time. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae108
skills.summary: Render Kraken2 per-sample classification reports as interactive taxonomic visualizations — a Sankey diagram of read flow across ranks, a click-to-explore Sunburst, and a most-abundant-species table — inside the Nanometa Live Dash GUI so users can explore a sample's taxonomic composition in real time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or unclassified Kraken2 output rather than kreport2 report files — classification must already be done (delegated to the nanometanf pipeline). A static publication figure is needed rather than an interactive dashboard view; the Sankey/Sunburst are Dash callback-driven components, not print exports.

skills.description: Use when Kraken2 per-sample report files (.kreport2.txt) must be parsed to extract exact read counts for watchlist taxids (e.g., E. coli 562, S. aureus 1280, B. anthracis 1392, Y. pestis 632, C. botulinum 1491) feeding downstream validation.
skills.name: taxonomic-read-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-read-count-aggregation Use when Kraken2 per-sample report files (.kreport2.txt) must be parsed to extract exact read counts for watchlist taxids (e.g., E. coli 562, S. aureus 1280, B. anthracis 1392, Y. pestis 632, C. botulinum 1491) feeding downstream validation. You need clade-wide abundance percentages — the 'cumul_reads' / '%' columns of the Kraken2 report, not this direct-read extraction, are the wrong tool since this skill deliberately excludes descendant reads. Input is raw Kraken2 classified-read output (kraken2 output lines) rather than report files (.kreport2.txt); the parsing assumes the six-column report schema. Analysis requires genus- or family-level counting — this skill retains only species-level rank codes (S, S1, S2, S3). http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Aggregates per-sample, per-taxon read counts for user-defined species of interest from Kraken2 report files (.kreport2.txt) so Nanometa Live can surface pathogen watchlist detections with direct read assignments rather than clade totals. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae108
skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample, per-taxon read counts for user-defined species of interest from Kraken2 report files (.kreport2.txt) so Nanometa Live can surface pathogen watchlist detections with direct read assignments rather than clade totals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need clade-wide abundance percentages — the 'cumul_reads' / '%' columns of the Kraken2 report, not this direct-read extraction, are the wrong tool since this skill deliberately excludes descendant reads. Input is raw Kraken2 classified-read output (kraken2 output lines) rather than report files (.kreport2.txt); the parsing assumes the six-column report schema. Analysis requires genus- or family-level counting — this skill retains only species-level rank codes (S, S1, S2, S3).

skills.description: Use when per-sample Kraken2 kreport2 files are available and the goal is to explore a sample's taxonomic composition interactively, e.g. inspecting how sequencing reads distribute across rank levels during an Oxford Nanopore run.
skills.name: taxonomic-read-flow-sankey-visualization
skills.search_text: taxonomic-read-flow-sankey-visualization Use when per-sample Kraken2 kreport2 files are available and the goal is to explore a sample's taxonomic composition interactively, e.g. inspecting how sequencing reads distribute across rank levels during an Oxford Nanopore run. Input is not Kraken2 report output (e.g. raw FASTQ, minimap2 coverage files, or BLAST results) — the loader expects kreport2 columns The goal is per-sample quality control (read length, filtering statistics) rather than taxonomic composition — use the QC panel instead No GUI/dashboard interaction is needed and only numeric abundance tables are required — a plain pandas aggregation suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Render Kraken2 per-sample taxonomic classification output from the Nanometa Live/nanometanf pipeline as interactive read-flow visualizations — a Sankey diagram of read distribution across taxonomic ranks, a click-to-explore Sunburst from the same clade hierarchy, and a most-abundant-species table — inside the Dash GUI. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae108

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not Kraken2 report output (e.g. raw FASTQ, minimap2 coverage files, or BLAST results) — the loader expects kreport2 columns The goal is per-sample quality control (read length, filtering statistics) rather than taxonomic composition — use the QC panel instead No GUI/dashboard interaction is needed and only numeric abundance tables are required — a plain pandas aggregation suffices

skills.description: Use when an ONT- or PacBio-sequenced 10x Genomics 5'-anchored TCR/cDNA amplicon FASTQ has been processed with nanoranger in 5p10X_XCR mode and you need to count cell barcodes with a detected TCR and benchmark against Illumina-derived counts.
skills.name: tcr-positive-cell-count-reporting
skills.search_text: tcr-positive-cell-count-reporting Use when an ONT- or PacBio-sequenced 10x Genomics 5'-anchored TCR/cDNA amplicon FASTQ has been processed with nanoranger in 5p10X_XCR mode and you need to count cell barcodes with a detected TCR and benchmark against Illumina-derived counts. The input is raw ONT/PacBio long reads that have not yet been processed by nanoranger — run the 5p10X_XCR workflow first; this skill only aggregates and counts per-cell calls. The library is a whole-transcriptome scRNA-seq or SNV/fusion/isoform nanoranger run rather than a TCR-targeted 10x amplicon — per-cell TCR counting does not apply. You need clone-level clonotype annotation or V(D)J diversity metrics rather than a simple count of TCR-positive cells; a dedicated repertoire tool (e.g. MiXCR) is the wrong scope here but a different analysis is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Aggregates per-cell TCR calls produced by nanoranger in 5p10X_XCR mode from ONT-sequenced 10x Genomics TCR cDNA amplicons into a single count of cells with a detectable TCR, reportable as tcr_cell_counts.csv and checkable against the paper's reference value of 5653 ONT cells (vs. 5767 Illumina cells). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Aggregates per-cell TCR calls produced by nanoranger in 5p10X_XCR mode from ONT-sequenced 10x Genomics TCR cDNA amplicons into a single count of cells with a detectable TCR, reportable as tcr_cell_counts.csv and checkable against the paper's reference value of 5653 ONT cells (vs. 5767 Illumina cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw ONT/PacBio long reads that have not yet been processed by nanoranger — run the 5p10X_XCR workflow first; this skill only aggregates and counts per-cell calls. The library is a whole-transcriptome scRNA-seq or SNV/fusion/isoform nanoranger run rather than a TCR-targeted 10x amplicon — per-cell TCR counting does not apply. You need clone-level clonotype annotation or V(D)J diversity metrics rather than a simple count of TCR-positive cells; a dedicated repertoire tool (e.g. MiXCR) is the wrong scope here but a different analysis is needed.

skills.description: Use when comparing polishing methods on repeat-rich TE regions of a HiFi assembly and you need per-element alignment identity against reference TE sequences to quantify correction versus overcorrection.
skills.name: te-alignment-identity-quantification
skills.search_text: te-alignment-identity-quantification Use when comparing polishing methods on repeat-rich TE regions of a HiFi assembly and you need per-element alignment identity against reference TE sequences to quantify correction versus overcorrection. Input TE sequences are already aligned and identity scores computed — re-running asm10 alignment adds no information The goal is read-to-reference mapping accuracy of noisy long reads rather than assembly-to-assembly consensus identity of finished TE sequences (use map-hifi/map-pb presets instead) Genome is assembled from noisy short reads without HiFi data; the underlying polishing methods and the identity gain expectations do not transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Quantifies transposable-element (TE) consensus accuracy after genome polishing by aligning polished TE sequences to curated TE references with minimap2 (-cx asm10) and computing per-TE identity ratios, enabling detection of both corrections and overcorrections in highly repetitive regions. genomics/v1 10.1093/gpbjnl/qzad009
skills.summary: Quantifies transposable-element (TE) consensus accuracy after genome polishing by aligning polished TE sequences to curated TE references with minimap2 (-cx asm10) and computing per-TE identity ratios, enabling detection of both corrections and overcorrections in highly repetitive regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input TE sequences are already aligned and identity scores computed — re-running asm10 alignment adds no information The goal is read-to-reference mapping accuracy of noisy long reads rather than assembly-to-assembly consensus identity of finished TE sequences (use map-hifi/map-pb presets instead) Genome is assembled from noisy short reads without HiFi data; the underlying polishing methods and the identity gain expectations do not transfer

skills.description: Use when evaluating TE insertion caller performance on nanopore data against a curated truth set — i.e., when callset VCFs must be matched to known insertions to compute precision, recall, and F1 at defined read-support thresholds and distance margins.
skills.name: te-insertion-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: te-insertion-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating TE insertion caller performance on nanopore data against a curated truth set — i.e., when callset VCFs must be matched to known insertions to compute precision, recall, and F1 at defined read-support thresholds and distance margins. Input is a single-sample detection/annotation task without a truth set — use RetroInspector's detection/annotation/genotyping mode instead of benchmarking Data is short-read sequencing (e.g., for MELT-style TE analysis) rather than nanopore long reads aligned to GRCh38 The reference genome or truth set coordinates are not on the same assembly (GRCh38) as the predictions, since matching depends on SURVIVOR coordinate comparison at 100/500 bp margins http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Benchmarking protocol for quantifying precision, recall, and F1-score of TE insertion detection pipelines (RetroInspector, cuteSV, Sniffles2, SVIM combinations) against the HGSVC truth set of 5,630 TE insertions, matching predicted insertions with SURVIVOR at 100 bp and 500 bp distance margins. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for quantifying precision, recall, and F1-score of TE insertion detection pipelines (RetroInspector, cuteSV, Sniffles2, SVIM combinations) against the HGSVC truth set of 5,630 TE insertions, matching predicted insertions with SURVIVOR at 100 bp and 500 bp distance margins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-sample detection/annotation task without a truth set — use RetroInspector's detection/annotation/genotyping mode instead of benchmarking Data is short-read sequencing (e.g., for MELT-style TE analysis) rather than nanopore long reads aligned to GRCh38 The reference genome or truth set coordinates are not on the same assembly (GRCh38) as the predictions, since matching depends on SURVIVOR coordinate comparison at 100/500 bp margins

skills.description: Use when you have a BAM/CRAM of PacBio or ONT long reads aligned to a reference plus a fasta of insertion sequences to detect, and you need to call non-reference TE insertions as VCF INS:ME variants.
skills.name: te-insertion-candidate-clustering
skills.search_text: te-insertion-candidate-clustering Use when you have a BAM/CRAM of PacBio or ONT long reads aligned to a reference plus a fasta of insertion sequences to detect, and you need to call non-reference TE insertions as VCF INS:ME variants. Input is short-read data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for detection of transposable element insertions in long-read data (PacBio or ONT) Reference or TE fasta is absent — sTELLeR needs a bam or cram file, the reference used to align it, and a fasta file with insertion sequences to look for You only need reference-TE annotation rather than non-reference insertion calling — this skill targets non-reference TE detection and variant-style output http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Cluster candidate TE insertion signatures from long-read data and align candidate insertion sequences to a TE fasta (e.g. fasta/TEfastasequences.fa) with minimap2, then refine consensus positions and filter calls by support depth, mapping quality, and coverage before writing haplotype-aware VCF output. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Cluster candidate TE insertion signatures from long-read data and align candidate insertion sequences to a TE fasta (e.g. fasta/TEfastasequences.fa) with minimap2, then refine consensus positions and filter calls by support depth, mapping quality, and coverage before writing haplotype-aware VCF output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read data — sTELLeR is designed and tested for detection of transposable element insertions in long-read data (PacBio or ONT) Reference or TE fasta is absent — sTELLeR needs a bam or cram file, the reference used to align it, and a fasta file with insertion sequences to look for You only need reference-TE annotation rather than non-reference insertion calling — this skill targets non-reference TE detection and variant-style output

skills.description: Use when evaluating the accuracy of a long-read TE insertion callset — e.g. after merging cuteSV and Sniffles2 outputs — by computing precision and recall against a benchmark set and choosing between strict vs lax filtering criteria.
skills.name: te-insertion-precision-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: te-insertion-precision-recall-evaluation Use when evaluating the accuracy of a long-read TE insertion callset — e.g. after merging cuteSV and Sniffles2 outputs — by computing precision and recall against a benchmark set and choosing between strict vs lax filtering criteria. No curated truth/benchmark set exists for the samples — precision and recall cannot be computed, so this skill is inapplicable Callsets come from a single caller with no strict/lax intersection/union distinction to evaluate The task is TE detection or annotation itself rather than accuracy assessment of existing callsets http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Benchmarks TE insertion callsets from merged cuteSV/Sniffles2 calls against a curated truth set using SURVIVOR, comparing strict (intersection) vs lax (union) caller-agreement criteria to quantify the precision–recall trade-off. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks TE insertion callsets from merged cuteSV/Sniffles2 calls against a curated truth set using SURVIVOR, comparing strict (intersection) vs lax (union) caller-agreement criteria to quantify the precision–recall trade-off.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No curated truth/benchmark set exists for the samples — precision and recall cannot be computed, so this skill is inapplicable Callsets come from a single caller with no strict/lax intersection/union distinction to evaluate The task is TE detection or annotation itself rather than accuracy assessment of existing callsets

skills.description: Use when a nanopore TE-insertion callset contains SVA calls that must be resolved to the newer SVA F1 family, which Dfam lacks and RepeatMasker annotates only as generic SVA, via sequence evidence (MAST2 thumbprint).
skills.name: te-insertion-sequence-classification
skills.search_text: te-insertion-sequence-classification Use when a nanopore TE-insertion callset contains SVA calls that must be resolved to the newer SVA F1 family, which Dfam lacks and RepeatMasker annotates only as generic SVA, via sequence evidence (MAST2 thumbprint). When classifying TE families that ARE represented in Dfam — those are recovered by the pipeline's RepeatMasker-on-Dfam step, not by this MAST2-thumbprint search When input is short-read data: RetroInspector is built for nanopore sequencing, and the reassembled insertion sequences this filter consumes come from long-read-supported reassembly For non-SVA insertions (L1, Alu, etc.) that lack the MAST2 fragment — the search is specific to SVA-called records http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 A discrete RetroInspector step that reclassifies called SVA insertions as SVA F1 by BLAST-searching reassembled insertion sequences for the MAST2 thumbprint fragment, since SVA F1 is absent from Dfam and RepeatMasker otherwise reports these elements only as generic SVA (SVA F). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: A discrete RetroInspector step that reclassifies called SVA insertions as SVA F1 by BLAST-searching reassembled insertion sequences for the MAST2 thumbprint fragment, since SVA F1 is absent from Dfam and RepeatMasker otherwise reports these elements only as generic SVA (SVA F).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When classifying TE families that ARE represented in Dfam — those are recovered by the pipeline's RepeatMasker-on-Dfam step, not by this MAST2-thumbprint search When input is short-read data: RetroInspector is built for nanopore sequencing, and the reassembled insertion sequences this filter consumes come from long-read-supported reassembly For non-SVA insertions (L1, Alu, etc.) that lack the MAST2 fragment — the search is specific to SVA-called records

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a TE/SV insertion caller's VCF output against a curated truth set and you need precision, recall, and F1 computed from position-matched variants at a defined base-pair margin.
skills.name: te-insertion-truth-set-matching
skills.search_text: te-insertion-truth-set-matching Use when benchmarking a TE/SV insertion caller's VCF output against a curated truth set and you need precision, recall, and F1 computed from position-matched variants at a defined base-pair margin. The callsets are not insertion callsets in a matchable variant format (e.g., raw FASTQ or unassembled contigs) — caller output must first be converted to VCF The goal is genotyping concordance rather than insertion detection benchmarking (the article evaluated HGSV2 genotyping separately from the truth-set matching) Tools were run with incomparable compute resources — timing comparisons are invalid (the paper excluded GraffiTE because it used 96 threads when assigned 32) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Matches TE insertion callsets (VCF) from long-read detection tools against a curated truth set with SURVIVOR at a strict 100 bp and a permissive 500 bp distance margin, then computes precision, recall, and F1 per tool, as done to benchmark RetroInspector against PALMER and GraffiTE on the HGSV nanopore samples. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Matches TE insertion callsets (VCF) from long-read detection tools against a curated truth set with SURVIVOR at a strict 100 bp and a permissive 500 bp distance margin, then computes precision, recall, and F1 per tool, as done to benchmark RetroInspector against PALMER and GraffiTE on the HGSV nanopore samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The callsets are not insertion callsets in a matchable variant format (e.g., raw FASTQ or unassembled contigs) — caller output must first be converted to VCF The goal is genotyping concordance rather than insertion detection benchmarking (the article evaluated HGSV2 genotyping separately from the truth-set matching) Tools were run with incomparable compute resources — timing comparisons are invalid (the paper excluded GraffiTE because it used 96 threads when assigned 32)

skills.name: telobait-capture-read-parsing
skills.search_text: telobait-capture-read-parsing Use when input is long-read data (fasta/fastq/bam/pacbio-bam) from the telobait telomere-capture wet-lab workflow and per-read telomere lengths or telomeric-read tables are needed. Input is vanilla whole-genome sequencing long-read data with no telobait capture — use telomap's wgs mode instead, since telobait mode 'requires data generated from a wet lab telomere capturing method'. Measuring telomere length of ALT cells, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity. Barcode or capture-oligo sequences are unavailable — the required -c/-b FASTA files cannot be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Identify and parse telomere-containing reads from telobait-capture PacBio HiFi long-read data using telomap, which aligns the capture oligo and sample barcode at read ends and demarcates the telomeric tract at nucleotide resolution. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Identify and parse telomere-containing reads from telobait-capture PacBio HiFi long-read data using telomap, which aligns the capture oligo and sample barcode at read ends and demarcates the telomeric tract at nucleotide resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is vanilla whole-genome sequencing long-read data with no telobait capture — use telomap's wgs mode instead, since telobait mode 'requires data generated from a wet lab telomere capturing method'. Measuring telomere length of ALT cells, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity. Barcode or capture-oligo sequences are unavailable — the required -c/-b FASTA files cannot be constructed.

skills.search_text: telobait-sample-barcode-demultiplexing Use when long reads come from telobait-capture libraries with sample barcodes embedded in the telobaits, and reads must be assigned to their source sample for per-sample telomere length quantification. Input reads are vanilla whole-genome sequencing (WGS) long reads with no telobait capture barcodes — use telomap's WGS mode instead, which reports NA for OLIGO and BARCODE. Data were not generated with the wet-lab telobait capture method, so no capture_oligo.fa or barcodes.fa are available. Input is already-demultiplexed, per-sample read sets where barcode assignment has already been performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Demultiplexes telobait-captured PacBio HiFi telomere sequencing reads to individual samples (e.g., patient PBL samples) using telomap in telobait mode, which matches the sample-specific barcodes embedded in the telobaits so each sample can be quantified separately. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Demultiplexes telobait-captured PacBio HiFi telomere sequencing reads to individual samples (e.g., patient PBL samples) using telomap in telobait mode, which matches the sample-specific barcodes embedded in the telobaits so each sample can be quantified separately.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are vanilla whole-genome sequencing (WGS) long reads with no telobait capture barcodes — use telomap's WGS mode instead, which reports NA for OLIGO and BARCODE. Input is already-demultiplexed, per-sample read sets where barcode assignment has already been performed.

skills.description: Use when you have a telomap sample.telomap.tsv with per-read RAW_TELOMERE_LEN, TELOMERE_LEN, TELOMERE_START/END coordinates and need to count TRF1/TRF2 binding motifs and compute binding-site density per kb of canonical telomere.
skills.name: telomere-repeat-motif-counting
skills.search_text: telomere-repeat-motif-counting Use when you have a telomap sample.telomap.tsv with per-read RAW_TELOMERE_LEN, TELOMERE_LEN, TELOMERE_START/END coordinates and need to count TRF1/TRF2 binding motifs and compute binding-site density per kb of canonical telomere. Input is raw long reads (FASTA/FASTQ/BAM) rather than an annotated telomap output table — run telomap first to identify telomeric reads and TELOMERE_START/END coordinates Telomeres are from ALT cells, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity and cannot be fully measured by this workflow The goal is total telomere length measurement rather than motif/binding-site density — use RAW_TELOMERE_LEN/TELOMERE_LEN directly instead of motif counting http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Counts occurrences of shelterin binding motifs (e.g. the TRF1/TRF2 motif 5'-TTAGGGTTA-3') within extracted telomeric repeat tracts from telomap per-read output, and normalizes counts by canonical telomere length to compare binding-site density across samples. This quantifies how telomeric variant sequences (TVSs) disrupt canonical (5'-TTAGGG-3')n continuity and thus shelterin binding at chromosome ends. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Counts occurrences of shelterin binding motifs (e.g. the TRF1/TRF2 motif 5'-TTAGGGTTA-3') within extracted telomeric repeat tracts from telomap per-read output, and normalizes counts by canonical telomere length to compare binding-site density across samples. This quantifies how telomeric variant sequences (TVSs) disrupt canonical (5'-TTAGGG-3')n continuity and thus shelterin binding at chromosome ends.

Measuring telomere length of ALT (alternative lengthening of telomeres) cells whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi DNA polymerase processivity limits Input data is short-read sequencing (e.g., Illumina) — the workflow is designed specifically for long-read platforms Subtelomeric regions are expected to be too short (e.g., after aggressive restriction enzyme trimming with RsaI and HinfI) for unambiguous chromosome-end identification against T2T-CHM13 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scans long-read (PacBio HiFi) sequencing data for telomeric sequences using the telomap tool, identifying telomeric reads and measuring telomere lengths at nucleotide resolution by demarcating telomeric regions via consecutive canonical TTAGGG repeats and quantifying both raw and motif-count-based lengths per read. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7

skills.description: Use when you have telomeric reads (FASTQ/BAM from WGS or telobait-captured PacBio HiFi data) already flagged by telomap and need to group them by chromosome end via subtelomeric consensus anchors before per-end analyses.
skills.name: telomeric-read-anchor-extraction
skills.search_text: telomeric-read-anchor-extraction Use when you have telomeric reads (FASTQ/BAM from WGS or telobait-captured PacBio HiFi data) already flagged by telomap and need to group them by chromosome end via subtelomeric consensus anchors before per-end analyses. Input reads have not yet been screened for telomeric sequence by telomap (e.g. raw whole-genome long reads without the telomere-identification step) Subtelomeric regions are too short for unambiguous chromosome-end identification (e.g. after RsaI/HinfI trimming) against T2T-CHM13, so anchors would map ambiguously Analysis goal is ALT-cell telomere length, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi read length and are incompatible with this pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Clusters the 5' non-telomeric subtelomeric segments of telomeric reads identified by telomap and builds a 100 bp consensus anchor per cluster, enabling individual telomeric reads to be assigned to specific chromosome ends for per-end analyses such as TVS signature plots. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35823-7
skills.summary: Clusters the 5' non-telomeric subtelomeric segments of telomeric reads identified by telomap and builds a 100 bp consensus anchor per cluster, enabling individual telomeric reads to be assigned to specific chromosome ends for per-end analyses such as TVS signature plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been screened for telomeric sequence by telomap (e.g. raw whole-genome long reads without the telomere-identification step) Subtelomeric regions are too short for unambiguous chromosome-end identification (e.g. after RsaI/HinfI trimming) against T2T-CHM13, so anchors would map ambiguously Analysis goal is ALT-cell telomere length, whose very long telomeres exceed PacBio HiFi read length and are incompatible with this pipeline
