skills.name: telomeric-variant-sequence-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: telomeric-variant-sequence-distribution-analysis Use when you need to characterize and compare the per-nucleotide distribution of non-canonical telomeric variant sequences (TVS) within telomere repeat regions from telomap-processed long reads, e.g. to test whether a TVS signature at a specific chromosome end is patient-unique. skills.when_to_use_negative: Telomere length estimation only (use RAW_TELOMERE_LEN/TELOMERE_LEN summaries instead of per-nucleotide TVS profiling) ALT cells with very long telomeres — the article notes the PacBio HiFi method is incompatible with measuring telomeres of ALT cells, so TVS signatures cannot be derived there Reads lacking unambiguous chromosome-end assignment because the subtelomeric region is too short (a known limitation of RsaI/HinfI trimming against T2T-CHM13)

skills.description: Use when per-read methylation scores (e.g. Megalodon, DeepSignal) or consensus predictions must be converted to per-site methylation frequencies on a mixture dataset of known proportion and scored against expected frequencies.
skills.name: tenfold-cross-validation-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: tenfold-cross-validation-performance-evaluation Use when per-read methylation scores (e.g. Megalodon, DeepSignal) or consensus predictions must be converted to per-site methylation frequencies on a mixture dataset of known proportion and scored against expected frequencies. The input has no ground-truth methylation frequencies (e.g. wild-type samples without controlled mixtures or WGBS reference), so expected-frequency-based metrics like RMSE and the 10% window proportion cannot be computed The analysis targets raw per-read methylation scores rather than aggregated per-site methylation frequency predictions The goal is comparing individual tools against each other without a trained consensus model, where a different benchmarking protocol applies http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluates per-site CpG methylation frequency predictions from nanopore methylation tools and METEORE consensus models on a controlled mixture dataset, using Pearson r, r^2, RMSE, ROC and precision-recall curves derived from tenfold cross-validation, plus the proportion of sites within the expected 10% window of the known mixture proportion. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-23778-6
skills.summary: Evaluates per-site CpG methylation frequency predictions from nanopore methylation tools and METEORE consensus models on a controlled mixture dataset, using Pearson r, r^2, RMSE, ROC and precision-recall curves derived from tenfold cross-validation, plus the proportion of sites within the expected 10% window of the known mixture proportion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input has no ground-truth methylation frequencies (e.g. wild-type samples without controlled mixtures or WGBS reference), so expected-frequency-based metrics like RMSE and the 10% window proportion cannot be computed The analysis targets raw per-read methylation scores rather than aggregated per-site methylation frequency predictions The goal is comparing individual tools against each other without a trained consensus model, where a different benchmarking protocol applies

skills.description: Use when you need to execute the MIRIAM cell-segmentation pipeline over many TMA cores across two software implementations and quantify cross-implementation segmentation agreement per image.
skills.name: tissue-microarray-image-batch-processing
skills.search_text: tissue-microarray-image-batch-processing Use when you need to execute the MIRIAM cell-segmentation pipeline over many TMA cores across two software implementations and quantify cross-implementation segmentation agreement per image. You are comparing MIRIAM against alternative segmentation methods (Mesmer, Voronoi) against manual annotation — that benchmark uses 240 sub-images across three manually annotated TMA cores with different reported DSC/JSC values (MIRIAM DSC 0.65 ± 0.08), not the Matlab-vs-Python comparison. Your images are not multiplexed tissue images (e.g., single-channel microscopy or non-TMA whole-slide data) — the pipeline and its agreement thresholds were established on colon adenoma TMA cores and a breast carcinoma MIBI dataset. You only need marker quantification or t-SNE shape analysis downstream and do not intend to verify cross-implementation segmentation consistency. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Batch-runs the MIRIAM segmentation pipeline (random-forest pixel classification plus internal-membrane-based cell separation) over tissue microarray cores in both Matlab (R2018b) and Python (3.7) environments, then compares the two implementations per image using cell-membrane Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity coefficients. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Batch-runs the MIRIAM segmentation pipeline (random-forest pixel classification plus internal-membrane-based cell separation) over tissue microarray cores in both Matlab (R2018b) and Python (3.7) environments, then compares the two implementations per image using cell-membrane Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are comparing MIRIAM against alternative segmentation methods (Mesmer, Voronoi) against manual annotation — that benchmark uses 240 sub-images across three manually annotated TMA cores with different reported DSC/JSC values (MIRIAM DSC 0.65 ± 0.08), not the Matlab-vs-Python comparison. Your images are not multiplexed tissue images (e.g., single-channel microscopy or non-TMA whole-slide data) — the pipeline and its agreement thresholds were established on colon adenoma TMA cores and a breast carcinoma MIBI dataset. You only need marker quantification or t-SNE shape analysis downstream and do not intend to verify cross-implementation segmentation consistency.

skills.description: Use when testing whether circRNA isoforms flagged as tissue-specific by per-tissue read-count criteria are enriched in tissue-specific parental genes, or when computing tissue-specificity scores (tau) from multi-tissue gene TPM tables.
skills.name: tissue-specificity-classification
skills.search_text: tissue-specificity-classification Use when testing whether circRNA isoforms flagged as tissue-specific by per-tissue read-count criteria are enriched in tissue-specific parental genes, or when computing tissue-specificity scores (tau) from multi-tissue gene TPM tables. Input data covers fewer than the 12 tissues used in the isoCirc catalog — tau computed on n tissues uses the (n-1) normalization and yields non-comparable classifications The analysis goal is circRNA isoform detection or BSJ consensus calling itself — use the isoCirc pipeline (pip install isocirc; bedtools, minimap2) instead Expression is provided as counts without normalization to comparable scales across tissues — convert to TPM first, as tau depends on relative per-gene expression profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies parental genes as tissue-specific using Yanai's tau index computed on GTEx V8 median gene TPM values across 12 human tissues, then tests whether isoCirc-identified tissue-specific circRNA isoforms are enriched among these genes via a one-sided Fisher's exact test on a 2x2 contingency table (p < 2.2e-16). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-20459-8
skills.summary: Classifies parental genes as tissue-specific using Yanai's tau index computed on GTEx V8 median gene TPM values across 12 human tissues, then tests whether isoCirc-identified tissue-specific circRNA isoforms are enriched among these genes via a one-sided Fisher's exact test on a 2x2 contingency table (p < 2.2e-16).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data covers fewer than the 12 tissues used in the isoCirc catalog — tau computed on n tissues uses the (n-1) normalization and yields non-comparable classifications The analysis goal is circRNA isoform detection or BSJ consensus calling itself — use the isoCirc pipeline (pip install isocirc; bedtools, minimap2) instead Expression is provided as counts without normalization to comparable scales across tissues — convert to TPM first, as tau depends on relative per-gene expression profiles

skills.description: Use when manually annotated multiplexed tissue images (e.g., TMA cores) are available and you need to quantitatively compare cell-segmentation methods against ground-truth membranes using DSC/JSC.
skills.name: tma-subimage-tiling-and-benchmarking
skills.search_text: tma-subimage-tiling-and-benchmarking Use when manually annotated multiplexed tissue images (e.g., TMA cores) are available and you need to quantitatively compare cell-segmentation methods against ground-truth membranes using DSC/JSC. No manually annotated ground-truth membranes exist for the images — the skill requires annotated TMA cores to compute DSC/JSC (the article notes no accession or availability details for the manually annotated ground-truth data) The tissue type or segmentation goal differs from columnar epithelial membranes in multiplexed tissue images, e.g., Mesmer was not trained on colorectal adenomas (only mouse small intestine, normal human colon, and colorectal cancer), so benchmark transfer must be re-validated The input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm marker intensities) rather than image masks — segmentation benchmarking is then moot http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 A segmentation benchmarking skill that tiles manually annotated TMA cores into 512x512 sub-images, runs competing cell-segmentation pipelines (MIRIAM, Mesmer, Voronoi), and scores each against ground-truth membrane annotations with image-level and per-cell Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity. genomics/v1 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: A segmentation benchmarking skill that tiles manually annotated TMA cores into 512x512 sub-images, runs competing cell-segmentation pipelines (MIRIAM, Mesmer, Voronoi), and scores each against ground-truth membrane annotations with image-level and per-cell Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No manually annotated ground-truth membranes exist for the images — the skill requires annotated TMA cores to compute DSC/JSC (the article notes no accession or availability details for the manually annotated ground-truth data) The tissue type or segmentation goal differs from columnar epithelial membranes in multiplexed tissue images, e.g., Mesmer was not trained on colorectal adenomas (only mouse small intestine, normal human colon, and colorectal cancer), so benchmark transfer must be re-validated The input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm marker intensities) rather than image masks — segmentation benchmarking is then moot

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to an artificial tRNA genome (mature tRNA ± 50 nt flanks) and each unique read must be assigned a tncRNA subtype based on where it cleaves from the pre-tRNA or mature tRNA.

skills.search_text: tncrna-subtype-classification-by-cleavage-position Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to an artificial tRNA genome (mature tRNA ± 50 nt flanks) and each unique read must be assigned a tncRNA subtype based on where it cleaves from the pre-tRNA or mature tRNA. Input outputs are already standardized, non-heterogeneous BED files with valid confidence columns — re-thresholding would double-apply cut-offs Single-tool analysis with no need for cross-tool comparison, where converting to the common BED schema adds no benchmarking value Tools that failed to run or produced empty output files, which the article reports for several tools — thresholds cannot be meaningfully applied to absent calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 A post-processing procedure from the NanOlympicsMod pipeline that parses the heterogeneous raw outputs of 14 m6A detection tools (e.g. Nanom6A probabilities, Yanocomp/DiffErr FDR, DRUMMER p-values, EpiNano error statistics), converts them to genomic coordinates, and applies per-tool 'default' or 'relaxed' significance cut-offs to write standardized BED files of modification calls. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae001
skills.summary: A post-processing procedure from the NanOlympicsMod pipeline that parses the heterogeneous raw outputs of 14 m6A detection tools (e.g. Nanom6A probabilities, Yanocomp/DiffErr FDR, DRUMMER p-values, EpiNano error statistics), converts them to genomic coordinates, and applies per-tool 'default' or 'relaxed' significance cut-offs to write standardized BED files of modification calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input outputs are already standardized, non-heterogeneous BED files with valid confidence columns — re-thresholding would double-apply cut-offs Single-tool analysis with no need for cross-tool comparison, where converting to the common BED schema adds no benchmarking value Tools that failed to run or produced empty output files, which the article reports for several tools — thresholds cannot be meaningfully applied to absent calls

skills.description: Use when de novo assembled contigs (e.g. from Canu in ViMOP) must be matched to known viral reference genomes to enable reference-guided consensus genome reconstruction from untargeted nanopore reads.
skills.name: top-hit-selection-and-tie-breaking
skills.search_text: top-hit-selection-and-tie-breaking Use when de novo assembled contigs (e.g. from Canu in ViMOP) must be matched to known viral reference genomes to enable reference-guided consensus genome reconstruction from untargeted nanopore reads. When reads or contigs should not be matched against a known-reference database — e.g. the goal is discovery of novel viruses, since ViMOP targets known virus species When the target virus is absent from the ViMOP_DB reference database — contigs with no database entry will not obtain a reference (Centrifuge classifies such contigs as unmatched or partial) For large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox), where the authors warn resulting assemblies may be inaccurate drafts http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Reference identification step of the ViMOP pipeline: each de novo assembled contig is searched by BLAST against the ViMOP_DB virus reference database, and the highest-scoring hit is assigned as that contig's reference genome for downstream reference-guided consensus assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Reference identification step of the ViMOP pipeline: each de novo assembled contig is searched by BLAST against the ViMOP_DB virus reference database, and the highest-scoring hit is assigned as that contig's reference genome for downstream reference-guided consensus assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads or contigs should not be matched against a known-reference database — e.g. the goal is discovery of novel viruses, since ViMOP targets known virus species When the target virus is absent from the ViMOP_DB reference database — contigs with no database entry will not obtain a reference (Centrifuge classifies such contigs as unmatched or partial) For large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox), where the authors warn resulting assemblies may be inaccurate drafts

skills.description: Use when a trained PyTorch MLP from the k-mer size sweep (k=7-25) has been selected (k=21) and must be packaged as a deployable artifact consumed by z-calling-base with -k 21.
skills.name: torchscript-model-export
skills.search_text: torchscript-model-export Use when a trained PyTorch MLP from the k-mer size sweep (k=7-25) has been selected (k=21) and must be packaged as a deployable artifact consumed by z-calling-base with -k 21. Exporting the single-nucleotide A/Z calling model — that artifact is model/k11-mixed-AZ/scripted_m11.pth and must be invoked with -k 11, not -k 21 No GPU-accelerated inference is needed — the tool is explicitly designed for CPU-only Linux environments The read-level dZ/canonical decision — that step uses the pre-trained SVM (model/svm/k21ReadClassifier), not the exported TorchScript module http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Serializes the selected k-mer-specific PyTorch MLP (e.g., the k=21 full-substitution model trained on E. coli full-Z vs full-dA kinetic features) as a TorchScript artifact (scripted_m21.pth) that the C++ z-calling-base executable can load for CPU inference. genomics/v1 10.1038/s42003-026-09849-8
skills.summary: Serializes the selected k-mer-specific PyTorch MLP (e.g., the k=21 full-substitution model trained on E. coli full-Z vs full-dA kinetic features) as a TorchScript artifact (scripted_m21.pth) that the C++ z-calling-base executable can load for CPU inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Exporting the single-nucleotide A/Z calling model — that artifact is model/k11-mixed-AZ/scripted_m11.pth and must be invoked with -k 11, not -k 21 No GPU-accelerated inference is needed — the tool is explicitly designed for CPU-only Linux environments The read-level dZ/canonical decision — that step uses the pre-trained SVM (model/svm/k21ReadClassifier), not the exported TorchScript module

skills.description: Use when MAF-format somatic mutation data with fixed-signature sample contributions (e.g. SBS1* from InverseNMF) must be grouped by gene hotspot status such as TP53 R342* to test mutation-specific signature associations.
skills.name: tp53-mutation-group-stratification
skills.search_text: tp53-mutation-group-stratification Use when MAF-format somatic mutation data with fixed-signature sample contributions (e.g. SBS1* from InverseNMF) must be grouped by gene hotspot status such as TP53 R342* to test mutation-specific signature associations. When the aim is de novo extraction of mutational signatures rather than testing a known signature (SBS1*) against predefined gene-mutation groups — use denovoNMF instead of InverseNMF-based grouping When the cohort lacks sufficient TP53 R342* mutated samples to compute a stable group median, since the contrast depends on per-group medians When mutations of interest are not representable in the MAF fields joined on Tumor_Sample_Barcode and Hugo_Symbol (e.g. non-coding or structural variants) http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Stratify ESCC exon-sequenced samples into TP53 R342*-mutated, other-TP53-mutant, and TP53 wild-type groups, then compare per-sample SBS1* (age signature) contribution medians to test whether the R342* hotspot is specifically linked to age-signature activity. genomics/v1 10.1002/cam4.4717
skills.summary: Stratify ESCC exon-sequenced samples into TP53 R342*-mutated, other-TP53-mutant, and TP53 wild-type groups, then compare per-sample SBS1* (age signature) contribution medians to test whether the R342* hotspot is specifically linked to age-signature activity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the aim is de novo extraction of mutational signatures rather than testing a known signature (SBS1*) against predefined gene-mutation groups — use denovoNMF instead of InverseNMF-based grouping When the cohort lacks sufficient TP53 R342* mutated samples to compute a stable group median, since the contrast depends on per-group medians When mutations of interest are not representable in the MAF fields joined on Tumor_Sample_Barcode and Hugo_Symbol (e.g. non-coding or structural variants)

skills.description: Use when nanopore DRS FASTQ reads must be quantified against a known transcriptome (e.g. SIRV spike-ins or GENCODE), reads map to multiple isoforms, and per-transcript raw/est_count/tpm abundances are the required output.
skills.name: tpm-abundance-normalization
skills.search_text: tpm-abundance-normalization Use when nanopore DRS FASTQ reads must be quantified against a known transcriptome (e.g. SIRV spike-ins or GENCODE), reads map to multiple isoforms, and per-transcript raw/est_count/tpm abundances are the required output. Input is short-read RNA-seq — use a short-read-aware quantifier (Salmon, kallisto) instead; NanoCount is developed specifically for DRS Reads are already quantified or you already hold a per-transcript count/TPM feature table — re-running EM would be redundant The goal is discovering novel unannotated isoforms from genome-spliced alignments rather than quantifying annotated transcriptome references http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate transcript abundances from Oxford Nanopore direct-RNA sequencing (DRS) alignments using NanoCount's DRS-specific filtering and expectation-maximisation (EM) algorithm, which resolves multi-mapping reads and reports per-transcript raw abundance, est_count and tpm. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab1129
skills.summary: Estimate transcript abundances from Oxford Nanopore direct-RNA sequencing (DRS) alignments using NanoCount's DRS-specific filtering and expectation-maximisation (EM) algorithm, which resolves multi-mapping reads and reports per-transcript raw abundance, est_count and tpm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq — use a short-read-aware quantifier (Salmon, kallisto) instead; NanoCount is developed specifically for DRS Reads are already quantified or you already hold a per-transcript count/TPM feature table — re-running EM would be redundant The goal is discovering novel unannotated isoforms from genome-spliced alignments rather than quantifying annotated transcriptome references

skills.description: Use when planning sequencing depth for transcript discovery: given transcript abundances (TPM) from LRTS/PacBio data and a two-copy IsoSeq discovery threshold, estimate observation probability as a function of depth.
skills.name: tpm-based-sampling-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: tpm-based-sampling-probability-estimation Use when planning sequencing depth for transcript discovery: given transcript abundances (TPM) from LRTS/PacBio data and a two-copy IsoSeq discovery threshold, estimate observation probability as a function of depth. Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than aligned full-length transcript (LRTS bam) data, since the model is built for IsoTools' LRTS saturation analysis The goal is alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing (beta-binomial differential analysis), which are separate IsoTools capabilities No TPM abundance estimates are available and only read counts without transcript-level quantification exist http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A model-based saturation analysis for Long Read Transcriptome Sequencing (LRTS) that fits a negative binomial observation-probability model — with parameters n (sequencing depth), r (minimum required coverage), and p (per-transcript sampling probability proportional to RNA concentration/TPM) — to estimate how much depth is needed to detect transcripts, applied with IsoTools' saturation analysis workflow (notebooks/04_saturation_analysis.ipynb). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: A model-based saturation analysis for Long Read Transcriptome Sequencing (LRTS) that fits a negative binomial observation-probability model — with parameters n (sequencing depth), r (minimum required coverage), and p (per-transcript sampling probability proportional to RNA concentration/TPM) — to estimate how much depth is needed to detect transcripts, applied with IsoTools' saturation analysis workflow (notebooks/04_saturation_analysis.ipynb).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than aligned full-length transcript (LRTS bam) data, since the model is built for IsoTools' LRTS saturation analysis The goal is alternative splicing event detection or differential splicing (beta-binomial differential analysis), which are separate IsoTools capabilities No TPM abundance estimates are available and only read counts without transcript-level quantification exist

skills.description: Use when genotyping targeted STR/TR loci from long PacBio HiFi reads with a BAM read-reference alignment and an STR anchor configure file, and you must locate TR locus boundaries, validate repeat motifs, and report phased haplotype alleles.
skills.name: tr-allele-motif-validation
skills.search_text: tr-allele-motif-validation Use when genotyping targeted STR/TR loci from long PacBio HiFi reads with a BAM read-reference alignment and an STR anchor configure file, and you must locate TR locus boundaries, validate repeat motifs, and report phased haplotype alleles. Input is short-read sequencing data — MacroHapCaller is designed for long NGS reads, especially PacBio HiFi reads, where anchors span the locus The TR loci lack known flanking anchor sequences or a Motif_must_present repeat unit — the anchor match and motif validation steps cannot be configured The goal is genome-wide de novo STR discovery rather than genotyping a panel of targeted loci listed in the anchor configure file http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Anchor-based tandem repeat (STR) allele calling in MacroHapCaller: sliding-window anchor matching by edit distance around each targeted TR locus, followed by motif validation of the inter-anchor sequence and read-support filtering to produce a phased TR-allele table. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Anchor-based tandem repeat (STR) allele calling in MacroHapCaller: sliding-window anchor matching by edit distance around each targeted TR locus, followed by motif validation of the inter-anchor sequence and read-support filtering to produce a phased TR-allele table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read sequencing data — MacroHapCaller is designed for long NGS reads, especially PacBio HiFi reads, where anchors span the locus The TR loci lack known flanking anchor sequences or a Motif_must_present repeat unit — the anchor match and motif validation steps cannot be configured The goal is genome-wide de novo STR discovery rather than genotyping a panel of targeted loci listed in the anchor configure file

skills.description: Use when training the ConsensuSV-ONT CNN variant filter: you have encoded SV images plus high-quality/low-quality labels and need a per-sample split to measure generalisation without leaking variants between samples.
skills.name: train-validation-test-sample-splitting
skills.search_text: train-validation-test-sample-splitting Use when training the ConsensuSV-ONT CNN variant filter: you have encoded SV images plus high-quality/low-quality labels and need a per-sample split to measure generalisation without leaking variants between samples. Variants from the same sample are split across train and validation sets — this leaks sample-level signal and invalidates the generalisation check You need per-callers consensus calling or SV detection itself; this skill only covers training the CNN filter, not running the six SV callers Your variants are not encoded as images and lack high-quality/low-quality labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Partition encoded structural-variant images from ConsensuSV-ONT into train, validation, and held-out test sets split by sample, so the binary CNN (50x50x3 Conv3D model) can be fit while validation AUC/loss and per-epoch Truvari metrics monitor generalisation. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Partition encoded structural-variant images from ConsensuSV-ONT into train, validation, and held-out test sets split by sample, so the binary CNN (50x50x3 Conv3D model) can be fit while validation AUC/loss and per-epoch Truvari metrics monitor generalisation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants from the same sample are split across train and validation sets — this leaks sample-level signal and invalidates the generalisation check You need per-callers consensus calling or SV detection itself; this skill only covers training the CNN filter, not running the six SV callers Your variants are not encoded as images and lack high-quality/low-quality labels

skills.description: Use when fitting a small Keras CNN classifier (e.g. three Conv3D+BatchNormalization+MaxPooling3D blocks on encoded SV images) and you need per-epoch generalisation signals — validation Truvari precision/recall/F1, AUC, loss and learning rate — to decide when to reduce the learning rate.
skills.name: training-generalization-monitoring
skills.search_text: training-generalization-monitoring Use when fitting a small Keras CNN classifier (e.g. three Conv3D+BatchNormalization+MaxPooling3D blocks on encoded SV images) and you need per-epoch generalisation signals — validation Truvari precision/recall/F1, AUC, loss and learning rate — to decide when to reduce the learning rate. Evaluating final performance on the held-out test sample — that sample must stay untouched during training and per-epoch monitoring. Upstream consensus SV calling or filtering of caller outputs — this skill covers only CNN training dynamics, not the six-caller consensus stage. Datasets that cannot be split by sample into training/validation/test (one sample each) — the generalisation signal in this method is defined on a per-sample validation split. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Monitors per-epoch training dynamics of the ConsensuSV-ONT binary CNN (59,929-param Keras Conv3D model on 50x50x3 structural-variant images) by logging validation Truvari precision/recall/F1, AUC, loss and learning rate, so that the epoch-2 generalisation plateau and the onset of overfitting can be detected and the learning rate reduced during training. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Monitors per-epoch training dynamics of the ConsensuSV-ONT binary CNN (59,929-param Keras Conv3D model on 50x50x3 structural-variant images) by logging validation Truvari precision/recall/F1, AUC, loss and learning rate, so that the epoch-2 generalisation plateau and the onset of overfitting can be detected and the learning rate reduced during training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating final performance on the held-out test sample — that sample must stay untouched during training and per-epoch monitoring. Upstream consensus SV calling or filtering of caller outputs — this skill covers only CNN training dynamics, not the six-caller consensus stage. Datasets that cannot be split by sample into training/validation/test (one sample each) — the generalisation signal in this method is defined on a per-sample validation split.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a ClinVar-trained pathogenicity classifier (e.g. eDiVA-Score) on HGMD-derived benchmarks (DM/DM? positives vs GnomAD negatives) to remove training-set variants and avoid leakage-inflated AUC.
skills.name: training-set-leakage-exclusion
skills.search_text: training-set-leakage-exclusion Use when benchmarking a ClinVar-trained pathogenicity classifier (e.g. eDiVA-Score) on HGMD-derived benchmarks (DM/DM? positives vs GnomAD negatives) to remove training-set variants and avoid leakage-inflated AUC. The classifier under evaluation was not trained on ClinVar or HGMD-derived data, so no training-set overlap with the benchmark positives is possible The variant set has already been de-duplicated against the classifier's training variants and ClinVar annotations You are using the benchmark variants themselves for model training or feature engineering — exclusion is meant for evaluation only, not as a data-cleaning step Excludes variants used to train a pathogenicity classifier (eDiVA-Score's 15,000 ClinVar pathogenic variants) and all ClinVar-annotated variants from HGMD/GnomAD evaluation sets before computing ROC/AUC, so benchmark results are not inflated by variants the model saw during training. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772
skills.summary: Excludes variants used to train a pathogenicity classifier (eDiVA-Score's 15,000 ClinVar pathogenic variants) and all ClinVar-annotated variants from HGMD/GnomAD evaluation sets before computing ROC/AUC, so benchmark results are not inflated by variants the model saw during training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The classifier under evaluation was not trained on ClinVar or HGMD-derived data, so no training-set overlap with the benchmark positives is possible The variant set has already been de-duplicated against the classifier's training variants and ClinVar annotations You are using the benchmark variants themselves for model training or feature engineering — exclusion is meant for evaluation only, not as a data-cleaning step

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw PacBio subreads or uncompiled Iso-Seq cluster output that has not yet been assembled into an IsoPops database via compile_raw_db/process_db Goal is isoform discovery/detection rather than curation — filtering imposes the paper's abundance and exon-count thresholds and will discard rare transcripts that a discovery run should retain Input is short-read RNA-seq data, which cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase transcript sequences needed for exon-boundary-based filtering

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short-read RNA-seq rather than nanopore direct RNA sequencing — Salmon's error model should not be disabled and DRS-specific 3'-end filtering does not apply No ground-truth abundance data (e.g. spike-ins with known concentrations) exist, so quantification accuracy cannot be evaluated against expected values The goal is gene-level rather than transcript/isoform-level abundance estimation, which these isoform-resolving quantifiers are not designed to benchmark

skills.search_text: transcript-annotation-classification Use when you have a PacBio Iso-seq full-length transcript FASTA and need to classify each read against a reference annotation (e.g., hg38) to detect known vs novel splice junctions, isoforms, or gene fusions. skills.description: Use when you have IsoCon final_candidates.fa transcripts from targeted Iso-Seq sequencing of highly similar gene copies (e.g., Y chromosome ampliconic families) and need to collapse exon-level isoforms into transcript groups and count coding vs non-coding members per family.
skills.name: transcript-family-maximal-clique-grouping
skills.search_text: transcript-family-maximal-clique-grouping Use when you have IsoCon final_candidates.fa transcripts from targeted Iso-Seq sequencing of highly similar gene copies (e.g., Y chromosome ampliconic families) and need to collapse exon-level isoforms into transcript groups and count coding vs non-coding members per family. Transcripts come from distinct, non-duplicated genes where isoform redundancy is already resolved by a reference annotation — clique grouping would merge genuinely different isoforms or be unnecessary. Differences between transcripts include substitutions or short indels rather than only large exon-level indels — such pairs must not be grouped together. skills.search_text: transcript-isoform-weighted-sampling Use when building simulated RNA-seq transcriptomes where the splicing order of adjacent introns (UPFI vs DOFI) must vary per transcript while gene/transcript selection reflects transcript exon-count complexity, to validate a splicing-order quantification tool like Insplico. skills.description: Decision support for detecting and ranking SNP candidates from MinION reads aligned to a target with LAST, when you need transition/transversion-weighted polymorphism probabilities from a MAF alignment.
skills.name: transition-transversion-probability-weighting
skills.search_text: transition-transversion-probability-weighting Decision support for detecting and ranking SNP candidates from MinION reads aligned to a target with LAST, when you need transition/transversion-weighted polymorphism probabilities from a MAF alignment. Input reads are not from Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing or have not been aligned to a target with LAST, since the weighting and p-error estimation depend on LAST reliability scores A more sophisticated SNP-calling statistic is required — the article notes current detection statistics are not yet sophisticated and more advanced evaluation is planned future work The task is consensus base calling at low coverage: positions with fewer than 10 reads get a gap assigned, so below this depth the polymorphism table is unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3573 NanoPipe's SNP-candidate scoring method: alternate nucleotides are flagged when they cover ≥20% of reads and ≥30% of maximum contig coverage, then weighted probabilities are computed by multiplying relative nucleotide frequencies by transition (factor 2) versus transversion (factor 1) weights and rescaled so the top candidate has a joint probability of 1. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy169

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not from Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing or have not been aligned to a target with LAST, since the weighting and p-error estimation depend on LAST reliability scores A more sophisticated SNP-calling statistic is required — the article notes current detection statistics are not yet sophisticated and more advanced evaluation is planned future work The task is consensus base calling at low coverage: positions with fewer than 10 reads get a gap assigned, so below this depth the polymorphism table is unreliable

The variant calls are indels or structural variants — Longshot only calls SNVs (indels must be given in an input VCF for genotyping), and the density filter targets SNV false-positive clusters. The goal is de novo discovery of variant truth rather than quality assessment/benchmarking of existing call sets against annotation strata. The input regions are non-repetitive, high-mappability regions where short-read calling is already reliable — the Ts/Tv contrast between callers is diagnostic specifically in poorly mappable duplicated sequence. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Compute per-stratum transition/transversion (Ts/Tv) ratios for SNV call sets — here, Longshot calls on PacBio SMS reads versus FreeBayes calls on Illumina reads — intersected with segmental-duplication identity strata, to expose mappability-driven false positives and benchmark calling accuracy. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y

skills.search_text: trio-de-novo-variant-detection Use when you have aligned CRAM/BAM reads (Illumina WGS/WES or PacBio HiFi) from a parent-child trio and need to identify variants present in the offspring but absent from both parents. You have low-quality or inaccurate long reads rather than highly accurate short-read or PacBio HiFi data You lack access to BAM/CRAM files and only have VCFs — use HAT-FLEX for drop-in trio DNV detection on existing VCFs instead Input is not a parent-child trio (HAT is designed for trio de novo detection, not somatic or population calling) http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Detect de novo variants (DNVs) from a parent-child sequenced trio by running variant calling (GPU-accelerated Hare or open-source Tortoise), GLnexus family-level joint genotyping, and HAT's custom de novo variant filter on aligned CRAM/BAM reads. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775
skills.summary: Detect de novo variants (DNVs) from a parent-child sequenced trio by running variant calling (GPU-accelerated Hare or open-source Tortoise), GLnexus family-level joint genotyping, and HAT's custom de novo variant filter on aligned CRAM/BAM reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have low-quality or inaccurate long reads rather than highly accurate short-read or PacBio HiFi data You lack access to BAM/CRAM files and only have VCFs — use HAT-FLEX for drop-in trio DNV detection on existing VCFs instead Input is not a parent-child trio (HAT is designed for trio de novo detection, not somatic or population calling)

skills.description: Use when corrected long reads from diploid (trio-classified) datasets must be scored for how faithfully each parental haplotype's k-mers are retained, e.g. comparing haplotype-aware vs. standard error correction.
skills.name: trio-diploid-dataset-haplotype-analysis
skills.search_text: trio-diploid-dataset-haplotype-analysis Use when corrected long reads from diploid (trio-classified) datasets must be scored for how faithfully each parental haplotype's k-mers are retained, e.g. comparing haplotype-aware vs. standard error correction. Input reads are Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi, where the article reports PECAT achieves mediocre performance (Supplementary Table 12 and Supplementary Figs. 21–24) No trio classification or parent-specific k-mer sets are available, since the consistency/completeness metrics are defined over parent-specific k-mer pairs SNP-calling from corrected reads alone is the goal — the article notes that after error correction it is not possible to accurately call SNPs just by aligning corrected reads as Hifiasm did for HiFi reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Evaluates haplotype-specific k-mer consistency and completeness of error-corrected long reads on seven trio-classified diploid datasets (S. cerevisiae SK1×Y12, A. thaliana Col-0×Cvi-0, A. thaliana Col-0×C24, D. melanogaster ISO1×A4, B. taurus Angus×Brahman, B. taurus Bison×Simmental, HG002), benchmarking PECAT's haplotype-aware correction against Canu, FALCON, MECAT2, and NECAT. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-47349-7
skills.summary: Evaluates haplotype-specific k-mer consistency and completeness of error-corrected long reads on seven trio-classified diploid datasets (S. cerevisiae SK1×Y12, A. thaliana Col-0×Cvi-0, A. thaliana Col-0×C24, D. melanogaster ISO1×A4, B. taurus Angus×Brahman, B. taurus Bison×Simmental, HG002), benchmarking PECAT's haplotype-aware correction against Canu, FALCON, MECAT2, and NECAT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are Nanopore duplex or PacBio HiFi, where the article reports PECAT achieves mediocre performance (Supplementary Table 12 and Supplementary Figs. 21–24) No trio classification or parent-specific k-mer sets are available, since the consistency/completeness metrics are defined over parent-specific k-mer pairs SNP-calling from corrected reads alone is the goal — the article notes that after error correction it is not possible to accurately call SNPs just by aligning corrected reads as Hifiasm did for HiFi reads

skills.summary: Parses per-caller trio VCF files from the GIAB Ashkenazi Trio (HG002/HG003/HG004) ONT sup-datasets, extracts biallelic SNV genotypes, and computes the Mendelian Consistency Rate (MCR) to benchmark SNV callers such as miniSNV, Clair3, and Longshot on inheritance consistency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore FASTQ/BAM rather than called variant VCFs — variant calling must happen first (e.g. via miniSNV's chr_chunk_task.py pipeline) VCFs contain only indels, structural variants, or multiallelic sites — the workflow extracts biallelic SNV genotypes only Samples are not a parent–child trio (no parental genotypes to check inheritance against)

skills.description: Use when single-end sRNA-seq FASTQ reads (quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed) must be classified as tRNA-derived fragments and halves and assigned to tRF/tRH subtypes in plant genomes.
skills.name: trna-derived-fragment-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: trna-derived-fragment-subtype-classification Use when single-end sRNA-seq FASTQ reads (quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed) must be classified as tRNA-derived fragments and halves and assigned to tRF/tRH subtypes in plant genomes. The goal is profiling miRNAs, piRNAs, or rRNAs rather than tRNA-derived small RNAs (an annotation pipeline like SPORTS1.0 covers broader canonical small RNA classes). Existing detection tools such as tDRmapper, MINTmap, or tRF2Cancer are a fit only for human datasets — this skill is designed for plant tncRNAs; do not expect human-trained tooling assumptions to transfer. Input is paired-end RNA-seq or long-read data; the pipeline is built for single-end small RNA reads fastq files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Classification and quantification of plant tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs, 14–50 nt) into subtypes (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, leader-tRF, 5'tRH, 3'tRH, other tRF) based on mapped position on mature tRNAs and their 50 bp leader/trailer flanks, as implemented in the tncRNA Toolkit. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Classification and quantification of plant tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs, 14–50 nt) into subtypes (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, leader-tRF, 5'tRH, 3'tRH, other tRF) based on mapped position on mature tRNAs and their 50 bp leader/trailer flanks, as implemented in the tncRNA Toolkit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is profiling miRNAs, piRNAs, or rRNAs rather than tRNA-derived small RNAs (an annotation pipeline like SPORTS1.0 covers broader canonical small RNA classes). Existing detection tools such as tDRmapper, MINTmap, or tRF2Cancer are a fit only for human datasets — this skill is designed for plant tncRNAs; do not expect human-trained tooling assumptions to transfer. Input is paired-end RNA-seq or long-read data; the pipeline is built for single-end small RNA reads fastq files.

skills.description: Use when building a tRNA reference for plant small RNA-seq analysis: a genome FASTA is available and tRNA-derived fragments (tRFs, tRNA halves) must be detected and classified against a curated tRNA gene pool.
skills.name: trna-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: trna-gene-annotation Use when building a tRNA reference for plant small RNA-seq analysis: a genome FASTA is available and tRNA-derived fragments (tRFs, tRNA halves) must be detected and classified against a curated tRNA gene pool. Input is already a small RNA FASTQ to be classified — this skill only builds the tRNA reference/index; use the downstream tncRNA prediction step instead. The genome FASTA headers do not follow the '>chr[Num]' convention and cannot be renamed, since the Toolkit's scripts rely on 'chr' prefixes for automated nuclear/organellar separation. Working with human or animal tncRNA detection, where tools like tDRmapper, MINTmap, or tRF2Cancer (trained on human datasets) may be more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predicts nuclear and organellar tRNA genes with tRNAscan-SE, filters out pseudogenes and low-scoring tRNAs (score < 50), and constructs a masked artificial genome with mature/leader/trailer tRNA FASTA appendices for bowtie indexing in the tncRNA Toolkit. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Predicts nuclear and organellar tRNA genes with tRNAscan-SE, filters out pseudogenes and low-scoring tRNAs (score < 50), and constructs a masked artificial genome with mature/leader/trailer tRNA FASTA appendices for bowtie indexing in the tncRNA Toolkit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small RNA FASTQ to be classified — this skill only builds the tRNA reference/index; use the downstream tncRNA prediction step instead. The genome FASTA headers do not follow the '>chr[Num]' convention and cannot be renamed, since the Toolkit's scripts rely on 'chr' prefixes for automated nuclear/organellar separation. Working with human or animal tncRNA detection, where tools like tDRmapper, MINTmap, or tRF2Cancer (trained on human datasets) may be more appropriate.

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq reads map to tRNA loci and you must classify them into tRF-5s, tRF-3s, tRF-1s, or tRNA halves by progenitor isoacceptor (e.g. GluCTC, GlyTCC, LeuTAA, ProCGG) and cleavage position.
skills.name: trna-isoacceptor-classification
skills.search_text: trna-isoacceptor-classification Use when small RNA-seq reads map to tRNA loci and you must classify them into tRF-5s, tRF-3s, tRF-1s, or tRNA halves by progenitor isoacceptor (e.g. GluCTC, GlyTCC, LeuTAA, ProCGG) and cleavage position. Input reads are human or non-plant small RNA data — the referenced detection tools (tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) are trained/tested on human datasets while this classification workflow was validated on six angiosperms Reads map ambiguously to both tRNA-flank artificial chromosomes and other genomic regions — such reads must not be classified as tncRNAs since only exclusively mapping reads qualify The goal is de novo small RNA discovery unrelated to tRNA origin (e.g. miRNA or piRNA profiling) http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Classifies tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs) by their progenitor mature tRNA isoacceptor and cleavage position, enabling codon-dependent cleavage analysis (e.g. detecting the conserved AG::TGG tRF-5::tRNA interface motif) rather than treating reads as random tRNA degradation products. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Classifies tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs) by their progenitor mature tRNA isoacceptor and cleavage position, enabling codon-dependent cleavage analysis (e.g. detecting the conserved AG::TGG tRF-5::tRNA interface motif) rather than treating reads as random tRNA degradation products.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are human or non-plant small RNA data — the referenced detection tools (tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) are trained/tested on human datasets while this classification workflow was validated on six angiosperms Reads map ambiguously to both tRNA-flank artificial chromosomes and other genomic regions — such reads must not be classified as tncRNAs since only exclusively mapping reads qualify The goal is de novo small RNA discovery unrelated to tRNA origin (e.g. miRNA or piRNA profiling)

skills.description: Use when you have a sorted BAM of small RNA reads aligned to an artificial tRNA-masked genome and a masked reference FASTA, and you need to infer which modified nucleosides occur at covered positions on mature tRNAs and their 50 bp leader/trailer flanks.
skills.name: trna-modification-site-prediction
skills.search_text: trna-modification-site-prediction Use when you have a sorted BAM of small RNA reads aligned to an artificial tRNA-masked genome and a masked reference FASTA, and you need to infer which modified nucleosides occur at covered positions on mature tRNAs and their 50 bp leader/trailer flanks. When the input reads were mapped with permissive mismatch settings and base misidentification from sequencing errors would inflate false modification calls — the article notes that allowing a single mismatch 'may lead to base misidentification, and hence causes the inflation of the false negatives' When the goal is tncRNA discovery/quantification rather than modification inference — use the tncRNA Toolkit prediction mode instead of the HAMR step When reads are not restricted to the artificial chromosomes (tRNA plus 50 nt leader/trailer), since ambiguous reads from non-tRNA regions must be excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Predict modified nucleoside sites on tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs) using HAMR v1.2 with the eukaryotic tRNA modification model, applied to small RNA-seq alignments against a masked artificial genome, and aggregate modification calls across species to assess conservation. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Predict modified nucleoside sites on tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tncRNAs) using HAMR v1.2 with the eukaryotic tRNA modification model, applied to small RNA-seq alignments against a masked artificial genome, and aggregate modification calls across species to assess conservation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input reads were mapped with permissive mismatch settings and base misidentification from sequencing errors would inflate false modification calls — the article notes that allowing a single mismatch 'may lead to base misidentification, and hence causes the inflation of the false negatives' When the goal is tncRNA discovery/quantification rather than modification inference — use the tncRNA Toolkit prediction mode instead of the HAMR step When reads are not restricted to the artificial chromosomes (tRNA plus 50 nt leader/trailer), since ambiguous reads from non-tRNA regions must be excluded

skills.description: Use when constructing a tRNA reference set for tncRNA detection and tRNAscan-SE predictions must be filtered to eliminate pseudogenes and low-scoring tRNAs before genome masking and index building.
skills.name: trna-prediction-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: trna-prediction-quality-filtering Use when constructing a tRNA reference set for tncRNA detection and tRNAscan-SE predictions must be filtered to eliminate pseudogenes and low-scoring tRNAs before genome masking and index building. The input is already a curated tRNA annotation or GtRNAdb gene set rather than raw tRNAscan-SE predictions needing pseudogene removal The goal is tncRNA read classification/quantification itself rather than reference curation — that downstream step uses bowtie '-v2 --best' alignment against the already-built artificial genome index The organism's genome headers do not follow the '>chr' naming convention required by tncRNA Toolkit automation, since nuclear/organellar separation depends on it http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Quality-filtering step of the tncRNA Toolkit reference build that removes tRNA pseudogenes and low-scoring predictions from the tRNAscan-SE gene pool so only genuine, high-confidence tRNAs (score ≥ 50) feed the artificial genome index. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Quality-filtering step of the tncRNA Toolkit reference build that removes tRNA pseudogenes and low-scoring predictions from the tRNAscan-SE gene pool so only genuine, high-confidence tRNAs (score ≥ 50) feed the artificial genome index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated tRNA annotation or GtRNAdb gene set rather than raw tRNAscan-SE predictions needing pseudogene removal The goal is tncRNA read classification/quantification itself rather than reference curation — that downstream step uses bowtie '-v2 --best' alignment against the already-built artificial genome index The organism's genome headers do not follow the '>chr' naming convention required by tncRNA Toolkit automation, since nuclear/organellar separation depends on it

skills.description: Use when a PacBio Iso-Seq/lrCaptureSeq isoform database (IsoPops Database compiled from transcript FASTA, abundance table, GFF, and ORF FASTA) may contain truncated transcripts that should be removed before downstream isoform counting or GFF3 export.
skills.name: truncated-transcript-detection
skills.search_text: truncated-transcript-detection Use when a PacBio Iso-Seq/lrCaptureSeq isoform database (IsoPops Database compiled from transcript FASTA, abundance table, GFF, and ORF FASTA) may contain truncated transcripts that should be removed before downstream isoform counting or GFF3 export. Input is raw PacBio subreads or unclustered consensus reads that have not yet been compiled into an IsoPops Database with compile_raw_db/process_db. The goal is de novo transcript discovery or genome annotation rather than curating an existing isoform catalog from targeted lrCaptureSeq data. Short-read RNA-seq data alone is the input — typical read lengths <200 bp cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase isoforms, so truncation filtering of full-length transcripts is not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 IsoPops-based detection and removal of truncated transcript artifacts from lrCaptureSeq isoform catalogs, applied after exon-count and abundance floors and before the bottom-5% abundance filter, to yield the final curated catalog (≈4116 isoforms from 8287 pre-filter isoforms across 30 targeted genes). genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17009-7
skills.summary: IsoPops-based detection and removal of truncated transcript artifacts from lrCaptureSeq isoform catalogs, applied after exon-count and abundance floors and before the bottom-5% abundance filter, to yield the final curated catalog (≈4116 isoforms from 8287 pre-filter isoforms across 30 targeted genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw PacBio subreads or unclustered consensus reads that have not yet been compiled into an IsoPops Database with compile_raw_db/process_db. The goal is de novo transcript discovery or genome annotation rather than curating an existing isoform catalog from targeted lrCaptureSeq data. Short-read RNA-seq data alone is the input — typical read lengths <200 bp cannot resolve full-length multi-kilobase isoforms, so truncation filtering of full-length transcripts is not applicable.

skills.description: Use when nanopore >50-kb CNV call sets (lra/minimap2/NGMLR pipelines) must be polished and benchmarked against a well-characterized truth set such as NA19240/Chaisson, using coverage support as the filtering criterion.
skills.name: truth-set-concordance-evaluation
skills.search_text: truth-set-concordance-evaluation Use when nanopore >50-kb CNV call sets (lra/minimap2/NGMLR pipelines) must be polished and benchmarked against a well-characterized truth set such as NA19240/Chaisson, using coverage support as the filtering criterion. The call set contains SV types other than deletions and duplications (e.g., INV, INS, BND) — disCoverage's coverage test can only be applied to DEL/DUP No putative SV list exists and de novo calling is the goal — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions from another technique or multi-sample analysis Coverage in the sample is too non-uniform (local peaks/valleys, unresolved regions) for the coverage-difference test to discriminate true from false calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Evaluates >50-kb DEL/DUP nanopore SV call sets against a gold-standard truth set (NA19240 with the Chaisson et al. set) by running disCoverage's coverage-difference test per aligner call set, discarding calls lacking coverage support and checking how many truth-set SVs are coverage-supported. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: Evaluates >50-kb DEL/DUP nanopore SV call sets against a gold-standard truth set (NA19240 with the Chaisson et al. set) by running disCoverage's coverage-difference test per aligner call set, discarding calls lacking coverage support and checking how many truth-set SVs are coverage-supported.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The call set contains SV types other than deletions and duplications (e.g., INV, INS, BND) — disCoverage's coverage test can only be applied to DEL/DUP No putative SV list exists and de novo calling is the goal — disCoverage is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions from another technique or multi-sample analysis Coverage in the sample is too non-uniform (local peaks/valleys, unresolved regions) for the coverage-difference test to discriminate true from false calls

skills.search_text: truth-set-genotype-concordance-evaluation Use when a genotyping stage (e.g., RetroInspector's Sniffles2-based genotyper) must be scored against a curated, genotyped truth set such as the 11-case HGSVC2 cohort, to quantify per-allele genotype accuracy. Evaluating insertion *detection* (precision/recall of call presence) against the HGSVC 5,630-insertion truth set — that is a call-level benchmark, not a genotype concordance evaluation No curated, genotyped truth set exists for the cohort, so concordance cannot be computed and results are uninterpretable The goal is TE annotation, enrichment, or reassembly quality rather than genotyping accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks a variant genotyping stage by computing per-allele genotype concordance of called TE insertion/deletion genotypes against a curated truth set (the HGSV2/HGSVC2 cohort), yielding precision metrics per variant-caller combination. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7

skills.description: Use when a TE/SV detection callset must be quantitatively scored against a validated truth set (e.g., HGSVC BAM/VCF truth insertions) to report precision/recall/F1 at a defined bp distance margin.
skills.name: truth-set-matching-distance-margin
skills.search_text: truth-set-matching-distance-margin Use when a TE/SV detection callset must be quantitatively scored against a validated truth set (e.g., HGSVC BAM/VCF truth insertions) to report precision/recall/F1 at a defined bp distance margin. No experimentally validated truth set exists for the samples/genome, so matched calls cannot be interpreted as true positives (incomplete truth sets inflate apparent false positives) The callset contains SNVs or short indels well below the structural-variant scale (>50 bp) where coordinate-distance matching is meaningful Data are not nanopore/human-genome structural variant calls aligned to a reference (e.g., GRCh38) — the thresholds and margins were calibrated for long-read human SV benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmark TE insertion detection by matching a pipeline's predicted insertions against a curated truth set (e.g., the 5,630 HGSVC TE insertions) with SURVIVOR using a fixed coordinate distance margin (100 bp default, 500 bp expanded), then computing precision, recall, and F1-score per filtering threshold. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Benchmark TE insertion detection by matching a pipeline's predicted insertions against a curated truth set (e.g., the 5,630 HGSVC TE insertions) with SURVIVOR using a fixed coordinate distance margin (100 bp default, 500 bp expanded), then computing precision, recall, and F1-score per filtering threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No experimentally validated truth set exists for the samples/genome, so matched calls cannot be interpreted as true positives (incomplete truth sets inflate apparent false positives) The callset contains SNVs or short indels well below the structural-variant scale (>50 bp) where coordinate-distance matching is meaningful Data are not nanopore/human-genome structural variant calls aligned to a reference (e.g., GRCh38) — the thresholds and margins were calibrated for long-read human SV benchmarking
