skills.search_text: two-proportions-z-test-hypothesis-testing Use when you have a reconstructed IsoTools Transcriptome (from PacBio/SequelII LRTS bam files plus gff3/gtf reference annotation) split into control/treatment groups and need counts of differential splicing events or TSS/PAS usage shifts. Input is short-read RNA-seq only (no long-read bam files) — IsoTools' event extraction and z-test require full-length transcript alignments; use short-read tools like rMATS directly No reference annotation in gff3/gtf format is available and none can be supplied, since Transcriptome.from_reference is required before event definition The goal is transcript reconstruction or QC rather than differential event testing between sample groups http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Detect differential alternative splicing, TSS and PAS usage between sample groups from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) using IsoTools' two-proportions z-test with FDR correction, validated against short-read rMATS quantification. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad364
skills.summary: Detect differential alternative splicing, TSS and PAS usage between sample groups from long-read transcriptome sequencing (LRTS) using IsoTools' two-proportions z-test with FDR correction, validated against short-read rMATS quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq only (no long-read bam files) — IsoTools' event extraction and z-test require full-length transcript alignments; use short-read tools like rMATS directly No reference annotation in gff3/gtf format is available and none can be supplied, since Transcriptome.from_reference is required before event definition The goal is transcript reconstruction or QC rather than differential event testing between sample groups

skills.description: Use when you have pseudobulk per cell-type isoform counts (e.g. from scywalker's pseudobulk module) for two cell groups and need genes with significant differential transcript usage at gene- and transcript-level FDR control.
skills.name: two-stage-hierarchical-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: two-stage-hierarchical-fdr-correction Use when you have pseudobulk per cell-type isoform counts (e.g. from scywalker's pseudobulk module) for two cell groups and need genes with significant differential transcript usage at gene- and transcript-level FDR control. Input is per-cell or bulk gene-level (not isoform/transcript-level) counts — DTU testing requires multi-isoform genes; use differential expression instead More than two group levels with a simple two-group design — the described workflow uses a two-group comparison design matrix and would need redesign Counts come from short-read data or non-scywalker pseudo-bulk files with a different isoform id schema that lacks transcript-to-gene mapping required for the two-stage split http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies DRIMSeq's Dirichlet-multinomial gene-level screening followed by stageR hierarchical two-stage FDR correction to identify genes with differential transcript usage (gDTU) between cell groups and assign per-transcript tFDR values from scywalker pseudobulk isoform counts. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Applies DRIMSeq's Dirichlet-multinomial gene-level screening followed by stageR hierarchical two-stage FDR correction to identify genes with differential transcript usage (gDTU) between cell groups and assign per-transcript tFDR values from scywalker pseudobulk isoform counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is per-cell or bulk gene-level (not isoform/transcript-level) counts — DTU testing requires multi-isoform genes; use differential expression instead More than two group levels with a simple two-group design — the described workflow uses a two-group comparison design matrix and would need redesign Counts come from short-read data or non-scywalker pseudo-bulk files with a different isoform id schema that lacks transcript-to-gene mapping required for the two-stage split

skills.description: Use when writing pixel-level-normalized multiplex tissue imaging data back to a 16-bit OME-TIFF stack and a normalization factor <1 would otherwise compress intensities into a narrow uint16 band, creating rounding spikes at low intensities.
skills.name: uint16-intensity-rescaling-with-rounding-spike-avoidance
skills.search_text: uint16-intensity-rescaling-with-rounding-spike-avoidance Use when writing pixel-level-normalized multiplex tissue imaging data back to a 16-bit OME-TIFF stack and a normalization factor <1 would otherwise compress intensities into a narrow uint16 band, creating rounding spikes at low intensities. Input is already a single-cell feature table (e.g., .h5ad per-cell intensity data) — use UniFORM's feature-level workflow instead of the pixel-level stretching mechanism Data is multiplexed immunohistochemistry (mIHC) with chromogenic detection, where enzyme-catalyzed colorimetric amplification produces non-linear signal intensities incompatible with linear normalization factors Images contain significant extracellular signal or compromised segmentation masks, since UniFORM performs pixel-level normalization exclusively within nuclear or cellular segmentation masks http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 A post-normalization stretching mechanism in UniFORM's pixel-level pipeline that applies a stretching factor—derived from the most-compressed sample—to restore intensity ranges to pre-normalization levels before rescaling to uint16, preventing rounding-spike compression artifacts in the OME-TIFF output. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172
skills.summary: A post-normalization stretching mechanism in UniFORM's pixel-level pipeline that applies a stretching factor—derived from the most-compressed sample—to restore intensity ranges to pre-normalization levels before rescaling to uint16, preventing rounding-spike compression artifacts in the OME-TIFF output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single-cell feature table (e.g., .h5ad per-cell intensity data) — use UniFORM's feature-level workflow instead of the pixel-level stretching mechanism Data is multiplexed immunohistochemistry (mIHC) with chromogenic detection, where enzyme-catalyzed colorimetric amplification produces non-linear signal intensities incompatible with linear normalization factors Images contain significant extracellular signal or compromised segmentation masks, since UniFORM performs pixel-level normalization exclusively within nuclear or cellular segmentation masks

skills.description: Use when mapping FLNC (full-length non-chimeric) Iso-Seq reads to a genome for which a GTF exon annotation exists, and accurate splice alignment around small exons is required.
skills.name: ultra-genome-alignment-with-gtf
skills.search_text: ultra-genome-alignment-with-gtf Use when mapping FLNC (full-length non-chimeric) Iso-Seq reads to a genome for which a GTF exon annotation exists, and accurate splice alignment around small exons is required. No GTF annotation is available for the reference genome — the pipeline falls back to minimap2 splice-aware alignment instead of uLTRA. The GTF is malformed — uLTRA produces spurious alignments in that case, so the annotation should be validated first. Reads are short genomic reads or non-transcriptomic data — uLTRA targets splice alignment of long transcriptomic reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns PacBio Iso-Seq FLNC reads onto a reference genome with uLTRA, a splice-aware aligner guided by exon annotations, as implemented in the nf-core/isoseq mapping step; uLTRA is chosen when a GTF annotation is available for the genome, and falls back to minimap2 when it is not. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad150
skills.summary: Aligns PacBio Iso-Seq FLNC reads onto a reference genome with uLTRA, a splice-aware aligner guided by exon annotations, as implemented in the nf-core/isoseq mapping step; uLTRA is chosen when a GTF annotation is available for the genome, and falls back to minimap2 when it is not.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No GTF annotation is available for the reference genome — the pipeline falls back to minimap2 splice-aware alignment instead of uLTRA. The GTF is malformed — uLTRA produces spurious alignments in that case, so the annotation should be validated first. Reads are short genomic reads or non-transcriptomic data — uLTRA targets splice alignment of long transcriptomic reads.

skills.description: Use when a long-read correction run targets a genome-scale ONT dataset (e.g., 113 Gbp human data, ultra-long reads up to 1.5 Mbp) and runtime, RAM, core count, and disk for overlaps must be planned before launching.
skills.name: ultra-long-read-dataset-resource-management
skills.search_text: ultra-long-read-dataset-resource-management Use when a long-read correction run targets a genome-scale ONT dataset (e.g., 113 Gbp human data, ultra-long reads up to 1.5 Mbp) and runtime, RAM, core count, and disk for overlaps must be planned before launching. The dataset is small (e.g., a few hundred Mbp of simulated or bacterial reads) where default tmpdir on the working directory and modest RAM suffice, as in the README's 10x example dataset. The goal is assembly polishing rather than read self-correction, which uses CONSENT-polish and does not require the ~5 TB overlaps staging described here. Corrections require reference-based alignment of short reads (e.g., CoLoRMAP, HECiL style), not self-correction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Provisioning and executing long-read self-correction (e.g., CONSENT) on ultra-large ONT datasets with reads up to 1.5 Mbp by pre-planning multi-day runtimes, ~100 GB RAM, multi-core parallelism, and ~5 TB of disk for the temporary overlaps file. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Provisioning and executing long-read self-correction (e.g., CONSENT) on ultra-large ONT datasets with reads up to 1.5 Mbp by pre-planning multi-day runtimes, ~100 GB RAM, multi-core parallelism, and ~5 TB of disk for the temporary overlaps file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small (e.g., a few hundred Mbp of simulated or bacterial reads) where default tmpdir on the working directory and modest RAM suffice, as in the README's 10x example dataset. The goal is assembly polishing rather than read self-correction, which uses CONSENT-polish and does not require the ~5 TB overlaps staging described here. Corrections require reference-based alignment of short reads (e.g., CoLoRMAP, HECiL style), not self-correction.

skills.description: Use when input is a large FASTA of long and similar nucleotide sequences (e.g., mtDB benchmark genomes duplicated 20x/50x/100x, or VARV/E.coli-scale datasets) where stand-alone MSA tools time out or are prohibitively slow.
skills.name: ultralong-genome-sequence-handling
skills.search_text: ultralong-genome-sequence-handling Use when input is a large FASTA of long and similar nucleotide sequences (e.g., mtDB benchmark genomes duplicated 20x/50x/100x, or VARV/E.coli-scale datasets) where stand-alone MSA tools time out or are prohibitively slow. Sequences are short or highly divergent — FMAlign2's MEM-based segmentation targets ultra-long and similar nucleotide sequences; FMAlign's time-saving advantage converges with stand-alone methods as sequence count grows (e.g., at mt 100x), so stand-alone HAlign3 may be faster on some mtDB inputs Alignment involves protein sequences — the method is explicitly a multiple nucleotide sequence alignment algorithm http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A skill for aligning ultra-long nucleotide sequence sets (sequences approaching billions of bases) by wrapping existing MSA backends (MAFFT, Clustal Omega, HAlign3, HAlign4) with FMAlign2, which segments sequences via suffix-array maximal exact matches (MEMs) and a vertical division strategy with parallel subMSA execution. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae014
skills.summary: A skill for aligning ultra-long nucleotide sequence sets (sequences approaching billions of bases) by wrapping existing MSA backends (MAFFT, Clustal Omega, HAlign3, HAlign4) with FMAlign2, which segments sequences via suffix-array maximal exact matches (MEMs) and a vertical division strategy with parallel subMSA execution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are short or highly divergent — FMAlign2's MEM-based segmentation targets ultra-long and similar nucleotide sequences; FMAlign's time-saving advantage converges with stand-alone methods as sequence count grows (e.g., at mt 100x), so stand-alone HAlign3 may be faster on some mtDB inputs Alignment involves protein sequences — the method is explicitly a multiple nucleotide sequence alignment algorithm

skills.description: Use when self-correcting ONT long reads that include ultra-long molecules (up to 1.5 Mbp, e.g. full human datasets), or when deciding whether error correction improves Miniasm/Flye assembly quality versus raw reads.
skills.name: ultralong-ont-read-handling
skills.search_text: ultralong-ont-read-handling Use when self-correcting ONT long reads that include ultra-long molecules (up to 1.5 Mbp, e.g. full human datasets), or when deciding whether error correction improves Miniasm/Flye assembly quality versus raw reads. Reads are short reads or require hybrid correction with short-read alignment (e.g. CoLoRMAP/HECiL-style workflows); CONSENT is a self-correction method using only long-read overlaps The goal is polishing an existing raw assembly rather than read correction — use CONSENT-polish instead Turnaround must be fast: CONSENT's correction step runtime tends to be higher than other state-of-the-art methods, and on human chr 1 it is almost four times faster than Canu but still takes days-scale compute http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3489 Correct and assess ultra-long Oxford Nanopore long reads (up to 1.5 Mbp) with CONSENT, the only self-correction method that efficiently scales to ultra-long ONT data, and evaluate the impact of correction on downstream Miniasm/Flye assemblies with QUAST-LG. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80757-5
skills.summary: Correct and assess ultra-long Oxford Nanopore long reads (up to 1.5 Mbp) with CONSENT, the only self-correction method that efficiently scales to ultra-long ONT data, and evaluate the impact of correction on downstream Miniasm/Flye assemblies with QUAST-LG.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are short reads or require hybrid correction with short-read alignment (e.g. CoLoRMAP/HECiL-style workflows); CONSENT is a self-correction method using only long-read overlaps The goal is polishing an existing raw assembly rather than read correction — use CONSENT-polish instead Turnaround must be fast: CONSENT's correction step runtime tends to be higher than other state-of-the-art methods, and on human chr 1 it is almost four times faster than Canu but still takes days-scale compute

skills.description: Use when raw 10x-structured Oxford nanopore FASTQ must be demultiplexed by cell barcode and UMI before read alignment or isoform/gene reconstruction, and no matching short-read data is available.
skills.name: umi-and-barcode-extraction-from-nanopore-reads
skills.search_text: umi-and-barcode-extraction-from-nanopore-reads Use when raw 10x-structured Oxford nanopore FASTQ must be demultiplexed by cell barcode and UMI before read alignment or isoform/gene reconstruction, and no matching short-read data is available. Input reads lack the 10x structure (no CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT-flanked 16-bp barcode + 12-bp UMI), e.g. user-specified non-10x protocols or PacBio data without the appropriate options Matching short-read data is available and already provides demultiplexed cell barcodes (scywalker targets analysis 'without the need for matching short read data') Reads are already demultiplexed FASTQs with barcode/UMI in read names — proceed directly to alignment/isoform calling instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Scywalker's droplet barcoding module extracts the 16-bp cell barcode and 12-bp UMI from 10x-structured Oxford nanopore FASTQ reads using the 10x v3 adapter (CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT), then calls droplet barcodes by iterative top-count selection with edit-distance-1 correction against the 10x 737K-august-2016 whitelist. It emits a demultiplexed FASTQ in which the corrected barcode and UMI are carried with each read for downstream single-cell isoform analysis. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Scywalker's droplet barcoding module extracts the 16-bp cell barcode and 12-bp UMI from 10x-structured Oxford nanopore FASTQ reads using the 10x v3 adapter (CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT), then calls droplet barcodes by iterative top-count selection with edit-distance-1 correction against the 10x 737K-august-2016 whitelist. It emits a demultiplexed FASTQ in which the corrected barcode and UMI are carried with each read for downstream single-cell isoform analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack the 10x structure (no CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT-flanked 16-bp barcode + 12-bp UMI), e.g. user-specified non-10x protocols or PacBio data without the appropriate options Matching short-read data is available and already provides demultiplexed cell barcodes (scywalker targets analysis 'without the need for matching short read data') Reads are already demultiplexed FASTQs with barcode/UMI in read names — proceed directly to alignment/isoform calling instead

skills.description: Use when you have a barcode-, UMI- and gene-tagged Nanopore BAM (with BC, U8, GE tags) and need one consensus cDNA per cell-UMI molecule for downstream isoform or variant analysis (Sicelore Step 4.b).
skills.name: umi-based-read-grouping
skills.search_text: umi-based-read-grouping Use when you have a barcode-, UMI- and gene-tagged Nanopore BAM (with BC, U8, GE tags) and need one consensus cDNA per cell-UMI molecule for downstream isoform or variant analysis (Sicelore Step 4.b). Input SAM records lack BC, U8 or GE tags (e.g. unannotated BAM from before Step 3 UMI assignment) — no molecules can be formed You want to build matrices directly from cellBC-UMI annotated long-reads without error correction (Sicelore Step 4 option a) rather than from consensus molecules UMIs are covered by fewer reads than needed for consensus (only single/double-read molecules exist), where consensus building reduces to read selection, not poa/racon error correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Groups Nanopore SAM records per cell barcode and UMI and computes a single error-corrected consensus cDNA per molecule using Sicelore's ComputeConsensus (poa multiple alignment polished with racon). This is the UMI-guided error-correction core of ScNaUmi-seq that turns noisy long reads into high-accuracy molecule sequences. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Groups Nanopore SAM records per cell barcode and UMI and computes a single error-corrected consensus cDNA per molecule using Sicelore's ComputeConsensus (poa multiple alignment polished with racon). This is the UMI-guided error-correction core of ScNaUmi-seq that turns noisy long reads into high-accuracy molecule sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input SAM records lack BC, U8 or GE tags (e.g. unannotated BAM from before Step 3 UMI assignment) — no molecules can be formed You want to build matrices directly from cellBC-UMI annotated long-reads without error correction (Sicelore Step 4 option a) rather than from consensus molecules UMIs are covered by fewer reads than needed for consensus (only single/double-read molecules exist), where consensus building reduces to read selection, not poa/racon error correction

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore long reads from a 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq library must be converted into per-cell gene/isoform UMI count matrices via consensus sequences and strict Gencode isoform assignment.
skills.name: umi-consensus-read-mapping
skills.search_text: umi-consensus-read-mapping Use when raw Nanopore long reads from a 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq library must be converted into per-cell gene/isoform UMI count matrices via consensus sequences and strict Gencode isoform assignment. Input is raw short-read (Illumina) scRNA-seq data rather than Nanopore/PacBio long reads — Sicelore's long-read consensus and isoform assignment do not apply. The goal is novel isoform discovery from unannotated splice junctions rather than assignment of UMIs to known Gencode transcript isoforms (METHOD=STRICT discards novel structures). Only cell barcode/UMI-tagged long reads exist without UMI consensus FASTQs from ComputeConsensus, i.e. Step 4 option a (IsoformMatrixReads) would be used instead of the molecules-based path. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Maps UMI-guided error-corrected consensus reads from Nanopore single-cell data to a reference genome and assigns them to annotated transcript isoforms, producing gene-, isoform-, and junction-level UMI count matrices with Sicelore. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Maps UMI-guided error-corrected consensus reads from Nanopore single-cell data to a reference genome and assigns them to annotated transcript isoforms, producing gene-, isoform-, and junction-level UMI count matrices with Sicelore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short-read (Illumina) scRNA-seq data rather than Nanopore/PacBio long reads — Sicelore's long-read consensus and isoform assignment do not apply. The goal is novel isoform discovery from unannotated splice junctions rather than assignment of UMIs to known Gencode transcript isoforms (METHOD=STRICT discards novel structures). Only cell barcode/UMI-tagged long reads exist without UMI consensus FASTQs from ComputeConsensus, i.e. Step 4 option a (IsoformMatrixReads) would be used instead of the molecules-based path.

skills.description: Use when you have long-read single-cell (10x ONT) count matrices and a matching short-read Cell Ranger run of the same library and want to quantify cell barcode detection and quantification agreement via correlation.
skills.name: umi-count-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: umi-count-correlation-analysis Use when you have long-read single-cell (10x ONT) count matrices and a matching short-read Cell Ranger run of the same library and want to quantify cell barcode detection and quantification agreement via correlation. No matched short-read (Cell Ranger) data exist for the library — scywalker is designed to analyse 10x nanopore data without matching short reads, so this correlation is impossible and validation must use other signals The datasets come from different libraries or samples, so cell-level correlation would be meaningless Comparing bulk (not per-cell) long-read quantification only, where per-cell correlation of emptydrops-filtered cells does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark long-read single-cell pipelines by computing Pearson correlations of their UMI count matrices against a matching short-read (Cell Ranger) quantification, at the cell level and the gene-per-cell level, as done for scywalker vs BLAZE-FLAMES vs ONT wf-single-cell on scmixology2. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae549
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read single-cell pipelines by computing Pearson correlations of their UMI count matrices against a matching short-read (Cell Ranger) quantification, at the cell level and the gene-per-cell level, as done for scywalker vs BLAZE-FLAMES vs ONT wf-single-cell on scmixology2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched short-read (Cell Ranger) data exist for the library — scywalker is designed to analyse 10x nanopore data without matching short reads, so this correlation is impossible and validation must use other signals The datasets come from different libraries or samples, so cell-level correlation would be meaningless Comparing bulk (not per-cell) long-read quantification only, where per-cell correlation of emptydrops-filtered cells does not apply

skills.description: Use when ScNaUmi-seq 10x-linked Nanopore reads are available and you need UMI-guided error-corrected consensus molecules to call site-level sequence variation (SNPs/RNA editing) per molecule or per cell at defined genomic positions.
skills.name: umi-error-corrected-consensus-analysis
skills.search_text: umi-error-corrected-consensus-analysis Use when ScNaUmi-seq 10x-linked Nanopore reads are available and you need UMI-guided error-corrected consensus molecules to call site-level sequence variation (SNPs/RNA editing) per molecule or per cell at defined genomic positions. Input reads have not been cell-barcode/UMI assigned and collapsed into consensus molecules (Sicelore steps 1-4b must run first; raw Nanopore reads are too noisy for per-position editing calls) The analysis goal is cell-by-cell SNV calling on high-coverage data where stricter molecule filters (MINRN > 0) are appropriate and permissive MINRN=0/MINQV=0 retention is unnecessary The target variants are short-read-only splice/junction events rather than sequence variation at defined genomic positions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates per-UMI consensus molecules from Nanopore long reads with Sicelore (step 4.b, using spoa POA consensus) and queries the error-corrected molecules BAM for sequence variation such as A-to-I RNA editing at specific loci, e.g. Gria2 Q/R and R/G sites in E18 mouse brain ScNaUmi-seq data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17800-6
skills.summary: Generates per-UMI consensus molecules from Nanopore long reads with Sicelore (step 4.b, using spoa POA consensus) and queries the error-corrected molecules BAM for sequence variation such as A-to-I RNA editing at specific loci, e.g. Gria2 Q/R and R/G sites in E18 mouse brain ScNaUmi-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not been cell-barcode/UMI assigned and collapsed into consensus molecules (Sicelore steps 1-4b must run first; raw Nanopore reads are too noisy for per-position editing calls) The analysis goal is cell-by-cell SNV calling on high-coverage data where stricter molecule filters (MINRN > 0) are appropriate and permissive MINRN=0/MINQV=0 retention is unnecessary The target variants are short-read-only splice/junction events rather than sequence variation at defined genomic positions

skills.description: Use when processing long reads from 10x Genomics 5'-anchored whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries and per-read cell-barcode and UMI tags are needed before downstream mutation or isoform calling.
skills.name: umi-extraction-from-single-cell-cdna-reads
skills.search_text: umi-extraction-from-single-cell-cdna-reads Use when processing long reads from 10x Genomics 5'-anchored whole-transcriptome cDNA libraries and per-read cell-barcode and UMI tags are needed before downstream mutation or isoform calling. Input is short-read 10x Read 1 data where barcodes/UMIs are provided directly in the read header rather than embedded in long cDNA softclips The library is not 5'-anchored 10x Genomics chemistry, since the barcode-UMI motif search assumes the barcode-UMI cassette lies in the 5' softclip UMIs have a known whitelist available — in that case whitelist-based correction, not starcode distance-3 clustering, is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns 10x Genomics cell barcodes and extracts 10 nt UMIs from long-read single-cell cDNA sequences (ONT/PacBio) via N-padded-whitelist STAR alignment, then corrects UMI sequencing error downstream by starcode clustering. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Assigns 10x Genomics cell barcodes and extracts 10 nt UMIs from long-read single-cell cDNA sequences (ONT/PacBio) via N-padded-whitelist STAR alignment, then corrects UMI sequencing error downstream by starcode clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read 10x Read 1 data where barcodes/UMIs are provided directly in the read header rather than embedded in long cDNA softclips The library is not 5'-anchored 10x Genomics chemistry, since the barcode-UMI motif search assumes the barcode-UMI cassette lies in the 5' softclip UMIs have a known whitelist available — in that case whitelist-based correction, not starcode distance-3 clustering, is appropriate

skills.description: Use when patient symptoms are encoded as HPO codes and must be translated to UMLS CUIs to seed downstream gene-disease association retrieval, e.g. in the VIBE prioritization pipeline.
skills.name: umls-metathesaurus-concept-lookup
skills.search_text: umls-metathesaurus-concept-lookup Use when patient symptoms are encoded as HPO codes and must be translated to UMLS CUIs to seed downstream gene-disease association retrieval, e.g. in the VIBE prioritization pipeline. The phenotypes are already provided as UMLS CUIs or as free text not resolvable to HPO terms (no HPO-to-CUI crosswalk is needed, or HPO matching is not possible). The goal is direct gene prioritization output (ranked gene list with GDA scores) rather than the intermediate ontology crosswalk — use the full VIBE run instead. Only HPO-to-ORDO or HPO-to-DisGeNET-PDA branches are needed without UMLS Metathesaurus CUI matching. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) search terms (e.g. HP:0002996, HP:0001377) to UMLS CUIs (concept unique identifiers) using an optimized SPARQL query executed against VIBE's TDB triple store, as the first step of phenotype-based disease gene prioritization. genomics/v1 10.1002/ggn2.10023
skills.summary: Maps Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) search terms (e.g. HP:0002996, HP:0001377) to UMLS CUIs (concept unique identifiers) using an optimized SPARQL query executed against VIBE's TDB triple store, as the first step of phenotype-based disease gene prioritization.

skills.name: variant-caller-ablation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: variant-caller-ablation-benchmarking Decision support for quantifying whether a variant caller's prior-knowledge component (e.g. known common variants as variation backgrounds) measurably improves precision, recall, or F1 on benchmark datasets such as HG002 ONT k12/k14 reads. The goal is to compare different variant callers against each other (e.g. miniSNV vs Clair3 vs Longshot) rather than to isolate the effect of a single caller's internal feature via ablation. Input is raw signal/FASTQ without a sorted, indexed BAM aligned to GRCh38 — miniSNV requires samtools-indexed sorted BAM input. The organism or sample lacks a population VCF of known common variants, so the variation-background index cannot be built. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 An ablation benchmarking protocol that quantifies how a variant caller's population-variation background (e.g. miniSNV's known-common-variant index from the 1000 Genomes VCF) affects SNV calling precision, recall, and F1 against a GIAB truth set. It isolates the contribution of prior-knowledge features by running the caller with the feature enabled versus disabled under otherwise identical parameters. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: An ablation benchmarking protocol that quantifies how a variant caller's population-variation background (e.g. miniSNV's known-common-variant index from the 1000 Genomes VCF) affects SNV calling precision, recall, and F1 against a GIAB truth set. It isolates the contribution of prior-knowledge features by running the caller with the feature enabled versus disabled under otherwise identical parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare different variant callers against each other (e.g. miniSNV vs Clair3 vs Longshot) rather than to isolate the effect of a single caller's internal feature via ablation. Input is raw signal/FASTQ without a sorted, indexed BAM aligned to GRCh38 — miniSNV requires samtools-indexed sorted BAM input. The organism or sample lacks a population VCF of known common variants, so the variation-background index cannot be built.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is from a completely novel sequencing technology/chemistry for which no high-quality GIAB-style training dataset exists — Clairvoyante cannot be applied in that setting The goal is indel calling on ONT data — the paper reports the Indel F1-score remains around 50%, so benchmark results will not be representative of production indel accuracy Variants of interest have two or more alternative alleles — the current Clairvoyante design ignores such variants, biasing comparisons

skills.description: Decision support for choosing which SV caller pairing and minimum supporting-read threshold to configure in RetroInspector (or a similar nanopore TE-detection pipeline) when performance must be quantified against a curated truth set such as HGSVC.
skills.name: variant-caller-combination-comparison
skills.search_text: variant-caller-combination-comparison Decision support for choosing which SV caller pairing and minimum supporting-read threshold to configure in RetroInspector (or a similar nanopore TE-detection pipeline) when performance must be quantified against a curated truth set such as HGSVC. When the goal is TE detection performance of RetroInspector itself against external pipelines (PALMER, GraffiTE) rather than an internal caller-combination ablation When short-read data is the input — this comparison is grounded in nanopore long-read alignment against GRCh38 When a quick production run is needed with the pipeline defaults, since the article already establishes cuteSV+Sniffles2 with at least 3 supporting reads as the default (and recommended) settings of RetroInspector http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmark structural-variant caller combinations (cuteSV+Sniffles2 versus Sniffles2+SVIM) for transposable-element insertion detection in nanopore data, filtering calls by a supporting-read threshold and scoring precision/recall/F1 against the HGSV truth set. skills.summary: Benchmark structural-variant caller combinations (cuteSV+Sniffles2 versus Sniffles2+SVIM) for transposable-element insertion detection in nanopore data, filtering calls by a supporting-read threshold and scoring precision/recall/F1 against the HGSV truth set. skills.description: Use when comparing the sensitivity/specificity of TR or variant callers on simulated long-read BAMs with a known truth set, or when reproducing per-class precision/recall/F1 benchmark tables at defined discrepancy thresholds.
skills.name: variant-caller-metric-comparison
skills.search_text: variant-caller-metric-comparison Use when comparing the sensitivity/specificity of TR or variant callers on simulated long-read BAMs with a known truth set, or when reproducing per-class precision/recall/F1 benchmark tables at defined discrepancy thresholds. Input is real (non-simulated) human whole-genome sequencing data without a truth set — validation then requires orthogonal Illumina FM indexes rather than per-class recall/precision/F1 against simulated truth. The genome contains unassembled regions such as human centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats in. The aim is TR profiling in polyploid species or haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3574 Benchmark two long-read tandem repeat callers (TRiCoLOR and NCRF) on VISOR-simulated haplotype-resolved ONT and PacBio BAMs by computing per-class recall, precision, and F1 against a simulated truth set at 1-motif and 2-motif discrepancy thresholds. This reproduces the TRiCoLOR paper's head-to-head comparison showing TRiCoLOR's superior recall on contractions, small expansions, and long expansions. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Benchmark two long-read tandem repeat callers (TRiCoLOR and NCRF) on VISOR-simulated haplotype-resolved ONT and PacBio BAMs by computing per-class recall, precision, and F1 against a simulated truth set at 1-motif and 2-motif discrepancy thresholds. This reproduces the TRiCoLOR paper's head-to-head comparison showing TRiCoLOR's superior recall on contractions, small expansions, and long expansions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) human whole-genome sequencing data without a truth set — validation then requires orthogonal Illumina FM indexes rather than per-class recall/precision/F1 against simulated truth. The genome contains unassembled regions such as human centromeres and telomeres, which TRiCoLOR cannot identify repeats in. The aim is TR profiling in polyploid species or haploid chromosomes (e.g., the human Y chromosome), which TRiCoLOR does not support.

skills.description: Use when calling germline SNVs and small indels genome-wide with Clairvoyante on HG001/NA12878 BAMs and you need to set the alternative allele frequency cutoff and training sampling configuration to match published metrics.
skills.name: variant-caller-threshold-configuration
skills.search_text: variant-caller-threshold-configuration Use when calling germline SNVs and small indels genome-wide with Clairvoyante on HG001/NA12878 BAMs and you need to set the alternative allele frequency cutoff and training sampling configuration to match published metrics. Data are multi-allelic or require detection of two or more alternative alleles at a position — Clairvoyante's current design ignores such variants and network version 3 outputs only one alternative allele per position. Calling somatic variants or trio-sample-based variants — these were not yet supported in this Clairvoyante version. Input alignments are long indel-dominated and you need exact alternative alleles >4 bp — Clairvoyante provides exact alleles only for indels ≤4 bp, and ONT indel F1 remains ~50%. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Configure the Clairvoyante variant caller's calling and training parameters — notably the alternative allele frequency cutoff (0.2 for whole-genome HG001 evaluation) and truth-to-non-variant sample pairing — to reproduce its reported F1-scores across Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Configure the Clairvoyante variant caller's calling and training parameters — notably the alternative allele frequency cutoff (0.2 for whole-genome HG001 evaluation) and truth-to-non-variant sample pairing — to reproduce its reported F1-scores across Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are multi-allelic or require detection of two or more alternative alleles at a position — Clairvoyante's current design ignores such variants and network version 3 outputs only one alternative allele per position. Calling somatic variants or trio-sample-based variants — these were not yet supported in this Clairvoyante version. Input alignments are long indel-dominated and you need exact alternative alleles >4 bp — Clairvoyante provides exact alleles only for indels ≤4 bp, and ONT indel F1 remains ~50%.

skills.search_text: variant-calling-f1-evaluation Use when assessing how faithfully a simulated ONT read set recapitulates real variant-calling performance, or when quantifying sensitivity of variant detection to simulator noise parameters (e.g. sigma_amp, duration SD) or genomic context (homopolymer/STR). Input reads are already real experimental reads and the goal is raw variant calling rather than simulator fidelity assessment The analysis targets methylation/modified-base status rather than small-variant SNP/indel detection performance Downstream analysis is de novo bacterial assembly or abundance correlation rather than variant-level benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Evaluate small-variant calling fidelity of simulated nanopore reads by aligning Dorado-basecalled FASTQ/BAM to a reference, calling variants, and computing SNP/indel F1-scores — optionally swept across noise parameters or stratified by homopolymer/STR context. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag402
skills.summary: Evaluate small-variant calling fidelity of simulated nanopore reads by aligning Dorado-basecalled FASTQ/BAM to a reference, calling variants, and computing SNP/indel F1-scores — optionally swept across noise parameters or stratified by homopolymer/STR context.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already real experimental reads and the goal is raw variant calling rather than simulator fidelity assessment The analysis targets methylation/modified-base status rather than small-variant SNP/indel detection performance Downstream analysis is de novo bacterial assembly or abundance correlation rather than variant-level benchmarking

skills.description: Use when you have raw pooled whole-genome sequencing reads, a reference-free set of predicted exon sequences (e.g. from EXFI's splice graph), and need exonic SNPs/indels suitable for downstream genotyping.
skills.name: variant-calling-from-pooled-genomic-reads
skills.search_text: variant-calling-from-pooled-genomic-reads Use when you have raw pooled whole-genome sequencing reads, a reference-free set of predicted exon sequences (e.g. from EXFI's splice graph), and need exonic SNPs/indels suitable for downstream genotyping. A reference genome is available and reliable — a splice-aware aligner such as GMAP plus standard reference-based variant calling would be the more direct route You need exact genomic coordinates of variants; reads are mapped here to predicted exon sequences, not to a reference genome, so positions are relative to predicted exons The goal is exon/splice-graph prediction itself — use the EXFI build_baited_bloom_filter/build_splice_graph steps instead; this skill covers only the downstream read mapping and SNP calling http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Discovery and genotyping of exonic SNPs/indels by mapping raw pooled-sequence (Pool-Seq) genomic reads onto predicted exon sequences (e.g. EXFI output) and calling variants with BCFTools, applying quality and proximity filters to retain genotypable variants. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Discovery and genotyping of exonic SNPs/indels by mapping raw pooled-sequence (Pool-Seq) genomic reads onto predicted exon sequences (e.g. EXFI output) and calling variants with BCFTools, applying quality and proximity filters to retain genotypable variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome is available and reliable — a splice-aware aligner such as GMAP plus standard reference-based variant calling would be the more direct route You need exact genomic coordinates of variants; reads are mapped here to predicted exon sequences, not to a reference genome, so positions are relative to predicted exons The goal is exon/splice-graph prediction itself — use the EXFI build_baited_bloom_filter/build_splice_graph steps instead; this skill covers only the downstream read mapping and SNP calling

skills.description: Use when benchmarking germline SNV/small-indel callers (e.g., Clairvoyante vs. Nanopolish) on ONT reads against a GIAB truth set, and you need F1, FPR, FNR and precision at a restricted site set such as 1KGp3 common variants.
skills.name: variant-calling-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: variant-calling-metrics-computation Use when benchmarking germline SNV/small-indel callers (e.g., Clairvoyante vs. Nanopolish) on ONT reads against a GIAB truth set, and you need F1, FPR, FNR and precision at a restricted site set such as 1KGp3 common variants. The goal is somatic or trio-based variant calling — the paper explicitly plans but does not support these. Evaluating indel calling on ONT data as the primary metric — Clairvoyante's ONT indel F1-score remains around 50%, so these metrics will not reflect acceptable indel performance. Novel sequencing technologies/chemistries lacking a high-quality GIAB-style training dataset — Clairvoyante cannot be applied there, and metrics would be uninterpretable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark a germline small-variant caller (Clairvoyante on ONT data) and a baseline caller (Nanopolish) against the GIAB HG001 v3.3.2 truth set by restricting calls to 1KGp3 common variant sites and computing F1-score, FPR, FNR, and precision per caller. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a germline small-variant caller (Clairvoyante on ONT data) and a baseline caller (Nanopolish) against the GIAB HG001 v3.3.2 truth set by restricting calls to 1KGp3 common variant sites and computing F1-score, FPR, FNR, and precision per caller.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is somatic or trio-based variant calling — the paper explicitly plans but does not support these. Evaluating indel calling on ONT data as the primary metric — Clairvoyante's ONT indel F1-score remains around 50%, so these metrics will not reflect acceptable indel performance. Novel sequencing technologies/chemistries lacking a high-quality GIAB-style training dataset — Clairvoyante cannot be applied there, and metrics would be uninterpretable.

skills.description: Use when raw WGS/WES FASTQ files must be converted into annotated variant calls and the full tool chain (FastQC to HaplotypeCaller) plus HPC resource allocation needs to be scripted and launched automatically.
skills.name: variant-calling-pipeline-orchestration
skills.search_text: variant-calling-pipeline-orchestration Use when raw WGS/WES FASTQ files must be converted into annotated variant calls and the full tool chain (FastQC to HaplotypeCaller) plus HPC resource allocation needs to be scripted and launched automatically. The current JWES version offers only a command-line interface, so an interactive/GUI workflow is required Data are not WGS/WES FASTQ/FASTA sequence files (e.g. gene-expression matrices) — the pipeline targets sequence data for variant discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Orchestrates the JWES end-to-end WGS/WES variant-calling chain—FastQC QC, Trimmomatic trimming, BWA alignment to hg38, SortSam, MarkDuplicates, SAMtools indexing, and GATK realignment/recalibration/variant-calling steps—and deploys it as an auto-generated Slurm job on HPC. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261

skills.when_to_use_negative: The current JWES version offers only a command-line interface, so an interactive/GUI workflow is required Data are not WGS/WES FASTQ/FASTA sequence files (e.g. gene-expression matrices) — the pipeline targets sequence data for variant discovery

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a long-read SNV caller's accuracy on GIAB PacBio genomes (NA12878, NA24385, NA24149, NA24143) or assessing how precision/recall change with sub-sampled coverage (e.g. 28x to 64x).
skills.name: variant-calling-precision-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: variant-calling-precision-recall-evaluation Use when benchmarking a long-read SNV caller's accuracy on GIAB PacBio genomes (NA12878, NA24385, NA24149, NA24143) or assessing how precision/recall change with sub-sampled coverage (e.g. 28x to 64x). The question is structural variant or indel calling accuracy — Longshot only calls SNVs and accurate short indel calling with SMS reads is noted as challenging due to high insertion/deletion error rates. The truth set is not a short-read-derived high-confidence call set (e.g. de novo assemblies without benchmark regions) — GIAB sets are biased in favor of short-read technologies, so some caller false positives may be truth-set false negatives. Input is raw reads without an indexed, sorted BAM/CRAM aligned to the reference used by the truth set — variant-level comparison requires coordinate-matched calls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Evaluates SNV caller accuracy on whole-genome PacBio SMS data by comparing caller VCFs against GIAB high-confidence truth sets and computing precision (TP/(TP+FP)) and recall (TP/(TP+FN)), optionally as a function of coverage. This is the benchmarking approach used to show Longshot's accuracy (e.g. P=0.995, R=0.968 on NA12878 44x) versus WhatsHap and Clairvoyante. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Evaluates SNV caller accuracy on whole-genome PacBio SMS data by comparing caller VCFs against GIAB high-confidence truth sets and computing precision (TP/(TP+FP)) and recall (TP/(TP+FN)), optionally as a function of coverage. This is the benchmarking approach used to show Longshot's accuracy (e.g. P=0.995, R=0.968 on NA12878 44x) versus WhatsHap and Clairvoyante.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is structural variant or indel calling accuracy — Longshot only calls SNVs and accurate short indel calling with SMS reads is noted as challenging due to high insertion/deletion error rates. The truth set is not a short-read-derived high-confidence call set (e.g. de novo assemblies without benchmark regions) — GIAB sets are biased in favor of short-read technologies, so some caller false positives may be truth-set false negatives. Input is raw reads without an indexed, sorted BAM/CRAM aligned to the reference used by the truth set — variant-level comparison requires coordinate-matched calls.

skills.description: Use when you need to merge SV/TE insertion calls from multiple nanopore variant callers and quantify callset accuracy against a curated truth set (e.g., the HGSVC 5,630-insertion truth set).
skills.name: variant-callset-intersection-filtering
skills.search_text: variant-callset-intersection-filtering Use when you need to merge SV/TE insertion calls from multiple nanopore variant callers and quantify callset accuracy against a curated truth set (e.g., the HGSVC 5,630-insertion truth set). The data are short-read sequencing data — the article benchmarks RetroInspector's strict/lax criteria specifically on nanopore long-read calls, and short-read TE tools (e.g., MELT) are a different regime You have only a single caller's output and cannot form the intersection — the strict criterion requires both cuteSV and Sniffles2 to report the insertion You want the highest recall of all insertions rather than TE-focused precision — under the strict criterion overall insertion recall was only 16.34%, so a lax criterion is the wrong skill here http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Combines structural variant callsets from two long-read callers (cuteSV and Sniffles2) by intersecting insertions and filtering on a user-set supporting-read threshold, then benchmarks the merged callset against a truth set with SURVIVOR to compute precision, recall, and F1-score for TE insertion detection. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Combines structural variant callsets from two long-read callers (cuteSV and Sniffles2) by intersecting insertions and filtering on a user-set supporting-read threshold, then benchmarks the merged callset against a truth set with SURVIVOR to compute precision, recall, and F1-score for TE insertion detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are short-read sequencing data — the article benchmarks RetroInspector's strict/lax criteria specifically on nanopore long-read calls, and short-read TE tools (e.g., MELT) are a different regime You have only a single caller's output and cannot form the intersection — the strict criterion requires both cuteSV and Sniffles2 to report the insertion You want the highest recall of all insertions rather than TE-focused precision — under the strict criterion overall insertion recall was only 16.34%, so a lax criterion is the wrong skill here

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify SNV/indel variant-calling accuracy — precision and recall — of one or more callsets against a benchmark truth set such as GIAB NA12878.
skills.name: variant-callset-truth-matching-with-rtgtools
skills.search_text: variant-callset-truth-matching-with-rtgtools Use when you need to quantify SNV/indel variant-calling accuracy — precision and recall — of one or more callsets against a benchmark truth set such as GIAB NA12878. Input is a raw sequencing signal file (BLOW5/POD5) — basecalling, alignment, and variant calling must precede truth matching No curated truth variant set exists for the sample/genome — precision and recall cannot be computed Goal is signal-similarity assessment rather than downstream variant-detection performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scores a called VCF (e.g. Clair3 output from simulated nanopore reads) against a curated truth VCF (Genome in a Bottle NA12878) with RTGtools, compiling true positives, false positives, recall, and precision per simulator or pipeline variant. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae744
skills.summary: Scores a called VCF (e.g. Clair3 output from simulated nanopore reads) against a curated truth VCF (Genome in a Bottle NA12878) with RTGtools, compiling true positives, false positives, recall, and precision per simulator or pipeline variant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw sequencing signal file (BLOW5/POD5) — basecalling, alignment, and variant calling must precede truth matching No curated truth variant set exists for the sample/genome — precision and recall cannot be computed Goal is signal-similarity assessment rather than downstream variant-detection performance

skills.description: Use when a Novel-X (or similar linked-read insertion caller) VCF has been produced and you must characterize callset biology: how many insertions sit in reference repeats, in non-uniquely mappable regions, or overlap annotated genes.
skills.name: variant-callset-vcf-processing
skills.search_text: variant-callset-vcf-processing Use when a Novel-X (or similar linked-read insertion caller) VCF has been produced and you must characterize callset biology: how many insertions sit in reference repeats, in non-uniquely mappable regions, or overlap annotated genes. You need to CALL insertions rather than characterize an existing callset — run the Novel-X pipeline itself (novel-x.py) instead; this skill starts from a VCF. The callset contains variants shorter than 300 bp — Novel-X explicitly filters these out, and the annotation workflow was validated only on insertions >300 bp. You need per-base haplotype-resolved validation rather than positional annotation — use a T2T/CHM13 assembly comparison as in the paper's validation strategy instead of track intersections. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Characterize a structural-variant (NRS insertion) VCF callset — here the 226 Novel-X insertions on CHM1 10x data — by annotating breakpoints against RepeatMasker repeats, UCSC Umap mappability tracks (k100/k50), and GENCODE v24 gene models, yielding per-category counts that can be checked against published values. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac653
skills.summary: Characterize a structural-variant (NRS insertion) VCF callset — here the 226 Novel-X insertions on CHM1 10x data — by annotating breakpoints against RepeatMasker repeats, UCSC Umap mappability tracks (k100/k50), and GENCODE v24 gene models, yielding per-category counts that can be checked against published values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to CALL insertions rather than characterize an existing callset — run the Novel-X pipeline itself (novel-x.py) instead; this skill starts from a VCF. The callset contains variants shorter than 300 bp — Novel-X explicitly filters these out, and the annotation workflow was validated only on insertions >300 bp. You need per-base haplotype-resolved validation rather than positional annotation — use a T2T/CHM13 assembly comparison as in the paper's validation strategy instead of track intersections.

Input contains somatic tumor variants — use PCGR's oncogenicity/actionability classification instead of CPSR's germline ACMG/AMP classification The goal is to re-run CharGer itself rather than to reuse its published comparator rates (72.4%/97.2% custom, 56.2%/98.1% ACMG-based) for the same benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Benchmark automated germline variant classification algorithms (CPSR's >30 refined ACMG/AMP criteria vs CharGer custom and ACMG-based algorithms) by computing sensitivity and specificity on a gold-standard set of 788 PCGP variants with ground-truth pathogenicity labels. genomics/v1 10.1002/ijc.33749

skills.description: Use when germline SNV/InDel VCF calls from a single sample need automated ACMG/AMP classification (Pathogenic to Benign) against cancer predisposition gene panels, with per-variant criteria codes and scores reported.
skills.name: variant-classification-tsv-reporting
skills.search_text: variant-classification-tsv-reporting Use when germline SNV/InDel VCF calls from a single sample need automated ACMG/AMP classification (Pathogenic to Benign) against cancer predisposition gene panels, with per-variant criteria codes and scores reported. The query variants are somatic tumor aberrations — use PCGR's oncogenicity/actionability classification (VICC/CGC/ClinGen and AMP/ASCO/CAP guidelines) instead Variants are not designated 'PASS' in the VCF FILTER column, as only PASS variants are used for CPSR reporting The goal is interactive HTML reporting of prognosis/diagnosis/drug-response biomarkers rather than the ACMG classification scoring step itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Automated ACMG/AMP pathogenicity classification of germline variants using CPSR's Sher Loc-derived point-based scoring of 30+ refined criteria, with per-variant results (score, classification, '|'-separated ACMG_CODE) written to a TSV file. genomics/v1 10.1002/ijc.33749
skills.summary: Automated ACMG/AMP pathogenicity classification of germline variants using CPSR's Sher Loc-derived point-based scoring of 30+ refined criteria, with per-variant results (score, classification, '|'-separated ACMG_CODE) written to a TSV file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query variants are somatic tumor aberrations — use PCGR's oncogenicity/actionability classification (VICC/CGC/ClinGen and AMP/ASCO/CAP guidelines) instead Variants are not designated 'PASS' in the VCF FILTER column, as only PASS variants are used for CPSR reporting The goal is interactive HTML reporting of prognosis/diagnosis/drug-response biomarkers rather than the ACMG classification scoring step itself

skills.search_text: variant-count-aggregation-and-percentage-computation Use when a snpEff-annotated VCF/CSV of called variants (e.g. from a JWES run) must be classified by coding vs noncoding gene regions and summarized per chromosome with counts and percentage shares. skills.search_text: variant-count-summary-reporting Use when validating BAF/SNP filtering in a CNVpytor .pytor analysis: i.e., when you need to count heterozygous variants before and after -mask_snps P-mask filtering and reproduce the paper's ~22% removal statistic. Input VCF contains variant classes CNVpytor ignores (CNVpytor imports only SNPs and single-letter indels; all other variants are ignored), so counts would be misleading The goal is RD-based CNV calling or call filtering (e.g., Q0_range, size_range, p_range in view mode), not SNP/BAF mask-filtering statistics Analysis on a non-human genome or assembly where the 1000 Genomes Project strict mask (built for hg19/GRCh37-style human data) does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies heterozygous variant retention under CNVpytor's 1000 Genomes Project strict-mask (P-mask) SNP filter, reporting total, retained, and removed counts plus the removed fraction (~22%) as a CSV summary. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Quantifies heterozygous variant retention under CNVpytor's 1000 Genomes Project strict-mask (P-mask) SNP filter, reporting total, retained, and removed counts plus the removed fraction (~22%) as a CSV summary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input VCF contains variant classes CNVpytor ignores (CNVpytor imports only SNPs and single-letter indels; all other variants are ignored), so counts would be misleading The goal is RD-based CNV calling or call filtering (e.g., Q0_range, size_range, p_range in view mode), not SNP/BAF mask-filtering statistics Analysis on a non-human genome or assembly where the 1000 Genomes Project strict mask (built for hg19/GRCh37-style human data) does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have VCF variant calls near splice sites and want to predict delta-PSI for exon skipping events, especially for CAGI vex-seq-style benchmarks or prioritizing splicing-disrupting variants.
skills.name: variant-delta-psi-prediction
skills.search_text: variant-delta-psi-prediction Use when you have VCF variant calls near splice sites and want to predict delta-PSI for exon skipping events, especially for CAGI vex-seq-style benchmarks or prioritizing splicing-disrupting variants. Variants in intergenic regions or more than 200 bp away from splice sites — the pipeline filters these out, so predictions will not be produced No experimental wild-type PSI is available — PCCs drop by about 0.1 when running without the '-p' option Branch point sequence or pre-mRNA secondary structure effects are the target — PredPSI-SVR does not include these features due to limited sample size http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Predict the change of percent spliced in (delta-PSI) caused by genetic variants using PredPSI-SVR, a support vector regression model trained on the CAGI 5 vex-seq dataset with 42 splicing-related features (8 greedily selected for the final model). genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Predict the change of percent spliced in (delta-PSI) caused by genetic variants using PredPSI-SVR, a support vector regression model trained on the CAGI 5 vex-seq dataset with 42 splicing-related features (8 greedily selected for the final model).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants in intergenic regions or more than 200 bp away from splice sites — the pipeline filters these out, so predictions will not be produced No experimental wild-type PSI is available — PCCs drop by about 0.1 when running without the '-p' option Branch point sequence or pre-mRNA secondary structure effects are the target — PredPSI-SVR does not include these features due to limited sample size

skills.description: Use when variant records (chromosome, reference position, gene assignment) from WGS/WES calling need to be rendered as a per-gene/per-chromosome Circos histogram for variant data interpretation.
skills.name: variant-distribution-visualization
skills.search_text: variant-distribution-visualization Use when variant records (chromosome, reference position, gene assignment) from WGS/WES calling need to be rendered as a per-gene/per-chromosome Circos histogram for variant data interpretation. The analysis goal requires dynamic heat maps, gene pathways/networks, or cluster maps — the paper notes these advanced visualizations are not yet implemented in JWES. The user needs an interactive or clinician-friendly visualization interface — the current JWES version only offers a command-line interface. Input data is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than called/annotated variants — the data processing module (FastQC, Trimmomatic, BWA, HaplotypeCaller) must run first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 A method for reconstructing the JWES data visualization module's Circos-plot generation, which presents chromosome-based variant distribution as a simplified Circos plot with two histograms: color-coded variants in protein-coding genes and black-coded variants in noncoding genes. genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261
skills.summary: A method for reconstructing the JWES data visualization module's Circos-plot generation, which presents chromosome-based variant distribution as a simplified Circos plot with two histograms: color-coded variants in protein-coding genes and black-coded variants in noncoding genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal requires dynamic heat maps, gene pathways/networks, or cluster maps — the paper notes these advanced visualizations are not yet implemented in JWES. The user needs an interactive or clinician-friendly visualization interface — the current JWES version only offers a command-line interface. Input data is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than called/annotated variants — the data processing module (FastQC, Trimmomatic, BWA, HaplotypeCaller) must run first.

skills.description: Use when a reference genome has been selected (highest-scoring BLAST hit from de novo contigs) and a reference-based consensus genome must be reconstructed from trimmed nanopore reads, including large-indel integration and polishing.
skills.name: variant-integrated-draft-reference-construction
skills.search_text: variant-integrated-draft-reference-construction Use when a reference genome has been selected (highest-scoring BLAST hit from de novo contigs) and a reference-based consensus genome must be reconstructed from trimmed nanopore reads, including large-indel integration and polishing. Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox): the README states assemblies may contain inaccuracies and should only be regarded as draft genomes No well-fitting reference genome was identified for the sample (BLAST finds no suitable viral reference), since this module is inherently reference-guided A de novo assembly is required instead of a reference-anchored consensus; this skill deliberately projects reads onto a known viral reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 ViMOP's reference-guided consensus assembly module: after BLAST identifies a reference genome, nanopore reads are remapped, large indels called with Sniffles2 are applied to the reference via BCFtools consensus, and the draft is polished to a final consensus FASTA with Medaka (or a Samtools fallback). This turns untargeted nanopore reads into a consensus virus genome anchored on a known reference. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: ViMOP's reference-guided consensus assembly module: after BLAST identifies a reference genome, nanopore reads are remapped, large indels called with Sniffles2 are applied to the reference via BCFtools consensus, and the draft is polished to a final consensus FASTA with Medaka (or a Samtools fallback). This turns untargeted nanopore reads into a consensus virus genome anchored on a known reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox): the README states assemblies may contain inaccuracies and should only be regarded as draft genomes No well-fitting reference genome was identified for the sample (BLAST finds no suitable viral reference), since this module is inherently reference-guided A de novo assembly is required instead of a reference-anchored consensus; this skill deliberately projects reads onto a known viral reference

skills.description: Use when preparing a MacroHapCaller run and you must define which STR loci, SNPs, and InDels are genotyped, or when planned private mutations must be added to the panel because unlisted variants are not reported.
skills.name: variant-panel-config-authoring
skills.search_text: variant-panel-config-authoring Use when preparing a MacroHapCaller run and you must define which STR loci, SNPs, and InDels are genotyped, or when planned private mutations must be added to the panel because unlisted variants are not reported. You expect de novo or private mutations absent from the configure files to be reported — MacroHapCaller v0.3 discards InDels (and other targeted variants) not present in the configure files You need genotyping of untargeted genome-wide variants rather than a user-supplied panel of STRs, SNPs, and InDels Your variant coordinates refer to a different reference build than the BAM alignment (e.g. not GRCh38 GCA_000001405.15 no-alt analysis set), since positions will not match http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Author the three MacroHapCaller configure files — STR anchor config, InDel BED, and SNP panel position file — that define the targeted variant loci genotyped and phased from long reads. The configure files gate which variants are called: any variant absent from them is silently discarded, so panel content directly determines macrohaplotype composition. genomics/v1 10.1002/elps.202300143
skills.summary: Author the three MacroHapCaller configure files — STR anchor config, InDel BED, and SNP panel position file — that define the targeted variant loci genotyped and phased from long reads. The configure files gate which variants are called: any variant absent from them is silently discarded, so panel content directly determines macrohaplotype composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You expect de novo or private mutations absent from the configure files to be reported — MacroHapCaller v0.3 discards InDels (and other targeted variants) not present in the configure files You need genotyping of untargeted genome-wide variants rather than a user-supplied panel of STRs, SNPs, and InDels Your variant coordinates refer to a different reference build than the BAM alignment (e.g. not GRCh38 GCA_000001405.15 no-alt analysis set), since positions will not match

skills.search_text: variant-pathogenicity-feature-ranking Use when a trained variant-classification random forest (e.g. eDiVA-Score with 11 annotation features) must be inspected to determine which features — allele frequency, functional impact, conservation — contribute most to pathogenicity prediction. The variant annotations have not yet been computed by eDiVA-Annotate — eDiVA-Score requires the annotation columns to be calculated first The goal is causal-variant prioritization in a family/pedigree (use the eDiVA-Prioritize inheritance-mode filtering workflow instead of model introspection) The classifier is not a tree ensemble — randomForest::importance Gini/accuracy metrics do not apply to non-forest models http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Reproduces the feature-importance ranking of the eDiVA-Score random forest pathogenicity predictor (R 'randomForest', 1000 trees, five-fold cross validation, 11 annotation features), identifying which genomic and evolutionary signatures drive variant pathogenicity classification. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23772
skills.summary: Reproduces the feature-importance ranking of the eDiVA-Score random forest pathogenicity predictor (R 'randomForest', 1000 trees, five-fold cross validation, 11 annotation features), identifying which genomic and evolutionary signatures drive variant pathogenicity classification.

skills.description: Use when comparing or validating SNV call sets from Longshot (PacBio SMS reads) and FreeBayes (Illumina reads), or when filtering candidate SNVs by genotype quality, read depth, density, or strand bias before counting or intersecting with GIAB/segmental-duplication regions.
skills.name: variant-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: variant-quality-filtering Use when comparing or validating SNV call sets from Longshot (PacBio SMS reads) and FreeBayes (Illumina reads), or when filtering candidate SNVs by genotype quality, read depth, density, or strand bias before counting or intersecting with GIAB/segmental-duplication regions. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than an existing VCF of candidate SNVs — variant calling (Longshot/FreeBayes) must happen first The goal is structural variant or copy-number calling — Longshot only calls SNVs, and these filters target SNV false positives Comparing call sets without aligning caller-specific GQ cutoffs — the fixed GQ=50 short-read cutoff vs. the variable Longshot cutoff must both be applied or counts are not comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply paper-specific quality filters to SNV call sets so that short-read (FreeBayes) and long-read (Longshot) calls are comparable: genotype-quality cutoffs, read-depth ceilings, SNV density and strand-bias filters, and optional common-indel filtering. This reduces coverage-driven and mapping-driven false positives, especially in segmental duplications. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12493-y
skills.summary: Apply paper-specific quality filters to SNV call sets so that short-read (FreeBayes) and long-read (Longshot) calls are comparable: genotype-quality cutoffs, read-depth ceilings, SNV density and strand-bias filters, and optional common-indel filtering. This reduces coverage-driven and mapping-driven false positives, especially in segmental duplications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than an existing VCF of candidate SNVs — variant calling (Longshot/FreeBayes) must happen first The goal is structural variant or copy-number calling — Longshot only calls SNVs, and these filters target SNV false positives Comparing call sets without aligning caller-specific GQ cutoffs — the fixed GQ=50 short-read cutoff vs. the variable Longshot cutoff must both be applied or counts are not comparable

skills.description: Use when per-sample VCF callsets from cuteSV and Sniffles2 contain malformed records (negative or 0 coordinates on decoy/scaffold regions) or unfiltered calls that must pass a supporting-read threshold before strict/lax merging or benchmarking.

skills.description: Use when you have a consensus VCF of candidate SVs plus a minimap2 BAM of quality-passing ONT reads and need image tensors (50x50x3) as CNN input for high-quality variant filtering.
