skills.search_text: variant-region-image-encoding Use when you have a consensus VCF of candidate SVs plus a minimap2 BAM of quality-passing ONT reads and need image tensors (50x50x3) as CNN input for high-quality variant filtering. Input is short-read (Illumina/PacBio) data rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, which is the scope of ConsensuSV-ONT You already have feature tables or per-variant quality scores and do not need image-encoded CNN filtering No alignment BAM exists yet — run the alignment-generation step of the ConsensuSV-ONT pipeline first http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Encodes candidate structural variants from ConsensuSV-ONT into fixed 50x50x3 images built from per-read alignment features over the variant region (expanded by the variant size on both sides), so a CNN can filter high-quality SV calls. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Encodes candidate structural variants from ConsensuSV-ONT into fixed 50x50x3 images built from per-read alignment features over the variant region (expanded by the variant size on both sides), so a CNN can filter high-quality SV calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina/PacBio) data rather than Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, which is the scope of ConsensuSV-ONT You already have feature tables or per-variant quality scores and do not need image-encoded CNN filtering No alignment BAM exists yet — run the alignment-generation step of the ConsensuSV-ONT pipeline first

skills.description: Use when you have a VCF of variants near exon skipping events and need predicted ΔΨ values or prioritization of splicing-affecting (e.g. synonymous) mutations on hg19.
skills.name: variant-splicing-effect-prediction
skills.search_text: variant-splicing-effect-prediction Use when you have a VCF of variants near exon skipping events and need predicted ΔΨ values or prioritization of splicing-affecting (e.g. synonymous) mutations on hg19. Variants are far from splice sites: the tool automatically drops intergenic variants and those more than 200 bp from splice sites, so distant variants yield no predictions. Exons lack experimental wild-type Ψ and high accuracy is required: PredPSI-SVR-noPSI loses about 0.1 PCC on both training and test sets. Branch point or pre-mRNA secondary-structure effects are the target: PredPSI-SVR does not include these features effectively due to limited sample numbers. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Predict the change of percent spliced in (ΔΨ) caused by genetic variants using the PredPSI-SVR support vector regression model trained on 42 splicing-related features (eight selected by greedy feature selection) from the CAGI 5 vex-seq challenge data. genomics/v1 10.1002/humu.23785
skills.summary: Predict the change of percent spliced in (ΔΨ) caused by genetic variants using the PredPSI-SVR support vector regression model trained on 42 splicing-related features (eight selected by greedy feature selection) from the CAGI 5 vex-seq challenge data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants are far from splice sites: the tool automatically drops intergenic variants and those more than 200 bp from splice sites, so distant variants yield no predictions. Exons lack experimental wild-type Ψ and high accuracy is required: PredPSI-SVR-noPSI loses about 0.1 PCC on both training and test sets. Branch point or pre-mRNA secondary-structure effects are the target: PredPSI-SVR does not include these features effectively due to limited sample numbers.

skills.description: Use when a set of long-read-derived TR/variant calls (e.g., TRiCoLOR BCF output from ONT or PB haplotype-resolved BAMs) needs an independent, short-read-based validation ratio computed from same-sample Illumina data.
skills.name: variant-validation-against-fm-indexes
skills.search_text: variant-validation-against-fm-indexes Use when a set of long-read-derived TR/variant calls (e.g., TRiCoLOR BCF output from ONT or PB haplotype-resolved BAMs) needs an independent, short-read-based validation ratio computed from same-sample Illumina data. No Illumina short-read data or pre-built FM indexes are available for the same samples, so FM-index lookup cannot be performed Validating variant types other than the TRs TRiCoLOR calls (e.g., SNVs or structural variants outside ≥50 bp tandem repeats), which the FM-index TR validation approach was not designed to score Repeats located in unassembled genome regions (centromeres, telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify in the first place http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Validate de novo tandem repeat calls from long-read data by checking whether each variant is present in alignment-free Illumina FM indexes of the same sample, counting calls as valid when found with ≤2 bp discrepancies, and optionally confirming non-reference alleles against an assembly-based truth set. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa101
skills.summary: Validate de novo tandem repeat calls from long-read data by checking whether each variant is present in alignment-free Illumina FM indexes of the same sample, counting calls as valid when found with ≤2 bp discrepancies, and optionally confirming non-reference alleles against an assembly-based truth set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No Illumina short-read data or pre-built FM indexes are available for the same samples, so FM-index lookup cannot be performed Validating variant types other than the TRs TRiCoLOR calls (e.g., SNVs or structural variants outside ≥50 bp tandem repeats), which the FM-index TR validation approach was not designed to score Repeats located in unassembled genome regions (centromeres, telomeres), which TRiCoLOR cannot identify in the first place

skills.description: Use when correcting noisy long reads from mixed samples (metagenomes, diploid/triploid/tetraploid or polyploid genomes) where consensus-template correctors mask low-frequency haplotype variants, and lower corrected error rates are the priority.
skills.name: variation-graph-based-error-correction
skills.search_text: variation-graph-based-error-correction Use when correcting noisy long reads from mixed samples (metagenomes, diploid/triploid/tetraploid or polyploid genomes) where consensus-template correctors mask low-frequency haplotype variants, and lower corrected error rates are the priority. Minimizing compute is the goal: on large datasets VeChat has longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competitors (e.g. Daccord achieved the lowest error rate on the human gut microbiome dataset while VeChat only matched read accuracy). Input reads are already corrected or the goal is polishing an assembled contig/consensus — Racon is the consensus module for correcting raw contigs, and VeChat targets raw long-read self-correction. The study scope is haplotype-aware correction; exploring optimal preprocessing/error-correction/assembly pipeline combinations for polyploid, cancer or metagenomic settings was explicitly left as future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Haplotype-aware self-correction of noisy long reads (PacBio CLR or ONT) using variation graphs instead of consensus templates, so that true low-frequency haplotype variants are not masked as errors. Implemented by VeChat in a two-cycle workflow built on Minimap2 overlaps and POA graph construction. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Haplotype-aware self-correction of noisy long reads (PacBio CLR or ONT) using variation graphs instead of consensus templates, so that true low-frequency haplotype variants are not masked as errors. Implemented by VeChat in a two-cycle workflow built on Minimap2 overlaps and POA graph construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Minimizing compute is the goal: on large datasets VeChat has longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competitors (e.g. Daccord achieved the lowest error rate on the human gut microbiome dataset while VeChat only matched read accuracy). Input reads are already corrected or the goal is polishing an assembled contig/consensus — Racon is the consensus module for correcting raw contigs, and VeChat targets raw long-read self-correction. The study scope is haplotype-aware correction; exploring optimal preprocessing/error-correction/assembly pipeline combinations for polyploid, cancer or metagenomic settings was explicitly left as future work.

skills.description: Use when correcting errors in noisy long reads (PacBio CLR or ONT) from mixed samples such as metagenomes or polyploid genomes, where consensus-template correction would mask low-frequency haplotype variants as errors.
skills.name: variation-graph-construction-and-pruning
skills.search_text: variation-graph-construction-and-pruning Use when correcting errors in noisy long reads (PacBio CLR or ONT) from mixed samples such as metagenomes or polyploid genomes, where consensus-template correction would mask low-frequency haplotype variants as errors. Input is already error-corrected or high-accuracy (e.g. PacBio HiFi/CCS) reads — graph pruning targets raw noisy CLR/ONT reads The goal is a consensus sequence template rather than haplotype-aware correction — VeChat's graph approach is designed to avoid consensus-induced biases Computational resources are tightly constrained on very large datasets — VeChat experiences longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competing tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs ad-hoc variation graphs from raw long-read alignment piles via partial order alignment (POA) and iteratively prunes error-induced nodes and edges — the core graph-building step of VeChat's haplotype-aware error correction for PacBio/ONT reads. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Constructs ad-hoc variation graphs from raw long-read alignment piles via partial order alignment (POA) and iteratively prunes error-induced nodes and edges — the core graph-building step of VeChat's haplotype-aware error correction for PacBio/ONT reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already error-corrected or high-accuracy (e.g. PacBio HiFi/CCS) reads — graph pruning targets raw noisy CLR/ONT reads The goal is a consensus sequence template rather than haplotype-aware correction — VeChat's graph approach is designed to avoid consensus-induced biases Computational resources are tightly constrained on very large datasets — VeChat experiences longer runtimes and higher peak memory usage than competing tools

skills.description: Use when correcting noisy long reads (PacBio/ONT) read-by-read: after computing a read alignment pile for a target read, each window of the pile must be turned into a variation graph whose optimal path yields the corrected subread.
skills.name: variation-graph-construction-partial-order-alignment
skills.search_text: variation-graph-construction-partial-order-alignment Use when correcting noisy long reads (PacBio/ONT) read-by-read: after computing a read alignment pile for a target read, each window of the pile must be turned into a variation graph whose optimal path yields the corrected subread. Cycle-2 consensus derivation: here haplotype-aware consensus sequences are derived from the variation graphs by a dynamic programming algorithm without re-pruning the graph, so the iterative POA-construct-and-prune step should not be repeated If the goal is conventional consensus-template error correction rather than haplotype-aware correction — VeChat's rationale is that graph-based references capture variants of lower frequency that consensus templates mask as errors When a curated reference/pangenome graph already exists and alignment-to-reference is the intended task, rather than constructing an ad-hoc graph from raw reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Builds an ad-hoc variation graph for a window of a long-read alignment pile using the partial order alignment (POA) algorithm from the modified Racon module bundled with VeChat, as the substrate for haplotype-aware error correction and pruning. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-34381-8
skills.summary: Builds an ad-hoc variation graph for a window of a long-read alignment pile using the partial order alignment (POA) algorithm from the modified Racon module bundled with VeChat, as the substrate for haplotype-aware error correction and pruning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cycle-2 consensus derivation: here haplotype-aware consensus sequences are derived from the variation graphs by a dynamic programming algorithm without re-pruning the graph, so the iterative POA-construct-and-prune step should not be repeated If the goal is conventional consensus-template error correction rather than haplotype-aware correction — VeChat's rationale is that graph-based references capture variants of lower frequency that consensus templates mask as errors When a curated reference/pangenome graph already exists and alignment-to-reference is the intended task, rather than constructing an ad-hoc graph from raw reads

skills.description: Use when a methylation-based phasing tool has chained SNV phase blocks in a VCF and you need to verify block connections against GIAB trio-phased truth, computing corrected N50 and switch-error cost.
skills.name: vcf-block-relationship-validation
skills.search_text: vcf-block-relationship-validation Use when a methylation-based phasing tool has chained SNV phase blocks in a VCF and you need to verify block connections against GIAB trio-phased truth, computing corrected N50 and switch-error cost. Phasing sex chromosomes in clinical samples — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype patterns, and MethPhaser/README explicitly excludes sex chromosomes No trio-phased truth set is available for the sample, making corrected-N50 and connection-level validation impossible Initial SNV phasing has very high error (e.g., very high hamming distance in R9 80x results), which negatively impacts MethPhaser accuracy and invalidates the connection judgments http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Validates methylation-chained SNV phase-block relationships (e.g., from MethPhaser) against a trio-phased truth VCF, quantifying how many block connections are correct and the switch-error cost of joining blocks. This distinguishes genuine N50 gains from incorrectly connected blocks on benchmarks such as HG002. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: Validates methylation-chained SNV phase-block relationships (e.g., from MethPhaser) against a trio-phased truth VCF, quantifying how many block connections are correct and the switch-error cost of joining blocks. This distinguishes genuine N50 gains from incorrectly connected blocks on benchmarks such as HG002.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Phasing sex chromosomes in clinical samples — random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype patterns, and MethPhaser/README explicitly excludes sex chromosomes No trio-phased truth set is available for the sample, making corrected-N50 and connection-level validation impossible Initial SNV phasing has very high error (e.g., very high hamming distance in R9 80x results), which negatively impacts MethPhaser accuracy and invalidates the connection judgments

skills.description: Use when merging per-sample SV/TE insertion VCF callsets from two variant callers and you must choose between caller agreement (strict/intersection) and caller union (lax) to tune the precision-recall trade-off.
skills.name: vcf-callset-intersection-union-filtering
skills.search_text: vcf-callset-intersection-union-filtering Use when merging per-sample SV/TE insertion VCF callsets from two variant callers and you must choose between caller agreement (strict/intersection) and caller union (lax) to tune the precision-recall trade-off. Input is a single-caller VCF with no second callset to intersect/union — there is no caller-agreement signal to exploit The goal is de novo TE detection or annotation rather than callset-level precision/recall tuning after variant calling Variants are short-read SNV/small-indel calls rather than long-read structural or TE insertion calls suited to SURVIVOR comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Builds strict and lax filtered TE-insertion callsets from merged cuteSV and Sniffles2 VCFs by taking, respectively, the intersection (both callers) or union (either caller) of insertions at a shared read-evidence threshold, to trade precision against recall. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Builds strict and lax filtered TE-insertion callsets from merged cuteSV and Sniffles2 VCFs by taking, respectively, the intersection (both callers) or union (either caller) of insertions at a shared read-evidence threshold, to trade precision against recall.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-caller VCF with no second callset to intersect/union — there is no caller-agreement signal to exploit The goal is de novo TE detection or annotation rather than callset-level precision/recall tuning after variant calling Variants are short-read SNV/small-indel calls rather than long-read structural or TE insertion calls suited to SURVIVOR comparison

skills.description: Use when multiple TE-insertion caller VCFs (e.g. sTELLeR, TLDR from PacBio/ONT lrGS and RetroSeq, MELT2 from short-read BAMs) must be merged into a common representation to compute caller agreement and overlap statistics.
skills.name: vcf-callset-merging-across-callers
skills.search_text: vcf-callset-merging-across-callers Use when multiple TE-insertion caller VCFs (e.g. sTELLeR, TLDR from PacBio/ONT lrGS and RetroSeq, MELT2 from short-read BAMs) must be merged into a common representation to compute caller agreement and overlap statistics. The callsets are already in a common normalized VCF schema — merging directly without re-normalization risks duplicate/incorrect overlaps Comparing a single caller's output against a reference truth set rather than computing inter-caller overlap statistics Input BAMs are not the expected sequencing type for the caller (e.g. running sTELLeR with --style pb on short-read data instead of PacBio CLR or ONT) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Normalizes and merges transposable element insertion (TEI) callsets from multiple callers — long-read (sTELLeR, TLDR) and short-read (RetroSeq, MELT2) — into a common INS:ME VCF representation so pairwise and four-way overlaps can be tallied, as done to reproduce the HG004 Fig 2b overlap analysis (642 TEs shared by all four callers). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae686
skills.summary: Normalizes and merges transposable element insertion (TEI) callsets from multiple callers — long-read (sTELLeR, TLDR) and short-read (RetroSeq, MELT2) — into a common INS:ME VCF representation so pairwise and four-way overlaps can be tallied, as done to reproduce the HG004 Fig 2b overlap analysis (642 TEs shared by all four callers).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The callsets are already in a common normalized VCF schema — merging directly without re-normalization risks duplicate/incorrect overlaps Comparing a single caller's output against a reference truth set rather than computing inter-caller overlap statistics Input BAMs are not the expected sequencing type for the caller (e.g. running sTELLeR with --style pb on short-read data instead of PacBio CLR or ONT)

skills.description: Use when you have ≥2 caller VCFs and a benchmark truth VCF (e.g. GIAB HG002) plus a confidence-region BED, and need per-event-class precision/recall/F1 to rank SV callers or reproduce a benchmark table.
skills.name: vcf-callset-precision-recall-computation
skills.search_text: vcf-callset-precision-recall-computation Use when you have ≥2 caller VCFs and a benchmark truth VCF (e.g. GIAB HG002) plus a confidence-region BED, and need per-event-class precision/recall/F1 to rank SV callers or reproduce a benchmark table. The question is small-variant (SNP/short-indel) accuracy, e.g. the syndip/CHM-eval small-variant benchmark — CHM-eval, not svbench, targets that task You only have a single call set and no benchmark truth VCF, so precision/recall against a reference is undefined Comparison must be genotype-concordance or insertion-sequence-accuracy oriented (e.g. full-length insertion sequences in PE data, which the paper explicitly leaves unresolved) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes precision, recall and F1 for SV/indel VCF call sets against a benchmark truth set using svbench, the evaluator released with the dysgu paper, so competing callers (dysgu, SVIM, NanoVar, Sniffles, Manta) can be compared on the same GIAB HG002 benchmark restricted to deletion and insertion event classes. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Computes precision, recall and F1 for SV/indel VCF call sets against a benchmark truth set using svbench, the evaluator released with the dysgu paper, so competing callers (dysgu, SVIM, NanoVar, Sniffles, Manta) can be compared on the same GIAB HG002 benchmark restricted to deletion and insertion event classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is small-variant (SNP/short-indel) accuracy, e.g. the syndip/CHM-eval small-variant benchmark — CHM-eval, not svbench, targets that task You only have a single call set and no benchmark truth VCF, so precision/recall against a reference is undefined Comparison must be genotype-concordance or insertion-sequence-accuracy oriented (e.g. full-length insertion sequences in PE data, which the paper explicitly leaves unresolved)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking SNV variant callers (e.g. miniSNV vs Clair3 vs Longshot) on ONT Dorado sup-basecalled data by scoring each caller's VCF against GIAB truth VCFs within GIAB stratification regions to obtain F1, recall, and HDR.
skills.name: vcf-comparison-across-callers
skills.search_text: vcf-comparison-across-callers Use when benchmarking SNV variant callers (e.g. miniSNV vs Clair3 vs Longshot) on ONT Dorado sup-basecalled data by scoring each caller's VCF against GIAB truth VCFs within GIAB stratification regions to obtain F1, recall, and HDR. Input data is not ONT long-read nanopore data (e.g. short-read or PacBio HiFi) — the benchmark signal and caller selection (miniSNV, Clair3, Longshot with ONT models) are specific to ONT R10.4.1 kit v14 sup-basecalled reads You need validated production variant calls rather than a comparison/benchmark — rerio research models 'have not been scrutinized nor validated' by ONT Truth-set stratification files are unavailable — the reported F1/recall and HDR comparisons are computed only within GIAB v3.3 stratification regions and are not reproducible against whole-genome comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark multiple SNV callers on ONT long-read data by comparing each caller's VCF against GIAB truth VCFs within GIAB v3.3 stratification regions, computing precision, recall, F1, and homozygous discovery rate (HDR) per caller per sample. This is the evaluation framework used to show miniSNV exceeding 99.7% F1/recall against Clair3 and Longshot. genomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae473
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple SNV callers on ONT long-read data by comparing each caller's VCF against GIAB truth VCFs within GIAB v3.3 stratification regions, computing precision, recall, F1, and homozygous discovery rate (HDR) per caller per sample. This is the evaluation framework used to show miniSNV exceeding 99.7% F1/recall against Clair3 and Longshot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not ONT long-read nanopore data (e.g. short-read or PacBio HiFi) — the benchmark signal and caller selection (miniSNV, Clair3, Longshot with ONT models) are specific to ONT R10.4.1 kit v14 sup-basecalled reads You need validated production variant calls rather than a comparison/benchmark — rerio research models 'have not been scrutinized nor validated' by ONT Truth-set stratification files are unavailable — the reported F1/recall and HDR comparisons are computed only within GIAB v3.3 stratification regions and are not reproducible against whole-genome comparisons

skills.description: Use when multiple SV callers each emit their own VCF for the same long-read (ONT) sample and a single, non-overlapping candidate VCF is needed as input to consensus filtering or scoring.
skills.name: vcf-file-format-handling
skills.search_text: vcf-file-format-handling Use when multiple SV callers each emit their own VCF for the same long-read (ONT) sample and a single, non-overlapping candidate VCF is needed as input to consensus filtering or scoring. Input is a single VCF from one caller with no overlapping callsets to reconcile — Truvari merge/collapse would add no value The task is short-variant (SNV/indel) calling from Illumina data rather than structural variant consensus from ONT long reads, which is the scope of ConsensuSV-ONT VCFs are final, already-collapsed consensus outputs that only need downstream CNN filtering of high-quality variants http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Combines and de-replicates structural variant calls delivered in VCF format: per-caller VCFs from the six independent ONT SV callers in ConsensuSV-ONT are merged with Truvari and collapsed into a single non-redundant candidate set per sample. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-01486-1
skills.summary: Combines and de-replicates structural variant calls delivered in VCF format: per-caller VCFs from the six independent ONT SV callers in ConsensuSV-ONT are merged with Truvari and collapsed into a single non-redundant candidate set per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single VCF from one caller with no overlapping callsets to reconcile — Truvari merge/collapse would add no value The task is short-variant (SNV/indel) calling from Illumina data rather than structural variant consensus from ONT long reads, which is the scope of ConsensuSV-ONT VCFs are final, already-collapsed consensus outputs that only need downstream CNN filtering of high-quality variants

skills.description: Use when a dysgu-generated SV VCF (or a merged multi-sample dysgu VCF combining paired-end, PacBio and ONT calls) needs quality filtering, especially before benchmarking or when combining callsets from different runs.
skills.name: vcf-filtering-by-model-probability
skills.search_text: vcf-filtering-by-model-probability Use when a dysgu-generated SV VCF (or a merged multi-sample dysgu VCF combining paired-end, PacBio and ONT calls) needs quality filtering, especially before benchmarking or when combining callsets from different runs. Input VCFs come from callers other than dysgu, which do not emit the gradient-boosting model probability used for stratification Merging has not yet been performed — the README states filtering is generally recommended after any merging, not before Somatic/cohort analysis where a normal sample or panel of normals should be used with 'dysgu filter' rather than single-sample probability filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Filter structural variant calls in a VCF by dysgu's machine-learning model probability instead of manual pass/fail criteria, using calibrated thresholds such as max model probability ≥0.5 for PacBio and ≥0.35 for ONT callsets. This probability-based stratification underpins dysgu's merged PE+LR callsets benchmarked against the GIAB HG002 truth set. genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Filter structural variant calls in a VCF by dysgu's machine-learning model probability instead of manual pass/fail criteria, using calibrated thresholds such as max model probability ≥0.5 for PacBio and ≥0.35 for ONT callsets. This probability-based stratification underpins dysgu's merged PE+LR callsets benchmarked against the GIAB HG002 truth set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input VCFs come from callers other than dysgu, which do not emit the gradient-boosting model probability used for stratification Merging has not yet been performed — the README states filtering is generally recommended after any merging, not before Somatic/cohort analysis where a normal sample or panel of normals should be used with 'dysgu filter' rather than single-sample probability filtering

skills.description: Use when a joint-genotyped SV VCF carries a GQ quality field and the goal is to trade call count for a higher concordant-call proportion, e.g. before pedigree or truth-set concordance comparison.
skills.name: vcf-genotype-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: vcf-genotype-quality-filtering Use when a joint-genotyped SV VCF carries a GQ quality field and the goal is to trade call count for a higher concordant-call proportion, e.g. before pedigree or truth-set concordance comparison. skills.description: Reference for merging insertion VCF callsets when callers (cuteSV, Sniffles2) do not report consensus inserted sequences, or when coordinate-only merging (e.g., SURVIVOR) collapses distinct insertion events at near-identical positions.
skills.name: vcf-record-manipulation-for-insertions
skills.search_text: vcf-record-manipulation-for-insertions Reference for merging insertion VCF callsets when callers (cuteSV, Sniffles2) do not report consensus inserted sequences, or when coordinate-only merging (e.g., SURVIVOR) collapses distinct insertion events at near-identical positions. Input callsets contain only deletions or other SV classes — this method targets insertion records where inserted sequence matters for identity A coordinate-only merge at a wide threshold is sufficient and distinguishing inserted sequences is unnecessary, e.g., when only approximate event counts are needed Input reads are short reads; reassembly from supporting reads with spoa assumes long nanopore reads spanning the insertion http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Sequence-aware merging of insertion VCF records from long-read variant callers: RetroInspector reassembles inserted sequences from supporting reads (pysam + spoa consensus) and merges insertion calls using coordinates, length, and Levenshtein sequence distance instead of coordinates alone. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-98847-7
skills.summary: Sequence-aware merging of insertion VCF records from long-read variant callers: RetroInspector reassembles inserted sequences from supporting reads (pysam + spoa consensus) and merges insertion calls using coordinates, length, and Levenshtein sequence distance instead of coordinates alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input callsets contain only deletions or other SV classes — this method targets insertion records where inserted sequence matters for identity A coordinate-only merge at a wide threshold is sufficient and distinguishing inserted sequences is unnecessary, e.g., when only approximate event counts are needed Input reads are short reads; reassembly from supporting reads with spoa assumes long nanopore reads spanning the insertion

skills.description: Use when a variant-caller output VCF must be scored for accuracy against a truth set (e.g., GIAB v3.3.2 HG001) on defined benchmark regions, producing FPR/FNR/precision/F1 metrics.
skills.name: vcf-truth-set-benchmarking-rtg-vcfeval
skills.search_text: vcf-truth-set-benchmarking-rtg-vcfeval Use when a variant-caller output VCF must be scored for accuracy against a truth set (e.g., GIAB v3.3.2 HG001) on defined benchmark regions, producing FPR/FNR/precision/F1 metrics. The sample has no high-quality GIAB-style truth dataset available, as the paper notes this hinders applying the pipeline to completely novel sequencing technologies and chemistries Evaluating variants outside the benchmark regions (e.g., whole-genome rather than 1KGp3 common-variant stratification) — metrics will not be comparable to region-stratified published values The VCF contains multi-allelic variants or indels >4 bp requiring exact alternative alleles, which the current Clairvoyante design ignores or cannot resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark a caller-generated VCF against a GIAB truth VCF using RTG vcfeval, restricted to matched regions, and derive FPR, FNR, precision, and F1-score from the confusion counts. This is the evaluation protocol the Clairvoyante paper used to report variant-calling accuracy on HG001 across Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore data. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a caller-generated VCF against a GIAB truth VCF using RTG vcfeval, restricted to matched regions, and derive FPR, FNR, precision, and F1-score from the confusion counts. This is the evaluation protocol the Clairvoyante paper used to report variant-calling accuracy on HG001 across Illumina, PacBio, and Oxford Nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample has no high-quality GIAB-style truth dataset available, as the paper notes this hinders applying the pipeline to completely novel sequencing technologies and chemistries Evaluating variants outside the benchmark regions (e.g., whole-genome rather than 1KGp3 common-variant stratification) — metrics will not be comparable to region-stratified published values The VCF contains multi-allelic variants or indels >4 bp requiring exact alternative alleles, which the current Clairvoyante design ignores or cannot resolve

skills.description: Use when a variant-calling VCF (e.g., Clairvoyante or Nanopolish output for HG001 Illumina/PacBio/ONT data) must be scored against the GIAB v3.3.2 HG001 truth set to produce F1, FPR, FNR, and precision metrics.
skills.name: vcf-truth-set-comparison
skills.search_text: vcf-truth-set-comparison Use when a variant-calling VCF (e.g., Clairvoyante or Nanopolish output for HG001 Illumina/PacBio/ONT data) must be scored against the GIAB v3.3.2 HG001 truth set to produce F1, FPR, FNR, and precision metrics. Evaluating somatic or trio-based variant calling — Clairvoyante and this GIAB-HG001 benchmark target germline SNV/small-indel calling only Evaluating a technology/chemistry with no high-quality GIAB-style truth dataset available for training and benchmarking Assessing long-indel accuracy — the caller only provides exact alternative alleles for indels ≤4 bp, so indel-dominated comparisons (especially ONT indels, F1 ~50%) require extra caution http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Benchmark a caller's VCF against the Genome-in-a-Bottle v3.3.2 HG001 truth dataset using RTG vcfeval haplotype-aware genotype matching, then derive FPR, FNR, precision, and F1 per sequencing technology. This is the evaluation scheme used to validate Clairvoyante's reported F1-scores of 99.67/95.78/90.53% at 1KP common variants and 98.65/92.57/87.26% genome-wide. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-09025-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a caller's VCF against the Genome-in-a-Bottle v3.3.2 HG001 truth dataset using RTG vcfeval haplotype-aware genotype matching, then derive FPR, FNR, precision, and F1 per sequencing technology. This is the evaluation scheme used to validate Clairvoyante's reported F1-scores of 99.67/95.78/90.53% at 1KP common variants and 98.65/92.57/87.26% genome-wide.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating somatic or trio-based variant calling — Clairvoyante and this GIAB-HG001 benchmark target germline SNV/small-indel calling only Evaluating a technology/chemistry with no high-quality GIAB-style truth dataset available for training and benchmarking Assessing long-indel accuracy — the caller only provides exact alternative alleles for indels ≤4 bp, so indel-dominated comparisons (especially ONT indels, F1 ~50%) require extra caution

skills.description: Use when a called-variant VCF (e.g., from Longshot on PacBio SMS reads) must be validated or compared against a ground-truth or short-read call set (e.g., ground_truth_variants.vcf, GIAB high-confidence sets).
skills.name: vcf-variant-call-comparison
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-call-comparison Use when a called-variant VCF (e.g., from Longshot on PacBio SMS reads) must be validated or compared against a ground-truth or short-read call set (e.g., ground_truth_variants.vcf, GIAB high-confidence sets). The task requires short indel calling from SMS reads — Longshot only calls SNVs and the article notes accurate short indel calling with SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate Input is structural-variant discovery rather than SNV genotyping — use assembly- or split-read-based SV callers instead (Longshot does not support SVs >50 bp even as genotyped variants) The truth set was generated from short-read data and the region of interest is a segmental duplication — the GIAB/Platinum Genomes sets are biased in favor of short-read technologies, so apparent Longshot false positives may be truth-set false negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call SNVs from long SMS reads with Longshot and benchmark the resulting VCF against a short-read-derived or ground-truth VCF to quantify calling accuracy. skills.summary: Call SNVs from long SMS reads with Longshot and benchmark the resulting VCF against a short-read-derived or ground-truth VCF to quantify calling accuracy. This is the core evaluation pattern used to show Longshot matches short-read precision (≥0.9999) on simulated diploid genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires short indel calling from SMS reads — Longshot only calls SNVs and the article notes accurate short indel calling with SMS reads is challenging due to the high insertion/deletion error rate Input is structural-variant discovery rather than SNV genotyping — use assembly- or split-read-based SV callers instead (Longshot does not support SVs >50 bp even as genotyped variants) The truth set was generated from short-read data and the region of interest is a segmental duplication — the GIAB/Platinum Genomes sets are biased in favor of short-read technologies, so apparent Longshot false positives may be truth-set false negatives

skills.search_text: vcf-variant-call-output Use when a local-assembly variant caller (Novel-X) has produced placed NRS insertion candidates and they must be serialized and threshold-filtered into a standard VCF for downstream benchmarking. skills.summary: Emit Novel-X's detected non-reference sequence (NRS) insertions as a parseable VCF named after the input BAM, retaining only calls > 300 bp whose summed anchor lengths exceed 300 bp to prevent false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The caller produced raw orphan contigs that have not yet been placed on the reference — placement/anchoring must precede VCF emission The insertion is 300 bp or shorter — the method's output filter is restricted to insertions > 300 bp, and small insertions often lack sufficient barcode coverage anyway The goal is general SNV/small-indel calling from short reads, not non-reference sequence insertion discovery from synthetic long reads

skills.search_text: vcf-variant-callset-handling Use when handling TE insertion callsets from nanopore-sequenced samples — e.g. polished bgzipped VCFs from cuteSV/Sniffles2 that need supporting-read filtering, 0/0 genotype removal, or SVA F1 re-labeling before downstream annotation or sample comparison. skills.description: Use when starting a CNVpytor analysis from VCF variant calls: you have a VCF with SNPs and small indels for a sample and need them stored in a .pytor file before -baf, -mask_snps, or -genotype steps.
skills.name: vcf-variant-import
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-import Use when starting a CNVpytor analysis from VCF variant calls: you have a VCF with SNPs and small indels for a sample and need them stored in a .pytor file before -baf, -mask_snps, or -genotype steps. The variants of interest are multi-base substitutions, large indels, or structural variants — CNVpytor ignores all VCF entries other than SNPs and single-letter indels. The analysis goal is read-depth-only CNV calling with no allele-imbalance evidence; use the -rd/-his/-partition/-call pipeline instead. You need variant filtering against a different mask than the 1000 Genomes Project strict (P) mask — -mask_snps is specifically tied to that resource. http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Import SNP and single-letter indel variant data from a VCF file into a CNVpytor .pytor (HDF5) root file, enabling downstream BAF likelihood and copy-number analysis. This is the prerequisite step for using allele imbalance as evidence for CNVs/CNAs. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giab074
skills.summary: Import SNP and single-letter indel variant data from a VCF file into a CNVpytor .pytor (HDF5) root file, enabling downstream BAF likelihood and copy-number analysis. This is the prerequisite step for using allele imbalance as evidence for CNVs/CNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variants of interest are multi-base substitutions, large indels, or structural variants — CNVpytor ignores all VCF entries other than SNPs and single-letter indels. The analysis goal is read-depth-only CNV calling with no allele-imbalance evidence; use the -rd/-his/-partition/-call pipeline instead. You need variant filtering against a different mask than the 1000 Genomes Project strict (P) mask — -mask_snps is specifically tied to that resource.

skills.search_text: vcf-variant-record-formatting Use when a Nextflow-based virus surveillance pipeline has reconstructed viral consensus genomes (reference-based or hybrid assembly) and structural variants must be detected with Sniffles2 and persisted as per-sample variant record files. No consensus genome has been reconstructed yet (e.g. input is still raw FASTQ/FAST5/POD5 or only preprocessed reads) — structural variant calling operates on assembled consensus genomes Only FASTA files were supplied as input without additional samples — these are consumed from the alignment step onwards, so per-sample variant detection workflows may not apply as expected The goal is SNP/small-variant calling on read alignments rather than structural variants of assembled genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Formats structural variants detected in nanopore-derived viral consensus genomes into per-sample variant record files, following the VirDetector pipeline's structured output conventions (VCF-style records alongside reference-assembly outputs in results.txt). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Formats structural variants detected in nanopore-derived viral consensus genomes into per-sample variant record files, following the VirDetector pipeline's structured output conventions (VCF-style records alongside reference-assembly outputs in results.txt).

skills.search_text: vcf-variant-record-formatting Use when final insertion candidates from a local-assembly pipeline (e.g. orphan contigs with anchor alignments) must be serialized as variant records, with length and anchor thresholds applied before writing the VCF. Input files are raw reads or FAST5/POD5 that have not yet been preprocessed, classified and assembled into consensus genomes — the BLAST step starts from consensus FASTA The virus of interest is absent from the VirDetector phylogenetic database (database/sequences.fasta), since both detection and the sequence selection for tree inference depend on it A single-reference-based placement (e.g. read mapping against a known reference) is already sufficient and no phylogenetic tree with database sequences is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects the virus present in a nanopore-sequenced sample by blasting the reconstructed consensus genomes against the VirDetector reference database (database/sequences.fasta) and taking the highest bit-score hit, then gathers all database sequences of that virus for downstream maximum-likelihood (IQ-TREE2) and Bayesian (MrBayes) phylogenetic inference. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf029
skills.summary: Selects the virus present in a nanopore-sequenced sample by blasting the reconstructed consensus genomes against the VirDetector reference database (database/sequences.fasta) and taking the highest bit-score hit, then gathers all database sequences of that virus for downstream maximum-likelihood (IQ-TREE2) and Bayesian (MrBayes) phylogenetic inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are raw reads or FAST5/POD5 that have not yet been preprocessed, classified and assembled into consensus genomes — the BLAST step starts from consensus FASTA The virus of interest is absent from the VirDetector phylogenetic database (database/sequences.fasta), since both detection and the sequence selection for tree inference depend on it A single-reference-based placement (e.g. read mapping against a known reference) is already sufficient and no phylogenetic tree with database sequences is required

skills.description: Use when de novo assembled contigs (e.g. no-target.contigs.fasta or re-assembly.contigs.fasta from Canu) must be assigned to known viral reference genomes to guide consensus assembly from untargeted nanopore reads.
skills.name: viromics-pipeline-output-structuring
skills.search_text: viromics-pipeline-output-structuring Use when de novo assembled contigs (e.g. no-target.contigs.fasta or re-assembly.contigs.fasta from Canu) must be assigned to known viral reference genomes to guide consensus assembly from untargeted nanopore reads. Input is raw nanopore FASTQ reads rather than assembled contigs — ViMOP's reference identification operates on contigs after de novo assembly, not directly on reads Viruses with no representative entry in the reference database or novel/novel-ish pathogens — contigs that match no entry cannot be assigned a reference Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) — ViMOP explicitly warns such assemblies may be inaccurate draft genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Reconstructs ViMOP's reference-identification module: each de novo assembled contig is BLAST-searched against the ViMOP_DB virus reference database, the highest-scoring hit is adopted as that contig's reference genome, and per-contig FASTA/TSV outputs are structured for downstream reference-guided assembly. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf687
skills.summary: Reconstructs ViMOP's reference-identification module: each de novo assembled contig is BLAST-searched against the ViMOP_DB virus reference database, the highest-scoring hit is adopted as that contig's reference genome, and per-contig FASTA/TSV outputs are structured for downstream reference-guided assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore FASTQ reads rather than assembled contigs — ViMOP's reference identification operates on contigs after de novo assembly, not directly on reads Viruses with no representative entry in the reference database or novel/novel-ish pathogens — contigs that match no entry cannot be assigned a reference Large DNA viruses with extensive repetitive regions (e.g. mpox) — ViMOP explicitly warns such assemblies may be inaccurate draft genomes

skills.description: Use when working with raw 2 μm bin count matrices from Visium HD (e.g., the 10X demo lung dataset) that show a striped per-bin count-total appearance caused by variable bin dimensions, prior to segmentation or cell reconstruction.
skills.name: visium-hd-bin-count-destriping
skills.search_text: visium-hd-bin-count-destriping Use when working with raw 2 μm bin count matrices from Visium HD (e.g., the 10X demo lung dataset) that show a striped per-bin count-total appearance caused by variable bin dimensions, prior to segmentation or cell reconstruction. Input is already an 8 μm bin matrix or a reconstructed cell-by-gene object — destriping targets the 2 μm bin-level striping artifact only The count matrix shows no striped per-bin total structure from variable bin dimensions; applying quantile rescaling would alter counts without benefit The goal is cell segmentation or bin-to-cell grouping (use bin2cell.stardist / bin2cell.bin_to_cell instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Corrects the striped count-total artifact in 2 μm Visium HD bins that arises from variable bin dimensions, by dividing each bin's counts by per-array-row and per-array-column 0.99 quantile factors (bin2cell.destripe) and rescaling the count matrix so corrected per-bin totals are preserved. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546
skills.summary: Corrects the striped count-total artifact in 2 μm Visium HD bins that arises from variable bin dimensions, by dividing each bin's counts by per-array-row and per-array-column 0.99 quantile factors (bin2cell.destripe) and rescaling the count matrix so corrected per-bin totals are preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an 8 μm bin matrix or a reconstructed cell-by-gene object — destriping targets the 2 μm bin-level striping artifact only The count matrix shows no striped per-bin total structure from variable bin dimensions; applying quantile rescaling would alter counts without benefit The goal is cell segmentation or bin-to-cell grouping (use bin2cell.stardist / bin2cell.bin_to_cell instead)

skills.description: Use when working with Visium HD 2 μm bin-resolution data (with a reference H&E or IF morphology image) and you need cell-level objects better than the default 8 μm bins for downstream annotation or spatial analysis.
skills.name: visium-hd-bin-to-cell-reconstruction
skills.search_text: visium-hd-bin-to-cell-reconstruction Use when working with Visium HD 2 μm bin-resolution data (with a reference H&E or IF morphology image) and you need cell-level objects better than the default 8 μm bins for downstream annotation or spatial analysis. Data are already at cell resolution (e.g. conventional single-cell RNA-seq or aggregated 8 μm bins) — bin grouping is unnecessary No reference morphology image is available and only the 8 μm output of Space Ranger is needed The task is custom probe design for Visium HD panels — use gene2probe instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Reconstructs cells from 2 μm Visium HD bins by grouping bins via morphology-image segmentation (StarDist on H&E or IF images) and/or gene-expression visualisation, after correcting the bin-dimension destriping artifact, to produce a cell-level AnnData that outperforms default 8 μm bins. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546
skills.summary: Reconstructs cells from 2 μm Visium HD bins by grouping bins via morphology-image segmentation (StarDist on H&E or IF images) and/or gene-expression visualisation, after correcting the bin-dimension destriping artifact, to produce a cell-level AnnData that outperforms default 8 μm bins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already at cell resolution (e.g. conventional single-cell RNA-seq or aggregated 8 μm bins) — bin grouping is unnecessary No reference morphology image is available and only the 8 μm output of Space Ranger is needed The task is custom probe design for Visium HD panels — use gene2probe instead

skills.description: Use when preparing Visium HD Space Ranger output (full-resolution H&E or IF tissue image plus spatial folder with scale factors) for bin2cell segmentation, because the default tissue image resolution is unsuitable for StarDist segmentation.
skills.name: visium-hd-morphology-image-rescaling
skills.search_text: visium-hd-morphology-image-rescaling Use when preparing Visium HD Space Ranger output (full-resolution H&E or IF tissue image plus spatial folder with scale factors) for bin2cell segmentation, because the default tissue image resolution is unsuitable for StarDist segmentation. The input is not Visium HD Space Ranger output with a raw full-resolution morphology image and scale factors The image is already at a controlled mpp within the 0.2–0.5 range suitable for StarDist segmentation Working with a platform lacking a reference morphology image paired to transcriptomic data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates a controlled-resolution morphology reference image for bin2cell by rescaling the raw Space Ranger Visium HD tissue image to a specified microns-per-pixel (mpp) value and cropping it to the tissue capture region, providing consistent input for downstream cell segmentation and plotting. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546
skills.summary: Generates a controlled-resolution morphology reference image for bin2cell by rescaling the raw Space Ranger Visium HD tissue image to a specified microns-per-pixel (mpp) value and cropping it to the tissue capture region, providing consistent input for downstream cell segmentation and plotting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not Visium HD Space Ranger output with a raw full-resolution morphology image and scale factors The image is already at a controlled mpp within the 0.2–0.5 range suitable for StarDist segmentation Working with a platform lacking a reference morphology image paired to transcriptomic data

skills.description: Use when training nanoHiMe emission parameters from a nanopolish eventalign file and you must iteratively reassign events to 6-mers via Viterbi decoding before EM fitting of Gaussian components.
skills.name: viterbi-iterative-kmer-realignment
skills.search_text: viterbi-iterative-kmer-realignment Use when training nanoHiMe emission parameters from a nanopolish eventalign file and you must iteratively reassign events to 6-mers via Viterbi decoding before EM fitting of Gaussian components. You need base-resolution 6mA prediction — the k-bar collapse of k-mers with 6mA at different positions means the model recognizes 6mA-containing vs non-6mA sites but cannot assign methylation to individual adenine positions You want methylation calls directly from raw signal without event alignment — this skill requires a nanopolish eventalign input, not FAST5 alone A pre-trained model covering your modification combination already suffices; retraining is only needed for new modification contexts http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 nanoHiMe trains per-6-mer emission distributions (Gaussian mixture omega/mu/sigma) by iteratively re-aligning nanopore event-level alignments to k-mers with the Viterbi algorithm and refitting the mixtures with expectation-maximization; k-mers with partially methylated adenines are collapsed to an averaged k-bar k-mer because parameters cannot be assigned position-precisely. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-35650-2
skills.summary: nanoHiMe trains per-6-mer emission distributions (Gaussian mixture omega/mu/sigma) by iteratively re-aligning nanopore event-level alignments to k-mers with the Viterbi algorithm and refitting the mixtures with expectation-maximization; k-mers with partially methylated adenines are collapsed to an averaged k-bar k-mer because parameters cannot be assigned position-precisely.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need base-resolution 6mA prediction — the k-bar collapse of k-mers with 6mA at different positions means the model recognizes 6mA-containing vs non-6mA sites but cannot assign methylation to individual adenine positions You want methylation calls directly from raw signal without event alignment — this skill requires a nanopolish eventalign input, not FAST5 alone A pre-trained model covering your modification combination already suffices; retraining is only needed for new modification contexts

skills.description: Use when benchmarking OTU recovery on post-chopSeq full-length 16S reads: cluster each mock-community FASTA directly with VSEARCH at 97% similarity to count OTUs/singletons and demonstrate whether direct clustering yields accurate richness estimates.
skills.name: vsearch-97-percent-identity-clustering
skills.search_text: vsearch-97-percent-identity-clustering Use when benchmarking OTU recovery on post-chopSeq full-length 16S reads: cluster each mock-community FASTA directly with VSEARCH at 97% similarity to count OTUs/singletons and demonstrate whether direct clustering yields accurate richness estimates. The goal is accurate OTU/richness estimation on noisy full-length nanopore reads — use the partition-based nanoClust approach instead, since direct 97% clustering is exactly the failure mode this skill demonstrates Input reads are raw un-corrected nanopore reads that have not been through chopSeq fragmentation/orientation correction and size selection Input is already an OTU table or feature table rather than FASTA reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 De novo clustering of full-length nanopore amplicon reads with VSEARCH (cluster_fast) at a 97% identity threshold to enumerate OTUs and singletons. In the NanoAmpli-Seq context it serves as a negative-control baseline showing that direct clustering of noisy full-length reads grossly inflates OTU richness. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy140
skills.summary: De novo clustering of full-length nanopore amplicon reads with VSEARCH (cluster_fast) at a 97% identity threshold to enumerate OTUs and singletons. In the NanoAmpli-Seq context it serves as a negative-control baseline showing that direct clustering of noisy full-length reads grossly inflates OTU richness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accurate OTU/richness estimation on noisy full-length nanopore reads — use the partition-based nanoClust approach instead, since direct 97% clustering is exactly the failure mode this skill demonstrates Input reads are raw un-corrected nanopore reads that have not been through chopSeq fragmentation/orientation correction and size selection Input is already an OTU table or feature table rather than FASTA reads

skills.description: Use when comparing computational cost of SV callers across the same paired-end Illumina or long-read BAM, or verifying claims that a caller (e.g. dysgu) is fastest on matched hardware.
skills.name: wall-clock-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: wall-clock-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing computational cost of SV callers across the same paired-end Illumina or long-read BAM, or verifying claims that a caller (e.g. dysgu) is fastest on matched hardware. The goal is variant-calling accuracy (precision/recall/F1), not speed — use a benchmarking framework like svbench against a GIAB truth set instead. Callers cannot be run on identical inputs and hardware (different read types, references, or thread counts), making runtime comparisons confounded. Manta is intended to be run in parallel — single-core timing under-represents its throughput ('data not shown' in the paper). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime and memory footprint of structural variant callers (dysgu, manta, delly, lumpy, nanovar) by running each on identical BAM inputs with default parameters under a wall-clock timer, then ranking callers per read type (PE vs LR). genomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac039
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime and memory footprint of structural variant callers (dysgu, manta, delly, lumpy, nanovar) by running each on identical BAM inputs with default parameters under a wall-clock timer, then ranking callers per read type (PE vs LR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is variant-calling accuracy (precision/recall/F1), not speed — use a benchmarking framework like svbench against a GIAB truth set instead. Callers cannot be run on identical inputs and hardware (different read types, references, or thread counts), making runtime comparisons confounded. Manta is intended to be run in parallel — single-core timing under-represents its throughput ('data not shown' in the paper).

skills.description: Use when comparing pipeline execution modes (piped/on-the-fly vs intermediary-file) and you need quantitative evidence — wall-clock seconds and bytes written to disk — that streaming avoids unnecessary disk I/O.
skills.name: wall-clock-runtime-measurement
skills.search_text: wall-clock-runtime-measurement Use when comparing pipeline execution modes (piped/on-the-fly vs intermediary-file) and you need quantitative evidence — wall-clock seconds and bytes written to disk — that streaming avoids unnecessary disk I/O. The goal is consensus accuracy or variant-calling fidelity rather than runtime and disk-I/O benchmarking of pipeline wiring The reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. human chromosomes) — memory scales linearly with reference length, so runtime benchmarking on such inputs may be dominated by memory constraints rather than I/O mode Only a single execution mode is available (no intermediary-file counterpart to compare against), so no disk-I/O reduction can be measured Benchmark the wall-clock time and disk bytes written of alternative pipeline wiring modes (e.g. streaming a read mapper's SAM output directly into ViralConsensus via a pipe versus writing an intermediary alignment file), using /usr/bin/time so that disk-I/O savings claims can be quantified rather than asserted. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad317
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock time and disk bytes written of alternative pipeline wiring modes (e.g. streaming a read mapper's SAM output directly into ViralConsensus via a pipe versus writing an intermediary alignment file), using /usr/bin/time so that disk-I/O savings claims can be quantified rather than asserted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is consensus accuracy or variant-calling fidelity rather than runtime and disk-I/O benchmarking of pipeline wiring The reference genome is ultra-long (e.g. human chromosomes) — memory scales linearly with reference length, so runtime benchmarking on such inputs may be dominated by memory constraints rather than I/O mode Only a single execution mode is available (no intermediary-file counterpart to compare against), so no disk-I/O reduction can be measured

skills.description: Use when comparing computational cost of tandem repeat decomposition tools (uTR vs TRF vs RepeatMasker) on simulated FASTA datasets and characterizing how error rate and average TR length drive uTR runtime.
skills.name: wall-clock-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: wall-clock-runtime-profiling Use when comparing computational cost of tandem repeat decomposition tools (uTR vs TRF vs RepeatMasker) on simulated FASTA datasets and characterizing how error rate and average TR length drive uTR runtime. The goal is prediction accuracy rather than runtime — use the check_uTR / check_RepeatMasker accuracy workflow (accuracy_uTR.txt, accuracy_RepeatMasker.txt) instead. The data are long repeat units (>20 nt) that require mTR preprocessing, not the short-unit runtime benchmark addressed here. Real long-read data is the target — the timing benchmark is defined on synthetic gendata datasets, not realdata.fasta. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarking procedure for measuring per-read wall-clock runtime of uTR against TRF and RepeatMasker on synthetic mosaic tandem repeat datasets, to reproduce the paper's finding that uTR is faster in most cases and that runtime grows with sequencing error rate and average mosaic TR length (Fig. 1C/1D trends). genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad185
skills.summary: Benchmarking procedure for measuring per-read wall-clock runtime of uTR against TRF and RepeatMasker on synthetic mosaic tandem repeat datasets, to reproduce the paper's finding that uTR is faster in most cases and that runtime grows with sequencing error rate and average mosaic TR length (Fig. 1C/1D trends).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is prediction accuracy rather than runtime — use the check_uTR / check_RepeatMasker accuracy workflow (accuracy_uTR.txt, accuracy_RepeatMasker.txt) instead. The data are long repeat units (>20 nt) that require mTR preprocessing, not the short-unit runtime benchmark addressed here. Real long-read data is the target — the timing benchmark is defined on synthetic gendata datasets, not realdata.fasta.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a streaming alignment-to-HLA-prediction pipeline (minimap2 piped into HLAminer.pl -a stream) and you need wall-clock elapsed time and maximum resident set size to compare against the protocol's reported performance envelope.
skills.name: wallclock-and-memory-benchmark-extraction
skills.search_text: wallclock-and-memory-benchmark-extraction Use when benchmarking a streaming alignment-to-HLA-prediction pipeline (minimap2 piped into HLAminer.pl -a stream) and you need wall-clock elapsed time and maximum resident set size to compare against the protocol's reported performance envelope. You need per-step profiling attribution — GNU time -v measures the whole piped command, though the article reports minimap2 dominates runtime and RAM anyway Your dataset is not a WGS long-read shotgun input (e.g. it is the MCF-7 PacBio RNA-seq demo) — runtime scales with read count, so the ~40 min / 35 GB envelope does not transfer You intend to save SAM files to disk rather than stream — the benchmark validates the streaming mode specifically and disk I/O would change the timing profile http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Profiles the streamed minimap2-to-HLAminer v1.4 workflow's wall-clock runtime and peak RAM using GNU time, to verify the protocol's reported benchmark (~40 min / up to 35 GB for a ~10x ONT WGS dataset) and confirm that minimap2 dominates resource use. genomics/v1 10.1002/cpz1.70124
skills.summary: Profiles the streamed minimap2-to-HLAminer v1.4 workflow's wall-clock runtime and peak RAM using GNU time, to verify the protocol's reported benchmark (~40 min / up to 35 GB for a ~10x ONT WGS dataset) and confirm that minimap2 dominates resource use.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-step profiling attribution — GNU time -v measures the whole piped command, though the article reports minimap2 dominates runtime and RAM anyway Your dataset is not a WGS long-read shotgun input (e.g. it is the MCF-7 PacBio RNA-seq demo) — runtime scales with read count, so the ~40 min / 35 GB envelope does not transfer You intend to save SAM files to disk rather than stream — the benchmark validates the streaming mode specifically and disk I/O would change the timing profile

skills.description: Use when comparing runtime or memory footprints of compression tools on nanopore FASTQ datasets, or when reproducing the paper's Tables 3-4 timing/memory results with 20 threads.
skills.name: wallclock-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: wallclock-runtime-profiling Use when comparing runtime or memory footprints of compression tools on nanopore FASTQ datasets, or when reproducing the paper's Tables 3-4 timing/memory results with 20 threads. The goal is compression ratio (bits per base) rather than runtime/memory resource usage Input data is not FASTQ nanopore reads, e.g. quality scores or read identifiers that NanoSpring does not compress The comparison targets reference-based compressors like RENANO rather than the reference-free tools benchmarked here http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark wall-clock time and peak memory usage of FASTQ compressors/decompressors (NanoSpring, CoLoRd, gzip, ENANO) on the paper's nanopore datasets at a fixed thread count (20 threads) to reproduce Tables 3-4 and expose resource-usage trade-offs. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-29267-8
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock time and peak memory usage of FASTQ compressors/decompressors (NanoSpring, CoLoRd, gzip, ENANO) on the paper's nanopore datasets at a fixed thread count (20 threads) to reproduce Tables 3-4 and expose resource-usage trade-offs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is compression ratio (bits per base) rather than runtime/memory resource usage Input data is not FASTQ nanopore reads, e.g. quality scores or read identifiers that NanoSpring does not compress The comparison targets reference-based compressors like RENANO rather than the reference-free tools benchmarked here

skills.description: Use when comparing computational cost (running time and peak RAM) of multiple transcriptome assemblers on large FASTQ RNA-Seq datasets, e.g. to reproduce Table 5-style resource benchmarks before choosing an assembler for big SRA libraries.
skills.name: wallclock-time-measurement-of-assembly-runs
skills.search_text: wallclock-time-measurement-of-assembly-runs Use when comparing computational cost (running time and peak RAM) of multiple transcriptome assemblers on large FASTQ RNA-Seq datasets, e.g. to reproduce Table 5-style resource benchmarks before choosing an assembler for big SRA libraries. The goal is assembly quality comparison (assembled genes/isoforms, misassemblies) rather than resource usage — use rnaQUAST-based evaluation instead of timing benchmarks Input is metatranscriptome data, which the rnaSPAdes approach was not designed or evaluated for Datasets are small simulated or low-coverage libraries where the large-scale RAM/time differences (tens to hundreds of GB) do not manifest http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark protocol for measuring wall-clock execution time and peak RAM consumption of de novo transcriptome assemblers (rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, SOAPdenovo-Trans, BinPacker, Bridger) run on the two largest RNA-Seq datasets (Human large and Arabidopsis), reproducing the resource-usage comparison of Table 5 in the rnaSPAdes paper. genomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz100
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for measuring wall-clock execution time and peak RAM consumption of de novo transcriptome assemblers (rnaSPAdes, SPAdes, Trinity, SOAPdenovo-Trans, BinPacker, Bridger) run on the two largest RNA-Seq datasets (Human large and Arabidopsis), reproducing the resource-usage comparison of Table 5 in the rnaSPAdes paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembly quality comparison (assembled genes/isoforms, misassemblies) rather than resource usage — use rnaQUAST-based evaluation instead of timing benchmarks Input is metatranscriptome data, which the rnaSPAdes approach was not designed or evaluated for Datasets are small simulated or low-coverage libraries where the large-scale RAM/time differences (tens to hundreds of GB) do not manifest

skills.description: Use when raw PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles of variable length (N x 20) must be converted into fixed-length evolutionary feature vectors for sequence-level protein classification such as DNA-binding protein detection.
skills.name: wavelet-coefficient-statistics-extraction
skills.search_text: wavelet-coefficient-statistics-extraction Use when raw PSI-BLAST PSSM profiles of variable length (N x 20) must be converted into fixed-length evolutionary feature vectors for sequence-level protein classification such as DNA-binding protein detection. The input is already a fixed-length feature table (e.g. precomputed DDE, NMBAC or PSSM-DBT .mat files) rather than variable-length PSSM profiles The analysis requires residue-level (position-resolved) rather than sequence-level features, since DWT coefficient statistics discard positional detail No PSSM profile can be generated (e.g. no PSI-BLAST or nr database available), since the whole descriptor depends on evolutionary profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Encodes a protein's PSSM evolutionary profile as 20 discrete signals and compresses each via 4-scale Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), yielding the 1040-dimension PSSM-DWT descriptor used in the iDBP-DEP DNA-binding protein predictor. genomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000006
skills.summary: Encodes a protein's PSSM evolutionary profile as 20 discrete signals and compresses each via 4-scale Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), yielding the 1040-dimension PSSM-DWT descriptor used in the iDBP-DEP DNA-binding protein predictor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a fixed-length feature table (e.g. precomputed DDE, NMBAC or PSSM-DBT .mat files) rather than variable-length PSSM profiles The analysis requires residue-level (position-resolved) rather than sequence-level features, since DWT coefficient statistics discard positional detail No PSSM profile can be generated (e.g. no PSI-BLAST or nr database available), since the whole descriptor depends on evolutionary profiles

skills.description: Use when simulating GWAS summary or individual-level data for MR method evaluation where instrument strength must be controlled or held at a specific first-stage F-statistic rather than arising from winner's-curse P-value selection.
skills.name: weak-instrument-f-statistic-evaluation
skills.search_text: weak-instrument-f-statistic-evaluation Use when simulating GWAS summary or individual-level data for MR method evaluation where instrument strength must be controlled or held at a specific first-stage F-statistic rather than arising from winner's-curse P-value selection. The goal is to study winner's-curse / P-value-selected instruments — simmrd's default simtype = 'winners' with IV_Pvalue_threshold = 5e-8 is the appropriate regime instead The task is applying MR to real observed GWAS data rather than generating simulated replicates for method evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates MR simulation replicates with instruments whose strength is pinned to a target first-stage F-statistic (e.g. F = 10) using simmrd's weak-instrument mode, enabling evaluation of MR estimators under controlled weak-IV bias. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22544
skills.summary: Generates MR simulation replicates with instruments whose strength is pinned to a target first-stage F-statistic (e.g. F = 10) using simmrd's weak-instrument mode, enabling evaluation of MR estimators under controlled weak-IV bias.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to study winner's-curse / P-value-selected instruments — simmrd's default simtype = 'winners' with IV_Pvalue_threshold = 5e-8 is the appropriate regime instead The task is applying MR to real observed GWAS data rather than generating simulated replicates for method evaluation

skills.description: Use when a putative DEL/DUP call (e.g., from Sniffles/CuteSV/SVIM/NanoVar nanopore pipelines) needs coverage-based validation: supported if coverage shift >=40% with Welch t-test p < 0.05, discarded otherwise.
skills.name: welchs-t-test-significance-testing
skills.search_text: welchs-t-test-significance-testing Use when a putative DEL/DUP call (e.g., from Sniffles/CuteSV/SVIM/NanoVar nanopore pipelines) needs coverage-based validation: supported if coverage shift >=40% with Welch t-test p < 0.05, discarded otherwise. The SVs to check are not deletions or duplications — coverage analysis can only be applied to 'some types, namely deletions and duplications' (e.g., inversions or translocations are out of scope) You need to discover SVs de novo — disCoverage 'is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions', which must come from another technique or multi-sample analysis The region has severe local coverage peaks/valleys (e.g., centromeres or >10 Mb artifact-like SVs), where coverage-based shifts do not reliably indicate copy-number changes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 disCoverage supports or discards putative deletions and duplications by comparing the coverage of the SV interval with its 1-Mb flanking surroundings using a 40% relative coverage-shift threshold and Student's t-test (Welch's approximation) implemented in R, labelling an SV as supported only when both criteria pass. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.jare.2022.10.012
skills.summary: disCoverage supports or discards putative deletions and duplications by comparing the coverage of the SV interval with its 1-Mb flanking surroundings using a 40% relative coverage-shift threshold and Student's t-test (Welch's approximation) implemented in R, labelling an SV as supported only when both criteria pass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SVs to check are not deletions or duplications — coverage analysis can only be applied to 'some types, namely deletions and duplications' (e.g., inversions or translocations are out of scope) You need to discover SVs de novo — disCoverage 'is not a variant caller and needs putative SV positions', which must come from another technique or multi-sample analysis The region has severe local coverage peaks/valleys (e.g., centromeres or >10 Mb artifact-like SVs), where coverage-based shifts do not reliably indicate copy-number changes

skills.name: wgs-read-downsampling-coverage-normalization
skills.search_text: wgs-read-downsampling-coverage-normalization Use when input BAM/CRAM files are sequenced far above the coverage needed for short-read variant calling (e.g. GIAB HG002/HG003/HG004 trio at ~300x) and the caller workflow expects ~30x WGS coverage. Input BAM/CRAM is already at or near the target coverage (e.g. the 1000 Genomes NA12878 WGS 30x sample) — subsampling would discard data needlessly The downstream caller is designed for the original high depth, e.g. when benchmarking on the full ~300x GIAB data rather than reproducing the ~30x call set Input is long-read PacBio HiFi data at typical HiFi depths — this normalization was defined for high-depth Illumina short-read trio data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Normalizes high-coverage Illumina WGS trio data (e.g. GIAB AshkenazimTrio ~300x) down to a target coverage such as ~30x with deterministic samtools subsampling, so that downstream de novo variant calling (HAT/Hare/Tortoise) operates at a comparable coverage to standard WGS benchmarks. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad775

skills.description: Use when you have an assembled transcriptome (FASTA) plus raw WGS reads (FASTQ, gzipped allowed) and need to cheaply discard reads outside the transcriptome before splice-graph or k-mer analyses, without alignment.
skills.name: wgs-read-filtering-against-transcriptome
skills.search_text: wgs-read-filtering-against-transcriptome Use when you have an assembled transcriptome (FASTA) plus raw WGS reads (FASTQ, gzipped allowed) and need to cheaply discard reads outside the transcriptome before splice-graph or k-mer analyses, without alignment. You only have raw WGS reads with no assembled transcriptome to bait the Bloom filter with You need mapping locations for the retained reads — biobloomcategorizer is faster than alignment but does not provide mapping positions The transcriptome is of poor quality or assembled from a single tissue, so filtering may discard reads from transcripts absent or fragmented in the bait set http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds a transcriptome-baited Bloom filter (biobloommaker, k=25) and uses biobloomcategorizer to discard WGS reads that do not share at least one k-mer with the assembled transcriptome, as the initial stage of EXFI's build_baited_bloom_filter module. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Builds a transcriptome-baited Bloom filter (biobloommaker, k=25) and uses biobloomcategorizer to discard WGS reads that do not share at least one k-mer with the assembled transcriptome, as the initial stage of EXFI's build_baited_bloom_filter module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw WGS reads with no assembled transcriptome to bait the Bloom filter with You need mapping locations for the retained reads — biobloomcategorizer is faster than alignment but does not provide mapping positions The transcriptome is of poor quality or assembled from a single tissue, so filtering may discard reads from transcripts absent or fragmented in the bait set

skills.description: Use when processing long reads (ONT/PacBio) from 5'-anchored 10x Genomics scRNA-seq cDNA libraries and you must recover per-read cell barcodes and 10 nt UMIs despite sequencing error and variable barcode/UMI positions.
