Input reads lack 5' softclips (e.g. 3'-anchored 10x libraries) so no barcode-UMI motif can be found within the 200 nt window Data are short-read Illumina 10x libraries where standard Cell Ranger barcode correction, not long-read alignment, is appropriate UMI-level error correction is the goal — UMIs have no whitelist and are instead collapsed downstream (e.g. starcode at Levenshtein distance 3) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assign cell barcodes and UMIs to ONT/PacBio single-cell long reads by end-to-end STAR alignment of 5'-softclip barcode-UMI candidates against an N-padded 10x Genomics barcode whitelist, tolerating ONT's higher sequencing error. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-44137-7
skills.summary: Assign cell barcodes and UMIs to ONT/PacBio single-cell long reads by end-to-end STAR alignment of 5'-softclip barcode-UMI candidates against an N-padded 10x Genomics barcode whitelist, tolerating ONT's higher sequencing error.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack 5' softclips (e.g. 3'-anchored 10x libraries) so no barcode-UMI motif can be found within the 200 nt window Data are short-read Illumina 10x libraries where standard Cell Ranger barcode correction, not long-read alignment, is appropriate UMI-level error correction is the goal — UMIs have no whitelist and are instead collapsed downstream (e.g. starcode at Levenshtein distance 3)

skills.description: Use when you have a snpEff-annotated VCF/CSV variant set from a JWES-processed sample and need coding/noncoding and per-chromosome distribution counts with percentages.

Input is a raw (unannotated) VCF lacking snpEff gene-region annotations — coding/noncoding classification cannot be made The goal is de novo variant calling or QC/trimming of FASTQ reads rather than summarizing already-called variants Sample size or variant count is so small that percentage shares per chromosome are not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Summarize snpEff-annotated variant calls from a JWES-processed WGS/WES sample by gene region (noncoding vs protein-coding) and by chromosome, producing a counts-and-percentages distribution table. This reproduces the SRR891275 analysis where 20,749 variants were split into 12,979 noncoding (~63%) and 7,770 protein-coding (~37%). genomics/v1 10.1002/2211-5463.13261

skills.description: Use when benchmarking exon/IEB prediction tools on species with a reference genome, and you need synthetic WGS reads plus a known GFF3 truth set to compute precision, recall, and F1.
skills.name: whole-genome-read-simulation
skills.search_text: whole-genome-read-simulation Use when benchmarking exon/IEB prediction tools on species with a reference genome, and you need synthetic WGS reads plus a known GFF3 truth set to compute precision, recall, and F1. The study species has no reference genome or reliable annotation — EXFI's purpose is the reference-free case, and no truth set exists to score the simulation The goal is real variant discovery rather than method benchmarking — simulated reads with a known error model will not reflect the input transcriptome quality issues seen in real samples (e.g., the single-tissue herring transcriptome) You need mapping locations, not just classification — Bloom filter classification is faster than alignment but does not provide mapping positions http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Simulates WGS reads from reference genomes (zebrafish GRCz10, human GRCh38, Ensembl release 91) with wgsim to create synthetic benchmark inputs for EXFI, whose splice graph and exon predictions can then be scored against known reference annotations. genomics/v1 10.1002/ece3.6587
skills.summary: Simulates WGS reads from reference genomes (zebrafish GRCz10, human GRCh38, Ensembl release 91) with wgsim to create synthetic benchmark inputs for EXFI, whose splice graph and exon predictions can then be scored against known reference annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study species has no reference genome or reliable annotation — EXFI's purpose is the reference-free case, and no truth set exists to score the simulation The goal is real variant discovery rather than method benchmarking — simulated reads with a known error model will not reflect the input transcriptome quality issues seen in real samples (e.g., the single-tissue herring transcriptome) You need mapping locations, not just classification — Bloom filter classification is faster than alignment but does not provide mapping positions

skills.description: Use when extending SNV-based phase blocks with ONT methylation signals: haplotagged BAM (MM/ML tags), a HapCUT2-phased VCF, and a WhatsHap GTF are available and allele-specific CpGs must be identified to assign untagged reads.
skills.name: wilcoxon-ranksum-allelic-methylation-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-ranksum-allelic-methylation-testing Use when extending SNV-based phase blocks with ONT methylation signals: haplotagged BAM (MM/ML tags), a HapCUT2-phased VCF, and a WhatsHap GTF are available and allele-specific CpGs must be identified to assign untagged reads. The input includes sex chromosomes: random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, so MethPhaser will not work on X/Y — restrict to autosomes. Coverage is below ~30X ONT reads: SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage, undermining the haplotag input to the rank sum test. The BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors — filter to primary alignments first or the test cannot run. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A statistical core of MethPhaser that applies the Wilcoxon rank sum test (p-value < 0.05) to base modification probabilities of SNV-haplotagged ONT reads to identify allele-specific (haplotype-specific) CpG methylation per phase block, which then drives methylation-based read voting and phase block bridging. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0
skills.summary: A statistical core of MethPhaser that applies the Wilcoxon rank sum test (p-value < 0.05) to base modification probabilities of SNV-haplotagged ONT reads to identify allele-specific (haplotype-specific) CpG methylation per phase block, which then drives methylation-based read voting and phase block bridging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input includes sex chromosomes: random X inactivation in females produces inconsistent haplotype methylation patterns, so MethPhaser will not work on X/Y — restrict to autosomes. Coverage is below ~30X ONT reads: SNV phasing methods (HapCUT2, WhatsHap) only work reasonably above that coverage, undermining the haplotag input to the rank sum test. The BAM contains secondary or supplementary alignments, which trigger pysam MM tag reading errors — filter to primary alignments first or the test cannot run.

The two sets of quality scores come from different, non-paired samples or projects (use an unpaired rank test instead) Inputs are already aggregated project-level counts rather than paired per-sample scores, since pairing information is required http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Non-parametric statistical test applied to paired per-sample metagenomic binning quality scores to determine whether one binner (SemiBin2) significantly outperforms another (SemiBin1 or VAMB) across the same samples. genomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad209

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data contain multiple cells per individual/sample and you must decide per gene whether random effects are needed in the mean and/or zero-inflation components before final differential expression inference.
skills.name: within-sample-correlation-assessment
skills.search_text: within-sample-correlation-assessment Use when scRNA-seq count data contain multiple cells per individual/sample and you must decide per gene whether random effects are needed in the mean and/or zero-inflation components before final differential expression inference. Genes already determined (or assumed) to require random effects under a fixed specification — set adhoc=FALSE and specify mean_re/zi_re directly instead of screening. Gene set testing with twosigmag: the README states the ad hoc procedure is not recommended because a common gene-level null is broken when some genes have random effects and others do not. Data with a single sample/individual per condition (no replicate individuals), where a sample-level ANOVA or variance component is not estimable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Determines, gene by gene, whether within-sample (individual-level) correlation in scRNA-seq counts requires random intercepts in a TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial model, via the ad hoc Pearson-residual ANOVA F-test screen and/or formal likelihood-ratio tests of variance components using test.vc.twosigma. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Determines, gene by gene, whether within-sample (individual-level) correlation in scRNA-seq counts requires random intercepts in a TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial model, via the ad hoc Pearson-residual ANOVA F-test screen and/or formal likelihood-ratio tests of variance components using test.vc.twosigma.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes already determined (or assumed) to require random effects under a fixed specification — set adhoc=FALSE and specify mean_re/zi_re directly instead of screening. Gene set testing with twosigmag: the README states the ad hoc procedure is not recommended because a common gene-level null is broken when some genes have random effects and others do not. Data with a single sample/individual per condition (no replicate individuals), where a sample-level ANOVA or variance component is not estimable.

skills.description: Use when running miRPursuit on sRNA fasta/fastq libraries and you must set or adjust workbench filtering parameters (min_length=18, max_length=26, min_abundance=5, trrna=true) before genome mapping.
skills.name: workbench-config-parameter-application
skills.search_text: workbench-config-parameter-application Use when running miRPursuit on sRNA fasta/fastq libraries and you must set or adjust workbench filtering parameters (min_length=18, max_length=26, min_abundance=5, trrna=true) before genome mapping. skills.search_text: z-score-feature-scaling-for-mti-data Use when feature-level MTI single-cell data (e.g., PRAD-CyCIF .h5ad from Zenodo record 16383766) must be scaled to comparable per-marker ranges prior to kNN graph building (e.g., 50 neighbors), Leiden clustering, or UMAP visualization. The input has uncorrected batch effects and the goal is batch correction: Z-score scaling does not mitigate batch-driven sample separation (the paper shows it is outperformed by UniFORM on kBET, silhouette, and clustering metrics) The data are pixel-level MTI (OME-TIFF) images or mIHC chromogenic data: UniFORM's feature-level pipeline and this scaling workflow target feature-level (per-cell) data, and mIHC non-linear signal amplification falls outside scope The analysis targets marker intensity distributions themselves (e.g., distribution alignment checks), where scaling would distort the raw intensity scales being compared Z-score scaling of marker intensity features in multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) AnnData objects to place all markers on a comparable scale before kNN graph construction, Leiden clustering, and UMAP. In the UniFORM paper this step is applied to both raw and UniFORM-normalized PRAD-CyCIF feature data to make before/after clustering comparisons fair. genomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101172
skills.summary: Z-score scaling of marker intensity features in multiplex tissue imaging (MTI) AnnData objects to place all markers on a comparable scale before kNN graph construction, Leiden clustering, and UMAP. In the UniFORM paper this step is applied to both raw and UniFORM-normalized PRAD-CyCIF feature data to make before/after clustering comparisons fair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input has uncorrected batch effects and the goal is batch correction: Z-score scaling does not mitigate batch-driven sample separation (the paper shows it is outperformed by UniFORM on kBET, silhouette, and clustering metrics) The data are pixel-level MTI (OME-TIFF) images or mIHC chromogenic data: UniFORM's feature-level pipeline and this scaling workflow target feature-level (per-cell) data, and mIHC non-linear signal amplification falls outside scope The analysis targets marker intensity distributions themselves (e.g., distribution alignment checks), where scaling would distort the raw intensity scales being compared

skills.description: Use when building simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks that require excess zeros plus overdispersed counts with within-sample correlation, mirroring the TWO-SIGMA simulation design (10 individuals x 1000 cells, ZINB with random effects).
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-data-generation
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-data-generation Use when building simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks that require excess zeros plus overdispersed counts with within-sample correlation, mirroring the TWO-SIGMA simulation design (10 individuals x 1000 cells, ZINB with random effects). Input is already real scRNA-seq count data that needs model fitting rather than simulated data generation The analysis requires hurdle/log-scale models (e.g. MAST-style) rather than zero-inflated negative binomial counts on the observed scale Only bulk RNA-seq data without drop-out or within-sample correlation is being simulated — a simpler NB model suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the TWO-SIGMA paper's simulation of zero-inflated negative binomial scRNA-seq count data with random effects, using the simulate_zero_inflated_nb_random_effect_data function from the twosigma R package to generate per-gene counts under specified drop-out and overdispersion parameters. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Reproduces the TWO-SIGMA paper's simulation of zero-inflated negative binomial scRNA-seq count data with random effects, using the simulate_zero_inflated_nb_random_effect_data function from the twosigma R package to generate per-gene counts under specified drop-out and overdispersion parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already real scRNA-seq count data that needs model fitting rather than simulated data generation The analysis requires hurdle/log-scale models (e.g. MAST-style) rather than zero-inflated negative binomial counts on the observed scale Only bulk RNA-seq data without drop-out or within-sample correlation is being simulated — a simpler NB model suffices

skills.description: Use when raw non-negative integer scRNA-seq counts (gene x cell matrix) must be modeled with excess zeros and overdispersion, while controlling cell-level/subject-level covariates and accommodating within-sample correlation across cells from the same individual.
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixed-model-fitting
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixed-model-fitting Use when raw non-negative integer scRNA-seq counts (gene x cell matrix) must be modeled with excess zeros and overdispersion, while controlling cell-level/subject-level covariates and accommodating within-sample correlation across cells from the same individual. Input counts are already normalized or transformed — the package expects raw non-negative integer counts and performs no normalization itself The goal is a set-level or contrast-matrix test rather than per-gene model fitting — use twosigmag instead (contrast-matrix support in twosigma_custom was noted as ongoing in the README) Genes are being pooled for competitive gene set testing where the ad hoc procedure is explicitly not recommended, since a common gene-level null is unclear when some genes have random effects and others do not http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits the TWO-SIGMA two-component zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model (logistic drop-out component + log-linear negative binomial conditional-mean component, each with optional sample-level random intercepts) to per-gene scRNA-seq counts using the twosigma R package's glmmTMB backend. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Fits the TWO-SIGMA two-component zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model (logistic drop-out component + log-linear negative binomial conditional-mean component, each with optional sample-level random intercepts) to per-gene scRNA-seq counts using the twosigma R package's glmmTMB backend.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input counts are already normalized or transformed — the package expects raw non-negative integer counts and performs no normalization itself The goal is a set-level or contrast-matrix test rather than per-gene model fitting — use twosigmag instead (contrast-matrix support in twosigma_custom was noted as ongoing in the README) Genes are being pooled for competitive gene set testing where the ad hoc procedure is explicitly not recommended, since a common gene-level null is unclear when some genes have random effects and others do not

skills.description: Use when analyzing raw (unnormalized) scRNA-seq count matrices with excess zeros and overdispersion, especially when cells are clustered within samples and covariate association testing (e.g., disease status) must account for within-sample correlation.
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixed-modeling
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixed-modeling Use when analyzing raw (unnormalized) scRNA-seq count matrices with excess zeros and overdispersion, especially when cells are clustered within samples and covariate association testing (e.g., disease status) must account for within-sample correlation. Input is log-transformed or otherwise normalized data — TWO-SIGMA models observed counts directly and performs no normalization Only a two-group comparison with no repeated measures, covariates, or within-sample correlation is needed — simpler DE tools such as SCDE, scDD, or MAST may suffice Gene set testing where some genes get random effects and others do not — the ad hoc procedure is explicitly not recommended for twosigmag because a common gene-level null is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit the TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial mixed-effects model to raw scRNA-seq counts, modeling drop-out via mixed-effects logistic regression and conditional mean via mixed-effects log-linear negative binomial regression using glmmTMB. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Fit the TWO-SIGMA zero-inflated negative binomial mixed-effects model to raw scRNA-seq counts, modeling drop-out via mixed-effects logistic regression and conditional mean via mixed-effects log-linear negative binomial regression using glmmTMB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is log-transformed or otherwise normalized data — TWO-SIGMA models observed counts directly and performs no normalization Only a two-group comparison with no repeated measures, covariates, or within-sample correlation is needed — simpler DE tools such as SCDE, scDD, or MAST may suffice Gene set testing where some genes get random effects and others do not — the ad hoc procedure is explicitly not recommended for twosigmag because a common gene-level null is required

skills.description: Use when raw integer scRNA-seq count data exhibit excess zeros and overdispersion, cells are nested within samples (within-sample correlation), and inference is needed on covariates such as a binary disease status beyond a two-group comparison.
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression Use when raw integer scRNA-seq count data exhibit excess zeros and overdispersion, cells are nested within samples (within-sample correlation), and inference is needed on covariates such as a binary disease status beyond a two-group comparison. Input is log-normalized or otherwise transformed expression (e.g. MAST-style log-scale input) — twosigma expects raw integer counts and performs no normalization itself The data are bulk RNA-seq or otherwise lack within-sample cell correlation — bulk pipelines like DESeq2 or edgeR are the appropriate alternative, and the random-effect machinery buys nothing The goal is competitive gene set testing where only some genes get random effects — the ad hoc procedure is explicitly not recommended there because the common gene-level null hypothesis is then unclear http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Fit the TWO-SIGMA two-component zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model to raw scRNA-seq counts per gene: a mixed-effects logistic regression for drop-out probability and a mixed-effects log-linear negative binomial regression for the conditional mean, both fitted with glmmTMB and admitting sample-level random intercepts. genomics/v1 10.1002/gepi.22361
skills.summary: Fit the TWO-SIGMA two-component zero-inflated negative binomial mixed model to raw scRNA-seq counts per gene: a mixed-effects logistic regression for drop-out probability and a mixed-effects log-linear negative binomial regression for the conditional mean, both fitted with glmmTMB and admitting sample-level random intercepts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is log-normalized or otherwise transformed expression (e.g. MAST-style log-scale input) — twosigma expects raw integer counts and performs no normalization itself The data are bulk RNA-seq or otherwise lack within-sample cell correlation — bulk pipelines like DESeq2 or edgeR are the appropriate alternative, and the random-effect machinery buys nothing The goal is competitive gene set testing where only some genes get random effects — the ad hoc procedure is explicitly not recommended there because the common gene-level null hypothesis is then unclear

skills.description: Use when preparing sparse single-cell isoform count matrices — especially after balancing/downsampling cell numbers across groups — for differential isoform usage (DIU) testing with DESeq2 or edgeR via acorde.
skills.name: zinbave-zero-inflation-weighting
skills.search_text: zinbave-zero-inflation-weighting Use when preparing sparse single-cell isoform count matrices — especially after balancing/downsampling cell numbers across groups — for differential isoform usage (DIU) testing with DESeq2 or edgeR via acorde. The input is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated pseudo-bulk counts, where zero inflation is not the dominant sparsity mechanism and ZinBWaVE weighting is unnecessary. The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than isoform-level differential isoform usage (DIU) within the acorde pipeline. The count matrix has already been weighted or the analysis plan does not include DESeq2/edgeR testing that can consume weights. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies ZinBWaVE zero-inflated Gaussian-model weights to single-cell isoform-level count matrices (e.g. the Tasic et al. Smart-Seq2 mouse visual cortex dataset) so that DIU testing with DESeq2 or edgeR in the acorde workflow accounts for excess zeros introduced by scRNA-seq sparsity and downsampling. genomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-29497-w
skills.summary: Applies ZinBWaVE zero-inflated Gaussian-model weights to single-cell isoform-level count matrices (e.g. the Tasic et al. Smart-Seq2 mouse visual cortex dataset) so that DIU testing with DESeq2 or edgeR in the acorde workflow accounts for excess zeros introduced by scRNA-seq sparsity and downsampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated pseudo-bulk counts, where zero inflation is not the dominant sparsity mechanism and ZinBWaVE weighting is unnecessary. The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than isoform-level differential isoform usage (DIU) within the acorde pipeline. The count matrix has already been weighted or the analysis plan does not include DESeq2/edgeR testing that can consume weights.
